3. Nitivakyamrita was written by Kundakundacharya.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
26.x: Statement 1 is correct: Samayasara, Pravachanasara and Panchastikaya are Kundakundacharya's works. Statement 2 is correct: Somadeva Suri was called 'Syadvadachala Simha' and wrote Yasastilaka Champu. Statement 3 is wrong: Nitivakyamrita is also by Somadeva Suri. So '1 only' is incomplete and options including 3 are wrong.
26.tq: Two traps: preacher of Syadvada = Kundakundacharya; title 'Syadvadachala Simha' and Nitivakyamrita = Somadeva Suri.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: **Kundakundacharya**, a **Digambara** philosopher, wrote **Samayasara, Pravachanasara, Panchastikaya**.
Statement 2 is correct: **Somadeva Suri** = "**Syadvadachala Simha**", author of **Yasastilaka Champu**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Nitivakyamrita** is also by **Somadeva Suri**.
xa: ⚠ "Preacher of Syadvada" = **Kundakundacharya** (APPSC 2008); "title Syadvadachala Simha" = **Somadeva Suri** (APPSC 2011).
**Syadvada** = conditioned predication.

26.s:
Match the philosophical school with its associated doctrine and select the correct answer using the code given below:

List-I (School)
a. Jainism
b. Buddhism
c. Ajivikas
d. Charvaka

List-II (Associated doctrine)
i. Materialism
ii. Anatta and pratityasamutpada
iii. Anekantavada, Syadvada and Nayavada
iv. Niyati or fate
26.x: Jainism is associated with Anekantavada, Syadvada and Nayavada; Buddhism with anatta and pratityasamutpada; Ajivikas with niyati; and Charvaka with materialism.
26.tq: Use school-specific doctrinal markers and eliminate the reversed philosophical associations.
xs: **Jainism – Anekantavada/Syadvada/Nayavada**, **Buddhism – anatta, pratityasamutpada**, **Ajivikas – niyati**, **Charvaka – materialism** — option **(1) a–iii, b–ii, c–iv, d–i**.
These are the contrasts the notes draw with other schools.
xa: Ajivika founder of note: **Makkhali Gosala**, once Mahavira's companion.
Jainism and Buddhism both **reject Vedic authority** and accept **karma and rebirth**.
Buddhism follows the **Middle Way**; Jainism **extreme asceticism**.

26.s: Who among the following is answered as the preacher of Syadvada?
26.x: Kundakundacharya, the great Digambara philosopher, is the answer for 'who preached Syadvada' (APPSC 2008). Somadeva Suri only bore the title 'Syadvadachala Simha' (the trap), Makkhali Gosala taught Ajivika niyati, and Bhadrabahu is linked with taking Jainism south.
26.tq: Preacher = Kundakunda; title = Somadeva.
xs: The "**preacher of Syadvada**" = **Kundakundacharya** — option **(2)** is correct (APPSC 2008).
⚠ **Somadeva Suri** only bore the **title** "**Syadvadachala Simha**" — the trap.
**Makkhali Gosala** taught Ajivika **niyati**; **Bhadrabahu** took Jainism south with Chandragupta.
xa: Kundakundacharya was a great **Digambara** philosopher: **Samayasara, Pravachanasara, Panchastikaya**.
Somadeva Suri wrote **Yasastilaka Champu** and **Nitivakyamrita**.
Syadvada: **syat** = "may be".

26.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

List-I (Practice)
a. Paryushana
b. Samvatsari
c. Pratikramana
d. Sallekhana

List-II (Association)
i. Introspection
 ii. Ritual fast unto death
 iii. Jain festival
 iv. Day of forgiveness

Which of the following is the correct combination?
26.x: Paryushana is the Jain festival, its last day Samvatsari is the day of forgiveness, Pratikramana is introspection, and Sallekhana is the ritual fast unto death.
26.tq: Start from the sure pair and complete the one-to-one matching.
xs: **Paryushana – Jain festival**, **Samvatsari – forgiveness day**, **Pratikramana – introspection**, **Sallekhana – fast unto death** — option **(1) a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii**.
**Samvatsari** is the **last day** of Paryushana.
xa: Tirthankara idols: **Padmasana** or **Kayotsarga**.
Sallekhana is a **Jain** practice — not Buddhist, Sufi or Parsi.
Chandragupta Maurya performed it at **Shravanabelagola**.

26.s: The images of Tirthankaras are traditionally shown in which of the following postures?
26.x: Jina images are commonly represented in Padmasana or in the standing Kayotsarga posture.
26.tq: Distinguish Jain image postures from Buddhist hand gestures and other sculptural forms.
xs: Tirthankara/Jina idols are shown in **Padmasana or Kayotsarga** — option **(1)** is correct.
The other postures are not Jain idol postures in the notes.
xa: **Paryushana** ends with **Samvatsari** (forgiveness day).
**Pratikramana** = introspection ritual.
**Digambara** monks are unclothed.

26.s:
Consider the following statements about Jain practice:
1. Jain householders observe milder vows called Anuvratas, which include non-adultery.
2. Strict Jain followers took up agriculture because it involved no injury to living beings.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
26.x: Statement 1 is correct: householders follow the milder Anuvratas (non-injury, non-stealing, non-adultery, truth, non-possession) and give cooked food to the needy. Statement 2 is wrong: because ahimsa extends to all life, strict followers avoided agriculture, which is why Jains came to have a trading base. So 1 only.
26.tq: Ahimsa to all life -> no farming -> trade.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: householders observe milder **Anuvratas** — non-injury, non-stealing, **non-adultery**, truth, non-possession.
Statement 2 is wrong: since **ahimsa** extends to all life forms, strict followers **avoided agriculture** — hence their **trading base**.
xa: Householders also give daily **charity of cooked food** to the needy.
Monks take the **Five Mahavratas**: **Ahimsa**, **Satya**, **Brahmacharya**, **Asteya**, **Aparigraha**.
**Sallekhana / Santhara** = ritual **fast unto death**; Chandragupta Maurya performed it at **Shravanabelagola**.
**Paryushana** ends with **Samvatsari** (forgiveness day); **Pratikramana** = introspection ritual.

26.s: Chandragupta Maurya is traditionally associated with which Jain practice at Shravanabelagola?
26.x: Chandragupta Maurya is traditionally said to have performed Sallekhana at Shravanabelagola.
26.tq: Match a historical personality with the distinctive practice associated with him.
xs: **Chandragupta Maurya** performed **Sallekhana** at **Shravanabelagola** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Kayotsarga** is an idol posture; **Pratikramana** is introspection; **Samvatsari** is forgiveness day.
xa: Sallekhana / **Santhara** = **ritual fast unto death** to purify karma.
The **Bhadrabahu-Chandragupta** route to Shravanabelagola ran through **Rayalaseema**.
"Santhara ... amongst - **Jains**" (APPSC G2 2017).

26.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Jain vows:
1. The four vows of Ahimsa, Satya, Asteya and Aparigraha were taught by Parshvanatha.
2. Mahavira added Aparigraha as the fifth vow.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
26.x: Statement 1 is correct: the four vows (chaturyama) - Ahimsa, Satya, Asteya, Aparigraha - were taught by Parshvanatha. Statement 2 is wrong: Aparigraha was already among the four; the fifth vow added by Mahavira was Brahmacharya (celibacy). Hence '1 only'.
26.tq: Four from Parshvanatha, fifth (Brahmacharya) from Mahavira.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: the four vows (**chaturyama**) — **Ahimsa, Satya, Asteya, Aparigraha** — were taught by **Parshvanatha**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Aparigraha** was already among the four; Mahavira added **Brahmacharya** (celibacy).
xa: ⚠ 4 vows = **Parshvanatha**; 5th (**Brahmacharya**) = **Mahavira**.
Householders keep milder **Anuvratas**.
Parshvanatha's followers **wore white**.

26.s: 'Santhara' is a ritual of fasting to death practised amongst the:
26.x: Santhara (Sallekhana) is a Jain ritual fast unto death at the end of life to purify karma (APPSC G2 2017). It is not a Buddhist, Sufi or Parsi practice.
26.tq: Santhara = Sallekhana = Jain.
xs: **Santhara** is a ritual fast to death among the **Jains** — option **(2)** is correct (APPSC G2 2017).
It is **not** Buddhist, Sufi or Parsi.
xa: Santhara = **Sallekhana** — **fast unto death** at life's end to purify karma.
**Chandragupta Maurya** performed it at **Shravanabelagola**.
**Paryushana**'s last day **Samvatsari** = forgiveness day.

26.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Jainism and Buddhism:
1. Jainism accepts the existence of an eternal soul, whereas Buddhism teaches anatta.
2. Jain karma is understood as material bondage, whereas Buddhist karma is associated with intention.
3. Both religions accept karma and rebirth.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
26.x: Jainism regards the soul as eternal and karma as material bondage. Buddhism teaches anatta and intention-based karma; both traditions accept karma and rebirth.
26.tq: Use the comparison-table method by checking each doctrine separately before selecting the coded combination.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: Jainism has an **eternal soul (jiva)**; Buddhism teaches **anatta**.
Statement 2: Jain karma = **material bondage**; Buddhist karma = **intention-based**.
Statement 3: both accept **karma and rebirth**.
xa: Penance: Jainism = **extreme asceticism**; Buddhism = **Middle Way**.
Texts: Jain **Agamas (Ardhamagadhi)**; Buddhist **Tripitaka (Pali)**.
Spread: Jainism **limited to India**; Buddhism **spread abroad**.

26.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Jainism — stricter practice of ahimsa, including in thought
Buddhism — severe self-mortification as the ideal
Buddhism — ahimsa stricter than the Jain practice
26.x: Jainism follows a stricter interpretation of ahimsa, extending even to thought. Buddhism follows the Middle Way and treats ahimsa as important but comparatively less strict.
26.tq: Test the reversed-comparison trap by distinguishing Jain austerity and ahimsa from the Buddhist Middle Way.
xs: **Jainism** practises a **stricter ahimsa**, **even in thought** — option **(1)** is correct.
The **Middle Way** avoiding extremes belongs to **Buddhism**, not Jainism.
**Severe self-mortification** is the **Jain** ideal; Buddhist ahimsa is **important but less strict**.
xa: Jain ahimsa extends to **all life forms** → vegetarianism, a **strict diet**.
Jain penance = **extreme asceticism**.
Ahimsa later **shaped Gandhi's philosophy**.

26.s:
With reference to the monastic practices and texts of Jainism and Buddhism, consider the following statements:
1. Digambara Jain monks traditionally remain unclothed.
2. Buddhist monks wear saffron robes.
3. Jain canonical texts are known as the Agamas and are associated with Ardhamagadhi.
4. The Buddhist canonical collection is the Tripitaka, written in Pali.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
26.x: All four statements correctly describe the monastic traditions and textual languages or collections associated with Jainism and Buddhism.
26.tq: Verify each religion-text and religion-monastic pair instead of relying on one familiar association.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Digambara** monks are **unclothed**; Buddhist monks wear **saffron robes**.
Jain texts = **Agamas (Ardhamagadhi)**; Buddhist texts = **Tripitaka (Pali)**.
xa: Goal: Jainism = **Kevala jnana**; Buddhism = **Nirvana/Buddhahood**.
Both used **Prakrit/Pali** and had **monastic orders for men and women**.
The **Digambara-Svetambara split** contributed to Jainism's decline.

26.s: Which of the following correctly expresses a doctrinal difference between Jainism and Buddhism?
o: Jainism spread widely abroad, whereas Buddhism remained confined to India.
Jainism associates liberation with kevala jnana, while Buddhism associates it with nirvana or Buddhahood.
Buddhism accepts an eternal soul in all things, while Jainism teaches anatta.
Jainism alone accepts karma and rebirth, while Buddhism rejects both.
26.x: Jainism uses the concept of kevala jnana, while Buddhism refers to nirvana or Buddhahood. Buddhism, unlike Jainism, spread extensively outside India.
26.tq: Identify the reversed doctrinal and geographical comparisons before choosing the precise distinction.
xs: Jainism's goal is **kevala jnana**; Buddhism's is **nirvana / Buddhahood** — option **(2)** is correct.
Option **(1)** reverses the spread: Jainism stayed **limited to India**, Buddhism **spread abroad**.
Option **(3)** reverses the soul doctrine: Jainism = **eternal soul**, Buddhism = **anatta**.
Option **(4)** fails: **both** accept **karma and rebirth**.
xa: Jain karma = **material bondage**; Buddhist karma = **intention-based**.
Both **reject Vedic authority** and are **non-theistic**.

26.s:
Consider the following statements about Jain centres in Andhra:
1. Kharavela built a Jain vihara near Vaddamanu.
2. The Jain basadi at Vaddamanu (Vardhamanapuram) was built by the Rashtrakuta ruler Indra III.
3. Danavulapadu, at Jammalamadugu in YSR Kadapa, was a Jain kshetra built by Rashtrakuta Indra III.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
26.x: Statement 2 is wrong: the basadi at Vaddamanu in Guntur was built by Samprati, Ashoka's grandson, in Mahavira's name. Statement 1 is correct: Kharavela also built a vihara near it. Statement 3 is correct: Danavulapadu was built by Indra III. So 1 and 3 only.
26.tq: Vaddamanu = Samprati (+ Kharavela); Danavulapadu = Indra III.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Kharavela** also built a Jain vihara near **Vaddamanu**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the basadi at **Vaddamanu** (Guntur) was built by **Samprati**, Ashoka's grandson, in Mahavira's name.
Statement 3 is correct: **Danavulapadu** (Jammalamadugu, YSR Kadapa) was built by Rashtrakuta **Indra III**.
xa: **Samprati** is called the "**Ashoka of Jainism**".
**Rayalaseema** (Kurnool-Anantapur) was a **Jain corridor** — the **Bhadrabahu-Chandragupta** route to Shravanabelagola.
**Early Kakatiyas were Jains** (APPSC G2 **2011**) — confirmed by **Siddeshwara Charitra**.
**Mahapadma Nanda** is said to have conquered Andhra and propagated Jainism.

26.s: Mahapadma Nanda is said to have contributed to the history of Jainism in Andhra by
o: building a Jain kshetra at Danavulapadu
constructing caves in the Nallamala hills
26.x: Mahapadma Nanda is said to have conquered Andhra and propagated Jainism there. The other activities are associated with different persons or developments.
26.tq: Identify the ruler's deed and avoid the swapped-patron trap.
xs: **Mahapadma Nanda** is said to have **conquered Andhra and propagated Jainism** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Danavulapadu** was built by Rashtrakuta **Indra III**; the **Nallamala** caves are ascetic caves of Rayalaseema.
xa: **Early Kakatiyas were Jains** (APPSC G2 2011).
**Samprati** built a basadi at **Vaddamanu** in Mahavira's name.
Rayalaseema (**Kurnool-Anantapur**) = **Jain corridor**.

26.s: Rayalaseema is described as a Jain corridor primarily because
o: the capital of the Rashtrakutas was located there
the Buddhist route from Sarnath to Bodh Gaya passed through the region
the Bhadrabahu–Chandragupta route to Shravanabelagola passed through Kurnool and Anantapur
all Jain Tirthankaras were born in Rayalaseema
26.x: The Bhadrabahu–Chandragupta route to Shravanabelagola passed through Kurnool and Anantapur, supporting the description of Rayalaseema as a Jain corridor.
26.tq: Follow the route-based clue and distinguish it from unsupported origin and capital claims.
xs: The **Bhadrabahu–Chandragupta** route to **Shravanabelagola** passed through **Kurnool and Anantapur** — option **(3)** is correct.
That is why **Rayalaseema** is called a **Jain corridor**.
xa: **Erramala and Nallamala** hills hold **ascetic caves**.
**Chandragupta Maurya** performed **Sallekhana** at Shravanabelagola.
**Sheetalanatha** (10th) is traditionally placed at **Bhadrachalam (Badalpuri)**.

26.s:
Consider the following statements about the early Kakatiyas:
1. They were Jains in their early phase.
2. Their overlords included the Rashtrakutas and Kalyani Chalukyas, who were Jains.
3. Siddeshwara Charitra confirms their Jain association.
4. Prolaraju's Hanamkonda inscription begins with a Jain prayer.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
26.x: All four statements describe the Jain association of the early Kakatiyas, their overlords, the literary evidence and Prolaraju's Hanamkonda inscription.
26.tq: Check political, literary and epigraphic evidence together before selecting the complete combination.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
The **early Kakatiyas were Jains** (APPSC G2 2011); their overlords, the **Rashtrakutas** and **Kalyani Chalukyas**, were Jains.
**Siddeshwara Charitra** confirms it; **Prolaraju's Hanamkonda inscription** begins with a **Jain prayer**.
xa: Rashtrakuta **Indra III** built the Jain kshetra at **Danavulapadu**.
The Jain early-Kakatiya phase recurs in **APPSC AP History**.
**Vaddamanu** (Guntur) had **Samprati**'s basadi.

26.s: Anekantavada is significant in modern ethical and social thought because it is regarded as a basis for
o: exclusive adherence to one philosophical doctrine
tolerance, pluralism and acceptance of multiple viewpoints
rejection of all forms of non-violence
26.x: Anekantavada recognises the many-sided nature of reality and is therefore cited as a basis of pluralism and tolerance.
26.tq: Apply the philosophical principle to a social situation rather than treating it as a mere technical term.
xs: **Anekantavada** = basis of **pluralism and tolerance** — option **(2)** is correct.
It holds that reality is **many-sided** and truth has **many facets**.
xa: **Syadvada** = **conditioned predication** (syat = "may be").
**Nayavada** = theory of **partial standpoints**.
"Preacher of Syadvada" = **Kundakundacharya** (APPSC 2008).

26.s: Which of the following factors contributed to the limited mass appeal and later decline of Jainism?
o: Severe austerities, loss of royal patronage and the Digambara–Svetambara split
Complete absence of monastic institutions and rejection of ahimsa
Exclusive dependence on overseas expansion and maritime trade
Acceptance of Vedic sacrifice and Brahmana supremacy
26.x: Jainism's severe austerities limited its mass appeal, while loss of royal patronage and the Digambara–Svetambara split contributed to its later decline.
26.tq: Select the option that combines the stated social, political and sectarian causes without reversing Jain doctrine.
xs: **Severe austerities** limited mass appeal; **loss of royal patronage** and the **Digambara–Svetambara split** caused decline — option **(1)** is correct.
Jainism had **monastic orders** and upheld **ahimsa**, so option **(2)** fails.
Jainism **rejected Vedic sacrifice** and **Brahmana supremacy**, so option **(4)** fails.
xa: Jainism stayed **limited to India**, unlike Buddhism.
**Digambara** monks are unclothed.
Mahavir Jayanti coverage (**Apr 2025**) revisited the five vows and **Sallekhana**.

26.s:
Match the Jain figure with the correct description:

List-I
(a) Rishabhdev
(b) Parshvanath
(c) Mahavira
(d) Mahaprajapati

List-II
(i) 24th and last Tirthankara
(ii) First Tirthankara
(iii) 23rd Tirthankara
(iv) First woman to enter the Buddhist Sangha
26.x: Rishabhdev was the first Tirthankara, Parshvanath the 23rd, Mahavira the 24th and last, and Mahaprajapati the first woman to enter the Buddhist Sangha, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv.
26.tq: Recall the place of each Tirthankara.
n: Mahaprajapati was the first woman to enter the Sangha. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Jainism recognizes 24 Tirthankaras. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Rishabhdev was also called Adinath. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Rishabhdev was the first Tirthankara. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Parshvanath was the twenty-third Tirthankara. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Mahavira was the twenty-fourth Tirthankara. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Mahavira was the last Tirthankara. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
xs: The correct match is **a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Rishabhdev** = **First Tirthankara**; **Parshvanath** = **23rd Tirthankara**.
**Mahavira** = **24th and last Tirthankara**; **Mahaprajapati** = **first woman** to enter the **Buddhist Sangha**.
xa: **Rishabhdev** is also called **Adinath**; symbol **Bull**; born at **Ayodhya**.
**Parshvanath**'s symbol is the **Serpent**; he **taught four restraints**; born **Varanasi**.
**Mahavira**'s symbol is the **Lion**; nirvana at **Pavapuri** in **527 BCE**.
⚠ **Mahaprajapati** is a Buddhist figure — the Buddha's **foster-mother**, not a Jain.

26.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Mahavira attained Kaivalya at Jrimbhik village on the bank of the Rijupalika River.
II. Mahavira attained Nirvana at Pavapuri in 527 BCE.
III. Parshvanath attained Nirvana at Sammed Shikhar.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
26.x: I, II and III are correct: Mahavira attained Kaivalya at Jrimbhik village on the Rijupalika, and Nirvana at Pavapuri in 527 BCE; Parshvanath attained Nirvana at Sammed Shikhar.
26.tq: Check each place and date separately.
n: Mahavira attained Kaivalya at Jrimbhik village. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Mahavira attained Kaivalya near the Rijupalika River. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Mahavira attained Nirvana at Pavapuri. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Mahavira's Nirvana occurred in 527 BCE. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Parshvanath attained Nirvana at Sammed Shikhar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
xs: All three statements **I, II and III** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
I: Mahavira attained **Kaivalya** at **Jrimbhik village** near the **Rijupalika River**.
II: Mahavira attained **Nirvana** at **Pavapuri** (near Rajgir, Bihar) in **527 BCE**.
III: **Parshvanath** attained **Nirvana** at **Sammed Shikhar** (Shikharji / Parasnath hill, Jharkhand).
xa: Mahavira was **born** at **Kundagram** near **Vaishali**.
**Neminatha** (22nd) attained nirvana at **Girnar**; **Rishabhadeva** at **Mount Kailash**.
**Munisuvrata** (20th) also attained nirvana at **Sammed Shikhar**.
⚠ Some notes give Mahavira's death as **c. 468 BC**; traditional date **527 BCE**.

26.s:
Consider the following statements:

I. Parshvanath taught four restraints.
II. Asteya is one of the Five Mahavratas.
III. Asteya denotes non-possession.
IV. Parshvanath was the 24th Tirthankara.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
26.x: I and II are correct: Parshvanath taught four restraints, and Asteya (non-stealing) is a Mahavrata. III is false because non-possession is Aparigraha, and IV is false because Parshvanath was the 23rd Tirthankara.
26.tq: Check each statement separately.
n: Parshvanath taught four restraints. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Asteya is one of the Five Mahavratas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
xs: Statements **I and II only** are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
I is correct: **Parshvanath** taught **four restraints** (chaturyama).
II is correct: **Asteya** is one of the **Five Mahavratas**.
III is wrong: non-possession is **Aparigraha**, not Asteya.
IV is wrong: Parshvanath was the **23rd** Tirthankara; **Mahavira** was the **24th**.
xa: The four vows of **Parsvanatha**: **Ahimsa, Satya, Asteya, Aparigraha**.
⚠ The **5th vow**, **Brahmacharya (celibacy)**, was **added by Mahavira**.
Parshvanatha renounced at **30**, got enlightenment after **84 days** of penance, and died at **100**.

26.s:
Consider the following statements about the contemporaries of the Buddha and Mahavira:
1. Prasenjit, the king of Kosala, was a contemporary of the Buddha.
2. Makkhali Gosala, the leader of the Ajivika sect, was a contemporary of Mahavira.
3. Bimbisara, a contemporary of the Buddha, was the king of Kosala.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
26.x: Statement 3 is wrong: Bimbisara was the king of Magadha, not Kosala. Statement 1 is correct: Prasenjit of Kosala lived in the Buddha's time. Statement 2 is correct: the Ajivika leader Makkhali Gosala was contemporary with Mahavira (and the Buddha). So 1 and 2 only.
26.tq: Bimbisara = Magadha; Prasenjit = Kosala.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Prasenjit**, the king of **Kosala**, was a contemporary of the Buddha.
Statement 2 is correct: **Makkhali Gosala**, leader of the **Ajivika** sect, was a contemporary of Mahavira.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Bimbisara** was the king of **Magadha**, not Kosala.
xa: **Gosala** was Mahavira's companion for about **six years**, then founded the **Ajivika** sect.
⚠ Some notes call Gosala Mahavira's "guru" — Jain texts make him a **disciple/companion**.
**Chetaka** (Lichchhavi) was Mahavira's **maternal uncle**; **Pradyota** of **Avanti** was a contemporary.
Other contemporary teachers: **Purana Kassapa**, **Ajita Kesakambalin**, **Pakudha Kachchayana**, **Sanjaya Belatthiputta**.

26.s: What does Samvara signify in Jainism?
o: Gradual reduction of food and liquid
26.x: Samvara is the stoppage of the inflow of karma. Elimination of existing karma is Nirjara, relativity of knowledge is Syadvada and gradual fasting is Sallekhana.
26.tq: Discriminate Samvara from Nirjara.
n: Samvara means stoppage of karmic inflow. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Nirjara means elimination of karma. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
xs: **Samvara** means **stoppage of karmic inflow** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Elimination of karma** is **Nirjara**, not Samvara.
**Relativity of knowledge** is **Syadvada**.
**Gradual reduction of food and liquid** is **Sallekhana** (Samadhi Maran).
xa: **Triratna**: **Right Faith**, **Right Knowledge**, **Right Conduct** — the path to moksha.
**Karma** in Jainism is **material bondage** of the soul causing rebirth.
Liberation: stop inflow + shed karma → **Kevala Jnana** → **Siddha** state.
**Tattva**: **origination, decay and permanence** (utpada-vyaya-dhrauvya).

26.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Triratna
(b) Syadvada
(c) Sallekhana
(d) Digambara

List-II
(i) Sky-clad
(ii) Relativity of knowledge
(iii) Right Faith, Right Knowledge and Right Conduct
(iv) Last vow involving gradual reduction of food and liquid
26.x: Triratna means Right Faith, Right Knowledge and Right Conduct, Syadvada is relativity of knowledge, Sallekhana is the last vow of fasting and Digambara means sky-clad, giving a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
26.tq: Recall the meaning of each Jain term.
n: The Triratna belongs to Jainism. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
The Triratna consists of Right Faith. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
The Triratna consists of Right Knowledge. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
The Triratna consists of Right Conduct. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Syadvada is associated with Saptabhanginaya. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Syadvada means relativity of knowledge. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Sallekhana is also called Samadhi Maran. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Sallekhana is the last vow. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Sallekhana involves gradual reduction of food and liquid. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Digambara is a Jain sect. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Digambara means sky-clad. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Triratna** = **Right Faith, Right Knowledge and Right Conduct**; **Syadvada** = **relativity of knowledge**.
**Sallekhana** = **last vow** of gradual reduction of food and liquid; **Digambara** = **sky-clad**.
xa: Jain Triratna = **Samyak Darshana**, **Samyak Jnana**, **Samyak Charitra** (Ratnatraya).
⚠ **Buddhist Triratna** = **Buddha, Dhamma, Sangha** — refuges, not a path.
**Syadvada** is associated with **Saptabhanginaya**.
"**Santhara** is a ritual of fasting to death amongst Jains" (APPSC G2 **2017**).

26.s:
Match the Jain term with its correct description:
List-I
(a) Ahimsa
(b) Satya
(c) Brahmacharya
(d) Aparigraha

List-II
(i) Non-possession
(ii) Truth
(iii) Non-violence
(iv) Chastity
26.x: Ahimsa is non-violence, Satya truth, Brahmacharya chastity and Aparigraha non-possession, giving a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
26.tq: Recall the meaning of each Mahavrata.
n: The Five Mahavratas belong to Jainism. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Ahimsa is one of the Five Mahavratas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Satya is one of the Five Mahavratas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Brahmacharya is one of the Five Mahavratas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Aparigraha is one of the Five Mahavratas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Ahimsa** = **non-violence**; **Satya** = **truth**.
**Brahmacharya** = **chastity**; **Aparigraha** = **non-possession**.
xa: The fifth Mahavrata is **Asteya** (non-stealing).
⚠ **Brahmacharya** was the **fifth vow added by Mahavira**; the other four come from **Parshvanatha**.
**Ahimsa** extends to all life forms → **vegetarianism**.
Householders take milder **Anuvratas** of the same vows.

27.s: A twelve-year famine in Magadha during Chandragupta Maurya’s reign led to the movement of Bhadrabahu and Chandragupta to
27.x: The famine tradition states that Bhadrabahu, the sixth Thera, travelled south with Chandragupta to Shravanabelagola in Karnataka.
27.tq: Link the famine, leaders and destination.
xs: The famine drove **Bhadrabahu** and **Chandragupta Maurya** south to **Shravanabelagola** (Karnataka) — so option **(2)** is correct.
The cause was a **12-year famine** in **Magadha** under Chandragupta Maurya; Bhadrabahu was the **6th Thera**.
**Vallabhi** was the seat of the **second Jain council**; **Mathura and Ujjain** became Jain centres only in the **early Christian era**.
xa: This southward spread was asked in **APPSC G2 2003**.
The route ran through **Rayalaseema** (**Kurnool**, **Anantapur**); early ascetic camps were in the **Erramala and Nallamala** caves.
Chandragupta, a disciple of Bhadrabahu, died by **sallekhana** at Shravanabelagola.
⚠ Bhadrabahu's group that went south became the **Digambaras**; **Sthulabhadra**'s group that stayed in Magadha became the **Svetambaras**.

27.s: The traditional route of the Jain migration from Magadha to Shravanabelagola passed through which Andhra region?
o: The Telangana plateau, including Warangal and Nizamabad
Coastal Andhra, including Srikakulam and Vizianagaram
The Godavari delta, including Rajahmundry and Amalapuram
27.x: The route is traditionally said to have passed through Rayalaseema, particularly Kurnool and Anantapur.
27.tq: Use the regional route rather than the final destination alone.
xs: The migration route passed through **Rayalaseema, including Kurnool and Anantapur** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Along this route, early Jain ascetic camps came up in the **Erramala and Nallamala** caves.
**Srikakulam-Vizianagaram** is linked instead with the influence of **Kharavela** of Kalinga.
xa: The migration followed a **12-year famine** in Magadha; **Bhadrabahu** led the monks with **Chandragupta Maurya** to **Shravanabelagola**.
AP angle: Jainism held the rocky **Rayalaseema** and North Coastal borderlands, while **Buddhism** held the **Krishna-Godavari delta**.
**Kundakundacharya** founded the **Saraswati gachcha** at **Konakondla** (Anantapur).

27.s: Which pair of regions became major Jain centres during the early Christian era?
27.x: Mathura and Ujjain became major Jain centres during the early Christian era.
27.tq: Recall the paired centres associated with the period.
xs: In the **early Christian era**, the major Jain centres were **Mathura and Ujjain** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Later the faith moved to **Gujarat** (Chalukyas) and **Karnataka** (Gangas, Rashtrakutas).
xa: Jainism survived in pockets of **Gujarat**, **Rajasthan**, **Karnataka** and **Tamil Nadu**.
The earlier southward spread took **Bhadrabahu** to **Shravanabelagola** after the **12-year famine**.
**Pataliputra** was the seat of the **first Jain council** (c. **300 BCE**), presided over by **Sthulabhadra**.

27.s: Who presided over the first Jain council traditionally held at Pataliputra?
27.x: Sthulabhadra presided over the first Jain council at Pataliputra.
27.tq: Separate council presidents by council and place.
xs: The first Jain council at **Pataliputra** (c. **300 BCE**) was presided over by **Sthulabhadra** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Devardhi Kshamashramana** presided over the **second** council at **Vallabhi** (**512 CE**).
**Arhabali** presided over the Andhra conference at **Venkatathatipuri**; **Hemachandra** is the 12th-century author of the **Parishishtaparvan**.
xa: The first council arranged the canon into **12 Angas** and led to the first split.
The second council wrote down the canon and added the **Upangas**, under **Maitraka** patronage.
⚠ **First** = Pataliputra – Sthulabhadra – 12 Angas; **Second** = Vallabhi – Devardhi Kshamashramana – Upangas.

27.s: Which of the following was an outcome associated with the first Jain council?
o: The canon was arranged into twelve Angas and the first sectarian division followed.
The complete canon was translated into Telugu.
The Upangas were added under Maitraka patronage.
27.x: The first council arranged the canon into twelve Angas and is traditionally associated with the first Jain split.
27.tq: Match a council with its institutional outcome.
xs: The first council arranged the **canon into twelve Angas**, and the **first sectarian division** followed — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Upangas** were added at the **second** council at **Vallabhi** under **Maitraka patronage**, not the first.
The **Sthanakvasi** sect was a much later **Svetambara** reform against idol worship.
xa: The first council met at **Pataliputra**, c. **300 BCE**, under **Sthulabhadra**.
The **12 Angas** were compiled by **Mahavira's Ganadharas**; they grew out of the earlier **14 Purvas**, now mostly lost.
Jain sacred texts (**Agamas / Siddhanta**) are in the eastern Prakrit **Ardhamagadhi**.

27.s:
Consider the following statements about the second Jain council:
1. It was held at Vallabhi in Gujarat in 512 CE under Maitraka patronage.
2. It was presided over by Sthulabhadra.
3. The canon was finally compiled and written down, and the Upangas were added.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
27.x: Statement 1 is correct: Vallabhi, 512 CE, Maitraka patronage. Statement 3 is correct: the canon was finally compiled and written, and Upangas added. Statement 2 is wrong: the second council was presided over by Devardhi Kshamashramana; Sthulabhadra presided over the first council at Pataliputra (c. 300 BCE). So '1 and 3 only'.
27.tq: First: Pataliputra-Sthulabhadra-12 Angas; Second: Vallabhi-Devardhi-written canon.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the second council met at **Vallabhi (Gujarat)** in **512 CE**, under **Maitraka patronage**.
Statement 2 is wrong: it was presided over by **Devardhi Kshamashramana**; **Sthulabhadra** led the first council at Pataliputra.
Statement 3 is correct: the canon was **finally compiled and written down**, and the **Upangas** added — so option **(2) 1 and 3 only** is correct.
xa: First council: **Pataliputra**, c. **300 BCE** — canon arranged into **12 Angas**.
A Jain conference at **Venkatathatipuri** in Andhra (Satavahana era) was presided over by **Arhabali**.
The **Svetambara canon**: **12 Angas, 12 Upangas, 10 Prakirnas, 6 Cheda Sutras, 4 Mula Sutras**.

27.s: A Jain conference held in Andhra during the Satavahana era was presided over by whom?
27.x: The Jain conference at Venkatathatipuri during the Satavahana era was presided over by Arhabali.
27.tq: Identify the regional council president from the Andhra context.
xs: The Jain conference at **Venkatathatipuri** in the **Satavahana era** was presided over by **Arhabali** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Sthulabhadra** presided over the first council (**Pataliputra**); **Devardhi Kshamashramana** the second (**Vallabhi**).
**Bhadrabahu** led the famine migration to **Shravanabelagola**.
xa: ⚠ Venkatathatipuri is an **Andhra conference** — not one of the two great councils.
**Srimukha (Simuka)** was the first **Satavahana** patron of Jainism in Andhra, with a basadi at **Kandapur**.
Per the **Kalpa Pradeepa** (Jinaprabha Suri), his **52 army chiefs built 52 Jain temples**.

27.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Sect)
 a. Digambara
 b. Svetambara
 c. Sthanakvasi
 d. Terapanthi

List-II (Feature or associated person)
 i. Acharya Bhikshu
 ii. White robes
 iii. Opposition to idol worship
 iv. Sky-clad monks

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
27.x: Digambaras are sky-clad, Svetambaras wear white robes, Sthanakvasis oppose idol worship, and Terapanthi was founded by Acharya Bhikshu.
27.tq: Start from the sure sect–dress pairs and complete the matching.
xs: **Digambara** = **sky-clad monks**; **Svetambara** = **white robes** (a–iv, b–ii).
**Sthanakvasi** = Svetambara reform **against idol worship**; **Terapanthi** = founded by **Acharya Bhikshu** (c–iii, d–i).
So option **(1) a–iv, b–ii, c–iii, d–i** is correct.
xa: Sthanakvasi was led by **Lonka Shah**; Terapanthi is an **18th-century** Svetambara sub-sect.
**Yapaniya** tried to bridge the two sects and was active in Andhra (the **Yapanacharyas**).
Digambara monks keep only a **broom and water pot**; Svetambara monks keep **14 items**, including clothes.

27.s: Which one of the following statements about the Digambara and Svetambara sects is NOT correct?
o: Digambaras hold that women can attain liberation in their existing body.
Svetambaras accept that women can attain liberation.
Digambara monks are described as sky-clad.
27.x: Digambara doctrine holds that women must be reborn as men before attaining moksha; Svetambaras accept the possibility of liberation for women.
27.tq: Find the reversed doctrinal comparison.
xs: The statement that is NOT correct is **(1)**: **Digambaras** deny women salvation directly — they must be **reborn as men** for moksha.
**Svetambaras** hold that women **can attain liberation**, so (2) is correct.
**Digambara** monks are **sky-clad** and **Svetambara** monks wear **white robes**, so (3) and (4) are correct.
xa: On Mahavira, Digambaras say he **never married**; Svetambaras say he **married Yashoda**.
Digambara monks own only a **broom and water pot**; Svetambara monks have **14 items** including clothes.
⚠ **Bhadrabahu**'s group went south → Digambara; **Sthulabhadra**'s stayed in Magadha → Svetambara.

27.s:
With reference to the two principal Jain sects, consider the following statements:
1. Bhadrabahu is associated with the group that went south.
2. Sthulabhadra is associated with the group that remained in Magadha.
3. Svetambaras are identified with white-clad monks.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
27.x: All three statements correctly describe the traditional distinction between the Digambara and Svetambara groups.
27.tq: Combine leader, migration and dress clues.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Bhadrabahu** led the group that **went south** (Digambaras).
Statement 2 is correct: **Sthulabhadra** led the group that **stayed in Magadha** (Svetambaras).
Statement 3 is correct: **Svetambaras** are the **white-clad** monks — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
xa: The split originated in the **12-year famine** under Chandragupta Maurya, per the **Parishishtaparvan**.
The formal split is dated to around the **3rd century CE**; another view links it to the first council (c. **300 BCE**).
**Yapaniya** was the bridge sect active in Andhra; **Sthanakvasi** and **Terapanthi** are Svetambara offshoots.

27.s: The sacred Jain texts are commonly designated as:
27.x: Jain sacred texts are called Agamas or Siddhanta. They were composed in the eastern Prakrit known as Ardhamagadhi.
27.tq: Use the exact technical term and distinguish Jain canonical vocabulary from Buddhist terms.
xs: Jain sacred texts are called the **Agamas or Siddhanta** — so option **(4)** is correct.
They are written in the eastern Prakrit **Ardhamagadhi**.
**Pitakas / Nikayas** are Buddhist; **Vedas / Brahmanas** and **Puranas / Itihasas** are Brahmanical.
xa: The earliest texts were the **14 Purvas**, now mostly lost; the Ganadharas compiled Mahavira's teaching into **12 Angas**.
The **Svetambara canon**: **12 Angas, 12 Upangas, 10 Prakirnas, 6 Cheda Sutras, 4 Mula Sutras**.
**Digambaras** reject this canon, holding that all original Angas were lost.

27.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Jain canon:
1. The 14 Purvas were the earliest Jain texts and are now mostly lost.
2. Mahavira's Ganadharas compiled his teaching into 14 Angas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
27.x: Statement 1 is correct: the 14 Purvas were the earliest texts, now mostly lost. Statement 2 is wrong: the Ganadharas compiled Mahavira's teaching into 12 Angas, not 14. Hence '1 only'.
27.tq: 14 Purvas (lost) -> 12 Angas.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **14 Purvas** were the earliest texts and are now **mostly lost**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the Ganadharas compiled Mahavira's teaching into **12 Angas**, not 14 — so option **(1) 1 only** is correct.
xa: The canon was arranged into **12 Angas** at the **first council** at **Pataliputra** under **Sthulabhadra**.
Key Angas: **Acharanga Sutra** (code of conduct for monks) and **Bhagavati Sutra** (doctrines).
Other early texts: **Sutrakritanga** and **Kalpasutra**.

27.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes the Digambara position from the Svetambara position regarding the Angas?
o: Digambaras hold that all the original Angas were lost, whereas Svetambaras preserve a canon including 12 Angas.
Digambaras preserve all 12 Angas, whereas Svetambaras reject every Anga.
Svetambaras hold that the Angas were lost, whereas Digambaras preserve the complete canon.
Both sects accept the same complete set of original Angas without variation.
27.x: The Svetambara canon includes twelve Angas, while Digambaras maintain that all the original Angas were lost and follow a separate canon.
27.tq: Test the sectarian distinction by reversing the positions as the distractor.
xs: **Digambaras** hold that **all the original Angas were lost**, while **Svetambaras** keep a canon with **12 Angas** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Digambaras therefore follow a **separate canon**.
xa: The Svetambara canon also has **12 Upangas, 10 Prakirnas, 6 Cheda Sutras and 4 Mula Sutras**.
The **Upangas** were added at the **second council** at **Vallabhi** (**512 CE**).
The **Tattvartha Sutra** (Umasvati) is accepted, in two versions, by **both sects**.

27.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Acharanga Sutra — code of conduct for monks
Kalpasutra — code of conduct exclusively for kings
27.x: Acharanga Sutra deals with the code of conduct for Jain monks. Bhagavati Sutra deals with doctrines, while Sutrakritanga and Kalpasutra are also early Jain texts.
27.tq: Use the subject matter of each text to detect the substituted description.
xs: **Acharanga Sutra** is the **code of conduct for monks** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Bhagavati Sutra** deals with **doctrines**, not medicine; the medical treatise is **Kalyanakaraka** by **Ugradityacharya**.
**Sutrakritanga** is an early **Jain** text, not a Buddhist chronicle; **Kalpasutra** is by **Bhadrabahu** (Jinacharitra, Sthaviravali, Samachari).
xa: Jain texts are in **Ardhamagadhi**; the **14 Purvas** came first, then the **12 Angas**.
Exam angle: odd-one-out — Jain texts (**Acharanga**, **Bhagavati**, **Kalpasutra**) vs Buddhist (**Dipavamsa**, **Mahavamsa**, **Divyavadana**, **Milindapanho**).

27.s:
Consider the following statements about the Svetambara Jain canon:
1. It contains 12 Angas and 12 Upangas.
2. It contains 10 Prakirnas.
3. It contains 4 Cheda Sutras and 6 Mula Sutras.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
27.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Svetambara canon has 12 Angas, 12 Upangas and 10 Prakirnas. Statement 3 reverses the numbers: there are 6 Cheda Sutras and 4 Mula Sutras. So '1 and 2 only'.
27.tq: Svetambara canon: 12-12-10-6-4 (Angas, Upangas, Prakirnas, Cheda, Mula).
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the Svetambara canon has **12 Angas** and **12 Upangas**.
Statement 2 is correct: it has **10 Prakirnas**.
Statement 3 is wrong — the numbers are reversed: **6 Cheda Sutras** and **4 Mula Sutras**. So option **(2) 1 and 2 only** is correct.
xa: **Digambaras** reject this canon and hold that all the original Angas were lost.
The canon was written down at the **second council**, **Vallabhi**, **512 CE**, under **Devardhi Kshamashramana**.
The earliest texts, the **14 Purvas**, are now mostly lost.

27.s: Which one of the following works is correctly matched with its author?
27.x: Kalpasutra is attributed to Bhadrabahu and includes Jinacharitra, Sthaviravali and Samachari. Parishishtaparvan is by Hemachandra, Mahapurana by Jinasena and Tattvartha Sutra by Umasvati.
27.tq: Start with the known author–work pair and reject the cross-paired scholars.
xs: **Kalpasutra** is by **Bhadrabahu** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Parishishtaparvan** is by **Hemachandra**, not Jinasena; **Mahapurana** is by **Jinasena**, not Umasvati.
**Tattvartha Sutra** is by **Umasvati**, not Hemachandra.
xa: Kalpasutra contains the **Jinacharitra**, **Sthaviravali** and **Samachari**.
**Samayasara**, **Yogasara**, **Pravachanasara** and **Panchastikaya** are by **Kundakundacharya**.
**Kalyanakaraka** (medical) = **Ugradityacharya**; **Yasastilaka Champu** and **Nitivakyamrita** = **Somadeva Suri**.

27.s: Parishishtaparvan, also known as Sthaviravali Charitra, was written by:
27.x: Parishishtaparvan or Sthaviravali Charitra was written by Hemachandra in the twelfth century. It is regarded as a source for the Svetambara–Digambara split.
27.tq: Combine the alternate title, author and period to avoid author substitution.
xs: **Parishishtaparvan (Sthaviravali Charitra)** was written by **Hemachandra** (12th c.) — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Jinasena** wrote the Mahapurana and Adipurana; **Somadeva Suri** the Yasastilaka Champu; **Umasvati** the Tattvartha Sutra.
xa: It is the source for the **Svetambara-Digambara split** and the **12-year famine** story.
Hemachandra's patron was **Kumarapala**, **Chalukya (Solanki)** of Gujarat.
⚠ **Kumarapala** – **Hemachandra**; **Amoghavarsha I** – **Jinasena**.

27.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Harivamsha Purana — Jain version of the Mahabharata
27.x: Jinendra Kalyanabhyudayamu was written by Appayacharya and dedicated to Kakatiya Prataparudra. Adipurana is by Jinasena, Yasastilaka Champu by Somadeva Suri, and Harivamsha Purana is the Jain version of the Mahabharata.
27.tq: Find the work with the swapped author while retaining the correct associations in the other pairs.
xs: The wrong pair is **(4)**: **Jinendra Kalyanabhyudayamu** is by **Appayacharya (Appayaryudu)**, not Hemachandra.
It was dedicated to Kakatiya **Prataparudra**.
The other pairs are right: **Yasastilaka Champu** — Somadeva Suri; **Adipurana** — Jinasena; **Harivamsha Purana** — Jain Mahabharata.
xa: **Hemachandra** wrote the **Parishishtaparvan** (Sthaviravali Charitra).
Somadeva Suri also wrote the **Nitivakyamrita**.
**Kalyanakaraka** (medical treatise) is by **Ugradityacharya**, composed at **Ramatirtham**.

27.s: Samayasara, a Jain work asked about in more than one examination, was written by
27.x: Samayasara (like Yogasara, Pravachanasara and Panchastikaya) is by Kundakundacharya, who founded the Saraswati gachcha at Konakondla in Anantapur. Hemachandra wrote Parishishtaparvan, Jinasena the Adipurana/Mahapurana, and Umasvati the Tattvartha Sutra.
27.tq: Samayasara, Yogasara = Kundakundacharya (Konakondla, Anantapur).
xs: **Samayasara** was written by **Kundakundacharya** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Hemachandra** wrote the Parishishtaparvan; **Jinasena** the Adipurana / Mahapurana; **Umasvati** the Tattvartha Sutra.
xa: Samayasara was asked in **2008** and **2019**; **Yogasara** in **2017** — both Kundakundacharya.
His other works: **Pravachanasara** and **Panchastikaya**.
He founded the **Saraswati gachcha** at **Konakondla**, Anantapur.

27.s: Which one of the following is a Buddhist work and NOT a Jain work?
27.x: Nettipakarana (like the Avadanashataka) is a Buddhist text (UPSC 2022). Kalpasutra (Bhadrabahu), Tattvartha Sutra (Umasvati) and Parishishtaparvan (Hemachandra) are Jain works.
27.tq: Nettipakarana, Avadanashataka = Buddhist.
xs: **Nettipakarana** is a **Buddhist** work — so option **(1)** is correct (**UPSC 2022**).
**Kalpasutra** (Bhadrabahu), **Tattvartha Sutra** (Umasvati) and **Parishishtaparvan** (Hemachandra) are Jain works.
xa: **Avadanashataka** is also Buddhist, not Jain.
Other Buddhist texts used as odd-ones-out: **Dipavamsa**, **Mahavamsa**, **Divyavadana**, **Milindapanho**.
Jain texts: **Acharanga**, **Bhagavati**, **Kalpasutra**, **Sutrakritanga**.

27.s:
Consider the following statements about the language and literature of Jainism:
1. Early Jains discarded Sanskrit and preached in the popular Prakrit.
2. The Jain canon was composed in Ardhamagadhi.
3. Jains produced the first grammar of Pali.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
27.x: Statement 1 is correct: early Jains used popular Prakrit instead of Sanskrit, which helped their spread. Statement 2 is correct: the canon is in Ardhamagadhi, an eastern Prakrit. Statement 3 is wrong: Jains wrote the earliest important works in Apabhramsa and its first grammar, not Pali (Pali is the language of the Buddhist Tripitaka). So '1 and 2 only'.
27.tq: Jain = Prakrit/Ardhamagadhi/Apabhramsa; Buddhist = Pali.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: early Jains **discarded Sanskrit** and preached in popular **Prakrit** — key to their spread.
Statement 2 is correct: the canon is in **Ardhamagadhi**.
Statement 3 is wrong: Jains wrote the earliest important works in **Apabhramsa** and its first grammar, not Pali — so option **(2) 1 and 2 only** is correct.
xa: Later Jain literature was rich in **Prakrit**, **Sanskrit** and regional languages (**Kannada**, **Tamil**, **Telugu**).
It covered **grammar**, **poetry** and **mathematics**.
Significance: Jainism enriched **Prakrit**, **Apabhramsa**, **Kannada** and **Telugu**.

27.s: Which social group formed the principal social base of Jainism in urban and commercial centres?
27.x: Traders, merchants and commercial communities supported Jainism, particularly in urban centres.
27.tq: Link the religion with its stated social base.
xs: Jainism's social base was **traders and merchants** (commercial communities) — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was linked with **banking** and **urban growth**.
xa: **Agriculture** was avoided because it **harms life** (strict ahimsa).
**Jain merchant guilds** moved along **Satavahana trade routes**.
In Andhra under the Eastern Chalukyas, **Shudras** adopted Jainism for social advancement.

27.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the social teachings of Jainism:
1. Jainism challenged caste hierarchy.
2. It stressed action over birth.
3. It promoted vegetarianism.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
27.x: Jainism challenged birth-based hierarchy, emphasised conduct and action, and promoted vegetarianism in accordance with ahimsa.
27.tq: Check whether all three related social principles belong together.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: Jainism **challenged caste hierarchy**.
Statement 2 is correct: it stressed **action over birth**.
Statement 3 is correct: it **promoted vegetarianism** — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
xa: In Andhra under the **Eastern Chalukyas**, **Shudras** adopted Jainism for social advancement.
Its base: **traders and merchants**; agriculture was avoided under **strict ahimsa**.
Decline: loss of **royal patronage**, sect split, **severe austerity**, no missionary zeal, rival **Bhakti** revival.

27.s: In the Eastern Chalukya period in Andhra, which group adopted Jainism for social advancement?
27.x: In Andhra under the Eastern Chalukyas, Shudras adopted Jainism as a means of social advancement.
27.tq: Use the region–period–social group combination.
xs: Under the **Eastern Chalukyas**, **Shudras** adopted Jainism for **social advancement** — so option **(2)** is correct.
This fits Jainism's challenge to **caste hierarchy** and its stress on **action over birth**.
xa: **Potla Cheruvu** was a famous Jain centre of the Eastern Chalukya period (**APPSC G2 2017**).
**Ayyana Mahadevi**, wife of **Vishnuvardhana**, built the **Nedumbasadi** at **Bejawada**.
**Vimaladitya** was a patron; **Durgaraja** built the **Kathikabharana Jinalaya** at **Dharmavaram**.

27.s: Kharavela, the Jain patron associated with the Hathigumpha inscription, belonged to which dynasty?
27.x: Kharavela was a Chedi or Mahameghavahana king of Kalinga in the second century BCE. His activities are known particularly from the Hathigumpha inscription.
27.tq: Use the dynasty–ruler association and reject swapped-ruler traps.
xs: **Kharavela** belonged to the **Chedi (Mahameghavahana)** dynasty of **Kalinga** — so option **(1)** is correct.
He ruled in the **2nd c. BCE** and is known from the **Hathigumpha inscription**.
**Udayin** was **Haryanka**; **Indra III** and **Amoghavarsha I** were **Rashtrakutas**; **Samprati** and **Chandragupta** were **Mauryas**.
xa: His influence reached **Srikakulam-Vizianagaram**; he built a Jain vihara near **Vardhamanapuram**.
The **Udayagiri-Khandagiri** rock-cut caves near **Bhubaneswar** were made under him.
⚠ **Samprati** = "Ashoka of Jainism"; **Kharavela** = Kalinga, Hathigumpha.

27.s:
Consider the following statements about Chandragupta Maurya:
1. He became a disciple of Bhadrabahu.
2. He migrated to the south.
3. He died by adopting sallekhana at Shravanabelagola.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
27.x: Chandragupta Maurya is traditionally described as a disciple of Bhadrabahu who migrated south and ended his life by sallekhana at Shravanabelagola.
27.tq: Check each statement independently before selecting the combined code.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Chandragupta Maurya** was a disciple of **Bhadrabahu**.
Statement 2 is correct: he **migrated south** with him after the **12-year famine**.
Statement 3 is correct: he died by **sallekhana** at **Shravanabelagola** — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
xa: Bhadrabahu was the **6th Thera**; this spread was asked in **APPSC G2 2003**.
**Samprati**, Ashoka's grandson, is the "**Ashoka of Jainism**".
**Udayin** (Haryanka), successor of Ajatashatru, was a devoted Jain per Jain tradition.

27.s: Samprati, the grandson of Ashoka, is popularly described in Jain tradition as the:
27.x: Samprati, the grandson of Ashoka, is known as the “Ashoka of Jainism” because of his role in spreading Jainism.
27.tq: Test the distinctive epithet rather than the dynasty alone.
xs: **Samprati**, Ashoka's grandson, is called the "**Ashoka of Jainism**" — so option **(1)** is correct.
He **spread Jainism in Andhra and the south**.
xa: His vihara was at **Vaddamanu** (Vaddemanu).
He ruled c. **230-215 BCE**; the PM inaugurated the **Samrat Samprati Museum** at **Koba, Gujarat** (Apr **2026**).
⚠ **Kharavela** = Kalinga, **Hathigumpha**; **Chandragupta Maurya** = disciple of **Bhadrabahu**.

27.s:
Consider the following statements about royal patrons of Jainism:
1. Amoghavarsha I, a Rashtrakuta ruler, was a patron of Jinasena.
2. Kumarapala, the patron of Hemachandra, belonged to the Western Ganga dynasty.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
27.x: Statement 1 is correct: Rashtrakuta Amoghavarsha I patronised Jinasena. Statement 2 is wrong: Kumarapala was a Chalukya (Solanki) ruler of Gujarat; the Western Gangas are linked with minister Chamundaraya and the Gommateshwara statue. Hence '1 only'.
27.tq: Kumarapala-Hemachandra = Gujarat Solankis; Gangas = Chamundaraya/Gommateshwara.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Amoghavarsha I** (Rashtrakuta) was a patron of **Jinasena**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Kumarapala** was a **Chalukya (Solanki) of Gujarat**, not a Western Ganga — so option **(1) 1 only** is correct.
The **Western Gangas** are linked with minister **Chamundaraya** and the **Gommateshwara** statue.
xa: Kumarapala is linked with 12th-c. councils at **Vallabhi** and **Mathura**, with **Hemachandra** presiding.
Rashtrakuta **Indra III** built a Jain kshetra at **Danavulapadu** (Kadapa).
Jinasena wrote the **Mahapurana** and **Adipurana** (life of Rishabha).

27.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Jainism in Andhra:
1. Srimukha or Simuka is regarded as the first Satavahana patron of Jainism.
2. According to the Kalpa Pradeepa, his 52 army chiefs built 52 Jain temples.
3. The Eastern Chalukyas and the Kakatiyas subsequently followed the Satavahana association with Jainism.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
27.x: Simuka or Srimukha is identified as the first Satavahana Jain patron; the Kalpa Pradeepa attributes 52 Jain temples to his 52 army chiefs. Eastern Chalukyas and Kakatiyas also followed this tradition.
27.tq: Combine the ruler, numerical detail and dynastic succession before choosing the code.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Srimukha (Simuka)** was the first Satavahana patron of Jainism in Andhra (basadi at **Kandapur**).
Statement 2 is correct: per the **Kalpa Pradeepa** (Jinaprabha Suri), his **52 army chiefs built 52 Jain temples**.
Statement 3 is correct: the order is **Satavahanas → Eastern Chalukyas → Kakatiyas** — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
xa: The early **Kakatiyas** were Jains (**Siddeshwara Charitra**).
Kakatiya minister Betana's wife **Mailama** built the **Kadalalaya Basadi** (**1117 CE** Padmakshi inscription).
Later, **Ganapatideva** persecuted Jains (Siddeshwara Charitra).

27.s:
Consider the following statements about the Mahamastakabhisheka:
1. It is performed for the Gommateshwara (Bahubali) statue every 12 years.
2. The 88th Mahamastakabhisheka was held in February 2018.
3. It is performed at Mount Abu in Rajasthan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
27.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Gommateshwara Mahamastakabhisheka is held every 12 years. Statement 2 is correct: the 88th was in February 2018. Statement 3 is wrong: Gommateshwara is at Shravanabelagola, Karnataka; Mount Abu has the Dilwara temples. So '1 and 2 only'.
27.tq: Gommateshwara = Shravanabelagola; Mount Abu = Dilwara.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **Mahamastakabhisheka** of **Gommateshwara (Bahubali)** is held every **12 years**.
Statement 2 is correct: the **88th** was in **February 2018**.
Statement 3 is wrong: it is at **Shravanabelagola**, Karnataka — **Mount Abu** has the **Dilwara** temples. So option **(2) 1 and 2 only** is correct.
xa: The statue was raised by **Chamundaraya**, a **Ganga** minister, c. **983 AD**.
The **Dilwara temples** were built by **Vimala Shah**, a Solanki minister, in **1031**.
Shravanabelagola is where **Chandragupta Maurya** died by **sallekhana**.

27.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Site)
 a. Dilwara temples
 b. Shravanabelagola
 c. Udayagiri-Khandagiri
 d. Sammed Shikhar

List-II (Region)
 i. Jharkhand
 ii. Karnataka
 iii. Rajasthan
 iv. Odisha

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
27.x: Dilwara is at Mount Abu in Rajasthan, Shravanabelagola is in Karnataka, Udayagiri-Khandagiri is in Odisha, and Sammed Shikhar is in Jharkhand.
27.tq: Start with the distinctive Shravanabelagola and Sammed Shikhar locations.
xs: **Dilwara temples** — Mount Abu, **Rajasthan** (a–iii); **Shravanabelagola** — **Karnataka** (b–ii).
**Udayagiri-Khandagiri** — **Odisha** (c–iv); **Sammed Shikhar** — **Jharkhand** (d–i).
So option **(1) a–iii, b–ii, c–iv, d–i** is correct.
xa: Sammed Shikhar (on **Parasnath hill**) marks **Parsvanatha's nirvana**.
Udayagiri-Khandagiri caves near **Bhubaneswar** were cut under **Kharavela**.
**Prabhasgiri (Pabhosa)** is near **Kaushambi**, Uttar Pradesh; the **Ellora** Jain caves are in Maharashtra.

27.s:
Which of the following statements about Gommateshwara is correct?
1. It is located at Shravanabelagola in Karnataka.
2. It is associated with Bahubali.
3. It was consecrated by Chamundaraya, a Ganga minister, around 983 CE.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
27.x: Gommateshwara is the Bahubali statue at Shravanabelagola, associated with Chamundaraya and dated to about 983 CE.
27.tq: Combine monument, identity, patron and date in a coded statement question.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Gommateshwara** stands at **Shravanabelagola**, Karnataka.
Statement 2 is correct: it is the statue of **Bahubali**.
Statement 3 is correct: it was raised by **Chamundaraya**, a **Ganga** minister, c. **983** — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
xa: Its **Mahamastakabhisheka** is held every **12 years**; the **88th** was in **February 2018**.
Chamundaraya served the **Western Gangas**, a Karnataka dynasty.
Shravanabelagola is where **Chandragupta Maurya** died by **sallekhana**, after migrating with **Bhadrabahu**.

27.s: Potla Cheruvu was a famous Jain centre during the reign of which dynasty in Andhra?
27.x: Potla Cheruvu was a prominent Jain centre during the Eastern Chalukya period.
27.tq: Use the dynasty–centre association to eliminate nearby Andhra patrons.
xs: **Potla Cheruvu** was a famous Jain centre in the **Eastern Chalukya** period — so option **(4)** is correct (**APPSC G2 2017**).
The Rashtrakutas are linked with **Danavulapadu**; Vijayanagara with **Devaraya II**'s Jinalaya in Pan Supari Bazar.
xa: Eastern Chalukya Jain sites: **Nedumbasadi** (Bejawada), **Ramatirtham** (Vizianagaram), **Kathikabharana Jinalaya** (Dharmavaram).
Order of Jain dynasties in Andhra: **Satavahanas → Eastern Chalukyas → Kakatiyas**.
Under the Eastern Chalukyas, **Shudras** adopted Jainism for social advancement.

27.s: Nedumba Vasati at Bejawada was built by:
27.x: Nedumba Vasati at Bejawada, or Vijayawada, was built by Ayyana Mahadevi, the wife of Eastern Chalukya Vishnuvardhana.
27.tq: Apply the person–foundation trap by separating the builder from other Jain patrons.
xs: **Nedumba Vasati** at **Bejawada** was built by **Ayyana Mahadevi**, wife of Eastern Chalukya **Vishnuvardhana** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Mailama** built the **Kadalalaya Basadi**; **Durgaraja** built the **Kathikabharana Jinalaya**; **Samprati** is linked with **Vaddamanu**.
xa: The village **Mushinikonda** was donated to the Nedumbasadi.
Bejawada = **Vijayawada**.
⚠ **Nedumbasadi** = Ayyana Mahadevi; **Kadalalaya Basadi** = Mailama; **Kathikabharana Jinalaya** = Durgaraja.

27.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Jain patronage among the Eastern Chalukyas:
1. Vimaladitya was one of the Eastern Chalukya patrons of Jainism.
2. Durgaraja built the Kathikabharana Jinalaya at Dharmavaram.
3. Kathikabharana Jinalaya was built at Danavulapadu.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
27.x: Vimaladitya was an Eastern Chalukya patron, and Durgaraja built the Kathikabharana Jinalaya at Dharmavaram. The statement placing it at Danavulapadu is false.
27.tq: Find the wrong location while retaining the correctly matched patron and monument.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Vimaladitya** was an Eastern Chalukya patron of Jainism.
Statement 2 is correct: **Durgaraja** built the **Kathikabharana Jinalaya** at **Dharmavaram**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Danavulapadu** (Kadapa) is linked with Rashtrakuta **Indra III** — so option **(1) 1 and 2 only** is correct.
xa: **Ayyana Mahadevi**'s **Nedumbasadi** at Bejawada is another Eastern Chalukya Jain site.
**Potla Cheruvu** was a famous Eastern Chalukya-era Jain centre (**APPSC G2 2017**).
Decline: a Jain monk fled **Rajaraja Narendra**'s persecution to **Hanamkonda** (Orugallu Kaifiyat).

27.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Jain centre)
a. Danavulapadu
b. Vijayawada
c. Munugodu
 d. Ramatirtham

List-II (Association)
i. Svetambara monastery Pudvithilakavasati
ii. Eastern Chalukya-era centre
iii. Nedumbasadi of Ayyana Mahadevi
iv. Rashtrakuta Indra III

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
27.x: Danavulapadu is associated with Rashtrakuta Indra III; Vijayawada with Ayyana Mahadevi’s Nedumbasadi; Munugodu with Pudvithilakavasati; and Ramatirtham with the Eastern Chalukya period.
27.tq: Start from the sure centre–patron pairs and then complete the remaining matches.
xs: **Danavulapadu** — Rashtrakuta **Indra III** (a–iv); **Vijayawada** — **Nedumbasadi** of Ayyana Mahadevi (b–iii).
**Munugodu** — Svetambara monastery **Pudvithilakavasati** (c–i); **Ramatirtham** — **Eastern Chalukya-era** centre (d–ii).
So option **(1) a–iv, b–iii, c–i, d–ii** is correct.
xa: Danavulapadu is in **Kadapa**; Ramatirtham (Ramagiri) is in **Vizianagaram**.
**Ugraditya** composed the **Kalyanakaraka** at Ramatirtham.
**Potla Cheruvu** was another famous Eastern Chalukya Jain centre (**APPSC G2 2017**).

27.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the decline and persecution of Jainism in the Andhra region are correct?
1. Ganapatideva persecuted Jains, as indicated in Siddeshwara Charitra.
2. A Jain monk fled the persecution of Rajaraja Narendra to Hanamkonda.
3. The account of the monk’s flight is associated with the Orugallu Kaifiyat.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
27.x: All three statements are correct. Ganapatideva’s persecution is mentioned in Siddeshwara Charitra, while the flight of a Jain monk to Hanamkonda from Rajaraja Narendra’s persecution is recorded in the Orugallu Kaifiyat.
27.tq: Check whether all three statements refer to the correct source, persecutor and refuge.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Ganapatideva** persecuted Jains (**Siddeshwara Charitra**).
Statement 2 is correct: a Jain monk fled **Rajaraja Narendra**'s persecution to **Hanamkonda**.
Statement 3 is correct: this flight is recorded in the **Orugallu Kaifiyat** — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
xa: The **Siddeshwara Charitra** also says the **early Kakatiyas were Jains**.
Ganapatideva's persecution at **Anmakonda** is tied to **Kalamukha / Vira Shaiva** hostility.
Decline factors: loss of **royal patronage**, sect split, **severe austerity**, no missionary zeal, rival **Bhakti** revival.

27.s: The Kadalalaya Basadi, known from the 1117 CE Padmakshi inscription, was built by
o: Mailama, wife of the Kakatiya minister Betana
27.x: Mailama, wife of the Kakatiya minister Betana, built the Kadalalaya Basadi (1117 CE Padmakshi inscription). Ayyana Mahadevi built the Nedumbasadi at Bejawada, Durgaraja the Kathikabharana Jinalaya at Dharmavaram, and Devaraya II a Jinalaya in Pan Supari Bazar.
27.tq: Kadalalaya Basadi = Mailama (Kakatiya), Padmakshi inscription.
xs: The **Kadalalaya Basadi** was built by **Mailama, wife of the Kakatiya minister Betana** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Its source is the **1117 CE Padmakshi inscription**.
**Ayyana Mahadevi** built the **Nedumbasadi**; **Durgaraja** the **Kathikabharana Jinalaya**; **Devaraya II** a Jinalaya in Pan Supari Bazar.
xa: The **early Kakatiyas** were Jains (**Siddeshwara Charitra**).
Later Kakatiya **Ganapatideva** persecuted Jains.
**Appayacharya**'s **Jinendra Kalyanabhyudayamu** was dedicated to Kakatiya **Prataparudra**.

27.s: Which one of the following correctly expresses the regional distribution of Jainism and Buddhism in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Jainism held the Krishna-Godavari delta, while Buddhism held Rayalaseema.
Jainism was confined to the eastern coast, while Buddhism held the North Coastal borderlands.
Jainism held the rocky Rayalaseema and North Coastal borderlands, while Buddhism held the Krishna-Godavari delta.
Both Jainism and Buddhism were confined exclusively to the Krishna-Godavari delta.
27.x: Jainism was associated with the rocky Rayalaseema and North Coastal borderlands, whereas Buddhism held the Krishna-Godavari delta.
27.tq: Use the reversed-region trap to distinguish the two religious zones.
xs: **Jainism** held the rocky **Rayalaseema** and **North Coastal borderlands**, while **Buddhism** held the **Krishna-Godavari delta** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Option (1) reverses the two faiths.
xa: The Jain migration route south passed through **Rayalaseema** (**Kurnool**, **Anantapur**).
Early Jain ascetic camps were in the **Erramala and Nallamala** caves.
**Kharavela**'s influence reached **Srikakulam-Vizianagaram** in the north coast.

27.s: Which of the following was NOT identified as a factor in the decline of Jainism?
27.x: The factors identified were loss of royal patronage, sectarian split, severe austerity, lack of missionary zeal and rival Bhakti revival. Expansion of missionary zeal was not a cause of decline.
27.tq: Look for the reversed meaning of a stated decline factor.
xs: **Expansion of missionary zeal** was NOT a factor — the notes cite **no missionary zeal** as a cause of decline. So option **(2)** is correct.
The real factors: **loss of royal patronage**, **sect split**, **severe austerity**, and a rival **Bhakti revival**.
xa: In Andhra, **Ganapatideva** persecuted Jains at **Anmakonda** (Kalamukha / Vira Shaiva hostility).
A Jain monk fled **Rajaraja Narendra**'s persecution to **Hanamkonda** (Orugallu Kaifiyat).

27.s: Jain literature contributed to the enrichment of which group of languages?
27.x: Jain literature enriched Prakrit, Apabhramsa, Kannada and Telugu.
27.tq: Select the complete language group without substituting neighbouring literary languages.
xs: Jain literature enriched **Prakrit, Apabhramsa, Kannada and Telugu** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Pali** is linked with Buddhism; Jains in fact **discarded Sanskrit** early and preached in **Prakrit**.
xa: The Jain canon is in **Ardhamagadhi**.
Jains wrote the **earliest important works in Apabhramsa** and its **first grammar**.
Later works covered **grammar**, **poetry** and **mathematics** in Prakrit, Sanskrit and regional languages.

27.s: In April 2026, the Prime Minister inaugurated the Samrat Samprati Museum connected with Jain heritage at which place?
27.x: The Samrat Samprati Museum was inaugurated at Koba in Gujarat to highlight Jain heritage.
27.tq: Link the current-affairs event with its precise place rather than the broader historical region.
xs: The **Samrat Samprati Museum** was inaugurated at **Koba in Gujarat** (Apr **2026**) — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Samprati** ruled c. **230-215 BCE**.
xa: Samprati, **Ashoka's grandson**, is the "**Ashoka of Jainism**".
He spread Jainism in **Andhra** and the south; his vihara was at **Vaddamanu**.
⚠ **Kharavela** = Kalinga, **Hathigumpha**; **Samprati** = Maurya.

28.s:
Consider the following statements about the family background of Siddhartha Gautama:
1. His father Suddhodana was the chief of the Sakya clan.
2. His mother Maya was a Koliya princess.
3. He was raised by Mahapajapati Gautami.
4. Yashodhara was his wife and Rahula was his son.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
28.x: All four statements correctly describe Siddhartha Gautama's clan, parents, foster mother, wife and son.
28.tq: Treat a biographical cluster as separate statements and verify every relationship.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: father **Suddhodana** was the **Shakya** chief at **Kapilavastu**.
Statement 2 is correct: mother **Maya** was a **Koliya** princess.
Statement 3 is correct: he was raised by foster-mother **Mahapajapati Gautami**.
Statement 4 is correct: wife **Yashodhara**, son **Rahula** — so option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4** is correct.
xa: He was **Siddhartha Gautama** of the **Sakya/Shakya** Kshatriya clan.
Charioteer **Channa** and horse **Kanthaka**; teachers **Alara Kalama** and **Uddaka Ramaputta**.
⚠ **Maya** = mother (Koliya); **Mahapajapati Gautami** = foster-mother; **Yashodhara** = wife.

28.s:
Consider the following statements about Siddhartha Gautama before his enlightenment:
1. His teachers were Alara Kalama and Uddaka Ramaputta.
2. He practised austerities with five ascetics for twelve years before abandoning them.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
28.x: Statement 1 is correct: Alara Kalama and Uddaka Ramaputta were his teachers. Statement 2 is wrong: he practised austerities with five ascetics for six years (twelve years of asceticism belongs to Mahavira), then abandoned them and was enlightened at 35. Hence '1 only'.
28.tq: Buddha: 6 years of austerities; Mahavira: 12 years.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: his teachers were **Alara Kalama** and **Uddaka Ramaputta**.
Statement 2 is wrong: he practised austerities with five ascetics for **six years**, not twelve — so option **(1) 1 only** is correct.
He then abandoned them and was enlightened at **35**.
xa: The **four sights** (old man, sick man, corpse, ascetic) led to the **Great Renunciation** at **29**.
Enlightenment came after defeating the temptation of **Mara**, at **Uruvela** under the Bodhi tree.
The **five former companions** later heard his first sermon at **Sarnath** and became Arhats.

28.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the role of Mara in the life of Gautama Buddha?
o: Mara was Buddha's first lay disciple.
Mara presided over the First Buddhist Council.
Mara tempted Buddha before his enlightenment.
Mara was the chief of the Sakya clan.
28.x: Mara is associated with the temptation of Gautama Buddha before his enlightenment.
28.tq: Distinguish a symbolic figure from historical persons in Buddha's biography.
xs: **Mara tempted** the Buddha **before his enlightenment** — so option **(3)** is correct.
He was enlightened at **35** after defeating Mara's temptation.
The first lay disciples were **Tapassu and Bhallika**; **Mahakassapa** presided over the First Council; **Suddhodana** was the Shakya chief.
xa: Enlightenment: **Uruvela**, under the **Bodhi tree**, on the bank of the **Niranjana** — today **Bodh Gaya**, Bihar.
⚠ Ages **29 – 35 – 80** = **Renunciation – Enlightenment – Parinirvana**.

28.s: Which one of the following statements about the succession after Buddha's death is correct?
o: Buddha appointed Bimbisara as the head of the Sangha.
The Dhamma and Vinaya were to serve as the teacher after Buddha's death.
Buddha formally appointed Ajatashatru as his successor.
Buddha nominated Devadatta as the permanent head of the Sangha.
28.x: Buddha did not name an individual successor; the Dhamma and Vinaya were to be the teacher after his death.
28.tq: Apply the distinction between a personal successor and an impersonal institutional authority.
xs: The Buddha named **no successor** — the **Dhamma and Vinaya** were to be the teacher — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Bimbisara** and **Ajatashatru** were **royal disciples** from Magadha, not heads of the Sangha.
xa: **Mahakassapa** presided over the **First Council** and led the Sangha after the Buddha.
At that council **Ananda** recited the **Sutta Pitaka** and **Upali** the **Vinaya Pitaka**.
Last words: "All composite things decay, strive diligently" (**appamadena sampadetha**).

28.s:
With reference to the events in the life of Gautama Buddha, consider the following statements:
1. The Great Renunciation took place at the age of 29.
2. Channa accompanied Siddhartha during the Great Renunciation.
3. Kanthaka was the horse associated with this event.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
28.x: The Great Renunciation occurred when Siddhartha was 29 years old, accompanied by the charioteer Channa and the horse Kanthaka.
28.tq: Use a cluster of closely related biographical details and eliminate options by checking each statement.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **Great Renunciation (Mahabhinishkramana)** was at age **29**.
Statements 2 and 3 are correct: **Channa** was his charioteer and **Kanthaka** his horse — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
xa: It followed the **four sights**: old man, sick man, corpse, ascetic.
It took place at **Kapilavastu**.
⚠ Ages **29 – 35 – 80** = **Renunciation – Enlightenment – Parinirvana**.

28.s:
Consider the following statements about places in the life of Gautama Buddha:
1. His birth at Lumbini (Rumindei, Nepal) is confirmed by an Ashokan inscribed pillar.
2. He attained enlightenment at Uruvela, on the bank of the Niranjana.
3. Kusinara, where he attained Mahaparinirvana, is identified with present-day Sarnath.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
28.x: Statement 1 is correct: an Ashokan pillar at Lumbini (Rumindei) confirms the birthplace. Statement 2 is correct: enlightenment was at Uruvela (Bodh Gaya) under the Bodhi tree on the Niranjana. Statement 3 is wrong: Kusinara is present-day Kushinagar (UP), capital of the Mallas; Sarnath (Deer Park) is the place of the first sermon. So '1 and 2 only'.
28.tq: Birth-Lumbini, Enlightenment-Bodh Gaya, First sermon-Sarnath, Death-Kushinagar.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Lumbini (Rumindei, Nepal)** is confirmed by an **Ashokan inscribed pillar**.
Statement 2 is correct: enlightenment was at **Uruvela**, on the bank of the **Niranjana** (Bodh Gaya).
Statement 3 is wrong: **Kusinara** is **Kushinagar, UP**; **Sarnath** is the site of the first sermon — so option **(2) 1 and 2 only** is correct.
xa: Birth: **c. 563 BCE**, on Vaishakha Purnima.
Kusinara was the capital of the **Mallas** (Deoria dist.).
Exam angle: "first sermon" = **Sarnath** (APPSC **2012**, **2018**).

28.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
28.x: Sankasya is associated with the descent of Buddha from Trayastrimsa heaven. The First Buddhist Council was held at Rajagriha.
28.tq: Find the one wrong event–place association among nearby Buddhist sites.
xs: The wrong pair is **(4)**: **Sankasya** is the site of the **descent from Trayastrimsa heaven**; the **First Council** was at **Rajagriha**.
The rest are right: **Vaishali** — monkey's honey offering; **Rajagriha** — taming of **Nalagiri**; **Shravasti** — **Twin Miracle**.
xa: **Vaishali** (Bihar) also hosted the **Second Council**.
**Shravasti** (UP) had the **Jetavana Vihara**.
These eight sites are the **Ashtamahasthanas**; **7 of the 8** are in India.

28.s:
With reference to the Ashtamahasthanas, consider the following statements:
1. Seven of the eight places are located in India.
2. Lumbini is one of the eight places.
3. Kushinagar is excluded because it is not associated with Buddha's life.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
28.x: Seven of the eight Ashtamahasthanas are in India, and Lumbini is one of them. Kushinagar is included because it is associated with Buddha's Mahaparinirvana.
28.tq: Use an exception-based statement to test both inclusion and geographical distribution.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **7 of the 8** Ashtamahasthanas are in **India**.
Statement 2 is correct: **Lumbini** (Nepal) is one of them.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Kushinagar** is included — it is the site of the **Mahaparinirvana**. So option **(1) 1 and 2 only** is correct.
xa: The eight: **Lumbini**, **Bodh Gaya**, **Sarnath**, **Kushinagar**, **Rajagriha**, **Shravasti**, **Vaishali**, **Sankasya**.
Lumbini is the one outside India — **Rumindei, Nepal**.
Kushinagar is in **UP** (Deoria dist.); the Buddha died there at **80**, in **483 BCE**.
