28.s: The first sermon of Gautama Buddha, known as Dhammachakra Pravartana, dealt primarily with:
o: The Four Noble Truths and the Noble Eightfold Path
The authority of the Vedas and sacrificial rituals
The theory of the four stages of life
28.x: Dhammachakra Pravartana, the first sermon at Sarnath, expounded the Four Noble Truths and the Noble Eightfold Path.
28.tq: Test the content of a famous event rather than its location, which is a common confusable fact.
xs: The first sermon set out the **Four Noble Truths** and the **Eightfold Path** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was given at the **Deer Park, Sarnath** (Rishipatana), near Varanasi.
The Buddha **rejected Vedic authority and sacrifice**, so (2) is wrong.
xa: **Dhammachakra Pravartana** = "**Turning the Wheel of Dharma**".
Audience: the **five former companions** — **Kondanna, Bhaddiya, Vappa, Mahanama, Assaji** — who became Arhats.
Asked as "first sermon = Sarnath" in APPSC **2012** and **2018**.

28.s: The phrase “Appamadena sampadetha”, associated with the last words of Gautama Buddha, conveys which of the following meanings?
28.x: “Appamadena sampadetha” means “strive diligently” and is associated with Buddha's last words.
28.tq: Translate a distinctive phrase rather than relying on the surrounding historical event.
xs: "**Appamadena sampadetha**" means **strive diligently** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The full last words: "**All composite things decay**, strive diligently".
xa: Mahaparinirvana: **Kusinara** (Kushinagar, UP), age **80**, **483 BCE**; some notes give c. **486** BC.
The Buddha named **no successor** — the **Dhamma and Vinaya** were to be the teacher.
The **last convert** was **Subhadda**, at Kusinara.

28.s: Which of the following groups consists entirely of the five former companions who became arhats after hearing Buddha's first sermon?
o: Bimbisara, Ajatashatru, Prasenajit, Udayana and Pradyota
Kondanna, Bhaddiya, Vappa, Mahanama and Assaji
Alara Kalama, Uddaka Ramaputta, Mara, Subhadda and Mahapajapati
Tapassu, Bhallika, Rahula, Channa and Ananda
28.x: The five former companions were Kondanna, Bhaddiya, Vappa, Mahanama and Assaji; they became arhats after the first sermon.
28.tq: Check completeness of a named list and reject options containing persons from other groups.
xs: The five former companions were **Kondanna, Bhaddiya, Vappa, Mahanama and Assaji** — so option **(2)** is correct.
They heard the first sermon at **Sarnath** and became **Arhats**.
(1) lists **royal** followers; **Tapassu and Bhallika** were the first **lay disciples**; **Alara Kalama** and **Uddaka Ramaputta** were his **teachers**.
xa: They were the five ascetics with whom he had practised austerities for **six years**.
The sermon covered the **Four Noble Truths** and the **Eightfold Path**.

28.s: Gautama Buddha attained Mahaparinirvana at approximately what age and in which year?
28.x: Buddha attained Mahaparinirvana at Kusinara at the age of 80, traditionally dated to 483 BCE; some accounts give an approximate alternative date.
28.tq: Separate the age and date of death from the commonly tested birth and enlightenment figures.
xs: The Buddha attained Mahaparinirvana at **80 years**, in **483 BCE** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**35**, c. **528 BCE** is his enlightenment; **29** is his renunciation; c. **563 BCE** is his birth.
xa: Some notes give c. **486** BC for the Mahaparinirvana.
Place: **Kusinara**, capital of the **Mallas** — Kushinagar, UP (Deoria dist.).
⚠ Ages **29 – 35 – 80** = **Renunciation – Enlightenment – Parinirvana**.

28.s: Who were regarded as the first lay disciples of Gautama Buddha?
28.x: The merchants Tapassu and Bhallika are regarded as Buddha's first lay disciples.
28.tq: Separate lay disciples from ordained companions, family members and royal followers.
xs: The first lay disciples were the merchants **Tapassu and Bhallika** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Kondanna** and **Assaji** were among the **five former companions**; **Rahula** was his son and **Channa** his charioteer.
**Bimbisara** and **Ajatashatru** were **royal disciples** of Magadha.
xa: The **last convert** was **Subhadda**, at Kusinara.
**Sariputta** and **Mahamoggallana** were the **chief disciples**.
**Upasaka** = lay follower.

28.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. Jina — Mahavira
2. Kevalin — Mahavira
3. Nigantha Nataputta — Mahavira
28.x: Jina, Kevalin and Nigantha Nataputta are all titles or designations associated with Mahavira, not the Buddha.
28.tq: Use confusable religious epithets and identify the person associated with all three terms.
xs: **Jina**, **Kevalin** and **Nigantha Nataputta** are all names of **Mahavira** — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
None of them is a title of the Buddha.
xa: The Buddha's epithets: **Buddha** (Awakened One), **Tathagata** ("thus-gone"), **Shakyamuni** (sage of the Shakyas).
"**Light of Asia**" is the title of **Edwin Arnold**'s poem.
⚠ This is a common **odd-one-out** trap.

28.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Disciple)

a. Ananda
b. Upali
c. Mahakassapa
 d. Subhadda

List-II (Association)
 i. Last convert
 ii. Recited the Vinaya Pitaka
 iii. Personal attendant and reciter of the Sutta Pitaka
 iv. Presided over the First Council

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
28.x: Ananda was the personal attendant and recited the Sutta Pitaka; Upali recited the Vinaya Pitaka; Mahakassapa presided over the First Council; Subhadda was the last convert.
28.tq: Start with the distinctive sure pair and eliminate codes containing swapped disciple roles.
xs: **Ananda** — personal attendant, recited the **Sutta Pitaka** (a–iii); **Upali** — recited the **Vinaya Pitaka** (b–ii).
**Mahakassapa** — presided over the **First Council** (c–iv); **Subhadda** — **last convert** (d–i).
So option **(1) a–iii, b–ii, c–iv, d–i** is correct.
xa: The First Council was held at **Rajagriha** (Rajgir).
Mahakassapa led the Sangha after the Buddha.
⚠ **Ananda** = Sutta; **Upali** = Vinaya; **Mahakassapa** = president.

28.s: The title 'Light of Asia', used for the Buddha, comes from
28.x: 'Light of Asia' is the title of Edwin Arnold's poem on the Buddha. It is not from an Ashokan inscription, the Mahavamsa or Dharmapala; the Buddha's own epithets are Buddha, Tathagata and Shakyamuni.
28.tq: Light of Asia = Edwin Arnold.
xs: "**Light of Asia**" is the title of **Edwin Arnold's poem** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The Buddha's own epithets are **Buddha**, **Tathagata** and **Shakyamuni**.
**Anagarika Dharmapala** founded the **Maha Bodhi Society** (**1891**); the **Rumindei** pillar confirms the birthplace.
xa: **Tathagata** = "thus-gone"; **Shakyamuni** = sage of the Shakyas.
⚠ **Jina**, **Kevalin** and **Nigantha Nataputta** = **Mahavira**, not the Buddha.

28.s: Which one of the following pairs of a royal disciple of the Buddha and his kingdom is NOT correctly matched?
28.x: Bimbisara and Ajatashatru ruled Magadha, Prasenajit ruled Kosala and Udayana ruled Kausambi. So Ajatashatru - Kosala is wrong.
28.tq: Magadha: Bimbisara, Ajatashatru; Kosala: Prasenajit; Kausambi: Udayana.
xs: The wrong pair is **(4)**: **Ajatashatru** ruled **Magadha**, not Kosala.
The rest are right: **Bimbisara** — Magadha; **Prasenajit** — **Kosala**; **Udayana** — **Kausambi**.
xa: The first lay disciples were the merchants **Tapassu and Bhallika**.
The **First Council** was held at **Rajagriha**, presided over by **Mahakassapa**.
The Buddha tamed the elephant **Nalagiri** at **Rajagriha**.

28.s: Which of the following correctly describes Nirvana in Buddhist teaching?
o: Liberation from suffering and extinction of craving
28.x: Nirvana is liberation from suffering, extinction of craving and freedom from the cycle of rebirth.
28.tq: Distinguish the central Buddhist goal from concepts belonging to other religious traditions.
xs: **Nirvana** is **liberation from suffering** and the **extinction of craving** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It also means freedom from the **cycle of rebirth**; it is the **main goal** (APPSC GS **2012**).
Vedic sacrifice was **rejected**, and God was neither affirmed nor denied.
xa: **Nirodha**, the third Noble Truth, says suffering can end — that cessation is Nirvana.
**Karma**: rebirth continues **till nirvana**.
Three marks: **Anicca**, **Anatta**, **Dukkha**.

28.s: The Buddhist Middle Path primarily rejects which of the following?
o: Both extreme asceticism and sensual indulgence
28.x: The Middle Path avoids both the extreme of severe asceticism and the opposite extreme of sensual indulgence.
28.tq: Identify the principle by applying it to the two extremes it avoids.
xs: The **Middle Path (Madhyama Marga)** rejects both **extreme asceticism** and **sensual indulgence** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The Buddha himself abandoned **six years** of austerities before enlightenment.
xa: The path to the end of suffering is the **Noble Eightfold Path** (**Magga**).
The teaching is likened to a **raft** — **upaya** (skilful means), not dogma.

28.s: Which one of the following statements about Buddhist doctrines is correct?
o: Anicca denotes impermanence and Anatta rejects a permanent self.
Anatta affirms a permanent and unchanging self.
Dukkha means that suffering is impossible.
Anicca denotes the permanence of all things.
28.x: Anicca means impermanence, while Anatta teaches that there is no permanent, unchanging self or atman. Dukkha denotes suffering.
28.tq: Separate the closely related doctrinal terms by their exact meanings.
xs: **Anicca** = impermanence and **Anatta** = no permanent self — so option **(1)** is correct.
Anatta **rejects** a permanent self (**atman**), so (2) is wrong; Anicca is impermanence, so (4) is wrong.
**Dukkha** means suffering — and **Nirodha** says it can end — so (3) is wrong.
xa: Anicca, Anatta and Dukkha are the **three marks**.
The first Noble Truth: life is suffering ("**sabbam dukkham**").

28.s: According to Buddhist teaching, karma is primarily understood as:
o: A ritual sacrifice prescribed in the Vedas
A denial of rebirth and moral causation
Intention-based morality in which present conditions arise from past actions
A divine decree that completely removes human choice
28.x: Buddhist karma is intention-based morality; the present state is linked to past actions, and rebirth continues until nirvana.
28.tq: Distinguish Buddhist moral causation from divine decree and ritual action.
xs: Buddhist karma is **intention-based morality**: the present state comes from **past actions** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Rebirth continues **till nirvana**.
Vedic authority and **sacrifice** were rejected, so (1) is wrong.
xa: The Buddha neither affirmed nor denied **God**.
**Nirvana** brings freedom from the **cycle of rebirth**.

28.s: Which of the following best describes the Buddha’s position regarding God and religious teaching?
o: He definitively denied every form of divine existence.
He definitively affirmed a creator God as the basis of liberation.
He neither affirmed nor denied God, and compared teaching to a raft or skilful means.
He made belief in God the first requirement for Sangha membership.
28.x: The Buddha neither affirmed nor denied God in this formulation. His teaching is compared to a raft and is understood as upaya, or skilful means, rather than dogma.
28.tq: Reject absolute formulations and identify the carefully qualified doctrinal position.
xs: He **neither affirmed nor denied God**, and likened his teaching to a **raft** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The raft stands for **upaya** (skilful means), not dogma.
Sangha membership was open to all **above 15**, regardless of caste — no belief in God was required.
xa: **Vedic authority** and **sacrifice** were rejected.
Significance: a **rational**, moderate, caste-open path.

28.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched in relation to the Four Noble Truths?
o: Magga — The permanence of worldly life
28.x: Samudaya identifies the cause of suffering, especially craving, ignorance and attachment. Dukkha is suffering, Nirodha is its cessation and Magga is the path.
28.tq: Match each Pali term with its precise doctrinal meaning rather than a related concept.
xs: **Samudaya** is the **cause of suffering** — craving (**tanha**), ignorance, attachment — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Dukkha** = suffering; **Nirodha** = cessation (Nirvana); **Magga** = the path.
xa: The four truths are called **Arya Satya**.
Magga = the **Noble Eightfold Path**.
⚠ **Samudaya** = cause; **Nirodha** = cessation; **Magga** = path.

28.s: Which one of the following is NOT included in the ethical discipline component of the Eightfold Path?
28.x: Ethics consists of Right Speech, Right Action and Right Livelihood. Right Mindfulness belongs to mental discipline.
28.tq: Find the element belonging to the neighbouring category of mental discipline.
xs: **Right Mindfulness** is not in the ethics group — so option **(2)** is correct.
It belongs to **Samadhi** (mental discipline) with **Right Effort** and **Right Concentration**.
**Sila** (ethics) = **Right Speech**, **Right Action**, **Right Livelihood**.
xa: **Prajna** (wisdom) = **Right View**, **Right Intention**.
Pali terms: Mindfulness = **sati**; Livelihood = **ajiva**; Action = **kammanta**.

28.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Element of the Eightfold Path)

a. Samma-ditthi
b. Sankappa
c. Vaca
 d. Samadhi

List-II (English rendering)
 i. Right Speech
 ii. Right Concentration
 iii. Right View
 iv. Right Intention

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
28.x: Samma-ditthi means Right View, Sankappa means Right Intention, Vaca means Right Speech and Samadhi means Right Concentration.
28.tq: Use the original terms and their English equivalents, beginning with the unmistakable language term Vaca.
xs: **Samma-ditthi** = **Right View** (a–iii); **Sankappa** = **Right Intention** (b–iv).
**Vaca** = **Right Speech** (c–i); **Samadhi** = **Right Concentration** (d–ii).
So option **(1) a–iii, b–iv, c–i, d–ii** is correct.
xa: Others: **Kammanta** = Action, **Ajiva** = Livelihood, **Vayama** = Effort, **Sati** = Mindfulness.
Groups: **Prajna** (wisdom), **Sila** (ethics), **Samadhi** (mental discipline).

28.s: The Buddhist doctrine which explains that every phenomenon arises owing to a cause is known as:
28.x: Pratityasamutpada is the doctrine of dependent origination, according to which phenomena arise through causal conditions.
28.tq: Test the exact doctrinal term against closely related Buddhist concepts.
xs: The doctrine that every phenomenon **arises from a cause** is **Pratityasamutpada** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is **dependent origination**, a chain of **12 nidanas**.
**Nirodha** = cessation; **Anicca** = impermanence; **Anatta** = no permanent self.
xa: The chain begins **avidya (ignorance) → samskara → vijnana** and ends in **old age and death**.
Links **9-12**: Upadana → Bhava → Jati → **Jara-marana**.

28.s:
Arrange the following links of Pratityasamutpada in their correct order:

A. Vijnana
B. Samskara
C. Avidya
D. Namarupa
28.x: The first four links are Avidya, Samskara, Vijnana and Namarupa.
28.tq: Start with the first link and follow the fixed doctrinal sequence.
xs: The first four links run **Avidya → Samskara → Vijnana → Namarupa** — C, B, A, D, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Avidya** = ignorance; **Vijnana** = consciousness.
xa: Links **5-8**: **Shadayatana** (six senses) → **Sparsha** (contact) → **Vedana** (feeling) → **Trishna** (craving).
Links **9-12**: **Upadana** → **Bhava** → **Jati** → **Jara-marana**.

28.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
28.x: Pravrajya means leaving lay life or going forth; Upasampada denotes full ordination.
28.tq: Find the swapped meanings in a confusable pair of technical terms.
xs: The wrong pair is **(1)**: **Pravrajya** means **going forth** — leaving lay life (head-shaving, robes) — not full ordination.
Full ordination is **Upasampada**, so (4) is right; **Bhikkhu / Bhikkhuni** are monk / nun on alms.
xa: **Uposatha** = **fortnightly** confession and rule-recitation (full/new moon).
**Vassa** = rainy-season retreat of **3 months**.
⚠ **Pravrajya** = going forth; **Upasampada** = full ordination; **Uposatha** = fortnightly confession.

28.s: The three refuges or pillars of Buddhism are:
28.x: The Triratna consists of Buddha as teacher, Dhamma as teaching and Sangha as the order.
28.tq: Test a standard three-part list with related doctrinal distractors.
xs: The three refuges (**Triratna**) are **Buddha, Dhamma and Sangha** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Buddha** = teacher; **Dhamma** = teaching; **Sangha** = order of monks and nuns.
xa: The Sangha were the **torch-bearers of Dhamma**; the organised Sangha drove Buddhism's spread.
**Vinaya** = the monastic code; **Uposatha** = fortnightly confession.

28.s:
Which of the following categories was excluded from membership of the Buddhist Sangha?

1. Criminals
2. Lepers
3. Persons with infectious diseases
4. Persons belonging to lower castes
28.x: Criminals, lepers and persons with infectious diseases were excluded. Caste was not a bar to admission for otherwise eligible persons.
28.tq: Separate explicit exclusions from the broad principle of caste-inclusive membership.
xs: **Criminals**, **lepers** and those with **infectious diseases** were excluded — so option **(2) 1, 2 and 3 only** is correct.
Statement 4 is wrong: the Sangha was open to all **above 15**, **regardless of caste**.
xa: **Women** were admitted after requests of **Ananda** and **Mahapajapati Gotami**.
Significance: Buddhism was a **caste-open**, socially accessible path.

28.s: The admission of women into the Buddhist Sangha was associated with the requests of:
28.x: Women were admitted after requests associated with Ananda and Mahapajapati Gotami, who became the first nun.
28.tq: Match the institutional development with the persons directly connected to it.
xs: Women were admitted after the requests of **Ananda and Mahapajapati Gotami** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Mahapajapati became the **first nun**.
**Upali** recited the Vinaya; **Mahakassapa** presided over the First Council; **Subhadda** was the last convert.
xa: The **Bhikkhuni Sangha** was taken to Sri Lanka by **Sanghamitta**.
It thrived **1,000+ years** until the Chola invasion of **1017 AD**.

28.s:
Consider the following statements about Buddhist monastic life:
1. Monks shaved their heads, wore yellow or saffron robes and lived on daily alms.
2. Vassa was a two-month rainy-season retreat.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
28.x: Statement 1 is correct: shaved heads, yellow/saffron robes and daily alms marked monastic life. Statement 2 is wrong: vassa was a three-month rainy-season retreat. Hence '1 only'.
28.tq: Vassa = 3-month rains retreat.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: monks had **shaved heads**, **yellow/saffron robes** and lived on **daily alms**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Vassa** was a **3-month** rainy-season retreat — so option **(1) 1 only** is correct.
xa: The Sangha had **democratic functioning** with power to punish.
**Uposatha** = fortnightly confession and rule-recitation.
**Parajika** = grave offence — expulsion.

28.s:
Vesak or Buddha Purnima commemorates which of the following events in the life of Gautama Buddha?
1. Birth
2. Enlightenment
3. Mahaparinirvana
4. First sermon at Sarnath
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
28.x: Vesak commemorates the birth, enlightenment and parinirvana of the Buddha. The first sermon at Sarnath is not included among the three events marked by Vesak.
28.tq: Separate the three defining events of Vesak from a related but distinct event in the Buddha’s life.
xs: **Vesak (Buddha Purnima)** marks the **birth**, **enlightenment** and **death** — so option **(1) 1, 2 and 3 only** is correct.
The **first sermon** at Sarnath is not one of the three.
xa: It falls on the **Vaisakha full moon**; the **UN recognised Vesak in 1999**.
Greetings by the President and PM on **1 May 2026** stressed **India-Nepal** Buddhist diplomacy.

28.s: Who founded the Maha Bodhi Society in 1891?
28.x: Anagarika Dharmapala founded the Maha Bodhi Society in 1891 to work for the restoration of Bodh Gaya to Buddhist control.
28.tq: Apply the founder–organisation association, a common history question pattern.
xs: The **Maha Bodhi Society (1891)** was founded by **Anagarika Dharmapala** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Its aim was to **restore Bodh Gaya** to Buddhist control.
**Shashanka** and **Pushyamitra Sunga** destroyed the original Bodhi tree; **Sariputta** was a chief disciple of the Buddha.
xa: The **Mahabodhi Temple** has been a **UNESCO site since 2002**.
Bodh Gaya = ancient **Uruvela**, on the **Niranjana**, where the Buddha was enlightened at **35**.

28.s: The relics of Sariputta and Mahamoggallana were sent from Sanchi to which country by the Ministry of Culture in June 2026?
28.x: In June 2026, the Ministry of Culture sent the relics of Sariputta and Mahamoggallana from Sanchi to Mongolia.
28.tq: Match the religious relics, source location and destination country without confusing them with India’s Nepal diplomacy reference.
xs: The relics of **Sariputta and Mahamoggallana** were sent from **Sanchi** to **Mongolia** (Jun **2026**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
They were the Buddha's **chief disciples**, and their relics are kept at Sanchi.
xa: On Buddha Purnima (**1 May 2026**), the President and PM's greetings stressed **India-Nepal** Buddhist diplomacy.
**Ananda** was the personal attendant; **Upali** recited the **Vinaya Pitaka**.

28.s: Bavari’s disciples, who came from the Godavari region, are associated with which development in the history of Buddhism?
o: They carried Buddhist relics from Sanchi to Mongolia.
They founded the Maha Bodhi Society at Bodh Gaya.
They secured UNESCO recognition for the Maha Bodhi Temple.
28.x: Bavari’s disciples from the Godavari region met the Buddha and helped bring Buddhism to Andhra.
28.tq: Connect the regional group with its specific role in the spread of Buddhism rather than with later institutional or heritage developments.
xs: **Bavari's disciples** from the **Godavari region** met the Buddha and **brought the faith to Andhra** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The relics went to **Mongolia** via the Ministry of Culture; the **Maha Bodhi Society** was founded by **Anagarika Dharmapala**.
xa: The **Mahabodhi Temple** is a **UNESCO** site since **2002**.
The organised **Sangha** drove Buddhism's spread.

28.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The original Bodhi Tree is stated to have been destroyed by Pushyamitra.
2. The original Bodhi Tree was later destroyed by Shashanka.
3. The Mahabodhi Temple became a UNESCO site in 2002.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
28.x: All three statements are correct in the stated account: destruction is attributed first to Pushyamitra and later to Shashanka, and the Mahabodhi Temple became a UNESCO site in 2002.
28.tq: Check each date and named-person association independently before selecting the combined code.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the original **Bodhi tree** was destroyed by **Pushyamitra Sunga** and by **Shashanka**.
Statement 3 is correct: the **Mahabodhi Temple** is a **UNESCO site since 2002** — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
xa: The **Maha Bodhi Society (1891)**, founded by **Anagarika Dharmapala**, worked to restore **Bodh Gaya**.
The Buddha was enlightened under the Bodhi tree at **Uruvela**, on the bank of the **Niranjana**, at **35**.

28.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Chaitya
(b) Vihara
(c) Stupa
(d) Vinaya Pitaka

List-II
(i) Monastic rules
(ii) Relic or burial tradition
(iii) Place of worship or prayer
(iv) Residence of monks
28.x: A Chaitya is a prayer hall, a Vihara a monks' residence, a Stupa a relic or burial mound and the Vinaya Pitaka the monastic rules, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
28.tq: Recall the function of each term.
n: A Chaitya was a place of worship. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
A Chaitya was a place of prayer. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
A Vihara was a residence of monks. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
A Stupa was associated with relics. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
A Stupa was associated with burial tradition. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
The Vinaya Pitaka contains monastic rules. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Chaitya** = **place of worship and prayer**; **Vihara** = **residence of monks**.
**Stupa** = **relics and burial tradition**; **Vinaya Pitaka** = **monastic rules**.
xa: **Anathapindika** donated **Jetavana Vihara**; **Vishakha** built **Pubharama**; **Bimbisara** built **Venuvana**.
Women were admitted as **Bhikshunis** at **Vaishali**; **Mahaprajapati** was the first woman in the Sangha.
**Sangha** membership was open to all **above 15**, regardless of caste.
**Vassa** = rainy-season retreat of **3 months**.

28.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Anathapindika
(b) Vishakha
(c) Bimbisara
(d) Buddhist Sangha
