37.x: All three statements are correct: Chandragupta had four provinces, these were ruled by Kumaras (royal princes) or governors helped by Mahamatras, and districts were called Vish or Ahara.
37.tq: Test several levels of administration together while keeping each statement independently verifiable.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Chandragupta** had **four provinces**.
Statement 2 is correct: they were ruled by **Kumaras** (royal princes) or governors, helped by **Mahamatras**.
Statement 3 is correct: districts were called **Vish / Ahara** — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
xa: Kumaras were also called **Kumaramatyas**.
District-level officers: **Rajukas, Pradeshikas, Yuktas** (UPSC **2025** key).
Governors named in sources: **Pushyagupta Vaishya** (Saurashtra) and **Yavanaraja Tushaspa** (under Ashoka).

37.s:
Which of the following officials were associated with the district level in the Mauryan administrative structure?
1. Rajukas
2. Pradeshikas
3. Yuktas
4. Gramika
Which of the statements given above are correct?
37.x: Rajukas, Pradeshikas and Yuktas were district-level officials. Gramika was the village head and therefore does not belong to the district-level group.
37.tq: Separate district officials from the village-level Gramika.
xs: **Rajukas, Pradeshikas and Yuktas** were district-level officers — option **(1) 1, 2 and 3 only** (UPSC **2025** key).
The **Gramika** was the **village head** (probably elected), not a district official.
xa: **Pradeshika**: district head for revenue and police; toured every **5 years** (Rock Edict III).
**Rajuka**: land survey and assessment, with **judicial powers** (Pillar Edict IV).
**Yukta**: subordinate revenue/secretarial officer, touring with the pradeshikas.
Sub-district: **Sthanika** (tax collector), **Gopa** (accountant over **5-10 villages**).

37.s:
Match List-I (Official) with List-II (Role):
a. Gopa
b. Sthanika
c. Gramika
i. Village head, probably elected
ii. Accountant over 5-10 villages
iii. Tax collector over a larger division
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
37.x: Gopa was the accountant over 5-10 villages (ii); Sthanika the tax collector over a larger division (iii); Gramika the village head, probably elected (i). So 'a-ii, b-iii, c-i' is right; the other codes swap Gopa and Sthanika or misplace the Gramika.
37.tq: Ladder upward: Gramika (village) -> Gopa (5-10 villages) -> Sthanika (larger division) -> district officers.
xs: **Gopa – accountant over 5-10 villages**, **Sthanika – tax collector over a larger division**, **Gramika – village head**: **a-ii, b-iii, c-i** — option **(1)**.
The other codes swap **Gopa** and **Sthanika** or misplace the Gramika.
xa: The **Gramika** was probably **elected** and worked with village elders.
Gopa and Sthanika were **sub-district** officers; above them were **Rajukas, Pradeshikas, Yuktas**.
The court ladder began at the **village** (Grama Sabha) and ended with the **king**.

37.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Rajukas dealt with land survey and assessment.
2. Rajukas possessed judicial powers.
3. Yuktas were subordinate revenue or secretarial officers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
37.x: All three statements are correct. Rajukas handled land survey and assessment and had judicial powers, while Yuktas served as subordinate revenue or secretarial officers.
37.tq: Combine the distinctive judicial and revenue functions of district officials with the subordinate role of Yukta.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Rajukas** handled **land survey and assessment**.
Statement 2 is correct: Rajukas had **judicial powers** (Pillar Edict IV).
Statement 3 is correct: **Yuktas** were subordinate **revenue/secretarial** officers — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
xa: Yuktas toured every **5 years** with the **pradeshikas** (Rock Edict III).
**Pradeshika** = district head for revenue and police.
⚠ **Agronomoi** (Megasthenes) were district officers for roads, irrigation and land measurement.

37.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Astynomoi — City administration through six municipal boards
Agronomoi — Roads, irrigation and land measurement
37.x: Rakshinas were the city police. Frontier forts were guarded by Anta-mahamattas; Agronomoi, Astynomoi and Dhamma Mahamattas have been correctly matched.
37.tq: Reject the wrong location-based assignment by separating city policing from frontier defence.
xs: **Rakshinas** were the **city police**, not guards of frontier forts — so option **(1)** is NOT correctly matched.
Frontier forts were guarded by the **Anta-mahamattas**.
**Dhamma Mahamatta** (Dhamma), **Astynomoi** (six municipal boards) and **Agronomoi** (roads, irrigation, land measurement) are correct.
xa: ⚠ **Agronomoi** = district; **Astynomoi** = city boards (both from **Megasthenes**).
**Gudhapurushas** were secret agents watching officials and provinces.
The **Antapala** was the frontier officer among the tirthas.

37.s: Which of the following groups consists only of titles that were NOT Mauryan officials?
37.x: Mahabaladhikrita, Mahadandanayaka and Mahasandhivigrahika were Gupta titles, not Mauryan officials. The other groups contain Mauryan administrative offices.
37.tq: Identify the out-group by recognising titles belonging to the Gupta administration.
xs: **Mahabaladhikrita, Mahadandanayaka and Mahasandhivigrahika** are **Gupta** titles, not Mauryan — option **(1)**.
**Panyadhyaksha, Sulkadhyaksha, Sitadhyaksha** are Mauryan **Adhyakshas**.
**Samaharta, Sannidhata** are tirthas and **Rajuka, Gopa, Gramika** local Mauryan officers.
xa: ⚠ **Bhagadugha** and **Sangrahitri** are **Vedic** titles — also not Mauryan.
⚠ Mauryan **Samaharta** (collector) vs Vedic **Sangrahitri** — a confusable pair.

37.s:
Arrange the following Mauryan settlement units from largest to smallest:
A. Sangrahana
B. Sthaniya
C. Kharvatika
D. Dronamukha
37.x: Sthaniya consisted of 800 villages, Dronamukha 400, Kharvatika 200 and Sangrahana 10; therefore the order is B, D, C, A.
37.tq: Arrange units by their numerical size, beginning with the largest figure.
xs: Largest to smallest: **Sthaniya (800) → Dronamukha (400) → Kharvatika (200) → Sangrahana (10)** — **B, D, C, A**, option **(1)**.
Options 2, 3 and 4 misplace Dronamukha or Kharvatika, or reverse the order.
xa: The same units appear in the **court ladder**: Village → **Sangrahana** → **Dronamukha** → **Janapada** → king.
Districts were called **Vish / Ahara**.
The **Gopa** kept accounts over **5-10 villages**.

37.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Manufactured goods committee — Inspection of manufactured goods
Committee for foreigners — Foreign residents and visitors
Commerce committee — Trade, prices, weights and measures
Sales-tax committee — Collection of land revenue
37.x: The sixth committee dealt with tax on sales, including imports and exports; it did not collect land revenue.
37.tq: Find the wrong function by distinguishing sales taxation from land revenue administration.
xs: The **6th committee** collected the **tax on sales** (imports and exports), not land revenue — so option **(4)** is NOT correctly matched.
The **5th** inspected manufactured goods, the **2nd** dealt with **foreigners**, the **4th** with trade, prices, weights and measures.
xa: The sales tax was **one-tenth**; **tax evasion on sales** was punishable by **death** (Megasthenes).
Land revenue was collected directly by **royal officials**; Megasthenes says the **king owned all land**.
Committee **1**: crafts and industries; committee **3**: census (births and deaths).

37.s:
Consider the following statements about Mauryan espionage:
1. Spies called gudhapurushas watched officials and provinces.
2. Samstha spies were wandering agents and Sanchara spies were stationary agents.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
37.x: Statement 1 is correct: gudhapurushas watched officials and provinces. Statement 2 is wrong: it is the reverse - Samstha were stationary and Sanchara were wandering. So '1 only' is right; '2 only', 'Both' and 'Neither' are wrong.
37.tq: Sanchara ~ 'sanchar' (move about) = wandering; Samstha ~ 'sthana' (place) = stationary.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **gudhapurushas** (spies) watched **officials and provinces**.
Statement 2 is wrong: it is reversed — **Samstha** spies were **stationary**, **Sanchara** spies **wandering**. So option **(1) 1 only**.
xa: Samstha guises: **kapatika, udasthita, grihapatika, vaidehaka, tapasa**.
Sanchara guises: **satri, tikshna, rasada, parivrajika** (women).
Spies worked under the **mahamatyapasarpa**.

37.s:
Consider the following statements about Mauryan courts:
1. Dharmasthiya courts tried civil cases such as marriage, contract and inheritance.
2. Kantakashodhana courts, meaning 'removal of thorns', also tried civil cases.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
37.x: Statement 1 is correct: Dharmasthiya courts were civil courts (marriage, contract, inheritance). Statement 2 is wrong: Kantakashodhana ('removal of thorns') courts were criminal courts. So '1 only' is right; '2 only', 'Both' and 'Neither' are wrong.
37.tq: Thorns removed = criminals removed: Kantakashodhana is criminal; Dharmasthiya is civil.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Dharmasthiya** courts tried **civil** cases — marriage, contract, inheritance.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Kantakashodhana** ("removal of thorns") courts tried **criminal** cases. So option **(1) 1 only**.
xa: Each court had **three judges and three amatyas**.
Kantakashodhana courts were presided over by **pradeshtris**.
⚠ **Dharmasthiya** = civil; **Kantakashodhana** = criminal.

37.s: Which of the following represents the correct hierarchy of Mauryan courts from the lowest to the highest level?
37.x: The judicial ladder proceeded from the village court to Sangrahana, Dronamukha, Janapada and finally the king.
37.tq: Arrange the administrative levels from the smallest judicial forum to the supreme authority.
xs: The court ladder ran **Village (Grama Sabha) → Sangrahana → Dronamukha → Janapada → king** — option **(2)**.
The **king** was the **final authority** and supreme judge.
xa: Settlement units: **Sangrahana = 10** villages, **Dronamukha = 400**, **Sthaniya = 800**.
Main courts: **Dharmasthiya** (civil), **Kantakashodhana** (criminal).
**Rajukas** at the district level also had **judicial powers**.

37.s:
Consider the following statements about Mauryan punishments:
1. Punishments included fines, amputation, mutilation and death.
2. The severity of punishment varied according to varna.
3. Megasthenes described a fully codified written penal code.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
37.x: Punishments included fines, amputation, mutilation and death, and their severity varied by varna. Megasthenes stated that there was no written code.
37.tq: Identify the false statement created by reversing an explicit qualification about written law.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: punishments included **fines, amputation, mutilation and death**.
Statement 2 is correct: **severity depended on varna**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Megasthenes** says there was **no written code** — so option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
xa: Civic offences like **dumping dirt** on streets drew fines.
Slave rules: selling a **pregnant slave** without arranging maternity was punished.
**Tax evasion on sales** was punishable by **death** (Megasthenes).

37.s: In the Mauryan administration, the term 'Pradvivaka' is associated with the
37.x: Pradvivaka was the chief judicial adviser or judge (APPSC G2 2019: judicial system). Revenue was under the Samaharta, espionage under the gudhapurushas, and the municipal boards were the Astynomoi of Megasthenes.
37.tq: Pradvivaka = chief judge (APPSC G2 2019).
xs: The **Pradvivaka** was the chief judicial adviser/judge — so it belongs to the **judicial system**, option **(2)** (APPSC G2 **2019**).
Revenue was under the **Samaharta**; espionage used **gudhapurushas**; municipal boards were Megasthenes' **Astynomoi**.
xa: Courts: **Dharmasthiya** (civil) and **Kantakashodhana** (criminal), each with three judges and three amatyas.
**Vyavaharika** = civil judge; **Pradeshtri** = criminal justice.
The **king** was the supreme judge.

37.s:
Match List-I (Revenue term) with List-II (Meaning):
a. Sita
b. Pranaya
c. Vivita
i. Pasture land and its dues
ii. Emergency tax ('gift of affection')
iii. Income from crown land
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
37.x: Sita was income from crown land (iii); Pranaya the emergency tax or 'gift of affection' (ii); Vivita pasture land and its dues (i). So 'a-iii, b-ii, c-i' is right; the other codes swap at least two meanings.
37.tq: Sita = crown land (Sitadhyaksha ran state farms); Pranaya = 'affection' gift in emergencies.
xs: **Sita – income from crown land**, **Pranaya – emergency tax ("gift of affection")**, **Vivita – pasture land dues**: **a-iii, b-ii, c-i** — option **(1)**.
The other codes swap at least two meanings.
xa: **Bhaga** = king's share of produce, normally **1/6** (Megasthenes: **1/4 to 1/6**).
**Hiranya** = tax paid only in **cash**; **Vana** = income from **forests**.
**Pindakara** = tax on **groups of villages**; **Bali** = additional levy.

37.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Pindakara — Tax assessed on groups of villages
Pranaya — Tax paid only in cash
37.x: Pindakara was a tax assessed collectively on groups of villages. Bhaga was the king’s share of produce, Pranaya an emergency tax and Hiranya a cash tax.
37.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate meanings assigned to neighbouring revenue terms.
xs: **Pindakara** was a tax assessed on **groups of villages** — option **(2)**.
**Bhaga** was the king's **share of produce**, not a forest tax (forest income = **Vana**).
**Pranaya** was an **emergency tax**; **Hiranya** was the tax paid only in **cash**; gardens gave **Setu**.
xa: Bhaga was normally **one-sixth**; at **Lumbini** it was cut to **one-eighth** (Rummindei pillar).
**Sita** = income from crown land; **Vivita** = pasture dues; **Bali** = additional levy.
Megasthenes says the **king owned all land**.

37.s: With reference to the Mauryan revenue system, which of the following statements is correct?
o: Bhaga was normally fixed at one-fourth of the produce.
Bhaga was normally the king’s one-sixth share of the produce.
Bhaga was collected only from merchants.
Bhaga was an emergency levy imposed during war.
37.x: Bhaga was normally the king’s share of agricultural produce, generally one-sixth. Megasthenes mentioned a range from one-fourth to one-sixth.
37.tq: Distinguish the normal rate from an alternative range mentioned by a historical observer.
xs: **Bhaga** was the king's **share of produce**, normally **one-sixth (1/6)** — option **(2)**.
**One-fourth** is only the upper end of **Megasthenes'** range (**1/4 to 1/6**), not the normal rate.
An emergency levy was **Pranaya**, not Bhaga.
xa: At **Lumbini**, bhaga was cut to **one-eighth** and bali exempted (Rummindei pillar).
**Bali** = additional levy/tribute.
Land revenue was the **main income** of the state.

37.s: Which statement about Mauryan land revenue, as described by Megasthenes, is correct?
o: The king was regarded as owning all land and revenue was collected directly by royal officials.
Revenue was collected exclusively through merchants.
Land was privately owned and taxes were collected by village assemblies.
Only forest land was treated as royal property.
37.x: Megasthenes stated that the king owned all land and that royal officials directly collected the revenue.
37.tq: Identify the authority responsible for ownership and collection instead of confusing it with local bodies.
xs: Megasthenes says the **king owned all land** and revenue was **collected directly by royal officials** — option **(1)**.
So land was not private, and collection was not through merchants or village assemblies.
xa: The king's share (**Bhaga**) per Megasthenes: **1/4 to 1/6**.
Revenue was gathered by the **Samaharta** (collector-general), helped by the **Bhagadhuk**.
**Tax evasion on sales** was punishable by **death** (Megasthenes).

37.s: With reference to Mauryan administration, Suvarnagiri was:
o: The southern capital of the empire
The northern capital of the empire
The principal centre of the Paura-janapada
37.x: Suvarnagiri was the southern capital of the Mauryan Empire. It was associated with the Dakshinapatha and the administration of the Deccan.
37.tq: Test the location and regional association of an administrative centre.
xs: **Suvarnagiri** was the **southern capital** of the empire — option **(1)**.
It was the capital of **Dakshinapatha** and governed the **Deccan**, with Andhra in its orbit.
The northern province (**Uttarapatha**) had its capital at **Taxila**.
xa: **Ujjain** = capital of **Avantirashtra**; **Tosali** = capital of **Kalinga**.
**Pataliputra** was the centre, under the emperor.
**Paura-janapada** assemblies were a check on the king, not a place.

37.s: Which one of the following best reflects the historical debate concerning the Arthashastra and Mauryan administration?
o: The Arthashastra describes an ideal administrative system, and the extent to which it was fully implemented remains disputed.
The Arthashastra describes only the actual practices of every Mauryan official without any theoretical element.
The Arthashastra was exclusively a religious text unrelated to administration.
The Arthashastra proves that the Mauryan Empire had no centralised administration.
37.x: The Arthashastra is understood to describe an ideal or normative administrative system. Historians debate how completely that ideal was implemented in practice.
37.tq: Distinguish a normative administrative model from its complete historical implementation.
xs: The **Arthashastra describes an ideal** system, and **how fully it was implemented is disputed** — option **(1)**.
It is an administrative text (Saptanga, tirthas, Adhyakshas), not a religious one.
Far from showing no centralisation, it describes a **highly centralised** state.
xa: The Mauryan state was the **first centralised bureaucratic empire**.
Megasthenes, by contrast, is an outside eyewitness — e.g. Pataliputra's **six committees of five**.
Kautilya: a kingdom **cannot run on one wheel**.

37.s: The Mauryan model of the Saptanga state and the 18 Tirthas was later adopted in Andhra by the
37.x: The Eastern Chalukyas (Ashtadasha Tirthas) and the Kakatiyas used the Saptanga and 18 Tirthas model. The Sungas, Kanvas, Indo-Greeks, Sakas, Kushanas and Western Kshatrapas are not linked with it.
37.tq: 18 Tirthas in Andhra = Eastern Chalukyas (Ashtadasha Tirthas), Kakatiyas.
xs: The **Eastern Chalukyas** (Ashtadasha Tirthas) and the **Kakatiyas** used the Saptanga and **18 Tirthas** model — option **(1)**.
The notes do not link the Sungas, Kanvas, Indo-Greeks, Sakas, Kushanas or Kshatrapas with it.
xa: ⚠ The Eastern Chalukya list (**Magallu** inscription) makes **Dandapala** a police chief; Kautilya's Dandapala heads the **army**.
⚠ The same list makes **Antapala** an inner-palace guard; the Mauryan Antapala was a **frontier** officer.
Each Mauryan tirtha drew **12,000 panas** a year.

38.s: Sita land in the Mauryan economy was:
o: Forest land reserved exclusively for hunting
Land donated permanently to Buddhist monasteries
Land owned collectively by village artisans
Crown land cultivated directly under state supervision
38.x: Sita was crown land cultivated for the state, under the supervision of the Sitadhyaksha, often using slaves and hired labourers.
38.tq: Directly identify the official economic meaning of a specialised term.
xs: **Sita** was **crown land cultivated directly for/under the state** — option **(4)**.
It was supervised by the **Sitadhyaksha** and worked often by **slaves and hired labourers**.
It was not forest, monastery or collective artisan land.
xa: The notes record **large-scale use of slaves** in farming on sita land.
**Dronavapa** = land sown with one **drona** of seed.
Revenue officials: **Samaharta**, **Gopa**, **Sthanika**.

38.s: Which one of the following statements about Mauryan agriculture is correct?
o: The state provided seed, cattle and tools as relief during drought and famine.
The state prohibited the use of hired labour on crown land.
Agriculture was treated as less important than long-distance trade.
Sita land was cultivated exclusively by free peasants.
38.x: Agriculture was the economic base, and the state provided relief such as seed, cattle and tools during drought and famine. Sita land also employed slaves and hired labourers.
38.tq: Apply the state-support principle to a famine situation.
xs: The state gave **seed, cattle and tools** as **famine relief** in drought and famine — option **(1)**.
Sita land used **slaves and hired labourers**, so hired labour was not banned nor were free peasants the only cultivators.
**Agriculture** was the **base** of the economy, not secondary to trade.
xa: Rainfall was measured in **drona** (rain gauge) near granaries, for **six regions**.
Mauryan rainfall records predate **Korea's Cheugugi** gauge (**1441 CE**).
Land revenue (**Bhaga**) was **1/4 to 1/6** of the produce (Megasthenes).

38.s:
Which of the following were under state monopoly or control in the Mauryan period?
1. Mining
2. Forestry
3. Salt
4. Liquor
5. Arms and metallurgy
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
38.x: The Mauryan state exercised monopoly or strong control over mining, forestry, salt, liquor, arms and metallurgy.
38.tq: Recognise the comprehensive state-control list rather than selecting only revenue items.
xs: The state controlled **mining, forestry, salt, liquor, arms and metallurgy** — all five, option **(4)**.
Mines and metals were run by the **Akaradhyaksha** as a **state monopoly**.
xa: **Iron** deposits near Magadha were one basis of **Magadhan power**.
**Tax evasion** could mean **death**.
Sale of goods was **state-supervised**.

38.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Mauryan economic regulation:
1. Sale of goods was supervised by the state.
2. Usury prevailed in the absence of banking.
3. NBPW was a typical Mauryan pottery.
4. Tax evasion was punishable only by a small fine.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: The state supervised the sale of goods, usury prevailed in the absence of banking, and NBPW was typical Mauryan pottery. Tax evasion could incur the death penalty, so statement 4 is false.
38.tq: Use the severe-penalty trap to identify the incorrect statement.
xs: Statements 1–3 are correct: **sale of goods was state-supervised**, **usury** prevailed without banking, and **NBPW** was the typical Mauryan pottery.
Statement 4 is wrong: **tax evasion could mean death**, not a small fine — so option **(1) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
xa: The Arthashastra's interest rate: **15% a year**; students, poor and sick got **debt relief**.
**Mauryan polish** on pillars has a metallic shine like **NBPW** pottery.
Punch-marked coins and **NBPW** sherds reach **Bangladesh, Odisha, Andhra and Karnataka**.

38.s: The annual rate of interest mentioned in the Arthashastra was:
38.x: The Arthashastra mentions an annual interest rate of 15 percent.
38.tq: Recall the exact percentage rather than a commonly assumed round figure.
xs: The Arthashastra fixes interest at **15 percent (15%) a year** — option **(3)**.
**Usury** prevailed because there was **no banking**.
xa: **Students, the poor and the sick** got relief from debt.
Imperial currency: **punch-marked silver coins**.
Sale of goods was **state-supervised**.

38.s: Which one of the following statements about Mauryan guilds is correct?
o: Good roads weakened the growth of crafts.
Shrenis were exclusively military units with no economic role.
Guilds were prohibited from supporting religious institutions.
Merchants, artisans and shrenis financed early Buddhist centres, including centres in Andhra.
38.x: Good roads and state incentives encouraged crafts, while merchants, artisans and shrenis financed early Buddhist centres, including those in Andhra.
38.tq: Connect infrastructure, craft growth and guild patronage without reversing the relationship.
xs: **Merchants (shreshthis), artisans and shrenis** financed early **Buddhist centres**, including in **Andhra** — option **(4)**.
Good roads and **state incentives** spread crafts — they did not weaken them.
Shrenis were economic guilds; their **military role** (shreni troops) was only one aspect.
xa: The Arthashastra counts **shreni troops** among the types of army.
Caravans were led by a **Sarthavaha**; the state took **road tax** for protection.
**Bhattiprolu** is the most ancient stupa in Andhra.

38.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Mauryan imperial currency?
o: Punch-marked silver coins bearing symbols such as peacocks and hills
Machine-struck gold coins bearing portraits of emperors
Copper coins bearing only inscriptions in Greek
Unmarked iron coins used exclusively for military payments
38.x: Mauryan imperial currency consisted mainly of punch-marked silver coins, often carrying symbols such as peacocks and hills.
38.tq: Use the distinctive combination of denomination form, metal and symbols.
xs: Imperial currency was **punch-marked silver coins** with symbols such as **peacocks and hills** — option **(1)**.
They were minted in **state mints**; **barter** continued alongside.
xa: The silver coin was the **Pana (karshapana)**; **Mashaka** and **Kakani** were copper; **Suvarna** gold.
Punch-marked silver panas go back to the **Mahajanapada** age (**6th century BCE**).
Pana was the APPSC G2 **2011** answer.

38.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
38.x: Suvarna was a gold coin. Mashaka and Kakani were copper, while Pana or karshapana was silver.
38.tq: Use the metal table to distinguish closely related coin names.
xs: **Suvarna** was the **gold** coin — option **(1)**.
**Mashaka** was **copper**, not silver; **Kakani** was **copper** (**1/4 mashaka**), not gold.
**Pana** (karshapana) was **silver**, not copper.
xa: "Mauryan silver coin was called" — **Pana**, not Niska, Kakini or Shatamana.
Punch-marked silver panas date to the **Mahajanapada** age.
Coins carried symbols such as **peacocks and hills**.

38.s: The silver coin of the Mauryan period mentioned in the Arthashastra was called
38.x: The Arthashastra names the silver coin pana (karshapana). Kakani was a copper coin worth a quarter mashaka; Niska and Shatamana are not the Mauryan silver coin named in the Arthashastra.
38.tq: Mauryan silver = Pana (karshapana); copper = mashaka, kakani; gold = suvarna.
xs: The Arthashastra's silver coin was the **Pana (karshapana)** — option **(3)** (APPSC G2 **2011**).
**Kakani** was a **copper** coin worth **1/4 mashaka**; Niska and Shatamana are not the Mauryan silver coin.
xa: **Mashaka** = copper; **Suvarna** = gold.
Punch-marked silver coins bore **peacocks and hills** symbols.
They were minted in **state mints**, with barter continuing.

38.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
38.x: Tamralipti was an east-coast port and the principal port of the Ganga basin. Bharukachchha and Sopara were west-coast ports.
38.tq: Look for the reversed coast association in an otherwise familiar port list.
xs: **Tamralipti** was on the **east** coast, not the west — so option **(4)** is NOT correctly matched.
**Sopara** and **Bharukachchha (Broach)** were **west**-coast ports.
xa: Tamralipti was the **main port of the Ganga basin** (APPSC **2012**).
**Bernis (Berenice)** was the **Red Sea** port for trade with **Egypt**.
The **Uttarapatha** ran from **Taxila** to **Tamralipti**.

38.s: The Uttarapatha connected which of the following routes?
o: Rajgir through Kalinga to Sri Lanka
38.x: Uttarapatha was the northern highway running from Taxila through Pataliputra to Tamralipti.
38.tq: Recall the route by identifying its north-western starting point and eastern terminus.
xs: **Uttarapatha** was the northern highway from **Taxila** through the Ganga valley / **Pataliputra** to **Tamralipti** — option **(2)**.
The southern route through Andhra was the **Dakshinapatha**.
xa: The **royal highway** ran from the north-west to Pataliputra.
Tamralipti was the **main port of the Ganga basin**.
Caravans were led by a **Sarthavaha**.

38.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes Dakshinapatha?
o: It was a royal road confined to the Ganga valley.
It was the great southern trade route, with the Krishna–Godavari delta as one of its nodes.
It was a sea route exclusively connecting Egypt and Sri Lanka.
It was the northern highway from Taxila to Tamralipti.
38.x: Dakshinapatha was the great southern trade route, and the Andhra region, including the Krishna–Godavari delta, was a node on it.
38.tq: Discriminate between the northern Uttarapatha and the southern Dakshinapatha.
xs: **Dakshinapatha** was the **great southern trade route**, with the **Krishna-Godavari delta** (Andhra) a node on it — option **(2)**.
The northern highway from Taxila to Tamralipti is the **Uttarapatha**.
xa: **Suvarnagiri** was the capital of the Dakshinapatha province.
Merchants, artisans and **shrenis** financed early Buddhist centres in **Andhra**.
West-coast ports: **Bharukachchha (Broach)** and **Sopara**.

38.s:
Consider the following statements about Mauryan trade:
1. Caravans were led by a Sarthavaha.
2. The state took road tax in return for protecting caravans.
3. Crafts spread despite poor roads and without any state incentive.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
38.x: Statement 1 is correct: caravans were led by a Sarthavaha. Statement 2 is correct: road tax was collected for protection. Statement 3 is wrong: good roads and state incentives spread crafts. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses statement 2, and the options with 3 accept a false statement.
38.tq: Sarthavaha leads caravans; roads + state incentives spread crafts.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: caravans were led by a **Sarthavaha**.
Statement 2 is correct: the state took **road tax** for protection.
Statement 3 is wrong: **good roads and state incentives** spread crafts — so option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
xa: Sale of goods was **state-supervised**.
The **royal highway** ran from the north-west to **Pataliputra**.
Interest: **15% a year** (Arthashastra).

38.s: The Red Sea port associated with Mauryan trade with Egypt was:
38.x: The Egyptian connection through the Red Sea was linked with the port of Bernis, or Berenice.
38.tq: Distinguish the foreign Red Sea port from the Indian coastal ports.
xs: **Berenice (Bernis)** was the **Red Sea** port for trade with **Egypt** — option **(4)**.
**Sopara** and **Bharukachchha** were Indian **west**-coast ports; **Tamralipti** was on the **east** coast.
xa: Foreign partners: **Greece, Persia, Egypt, Syria, Sri Lanka, Java, Sumatra**.
Exports: **diamonds, pearls, muslin, fine textiles**.
Tamralipti was the **main port of the Ganga basin** (APPSC **2012**).

38.s: Which of the following commodities was included among the exports of the Mauryan period?
38.x: Diamonds, pearls, muslin and fine textiles were among the commodities exported during the period.
38.tq: Identify the historically appropriate export group from the stated commodity list.
xs: **Diamonds and pearls** were Mauryan exports — option **(2)**.
Other exports: **muslin** and **fine textiles**.
xa: Trade partners: **Greece, Persia, Egypt, Syria, Sri Lanka, Java, Sumatra**.
Ports: **Tamralipti** (east), **Bharukachchha** and **Sopara** (west).
Caravans were led by a **Sarthavaha**.

38.s: Megasthenes divided Indian society into how many classes in the Indica?
38.x: Megasthenes described seven classes: philosophers, farmers, herdsmen or hunters, artisans, soldiers, overseers and councillors.
38.tq: Directly recall the distinctive numerical classification.
xs: Megasthenes' **Indica** divides society into **seven** classes — option **(1)** (BPSC **2017**).
They are **philosophers, farmers, herdsmen/hunters, artisans, soldiers, overseers, councillors**.
xa: ⚠ **Nine** is Kautilya's count of **slave categories**, not Megasthenes' classes.
Megasthenes noted **hereditary occupation** and **endogamy**.
He said India had **no slavery** and theft was **rare**.

38.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Megasthenes' account of Indian society:
1. Occupations were generally hereditary.
2. Endogamy was practised.
3. Theft was common.
4. He reported that India had no slavery.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: Megasthenes described hereditary occupations and endogamy and stated that India had no slavery. He regarded theft as rare, making statement 3 false.
38.tq: Separate the three true social observations from the reversed statement about theft.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: occupations were **hereditary** and **endogamy** was practised.
Statement 4 is correct: Megasthenes said India had **no slavery**.
Statement 3 is wrong: he found **theft rare** — so option **(1) 1, 2 and 4 only**.
xa: ⚠ Megasthenes: **no slaves**; Kautilya: **nine categories of slaves** — sources differ.
He also noted there was **no written law**.
On the **Andhras** he noted **30 walled towns** (some notes say 80).

38.s: Which one of the following statements regarding social groups mentioned in the Arthashastra is correct?
o: Shudras were prohibited from owning land.
The Antyavasayins were seven classes of Greek philosophers.
The Antyavasayins were five mixed castes outside Aryan society.
38.x: Kautilya referred to five mixed castes called Antyavasayins as being outside Aryan society. Shudras could own land, while learned men were called Sishtas.
38.tq: Use a same-source discrimination question with swapped meanings as distractors.
xs: The **Antyavasayins** were **five mixed castes** outside Aryan society — option **(4)**.
**Shudras could own land**, so option 1 is wrong.
**Sishtas** were **learned men**, not hired labourers (those were **Karmakaras**).
xa: Centres of learning: **Taxila** (most famous), **Ujjain**, **Varanasi**.
**Chandalas** and **Shvapakas** (untouchables) grew in number.
Bhadrabahu's **Kalpasutra** belongs to this age.

38.s:
Which of the following was the most famous centre of learning among the following?
1. Taxila
2. Ujjain
3. Varanasi
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: All three were described as equally famous
38.x: Taxila was the most famous centre of learning among Taxila, Ujjain and Varanasi. All three were recognised centres, but they were not described as equally famous.
38.tq: Notice the comparison within a list instead of treating all listed places as identical.
xs: **Taxila** was the **most famous** centre of learning — option **(3)** (UKPSC **2010**).
**Ujjain** and **Varanasi** were also centres, but not equally famous.
xa: Learned men were called **Sishtas**.
Bhadrabahu's **Kalpasutra** belongs to this age.
Taxila was the capital of **Uttarapatha** and the start of the northern highway.

38.s:
In the Arthashastra, a person could become a slave through which of the following circumstances?
1. Birth
2. Sale
3. Capture in war
4. Judicial punishment
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
38.x: The Arthashastra recognised slavery arising through birth, sale, capture in war and judicial punishment.
38.tq: Use an inclusive list question to check every route into slavery.
xs: Slavery arose from **birth, sale (self-sale), capture in war and judicial punishment** — all four, option **(4)**.
But **no Arya** could be made a slave.
xa: Kautilya lists **nine categories of slaves** (dasas); Ashokan inscriptions also mention dasas.
Freedom could be gained **by payment**.
A female slave who bore her master a **son** became **free**.

38.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
38.x: Karmakaras were hired wage labourers. Vishti meant unpaid forced labour for the state, while shreni referred to a guild.
38.tq: Separate labour categories from tax, administrative and guild terms.
xs: **Karmakaras** were **wage (hired) labourers** — option **(1)**.
**Vishti** was **unpaid forced labour** for the state, not paid guild service.
**Shreni** meant a **guild**; the orchard tax was **Kara**; **Samaharta** was a revenue official.
xa: Vishti later became the Telugu **Vetti**.
**Moksha** = divorce; **Stridhana** = a woman's own property.
Seed-measure unit: **Dronavapa** (land sown with one drona of seed).

38.s: Which one of the following statements about female slaves is NOT correct?
o: Freedom could be obtained by payment.
A female slave who bore her master a son became free.
A penalty existed for selling a pregnant slave without arranging maternity protection.
The son of a female slave was denied any legal connection with the master.
38.x: The son of a female slave who bore her master a child was entitled to the legal status of the master's son. The other statements reflect protections or routes to freedom.
38.tq: Reject the statement that reverses the legal status of the child.
xs: Statement 4 is NOT correct — the son of a female slave by her master was **legitimate**, with the **legal status of the master's son**; option **(4)**.
The others are correct: freedom **by payment**, a female slave bearing her master a son became **free**, and a penalty for selling a **pregnant slave**.
xa: ⚠ UPSC **2022** set these three statements about the female slave.
Sources of slavery: **birth, sale, capture in war, judicial punishment**.
**No Arya** could be made a slave.

38.s: How many categories of slaves (dasas) are listed by Kautilya in the Arthashastra?
38.x: Kautilya lists nine categories of slaves. Seven is the number of Megasthenes' social classes, and four and twelve are not Kautilya's figure.
38.tq: Kautilya: 9 kinds of slaves; Megasthenes: 7 classes and 'no slavery'.
xs: Kautilya lists **nine** categories of slaves (dasas) — option **(3)**.
**Seven** is the number of Megasthenes' social classes.
xa: ⚠ Megasthenes said India had **no slaves** — the sources differ.
Ashokan inscriptions also mention **dasas**.
**Karmakaras** were wage labourers; **Vishti** was forced labour.

38.s: Stridhana in the Arthashastra referred to:
o: Property belonging exclusively to the king
A woman's own property, including jewellery and maintenance
Land held jointly by a village community
38.x: Stridhana was a woman's own property, including jewellery and resources for maintenance.
38.tq: Distinguish a personal property category from public and communal property.
xs: **Stridhana** was a **woman's own property** — **jewellery and maintenance** — option **(3)**.
It was not royal property, a tax on widows or village land.
xa: **Moksha** = divorce, allowed to a wife **deserted** by her husband.
**Widow remarriage** was permitted.
**Anuloma and pratiloma** inter-varna marriages occurred.

38.s:
Consider the following statements regarding women and marriage in the Arthashastra:
1. A wife deserted by her husband could seek divorce called moksha.
2. Remarriage of widows was permitted.
3. Remarriage of long-deserted wives was permitted.
4. Inter-varna marriages of both anuloma and pratiloma types occurred.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: The Arthashastra recognised moksha for a wife deserted by her husband, permitted widow and long-deserted-wife remarriage, and records both anuloma and pratiloma inter-varna marriages.
38.tq: Use the comprehensive option after verifying each legal and social provision.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: a **deserted wife** could seek divorce (**moksha**) (UPSC **1996**).
Statements 2 and 3 are correct: **widows** and **long-deserted wives** could remarry.
Statement 4 is correct: **anuloma and pratiloma** marriages occurred — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
xa: Divorce was also allowed for **mutual enmity** in certain marriage forms.
**Stridhana** = a woman's own property (jewellery, maintenance).
⚠ Some notes say widow remarriage ceased.

38.s: Which one of the following best describes the religious policy of the Mauryan state?
o: Liberal and tolerant practice with freedom of faith, alongside protection of varna and ashrama
Compulsory adherence to one officially enforced faith
Complete separation of religion from all state activity
38.x: Mauryan religious conditions were broadly liberal and tolerant, allowing freedom of faith, while the state continued to protect the institutions of varna and ashrama.
38.tq: Choose the option that preserves both tolerance and social regulation.
xs: Mauryan religious policy was **liberal and tolerant** — **free choice of faith**, no persecution — while the state protected **varna and ashrama**; option **(1)**.
There was no single enforced faith and no persecution.
xa: **Chandragupta** followed **Bhadrabahu** (Jainism) to Shravanabelagola.
**Ashoka and Dasaratha** gave caves to the **Ajivikas**.
**Brahmanism** continued — Kautilya was a Brahmana, **'dvijarshabh'**.

38.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Ajivikas in the Mauryan period:
1. Ashoka donated caves to the Ajivikas.
2. Dasaratha also donated caves to the Ajivikas.
3. The Barabar and Nagarjuni caves are associated with such donations.
4. Ashokan edicts identify the Ajivikas as Nirgranthas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: Ashoka and Dasaratha donated the Barabar and Nagarjuni caves to the Ajivikas. The edicts mention Ajivikas and Nirgranthas as distinct groups, so statement 4 is false.
38.tq: Separate the correctly associated cave donors from the swapped sectarian identification.
xs: Statements 1–3 are correct: **Ashoka** and **Dasaratha** gave the **Barabar/Nagarjuni** caves to the **Ajivikas**.
Statement 4 is wrong: **PE VII** names **Ajivikas and Nirgranthas** as separate groups — so option **(2) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
xa: The Barabar caves are **India's oldest surviving rock-cut caves** (**3rd c. BCE**).
They lie in **Jehanabad district, Bihar** (near Gaya).
The caves were later used by **Buddhist, Jain and Hindu** worshippers.

38.s:
Consider the following statements about religion in the Mauryan period:
1. Ashoka patronised Buddhism, stupas and the Sangha.
2. Brahmanism declined, and Kautilya himself rejected Brahmanical tradition.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
38.x: Statement 1 is correct: Ashoka patronised Buddhism, stupas and the Sangha. Statement 2 is wrong: Brahmanism continued, and Kautilya was a Brahmana called 'dvijarshabh'. So '1 only'; '2 only' and 'Both' accept the false claim, 'Neither' rejects statement 1.
38.tq: Brahmanism continued; Kautilya = dvijarshabh.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Ashoka** patronised **Buddhism, stupas and the Sangha**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Brahmanism continued**, and **Kautilya** was himself a Brahmana (**'dvijarshabh'**) — so option **(1) 1 only**.
xa: Policy was **liberal and tolerant**, with the state protecting **varna and ashrama**.
Tradition: Ashoka redistributed the relics into **84,000 stupas**.
**Chandragupta** followed **Bhadrabahu** (Jainism).

38.s:
Consider the following statements about Mauryan society:
1. Untouchable groups such as Chandalas and Shvapakas grew in number.
2. Ashokan edicts explicitly mention sati and list the varnas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
38.x: Statement 1 is correct: Chandalas and Shvapakas, untouchable groups, grew in number. Statement 2 is wrong: Ashokan edicts mention neither varna nor sati. So '1 only'; the options accepting statement 2 are wrong, and 'Neither' rejects statement 1.
38.tq: Edicts: no varna, no sati.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Chandalas and Shvapakas** (untouchables) **grew in number**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Ashokan edicts mention neither varna nor sati** — so option **(1) 1 only**.
xa: The **Antyavasayins** were **five mixed castes** outside Aryan society.
The state still protected **varna and ashrama**.
**Shudras could own land** (Arthashastra).

38.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Mauryan art:
1. The Mauryan period saw a shift from stone to wood as the main medium.
2. Royal (court) art included palaces, pillars, stupas and caves.
3. Yaksha-yakshi statues and terracotta figurines belonged to folk (popular) art.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
38.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the shift was from wood to stone, not the reverse. Statement 2 is correct: palaces, pillars, stupas and caves are royal art. Statement 3 is correct: yaksha-yakshi statues and clay/terracotta figurines are folk art. So only '2 and 3 only' fits; the other options include the reversed statement 1.
38.tq: Mauryan art = wood to stone; court vs folk streams.
xs: Statement 1 is wrong: the shift was from **wood to stone**, not the reverse.
Statement 2 is correct: **royal (court) art** covered **palaces, pillars, stupas, caves**.
Statement 3 is correct: **yaksha/yakshi statues** and clay/terracotta figurines were **folk (popular) art** — so option **(2) 2 and 3 only**.
xa: Yaksha/yakshi figures are the **earliest large-scale human sculptures** in Indian art.
Folk art arose from **folk worship**, not royal patronage.
Mauryan stone art **began Indian monumental architecture**.

38.s:
Consider the following pairs of Mauryan art objects and their findspots:
1. Nude male torso — Lohanipur (Patna)
2. Portrait slab of Ashoka — Kanaganahalli (Karnataka)
3. 80-pillared hall — Rampurva
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
38.x: Pair 1 is correct: the nude male torso comes from Lohanipur, Patna. Pair 2 is correct: the portrait slab of Ashoka is from Kanaganahalli, Karnataka. Pair 3 is wrong: the 80-pillared hall is at Kumrahar near Patna; Rampurva is known for the bull capital. So '1 only' misses pair 2, '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' wrongly accept pair 3.
38.tq: Kumrahar = 80-pillared hall; Rampurva = bull capital.
xs: Pair 1 is correct: the **nude male torso** comes from **Lohanipur** (Patna).
Pair 2 is correct: the **portrait slab of Ashoka** is from **Kanaganahalli** (Karnataka).
Pair 3 is wrong: the **80-pillared hall** is at **Kumrahar**; **Rampurva** gave the **bull** capital — so option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
xa: **Didarganj** (near Patna) gave the polished sandstone **chauri-bearer Yakshi**.
**Dhauli** (near Bhubaneswar) has the **rock-cut elephant**.
**Manibhadra Yaksha** (inscribed) is from **Parkham** (Mathura) — RPSC **2021** key.

38.s:
Which of the following are works of the Mauryan period?
1. Rock-cut elephant at Dhauli
2. Didarganj Yakshi
3. Sanchi stupa (original core)
4. Pillared hall at Kumrahar
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
38.x: All four are Mauryan: the Dhauli rock-cut elephant near Bhubaneswar, the polished Didarganj chauri-bearer Yakshi, Ashoka's brick stupa at Sanchi and the 80-pillared hall at Kumrahar. Every other option leaves out at least one Mauryan work.
38.tq: APPSC G1 2024 set: Dhauli, Didarganj, Sanchi, Kumrahar - all Mauryan.
xs: All four are Mauryan — **Dhauli elephant, Didarganj Yakshi, Sanchi stupa, Kumrahar hall** — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4** (APPSC G1 **2024**: all four).
**Dhauli** is near Bhubaneswar; the **Didarganj** Yakshi is of polished sandstone.
**Sanchi** has Ashoka's **brick** core; **Kumrahar** has the **80-pillared hall**.
xa: The Dhauli elephant (**3rd c. BCE**) is earlier than **Udayagiri Varaha**, Mahabalipuram and Lingaraja (UPSC **2015**).
Sanchi was later **stone-cased by the Sungas**; toranas added in the **Satavahana** period.
Kumrahar's hall had **8 rows x 10** polished pillars.

38.s: Mauryan pillars are best described as:
o: Fluted wooden shafts with bronze capitals
Multi-block granite pillars with square bases
Monolithic circular shafts of Chunar sandstone with a lustrous polish
Composite brick pillars covered with lime plaster
38.x: Mauryan pillars were monolithic, free-standing and circular, generally made of Chunar sandstone and finished with the characteristic Mauryan polish.
38.tq: Use a compact material-and-construction description for direct identification.
xs: Mauryan pillars were **monolithic**, free-standing, **circular** shafts of **Chunar sandstone** with a **lustrous polish** — option **(3)**.
They were **smooth** (not fluted), stone (not wood or brick) and had **no base**.
xa: **"Mauryan polish"** gives a metallic shine, like **NBPW** pottery.
The sandstone is **buff/grey**.
Sequence: shaft → **inverted lotus (ghanta)** → abacus → **capital animal**.

38.s:
Arrange the principal components of a Mauryan pillar from bottom to top:

A. Animal capital
B. Shaft
C. Bell-shaped inverted lotus
D. Abacus
38.x: The order is shaft, bell-shaped inverted lotus, abacus and crowning animal capital.
38.tq: Follow the physical sequence from the base upward.
xs: Bottom to top: **shaft → bell-shaped inverted lotus → abacus → animal capital** — **B, C, D, A**, option **(1)**.
The pillar had **no base**, so the shaft is the lowest part.
xa: Names: abacus = **chowki**, inverted lotus = **Baithaki / Ghantaki**, decorative band = **Mekhala**, animal = **Shirsha**.
Animals on capitals: **lion, bull, elephant**.
⚠ The distinct **inverted lotus** and round abacus are cited against Persian influence.

38.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Persian influence debate on Mauryan pillars:

1. Both traditions show polished surfaces and animal capitals.
2. Mauryan pillars generally have bases like Persian pillars.
3. Mauryan edicts resemble those of Darius in form and certain expressions.
4. Mauryan shafts are smooth, whereas Persian shafts are generally fluted.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is false because Mauryan pillars generally lack the bases characteristic of Persian pillars.
38.tq: Find the reversed comparison in the statement set.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: both have **polished surfaces and animal capitals**.
Statement 2 is wrong: Mauryan pillars have **no base**; Persian pillars do.
Statements 3 and 4 are correct: edicts resemble **Darius's** ("**lipi/dipi**"), and Mauryan shafts are **smooth**, not fluted — option **(2) 1, 3 and 4 only**.
xa: The Mauryan **inverted lotus** bell and round abacus with free-standing animals are distinct.
Verdict: the differences point to an **Indian adaptation**.
Edicts in both shift from **third person** to **first person**.

38.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Capital)

b. Bull

List-II (Site)

38.s: According to tradition, the relics of the Buddha originally preserved in eight stupas were redistributed by Ashoka into how many stupas?
38.x: Tradition states that Ashoka redistributed the Buddha’s relics from the original eight stupas into 84,000 stupas.
38.tq: Use the distinctive numerical association rather than confusing the original eight with the later traditional figure.
xs: Tradition says Ashoka redistributed the relics from **8** stupas into **84,000 stupas** — option **(4)**.
The original **8** stupas held the Buddha's relics.
xa: **Sanchi (Great Stupa)** has Ashoka's **brick** stupa over relics.
**Dharmarajika** stupas are at **Sarnath** and **Taxila**.
**Kesariya** (Bihar) is the **largest brick stupa**.

38.s:
Consider the following statements about stupas:
1. Sanchi has Ashoka's brick stupa built over relics.
2. The stone toranas with Jataka scenes at Sanchi were added in the Gupta period.
3. Kesariya in Bihar is described as the largest brick stupa.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
38.x: Statement 1 is correct: Ashoka built a brick stupa over relics at Sanchi. Statement 2 is wrong: the toranas with Jataka scenes were added in the Satavahana period, not the Gupta period. Statement 3 is correct: Kesariya is the largest brick stupa. So '1 and 3 only'; '1 only' misses Kesariya, and the options with 2 accept the wrong period.
38.tq: Sanchi toranas = Satavahana period.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: Sanchi has Ashoka's **brick stupa** over relics.
Statement 2 is wrong: the **toranas with Jataka scenes** were added in the **Satavahana** period, not Gupta.
Statement 3 is correct: **Kesariya** is the **largest brick stupa** — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
xa: The **Sungas** stone-cased the Sanchi stupa.
⚠ **Sanchi** = India's largest stupa; **Kesariya** = largest brick stupa.
**Bharhut** has sculpted railings with **narrative scenes**.

38.s:
Consider the following statements about Chandragupta's palace at Pataliputra:
1. Megasthenes compared it with the palaces of Susa and Ecbatana.
2. It was admired by Hiuen Tsang in the 5th century CE.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
38.x: Statement 1 is correct: Megasthenes compared it to Susa and Ecbatana. Statement 2 is wrong: it was Fa-Hien who admired it in the 5th century CE. So '1 only'; '2 only' and 'Both' accept the wrong pilgrim, 'Neither' rejects statement 1.
38.tq: 5th c. CE visitor = Fa-Hien.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Megasthenes** compared the palace to those of **Susa and Ecbatana**.
Statement 2 is wrong: it was **Fa-Hien** (**5th c. CE**), not Hiuen Tsang, who admired it — so option **(1) 1 only**.
xa: **Kumrahar** yielded the **80-pillared hall** (8 rows x 10).
**Bulandibagh** yielded remains of the **wooden palisade**.
The city was built mainly of **timber**.

38.s:
Consider the following statements about the city of Pataliputra during the Mauryan period:

1. Its principal construction material was timber.
2. It had a wooden wall with towers and gates.
3. Polished stone pillars were also used in important structures.
4. Its excavated remains show that the entire city was constructed exclusively of stone.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because Pataliputra was mainly a wooden city, although polished stone pillars were used in important structures.
38.tq: Reject the extreme word ‘exclusively’ in a material-comparison statement.
xs: Statements 1–3 are correct: Pataliputra was built mainly of **timber**, with a **wooden wall with towers and gates** and **polished stone pillars**.
Statement 4 is wrong: the city was not all stone — so option **(2) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
xa: **Bulandibagh** gave the **wooden palisade** remains.
**Kumrahar** gave the **80-pillared hall**, pillars polished and carved with vines.
Pataliputra was run by **6 committees of 5 members** (Megasthenes).

38.s: Which archaeological site yielded remains of the wooden palisade of Pataliputra?
38.x: Bulandibagh yielded remains of the wooden palisade associated with the city of Pataliputra.
38.tq: Associate the specific excavation site with the structural remains found there.
xs: **Bulandibagh** yielded the remains of a **wooden palisade** — option **(3)**.
**Kumrahar** gave the **80-pillared hall**; **Rampurva** the **bull** capital; **Sarnath** the four-lion capital.
xa: The city was mainly of **timber/wood**.
Megasthenes compared the palace to **Susa and Ecbatana**.
**Fa-Hien** (5th c. CE) admired the palace.

38.s: The seven caves located in the Barabar-Nagarjuni group are collectively known as:
38.x: The seven caves together are called Satghar, meaning ‘Seven Houses’.
38.tq: Direct recall of the collective name of a named group.
xs: The seven caves together are called **Satghar** ("**Seven Houses**") — option **(1)**.
They are **4** Barabar + **3** Nagarjuni caves.
xa: Carved from **granite** with a mirror polish; vaulted ceilings give an **echo**.
Barabar caves were **in the news** in **2026** as the "blueprint" of Indian rock-cut architecture.
Dedicated to the **Ajivikas**.

38.s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Lomas Rishi — Barabar
2. Gopika — Nagarjuni
3. Vadathika — Barabar
4. Karna Chopar — Barabar

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
38.x: Lomas Rishi and Karna Chopar belong to Barabar, while Gopika belongs to Nagarjuni. Vadathika is a Nagarjuni cave, so pair 3 is incorrect.
38.tq: Find the incorrectly assigned cave before selecting the coded combination.
xs: Pairs 1, 2 and 4 are correct: **Lomas Rishi** and **Karna Chopar** are Barabar caves, **Gopika** a Nagarjuni cave.
Pair 3 is wrong: **Vadathika** is a **Nagarjuni** cave — so option **(2) 1, 2 and 4 only**.
xa: Other Barabar caves: **Sudama**, **Viswamitra**; other Nagarjuni cave: **Vahiyaka**.
**Lomas Rishi** has the **earliest stone ogee arch**.
**Gopika** is the largest Nagarjuni cave and has inscriptions.

38.s: The dedicatory Brahmi inscriptions in the Barabar caves refer to Ashoka by which title?
38.x: The dedicatory Brahmi inscriptions refer to Ashoka as ‘King Piyadasi’.
38.tq: Test the exact royal title used in an inscription.
xs: The dedicatory **Brahmi** inscriptions call Ashoka **"King Piyadasi"** — option **(4)**.
**Three** Barabar caves carry Ashoka's inscriptions.
xa: ⚠ The inscriptions are **3rd c. BCE**, not 6th c. (UPPSC **2017**).
**Gopika** (Nagarjuni) also has inscriptions.
The caves were given to the **Ajivikas**.

38.s:
Consider the following statements about the Barabar and Nagarjuni caves:
1. They are located in Jehanabad district of Bihar, near Gaya.
2. Their dedicatory inscriptions belong to the 6th century BCE.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
38.x: Statement 1 is correct: the caves are in Jehanabad district, Bihar, near Gaya (not Guntur, AP, which is a mix-up with Nagarjunakonda). Statement 2 is wrong: the inscriptions are Mauryan, 3rd century BCE, not 6th century. So '1 only'; '2 only' and 'Both' accept the wrong date, 'Neither' rejects the correct location.
38.tq: Barabar = Jehanabad, Bihar; inscriptions 3rd c. BCE.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the caves are in **Jehanabad district, Bihar**, near **Gaya**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the inscriptions are **3rd c. BCE**, not **6th** c. (UPPSC **2017**) — so option **(1) 1 only**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes place the Nagarjuni caves in **Guntur, AP** — a mix-up with **Nagarjunakonda**.
The inscriptions are in **Brahmi** and call Ashoka **"King Piyadasi"**.
The caves were made by **Ashoka** and **Dasharatha**.

38.s: Which feature of the Lomas Rishi cave is regarded as an early example in Indian rock-cut architecture?
o: A stone ogee-shaped arch at the entrance
38.x: The Lomas Rishi entrance has the earliest known stone ogee, or horseshoe-shaped, arch. It imitates the form of a thatched wooden hut.
38.tq: Associate a distinctive architectural feature with its monument.
xs: **Lomas Rishi**'s entrance is the **earliest stone ogee-shaped (horseshoe) arch** — option **(1)**.
It copies a **thatched wooden hut** (the **Parnashala** style).
xa: Lomas Rishi is a **Barabar** cave, with **Sudama**, **Viswamitra** and **Karna Chopar**.
The caves are carved from **granite** with a mirror polish.
FIRSTs: earliest rock-cut caves = **Barabar**; earliest stone ogee arch = **Lomas Rishi**.

38.s: Which of the following are the oldest surviving rock-cut caves in India?
38.x: The Barabar caves in Bihar, dedicated by Ashoka to the Ajivikas in the 3rd century BCE, are India's oldest surviving rock-cut caves. Badami, Ajanta and Ellora are all later.
38.tq: Oldest rock-cut = Barabar (3rd c. BCE), not Badami (UPSC 2013).
xs: The **Barabar caves** are **India's oldest surviving rock-cut caves** (**3rd c. BCE**) — option **(3)**.
Not **Badami** (UPSC **2013** trap); Ajanta and Ellora are also later.
xa: They were dedicated by **Ashoka** to the **Ajivikas**.
**4 + 3 = Satghar** (Barabar + Nagarjuni).
**Guntupalli** chaitya (AP) is compared with the Barabar caves.

38.s: Which pair is correctly matched in relation to popular art of the Mauryan period?
38.x: The inscribed Manibhadra Yaksha was found at Parkham near Mathura. The Chauri-bearer Yakshi is from Didarganj, the Yakshi is associated with Besnagar, and the Yaksha with Noh.
38.tq: Start from the distinctive inscribed figure and eliminate shifted findspots.
xs: The inscribed **Manibhadra Yaksha** was found at **Parkham** (Mathura) — option **(1)** (RPSC **2021** key).
The **chauri-bearer Yakshi** is from **Didarganj**, not Noh.
The **Yakshi** is from **Besnagar**, and the **Yaksha** from **Noh** (Bharatpur).
xa: Yaksha/yakshi figures are the **earliest large-scale human sculptures**.
They came from **folk worship**, not royal patronage.
Yakshas were revered in **Jainism, Buddhism and Hinduism**.

38.s: Yaksha worship was shared by which of the following religious traditions?
38.x: Yakshas were revered in Jainism, Buddhism and Hinduism, showing the broad religious spread of their worship.
38.tq: Identify the complete set of traditions associated with a shared cult.
xs: Yakshas were revered in **Jainism, Buddhism and Hinduism** alike — option **(1)** (UPSC).
Their worship had **folk** origins, not royal patronage.
xa: Yaksha/yakshi statues are the **earliest large-scale human sculptures**.
The inscribed **Manibhadra Yaksha** is from **Parkham** (Mathura).
Yaksha from **Noh** (Bharatpur, Rajasthan).

38.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the antiquity of Indian structures?
o: Sanchi is regarded as the most ancient stupa in India and Bharhut as the most ancient in Andhra.
Bhattiprolu is regarded as the most ancient stupa in India and Sanchi as the most ancient in Andhra.
Bharhut is regarded as the most ancient stupa in India and Bhattiprolu as the most ancient stupa in Andhra.
Barabar caves are regarded as the most ancient stupa in India.
38.x:
Bharhut is called the most ancient stupa in India, while Bhattiprolu is called the most ancient stupa in Andhra.
⚠ Sources differ: the 'most ancient stupa' title goes to different sites in different texts (Bharhut, Sanchi, Piprahwa). This key follows the notes.
38.tq: Discriminate between similar claims about the oldest structures in India and Andhra.
xs: The notes call **Bharhut** the **most ancient stupa in India** and **Bhattiprolu** the **most ancient in Andhra** — option **(3)**.
**Barabar** are caves, not stupas; **Sanchi** is called India's **largest** stupa.
xa: ⚠ Separately, **Sanchi** is the **oldest stone structure** in India (APPSC key **2018**).
Bharhut is known for **sculpted railings with narrative scenes**.
**Bhattiprolu** is the AP angle — Andhra's oldest stupa.

38.s: Among the following, which is the correct chronological order from earliest to latest?
o: Dhauli elephant — Udayagiri Varaha — Mahabalipuram monuments — Lingaraja Temple
Udayagiri Varaha — Dhauli elephant — Lingaraja Temple — Mahabalipuram monuments
Dhauli elephant — Mahabalipuram monuments — Udayagiri Varaha — Lingaraja Temple
Lingaraja Temple — Dhauli elephant — Udayagiri Varaha — Mahabalipuram monuments
38.x: The Dhauli elephant belongs to the third century BCE and is earlier than the Gupta Udayagiri Varaha, Pallava monuments at Mahabalipuram and the Lingaraja Temple.
38.tq: Fix the earliest Mauryan item first, then place the later Gupta, Pallava and temple examples.
xs: Earliest to latest: **Dhauli elephant → Udayagiri Varaha → Mahabalipuram → Lingaraja** — option **(1)** (UPSC **2015**).
The **Dhauli elephant** is Mauryan (**3rd c. BCE**); **Udayagiri Varaha** is **Gupta** (Chandragupta II); **Mahabalipuram** is **Pallava**.
xa: Dhauli is near **Bhubaneswar, Odisha**.
The Dhauli elephant is one of the four works confirmed Mauryan (APPSC G1 **2024**).
Oldest rock-cut: **Barabar caves**.

38.s: Which one of the following is the oldest stone structure in India?
38.x: The Sanchi Stupa, begun under Ashoka, is the oldest of the four. Ajanta's caves are later (mostly Satavahana to Vakataka), Brihadeeswara is Chola (11th c.) and Konark is 13th-century.
38.tq: APPSC 2018 key: oldest stone structure = Sanchi Stupa.
xs: The **Sanchi Stupa** is the **oldest stone structure** in India among these — option **(2)** (APPSC key **2018**).
**Ajanta, Konark** and **Brihadeeswara** are all later.
xa: Sanchi's Ashokan **brick** core was **stone-cased by the Sungas**.
Oldest rock-cut structures: **Barabar caves**.
Some notes: **Bharhut** = most ancient stupa in India; **Bhattiprolu** = in Andhra.

38.x: The Sarnath capital has been adopted as the National Emblem of India.

xs: The **Sarnath** capital (four lions + Dharmachakra) is now India's **National Emblem** — option **(3)**.
The earliest stone ogee arch is **Lomas Rishi**; the largest brick stupa is **Kesariya**.
xa: Other capitals: **bull – Rampurva**, **single lion – Lauriya Nandangarh**, **elephant – Sankisa**.

xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Balirajgarh** fort is in **Madhubani, Bihar**.

xa: It was in the news in **Apr 2026**.
**Vaishya Tekri** (Ujjain) may hold a Mauryan stupa larger than Sanchi.

38.s: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the Mauryan rainfall records?
o: They were recorded after the invention of modern rain gauges in Europe.
They are contemporary only with the Pala period.
They predate Korea’s Cheugugi gauge of 1441 CE.
They post-date Korea’s Cheugugi gauge of 1441 CE.

xs: Mauryan rainfall records **predate Korea's Cheugugi gauge (1441 CE)** — option **(3)**.
Rainfall was measured in **drona** near granaries, for **six** regions.

38.s: Vaishya Tekri at Ujjain is significant in current archaeological discussions because it may contain:
o: A third-century BCE stupa larger than Sanchi, along with punch-marked and cast Avanti coins
The earliest known Iron Age settlement of South India
A Kushana palace containing only gold coins
A Gupta-period university at the Uttarapatha junction

xs: **Vaishya Tekri** (Ujjain) may hold a **3rd-century BCE Mauryan stupa, possibly larger than Sanchi**, and has yielded **punch-marked and cast Avanti coins** — option **(1)**.

**Balirajgarh** (Madhubani) also yielded **punch-marked coins**.
**Sanchi** is called India's **largest stupa**.
