I: **Stupa No. 1** at Sanchi is the **principal / primary stupa**.
II: **Stupa No. 2** holds remains of **Ashoka's Dhamma Mahamatras** (monks of the missionary era).
III: **Stupa No. 3** holds remains of **Sariputra and Mudgalayana** (Sariputta and Moggallana).
xa: **Sanchi** (Raisen, MP) is considered the **best stupa architecturally**.
Ashoka's brick stupa was later **stone-cased by the Sungas**.
**Bharhut** (Satna, MP) was discovered by **Alexander Cunningham**.

39.s:
Which of the following pairs correctly represents the two parts of the later Mauryan Empire?
1. Western part — Kunala and later Samprati
2. Eastern part — Dasharatha to Brihadratha
3. Western part — Brihadratha and Dasharatha
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
39.x: Kunala and later Samprati were associated with the western part, while Dasharatha through Brihadratha ruled the eastern part. Brihadratha and Dasharatha were not rulers of the western division.
39.tq: Reject the option that swaps the two territorial divisions.
xs: Pair 1 is correct: the **western** part was under **Kunala**, later **Samprati**.
Pair 2 is correct: the **eastern** part (Pataliputra) ran from **Dasharatha** to **Brihadratha**.
Pair 3 is wrong: Brihadratha and Dasharatha ruled the **east** — so option **(3) 1 and 2 only**.
xa: The **Vishnu Purana** lists **seven successors** of Ashoka.
Usual list: **Kunala, Dasharatha, Samprati, Shalishuka, Devavarman, Shatadhanvan, Brihadratha**.
The **Indo-Greeks** virtually replaced the western rulers by **180 BC**.

39.s: The western later Mauryan territories were virtually supplanted by the Indo-Greeks by about
39.x: The Indo-Greeks had virtually replaced the western later Mauryas by about 180 BC.
39.tq: Distinguish the date of western displacement from the dates of Mauryan succession.
xs: The **Indo-Greeks** virtually replaced the western later Mauryas by **180 BC** — option **(4)**.
**232 BC** is Ashoka's death; **187 BC** is the Sunga coup.
xa: The western rulers were **Kunala** and later **Samprati**.
Indo-Greek leaders: **Demetrius**, later **Menander**.
**Antiochus III** crossed the Hindu Kush c. **206 BC**.

39.s:
Which of the following was a major foreign threat to the Mauryan Empire after Ashoka?
1. Invasions by the Bactrian or Indo-Greek rulers
2. The advance of Demetrius and later Menander
3. The establishment of a Mauryan naval base in Greece
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
39.x: Bactrian or Indo-Greek invasions, including those associated with Demetrius and Menander, threatened the north-west. A Mauryan naval base in Greece was not a recorded development.
39.tq: Identify the two related external threats and reject the geographically implausible addition.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: **Bactrian (Indo-Greek) invasions** struck the north-west under **Demetrius**, later **Menander**.
Statement 3 is not in the record — so option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
xa: **Antiochus III (Seleucid)** crossed the Hindu Kush c. **206 BC**.
The **Great Wall of China** (c. **220 BC**) diverted **Scythian** tribes towards India.
**Menander (Milinda)** had his capital at **Sakala (Sialkot)**.

39.s: Antiochus III crossed the Hindu Kush around 206 BC and obtained tribute from
39.x: Antiochus III crossed the Hindu Kush around 206 BC and took tribute from the local ruler Subhagasena.
39.tq: Match the foreign ruler, approximate date and local ruler.
xs: **Antiochus III** took tribute from the local ruler **Subhagasena** — option **(4)**.
He was a **Seleucid** king who crossed the **Hindu Kush** c. **206 BC**.
**Demetrius** and **Menander** were Indo-Greek invaders; **Jalauka** ruled **Kashmir**.
xa: The **Great Wall** (c. **220 BC**) pushed **Scythian** tribes towards India.
The Mauryas **neglected frontier defence** (UPSC).
By **180 BC** the Indo-Greeks had virtually replaced the western Mauryas.

39.s: The construction of the Great Wall of China around 220 BC affected the Mauryan north-west mainly because it
o: diverted Scythian tribes westward and southward towards India
forced the Indo-Greeks to migrate to Egypt
ended all contact between China and India
enabled the Mauryas to control Bactria
39.x: The Great Wall diverted Scythian tribes towards the west and south, increasing pressure on regions near India while Mauryan frontier defence weakened.
39.tq: Trace the stated cause–effect chain in an external-threat question.
xs: The **Great Wall of China** (c. **220 BC**) **diverted Scythian tribes westward and south towards India** — option **(1)**.
This added to the pressure on a north-west frontier the Mauryas had **neglected**.
xa: **Antiochus III** crossed the Hindu Kush c. **206 BC**.
**Bactrian (Indo-Greek)** invasions under **Demetrius** and **Menander**.
Indo-Greek raids **drained resources**.

39.s: The Andhra or Deccan region broke away from Mauryan control under the
o: Satavahanas, who had earlier been Mauryan feudatories
39.x: The Satavahanas, earlier Mauryan feudatories, emerged as the breakaway power in the Andhra or Deccan region.
39.tq: Distinguish the Deccan breakaway power from the powers of Kalinga and the north-west.
xs: **Andhra/Deccan** broke away under the **Satavahanas**, earlier **Mauryan feudatories** — option **(2)**.
**Kharavela** (Chedi) led **Kalinga**; the **Kanvas** ruled Magadha; **Menander** was Indo-Greek in the north-west.
xa: The Puranas call the Satavahanas **Andhra-bhrityas**.
Founder: **Simuka (Srimukha)**.
Ashokan edicts at **Erragudi** and **Rajula Mandagiri** (Kurnool) show Mauryan rule in Andhra.

39.s: Yajnasena, mentioned in Malavikagnimitram, was associated with the breakaway of
39.x: Yajnasena is associated with Vidarbha in the account of the regions that broke away after Ashoka.
39.tq: Use the source–person–region triple association.
xs: **Yajnasena** (Malavikagnimitram) is linked with the breakaway of **Vidarbha** — option **(2)** (UPSC).
**Kalinga** broke away under the **Chedis (Kharavela)**; **Kashmir** under **Jalauka**.
xa: **Malavikagnimitram** is by **Kalidasa**.
It also records **Vasumitra** defeating a **Yavana** army on the **Sindhu**.
The **north-west** fell to the **Indo-Greeks**.

39.s: Who founded the Sunga dynasty in Magadha?
39.x: Pushyamitra Sunga founded the Sunga dynasty after overthrowing the Mauryas.
39.tq: Use the founder–dynasty association directly.
xs: The Sunga dynasty was founded by **Pushyamitra Sunga**, the Mauryan **commander-in-chief (senani)** — option **(3)**.
**Brihadratha** was the last Maurya; **Vasudeva Kanva** founded the **Kanva** dynasty.
xa: The Sungas were the **immediate successors** of the Mauryas in Magadha (APPSC G2 **2003**).
Pushyamitra was a **Brahmana** of the **Bharadvaja gotra**.
He performed **two Ashvamedhas**.

39.s: Pushyamitra Sunga seized power from the Mauryas by
o: defeating the Indo-Greeks in the north-west
obtaining the throne through a council of ministers
assassinating Brihadratha during an army review
marrying into the Mauryan royal family
39.x: Pushyamitra, the Mauryan commander-in-chief, killed Brihadratha during a military review, thereby carrying out a military coup.
39.tq: Identify the actor, occasion and manner of accession.
xs: Pushyamitra **assassinated Brihadratha at a military review** of the army — option **(3)** (APPSC **2023**; BPSC **2008**).
It was a **military coup** by the Mauryan **commander-in-chief**.
xa: The army-review detail comes from **Bana's Harshacharita**.
Year: **187 BC** (UPSC); some notes say c. **185 BCE**.
⚠ BPSC **2008** key — the king killed was **Brihadratha**.

39.s: The Sunga dynasty was founded approximately in
39.x: The Sunga dynasty is generally dated to 187 BC, though some accounts give approximately 185 BCE.
39.tq: Distinguish the close alternative dates by placing the key in the chronological sequence.
xs: The Sungas came to power in **187 BC** (UPSC) — option **(3)**.
Some notes and the AP History PYQ book give c. **185 BCE**.
**232 BC** is Ashoka's death; **206 BC** Antiochus III; **180 BC** the Indo-Greek takeover in the west.
xa: The coup: **Pushyamitra** killed **Brihadratha** at a military review.
Order in Magadha: **Mauryas → Sungas → Kanvas**.
The Kanvas ruled c. **73-28 BC**.

39.s: Which one of the following represents the correct chronological order of the dynasties that ruled Magadha?
39.x: The Mauryas were followed by the Sungas, who were subsequently succeeded by the Kanvas.
39.tq: Fix the first dynasty and then identify the immediate successor.
xs: The order in Magadha was **Mauryas → Sungas → Kanvas** — option **(1)**.
Then came the **Satavahana** conquest.
xa: Sungas founded by **Pushyamitra** in **187 BC**.
Kanvas founded by **Vasudeva Kanva**, who killed the last Sunga **Devabhuti**.
The last Kanva, **Susharman**, was ended by the **Andhras/Satavahanas**.

39.s:
Consider the following pairs of theories of Mauryan decline and historians:
1. Brahmanical reaction — H. P. Shastri
2. Ashoka's pacifism — D. D. Kosambi
3. Financial crisis — D. D. Kosambi
4. Over-centralisation — Romila Thapar
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
39.x: Pair 1 is correct: H. P. Shastri gave the Brahmanical reaction theory. Pair 2 is wrong: the pacifism theory is H. C. Raychaudhuri's. Pair 3 is correct: Kosambi gave the financial crisis theory. Pair 4 is correct: Romila Thapar stressed over-centralisation. So '1, 3 and 4 only'; every other option includes pair 2 or leaves out a correct pair.
39.tq: Pacifism = Raychaudhuri; finance = Kosambi.
xs: Pair 1 is correct: **Brahmanical reaction — H.P. Shastri**.
Pair 2 is wrong: **Ashoka's pacifism** is **H.C. Raychaudhuri**'s theory, not Kosambi's.
Pairs 3 and 4 are correct: **financial crisis — D.D. Kosambi**; **over-centralisation — Romila Thapar** — option **(2) 1, 3 and 4 only**.
xa: Raychaudhuri: after **Kalinga**, non-violence **dulled the army's fighting spirit**.
Kosambi: army, bureaucracy and **Dhamma** spending emptied the treasury; **debased** coins.
**Divyavadana** evidence: revolts at **Taxila** against wicked officials.

39.s: Which one of the following is NOT identified as a factor in the decline of the Mauryan Empire?
o: Weak and oppressive successors after Ashoka
A permanent alliance with the Indo-Greeks
39.x: A permanent alliance with the Indo-Greeks was not a cause of Mauryan decline. Indo-Greek raids and pressure were among the external problems faced by the empire.
39.tq: Find the option that reverses the recorded cause into an alliance.
xs: A **permanent alliance with the Indo-Greeks** was not a cause — option **(4)**; the Indo-Greeks were in fact **invaders**.
**Weak, oppressive successors**, **neglect of the north-west frontier** and **super-heavy taxation** are all listed causes (UPSC).
xa: Indo-Greek raids **drained resources**.
Financial strain: **Dhamma** spending, gifts to the **Sangha**, **debased** coins.
Taxes fell even on **actors and prostitutes** (Arthashastra).

39.s: Which one of the following was cited as evidence for the financial crisis of the Mauryan Empire?
o: Reduction in expenditure on the army
Debasement of later punch-marked coins through increased alloy in silver
Increase in the purity of later silver coins
39.x: The increased alloy content in later punch-marked silver coins has been interpreted as evidence of fiscal strain and debasement.
39.tq: Use the financial indicator and reject its exact opposite.
xs: **Debasement of later punch-marked coins** — more **alloy in the silver** — is evidence for the financial crisis — option **(3)**.
This is **D.D. Kosambi**'s **financial crisis** theory.
xa: Other evidence: heavy spending on the **Dhamma mission** and donations to the **Sangha**.
**New taxes on everything**, even actors and prostitutes → revenue hunger.
Kosambi: a huge **army** and **bureaucracy** emptied the treasury.

39.s:
Ashoka’s expenditure on which of the following was regarded as a strain on the Mauryan treasury?
1. Dhamma missions
2. Donations to the Buddhist Sangha
3. Construction of Indo-Greek fortifications
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
39.x: Spending on Dhamma missions and donations to the Buddhist Sangha was considered a burden on the treasury. Construction of Indo-Greek fortifications was not cited as such an expenditure.
39.tq: Separate the two recorded fiscal burdens from the invented third item.
xs: **Dhamma missions** and **donations to the Buddhist Sangha** strained the treasury — option **(3) 1 and 2 only** (UPSC).
**Indo-Greek fortifications** are not mentioned in the notes.
xa: This supports **Kosambi**'s **financial crisis** theory.
Coins were **debased** — more alloy in the silver.
⚠ **Raychaudhuri** blamed Ashoka's **pacifism**, not his spending.

39.s: Pushyamitra Sunga belonged to which gotra and held which position before founding the Sunga dynasty?
39.x: Pushyamitra Sunga was a Brahmana of the Bharadvaja gotra and served as a senapati.
39.tq: Test the identity of a ruler through the paired details of lineage and office.
xs: Pushyamitra was a **Brahmana senapati** of the **Bharadvaja gotra** — option **(4)**.
He was the Mauryan **commander-in-chief (senani)** who killed Brihadratha.
xa: He led a strong **Brahmanical revival** with **two Ashvamedhas**.
**Patanjali** is linked with his court.
The Sunga core: **Magadha, Malwa-Vidisha, Narmada valley**.

39.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Pushyamitra Sunga:
1. He performed two Ashvamedha sacrifices.
2. The Ayodhya inscription of Dhanadeva refers to his Ashvamedhas.
3. Patanjali is associated with his court.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
39.x: All three statements are correct. Pushyamitra performed two Ashvamedhas, the Ayodhya inscription of Dhanadeva is associated with this tradition, and Patanjali is linked with his court.
39.tq: Verify a ruler by separating ritual evidence, inscriptional evidence and court associations.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: Pushyamitra performed **two Ashvamedhas**.
Statement 2 is correct: they are recorded in the **Ayodhya inscription of Dhanadeva**.
Statement 3 is correct: **Patanjali** is linked with his court — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
xa: He was a **Brahmana** of the **Bharadvaja gotra**.
⚠ **Divyavadana** calls him a **persecutor of Buddhists** — disputed.
His grandson **Vasumitra** beat a **Yavana** army on the **Sindhu**.

39.s: Which statement best reflects the Buddhist persecution debate concerning Pushyamitra Sunga?
o: The debate concerns only his patronage of Jainism and not Buddhism.
The allegation is universally accepted because all Buddhist monuments were destroyed under him.
The allegation occurs in Buddhist texts, whereas the growth of Sanchi and Bharhut under Sunga rule provides a contrasting line of evidence.
The allegation is found only in Greek accounts and is rejected by all Indian sources.
39.x: Divyavadana describes Pushyamitra as a persecutor of Buddhists, but the growth of Sanchi and Bharhut under Sunga rule complicates that claim.
39.tq: Balance a literary allegation against material and archaeological evidence instead of accepting an extreme conclusion.
xs: The persecution charge comes from **Buddhist texts (Divyavadana)**, while the **growth of Sanchi and Bharhut** under Sunga rule points the other way — option **(3)**.
It is neither universally accepted nor a Greek claim.
xa: Against the **Brahmanical-reaction** theory: Pushyamitra was a **Mauryan general**, and **Buddhist art thrived** under the Sungas.
The Sungas **stone-cased** Ashoka's brick stupa at Sanchi.
Pushyamitra led a **Brahmanical revival** (two Ashvamedhas).

39.s: According to Malavikagnimitram, who defeated a Yavana army on the Sindhu river?
39.x: Malavikagnimitram records that Vasumitra, the grandson of Pushyamitra, defeated a Yavana army on the Sindhu river.
39.tq: Distinguish the commander who won the battle from the ruler whose dynasty was involved.
xs: **Kalidasa's Malavikagnimitram** says **Vasumitra**, Pushyamitra's grandson, defeated a **Yavana** army on the **Sindhu** — option **(4)**.
**Menander** and **Demetrius** were the Indo-Greek (Yavana) side.
xa: The same play names **Yajnasena** of **Vidarbha**.
Pushyamitra held the Ganga heartland against **Demetrius** and **Menander**.
Menander debated **Nagasena** in the **Milindapanho**.

39.s: Which statement regarding the end of the Kanva dynasty is correct?
o: Susharman was overthrown by the Andhras or Satavahanas.
Bhumimitra was defeated by Kharavela at Kalinga.
39.x: The last Kanva ruler, Susharman, was ended by the Andhras or Satavahanas.
39.tq: Identify the correct ruler–successor relationship rather than a famous neighbouring power.
xs: The last Kanva, **Susharman**, was ended by the **Andhras/Satavahanas** — option **(1)**.
**Vasudeva** founded the dynasty; **Menander**, **Kharavela** and **Pushyamitra** are not linked to the Kanva end.
xa: Kanva kings: **Vasudeva, Bhumimitra, Narayana, Susharman** (c. **73-28 BC**).
The Satavahanas **defeated the Sunga-Kanva line**.
Satavahana founder: **Simuka (Srimukha)**.

39.s: The Kanva dynasty was founded by Vasudeva Kanva after he killed the last Sunga ruler
39.x: Vasudeva Kanva, a Brahmana minister, killed Devabhuti, the last Sunga, and seized power. Vasumitra and Agnimitra were earlier Sungas, and Brihadratha was the last Maurya, killed by Pushyamitra.
39.tq: Devabhuti (last Sunga) killed by Vasudeva Kanva; Brihadratha (last Maurya) killed by Pushyamitra.
xs: **Vasudeva Kanva**, a Brahmana minister, killed the last Sunga **Devabhuti** — option **(3)** (UPSC **2003**).
**Vasumitra** was Pushyamitra's grandson; **Brihadratha** was the last Maurya, killed by **Pushyamitra**.
xa: The Kanvas ruled c. **73-28 BC**.
The last Kanva **Susharman** fell to the **Satavahanas**.
Order: **Mauryas → Sungas → Kanvas**.

39.s:
Consider the following statements about the Hathigumpha inscription:
1. It gives a year-by-year record of Kharavela's reign.
2. It is in the Udayagiri-Khandagiri caves of Odisha.
3. It belongs to the 4th century BC.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
39.x: Statement 1 is correct: it is a year-by-year record of Kharavela's reign. Statement 2 is correct: it is in the Udayagiri-Khandagiri caves, Odisha. Statement 3 is wrong: it belongs to the 2nd century BC. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses the location and the options with 3 accept the wrong date.
39.tq: Hathigumpha: Kharavela, 2nd c. BC, Odisha.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Hathigumpha** gives a **year-by-year record** of **Kharavela**'s reign.
Statement 2 is correct: it is in the **Udayagiri-Khandagiri caves**, Odisha.
Statement 3 is wrong: it is of the **2nd c. BC**, not the 4th — so option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
xa: Kharavela was a **Jaina** king of the **Chedi (Mahameghavahana)** line.
He raided **Magadha** and brought back the **Jina image** the Nandas had taken.
⚠ **Nanaghat** is **Naganika**'s inscription, not Rudradaman's.

39.s:
Consider the following statements about Kharavela:
1. He raided Magadha and brought back the Jina image taken by the Nandas.
2. He sent an army west only after an alliance with Satakarni.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
39.x: Statement 1 is correct: Kharavela raided Magadha and recovered the Jina image the Nandas had taken. Statement 2 is wrong: he sent an army west ignoring Satakarni, not in alliance with him. So '1 only'.
39.tq: Kharavela ignored Satakarni.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: Kharavela **raided Magadha** and brought back the **Jina image** the **Nandas** had taken.
Statement 2 is wrong: he sent an army west **ignoring Satakarni**, not in alliance — so option **(1) 1 only**.
xa: His deeds are in the **Hathigumpha** inscription (Udayagiri-Khandagiri, Odisha).
He was a **Jaina** king of the **Chedi** line.
⚠ **Nanaghat** = **Naganika**.

39.s: Which one of the following pairs of ruler and inscription is correctly matched?
39.x: Kharavela's Hathigumpha inscription is in the Udayagiri-Khandagiri caves of Odisha. The Nanaghat inscription belongs to the Satavahana queen Naganika, so pairing it with Rudradaman or Kharavela is wrong, and Naganika has nothing to do with Hathigumpha.
39.tq: Hathigumpha = Kharavela; Nanaghat = Naganika; Junagadh = Rudradaman.
xs: **Kharavela – Hathigumpha** is correct — option **(2)**.
**Nanaghat** is the inscription of **Naganika**, so pairing it with **Rudradaman** or Kharavela is wrong.
Naganika has nothing to do with Hathigumpha.
xa: Hathigumpha is in the **Udayagiri-Khandagiri caves**, Odisha, **2nd c. BC**.
It gives a **year-by-year** record of Kharavela's reign.
Kharavela was a **Jaina** king of the **Chedi (Mahameghavahana)** line.

39.s: Who was regarded as the founder of the Satavahana dynasty?
39.x: Simuka, also known as Srimukha, is regarded as the founder of the Satavahana dynasty.
39.tq: Distinguish the dynasty's founder from rulers and founders of neighbouring post-Mauryan houses.
xs: The Satavahana founder was **Simuka (Srimukha)** — option **(3)**.
**Vasumitra** was a Sunga; **Vasudeva Kanva** founded the Kanvas; **Satakarni** was the king Kharavela ignored.
xa: The Puranas call the Satavahanas **Andhra-bhrityas**.
They were **feudatories of the Mauryas** before independence.
They were the **first to unite the Krishna-Godavari region**.

39.s:
Consider the following statements about the Satavahanas:
1. They were feudatories of the Mauryas before becoming independent in the Deccan.
2. The Puranas refer to them as Andhra-bhrityas.
3. They were the first to unite the Krishna-Godavari region.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
39.x: All three statements are correct. The Satavahanas began as Mauryan feudatories, are called Andhra-bhrityas in the Puranas, and united the Krishna-Godavari region.
39.tq: Combine political origin, textual nomenclature and regional expansion in one coded question.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the Satavahanas were **Mauryan feudatories** who became independent in the **Deccan**.
Statement 2 is correct: the Puranas call them **Andhra-bhrityas**.
Statement 3 is correct: they **first united the Krishna-Godavari region** — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
xa: Founder: **Simuka (Srimukha)**.
They **defeated the Sunga-Kanva line**, ending **Susharman**.
Other Deccan feudatory chiefs: **Bhojas, Maharathis, Rashtrikas**.

39.s: Which of the following is the most appropriate broad explanation for the decline of the Mauryan Empire?
o: Structural weakness and weak successors are stressed, and no single theory is universally accepted.
The empire declined only because of Indo-Greek naval attacks.
A single religious reaction completely explains the decline.
The decline was caused exclusively by the success of the Satavahanas in Tamilakam.
39.x: Historians do not accept one single explanation; contemporary interpretations stress structural weakness and weak successors, while also debating religious explanations.
39.tq: Reject an exclusive single-cause explanation when the historical issue involves competing interpretations.
xs: **No single theory is accepted**; historians stress **structural weakness and weak successors** — option **(1)**.
They place this **over religious reaction**, and the Indo-Greeks were only one pressure.
xa: Debate: the **Ashoka-blame** thesis vs **structural causes**.
**Thapar**: over-centralisation; **Kosambi**: financial crisis.
Pushyamitra's alleged **persecution** of Buddhists is also debated.

40.s: Which literary work contains the earliest reference to the Andhras as a people in the story of Sunahshepa?
40.x: The Aitareya Brahmana gives the earliest literary reference to the Andhras. In the Sunahshepa story, Vishwamitra cursed fifty of his sons to become Andhras, Pundras and Pulindas.
40.tq: Identify the earliest source by linking the text with its distinctive narrative.
xs: The **Aitareya Brahmana** gives the first mention of the Andhras as a people — option **(4)**.
In the **Sunahshepa** story, **Vishwamitra** cursed his **50 sons** to become **Andhras, Pundras, Pulindas**.
The **Mahabharata** and **Vayu Purana** mention the Andhras later; the **Mahavamsa** is a Buddhist chronicle.
xa: ⚠ **Aitareya Brahmana** = first mention; **Rigveda** = no mention.
The first **foreign** source to mention the Andhras is Megasthenes' **Indica**.
The **13th Major Rock Edict** lists the Andhras among peoples following Ashoka's Dhamma.

40.s:
With reference to early literary references to Andhra, consider the following statements:
1. The Rigveda does not mention the Andhras.
2. The Mahabharata states that the Andhras fought on the side of the Kauravas.
3. The Vayu Purana places the Andhras in the Deccan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
40.x: All three statements are correct. The Rigveda has no reference to the Andhras, while the Mahabharata associates them with the Kaurava side and the Vayu Purana places them in the Deccan.
40.tq: Check each statement against the source-wise comparison rather than relying on a single familiar reference.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **Rigveda** does not mention the Andhras.
Statement 2 is correct: in the **Mahabharata** the Andhras fought for the **Kauravas**.
Statement 3 is correct: the **Vayu Purana** places the Andhras in the **Deccan** — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
xa: First mention: **Aitareya Brahmana** (Sunahshepa story).
**Anguttara Nikaya** names **Assaka**.
**Kathavatthu** names the **Andhakas** as a Buddhist school.

40.s: The term “Andhakaratta” should be associated, for APPSC purposes, with which literary tradition?
40.x: The APPSC key associates “Andhakaratta” with Jain literature. The term is a source-sensitive fact and should not be confused with the Buddhist references to Andhra.
40.tq: Resolve a source-tradition confusion by matching the term with the examination-standard association.
xs: For APPSC, **"Andhakaratta"** goes with **Jain literature** — the APHQ book's **2017** key — option **(4)**.
Some notes say **Buddhist** literature; go with the key in APPSC questions.
xa: ⚠ Do not confuse it with the **Andhakas** — a Buddhist school in the **Kathavatthu**.
**"Andhapatha"** is from the **Vinayavatthu** (G2 **2019**).
The Bhimasena Jataka demarcates the Andhra region ("**Andhra Padha**").

40.s: The Chulla-Kalinga Jataka refers to a king of Asmaka (Assaka) who defeated:
40.x: The Chulla-Kalinga Jataka records the Kalinga-Assaka conflict, in which the king of Assaka defeated the king of Kalinga; the other options are much later rulers.
40.tq: Link the literary source with the specific conflict it records.
xs: The **Chulla-Kalinga Jataka** records the **Asmaka king Satakarni** defeating **Kharavela**, the **king of Kalinga** — option **(4)** (G2 **2008**).
**Srisantamula, Rudradaman** and **Nahapana** are not part of this story.
xa: **Assaka (Asmaka)** was a Mahajanapada on the **Godavari**, capital **Bodhan (Podana)**.
**Anguttara Nikaya** names Assaka.
⚠ Kharavela's own record is the **Hathigumpha** inscription.

40.s: Which text refers to the 'Andhapatha' (Andhra Path)?
40.x: The Vinayavatthu mentions Andhapatha (APPSC G2 2019). The Suttanipata has the Bavari story, the Kathavatthu mentions the Andhaka school, and the Mahavamsa is a Sri Lankan Buddhist chronicle.
40.tq: Andhra Path = Vinayavatthu, not Suttanipata or the Jatakas.
xs: The **Vinayavatthu** mentions **"Andhapatha" (Andhra Path)** — option **(2)** (G2 **2019**).
The **Suttanipata** has the **Bavari** story; the **Kathavatthu** names the **Andhakas**; the **Mahavamsa** is a Buddhist chronicle.
xa: The **Bhimasena Jataka** marks out the region as **Andhrapatha**.
Exam angle: Andhra Path = Vinayavatthu, not Suttanipata or the Jatakas.
**Chulla-Kalinga Jataka**: Asmaka king **Satakarni** defeats **Kharavela**.

40.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Janapada)
A. Assaka
B. Mulaka
C. Andhra
D. Asmaka

List-II (Associated feature)
1. Capital at Pratishthana
2. Trade route of Dakshinapatha
3. Capital at Bodhan
4. Alternative name of Assaka

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
40.x: Assaka had its capital at Bodhan; Mulaka had its capital at Pratishthana; Andhra lay on the Dakshinapatha trade route; and Asmaka was another name for Assaka.
40.tq: Start from the sure capital pair and then complete the remaining one-to-one associations.
xs: **Assaka – capital Bodhan**, **Mulaka – capital Pratishthana**, **Andhra – Dakshinapatha route**, **Asmaka – another name for Assaka**: **A-3, B-1, C-2, D-4** — option **(1)**.
Options 2 and 4 misplace Bodhan; option 3 swaps Mulaka and Andhra.
xa: Assaka lay on the **Godavari**; Bodhan is also called **Podana** (G2 **2012**).
**Bavari** settled on the Godavari in **Assaka** territory.
Andhra merchant guilds used **Kalingapatnam**, later **Masulipatnam**.

40.s: Which statement correctly describes the commercial connections of the Andhra region?
o: Andhra was outside the major trade routes and had no merchant guilds.
Andhra lay on the Uttarapatha route, and guilds used only Amaravati.
Andhra lay on the Dakshinapatha route, but its guilds used only Bodhan.
Andhra lay on the Dakshinapatha trade route, and merchant guilds used Kalingapatnam and later Masulipatnam.
40.x: Andhra formed part of the Dakshinapatha trade route. Merchant guilds used Kalingapatnam and later Masulipatnam as important commercial points.
40.tq: Compare the trade route with the named commercial centres and reject exclusive wording.
xs: Andhra lay on the **Dakshinapatha** route, and **merchant guilds** used **Kalingapatnam, later Masulipatnam** — option **(4)**.
The northern route was the **Uttarapatha**; **Bodhan** was the capital of **Assaka**, not a port.
xa: The Serivanija Jataka has merchants trading to **Andhapura**, across the **Telavaha**.
**Mulaka**, a neighbouring janapada, had its capital at **Pratishthana**.
**Assaka** lay on the **Godavari**.

40.s: Bavari, who settled in Assaka territory on the Godavari, was originally a Brahmin teacher from:
40.x: Bavari was a Brahmin teacher from Kosala who settled on the Godavari in Assaka territory.
40.tq: Identify the person through the origin–settlement combination.
xs: **Bavari** was a Brahmin teacher from **Kosala** — option **(4)**.
He settled on the **Godavari** in **Assaka** territory.
xa: He sent **16 disciples** to the Buddha (Suttanipata, Parayana-vagga).
So Buddhist ideas reached the Godavari **before the Mauryan expansion**.
Assaka's capital was **Bodhan (Podana)**.

40.s: According to the Bavari legend, how many disciples were sent to the Buddha?
40.x: Bavari sent sixteen disciples to meet the Buddha. The episode is preserved in the Suttanipata, in the Parayana-vagga.
40.tq: Fix the exact number associated with a narrative episode and distinguish it from nearby conventional numbers.
xs: **Bavari** sent **16 (sixteen) disciples** to the Buddha — option **(3)**.
The story is in the **Suttanipata (Parayana-vagga)**.
xa: Bavari was a Brahmin from **Kosala**, settled on the **Godavari** in Assaka.
It shows Buddhism reached the Godavari **before the Mauryas**.
⚠ "Andhra Path" is in the **Vinayavatthu**, not the Suttanipata.

40.s: What historical inference is supported by the Bavari legend?
o: Buddhist contact with Andhra began only during the Satavahana period.
Buddhism reached the Godavari region only after Ashoka’s death.
The Godavari region was outside Assaka territory during the early period.
Buddhist ideas had reached the Godavari region before Mauryan expansion.
40.x: The Bavari legend indicates that Buddhist ideas had reached the Godavari region before Mauryan expansion, showing early contact between the region and Buddhism.
40.tq: Draw the chronological inference from the legend rather than confusing later institutionalisation with initial contact.
xs: The Bavari legend shows **Buddhist ideas had reached the Godavari region before the Mauryan expansion** — option **(4)**.
So contact did not begin with the Satavahanas or after Ashoka; Bavari himself lived in **Assaka** territory on the Godavari.
xa: He sent **16 disciples** to the Buddha.
Later, **Mahadeva Bhikshu** — sent by Ashoka — was the first Buddhist teacher in Andhra.
The **Mauryan phase** made Buddhism **institutional** in Andhra.

40.s:
Consider the following statements about Ashokan inscriptions in Andhra:
1. The Erragudi inscription, in present Nandyal district, is in Prakrit language and Brahmi script.
2. The Erragudi edict asks teachers to inculcate Dhamma in pupils and appoints Rajukas for justice and welfare.
3. Rajula Mandagiri has a fragment of an Ashokan pillar edict.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
40.x: Statement 1 is correct: Erragudi (Kurnool, now Nandyal) is in Prakrit and Brahmi. Statement 2 is correct: it speaks of teachers inculcating Dhamma and of Rajukas. Statement 3 is wrong: Rajula Mandagiri has a minor edict; the pillar-edict fragment is at Amaravati. So '1 and 2 only'.
40.tq: Pillar fragment = Amaravati; minor edict = Rajula Mandagiri.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Erragudi** (Kurnool; now **Nandyal** district) is in **Prakrit** and **Brahmi**.
Statement 2 is correct: it says teachers must **inculcate Dhamma in pupils** (G2 **2008**) and appoints **Rajukas**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Rajula Mandagiri** has a **minor edict**; the pillar-edict fragment is at **Amaravati** — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
xa: Andhra came under Ashoka after the **Kalinga War**.
The Rajukas were appointed for **justice and welfare**.
The **13th Major Rock Edict** names the Andhras among Dhamma followers.

40.s: Who is associated with the first Buddhist teaching mission to Andhra and the enshrinement of Buddha’s bone relics at Amaravati?
40.x: Ashoka sent Mahadeva Bhikshu to Amaravati. He is regarded as the first Buddhist teacher in Andhra and is associated with enshrining Buddha’s bone relics there.
40.tq: Identify the missionary figure by matching the person with the specific act and destination.
xs: **Mahadeva Bhikshu**, sent by Ashoka to **Amaravati** (Andhra tradition), was the **first Buddhist teacher in Andhra** and enshrined the Buddha's **bone relics** there — option **(4)**.
**Bavari** sent disciples to the Buddha; **Megasthenes** was a Greek ambassador.
xa: Amaravati also has a **fragment of an Ashokan pillar edict**.
Amaravati-Dharanikota = **Andhranagari / Dhanyakataka** on the **Krishna**.
**P.C. Ray** identified the river there as the Krishna.

40.s: Which early historic site in Krishna district shows continuous occupation from Mauryan to Satavahana times?
40.x: Gudiwada Dibba in Krishna district is an early historic mound showing continuous occupation from Mauryan to Satavahana times.
40.tq: Use the site–district–cultural sequence combination for archaeological identification.
xs: **Gudiwada Dibba** (Krishna district) shows continuous occupation from **Mauryan to Satavahana** times — option **(2)**.
**Adurru** was a Mahasanghika centre; **Rajula Mandagiri** has an Ashokan minor edict; **Nagarjunakonda** is ancient Sriparvata.
xa: The **Nagarjunasagar valley** digs give material proof of early Andhra settlement.
⚠ Some notes place **Siddharthaka chaitya** at Gudiwada; the key says **Guntupalli**.
Andhra was a distinct region **before the Satavahanas**.

40.s: Adurru, located in East Godavari district, was an important centre of the:
40.x: Adurru in East Godavari district was a Mahasanghika Buddhist centre.
40.tq: Match the archaeological site with its religious affiliation.
xs: **Adurru** (East Godavari) was a **Mahasanghika** Buddhist centre — option **(4)**.
The **Andhakas** were a separate Buddhist school (Kathavatthu, Third Council).
xa: **Gudiwada Dibba** shows Mauryan-to-Satavahana occupation.
**Nagarjunasagar valley** excavations prove early Andhra settlement.
The Mauryan phase made Buddhism **institutional** in Andhra.

40.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
40.x: Siddharthaka Chaitya is identified with Guntupalli in Eluru district. Sriparvata is Nagarjunakonda, Andhranagari is Amaravati-Dharanikota, and Andhapura is associated with the Telavaha crossing in the Serivanija Jataka.
40.tq: Start with the sure ancient-name–modern-site pair and eliminate the swapped identifications.
xs: **Siddharthaka chaitya** = **Guntupalli** (Eluru district) — option **(1)** (G2 **2008** key).
**Sriparvata** = **Nagarjunakonda**, not Amaravati; **Andhranagari** = **Amaravati-Dharanikota**, not Nagarjunakonda.
**Andhapura** was reached across the **Telavaha** (Serivanija Jataka), not Dharanikota.
xa: ⚠ Some notes put Siddharthaka at **Gudiwada** — go with the key.
Sriparvata is also called **Vijayapuri**.
**Guntupalli** chaitya is compared with the **Barabar caves**.

40.s: Andhranagari or Dhanyakataka is identified with:
40.x: Andhranagari, also called Dhanyakataka, is identified with Amaravati-Dharanikota on the Krishna River. The river identification is associated with P. C. Ray.
40.tq: Distinguish ancient place names by combining the modern site and river clues.
xs: **Andhranagari / Dhanyakataka** = **Amaravati-Dharanikota on the Krishna** — option **(1)**.
**P.C. Ray** identified the river there as the **Krishna**.
**Guntupalli** = Siddharthaka chaitya; **Bodhan** was Assaka's capital; **Nagarjunakonda** = Sriparvata.
xa: **Mahadeva Bhikshu** enshrined the Buddha's **bone relics** at Amaravati.
Amaravati has a fragment of an **Ashokan pillar edict**.
**Sriparvata / Vijayapuri** = Nagarjunakonda.

40.s:
Assertion (A): Andhra had a distinct regional identity before the rise of the Satavahanas.
Reason (R): Early literary, epigraphic and archaeological evidence refers to Andhra as a region or people before the Satavahana period.

Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
40.x: Both A and R are true and R explains A. Andhra appears as a people or region in the Aitareya Brahmana, Buddhist and Jataka texts, Megasthenes' Indica and Ashoka's 13th Rock Edict, and in sites such as Gudiwada Dibba and the Nagarjunasagar valley, all before the Satavahanas.
40.tq: Test whether the evidence stated in the Reason directly explains the historical conclusion in the Assertion.
xs: Both A and R are true and **R is the correct explanation of A** — option **(1)**: Andhra was a **distinct region before the Satavahanas**.
Literary: **Aitareya Brahmana**, **Vinayavatthu**, Jatakas, Megasthenes' **Indica**, the **13th Major Rock Edict**.
Archaeological: **Gudiwada Dibba** and the **Nagarjunasagar valley** digs.
xa: The **Mauryan phase** made Buddhism **institutional**.
Megasthenes counted **30 forts** of the Andhras.
Ashokan edicts in Andhra: **Erragudi**, **Rajula Mandagiri**, **Amaravati**.

40.s: Which statement best describes the significance of the Mauryan phase for Buddhism in Andhra?
o: It made Buddhism institutional in the region
It led to the disappearance of Buddhism from Andhra
It replaced Buddhism with Jainism as the state religion
It introduced Vajrayana Buddhism for the first time
40.x: The Mauryan phase made Buddhism institutional in Andhra, which was already a distinct region before the Satavahanas.
40.tq: Ashoka's Mauryan era = Buddhism gets institutions in Andhra.
xs: The **Mauryan phase made Buddhism institutional** in Andhra — option **(1)**.
Buddhism did not disappear or yield to Jainism as a state religion.
xa: **Mahadeva Bhikshu**, sent by Ashoka, was the first Buddhist teacher in Andhra.
Buddhist ideas had reached the Godavari even **before** the Mauryas (**Bavari**).
Andhra was already a **distinct region** before the Satavahanas.

41.s: The Yavana advance on Saketa, Panchala, Mathura and Pataliputra is described in which source?
41.x: The Gargi Samhita records the Yavana advance on Saketa, Panchala, Mathura and Pataliputra.
41.tq: Match a source with its distinctive historical information.
xs: The **Gargi Samhita** (Yuga Purana) records the **Yavana advance on Saketa, Panchala, Mathura and Pataliputra** — option **(3)**.
The **Ayodhya inscription** records Pushyamitra's **two Ashvamedhas**; the **Divyavadana** calls him a persecutor; the **Harshacharita** tells of Brihadratha's killing.
xa: The Yavana invasion is recorded in **Gargi Samhita, Mahabhashya and Malavikagnimitram** (APPSC G1 **2022**).
⚠ It is NOT in Visakhadatta's **Mudrarakshasa**, which is about Chandragupta Maurya.
The **Mahabhashya** mentions the Yavana siege of **Saketa** and **Madhyamika**.

41.s:
Consider the following pairs of sources and what they record:
a. Malavikagnimitram — Vasumitra's victory over the Yavanas on the Sindhu
b. Harshacharita — Pushyamitra killing Brihadratha while showing him the army
c. Divyavadana — Pushyamitra as a generous patron of Buddhists
d. Ayodhya inscription of Dhana — Pushyamitra's two Ashvamedhas
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
41.x: Pairs a, b and d are correct. Pair c is wrong: the Divyavadana portrays Pushyamitra as a persecutor of Buddhists, not a patron. So 'a, b and d only'; 'a and b only' leaves out the Ayodhya inscription and the options with c accept the false pair.
41.tq: Divyavadana = persecutor story.
xs: Pair a is correct: **Malavikagnimitram** — **Vasumitra** beat the Yavanas on the **Sindhu**.
Pair b is correct: **Harshacharita** — Pushyamitra killed **Brihadratha** while showing him the army.
Pair c is wrong: the **Divyavadana** calls Pushyamitra a **persecutor** of Buddhists; pair d is correct — option **(2) a, b and d only**.
xa: The **Ayodhya inscription of Dhana(deva)** records **two Ashvamedhas** (UPSC).
The **Harshacharita** was written by **Banabhatta**.
**Taranatha** (16th c.) also portrays him as a persecutor.

41.s: Visakhadatta's Mudrarakshasa is not generally used as evidence for the Yavana invasion during Pushyamitra's reign because it deals primarily with:
o: The Satavahana conquest of the Deccan
41.x: Mudrarakshasa concerns Chandragupta Maurya and the establishment of Mauryan power, not the Yavana invasion during Pushyamitra's reign.
41.tq: Use the NOT-supported source distinction and reject a famous but contextually unsuitable work.
xs: **Mudrarakshasa** deals with **Chandragupta Maurya** — option **(2)** — so it is not a source for the Yavana invasion (APPSC G1 **2022** trap).
The Yavana invasion is in the **Gargi Samhita, Mahabhashya and Malavikagnimitram**.
xa: Mudrarakshasa is by **Visakhadatta**.
Gargi Samhita: Yavanas advanced on **Saketa, Panchala, Mathura, Pataliputra**.
Mahabhashya: Yavana siege of **Saketa** and **Madhyamika**.

41.s:
Arrange the following dynasties in chronological order of their rule:
A. Kanva
B. Maurya
C. Kushana
D. Sunga
41.x: The sequence is Maurya, Sunga, Kanva and Kushana.
41.tq: Fix the first and last dynasties, then place the intervening Sunga and Kanva periods.
xs: The order is **Maurya → Sunga → Kanva → Kushana** — **B, D, A, C**, option **(1)** (BPSC **2025**).
Mauryas c. **321-187 BC**; Sungas **187-75 BC**; Kanvas c. **73-28 BC**.
xa: UPSC dates the Sungas **187-78 BC**; APHQ **185-73 BCE**.
The Kanvas had **4** kings.
The Puranas say the **Satavahanas** defeated the Sungas and Kanvas.

41.s: According to the Puranic tradition, which dynasties were defeated by the Satavahanas?
41.x: The Puranas state that the Satavahanas defeated the Sunga and Kanva dynasties.
41.tq: Identify the specific predecessor dynasties associated with a later dynastic conquest.
xs: The Puranas say the **Satavahanas defeated the Sungas and Kanvas** (Sunga and Kanva dynasties) — option **(3)**.
**Simuka (Srimukha)**, the Satavahana founder, overthrew the last Kanva **Susharman**.
xa: AP angle: **Satakarni I** is said to have defeated **Pushyamitra**.
The Sungas had already lost the **Deccan** to the Satavahanas.
Order: **Maurya → Sunga → Kanva → Kushana**.

41.s:
Consider the following statements about the Sungas:
1. They were Brahmins.
2. Their heartland was Magadha, Malwa-Vidisha and the Narmada valley.
3. They lost the north-west to the Satavahanas and the Deccan to the Yavanas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
41.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Sungas were Brahmins. Statement 2 is correct: their heartland was Magadha, Malwa-Vidisha and the Narmada valley. Statement 3 is wrong: it is reversed; the north-west went to the Yavanas and the Deccan to the Satavahanas. So '1 and 2 only'.
41.tq: Reverse-pairing trap: NW = Yavanas, Deccan = Satavahanas.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the Sungas were **Brahmins**.
Statement 2 is correct: their heartland was **Magadha, Malwa-Vidisha and the Narmada valley**.
Statement 3 is wrong: it is reversed — the **north-west** went to the **Yavanas**, the **Deccan** to the **Satavahanas**. So option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
xa: They broadly kept the **Mauryan administrative institutions**.
Feudatories **Bhojas, Maharathis, Rastrikas** rose.
Pushyamitra's dominions included **Pataliputra, Ayodhya and Vidisha**.

41.s:
With reference to the Sunga rulers, consider the following pairs:
1. Agnimitra — Viceroy at Vidisha
2. Vasumitra — Defeat of the Yavanas on the Sindhu
3. Bhagabhadra — Court visited by Heliodorus
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
41.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. Agnimitra served as viceroy at Vidisha, Vasumitra defeated the Yavanas on the Sindhu, and Heliodorus came to Bhagabhadra’s court.
41.tq: Start from the sure ruler–event pairs and verify the remaining pair.
xs: Pair 1 is correct: **Agnimitra** was viceroy at **Vidisha**.
Pair 2 is correct: **Vasumitra** defeated the Yavanas on the **Sindhu**.
Pair 3 is correct: **Heliodorus** came to **Bhagabhadra**'s court — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
xa: ⚠ **Agnimitra** = son; **Vasumitra** = grandson of Pushyamitra.
Agnimitra fought **Yajnasena of Vidarbha**.
Heliodorus set up the **Besnagar pillar** near Vidisha.

41.s: Agnimitra, a prominent Sunga ruler, is associated with which of the following developments?
o: Receiving the Besnagar pillar from Heliodorus
Defeating the Yavanas on the Sindhu
41.x: Agnimitra is noted for fighting Yajnasena of Vidarbha. The defeat of the Yavanas on the Sindhu is associated with Vasumitra, while the other alternatives refer to different historical contexts.
41.tq: Use the ruler–deed association and reject deeds belonging to neighbouring dynasties or rulers.
xs: **Agnimitra** fought **Yajnasena of Vidarbha** — option **(4)** (UPSC).
The **Sindhu** victory was **Vasumitra**'s; Heliodorus came to **Bhagabhadra**; the Kanvas were ended by **Simuka**.
xa: Agnimitra was Pushyamitra's son and viceroy at **Vidisha**.
He is the hero of Kalidasa's **Malavikagnimitram**.
The last Sunga was **Devabhuti**.

41.s:
Consider the following statements about Sunga rule:
1. The Sungas broadly kept the Mauryan administrative institutions.
2. Powerful feudatories such as the Bhojas, Maharathis and Rastrikas rose in this period.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
41.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Sungas broadly kept Mauryan administrative institutions. Statement 2 is correct: Bhojas, Maharathis and Rastrikas rose as powerful feudatories. So 'Both 1 and 2'; '1 only' and '2 only' each leave out a true statement and 'Neither' rejects both.
41.tq: Sunga: Mauryan administration kept; feudatories rose.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the Sungas **broadly kept Mauryan administrative institutions**.
Statement 2 is correct: powerful feudatories — **Bhojas, Maharathis, Rastrikas** — rose. So option **(3) Both 1 and 2**.
xa: Sunga heartland: **Magadha, Malwa-Vidisha, Narmada valley**.
The Sungas were **Brahmins**.
The north-west was lost to the **Yavanas**, the Deccan to the **Satavahanas**.

41.s:
Consider the following statements about Pushyamitra Sunga:
1. He came to power c. 187 BC after killing Brihadratha.
2. His dominions reached the Narmada and included Pataliputra, Ayodhya and Vidisha.
3. He defeated Menander after the Greeks challenged his sacrificial horse.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
41.x: Statement 1 is correct: he killed Brihadratha c. 187 BC. Statement 2 is correct: his dominions reached the Narmada with Pataliputra, Ayodhya and Vidisha. Statement 3 is wrong: the Bactrian Greek he defeated over the sacrificial horse was Demetrius. So '1 and 2 only'.
41.tq: Sacrificial horse challenge = Demetrius.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: Pushyamitra killed **Brihadratha** in **187 BC** (APPSC GS **2023** key).
Statement 2 is correct: his dominions reached the **Narmada**, with **Pataliputra, Ayodhya and Vidisha** (UPSC).
Statement 3 is wrong: the Bactrian Greek he defeated over the **sacrificial horse** was **Demetrius**, not Menander — so option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
xa: He was the Mauryan **commander-in-chief**.
He performed **two Ashvamedhas** (Ayodhya inscription of Dhana).
**Patanjali** is believed to have been his royal priest.

41.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the debate on Pushyamitra's attitude towards Buddhism:
1. Divyavadana and Taranatha portray him as a persecutor of Buddhists.
2. Romila Thapar and Etienne Lamotte regard the persecution account as exaggerated and sectarian.
3. Buddhist artistic activity completely disappeared during his reign.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
41.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Buddhist art continued to flourish at Sanchi, Bharhut and Bodh Gaya, so statement 3 is false.
41.tq: Find the false absolute statement and separate literary tradition from modern historical interpretation.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **Divyavadana** and **Taranatha** (16th c.) call him a persecutor — destroying stupas, a bounty on monks' heads.
Statement 2 is correct: **Romila Thapar and Etienne Lamotte** call this **exaggerated and sectarian**.
Statement 3 is wrong: Buddhist art **flourished** at **Sanchi, Bharhut and Bodh Gaya** — so option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
xa: Royal patronage fell, but **merchants and guilds** kept funding Buddhism.
Hostility was probably aimed at monasteries **allied with the Indo-Greeks**.
One tradition blames him for destroying the original **Bodhi Tree**.

41.s:
Consider the following statements offered against the theory that Pushyamitra persecuted Buddhists:
1. Merchants and guilds kept funding Buddhism even as royal patronage fell.
2. Any hostility was probably aimed at monasteries allied with the Indo-Greeks.
3. Buddhist art at Sanchi, Bharhut and Bodh Gaya declined under his rule.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
41.x: Statement 1 is correct: merchants and guilds kept funding Buddhism. Statement 2 is correct: hostility was probably aimed at monasteries allied with the Indo-Greeks. Statement 3 is wrong: Buddhist art flourished at Sanchi, Bharhut and Bodh Gaya, which is itself an argument against persecution. So '1 and 2 only'.
41.tq: Sanchi/Bharhut flourished = argument against persecution.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **merchants and guilds** kept funding Buddhism as royal patronage fell.
Statement 2 is correct: hostility was probably aimed at monasteries **allied with the Indo-Greeks**.
Statement 3 is wrong: Buddhist art **flourished** at **Sanchi, Bharhut and Bodh Gaya** — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
xa: Critics of the persecution story: **Romila Thapar** and **Etienne Lamotte**.
Bharhut inscriptions name **guilds of ivory workers and stone carvers** as donors.
The persecution charge comes from the **Divyavadana** and **Taranatha**.

41.s: The tradition concerning the destruction of the original Bodhi Tree at Bodh Gaya is associated with which two rulers?
o: Pushyamitra Sunga and Shashanka of Gauda
41.x: One tradition attributes destruction of the original Bodhi Tree to Pushyamitra and also records a similar act by Shashanka of Gauda in the seventh century CE.
41.tq: Discriminate between rulers associated with similar acts in different periods.
xs: One tradition blames **Pushyamitra Sunga** for destroying the original **Bodhi Tree**, and **Shashanka of Gauda** did the same in the **7th c.** — option **(4)**.
**Ashoka**, **Devabhuti**, **Vasudeva Kanva** and **Antialcidas** have no such tradition in the notes.
xa: This was in the news in **2026** with the listing of the **Ashtamahasthana** (**8** Buddhist sacred sites).
The persecution charge rests on the **Divyavadana** and **Taranatha**.
**Bodh Gaya** has an early stone railing of the Sunga period.

41.s: Heliodorus erected the Besnagar pillar while serving as ambassador of:
41.x: Heliodorus was the ambassador of the Indo-Greek king Antialcidas at the court of the Sunga king Bhagabhadra.
41.tq: Use the ambassador–sending ruler–receiving court relationship precisely.
xs: **Heliodorus** was ambassador of the **Indo-Greek king Antialcidas** — option **(2)**.
He came to the court of the **Sunga king Bhagabhadra**, not Pushyamitra.
**Demetrius** was the Bactrian Greek Pushyamitra defeated.
xa: Heliodorus was a native of **Taxila**.
The pillar is at **Besnagar**, near **Vidisha (MP)**.
He called himself a **Bhagavata**.

41.s:
Consider the following statements about the Besnagar pillar:
1. Heliodorus, who erected it, was a native of Taxila.
2. It stands at Besnagar near Vidisha in Madhya Pradesh.
3. Its inscription is in Sanskrit written in Kharoshthi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
41.x: Statement 1 is correct: Heliodorus was from Taxila. Statement 2 is correct: the pillar is at Besnagar near Vidisha (MP). Statement 3 is wrong: the inscription is Prakrit in Brahmi script. So '1 and 2 only'.
41.tq: Besnagar: Prakrit / Brahmi.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Heliodorus** was a native of **Taxila**.
Statement 2 is correct: the pillar is at **Besnagar near Vidisha (MP)**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the inscription is **Prakrit** in **Brahmi** — so option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
xa: It is a **Garuda-dhvaja** dedicated to **Vasudeva**.
It is the **earliest inscriptional proof of Bhagavatism**.
Heliodorus served the Indo-Greek king **Antialcidas**.

41.s: The Besnagar pillar is best described as a:
41.x: The Besnagar monument is a Garuda-dhvaja dedicated to Vasudeva, and Heliodorus describes himself as a Bhagavata.
41.tq: Distinguish religious symbols and dedications associated with different traditions.
xs: The Besnagar pillar is a **Garuda-dhvaja dedicated to Vasudeva** — option **(4)**.
Heliodorus calls himself a **Bhagavata**.
xa: It is the **earliest inscriptional proof of Bhagavatism** (early Vaishnavism).
It also shows the absorption of **foreigners** into Indian religion.
It was set up at the court of **Bhagabhadra**.

41.s: The major historical significance of the Besnagar pillar lies in its evidence for:
o: The earliest use of iron in the Ganga valley
The establishment of the Kanva dynasty
Early Bhagavatism and the absorption of a foreigner into an Indian religious tradition
41.x: The pillar is early inscriptional evidence of Bhagavatism, an early form of Vaishnavism, and shows the assimilation of a foreigner into an Indian religious tradition.
41.tq: Identify the broader significance rather than merely the monument's location.
xs: The pillar is the **earliest inscriptional proof of Bhagavatism** and shows the **absorption of a foreigner** into Indian religion — option **(3)**.
**Heliodorus**, a Greek from **Taxila**, calls himself a **Bhagavata**.
xa: It is a **Garuda-dhvaja** to **Vasudeva**.
Language/script: **Prakrit / Brahmi**.
Bhagavatism's rise is part of the Sunga period's significance.

41.s:
Consider the following statements about Patanjali and the Mahabhashya:
1. The Mahabhashya comments on Panini's Ashtadhyayi through Katyayana's Varttikas.
2. It gives evidence on 2nd-century-BCE society, geography, language and Yavana raids.
3. Patanjali is believed to have been the royal priest of Vasudeva Kanva.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
41.x: Statement 1 is correct: the grammarian trio is Panini-Katyayana-Patanjali. Statement 2 is correct: the Mahabhashya is evidence for 2nd-century-BCE society and the Yavana raids. Statement 3 is wrong: Patanjali was a contemporary and believed royal priest of Pushyamitra Sunga. So '1 and 2 only'.
41.tq: Patanjali = Pushyamitra's priest.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **Mahabhashya** comments on **Panini's Ashtadhyayi** through **Katyayana's Varttikas**.
Statement 2 is correct: it is evidence on **2nd-century-BCE** society, geography, language and **Yavana raids**.
Statement 3 is wrong: Patanjali was the believed royal priest of **Pushyamitra**, not Vasudeva Kanva — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
xa: Grammarian trio: **Panini-Katyayana-Patanjali**.
The Mahabhashya says "we perform sacrifices for **Pushyamitra**".
It mentions the Yavana siege of **Saketa** and **Madhyamika**.

41.s: Which development is associated with the Sunga court?
o: Replacement of Sanskrit by Greek as the court language
Introduction of Persian as the official language
Revival of classical Sanskrit, while Ashoka had used Prakrit
41.x: The Sunga court encouraged a revival of classical Sanskrit, in contrast to Ashoka's prominent use of Prakrit.
41.tq: Use a court-language comparison and reject an absolute claim of linguistic replacement.
xs: The Sunga court led a **revival of classical Sanskrit**, while **Ashoka** had used **Prakrit** — option **(4)**.
Greek or Persian were not court languages, and Prakrit did not vanish — the **Besnagar** inscription itself is in Prakrit.
xa: **Patanjali**'s Mahabhashya belongs to this revival.
The **Manusmriti** took early shape in this period.
The Sunga period saw a **Brahmanical revival**.

41.s: The Manusmriti is said to have taken its early shape during the Sunga period and classified foreigners as:
41.x: The Manusmriti took early shape in this period and classified foreigners as Vratya Kshatriyas.
41.tq: Recall the exact technical social category instead of a broad caste label.
xs: The **Manusmriti**, taking shape in this period, classed foreigners as **"Vratya Kshatriyas"** — option **(4)**.
So foreigners were fitted into the varna order as Kshatriyas who had lapsed, not as Shudras or Brahmanas.
xa: Foreigners were also absorbed via **Bhagavatism** — e.g. **Heliodorus**.
The Sunga court revived **classical Sanskrit**.
The period is marked by a **Brahmanical revival**.

41.s:
Consider the following statements about Sanchi:
1. Ashoka's brick stupa was encased in stone and given stone railings (vedika).
2. Its toranas carry Jataka tales and scenes from the Buddha's life.
3. Its south torana is linked to Pushyamitra through the inscription of Ananda.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
41.x: Statement 1 is correct: the brick stupa was encased in stone with railings. Statement 2 is correct: the toranas show Jataka tales and the Buddha's life. Statement 3 is wrong: the inscription of Ananda links the south torana to Satakarni II, so the gateways are often dated to the Satavahana period. So '1 and 2 only'.
41.tq: South torana = Satakarni II (Ananda inscription).
xs: Statement 1 is correct: Ashoka's brick stupa was **encased in stone** with **stone railings (vedika)**.
Statement 2 is correct: the **toranas** carry **Jataka tales** and the Buddha's life.
Statement 3 is wrong: Ananda's inscription links the south torana to **Satakarni II**, not Pushyamitra — so option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
xa: The gateways are therefore often dated to the **Satavahana** period.
**Bharhut** has railings and gateways of early **narrative art**.
**Bodh Gaya** has an early stone railing.

41.s: Which statement about Bharhut is correct?
o: Its inscriptions record only royal donations by the Mauryan emperors.
Its inscriptions name guilds of ivory workers and stone carvers who financed the monument.
It was situated near Taxila and was built by Indo-Greek rulers.
It contained no railings or gateways of narrative art.
41.x: Bharhut's inscriptions mention guilds of ivory workers and stone carvers who contributed to its construction and decoration.
41.tq: Use the patronage detail to distinguish Bharhut from royal-only monuments.
xs: **Bharhut** inscriptions name the **guilds of ivory workers and stone carvers** who paid for it — option **(2)**.
It has **railings and gateways** of early **narrative art**, in **MP**, not near Taxila.
xa: "The Bharhut stupa is a fine example of **Shunga** architecture" (RPSC **2023**).
Guild funding fits the view that **merchants and guilds** kept funding Buddhism.
The art shifted from **wood/ivory to stone**.

41.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Mathura — beginning of Gupta temple architecture under the Sungas
Bharhut — early narrative art in railings and gateways
41.x: Mathura sculpture began under the Sungas, but Gupta temple architecture did not begin there under the Sungas. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
41.tq: Find the one anachronistic or wrongly attributed cultural development.
xs: **Mathura** saw the **Mathura style of sculpture** begin under the Sungas — not Gupta temple architecture; so option **(3)** is NOT correctly matched.
**Bodh Gaya** (early stone railing), **Sanchi** (toranas with Jataka scenes), **Bharhut** (narrative railings, gateways) are correct.
xa: Sanchi's south torana is linked to **Satakarni II** (inscription of Ananda).
Bharhut was paid for by guilds of **ivory workers and stone carvers**.
Transition: **wood/ivory → stone**.

41.s: Which one of the following best describes the broader cultural significance of the Sunga period?
o: Complete disappearance of Brahmanical traditions and decline of Buddhist art
Exclusive promotion of Jainism and rejection of all forms of image-making
Brahmanical revival, rise of Bhagavatism and development of stone Buddhist art
Replacement of religious traditions by a purely secular imperial culture
41.x: The Sunga period is associated with Brahmanical revival, the rise of Bhagavatism and the development of stone Buddhist art.
41.tq: Choose the option that combines the three stated cultural developments without an absolute distortion.
xs: The Sunga period stands for **Brahmanical revival, the rise of Bhagavatism and stone Buddhist art** — option **(3)**.
Brahmanism grew (two **Ashvamedhas**), and Buddhist art flourished at **Sanchi** and **Bharhut**.
xa: Bhagavatism: the **Besnagar** Garuda-dhvaja of **Heliodorus**.
Debate: Pushyamitra as persecutor (**Divyavadana**) vs the archaeology of Sanchi and Bharhut.
The court revived **classical Sanskrit**.

41.s: According to the traditional account associated with Andhra history, which ruler is said to have defeated Pushyamitra Sunga?
41.x: Satakarni I is said to have defeated Pushyamitra Sunga. Simuka is associated with ending the Kanva dynasty, while Vasumitra is linked with the defeat of the Yavanas on the Sindhu.
41.tq: Distinguish closely related dynastic and military associations.
xs: AP angle: **Satakarni I** is said to have defeated **Pushyamitra** — option **(4)**.
**Simuka** ended the **Kanvas**; **Vasumitra** beat the Yavanas; **Yajnasena** of Vidarbha fought **Agnimitra**.
xa: The Puranas say the **Satavahanas** defeated the Sungas and Kanvas.
**Satakarni II** is linked to Sanchi's south torana.
The Sungas lost the **Deccan** to the Satavahanas.

41.s: The Shunga dynasty ruled approximately during which period?
41.x: The Shungas ruled from about 185 BCE, when Brihadratha was killed, to about 73 BCE, when Vasudeva Kanva killed Devabhuti.
41.tq: Recall the start and end dates of Shunga rule.
n: The Shunga dynasty existed approximately from 185 BCE to 73 BCE. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #143 · pp 248-250]
xs: The **Shunga dynasty** ruled approximately **185 BCE to 73 BCE** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It began when **Pushyamitra Shunga** assassinated **Brihadratha**, the last Mauryan, in **185 BCE**.
It ended when **Devabhuti**, the last Shunga, was killed by his minister **Vasudeva Kanva**.
xa: ⚠ Sources differ: other notes give **187-75 BC** (UPSC: **187-78 BC**).
⚠ APPSC GS **2023** key dates Brihadratha's killing to **187 BC**.
Sequence: **Maurya → Sunga → Kanva → Kushana** (BPSC **2025**).
The **Kanvas** ruled c. **73-28 BC**; their last king **Susharman** was overthrown by **Simuka**.

41.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Pushyamitra Shunga performed two Ashwamedha Yajnas.
The ceremonies were organised under Patanjali's supervision.
Pushyamitra Shunga performed three Ashwamedha Yajnas.
The Ayodhya Inscription provides information about two Ashwamedha Yajnas.
41.x: Option C is incorrect: Pushyamitra performed two, not three, Ashwamedha yajnas. The Ayodhya inscription records the two sacrifices, and Patanjali is linked with them.
41.tq: Check the number in each statement.
n: Pushyamitra Shunga performed two Ashwamedha Yajnas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #143 · pp 248-250]
The Ayodhya Inscription provides information about Pushyamitra Shunga's two Ashwamedha Yajnas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #143 · pp 248-250]
Patanjali supervised the organization of Pushyamitra Shunga's two Ashwamedha ceremonies. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #143 · pp 248-250]
xs: Statement **(3)** is incorrect: Pushyamitra performed **two**, not three, **Ashwamedha Yajnas** — so option **(3)** is the answer.
(1) is correct: he **performed two Ashwamedha Yajnas**.
(2) is correct: **Patanjali** supervised the organisation of the two ceremonies.
(4) is correct: the **Ayodhya Inscription** (of **Dhana**) records the two sacrifices.
xa: **Patanjali** wrote the **Mahabhashya** and was a contemporary of **Pushyamitra**.
The **Greeks** had challenged his sacrificial horse; he defeated Bactrian Greek **Demetrius**.
Pushyamitra's dominions reached the **Narmada**, including **Pataliputra, Ayodhya and Vidisha**.

41.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Malavikagnimitram was written by Kalidasa.
II. Agnimitra is the protagonist of Malavikagnimitram.
III. Agnimitra was the son of Pushyamitra Shunga.
IV. Malavikagnimitram was the first play of Kalidasa.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
41.x: All four are correct: Kalidasa wrote Malavikagnimitram as his first play, and its hero Agnimitra was the son of Pushyamitra Shunga.
41.tq: Check each statement separately.
n: Malavikagnimitram was written by Kalidasa. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #143 · pp 248-250]
Malavikagnimitram was the first play of Kalidasa. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #143 · pp 248-250]
Agnimitra was the protagonist of Malavikagnimitram. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #143 · pp 248-250]
Agnimitra was the son of Pushyamitra Shunga. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #143 · pp 248-250]
Kalidasa was the author of Malavikagnimitram. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #143 · pp 248-250]
xs: All four statements **I, II, III and IV** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
I and IV: **Malavikagnimitram** was written by **Kalidasa** — his **first play**.
II: **Agnimitra** of **Vidisha** is its **protagonist**; the love story of Agnimitra and **Malavika**.
III: **Agnimitra** was the **son of Pushyamitra Shunga**.
xa: In the play, **Vasumitra** defeats the **Yavanas** on the **Sindhu**.
It also records Agnimitra's war with **Vidarbha** (**Yajnasena**).
⚠ **Agnimitra** = son (Vidisha viceroy); **Vasumitra** = grandson (beat the Yavanas).

41.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Malavikagnimitram
(b) Mahabhashya
(c) Mrichchhakatikam
(d) Malavika

List-II
(i) Sudraka
(ii) Literary character associated with Agnimitra
(iii) Kalidasa
(iv) Patanjali
41.x: Malavikagnimitram is by Kalidasa, Mahabhashya by Patanjali, Mrichchhakatikam by Sudraka, and Malavika is the heroine loved by Agnimitra, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
41.tq: Recall the author of each work.
n: Patanjali was the author of Mahabhashya. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #143 · pp 248-250]
Malavikagnimitram was written by Kalidasa. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #143 · pp 248-250]
Malavikagnimitram concerns the love story of Agnimitra of Vidisha and Malavika. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #143 · pp 248-250]
Kalidasa was the author of Malavikagnimitram. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #143 · pp 248-250]
Patanjali was the author of Mahabhashya. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #143 · pp 248-250]
Mrichchhakatikam was written by Sudraka. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #143 · pp 248-250]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Malavikagnimitram** = **Kalidasa**; **Mahabhashya** = **Patanjali**.
**Mrichchhakatikam** = **Sudraka**; **Malavika** = the character loved by **Agnimitra**.
xa: The **Mahabhashya** is a commentary on **Panini's Ashtadhyayi** through **Katyayana's** Varttikas.
**Grammarian trio** = **Panini-Katyayana-Patanjali**.
Mahabhashya records the **Yavana** siege of **Saketa** and **Madhyamika**.

41.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Brihadratha
(b) Pushyamitra Shunga
(c) Devabhuti
(d) Vasudeva Kanva

List-II
(i) Minister/Amatya who killed Devabhuti
(ii) Founder of the Shunga dynasty
(iii) Last Mauryan ruler
(iv) Last ruler of the Shunga dynasty
41.x: Brihadratha was the last Mauryan, Pushyamitra founded the Shungas, Devabhuti was the last Shunga and Vasudeva Kanva was the minister who killed him, giving a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
41.tq: Recall the role of each ruler.
n: Pushyamitra Shunga founded the Shunga dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #143 · pp 248-250]
Brihadratha was the last Mauryan ruler. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #143 · pp 248-250]
Devabhuti was the last ruler of the Shunga dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #143 · pp 248-250]
Devabhuti was killed by his minister, Amatya Vasudeva Kanva. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #143 · pp 248-250]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Brihadratha** = **last Mauryan ruler**; **Pushyamitra Shunga** = **founder of the Shunga dynasty**.
**Devabhuti** = **last Shunga ruler**; **Vasudeva Kanva** = the **Amatya** who killed Devabhuti.
xa: **Pushyamitra** was Brihadratha's **commander**; he killed him in **185 BCE**.
**Harshacharita** says Pushyamitra killed Brihadratha while showing him the army.
Pushyamitra and the succeeding **Kanvas** were described as **Brahmins**.

41.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Pushyamitra Shunga
(b) Vasudeva Kanva
(c) Simuka
(d) Sthanakvasi

List-II
(i) Lonka sect
(ii) Susharma
(iii) Brihadratha Maurya
(iv) Devabhuti
41.x: Pushyamitra replaced Brihadratha Maurya, Vasudeva Kanva replaced Devabhuti, Simuka replaced Susharma, and the Sthanakvasi sect grew out of the Lonka sect, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
41.tq: Link each founder to the predecessor he replaced.
n: Pushyamitra Shunga succeeded Brihadratha Maurya. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 95-96]
Vasudeva Kanva succeeded Devabhuti. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 95-96]
Simuka succeeded Susharma. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 95-96]
Sthanakvasi succeeded the Lonka sect. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 95-96]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Pushyamitra Shunga** succeeded **Brihadratha Maurya**; **Vasudeva Kanva** succeeded **Devabhuti**.
**Simuka** succeeded **Susharma** (Kanva); **Sthanakvasi** grew out of the **Lonka sect**.
xa: **Simuka** (Srimukha) founded the **Satavahana** dynasty.
The **Puranas** say the Satavahanas defeated the **Sunga** and **Kanva** dynasties.
**Nanda Dynasty** succeeded the **Shishunaga Dynasty**.

41.s:
Arrange the following dynasties from predecessor to successor:
A. Aravidu Dynasty
B. Sangama Dynasty
C. Tuluva Dynasty
D. Saluva Dynasty
41.x: Vijayanagara was ruled by the Sangama (from 1336), Saluva (1485), Tuluva (1505) and Aravidu (1570) dynasties in turn, giving B, D, C, A.
41.tq: Arrange the Vijayanagara dynasties by year.
n: The Saluva Dynasty succeeded the Sangama Dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 95-96]
The Tuluva Dynasty succeeded the Saluva Dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 95-96]
The Aravidu Dynasty succeeded the Tuluva Dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 95-96]
xs: The order is **B, D, C, A** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Sangama** → **Saluva** → **Tuluva** → **Aravidu**.
The **Saluva** succeeded the **Sangama**, the **Tuluva** succeeded the **Saluva**, and the **Aravidu** succeeded the **Tuluva**.
xa: Delhi Sultanate: **Slave → Khalji → Tughlaq → Sayyid → Lodi**.
**Nanda** succeeded **Shishunaga** in Magadha.
**Vasudeva Kanva** succeeded **Devabhuti** of the Shunga dynasty.

41.s:
Match each dynasty in List-I with its immediate predecessor in List-II:

List-I
(a) Khalji Dynasty
(b) Tughlaq Dynasty
(c) Sayyid Dynasty
(d) Lodi Dynasty

List-II
(i) Sayyid Dynasty

(iii) Tughlaq Dynasty
(iv) Khalji Dynasty
41.x: Each dynasty's predecessor: Khalji after Slave, Tughlaq after Khalji, Sayyid after Tughlaq, and Lodi after Sayyid, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
41.tq: Recall the order of the Delhi Sultanate dynasties.
n: The Khalji Dynasty succeeded the Slave Dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 95-96]
The Tughlaq Dynasty succeeded the Khalji Dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 95-96]
The Sayyid Dynasty succeeded the Tughlaq Dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 95-96]
The Lodi Dynasty succeeded the Sayyid Dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 95-96]
xs: The correct match is **a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Khalji** after the **Slave** dynasty; **Tughlaq** after the **Khalji**.
**Sayyid** after the **Tughlaq**; **Lodi** after the **Sayyid**.
xa: Vijayanagara: **Sangama → Saluva → Tuluva → Aravidu**.
Magadha: **Shishunaga → Nanda**; later **Maurya → Shunga → Kanva**.
**Simuka** succeeded **Susharma** of the Kanva dynasty.

41.s: Which dynasty immediately preceded the Nanda Dynasty in Magadha?
41.x: The Nanda dynasty replaced the Shishunaga dynasty in Magadha, Mahapadma Nanda having overthrown the last Shishunaga king. The Haryankas came before the Shishunagas; the Mauryas and Shungas came after the Nandas.
41.tq: Recall the Magadhan sequence: Haryanka, Shishunaga, Nanda, Maurya.
n: The Nanda Dynasty succeeded the Shishunaga Dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 95-96]
xs: The **Shishunaga Dynasty** immediately preceded the **Nanda Dynasty** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Haryanka** dynasty (founder **Bimbisara**) came earlier.
The **Maurya** and **Shunga** dynasties came after the Nandas.
xa: **Pushyamitra Shunga** succeeded **Brihadratha Maurya**.
Sequence: **Maurya → Sunga → Kanva → Kushana** (BPSC **2025**).
**Simuka** succeeded **Susharma** of the Kanva dynasty.

41.s: Who founded the Haryanka dynasty?
41.x: Bimbisara founded the Haryanka dynasty of Magadha. Simuka founded the Satavahanas, Pushyamitra Shunga the Shungas and Vasudeva Kanva the Kanvas.
41.tq: Match each founder with his dynasty.
n: Bimbisara founded the Haryanka dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
Bimbisara was the founder of the Haryanka dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
Vasudeva Kanva founded the Kanva dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
Simuka founded the Satavahana dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
Pushyamitra Shunga founded the Shunga dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
xs: **Bimbisara** founded the **Haryanka** dynasty — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Vasudeva Kanva** founded the **Kanva** dynasty.
**Simuka** founded the **Satavahana** dynasty.
**Pushyamitra Shunga** founded the **Shunga** dynasty.
xa: **Simuka** is also known as **Sindhuk** and **Shiprak**.
**Vakataka** — **Pravarasena I**; **Ikshvaku** — **Shrisantamula**.
**Pala** — **Gopala**; **Sena** — **Samantasena**.

41.s:

xa: ⚠ First **large-scale** gold = **Kushanas (Vima Kadphises)**.
