**Long vs short chronology** is unresolved.
The **Nasik Prasasti** is the main source for **Gautamiputra's** reign.
xa: Restruck coins confirm the Prasasti's claims.
⚠ Bellary home view: APPSC **2017** key = **R.G. Bhandarkar**.

46.s: Why are the conquest claims of the Nasik Prasasti treated with caution by historians?
o: It was composed several centuries after the Satavahana dynasty ended.
It was written by a foreign enemy of the Satavahanas.
It is a family eulogy and may exaggerate the conquests.
It contains no reference to any ruler or territory.
46.x: The Nasik Prasasti is a family eulogy, so its claims of conquest may be exaggerated even though its evidence remains important.
46.tq: Apply source criticism by identifying the purpose and bias of the inscription.
xs: The Nasik Prasasti is a **family eulogy**, so its **claims of conquest** may be **exaggerated** — option **(3)** is correct.
It was issued by **Gautami Balasri**, his mother, in the reign of her grandson — not by a foreign enemy, nor centuries later.
xa: It names regions such as **Aparanta**, **Anupa**, **Vidarbha**, **Akara**, **Avanti**.
The **Jogalthambi hoard** of restruck coins confirms part of its claims.

46.s: Which statement correctly identifies the chronological problem connected with the Salivahana era?
o: The era is unrelated to any Satavahana chronology.
The era began in 230 BCE and exactly matches Simuka’s reign.
The era is dated to AD 78, but attributing it to Gautamiputra does not fit his c. 106–130 CE dates.
The era began in AD 150 and exactly matches Rudradaman’s inscription.
46.x: Gautamiputra is credited in the tradition with the Salivahana era of AD 78, but that attribution conflicts with the dates c. 106–130 CE assigned to his reign.
46.tq: Compare the era date with the ruler’s proposed reign instead of accepting a famous attribution automatically.
xs: The **Salivahana era** is **AD 78**, but crediting it to **Gautamiputra** does not fit his c. **106–130 CE** dates — option **(3)** is correct.
**Simuka** is placed c. **230-207 BCE**, not linked to this era.
xa: Rudradaman's Junagadh record is c. **150 CE**.
Gautamiputra was the **23rd** king.

46.s:
Assertion (A): Hala was associated with the title Kavivatsala.
Reason (R): Hala belonged to the Satavahana dynasty.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
46.x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Hala was a Satavahana king and was called Kavivatsala, but the title comes from his love of poetry, not from his dynasty.
46.tq: Check whether R is the cause of A.
xs: Both **A and R are true**, but **R is not the correct explanation** of A — so option **(2)** is correct.
A: **Hala** bore the title **Kavivatsala**.
R: Hala was a **Satavahana** king (**17th**) — his dynasty does not explain the title.
He authored the **Gatha Saptasati**, which fits a poet-patron title.
xa: Hala reigned **5** years.
⚠ **Lilavati** (Sri Lankan princess) was Hala's queen.
⚠ The **Gathasaptasati** does **not** narrate early Satavahana history (G2 **2017**).

46.s:
How many of the following are associated with the Satavahana dynasty?
I. Devinaganika
II. Hala
III. Gautamiputra Satakarni
IV. Virapurushadatta
46.x: Three are Satavahana: Devinaganika, Hala and Gautamiputra Satakarni. Virapurushadatta was an Ikshvaku king.
46.tq: Recall the dynasty of each person.
xs: **Only three** are Satavahana — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Devinaganika**, **Hala** and **Gautamiputra Satakarni** belong to the **Satavahana** dynasty.
**Virapurushadatta** was an **Ikshvaku** king.
xa: **Devinaganika** acted as **regent** during her son's minority (APPSC **2019**).
**Hala** = **Kavivatsala**; **Gautamiputra** = **Thrisamudrapati** (some notes).
Virapurushadatta's reign was the **golden age of Buddhism**.

46.s:
Assertion (A): The period of Virapurushadatta was described as the golden age of Buddhism.
Reason (R): Buddhism flourished during the reign of Virapurushadatta.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
46.x: Both are true and R explains A: Virapurushadatta's reign is called the golden age of Buddhism because Buddhism flourished at Nagarjunakonda under him.
46.tq: Check whether R is the cause of A.
n: Buddhism flourished during the reign of Virapurushadatta. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 38-39]
The reign of Virapurushadatta was regarded as the golden age of Buddhism. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 38-39]
xs: Both **A and R are true**, and **R is the correct explanation** of A — so option **(1)** is correct.
A: **Virapurushadatta**'s reign is described as the **golden age of Buddhism**.
R: **Buddhism flourished** in his reign — which is why it is so called.
xa: Virapurushadatta was a popular **Ikshvaku** king.
**Upasika Bodhisri** contributed to Buddhism.
The **Ikshvakus** succeeded the Satavahanas in Andhra.

46.s: In the inscriptional context, what does the term ‘Gulmika’ denote?
46.x: In these inscriptions Gulmika means a feudatory chief. Munyada is the term for a political employee.
46.tq: Discriminate Gulmika from Munyada.
n: Gulmika means a feudatory chief. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
xs: **Gulmika** means a **feudatory chief** — so option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ The administration topic's key gives **village headman** for Gulmika.
A **guild of weavers** relates to **Ushavadatta**'s Nasik deposit, not to Gulmika.
xa: All Satavahana inscriptions are in **Prakrit**, **Brahmi** script.
They were studied by **Buhler**.
The **earliest** inscriptions come from **Maharashtra** (G2 **2025**).

46.s:
Assertion (A): The Nasik inscription was issued by Gautami Balasri during the reign of Vasishtiputra Pulomavi.
Reason (R): Ushavadatta’s investment mentioned in the Nasik inscription carried an interest rate of 12%.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
46.x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Gautami Balasri issued the Nasik inscription in Vasishtiputra Pulumavi's reign, while the 12 percent interest relates to Ushavadatta's separate Nasik record.
46.tq: Check whether R is the cause of A.
n: The Nasik inscription was issued by Gautami Balasri during the reign of Vasishtiputra Pulomavi. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
The interest rate on Ushavadatta’s investment was 12%. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
xs: Both **A and R are true**, but **R is not the correct explanation** of A — so option **(2)** is correct.
A: the **Nasik inscription** was issued by **Gautami Balasri** during **Vasishtiputra Pulomavi**'s reign.
R: **Ushavadatta** invested **2,000 Karshapanas** in a **weavers' guild** at **12%** — a separate Nasik record.
xa: The Nasik Prasasti records the **military achievements** of **Gautamiputra Satakarni**, in **Prakrit prose**.
Ushavadatta was **Nahapana's son-in-law**; the guild was at **Govardhana**.
**Ayama**, his minister, issued the **Junnar** inscription.

46.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Ajanta
(b) Nasik
(c) Bhairavakonda
(d) Guntupalli

List-II
(i) Centre for the Rajagirika school of Buddhists
(ii) Nasik Cave Inscription
(iii) “Swetagaja Jataka” painting
(iv) Eight caves and centre of Saivism
46.x: Ajanta has the Swetagaja Jataka painting, Nasik has the Nasik Cave Inscription, Bhairavakonda has eight caves and was a Saiva centre, and Guntupalli was the Rajagirika Buddhist centre, giving a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
46.tq: Recall the feature of each site.
n: The “Swetagaja Jataka” painting can be seen in Ajanta Cave No. 10. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 8-9]
The Nasik Cave Inscription is located at Nasik. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 8-9]
Bhairavakonda has eight caves. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 8-9]
Bhairavakonda was a centre of Saivism. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 8-9]
Guntupalli was a centre for the Rajagirika school of Buddhists. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 8-9]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Ajanta** = "**Swetagaja Jataka**" painting (**Cave No. 10**); **Nasik** = **Nasik Cave Inscription**.
**Bhairavakonda** = **eight caves**, centre of **Saivism**; **Guntupalli** = **Rajagirika school** centre.
xa: **Bhairavakonda** is in **Nellore** district.
**Guntupalli** is near **Kamavarapukota**, **Eluru** district.
The Nasik inscription was issued by **Gautami Balasri**.

46.s:
How many of the following statements are correct?

1. Bhairavakonda has eight caves.
2. Bhairavakonda is a centre of Saivism.
3. Guntupalli is a centre for the Rajagirika school of Buddhists.
4. Guntupalli is located in Nellore district.
46.x: Three are correct: Bhairavakonda has eight caves and was a Saiva centre, and Guntupalli was the Rajagirika Buddhist centre. Statement 4 is false because Guntupalli is near Kamavarapukota in Eluru district, not Nellore.
46.tq: Check the district in each statement.
n: Bhairavakonda has eight caves. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 8-9]
Bhairavakonda was a centre of Saivism. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 8-9]
Guntupalli is near Kamavarapukota in Eluru district. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 8-9]
Guntupalli was a centre for the Rajagirika school of Buddhists. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 8-9]
xs: **Only three** statements (1, 2, 3) are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
1 and 2: **Bhairavakonda** has **eight caves** and is a **centre of Saivism**.
3: **Guntupalli** is a centre for the **Rajagirika school** of Buddhists.
4 is wrong: Guntupalli is near **Kamavarapukota**, **Eluru** district; **Nellore** is Bhairavakonda's district.
xa: The **Swetagaja Jataka** is in **Ajanta Cave No. 10**.
The **Nasik Cave Inscription** mentions the military achievements of **Gautamiputra Satakarni**.
**Amaravati** inscription holds the first Telugu word **"Nagabu"**.

47.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Satavahana kingship:
1. Kingship was hereditary and patriarchal.
2. The king was regarded as an upholder of dharma.
3. Satavahana power was more decentralised than Mauryan power.
4. Succession was based exclusively on election by feudatories.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
47.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Satavahana kingship was hereditary and patriarchal, and it was comparatively decentralised; succession was not exclusively elective.
47.tq: Reject the invented constitutional rule while retaining the three connected features of kingship.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: kingship was **hereditary and patriarchal**.
Statement 2 correct: the king was the **upholder of dharma** (Dharmashastra ideal).
Statement 3 correct: it was **decentralised vs the Mauryas**; statement 4 wrong — succession was **hereditary**, not elective.
xa: Titles: **Maharaja, Raja-Raja**.
The **Mantri Parishad** helped the king.
Mauryan = **centralised**; Satavahanas = decentralised with Mauryan-style officers (**Amatya, Mahamatra**).

47.s: The use of maternal gotra names by Satavahana rulers is known as the practice of:
47.x: Satavahana rulers used matronymics, or names derived from the mother’s lineage or gotra. This practice began with Gautamiputra Satakarni.
47.tq: Distinguish the maternal naming practice from the more familiar paternal term.
xs: Maternal gotra names are **matronymics** — option **(3)** is correct.
They began with **Gautamiputra Satakarni**.
xa: Examples: **Gautamiputra**, **Vasishthiputra**.
They show **respect for mothers**, yet society stayed **patriarchal**.
Gautamiputra's titles: **Ekabrahmana**, **Varnasankarya nirodhaka**.

47.s: Which one of the following correctly states the role associated with Gautami Balasri?
o: She founded the Chutu dynasty in Mysore.
She issued the Naneghat inscription as regent for minor sons.
She issued the Nasik inscription during the reign of her grandson Pulumavi.
She commanded the Roman fleet at Arikamedu.
47.x: Gautami Balasri issued the Nasik inscription during the reign of her grandson Pulumavi. Naganika is associated with regency for her minor sons and the Naneghat inscription.
47.tq: Separate two prominent queen mothers by inscription and political role.
xs: **Gautami Balasri** issued the **Nasik** inscription in the reign of her grandson **Pulumavi** — option **(3)** is correct.
The **Naneghat** inscription was issued by **Naganika**, regent for her minor sons.
The **Chutus** were feudatories in **Mysore**, not founded by Balasri.
xa: The Nasik inscription names **Govardhana** the most prominent **ahara**.
Queens **Naganika** and **Balasri** issuing inscriptions show women were **respected**.
Balasri donated a **vihara**.

47.s: The officer who administered regions and was responsible for the day-to-day military affairs of the Satavahana kingdom was the
47.x: The Mahasenapati was the military chief who handled the day-to-day military administration of regions. The king remained the supreme commander.
47.tq: Distinguish the supreme commander from the officer handling routine military affairs.
xs: The **Mahasenapati** ran **day-to-day military affairs** — option **(3)** is correct.
The **king** was the **supreme commander**.
**Raja** and **Mahabhoja** were feudatory titles; the **Gaulmika** was a village headman.
xa: Senapati / Mahasenapati was the military chief administering regions.
**Mahatalavara** = commander of border provinces.
Army (Pliny): **1,00,000 infantry, 2,000 cavalry, 1,000 elephants**.

47.s:
Consider the following pairs of Satavahana officers and their functions:
1. Heranika - Treasurer
2. Rajjugahaka - Land surveyor
3. Pattikapala - Kept records of the king's orders
4. Akshapatakas - Wrote and kept records of the king's orders
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
47.x: Pairs 1, 2 and 4 are correct: Heranika was the treasurer, Rajjugahaka the land surveyor, and the Akshapatakas wrote and kept records of the king's orders. Pair 3 is wrong: the Pattikapala drafted land-grant and gift inscriptions. So 1, 2 and 4 only (A); B, C and D all include pair 3.
47.tq: Pattikapala drafts grants; Akshapatakas keep the orders - do not swap them.
xs: Pairs **1, 2 and 4** are correct — option **(1)**.
**Heranika** = **treasurer**; **Rajjugahaka** = **land surveyor**.
Pair 3 wrong: **Pattikapala** drafted **land-grant and gift inscriptions**.
**Akshapatakas** wrote and kept records of the king's orders.
xa: ⚠ **Heranika** = treasurer; **Bhandagarika** = stores; **Rajjugahaka** = surveyor; **Pradeshika** = police.
**Mahatalavara** = commander of border provinces.

47.s:
With reference to the Gulmika, consider the following statements:
1. A Gulmika was associated with a group of villages called a Gulma.
2. The office was connected with village-level administration and law and order.
3. The post remained strictly non-hereditary throughout the Satavahana period.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
47.x: A Gulmika headed a Gulma, a cluster of villages, and could supervise law and order. The post later became hereditary, so statement 3 is false.
47.tq: Reject the absolute claim and retain the two statements supported by administrative practice.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: the **Gulmika** headed a **Gulma**, a cluster of villages.
Statement 2 correct: he supervised villages and **kept law and order** (Myakadoni).
Statement 3 wrong: village heads' posts **became hereditary**, helping **feudalism** grow.
xa: Key answer: **village headman** (G2 **2008**); some notes say "feudatory chief".
Villagers owed **vetti** (forced labour).

47.s: The hereditary character of village headships and the obligation of villagers to perform vetti contributed respectively to:
o: The decline of agriculture and the abolition of taxation
The growth of feudalism and the prevalence of forced labour
The rise of guilds and the disappearance of villages
The growth of Roman trade and the spread of Buddhism
47.x: Hereditary village offices encouraged feudal tendencies, while vetti referred to forced labour owed by villagers.
47.tq: Link the institutional change with its stated social and economic consequence.
xs: Hereditary village headships → **growth of feudalism**; **vetti** → **forced labour** — option **(2)** is correct.
Village heads were often **military officers**.
xa: The **Kamasutra** records **forced labour (vetti)** by women.
Tax-free land grants were also a **root of the early-medieval feudal order**.
**Mahatalavaras / Mahasenadhipatis** grew into **feudal lords**.

47.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the administrative hierarchy of the Satavahana state from the larger unit to the smaller unit?
47.x: Rashtra was a province, Ahara a district or province, Vishaya a sub-division and Grama the village unit.
47.tq: Arrange administrative units by territorial scale, from largest to smallest.
xs: Hierarchy: **Rashtra – Ahara – Vishaya – Grama** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Rashtra** = province; **Ahara** = district; **Vishaya** = sub-division; **Grama** = village (lowest unit).
xa: Heads: **Maharashtrika** (Rashtra), **Amatya** / Mahamatra (Ahara), **Vishayapati** (Vishaya).
Village head: **Gramika / Gulmika / Gramani**.
Vishaya is **also recorded as Nigama**.

47.s: Which of the following was regarded as the most prominent Ahara according to the Nasik inscription?
47.x: Govardhana was identified as the most prominent Ahara in the Nasik inscription.
47.tq: Use the inscription-linked place clue to distinguish among similarly named Aharas.
xs: **Govardhana** was the most prominent **Ahara** per the **Nasik** inscription — option **(4)** is correct.
**Mamala**, **Kodura** and **Vaijayanti** were other aharas named in inscriptions.
xa: Other aharas: **Satavahani**, **Sopara**.
**Ushavadata** deposited money with the **Govardhana weavers' guild**.
Govardhana was also a **major town**.

47.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Aharas far from the capital were administered by military officers.
2. A Gramani could be responsible for five or ten villages.
3. A group of villages was known as a Gulma.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
47.x: All three statements are correct. Distant Aharas were entrusted to Mahasenadhipatis, a Gramani could oversee five or ten villages, and a cluster of villages was called a Gulma.
47.tq: Check each statement against the administrative scale and its exception for distant regions.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
Statement 1: **distant aharas** were run by military officers (**Mahasenadhipatis**).
Statement 2: a **Gramani** had **5 or 10 villages**.
Statement 3: a group of villages = **Gulma**.
xa: The **Gulmika** headed a Gulma.
⚠ **Nigama Sabha** = cities; **Gulma** = group of villages.

47.s: Which inscription refers to the Nigama Sabha in the context of Satavahana urban administration?
47.x: The Nigama Sabha, the urban council that administered towns, is referred to in the Bhattiprolu inscription (one PYQ-book explanation cites Naneghat, which is not an option here). The Allahabad pillar is Samudragupta's, Hathigumpha is Kharavela's, and Junagadh is Rudradaman's.
47.tq: Identify the inscription linked specifically with the urban council reference.
xs: The **Nigama Sabha** is referred to in the **Bhattiprolu inscription** — option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ A PYQ-book explanation cites **Naneghat**, which is not an option here.
**Junagadh** is **Rudradaman's** record — the first complete Sanskrit inscription.
xa: The Nigama Sabha administered **cities, not villages** (APPSC G2 **2008**).
Its members were **Gahapatis** (Karshaka pratinidhi).
AP angle: **Bhattiprolu** — "Nigama sabha".

47.s: Which of the following sets contains only towns associated with the Satavahana urban network?
47.x: Barukaccha, Sopara, Kalyan and Govardhana are included among the major Satavahana towns. The other sets combine urban centres from different historical contexts.
47.tq: Check whether every member belongs to the same stated urban network.
xs: **Barukaccha, Sopara, Kalyan and Govardhana** are Satavahana towns — option **(3)** is correct.
They are on the list of **major towns**.
xa: Other towns: **Pratishthana, Kondapur, Dhanyakataka, Vijayapuri, Nasik**.
West coast ports: **Bharukachha, Sopara, Kalyan, Vyjayantipura**.
Town administration lay with the **Nigama Sabha**.

47.s: The Nigama Sabha of the Satavahana period was:
o: An urban council that administered towns, with Gahapatis as members
A council of ministers advising the king
An assembly of guild heads that fixed coin weights
47.x: The Nigama Sabha was the town council that administered cities, not villages (APPSC G2 2008); its members were Gahapatis. Villages were under Gramanis/Gulmikas, the king's council was the Mantri Parishad, and guilds were headed by Shreshthis.
47.tq: Nigama Sabha = city, not village.
xs: The **Nigama Sabha** was an **urban council** that administered **towns**, with **Gahapatis** as members — option **(2)** is correct.
It ran **cities, not villages** (APPSC G2 **2008**).
The king's council was the **Mantri Parishad**; guilds were headed by **Shreshthis**.
xa: Gahapati = **Karshaka pratinidhi** (farmers' representative).
It is referred to in the **Bhattiprolu** inscription.

47.s:
Consider the following statements about Satavahana administrative terms:
1. Raja was the highest feudatory and could issue coins.
2. Mahabhoja denoted a powerful local feudatory chief.
3. The Nigama sabha administered villages.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
47.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Raja was the highest feudatory with the right to issue coins. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Nigama sabha administered cities (towns), not villages (Bhattiprolu inscription). So 1 and 2 only (A); B, C and D include the false statement 3.
47.tq: Nigama sabha = town council; village level was under the Gaulmika.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: the **Raja** was the **highest feudatory** and could **issue coins**.
Statement 2 correct: **Mahabhojas** were powerful local feudatory chiefs.
Statement 3 wrong: the **Nigama sabha** administered **cities**, not villages.
xa: Grading: **Raja > Mahabhoja > Senapati**.
Mahabhojas were **hereditary**, in the **Konkan** region.

47.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
47.x: The Mahabhojas were associated with the Konkan region. Chutus, Kuras and Ikshvakus are correctly linked with Mysore, Kolhapur and Vijayapuri respectively.
47.tq: Use the location trap by matching each feudatory with its recorded regional base.
xs: **Mahabhojas — Eastern Bengal** is wrongly matched — option **(4)** is the answer.
The Mahabhojas were in the **Konkan** region.
**Chutus — Mysore**, **Kuras — Kolhapur**, **Ikshvakus — Vijayapuri** are correct.
xa: These **Samanta rajyas** paid **annual tribute** and sent troops.
After the fall, many feudatories became **independent**.

47.s:
Consider the following statements about the Maharathis:
1. They were hereditary feudatories.
2. They collected and remitted taxes.
3. They were mainly associated with the western Deccan.
4. They were prohibited from issuing coins under all circumstances.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
47.x: Maharathis were hereditary tax-collecting feudatories of the western Deccan. The absolute prohibition in statement 4 is incorrect, as Sadakana Chutukadananda issued his own coins.
47.tq: Spot the absolute statement that conflicts with the recorded coin-issuing example.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
**Maharathis** were **hereditary**, **collected and remitted taxes**, in the **western Deccan**.
Statement 4 wrong: Maharathi **Sadakana Chutukadananda** issued his own coins.
xa: **Naganika** was the daughter of Maharathi **Tranakayiro**.
The **Raja** was the highest feudatory with the right to issue coins.

47.s: The omission of the emperor’s name in the inscriptions of the Mahabhojas is generally taken to indicate their:
o: Complete dependence on the central administration
47.x: The omission of the emperor’s name suggests that the Mahabhojas enjoyed a near-independent position within the Satavahana political structure.
47.tq: Infer political status from the epigraphic feature rather than from the title alone.
xs: Mahabhoja inscriptions **omit the emperor's name** → a **near-independent position** — option **(4)** is correct.
They were **hereditary** chiefs, so option (3) is wrong.
xa: They were in the **Konkan** region.
Grading: **Raja > Mahabhoja > Senapati**.

47.s: Mahatalavaras or Mahasenadhipatis in the later Satavahana phase were primarily:
o: Generals placed in charge of border provinces
47.x: Mahatalavaras or Mahasenadhipatis were generals entrusted with border provinces and later developed into feudal lords.
47.tq: Match the military title with its territorial responsibility.
xs: **Mahatalavaras / Mahasenadhipatis** were **generals in charge of border provinces** — option **(3)** is correct.
They belong to the **later phase** and **grew into feudal lords**.
Land surveyor = **Rajjugahaka**; treasurer = **Heranika**.
xa: Distant aharas were also run by **Mahasenadhipatis**.
After the fall, many feudatories became **independent**.

47.s: Which of the following statements regarding Satavahana military and administrative centres is correct?
o: Skandhavara was a city assembly, whereas Kataka denoted land revenue.
Kataka was a temporary campaign camp, whereas Skandhavara was a permanent garrison.
Kataka was a permanent military camp or fortified administrative centre, whereas Skandhavara was a temporary campaign camp.
Both Kataka and Skandhavara referred exclusively to tax-free villages granted to Brahmanas.
47.x: Kataka denoted a permanent military camp, garrison or fortified administrative centre, generally located in cities. Skandhavara was a temporary military camp used during campaigns.
47.tq: Separate the two look-alike military terms by permanence and purpose.
xs: **Kataka** = **permanent military camp** or fortified administrative centre; **Skandhavara** = **temporary campaign camp** — option **(3)** is correct.
Option (2) reverses them.
Katakas were located in **cities**.
xa: Both served as **administrative centres when the king was present** (APPSC G1 **2024**).
Distractors: tax-free monk villages, rock-cut areas.

47.s: According to Pliny, the Satavahana army consisted of
47.x: Pliny mentions 1,00,000 infantry, 2,000 cavalry and 1,000 elephants in the Satavahana army.
47.tq: Match each numerical component with the correct military category instead of relying on the total alone.
xs: Pliny: **1,00,000 infantry, 2,000 cavalry, 1,000 elephants** — option **(1)** is correct.
The other options change or swap the numbers.
xa: The army was **Chaturanga bala** plus **archers**.
King = supreme commander; **Mahasenapati** ran daily military affairs.
Pliny also complained of the **drain of Roman gold** to India.

47.s: According to the arrangement depicted in Amaravati sculptures, which sequence correctly represents the deployment of Satavahana forces?
o: Infantry in front, cavalry and elephants on the flanks, archers at the rear
Cavalry in front, infantry on the flanks, elephants at the rear
Elephants in front, archers on the flanks, cavalry at the rear
Archers in front, elephants at the rear, infantry on the flanks
47.x: Amaravati sculptures show infantry in front, cavalry and elephants on the flanks, and archers at the rear.
47.tq: Reconstruct the battlefield arrangement by fixing the front and rear positions first.
xs: Amaravati sculptures show **infantry in front, cavalry and elephants on the flanks, archers at the rear** — option **(1)** is correct.
The other options misplace the **archers**, who stood at the **rear**.
xa: The army was **Chaturanga bala** + archers.
**Mahasenapati** handled day-to-day military affairs.
Pliny's figures: **1,00,000** infantry.

47.s: In Satavahana inscriptions, the terms 'Katakas' and 'Skandhavaras' refer to:
o: Tax-free villages granted to Buddhist monks
Military camps that served as administrative centres when the king was present
47.x: Katakas (permanent camps/garrisons) and Skandhavaras (temporary campaign camps) both served as administrative centres when the king stayed there - the APPSC G1 2024 key. Tax-free monk villages, rock-cut caves and guilds are the usual distractors.
47.tq: Kataka/Skandhavara = military camps used as admin centres.
xs: **Katakas and Skandhavaras** were **military camps** that served as **administrative centres when the king was present** — option **(3)** is correct (APPSC G1 **2024** key).
**Kataka** = permanent camp in cities; **Skandhavara** = temporary campaign camp.
Tax-free monk villages, rock-cut caves and guilds are the usual distractors.
xa: Guilds of weavers = **Kolika**; oil pressers = **Tailika / Tilapishaka**.
Tax-free grants (**agraharas**) went to Brahmanas and Buddhist monks.

47.s: The term Bhaga in the Satavahana revenue system referred to:
o: A trade tax collected from Roman merchants
The king’s one-sixth share of the harvest
47.x: Bhaga was the king’s share of the harvest, fixed at one-sixth.
47.tq: Recall the precise fraction attached to the named revenue term.
xs: **Bhaga** was the king's share of the harvest — **1/6** — option **(2)** is correct.
Forced labour was **vetti**; the artisans' tax was **Karukara**.
xa: **Deya-meya / Bhodga** = king's share of produce, collected **in kind**.
Chief income: **land revenue**.
⚠ **Bhaga** = land revenue (**1/6**); **Karukara** = artisans' tax.

47.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Karukara — Tax paid by artisans and professionals
Bhaga — Tax paid only in Roman coins
Deya-meya — Tax on foreign traders alone
47.x: Karukara was the tax imposed on artisans and professionals. Bhaga was the king’s share of harvest, Kara a general levy and Deya-meya the king’s share of produce collected in kind.
47.tq: Separate the general levy, produce share and occupational tax by their exact meanings.
xs: **Karukara** — tax paid by **artisans / professionals** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Bhaga** was the **1/6** land revenue, not paid only in Roman coins.
**Kara** was a **general tax**, not forced labour (that was **vetti**); **Deya-meya** was the king's share of produce in kind.
xa: Taxes were collected in **cash and kind**.
Other income: **tribute from feudatories** + trade taxes.

47.s:
Consider the following statements about Satavahana land grants:
1. These grants became a root of the later early-medieval feudal order.
2. Under Gautamiputra's Nasik grants, royal officers and soldiers retained the right to enter the granted land.
3. The Satavahanas were the first rulers to make tax-free land grants to Brahmanas and Buddhist monks.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
47.x: Statement 3 is correct: the Satavahanas made the first tax-free grants (agraharas) to Brahmanas and Buddhist monks. Statement 1 is correct: such grants were the root of the early-medieval feudal order. Statement 2 is wrong: the Nasik grants barred royal officers and soldiers from entering, banned digging for salt and freed the land from district police and royal dues. So '1 and 3 only'.
47.tq: Immunity = officers and soldiers could NOT enter.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: tax-free grants became the **root of the later early-medieval feudal order**.
Statement 2 is wrong: under Gautamiputra's **Nasik grants**, **royal officers and soldiers could not enter** the land.
Statement 3 is correct: the Satavahanas were the **first to make tax-free land grants (agraharas)** to **Brahmanas and Buddhist monks**.
xa: Other immunities: **no digging for salt**; free of **district police** and **royal dues**.
**Naneghat**: **Satakarni I** gave land, cows (**godhana**) and gold to Brahmins.
**Gautamiputra** gave a village at **Tirasmri** to monks + **100 nivartanas** of his own land.

47.s: Which of the following statements regarding Satakarni I and Gautamiputra Satakarni is correct?
o: Satakarni I granted land, cows and gold to Brahmanas at Naneghat, while Gautamiputra granted a village at Tirasmri to monks and 100 nivartanas of his own land.
Satakarni I granted Tirasmri to monks, while Gautamiputra made the Naneghat donation to Brahmanas.
Both rulers granted only military camps and imposed taxes on the recipients.
Neither ruler is associated with land grants to religious beneficiaries.
47.x: At Naneghat, Satakarni I gave land, cows or godhana, and gold to Brahmanas. Gautamiputra gave the village of Tirasmri to monks along with 100 nivartanas of his own land.
47.tq: Compare two rulers by separating the place, beneficiaries and contents of their grants.
xs: **Satakarni I** gave **land, cows and gold** to Brahmins at **Naneghat**; **Gautamiputra** gave **Tirasmri** village to monks and **100 nivartanas** — option **(1)** is correct.
Option (2) swaps the two rulers.
xa: Cows = **godhana**.
The Satavahanas were **first** to make **tax-free** land grants.
Immunities: **no entry** for royal officers and soldiers; **no salt digging**.

47.s: Which of the following statements regarding agriculture under the Satavahanas is correct?
o: The main crops were barley and sugarcane, and transplantation was unknown.
Agriculture was confined to dry farming in the Deccan plateau.
Cultivation expanded mainly in the Narmada–Tapi basin and wheat was the principal crop.
Cultivation expanded in the Krishna–Godavari basin, with paddy transplantation and rice and cotton as important crops.
47.x: The Satavahanas expanded cultivation in the Krishna–Godavari basin. Paddy transplantation was practised, and rice and cotton were the main crops.
47.tq: Combine the basin, agricultural practice and crop clues before selecting the precise statement.
xs: Cultivation spread in the **Krishna–Godavari basin**, with **paddy transplantation**, and **rice and cotton** as main crops — option **(4)** is correct.
So barley/sugarcane, dry farming only, or wheat in the Narmada–Tapi basin are wrong.
xa: Irrigation: **ghatiyantras**, made by the **Udayantrika** guild.
Farm surplus fed **urban growth, trade and crafts**.

47.s:
Consider the following statements about the Shreni system:
1. A Shreni was an organisation of traders and artisans belonging to one craft.
2. Guilds fixed rules of work, quality standards, prices and wages.
3. Every guild was registered with a central state authority.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
47.x: Shrenis organised traders and artisans of a particular craft and regulated work, quality, prices, wages and conduct. They were not registered with a central state authority, making statement 3 false.
47.tq: Identify the wrong institutional claim about compulsory central registration.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: a **Shreni** was an organisation of **traders and artisans** of one craft.
Statement 2 correct: guilds fixed **rules of work, quality standards, prices and wages**.
Statement 3 wrong: guilds were **not registered with a central state authority** (UPSC **2012**).
xa: Guild head: **jetthaka** (Pali); Satavahana-era president **Shreshthi** (Sethi, Shetti).
Guilds acted as **banks** — interest on deposits **12%** (APPSC **2019**).

47.s: Which one of the following statements about ancient Indian guilds is NOT correct?
o: They could function as banking institutions.
They regulated the conduct of their members.
They included organisations of both traders and artisans.
They existed only in northern India.
47.x: Guilds existed across India, not only in the north. They regulated members, included traders and artisans, and also accepted deposits as banks.
47.tq: Find the geographically restrictive statement that contradicts the wider distribution of guilds.
xs: "Existed **only in northern India**" is wrong — option **(4)** is the answer.
Guilds existed **across India, not only in the north** (RPSC **2018**).
They acted as **banks**, controlled members' conduct, and included **traders and artisans**.
xa: Interest on guild deposits: **12%** (APPSC **2019**).
Guilds = **shrenis (Srenulu)**.

47.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer.

List-I (Guild)
 a. Tailika
 b. Kulara
 c. Gandhika
 d. Sarthavaha

List-II (Trade)
 i. Perfume
 ii. Long-distance trade
 iii. Oil
 iv. Pottery
47.x: Tailika denotes the oil guild, Kulara the potters, Gandhika the perfume traders and Sarthavaha the long-distance traders.
47.tq: Start from the familiar trade associations and eliminate codes with swapped occupations.
xs: Correct match: **a–iii, b–iv, c–i, d–ii** — option **(1)**.
**Tailika** = **oil** pressers; **Kulara** = **potters**.
**Gandhika** = **perfumers**; **Sarthavaha** = **long-distance / foreign traders**.
xa: **Kolika** = weavers; **Padhika** = butchers (Katikavaru).
**Malakara** = florists; **Udayantrika** = water-machines.

47.s:
Consider the following pairs of Satavahana guilds and their crafts:
1. Kolika - Weavers
2. Padhika - Potters
3. Tilapishaka - Oil-pressers
4. Udayantrika - Water-machines (ghatiyantras)
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
47.x: Pairs 1, 3 and 4 are correct: Kolika were weavers, Tilapishaka oil-pressers and Udayantrika made water-machines. Pair 2 is wrong: Padhika were butchers; potters were Kulara/Kularika. So only three pairs (C); 'one' and 'two' undercount and 'all four' ignores the Padhika error.
47.tq: Padhika = butchers (Katikavaru), Kolika = weavers - the two exam favourites.
xs: **Only three pairs** are correct (1, 3, 4) — option **(3)**.
**Kolika** = **weavers**; **Tilapishaka** = **oil pressers**; **Udayantrika** = **water-machines**.
Pair 2 wrong: **Padhika** = **butchers**; potters were **Kulara / Kularika**.
xa: **Ushavadata** deposited **2,000 karshapanas** with the **Govardhana weavers' guild** at **12%** a year.
Exam angle: Kolika = weavers; Padhika = butchers.

47.s: The head of a guild in the Satavahana period was generally known as:
47.x: A guild was headed by a Sethi or Shreshthi. Sarthavaha referred to a long-distance or foreign trader, while Gahapati was connected with urban administration.
47.tq: Distinguish the guild office-holder from urban and trading terms.
xs: A guild was headed by the **Sethi or Shreshthi** (also **Shetti**) — option **(2)** is correct.
**Gulmika** was a village headman; **Sarthavaha** a long-distance / foreign trader; **Gahapati** a member of the urban **Nigama Sabha**.
xa: In Pali the guild head is the **jetthaka**.
Guilds = **shrenis (Srenulu)**, organisations of **traders and artisans** of one craft.
Guilds fixed **rules of work, quality standards, prices and wages**.

47.s: Guilds in the Satavahana period performed which of the following economic functions?
o: They acted as banks and paid interest on deposits.
They issued only royal land grants.
They functioned exclusively as military units.
47.x: Guilds acted as banking institutions: they accepted deposits and paid interest, including payments benefiting monasteries.
47.tq: Identify the economic function from the institutional role rather than the occupational label.
xs: Guilds **acted as banks** — they **took deposits and paid interest** — option **(2)** is correct.
They paid interest to **monasteries**, so they did not prohibit monastic deposits.
xa: Interest on deposits: **12%** (APPSC **2019**).
**Ushavadata's** Nasik inscription records deposits with the **Govardhana weavers' guild**.
Guilds were **not registered with a central state authority** (UPSC **2012**).

47.s: Ushavadata’s Nashik inscription indicates that the weavers’ guild of Govardhana accepted deposits at which rates?
o: 2,000 karshapanas at 3% per month and 1,000 at 1% per year
1,000 karshapanas at 2% per month and 2,000 at three-fourths of 1% per year
2,000 karshapanas at 1% per month and 1,000 at three-fourths of 1% per month
3,000 karshapanas at a uniform rate of 1% per month
47.x: The Nashik inscription records deposits of 2,000 karshapanas at 1% monthly interest and 1,000 karshapanas at three-fourths of 1% monthly interest.
47.tq: Separate the two deposit amounts and match each with its precise interest rate.
xs: **2,000 karshapanas at 1% a month** and **1,000 at 3/4% a month** — option **(3)** is correct.
The deposits were with the **Govardhana weavers' guild** (Nasik inscription of **Ushavadata**).
The first gave **12% a year**, buying robes for monks; the second met monks' **other needs**.
xa: Ushavadata = **Rishabhadatta / Vrishabhadatta**, **Nahapana's son-in-law**.
The Rishabhadatta inscription gives **1 gold coin = 35 karshapanas**.

47.s: Which route correctly represents the inland commercial connection from Ujjain to Bharuch?
47.x: The inland route from Ujjain to Bharuch passed through Paithan and Tagara.
47.tq: Reconstruct the route by identifying the intermediate inland centres.
xs: **Ujjain → Bharuch (Barygaza)** ran **via Paithan and Tagara** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Paithan → Sopara** ran via **Aurangabad**; **Arikamedu → Red Sea** via **Sri Lanka** and the **Arabian Sea**.
xa: **Tagara (Ter)** was an emporium linked to coastal ports.
**Pratishthana (Paithan)** was capital + inland trade centre on the **Godavari**.
NextGenIAS **2026** maps the **Ujjain-Paithan-Tagara-Bharuch** route.

47.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
47.x: Guntupalli was associated with copper and iron, not gold. Guduru, Vinukonda and Palnadu were associated respectively with fine cotton, metal and diamonds.
47.tq: Find the changed commodity in an otherwise familiar centre–product list.
xs: **Guntupalli — Gold** is wrongly matched — option **(4)** is the answer.
**Guntupalli** = **copper, iron**.
**Palnadu** = **diamonds**; **Guduru** = **fine cotton**; **Vinukonda** = **metal**.
xa: **Vidisha** = **cloth, ivory**.
**Karimnagar-Warangal**: iron ore worked.

47.s: Which of the following statements about Satavahana inland trade is correct?
o: Tagara was an emporium linked to coastal ports.
Vengi was exclusively a military camp.
Pratishthana was only a religious settlement and not a trade centre.
The Satavahanas were known for avoiding the construction of roads.
47.x: Tagara was an important emporium linked to coastal ports. Pratishthana was both a capital and inland trade centre, Vengi was a trade centre, and the Satavahanas were famed as road builders.
47.tq: Choose the careful functional description and reject reversed or extreme claims.
xs: **Tagara (Ter)** was an **emporium linked to coastal ports** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Pratishthana** was both **capital and trade centre**, so option (3) is wrong.
The Satavahanas were famed as **road builders** (**Mahapatha nirmatalu**), so option (4) is wrong.
xa: Inland centres: **Pratishthana**, **Tagara**, **Ujjain**.
Route: **Ujjain → Paithan → Tagara → Bharuch**.

47.s: The Satavahanas were famed as road builders, described by the expression:
47.x: Mahapatha nirmatalu means builders or makers of great roads and is associated with the Satavahanas.
47.tq: Identify the exact historical expression rather than its general translation alone.
xs: The Satavahanas were famed as **Mahapatha nirmatalu** (road builders) — option **(3)** is correct.
Their routes linked **Ujjain, Paithan, Tagara** and **Bharuch**.
xa: **Paithan → Sopara** ran via **Aurangabad**.
**Tagara (Ter)** was a hub linked to coastal ports.

47.s: Which Satavahana port was known in Greek accounts as Barygaza?
47.x: Bharuch was known as Barygaza. It came under Satavahana control after the defeat of Nahapana.
47.tq: Discriminate between the Indian port name and its foreign commercial designation.
xs: **Bharuch** was **Barygaza** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Bharukachha** (Bharuch), Gujarat, was on the **west** coast.
**Kantakasela** = **Ghantasala**, an east-coast port; **Sopara** and **Kalyan** are Maharashtra ports.
xa: It came under Satavahana control after **Nahapana's** defeat.
It was the end of the **Ujjain → Paithan → Tagara** route.

47.s: Which of the following ports was destroyed by the Sakas, according to the Periplus?
47.x: The Periplus records that Kalyan was destroyed by the Sakas. Kantakasela and Maisolia were east-coast ports, while Motupalli belonged to a later Eastern Chalukya context.
47.tq: Match the specific event with the correct port instead of merely identifying a port.
xs: The Periplus says **Kalyan** was **destroyed by the Sakas** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Maisolia** and **Kantakasela** were east-coast ports; **Motupalli** a later **Eastern Chalukya-era** port.
xa: Kalyan is near **Mumbai**; ⚠ some notes wrongly place it in **Karnataka**.
**Koddura** was the only east-coast port per the Periplus.

47.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Port/Centre)
a. Maisolia
b. Kantakossyla
c. Koddura
d. Dhanyakataka

List-II (Identification)
i. Amaravati/Dharanikota
ii. Gudur area
iii. Machilipatnam
iv. Ghantasala

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
47.x: Maisolia was identified with Machilipatnam, Kantakossyla with Ghantasala, Koddura with the Gudur area, and Dhanyakataka with Amaravati/Dharanikota.
47.tq: Start from the sure port–place pairs and eliminate codes.
xs: Correct match: **a–iii, b–iv, c–ii, d–i** — option **(1)**.
**Maisolia** = **Machilipatnam**; **Kantakossyla** = **Ghantasala**.
**Koddura** = **Gudur area**, Krishna; **Dhanyakataka** = **Amaravati/Dharanikota**.
xa: Maisolia was known for **textiles** (Ptolemy).
Koddura was the **only east-coast port** per the **Periplus**.
**Kalingapatnam** lay on the **Srikakulam** coast.

47.s: Which one of the following was regarded as the only east-coast port of the Satavahana period in the Periplus?
47.x: Koddura, identified with the Gudur area in Krishna, was described in the Periplus as the only east-coast port.
47.tq: Use the distinctive superlative description to identify the port.
xs: The Periplus calls **Koddura** the **only east-coast port** — option **(1)** is correct.
Koddura is in the **Gudur area, Krishna**.
**Maisolia** = Machilipatnam; **Kantakossyla** = Ghantasala; **Dhanyakataka** = Amaravati.
xa: ⚠ **Maisolia** = Machilipatnam; **Kantakossyla** = Ghantasala; **Koddura** = only east-coast port.
Other AP ports: **Motupalli**, **Kottapatnam** (APHQ).

47.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Bharukachha was situated on the western coast in present-day Gujarat.
2. Sopara and Kalyan were west-coast ports of Maharashtra.
3. Kalyan was a port of Karnataka.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
47.x: Bharukachha was Bharuch in Gujarat, while Sopara and Kalyan were west-coast ports in Maharashtra. The statement locating Kalyan in Karnataka is incorrect.
47.tq: Check the geographical location carefully and reject the swapped-state trap.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: **Bharukachha** = **Bharuch**, Gujarat, west coast.
Statement 2 correct: **Sopara** and **Kalyan** are west-coast ports of **Maharashtra**.
Statement 3 wrong: **Kalyan** is near **Mumbai**; APP wrongly places it in Karnataka.
xa: The Periplus says Kalyan was **destroyed by the Sakas**.
**Vyjayantipura** was another west-coast port.

47.s: Bhavaviveka is associated with which vihara in the Satavahana sphere?
47.x: Bhavaviveka is described as the acharya at the Sriparvatam vihara.
47.tq: Identify the person–institution association without confusing nearby Buddhist centres.
xs: **Bhavaviveka** was acharya at the **Sriparvatam** vihara — option **(3)** is correct (G2 **2019** key).
⚠ Some notes say **Dhanyakataka**; the key says Sriparvatam.
xa: Buddhist viharas grew beside the trade centres.
**Nagarjuna** is linked to **Sriparvata** in Andhra.

47.s: Who described the drain of Roman gold and referred to fine cloth in connection with Indian trade?
o: The anonymous author of the Periplus
47.x: Pliny, writing in Latin in Natural History, referred to the drain of Roman gold and fine cloth. Ptolemy and the Periplus supplied other commercial references.
47.tq: Match the author with both the work and the distinctive commercial observation.
xs: **Pliny** in **Natural History** (Latin) wrote of the **drain of Roman gold** and **fine cloth** — option **(1)** is correct.
The **Periplus** (anonymous Greek) called **Arikamedu** the "market street of the Romans".
xa: The drain: about **12.5 million denarii a year** (some notes say "**5** crore gold coins").
Pliny also gave the Satavahana army: **1,00,000 infantry**.

47.s: The Periplus associated Arikamedu with which description?
o: A centre of Roman gold mines
A royal mint of the Satavahanas
A market street of the Romans
47.x: The anonymous Greek Periplus described Arikamedu as the “market street of the Romans.”
47.tq: Recall the distinctive descriptive phrase linked to the source and site.
xs: The Periplus called **Arikamedu** the "**market street of the Romans**" — option **(4)** is correct.
The Periplus is an **anonymous Greek** text.
xa: Route: **Arikamedu → Red Sea** via **Sri Lanka** and the Arabian Sea.
The Periplus also names **Koddura** as the only east-coast port.

47.s: Which of the following commodities was imported rather than exported in Satavahana overseas trade?
47.x: Camphor from China was an import. Spices, ivory, muslin, pearls and diamonds were listed among exports.
47.tq: Separate exports from imports by identifying the direction of movement.
xs: **Camphor from China** was an **import** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Muslin**, **ivory** and **pearls** were **exports**.
xa: Imports: **wine** (Italy, Arabia), **copper**, **gold and silver coins**, gold (Malaya, Sumatra), **silk and camphor** (China).
Exports: fine textiles/muslin (**Mallaselai**), silk, gems, diamonds, spices, pepper, **Wootz steel**.

47.s: Roman coins associated with Satavahana-period trade have been found at:
47.x: Roman coins have been found at Bhattiprolu and Nagarjunakonda. The gold coin of Constantine found at Kudali Sangameswaram belongs to a later period.
47.tq: Use the archaeological-site pair and avoid confusing a later-period find with Satavahana evidence.
xs: Roman coins have been found at **Bhattiprolu and Nagarjunakonda** — option **(2)** is correct.
The **Constantine** gold coin at **Kudali Sangameswaram** belongs to a **later** period.
xa: Roman gold coins also circulated at **Salihundam**, **Vinukonda**, **Nellore**.
AP angle: Roman coins at **Salihundam, Vinukonda, Nagarjunakonda**.

47.s: Which statement regarding the decline of Satavahana-era Roman trade is correct?
o: Roman trade declined after the Satavahanas.
Roman trade began only after the Satavahanas.
Roman trade flourished after the Satavahanas without interruption.
Roman trade was confined exclusively to inland villages.
47.x: Roman trade declined after the Satavahanas. The claim that it flourished in the post-Satavahana period is incorrect.
47.tq: Reject the reversed chronological comparison between the Satavahana and post-Satavahana periods.
xs: **Roman trade declined after the Satavahanas** — option **(1)** is correct.
It **peaked under** the Satavahanas.
xa: ⚠ "Trade flourished post-Satavahana" is **false** (G2 **2025** A-R: A false, R true).
**Pliny** complained of Rome's gold draining to India.

47.s: Gautamiputra Satakarni’s monetary policy included:
o: Issuing only bilingual coins in Greek and Latin
Replacing all silver coins with gold coins
47.x: Gautamiputra Satakarni restruck the silver coins of Nahapana.
47.tq: Identify the action associated with the ruler and reject absolute monetary claims.
xs: **Gautamiputra** **restruck Nahapana's silver coins** — option **(3)** is correct.
The proof is the **Jogalthambi hoard** — **13,270** coins.
The Satavahanas issued **no gold coins**, and bilingual coins were **Prakrit + Dravidian**, not Greek-Latin.
xa: **Portrait coins** began with **Gautamiputra**.
The **Ujjain symbol** appears on the reverse of coins.

47.s: The legend ‘Siri Chimuka Sata’ is associated with the mint at:
47.x: The Kondapur mint in Medak is associated with the legend ‘Siri Chimuka Sata’.
47.tq: Pair the distinctive legend with its mint location.
xs: The **Kondapur (Medak)** mint bears the legend "**Siri Chimuka Sata**" — option **(1)** is correct.
Kondapur is the Satavahana **mint** named in the sources; the legend, like all coin legends, is in **Prakrit, Brahmi script**.
xa: Technique: **punch-marked** first, then **die-struck**.
Shapes: **round, square, rectangular**.

47.s: Portrait coins in the Satavahana period represent
o: a Gupta innovation copied by the Satavahanas
an indigenous innovation, beginning with Gautamiputra Satakarni
a Roman practice introduced only under Yajna Sri Satakarni
a practice restricted to copper coins of Hala
47.x: Portrait coins are regarded as an indigenous innovation, and their issue began with Gautamiputra Satakarni. Silver portrait coins became common after him.
47.tq: Link the innovation, initiator and subsequent development in one precise association.
xs: **Portrait coins** were an **indigenous innovation**, beginning with **Gautamiputra Satakarni** — option **(2)** is correct (UPSC).
**Silver portrait coins** became common after him.
xa: Later rulers issued **bilingual** silver portrait coins (**Prakrit + Dravidian**).
First portrait coins → **Gautamiputra**; ship-motif coins → Satavahanas.

47.s: Bilingual silver portrait coins of later Satavahana rulers carried which languages on their two sides?
47.x: The bilingual silver portrait coins carried Prakrit on one side and a Dravidian language on the other.
47.tq: Distinguish languages from scripts: Brahmi is the script, whereas Prakrit and a Dravidian language are the linguistic forms.
xs: Bilingual coins carry **Prakrit** on one side and a **Dravidian language** on the other — option **(1)** is correct (G2 **2025** key).
They are **silver portrait coins of later rulers**.
xa: Ordinary legends are in **Prakrit, Brahmi script**.
Common people spoke **Desi Bhasha** (Dravidian).

47.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Satavahana coin legends?
o: They were exclusively in Tamil written in Greek script.
They were in Paisachi written in Roman script.
They were generally in Prakrit written in Brahmi script.
They were exclusively in Sanskrit written in Kharosthi script.
47.x: Satavahana coin legends were generally in Prakrit and written in Brahmi script.
47.tq: Keep language and script separate while identifying the standard form of the legends.
xs: Coin legends were in **Prakrit**, in **Brahmi script** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Paisachi** was the **Brihatkatha's** language, not used on coins.
xa: All Satavahana inscriptions are in **Prakrit-Brahmi**.
Later bilingual coins added a **Dravidian** language.

47.s: The Ujjain symbol appearing on the reverse of Satavahana coins is represented by
o: a circle divided into eight segments
47.x: The Ujjain symbol is described as a cross with four circles and appears on the reverse of Satavahana coins.
47.tq: Translate the visual description into the correct numismatic symbol.
xs: The **Ujjain symbol** is **a cross with four circles** — option **(4)** is correct.
It appears on the **reverse** of Satavahana coins.
xa: Other symbols: **bull, ship, swastika, triratna**.
Motifs: **elephant, horse, lion, camel, chaitya, dharmachakra**.

47.s: Iron coins with a copper coating are associated with
47.x: Iron coins with a copper coating are attributed to the Shalankayanas, not the Satavahanas.
47.tq: Avoid assigning a distinctive coin type to the better-known neighbouring dynasty.
xs: **Iron coins with copper coating** belong to the **Shalankayanas** — option **(4)** is correct.
They are **not Satavahana** coins.
xa: ⚠ Satavahanas: **lead** most common; **no gold coins**.
Potin = **copper-tin-lead** alloy.

47.s: Which statement regarding the issue of ship-motif coins is correct?
o: Every later Satavahana ruler issued ship-motif coins.
No later Satavahana ruler issued ship-motif coins after the rulers associated with the motif.
Ship-motif coins were issued exclusively by the Shalankayanas.
Only Gautamiputra Satakarni issued ship-motif coins.
47.x: The cited account associates ship-motif coins with Vasishthiputra Pulumavi and Yajna Sri Satakarni and states that no later ruler issued them.
47.tq: Watch for the extreme word “every” and distinguish the known issuers from later rulers.
xs: **No later ruler** issued ship coins (G2 **2025**) — option **(2)** is correct.
Ship coins are linked to **Vasishthiputra Pulumavi** (ship-motif) and **Yajna Sri Satakarni** (ship-with-anchor).
Not every later ruler, not the **Shalankayanas**, and not **Gautamiputra**.
xa: Some notes credit **Pulumavi**, others name coins of **both kings**.
Yajna Sri's coins show trade with **Siam, Java, Borneo**.

47.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes the terms used in the exchange account?
o: A silver coin was called a karshapana, while one suvarna was equal to 35 karshapanas.
A gold coin was called a karshapana and a silver coin a suvarna.
A silver coin was called a suvarna, while one karshapana was equal to 35 suvarnas.
Both suvarna and karshapana denoted only copper coins.
47.x: The silver coin was called a karshapana, and one suvarna was equivalent to 35 karshapanas.
47.tq: Discriminate between two similar monetary terms by checking denomination and exchange value.
xs: A silver coin was the **karshapana**, and **1 suvarna = 35 karshapanas** — option **(1)** is correct.
Option (3) reverses the ratio.
xa: Source: the **Rishabhadatta inscription** (**1 gold coin = 35 karshapanas**).
The Satavahanas issued **no gold coins** — gold was **bullion**.
⚠ Some notes list gold **"Suvarnas"** among their coins.

47.s: Who is associated with making Sanskrit the royal language during the Satavahana period?
47.x: Kuntala Satakarni, regarded as the thirteenth Satavahana king, is associated with making Sanskrit the royal language.
47.tq: Match the language policy with the specific ruler rather than with a better-known Satavahana king.
xs: **Kuntala Satakarni** (**13th** king) made **Sanskrit** the royal language — option **(4)** is correct.
**Hala** (**17th**) compiled the Gathasaptasati in **Maharashtri Prakrit**.
xa: The **Katantra** grammar was composed for Kuntala Satakarni so he could learn Sanskrit quickly.
His court had **Gunadhya** and **Sarvavarma**.
**Gunadhya** wrote the **Brihatkatha** in **Paishachi**.

47.s:
With reference to the development of Sanskrit and Telugu in the Deccan, consider the following statements:
1. Sanskrit became prominent under the Ikshvakus.
2. The Junagadh inscription of Rudradaman is regarded as the first complete Sanskrit inscription.
3. ‘Nagabu’ is identified as the first Telugu word in the Amaravati inscription.
4. ‘Vepuru’ occurs in the Myakadoni inscription.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
47.x: All four statements are correct. Sanskrit became prominent under the Ikshvakus; Rudradaman’s Junagadh inscription is the first complete Sanskrit inscription, while Nagabu and Vepuru occur in the Amaravati and Myakadoni inscriptions respectively.
47.tq: Track the ruler, inscription and word-location pairs separately before selecting the combined code.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)**.
Statement 1: **Sanskrit** became prominent under the **Ikshvakus**.
Statement 2: **Rudradaman's Junagadh** is the **first complete Sanskrit inscription**.
Statements 3, 4: "**Nagabu**" is in the **Amaravati** inscription; "**Vepuru**" in **Myakadoni**.
xa: Royal language: **Prakrit**, in **Brahmi**.
Desi words in the **Gathasaptasati**: **atta, addam, potta**.

47.s: Which statement best reflects the social conditions under the Satavahanas?
o: Chaturvarna operated, while Sakas and Yavanas could be absorbed into society.
Caste mobility was impossible under every circumstance.
The Satavahanas abolished Brahmanical social ideology.
Foreign groups were permanently excluded from the social order.
47.x: Chaturvarna operated, and the absorption of Sakas and Yavanas indicates social mobility despite continuing Brahmanical ideology.
47.tq: Reconcile the coexistence of social hierarchy and mobility instead of choosing an absolute claim.
xs: **Chaturvarna** operated, while **Sakas/Yavanas** were **absorbed into society** — option **(1)** is correct.
Gautamiputra's titles show **Brahmanical ideology** amid this **mobility**, so it was not abolished.
xa: Four-varna system: **chaturvarna** (G2 **2008**).
Title **Varnasankarya nirodhaka** = stopper of the mixing of varnas.
Occupational groups: **Gandhikas**, weavers, oil pressers, potters, florists, merchants.

47.s:
Consider the following statements about religious patronage in Satavahana society:
1. Satavahana kings followed Vedic religion, performing sacrifices such as the Ashvamedha.
2. Queens and women donors patronised Buddhism.
3. Gautami Balasri donated a Jain basadi.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
47.x: Statement 1 is correct: the kings followed Vedic religion (Ashvamedha). Statement 2 is correct: queens and women donors supported Buddhism. Statement 3 is wrong: Gautami Balasri donated a Buddhist vihara, not a Jain basadi. So 1 and 2 only (A); B, C and D include the false statement 3.
47.tq: Kings Vedic, queens Buddhist - Gautami Balasri's gift was a vihara.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: kings followed **Vedic religion** (**Ashvamedha**).
Statement 2 correct: **queens and women donors** patronised **Buddhism**.
Statement 3 wrong: **Gautami Balasri** donated a **vihara**, not a Jain basadi.
xa: Women made independent donations at **Bharhut, Sanchi and Amaravati**.
⚠ "Women were looked down upon" is an incorrect option (G2 **2008**).

47.s: Gautamiputra Satakarni described himself by which pair of expressions?
47.x: Gautamiputra Satakarni called himself Ekabrahmana and Varnasankarya nirodhaka, the stopper of the mixing of varnas.
47.tq: Recall the exact paired royal epithets rather than their general meaning alone.
xs: Gautamiputra called himself **Ekabrahmana** and **Varnasankarya nirodhaka** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Maharashtrika** and **Vishayapati** were administrative heads; **Sarthavaha** and **Gandhika** were occupational groups.
xa: Varnasankarya nirodhaka = **stopper of the mixing of varnas**.
⚠ **Kavivatsala** = **Hala**; **Trisamudradhipati** = **Yajna Sri**.
**Matronymics** began with Gautamiputra.

47.s:
Which of the following provides evidence that women held a respected position in Satavahana society?
1. Naganika and Gautami Balasri issued inscriptions.
2. Kings used matronymics.
3. Women were completely excluded from religious donations.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
47.x: Naganika and Gautami Balasri issued inscriptions, and the use of matronymics indicates the social importance of maternal identity. Women were not excluded from donations, so statement 3 is false.
47.tq: Reject the absolute exclusion statement and retain the two positive pieces of evidence.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(3)**.
Statement 1 correct: **Naganika** and **Gautami Balasri** issued inscriptions.
Statement 2 correct: kings used **matronymics**.
Statement 3 wrong: women made **independent donations** at **Bharhut, Sanchi and Amaravati**.
xa: Women poets contributed to the **Gathasaptasati**.
**Queens and women donors** patronised **Buddhism**.

47.s: Women made independent donations without naming husbands or fathers at which group of sites?
47.x: Independent donations by women, without naming husbands or fathers, are recorded at Bharhut, Sanchi and Amaravati.
47.tq: Recall the complete site group rather than an individual location.
xs: Women's independent donations were made at **Bharhut, Sanchi and Amaravati** — option **(1)** is correct.
They did so **without naming husbands or fathers**.
xa: **Gautami Balasri** donated a **vihara**.
Kings followed **Vedic religion** (Ashvamedha), while queens patronised **Buddhism**.
Some women were **artisans or merchants**.

47.s:
Which of the following statements about women in the Satavahana period is correct?
1. Some women worked as artisans or merchants.
2. Women poets contributed to the Gathasaptasati.
3. The Kamasutra records forced labour called vetti performed by women.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
47.x: The evidence includes women artisans and merchants, women poets in the Gathasaptasati, and the Kamasutra's reference to vetti or forced labour performed by women.
47.tq: Combine social, literary and negative evidence instead of treating the status as uniformly positive.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
Statement 1: some women were **artisans or merchants**.
Statement 2: **women poets** contributed to the **Gathasaptasati**.
Statement 3: the **Kamasutra** records **forced labour (vetti)** by women — the negative side.
xa: Women poets: **Anulakshmi, Anupalabdha, Reva (Revati), Madhavi**.
Villagers in general owed **vetti** (forced labour).

47.s:
Consider the following statements about Satavahana-associated works:
1. Brihatkatha was written by Gunadhya in Paishachi Prakrit.
2. Katantra was a Sanskrit grammar associated with Sarvavarma.
3. Lilavati Parinayam was written by Kutuhala in Prakrit.
4. Harivijaya was written by Sarvasena in Prakrit.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
47.x: All four statements are correct. Brihatkatha is associated with Gunadhya, Katantra with Sarvavarma, Lilavati Parinayam with Kutuhala, and Harivijaya with Sarvasena.
47.tq: Verify each work through its author–language combination instead of relying on a single familiar pairing.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**Brihatkatha** — **Gunadhya**, **Paishachi** Prakrit; **Katantra** — **Sarvavarma**, Sanskrit grammar.
**Lilavati Parinayam** — **Kutuhala**, Prakrit; **Harivijaya** — **Sarvasena**, Prakrit.
xa: Lilavati Parinayam is in **Maharashtri Prakrit**.
Katantra was composed in **Kuntala Satakarni's** time.
**Kamasutra, Nyayabhashya** — **Vatsyayana**.

47.s:
Brihatkatha served as the base for which of the following works?
1. Kathasaritsagara
2. Brihatkatha Manjari
3. Lilavati Parinayam
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
47.x: Brihatkatha formed the basis of Kathasaritsagara by Somadeva Suri and Brihatkatha Manjari by Kshemendra. Lilavati Parinayam is a separate work associated with Kutuhala.
47.tq: Separate derivative works from an unrelated literary title.
xs: Brihatkatha was the base of **Kathasaritsagara** and **Brihatkatha Manjari** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Kathasaritsagara** is by **Somadeva Suri**; **Brihatkatha Manjari** by **Kshemendra**.
**Lilavati Parinayam** is a separate work by **Kutuhala**.
xa: **Brihatkatha Shloka Sangraha** — **Buddhasvami**.
Sanskrit translation — **Durvinita** (Ganga).

47.s:
Consider the following statements about works of the Satavahana age and their authors:
1. Samayasara is a Jain philosophical work of Kundakundacharya.
2. Suhrullekha and Ratnavali are works of Acharya Nagarjuna.
3. Kathasaritsagara was written by Kshemendra.
4. Kamasutra and Nyayabhashya are associated with Vatsyayana.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
47.x: Statement 1 is correct: Samayasara is Kundakundacharya's Jain treatise. Statement 2 is correct: Suhrullekha and Ratnavali are Nagarjuna's. Statement 3 is wrong: Kathasaritsagara is by Somadeva Suri; Kshemendra wrote Brihatkatha Manjari. Statement 4 is correct. So 1, 2 and 4 only (A); B, C and D all include the false statement 3.
47.tq: Kathasaritsagara = Somadeva; Kshemendra = Brihatkatha Manjari - both retell Gunadhya.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 4** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: **Samayasara** is **Kundakundacharya's** Jain treatise.
Statement 2 correct: **Suhrullekha** and **Ratnavali** are by **Acharya Nagarjuna**.
Statement 3 wrong: **Kathasaritsagara** is by **Somadeva Suri**; **Kshemendra** wrote **Brihatkatha Manjari**.
Statement 4 correct: **Kamasutra** and **Nyayabhashya** — **Vatsyayana**.
xa: **Yogasara** — **Kundakundacharya** (G2 **2017** key).
**Prajnaparamita** — traditionally attributed to **Nagarjuna**.

47.s: As per the APPSC Group 2 (2017) key, the Yogasara is attributed to:
47.x: The G2 2017 key attributes the Yogasara to Kundakundacharya, who also wrote the Jain Samayasara. Some sources name Nagarjuna (author of Suhrullekha and Ratnavali) - the trap. Gunadhya wrote the Brihatkatha and Vatsyayana the Kamasutra.
47.tq: Yogasara & Samayasara = Kundakundacharya (APPSC key).
xs: The G2 **2017** key gives **Yogasara** to **Kundakundacharya** — option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ Some notes say **Nagarjuna**, who wrote **Suhrullekha** and **Ratnavali**.
**Gunadhya** wrote the **Brihatkatha**; **Vatsyayana** the **Kamasutra**.
xa: Kundakundacharya also wrote the **Samayasara**, a Jain philosophical work.
Nagarjuna's works are in **Sanskrit**.

47.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Gathasaptasati?
o: A Paisachi grammar written in the Kuntala Satakarni period
A collection of Buddhist verses composed in Brahmi script
An anthology of 700 Maharashtri Prakrit verses dealing mainly with love, rural life and nature
A Sanskrit treatise on Jain philosophy containing 700 chapters
47.x: Gathasaptasati, or Sattasai, is an anthology of 700 gathas in Maharashtri Prakrit, dealing chiefly with love, rural life and nature.
47.tq: Identify the work through its distinctive combination of number, language and subject matter.
xs: The Gathasaptasati is an anthology of **700 Maharashtri Prakrit** gathas on **love, rural life and nature** — option **(3)** is correct.
The **Katantra** is a Sanskrit grammar; **Samayasara** a Jain treatise.
xa: It opens with a **prayer to Shiva**.
It is the **most important literary source** for Satavahana society.
⚠ **700** gathas = Gathasaptasati; **7,000** verses in **7** stories = Brihatkatha.

47.s:
Consider the following statements about Gathasaptasati:
1. It is regarded as an important literary source for Satavahana society.
2. It is a reliable source for the political history of the early Satavahanas.
3. It contains descriptions of rural life and nature.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
47.x: Gathasaptasati is an important source for Satavahana social life and describes rural life and nature. It is not considered a source for early Satavahana political history.
47.tq: Find the excluded use of a source; the political-history statement reverses the source’s character.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(3)**.
Statement 1 correct: it is the **most important literary source for Satavahana society**.
Statement 2 wrong: it is **not** a source for **early Satavahana political history** (APPSC **2017**).
Statement 3 correct: it describes **rural life and nature**.
xa: It has **700 Prakrit gathas**, mainly **love and romance** (G2 **2025**).
It is the first work covering all the **Navarasas**.

47.s:
Which of the following women are associated with contributions to Gathasaptasati?
1. Anulakshmi
2. Anupalabdha
3. Reva
4. Madhavi
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
47.x: Anulakshmi, Anupalabdha, Reva or Revati, and Madhavi are identified as women contributors to Gathasaptasati.
47.tq: Cover the complete membership of a named list rather than relying on one familiar name.
xs: All four — **Anulakshmi, Anupalabdha, Reva (Revati), Madhavi** — are women contributors — option **(4)**.
This answers "which text has contributions by women" (APPSC **2017** key).
xa: Women poets in the Gathasaptasati are part of the evidence that women were **respected**.
It was compiled by **Hala** in **Maharashtri Prakrit**.

47.s: Which one of the following is NOT associated with the social picture presented in Gathasaptasati?
o: Compulsory military training for all women
47.x: Gathasaptasati refers to sati, the absence of child marriage and the plight of wives of seafaring merchants. It does not mention compulsory military training for all women.
47.tq: Locate the outsider by comparing each option with the social themes attributed to the text.
xs: **Compulsory military training for all women** is not in the Gathasaptasati — option **(3)** is the answer.
It does show **Sati**, **absence of child marriage** and the plight of wives of **seafaring merchants**.
xa: It also shows **prostitution** and the **hanging of criminals**.
**Brundagana** (choral singing) and **house-wall paintings**.
Rural life, **sugar and jaggery**.

47.s:
Consider the following statements about the cultural information found in Gathasaptasati:
1. It refers to sugar and jaggery.
2. It mentions group dances and choral singing called Brundagana.
3. It provides evidence of house-wall paintings.
4. It refers to the hanging of criminals.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
47.x: All four features—sugar and jaggery, Brundagana, house-wall paintings and hanging of criminals—are included in the social picture associated with Gathasaptasati.
47.tq: Treat each social detail as an independent statement and select the complete combination.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)**.
It mentions **sugar and jaggery** and **Brundagana** (choral singing) with couple/choir dances.
It shows **house-wall paintings** and the **hanging of criminals**.
xa: Other items: **Sati**, **absence of child marriage**, prostitution.
Plight of wives of **seafaring merchants**.

47.s: Which of the following sets contains only early Telugu or Desi words associated with Gathasaptasati?
47.x: Atta, Addam, Potta and Pilla are among the early Telugu words associated with Gathasaptasati. Other recorded examples include Padi, Pandi, Ammi and Tuppu.
47.tq: Recognise the linguistic list by separating vernacular words from technical historical terms.
xs: **Atta, Addam, Potta, Pilla** are early Telugu (Desi) words — option **(4)** is correct.
The other sets are **Buddhist** or **administrative** terms.
xa: Fuller list: **Atta, Addam, Potta, Padi, Pandi, Pilla, Ammi, Tuppu**.
They are the **earliest traces of Telugu**.
First Telugu word: **"Nagabu"** (Amaravati); **"Vepuru"** in Myakadoni.

47.s: Gathasaptasati is described as the first literary work to deal with
47.x: Gathasaptasati is described as the first literary work covering all the Navarasas.
47.tq: Match the work with its distinctive literary classification rather than its language alone.
xs: The Gathasaptasati is the first literary work covering all **Navarasas** — option **(3)** is correct.
It has **700** Prakrit gathas, mainly **love and romance**.
xa: It opens with a **prayer to Shiva**.
Women contributors: **Anulakshmi, Anupalabdha, Reva, Madhavi**.

47.s:
Consider the following statements about Hala:
1. He compiled the Gathasaptasati in Maharashtri Prakrit and honoured the poets Kumarila and Sripalita.
2. He made Sanskrit the royal language of the Satavahanas.
3. He bore the title Kavivatsala.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
47.x: Statement 3 is correct: Hala, the 17th king, was called Kavivatsala. Statement 1 is correct: he compiled the Gathasaptasati in Maharashtri Prakrit and honoured Kumarila and Sripalita; his reign was the golden age of Prakrit. Statement 2 is wrong: Kuntala Satakarni (13th king) made Sanskrit the royal language. So '1 and 3 only'.
47.tq: Kavivatsala = Hala; Ekabrahmana = Gautamiputra; Trisamudradhipati = Yajna Sri.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Hala** compiled the **Gathasaptasati** in **Maharashtri Prakrit** and honoured **Kumarila and Sripalita**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Kuntala Satakarni** (**13th king**) made **Sanskrit** the royal language.
Statement 3 is correct: Hala (**17th king**) bore the title **Kavivatsala** (G2 **2008**).
xa: Hala's reign = **golden age of Prakrit**.
Hala married Sinhala princess **Lilavati** at the **Bhimeswara temple, Draksharamam** — told in **Lilavati Parinayam** (Kutuhala).
⚠ **Kavivatsala** = **Hala**; **Ekabrahmana** = **Gautamiputra**; **Trisamudradhipati** = **Yajna Sri**.

47.s: Lilavati Parinayam, written by Kutuhala in Prakrit, deals primarily with which event?
o: The conquest of Kalyan by the Sakas
The composition of Katantra for Kuntala Satakarni
The marriage of Hala and Lilavati at Draksharamam
The quarrel between Gunadhya and Sarvavarma at the royal court
