o: Pala sculpture was mainly made of marble and ivory, while manuscripts were written on birch bark only.
Pala art included bronze and black-stone sculpture, along with illustrated palm-leaf Buddhist manuscripts.
Pala artists worked exclusively in gold and produced only royal genealogies.
Pala sculpture was confined to terracotta and did not include stone images.
69.x: Pala art is known for bronze and black-stone or basalt sculpture and illustrated Buddhist manuscripts written on palm leaves.
69.tq: Use the materials-based distinction to reject exclusive and reversed claims.
xs: Pala art: **bronze** and **black-stone (basalt)** sculpture plus **palm-leaf illustrated Buddhist manuscripts** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Terracotta** was also used — at **Somapura** and on Vikramashila's walls — so Pala art was not confined to it.
xa: Artists: **Dhiman** and his son **Vitapala** (per **Taranatha**).
**Pala-style bronzes** reached Southeast Asia.
Somapura: grand scale, rich **terracotta** ornamentation.

69.s: Dhiman and Vitapala, mentioned in connection with Pala art, were:
o: Authors of Ramacharita and Buddhist texts
Artists, with Vitapala being the son of Dhiman
Rulers of Magadha and Bengal respectively
69.x: Dhiman and his son Vitapala were noted artists associated with Pala art, as recorded by Taranatha.
69.tq: Avoid the person–profession and father–son identity trap.
xs: **Dhiman** and his son **Vitapala** were Pala **artists** — option **(3)** is correct.
They are known from **Taranatha**.
**Ramacharita** is by **Sandhyakar Nandi**, not these two.
xa: Pala sculpture: **bronze** and black-stone (**basalt**).
Manuscripts: **palm-leaf illustrated** Buddhist manuscripts.
Pala-style bronzes in **Southeast Asia** show maritime exchange.

69.s: Who wrote Ramacharita, a work dealing with Ramapala and the Kaivarta peasant revolt?
69.x: Ramacharita was written by Sandhyakar Nandi and deals with Ramapala and the Kaivarta peasant revolt.
69.tq: Match the literary work with its author and subject.
xs: **Sandhyakar Nandi** wrote **Ramacharita** — option **(3)** is correct.
It deals with **Ramapala** and the **Kaivarta** peasant revolt.
**Jayadeva** was **Lakshmanasena**'s poet; **Taranatha** recorded the artists **Dhiman** and **Vitapala**.
xa: Ramapala (c. **1072-1126**) was the last strong Pala.
Ramapala founded **Jagaddala**.
**Atisha Dipankara** of Vikramashila revived Buddhism in Tibet.

69.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes literary activity under the Palas?
o: Buddhist texts were compiled at Nalanda under Dharmapala, and Jagaddala translated books into Tibetan.
Ramacharita was composed at Jagaddala by Jayadeva and dealt with Southeast Asian trade.
Jagaddala was devoted exclusively to military training and produced no translations.
Nalanda translated all Pala records into Sanskrit under Ramapala.
69.x: Buddhist texts were compiled at Nalanda under Dharmapala, while Jagaddala became associated with translating books into Tibetan.
69.tq: Compare the distinct literary functions of Nalanda and Jagaddala.
xs: Buddhist texts were compiled at **Nalanda under Dharmapala**, and **Jagaddala** translated books into **Tibetan** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Ramacharita** is by **Sandhyakar Nandi** on Ramapala's Kaivarta revolt — not by Jayadeva.
xa: **Sakya Sri Bhadra** of Jagaddala took **Tantric Buddhism** to Tibet.
**Dharmapala's seal** was found at Nalanda.
Jagaddala was sacked in the early **13th c.**

69.s: Which of the following statements about Andhra's connection with Nalanda is correct?
o: Andhra's Dharmakirti founded Vikramashila during the reign of Gopala.
Dharmakirti was the Pala king who granted five villages to Balaputradeva.
Dharmakirti translated the Ramacharita into Tibetan at Jagaddala.
Andhra's Dharmakirti taught at Nalanda and had studied under Dharmapala of Kanchi, who was the head of Nalanda.
69.x: Andhra's Dharmakirti taught at Nalanda and studied under the Nalanda head Dharmapala of Kanchi. This Dharmapala should not be confused with the Pala ruler Dharmapala.
69.tq: Separate two persons with the same name by institution and regional identity.
xs: Andhra's **Dharmakirti** taught at **Nalanda** and studied under its head **Dharmapala of Kanchi** — option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ This Dharmapala of Kanchi is **not the Pala king**.
**Vikramashila** was founded by king **Dharmapala**; the **five villages** were granted by **Devapala**.
xa: Dharmapala of Kanchipuram was an **earlier head** of Nalanda; **Shilabhadra** headed it in Harsha's time.
**Ramacharita** is by **Sandhyakar Nandi**.

69.s:
Consider the following statements about Nalanda University:
I. It was located in Bihar.
II. It was founded in the 5th century AD.
III. It had a Gupta foundation.
IV. It was a major Buddhist centre of learning.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
69.x: All four are correct: Nalanda in Bihar was founded in the 5th century AD by the Gupta ruler Kumaragupta I and became a major Buddhist centre of learning.
69.tq: Check each statement separately.
n: Nalanda University was located in Bihar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 60-64]
Nalanda University was founded in the 5th century AD. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 60-64]
Nalanda University had a Gupta foundation. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 60-64]
Nalanda University was a major Buddhist centre of learning. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 60-64]
xs: **All four** statements are correct — option **(3) I, II, III and IV**.
I and III: Nalanda was **located** in **Bihar** and was a **Gupta foundation**, founded by **Kumaragupta I**.
II and IV: it was founded in the **5th century AD** and became a **major Buddhist centre** of **higher learning**.
xa: It **attracted students** from **China, Tibet, Greece, Persia** and other regions.
**Nava Nalanda Mahavihara** — **Bhikshu Jagadish Kashyap**; foundation stone laid on **20 November 1951**.
⚠ **Nalanda** is Gupta-founded; the other four mahaviharas are **Pala** foundations.
**Vikramashila** was founded by **Dharmapala**; **Odantapuri** by **Gopala**.

70.s: The term ‘Pratihara’ is traditionally interpreted as meaning:
70.x: Pratihara means door-keeper. The dynasty claimed descent from Lakshmana, who was regarded as Rama's door-keeper brother.
70.tq: Distinguish the literal meaning of the dynastic name from its origin legend.
xs: "Pratihara" means **door-keeper** — option **(1)** is correct.
The dynasty claimed descent from **Lakshmana**, Rama's door-keeper brother.
"Fire-born" refers to the separate **Agnikula legend** of **Mount Abu**.
xa: "**Gurjara**" is read as a tribe/people or as the region **Gurjaratra**.
Capitals: **Bhinmal → Ujjain/Avanti → Kannauj (Mahodaya)**.
Founder **Nagabhata I** (c. **730-760**) resisted the Arabs.

70.s: According to the Agnikula legend in Prithviraj Raso, which group of dynasties was born from the fire-pit at Mount Abu?
70.x: The Agnikula legend associates the Pratiharas, Chaulukyas, Paramaras and Chauhans with birth from the fire-pit at Mount Abu.
70.tq: Recall the complete legendary group rather than a partial pair.
xs: The Agnikula clans are the **Pratiharas, Chaulukyas, Paramaras and Chauhans** — option **(1)** is correct.
The legend, from **Prithviraj Raso**, has them born from the fire-pit at **Mount Abu**.
xa: **Chauhans**, **Paramaras** and **Chaulukyas** later broke away from the Pratiharas as feudatories.
"Pratihara" = **door-keeper**.
Pratihara temple style peaked at **Khajuraho**.

70.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Kannauj around 916 CE — Mahipala I defeated Indra III
Bundelkhand campaign — Govinda III defeated Nagabhata II
Early ninth-century Kannauj — Nagabhata II defeated Chakrayudha
70.x: Around 916 CE, Indra III defeated Mahipala I and sacked Kannauj. The other three pairs correctly identify the campaigns and victors.
70.tq: Find the reversed victor–defeated pair in the battle table.
xs: "**Mahipala I** defeated **Indra III**" is wrong — option **(1)** is the answer.
Around **916**, **Indra III** sacked Kannauj, defeating Mahipala I.
**Govinda III** beat **Nagabhata II** (Bundelkhand); Nagabhata II ousted **Chakrayudha** and beat **Dharmapala** near **Monghyr**.
xa: **Mahmud of Ghazni** attacked Kannauj in **1018**.
⚠ **Vatsaraja** lost to Dhruva; **Nagabhata II** to Govinda III.
Rajashekhara served **Mahipala I** as well as Mahendrapala I.

70.s: Who among the following is regarded as the founder of the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty and is known for resisting Arab expansion?
70.x: Nagabhata I is regarded as the founder of the dynasty and successfully resisted Arab expansion.
70.tq: Use the ruler–achievement association to identify the correct answer.
xs: **Nagabhata I** (c. **730-760**) was the founder and **resisted the Arabs** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Nagabhata II** made Kannauj capital; **Vatsaraja** began the tripartite struggle; **Mihira Bhoja** was the zenith.
xa: The Pratiharas kept Arab rule confined to **Sindh**.
⚠ Nagabhata I = founder, Arabs; Nagabhata II = Kannauj capital.
Sulaiman praised Pratihara cavalry as the **best in India**.

70.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the achievement of Vatsaraja?
o: He made Kannauj the capital after defeating Chakrayudha.
He was responsible for the sack of Kannauj by Indra III.
He founded the dynasty by defeating the Arabs in Sindh.
He took Kannauj, defeated Dharmapala and was later defeated by Dhruva.
70.x: Vatsaraja took Kannauj and defeated Dharmapala, but was later defeated by the Rashtrakuta ruler Dhruva, marking the beginning of the tripartite struggle.
70.tq: Match the ruler with the complete sequence of his major achievements.
xs: **Vatsaraja** took Kannauj, beat **Dharmapala** and was then defeated by **Dhruva** — option **(4)** is correct.
That clash marked the **start of the tripartite struggle**.
Ousting **Chakrayudha** was **Nagabhata II**'s; the sack by **Indra III** came under **Mahipala I**; Arab resistance was **Nagabhata I**'s.
xa: Vatsaraja ruled c. **780-800**.
Some notes say he made Kannauj capital; others say he only conquered it.

70.s:
Consider the following statements about Nagabhata II:
1. He ousted Chakrayudha.
2. He defeated Dharmapala near Monghyr.
3. He was defeated by Govinda III.
4. He made Kannauj his capital.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
70.x: All four are correct: Nagabhata II ousted Chakrayudha, beat Dharmapala near Monghyr, was himself defeated by Rashtrakuta Govinda III, and made Kannauj the Pratihara capital. Hence D.
70.tq: Check each ruler-specific achievement separately before selecting the coded combination.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Nagabhata II** ousted **Chakrayudha** and beat **Dharmapala** near **Monghyr**.
He was defeated by **Govinda III** and made **Kannauj** the capital.
xa: Govinda III's defeat of him came in a **Bundelkhand** campaign.
His grandson **Mihira Bhoja** was the son of **Ramabhadra**.
The **Gwalior prashasti** records his victories.

70.s: Mahendrapala I was known by which of the following titles?
70.x: Mahendrapala I is described as the “Maharajadhiraja of Aryavarta.”
70.tq: Discriminate between titles belonging to different rulers.
xs: **Mahendrapala I** was "**Maharajadhiraja of Aryavarta**" — option **(3)** is correct.
**Adivaraha** was **Mihira Bhoja**'s title, not Mahendrapala's.
xa: Mahendrapala I ruled c. **890-910**.
He patronised the poet **Rajashekhara**.
With Bhoja he held Kannauj for decades.

70.s: Mihira Bhoja was the grandson of Nagabhata II because he was the son of:
70.x: Mihira Bhoja was the son of Ramabhadra and therefore the grandson of Nagabhata II.
70.tq: Use the correct generational relationship to avoid the son-versus-grandson trap.
xs: Mihira Bhoja was the son of **Ramabhadra**, so the **grandson of Nagabhata II** — option **(4)** is correct.
He was **not** Nagabhata II's son (CGPSC 2022).
xa: Bhoja's capital: **Kannauj (Mahodaya)**.
Title **Adivaraha** — a devotee of Vishnu.
Bhoja ruled c. **836-890**, the dynasty's zenith.

70.s: Which title of Mihira Bhoja reflects his devotion to Vishnu and also appears as a legend on his coins?
70.x: Mihira Bhoja bore the title Adivaraha, reflecting his devotion to Vishnu; Adivaraha also appeared on his coins.
70.tq: Match the ruler with the title and its numismatic association.
xs: **Adivaraha** reflects Bhoja's devotion to Vishnu and appears on his coins — option **(3)** is correct (UPPSC 2017).
**Juzr** was Sulaiman's name for him; **Aryavarta** is in Mahendrapala I's title; **Mahodaya** = Kannauj.
xa: Al-Masudi called him "**Baura**".
Bhoja built the **Teli-ka-Mandir**, Gwalior.

70.s:
Consider the following statements about the career of Mihira Bhoja:
1. He suffered early defeats at the hands of the Palas, Rashtrakutas and Kalachuris, but later made a comeback.
2. His expansion was checked by Sankaravarman of Kashmir and the Rashtrakuta Krishna II.
3. His expansion was checked by the Chola ruler Rajendra Chola.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
70.x: Statement 1 is correct: early defeats by Palas, Rashtrakutas and Kalachuris were followed by a comeback. Statement 2 is correct: Sankaravarman of Kashmir, Rashtrakuta Krishna II and Pala Devapala checked him. Statement 3 is wrong: Rajendra Chola defeated the Pala Mahipala I, not Mihira Bhoja. Hence B; A misses statement 2, C and D include statement 3.
70.tq: Bhoja's checkers: Kashmir (Sankaravarman), Rashtrakuta (Krishna II), Pala (Devapala) - no southern Chola.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: early defeats by **Palas, Rashtrakutas, Kalachuris**, then a **comeback** — correct.
Statement 2: checked by **Sankaravarman of Kashmir** and Rashtrakuta **Krishna II** — correct.
Statement 3: the notes name **Pala Devapala** as the third check, not **Rajendra Chola** — wrong.
xa: Bhoja's title: **Adivaraha**.
Sulaiman called him "**Juzr**".

70.s: Who built the Teli-ka-Mandir at Gwalior according to the historical association given below?
70.x: The Teli-ka-Mandir at Gwalior is associated with Mihira Bhoja.
70.tq: Match the monument with its associated ruler.
xs: **Mihira Bhoja** built the **Teli-ka-Mandir, Gwalior** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Indra III** was a Rashtrakuta raider; **Mahendrapala I** patronised Rajashekhara; **Nagabhata I** was the founder.
xa: Bhoja's capital: **Kannauj (Mahodaya)**.
Title: **Adivaraha**, a Vishnu devotee.
Pratihara temple style peaked at **Khajuraho**.

70.s:
Consider the following statements about Arab accounts of Mihira Bhoja:
1. Sulaiman called him 'Juzr' or 'Al-Juzr'.
2. Al-Masudi called him 'Adivaraha'.
3. Sulaiman praised his army, wealth and security and regarded his cavalry as the best in India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
70.x: Statement 1 is correct: Sulaiman (mid-9th century) called him Juzr/Al-Juzr. Statement 2 is wrong: Al-Masudi called him 'Baura'; Adivaraha was Bhoja's own title on his coins. Statement 3 is correct: Sulaiman praised his army, wealth, security and cavalry. Hence C; A, B and D include statement 2.
70.tq: Sulaiman - Juzr; Al-Masudi - Baura; Adivaraha is Bhoja's own Vaishnava title.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(3) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1: **Sulaiman** called him "**Juzr**" / "Al-Juzr" — correct.
Statement 2: **Al-Masudi** called him "**Baura**"; **Adivaraha** was Bhoja's own title — wrong.
Statement 3: Sulaiman praised his army, wealth, security and **best cavalry in India** — correct.
xa: Sulaiman came in the mid-**9th c.**, in **Bhoja I**'s reign (RPSC 2023).
Sulaiman named **Amoghavarsha** one of the four great kings of the world.

70.s: Which of the following works was NOT written by Rajashekhara?
70.x: Prabandhachintamani was written by Merutunga, whereas Kavyamimamsa, Karpuramanjari and Viddhasalabhanjika were works of Rajashekhara.
70.tq: Use the author–work distinction to identify the wrongly attributed work.
xs: **Prabandhachintamani** is not Rajashekhara's — it is by **Merutunga** — option **(3)** is the answer (MPPSC 2025).
Rajashekhara wrote **Kavyamimamsa**, **Karpuramanjari** and **Viddhasalabhanjika**.
xa: **Kavyamimamsa** is on poetics; **Karpuramanjari** is a **Prakrit play**.
Rajashekhara was court poet of **Mahendrapala I** (and **Mahipala I**).

70.s: Rajashekhara was associated with the courts of which of the following rulers?
70.x: Rajashekhara was the court poet of Mahendrapala I and was also associated with the court of Mahipala I.
70.tq: Match the court poet with both of his recorded patrons.
xs: Rajashekhara served **Mahendrapala I** and **Mahipala I** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Indra III** and **Krishna II** were Rashtrakutas, not his patrons.
xa: Works: **Kavyamimamsa**, **Karpuramanjari**, **Viddhasalabhanjika**.
Mahendrapala I ruled c. **890-910**.
Kannauj was sacked by **Indra III** under Mahipala I.

70.s:
Which of the following developments contributed to the decline of the Gurjara-Pratiharas?
1. The raid on Kannauj by Rashtrakuta Indra III.
2. The attack on Kannauj by Mahmud of Ghazni in 1018.
3. The secession of feudatories such as the Chandelas, Chauhans, Paramaras and Chaulukyas.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
70.x: All three developments weakened the Pratihara power: Indra III raided Kannauj, Mahmud of Ghazni attacked it in 1018, and several feudatories became independent.
70.tq: Combine military raids and political fragmentation when assessing dynastic decline.
xs: All three caused the decline — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Indra III**'s raid on Kannauj and **Mahmud of Ghazni**'s attack in **1018**.
Feudatories broke away: **Chandelas**, **Chauhans**, **Paramaras**, **Chaulukyas**.
xa: The **Chandelas** were based at **Khajuraho**.
Pratihara temple style peaked at **Khajuraho** (UNESCO site).
Indra III's sack is dated c. **916**.

70.s: The Pratihara temple style is stated to have reached its peak at:
70.x: The Pratihara temple style is stated to have peaked at Khajuraho, built by the Chandelas (originally Pratihara feudatories) and now a UNESCO site.
70.tq: Match the architectural style with its principal associated location.
xs: Pratihara temple style peaked at **Khajuraho** — option **(1)** is correct.
Khajuraho is the **Chandela** base and a **UNESCO site**.
**Gwalior** has Bhoja's **Teli-ka-Mandir**; **Bhinmal** was the early capital.
xa: The Chandelas broke away as Pratihara **feudatories**.
Others that broke away: **Chauhans**, **Paramaras**, **Chaulukyas**.

70.s: Which one of the following best expresses the historical significance of the Gurjara-Pratiharas in relation to Arab expansion?
o: They extended Arab rule from Sindh to Kannauj.
They supported Muhammad bin Qasim's conquest of northern India.
They were the main power that kept Arab rule confined to Sindh.
They replaced the Arab administration of Multan with Pala rule.
70.x: The Gurjara-Pratiharas were the principal power that helped keep Arab rule confined to Sindh.
70.tq: Select the broad significance statement that follows from the resistance episodes.
xs: The Pratiharas were the **main power that kept Arab rule confined to Sindh** — option **(3)** is correct.
Founder **Nagabhata I** (c. **730-760**) **resisted the Arabs**.
xa: Sulaiman praised Pratihara **cavalry** as the best in India.
He also praised their **army, wealth and security**.
Hiuen Tsang had described the **Sun temple of Multan**.

70.s: Which one of the following comparisons is correct?
o: Sulaiman identified Mahendrapala as one of the four great kings of the world and criticised the Pratiharas.
Sulaiman praised Amoghavarsha's cavalry as the best in India, while Mihira Bhoja was ignored.
Sulaiman described the Palas as the only great power and denied the importance of the Rashtrakutas.
Sulaiman praised Pratihara cavalry, while Amoghavarsha was named one of the four great kings of the world.
70.x: Sulaiman praised the Pratihara cavalry, while he named Amoghavarsha of the Rashtrakutas as one of the four great kings of the world.
70.tq: Keep the two separate observations in the comparison attached to the correct ruler and dynasty.
xs: Sulaiman **praised Pratihara cavalry**, but named **Amoghavarsha** one of the **four great kings of the world** — option **(4)** is correct.
He called Bhoja "**Juzr**" and praised his army — Bhoja was not ignored.
xa: Sulaiman came in the mid-**9th c.**, in **Bhoja I**'s reign.
Al-Masudi called Bhoja "**Baura**".
⚠ **Juzr** = Sulaiman's name; **Baura** = Al-Masudi's.

70.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
 a. Pratihara first capital
 b. Pratihara later capital
 c. Mihir Bhoja's title
 d. Mihir Bhoja's religion

List-II
 i. Vaishnavism
 ii. Adivaraha / Prabhasa
 iii. Ujjain
 iv. Kannauj
70.x: The Pratiharas first ruled from Ujjain and later from Kannauj; Mihir Bhoja took the titles Adivaraha and Prabhasa and followed Vaishnavism, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
70.tq: Recall each Pratihara capital and Mihir Bhoja's titles.
n: Ujjain was the first capital of the Pratiharas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144 · pp 250-252]
Kannauj was the later capital of the Pratiharas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144 · pp 250-252]
Mihir Bhoja was known by the title Adivaraha. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144 · pp 250-252]
Mihir Bhoja was known by the title Prabhasa. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144 · pp 250-252]
Mihir Bhoja followed Vaishnavism. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144 · pp 250-252]
Mihir Bhoja made Kannauj his capital. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144 · pp 250-252]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i** — option **(2)**.
Pratihara **first capital** → **Ujjain**; **later capital** → **Kannauj**.
**Mihir Bhoja's titles** → **Adivaraha / Prabhasa**; his religion → **Vaishnavism**.
xa: The dynasty was **founded** by **Nagabhata I**.
⚠ Other notes give an earlier capital at **Bhinmal** (Rajasthan), before Ujjain.
"Pratihara" = door-keeper; they claimed descent from **Lakshmana**.
Mihira Bhoja was the **grandson of Nagabhata II** (son of **Ramabhadra**).

70.s:
Arrange the following Pratihara rulers in the correct chronological order:
A. Mahendrapala I
B. Mahipala
C. Vatsaraja
D. Nagabhata II
70.x: The Pratihara order is Vatsaraja, Nagabhata II, Mihir Bhoja, Mahendrapala I and Mahipala. The four listed therefore run C, D, A, B.
70.tq: Arrange the Pratihara rulers in order of succession.
n: Vatsaraja preceded Nagabhata II in the Pratihara chronology. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144 · pp 250-252]
Nagabhata II preceded Mahendrapala I in the Pratihara chronology. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144 · pp 250-252]
Mahendrapala I preceded Mahipala in the Pratihara chronology. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144 · pp 250-252]
xs: The correct order is **C, D, A, B** — option **(3)**.
Chronology: **Vatsaraja** → **Nagabhata II** → **Mahendrapala I** → **Mahipala** (UPPSC 2017).
**Mihira Bhoja** (c. **836-890**) came between Nagabhata II and Mahendrapala I.
xa: **Vatsaraja** (c. **780-800**) took Kannauj but was defeated by **Dhruva**.
**Nagabhata II** ousted **Chakrayudha** and beat **Dharmapala** near **Monghyr**.
**Mahendrapala I** (c. **890-910**) was patron of **Rajashekhara**.
Under **Mahipala I**, Kannauj was sacked by **Indra III** (c. **916**).

70.s: Mihir Bhoja captured Kannauj around which year?
70.x: Mihir Bhoja captured Kannauj around 836 AD and made it the Pratihara capital. 629 AD relates to Hiuen Tsang's journey.
70.tq: Place Mihir Bhoja in the early 9th century.
n: Mihir Bhoja captured Kannauj around 836 AD. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144 · pp 250-252]
xs: **Mihir Bhoja** captured **Kannauj** around **836 AD** and made it his capital — option **(1)**.
His reign: c. **836-890**, the **zenith** of the dynasty.
**916** is when **Indra III** sacked Kannauj under **Mahipala I**.
xa: ⚠ Other notes say **Nagabhata II** made Kannauj the capital.
Titles: **Adivaraha** (UPPSC 2017) and **Prabhasa**; he followed **Vaishnavism**.
The **Barah copper plate** mentions a skandhavara at **Mahodaya**.
He built **Teli-ka-Mandir, Gwalior**.

70.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Muhammad-bin-Qasim’s invasion was an Arab invasion.
II. Dahir was defeated and killed by Muhammad-bin-Qasim.
III. Muhammad-bin-Qasim’s conquest was largely confined to Sindh and Multan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
70.x: All three are correct: Muhammad bin Qasim led the Arab invasion, killed Raja Dahir, and his conquest stayed largely within Sindh and Multan.
70.tq: Check each statement separately.
n: Muhammad-bin-Qasim’s invasion was an Arab invasion. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 78-80]
Dahir was defeated and killed by Muhammad-bin-Qasim. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 78-80]
Muhammad-bin-Qasim’s conquest was largely confined to Sindh and Multan. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 78-80]
xs: **All three** statements are correct — option **(3) I, II and III**.
I: **Muhammad-bin-Qasim**'s conquest of **Sindh** in **712 AD** was an **Arab invasion**.
II: **Dahir** was **defeated and killed** by him.
III: his conquest **remained largely confined** to **Sindh** and **Multan**.
xa: The date is also given as **711–12 CE**.
The Pratiharas were the main power that kept Arab rule confined to **Sindh**.
Founder **Nagabhata I** (c. **730-760**) **resisted the Arabs**.
**Mahmud of Ghazni** attacked Kannauj in **1018**.

71.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Rashtrakuta capitals is correct?
1. The early seat was in the Elapura or Ellora region.
2. Dantidurga’s inscription is found in the Dashavatara cave at Ellora.
3. Manyakheta was built by Amoghavarsha I.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
71.x: The early Rashtrakuta seat was in the Elapura region, Dantidurga’s inscription is in Ellora’s Dashavatara cave, and Amoghavarsha I built Manyakheta.
71.tq: Distinguish the early Elapura seat and inscription from the later capital of Manyakheta.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: early seat = **Elapura (Ellora)** region — correct.
Statement 2: Dantidurga's inscription is in Ellora's **Dashavatara cave** — correct.
Statement 3: **Manyakheta** was built by **Amoghavarsha I** (UPSC) — correct.
xa: ⚠ Trap: some notes say **Dantidurga** made Manyakheta his capital — it was Amoghavarsha's work.
Manyakheta = **Malkhed, Karnataka**.
Paramara **Siyaka II** later sacked Manyakheta.

71.s: Manyakheta, also known as Malkhed, is located in present-day:
71.x: Manyakheta or Malkhed is in Karnataka and was built by Amoghavarsha I.
71.tq: Use the present geographical location to resolve the historical capital question.
xs: **Manyakheta (Malkhed)** is in **Karnataka** — option **(4)** is correct.
It was built by **Amoghavarsha I** (UPSC).
xa: The earlier seat was the **Elapura (Ellora)** region.
Paramara **Siyaka II** sacked Manyakheta after defeating **Khottiga** on the **Narmada**.
**Tailapa II** of Kalyani overthrew the line c. **973**.

71.s:
Consider the following pairs (Rashtrakuta ruler - achievement):
1. Dantidurga - overthrew the Badami Chalukya Kirtivarman II
2. Krishna III - rock-cut Kailasa (Shiva) temple at Ellora
3. Krishna III - victory over the Cholas at Takkolam
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
71.x: Pair 1 is correct: Dantidurga, the founder, overthrew Kirtivarman II. Pair 2 is wrong: the Kailasa temple at Ellora was built by Krishna I, not Krishna III (APPSC G1 2024 wrong pair). Pair 3 is correct: Krishna III beat the Cholas at Takkolam. Hence C; A, B and D include pair 2.
71.tq: Krishna I = Kailasa, Ellora; Krishna III = Takkolam and Ponna.
xs: Pairs 1 and 3 are correct — option **(3) 1 and 3 only**.
Pair 1: **Dantidurga** overthrew Badami Chalukya **Kirtivarman II** — correct.
Pair 2: the **Kailasa temple, Ellora** was built by **Krishna I**, not Krishna III — wrong (APPSC G1 2024 wrong pair).
Pair 3: **Krishna III** beat the Cholas at **Takkolam** — correct.
xa: Takkolam (**949 CE**): Chola **Parantaka I** defeated, prince **Rajaditya** killed.
Krishna III patronised the poet **Ponna**.
The Kailasa is a **monolithic** temple.

71.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Dhruva:
1. He was the first Rashtrakuta ruler to proceed towards northern India.
2. He defeated Vatsaraja and Dharmapala.
3. He subdued the Eastern Chalukyas and the Gangas of Talakad.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
71.x: Dhruva was the first Rashtrakuta ruler to move north, defeated Vatsaraja and Dharmapala, and subdued the Eastern Chalukyas and the Gangas of Talakad.
71.tq: Check each statement against the ruler’s complete military profile before selecting the inclusive combination.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statements 1 and 2: **Dhruva** (**780-793**) was **first to go north**, beating **Vatsaraja** and **Dharmapala** — correct.
Statement 3: he subdued the **Eastern Chalukyas** and **Gangas of Talakad** — correct.
xa: Against Vengi he acted through **Vemulavada Arikesari I**, beating **Vishnuvardhana IV**.
Vishnuvardhana IV gave his daughter **Shila Mahadevi** to Dhruva.
His successor **Govinda III** reached the **Himalayas**.

71.s: Which one of the following was a military achievement of Govinda III?
o: Sacking Kannauj in the reign of Indra III
Defeating Nagabhata II and Dharmapala and reaching the Himalayas
71.x: Govinda III defeated Nagabhata II and Dharmapala and is said in the Sanjan plates to have reached the Himalayas.
71.tq: Separate the military achievements of successive Rashtrakuta rulers instead of matching all northern campaigns together.
xs: **Govinda III** defeated **Nagabhata II** and **Dharmapala** and **reached the Himalayas** — option **(2)** is correct.
His Himalayan march is recorded in the **Sanjan plates**; defeat of Nagabhata II: UKPSC 2021.
**Takkolam** was **Krishna III**'s victory; **Tailapa II** overthrew the Rashtrakutas.
xa: Govinda III reigned **793-814**.
His title: **Prabhutavarsha**.
He was followed by **Amoghavarsha I** (**814-878**).

71.s:
Arrange the following Rashtrakuta rulers in chronological order of their reigns:
A. Govinda III
B. Dantidurga
C. Amoghavarsha I
D. Dhruva
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
71.x: The sequence is Dantidurga, Dhruva, Govinda III and Amoghavarsha I. Their approximate reign periods were 753–756, 780–793, 793–814 and 814–878 respectively.
71.tq: Fix the earliest and latest rulers first, then place the two intervening reigns by their dates.
xs: Order: **Dantidurga → Dhruva → Govinda III → Amoghavarsha I** — option **(1) B, D, A, C**.
Dantidurga c. **753-756**; Dhruva **780-793**.
Govinda III **793-814**; Amoghavarsha I **814-878**.
xa: **Krishna I** (Kailasa temple) came after Dantidurga.
**Krishna III** (Takkolam, **949 CE**) came later.
Some notes date Krishna I's death to "**722 CE**" — impossible after Dantidurga (**753**).

71.s: Amoghavarsha I is particularly associated with which of the following combinations?
71.x: Amoghavarsha I built Manyakheta, was associated with Kavirajamarga, and is described as a Jain ruler or patron.
71.tq: Use a cluster of contributions to identify the ruler rather than relying on a single isolated fact.
xs: Amoghavarsha I = **Manyakheta**, **Kavirajamarga** and **Jainism** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Kailasa** = Krishna I; **Takkolam** = Krishna III; **Gadayuddha** = **Ranna**; **Hiranyagarbha** = Dantidurga.
xa: Amoghavarsha won at **Vingavalli** (title **Viranarayana**); also titled **Nripatunga**.
He also wrote the Sanskrit Jain text **Prashnottara Ratnamalika**.
**Sulaiman** called him one of the **four great kings** of the world.

71.s: Which of the following statements about the end of the Rashtrakuta line is correct?
o: Paramara Siyaka II defeated Khottiga on the Narmada and sacked Manyakheta; Tailapa II later overthrew the line.
Khottiga defeated Paramara Siyaka II on the Narmada and captured Manyakheta.
Tailapa II was defeated by Khottiga and restored Rashtrakuta rule at Manyakheta.
Krishna III ended the Rashtrakuta line after losing Manyakheta to the Cholas.
71.x: Paramara Siyaka II defeated Khottiga on the Narmada and sacked Manyakheta. Tailapa II of the Kalyani Chalukyas subsequently overthrew the Rashtrakuta line around 973 CE.
71.tq: Watch for the reversal of victor and defeated ruler in the final phase of a dynasty.
xs: Paramara **Siyaka II** defeated **Khottiga** on the **Narmada** and sacked **Manyakheta**; **Tailapa II** then overthrew the line — option **(1)** is correct.
Tailapa II of **Kalyani** ended the dynasty c. **973**.
**Krishna III** in fact **defeated** the Cholas at Takkolam.
xa: The Kannada poet **Ranna** was patronised by Western Chalukya **Tailapa II**.
Manyakheta was built by **Amoghavarsha I**.

71.s: Which one of the following statements about the Rashtrakuta–Vengi conflict is correct?
o: The conflict continued for approximately two centuries.
It was exclusively a conflict between the Rashtrakutas and the Cholas.
It began only after the fall of the Rashtrakutas in 973 CE.
It was confined to a single battle during Dantidurga’s reign.
71.x: The Rashtrakuta–Vengi conflict continued for approximately 200 years and involved repeated struggles with the Eastern Chalukyas.
71.tq: Use the approximate duration to distinguish a prolonged dynastic conflict from a single campaign.
xs: The Rashtrakuta-Vengi conflict continued for **about 200 years** — roughly **two centuries** — option **(1)** is correct.
It ran from **Dantidurga** vs **Vijayaditya I** to **Krishna II** vs **Gunaga Vijayaditya III** — not a single battle, and against the **Eastern Chalukyas**, not the Cholas.
xa: **Vijayaditya II** fought **108 battles**.
**Amoghavarsha** won at **Vingavalli**.
**Dhruva** won through **Vemulavada Arikesari I**.

71.s:
Consider the following statements about the Rashtrakuta-Vengi conflict:
1. Vijayaditya II fought 108 battles against Rashtrakuta forces.
2. Gunaga Vijayaditya III defeated Krishna II after the death of Amoghavarsha I.
3. Vishnuvardhana IV defeated Dhruva and forced him to give his daughter Shila Mahadevi in marriage.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
71.x: Statement 1 is correct: Vijayaditya II fought 108 battles. Statement 2 is correct: Gunaga Vijayaditya III defeated Krishna II after Amoghavarsha's death. Statement 3 is wrong: Dhruva (through Vemulavada Arikesari I) beat Vishnuvardhana IV, who then gave his daughter Shila Mahadevi to Dhruva. Hence A; B, C and D include statement 3.
71.tq: In the Vengi wars, Dhruva won and received Shila Mahadevi; the Eastern Chalukya high points are Vijayaditya II (108 battles) and Gunaga Vijayaditya III (beat Krishna II).
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **Vijayaditya II** fought **108 battles** — correct.
Statement 2: **Gunaga Vijayaditya III** beat **Krishna II** after Amoghavarsha's death — correct.
Statement 3: **Dhruva** beat **Vishnuvardhana IV**, who then gave **Shila Mahadevi** to Dhruva — wrong.
xa: Dhruva acted through **Vemulavada Arikesari I**.
Vijayaditya II built **108 Shiva temples** and named **Vijayawada**.

71.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Dhruva acted through Vemulavada Arikesari I against the Eastern Chalukyas.
2. Vishnuvardhana IV gave his daughter Shila Mahadevi in marriage to Dhruva.
3. Amoghavarsha I won at Vingavalli and assumed the title Viranarayana.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
71.x: All three are correct: Dhruva acted through Vemulavada Arikesari I to beat Vishnuvardhana IV, who then gave his daughter Shila Mahadevi to Dhruva; Amoghavarsha I won at Vingavalli and took the title Viranarayana. Hence D.
71.tq: Check the sequence of alliance, marriage and battlefield outcome across the Vengi conflict.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **Dhruva** acted through **Vemulavada Arikesari I** — correct.
Statement 2: **Vishnuvardhana IV** gave daughter **Shila Mahadevi** to Dhruva — correct.
Statement 3: **Amoghavarsha I** won at **Vingavalli**, title **Viranarayana** — correct.
xa: Later **Gunaga Vijayaditya III** defeated **Krishna II**.
The conflict lasted about **200 years**.
Amoghavarsha's other title: **Nripatunga**.

71.s: What was the immediate result of the battle of Takkolam in 949 CE?
o: Gunaga Vijayaditya III defeated Krishna II and captured Takkolam.
Krishna III defeated Chola king Parantaka I, and Chola prince Rajaditya was killed.
Dhruva defeated Pallava ruler Nandivarman, and Rajaditya became king.
Amoghavarsha defeated Parantaka I and annexed Vengi.
71.x: At Takkolam in 949 CE, Krishna III defeated the Cholas under Parantaka I, and the Chola prince Rajaditya was killed.
71.tq: Combine the date, victor, defeated ruler and notable casualty to identify the correct battle account.
xs: At **Takkolam** (**949 CE**) **Krishna III** defeated Chola **Parantaka I**, and prince **Rajaditya** was killed — option **(2)** is correct.
**Gunaga Vijayaditya III** vs **Krishna II** was a Vengi war; **Vingavalli** was Amoghavarsha's victory.
xa: Krishna III patronised **Ponna** (Santipurana).
⚠ The Ellora Kailasa is **Krishna I**'s, not Krishna III's.
**Tailapa II** ended the line c. **973**.

71.s: Which of the following title–ruler pairs is NOT correctly matched?
71.x: Balhara, or Vallabharaja, was a title generally used for Rashtrakuta kings, not exclusively for Govinda III. Nripatunga and Viranarayana were titles of Amoghavarsha I, while Prabhutavarsha was associated with Govinda III.
71.tq: Reject an over-specific title assignment when the title was used generally for a dynasty’s kings.
xs: "**Balhara — Govinda III exclusively**" is wrong — option **(4)** is the answer.
**Balhara** (Vallabharaja) was used for **Rashtrakuta kings generally**.
**Nripatunga** and **Viranarayana** = **Amoghavarsha I**; **Prabhutavarsha** = **Govinda III** — correct.
xa: Balhara: contemporary of **Al-Masudi** (APPSC G1 2024).
Viranarayana came after the victory at **Vingavalli**.

71.s: Arab writers used the term ‘Balhara’ for:
o: The Chola kings who ruled at Takkolam
71.x: Balhara is the Arab form associated with Vallabharaja and was used generally for Rashtrakuta kings. Al-Masudi was a contemporary source for this usage.
71.tq: Avoid the trap of assigning a dynastic title to one particular ruler when it had broader usage.
xs: Arab writers used "**Balhara**" for **Rashtrakuta kings generally** — option **(4)** is correct.
It is the Arab form of **Vallabharaja**; Al-Masudi was contemporary (APPSC G1 2024).
xa: **Sulaiman** called **Amoghavarsha I** one of the four great kings of the world.
Amoghavarsha's titles: **Nripatunga**, **Viranarayana**.
Govinda III's title: **Prabhutavarsha**.

71.s:
Consider the following statements about literary works of the Rashtrakuta period:
1. Kavirajamarga, associated with Amoghavarsha I, is the earliest work on Kannada poetics.
2. Prashnottara Ratnamalika of Amoghavarsha I is a Kannada work.
3. Ganitasarasangraha, a Sanskrit work on mathematics, was written by Mahaviracharya.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
71.x: Statement 1 is correct: Kavirajamarga (c. 850) by Amoghavarsha I is the earliest work on Kannada poetics. Statement 2 is wrong: Prashnottara Ratnamalika is a Sanskrit Jain text. Statement 3 is correct: Mahaviracharya wrote the Sanskrit mathematical work Ganitasarasangraha. Hence C; A, B and D include statement 2.
71.tq: Amoghavarsha wrote in two languages: Kavirajamarga in Kannada, Prashnottara Ratnamalika in Sanskrit.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(3) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1: **Kavirajamarga** (c. **850**) by **Amoghavarsha I** = earliest work on **Kannada poetics** — correct.
Statement 2: **Prashnottara Ratnamalika** is a **Sanskrit** Jain text — wrong.
Statement 3: **Mahaviracharya** wrote the Sanskrit maths work **Ganitasarasangraha** — correct.
xa: Pampa wrote **Vikramarjuna Vijaya** (Pampa Bharata) in Kannada.
**Nalachampu** by **Trivikrama Bhatta** = first champu.

71.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
71.x: Nalachampu was written by Trivikrama Bhatta. Halayudha was the author of Kavirahasya.
71.tq: Identify the incorrect author–work pairing after separating the closely associated Sanskrit works.
xs: **Nalachampu — Halayudha** is wrong — option **(4)** is the answer.
**Nalachampu** is by **Trivikrama Bhatta**; **Halayudha** wrote **Kavirahasya**.
**Santipurana** (Ponna), **Adipurana** (Pampa) and **Ganitasarasangraha** (Mahaviracharya) are correct.
xa: Nalachampu is the **first champu**.
⚠ **Adipurana**: Pampa = **Kannada**; **Jinasena** = **Sanskrit**.

71.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Pampa’s Adipurana is a Kannada work concerning the life of Rishabhadeva.
2. Jinasena wrote a Sanskrit Adipurana.
3. Pampa was a Telugu-origin poet associated with Kannada literature.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
71.x: All three statements are correct. Pampa wrote a Kannada Adipurana, Jinasena wrote a Sanskrit Adipurana, and Pampa is described as Telugu-origin or Telugu-born.
71.tq: Retain the distinction between two Adipuranas and the poet’s regional origin.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **Pampa**'s **Adipurana** is in **Kannada**, on the life of **Rishabhadeva** — correct.
Statement 2: **Jinasena** wrote a **Sanskrit** Adipurana — correct.
Statement 3: Pampa is a **Telugu-origin** poet (APPSC G2 2012) — correct.
xa: Pampa also wrote **Vikramarjuna Vijaya** (Pampa Bharata).
His patron: **Arikesari II** of the **Vemulavada Chalukyas**.

71.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Poet)
a. Pampa
b. Ponna
c. Ranna
d. Swayambhu

List-II (Association)
i. Apabhramsha poet linked to the court
ii. Patronised by Krishna III
iii. Patronised by Arikesari II
iv. Patronised by Tailapa II

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
71.x: Pampa was patronised by Arikesari II, Ponna by Krishna III, Ranna by Tailapa II, and Swayambhu was an Apabhramsha poet linked to the court.
71.tq: Start with the sure patron–poet pair and use elimination for the remaining court associations.
xs: Correct code: **a–iii, b–ii, c–iv, d–i** — option **(1)**.
**Pampa** — **Arikesari II**; **Ponna** — **Krishna III**.
**Ranna** — **Tailapa II**; **Swayambhu** — **Apabhramsha** poet of the court.
xa: Pampa, Ponna and Ranna = the Kannada **Ratnatraya**.
Ranna wrote **Gadayuddha**; Ponna wrote **Santipurana**.
In Pampa's epic, **Arjuna** is modelled on his patron.

71.s: The Kannada ‘Ratnatraya’ traditionally refers to which group?
71.x: The Kannada Ratnatraya consisted of Pampa, Ponna and Ranna, the three celebrated Kannada poets associated with major royal patrons.
71.tq: Identify the complete literary triad rather than one poet or one patron.
xs: The Kannada **Ratnatraya** = **Pampa, Ponna and Ranna** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Trivikrama Bhatta**, **Halayudha** and **Jinasena** wrote in **Sanskrit**; **Swayambhu** wrote in Apabhramsha.
xa: Patrons: Pampa — **Arikesari II**; Ponna — **Krishna III**; Ranna — **Tailapa II**.
The Rashtrakuta age = **golden age of Kannada**.

71.s:
Which of the following statements about Pampa’s literary association is correct?
1. He wrote Vikramarjuna Vijaya, also known as Pampa Bharata.
2. Arjuna in the epic was modelled on his patron Arikesari II.
3. He was hailed as a Telugu-born poet despite writing in Kannada.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
71.x: All three statements are correct. Pampa wrote Vikramarjuna Vijaya in Kannada, modelled Arjuna on Arikesari II, and is noted as a Telugu-born or Telugu-origin poet.
71.tq: Combine title, patronal influence and regional identity while avoiding the language–origin confusion.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: Pampa wrote **Vikramarjuna Vijaya** (**Pampa Bharata**) — correct.
Statement 2: **Arjuna** was modelled on patron **Arikesari II** — correct.
Statement 3: Pampa is hailed as **Telugu-born**, writing in **Kannada** — correct.
xa: Arikesari II was of the **Vemulavada Chalukyas**, a Rashtrakuta feudatory.
Pampa's **Adipurana** tells the life of **Rishabhadeva**.
⚠ Some notes make Pampa contemporary of **Vijayaditya I** — a slip.

71.s: Which ruler was visited by Sulaiman, who regarded him as one of the four great kings of the world?
71.x: Sulaiman visited the court of Amoghavarsha I and considered him one of the four great kings of the world.
71.tq: Use the foreign visitor–ruler association to identify the correct reign.
xs: **Sulaiman** visited in **Amoghavarsha I**'s reign and called him one of the **four great kings of the world** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Indra III** sacked Kannauj; **Krishna III** won at Takkolam; **Dantidurga** founded the line.
xa: Sulaiman also praised **Pratihara cavalry**.
Arab writers called Rashtrakuta kings "**Balhara**".
Amoghavarsha ruled **814-878**.

71.s: Vijayaditya II of the Eastern Chalukyas is associated with which cultural and religious contribution?
o: Construction of 108 Shiva temples and the naming of Vijayawada
Construction of the Kailasa temple at Ellora
Establishment of Manyakheta as the Rashtrakuta capital
71.x: Vijayaditya II is associated with the construction of 108 Shiva temples and with the naming of Vijayawada.
71.tq: Match the regional contribution to the correct Eastern Chalukya ruler rather than to a Rashtrakuta monarch.
xs: **Vijayaditya II** built **108 Shiva temples** and named **Vijayawada** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Kailasa** = **Krishna I**; **Manyakheta** and **Kavirajamarga** = **Amoghavarsha I**.
xa: Vijayaditya II fought **108 battles** against the Rashtrakutas.
**Pampa** is hailed in AP as a **Telugu-born** poet.
The Rashtrakuta-Vengi war lasted about **200 years**.

71.s: Who established the Rashtrakuta dynasty/Empire in 753 AD?
71.x: Dantidurga founded the Rashtrakuta empire in 753 CE by overthrowing the Badami Chalukya Kirtivarman II. Krishna I, Govinda III and Amoghavarsha I were later rulers.
71.tq: Recall the founder of the dynasty.
n: Dantidurga established the Rashtrakuta dynasty in 753 AD. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #146 · pp 255-256]
Dantidurga established the Rashtrakuta Empire in 753 AD. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #146 · pp 255-256]
xs: **Dantidurga** established the **Rashtrakuta dynasty** in **753 AD** — option **(1)**.
He overthrew the Badami Chalukya **Kirtivarman II** (UPSC 2006).
**Krishna I**, **Govinda III** and **Amoghavarsha I** were later rulers.
xa: Dantidurga performed the **Hiranyagarbha** ritual at **Ujjayini**.
He was a contemporary of Eastern Chalukya **Vijayaditya I**.
His inscription is in Ellora's **Dashavatara cave**.
⚠ **Manyakheta** was built by **Amoghavarsha I**, not Dantidurga.

71.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Amoghavarsha I was born in 800 AD.
Amoghavarsha I was born in a military camp.
Amoghavarsha I was born at Manyakheta.
Amoghavarsha I was born at Shribhavan.
71.x: Option C is incorrect: Amoghavarsha I was born in 800 CE at Shribhavan, near the Narmada, in a military camp, not at Manyakheta. Manyakheta was the Rashtrakuta capital he built.
71.tq: Check the birthplace in each statement.
n: Amoghavarsha I was born in 800 AD. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #146 · pp 255-256]
Amoghavarsha I was born at Shribhavan. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #146 · pp 255-256]
Amoghavarsha I was born in a military camp. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #146 · pp 255-256]
Shribhavan was on or near the Narmada. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #146 · pp 255-256]
xs: The incorrect statement is **Amoghavarsha I was born at Manyakheta** — option **(3)**.
He was **born** in **800 AD** at **Shribhavan** (near the **Narmada**) in a **military camp** (UPPSC 2013).
**Manyakheta** (Malkhed, Karnataka) was the capital **he built**.
xa: Amoghavarsha I wrote the **Kannada Kavirajamarga** (c. **850**).
He won at **Vingavalli** over the Eastern Chalukyas (title **Viranarayana**).
His titles include **Nripatunga**.
**Sulaiman** called him one of the **four great kings** of the world.

71.s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Kailasa Temple
(b) Kailasa Temple's cave number
(c) Kailasa Temple's architectural style
(d) Kailasa Temple's builder

List-II
(i) Dravidian architecture
(ii) Krishna I
(iii) Ellora, Cave 16
(iv) Rashtrakutas
71.x: The Kailasa temple was a Rashtrakuta work, cut as Cave 16 at Ellora, built in the Dravidian style and built under Krishna I, giving a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii.
71.tq: Recall each detail of the Kailasa temple.
n: The Kailasa Temple at Ellora was built by the Rashtrakutas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #146 · pp 255-256]
Krishna I built the Kailasa Temple. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #146 · pp 255-256]
The Kailasa Temple is located in Cave 16 at Ellora. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #146 · pp 255-256]
The Kailasa Temple follows Dravidian architecture. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #146 · pp 255-256]
xs: The correct match is **a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii** — option **(1)**.
**Kailasa Temple** → **Rashtrakutas**; cave number → **Ellora, Cave 16**.
Style → **Dravidian architecture**; builder → **Krishna I**.
xa: It was **designed to recall Mount Kailasa**, Shiva's abode.
⚠ APPSC G1 2024 wrong pair: "**Krishna III** — rock-cut Shiva temple at Ellora"; it was **Krishna I**.
The **Elephanta Caves** were also built by the Rashtrakutas.
**Ellora** has **Buddhist, Hindu and Jain** rock-cut caves side by side.

71.s:
How many of the following traditions are represented among the rock-cut caves at Ellora?

1. Buddhist
2. Hindu
3. Jain
4. Shakta
71.x: Three: Buddhist, Hindu and Jain rock-cut caves stand side by side at Ellora. Shakta is a Hindu sect the Rashtrakutas patronised, not a separate group of caves.
71.tq: Recall the three cave groups at Ellora.
n: Rashtrakuta rulers patronized Shakta traditions. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #146 · pp 255-256]
Buddhist rock-cut caves coexist at Ellora. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #146 · pp 255-256]
Hindu rock-cut caves coexist at Ellora. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #146 · pp 255-256]
Jain rock-cut caves coexist at Ellora. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #146 · pp 255-256]
xs: **Only three** — option **(3)**.
At **Ellora**, **Buddhist**, **Hindu** and **Jain** rock-cut caves **coexist**.
**Shakta** is a tradition the Rashtrakutas patronised, not a separate group of caves.
xa: The Rashtrakutas patronised **Shaiva**, **Vaishnava** and **Shakta** traditions, with a leaning to **Jainism**.
**Kailasa Temple** = **Cave 16**, built by **Krishna I**.
**Jinasena**, a Jain scholar, wrote the **Adipurana**.
Early seat: **Elapura (Ellora)** region.

71.s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Kailasa Temple, Ellora
(b) Jinasena
(c) Hiranyagarbha ritual
(d) Kavirajamarga

List-II
(i) Shaiva rock-cut monument
(ii) Jain scholar, author of the Adipurana

72.s: Who among the following travellers ranked the Rashtrakuta king among the four great kings of the world?

72.s:

72.s:

**Vaishnavism** and **Buddhism** had royal patronage, no persecution.

72.s:

72.x: All three statements are correct. Rashtrakuta religious policy included Shaiva royal affiliation, patronage of Vaishnavism and Buddhism without persecution, and accommodation of Muslim Arab merchants in ports.

xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.

72.s:
Consider the following statements about the Ellora caves:

India-Jordan **Petra-Ellora** twinning agreement (**2026**).

72.s:

72.s:

73.s: The Badami cliff inscription records that Vatapi was fortified by Pulakesin I in

xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: Pulakesin II was **Dakshinapatheshwara**, against Harsha's **Uttarapatheshwara**.

xa: Reign: **609-642 CE**; first South Indian king to issue **gold coins**.
He did defeat Pallava **Mahendravarman I**, recorded in the **Maruturu and Kopparam** inscriptions.
The **Aihole inscription** records the victory over **Harsha** at the **Narmada**.

73.s: During the eastern campaign of Pulakesin II, which sequence is correct?
o: Vengi conquest—defeat of Durjayas—conquest of Kosala and Kalinga—appointment of Vishnuvardhana
Conquest of Kosala and Kalinga—march to Vengi—defeat of Durjayas—appointment of Vishnuvardhana
Appointment of Vishnuvardhana—conquest of Kosala—defeat of Durjayas—march to Vengi
Defeat of Durjayas—appointment of Vishnuvardhana—conquest of Kalinga—march to Vengi
73.x: Pulakesin II conquered Kosala and Kalinga, marched to Vengi, defeated the Durjayas and appointed Kubja Vishnuvardhana there.
73.tq: Follow the campaign route from the initial conquests to the administrative appointment.
xs: Order: conquest of **Kosala and Kalinga** → march on **Vengi** → defeat of the **Durjayas** → appointment of **Kubja Vishnuvardhana** — option **(2)**.
After the Durjayas, Pulakesin II also defeated Pallava **Mahendravarman I**.
xa: Kubja Vishnuvardhana appointed in **617 CE** (**Satara inscription**); declared independence in **624 CE** = **Eastern Chalukyas**.
⚠ **617** = appointment; **624** = independence.
Vengi was held by the **Durjaya** dynasty before Pulakesin II's conquest.

73.s:
Consider the following statements about the foreign contacts of Pulakesin II:
1. He exchanged embassies with the Persian king Khusrau II.
2. A painting in Ajanta Cave 1 is conclusively identified as this Persian embassy.
3. Hiuen Tsang visited his kingdom and praised him along with Harsha and Narasimhavarman.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
73.x: Statement 1 is correct: embassies were exchanged with Khusrau II. Statement 2 is wrong: the Ajanta Cave 1 painting was once read as this embassy, but that identification is now doubted. Statement 3 is correct: Hiuen Tsang praised him in the Si-yu-ki. So C; A, B and D include statement 2.
73.tq: Watch absolute words like 'conclusively' - the Ajanta identification is doubted.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: Pulakesin II exchanged embassies with Persian king **Khusrau II**.
Statement 2 is **wrong**: the **Ajanta Cave 1** painting was once read as this embassy, but the identification is **now doubted**.
Statement 3 is **correct**: **Hiuen Tsang** visited and praised him with **Harsha** and **Narasimhavarman** (Si-yu-ki) — so **1 and 3 only**, option **(3)**.
xa: China-India relations under the Chalukyas are described by **Ma Twan-lin** (UPPSC 2014 key: "Matwalin").
Pulakesin II was the first South Indian king to issue **gold coins**.
Hiuen Tsang's account is the **Si-yu-ki**.

73.s: The Chinese account of China–India relations under the Chalukyas is credited to
73.x: The account of China–India relations under the Chalukyas is credited to Ma Twan-lin, also rendered in some references as Matwalin. Hiuen Tsang visited Pulakesin II's kingdom and praised him in comparison with Harsha and Narasimhavarman.
73.tq: Separate the Chinese historian credited with the account from the visiting traveller.
xs: The Chinese account of China-India relations under the Chalukyas is credited to **Ma Twan-lin** — option **(4)**; the **UPPSC 2014** key spells it "Matwalin".
**Hiuen Tsang** visited Pulakesin II and praised him in the **Si-yu-ki**, but the relations account is Ma Twan-lin's.
**Ravikirti** was the Jain court poet who wrote the **Aihole inscription**.
xa: Pulakesin II exchanged embassies with Persian **Khusrau II**.
The **Ajanta Cave 1** painting once read as the Persian embassy — identification **now doubted**.
Hiuen Tsang praised him along with **Harsha** and **Narasimhavarman**.

73.s:
Consider the following statements about the Aihole inscription:
1. It is a Sanskrit prasasti in verse composed by Ravikirti, the Jain court poet of Pulakesin II.
2. It is dated 634-35 CE (Saka 556).
3. It is engraved on the Virupaksha temple at Pattadakal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
73.x: Statement 1 is correct: Ravikirti, a Jain poet, wrote this Sanskrit verse prasasti. Statement 2 is correct: it is dated 634-35 CE (Saka 556). Statement 3 is wrong: it is at the Meguti Jain temple, Aihole; the Virupaksha temple at Pattadakal was built by Lokamahadevi. So A; B, C and D include statement 3.
73.tq: Jain poet, Jain temple: Ravikirti at the Meguti temple.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: a **Sanskrit** prasasti in verse by **Ravikirti**, Jain court poet of Pulakesin II.
Statement 2 is **correct**: dated **634-35 CE** (**Saka 556**); some notes give 634 CE.

Statement 3 is **wrong**: it is at the **Meguti Jain temple, Aihole**; the **Virupaksha temple, Pattadakal** was built by **Lokamahadevi**, queen of Vikramaditya II — so option **(1)**, **1 and 2 only**.
xa: It names the poets **Kalidasa** and **Bharavi** (UPSC 1994, UPPSC 2013).
Victories listed include **Harsha** (Narmada), **Kadambas** (Banavasi), **Kalinga** and **Pishtapura (Pithapuram)**.
It calls **Kirtivarman I** "the **night of doom**" to the Nalas, Mauryas and Kadambas.

73.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the victories recorded in the Aihole inscription:
1. Pulakesin II is said to have defeated Harsha at the Narmada.
2. The inscription mentions victories over Kosala and Kalinga.
3. Pishtapura mentioned in the record is identified with Pithapuram.
4. The Pallavas are absent from the list of opponents.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
73.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the Pallavas are included among the opponents listed in the inscription.
73.tq: Test the positive list first, then identify the statement that reverses an explicitly recorded fact.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: Pulakesin II defeated **Harsha** at the **Narmada**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: **Kosala** and **Kalinga** are in the list.
Statement 3 is **correct**: **Pishtapura** = **Pithapuram**.
Statement 4 is **wrong**: the **Pallavas** are listed among the opponents — so **1, 2 and 3 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Other opponents: **Kadambas** (Banavasi), **Gangas**, **Alupas**, **Mauryas of Konkan**, **Latas**, **Malavas**, **Gurjaras**.
Author **Ravikirti**; date **634-35 CE**; at the **Meguti Jain temple**.
Pithapuram later became the capital of the **Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi**.

73.s: The description of Kirtivarman I as ‘the night of doom’ in the Aihole inscription refers particularly to his victories over the
73.x: Kirtivarman I is described as the ‘night of doom’ to the Nalas, Mauryas and Kadambas.
73.tq: Pair the distinctive epithet with the exact group of defeated powers.
xs: The Aihole inscription calls **Kirtivarman I** "the night of doom" to the **Nalas, Mauryas and Kadambas** — option **(4)**.
**Kosala, Kalinga, Alupas, Harsha, Pallavas, Gangas, Latas, Malavas, Gurjaras** are among **Pulakesin II**'s victories in the same record.
xa: Kirtivarman I is noted for **expansion** and the **Bahusuvarna-Agnishtoma** sacrifice (**Mahakuta pillar inscription**).
He left **minor sons**, so his brother **Mangalesha** became regent.
The inscription is by **Ravikirti**, Jain court poet of Pulakesin II.

73.s: The Maruturu and Kopparam inscriptions associate Pulakesin II with which achievement in Andhra?
o: Foundation of the Eastern Chalukya kingdom at Pithapuram
Defeat of Harsha on the banks of the Godavari
Defeat of the Pallava ruler Mahendravarman I and control over the land between the Krishna and Godavari
Appointment of Kubja Vishnuvardhana as governor of Kalinga
73.x: The Maruturu and Kopparam inscriptions record Pulakesin II's defeat of Mahendravarman I and his securing of the territory between the Krishna and Godavari rivers.
73.tq: Match the inscription with the achievement rather than with a nearby Chalukya event.
xs: The **Maruturu and Kopparam** inscriptions record Pulakesin II's defeat of Pallava **Mahendravarman I**, securing the land between the **Krishna and Godavari** — option **(3)**.
**Harsha** was stopped at the **Narmada**, not the Godavari; the **Eastern Chalukya** kingdom grew from **Kubja Vishnuvardhana**'s independence in **624 CE**.
Kubja Vishnuvardhana was appointed viceroy of **Vengi** (Satara inscription), not of Kalinga.
xa: Mangalagiri = "**Mangalapura**": APPSC-GS 2018 key → **Marturu**; APPSC G2 2019 → **Kopparam**.
⚠ If both appear as options, choose **Marturu**.
Kubja Vishnuvardhana's own inscriptions: **Chipurupalli, Kopparam, Chejarala, Timmapuram**.

73.s: Which one of the following inscriptions records the appointment of Kubja Vishnuvardhana as viceroy of Vengi?
73.x: The Satara inscription of 617 CE records Pulakesin II's appointment of his brother Kubja Vishnuvardhana as viceroy of Vengi.
73.tq: Use the inscription–event pair; nearby inscriptions are used as person-and-deed traps.
xs: The **Satara inscription (617 CE)** records the appointment of Pulakesin II's brother **Kubja Vishnuvardhana** as viceroy of **Vengi** — option **(2)**.
The **Badami cliff inscription** (543 CE) records Pulakesin I's fortification of Vatapi; the **Aihole inscription** is Ravikirti's prasasti; **Kopparam** records the defeat of Mahendravarman I.
xa: Vishnuvardhana declared independence in **624 CE** = **Eastern Chalukyas**.
⚠ **617 CE** = appointment; **624 CE** = independence.
His own inscriptions: **Chipurupalli, Kopparam, Chejarala, Timmapuram**.

73.s: Which inscription of Pulakesin II refers to Mangalagiri as 'Mangalapura', according to the APPSC-GS 2018 key?
73.x: The APPSC-GS 2018 key gives the Marturu inscription (an APPSC G2 2019 source names Kopparam; if both appear, choose Marturu). The Aihole inscription is Ravikirti's prasasti, the Satara inscription records Kubja Vishnuvardhana's appointment to Vengi, and Timmapuram is an inscription of Kubja Vishnuvardhana himself.
73.tq: Mangalapura = Mangalagiri → Marturu inscription (Kopparam per one key).
xs: Per the **APPSC-GS 2018** key and APP notes, the **Marturu (Maruturu) inscription** calls Mangalagiri "**Mangalapura**" — option **(3)**.
**Aihole** is Ravikirti's prasasti; **Satara** records Kubja Vishnuvardhana's appointment; **Timmapuram** is Kubja Vishnuvardhana's own inscription calling him 'Maharaja'.
xa: ⚠ **APPSC G2 2019** (Carpe Diem PYQ book) names the **Kopparam inscription** — learn both; if both are options, choose **Marturu**.
Maruturu and Kopparam record the defeat of **Mahendravarman I** and the land between **Krishna and Godavari**.

73.s: Which statement correctly describes the end of the Badami Chalukya dynasty?
o: Dantidurga overthrew Kirtivarman II and founded the Rashtrakutas.
Vikramaditya II ended the dynasty after conquering Kanchi.
Kirtivarman II overthrew Dantidurga and founded the Rashtrakutas.
Kubja Vishnuvardhana ended the dynasty after declaring independence at Vengi.
73.x: The last ruler, Kirtivarman II, was overthrown by Dantidurga, who founded the Rashtrakuta power around 753-757 CE.
73.tq: Apply the founder–overthrower trap to distinguish the two successor powers.
xs: The last ruler **Kirtivarman II** was overthrown by **Dantidurga**, founder of the **Rashtrakutas** (c. **753-757 CE**) — option **(1)**.
**Vikramaditya II** took **Kanchi** thrice but spared it; he did not end the dynasty.
**Kubja Vishnuvardhana**'s independence in **624 CE** founded the Eastern Chalukyas, not the end of Badami.
xa: Dynasty span: c. **543-757 CE**.
Founder: **Pulakesin I** (c. **543**), who performed the **Ashvamedha**.
FIRST/LAST pair: first South Indian gold coins = **Pulakesin II**; last ruler = **Kirtivarman II**.

73.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Ruler)
a. Pulakesin I
b. Kirtivarman I
c. Mangalesha
d. Vikramaditya I

List-II (Achievement)
i. Restored Chalukya power after Pallava occupation of Vatapi

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
73.x: Pulakesin I founded the independent kingdom; Kirtivarman I expanded it and became the ‘night of doom’; Mangalesha ruled as regent and extended the territory; Vikramaditya I restored power after Pallava occupation.
73.tq: Start with the distinctive regent and restoration pairs, then complete the remaining matches.
xs: **a–iii**: **Pulakesin I** founded the independent kingdom with capital **Badami**.
**b–ii**: **Kirtivarman I** — expansion; called the "**night of doom**".
**c–iv**: **Mangalesha** ruled as **regent**, kingdom from **south Gujarat** to **Bellary-Kurnool**; **d–i**: **Vikramaditya I** restored power after Pallava occupation of Vatapi — option **(1)**.
xa: **Vikramaditya I** reigned **655-680**; **Mangalesha** **597-609**.
**Vikramaditya II** took **Kanchi** thrice but spared it.
Pulakesin I performed the **Ashvamedha**; Kirtivarman I the **Bahusuvarna-Agnishtoma**.

73.s: The earliest rock-cut caves at Badami are associated with
73.x: Mangalesha is associated with the earliest rock-cut caves at Badami.
73.tq: Use the ruler–monument association rather than the better-known founder association.
xs: The **earliest rock-cut caves at Badami** are associated with **Mangalesha** (597-609) — option **(4)**.
**Pulakesin I** is the founder who fortified Vatapi; **Kirtivarman I** is known for expansion; **Vikramaditya II** for Kanchi and the **Virupaksha temple** link.
xa: Mangalesha ruled as **regent** for Kirtivarman I's **minor sons**.
His kingdom ran from **south Gujarat** to **Bellary-Kurnool**.
He was killed by **Pulakesin II** at **Elapattu-Simbige** (c. 609-10 CE).

73.s: Which ruler took Kanchi three times but spared the city and is associated with the Virupaksha temple at Pattadakal?
73.x: Vikramaditya II took Kanchi three times but spared it. His queen Lokamahadevi built the Virupaksha temple at Pattadakal.
73.tq: Link the repeated conquest and temple achievement to the same ruler.
xs: **Vikramaditya II** took **Kanchi** thrice but spared it — option **(2)**.
The **Virupaksha temple, Pattadakal** was built by his queen **Lokamahadevi**.
**Vikramaditya I** (655-680) restored Chalukya power after the Pallava occupation of Vatapi; **Kirtivarman II** was the last ruler.
xa: ⚠ Do not confuse the Virupaksha temple with the **Meguti Jain temple, Aihole**, site of the Aihole inscription.
Last ruler **Kirtivarman II** fell to **Dantidurga** (c. **753-757 CE**).

73.s:
Which of the following statements about the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi is correct?
1. Their emergence followed Pulakesin II's conquest of Vengi.
2. Kubja Vishnuvardhana was appointed at Vengi in 617 CE.
3. Vishnuvardhana declared independence in 624 CE.
4. Their capital was Pithapuram.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
73.x: All four statements are correct. Pulakesin II's Vengi conquest led to the Eastern Chalukya line, with Vishnuvardhana's appointment in 617 CE, independence in 624 CE and Pithapuram as capital.
73.tq: Combine political origin, dates and capital before choosing the complete coded option.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: Pulakesin II's **Vengi conquest** created the **Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi**.
Statements 2 and 3 are **correct**: **Kubja Vishnuvardhana** appointed in **617 CE**, independence in **624 CE**.
Statement 4 is **correct**: their capital was **Pithapuram** — so all four, option **(4)**.
xa: **Dandin** called Vengi "**Andhra Nagaram**".
The appointment is recorded in the **Satara inscription (617 CE)**.
First epigraphic reference to **Guntur** (as Kumturu) = **Pune copper plates** of Eastern Chalukya **Vishnuvardhana II**, **669 CE**.

73.s: Dandin referred to Vengi as
73.x: The literary author Dandin called Vengi ‘Andhra Nagaram’.
73.tq: Match the literary author with the distinctive geographical designation.
xs: **Dandin** called Vengi "**Andhra Nagaram**" — option **(4)**.
"**Mangalapura**" is Mangalagiri in the Marturu/Kopparam inscription; **Vatapi** is the Badami capital.
xa: Vengi conquest by Pulakesin II created the **Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi**, capital **Pithapuram**.
Before the conquest Vengi was held by the **Durjaya** dynasty.
**Kubja Vishnuvardhana**: appointed **617 CE**, independent **624 CE**.

73.s: The first epigraphic reference to Guntur, as Kumturu, is found in the Pune copper plates of
73.x: The Pune copper plates of Eastern Chalukya Vishnuvardhana II, dated 669 CE, contain the first epigraphic reference to Guntur as Kumturu.
73.tq: Separate the similarly named Vishnuvardhana rulers by linking the record to the specific copper plates.
xs: The first epigraphic reference to **Guntur** (as **Kumturu**) is in the **Pune copper plates** of Eastern Chalukya **Vishnuvardhana II**, **669 CE** — option **(1)**.
**Kubja Vishnuvardhana** was the first Eastern Chalukya; his inscriptions are **Chipurupalli, Kopparam, Chejarala, Timmapuram**.
xa: Name evolution: **Kumturu → Gomturu → Gunturu**.
Source: **ASI Epigraphy**.
Mangalagiri appears as "**Mangalapura**" in the **Marturu** inscription of Pulakesin II.

73.s: Which pair correctly represents the first and last rulers in the specified Chalukya context?
o: First South Indian issuer of gold coins—Mangalesha; last Badami Chalukya ruler—Pulakesin II
First South Indian issuer of gold coins—Pulakesin I; last Badami Chalukya ruler—Dantidurga
First South Indian issuer of gold coins—Kirtivarman I; last Badami Chalukya ruler—Vikramaditya I
First South Indian issuer of gold coins—Pulakesin II; last Badami Chalukya ruler—Kirtivarman II
73.x: Pulakesin II is identified as the first South Indian king to issue gold coins, while Kirtivarman II was the last ruler of the Badami Chalukya dynasty.
73.tq: Separate the first-achievement fact from the last-ruler fact before matching the pair.
xs: First South Indian king to issue **gold coins** = **Pulakesin II**; last Badami Chalukya ruler = **Kirtivarman II** — option **(4)**.
**Dantidurga** overthrew Kirtivarman II and founded the **Rashtrakutas**; he was not a Chalukya.
xa: Kirtivarman II fell c. **753-757 CE**; dynasty span c. **543-757 CE**.
Pulakesin II reigned **609-642 CE**, titles **Dakshinapatheshwara** and **Paramesvara**.
Founder: **Pulakesin I**, capital **Badami**.

73.s: The Badami Chalukyas ruled approximately during which period?
73.x: The Badami (Vatapi) Chalukyas ruled from about 543 CE, under Pulakeshin I, to 753 CE, when Dantidurga overthrew Kirtivarman II. The other ranges are reigns of single kings: Vikramaditya I, Pulakeshin II and Kirtivarman II.
73.tq: Discriminate the dynasty's span from individual reigns.
n: The Badami Chalukya dynasty existed from c. 543 to 753 CE. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
The Badami Chalukya dynasty was also called the Chalukyas of Badami. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
The Badami Chalukya dynasty was also called the Vatapi Chalukyas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
xs: The Badami Chalukyas ruled **c. 543–753 CE** — option **(2)**.
They began with **Pulakeshin I** (c. **543**) and ended when **Dantidurga** overthrew **Kirtivarman II**.
The other ranges are single reigns: **Vikramaditya I** (c. **655-680**), **Pulakeshin II** (**610-642**), **Kirtivarman II** (c. **746-753**).
xa: ⚠ Other notes give the span as c. **543-757 CE**.
Capital **Vatapi** = present-day **Badami**, **Bagalkot**, Karnataka.
Their rule was mainly confined to the **Deccan** and **Southern India**.
**Vikramaditya II** (c. **733-746**) captured **Kanchi** three times.

xa: Mangalesha made the **earliest rock-cut caves at Badami**.

73.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Vatapi was the capital of the Badami Chalukyas.
The Badami Chalukyas ruled mainly in the Deccan and Southern India.
Kanchi was the capital of the Badami Chalukyas.
Vatapi is identified with present-day Badami in Bagalkot, Karnataka.

Bharavi is mentioned in the Aihole Inscription. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
Ravikirti compared his fame with the fame of Kalidasa and Bharavi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
xs: **Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A** — option **(1)**.
A is true: the **Aihole Inscription** mentions **Kalidasa** and **Bharavi**.
R is true: its composer **Ravikirti** **compared his fame** with theirs, which is why they are named.
xa: It is in **Sanskrit** and **Southern Brahmi**, dated **634 CE** (Saka era).
It is preserved at the **Meguti Jain Temple**, Aihole.
Ravikirti was the **Jain court poet** of Pulakesin II.
It lists Pulakesin II's victories over **Harsha**, Kadambas, Gangas, **Kalinga**, **Pishtapura**.

73.s: Which inscription of 630 CE does not mention Harsha among the defeated enemies of Pulakeshin II?
73.x: The Lohnara inscription of 630 CE lists enemies defeated by Pulakeshin II but does not include Harsha. The Aihole inscription of 634 CE does record his victory over Harsha.
73.tq: Discriminate the Lohnara inscription from the Aihole inscription.
n: The Lohnara inscription dates to 630 CE. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
The Lohnara inscription does not mention Harsha among the defeated enemies. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
Pulakeshin II and Harsha were an important enemy pair. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
xs: The **Lohnara inscription** (**630 CE**) does **not mention Harsha** among the defeated enemies — option **(4)**.
The **Aihole inscription** (**634 CE**), at the **Meguti** temple, does record the victory over Harsha.
The **Madapura Lake** inscription concerns **Vikramaditya I** and land grants.
xa: Pulakeshin II stopped Harsha on the **Narmada** (**630–634 CE**).
Title after that war: **Paramesvara**.
Other titles: **Satyashraya, Prithvivallabha**.
Pulakeshin II reigned **609-642 CE**.

73.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding the Pallava conflict with the Badami Chalukyas?
o: Narasimhavarman I captured and destroyed Vatapi in 642 CE.
Narasimhavarman I restored Chalukya power after the Pallava invasion.
Narasimhavarman I assumed the title Vatapikonda.
Narasimhavarman I was a Pallava king.
73.x: Option B is incorrect: it was the Chalukya Vikramaditya I who restored Chalukya power. The Pallava Narasimhavarman I captured and destroyed Vatapi in 642 CE and took the title Vatapikonda.
73.tq: Discriminate the Pallava conqueror from the Chalukya restorer.
n: Pallava king Narasimhavarman I captured Vatapi in 642 CE. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
Narasimhavarman I destroyed Vatapi in 642 CE. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
Narasimhavarman I assumed the title Vatapikonda. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
Vikramaditya I restored Chalukya power after the Pallava invasion. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
xs: The incorrect statement is that **Narasimhavarman I restored Chalukya power** — option **(2)**.
It was the Chalukya **Vikramaditya I** who **restored Chalukya power** after the Pallava invasion.
The others are correct: Pallava **Narasimhavarman I** captured and destroyed **Vatapi** in **642 CE** and took the title **Vatapikonda**.
xa: **Narasimhavarman I** and **Pulakeshin II** were an important enemy pair.
Pulakeshin II and **Harsha** were the other enemy pair.
**Kirtivarman II** was the **last ruler**, overthrown by **Dantidurga**.
**Vikramaditya II** defeated the Pallavas **three times**.

73.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Badami or Vatapi
(b) Kanchi
(c) Tanjore
(d) Narmada

List-II
(i) Cholas
(ii) Pallavas
(iii) Chalukyas
(iv) Site of Pulakeshin II's conflict with Harsha
73.x: Badami (Vatapi) was the Chalukya capital, Kanchi the Pallava capital, Tanjore the Chola capital, and the Narmada the site where Pulakeshin II checked Harsha, giving a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv.
73.tq: Match each place with its dynasty or event.
n: Pulakeshin II defeated or stopped Harshavardhana on the Narmada. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
Badami and Vatapi were associated with the Chalukyas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
Kanchi was associated with the Pallavas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
Tanjore was associated with the Cholas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
Pulakeshin II and Harsha were an important enemy pair. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv** — option **(4)**.
**Badami / Vatapi** → **Chalukyas**; **Kanchi** → **Pallavas**.
**Tanjore** → **Cholas**; **Narmada** → site of Pulakeshin II's conflict with **Harsha**.
xa: Vatapi was destroyed by **Narasimhavarman I** in **642 CE**.
**Vengi**: **Kubja Vishnuvardhana** appointed in **617 CE**, independent in **624 CE**.
The **Maruturu and Kopparam** inscriptions record victory over Pallava **Mahendravarman I**.
Mangalagiri = "**Mangalapura**" — Marturu (APPSC-GS 2018) vs Kopparam (APPSC G2 2019).

73.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Aihole inscription is incorrect?
o: It is a key source for the history of Pulakeshin II.
It was written in Prakrit and Southern Brahmi.
It was written in Sanskrit and Southern Brahmi.
73.x: Option B is incorrect: the Aihole inscription is in Sanskrit, not Prakrit, written in Southern Brahmi. It was composed by Ravikirti and is the key source for Pulakeshin II.
73.tq: Check the language of the inscription.
n: The Aihole Inscription is a key source for Pulakeshin II. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
Ravikirti composed the Aihole Inscription. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
The Aihole Inscription is in Sanskrit and Southern Brahmi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
xs: The incorrect statement is that the Aihole inscription was in **Prakrit and Southern Brahmi** — option **(2)**.
It is in **Sanskrit** and **Southern Brahmi**.
The others are correct: it is a **key source** for **Pulakeshin II** and was **composed by Ravikirti**.
xa: Dated **634 CE** by the **Saka era**; preserved at the **Meguti Jain Temple**.
It names **Kalidasa** and **Bharavi**.
It calls **Kirtivarman I** "the night of doom" to Nalas, Mauryas and Kadambas.
⚠ **Ravikirti** = poet; **Gunda Anivaritachari** = architect.

74.s: The Aihole inscription recording the Narmada victory of Pulakesin II belongs to which year?
74.x: The Aihole record is dated 634 CE. It was composed by Ravikirti and records the defeat of Harsha.
74.tq: Distinguish the date of the inscription from dates associated with Harsha's reign and the battle.
xs: The **Aihole inscription** recording the Narmada victory is dated **634 CE** — option **(3)**.
**618** is the date of the battle itself (JPSC 2016 key), not of the record.
It was composed by **Ravikirti**.
xa: ⚠ Since Aihole (634 CE) records the battle, the **637** date in some notes cannot be right — the battle must be earlier.
**Hiuen Tsang's** account confirms Harsha's defeat.
Victor **Pulakesin II** (UPPSC 2016); river **Narmada** (UPSC 2003).

74.s:
The account of the conflict between Pulakesin II and Harsha is found in which of the following sources?
1. Aihole inscription composed by Ravikirti
2. Account of Hiuen Tsang
3. Kailasanatha temple inscription of Kanchi
Which of the statements given above are correct?
74.x: The Aihole inscription of Pulakesin II, composed by Ravikirti, and Hiuen Tsang’s account confirm the conflict. The Kailasanatha temple inscription is not the cited source for this event.
74.tq: Split the options by identifying the two sources directly associated with the event.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: the **Aihole inscription** by **Ravikirti** records the conflict.
Statement 2 is **correct**: **Hiuen Tsang's** account confirms it.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: the **Kailasanatha** temple at Kanchi carries **Vikramaditya II**'s **Kannada inscription** from his occupation of Kanchi — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(3)**.
xa: Battle date: **618 CE** (JPSC 2016 key); must predate **634 CE**.
Victor: **Pulakesin II** (UPPSC 2016).
Titles from this war: **Paramesvara** and **Dakshinapatheshwara**.

74.s: Pulakesin II assumed the title ‘Paramesvara’ after his conflict with Harsha. He was also styled as:
