**Kubja Vishnuvardhana** was the **founder**; **Rajaraja Narendra** the patron of **Nannaya**; **Chalukya Bhima I** built the **Pancharamas**.
xa: Title: **Tripura Martya Maheshwara** — for victories over **Kiranapuram, Achalapuram and Kandukur**.
He developed **Kandukuru as Bejawada** and built the **Bikkavolu** Shiva temples.
His commander **Panduranga** issued the **Addanki inscription**.

78.s: What was the official language of the Eastern Chalukyas, used in most of their about 100 donation inscriptions?
78.x: Sanskrit was the official language, and most of the about 100 donation inscriptions are in Sanskrit. Telugu rose later as a literary language under their patronage; Prakrit and Kannada were not their official language.
78.tq: Official = Sanskrit; literary rise = Telugu.
xs: The official language was **Sanskrit** — option **(3)**; most of the about **100** donation inscriptions are in Sanskrit.
**Telugu** rose later as the literary language, under **Rajaraja Narendra**'s patronage of **Nannaya**.
xa: **Addanki** = first Telugu **verse** inscription; **Kalamalla** (c. **575 CE**) = first Telugu inscription.
Emblem: **Boar (Varaha)**.
They turned Telugu into a **literary language**.

78.s: Which of the following correctly describes the contribution of Vishnuvardhana III?
o: He founded the Rajaraja temple at Bikkavolu.
He gave Mushikonda village to the Jains.
He defeated Satyasraya with Chola assistance.
78.x: Vishnuvardhana III patronised Vedic and Jain faiths and granted Mushikonda village to the Jains.
78.tq: Avoid the ruler–achievement swap by linking the grant to Vishnuvardhana III.
xs: **Vishnuvardhana III** gave **Mushikonda** village to the **Jains** — option **(3)**; he patronised **Vedic and Jain** faiths.
**Pancharamas** = **Chalukya Bhima I**; **Rajaraja temple, Bikkavolu** = **Rajaraja Narendra**; beating **Satyasraya** with Chola help = **Saktivarman I** (**1006**).
xa: He took the throne back from **Kokkili**, who then set up the **Yalamanchili** kingdom.
APP gives him the titles **Tribhuvanankusa, Samasta Bhuvanashraya** (with Jayasimha I).
**Potla Cheruvu** was a popular Jain centre of the period.

78.s:
With reference to Chalukya Bhima I, consider the following statements:
1. He is credited with 360 battles in the Pithapuram inscription of Mallappadeva.
2. He ruled for 30 years.
3. He built the Pancharamas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: All three statements are associated with Chalukya Bhima I: the 360 battles, a 30-year reign and the construction of the Pancharamas.
78.tq: Combine the numerical, duration and architectural clues belonging to one ruler.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **360 battles** per **Mallappadeva's Pithapuram inscription**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: he ruled **30 years**.
Statement 3 is **correct**: he built the **Pancharamas** — so all three, option **(4)**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes credit the **360 battles** to **Gunaga Vijayaditya**.
Title: **Kollabhiganda** (G2 2012 key).
He repelled **Krishna II** at **Niravadyapura and Peruvanguru**; **Kakumanu** inscription names a **Setti Shreshthi**.

78.s: The Addanki inscription was issued by Panduranga, the commander of:
78.x: Panduranga, the commander of Gunaga Vijayaditya III, issued the Addanki inscription.
78.tq: Identify the subordinate–ruler relationship instead of attributing the inscription directly to a king.
xs: The **Addanki inscription** was issued by **Panduranga**, commander of **Gunaga Vijayaditya III** — option **(2)**.
It is the **first Telugu verse inscription**.
xa: ⚠ **Addanki** = first Telugu **verse** inscription; **Kalamalla** (c. **575 CE**, Renati Choda **Dhananjaya**) = first Telugu inscription.
Gunaga Vijayaditya III = **greatest** Eastern Chalukya (APHQ 2011).
He defeated **Krishna II** and Kalinga king **Devendravarma**.

78.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Kubja Vishnuvardhana declared independence
B. Saktivarman I defeated Satyasraya
C. Rajaraja Narendra was crowned
D. Vijayaditya VII was ousted by Rajendra Chalukya
78.x: The events occurred in 624 CE, 1006 CE, 1022 CE and 1070 CE respectively.
78.tq: Place the events by their dates before comparing the middle positions.
xs: Order **A, B, C, D** — option **(1)**.
**Kubja Vishnuvardhana** declared independence in **624 CE**; **Saktivarman I** beat Satyasraya's army in **1006**.
**Rajaraja Narendra** was crowned **16 August 1022**; **Rajendra Chalukya** ousted **Vijayaditya VII** in **1070**.
xa: Vimaladitya was crowned in **May 1011**.
**Koppam (1053)**: Rajadhiraja I killed by **Ahavamalla Someshwara**.
Line ends with **Vijayaditya VII**'s death in **1075**.

78.s: Vijayaditya VII, the last ruler of the Eastern Chalukyas, was ousted in 1070 CE by:
o: Rajendra Chalukya, later known as Kulottunga I
78.x: Rajendra Chalukya ousted Vijayaditya VII in 1070 CE and later became known as Kulottunga I.
78.tq: Identify the successor’s alternate name to avoid a person–title confusion.
xs: **Vijayaditya VII** was ousted in **1070** by **Rajendra Chalukya**, later **Kulottunga I** — option **(2)**.
**Jatachoda Bhima** killed Danarnava earlier; **Satyasraya** attacked Vengi in **1006**; **Rajaraja Chola I** was Kundavva's father.
xa: Vijayaditya VII (**1070-1075**) was the last ruler; his death in **1075** = end of the line.
He was the son of **Melama**, backed by **Kalyani Jayasimha II** in the succession war.
First Chalukya-Chola king = **Kulothunga I**; end date debated: **1075**, or **1189 CE** counting the Chalukya-Chola phase.

78.s: Who seized Vengi after killing Danarnava during the interlude in Eastern Chalukya history?
78.x: The Telugu Choda ruler Jatachoda Bhima killed Danarnava and seized Vengi until Danarnava’s sons recovered it with Chola assistance.
78.tq: Track the succession interruption through the killer and the displaced ruler.
xs: **Jatachoda Bhima**, Telugu Choda of **Pedakallu**, killed **Danarnava** and occupied Vengi — option **(4)**.
**Kokkili** was the rival of **Vishnuvardhana III**; **Satyasraya** was the Kalyani king of **1006**.
xa: Danarnava's sons **Saktivarma I** and **Vimaladitya** fled to **Rajaraja Chola**.
They recovered Vengi with **Chola** help.
Vimaladitya later married **Melama**, daughter of Jatachoda Bhima.

78.s: Which of the following is the correct sequence of capitals of the Eastern Chalukyas in the order stated for their early and later rulers?
78.x: Kubja Vishnuvardhana used Pithapuram as the first capital, Jayasimha Vallabha I used Vengi, and Rajamahendravaram was associated with Amma I and Rajaraja Narendra.
78.tq: Order capitals by ruler association rather than by present-day prominence.
xs: Sequence **Pithapuram → Vengi → Rajamahendravaram** — option **(1)**.
**Kubja Vishnuvardhana**: Pithapuram; **Jayasimha I**: Vengi; **Ammaraja I**: Rajamahendravaram, later beautified by **Rajaraja Narendra**.
xa: ⚠ Sources differ: another sequence is **Vengipura (Pedavegi) → Rajahmundry → Pithapuram → Vengi** again.
Vengi = **Pedavegi, near Eluru**.
APPSC G2 2008 key: Rajaraja Narendra "**built Rajahmundry**".

78.s: Which one of the following title–ruler pairs is NOT correctly matched?
78.x: Chalukya Chandra was the title of Saktivarma I, not Vimaladitya. Vimaladitya bore the titles Rajamartanda and Mummadi Bhima.
78.tq: Find the swapped ruler in a title table, especially where two rulers belong to the same dynastic phase.
xs: **Chalukya Chandra — Vimaladitya** is wrong — option **(1)**: Chalukya Chandra was **Saktivarman I**.
Vimaladitya's titles were **Rajamartanda** and **Mummadi Bhima**.
The others are right: **Narendramrigaraja** — Vijayaditya II; **Rajamahendra** — Ammaraja I; **Vishamasiddhi** — Kubja Vishnuvardhana.
xa: **Kollabhiganda** — **Chalukya Bhima I** (G2 2012 key).
**Tripura Martya Maheshwara** — **Gunaga Vijayaditya III**.
**Rajaraja Narendra**: Kavyageetha Priyudu, Rajarajanarayana, Baraganda Bhairava.

78.s: According to the APPSC key, the victories commemorated by the title Tripura-martya-Maheswara were over
78.x: The APPSC key identifies Kiranapuram, Achalapuram and Kandukur as the three cities. This triplet is associated with Gunaga Vijayaditya III's title Tripura-martya-Maheswara.
78.tq: Use the officially keyed triplet and distinguish it from the commonly confused alternative list.
xs: APPSC key: **Kiranapuram, Achalapuram and Kandukur** — option **(3)**.
The title **Tripura-martya-Maheswara** belongs to **Gunaga Vijayaditya III** (G2 2012 key).
⚠ Some notes give **Nellore, Kiranapura, Achalapura** — the favourite distractor; follow the key.
xa: **Dharanikota, Kollipaka, Koppam** relate to **Rajadhiraja I**'s campaign (**1053**).
Gunaga Vijayaditya III developed **Kandukuru as Bejawada**.

78.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Chalukya Bhima — Kollabhiganda
2. Saktivarma I — Chalukya Chandra
3. Vimaladitya — Rajamartanda
4. Rajaraja Narendra — Rajarajanarayana
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
78.x: All four pairs are correct. Chalukya Bhima was associated with Kollabhiganda, Saktivarma I with Chalukya Chandra, Vimaladitya with Rajamartanda, and Rajaraja Narendra with Rajarajanarayana.
78.tq: Verify each title pair independently and watch for the common Kollabhiganda attribution trap.
xs: Pair 1 **correct**: **Chalukya Bhima — Kollabhiganda** (G2 2012 key).
Pair 2 **correct**: **Saktivarma I — Chalukya Chandra**; pair 3 **correct**: **Vimaladitya — Rajamartanda**.
Pair 4 **correct**: **Rajaraja Narendra — Rajarajanarayana** — so all four, option **(4)**.
xa: Vimaladitya also bore **Mummadi Bhima**.
Rajaraja Narendra also: **Kavyageetha Priyudu**, **Baraganda Bhairava**.
⚠ Some notes give **Kollabhiganda** to **Vijayaditya IV**.

78.s: According to the APPSC key, the title 'Kollabhiganda' belongs to which Eastern Chalukya ruler?
78.x: The key (G2 2012) credits Kollabhiganda to Chalukya Bhima I. Some sources give it to Vijayaditya IV, who ruled six months after Bhima: that is the trap. Ammaraja I bore Rajamahendra and Gunaga Vijayaditya III bore Tripura Martya Maheshwara.
78.tq: Kollabhiganda = Chalukya Bhima I; follow the key.
xs: The APPSC key (G2 2012) gives **Kollabhiganda** to **Chalukya Bhima I** — option **(2)**.
⚠ Trap: some notes give it to **Vijayaditya IV**, who ruled **six months** after Chalukya Bhima; also a princess Kollabhiganda.
**Ammaraja I** = **Rajamahendra**; **Gunaga Vijayaditya III** = **Tripura Martya Maheshwara**.
xa: Chalukya Bhima I built the **Pancharamas** and ruled **30 years**.
**360 battles** per Mallappadeva's **Pithapuram** inscription.

78.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Vishnuvardhana IV:
1. He backed Govinda III in the Rashtrakuta succession war.
2. He was defeated by Dhruva.
3. Dhruva married his daughter Sheela Mahadevi.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: All three statements are correct. Vishnuvardhana IV supported Govinda III, was defeated by Dhruva, and strengthened the relationship through Dhruva's marriage to Sheela Mahadevi.
78.tq: Combine the ruler, opponent and marriage-alliance facts before selecting the coded combination.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **Vishnuvardhana IV** backed **Govinda III** in the Rashtrakuta succession war.
Statement 2 is **correct**: he was defeated by **Dhruva**.
Statement 3 is **correct**: Dhruva married his daughter **Sheela Mahadevi** — the alliance saved his kingdom — so all three, option **(4)**.
xa: The Rashtrakuta conflict began under **Vijayaditya I** with **Dantidurga**.
**Vijayaditya II** fought **Amoghavarsha**; **Gunaga Vijayaditya** defeated **Krishna II**.

78.s: Vijayaditya II is traditionally associated with which of the following achievements?
o: Winning 18 battles in one regnal year
78.x: Vijayaditya II is traditionally said to have fought 108 battles in 12 years. The 108 temples were commemorative constructions associated with these victories.
78.tq: Match the distinctive number with the correct activity rather than with a related monument or inscription.
xs: **Vijayaditya II** traditionally fought **108 battles in 12 years** — option **(3)**.
He built **108 Shiva temples** (not Buddhist monasteries) to commemorate the victories (APPSC G2 2019).
xa: Title: **Narendramrigaraja**.
Opponent: Rashtrakuta **Amoghavarsha**.
Temples recorded in the **Sataluru** inscription.

78.s: After 973 CE, the principal rival of the Eastern Chalukyas was the
78.x: After 973 CE, the Kalyani Chalukyas emerged as the principal rival of the Eastern Chalukyas. Satyasraya and Someshvara I are associated with this later phase.
78.tq: Identify the change in the rival dynasty by using the chronological marker.
xs: After **973 CE** the main rival was the **Kalyani Chalukyas** — option **(4)**.
Kalyani kings involved: **Satyasraya** (**1006**) and **Someshvara I**.
xa: **Saktivarma I** beat Satyasraya's general **Bayyalanambi** with Chola help.
In the succession war **Kalyani Jayasimha II** backed **Vijayaditya VII**.
After **Koppam (1053)** Rajaraja Narendra had to accept **Kalyani suzerainty**.

78.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
78.x: Chalukya Bhima I fought Krishna II, not Dhruva. Vijayaditya II fought the Rashtrakutas under Amoghavarsha, while Gunaga Vijayaditya defeated Krishna II and the Kalinga king Devendravarma.
78.tq: Find the swapped opponent, a standard ruler-with-deed trap.
xs: **Chalukya Bhima I — Dhruva** is wrong — option **(4)**: Chalukya Bhima I repelled **Krishna II**; **Dhruva** defeated **Vishnuvardhana IV**.
The others are right: **Gunaga Vijayaditya** defeated **Devendravarma** and **Krishna II**; **Vijayaditya II** fought **Amoghavarsha**.
xa: Dhruva married Vishnuvardhana IV's daughter **Sheela Mahadevi**.
Chalukya Bhima I repelled Krishna II at **Niravadyapura and Peruvanguru**.

78.s: In 1006 CE, Satyasraya sent Bayyalanambi against Vengi. Who defeated Bayyalanambi?
o: Vijayaditya VII with Rajendra Chola's assistance
78.x: Saktivarma I defeated Bayyalanambi with Chola help in 1006 CE. Satyasraya of the Kalyani Chalukyas had sent Bayyalanambi against Vengi.
78.tq: Track the combatant, the opposing commander and the external support separately.
xs: **Saktivarma I** beat **Bayyalanambi** with **Chola** help in **1006** — option **(4)**.
Bayyalanambi was sent by **Satyasraya** of Kalyani.
xa: Saktivarma's coins are found in **Arakan (Burma)**.
He and **Vimaladitya** had recovered Vengi from **Jatachoda Bhima** with Chola help.
Title: **Chalukya Chandra**.

78.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Vimaladitya — Kundavva, daughter of Rajaraja Chola I
2. Vimaladitya — Melama, daughter of Jatachoda Bhima
3. Rajaraja Narendra — Ammanga Devi, daughter of Rajendra Chola
Which of the pairs given above are correct?
78.x: All three pairs are correct. Vimaladitya married both Kundavva and Melama, while Rajaraja Narendra married Ammanga Devi, the daughter of Rajendra Chola.
78.tq: Check each marriage independently because the same ruler is linked with two different marital alliances.
xs: Pair 1 **correct**: **Vimaladitya — Kundavva**, daughter of **Rajaraja Chola I**.
Pair 2 **correct**: Vimaladitya also married **Melama**, daughter of **Jatachoda Bhima**.
Pair 3 **correct**: **Rajaraja Narendra — Ammanga Devi**, daughter of **Rajendra Chola** — so all three, option **(4)**.
xa: ⚠ Kundavva's son = **Rajaraja Narendra**; Melama's son = **Vijayaditya VII**.
Rajaraja Narendra crowned **16 August 1022**.

78.s: Who supported Rajaraja Narendra in his succession war against Vijayaditya VII?
78.x: Rajaraja Narendra, the son of Kundavva, was supported by Rajendra I. Vijayaditya VII, the son of Melama, was supported by Kalyani Jayasimha II.
78.tq: Distinguish the two rival claimants by matching each with his external supporter.
xs: **Rajaraja Narendra** (son of Kundavva) was backed by **Rajendra I** — option **(1)**.
**Vijayaditya VII** (son of Melama) was backed by **Kalyani Jayasimha II**.
**Satyasraya** attacked in **1006**; **Ahavamalla Someshwara** killed Rajadhiraja I at Koppam.
xa: Rajaraja Narendra was crowned **16 August 1022**.
He married **Ammanga Devi**, daughter of Rajendra Chola.
After **Koppam (1053)** he had to accept Kalyani suzerainty.

78.s: At Koppam in 1053, who killed Rajadhiraja I?
78.x: Ahavamalla Someshwara killed Rajadhiraja I at Koppam in 1053. Rajadhiraja had earlier won at Dharanikota and burnt Kollipaka.
78.tq: Match the battlefield casualty with the ruler responsible for the decisive reversal.
xs: At **Koppam (1053)**, **Ahavamalla Someshwara** killed **Rajadhiraja I** — option **(4)**.
Rajadhiraja I had earlier won at **Dharanikota** and burnt **Kollipaka**.
xa: Result: **Rajaraja Narendra** had to accept **Kalyani suzerainty**.
**Jayasimha II** of Kalyani had backed **Vijayaditya VII**.
**Satyasraya** was the Kalyani king of **1006**.

78.s: Who among the following developed Kandukuru as another ‘Bejawada’?
o: Vijayaditya III, also known as Gunaga Vijayaditya
78.x: Vijayaditya III, or Gunaga Vijayaditya, developed Kandukuru as another Bejawada.
78.tq: Distinguish the ruler associated with town development from rulers linked with capitals.
xs: **Vijayaditya III (Gunaga Vijayaditya)** developed **Kandukuru** as another "**Bejawada**" — option **(4)** (APPSC G2 2019 key).
**Kubja Vishnuvardhana** = Pithapuram; **Jayasimha Vallabha I** = Vengi; **Ammaraja I** = Rajamahendravaram.
xa: **Vijayawada** was developed by **Yuddhamalla** (CDX); APP says Bezawada took the name after Vijayaditya.
Gunaga Vijayaditya III: **greatest** king; **Bikkavolu** temples.

78.s: The capital of the Eastern Chalukyas was shifted to Vengi by
78.x: Jayasimha Vallabha I shifted the capital from Pithapuram to Vengi, identified with Pedavegi.
78.tq: Match a capital change with the ruler responsible for it.
xs: **Jayasimha Vallabha I** shifted the capital to **Vengi** (Pedavegi, near Eluru) — option **(4)**.
**Kubja Vishnuvardhana** ruled from **Pithapuram**; **Amma I** made **Rajamahendravaram** capital.
xa: Jayasimha I issued the **Vipparla inscription** (G2 2017 key).
Title: **Samastha Bhuvanashraya**.
Core territory: **Venginadu** (Krishna-Godavari doab).

78.s:
Consider the following statements about Rajamahendravaram (Rajahmundry):
1. Ammaraja I made it his capital.
2. Rajaraja Narendra ruled from it and beautified it.
3. Jayasimha Vallabha I shifted the capital from Pithapuram to Rajamahendravaram.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Ammaraja I made Rajamahendravaram his capital and Rajaraja Narendra ruled from it and made it famous (the G2 2008 key says he 'built Rajahmundry'). Statement 3 is wrong: Jayasimha Vallabha I shifted the capital to Vengi. So B; A misses 2, C and D include the false 3.
78.tq: Pithapuram (Kubja) -> Vengi (Jayasimha I) -> Rajamahendravaram (Amma I, RRN).
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **Ammaraja I** made **Rajamahendravaram** his capital.
Statement 2 is **correct**: **Rajaraja Narendra** ruled from it and beautified it (G2 2008 key: "built Rajahmundry").
Statement 3 is **wrong**: **Jayasimha Vallabha I** shifted the capital to **Vengi** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Ammaraja I's title: **Rajamahendra**; **Chekurru** copper plate.
Rajaraja Narendra built a **Vishnu temple** at Rajahmundry.

78.s: In Dandin's Dashakumaracharita, Vengi is referred to as
78.x: Dandin calls Vengi 'Andhra Nagaram'. Mangalapura is Mangalagiri in the Kopparam inscription, Pishtapura is Pithapuram, and Rajamahendra is a title of Ammaraja I.
78.tq: Dandin: Vengi = Andhra Nagaram.
xs: **Dandin**'s **Dashakumaracharita** calls Vengi "**Andhra Nagaram**" — option **(2)**.
**Mangalapura** = Mangalagiri (Kopparam inscription); **Pishtapura** = Pithapuram; **Rajamahendra** = Ammaraja I's title.
xa: Vengi = **Pedavegi**, near **Eluru**.
Capital moved to Vengi by **Jayasimha Vallabha I**.

78.s: The Addanki inscription is notable because it is associated with
o: Pandaranga and the first Telugu verse inscription
Chalukya Bhima I's military victory at Peruvanguru
Rajaraja Narendra's grant to Narayana Bhattu
78.x: The Addanki inscription is associated with Pandaranga, the general of Gunaga Vijayaditya III, and is regarded as the first Telugu verse inscription.
78.tq: Identify the record through its unique person-and-content combination.
xs: **Addanki** is linked with **Pandaranga** (general of Gunaga Vijayaditya III) and is the **first Telugu verse inscription** — option **(1)**.
Kubja's **18th** regnal year = **Chipurupalli**; Peruvanguru = Chalukya Bhima I; grant to Narayana Bhattu = **Nandampudi**.
xa: ⚠ **Kalamalla** (c. **575 CE**, Renati Choda Dhananjaya) = first Telugu inscription.
Kalamalla **predates Nannaya**.
**Magallu inscription** first mentions the **Kakatiyas**.

78.s:
Which of the following inscription–ruler pairs is correctly matched?
1. Kakumanu — Chalukya Bhima I
2. Nandampudi — Rajaraja Narendra
3. Korumelli plates — Rajaraja Narendra
4. Vipparla — Jayasimha Vallabha
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
78.x: All four pairs are correct. The Nandampudi inscription records Rajaraja Narendra's grant to Narayana Bhattu, written by Nannaya, and the Korumelli plates are also associated with Rajaraja Narendra.
78.tq: Confirm the sure inscription pairs first and then test the remaining records individually.
xs: Pair 1 **correct**: **Kakumanu — Chalukya Bhima I** (names a Setti Shreshthi).
Pairs 2 and 3 **correct**: **Nandampudi** and **Korumelli plates** — **Rajaraja Narendra**.
Pair 4 **correct**: **Vipparla — Jayasimha Vallabha** — so all four, option **(4)**.
xa: **Nandampudi**: grant to **Narayana Bhattu**, written by **Nannaya**.
⚠ APPSC G2 2017 key marked Nannaya as the **donee** — know both.
**Sataluru** = Vijayaditya II; **Chekurru** = Ammaraja I.

78.s: Who among the following is associated with the Kaluchumbarru grant for a Jain temple?
78.x: Chamekamba, a courtesan during the reign of Ammaraja II, secured the Kaluchumbarru grant for a Jain temple.
78.tq: Test an unusual person–grant association, a common source of identity traps.
xs: **Chamekamba**, courtesan under **Ammaraja II**, won the **Kaluchumbarru** grant for a Jain temple — option **(4)**.
**Ayyana Mahadevi** built the Jain **Nedumba (Nadumbi) Vasati** near Vijayawada; **Kundavva** was the Chola mother of Rajaraja Narendra.
xa: ⚠ Ayyana Mahadevi = queen of **Kubja Vishnuvardhana** per G2 2025 key (some notes: Gunaga Vijayaditya III).
**Vishnuvardhana III** granted **Mushikonda** to Jains; **Potla Cheruvu** was a popular Jain centre.
Mother goddess: **Kushmandini** (APPSC G2 2019 key).

78.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
78.x: Kushmandini was the mother goddess of the Eastern Chalukyas (APPSC G2 2019 key). Hariti-putra is a matronymic, not a goddess; Kalyanakaraka is Ugradityacharya's medical treatise, not a Shaiva school (the Shaiva sects were Kapalika, Kalamukha and Pasupata); and the leading Jain centre was Potlacheruvu.
78.tq: Separate a deity name from a dynastic title, text and place name.
xs: The Eastern Chalukya **mother goddess** was **Kushmandini** — option **(1)** (APPSC G2 2019 key).
**Hariti Putra** is a **matronymic** used in inscriptions, not a goddess.
**Kalyanakaraka** is **Ugradityacharya**'s work on **medicine**, not a Shaiva school; the popular Jain centre was **Potla Cheruvu**.
xa: Faith: **Shaivism** dominant (**108 Shaivalayas**); **Kapalikas** emerged from the **Misra Saivam** school.
Policy: mainly Shaiva but tolerant — patronised **Jainism + Buddhism**.
Jain patrons: **Ayyana Mahadevi** (Nedumba Vasati), **Chamekamba** (Kaluchumbarru grant), **Vishnuvardhana III** (Mushikonda).

78.s: As per the APPSC Group 2 (2025) key, Ayyana Mahadevi, who built the Jain Nedumba (Nadumbi) Vasati near Vijayawada, was the queen of
78.x: The 2025 key makes Ayyana Mahadevi the queen of Kubja Vishnuvardhana. Some sources say Gunaga Vijayaditya III, but the key disagrees. Ammaraja II is linked to Chamekamba and the Kaluchumbarru grant; Vimaladitya married Kundavai.
78.tq: Nedumba Vasati = Ayyana Mahadevi, queen of Kubja (key).
xs: Per the **G2 2025** key, **Ayyana Mahadevi** was queen of **Kubja Vishnuvardhana** — option **(2)**.
She built the Jain **Nedumba (Nadumbi) Vasati** near/at **Vijayawada**.
⚠ Some notes make her queen of **Gunaga Vijayaditya III** — the official key disagrees.
xa: **Chamekamba**, courtesan under **Ammaraja II**, won the **Kaluchumbarru** grant for a Jain temple.
**Vimaladitya** married **Kundavva** and **Melama**.
Kubja also built the **Kunti Madhava** temple, Pithapuram.

78.s: Kunti Madhava temple at Pithapuram is associated with which ruler?
78.x: Kubja Vishnuvardhana is credited with the Kunti Madhava temple at Pithapuram.
78.tq: Use the temple–builder pair rather than confusing it with later Vengi temples.
xs: The **Kunti Madhava** temple at **Pithapuram** is credited to **Kubja Vishnuvardhana** — option **(2)**.
**Rajaraja Narendra** built the **Rajaraja temple**, Bikkavolu; **Chalukya Bhima I** the **Bhimeswara** temples.
xa: Pithapuram (**Pishtapura**) was Kubja's **first capital**.
Kubja = founder; brother of **Pulakesin II**; independent in **624 CE**.
⚠ "108 Shaivalayas" → **Vijayaditya II**, not Kubja.

78.s:
Consider the following statements about Eastern Chalukya temple architecture:
1. It is described as the Vesara or Chalukya style, blending a Dravidian vimana with Buddhist influence.
2. The Vengi school built its temples mainly of local granite.
3. Vengi school temples stand on a raised jagati.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: Statement 1 is correct: the style is called Vesara/Chalukya, a Dravidian vimana with Buddhist influence. Statement 2 is wrong: the Vengi school used local sandstone, not granite. Statement 3 is correct: it uses a raised jagati. So 1 and 3 only (B); A and D include the false statement 2, C drops the true statement 1.
78.tq: Vengi school = Dravida + local sandstone + raised jagati; swap of the material is the trap.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **Vesara / Chalukya style** = Dravidian **vimana** + **Buddhist** influence.
Statement 2 is **wrong**: the **Vengi school** used **local sandstone**, not granite.
Statement 3 is **correct**: Vengi-school temples stand on a **raised jagati** — so **1 and 3 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: The Vengi school is described as **Dravida** style.
Key temples: **Pancharamas** (Bhimarama, Draksharama).
**Bikkavolu** temples: Gunaga Vijayaditya III; **Rajaraja temple**: Rajaraja Narendra.

78.s: Which group of temples at Bikkavolu is associated with Gunaga Vijayaditya III?
78.x: The Bikkavolu Shiva temples of Mukteshwara, Vijayeshwara and Chandrashekhara are attributed to Gunaga Vijayaditya III.
78.tq: Start from the sure temple group and match it to its builder.
xs: **Gunaga Vijayaditya III** built the **Bikkavolu** Shiva temples — **Mukteshwara, Vijayeshwara, Chandrashekhara** — option **(1)**.
**Kunti Madhava** = Kubja; **Bhimeswara** = Chalukya Bhima I; **Rajaraja temple**, Rajahmundry **Vishnu** temple and **Kalidindi** = Rajaraja Narendra.
xa: **Vijayeshwara** has carved **Ganga and Yamuna** figures.
Gunaga Vijayaditya III = **greatest** king (APHQ 2011).
He developed **Kandukuru as Bejawada**.

78.s: The Bhimeswara temples at Draksharama and Samalkot are attributed to:
78.x: The Bhimeswara temples at Draksharama and Samalkot, also called Chalukya Bhimavaram, are associated with Chalukya Bhima I.
78.tq: Distinguish the Bhimeswara temples from the separate 108-temple tradition.
xs: The **Bhimeswara** temples at **Draksharama** and **Samalkot (Chalukya Bhimavaram)** are attributed to **Chalukya Bhima I** — option **(2)**.
**Vijayaditya II** = **108 Shiva temples**; **Kubja** = **Kunti Madhava**; **Rajaraja Narendra** = Rajaraja temple.
xa: Chalukya Bhima I built the **Pancharamas** (Bhimarama, Draksharama).
He ruled **30 years**; **360 battles** per Mallappadeva's Pithapuram inscription.
Title: **Kollabhiganda**.

78.s: Which of the following is included among the Pancharamas associated with the Eastern Chalukya temple tradition?
78.x: Bhimarama and Draksharama are included among the key Pancharama temples mentioned in the Eastern Chalukya tradition.
78.tq: Recognise a Pancharama name rather than a nearby Bikkavolu or Pithapuram temple.
xs: **Bhimarama** is one of the **Pancharamas** — option **(4)**; **Draksharama** is another.
**Vijayeshwara** and **Chandrashekhara** are Bikkavolu temples; **Kunti Madhava** is at Pithapuram.
xa: The Pancharamas were built by **Chalukya Bhima I**.
**Bhimeswara** temples: **Draksharama** and **Samalkot**.
Dominant faith: **Shaivism**.

78.s: Which inscription records Vijayaditya II's association with 108 temples?
78.x: The Sataluru inscription records Vijayaditya II's association with the 108 temples. Addanki is associated with Pandaranga and the first Telugu verse inscription.
78.tq: Separate two inscription records by matching their distinctive content.
xs: The **Sataluru** inscription records **Vijayaditya II**'s **108 Shiva temples** ("**Narendra Mrigeswara**") — option **(3)**.
**Addanki** = Pandaranga (first Telugu verse inscription); **Cheepurupalli** = Kubja's 18th regnal year; **Kopparam** = Pulakesin II.
xa: Vijayaditya II fought **108 battles in 12 years** (APPSC G2 2019).
Title: **Narendramrigaraja**.
⚠ "108 Shaivalayas" → **Vijayaditya II**, not Kubja or Vishnuvardhana III/IV.

78.s: Nannaya Bhattaraka is regarded as the Adi Kavi of Telugu literature primarily because he
o: composed the first Telugu literary work, Andhra Mahabharatamu
founded the first Telugu literary academy at Vengi
translated the complete Ramayana into Telugu
introduced the prose style into Sanskrit literature
78.x: Nannaya Bhattaraka is regarded as Adi Kavi because Andhra Mahabharatamu is considered the first major Telugu literary work.
78.tq: Use the exact title and achievement associated with the poet.
xs: **Nannaya** is Adi Kavi because his **Andhra Mahabharatamu** (c. **1045-65**) is the **first Telugu literary work** — option **(1)**.
It was a Mahabharata, not a Ramayana; and his style was **Champu** in Telugu.
xa: He was court poet of **Rajaraja Narendra**.
Titles: **Adikavi, Vagadheeshwara, Shabda Shasanudu**.
Collaborator **Narayana Bhattu** received the **Nandampudi** agrahara.

78.s: Andhra Mahabharatamu of Nannaya is written in which literary style?
o: Champu style combining verse and prose
78.x: Nannaya's Andhra Mahabharatamu follows the Champu style, which combines verse and prose.
78.tq: Discriminate between closely related literary forms by identifying the defining feature.
xs: **Andhra Mahabharatamu** is in **Champu** style — **verse + prose** — option **(3)**.
It is neither purely prose nor a single metre: Champu mixes both forms.
xa: Written c. **1045-65**; the **first Telugu literary work**.
Nannaya = **Adi Kavi**, court poet of **Rajaraja Narendra**.
His title **Shabda Shasanudu**.
The Vengi court laid the base for **Telugu literature**.

78.s: Which of the following titles was NOT associated with Nannaya Bhattaraka?
78.x: Ashtabhasha Kavisekhara was the title of Narayana Bhattu. Nannaya was known as Adikavi, Vagadheeshwara and Shabda Shasanudu.
78.tq: Find the title belonging to the collaborator rather than the principal poet.
xs: **Ashtabhasha Kavisekhara** was **Narayana Bhattu**'s title, not Nannaya's — option **(4)**.
Nannaya's titles: **Adikavi**, **Vagadheeshwara**, **Shabda Shasanudu**.
xa: Narayana Bhattu was Nannaya's **collaborator** and received **Nandampudi** agrahara.
**Chellavva**: "**Gandharva-Vidya-Visarada**".
Nannaya wrote **Andhra Mahabharatamu** in **Champu** style.

78.s: The earliest Telugu inscription mentioned in connection with the pre-Nannaya period is the
78.x: The Kalamalla inscription, dated approximately to 575 CE and associated with Renati Choda Dhananjaya, predates Nannaya.
78.tq: Use the earliest-date clue to distinguish inscriptions from different periods.
xs: The first Telugu inscription, predating Nannaya, is **Kalamalla** (c. **575 CE**, Renati Choda **Dhananjaya**) — option **(1)**.
**Vipparla** = Jayasimha I; **Magallu** first mentions the **Kakatiyas**; **Nandampudi** = Rajaraja Narendra's grant written by Nannaya.
xa: ⚠ **Addanki** = first Telugu **verse** inscription; Kalamalla = first Telugu inscription.
Eastern Chalukya official language: **Sanskrit**.

78.s: Regarding the Nandampudi inscription, which of the following is correct?
o: Nannaya composed it and Narayana Bhattu received the agrahara
Narayana Bhattu composed it and Nannaya received the agrahara
Pandaranga composed it and Nannaya received the agrahara
Nannaya composed it and Ugradityacharya received the agrahara
78.x: Nannaya composed the Nandampudi inscription, which records the agrahara granted to his collaborator Narayana Bhattu under Rajaraja Narendra. Trap: the APPSC G2 2017 key marked Nannaya as the donee, so know both. Pandaranga is linked to Addanki and Ugradityacharya to Kalyanakaraka.
78.tq: Nandampudi: written by Nannaya, grant to Narayana Bhattu.
xs: **Nannaya composed** the **Nandampudi** inscription and **Narayana Bhattu received** the agrahara — option **(1)**.
⚠ Trap: the **APPSC G2 2017** key marked Nannaya as the **donee** — know both.
**Pandaranga** belongs to **Addanki**; **Ugradityacharya** to **Kalyanakaraka**.
xa: The grant was made by **Rajaraja Narendra**.
Narayana Bhattu's title: **Ashtabhasha Kavisekhara**.

78.s: Pavuluri Ganitamu, regarded as the first scientific text in Telugu, is a verse rendering of
78.x: Pavuluri Ganitamu renders Mahaviracharya's Ganitasarasangraham in Telugu verse. Kalyanakaraka is a medical work, Kavijanasrayam a work of Vemulavada Bhimakavi, and Andhra Mahabharatamu the first Telugu literary work.
78.tq: First Telugu science text = Pavuluri Ganitamu (maths).
xs: **Pavuluri Ganitamu** is a Telugu verse rendering of **Mahaviracharya's Ganitasarasangraham** — option **(2)**.
**Kalyanakaraka** is Ugradityacharya's medical work; **Kavijanasrayam** is Vemulavada Bhimakavi's; **Andhra Mahabharatamu** is Nannaya's.
xa: It is the **first scientific text in Telugu**.
First Telugu **literary** work = Nannaya's **Mahabharata**.

78.s: Who held the title 'Gandharva-Vidya-Visarada' in the Eastern Chalukya period?
78.x: Chellavva, the court singer and dancer, held the title Gandharva-Vidya-Visarada (APPSC G2 2019). Chamekamba won the Kaluchumbarru grant, Kundavva was Vimaladitya's Chola queen, and Ayyana Mahadevi built the Nedumba Vasati.
78.tq: Gandharva (music) = Chellavva.
xs: **Chellavva** held the title "**Gandharva-Vidya-Visarada**" — option **(3)** (APPSC G2 2019).
**Chamekamba** won the **Kaluchumbarru** grant; **Kundavva** was Vimaladitya's Chola queen; **Ayyana Mahadevi** built the **Nedumba Vasati**.
xa: Nannaya's titles: **Adikavi, Vagadheeshwara, Shabda Shasanudu**.
Narayana Bhattu: **Ashtabhasha Kavisekhara**.

78.s: The Magallu inscription is significant in Andhra history because it is regarded as the first inscription to mention the
78.x: The Magallu inscription is noted as the first inscription mentioning the Kakatiyas.
78.tq: Identify the dynasty connected with a landmark inscription rather than the dynasty ruling at the time.
xs: The **Magallu inscription** is the first to mention the **Kakatiyas** — option **(4)**.
It is listed among the Eastern Chalukya-era inscriptions, but its fame is this first reference to the Kakatiyas.
xa: First Telugu inscription: **Kalamalla** (c. **575 CE**).
**Addanki** = first Telugu **verse** inscription.

78.s: Which of the following chronological periods is correctly matched with the dynasty or political phase?
78.x: The Eastern Chalukyas ruled approximately from 624 to 1075 CE. The other periods belong respectively to the Chalukya-Chola phase, Kakatiyas and Vijayanagara.
78.tq: Check the date range against the dynasty before accepting the sequence-related option.
xs: **Eastern Chalukyas — 624-1075 CE** is correct — option **(1)**.
**1076-c.1210** is the **Chalukya-Chola era / Mandalika Yugam**; **1163-1323** the **Kakatiyas**; **1336-1646** **Vijayanagara**.
xa: End date debate: **1075**, or **1189 CE** counting the Chalukya-Chola phase.

78.s: As per the APPSC Group 2 (2019) key, the Kesari Samudra lake is credited to
78.x: The 2019 key credits the Kesari Samudra lake to Rudradeva. Some sources credit Beta Raja II with the Kesari tank, which is the trap; Vijayaditya VII and Rajaraja Narendra were Eastern Chalukya rulers with no link to it.
78.tq: Kesari Samudra = Rudradeva (key).
xs: The **APPSC G2 2019** key credits the **Kesari Samudra lake** to **Rudradeva** — option **(2)**.
⚠ Some notes credit **Beta Raja II** with the Kesari tank — follow the key.
xa: The **Magallu inscription** first mentions the Kakatiyas.

78.s: Which of the following best expresses the major cultural significance of the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi?
o: They confined literary activity exclusively to Sanskrit.
They ended the use of Telugu in the Vengi region.
They turned Telugu into a literary language.
They replaced Telugu with Tamil as the court language.
78.x: A major significance of the Eastern Chalukyas was that they helped turn Telugu into a literary language and laid the foundation for Telugu literature.
78.tq: Identify the positive cultural consequence and reject absolute or reversed statements.
xs: The Eastern Chalukyas **turned Telugu into a literary language** — option **(3)**.
Though **Sanskrit** was the official language, the **Vengi court** laid the base for Telugu literature with **Nannaya**.
xa: First Telugu literary work: Nannaya's **Mahabharata**, under **Rajaraja Narendra**.
They ruled Andhra about **4.5 centuries** (**624-1075**).
Also: **Pavuluri Ganitamu**, first scientific text in Telugu.

78.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the core territory and capitals of the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi?
o: The Pennar-Tungabhadra doab; Kalyana, Warangal and Devagiri
The Godavari-Narmada region; Pataliputra, Ujjain and Kannauj
The Krishna-Godavari doab; Pithapuram, Pedavegi and Rajahmundry
The Krishna-Godavari doab; Kanchi, Madurai and Tanjavur
78.x: The core territory was the Krishna-Godavari doab, known as Venginadu. The capitals included Pithapuram, Pedavegi and Rajahmundry.
78.tq: Separate the correct territorial region from similarly named South Indian political centres.
xs: Core territory: **Krishna-Godavari doab (Venginadu)**; capitals **Pithapuram, Pedavegi, Rajahmundry** — option **(3)**.
**Kanchi** was Pallava; the other options name no Eastern Chalukya capital.
xa: Pithapuram = first capital (**Kubja**); Vengi/Pedavegi = **Jayasimha I**; Rajahmundry = **Ammaraja I**, beautified by **Rajaraja Narendra**.
Dandin called Vengi "**Andhra Nagaram**".

78.s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Rajaraja Narendra was associated with Rajamahendravaram.
Statement B: Rajaraja Narendra began the Telugu Mahabharata translation.
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
78.x: A is true: Rajaraja Narendra ruled from Rajamahendravaram. B is false because it was his court poet Nannaya who began the Telugu Mahabharata; the king was the patron.
78.tq: Discriminate the patron from the poet.
n: Rajaraja Narendra was associated with Rajamahendravaram. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #145 · pp 254-255]
Nannaya began the translation of the Telugu Mahabharata, known as the Andhra Mahabharatam. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #145 · pp 254-255]
xs: **Statement A is true, Statement B is false** — option **(3)**.
A is true: **Rajaraja Narendra** is **associated** with **Rajamahendravaram**.
B is false: it was **Nannaya** who **began** the translation of the **Telugu Mahabharata**; Rajaraja Narendra was his **patron**.
xa: Rajaraja Narendra was **connected** with the **Chola royal family** through **marriage**.
He was crowned on **16 August 1022** and married **Ammanga Devi**, daughter of Rajendra Chola.
Nannaya's titles: **Adikavi, Vagadheeshwara, Shabda Shasanudu**.
Rajaraja Narendra's titles: **Kavyageetha Priyudu, Rajarajanarayana**.

78.s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
 a. Kubja Vishnuvardhana
 b. Rajaraja Narendra
 c. Nannaya
 d. Matwalin

List-II
 i. Account of China–India relations
 ii. Patron of Nannaya
 iii. Founder of the Eastern Chalukyas
 iv. Began the Telugu Mahabharata translation
78.x: Kubja Vishnuvardhana founded the Eastern Chalukyas, Rajaraja Narendra was Nannaya's patron, Nannaya began the Telugu Mahabharata, and Matwalin wrote of China–India relations, giving a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
78.tq: Recall the role of each person.
n: Kubja Vishnuvardhana founded the Eastern Chalukya dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #145 · pp 254-255]
Nannaya was patronised by Rajaraja Narendra. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #145 · pp 254-255]
Nannaya began the translation of the Telugu Mahabharata, known as the Andhra Mahabharatam. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #145 · pp 254-255]
Matwalin was a traveller associated with an account of China–India relations during Chalukya rule. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #145 · pp 254-255]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i** — option **(2)**.
**Kubja Vishnuvardhana** → **founder** of the Eastern Chalukyas; **Rajaraja Narendra** → **patron of Nannaya**.
**Nannaya** → **began** the **Telugu Mahabharata** translation; **Matwalin** → account of **China–India relations**.
xa: Kubja Vishnuvardhana was **brother** of **Pulakeshin II**; viceroy **617 CE**, independent **624 CE**.
Nannaya's **Andhra Mahabharatamu** (c. **1045-65**) is the **first Telugu literary work**, in **Champu** style.
**Narayana Bhattu** collaborated and received the **Nandampudi** agrahara.
Eastern Chalukya rule: **624-1075 CE**.

78.s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
 a. Eastern Chalukyas
 b. Cholas
 c. Kubja Vishnuvardhana
 d. Kulottunga I

List-II
 i. Dynasty that repeatedly fought and intermarried with the Eastern Chalukyas
 ii. Founder of the Eastern Chalukya dynasty
 iii. Dynasty of Vengi whose succession became intertwined with the Cholas
 iv. Rajendra Chalukya, who united the Eastern Chalukya and Chola lines

Options:
78.x: The Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi saw their succession tied up with the Cholas, the Cholas fought and intermarried with them, Kubja Vishnuvardhana founded the Eastern Chalukya line, and Kulottunga I was Rajendra Chalukya who united both lines, giving a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv.
78.tq: Recall how the two dynasties merged.
n: The Eastern Chalukyas had repeated political interaction and conflict with the Cholas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #145 · pp 254-255]
Eastern Chalukya succession became increasingly intertwined with the Chola dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #145 · pp 254-255]
Rajendra Chalukya emerged from the Eastern Chalukya–Chola line. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #145 · pp 254-255]
Rajendra Chalukya was also known as Kulottunga I. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #145 · pp 254-255]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv** — option **(1)**.
**Eastern Chalukyas** → Vengi dynasty whose **succession became intertwined** with the Cholas; **Cholas** → repeatedly fought and intermarried with them.
**Kubja Vishnuvardhana** → **founder**; **Kulottunga I** → **Rajendra Chalukya**, who **united** the Eastern Chalukya and Chola lines.
xa: **Vimaladitya** married **Kundavva (Kundavai)**, daughter of **Rajaraja Chola I**.
⚠ **Kundavva** = mother of **Rajaraja Narendra**; **Melama** = mother of **Vijayaditya VII**.
**Vijayaditya VII**, the last ruler, died in **1075**.
First Chalukya-Chola king = **Kulothunga I**.

78.s:
How many of the following statements are correct?
1. The Eastern Chalukyas originated as a branch of the Badami Chalukyas.
2. Kubja Vishnuvardhana was the brother of Pulakeshin II.
3. Vengi was the core region of the Eastern Chalukyas.
4. Rajamahendravaram was unrelated to the Eastern Chalukyas.
78.x: Three are correct: the Eastern Chalukyas branched from the Badami line, Kubja Vishnuvardhana was Pulakeshin II's brother, and Vengi was their core region. Statement 4 is false because Rajamahendravaram later became their important centre.
78.tq: Check each statement separately.
n: The Eastern Chalukyas originated as a branch of the Badami Chalukyas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #145 · pp 254-255]
Kubja Vishnuvardhana was the brother of Pulakeshin II. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #145 · pp 254-255]
The core region of the Eastern Chalukyas was Vengi in present-day Andhra Pradesh. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #145 · pp 254-255]
Rajamahendravaram, also known as Rajahmundry, later became an important centre. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #145 · pp 254-255]
Rajaraja Narendra was associated with Rajamahendravaram. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #145 · pp 254-255]
xs: **Only three** statements are correct — option **(3)**.
Correct: the Eastern Chalukyas **originated** as a **branch** of the **Badami Chalukyas**; **Kubja Vishnuvardhana** was **brother** of **Pulakeshin II**; **Vengi** was the **core region**.
Statement 4 is wrong: **Rajamahendravaram (Rajahmundry)** later became an **important centre** of the dynasty.
xa: First capital: **Pithapuram**; **Jayasimha I** moved it to **Vengi**.
Emblem: **Boar (Varaha)**; official language **Sanskrit**.
Greatest ruler: **Gunaga Vijayaditya III** (APHQ 2011).
Inscriptions use the matronymic **"Hariti Putra"**.

78.s: Which Eastern Chalukya ruler is credited with building 108 Saiva temples, also known as Narendraeswara temples?
78.x: Vijayaditya II (Narendra Mrigaraja) of the Eastern Chalukyas built 108 Saiva temples called Narendreswara temples. Vijayaditya IV was Kollabhighanda, Gunaga Vijayaditya was Vijayaditya III, and Rudra Deva was a Kakatiya.
78.tq: Discriminate among the Vijayadityas.
n: Vijayaditya II belonged to the Eastern Chalukya dynasty. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 47-48]
Vijayaditya II built 108 Saiva temples. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 47-48]
Vijayaditya II built Narendraeswara temples. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 47-48]
Rudra Deva belonged to the Kakatiya dynasty. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 47-48]
xs: **Vijayaditya II** built the **108 Saiva temples**, the **Narendraeswara** temples — option **(1)**.
He fought **108 battles** and built **108 Shiva temples** (APPSC G2 2019); title **Narendramrigaraja**.
**Vijayaditya IV** had the title **Kollabhighanda**; **Gunaga Vijayaditya** had **Tripura-Martya-Maheswara**.
xa: The **Sataluru** inscription records the 108 temples ("Narendra Mrigeswara").
⚠ Other notes (G2 2012 key; APHQ) give **Kollabhiganda** to **Chalukya Bhima I**.
Gunaga Vijayaditya won victories over **Kiranapuram, Achalapuram and Kandukur** (G2 2012 key).
Exam angle: "**108 Shaivalayas**" → Vijayaditya II, not Kubja or Vishnuvardhana III/IV.

78.s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Marturu inscription refers to Mangalagiri as Mangalapura.
Statement B: The Vipparla inscription was issued by Jayasimha Vallabha.
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
78.x: Both are true: the Marturu inscription calls Mangalagiri by the name Mangalapura, and the Vipparla inscription was issued by Jayasimha Vallabha, the Eastern Chalukya ruler.
78.tq: Check each statement separately.
n: The Marturu inscription refers to Mangalagiri as Mangalapura. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
The Vipparla inscription was issued by Jayasimha Vallabha. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
xs: **Both Statement A and Statement B are true** — option **(1)**.
A is true: the **Marturu** inscription of **Pulakesin II** calls **Mangalagiri** **Mangalapura**.
B is true: the **Vipparla** inscription was issued by **Jayasimha Vallabha** / Jayasimha I (APPSC G2 2017).
xa: The **Kopparam** inscription also calls Mangalagiri "Mangalapura" (G2 2019 key).
**Magallu** inscription of **Danarnava** gives the **first mention** of the **Kakatiyas**.
**Nandampudi** grant of Rajaraja Narendra was **written by Nannaya**.
⚠ **Addanki** = first Telugu **verse** inscription; **Kalamalla** = first Telugu inscription.

78.s: The Porumamilla inscription is related to which person?
78.x: The Porumamilla tank inscription, which lays down 12 rules for tank construction, is associated with Prince Bhaskara Bhavadura. Rudrapurushadatta was an Ikshvaku king and Dhananjaya Varma issued the Kalamalla inscription.
78.tq: Recall the patron named in the Porumamilla tank record.
n: The Porumamilla inscription is associated with Prince Bhaskara Bhavadura. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
xs: The **Porumamilla** inscription is related to **Prince Bhaskara Bhavadura** — option **(4)**.
It lays down **12 rules** for **tank construction**.
**Rudrapurushadatta** was not its author; **Dhananjaya** (Renati Choda) issued the **Kalamalla** inscription (c. **575 CE**).
xa: **Pithapuram** inscription of **Prithvisvara** of Velanadu mentions **Kolleru Lake**.
**Chekurru** plate — **Ammaraja I**.
**Kakumanu** — **Chalukya Bhima I**, names a **Setti Shreshthi**.
**Chipurupalli** inscription — Kubja's **18th regnal year**, names the scholar **Madhavasharma**.

79.s: The Ashtadasa Tirthas in Eastern Chalukya administration referred to:
79.x: The kingdom followed the Saptanga idea and had Ashtadasa Tirthas, meaning eighteen offices.
79.tq: Discriminate between an administrative number and similarly structured territorial or religious lists.
xs: **Ashtadasa Tirthas** = **18 offices** — option **(1)**.
They went with the **Saptanga** idea of the state; the territorial units were **Vishaya / Mandala** and the **Nadus**.
xa: **Tirthulu** = council of ministers; **Samaharta** = chief.
**Vishayapati / Mandaleswara** headed a Vishaya / Mandala.
**Vanneyus** = toll collectors.

79.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Eastern Chalukya council of ministers is correct?
o: It was called Agraharas, and the Grameyaka was its chief member.
It was called Basadis, and the Vishayapati was its chief member.
It was called Ghatikas, and the Mandaleswara was its chief member.
It was called Tirthulu, and the Samaharta was its chief member.
79.x: The council of ministers was called Tirthulu, and the Samaharta was the chief among its members.
79.tq: Match the body and its leading officer, using nearby administrative terms as distractors.
xs: The council of ministers was **Tirthulu**, with the **Samaharta** as chief — option **(4)**.
**Agraharas** were tax-free Brahmin villages; **Ghatikas** were Sanskrit schools; **Grameyaka** was a village head; **Mandaleswara** headed a Mandala.
xa: The king was assisted by the **Yuvaraja**.
**Ashtadasa Tirthas** = 18 offices.
**Sthanadhipati** managed temples.

79.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Vishaya or Mandala — Vishayapati or Mandaleswara
79.x: The state was organised into Vishayas or Mandalas under a Vishayapati or Mandaleswara.
79.tq: Match the territorial level with its officer while rejecting officers belonging to other institutions.
xs: **Vishaya / Mandala — Vishayapati / Mandaleswara** is correct — option **(1)**.
The **village** head was **Grameyaka / Gramani / Urgavunda**; **Samaharta** was chief of the ministers; **Sthanadhipati** managed temples.
xa: Nadus: **Venginadu** (Krishna, Godavari), **Kammanadu** (Bapatla, Ongole, Narasaraopet), **Pakanadu** (Nellore).
**Vanneyus** = toll collectors.

79.s: Which of the following Nadus was associated with the Nellore region?
79.x: Pakanadu was associated with Nellore. Venginadu covered parts of Krishna and Godavari, while Kammanadu included Bapatla, Ongole and Narasaraopet.
79.tq: Use the geographical association to distinguish the named territorial units.
xs: **Pakanadu** = **Nellore** — option **(4)**.
**Venginadu** = Krishna, Godavari; **Kammanadu** = **Bapatla, Ongole, Narasaraopet**; **Palnadu** is listed without a region.
xa: The **Asanapura** Ghatika, headed by **Mandasharma**, was in **Kammanadu**.
Core territory of the dynasty = **Venginadu**.

79.s: Brahmins who received agraharas are stated to have performed which rituals?
79.x: Brahmins receiving tax-free agraharas performed Hiranyagarbha and Bahusuvarna rituals.
79.tq: Match the social beneficiaries with the rituals associated with their privilege.
xs: Brahmins of the **agraharas** performed **Hiranyagarbha and Bahusuvarna** rituals — option **(4)**.
**Hallisaka (Kolatam)** is a dance; **Tarka** and **Vyakarana** are Ghatika subjects.
xa: Agraharas were **tax-free villages**.
Grants came from the **Badami Chalukya** model.
**Jayasimha I** performed the **Ashvamedha**.

79.s: Which development is associated with Jayasimha II?
o: The Boyas founded the merchant headquarters at Penugonda.
The Koya Kottalu were drawn into the Brahmanical fold.
The Venginadu was divided into eighteen offices.
79.x: Under Jayasimha II, groups such as the Koya Kottalu were assimilated into the Brahmanical fold.
79.tq: Identify the ruler associated with tribal assimilation rather than with religious construction or administration.
xs: Under **Jayasimha II**, the **Koya Kottalu** and others were drawn into the **Brahmanical fold** — option **(2)**.
**Penugonda** was the merchant guild HQ; the **Pancharamas** were built by **Chalukya Bhima I**, not Jains.
xa: **Panduranga** subdued the **Boyas**.
Society: **varna-based**, Brahmin privilege.

79.s: Who subdued the Boyas?
79.x: Panduranga subdued the Boyas, while Jayasimha II is associated with the assimilation of the Koya Kottalu.
79.tq: Separate two related social developments by matching each group with its stated agent.
xs: **Panduranga** subdued the **Boyas** — option **(1)**.
**Jayasimha II** is linked with the assimilation of the **Koya Kottalu**.
xa: Panduranga, commander of **Gunaga Vijayaditya III**, also issued the **Addanki** inscription.
Vishnuvardhana III gave **Mushikonda** to Jains; **Ammaraja II** made the **Kaluchumbarru** grant.

79.s: Which of the following statements regarding overseas trade is correct?
o: Rajaraja Narendra sent 72 merchants to China, while Saktivarma prohibited overseas trade.
Overseas trade was confined to Karnataka and did not reach Burma or China.
Saktivarma’s coins have been found in Arakan, and trade with the eastern islands continued under Rajaraja Narendra.
Saktivarma’s coins have been found only at Penugonda, and eastern-island trade ended under Rajaraja Narendra.
79.x: Saktivarma’s coins have been found in Arakan, Burma, and trade with the eastern islands continued under Rajaraja Narendra. The dispatch of 72 merchants to China is associated with Kulothunga I.
79.tq: Separate the rulers and regions associated with different overseas trade facts.
xs: **Saktivarma**'s coins are found in **Arakan (Burma)**, and **eastern-island trade** went on under **Rajaraja Narendra** — option **(3)**.
The **72 merchants to China** were sent by **Kulothunga I**, not Rajaraja Narendra.
xa: Merchant guild HQ (medieval Andhra): **Penugonda**.
Saktivarma I had beaten Kalyani Satyasraya's army with Chola help.

79.s: Which place was the headquarters of the merchant guilds in medieval Andhra?
79.x: Penugonda was the headquarters of the merchant guilds. Pithapuram and Vengi were Eastern Chalukya capitals, and Arakan in Burma is where Saktivarma's coins were found.
79.tq: Guild HQ = Penugonda.
xs: **Penugonda** was the HQ of the merchant guilds — option **(2)**.
**Pithapuram** and **Vengi** were capitals; **Arakan (Burma)** is where **Saktivarma**'s coins were found.
xa: **Kulothunga I** sent **72 merchants to China**.
Trade with the **eastern islands** under **Rajaraja Narendra**.

79.s: Which Eastern Chalukya ruler is stated to have performed the Ashvamedha?
79.x: Jayasimha I performed the Ashvamedha, while royal prashastis also boast of several Ashvamedhas.
79.tq: Directly identify the ruler associated with a specific Vedic ritual.
xs: **Jayasimha I** performed the **Ashvamedha** — option **(4)**.
**Vijayaditya II** built **108 temples**; **Vimaladitya** became a Jain; **Danarnava** was Vaishnava.
xa: Royal prashastis boast of many Ashvamedhas.
Danarnava built the **Mandavya Narayana** temple, **Samalkot**.
**Chalukya Bhima I**: **Pancharamas**.

79.s: Which of the following were the Shaiva sects prevalent under the Eastern Chalukyas?
79.x: The Shaiva sects of the period were Kapalika, Kalamukha and Pasupata. Pancharatra and Vaikhanasa are Vaishnava traditions, and Virashaiva persecution came later in the Kakatiya age.
79.tq: Shaiva trio: Kapalika, Kalamukha, Pasupata.
xs: The Shaiva sects were **Kapalika, Kalamukha and Pasupata** — option **(1)**.
**Virashaiva** persecution of Jains came later, in the **Kakatiya** age; **Pancharatra** and **Vaikhanasa** are not Shaiva sects.
xa: Shaivism was **dominant**; custom of a **temple for each battle**.
Kapalikas emerged from the **Misra Saivam** school.
Royal title **Parama Maheshwara** reflects Shaiva faith.

79.s:
Consider the following statements about Jainism and Buddhism under the Eastern Chalukyas:
1. Vimaladitya was the only Vengi Chalukya king to become a Jain.
2. Potlacheruvu was a famous Buddhist centre of the period.
3. Under Brahmanical pressure many Jains, including the family of Basaveshwara, migrated to Karnataka.
4. Buddhism, though declining, survived at Amaravati and Nagarjunakonda.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
79.x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Potlacheruvu was a famous Jain centre, not Buddhist. Hence B; A, C and D all include the false statement 2.
79.tq: Potlacheruvu = Jain (G2 2017 key); Buddhism lingered only at Amaravati and Nagarjunakonda.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **Vimaladitya** was the **only Vengi Chalukya king to become a Jain**.
Statement 2 is **wrong**: **Potlacheruvu** was the leading **Jain** centre.
Statements 3 and 4 are **correct**: Jains incl. **Basaveshwara**'s family moved to **Karnataka**; Buddhism survived at **Amaravati** and **Nagarjunakonda** — so option **(2)**.
xa: Vimaladitya built the **Ramakonda** cave temple, Ramatirtham, for his guru **Trikala Yogi Siddhanta Deva**.
Jain pupils began studies with "**Om Namah Siddham**".

79.s: Vimaladitya built the Ramakonda cave temple at Ramatirtham for whom?
o: His Jain guru Trikala Yogi Siddhanta Deva
79.x: Vimaladitya built the Ramakonda cave temple for his Jain guru Trikala Yogi Siddhanta Deva, as recorded in the Ramateertham inscription.
79.tq: Link the donor, monument and religious teacher rather than confusing the site with another grant.
xs: **Vimaladitya** built the **Ramakonda** cave temple for his Jain guru **Trikala Yogi Siddhanta Deva** — option **(1)**.
Source: the **Ramateertham inscription**; site **Ramatirtham** (Vizianagaram).
xa: Vimaladitya was the **only Vengi Chalukya king to become a Jain**.
Other Jain grants: **Mushikonda** (Vishnuvardhana III), **Kaluchumbarru** (Ammaraja II), **Nedumba Vasati** (Ayyana Mahadevi).

79.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Mushikonda village — Vishnuvardhana III; Kaluchumbarru grant — Ammaraja II
Mushikonda village — Ammaraja II; Kaluchumbarru grant — Vimaladitya
Mushikonda village — Ayyana Mahadevi; Kaluchumbarru grant — Kubja Vishnuvardhana
Mushikonda village — Danarnava; Kaluchumbarru grant — Chalukya Bhima I
79.x: Vishnuvardhana III granted Mushikonda village to Jains, while Ammaraja II made the Kaluchumbarru grant at the request of Chamekamba.
79.tq: Start from the sure donor–grant pair and check that the two royal donors are not interchanged.
xs: **Mushikonda — Vishnuvardhana III**; **Kaluchumbarru — Ammaraja II** — option **(1)**.
The Kaluchumbarru grant was made at the request of **Chamekamba**.
xa: **Ayyana Mahadevi** built the **Nedumba Vasati**, Vijayawada.
**Vimaladitya** built the **Ramakonda** cave temple.
Vishnuvardhana III's title: **Kavi Pandita Kamadhenu**.

79.s: Who built the Jain Nedumba Vasati at Vijayawada?
79.x: Queen Ayyana Mahadevi built the Nedumba Vasati (APPSC G2 2025; the key makes her the wife of Kubja Vishnuvardhana). Chamekamba obtained the Kaluchumbarru grant, Kundavva was Vimaladitya's Chola queen and Chellavva was a court singer.
79.tq: Nedumba Vasati = Ayyana Mahadevi.
xs: Queen **Ayyana Mahadevi** built the **Nedumba Vasati**, Vijayawada — option **(2)**.
**Chamekamba** obtained the **Kaluchumbarru** grant; **Chellavva** was a court singer and dancer.
xa: ⚠ G2 2025 key: wife of **Kubja Vishnuvardhana**; the APHQ book says **Gunaga Vijayaditya**.
Leading Jain centre: **Potlacheruvu** (G2 2017 key).

79.s:
Consider the following statements about Eastern Chalukya temples:
1. Temples received land endowments from kings and vassals.
2. Musicians and dancers could be attached to temples and courts.
3. Chellavva is an example of such a court-linked singer and dancer.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
79.x: All three statements are correct. Kings and vassals made land endowments, while musicians and dancers such as Chellavva were attached to temples and courts.
79.tq: Combine temple finance with its personnel and test whether the illustrative example fits both institutions.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: temples got **land endowments** from kings and vassals.
Statement 2 is **correct**: **musicians and dancers** were attached to temples and courts.
Statement 3 is **correct**: **Chellavva** is such an example — so all three, option **(4)**.
xa: Popular dance: **Hallisaka (Kolatam)**.
Instrument sculptures at **Bhairavakona** (Nellore): **veena, mridangam, cymbals**.
Temple manager: **Sthanadhipati**.

79.s: Hallisaka, identified with Kolatam, was regarded as:
79.x: Hallisaka, or Kolatam, was a popular dance associated with the cultural life of the period.
79.tq: Distinguish a performing art from administrative and fiscal terminology.
xs: **Hallisaka (Kolatam)** was a **popular dance** — option **(2)**.
It is not a revenue, office or Jain formula — the Jain opening formula was "**Om Namah Siddham**".
xa: Court singer and dancer: **Chellavva**.
Instrument sculptures at **Bhairavakona**: **veena, mridangam, cymbals**.

79.s: Ghatikas in the Eastern Chalukya period were:
o: Military cantonments attached to royal forts
Jain cave temples used for royal burials
Advanced Sanskrit schools attached to agraharas or temples
Merchant guilds situated at coastal ports
79.x: Ghatikas were advanced Sanskrit schools attached to agraharas or temples.
79.tq: Apply the institutional definition while rejecting misleading associations with military, commercial and temple structures.
xs: **Ghatikas** were **advanced Sanskrit schools** attached to **agraharas or temples** — option **(3)**.
Merchant guilds were headquartered at **Penugonda**, a separate institution.
xa: Heads: **Ghatika Samanyulu** — e.g. **Mandasharma** at **Asanapura**, Kammanadu.
Subjects: **Vedas, Vedangas, Dharmashastras, Tarka, Vyakarana, Arthashastra, Dhanurveda, Ayurveda**.

79.s: The heads of Ghatikas were known as:
79.x: The heads of Ghatikas were called Ghatika Samanyulu.
79.tq: Match the educational institution with its specialised headship title.
xs: Ghatika heads were the **Ghatika Samanyulu** — option **(3)**.
**Sthanadhipati** managed temples; **Vanneyus** collected tolls; **Vishayapati** headed a Vishaya.
xa: Example: **Mandasharma** at **Asanapura** Ghatika, Kammanadu.
His son **Katikasharma** appears in the **Nidamarru** inscription.

79.s: Which of the following subjects was NOT included among the subjects taught in Ghatikas?
79.x: Ghatikas taught subjects such as Vedas, Vedangas, Dharmashastras, Tarka, Vyakarana, Arthashastra, Dhanurveda and Ayurveda. Hallisaka was a popular dance, not an academic subject.
79.tq: Separate the educational curriculum from a performing-art term.
xs: **Hallisaka** was not a Ghatika subject — option **(4)**; it is a popular dance (**Kolatam**).
Subjects taught: **Vedas, Vedangas, Dharmashastras, Tarka, Vyakarana, Arthashastra, Dhanurveda, Ayurveda**.
xa: Ghatikas were **advanced Sanskrit schools**.
Jain pupils began with "**Om Namah Siddham**".

79.s: Who composed the medical treatise Kalyanakaraka?
79.x: Ugradityacharya composed Kalyanakaraka, a medical treatise of the Eastern Chalukya period.
79.tq: Directly match an author with a specialised work while avoiding the previously tested item wording.
xs: **Ugradityacharya** composed the medical treatise **Kalyanakaraka** — option **(1)** (G2 2012, 2019 keys).
**Bhattavamana** wrote the **Kavyalankara Sutras**; **Katikasharma** and **Mandasharma** were Ghatika scholars.
xa: Ghatikas also taught **Ayurveda**.
Bhattavamana's title: **Kavi Vrishabha**.

79.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
79.x: Bhattavamana wrote Kavyalankara Sutras and held the title Kavi Vrishabha.
79.tq: Start with the sure author–work pair and eliminate swapped authors and titles.
xs: **Bhattavamana — Kavyalankara Sutras** is correct — option **(1)**; his title was **Kavi Vrishabha**.
**Ugradityacharya** wrote **Kalyanakaraka**; **Mallappa** was Chellavva's father; **Kavyageetha Priyudu** was **Rajaraja Narendra**'s title.
xa: Bhattavamana's patron: **Chalukya Bhima I**.
Chellavva: **Gandharva-vidya-visarada**.

79.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Vishnuvardhana III — Kavi Pandita Kamadhenu
2. Ammaraja II — Kavigayaka Kalpataru
3. Rajaraja Narendra — Kavyageetha Priyudu
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
79.x: All three pairs are correct: the respective royal titles were Kavi Pandita Kamadhenu, Kavigayaka Kalpataru and Kavyageetha Priyudu.
79.tq: Verify each title–ruler pair independently before selecting the coded combination.
xs: Pair 1 **correct**: **Vishnuvardhana III — Kavi Pandita Kamadhenu**.
Pair 2 **correct**: **Ammaraja II — Kavigayaka Kalpataru**.
Pair 3 **correct**: **Rajaraja Narendra — Kavyageetha Priyudu** — so all three, option **(4)**.
xa: Vishnuvardhana III also granted **Mushikonda** to Jains.
Ammaraja II made the **Kaluchumbarru** grant at **Chamekamba**'s request.

79.s: Which statement regarding Chellavva’s patronage is correct?
o: She was patronised by Vimaladitya, who granted her Mushikonda.
She was patronised by Chalukya Bhima I, who granted her Attili.
She was patronised by Danarnava, who granted her Pithapuram.
She was patronised by Rajaraja Narendra, who granted her Ramatirtham.
79.x: Chellavva was patronised by Chalukya Bhima I, who gave her Attili village and two kandikas of land.
79.tq: Discriminate among nearby royal patrons by linking the artist, patron and grant.
xs: **Chalukya Bhima I** patronised **Chellavva** and gave her **Attili** village — option **(2)** (G2 2011 key).
He also gave **2 kandikas** of land; **Mushikonda** was Vishnuvardhana III's grant to Jains and **Ramatirtham** is linked with Vimaladitya.
xa: ⚠ Some notes say **Gunaga Vijayaditya** gave her Attili — the key and most notes credit Chalukya Bhima I.
Her father **Mallappa** is compared to **Tumburu** in the Attili inscription.

79.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the religious and cultural conditions under the Eastern Chalukyas:
1. Sanskrit served as the official language.
2. Patronage was extended to Jainism, Buddhism and Hinduism.
3. The persecution of Jains at Potlacheruvu occurred during the Eastern Chalukya period.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
79.x: Sanskrit was the official language, and patronage of Jainism, Buddhism and Hinduism indicates religious tolerance. The persecution of Jains at Potlacheruvu occurred later in the Kakatiya age, not during the Eastern Chalukya period.
79.tq: Find the chronological mismatch in the statement linking Potlacheruvu with the Eastern Chalukyas.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **Sanskrit** was the official language.
Statement 2 is **correct**: patronage of **Jainism + Buddhism** with **Hinduism** = religious tolerance.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: **Kalamukha + Virashaiva** persecution of Jains (**Potlacheruvu** attacked) came later, in the **Kakatiya** age — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: **Vimaladitya** even became a Jain.
Buddhism survived at **Amaravati** and **Nagarjunakonda**.

79.s: Which statement about Panchadarla in Anakapalli is correct?
o: It contains the only two-flagpole temple in Andhra Pradesh.
Its inscriptions record the construction of the Ramappa vimana.
Its temple is exclusively a Kalinga-style monument of the Eastern Gangas.
Its Uma Dharmalingeswara Temple has Eastern Chalukya and fifteenth-century inscriptions.
79.x: The Uma Dharmalingeswara Temple at Panchadarla has Eastern Chalukya and fifteenth-century inscriptions.
79.tq: Distinguish the inscriptional identity of Panchadarla from the better-known north-coastal temples.
xs: **Panchadarla**'s **Sri Uma Dharmalingeswara** shrine has pillars inscribed in **Eastern Chalukya** and **15th-century** eras — option **(4)**.
It is at **Dharapalem, Anakapalli district** (Aug **2026**).
xa: **ASI** recorded **17 inscriptions** there in **1899**.
They are published in **South Indian Inscriptions Vol. VI**.

80.s: The Eastern Chalukya temples are primarily associated with which architectural style, as identified by the Vengi School tradition?
o: Vesara style developed exclusively under the Rashtrakutas
Nagara style with exclusively Buddhist features
Dravida style enriched by Pallava, Badami Chalukya and local Andhra features
80.x: The Eastern Chalukyas mainly followed the Dravida style, combining Pallava and Badami Chalukya influences with local Andhra features. This regional tradition is also called the Vengi School.
80.tq: Identify the defining combination of architectural influences rather than a single dynasty.
xs: Eastern Chalukya temples follow the **Dravida style enriched by Pallava (Kanchi), Badami Chalukya and local Andhra features** — so option **(4)** is correct.
This regional tradition is called the **Vengi School**; it is not Indo-Islamic, not exclusively Buddhist Nagara, and not a Rashtrakuta-only Vesara.
Temples were built of local **laterite and limestone**, concentrated in the **Krishna-Godavari delta**.
xa: Another name for it: **Vesara (Chalukya) style** — a blend of the **Dravidian vimana** with **Buddhist art**.
Model temple: **Draksharama Bhimeswara** = **Chalukya-Chola style** (G2 **2025** key, asked twice).
⚠ Trap distractors: **Brihadeeswara** (Imperial Chola, Thanjavur), **Padmakshi** (Kakatiya, Hanamkonda), **Lepakshi** (Vijayanagara).

80.s:
Consider the following statements about Eastern Chalukya temple architecture:
1. The temples were built only of imported granite.
2. Some accounts call the style Vesara or Chalukya style, a blend of the Dravidian vimana with Buddhist art.
3. Temple building was concentrated in the Krishna-Godavari delta.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
80.x: Statement 2 is correct: the Vengi School is also called Vesara (Chalukya) style. Statement 1 is wrong: local laterite and limestone were used. Statement 3 is correct: building was concentrated in the Krishna-Godavari delta. So 2 and 3 only.
80.tq: Vengi School = local laterite and limestone in the delta.
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — option **(3) 2 and 3 only**.
Statement 2 is correct: the style is also called **Vesara (Chalukya) style** — **Dravidian vimana + Buddhist art** (the **Vengi School**).
Statement 3 is correct: building was **concentrated in the Krishna-Godavari delta**.
Statement 1 is wrong: they used local **laterite and limestone**, not imported granite.
xa: Base style: mainly **Dravida** + **Pallava (Kanchi)** and **Badami Chalukya** influences.
**Draksharama Bhimeswara** = model **Chalukya-Chola style** temple (G2 2025 key).
⚠ Distractors: **Brihadeeswara** (Chola), **Padmakshi** (Kakatiya), **Lepakshi** (Vijayanagara).
**Vijayeswara** temple at Bikkavolu has **Ganga and Yamuna** carvings.

80.s: Which temple is the model of the Chalukya-Chola style, combining Pallava and early Chalukya features into an independent regional style?
80.x: The Draksharama Bhimeswara temple exemplifies the Chalukya-Chola style (APPSC G2 2025 key, asked twice). Brihadeeswara is Imperial Chola, Padmakshi is Kakatiya and Lepakshi is Vijayanagara: the trap distractors.
xs: The **Draksharama Bhimeswara temple** is the model of the **Chalukya-Chola style** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Brihadeeswara** (Thanjavur) is Imperial Chola; **Padmakshi** (Hanamkonda) is Kakatiya; **Lepakshi** is Vijayanagara.
This was the G2 **2025** key, asked twice.
xa: Draksharama Bhimeswara was built by **Chalukya Bhima I**.
Draksharama is one of the **Trilinga kshetras** and one of the **Pancharamas**.
Its twin: the two-storeyed **Kumararama** at **Samalkot**, closely similar in plan.

80.s:
Consider the following statements about the 108 Shiva temples of the Eastern Chalukyas:
1. They were built by Vijayaditya II (Narendramrigaraja) and called Narendresvaralayas or Narendra Mrigeswaralayas.
2. The source for this claim is the Kopparam inscription.
3. One temple was built at each of his 108 battle sites.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
80.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: Vijayaditya II built 108 Shiva temples, one at each of his 108 battle sites. Statement 2 is wrong: the source is the Sataluru inscription; Kopparam is Pulakesin II's record. So B; A omits the true statement 3, C and D include the false statement 2.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: **Vijayaditya II (Narendramrigaraja)** built them, called **Narendresvaralayas / Narendra Mrigeswaralayas**.
Statement 3 correct: one temple at each of his **108 battle sites**.
Statement 2 wrong: the source is the **Sataluru inscription**, not Kopparam.
xa: This fact was keyed in G2 **2008, 2012, 2019 and 2025**.
**Chalukya Bhima I** built the **Pancharamas** / made them Shaiva kshetras.
**Kubja Vishnuvardhana** built the **Kunti Madhava** temple at **Pithapuram**.

80.s: Who is associated with building the Pancharamas or making them Shaiva kshetras?
80.x: Chalukya Bhima I is associated with building the Pancharamas or establishing them as Shaiva kshetras.
80.tq: Use the builder–religious foundation association rather than the place-based clues.
xs: **Chalukya Bhima I** built the **Pancharamas** or made them Shaiva kshetras — option **(1)** is correct.
**Danarnava** built the **Mandavya Narayana** temple at Samalkot; **Kubja Vishnuvardhana** built **Kunti Madhava** at Pithapuram.
xa: Chalukya Bhima I also built **Bhimeswara (Draksharama)**, **Kumararama (Samalkot)** in memory of his son, and **Someswara (Somarama)** at Gunupudi.
He also built the **Kumaraswamy temple** at **Chebrolu**.
His commander **Bhattupu** built the **Parvateswara** temple on **Indrakeeladri**, Bezawada.

80.s:
Consider the following statements about Eastern Chalukya temples:
1. The Mandavya Narayana (Raja Narayana) temple at Samalkot was built by Danarnava.
2. The Parvateswara temple at Indrakeeladri, Bezawada, was built by Rajaraja Narendra.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
80.x: Statement 1 is correct: Danarnava built the Mandavya Narayana temple at Samalkot. Statement 2 is wrong: the Parvateswara temple was built by Bhattupu, the commander of Chalukya Bhima I; Rajaraja Narendra is linked with the Rajahmundry temples. So 1 only.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: the **Mandavya Narayana (Raja Narayana)** temple at **Samalkot** was built by **Danarnava**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the **Parvateswara** temple at **Indrakeeladri** was built by **Bhattupu**, **Chalukya Bhima**'s commander.
xa: **Rajaraja Narendra** built the **Kotilingala, Markandeya and Vishnu** temples at **Rajahmundry**.
**Kunti Madhava**, Pithapuram — **Kubja Vishnuvardhana**.
Kumaraswamy temple, **Chebrolu** — **Chalukya Bhima I**.
**Golingeswara** is the only Bikkavolu temple still standing.

80.s:
Consider the following statements about Rajahmundry:
1. It was established as the Eastern Chalukya capital by Ammaraja Vishnuvardhana on the banks of the Godavari.
2. Its Kotilingala, Markandeya and Vishnu temples are linked with Rajaraja Narendra, and the Vishnu temple later became the Pedda Masjid under the Tughlaqs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
80.x: Statement 1 is correct: Ammaraja Vishnuvardhana made Rajahmundry the capital on the Godavari. Statement 2 is correct: Rajaraja Narendra is linked with these temples, and the Vishnu temple became the Pedda Masjid. So both.
80.tq: Rajahmundry = Godavari; Pedda Masjid was a Vishnu temple.
xs: **Both** statements are correct — option **(3) Both 1 and 2**.
Statement 1: **Rajahmundry** was established as the Eastern Chalukyan capital by **Ammaraja Vishnuvardhana** on the **banks of the Godavari**.
Statement 2: its **Kotilingala, Markandeya and Vishnu** temples are linked with **Rajaraja Narendra**; the Vishnu temple became the **Pedda Masjid** under the **Tughlaqs**.
xa: Rajahmundry is called the **cultural capital of the Andhras**.
**Ammaraju** and **Chalukya Bhima I** are linked with **Bhimeshwara** temples on the Godavari.
Rajaraja Narendra built **three Shiva temples** at **Kalidindi** for fallen Chola soldiers.
⚠ 2025 key marked "Rajaraja Narendra built the **Rajarajeswara temple at Biccavole**" as **incorrect**.

80.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Temple)
a. Bhimeswara
b. Kumararama
c. Kumaraswamy
d. Someswara

List-II (Place)
i. Chebrolu
ii. Gunupudi near Bhimavaram
iii. Draksharama
iv. Samalkot

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
80.x: Bhimeswara is at Draksharama, Kumararama at Samalkot, Kumaraswamy at Chebrolu and Someswara at Gunupudi near Bhimavaram.
80.tq: Start from the sure temple–place pairs and eliminate codes containing a mismatch.
xs: Correct match: **a–iii, b–iv, c–i, d–ii** — option **(1)**.
**Bhimeswara** – **Draksharama**; **Kumararama** – **Samalkot**.
**Kumaraswamy** – **Chebrolu**; **Someswara (Somarama)** – **Gunupudi, near Bhimavaram**.
xa: All four were built by **Chalukya Bhima I**.
Kumararama (**Kumara Bhimeswara**) was built in memory of his son.
⚠ **Chalukya Bhimavaram** = Samalkot; **Palakollu** = **Ksheerarama**.

80.s:
Which of the following correctly represents the Pancharama shrine, place and district?
1. Draksharama — Draksharama — East Godavari
2. Kumararama — Samalkot — East Godavari
3. Ksheerarama — Palakollu — West Godavari
4. Amararama — Amaravati — Guntur
80.x: All four listed associations are correct according to the traditional undivided-district designations: Draksharama and Kumararama in East Godavari, Ksheerarama in West Godavari and Amararama in Guntur.
80.tq: Check each place–district pair independently before selecting the complete combination.
xs: All four pairs are correct — option **(4)**.
**Draksharama** and **Kumararama (Samalkot)**: **East Godavari**.
**Ksheerarama (Palakollu)**: **West Godavari**; **Amararama (Amaravati)**: **Guntur**.
xa: The fifth: **Somarama** at **Gunupudi, Bhimavaram** (West Godavari).
All except **Ksheerarama** are **two-storeyed**.
Literary sources: **Skanda Purana** and Srinatha's **Bhimeswara Puranam**.

80.s:
Consider the following statements about the Pancharama temples:
1. All except Ksheerarama are two-storeyed temples.
2. The Skanda Purana is one of the literary sources associated with them.
3. Srinatha's Bhimeswara Puranam is another literary source associated with them.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
80.x: All three statements are correct. Ksheerarama is the exception to the two-storeyed form, and the Skanda Purana and Srinatha's Bhimeswara Puranam are associated literary sources.
80.tq: Combine an architectural exception with the two literary-source associations.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
