Trade in horses and spices; Anjuvannam represented foreign merchants
89.x: Arab trade on the west coast prominently involved horses and spices, while Anjuvannam was associated with foreign merchants.
89.tq: Discriminate between commodities and the institutional identity of a merchant body.
xs: West-coast **Arab** trade was in **horses and spices**, and **Anjuvannam** was a **foreign-merchant** body, so option **(4)** is correct.
**Local market assemblies** were the **nagarams**.
xa: Arab merchants were active on the **Coromandel coast**.
**Horses** were a major import.
**Kaveripattinam** traded with **Sri Lanka**, **SE Asia** and **Rome**.

89.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Kaveripattinam — Port at the mouth of the Kaveri
89.x: Kaveripattinam, not Nagapattinam, was the early Chola capital and a port at the mouth of the Kaveri.
89.tq: Find the swapped capital description among otherwise familiar port associations.
xs: **Nagapattinam** was the **chief Chola port**, not the early Chola capital, so option **(1)** is the wrong pair.
The early Chola capital and port at the **Kaveri** mouth was **Kaveripattinam (Poompuhar)**.
xa: Kaveripattinam is named in the **Periplus**.
Nagapattinam had the **Srivijaya-built Buddhist vihara**.
Tamil Nadu began the **third phase** of underwater exploration at **Poompuhar** on **8 Sep 2026**.

89.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
89.x: Kasu was a gold coin. Nagarams were market centres, Erivirappattanas were protected mercantile towns, and Kaveripattinam was a port and early Chola capital.
89.tq: Test precise institutional meanings by identifying the single correctly matched pair.
xs: **Kasu** = **gold coin** is correctly matched, so option **(4)** is correct.
**Nagarams** were **market centres**, **Erivirappattanas** were **protected mercantile towns**, and **Kaveripattinam** was a port.
xa: ⚠ The question swaps the meanings of Nagarams and Erivirappattanas.
**Kaveripattinam (Poompuhar)** was the early Chola capital.
Earlier Poompuhar finds include wharves, **4th-century BCE** pottery and a **lighthouse**.

89.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched in relation to architectural styles in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Draksharama Bhimeswara — exclusively Imperial Chola style
89.x: Draksharama Bhimeswara represents the independent Chalukya-Chola style. Brihadeeswara is Imperial Chola, while Padmakshi at Hanamkonda is Kakatiya.
89.tq: Use the regional architectural comparisons to reject swapped dynastic styles.
xs: **Draksharama Bhimeswara** = **independent Chalukya-Chola** style is correctly matched, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Brihadeeswara** is **Imperial Chola** (Thanjavur), and **Padmakshi (Hanamkonda)** is **Kakatiya**.
xa: The Draksharama style blends **Pallava** and **early Chalukya** elements.
Temple styles were asked in **APHQ 2025** and **APPSC 2025**.
**Kulottunga I** built **Kulottunga Cholapuram** (Visakhapatnam).

89.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the comparative development of Dravidian art?
o: The Pallavas laid its foundation and the Cholas developed it on a monumental scale.
The Cholas laid its foundation and the Pallavas built its monumental culmination.
The Rashtrakutas alone created the Dravidian tradition.
The Hoysalas laid its foundation and the Kakatiyas completed it.
89.x: The comparison states that the Pallavas laid the foundation of Dravidian art, while the Cholas built its monumental culmination.
89.tq: Preserve the direction of the comparison instead of reversing the contributions of the Pallavas and Cholas.
xs: The **Pallavas laid the foundation** of Dravidian art and the **Cholas built the cathedral**, so option **(1)** is correct.
The Cholas moved from **rock-cut caves** to massive **free-standing structural temples**, the zenith of the **Dravida** style.
xa: Chola-style building continued under the **Kalyani Chalukyas** and **Hoysalas**.
Pallava monuments: **Seven Pagodas** and **Shore Temple** at Mahabalipuram.
Chola zenith features: massive **vimanas**, **Nandi mandapas**, **enclosure walls**.

89.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
 a. Brihadeeswara Temple
 b. Gangaikondacholapuram
 c. Airavatesvara Temple
 d. Abolition of tolls

List-II
 i. Rajaraja II
 ii. Rajendra I
 iii. Rajaraja I
 iv. Kulottunga I
89.x: Rajaraja I built the Brihadeeswara temple, Rajendra I built Gangaikondacholapuram, Rajaraja II built the Airavatesvara temple at Darasuram, and Kulottunga I abolished tolls, giving a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv.
89.tq: Recall the builder of each monument.
n: Rajaraja I was associated with the Brihadeeswara Temple. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
Gangaikondacholapuram is associated with Rajendra I. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
The Airavatesvara Temple is associated with Rajaraja II. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
Rajendra I built the Chola Gangam, a huge artificial lake. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv** — option **(2)**.
**Brihadeeswara Temple** → **Rajaraja I** (completed **1010 CE**); **Gangaikondacholapuram** → **Rajendra I**.
**Airavatesvara Temple** (Darasuram) → **Rajaraja II**; **abolition of tolls** → **Kulottunga I**.
xa: All three temples form the UNESCO **"Great Living Chola Temples"** (Thanjavur **1987**, extended **2004**).
⚠ **Chidambaram** is **not** in the group.
Vimanas: Thanjavur **216 ft**, Gangaikondacholapuram **180 ft**.
Airavatesvara has a stone chariot and **"Musical Steps"**.

89.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
89.x: Option C is incorrect: the Dilwara Jain temples are at Mount Abu in Rajasthan, while Morena is known for the circular Chausath Yogini temple. Jagannath–Puri, Virupaksha–Hampi and Konark–Odisha are right.
89.tq: Check the place in each statement.
n: Jagannath is in Puri. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 110-111]
Konark is in Odisha. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 110-111]
Virupaksha is in Hampi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 110-111]
Dilwara is in Mount Abu. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 110-111]
Chausath Yogini is in Morena. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 110-111]
xs: The incorrect statement is **Dilwara is associated with Morena** — option **(3)**.
**Dilwara** is at **Mount Abu** — a **Jain** temple made of **marble**.
**Morena** has the **circular Chausath Yogini** temple.
The others are correct: **Jagannath — Puri**, **Virupaksha — Hampi**, **Konark — Odisha**.
xa: **Lingaraj** (Bhubaneswar), **Jagannath** and **Konark** are in **Nagara style**.
Virupaksha belongs to the **South Indian temple tradition**.
**Kandariya Mahadev**, Khajuraho — Nagara.
**Kailasanathar**, Kanchipuram — **Rajsimha style**.

89.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Lingaraj
(b) Jagannath
(c) Virupaksha
(d) Dilwara

List-II
(i) Mount Abu
(ii) Hampi
(iii) Bhubaneswar
(iv) Puri
89.x: Lingaraj is in Bhubaneswar, Jagannath in Puri, Virupaksha in Hampi and Dilwara at Mount Abu, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
89.tq: Recall the location of each temple.
n: Lingaraj is in Bhubaneswar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 110-111]
Jagannath is in Puri. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 110-111]
Virupaksha is in Hampi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 110-111]
Dilwara is in Mount Abu. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 110-111]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i** — option **(3)**.
**Lingaraj** → **Bhubaneswar**; **Jagannath** → **Puri**.
**Virupaksha** → **Hampi**; **Dilwara** → **Mount Abu**.
xa: Dilwara is a **Jain** temple of **marble**.
**Chausath Yogini** at **Morena** is **circular**.
**Khajuraho** (Madhya Pradesh) — **Nagara style**.
Nagara towers: curvilinear **shikhara**; Dravida: pyramidal **vimana**.

89.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Kailasanathar
(b) Mahabalipuram Rathas
(c) Chausath Yogini
(d) Khajuraho

List-II
(i) Circular
(ii) Nagara
(iii) Rajsimha style
(iv) Mamalla style
89.x: Kailasanathar is in the Rajasimha style, the Mahabalipuram Rathas in the Mamalla style, Chausath Yogini is circular and Khajuraho is Nagara, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
89.tq: Link each temple with its architectural style.
n: Khajuraho has the Nagara style. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 110-111]
Kailasanathar has the Rajsimha style. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 110-111]
Mahabalipuram Rathas have the Mamalla style. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 110-111]
Chausath Yogini is circular. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 110-111]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii** — option **(2)**.
**Kailasanathar** (Kanchipuram) → **Rajsimha style**; **Mahabalipuram Rathas** → **Mamalla style**.
**Chausath Yogini** (Morena) → **Circular**; **Khajuraho** → **Nagara**.
xa: **Vesara** = hybrid of Nagara and Dravida, pioneered by the **Badami Chalukyas**.
**Teli temple, Gwalior** — pinnacle in **Dravida** style (UPPSC 2016 key).
UPPSC 2018 chronology: **Seven Pagodas → Shore Temple → Brihadeeswara → Gangaikondacholapuram**.
⚠ **Vimana** = Dravida tower; **shikhara** = Nagara tower.

90.s: Which one of the following was the earlier capital of the Hoysalas?
90.x: Belur was the earlier capital of the Hoysalas, before Dwarasamudra became their capital.
90.tq: Use the capital-sequence distinction rather than confusing a capital with a temple site.
xs: **Belur** was the **earlier capital** of the Hoysalas, so option **(2)** is correct.
The later capital was **Dwarasamudra** (modern **Halebid**). **Somanathapura** is a temple site, **Talakad** a battle site and **Devagiri** the Yadava capital.
xa: ⚠ **Dwarasamudra** = old name; **Halebid** = modern name.
Hoysala monuments at **Halebid and Belur** (**UPSC 2001**).
Belur's **Chennakeshava** temple was built by **Vishnuvardhana** in **1117**.

90.s: Which Hoysala ruler made the Hoysalas independent after defeating Yadava Bhillama?
90.x: Veera Ballala II defeated Yadava Bhillama and made the Hoysalas independent; his reign is given as 1170–1220.
90.tq: Link the victory and political consequence to the correct ruler.
xs: **Veera Ballala II** (**1170-1220**) defeated Yadava **Bhillama** and made the Hoysalas **independent**, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Narasimha II** (**1220-1254**) fought the Yadavas, and **Narasimha III** was defeated by the Pandyas.
xa: **Nripa Kama II** was an early chief under the **Western Chalukyas**.
**Vishnuvardhana** took **Talakad** from the Cholas.
The Yadavas of **Devagiri** fought constant wars with the Hoysalas.

90.s: Which event is associated with Narasimha III?
o: Victory over the Cholas at Talakad
Defeat of Yadava Ramachandra’s forces in 1305
90.x: Narasimha III was defeated by the Pandya ruler Maravarman Kulasekhara. The Keshava Temple at Somanathapura was also built during his reign.
90.tq: Use the swapped-ruler trap by matching the achievement to the correct reign.
xs: **Narasimha III** (**1254-1295**) was defeated by Pandya **Maravarman Kulasekhara**, so option **(1)** is correct.
Bhillama's defeat was **Veera Ballala II's**, Talakad was **Vishnuvardhana's**, and the **1305** victory was **Ballala III's**.
xa: **Somanathapura** was built in his reign, by his general **Somanatha** (**1268**).
Its **Keshava** temple has the best-preserved **star-shaped plan**.
The sculptor **Mallitamma** signed his work at Somanathapura.

90.s: What was the original name of Vishnuvardhana?
90.x: Vishnuvardhana was originally known as Bittideva, also called Bittiga.
90.tq: Test a ruler’s original name directly, a common history recall pattern.
xs: Vishnuvardhana's original name was **Bittideva (Bittiga)**, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Ketamalla** was his officer who built **Hoysaleswara**, **Pedarudru** was a **Kakatiya** commander and **Bhillama** was a **Yadava**.
xa: He converted from **Jain** to **Vaishnava** under **Ramanuja**.
His queen **Shantala Devi** remained a **Jain**.
⚠ **Bittideva** = Vishnuvardhana; **Talakadugonda** = his Talakad title.

90.s:
Consider the following statements about Vishnuvardhana:
1. He converted from Jainism to Vaishnavism under Ramanuja, who had taken refuge in Hoysala territory from Chola persecution.
2. His queen Shantala Devi also became a Vaishnava, and the court stopped patronising Jain basadis.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
90.x: Statement 1 is correct: Bittideva became a Vaishnava under Ramanuja. Statement 2 is wrong: Shantala Devi stayed a Jain and the court kept patronising Jain basadis. So '2 only', 'Both' and 'Neither' are wrong.
90.tq: King turned Vaishnava, queen stayed Jain - religious tolerance.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct, so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Bittideva** turned from **Jain** to **Vaishnava** under **Ramanuja**, who had fled **Chola persecution**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Shantala Devi stayed a Jain**, and the court kept patronising **Jain basadis**.
xa: Vishnuvardhana built **Chennakeshava, Belur** in **1117**.
He defeated the Cholas at **Talakad** and took the title **Talakadugonda**.
A **veeragallu** found at **Neeragunda** may settle the date of his death.

90.s: Vishnuvardhana assumed the title ‘Talakadugonda’ after his victory over the:
90.x: Vishnuvardhana defeated the Cholas at Talakad and assumed the title Talakadugonda.
90.tq: Connect the victory site with the title derived from it.
xs: **Vishnuvardhana** took the title **Talakadugonda** after defeating the **Cholas at Talakad**, so option **(3)** is correct.
The **Yadavas of Devagiri** and the **Pandyas** were later Hoysala rivals, not the enemy at Talakad.
xa: After Talakad he built **Chennakeshava, Belur** (**1117**).
He expanded the kingdom and built **Belur**.
His original name was **Bittideva**.

90.s: Which one of the following statements about Hoysala decline is correct?
o: The Hoysalas faced constant wars with the Yadavas of Devagiri and the Pandyas.
The Hoysalas maintained uninterrupted peace with both the Yadavas and the Pandyas.
The Pandyas were defeated by Narasimha III and became permanent Hoysala allies.
The Yadavas of Devagiri never attacked the Hoysala kingdom.
90.x: The Hoysalas were involved in constant wars with the Yadavas of Devagiri and the Pandyas. Singhana defeated the Hoysalas, while Mahadeva Yadava was defeated by them; Narasimha III was defeated by the Pandyas.
90.tq: Reject absolute peace claims and identify the accurate cause of political decline.
xs: The Hoysalas fought **constant wars** with the **Yadavas of Devagiri** and the **Pandyas**, so option **(1)** is correct.
Yadava **Singhana** defeated the Hoysalas, and **Mahadeva Yadava** was defeated by them.
The **Pandyas** defeated **Narasimha III**. They did not become allies.
xa: **Malik Kafur** took **Dwarasamudra** in **1311**.
**Ballala III** died in **1342**, and the space passed to **Vijayanagara**.
**Veera Ballala II** defeated Yadava **Bhillama**.

90.s: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct regarding Malik Kafur’s southern campaign?
o: Dwarasamudra was one of the southern capitals attacked by Malik Kafur.
Malik Kafur attacked Dwarasamudra only after the kingdom had passed to Vijayanagara.
The four affected powers included the Yadavas, Kakatiyas, Hoysalas and Pandyas.
90.x: Malik Kafur took Dwarasamudra in 1311, before the Hoysala kingdom’s space passed to Vijayanagara. The Yadavas, Kakatiyas, Hoysalas and Pandyas were among the four southern powers affected by his campaign.
90.tq: Use chronology to identify the statement that places an event after the wrong political transition.
xs: Statement 3 is NOT correct: Kafur took **Dwarasamudra** in **1311**, long before the kingdom passed to **Vijayanagara** (after **1342**). So option **(3)** is the answer.
Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct: Dwarasamudra was one of **four** southern capitals attacked (**Yadavas**, **Kakatiyas**, **Hoysalas**, **Pandyas**).
xa: **Halebidu** ("old city") got its name after the **Delhi armies** sacked Dwarasamudra.
The ruler then was **Ballala III** (**1295-1342**).
Vijayanagara architecture followed the **Hoysala** and **Pandya** styles.

90.s: Ballala III died in which year, after which the space of the Hoysala kingdom passed to Vijayanagara?
90.x: Ballala III died in 1342, and the political space of the Hoysala kingdom subsequently passed to Vijayanagara.
90.tq: Distinguish the dates of the Yadava conflict, Malik Kafur’s attack and Ballala III’s death.
xs: **Ballala III** died in **1342**, and the kingdom's space passed to **Vijayanagara**, so option **(3)** is correct.
**1305** was his victory over Yadava **Ramachandra's** forces; **1311** was **Malik Kafur's** capture of Dwarasamudra.
xa: He was defeated by Kakatiya commander **Pedarudru** after **1316**.
Kafur attacked the **Yadavas**, **Kakatiyas**, **Hoysalas** and **Pandyas**.

90.s:
Consider the following statements about Hoysala temples:
1. The Hoysaleswara temple at Halebid is dedicated to Shiva.
2. The Hoysaleswara temple was built by Ketamalla, an officer of Vishnuvardhana.
3. The Chennakeshava temple at Belur was built by Narasimha III.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
90.x: Statement 1 is correct: Hoysaleswara is a Shiva temple. Statement 2 is correct: it was built by Ketamalla, Vishnuvardhana's officer (c. 1121). Statement 3 is wrong: Chennakeshava at Belur was built by Vishnuvardhana (1117); Somanathapura's Keshava temple belongs to Narasimha III's reign. So '2 only' is incomplete and options with 3 are wrong.
90.tq: Belur = Vishnuvardhana; Halebid = Ketamalla; Somanathapura = Somanatha under Narasimha III.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct, so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Hoysaleswara**, Halebid, is a **Shiva** temple.
Statement 2 is correct: it was built by **Ketamalla**, an officer of **Vishnuvardhana**, c. **1121**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Chennakeshava, Belur** was built by **Vishnuvardhana** (**1117**), not **Narasimha III**.
xa: ⚠ Hoysaleswara = **Shiva**; Belur and Somanathapura = **Vishnu**.
**Somanathapura** was built in **Narasimha III's** reign (**1268**).
Hoysaleswara is classed as **Vesara** (**CGPSC 2023**).

90.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Keshava Temple at Somanathapura?
o: It is dedicated to Shiva and was built by Ketamalla.
It is dedicated to Vishnu and was built by Somanatha.
It is dedicated to Vishnu and was built by Vishnuvardhana.
It is dedicated to Shiva and was built by Narasimha III.
90.x: The Keshava Temple at Somanathapura is dedicated to Vishnu and was built in 1268 by Somanatha, the general of Narasimha III.
90.tq: Check the deity and builder together to defeat a swapped-pair option.
xs: The **Keshava** temple, Somanathapura, is a **Vishnu** temple built by **Somanatha**, general of **Narasimha III**, in **1268**, so option **(2)** is correct.
**Ketamalla** built the **Shiva** temple at Halebid, and **Vishnuvardhana** built Belur.
xa: It has the best-preserved **star-shaped plan** (**UPSC**).
The sculptor **Mallitamma** left his signature there.
It is part of the UNESCO **Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas** (**2023**).

90.s: Which one of the following temples is noted for having the best-preserved star-shaped plan?
90.x: The Keshava Temple at Somanathapura is regarded as having the best-preserved star-shaped plan.
90.tq: Use the distinctive architectural superlative to distinguish the three major temples.
xs: The **Keshava temple, Somanathapura** has the best-preserved **star-shaped plan**, so option **(4)** is correct (**UPSC**).
**Hoysaleswara** (Halebid) and **Chennakeshava** (Belur) are the other two Hoysala ensemble temples.
xa: The stellate plan originated under the **Chalukyas** (**6th c.**) and peaked under the **Hoysalas** (**12th c.**).
The **Kalyani Chalukyas** passed on **soapstone** and **star plans**.
The temples stand on a raised **jagati** about **1 m** high.

90.s: The Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas were inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in:

Consider the following statements about the Dnyaneshwari:
1. It is a Sanskrit commentary on the Upanishads.
2. It was written in 1290 at Nevasa, in the reign of Ramachandra.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
91.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the Dnyaneshwari is a Marathi commentary on the Gita. Statement 2 is correct: it was written in 1290 at Nevasa under Ramachandra. So 2 only.
91.tq: Dnyaneshwari = Marathi Gita commentary, 1290.
xs: Only statement **2** is correct — option **(2) 2 only**.
Statement 1 is wrong: the **Dnyaneshwari** is a **Marathi** commentary on the **Gita**.
Statement 2 is correct: it was written in **1290** at **Nevasa**, in **Ramachandra**'s reign.
xa: Bhakti saints **Dnyaneshwar, Namdev**, later **Tukaram, Ramdas** took Gita ideas into Marathi.
The Yadavas encouraged **Marathi**; Sanskrit was the language of scholarship.
**Hemadri** served **Mahadeva and Ramachandra** as **Shrikaranadhipa**.
⚠ **Sangita Ratnakara** = **Sarngadeva**; **Chaturvarga Chintamani** = **Hemadri**.

91.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Chakradhar Swami — Founder of the Mahanubhava sect
Dnyaneshwar — Founder of the Mahanubhava sect
91.x: The Mahanubhava sect was founded by Chakradhar Swami. Dnyaneshwar composed the Dnyaneshwari; he did not found the Mahanubhava sect.
91.tq: Separate the founder, author and literary work in a cultural movement.
xs: **Dnyaneshwar** did not found the **Mahanubhava** sect, so option **(4)** is the wrong pair.
The founder was **Chakradhar Swami**. Dnyaneshwar wrote the **Dnyaneshwari**.
The other pairs are correct: **Lilacharitra** = first Marathi prose work, by the Mahanubhava author **Mhaimbhat**.
xa: The Dnyaneshwari was written in **1290** at Nevasa.
Other Bhakti saints: **Namdev**, later **Tukaram** and **Ramdas**.
The Yadavas' mother tongue was **Marathi**.

91.s:
Consider the following statements about the Delhi Sultanate and the Yadavas:
1. In 1295, Alauddin Khalji, acting for Sultan Jalaluddin, defeated Ramachandra at Devagiri, and the Yadavas became Delhi vassals.
2. During Malik Kafur's campaign of 1307-08, Harapaladeva submitted and was taken to Delhi.
3. After 1323, Devagiri's vizier Malik Burhanuddin was given charge of conquered Andhra.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
91.x: Statement 1 is correct: the 1295 raid by Alauddin (for Jalaluddin) made the Yadavas Delhi vassals. Statement 2 is wrong: in 1307-08 it was Ramachandra who submitted and was taken to Delhi; Harapaladeva was killed in Mubarak Khalji's invasion of 1317-18. Statement 3 is correct: Malik Burhanuddin got charge of Andhra after 1323. So options with 2 are wrong.
91.tq: 1295 Alauddin; 1307-08 Ramachandra submits; 1317-18 Harapaladeva killed.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct, so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: in **1295** **Alauddin Khalji** (for **Jalaluddin**) defeated **Ramachandra**, and the Yadavas became Delhi vassals.
Statement 2 is wrong: in **1307-08** it was **Ramachandra** who submitted. **Harapaladeva** was killed in **1317-18**.
Statement 3 is correct: after **1323** **Malik Burhanuddin** got charge of Andhra.
xa: The **1295** raid also took **Ellichpur**. Many texts date it **1296**.
After 1323, **Devagiri** was the Sultanate's **Deccan base**.
Harapaladeva was killed in **Mubarak Khalji's** invasion.

91.s: Which sequence correctly represents the major Delhi Sultanate interventions in the Yadava kingdom?
o: 1295 first invasion; 1307–08 Malik Kafur’s campaign; 1313 Shankaradeva killed; 1317–18 Harapaladeva killed
1307–08 first invasion; 1295 Shankaradeva killed; 1317–18 Malik Kafur’s campaign; 1313 kingdom founded
1313 first invasion; 1295 Harapaladeva killed; 1307–08 kingdom restored; 1317–18 Ramachandra crowned
1295 Harapaladeva killed; 1313 Malik Kafur appointed vizier; 1307–08 Devagiri founded; 1317–18 Ramachandra submits
91.x: The sequence was the 1295 first invasion, Malik Kafur’s 1307–08 campaign, Shankaradeva’s death in 1313, and Harapaladeva’s death in 1317–18.
91.tq: Use the dated invasion sequence from first defeat to dynastic extinction.
xs: The sequence is **1295** first invasion → **1307-08** Kafur's campaign → **1313** Shankaradeva killed → **1317-18** Harapaladeva killed, so option **(1)** is correct.
Shankaradeva (**1311-1313**) died in **Malik Kafur's** invasion, and Harapaladeva in **Mubarak Khalji's**.
xa: The 1295 invasion was the **first Muslim invasion of the South**.
In 1307-08 **Ramachandra** submitted and was taken to Delhi.
Devagiri was the first southern kingdom to fall, opening the road to **Warangal**, **Dwarasamudra** and **Madurai**.

91.s: The importance of Devagiri in the expansion of the Delhi Sultanate lay in the fact that it
o: was the first southern kingdom to fall to Delhi and opened routes towards major southern kingdoms
prevented all further Delhi campaigns into the Deccan
was the first capital established by the Hoysalas in northern India
served as the original capital of the Kakatiyas
91.x: Devagiri was the first southern kingdom to fall to Delhi, opening the road to Warangal, Dwarasamudra and Madurai.
91.tq: Apply the historical significance of a strategic conquest.
xs: **Devagiri** was the **first southern kingdom to fall to Delhi** and opened the road to **Warangal**, **Dwarasamudra** and **Madurai**, so option **(1)** is correct (**UPSC**).
Devagiri was the **Yadava** capital, founded by **Bhillama V**, not a Hoysala or Kakatiya capital.
xa: First raid: **1295**, by **Alauddin Khalji**.
After **1323**, Devagiri = the Sultanate's **Deccan base**.
**Malik Burhanuddin** was the vizier of Devagiri.

91.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Yadavas were centred on Devagiri.
The Yadavas were identified with western India.
The Yadavas were centred on Warangal.
The Yadavas were associated with the Deccan.
91.x: Option C is incorrect: the Yadavas (Seunas) were centred on Devagiri in the western Deccan. Warangal was the Kakatiya capital.
91.tq: Match each capital with its dynasty.
n: Warangal was an important capital of the Kakatiyas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #149-2 · pp 260-261]
The Yadava realm was located in western India and the Deccan. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #149-2 · pp 260-261]
The Yadava realm was centred on Devagiri. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #149-2 · pp 260-261]
xs: The incorrect statement is **the Yadavas were centred on Warangal** — option **(3)**.
The Yadavas (**Seuna** rulers) were **centred on Devagiri**, in **western India** and the **Deccan**.
**Warangal** was the **Kakatiya** capital.
xa: The Yadavas ruled around **1187–1317 AD**, first as feudatories of the **Western Chalukyas**.
**Bhillama V** founded **Devagiri**; **Singhana II** was the greatest; **Harapaladeva** the last.
**1295**: first Muslim invasion of the South, on Devagiri — **Alauddin Khalji** defeated **Ramachandra**.
Devagiri was the **first southern kingdom** to fall to Delhi.

92.s: Which one of the following correctly states the two principal views regarding the progenitor of the Kakatiyas?
o: Prola I of Hanamkonda and Beta I of Orugallu
Kakara Gundana of Magallu and Venna Bhupati of Bayyaram
Rudradeva of Anumakonda and Ganapatideva of Motupalli
Danarnava of Vengi and Durjaya of Pithapuram
92.x: The progenitor is identified in different traditions as Kakara Gundana of Magallu or Venna Bhupati of Bayyaram.
92.tq: Compare competing origin traditions without treating one disputed view as exclusive.
xs: The progenitor is either **Kakara Gundana** (**Magallu**) or **Venna Bhupati** (**Bayyaram**), so option **(2)** is correct.
The **Magallu grant** (**956 CE**) of Eastern Chalukya **Danarnava** names Gundana, and the **Bayyaram** inscription names Venna.
**Danarnava** issued the Magallu grant and was not a Kakatiya progenitor.
xa: The Bayyaram inscription traces the line from **Durjaya**.
The **Bayyaram tank** inscription (**1219**), by **Mailamba**, gives the best genealogy of the early Kakatiyas.
First mention of the Kakatiyas = **Magallu 956**.

92.s:
Consider the following statements about the Kakatiyas:
1. Their Samanta (feudatory) phase lasted from 956 to 1162 and their sovereign phase from 1163 to 1323.
2. The early Kakatiyas were Shaivas who later became Jains.
3. They were Shudras by caste, and Sanskrit was their official language.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
92.x: Statement 1 is correct: Samanta 956-1162, sovereign 1163-1323. Statement 2 is wrong: the early Kakatiyas were Jains who later became Shaivas (APPSC G2 2011). Statement 3 is correct: their caste is given as Shudras and their official language as Sanskrit. So '1 only' is incomplete and options with 2 are wrong.
92.tq: Jain first, Shaiva later - the order is the trap.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct, so option **(3)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: the **Samanta** phase ran **956-1162**, and the **sovereign** phase **1163-1323**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the early Kakatiyas were **Jains** who later became **Shaivas** (**APPSC G2 2011**).
Statement 3 is correct: they were **Shudras**, with **Sanskrit** as their official language.
xa: Emblem: **Garuda** (Rashtrakuta phase) → **Varaha** (Kalyani Chalukya phase).
Clan deity **Kakatamma (Kakati Devi)** = the Jain **Kushmandini** absorbed into Hinduism.
**Telugu** replaced Sanskrit in inscriptions from **Ganapatideva's** reign.

92.s: ‘Kakati’ in the explanation of the Kakatiya clan deity is associated with which meaning?
92.x: Kakati means gourd. Kakatamma, or Kakati Devi, was associated with the Jain Kushmandini before being absorbed into Hindu tradition.
92.tq: Discriminate the exact etymological meaning from emblem and deity associations.
xs: **"Kakati"** means **gourd**, so option **(1)** is correct.
The clan deity **Kakatamma (Kakati Devi)** was the Jain **Kushmandini**, absorbed into Hinduism.
xa: The early Kakatiyas were **Jains** (**APPSC G2 2011**), later **Shaivas**.
The **Varaha** (boar) was their emblem in the Kalyani Chalukya phase.
The **Garuda** was their emblem in the Rashtrakuta phase.

92.s:
Consider the following statements about the early Kakatiyas:
1. Their early territorial base was the Hanamkonda Vishaya.
2. They were first feudatories of the Kalyani Chalukyas and later of the Rashtrakutas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
92.x: Statement 1 is correct: the base was Hanamkonda Vishaya (modern Karimnagar, Warangal, Khammam). Statement 2 is wrong: the order is reversed; they served the Rashtrakutas first and then the Kalyani Chalukyas. So 1 only.
92.tq: Rashtrakutas first, then Kalyani Chalukyas (emblem Garuda -> Varaha).
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: the base was **Hanamkonda Vishaya** (modern **Karimnagar, Warangal, Khammam**).
Statement 2 is wrong: the order is reversed — first the **Rashtrakutas** (APPSC G2 2005 key), **then** the **Kalyani Chalukyas**.
xa: ⚠ Another key answers **Eastern Chalukyas** — first mention in **Danarnava**'s **Magallu** grant.
Phases: **samanta 956-1162**, **sovereign 1163-1323**.
Emblem changed **Garuda → Varaha**.
Early Kakatiyas were **Jains** (APPSC G2 2011 key), later **Shaivas**.

92.s: Which of the following statements about Beta I is correct?
o: He was known as Garuda Beta and obtained Anumakonda Vishaya through his aunt Viriyala Kamasani.
He invaded the Yadavas to avenge Rudradeva.
He was known as Arigajakesari and built Kesamudram tank.
He founded Orugallu and composed Nitisara.
92.x: Beta I (Garuda Beta) obtained Anumakonda Vishaya through his aunt Viriyala Kamasani. The other options belong to other rulers: avenging Rudradeva by invading the Yadavas was Mahadeva (B), Arigajakesari and the Kesamudram tank were Prola I (C), and founding Orugallu and writing Nitisara were Rudradeva (D).
92.tq: Use the ruler-achievement association and reject deeds belonging to neighbouring rulers.
xs: **Beta I (Garuda Beta)** got **Anumakonda Vishaya** through his aunt **Viriyala Kamasani**, so option **(1)** is correct.
Avenging Rudradeva was **Mahadeva**; **Arigajakesari** and the **Kesamudram** tank were **Prola I**; **Orugallu** and the **Nitisara** were **Rudradeva**.
xa: Beta I was the first Kakatiya to come to **Hanamkonda** (**Bayyaram** inscription).
He attacked **Kanchi** (**1051**) for **Someshwara I**.
His title: **Chola Chamuvardhi Pramadhana** ('Cholachamu Vari Pramathana').

92.s: Prola I is associated with which combination of titles and achievement?
o: Arigajakesari; Samadhigata Panchamahasabda; construction of Kesamudram tank
Cholachamu Vari Pramathana; Vidyabhushana; construction of the Thousand Pillar Temple
Vidyabhushana; Kanchi Churakara; construction of Arikesari Samudram
Samadhigata Panchamahasabda; Rayagaja Kesari; construction of Ramappa temple
92.x: Prola I bore the titles Arigajakesari and Samadhigata Panchamahasabda and built Kesamudram tank.
92.tq: Start from the sure title and verify the achievement attached to the same ruler.
xs: **Prola I** bore the titles **Arigajakesari** and **Samadhigata Panchamahashabda** and built the **Kesamudram** tank, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Vidyabhushana** was **Rudradeva's** title, and **Rayagajakesari** was **Rudramadevi's**.
xa: ⚠ **Kesamudram** = Prola I; **Kesari Samudram** = Rudradeva; **Arikesari Samudram** = Prola II.
⚠ **APPSC 2025** treated "Prolaraja bore the title Arikesari" as **incorrect**.
Prola I made **Anumakonda** the capital (**1052-1076**).

92.s: Which change is associated with Prola I during the development of the Kakatiya polity?
o: The capital changed from Orugallu to Anumakonda.
The emblem changed from Varaha to Garuda.
The capital changed from Hanamkonda to Kanchi.
The emblem changed from Garuda to Varaha.
92.x: During Prola I’s period, the Kakatiya emblem changed from Garuda to Varaha.
92.tq: Discriminate between the two directions of an emblem change.
xs: Under **Prola I** the emblem changed from **Garuda to Varaha**, so option **(4)** is correct.
Option (2) reverses the change. Prola I also made **Anumakonda**, not Orugallu or Kanchi, the capital.
xa: Garuda belonged to the **Rashtrakuta** phase; Varaha to the **Kalyani Chalukya** phase.
Prola I served **Someshwara I** and **Vikramaditya VI**.

92.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Beta II — Shivapura and Betesvaralayam
2. Durgaraja — donations to the Betesvara temple
3. Prola II — victory pillar at Srisailam
4. Mahadeva — construction of Ramappa temple
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
92.x: Beta II built Shivapura and Betesvaralayam, Durgaraja made donations to the Betesvara temple, and Prola II erected a victory pillar at Srisailam. Ramappa temple belongs to the reign of Ganapatideva, not Mahadeva.
92.tq: Find the swapped ruler–achievement statement before selecting the coded combination.
xs: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Beta II** built **Shivapura** and **Betesvaralayam**; **Durgaraja** made donations to the **Betesvara** temple (**Kazipet Dargah** inscription).
**Prola II** set up a **victory pillar at Srisailam**.
Pair 4 is wrong: the **Ramappa** temple was built by **Recherla Rudra** (**1213**) in **Ganapatideva's** reign.
xa: Beta II's title: **Vikrama Chakri**.
**Mahadeva** (**1195-1199**) died in the revenge war against the Yadavas.
Ramappa = UNESCO World Heritage Site, **2021**.

92.s: Beta II was initiated into Saivism by Rameswara Pandita of which institution?
92.x: Beta II was initiated into Saivism by Rameswara Pandita of the Srisailam Mallikarjuna matha.
92.tq: Identify the religious teacher through the institution associated with him.
xs: **Beta II** was initiated into Saivism by **Rameswara Pandita** of the **Srisailam Mallikarjuna matha**, so option **(1)** is correct (**APPSC 2025**).
He gave his guru **Vaijanapalli**, as recorded in the **Thousand Pillar** inscription.
xa: Beta II ruled **1076-1108**.
His title was **Vikrama Chakri**.
**Mahadeva's** guru was **Dhruveshwara Pandita**.

92.s:
Consider the following statements about Rudradeva (Prataparudra I):
1. He declared Kakatiya independence in 1163, as recorded in the Thousand Pillar inscription.
2. The APPSC 2019 key credits him with building Kesari Samudram.
3. He was killed by the Hoysala ruler Veera Ballala II.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
92.x: Statement 1 is correct: Rudradeva declared independence in 1163 (Thousand Pillar inscription). Statement 2 is correct: the APPSC 2019 key gives Kesari Samudram to Rudradeva. Statement 3 is wrong: he was killed by the Yadava Jaitugi, not a Hoysala. So '1 only' is incomplete and options with 3 are wrong.
92.tq: Rudradeva: 1163 independence, Thousand Pillar temple, Kesari Samudram, killed by Jaitugi.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct, so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Rudradeva** declared **independence in 1163** (Thousand Pillar/Anumakonda inscription).
Statement 2 is correct: the **APPSC 2019** key gives **Kesari Samudram** to Rudradeva.
Statement 3 is wrong: he was killed by the Yadava **Jaitugi**, not a Hoysala.
xa: He founded **Orugallu** and wrote the **'Nitisara'**.
The inscription was found by **J.S. Fleet** and composed by **Achitendru**.
Titles: **Vidyabhushana**, **Vinaya Vibhushanudu**.

92.s: Which of the following statements regarding Mahadeva is correct?
o: He built the Jain Kadalalaya at Anumakonda.
He invaded the Yadavas to avenge Rudradeva and died in battle while crossing a river on an elephant.
He issued the Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam in 1244.
He founded Orugallu and completed its fortifications.
92.x: Mahadeva invaded the Yadavas to avenge Rudradeva and died in battle, reportedly on an elephant while crossing a river.
92.tq: Use the unusual detail of the ruler’s death to identify the correct statement.
xs: **Mahadeva** invaded the Yadavas to **avenge Rudradeva** and died fighting, on an **elephant**, while crossing a river, so option **(2)** is correct.
The Kadalalaya was built by **Chetanamatya**, Motupalli is **Ganapatideva's** and Orugallu was founded by **Rudradeva**.
xa: Mahadeva ruled **1195-1199**.
His guru was **Dhruveshwara Pandita**.
His son **Ganapatideva** was held captive by **Jaitugi**.

92.s: Which one of the following combinations relating to Ganapatideva is correctly matched?
o: 63-year reign; Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam of 1244; Ramappa temple built during his reign
44-year reign; Draksharamam inscription of 1158; Thousand Pillar Temple built during his reign
19-year reign; Bayyaram inscription; Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya at Sanigaram
8-year reign; Kazipet Dargah inscription; Swayambhu temple built during his reign
92.x: Ganapatideva ruled for 63 years, issued the Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam in 1244, and Ramappa temple was built during his reign by Recherla Rudra.
92.tq: Match the ruler with the period length, charter and monumental achievement.
xs: **Ganapatideva** ruled **63 years**, issued the **Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam** (**1244**), and **Ramappa** was built in his reign, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Draksharamam** (**1158**) describes Rudradeva's accession, and the **Thousand Pillar** temple is Rudradeva's (**1163**).
xa: His reign: **1199-1262**; title **Andhra Deshadhiswara**.
He granted the **Ganapavaram** villages.
He built the **Lakkavaram** and **Ghanapur** tanks.

92.s: Which of the following set contains only works or grants associated with Ganapatideva’s reign?
o: Ramappa temple, Lakkavaram tank, Ghanapur tank and Ganapavaram villages
Arikesari Samudram, victory pillar at Srisailam and Betesvaralayam
Thousand Pillar Temple, Kadalalaya Jainavasadi and Kesamudram tank
Kesamudram tank, Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya and Swayambhu temple
92.x: Ramappa temple, the Lakkavaram and Ghanapur tanks, and the grant of Ganapavaram villages are associated with Ganapatideva’s reign.
92.tq: Eliminate sets containing achievements of different Kakatiya rulers.
xs: **Ramappa** temple, the **Lakkavaram** and **Ghanapur** tanks and the **Ganapavaram** villages all belong to **Ganapatideva's** reign, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Arikesari Samudram** and the Srisailam pillar are **Prola II's**; **Kesamudram** is **Prola I's**; the **Thousand Pillar** temple is **Rudradeva's**.
xa: **Chouda Samudram** was built by **Malyala Chauda Senani**.
**Betesvaralayam** was built by **Beta II**.
Exam angle: match **tank → builder** and **ruler → temple**.

92.s:
Arrange the following Kakatiya rulers in chronological order of their reigns:
A. Prola II
B. Beta II
C. Rudradeva
D. Mahadeva
92.x: The order is Beta II (1076–1108), Prola II (1116–1157), Rudradeva (1158–1195), and Mahadeva (1195–1199).
92.tq: Fix the sequence using the beginning and end of each ruler’s reign.
xs: The order is **Beta II** (**1076-1108**) → **Prola II** (**1116-1157**) → **Rudradeva** (**1158-1195**) → **Mahadeva** (**1195-1199**), i.e. B, A, C, D. So option **(1)** is correct.
**Durgaraja** (**1108-1116**) came between Beta II and Prola II.
xa: **Ganapatideva** followed (**1199-1262**).
Then **Rudrama Devi** (**1262-1289**).
Last ruler: **Prataparudra II**.

92.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the names associated with the Kakatiya capital:
1. Andhranagari was a name used for Orugallu under Ganapatideva.
2. Sultanpur was the name given to Orugallu after the conquest of 1323.
3. Orugallu was the early capital made by Prola I.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
92.x: Andhranagari was used under Ganapatideva, and Sultanpur was the name given after the conquest of 1323. The early capital was Anumakonda or Hanamkonda, not Orugallu.
92.tq: Split the statements by distinguishing the successive names and stages of the capital.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct, so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Andhranagari** was used under **Ganapatideva**.
Statement 2 is correct: it was renamed **Sultanpur** after **1323**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Prola I's** capital was **Anumakonda (Hanamkonda)**, not Orugallu.
xa: **Prola II** developed Hanamkonda.
⚠ "Who shifted the capital to Orugallu?" → **Rudradeva**.
**Ganapatideva** completed Orugallu.

92.s: With reference to the development of the Kakatiya capital, which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Prola I — made Orugallu the capital
Rudradeva — gave Orugallu the name Sultanpur
92.x: Prola II developed Hanamkonda. Prola I made Anumakonda the capital, Rudradeva shifted the capital to Orugallu, and Sultanpur was the post-1323 name.
92.tq: Match each ruler with the correct stage in the evolution of the capital.
xs: **Prola II** = **developed Hanamkonda** is correctly matched, so option **(2)** is correct.
**Prola I** made **Anumakonda**, not Orugallu, the capital; **Rudradeva** shifted the capital to Orugallu; **Sultanpur** was the post-**1323** name.
xa: Rudradeva began the **Warangal fort**.
**Ganapatideva** completed Orugallu and moved the court there.
Orugallu = "**single rock**".

92.s: Which of the following correctly describes the respective roles of Rudradeva and Ganapatideva in relation to Orugallu?
o: Rudradeva began fortifying Orugallu, while Ganapatideva completed it and fully moved the court there.
Ganapatideva shifted the capital to Orugallu, while Rudradeva renamed it Sultanpur.
Rudradeva abandoned Orugallu, while Ganapatideva restored Hanamkonda as the capital.
Rudradeva completed the city and Ganapatideva began its fortification.
92.x: Rudradeva shifted the capital and began fortifying Orugallu. Ganapatideva completed the city and fully transferred the court there.
92.tq: Separate the initiating ruler from the ruler who completed the work.
xs: **Rudradeva** began fortifying **Orugallu**, and **Ganapatideva** completed it and fully moved the court there, so option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ The "who shifted" answer is **Rudradeva** (**APPSC G2 2019**). Some notes say Ganapati made the final transfer.
xa: The fortification became the **Warangal fort**.
Under Ganapatideva the city was called **Andhranagari**.
After **1323** it was **Sultanpur**.

92.s:
Consider the following statements about Ganapatideva:
1. He was released from Yadava captivity in 1199; his first inscription is at Manthena.
2. He bore the title 'Andhra Deshadhiswara' and unified Telugudesam.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
92.x: Statement 1 is correct: released in 1199, first inscription Manthena (26 Dec 1199). Statement 2 is correct: he bore the title Andhra Deshadhiswara and unified Telugudesam. So both.
92.tq: Ganapatideva = 1199 release, Andhra Deshadhiswara.
xs: **Both** statements are correct — option **(3) Both 1 and 2**.
Statement 1: **Ganapatideva** was released from Yadava captivity in **1199**; his first inscription is at **Manthena** (**26 Dec 1199**).
Statement 2: he bore the title **'Andhra Deshadhiswara'** and unified **Telugudesam**.
xa: General **Recherla Rudra** crushed revolts and installed him.
He married Pinnachodi's daughters **Narama and Perama**; their brother **Jayapa** became Gajasahani.
He ruled **1199-1262** (**63 years**), the greatest Kakatiya.
**Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam** (**1244**) protected foreign traders.

92.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Ganapatideva and the Velanati Chodas:
1. Ganapatideva and Choda Tikka of Nellore jointly killed Prithviswara in 1210.
2. Both rulers assumed the title Prithviswara Shirakhandika Kreeda Vinoda.
3. The Velanati kingdom came to an end in 1210.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
92.x: All three statements are correct. Prithviswara was killed in 1210, the joint title was adopted by Ganapatideva and Choda Tikka, and the Velanati kingdom ended in that year.
92.tq: Check the linked event, title and consequence as one chronological cluster.
xs: All three statements are correct, so option **(4)** is correct.
**Ganapatideva** and Nellore's **Choda Tikka** jointly killed **Prithviswara** in **1210**.
Both took the title **"Prithviswara Shirakhandika Kreeda Vinoda"**, and the **Velanati** kingdom ended in **1210**.
xa: Final end of the Velanati Chodas: **Mummadi Rajendra Chola** killed in **1257**.
Prithviswara's **Pithapuram** inscription names **Kolleru Lake**.
General **Mutyalachaundaraya** took **Divi**.

92.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the political arrangements made by Ganapatideva after the coastal campaign?
o: He married the daughters of Prithviswara and appointed Akkana as Gajasahani.
He married the daughters of Pinnachodi and appointed their brother Jayapa as Gajasahani.
He married the daughters of Mummadi Rajendra Chola and appointed Bayyana as Gajasahani.
He married the daughters of Manumasiddhi and appointed Tikkana as Gajasahani.
92.x: Ganapatideva married Pinnachodi's daughters Narama and Perama, and appointed their brother Jayapa as Gajasahani, the chief of the elephant forces.
92.tq: Test a multi-person relationship by separating family ties from political office.
xs: Ganapatideva married **Pinnachodi's** daughters **Narama** and **Perama** and made their brother **Jayapa** **'Gajasahani'**, so option **(2)** is correct.
**Gajasahani** = chief of the **elephant force**.
**Akkana** and **Bayyana** were allies against **Manumasiddhi**, and **Tikkana** was a poet-envoy.
xa: The coastal campaign began **from 1201**.
**Mutyalachaundaraya** took **Divi**.
Ganapatideva held coastal Andhra firmly.

92.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. In 1257, Ganapatideva allied with Akkana and Bayyana and killed Mummadi Rajendra Chola, finally ending the Velanati Chodas.
2. Tikkana dedicated his Nirvachanottara Ramayana to Ganapatideva.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
92.x: Statement 1 is correct: the 1257 alliance killed Mummadi Rajendra Chola, the final end of the Velanati Chodas. Statement 2 is wrong: Tikkana dedicated the Nirvachanottara Ramayana to Manumasiddhi of Nellore. So '2 only', 'Both' and 'Neither' are wrong.
92.tq: Tikkana's patron = Manumasiddhi; he went as envoy to Ganapatideva.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct, so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: in **1257** Ganapatideva allied with **Akkana** and **Bayyana** and killed **Mummadi Rajendra Chola**, the final end of the Velanati Chodas.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Tikkana** dedicated his **Nirvachanottara Ramayana** to **Manumasiddhi**, not Ganapatideva.
xa: Ganapatideva restored **Manumasiddhi II** to the Nellore throne.
**Tikkana** went as envoy to seek his help.
**Akkana** and **Bayyana** were enemies of Manumasiddhi.

92.s: Which of the following correctly describes the consequence of the Battle of Muttukur?
o: Nellore fell to the Pandyas in 1263.
The Kakatiyas captured Divi from the Pandyas in 1263.
The Velanati kingdom was founded in 1263.
Ganapatideva was released from Yadava captivity in 1263.
92.x: The Pandyas defeated Ganapatideva in 1263, and Nellore fell to them after the Battle of Muttukur.
92.tq: Link the battle with its immediate territorial consequence.
xs: After the **Battle of Muttukur** (**1263**), **Nellore fell** to the **Pandyas**, so option **(1)** is correct (**APPSC G2 2017**).
The **Pandyas** defeated **Ganapatideva** there.
xa: Despite this, he still held **coastal Andhra** firmly.
The battle is also spelt **Muthukuru**.
He had earlier restored **Manumasiddhi II** at Nellore.

92.s:
Consider the following statements about Ganapatideva and Nellore:
1. He restored Manumasiddhi II to the Nellore throne.
2. The poet Tikkana went to him as envoy to seek his help.
3. After his defeat by the Pandyas at Muttukur, he lost all control over coastal Andhra.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
92.x: Statement 1 is correct: Ganapatideva restored Manumasiddhi II. Statement 2 is correct: Tikkana went as envoy. Statement 3 is wrong: Nellore fell to the Pandyas after Muttukur (1263), but Ganapatideva still held coastal Andhra firmly. So only two.
92.tq: Muttukur 1263 = Nellore lost, coast kept.
xs: **Only two** statements are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is correct: Ganapatideva **restored Manumasiddhi II** to the Nellore throne.
Statement 2 is correct: the poet **Tikkana** went as **envoy** to seek his help.
Statement 3 is wrong: after **Muttukur (1263)** only **Nellore** came under **Pandya** control.
xa: In **1210** Ganapati and **Choda Tikka** killed **Prithviswara** — end of the Velanati kingdom.
**1257**: killing of **Mummadi Rajendra Chola** = final end of the Velanati Chodas.
General **Mutyalachaundaraya** took **Divi** (from **1201**).
Tikkana dedicated his **Nirvachanottara Ramayana** to Manumasiddhi.

92.s:
Consider the following statements about the Kakatiyas and the Hoysalas:
1. Prataparudra's commander Pedarudru defeated Hoysala Ballala III after 1316.
2. Hoysala Veera Ballala II's push into the Krishna-Tungabhadra region led Jaitugi to release Ganapatideva.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
92.x: Statement 2 is correct: Veera Ballala II's advance was the reason Jaitugi freed Ganapati. Statement 1 is correct: Pedarudru defeated Ballala III after 1316. So both.
92.tq: Ballala II -> release of Ganapati; Ballala III -> beaten by Pedarudru.
xs: **Both** statements are correct — option **(3) Both 1 and 2**.
Statement 1: Prataparudra's commander **Pedarudru** defeated Hoysala **Ballala III** after **1316**.
Statement 2: **Veera Ballala II**'s push into the **Krishna-Tungabhadra** region was the reason **Jaitugi** freed **Ganapati**.
xa: **Jaitugi** killed **Rudradeva**; **Mahadeva** died in the revenge war.
The Yadava conflict began under **Prola II**.
**Velanati Chodas** killed **Prola II**; Rudradeva avenged him.
Rudradeva defeated the **Kalachuri** confederacy in **1159**.

92.s:
Consider the following statements about Prola II:
1. He was killed fighting the Kalachuri confederacy.
2. The Kakatiya conflict with the Yadavas (Sevunas of Devagiri) began in his reign.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
92.x: Statement 2 is correct: the Yadava conflict began under Prola II. Statement 1 is wrong: Prola II was killed by the Velanati Chodas; Rudradeva avenged him. The Kalachuri confederacy was defeated by Rudradeva in 1159. So 2 only.
92.tq: Prola II killed by Velanati Chodas.
xs: Only statement **2** is correct — option **(1) 2 only**.
Statement 2 is correct: the conflict with the **Yadavas (Sevunas of Devagiri)** began under **Prola II**.
Statement 1 is wrong: Prola II was **killed by the Velanati Chodas**; the **Kalachuri confederacy** was defeated by **Rudradeva** in **1159**.
xa: Prola II (**1116-1157**) set up a **victory pillar** at **Srisailam**.
He is credited with **Arikesari Samudram** and the **Swayambhu** temple.
Rudradeva made **Vellanki Gangadhara** viceroy of Sabbinadu.
Rudradeva declared **independence** in **1163**.

92.s: Which of the following was defeated by Rudradeva?
92.x: Rudradeva defeated the Telugu Chodas and Tailapa III. The Muttukur victory over Ganapatideva belonged to the Pandyas, while Ballala III was defeated later by Pedarudru.
92.tq: Find the option assigning a later or different ruler’s victory to Rudradeva.
xs: **Rudradeva** defeated the **Telugu Chodas** and **Tailapa III**, so option **(2)** is correct.
**Ballala III** was defeated by **Pedarudru** after **1316**, and the **Pandyas** defeated Ganapati at **Muttukur** (**1263**).
xa: Rudradeva defeated the **Kalachuri** confederacy (**Mailagi**, **Medaraja**, **Dommaraja**) in **1159**.
He avenged Prola II against the **Velanati Chodas**.
He declared independence in **1163**.

92.s:
Consider the following statements about Rudrama Devi:
1. Ganapatideva had no son, and she was raised as a son (putrika) to succeed him.
2. She ruled from 1262 to 1289.
3. Her training was guided by her aunt Mailamba.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
92.x: Statement 1 is correct: she was raised as a putrika because Ganapatideva had no son. Statement 2 is correct: she ruled 1262-1289. Statement 3 is wrong: her mother Kupama Devi guided her training; Mailamba was Ganapatideva's sister. So only two.
92.tq: Kupama Devi = Rudrama's mother and guide.
xs: **Only two** statements are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is correct: **Ganapatideva** had **no son**, so **Rudrama Devi** was raised as a son (**putrika**).
Statement 2 is correct: she ruled **1262-1289**.
Statement 3 is wrong: her mother **Kupama Devi** guided her training; **Mailamba** was Ganapati's sister.
xa: Ganapati's daughters: **Rudramamba** (m. **Veerabhadra**) and **Ganapamba** (m. the **Kota** chief).
Sisters **Mailamba** and **Kundamamba** married sons of **Natavadi Buddharaja**.
Mailamba issued the **Bayyaram tank** inscription (**1219**).
Rudrama Devi was the **fourth independent ruler**.

92.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Recherla Rudra — Kakatiya Rajya Bharadhureya
2. Prasadaditya — Kakatiya Rajya Sthapanacharya
3. Malyala Chauda Senani — Chouda Samudram
4. Kamasani — Gudur inscription
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
92.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Recherla Rudra bore the title Kakatiya Rajya Bharadhureya; Prasadaditya was Sthapanacharya; Chauda Senani built Chouda Samudram; and Kamasani’s role is recorded in the Gudur inscription.
92.tq: Verify each family–member–title or achievement pair independently before using the coded options.
xs: All four pairs are correct, so option **(4)** is correct.
**Recherla Rudra** = **'Kakatiya Rajya Bharadhureya'**; **Prasadaditya** (Kayastha) = **'Kakatiya Rajya Sthapanacharya'**.
**Malyala Chauda Senani** built **Chouda Samudram**; **Kamasani** is recorded in the **Gudur** inscription.
xa: Prasadaditya was also **'Raya Pitamahanka'**.
Kamasani (**Viriyala**) made **Garuda Beta** a Chalukya vassal.
**Malyala Gundiya** and **Viriyala Suri** backed **Rudrama**.

92.s: Which family of Kakatiya feudatories is associated with Kamasani?
92.x: Kamasani belonged to the Viriyala family and made Garuda Beta a Chalukya vassal, as recorded in the Gudur inscription.
92.tq: Use the family–member association to separate the four feudatory groups.
xs: **Kamasani** belonged to the **Viriyala** family, so option **(3)** is correct.
She made **Garuda Beta** a Chalukya vassal (**Gudur** inscription).
xa: **Beta I** got **Anumakonda Vishaya** through his aunt **Viriyala Kamasani**.
**Viriyala Suri** backed **Rudrama**.
**Recherla** = Rudra; **Kayastha** = Prasadaditya; **Malyala** = Gundiya, Chauda Senani.

92.s: Recherla Rudra is associated with which combination?
o: Saving the kingdom during Ganapati’s captivity and constructing the Ramappa temple and tank at Palampet
Restoring Manumasiddhi II and serving as an envoy to the Pandyas
Building Chouda Samudram and making Garuda Beta a Chalukya vassal
Defeating Hoysala Ballala III and ruling the Nellore region
92.x: Recherla Rudra saved the kingdom during Ganapati’s captivity and is associated with the Ramappa temple and tank at Palampet.
92.tq: Start from the sure achievement and reject combinations assembled from different feudatories.
xs: **Recherla Rudra** saved the kingdom during **Ganapati's captivity** and built the **Ramappa** temple and tank at **Palampet**, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Chouda Samudram** was **Malyala Chauda Senani's**, and **Kamasani** made Garuda Beta a vassal.
xa: His title was **'Kakatiya Rajya Bharadhureya'** (bearer of the Kakatiya realm's burden).
The **Palampet** inscription is dated **1213**.
He crushed revolts and installed **Ganapatideva**.

92.s: Which inscription is correctly matched with its issuer and historical significance?
o: Magallu grant — Eastern Chalukya Danarnava — first mention of the Kakatiya family
Bayyaram inscription — Rudradeva — protection to foreign traders
Motupalli inscription — Mailamba — best genealogy of the early Kakatiyas
Thousand Pillar inscription — Ganapatideva — first mention of Gundyana
92.x: The Magallu grant of Eastern Chalukya Danarnava, dated 956, contains the first mention of the Kakatiya family through Gundyana.
92.tq: Start from the distinctive first-mention fact and eliminate exchanged issuers.
xs: The **Magallu grant** of Eastern Chalukya **Danarnava** (**956**) has the **first mention** of the Kakatiyas (Gundyana), so option **(1)** is correct.
**Bayyaram** was issued by **Mailamba** and gives the genealogy; **Motupalli** was **Ganapatideva's** grant protecting foreign traders.
The **Thousand Pillar** inscription is **Rudradeva's** (**1163**) declaration of independence.
xa: The Magallu grant names **Kakara Gundana** as progenitor; Bayyaram names **Venna**.
Phases: **Samanta 956-1162**, sovereign **1163-1323**.
First sovereign = **Rudradeva 1163**; last = **Prataparudra II**.

92.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Bayyaram tank inscription — 1219 — genealogy of the early Kakatiyas
Palampet inscription — 1213 — Ramappa temple during Ganapati's reign
Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam — 1244 — Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya
92.x: The Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam of 1244 concerns protection for foreign traders. Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya is associated with the Sanigaram inscription.
92.tq: Find the one exchanged fact in an inscription–date–content set.
xs: The **Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam** (**1244**) gave **protection to foreign traders**. It is not about the Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya, so option **(3)** is the wrong pair.
The **Juddha Mallajinalaya** is linked to the **Sanigaram** inscription, built by **Beta I's** minister **Naranayya**.
The other pairs are correct: **Bayyaram 1219**, **Palampet 1213**, **Draksharamam 1158**.
xa: Motupalli was issued by **Ganapatideva**.
**APPSC 2025** key matched Sanigaram to **Rudradeva**.
The **Draksharamam** inscription was issued by minister **Inangala Brahma Reddi**.

92.s:
Which of the following statements about the Thousand Pillar inscription is correct?
1. It is also known as the Anumakonda inscription.
2. It is dated 1163.
3. It is associated with Rudradeva.
4. It records the declaration of independence.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
92.x: All four statements are correct. The Anumakonda or Thousand Pillar inscription of 1163 is associated with Rudradeva and records Kakatiya independence.
92.tq: Combine alternative names, date, ruler and political significance before selecting the code.
xs: All four statements are correct, so option **(4)** is correct.
The **Anumakonda / Thousand Pillar** inscription is **Rudradeva's**, dated **1163**.
It declares **independence** and records **Prola II's conquests**.
xa: It was found by **J.S. Fleet** and composed by **Achitendru**.
⚠ The **APPSC 2025** key matched Anumakonda to **Prolaraja**, because it records Prola II's conquests.
The **Thousand Pillar (Rudreshwara)** temple was built by Rudradeva in **1163**.

92.s:
Which of the following is correctly matched?
1. Sanigaram — Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya
2. Palampet — Ramappa temple
3. Dharmasagara — Jalakaranda
4. Pithapuram — Kolleru Lake
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
92.x: All four pairs are correct. These inscriptions respectively refer to Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya, the Ramappa temple, Jalakaranda and Kolleru Lake.
92.tq: Use distinctive cultural and geographical references to secure the inscription pairs.
xs: All four pairs are correct, so option **(4)** is correct.
**Sanigaram** = Jain **Juddha Mallajinalaya**; **Palampet** = **Ramappa** temple (**1213**).
**Dharmasagara** = the instrument **'Jalakaranda'** (**APPSC 2019**); **Pithapuram** = **Kolleru Lake** (**APPSC G2 2017**).
xa: Pithapuram is a **Velanati** (Prithvisvara) record.
**Motupalli** (**1244**) = protection for foreign traders.
**Bayyaram** (**1219**) = best early genealogy.

92.s: In the APPSC 2025 matching question on Kakatiya inscriptions, which pairing of inscription and ruler was given in the key?
92.x: The APPSC 2025 key matched Anumakonda with Prolaraja, Motupalli with Ganapatideva, Bayyaram with Mailamba and Sanigaram with Rudradeva. So Motupalli-Rudradeva, Bayyaram-Ganapatideva and Sanigaram-Mailamba are all wrong pairings.
92.tq: APPSC 2025 key: Anumakonda-Prolaraja, Motupalli-Ganapati, Bayyaram-Mailamba, Sanigaram-Rudradeva.
xs: The **APPSC 2025** key matched the **Anumakonda** inscription to **Prolaraja**, so option **(1)** is correct.
The other key pairs were **Motupalli** = **Ganapatideva**, **Bayyaram** = **Mailamba**, **Sanigaram** = **Rudradeva**.
xa: ⚠ The Anumakonda inscription was issued by **Rudradeva** but records **Prola II's** conquests.
⚠ APPSC 2025 also treated "Prolaraja bore the title Arikesari" as **incorrect**.
Beta II's Saiva initiation by **Rameswara Pandita** was also an **APPSC 2025** point.

92.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
92.x: Prola I bore the title Arigajakesari. Vikrama Chakri belonged to Beta II, Vidyabhushana to Rudradeva, and Andhra Deshadhiswara to Ganapatideva.
92.tq: Start from the sure title–ruler pair and eliminate swapped holders.
xs: **Arigajakesari** = **Prola I** is correctly matched, so option **(1)** is correct (Bayyaram inscription).
**Vikrama Chakri** = **Beta II**; **Vidyabhushana** = **Rudradeva**; **Andhra Deshadhiswara** = **Ganapatideva**.
xa: Prola I also bore **Samadhigata Panchamahashabda**.
**Beta I's** title: **Chola Chamuvardhi Pramadhana**.
⚠ **APPSC 2025** read "Arikesari" as Prola II and marked it incorrect.

92.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Chola Chamuvardhi — Beta I
2. Vikrama Chakri — Beta II
3. Vinaya Vibhushanudu — Rudradeva
4. Andhra Deshadhiswara — Ganapatideva
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
92.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. These titles belonged respectively to Beta I, Beta II, Rudradeva and Ganapatideva.
92.tq: Verify each title–ruler pair before selecting the coded combination.
xs: All four pairs are correct, so option **(4)** is correct.
**Chola Chamuvardhi** = **Beta I**; **Vikrama Chakri** = **Beta II**.
**Vinaya Vibhushanudu** = **Rudradeva**; **Andhra Deshadhiswara** = **Ganapatideva**.
xa: Rudradeva was also **Vidyabhushana**.
**Arigajakesari** = **Prola I**.
**Rayagajakesari** = **Rudramadevi**.

92.s: Which of the following statements regarding the title Kumara Rudradeva is correct?
o: It was the feudatory title of the Samanta Kakatiyas.
It was held by Rudradeva during his accession.
It was the title of Ganapatideva after his victory over the Pandyas.
It was held by Prataparudra II at the time of his accession.
92.x: Kumara Rudradeva was the title borne by Prataparudra II at his accession.
92.tq: Separate a personal accession title from titles of earlier Kakatiya rulers.
xs: **Kumara Rudradeva** was **Prataparudra II's** title at **accession**, so option **(4)** is correct.
The feudatory title was **Mahamandaleswara**. **Rudradeva's** titles were **Vidyabhushana** and **Vinaya Vibhushanudu**.
xa: Prataparudra II was the **last** Kakatiya.
His commander **Pedarudru** defeated Hoysala **Ballala III** after **1316**.
An **APPSC 2017** key gives **Rayagajakesari** to **Prataparudra**.

92.s: Which Kakatiya ruler bore the title 'Rayagajakesari' for her victory over the Yadavas of Devagiri?
92.x: Rudramadevi bore the title Rayagajakesari for her victory over the Yadavas of Devagiri.
92.tq: Raya-gaja-kesari: the lioness Rudrama who beat the Yadavas.
xs: **Rudramadevi** bore **'Rayagajakesari'** for her victory over the **Yadavas of Devagiri**, so option **(2)** is correct (**APPSC-GS 2018**).
⚠ Another **APPSC 2017** key gives the title to **Prataparudra**.
xa: Rudrama repulsed Yadava **Mahadeva**.
**Arigajakesari** (similar-sounding) = **Prola I**.

92.s:
Consider the following statements about the Kakatiyas:
1. Telugu replaced Sanskrit in their inscriptions from the reign of Rudradeva.
2. They were the second dynasty after the Satavahanas to unify the Telugu-speaking regions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
92.x: Statement 2 is correct: after the Satavahanas, the Kakatiyas were the second to unify the Telugu lands (and the first to rule all Telugu-speakers). Statement 1 is wrong: Telugu replaced Sanskrit in inscriptions from Ganapatideva's reign. So 2 only.
92.tq: Telugu inscriptions from Ganapatideva.
xs: Only statement **2** is correct — option **(1) 2 only**.
Statement 2 is correct: the Kakatiyas were the **2nd dynasty after the Satavahanas** to **unify** the Telugu-speaking regions.
Statement 1 is wrong: **Telugu replaced Sanskrit** in inscriptions from **Ganapatideva**'s reign, not Rudradeva's.
xa: The Kakatiyas left **1,000+** inscriptions.
**Ramappa temple (Palampet)** became a UNESCO site in **2021**.
First mention = **Magallu 956**; first sovereign = **Rudradeva 1163**.
Last ruler = **Prataparudra II**.

92.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Ramappa Temple at Palampet?
o: It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site inscribed in 2016 and is noted for a circular platform and granite bricks.
It was built at Nellore and is noted for its rectangular platform and wooden roof.
It was constructed by the Pandyas at Muttukur and is noted for its floating stones.
It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site inscribed in 2021 and is noted for its star-shaped platform and floating bricks.
92.x: The Ramappa Temple at Palampet became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2021 and is noted for its star-shaped platform and floating bricks.
92.tq: Combine the location, recognition year and distinctive architectural features before selecting the complete description.
xs: The **Ramappa** temple, **Palampet** became a UNESCO site in **2021**, with a **star-shaped platform** and **floating bricks**, so option **(4)** is correct.
It was built by **Recherla Rudra** (**1213**). It is not at Nellore or Muttukur, and it was not inscribed in **2016**.
xa: It was built in **Ganapatideva's** reign.
Its builder's title was **'Kakatiya Rajya Bharadhureya'**.
The **Palampet** inscription records it.

92.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Magallu — First mention of the Kakatiyas, 956
Ganapatideva — First mention of the Kakatiyas, 956
92.x: The first mention of the Kakatiyas is associated with Magallu in 956. Rudradeva was the first sovereign in 1163, while Prataparudra II was the last ruler.
92.tq: Use the first–last distinction and attach each date to the correct historical milestone.
xs: **Magallu** = **first mention of the Kakatiyas, 956** is correctly matched, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Rudradeva** was the **first sovereign** (**1163**), and **Prataparudra II** was the **last**.
xa: The Magallu grant was issued by Eastern Chalukya **Danarnava**.
It names **Gundyana**.
The sovereign phase ended in **1323**, when Orugallu became **Sultanpur**.

92.s: According to the Musunuri inscription, how did Pratapa Rudra die?
o: He died while constructing a tank.
He died in a battle at Vijayapuri.
He died jumping into the Narmada.
92.x: The Musunuri (Vilasa) record of the Musunuri Nayakas says Prataparudra, captured by the Delhi army, died by jumping into the Narmada on the way to Delhi.
92.tq: Recall how the last Kakatiya king died.
n: Pratapa Rudra died by jumping into the Narmada. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
xs: **Pratapa Rudra** **died by jumping into the Narmada** — option **(4)**.
The notes record that he died by jumping into the **Narmada**.
He was not killed at **Motupalli** or **Vijayapuri**; Motupalli is linked with **Ganapatideva**'s **1244** Abhaya Sasanam.
xa: **Motupalli** inscription protected foreign traders.
**Tripuranthakam** inscription records **Ambadeva**'s victories.
**Dharmasagar** inscription names the instrument **Jalakaranda** (APPSC 2019).
**Bayyaram tank** inscription of **Mailamba** (**1219**) gives the best early genealogy.

92.s:
Assertion (A): The Kazipet inscription records the accession of Durga Nripathi to the throne.
Reason (R): The inscription is associated with Betha Raju II/Durgaraja.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
92.x: Both are true but R does not explain A: the Kazipet inscription belongs to Betha Raju II (Durgaraja) and records Durga Nripathi coming to the throne, but naming its issuer does not explain the accession.
92.tq: Check whether R is the cause of A.
n: The Kazipet inscription is associated with Betha Raju II and Durgaraja. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
Durga Nripathi ascended the throne. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
xs: **Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A** — option **(2)**.
A is true: the **Kazipet** inscription records that **Durga Nripathi ascended** the throne.
R is true: it is associated with **Betha Raju II** and **Durgaraja** — naming the issuer does not explain the accession.
xa: It also records **Durgaraja**'s donations to the **Betesvara** temple.
**Anumakonda** inscription (**1163**) of **Rudra Deva** declares independence; found by **J.S. Fleet**.
**Draksharama** inscription (**1158**) calls Rudra Deva **Vinaya Bhushan**.
APPSC 2025 key: Anumakonda = **Prolaraja**, Bayyaram = **Mailamba**.

92.s:
Consider the following statements:

I. The Rudreshwara Temple belongs to the Kakatiya Dynasty.
II. The Rudreshwara Temple was built in 1163 CE.
III. The Rudreshwara Temple was built by Rudradeva, also called Prataparudra I.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
92.x: All three are correct: the Rudreswara (Thousand Pillar) Temple is a Kakatiya temple built in 1163 CE by Rudradeva, also called Prataparudra I.
92.tq: Check the dynasty, year and builder separately.
n: Rudreshwara Temple belongs to the Kakatiya Dynasty. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 11-12]
Rudreshwara Temple was built in 1163 CE. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 11-12]
Rudreshwara Temple was built by Rudradeva, also called Prataparudra I. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 11-12]
xs: **All three** statements are correct — option **(4) I, II and III**.
I and II: the **Rudreshwara Temple** at **Anamakonda** belongs to the **Kakatiya Dynasty** and was built in **1163 CE**.
III: it was built by **Rudradeva**, also called **Prataparudra I**.
xa: The **Thousand-Pillar Temple** is credited to **Rudra Deva**; one note credits **Prola II** — follow Rudradeva, **1163**.
**Ramappa Temple**, Palampet — **Recharla Rudra**, **1213 AD**.
**Swayambhu Devalayam** and **Kesavala** — **Prola Raju II**.
Rudradeva shifted the capital from **Hanamkonda** to **Orugallu** (APPSC G2 2019).

92.s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
 a. Bhimeshwara Temple
 b. Thousand-Pillar Temple
 c. Swayambhu Devalayam and Kesavala
 d. Jaina Basthi

List-II
 i. Mailamma
 ii. Chalukya Bhima I
 iii. Prola Raju-II
 iv. Rudra Deva
92.x: The Bhimeswara Temple was built by Chalukya Bhima I, the Thousand-Pillar Temple by Rudra Deva, the Swayambhu Devalayam and Kesavala by Prola Raju II, and the Jaina Basthi by Mailamma, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
92.tq: Recall the builder of each monument.
n: Chalukya Bhima I built the Bhimeshwara Temple on the banks of the Godavari. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 25-27]
Rudra Deva built the Thousand-Pillar Temple at Anumakonda. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 25-27]
Prola Raju II built the Swayambhu Devalayam. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 25-27]
Prola Raju II built Kesavala. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 25-27]
Mailamma built the Jaina Basthi at Anamakonda. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 25-27]
xs: The correct match is **a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i** — option **(4)**.
**Bhimeshwara Temple** → **Chalukya Bhima I**; **Thousand-Pillar Temple** → **Rudra Deva**.
**Swayambhu Devalayam and Kesavala** → **Prola Raju-II** (Shiva); **Jaina Basthi** at Anamakonda → **Mailamma**, wife of **Bethanamathya**.
xa: ⚠ Other notes credit the **Kadalalaya Jainavasadi** to Prola II's minister **Chetanamatya** and wife **Mailama**.
⚠ **Kesamudram** = Prola I; **Kesari Samudram** = Rudradeva; **Arikesari Samudram** = Prola II.
**Ramappa** is an example of **Ekasila architecture**.
**Lakkavaram and Ghanapur** tanks — **Ganapatideva**.

92.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Yadavas
(b) Kakatiyas
(c) Hoysalas
(d) Pandyas

List-II
(i) Madura/Madurai
(ii) Devagiri
(iii) Warangal
(iv) Dwarasamudra
92.x: The Yadavas ruled from Devagiri, the Kakatiyas from Warangal, the Hoysalas from Dwarasamudra and the Pandyas from Madurai, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
92.tq: Match each dynasty with its capital.
n: The capital of the Yadava Dynasty was Devagiri. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #149-2 · pp 260-261]
Warangal was an important capital of the Kakatiyas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #149-2 · pp 260-261]
Dwarasamudra was an important capital of the Hoysalas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #149-2 · pp 260-261]
Madura or Madurai was an important capital of the Pandyas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #149-2 · pp 260-261]
xs: The correct match is **a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i** — option **(2)**.
**Yadavas** → **Devagiri**; **Kakatiyas** → **Warangal**.
**Hoysalas** → **Dwarasamudra**; **Pandyas** → **Madura/Madurai**.
xa: The Kakatiyas ruled the **Eastern Deccan** in the **12th–14th centuries CE**.
The Kakatiyas had a **conflict** with the **Seuna (Yadava)** rulers of Devagiri.
Early Kakatiya capital: **Anumakonda (Hanamkonda)**.
After **1323** Orugallu was renamed **Sultanpur**.

92.s:
How many of the following were defeated by Rudrama Devi?
1. Pandyas
2. Eastern Gangas
3. Seunas of Devagiri
4. Western Chalukyas
92.x: Three: Rudrama Devi defeated the Pandyas, the Eastern Gangas and the Seunas of Devagiri. The Western Chalukyas had declined long before her reign.
92.tq: Check each item against her reign.
n: Kakatiya Rudrama Devi defeated the Seuna rulers of Devagiri. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #149-2 · pp 260-261]
Rudrama Devi defeated the Pandyas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #149-2 · pp 260-261]
Rudrama Devi defeated the Eastern Gangas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #149-2 · pp 260-261]
xs: **Only three** — option **(3)**.
**Rudrama Devi** defeated the **Pandyas**, the **Eastern Gangas** (rulers of **Orissa**) and the **Seuna rulers** of **Devagiri**.
The **Western Chalukyas** are not among her listed victories.
xa: She was the **daughter** of **Ganapati Dev** and the **fourth independent ruler**.
She was a **female ruler** who succeeded as **putrika**.
Her title **Rayagajakesari** is credited for her victory over the **Yadavas** (APPSC-GS 2018 key).
⚠ Another APPSC key (2017) gives **Rayagajakesari** to **Prataparudra**.

92.s: Which dynasty ruled the Eastern Deccan during the 12th–14th centuries CE?
92.x: The Kakatiyas ruled the eastern Deccan from Warangal in the 12th–14th centuries. The Seunas (Yadavas) ruled the western Deccan, and the Eastern Gangas ruled Odisha.
92.tq: Discriminate the eastern and western Deccan dynasties.
n: The Kakatiya dynasty was located in the Eastern Deccan. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #150 · pp 261-261]
The Kakatiya dynasty existed during the 12th–14th centuries CE. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #150 · pp 261-261]
xs: The **Kakatiya Dynasty** ruled the **Eastern Deccan** in the **12th–14th centuries CE** — option **(3)**.
Their capital was **Warangal**.
The **Seuna / Yadava** dynasty ruled from **Devagiri** — they were the Kakatiyas' rivals.
xa: Rulers: **Rudradeva**, **Mahadeva**, **Ganapati Dev**, **Rudrama Devi**.
Rudrama Devi defeated the **Eastern Gangas** of **Orissa**.
The Kakatiyas were **Shudras** with **Sanskrit** as official language.
Clan deity: **Kakatamma (Kakati Devi)** = Jain **Kushmandini**.

92.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Rudradeva
(b) Mahadeva
(c) Ganapati Dev
(d) Rudrama Devi

List-II
(i) Daughter of Ganapati Dev
(ii) Came after Rudradeva
(iii) Also called Pratap Rudradeva I
(iv) Father of Rudrama Devi
92.x: Rudradeva was also called Prataparudra I, Mahadeva came after him, Ganapati Deva was Rudrama Devi's father, and Rudrama Devi was Ganapati Deva's daughter, giving a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
92.tq: Recall the order of Kakatiya rulers.
n: Rudradeva was also known as Pratap Rudradeva I. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #150 · pp 261-261]
Mahadeva came after Rudradeva. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #150 · pp 261-261]
Ganapati Dev was the father of Rudrama Devi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #150 · pp 261-261]
Rudrama Devi was the daughter of Ganapati Dev. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #150 · pp 261-261]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i** — option **(1)**.
**Rudradeva** → also **Pratap Rudradeva I**; **Mahadeva** → **came after Rudradeva**.
**Ganapati Dev** → **father of Rudrama Devi**; **Rudrama Devi** → **daughter of Ganapati Dev**.
xa: Rudradeva (**1163-1195**) founded **Orugallu** and wrote **'Nitisara'**.
Mahadeva (**1195-1199**) died fighting the Yadavas; guru **Dhruveshwara Pandita**.
Ganapatideva ruled **1199-1262**.
Rudrama Devi ruled **1262-1289**.

92.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Navabrahma temple complex at Alampur consists of nine temples.
The Thousand Pillars Temple at Anamakonda was built by Rudradeva.
The Ramappa Temple at Palampet was constructed by Krishnadevaraya.
The Ramappa Temple at Palampet was built by Recharla Rudra in 1213 AD.
92.x: Option C is incorrect: the Ramappa Temple at Palampet was built by Recharla Rudra in 1213 AD, not by Krishnadevaraya, who built the Hazara Ramaswamy Temple at Hampi. The other statements are right.
92.tq: Check the builder named in each statement.
n: Navabrahma is a nine-temple complex. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 11-12]
Navabrahma is located at Alampur, also called Alampuram. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 11-12]
The Ramappa Temple is located at Palampet in Warangal. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 11-12]
The Ramappa Temple was built by Recharla Rudra in 1213 AD. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 11-12]
