He built the **Veerashiro Mantapa** at Srisailam.

98.s:
Consider the following statements about Kumaragiri Reddi:
1. His accession was opposed by Pedakomati Vema.
2. Pedakomati Vema was pacified by being made a feudatory of Chandolu and designated as heir.
3. Kumaragiri made Rajahmundry a separate division under his son Anavota and later under Kataya Vema.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
98.x: All three statements are correct. Kumaragiri settled the succession opposition by assigning Pedakomati Vema the Chandolu feudatory position and heirship, and later divided the kingdom by creating a separate Rajahmundry division.
98.tq: Check the sequence of political settlement and administrative division rather than treating the events as unrelated.
xs: Statement 1 correct: **Pedakomati Vema** opposed Kumaragiri's accession.
Statement 2 correct: he was settled as **feudatory of Chandolu** and **heir**.
Statement 3 correct: Kumaragiri made **Rajahmundry** a separate division under his son **Anavota**, then **Kataya Vema** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: Kataya Vema took charge in **1395**; Pedakomati **resented** the division.
In **1402** Pedakomati seized **Kondavidu** and ousted Kumaragiri.
Kumaragiri was a **patron of dance** and celebrated **Vasantotsavams**.

98.s:
Arrange the following events relating to Kumaragiri Reddi in chronological order:
A. Kataya Vema was placed in charge of the Rajahmundry division.
B. Kumaragiri died in refuge at Rajahmundry.
C. Kumaragiri made Rajahmundry a separate division under Anavota.
D. Pedakomati Vema seized Kondavidu.
98.x: Rajahmundry was first placed under Anavota, later under Kataya Vema in 1395, and Pedakomati Vema seized Kondavidu in 1402 before Kumaragiri died in refuge at Rajahmundry.
98.tq: Anchor the sequence with the dated event of 1395 and the final event of 1402.
xs: Order: Rajahmundry under **Anavota** → under **Kataya Vema** (**1395**) → **Pedakomati** seizes Kondavidu (**1402**) → Kumaragiri dies in refuge at Rajahmundry — **C, A, D, B**, option **(1)**.
Anavota, Kumaragiri's son, died young.
xa: Kataya Vema ruled independently after **1402**.
The Rajahmundry kingdom lasted **1402-1448**.
Kataya Vema was Kumaragiri's **brother-in-law** and commander.

98.s: Which of the following statements about the political career of Kataya Vema Reddi is correct?
o: He built the Patala Ganga steps at Srisailam in 1346.
He seized Kondavidu in 1402 and caused Kumaragiri’s death.
He conquered the eastern region up to Cuttack and later administered Rajahmundry.
He abolished the tax on gold and issued the Abhaya Sasanam at Motupalli.
98.x: Kataya Vema, Kumaragiri’s brother-in-law and commander, conquered the eastern region up to Cuttack and later took charge of the Rajahmundry division. The other statements refer to Anavota or Pedakomati Vema, or to Prolaya Vema.
98.tq: Use the wrong-ruler trap by matching each deed with the correct ruler.
xs: **Kataya Vema** **conquered the east up to Cuttack** and later **administered Rajahmundry** — option **(3)** is correct.
**1346** Patala Ganga steps = **Prolaya Vema**; seizing **Kondavidu** in **1402** = **Pedakomati**.
Abolishing the **gold tax** and the **Abhaya Shasana** at Motupalli = **Anavota** and his minister **Somaya**.
xa: Kataya Vema defeated **Harihara II**; the **Sarpavaram** treaty married Harihara's daughter **Vijayalakshmi** to Kataya's son.
He was killed at **Kakaraparthi (1414)** by **Gajaraju Tippa**.
Title: **Kataka Churakara**.

98.s: Who financed the Vasantotsavams celebrated at the Reddi court?
98.x: The merchant Avachi Tippayya Setti funded the Vasantotsavams; this patronage is recorded in Srinatha's Haravilasam.
98.tq: Identify the patron by distinguishing the merchant from political and religious figures.
xs: Merchant **Avachi Tippayya Setti** funded the **Vasantotsavams** — option **(2)** is correct.
This is recorded in **Srinatha's Haravilasam**.
**Mallappa Odayar** was a Vijayanagara commander; **Ghoderayacharulu** were Shaiva gurus.
xa: Haravilasam was dedicated to **Tippayya Setti**, famous for overseas trade.
Haravilasam describes Reddi sea trade and **imports and exports** (APPSC 2019).
**Kumaragiri** celebrated the Vasantotsavams grandly.

98.s: The court dancer Lakumadevi, who was renowned in Bharatanatyam, was associated with the court of
98.x: Lakumadevi was the celebrated Bharatanatyam dancer at Kumaragiri Reddi's court. C. Narayana Reddy later wrote Karpura Vasanta Rayalu on Kumaragiri.
98.tq: Use the court–artist association and avoid substituting a neighbouring ruler.
xs: **Lakumadevi** was the court dancer of **Kumaragiri Reddi** (**APPSC G2 2012**) — option **(2)** is correct.
She was renowned in **Bharatanatyam**; Kumaragiri himself was an expert in it.
xa: **C. Narayana Reddy** wrote **Karpura Vasanta Rayalu** on Kumaragiri.
Kumaragiri's dance treatise: **Vasanta Rajiyam**.
**Devadasis** performed at Shiva temples such as the **Pancharamas**.

98.s: The musical instrument 'Jalakaranda', associated with the Reddi court of Kumaragiri, is mentioned in which inscription?
98.x: The Dharmasagara inscription mentions the 'Jalakaranda' (PYQ G2 2019). The Manyapuram inscription records Anavota's capital shift, Kaluvacheru was issued by Anitalli in 1423, and Sarpavaram concerns Kataya Vema's family and treaty with Harihara II.
98.tq: Jalakaranda = Dharmasagara inscription.
xs: **'Jalakaranda'** is mentioned in the **Dharmasagara inscription** (**PYQ G2 2019**) — option **(2)** is correct.
**Manyapuram** records Anavota's capital shift; **Kaluvacheru** was issued by **Anitalli** (**1423**); **Sarpavaram** concerns Kataya Vema's family.
xa: Kumaragiri's court dancer: **Lakumadevi**.
**Vasantotsavam** was the most popular festival, funded by **Avachi Tippaya Setti**.
**Pedakomati** wrote **Sangeeta Chintamani** on music.

98.s:
Match List-I (Rajamahendravaram figure) with List-II (role):
List-I
a. Allada Reddi
b. Veerabhadra Reddi
c. Vema (Veda) Reddi
d. Kataya Vema Reddi
List-II
i. Nominal king, restored in 1423 and 1429
ii. Regent who ran the state after 1414
iii. Prime minister and de facto ruler (1423-1448)
iv. Killed at Kakaraparthi in 1414 by Gajaraju Tippa
98.x: Allada Reddi was regent (1414-c.1420) for Veerabhadra; Veerabhadra was the nominal king, restored in 1423 and 1429; his brother Vema (Veda) Reddi was prime minister and de facto ruler; Kataya Vema was killed at Kakaraparthi (1414) by Gajaraju Tippa. Option A matches all. B swaps Allada and Veerabhadra; C swaps Veerabhadra and Vema; D swaps Allada and Kataya Vema.
98.tq: Regent (Allada) for the nominal king (Veerabhadra), while the brother (Vema) actually ruled.
xs: Correct match **a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv** — option **(1)**.
**Allada Reddi** – regent after **1414**; **Veerabhadra Reddi** – nominal king, restored **1423** and **1429**.
**Vema (Veda) Reddi** – prime minister and de facto ruler (**1423-1448**); **Kataya Vema** – killed at **Kakaraparthi** (**1414**) by **Gajaraju Tippa**.
xa: Allada's sons **Vema Reddi**, **Veerabhadra Reddi** and **Doddareddi** helped him in the east.
**Anitalli**, Kataya Vema's daughter, married **Veerabhadra Reddi**.
The line ended with **Veerabhadra** and **Vema** when **Kapileswara Gajapati** took Rajahmundry (**1448**).

98.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the role of Vijayanagara in Allada Reddi's conflict?
o: Deva Raya I supported Kataya Vema against the Kondavidu forces.
Mallappa Odayar founded the Rajahmundry branch of the Reddis.
Kapileswara Gajapati allied with Allada Reddi against Kondavidu.
Deva Raya II supported Annadeva in capturing Vengi.
98.x: Deva Raya I of Vijayanagara backed Kataya Vema, making Vijayanagara an ally of Allada Reddi's side.
98.tq: Identify the correct ally by matching the ruler with the action attributed to him.
xs: **Deva Raya I** of Vijayanagara backed **Kataya Vema** — option **(1)** is correct, making Vijayanagara **Allada Reddi's ally**.
**Annadeva** took Vengi with **Velama** support, not Deva Raya II's; **Kapileswara Gajapati** later annexed Rajahmundry.
**Mallappa Odayar** was a Vijayanagara commander who came to help in **1444**.
xa: Pedakomati beat Kataya Vema and **Deva Raya I's** army at **Attili-Kakaraparthi**.
The **Sarpavaram** treaty married **Harihara II's** daughter to Kataya's son.
**Deva Raya II** restored the Reddis as feudatories in **1429**.

98.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the opponents of Allada Reddi:
1. Pedakomati Vema Reddi attacked Rajahmundry in 1414.
2. Pedakomati Vema Reddi defeated Kataya Vema and Deva Raya I's army at Attili-Kakaraparthi.
3. Annadeva captured parts of Vengi with Velama support.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
98.x: All three statements are correct. Pedakomati Vema's campaign and Annadeva's Vengi expansion were significant challenges to Allada Reddi.
98.tq: Test a cluster of related military facts while using the complete combination as a plausible key.
xs: Statement 1 correct: **Pedakomati Vema** attacked **Rajahmundry** in **1414**.
Statement 2 correct: he beat **Kataya Vema** and **Deva Raya I's** army at **Attili-Kakaraparthi**.
Statement 3 correct: **Annadeva** took parts of **Vengi** with **Velama** support — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: Allada's ally was **Vijayanagara**.
Allada was helped in the east by his sons **Vema Reddi**, **Veerabhadra Reddi**, **Doddareddi**.
Kataya Vema was killed by **Gajaraju Tippa**, Pedakomati's ally.

98.s:
Consider the following statements about the civil war among the Reddis:
1. Pedakomati Vema ousted Kumaragiri in 1402.
2. Kumaragiri fled to Rajahmundry.
3. Kataya Vema subsequently ruled independently.
4. Kataya Vema spent his entire reign fighting Pedakomati Vema.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
98.x: All four statements are correct. The 1402 ouster of Kumaragiri shifted the conflict to Rajahmundry, where Kataya Vema ruled independently against Pedakomati.
98.tq: Check each chronological step in a political conflict before choosing the combination.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 correct: **Pedakomati** ousted **Kumaragiri** in **1402**, who fled to **Rajahmundry**.
Statements 3 and 4 correct: **Kataya Vema** then ruled **independently** and spent his **whole reign fighting Pedakomati** — so all four, option **(4)**.
xa: Kumaragiri died in refuge at Rajahmundry.
The rivalry ended with **Kondavidu's fall (1424)**.
Kataya Vema was killed at **Kakaraparthi (1414)**.

98.s: What was the immediate political consequence of the fall of Kondavidu in 1424?
o: Rajahmundry became a Gajapati province immediately.
Kondavidu became independent of both Vijayanagara and the Gajapati kingdom.
Rajahmundry survived for another 24 years as a Vijayanagara feudatory.
The Reddi rule over Rajahmundry ended in 1402.
98.x: Although Kondavidu fell in 1424, Rajahmundry continued for another 24 years as a feudatory of Vijayanagara.
98.tq: Distinguish the fall of one branch from the continued survival of the other branch.
xs: After Kondavidu fell in **1424**, **Rajahmundry survived another 24 years as a Vijayanagara feudatory** — option **(3)** is correct.
Kondavidu itself fell to **Vijayanagara (Deva Raya II)**.
Rajahmundry was annexed by **Kapileswara Gajapati** only in **1446-48**.
xa: Kondavidu's last ruler **Racha Vema** was killed by his own people over the **Puriti** tax.
**Srinatha** moved to the Rajahmundry court (patron **Veerabhadra Reddi**) after **1424**.
**Deva Raya I** annexed the **Kandukuru Reddis**.

98.s:
Arrange the following events concerning Rajahmundry in chronological order:
A. Veerabhadra and Vema recovered Rajahmundry.
B. Kapileswara Gajapati annexed Rajahmundry.
C. Ganga Ganapati took Rajahmundry.
D. Veerabhanu Deva occupied Rajahmundry.
98.x: The correct sequence is 1420, 1423, 1429 and 1446–48: Ganga Ganapati's capture, recovery by Veerabhadra and Vema, Veerabhanu's occupation, and Kapileswara's annexation.
98.tq: Anchor the sequence to the four dates and retain the earliest and latest events.
xs: Order: **Ganga Ganapati** took Rajahmundry (**1420**) → **Veerabhadra and Vema** recovered it (**1423**) → **Veerabhanu Deva** occupied it (**1429**) → **Kapileswara** annexed it (**1446-48**) — **C, A, D, B**, option **(1)**.
In **1429**, **Deva Raya II** expelled Veerabhanu up to **Simhachalam**.
xa: In **1435**, **Kapileswara Gajapati** took **Cuttack** and pressed on the Reddis.
A **1444** Draksharama inscription records **Mallappa Odayar** coming to help.
The **Kaluvacheru inscription (1423)** of **Anitalli** followed the recapture of Rajahmundry.

98.s: Who expelled Veerabhanu Deva up to Simhachalam and restored the Reddis as feudatories?
98.x: Deva Raya II expelled Veerabhanu Deva up to Simhachalam and restored the Reddis as Vijayanagara feudatories.
98.tq: Apply the who-did-what test to distinguish the two Deva Rayas.
xs: **Deva Raya II** expelled **Veerabhanu Deva** up to **Simhachalam** and restored the Reddis as feudatories (**1429**) — option **(2)** is correct.
**Deva Raya I** backed **Kataya Vema** earlier; **Mallappa Odayar** came to help in **1444**; **Kapileswara** annexed Rajahmundry later.
xa: After Deva Raya II's death, **Kapileswara Gajapati** annexed Rajahmundry (**1446-48**).
Deva Raya II also ended the **Kondavidu** line in **1424**.
Srinatha defeated **Gauda Dindima Bhatta**, court poet of **Devaraya II**.

98.s:
Consider the following statements about the later struggle for Rajahmundry:
1. Kapileswara Gajapati took Cuttack in 1435 and pressed against the Reddis.
2. A Draksharama inscription of 1444 records the arrival of Mallappa Odayar to help the Reddis.
3. After the death of Deva Raya II, Kapileswara Gajapati annexed Rajahmundry during 1446–48.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
98.x: All three are correct. Kapileswara took Cuttack in 1435 and pressed on the Reddis. The 1444 Draksharama inscription records the Vijayanagara commander Mallappa Odayar coming to help. After Deva Raya II's death, Kapileswara annexed Rajahmundry (1446–48).
98.tq: Combine event, inscription and date statements to test the late phase of the rivalry.
xs: Statement 1 correct: **Kapileswara Gajapati** took **Cuttack** in **1435** and pressed on the Reddis.
Statement 2 correct: a **1444 Draksharama** inscription records **Mallappa Odayar** coming to help.
Statement 3 correct: after **Deva Raya II's** death, Kapileswara **annexed Rajahmundry** (**1446-48**) — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: Kapileswara attacked in **1448**; Kondaveedu fell to him around **1450**.
The last Rajahmundry rulers were **Veerabhadra Reddi** and **Vema Reddi**.
After Rajahmundry fell (**1448**), **Srinatha** lived in poverty in **Palnadu**.

98.s:
Consider the following statements about the Reddi conflicts with neighbouring powers:

1. Mallaya Reddy defeated Hasan Gangu at Motupalli.
2. Gajarao Tippa defeated Firoz Shah's army at Kambhammetta in 1396.
3. The Bahmani attack on Kandukur was repelled in 1398.
4. Deva Raya I annexed the Kandukuru Reddis.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
98.x: All four statements are correct. The Reddis resisted Bahmani attacks at Motupalli and Kambhammetta, repelled the Kandukur attack in 1398, and later Deva Raya I annexed the Kandukuru Reddis.
98.tq: Track each opponent and episode separately before choosing the combined code.
xs: Statement 1 correct: **Mallaya Reddy** beat Bahmani founder **Hasan Gangu** at **Motupalli**.
Statements 2 and 3 correct: **Gajarao Tippa** beat **Firoz Shah's** army at **Kambhammetta (1396)**; the **Kandukur** attack was repelled (**1398**).
Statement 4 correct: **Deva Raya I** annexed the **Kandukuru Reddis** — so all four, option **(4)**.
xa: Senani **Mallareddy** drove Bahmani forces from **Amaravati** and restored the **Amareswara** temple.
Mallaya Reddy was **Prolaya Vema's brother**.
**Sivalinga Reddi** of Kandukuru wrote **Tatva Prakashika**.

98.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. Kataya Vema — Defeat of Harihara II
2. Annadevu — Seizure of parts of Vengi with Velama assistance
3. Anavota — Halt of the Kalinga Gangas on the Krishna
4. Pedakomati Vema — Recovery of lost territory in 1404
98.x: All four pairs are correct. Kataya Vema defeated Harihara II, Annadevu took parts of Vengi with Velama help, Anavota halted the Kalinga Gangas on the Krishna, and Pedakomati Vema recovered lost land from Vijayanagara in 1404.
98.tq: Use the opponent–episode pairing to eliminate ruler swaps.
xs: All four are right: **Kataya Vema** – defeat of **Harihara II**; **Annadevu** – parts of **Vengi** with **Velama** help.
**Anavota** – halted the **Kalinga Gangas** on the **Krishna**; **Pedakomati Vema** – recovered lost land in **1404** — so option **(4)**.
xa: Kataya Vema took **Tripurantakam** and **Vinukonda** from Vijayanagara (Srisailam later returned).
The **Sarpavaram** inscription records the treaty marrying Harihara's daughter **Vijayalakshmi** to Kataya's son.
**Anavema** defeated the **Kalinga Gajapatis**; Kataya Vema raided up to **Cuttack**.

98.s: What was the significance of the Sarpavaram inscription in the relations between Kataya Vema and Harihara II?
o: It recorded the surrender of Kondaveedu to the Gajapatis.
It recorded the restoration of the Amareswara temple.
It recorded a treaty under which Harihara II married his daughter Vijayalakshmi to Kataya Vema's son.
It recorded the appointment of Srinatha as Vidyadhikari.
98.x: The Sarpavaram inscription refers to a treaty arrangement in which Harihara II gave his daughter Vijayalakshmi in marriage to Kataya Vema's son.
98.tq: Identify the diplomatic consequence of a military conflict rather than its battlefield result.
xs: The **Sarpavaram** inscription records a **treaty** in which **Harihara II** married his daughter **Vijayalakshmi** to **Kataya Vema's son** — option **(3)** is correct.
It followed Kataya Vema's **defeat of Harihara II**, when he took **Tripurantakam** and **Vinukonda**.
The **Amareswara** temple was restored by **Vallaya Vemana**; Srinatha was **Pedakomati's** Vidyadhikari.
xa: Srisailam was later returned to Vijayanagara.
**Deva Raya I** of Vijayanagara later backed **Kataya Vema**.
Kataya Vema's title: **Kataka Churakara**.

98.s: Kondavidu passed to Vijayanagara in 1424 during the reign of which ruler?
98.x: After the death of Racha Vema Reddi, Kondavidu passed to Vijayanagara under Deva Raya II in 1424.
98.tq: Match the transfer year with the ruling power and ruler involved.
xs: Kondavidu passed to **Vijayanagara** under **Deva Raya II** in **1424** — option **(1)** is correct.
Its last ruler **Racha Vema Reddi** was killed by his own people over the **Puriti** tax.
**Deva Raya I** annexed the **Kandukuru** Reddis; **Kapileswara Gajapati** annexed **Rajahmundry** (**1448**).
xa: After **1424**, **Srinatha** joined the Rajahmundry Reddis (patron **Veerabhadra Reddi**).
Rajahmundry survived another **24 years** as a Vijayanagara feudatory.
Gajapati **Kapileswara** took Kondaveedu around **1450**.

98.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the end of the Rajahmundry branch of Reddi rule?
o: It was absorbed into Kondavidu after the fall of Racha Vema.
It was conquered by Deva Raya I in 1402.
It was annexed by Kapileswara Gajapati of Orissa in 1448.
It ended with the death of Kataya Vema in 1424.
98.x: The Rajahmundry branch, ruled at the end by Veerabhadra Reddi and Vema Reddi, was ended by Kapileswara Gajapati of Orissa in 1448.
98.tq: Distinguish the separate endings of the Kondavidu and Rajahmundry branches.
xs: The Rajahmundry branch was **annexed by Kapileswara Gajapati of Orissa in 1448** — option **(3)** is correct.
Its last rulers were **Veerabhadra Reddi** and **Vema Reddi**.
**Kataya Vema** died at **Kakaraparthi** in **1414**, not 1424.
xa: Kapileswara took **Cuttack** in **1435** and pressed on the Reddis.
A **1444** Draksharama inscription records **Mallappa Odayar** coming to help.
After Rajahmundry fell, **Srinatha** lived in poverty in **Palnadu**.

98.s: The village administrative system of the Reddis included how many Ayagars?
98.x: A Reddi village had twelve Ayagars, or village servants.
98.tq: Identify the exact numerical value instead of confusing the total with the principal office-holders.
xs: A Reddi village had **twelve (12) Ayagars** (village servants) — option **(2)** is correct.
The pattern was **inherited from the Kakatiyas**.
xa: Key Ayagars: **Karnam** (accountant), **Reddi/Peddakapu** (headman), **Talari** (watchman).
They were paid in **Manyam** land or a crop share (**Mera**).
The same decentralised pattern continued under the **Gajapatis**.

98.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Village functionary)
 a. Karnam
 b. Reddi or Peddakapu
 c. Talari

List-II (Function)
 i. Watchman
 ii. Accountant
 iii. Headman

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
98.x: The Karnam was the accountant, the Reddi or Peddakapu was the headman, and the Talari was the watchman.
98.tq: Start from the sure pair Karnam–accountant and complete the remaining functional matches.
xs: Correct match **a–ii, b–iii, c–i** — option **(1)**.
**Karnam** – **accountant**; **Reddi/Peddakapu** – **headman**; **Talari** – **watchman**.
xa: These three held village **judicial and police powers**.
They were among the **12 Ayagars**.
Ayagar lands were **tax-exempt**.

98.s:
The village Ayagars were generally remunerated through which of the following?
1. Manyam land
2. A share of the crop called Mera
3. Regular payment exclusively in gold coins

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
98.x: Ayagars were paid in Manyam land or through a crop share called Mera. Exclusive payment in gold coins is incorrect.
98.tq: Reject the extreme word “exclusively” and retain the two stated forms of remuneration.
xs: Ayagars were paid in **Manyam** land or a **crop share (Mera)** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
Exclusive payment in **gold coins** is wrong.
xa: There were **12 Ayagars**, a **Kakatiya** pattern.
Ayagar lands, temple lands and Brahmin grants were **tax-exempt**.
**Karnam**, **Reddi** and **Talari** held judicial and police powers.

98.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Tax)
a. Kanika
b. Pullari
c. Illari
d. Ari

List-II (Meaning)
i. House tax
ii. Land tax
iii. Grazing tax on cattle
iv. Presents or gifts due to the king or officials

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
98.x: Kanika meant presents or gifts; Pullari was the cattle-grazing tax; Illari was the house tax; and Ari was the land tax in Kakatiya usage.
98.tq: Start from the sure tax–meaning pair and eliminate codes with mismatched cesses.
xs: Correct match **a–iv, b–iii, c–i, d–ii** — option **(1)**.
**Kanika** – presents/gifts; **Pullari** – grazing tax on cattle; **Illari** – house tax; **Ari** – land tax.
xa: **Puriti Pannu** = tax on childbirth (**Rachavema**).
Inherited Kakatiya taxes: **Kanika**, **Pullari**, **Pannu**, **Siddhayam**, **Sangam**, **Darshanam**, **Niruvidi**, **Ardhayam**.
**Anavota** abolished the tax on gold.

98.s: Which Reddi ruler levied the oppressive 'Puriti Pannu' and was killed by his own people for it?
98.x: Racha Vema Reddi (1420-1424), the last Kondaveedu Reddi ruler, levied the Puriti Pannu (a tax on childbirth) and was killed by the public (APPSC G2 2019; PYQ 2018). Kumaragiri is known for Vasantotsavams and Anavema for charities. Anavota abolished a tax (on gold) rather than imposing one.
98.tq: Puriti Pannu = Rachavema, the last Kondaveedu ruler, killed by his people.
xs: **Racha Vema Reddi** levied the **Puriti Pannu** and was **killed by his own people** — option **(3)** is correct (**APPSC G2 2019**; PYQ **2018**).
He was the **last Kondaveedu ruler** (**1420-1424**).
**Kumaragiri** is known for **Vasantotsavams**; **Anavema** for **charities**; **Anavota** **abolished** the gold tax.
xa: Puriti Pannu = tax on the **delivery of a child**.
It is the textbook example of burdensome taxation in the **late, weakened Reddi phase**.
Rachavema also cut the **Jaganobbaganda** canals to feed his mother **Surambika's** tank.

98.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Anavota Reddi abolished the tax on gold.
2. Somaya was the minister of Anavota Reddi.
3. The Abhaya Sasanam at Motupalli was connected with encouraging trade.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
98.x: All three statements are correct. Anavota abolished the gold tax, while his minister Somaya issued the Abhaya Sasanam at Motupalli to encourage trade.
98.tq: Combine ruler, minister and purpose into one factual chain before choosing the code.
xs: Statement 1 correct: **Anavota Reddi** **abolished the tax on gold**.
Statement 2 correct: **Somaya** was his **minister**.
Statement 3 correct: Somaya's **Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam** encouraged **trade** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: It guaranteed merchants **protection from sea pirates**.
**Motupalli** was the chief Reddi port; Anavota developed its dock.
**Mallaya Reddy** had taken Motupalli from **Hasan Gangu**.

98.s: Who was the brother of Prolaya Vema Reddi associated with the capture of Motupalli?
98.x: Mallareddi, the brother of Prolaya Vema Reddi, took Motupalli from Hasan Gangu of the Bahmani Sultanate.
98.tq: Separate a family relationship from ministerial and military offices.
xs: **Mallareddi (Mallaya Reddy)**, Prolaya Vema's brother, took **Motupalli** by defeating **Hasan Gangu** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Kataya Vema** was Kumaragiri's brother-in-law; **Chennamanayaka** and **Mamidi Peddanamatya** were **Anavema's** army chief and minister.
xa: Hasan Gangu was the **Bahmani** founder.
**Anavota** later developed the Motupalli dock.
The **Kandukur** branch was Mallareddi's line.

98.s: The 'Andhra Path', an earlier trade route, is mentioned in which Buddhist text?
98.x: The Buddhist text Vinayavatthu mentions the 'Andhra Path' (APPSC 2019). Mahavamsa, Dipavamsa and Divyavadana are other Buddhist texts not linked to the Andhra Path.
98.tq: Andhra Path = Vinayavatthu; Reddi sea trade = Haravilasam.
xs: The **'Andhra Path'** is mentioned in the Buddhist text **Vinayavatthu** (**APPSC 2019**) — option **(2)** is correct.
It is an **earlier trade route** that preceded the Reddi port trade at Motupalli.
xa: **Motupalli** was the chief Reddi port.
**Srinatha's Haravilasam** describes Reddi sea trade (APPSC 2019).
The **Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam** of **Somaya** encouraged trade.

98.s: The Kaluvacheru inscription of 1423 was issued after which event?
o: The seizure of Kondavidu by Pedakomati Vema
The construction of Patala Ganga steps at Srisailam
The abolition of the gold tax by Anavota
98.x: Anitalli issued the Kaluvacheru inscription in 1423 after the recapture of Rajahmundry. It also provides information on the Musunuri-led liberation and Prolaya Vema Reddi’s service under the Nayakas.
98.tq: Associate an inscription with its date and the event immediately preceding its issue.
xs: **Anitalli** issued the **Kaluvacheru inscription** in **1423** after the **recapture of Rajahmundry** — option **(1)** is correct.
**1402** was Pedakomati's seizure of Kondavidu; the **Patala Ganga** steps were finished in **1346**.
xa: Kaluvacheru is a key source on the **Musunuri-led liberation**.
It also records **Prolaya Vema Reddi's** service under the **Nayakas**.
**Veerabhadra** and his brother **Vema** recovered Rajahmundry in **1423**.

98.s: Who constructed the Jaganobbaganda canals to supply water to the tank dug by Surambika?
o: Somaya, the minister of Anavota Reddi
98.x: Racha Vema, the son of Surambika, constructed the Jaganobbaganda canals to feed water into the tank dug by his mother.
98.tq: Identify the family relationship first, then connect the person with the associated irrigation work.
xs: **Racha Vema**, Surambika's **son**, cut the **'Jaganobbaganda'** canals to feed her tank — option **(3)** is correct.
**Surambika** was the wife of **Pedakomati Vema Reddi**.
xa: Tank name: **Govardhana Samudram** (APPSC G2 2019) or **Santana Sagaram** (APPSC GS 2018).
Royal women took an active part in welfare works such as tanks.
Racha Vema was the last Kondaveedu ruler, killed over the **Puriti** tax.

98.s: Which of the following statements is NOT correctly matched?
o: Patala Ganga steps — Pedakomati Vema Reddi
98.x: The Patala Ganga steps at Srisailam were associated with Prolaya Vema Reddi, not Pedakomati Vema Reddi. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
98.tq: Find the swapped ruler–work pair while checking the location and person together.
xs: **Patala Ganga steps — Pedakomati Vema Reddi** is wrong — option **(3)** is the answer; the steps (**1346**) were **Prolaya Vema Reddi's**.
The rest are right: **Kaluvacheru** – **Anitalli**; **Abhaya Sasanam** – **Somaya**; **Jaganobbaganda** canals – **Racha Vema**.
xa: Prolaya Vema also built steps to **Ahobilam** hill.
The **Srisailam** inscription (**1346**) records the Patala Ganga steps.
**Anavema** built the **Veerashiro Mantapa** at Srisailam.

98.s: Which community was primarily associated with inland and coastal trade during the Reddi period?
98.x: The Komatis were mainly engaged in inland and coastal trade.
98.tq: Distinguish occupational roles among the major social groups.
xs: The **Komatis** ran **inland and coastal trade** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Kammas, Kapus, Reddis and Velamas** were the **warrior-farmer** backbone, supplying most soldiers.
xa: The Brahmin-warrior-merchant order survived into **Gajapati** rule.
Merchant **Tippayya Setti** was famed for overseas trade.
**Motupalli** was the chief Reddi port.

98.s:
Consider the following statements about society during the Kakatiya–Reddi period:
1. Kammas, Kapus, Reddis and Velamas formed the warrior-farmer backbone.
2. These groups supplied most of the soldiers.
3. The Brahmin-warrior-merchant social order disappeared completely under Gajapati rule.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
98.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the Brahmin-warrior-merchant order survived into Gajapati rule.
98.tq: Reject the extreme word 'completely' and retain the two connected social facts.
xs: Statement 1 correct: **Kammas, Kapus, Reddis and Velamas** were the **warrior-farmer backbone**.
Statement 2 correct: they **supplied most soldiers**.
Statement 3 wrong: the **Brahmin-warrior-merchant** order **survived into Gajapati rule** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: **Komatis** ran inland and coastal trade.
Village administration also continued in the same decentralised pattern under the Gajapatis.
Village servants: the **12 Ayagars**.

98.s: The Kaluvacheru inscription was issued by Anithalli, the wife of which ruler?
98.x: Anithalli, wife of Veerabhadra Reddi, issued the Kaluvacheru inscription.
98.tq: Apply the relationship trap by matching the named queen with the correct husband.
xs: **Anithalli** was the wife of **Veerabhadra Reddi** — option **(1)** is correct.
She was the daughter of **Kataya Vema Reddi** and his **rightful heir**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes call her "**Allada Reddi's** wife" — most say Veerabhadra's, which is followed.
Veerabhadra was **Allada's second son** and nominal king (restored **1423** and **1429**).
The **Kaluvacheru inscription** dates to **1423**.

98.s:
Consider the following statements about Devadasis during the Reddi period:
1. They were trained in music, dance and ritual.
2. They were respected performers at Shiva temples.
3. Their activities were associated with the Pancharama temples.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
98.x: Devadasis were trained in music, dance and ritual and were respected performers at Shiva temples, including the Pancharamas.
98.tq: Combine the training, social role and temple association before selecting the coded option.
xs: Statement 1 correct: **Devadasis** were trained in **music, dance and ritual**.
Statements 2 and 3 correct: they were respected performers at **Shiva temples** such as the **Pancharamas** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: The Reddis **renovated and endowed** the Pancharama shrines.
Reddi-era renovations: **Draksharama Bhimesvara**, **Samarlakota Kumararama**.
Court dancer **Lakumadevi** served **Kumaragiri**.

98.s: Which religious combination is correctly associated with the Reddi period?
98.x: The Reddi kings followed Pashupata Shaivism, while the people largely followed Veerashaivism.
98.tq: Use the kings-versus-people comparison to avoid reversing the two sectarian affiliations.
xs: Reddi **kings** followed **Pashupata Shaivism**; the **people** followed **Veerashaivism** — option **(4)** is correct.
Option 2 swaps them; Buddhism and Jainism are not the Reddi faiths.
xa: **Bhairava** and **Mailara** worship were common.
Reddi kings were disciples of **Ghoderayacharulu** (Tripurantakam).
Later the Reddis moved towards **Vaishnavism** (Kumaragiri, Kataya Vema).

98.s:
Consider the following statements about religion under the Reddis:
1. The Ghoderayas propagated Shaivism from Tripurantakam.
2. The Reddi kings were disciples of Ghoderayacharulu.
3. The Vadagalai sect of Vedanta Desika's line set up a matha at Srisailam.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
98.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Ghoderayas spread Shaivism from Tripurantakam. Statement 2 is correct: Reddi kings were disciples of Ghoderayacharulu. Statement 3 is wrong: the Vadagalai matha was set up at Ahobilam, not Srisailam. Hence B, C and D are wrong.
98.tq: Shaiva centre = Tripurantakam (Ghoderayas); Vaishnava Vadagalai matha = Ahobilam.
xs: Statement 1 correct: the **Ghoderayas** spread Shaivism from **Tripurantakam**.
Statement 2 correct: Reddi kings were disciples of **Ghoderayacharulu**.
Statement 3 wrong: the **Vadagalai** matha was set up at **Ahobilam**, not Srisailam — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Vadagalai is **Vedanta Desika's** line.
**Kumaragiri** and **Kataya Vema** were Vaishnava patrons.
Kings: **Pashupata Shaivism**; people: **Veerashaivism**.

98.s: Which of the following pairs of rulers were patrons of Vaishnavism?
98.x: Kumaragiri and Kataya Vema were patrons of Vaishnavism. The Reddis gradually moved from Shaivism towards Vaishnavism in the later period.
98.tq: Identify the correct ruler pair before considering the broader religious transition.
xs: **Kumaragiri and Kataya Vema** were **Vaishnava** patrons — option **(1)** is correct.
The Reddis moved from **Shaivism towards Vaishnavism** later.
xa: The **Vadagalai** sect set up a matha at **Ahobilam**.
Reddi endowments went to **Srisailam**, **Simhachalam**, **Ahobilam**.
Earlier kings were **Pashupata Shaivas**.

98.s: Which ruler is associated with the construction of pilgrim rest-houses at Ahobilam and Srisailam and the rebuilding of the ramparts of Ahobilam and Mahanandi?
98.x: Prolaya Vema Reddi built the pilgrim rest-houses at Ahobilam and Srisailam and rebuilt the ramparts of Ahobilam and Mahanandi.
98.tq: Match the cluster of related temple works with the ruler rather than relying on one isolated monument.
xs: **Prolaya Vema Reddi** built the pilgrim **rest-houses (Vasatulas)** at **Ahobilam and Srisailam** and rebuilt the ramparts of **Ahobilam** and **Mahanandi** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Anavema** built the Veerashiro Mantapa; **Vallaya Vemana** restored the Amareswara temple.
xa: Prolaya Vema also built steps to **Patala Ganga** (**1346**) and **Ahobilam** hill.
He restored **agraharas** to Brahmins.
Title: **Nissivu Bhudana Parasurama**.

98.s: 'Sangeeta Chintamani', a work on music, was written by which Reddi ruler?
98.x: Pedakomati Vema Reddi, the scholar-king (1402-1420), wrote Sangeeta Chintamani (PYQ 2011, 2019) as well as Sahitya Chintamani and Srngara Dipika. Kumaragiri wrote Vasantarajiyam on dance, and Kataya Vema wrote Kumaragiri Rajiyam. No work is credited to Anavema.
98.tq: Sangeeta Chintamani = Pedakomati Vema. Do not confuse it with Sangeeta Sudhakaram, which is Velama Singabhupala's.
xs: **Sangeeta Chintamani** (music) was written by **Pedakomati Vema Reddi** (PYQ **2011**, **2019**) — option **(2)** is correct.
**Kumaragiri** wrote **Vasanta Rajiyam** (dance); **Kataya Vema** wrote **Kumaragiri Rajiyam**.
xa: Pedakomati (**1402-1420**) also wrote **Sahitya Chintamani** and **Srngara Dipika**.
⚠ **Sangeeta Sudhakaram** is by **Singabhupala II**, a **Recherla Velama** ruler, not a Reddi.
His court had **Srinatha** and **Vamana Bhatta Bana**.

98.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Vasantarajiyam, a Sanskrit work on dance, was written by Kumaragiri Reddi.
2. Kumaragiri Rajiyam, a commentary on Kalidasa's three plays, was written by Kumaragiri Reddi himself.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
98.x: Statement 1 is correct: Kumaragiri wrote Vasantarajiyam on dance. Statement 2 is wrong, and it is the trap: Kumaragiri Rajiyam was written by his brother-in-law Kataya Vema Reddi, and was only named after Kumaragiri.
98.tq: Kumaragiri Rajiyam is by Kataya Vema, not Kumaragiri.
xs: Statement 1 correct: **Kumaragiri** wrote **Vasantarajiyam**, a Sanskrit work on **dance**.
Statement 2 wrong: **Kumaragiri Rajiyam** was written by his brother-in-law **Kataya Vema Reddi** — so **1 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes credit Kumaragiri Rajiyam to Kumaragiri himself — the trap.
Kumaragiri Rajiyam is a commentary on **Kalidasa's three plays**.
Kumaragiri's title: **Karpura Vasanta Rayalu**.

98.s: Errana's Harivamsam was dedicated to which ruler?
98.x: Errana dedicated his Harivamsam to Prolaya Vema Reddi.
98.tq: This tests the author–patron relationship directly, a common history question pattern.
xs: **Errana's Harivamsam** was dedicated to **Prolaya Vema Reddi** — option **(2)** is correct.
Errana was his court poet at **Addanki** (PYQ G2 2011).
xa: Errana also wrote **Nrisimha Puranam** (PYQ G2 2017) and a **Ramayana**.
Titles: **Prabandha Parameswara**, **Sambhudasa**.
He completed the Telugu **Mahabharata** — last of the **Kavitrayam**.

98.s: Which of the following works was NOT associated with Errana?
98.x: Errana is associated with Aranya Parva shesham, Harivamsam and Nrusimha Puranam. Palnati Veera Charitra was one of Srinatha's works.

xs: **Palnati Veera Charitra** is **Srinatha's**, not Errana's — option **(3)** is the answer.
Errana's works: **Aranya Parva shesham**, **Harivamsam**, **Nrusimha Puranam**.
xa: Srinatha's other works: **Sringara Naishadham**, **Kasikhandam**, **Bhimakhandam**, **Haravilasam**.
Srinatha also wrote **Maruttarat Charitra** and **Sivaratri Mahatyam**.
Errana bridges **Nannaya** and **Tikkana**.

98.s: Which of the following descriptions of Errana is correct?
o: He was the first of the Kavitrayam and initiated the Telugu Mahabharata.
He was the last of the Kavitrayam and completed the Telugu Mahabharata.
He opened the Kavya Yuga through his independent Sanskrit compositions.
He was a court poet of the Vijayanagara emperor who translated the entire Sanskrit Mahabharata.
98.x: Errana was the last of the Kavitrayam and completed the Telugu Mahabharata by translating the remaining portion of the Aranya Parva.
98.tq: Use the first/last distinction to separate Errana from the other members and from Srinatha.
xs: Errana was the **last of the Kavitrayam** and **completed the Telugu Mahabharata** — option **(2)** is correct.
He translated the remaining part of the **Aranya Parva**.
**Srinatha**, not Errana, opened the **Kavya Yuga**.
xa: Errana was court poet of **Prolaya Vema Reddi**, not of Vijayanagara.
He bridges **Nannaya** and **Tikkana**.
Harivamsa was dedicated to **Prolaya Vema**.

98.s: Which of the following titles was borne by the poet Errana?
98.x: Errana was called Prabandha Parameswara and Sambhudasa. Kavi Sarvabhauma was Srinatha's title, and Sahitya Chudamani was Vamana Bhatta Bana's. Andhra Suratrana was a royal title (Anavema in the APPSC key, first borne by Kapaya Nayaka), not a poet's.
98.tq: Errana = Prabandha Parameswara, Sambhudasa; Srinatha = Kavi Sarvabhauma.
xs: Errana bore the title **Prabandha Parameswara** (also **Sambhudasa**) — option **(2)** is correct.
**Kavi Sarvabhauma** was **Srinatha's**; **Sahitya Chudamani** was **Vamana Bhatta Bana's**.
**Andhra Suratrana** was a royal title — **Anavema** in the APPSC G2 2011 key, first borne by **Kapaya Nayaka**.
xa: Vamana Bhatta Bana was also **Sahitya Samrajya Dhurandhara**.
Srinatha was honoured with **Kanakabhishekam** and **Ganda Penderam**.
Errana completed the Telugu Mahabharata.

Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Poet — Ruler

2. Bala Saraswati — Anavota Reddi
3. Srinatha — Pedakomati Vema Reddi
4. Vamana Bhatta Bana — Pedakomati Vema Reddi
98.x: Errana was associated with Prolaya Vema, Bala Saraswati with Anavota, and both Srinatha and Vamana Bhatta Bana were associated with Pedakomati Vema. Hence all four pairs are correctly matched.
98.tq: Start from the sure poet–ruler pairs and eliminate codes containing a swapped court.
xs: All four are right: **Errana** – **Prolaya Vema Reddi**; **Bala Saraswati** – **Anavota Reddi**.
**Srinatha** and **Vamana Bhatta Bana** – **Pedakomati Vema Reddi** — so option **(4)**.

98.s:
Consider the following statements about Srinatha:

1. His Sringara Naishadham was based on Sriharsha's Naishadhiyacharita.
2. He dedicated Sringara Naishadham to Mamidi Singana.
3. He dedicated Haravilasam to Tippayya Setti.
4. He wrote only devotional works and did not compose historical narratives.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
98.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because Srinatha also composed works such as Palnati Veeracharitra and Maruttarat Charitra.

xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Sringara Naishadham** was rendered from **Sriharsha's Naishadhiyacharita**.
Statement 2 is correct: Srinatha dedicated **Sringara Naishadham** to **Mamidi Singana**.
Statement 3 is correct: **Haravilasam** was dedicated to merchant **Tippayya Setti**, famous for overseas trade.
Statement 4 is wrong: Srinatha also wrote narratives such as **Palnati Veeracharitra** and **Maruttarat Charitra**.
xa: Other Srinatha works: **Kasikhandam**, **Bhimakhandam / Bhimeswara Puranam** and **Sivaratri Mahatyam**.
**Haravilasam** describes the **sea trade** and the **imports and exports** of the Reddi age (APPSC 2019).

98.s: Which one of the following works of Srinatha is specifically associated with Bhimeswara of Draksharamam?
98.x: Bhimakhandam, also known as Bhimeswara Puranam, praises Bhimeswara of Draksharamam.
98.tq: Use the work–theme association rather than confusing similarly named literary titles.
xs: **Bhimakhandam**, also called **Bhimeswara Puranam**, praises **Bhimeswara of Draksharamam** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Haravilasam** describes the **Motupalli sea trade** and was dedicated to **Tippayya Setti**.
**Sringara Naishadham** is based on **Sriharsha's Naishadhiyacharita**, dedicated to **Mamidi Singana**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes say Bhimakhandam is about the **Bhima river** — the main reading is the **Draksharamam** deity.
**Draksharama Bhimesvara** is one of the **Pancharama** shrines renovated in the Reddi era (Godavari region).
Other Srinatha works: **Palnati Veeracharitra**, **Maruttarat Charitra**, **Sivaratri Mahatyam**, **Kasikhandam**.

98.s:
Consider the following statements about Srinatha:
1. He belongs to the Kavya Yuga and prepared the way for the Prabandha style.
2. He is cited as evidence that birch bark was used for writing in the 15th century.
3. At Vijayanagara he defeated Gauda Dindima Bhatta, court poet of Devaraya II, and received Kanakabhishekam.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
98.x: Statement 1 is correct: Srinatha's era is the Kavya Yuga and he prepared the way for the Prabandha style. Statement 2 is wrong: he is cited as evidence for the use of paper, not birch bark. Statement 3 is correct: he defeated Gauda Dindima Bhatta of Devaraya II's court and was honoured with Kanakabhishekam and Ganda Penderam. So only C fits; A, B and D include the false statement 2.
98.tq: Srinatha + 15th century writing material = paper (PYQ G2 2012).
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: Srinatha belongs to the **Kavya Yuga** and prepared the way for the **Prabandha** style.
Statement 2 is wrong: Srinatha is cited (APPSC G2 2012) as evidence that **paper**, not birch bark, was used for writing in the **15th century**.
Statement 3 is correct: he defeated **Gauda Dindima Bhatta** of **Devaraya II's** court and got **Kanakabhishekam** and **Ganda Penderam**.
xa: Srinatha was **Vidyadhikari** (minister of education) to **Pedakomati Vema Reddi** and composed his Sanskrit inscriptions.
After Kondaveedu fell (**1424**) he joined the Rajahmundry Reddis (patron **Veerabhadra Reddi**) with **Bendapudi Annamatya's** help.
After Rajahmundry fell (**1448**) he lived in **poverty in Palnadu**.
He wrote more kavyas than any other Telugu poet.

98.s: Singabhupala II, the author of Sangeeta Sudhakaram, belonged to which political group?
98.x: Singabhupala II was a Recherla Velama ruler of Rachakonda, not a Reddi ruler, and he wrote Sangeeta Sudhakaram.

xs: **Singabhupala II** was a **Recherla Velama ruler of Rachakonda** — so option **(2)** is correct.

The **Recherla Velamas** and the **Musunuris** were the other two successor states after **1323**, with the Reddis.
**Vasanta Rajiyam** (on dance) was by **Kumaragiri Reddi**.

98.s: Srinatha held which office at the court of Pedakomati Vema Reddi?
98.x: Srinatha (Kavi Sarvabhauma) was Vidyadhikari, the minister of education, at Pedakomati Vema Reddi's court, and he composed Pedakomati's Sanskrit inscriptions. He held no post as chief minister, commander or royal preceptor.

xs: Srinatha was **Vidyadhikari (minister of education)** at **Pedakomati Vema Reddi's** court — so option **(1)** is correct.

xa: Srinatha's title: **Kavi Sarvabhauma** (c. **1365-1441**); court poet of Pedakomati (PYQ 2002).

Pedakomati was a scholar-king titled **Sarvajna Chakravarti**.

99.x: Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka led the liberation confederacy, the Vimochanodyamam (APPSC GS 2018; G2 2019). Recherla Singama, Prolaya Vema Reddi and Kolani Rudra were chiefs who took part in the movement but did not lead it.
99.tq: Leader of the liberation = Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka; Kaluvacheru grant names 75 Nayakas who backed him.
xs: **Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka** led the liberation confederacy (APPSC GS 2018; G2 2019) — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Recherla Singama**, **Prolaya Vema Reddi** and **Kolani Rudra** were participating chiefs, not the leader.
xa: Prolaya Nayaka was son of **Potinayaka**, of the **Kamma** clan.
He ruled from **Rekapalli** on the Godavari, near **Bhadrachalam** (APPSC G2 2017).
His **Vilasa copper-plate grant (1330)** records Tughluq atrocities and his relief measures.
Childless, he was succeeded by **Kapaya Nayaka**.

99.s: The Musunuri Nayaks belonged primarily to which community?
99.x: The Musunuris belonged to the Kamma community, also described as Chaturthanvayas.
99.tq: Distinguish the Musunuri community from the neighbouring ruling groups.
xs: The Musunuris belonged to the **Kamma** clan (the **Chaturthanvaya** lineage) — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **Velamas** were their rivals (Recherla of Rachakonda), and the **Reddis** formed a separate successor state.
xa: The surname comes from **Musunuru** village near **Vuyyuru** (Krishna district).
Prolaya Nayaka was the son of **Potinayaka**.
Velamas are also called **Padmanayakas**.

99.s: Prolaya Nayaka ruled from which place?
99.x: Prolaya Nayaka ruled from Rekapalli, situated on the Godavari in the forest region near Bhadrachalam.
99.tq: Separate the capital of Prolaya from the later Musunuri capital of Kapaya.
xs: Prolaya Nayaka ruled from **Rekapalli** — so option **(1)** is correct (APPSC G2 2017).
**Orugallu** was **Kapaya Nayaka's** capital from **1336**; **Rachakonda** and **Devarakonda** were **Recherla Velama** capitals.
xa: Rekapalli lay **on the Godavari**, in forest near **Bhadrachalam**.
The Velamas moved their capital from **Amanagallu to Rachakonda** under **Anapota Nayaka**.
Reddi capitals: **Addanki → Kondavidu → Rajahmundry**.

99.s:
Consider the following statements about the Vilasa copper-plate grant of 1330:
1. It describes the sufferings of the people under Tughluq rule.
2. It records Prolaya Nayaka's restoration of agraharas to Brahmins.
3. It was issued by the Reddi queen Anitalli.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
99.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Vilasa grant (1330) of Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka describes the Tughluq atrocities and his relief measures, including the restoration of agraharas. Statement 3 is wrong: Anitalli issued the Kaluvacheru grant of 1423, not the Vilasa grant.
99.tq: Vilasa 1330 = Prolaya Nayaka; Kaluvacheru 1423 = Anitalli.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: the **Vilasa grant (1330)** describes sufferings under **Tughluq** rule.
Statement 2 is correct: it records agrarian relief and **restoration of agraharas** to Brahmins.
Statement 3 is wrong: Reddi queen **Anitalli** issued the **Kaluvacheru grant (1423)**, not the Vilasa grant.
xa: The Vilasa grant was issued by **Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka**.
The **Kaluvacheru grant** names **75 Nayakas** who backed Prolaya.
**Polavaram, Ganapeshwaram and Palasamarri** records belong to **Kapaya Nayaka**.

99.s: Which of the following was NOT a title associated with Kapaya Nayaka?
99.x: Andhradeshadhiswara, Katakachurakara and Andhra Suratrana were associated with Kapaya Nayaka. Kavirajamarga is not one of his titles.
99.tq: Identify the unrelated famous term among titles belonging to the same historical setting.
xs: **Kavirajamarga** is not a title of Kapaya Nayaka — so option **(3)** is the answer.
His titles were **Andhra Suratrana**, **Andhradeshadhiswara** and **Katakachurakara**.
xa: Kapaya was the **first** to bear **Andhra Suratrana** (APPSC GS 2019); later **Anavema Reddi** too (APPSC G2 2011 key).
**Andhradesadhisvara** had earlier been held by Kakatiya **Ganapatideva**.
⚠ "First borne by" → **Kapaya**; "popular title of" with Anavema in the options → **Anavema Reddi**.

99.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Fall of Warangal
B. Issue of the Vilasa grant
C. Kapaya Nayaka’s capture of Orugallu
D. Battle of Bhimavaram
99.x: Warangal fell in 1323, the Vilasa grant was issued in 1330, Orugallu was captured in 1336, and the Battle of Bhimavaram occurred in 1367–68.
99.tq: Place the events by their stated years before checking the sequence options.
xs: Order: **A, B, C, D** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Fall of Warangal (1323)** → **Vilasa grant (1330)** → **Kapaya's capture of Orugallu (1336)** → **Battle of Bhimavaram (1367-68)**.
xa: Kapaya helped found the **Bahmani** kingdom in **1347** (Gulbarga).
Bahmani gains: **Kaulas (1350)**, **Bhuvanagiri (1356)**, **Golconda (1364-65)**.
Bhimavaram was the **last battle** of the Musunuri kingdom.

99.s:
Consider the following statements about the titles associated with Kapaya Nayaka:
1. He was known by the title Andhradesadhisvara.
2. He was known by the title Katakachurakara.
3. Andhradesadhisvara had earlier been held by Kakatiya Ganapatideva.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
99.x: Kapaya Nayaka is associated with both Andhradesadhisvara and Katakachurakara. The title Andhradesadhisvara had earlier been used by Kakatiya Ganapatideva.
99.tq: Check the title-holder details and the earlier association separately before selecting the combined code.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
Statements 1 and 2: Kapaya Nayaka bore **Andhradesadhisvara** and **Katakachurakara**.
Statement 3: **Andhradesadhisvara** was earlier held by Kakatiya **Ganapatideva**.
xa: Kapaya was the **first holder** of **Andhra Suratrana** (APPSC GS 2019).
⚠ **Kataka Churakara** is also listed as a title of Reddi **Kataya Vema** in Reddi notes.
Kapaya ruled **1336-1368** from **Orugallu**.

99.s: In the recovery of Warangal in 1336, Kapaya Nayaka acted together with
o: Hoysala Veera Ballala III, Prolaya Vema Reddi and Singama
Bukka I, Mahmud Gawan and Sultan Quli Qutb Shah
Annadevu, Kataya Vema and Pedakomati Vema Reddi
Hasan Gangu, Firoz Shah Tughlaq and Vinayaka Deva
99.x: In 1336, Kapaya Nayaka, Hoysala Veera Ballala III, Prolaya Vema Reddi and Singama took Warangal from Malik Maqbul.
99.tq: Start with the sure association of the liberation coalition and reject later-period figures.
xs: In **1336** Kapaya took Warangal with **Hoysala Veera Ballala III, Prolaya Vema Reddi and Singama** — so option **(1)** is correct.
They took **Orugallu** from **Malik Maqbool**.
**Bukka I** was sought later against the Bahmanis; **Hasan Gangu** was helped by Kapaya in **1347**; **Sultan Quli Qutb Shah** came much later.
xa: Kapaya then ruled the old **Kakatiya** realm from **Orugallu**.
Simultaneously **Singama** cleared Nalgonda-Mahabubnagar and **Prolaya Vema Reddi** cleared Kammanadu-Pakanadu.

99.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the simultaneous territorial activities of the three leaders in 1336?
o: Kapaya took Warangal, Singama cleared Nalgonda–Mahabubnagar, and Prolaya Vema Reddi cleared Kammanadu–Pakanadu
Singama took Warangal, Kapaya cleared Kammanadu–Pakanadu, and Prolaya Vema Reddi cleared Nalgonda–Mahabubnagar
Prolaya Vema Reddi took Warangal, Kapaya cleared Nalgonda–Mahabubnagar, and Singama cleared Vengi
Kapaya took Vengi, Singama cleared Kammanadu–Pakanadu, and Prolaya Vema Reddi took Warangal

99.tq: Match each leader with the correct region and detect the swapped assignments.
xs: **Kapaya** took Warangal, **Singama** cleared **Nalgonda–Mahabubnagar**, and **Prolaya Vema Reddi** cleared **Kammanadu–Pakanadu** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Kammanadu-Pakanadu lay **south of the Krishna**.
xa: Kapaya's ally was **Hoysala Veera Ballala III**; Warangal was taken from **Malik Maqbul** in **1336**.
Kapaya appointed **Anapota Nayaka** as governor at **Vengi**.
**Singama Nayaka I** later expanded up to the **Krishna** and into the **Krishna-Tungabhadra doab**.

99.s: The title 'Andhra Suratrana' was first borne by:
99.x: Musunuri Kapaya Nayaka was the first to bear Andhra Suratrana (APPSC GS 2019). Anavema Reddi used it later and is the APPSC G2 2011 key answer for 'popular title of'. Prolaya Vema and Singama Nayaka I did not bear it.
99.tq: 'First borne by' = Kapaya; 'popular title of', with Anavema among the options = Anavema.
xs: **Kapaya Nayaka** was the first to bear **Andhra Suratrana** (APPSC GS 2019) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Anavema Reddi** bore it later (APPSC G2 2011 key for "popular title of").
**Prolaya Vema Reddi** and **Singama Nayaka I** are not recorded with this title.
xa: Kapaya's other titles: **Andhradeshadhiswara** and **Katakachurakara**.
⚠ "First borne by" → Kapaya; "popular title of" with Anavema in options → Anavema.
Kapaya was paternal nephew (some notes: cousin) of **Prolaya Nayaka**.

99.s: Kapaya Nayaka helped Hasan Gangu in founding the Bahmani kingdom in
99.x: Kapaya Nayaka helped Hasan Gangu, also known as Zafar Khan, establish the Bahmani kingdom at Gulbarga in 1347.
99.tq: Keep the year and place together to avoid confusing the Bahmani foundation with later territorial losses.
xs: Kapaya helped **Hasan Gangu (Zafar Khan)** found the **Bahmani** kingdom in **1347 at Gulbarga** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**1356** is the loss of **Bhuvanagiri**, **1367** Bhimavaram, and **1336** the recovery of Warangal.
xa: Kapaya then lost to the Bahmanis: **Kaulas (1350)**, **Bhuvanagiri (1356)**, **Golconda (1364-65)**.
His son **Vinayaka Deva** was burnt alive by **Muhammad Shah I** (1361-62).
Same wave: **Harihara-Bukka** founded Vijayanagara in **1336**.

99.s:

xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.

Statement 3 is wrong: after helping found the Bahmani kingdom (**1347**) he **lost** forts and his son to it.
xa: The truce of **1364-65** ceded **Golconda**, which became the boundary.
A **turquoise throne** was among the gifts.
He lost **400 elephants**, **250 horses** and **33 lakhs** with Golconda.

99.s:

Son **Vinayaka Deva** was killed in **1361/1362**.
Kapaya died at **Bhimavaram (1367-68)**.

99.s: Which of the following correctly describes the truce of 1364–65 between Kapaya Nayaka and the Bahmanis?
o: Bhuvanagiri was ceded along with the turquoise throne
Kaulas was restored to Kapaya and Bhuvanagiri was made the boundary
The Bahmanis abandoned Telangana and recognised Kapaya’s sovereignty over Golconda

xs: Under the **1364–65 truce**, **Golconda fort was ceded with huge wealth** and **Golconda became the boundary** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Bhuvanagiri** had been lost earlier, in **1356**, and **Kaulas** in **1350**; neither was restored.
xa: Wealth ceded: **400 elephants**, **250 horses** and **33 lakhs** in treasure.
A **turquoise throne** was among the gifts.
Kapaya sought help from **Bukka I** and **Firoz Shah Tughlaq** against the Bahmanis.

99.s: Who founded the Recherla Velama lineage?

xs: **Betala Nayudu** founded the Recherla Velama lineage — so option **(4)** is correct.

**Sarvagna Singa Bhupala** was a later Sanskrit **scholar-king** of Rachakonda.
xa: Family history: **Velugoti Varivamsavali**.
Velamas are also called **Padmanayakas**.
The kingdom ended when **Sultan Quli Qutb Shah** annexed Rachakonda and Devarakonda.

99.s: Which one of the following statements about Singama Nayaka I is correct?
o: He founded the independent kingdom and expanded towards the Krishna and the Krishna-Tungabhadra doab
He shifted the capital from Rachakonda to Amanagallu
He founded the Bahmani kingdom at Gulbarga
He defeated Sultan Quli Qutb Shah and recovered Devarakonda
99.x: Singama Nayaka I founded the independent Velama kingdom and expanded to the Krishna and into the Krishna-Tungabhadra doab.
99.tq: Reject options assigning later rulers’ actions to the kingdom’s founder.
xs: **Singama Nayaka I** founded the **independent kingdom** and expanded up to the **Krishna** and into the **Krishna-Tungabhadra doab** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The capital shift (**Amanagallu → Rachakonda**) was by his son **Anapota Nayaka**, not from Rachakonda to Amanagallu.
The **Bahmani** kingdom was founded by **Hasan Gangu**.
xa: In **1336** Singama expelled the Muslims from **Nalgonda and Mahabubnagar**.
**Kapaya Nayaka** failed to subdue him.
He was **killed fighting the chiefs of Jallipalli**.

99.s:
Consider the following statements about the Recherla Velama kingdom:

xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.

Statements 2 and 3: they ruled **1325-1475**, **about 150 years**, from Rachakonda and Devarakonda.

99.s: Which Sultan defeated the Velama chiefs and annexed both Rachakonda and Devarakonda?
o: Muhammad I of the Bahmani dynasty
99.x: Sultan Quli Qutb Shah, who ruled at Golconda from 1518 to 1543, defeated the Velama chiefs and annexed Rachakonda and Devarakonda.

xs: **Sultan Quli Qutb Shah** (Golconda, **1518-43**) defeated the Velama chiefs and annexed **Rachakonda and Devarakonda** — so option **(1)** is correct.

**Muhammad I** burnt **Vinayaka Deva**; **Firoz Shah Tughlaq** was approached by Kapaya for help.
xa: The Velamas later sided with the **Bahmanis and Gajapatis** against Vijayanagara and the Reddis.
**Devarakonda** (Nalgonda) was the second Velama branch capital.

99.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Betala Nayudu — Founder of the Recherla lineage
Singama Nayaka I — Killed in the Battle of Bhimavaram
Anapota Nayaka — Shifted the capital to Rachakonda
Sarvagna Singa Bhupala — Scholar-king of Rachakonda
99.x: Singama Nayaka I was killed fighting the chiefs of Jallipalli, whereas Anapota Nayaka defeated Kapaya at Bhimavaram.
99.tq: Find the swapped battlefield association among otherwise correctly matched pairs.
xs: **Singama Nayaka I — Killed in the Battle of Bhimavaram** is wrong — so option **(2)** is the answer.

The other pairs are correct: **Betala Nayudu** founder; **Anapota** moved the capital to **Rachakonda**; **Sarvagna Singa Bhupala** scholar-king.

99.s: Which work is the family history of the Recherla Velamas?
99.x: The Velugoti Varivamsavali is the family history of the Recherla Velamas. Madhura Vijayam is Gangadevi's poem, Rasarnava Sudhakara is Singabhupala's work on dramaturgy, and Tarikh-i-Ferishta is a Persian history of the Deccan sultans.

xs: **Velugoti Varivamsavali** is the family history of the Recherla Velamas — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Madhura Vijayam** is **Gangadevi's** work; **Rasarnava Sudhakara** is **Singabhupala's** work on dramaturgy.
**Tarikh-i-Ferishta** is a Persian history that calls Telangana **"Tilang"**.

Founder of the lineage: **Betala Nayudu**.
Kapaya's records: **Polavaram, Ganapeshwaram, Palasamarri**.

99.s: What was the principal consequence of Kapaya Nayaka’s decline in relation to the Reddis and Velamas?
o: The Reddis recovered coastal Andhra and the Velamas absorbed Musunuri Telangana
The Velamas restored the Musunuri kingdom in coastal Andhra
The Reddis captured Telangana and the Velamas occupied coastal Andhra

99.x: Kapaya’s decline enabled the Reddis to take coastal Andhra, while the Velamas absorbed Musunuri Telangana.

xs: After **Kapaya's** decline, the **Reddis took coastal Andhra** and the **Velamas absorbed Musunuri Telangana** — so option **(1)** is correct.

99.s: Madanayudu and his nephew Naganayudu invaded the Reddi kingdom primarily to avenge the death of whom?
99.x: Madanayudu and Naganayudu invaded the Reddi kingdom to avenge Singama.

xs: **Madanayudu** and nephew **Naganayudu** invaded the Reddi kingdom to avenge **Singama** — so option **(2)** is correct.

**Vinayaka Deva** (Kapaya's son) was killed by the Bahmanis, not the Reddis.

99.x: Madanayudu and Naganayudu defeated Anavota Reddi at Dharanikota, also called Dannala Kota.

xs: They defeated **Anavota Reddi** at **Dharanikota** (Dannala Kota) — so option **(2)** is correct.

**Dharanikota** was one of **Prolaya Vema Reddi's** forts.

99.s: Which of the following titles were associated with the Velama victory at Dharanikota?
99.x: After the victory over Anavota Reddi at Dharanikota, the titles Jagadabbaganda and Rayavesa Bhujanga were associated with the victors.

xs: The Dharanikota victory brought the titles **Jagadabbaganda** and **Rayavesa Bhujanga** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Andhra Suratrana** was **Kapaya Nayaka's** title (first holder), later **Anavema Reddi's**.
xa: The battle was **Madanayudu and Naganayudu** vs **Anavota Reddi**; the Velamas won.
Dharanikota is also called **Dannala Kota**.

100.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Kondaveedu:

Old Tamil of the Sangam texts

Telugu inscriptions in the fully developed medieval Telugu script
101.x: The Bhattiprolu inscriptions, dated approximately to 400 BCE in Guntur, use a variant of Brahmi and contain early Telugu place and personal names.
101.tq: Use the precise combination of date, place, script and linguistic evidence.
xs: The **Bhattiprolu stupa inscriptions** use a **Brahmi variant** carrying **early Telugu place and personal names** — so option **(3)** is correct.
They are dated c. **400 BCE**, in **Guntur**.
The fully developed Telugu script came only in the **11th-14th c.**
xa: Telugu script evolved from **Brahmi**.
Next stage: common **Old Kannada-Telugu** script (Kadamba-Chalukya).
The first Telugu word, **"Nagabu"**, is in the **Amaravati** inscription.

101.s: In the Prakrit age of Andhra, whose golden age came under Hala, the royal language was:
101.x: Prakrit was the royal language in this age (APPSC G2 2011 key), with its golden age under Hala. Sanskrit later became the official language of the Eastern Chalukyas; Telugu appears only as words in Prakrit records; Tamil is not the answer.
101.tq: Prakrit age: royal language Prakrit (G2 2011)
xs: The royal language of the Prakrit age was **Prakrit** (G2 2011 key) — so option **(3)** is correct.
Its golden age came under **Hala**.
Telugu then appears only as **words inside Prakrit records**.
xa: **Hala's Gatha Saptasati** has Telugu words like atta, addam, potta, pilla.
Later the official language was **Sanskrit** (G2 2008 key), with Telugu as the people's language.
**Mayidavolu** plates (Prakrit, c. **300 CE**) first record "Andhrapatha".

101.s:
Consider the following statements about the Gatha Saptasati:
1. It was compiled by the Satavahana king Hala.
2. It contains Telugu words such as atta, addam, potta and pilla.
3. It is written in the Telugu script with rounded letters.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
101.x: Statement 1 is correct: Hala compiled it. Statement 2 is correct: this Prakrit work holds early Telugu words. Statement 3 is wrong: it is a Prakrit text; the separate rounded Telugu script came only in the 11th-14th centuries. So only two.
101.tq: Telugu words inside a Prakrit text.
xs: **Only two** statements (1 and 2) are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Gatha Saptasati** is by the **Satavahana** king **Hala**.
Statement 2 is correct: it holds Telugu words like **atta, addam, potta, pilla** in a **Prakrit** text.
Statement 3 is wrong: the separate Telugu script with **rounded letters** came only in the **11th-14th c.**
xa: First Telugu word **"Nagabu"** — **Amaravati** inscription, identified by **Veturi Prabhakara Sastri**.
**"Vepuru"** occurs in the **Myakadoni** inscription.
The Gatha Saptasati **contained writing by women**.
Telugu script grew from **Brahmi**; **Bhattiprolu** inscriptions c. **400 BCE**.

101.s: The Kalamalla inscription, regarded as the earliest Telugu inscription, belongs to which dynasty?
101.x: The Kalamalla inscription of about 575 CE is associated with the Renati Chola ruler Erikal Mutturaju Dhananjaya.
101.tq: Identify the dynasty linked with the earliest inscription.
xs: **Kalamalla** (Kadapa, c. **575 CE**) belongs to the **Renati Cholas** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Issuer: **Dhanunjaya Varma** (Erikal Mutturaju Dhananjaya).
It is the **first Telugu inscription**, in **prose** (G2 2012 key).
xa: **Erragudipadu** (Punyakumara, Renati Chola) is the first **fully available** Telugu inscription, in geya style.
**Arumbhaka** is by **Erikal Mutturaju**, the same line as Kalamalla.
⚠ **Kalamalla** = first inscription (prose); **Addanki** = first poetic inscription.

101.s: Which inscription is regarded as the first fully available Telugu inscription and is written in a song or geya style?
101.x: The Erragudipadu inscription of Punyakumara of the Renati Cholas is regarded as the first fully available Telugu inscription and uses a song or geya style.
101.tq: Distinguish between the earliest inscription and the first fully available inscription.
xs: **Erragudipadu** is the **first fully available Telugu inscription**, in **song (geya) style** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It was issued by **Punyakumara**, a **Renati Chola**.
**Kalamalla** is the first Telugu inscription (prose); **Addanki** the first poetic one; **Vipparla** the "first complete early Telugu text".
xa: **Chejarla** (Kubja Vishnuvardhana) has over **50% Telugu** words.
**Vipparla** is credited to **Jayasimha Vallabha I** (APPSC key).

101.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Inscription)

a. Addanki
b. Bezawada
c. Sataluru
 d. Kandukur and Dharmavaram

List-II (Metre or significance)
 i. Seesa and Ataveladi verses
 ii. First Telugu poetic inscription; Taruvoja metre
 iii. Champakamala verse with prasa
 iv. First Madhyakkara poem

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
101.x: Addanki is linked with Taruvoja and the first Telugu poetic inscription; Bezawada with the first Madhyakkara poem; Sataluru with Champakamala and prasa; and Kandukur–Dharmavaram with Seesa and Ataveladi.
101.tq: Begin with the distinctive first-poem associations and then match the metres.
xs: Correct match: **a–ii, b–iv, c–iii, d–i** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Addanki** → **first Telugu poetic inscription**, **Taruvoja** metre; **Bezawada** → **first Madhyakkara** poem.
**Sataluru** → **Champakamala** verse with prasa; **Kandukur and Dharmavaram** → **Seesa** and **Ataveladi** verses.
xa: Addanki was issued by **Panduranga**, commander of **Gunaga Vijayaditya III**.
Bezawada was issued by **Yuddhamalla II** (Nagamalleswara temple).
Sataluru, Kandukur and Dharmavaram belong to **Gunaga Vijayaditya**.

101.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Lakshmipuram — Jayasimha I — first complete early Telugu prose inscription
Chejarla — Kubja Vishnuvardhana — more than 50 per cent Telugu words
Vipparla — Jayasimha Vallabha I — first complete early Telugu text
Pitikayagulla — Gunaga Vijayaditya — first Telugu poetic inscription
101.x: Pitikayagulla is associated with the eighth century and post-Badami Chalukya influence, particularly in relation to early Telugu script; it is not the first Telugu poetic inscription. That distinction belongs to Addanki.
101.tq: Spot the wrong issuer–inscription–significance combination.
xs: **Pitikayagulla — Gunaga Vijayaditya — first poetic inscription** is wrong — so option **(4)** is the answer.
**Pitikayagulla** is an **8th c.** early-Telugu-script record with post-Badami Chalukya influence, near **Bestavaripeta, Prakasam**.
The first poetic inscription is **Addanki** (Panduranga).
The others are correct: **Lakshmipuram — Jayasimha I**; **Chejarla — Kubja Vishnuvardhana** (over **50%** Telugu); **Vipparla — Jayasimha Vallabha I**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes (p.133) credit **Vipparla** to **Kubja Vishnuvardhana**.
Pitikayagulla was reported in **Jun 2026**; some notes place it in **Rayalaseema**.

101.s: The Chebrolu inscription is significant because it shows which of the following?
o: The transition from Sanskrit to Tamil exclusively
The first use of the Madhyakkara metre
101.x: The Chebrolu inscription is noted for showing the Marga and Desi forms.
101.tq: Identify the distinctive linguistic feature associated with an inscription.
xs: The **Chebrolu inscription** shows the **Marga and Desi** forms — so option **(2)** is correct.
The first **Madhyakkara** poem is the **Bezawada** inscription.
The earliest Telugu prose is **Kalamalla**.
xa: Kakatiya-era inscriptions: **Guduru** (Beta II), **Konidena** (Opili Siddhi), **Upparapalle** (Katamaraju), **Karimnagar** (Gangadhara).
The **Desi vs Marga** debate: Bhakti poets brought native Telugu idiom against heavy Sanskrit.

101.s: The Addanki inscription, the first Telugu poetic inscription, was issued by:
o: Panduranga, commander of Gunaga Vijayaditya III
101.x: The Addanki inscription in Taruvoja metre was issued by Panduranga (Pandaranga), commander of the Eastern Chalukya king Gunaga Vijayaditya III. Yuddhamalla II issued the Bezawada inscription, Punyakumara the Erragudipadu inscription and Kubja Vishnuvardhana the Chejarla inscription.
101.tq: Addanki = Panduranga (general of Gunaga Vijayaditya III), Taruvoja
xs: **Addanki** was issued by **Panduranga**, commander of Eastern Chalukya **Gunaga Vijayaditya III** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Yuddhamalla II** issued **Bezawada**; **Punyakumara** issued **Erragudipadu**; **Kubja Vishnuvardhana** issued **Chejarla**.
xa: Addanki is in **Taruvoja** metre — the **first Telugu verse**.
Bezawada is the **first Madhyakkara** poem.
**Sataluru**: Champakamala with prasa; **Kandukur**: Seesa and Ataveladi.

101.s:
Consider the following statements about language use in Eastern Chalukya inscriptions:
1. Sanskrit was the official language, while Telugu was the people's and favoured language.
2. In bilingual inscriptions, the eulogy was in Telugu and the grant details in Sanskrit.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
101.x: Statement 1 is correct: Sanskrit was official (G2 2008 key), Telugu the people's language. Statement 2 is wrong: it is reversed; the eulogy was in Sanskrit and the grant details in Telugu. So 1 only.
101.tq: Sanskrit praise, Telugu details.
xs: **1 only** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Sanskrit** was the **official language** (G2 **2008** key); **Telugu** was the people's and favoured language.
Statement 2 is wrong — reversed: the **eulogy** was in **Sanskrit** and the **grant details** in **Telugu**.
xa: **Nannaya** made Telugu a language for **high literature**.
**Chebrolu inscription** shows **Marga** and **Desi** forms.
**Addanki** = **first Telugu poetic inscription** (**Taruvoja** metre).

101.s:
Consider the following statements about pre-Nannaya Telugu:
1. The Kalamalla, Vipparla, Addanki and Bezawada inscriptions show that written Telugu, including verse, existed before Nannaya.
2. A complete pre-Nannaya Telugu literary text survives.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
101.x: Statement 1 is correct: Renati Chola and Chalukya prose and the poetic inscriptions prove written Telugu before the Mahabharata. Statement 2 is wrong: no pre-Nannaya literary text survives in the sources. So 1 only.
101.tq: Inscriptions yes, literary text no.
xs: **1 only** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Kalamalla** (prose, **575 CE**), **Vipparla**, **Addanki** and **Bezawada** prove written Telugu verse existed **before** the Mahabharata.
Statement 2 is wrong: **no pre-Nannaya literary text survives**.
xa: Nannaya relied on a written form tested through **five centuries** of inscriptions.
**Kalamalla** (Kadapa) by **Dhanunjaya Varma**, **Renati Chola** = **first Telugu inscription**.
**Bezawada** (**Yuddhamalla II**) = **first Madhyakkara** poem.
**Erragudipadu** (**Punyakumara**) = first fully available Telugu inscription.

101.s:
Arrange the following periods of Telugu literature in chronological order:
A. Nannaya age
B. Tikkana age
C. Srinatha age
D. Prabandha or Rayala age
101.x: The Nannaya age belongs to the 11th century, followed by the Tikkana age in the 13th century, the Srinatha age in the 15th century and the Prabandha or Rayala age in the 16th century.
101.tq: Place the periods by their century markers, then verify the sequence from earliest to latest.
xs: Order: **Nannaya (11th c.) → Tikkana (13th c.) → Srinatha (15th c.) → Prabandha/Rayala (16th c.)** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The other orders misplace these centuries.
xa: **Shiva Kavi Yugam** (**1060-1260**) lies between the Nannaya and Tikkana ages.
**Errana age** (14th c.) sits between Tikkana and Srinatha.
After the Prabandha age: **Dakshinatya** (**17th-18th c.**) and **Modern** (**19th c.** onward).

101.s:
Consider the following statements about the periodisation of Telugu literature:
1. All period boundaries are precise and uniformly fixed.
2. The Shiva Kavi Yugam is assigned to 1060-1260.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
101.x: Statement 2 is correct: Shiva Kavi Yugam = 1060-1260. Statement 1 is wrong: apart from the Shiva Kavi Yugam and the Errana age, the boundaries are approximate. So 2 only.
101.tq: Only Shiva Kavi Yugam and Errana age have firm dates.
xs: **2 only** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 2 is correct: the **Shiva Kavi Yugam** = **1060-1260**.
Statement 1 is wrong: boundaries other than **Shiva Kavi Yugam** and **Errana age** are **approximate**.
xa: **Nannaya age** — **11th c.**; **Tikkana age** — **13th c.**; **Errana age** — **14th c.**
**Srinatha age** — **15th c.**; **Prabandha (Rayala) age** — **16th c.**
**Dakshinatya** (southern Nayaka) age — **17th-18th c.**

101.s:
Consider the following pairs of poets and titles:
1. Nannaya - Vaganusasana
2. Errana - Ubhayakavimitrudu
3. Errana - Sambhudasa
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
101.x: Pair 1 is correct: Vaganusasana is Nannaya's title. Pair 3 is correct: Sambhudasa is Errana's. Pair 2 is wrong: Ubhayakavimitrudu is Tikkana's title; Errana's other title is Prabandha Parameswara. So 1 and 3 only.
101.tq: Ubhayakavimitra / Kavibrahma = Tikkana.
xs: Pairs **1 and 3 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Pair 1: **Vaganusasana** is **Nannaya's** title; pair 3: **Sambhudasa** is **Errana's**.
Pair 2 is wrong: **Ubhayakavimitrudu** is **Tikkana's** title.
xa: Errana's other title: **Prabandha Parameswara**.
Nannaya: **Adikavi**, **Vagadheeshwara**, **Vidyadvaitudu**, **Shabda Shasanudu**.
Tikkana: **Kavibrahma**, **Kavijana Raja**.
⚠ **Srinatha, Potana and Nannechoda are NOT in the Kavitraya**.

101.s:
Consider the following statements about Tikkana's Mahabharata:
1. He called his rendering 'Prabandha Mandali'.
2. He translated the remaining 15 parvas, from Virata to Swargarohana.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
101.x: Statement 2 is correct: Tikkana did the 15 parvas from Virata to Swargarohana. Statement 1 is correct: he called it Prabandha Mandali. So both.
101.tq: Tikkana = 15 parvas = Prabandha Mandali.
xs: **Both 1 and 2** are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Tikkana** called his rendering **"Prabandha Mandali"**.
He translated the remaining **15 parvas**, **Virata to Swargarohana**.
xa: **Nannaya** did **Adi, Sabha** and part of **Aranya** (**142 padyas**).
**Errana** completed the rest of **Aranya Parva**, linking the other two.
Tikkana's philosophy: **Harihara Advaita** — Bharatam dedicated to **Hariharanatha**.
Tikkana's patron: Nellore Choda **Manumasiddhi II**.

101.s:
Consider the following statements about the patrons of the Kavitraya:
1. Errana was the court poet of Rajaraja Narendra at Rajamahendravaram.
2. Tikkana was at the court of the Nellore Choda Manumasiddhi II, in the Kakatiya era.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
101.x: Statement 2 is correct: Tikkana served Manumasiddhi II of Nellore. Statement 1 is wrong: Errana was the court poet of Prolaya Vema Reddi (capital Addanki); Rajaraja Narendra patronised Nannaya. So 2 only.
101.tq: Nannaya - Rajaraja Narendra; Tikkana - Manumasiddhi II; Errana - Prolaya Vema.
xs: **2 only** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 2 is correct: **Tikkana** was at the court of Nellore Choda **Manumasiddhi II**, in the **Kakatiya** era (**Ganapatideva**).
Statement 1 is wrong: **Errana** was court poet of **Prolaya Vema Reddi** (capital **Addanki**); **Rajaraja Narendra** patronised **Nannaya**.
xa: Nannaya's patron **Raja Raja Narendra** ruled **1018-1061 CE** at **Rajamahendravaram**.
Telugu Mahabharata took **three** eras: **Eastern Chalukya, Kakatiya, Reddi**.
Errana's **Harivamsam** was dedicated to **Prolaya Vema**.

101.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer.

List-I (Poet)
A. Nannaya
B. Tikkana
C. Errana

List-II (Title)
1. Adikavi
2. Kavibrahma
3. Prabandha Parameswara

A  B  C
101.x: Nannaya is associated with Adikavi, Tikkana with Kavibrahma, and Errana with Prabandha Parameswara.
101.tq: Start from the sure poet–title pairs and eliminate codes that reverse the assignments.
xs: **Nannaya — Adikavi**, **Tikkana — Kavibrahma**, **Errana — Prabandha Parameswara** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The other codes swap these titles among the three poets.
xa: Errana is also **Sambhudasa**.
Tikkana is also **Ubhayakavimitrudu** and **Kavijana Raja**.
Nannaya is also **Vaganusasana**, **Vagadheeshwara**, **Shabda Shasanudu**.

101.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Srinatha — Member of the Kavitraya
2. Potana — Member of the Kavitraya
3. Nannechoda — Member of the Kavitraya
Which of the pairs given above is/are correct?
101.x: Srinatha, Potana and Nannechoda are not members of the Kavitraya. The Kavitraya consists of Nannaya, Tikkana and Errana.
101.tq: Use the exclusion list to identify the option in which no confusable poet is correctly included.
xs: **None** of the pairs is correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
