xs: **Both Statement A and Statement B are true** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Mahmud** of Ghazni invaded India during **1000–1027**.
His were **repeated invasions** — **17 raids**, not systematic conquest.
xa: His main objective: **wealth** and **plunder**.
**Somnath** campaign: **1025–1026**, under Solanki **Bhima I**.
Mahmud's reign: **998-1030 CE**.
⚠ **Alptigin** = founder; **Sabuktigin** = real founder.

102.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Main objective of Mahmud Ghazni
(b) Mathura
(c) Thanesar
(d) Somnath

List-II
(i) Sacked in 1018 on the way to Kannauj
(ii) Wealth and plunder
(iii) Chakraswamin temple raided in 1014
(iv) Coastal temple of Gujarat raided in 1025–26
102.x: Mahmud's main aim was wealth and plunder. He raided Thanesar's Chakraswamin temple in 1014, sacked Mathura in 1018 on his march to Kannauj, and raided Somnath in Gujarat in 1025–26, giving a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv.
102.tq: Recall the year and setting of each Ghaznavid raid.
n: Mahmud Ghazni’s main objective was wealth and plunder. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 78-80]
Mahmud Ghazni attacked Mathura. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 78-80]
Mahmud Ghazni attacked Thanesar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 78-80]
Mahmud Ghazni attacked Somnath. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 78-80]
xs: The correct match is **a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Mahmud's **main objective** = **wealth and plunder**.
**Thanesar**, **Mathura** and **Kanauj** were raided in **1014-1018**; **Somnath** (Gujarat) in **1025–1026**.
xa: Somnath loot was said to be **20 million dinars**.
**Nagarkot** (Kangra) was raided for temple treasure (**1009**).
The **Hindushahis** (**Jayapala, Anandapala**) were the first to resist.

102.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Muhammad Ghori's Gujarat campaign
(b) Defeated Muhammad Ghori
(c) Naika Devi
(d) Mount Abu

List-II
(i) Queen mother who acted as regent
(ii) 1178
(iii) Mularaja-II
(iv) Area near which the battle of Kasahrada was fought
102.x: Ghori's Gujarat campaign came in 1178. The boy-king Mularaja II, with his mother Naika Devi as regent, defeated him at Kasahrada near Mount Abu, Ghori's first defeat in India, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv.
102.tq: Separate the year, the king, the regent and the place of Ghori's first defeat.
n: Muhammad Ghori’s Gujarat campaign occurred in 1178. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 78-80]
Muhammad Ghori was defeated in the Gujarat campaign by Mularaja-II/Bhimdev-II. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 78-80]
Naika Devi was associated with Muhammad Ghori’s Gujarat campaign. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 78-80]
Mount Abu was associated with Muhammad Ghori’s Gujarat campaign. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 78-80]
xs: The correct match is **a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Ghori's **Gujarat campaign** came in **1178**; he was **defeated** by **Mularaja-II / Bhimdev-II** — his **first defeat** in India.
**Naika Devi** acted as **regent**; the battle was near **Mount Abu** (**Kayadara**).
xa: Ghori's **first invasion**: **Multan**, **1175**, via the **Gomal Pass**.
⚠ Mahmud's Somnath raid hit **Bhima I**; Ghori was beaten by **Bhimdev II**.

102.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Bakhtiyar Khalji conquered Bihar during 1193–1203 as part of Ghurid expansion.
II. During the Bihar campaign, Bakhtiyar Khalji destroyed Nalanda and Vikramshila and captured Odantpur.
III. Bakhtiyar Khalji conquered Bengal during 1198–1203.
IV. During the Bengal campaign, he captured or entered Nadiya, Lakshman Sen fled to East Bengal, and Lakhnauti was captured.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
102.x: All four are correct: Bakhtiyar Khalji took Bihar (1193–1203) for the Ghurids, destroying Nalanda and Vikramshila and taking Odantapuri, then took Bengal, entering Nadiya, driving Lakshman Sen east and seizing Lakhnauti.
102.tq: Check each statement separately.
n: Bakhtiyar Khalji conquered Bihar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 76-78]
Bakhtiyar Khalji’s Bihar campaign occurred during 1193–1203. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 76-78]
Bakhtiyar Khalji’s Bihar campaign was part of Ghurid expansion. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 76-78]
Bakhtiyar Khalji destroyed Nalanda. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 76-78]
Bakhtiyar Khalji destroyed Vikramshila. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 76-78]
Bakhtiyar Khalji captured Odantpur. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 76-78]
Bakhtiyar Khalji conquered Bengal. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 76-78]
Bakhtiyar Khalji’s Bengal campaign occurred during 1198–1203. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 76-78]
Bakhtiyar Khalji captured or entered Nadiya. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 76-78]
Lakshman Sen fled to East Bengal during Bakhtiyar Khalji’s Bengal campaign. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 76-78]
Bakhtiyar Khalji captured Lakhnauti. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 76-78]
xs: All four — **I, II, III and IV** — are correct, so option **(3)** is correct.
**Bakhtiyar Khalji** conquered **Bihar** in **1193–1203** (Ghurid expansion), destroying **Nalanda** and **Vikramshila** and capturing **Odantpur**.
He conquered **Bengal** in **1198–1203**: entered **Nadiya**, **Lakshman Sen** fled to **East Bengal**, **Lakhnauti** was captured.
xa: He was the real **founder of Turk rule in Bihar** (BPSC **2022**).
⚠ Other notes say Lakshmana Sena was driven out of Nadia in **1204**.
He ruled from **Lakhnauti**.

102.s:
Assertion (A): Al-Biruni authored Kitab Patanjal.
Reason (R): Al-Biruni translated Patanjali's Yoga-Sutra into Arabic under the title Kitab Patanjal.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
102.x: Both are true and R explains A: Al-Biruni is credited with Kitab Patanjal because he translated Patanjali's Yoga-Sutra into Arabic under that title.
102.tq: Check whether R is the cause of A.
n: Kitab Patanjal was written by Al-Biruni. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 40-45]
Al-Biruni translated Patanjali's Yoga-Sutra into Arabic under the title Kitab Patanjal. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 40-45]
xs: **Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Al-Biruni** translated **Patanjali's Yoga-Sutra** into **Arabic** under the title **Kitab Patanjal** — which is why he is its author.
xa: He also wrote **Kitab-ul-Hind** (**Tahqiq-i-Hind**) on Indian society and culture.
It was translated into English by **Edward Sachau** and into Hindi by **Rajnikant Sharma**.
Al-Biruni belonged to **Mahmud Ghaznavi's** period.

102.s:
Match the poet or scholar with the correct identity or work:
List-I
(a) Firdausi
(b) Unsuri
(c) Al-Biruni
(d) Utbi

List-II
(i) Poet laureate (Malik-ush-Shuara) of Mahmud Ghaznavi's court
(ii) Shahnama; Homer of the East
(iii) Kitab-ul-Yamini
(iv) Kitab-ul-Hind
102.x: Firdausi wrote the Shahnama, Unsuri was poet laureate of Mahmud's court, Al-Biruni wrote Kitab-ul-Hind and Utbi wrote Kitab-ul-Yamini, giving a-ii, b-i, c-iv, d-iii.
102.tq: Match each Ghaznavid writer with his single best-known work or office.
n: Firdausi wrote Shahnama. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 112-113]
Firdausi was known as the Homer of the East. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 112-113]
Unsuri was a Persian poet. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 112-113]
Uzari was a Persian poet. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 112-113]
Asjadi was a court poet. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 112-113]
xs: The correct match is **a-ii, b-i, c-iv, d-iii** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Firdausi** — **Shahnama**, the **Homer of the East**; **Unsuri** — Persian **court poet** of Mahmud.
**Al-Biruni** — **Kitab-ul-Hind**; **Utbi** — **Kitab-ul-Yamini**.
xa: **Baihaqi** wrote **Tarikh-i-Subuktigin**.
Other court poets: **Uzari**, **Asjadi**, **Farrukhi**.
The Shahnama was commissioned by **Mahmud**.

102.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Scholar/Poet)
a. Asjadi
b. Al-Biruni
c. Utbi
d. Baihaqi

List-II (Identity and association)
i. Court poet associated with Mahmud Ghaznavi
ii. Scholar of Mahmud Ghaznavi's period; author of Kitab-ul-Hind
iii. Historian and scholar associated with Mahmud Ghaznavi; author of Kitab-ul-Yamini
iv. Historian and scholar associated with Mahmud Ghaznavi; author of Tarikh-i-Subuktigin
102.x: Asjadi was a court poet of Mahmud, Al-Biruni wrote Kitab-ul-Hind, Utbi wrote Kitab-ul-Yamini and Baihaqi wrote Tarikh-i-Subuktigin, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
102.tq: Recall the identity of each scholar.
n: Asjadi was a court poet. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 113-115]
Asjadi was associated with Mahmud Ghaznavi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 113-115]
Al-Biruni was a scholar and historian. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 113-115]
Utbi was a historian and scholar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 113-115]
Utbi was associated with Mahmud Ghaznavi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 113-115]
Baihaqi was a historian and scholar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 113-115]
Baihaqi was associated with Mahmud Ghaznavi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 113-115]
xs: The correct match is **a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Asjadi** — **court poet** of **Mahmud Ghaznavi**; **Al-Biruni** — **Kitab-ul-Hind**.
**Utbi** — **Kitab-ul-Yamini**; **Baihaqi** — **Tarikh-i-Subuktigin**.
xa: **Firdausi** — **Shahnama**, "Homer of the East".
Al-Biruni's **Kitab Patanjal** = Arabic translation of Patanjali's Yoga-Sutra.
**Chachnama** (conquest of Sindh) — Persian translation by **Muhammad Ali bin Abu Bakr Kufi**.

103.s: The rise of the Chauhans of Ajmer, Chandelas of Bundelkhand and Paramaras of Malwa is principally associated with the
103.x: These Rajput states rose after the collapse of the Pratihara Empire, which led to political fragmentation in North India.
103.tq: Direct cause-and-effect recall.
xs: The Rajput states rose from the **collapse of the Pratihara Empire** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Out of that collapse came the **Chauhans of Ajmer**, the **Chandelas of Bundelkhand** and the **Paramaras of Malwa**.
With the Pratiharas gone, **North India became hyper-fragmented** into rival Rajput kingdoms.
xa: The **Agnikula** clans claimed birth from a sacrificial fire at **Mount Abu**: **Paramara, Pratihara, Chauhan, Solanki**.
The **Solankis** (Chalukyas of Gujarat) ruled from **Anahilapataka (Patan)**, c. **950-1300**.
The **Tomaras** held **Dhillika (Delhi)** until ousted by the **Chauhans** in the mid-12th century.

103.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Chahamana — Sakambhari, Ajmer and Delhi
2. Paramara — Malwa, Ujjain and Dhar
3. Chandela — Bundelkhand, Khajuraho and Mahoba
4. Gahadavala — Kanauj and Varanasi
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
103.x: All four regional and capital associations are correct.
103.tq: Verify the region–capital associations systematically.
xs: All four pairs are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4** is the answer.
Pair 1: the **Chahamanas (Chauhans)** moved from **Sakambhari** to **Ajmer** and **Delhi**.
Pair 2: the **Paramaras** ruled **Malwa** from **Ujjain** and **Dhar**.
Pair 3: the **Chandelas** ruled **Bundelkhand** from **Khajuraho** and **Mahoba**; pair 4: the **Gahadavalas** held **Kanauj** and **Varanasi**.
xa: Founders: Chauhan **Vasudeva**, Paramara **Upendra (Krishnaraja)**, Chandela **Nannuka**, Gahadavala **Chandradeva**, Solanki **Mularaja I**.
Key rulers: Chauhan **Prithviraj III**, Paramara **Bhoja**, Chandela **Dhanga** and **Vidyadhara**, Gahadavala **Jaichand**.
The **Kalachuris (Chedi)** ruled from **Tripuri (Jabalpur)**; founder **Kokalla I**.

103.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
103.x: The Paramara dynasty was founded by Upendra, also known as Krishnaraja. Anangapala founded the Tomara dynasty.
103.tq: Detect the swapped founder among neighbouring Rajput dynasties.
xs: **Paramara — Anangapala** is the wrong pair — so option **(1)** is the answer.
The Paramaras were founded by **Upendra (Krishnaraja)**; **Anangapala** founded the **Tomara** dynasty of **Dhillika (Delhi)**.
The other pairs are correct: **Kalachuri — Kokalla I**, **Gahadavala — Chandradeva**, **Chandela — Nannuka**.
xa: Notes link Anangapala with the **Mehrauli Iron Pillar** — ⚠ the pillar is a **Gupta** work, only moved to Delhi.
Solanki founder **Mularaja I**; Chauhan founder **Vasudeva**.
The Tomaras were ousted by the **Chauhans** in the mid-12th century.

103.s:
Consider the following statements about the Tomaras:
1. They ruled from Dhillika (Delhi), and their coins carried a horseman-and-bull motif.
2. The Tomara ruler Anangapala cast the Mehrauli Iron Pillar when he founded Dhillika.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
103.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Tomaras held Dhillika in Haryana, with 'Shri Samanta-deva' horseman-and-bull coins. Statement 2 is wrong: the Iron Pillar is a Gupta work only moved to Delhi. So 1 only.
103.tq: Mehrauli pillar = Gupta, moved to Delhi.
xs: **1 only** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: the **Tomaras** ruled from **Dhillika (Delhi)**; their coins carried a **horseman-and-bull** motif ("Shri Samanta-deva").
Statement 2 is wrong: the **Mehrauli Iron Pillar** is a **Gupta** work, only moved to Delhi.
xa: Tomara founder: **Anangapala**.
The Tomaras were ousted by the **Chauhans** in the mid-12th c.
Chauhan capital: Sakambhari → **Ajmer**; key ruler **Prithviraj III**.

103.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding theories of Rajput origin and their proponents?
103.x: The foreign-origin theory, which associates the Rajputs with Scythians, Hunas and Gurjaras, was propounded by Col. James Tod and V.A. Smith. G.H. Ojha and C.V. Vaidya supported the Kshatriya-descent theory, while the Agnikula tradition is associated with Chand Bardai’s Prithviraj Raso.
103.tq: Start with the sure author–theory pair and eliminate the swapped proponents.
xs: The **foreign-origin theory** (Scythian, Huna, Gurjara) is credited to **Col. James Tod** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**V.A. Smith** also backed the foreign-origin view.
**G.H. Ojha** and **C.V. Vaidya** argued **Kshatriya (ancient Indian) descent**, not the Agnikula theory.
The **Agnikula** theory comes from **Chand Bardai's Prithviraj Raso**.
xa: Agnikula = birth from a sacrificial fire at **Mount Abu**; four clans: **Paramara, Pratihara, Chauhan, Solanki**.
⚠ Notes that call the **Chandelas** Agnikula are off the traditional list.
Origin theories and the **"Indian feudalism"** thesis are the main debates on Rajput history.

103.s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the traditional four Agnikula Rajput clans?
103.x: The traditional four Agnikula clans are Paramara, Pratihara, Chauhan and Solanki (Chalukya). Some sources wrongly add the Chandelas, who are off the traditional list.
103.tq: Agnikula four = Paramara, Pratihara, Chauhan, Solanki
xs: The **Chandela** dynasty is not one of the traditional four Agnikula clans — so option **(3)** is the answer.
The four are **Paramara**, **Pratihara**, **Chauhan** and **Solanki**.
⚠ Some notes call the Chandelas "Agnikula" along with the Paramaras — that is off the traditional list.
xa: The Chandelas, founded by **Nannuka**, ruled **Bundelkhand** from **Khajuraho** and **Mahoba**.
Chandela rulers: **Dhanga**, **Vidyadhara**, **Kirtivarman**, **Paramardi**.
The Agnikula story comes from **Chand Bardai's Prithviraj Raso**.

103.s:
Consider the following statements about the feudal structure of Rajput society:
1. Land grants carried revenue, judicial and police rights.
2. R.S. Sharma's 'Indian feudalism' includes sub-infeudation and vishti (forced labour).
3. Village economies were open and commercially integrated.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
103.x: Statement 1 is correct: land grants carried revenue, judicial and police rights. Statement 2 is correct: Sharma's model includes sub-infeudation and vishti. Statement 3 is wrong: the model speaks of closed village economies. Hence 1 and 2 only; '1 only' misses 2, and options with 3 are wrong.
103.tq: Sharma's feudalism = sub-infeudation + vishti + CLOSED village economy.
xs: Only statements 1 and 2 are correct — so option **(2) 1 and 2 only** is the answer.
Statement 1 is correct: **land grants** carried **revenue, judicial and police rights**.
Statement 2 is correct: **R.S. Sharma's "Indian feudalism"** includes **sub-infeudation** and **vishti** (forced labour).
Statement 3 is wrong: Sharma describes **closed village economies**, not open ones.
xa: The "Indian feudalism" thesis is one of the main **debates** on Rajput society, along with origin theories.
**Jauhar** (self-immolation to avoid capture) and **sati** were practised in Rajput society.

103.s: Rajput warfare generally placed emphasis on
103.x: Rajput warfare emphasised direct combat and personal valour, with chivalry and clan honour receiving great importance.
103.tq: Confusable strategy discrimination.
xs: Rajput warfare stressed **direct combat with emphasis on personal valour** — so option **(3)** is correct (APPSC-GS 2025 key).
⚠ It was **not guerrilla**, **naval war** or **gunpowder** warfare.
**Chivalry** and **clan honour** came first.
xa: **Jauhar**: self-immolation to avoid capture, e.g. **Rani Padmini** of Chittor against **Alauddin Khalji**.
Rajput **land grants** carried revenue, judicial and police rights.

103.s: Which of the following statements regarding women and Rajput customs is correct?
o: Sati was entirely unknown in Rajput society
Rani Padmini performed naval warfare against Alauddin Khalji
Jauhar meant the ritual coronation of a queen after victory
Jauhar involved self-immolation to avoid capture
103.x: Jauhar was self-immolation by women to avoid capture. Rani Padmini of Chittor is cited as an example in the conflict with Alauddin Khalji; sati was also practised.
103.tq: Distinguish closely related social practices through their exact meanings.
xs: **Jauhar** was **self-immolation to avoid capture** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Rani Padmini** of Chittor is the example, against **Alauddin Khalji** — she did not fight a naval war.
**Sati** was also practised, so option (1) is wrong; jauhar was no coronation rite.
xa: Rajput warfare: **direct combat**, **personal valour**, chivalry and clan honour.
**Chittorgarh** was the **Guhila/Gehlot (Sisodia)** stronghold of **Mewar**.

103.s: Who is the author of ‘Prithviraj Raso’?
103.x: ‘Prithviraj Raso’ was authored by Chand Bardai and is associated with Prithviraj Chauhan.
103.tq: Direct author–work recall.
xs: **Prithviraj Raso** was written by **Chand Bardai** (APPSC 2018) — so option **(2)** is correct.
It celebrates **Prithviraj Chauhan** and carries the **Agnikula** origin story.
**Somadeva** wrote the play **Lalit Vigraharaja**, **Narapati** wrote **Bisaldeva Raso** and **Jagnik** wrote **Alha Khand**.
xa: ⚠ **Bisaldeva Raso** = Narapati (Nalha); **Prithviraj Raso** = Chand Bardai; **Alha Khand** = Jagnik.
**Khuman Raso** = **Dalpati Vijay**; **Shatrusal Raso** = **Dungar Singh** (RPSC 2024).

103.s:
Consider the following statements about Rajput court literature:
1. Bisaldeva Raso, on Vigraharaja IV, was written by Chand Bardai.
2. Alha Khand, linked with the Chandela Paramardi, was written by Jagnik.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
103.x: Statement 2 is correct: Alha Khand = Jagnik. Statement 1 is wrong: Bisaldeva Raso is by Narapati (Nalha); Chand Bardai wrote Prithviraj Raso. So 2 only.
103.tq: Prithviraj Raso = Chand Bardai; Bisaldeva Raso = Narapati Nalha; Alha Khand = Jagnik.
xs: **2 only** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 2 is correct: **Alha Khand** was written by **Jagnik** (MPPSC **2025**).
Statement 1 is wrong: **Bisaldeva Raso** is by **Narapati (Nalha)** (RPSC **2024**); **Chand Bardai** wrote **Prithviraj Raso**.
xa: **Khuman Raso** = **Dalpati Vijay**; **Shatrusal Raso** = **Dungar Singh**.
Bhoja wrote **Saraswati-Kanthabharana** and **Yuktikalpataru**.
Prithviraj Raso by Chand Bardai: APPSC **2018**.

103.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
103.x: ‘Navasahasanka Charita’ was written by Padmagupta, not Someshvara. ‘Samarangana Sutradhara’ was written by Bhoja.
103.tq: Find the swapped author in a work–author pair.
xs: **Navasahasanka Charita — Someshvara** is wrong — so option **(4)** is the answer.
**Navasahasanka Charita** is by **Padmagupta (Parimala)** on Paramara **Sindhuraja**; **Someshvara** wrote **Kirtikaumudi**.
The rest are correct: **Samarangana Sutradhara** by **Bhoja**; **Khuman Raso** by **Dalpati Vijay**; **Shatrusal Raso** by **Dungar Singh**.
xa: **Kirtikaumudi** praises **Vastupala**, the Vaghela minister.
Bhoja's other works: **Saraswati-Kanthabharana** (poetics/grammar), **Yuktikalpataru**, **Rajamartanda**.

103.s:
Consider the following statements about Bhojshala at Dhar:
1. It is an ASI-protected centre of Sanskrit learning linked to Bhoja, with a Saraswati (Vagdevi) temple.
2. It was turned into a mosque in the 12th century.
3. Muslims call it the Kamal Maula Mosque.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
103.x: Statement 1 is correct: Bhojshala is an ASI-protected learning centre linked to Bhoja with a Saraswati (Vagdevi) temple. Statement 2 is wrong: it became a mosque in the 14th century. Statement 3 is correct: Muslims call it Kamal Maula Mosque. Hence 1 and 3 only; '1 only' misses 3, and options with 2 are wrong.
103.tq: Bhojshala: Bhoja (11th c.) built it, converted in the 14th c.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — so option **(3) 1 and 3 only** is the answer.
Statement 1 is correct: an **ASI-protected** centre of Sanskrit learning linked to **Bhoja**, with a **Saraswati (Vagdevi)** temple.
Statement 2 is wrong: it was turned into a mosque in the **14th century**, not the 12th.
Statement 3 is correct: Muslims call it the **Kamal Maula Mosque**.
xa: The **Madhya Pradesh High Court** declared Bhojshala a **Hindu temple** on ASI findings (**May 2026**).
The ASI survey was ordered in **2024**; under a **2003** ASI arrangement both communities worshipped on separate days.

103.s:
Consider the following statements about Paramara Bhoja:
1. Bhojpur near Bhopal is known for a Sun temple and the Rani-ki-Vav.
2. The Udaipur Prashasti gives the Paramara genealogy and praises Bhoja.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
103.x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Bhojpur has an unfinished Shiva temple with a huge linga and the Bhojpur lake; the Sun temple is at Modhera and Rani-ki-Vav at Patan (Solanki). So 2 only.
103.tq: Bhojpur = unfinished Shiva temple + lake.
xs: **2 only** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 2 is correct: the **Udaipur Prashasti** gives the **Paramara genealogy** and praises **Bhoja**.
Statement 1 is wrong: **Bhojpur** has an unfinished **Shiva temple** with a huge linga and **Bhojpur lake**.
The **Modhera Sun temple** and **Rani-ki-Vav** are **Solanki** works.
xa: ⚠ **Rani-ki-Vav** was built by queen **Udayamati** in memory of **Bhima I**.
**Bhojshala, Dhar** = Bhoja's Sanskrit learning centre, a **Saraswati (Vagdevi)** temple.
Paramara capital: **Dhara**.

103.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Vimal Vasahi, Dilwara — Vimal Shah, minister of Bhima I
2. Luna Vasahi, Dilwara — Vastupala and Tejapala
3. Rani-ki-Vav — built by the queen of Kumarapala in his memory
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
103.x: Pair 1 is correct: Vimal Shah, Bhima I's minister, built Vimal Vasahi (c. 1031). Pair 2 is correct: the Vaghela ministers Vastupala-Tejapala built Luna Vasahi (1230). Pair 3 is wrong: Rani-ki-Vav was built by Udayamati, queen of Bhima I, in his memory. Hence 1 and 2 only; '1 only' misses 2, and options with 3 are wrong.
103.tq: Bhima I links Modhera, Vimal Vasahi (his minister) and Rani-ki-Vav (his queen Udayamati).
xs: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct — so option **(2) 1 and 2 only** is the answer.
Pair 1 is correct: **Vimal Shah**, minister of **Bhima I**, built **Vimal Vasahi** (**c. 1031**).
Pair 2 is correct: the Vaghela ministers **Vastupala-Tejapala** built **Luna Vasahi** (**1230**).
Pair 3 is wrong: **Rani-ki-Vav** was built by queen **Udayamati** in memory of **Bhima I**, not Kumarapala.
xa: Rani-ki-Vav is a **UNESCO** site.
⚠ **Vimal Vasahi** = Vimal Shah (Solanki, Rishabha); **Luna Vasahi** = Vastupala-Tejapala (Vaghela, Neminatha).
**Mahmud** sacked **Somnath** in **1025** during Bhima I's reign.

103.s: Which one of the following statements about Somnath is correct?
o: It is a Vaishnava temple in Madhya Pradesh
It was rebuilt in the Chalukya era and is dedicated to Shiva as a jyotirlinga
Its present temple was completed in 1299 immediately after Khalji’s attack
The Old Somnath temple was built by Vimal Shah in 1031
103.x: Somnath is a Shiva temple and jyotirlinga in Gujarat. It was rebuilt in the Chalukya era, while the present temple was completed in 1951; Ahilyabai Holkar built the Old Somnath temple in 1783.
103.tq: Reject wrong dates and builders attached to a famous monument.
xs: Somnath **was rebuilt in the Chalukya era** and is dedicated to **Shiva as a jyotirlinga** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is in **Gujarat**, not Madhya Pradesh, and is Shaiva, not Vaishnava.
The present temple was **completed in 1951**; **1299** was **Khalji's** attack, after which **Mahipala I** rebuilt it.
"Old Somnath" was built by **Ahilyabai Holkar** in **1783**; **Vimal Shah** built **Vimal Vasahi** (c. 1031).
xa: Style: **Maru-Gurjara** (Chaulukya) — **Garbhagriha**, **Sabha Mandapa**, **Nritya Mandapa**.
Chalukya-era rebuilding: **Bhima I**, then **Kumarapala**.
**Mahmud** sacked Somnath in **1025**.

103.s:
Consider the following statements about the Solankis of Gujarat:
1. Mularaja I founded the dynasty with its capital at Anahilapataka (Patan).
2. Mahmud sacked Somnath in 1025 during the reign of Kumarapala.
3. Bhima I built the Modhera Sun temple.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
103.x: Statement 1 is correct: Mularaja I founded the line at Anahilapataka (Patan). Statement 2 is wrong: Somnath was sacked in 1025 under Bhima I; Kumarapala later rebuilt it. Statement 3 is correct: Bhima I built the Modhera Sun temple. Hence 1 and 3 only; '1 only' misses 3, and options with 2 are wrong.
103.tq: Bhima I suffered Mahmud's raid (1025); Kumarapala rebuilt Somnath.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — so option **(3) 1 and 3 only** is the answer.
Statement 1 is correct: **Mularaja I** founded the Solankis with capital **Anahilapataka (Patan)**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Mahmud** sacked Somnath in **1025** under **Bhima I**, not Kumarapala.
Statement 3 is correct: **Bhima I** built the **Modhera Sun temple** (Surya).
xa: Bhima I's queen **Udayamati** built **Rani-ki-Vav** (UNESCO) in his memory.
Later Solankis: **Jayasimha Siddharaja** (patron of **Hemachandra**), **Kumarapala** (Jainism).
The Solankis ruled c. **950-1300**.

103.s: Which ruler is correctly matched with the Sahasralinga tank at Patan and patronage of Hemachandra?
103.x: Jayasimha Siddharaja patronised the Jain scholar Hemachandra and is associated with the Sahasralinga tank at Patan.
103.tq: Separate the contributions of successive Solanki rulers.
xs: **Jayasimha Siddharaja** patronised **Hemachandra** and built the **Sahasralinga tank** at Patan — so option **(3)** is correct.
Hemachandra wrote the **Siddha-Hema** grammar under him.
**Mularaja I** founded the dynasty; **Bhima I** built **Modhera**; **Kumarapala** took up **Jainism** under Hemachandra.
xa: Kumarapala **curbed animal slaughter** and rebuilt **Somnath**.
The Solankis were **Shaivas** who also patronised **Jainism**.

103.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Kumarapala encouraged Jainism under the influence of Hemachandra.
2. Kumarapala rebuilt Somnath.
3. Kumarapala curbed animal slaughter.
4. The Solankis were exclusively Buddhist rulers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
103.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The Solankis were Shaivas who also patronised Jainism, not exclusively Buddhist rulers.
103.tq: Identify the extreme and religiously swapped statement.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct — so option **(2) 1, 2 and 3 only** is the answer.
1: **Kumarapala** encouraged **Jainism** under **Hemachandra**; 2: he rebuilt **Somnath** after Bhima I.
3: he **curbed animal slaughter**.
4 is wrong: the Solankis were **Shaivas** who also patronised **Jainism**, not Buddhists.
xa: **Jayasimha Siddharaja** was Hemachandra's earlier patron (**Siddha-Hema** grammar).
Somnath was sacked by **Mahmud** in **1025** under **Bhima I**.

103.s:
Consider the following statements about Khajuraho:
1. The Kandariya Mahadeva temple there is dedicated to Vishnu.
2. The Khajuraho group of temples, built by the Chandelas, is in Madhya Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
103.x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Kandariya Mahadeva (by Vidyadhara) is a Shiva temple; the Lakshmana temple is Vishnu's. So 2 only.
103.tq: Kandariya Mahadeva = Shiva.
xs: **2 only** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 2 is correct: the **Khajuraho group** (UNESCO) was built by the **Chandelas**, **Madhya Pradesh**.
Statement 1 is wrong: **Kandariya Mahadeva** (by **Vidyadhara**) is a **Shiva** temple; **Lakshmana** is Vishnu's.
xa: Khajuraho also has **Jain** temples.
Chandela region: **Bundelkhand** (**Jejakabhukti**), Khajuraho and Mahoba.
Chandela rulers to know: **Dhanga**, **Vidyadhara**, Kirtivarman, **Paramardi**.

103.s: Which one of the following descriptions correctly refers to the Latina or Rekha-prasada type of Nagara temple tower?
o: A pyramidal tower with multiple terraces
103.x: Latina, also called Rekha-prasada, is characterised by a single curvilinear tower. Phamsana has a sloping, stepped roof, while Valabhi is barrel-vaulted.
103.tq: Separate the three Nagara tower forms by their distinctive roof profiles.
xs: **Latina / Rekha-prasada** is a **single curvilinear tower** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Phamsana** has a **sloping, stepped roof**; **Valabhi** is **barrel-vaulted**.
xa: Regional Nagara schools: **Khajuraho** (Chandela), **Odisha/Kalinga** (**rekha deul**), **Maru-Gurjara** (Solanki).
**Maru-Gurjara** often has a **Kirti-torana**.

103.s:
With reference to the Maru-Gurjara style, consider the following statements:
1. It is associated with the Solanki tradition.
2. It developed in the Gujarat-Rajasthan region.
3. It belongs broadly to the period from the eleventh to the thirteenth century.
4. It represents a fusion of the Maha-Maru and Maha-Gurjara traditions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
103.x: All four statements are correct. Maru-Gurjara is a Solanki-associated Nagara sub-style of Gujarat and Rajasthan, broadly dated to the eleventh–thirteenth centuries, and combines the Maha-Maru and Maha-Gurjara traditions.
103.tq: Check the dynasty, region, period and stylistic derivation as separate components of one architectural identification.
xs: All four statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4** is the answer.
**Maru-Gurjara** is the **Solanki** style of **Gujarat-Rajasthan**, of the **11th-13th c.**
It is a Nagara sub-style fusing **Maha-Maru** and **Maha-Gurjara**.
xa: It often has a **Kirti-torana**.
**Somnath** is in **Maru-Gurjara** (Chaulukya) style: **Garbhagriha**, **Sabha Mandapa**, **Nritya Mandapa**.
Other schools: **Khajuraho** (Chandela) and **Odisha/Kalinga** (**rekha deul**).

103.s: Which architectural feature is often associated with the Maru-Gurjara sub-style?
103.x: The Maru-Gurjara style, associated with the Solanki tradition of Gujarat and Rajasthan, often includes a Kirti-torana.
103.tq: Identify the specific architectural feature attached to the regional style, not merely its geographical location.
xs: The Maru-Gurjara sub-style often has a **Kirti-torana** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Rekha deul** belongs to the **Odisha/Kalinga** school; **Valabhi** is just a barrel-vaulted tower type.
xa: Maru-Gurjara = **Solanki**, **Gujarat-Rajasthan**, **11th-13th c.**, fusing **Maha-Maru** + **Maha-Gurjara**.
Shikhara types: **Latina** (single curvilinear), **Phamsana** (sloping, stepped), **Valabhi** (barrel-vaulted).

103.s: The Vijaya Stambha at Chittor was built by Rana Kumbha to commemorate his victory over
103.x: Rana Kumbha built the Vijaya Stambha at Chittor to commemorate his victory over Mahmud Khalji of Malwa.
103.tq: Separate the builder from the opponent associated with the monument.
xs: Rana Kumbha built the **Vijaya Stambha** at Chittor for his victory over **Mahmud Khalji of Malwa** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The builder Rana Kumbha is an APPSC G2 **2011** question.
⚠ **Alauddin Khalji** of Delhi is the **Rani Padmini** jauhar story, not this tower.
xa: ⚠ **Vijaya Stambha** = Rana Kumbha; **Kirti Stambha** = Jain merchant **Jijaji**.
Rana Kumbha also built **Kumbhalgarh** fort.

103.s:
Consider the following statements about Rajput monuments:
1. Kumbhalgarh fort was built by Rana Kumbha.
2. The Kirti Stambha at Chittor was built by the Jain merchant Jijaji in the 12th century.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
103.x: Statement 2 is correct: Kirti Stambha = Jijaji (Jeeja). Statement 1 is correct: Rana Kumbha built Kumbhalgarh (and the Vijaya Stambha). So both.
103.tq: Vijaya Stambha = Rana Kumbha; Kirti Stambha = Jijaji.
xs: **Both 1 and 2** are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Kumbhalgarh** fort was built by **Rana Kumbha**.
**Kirti Stambha**, Chittor, was built by Jain merchant **Jijaji (Jeeja)**, **12th c.**
xa: ⚠ **Vijaya Stambha** = **Rana Kumbha** (APPSC G2 **2011**); **Kirti Stambha** = **Jijaji**.
**Chittorgarh** = Guhila/Gehlot (Sisodia) stronghold of **Mewar**.
**Jauhar**: **Rani Padmini** of Chittor vs **Alauddin Khalji**.

103.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Bhojshala:
1. The Madhya Pradesh High Court declared Bhojshala a Hindu temple on the strength of Archaeological Survey of India findings.
2. The ASI survey of Bhojshala was ordered in 2024.
3. Under a 2003 ASI arrangement, members of both communities worshipped there on separate days.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
103.x: All three statements are correct. The Madhya Pradesh High Court relied on ASI findings in declaring Bhojshala a Hindu temple; the survey was ordered in 2024, while the 2003 arrangement provided for worship by the two communities on separate days.
103.tq: Combine judicial finding, survey year and administrative arrangement without confusing their sequence.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is the answer.
1: the **Madhya Pradesh High Court** declared Bhojshala a **Hindu temple** on **ASI findings** (**May 2026**).
2: the ASI survey was ordered in **2024**.
3: under a **2003** ASI arrangement both communities worshipped on **separate days**.
xa: Bhojshala at **Dhar** has a **Saraswati (Vagdevi)** temple and was linked to **Bhoja**.
It was turned into a mosque in the **14th century**; Muslims call it **Kamal Maula Mosque**.

103.s: Modhera, site of the Solanki Sun temple, is in the news because it:
o: Was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2022
Was fully solarised under an MNRE scheme, inaugurated on 9 October 2022
Was declared a Hindu temple by the Gujarat High Court
Became the site of the Somnath Swabhiman Parv
103.x: Modhera was fully solarised under an MNRE scheme (6 MW plant with 15 MWh storage), inaugurated on 9 October 2022. The court ruling on a temple concerned Bhojshala (MP High Court); Somnath Swabhiman Parv concerns Somnath; there was no 2022 UNESCO listing for Modhera.
103.tq: Modhera = solar village, 9 Oct 2022
xs: Modhera was **fully solarised under an MNRE scheme**, inaugurated **9 October 2022** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The project: a **6 MW** plant with **15 MWh** storage, costing **₹76.66 crore**.
The court ruling was on **Bhojshala** by the **Madhya Pradesh High Court**, not Gujarat.
xa: The **Modhera Sun temple** (Surya) was built by Solanki **Bhima I**, in Mehsana, Gujarat.
⚠ The Solanki UNESCO site in the notes is **Rani-ki-Vav**, built by queen **Udayamati**.

103.s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Harshavardhana shifted the capital from Thaneshwar to Kannauj.
Statement B: The Later Cholas shifted their capital from Tanjore to Gangaikondacholapuram.
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
103.x: Both are true: Harshavardhana moved his capital from Thaneshwar to Kannauj, and Rajendra Chola moved the Chola capital from Tanjore to Gangaikondacholapuram.
103.tq: Check each capital shift separately.
n: Harshavardhana shifted the capital from Thaneshwar to Kannauj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 51-53]
The Later Cholas shifted their capital from Tanjore to Gangaikondacholapuram. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 51-53]
Harshavardhana made Kannauj his capital. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 51-53]
xs: **Both Statement A and Statement B are true** — so option **(1)** is correct.
A: **Harshavardhana** shifted his capital from **Thaneshwar** to **Kannauj**.
B: the **Later Cholas** shifted from **Tanjore** to **Gangaikondacholapuram**, their imperial capital.
xa: **Guptas**: **Pataliputra**; **Chandragupta II** made **Ujjain** important.
**Gurjara-Pratiharas**: **Kannauj**.
**Senas**: **Nadia** (Nabadwip).

103.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Gurjara-Pratihara
(b) Paramara
(c) Solanki / Gujarat Chalukya
(d) Kalachuri

List-II
(i) Dhara
(ii) Kannauj
(iii) Tripuri
(iv) Anhilwada
103.x: The Gurjara-Pratiharas ruled from Kannauj, the Paramaras from Dhara, the Solankis from Anhilwada and the Kalachuris from Tripuri, giving a-ii, b-i, c-iv, d-iii.
103.tq: Recall the capital of each Rajput dynasty.
n: The Gurjara-Pratihara capital was Kannauj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 51-53]
The Paramara capital was Dhara. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 51-53]
The Solanki kingdom had Anhilwada as its capital. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 51-53]
The Solanki kingdom was also called the Gujarat Chalukya kingdom. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 51-53]
The Kalachuri capital was Tripuri. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 51-53]
xs: The correct match is **a-ii, b-i, c-iv, d-iii** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Gurjara-Pratihara** — **Kannauj**; **Paramara** — **Dhara**.
**Solanki / Gujarat Chalukya** — **Anhilwada**; **Kalachuri** — **Tripuri**.
xa: Solanki founder **Mularaja I**; capital also **Anahilapataka (Patan)**.
**Chandelas** — **Khajuraho** region; **Bundelkhand**.
Rajput states rose from the collapse of the **Pratihara** empire.

103.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Pallava
(b) Badami Chalukya
(c) Eastern Chalukya
(d) Chola

List-II
(i) Vengi
(ii) Kanchipuram
(iii) Tanjore
(iv) Vatapi
103.x: The Pallavas ruled from Kanchipuram, the Badami Chalukyas from Vatapi, the Eastern Chalukyas from Vengi and the Cholas from Tanjore, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.
103.tq: Recall the capital of each southern dynasty.
n: The Pallava capital was Kanchipuram. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 51-53]
The Badami Chalukya capital was Vatapi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 51-53]
The Eastern Chalukya capital was Vengi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 51-53]
The Chola capital was Tanjore. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 51-53]
Vatapi was also called Badami. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 51-53]
xs: The correct match is **a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Pallava** — **Kanchipuram**; **Badami Chalukya** — **Vatapi**.
**Eastern Chalukya** — **Vengi**; **Chola** — **Tanjore**.
xa: **Kalyani Chalukyas** — **Kalyani**.
Later Cholas moved to **Gangaikondacholapuram**.
**Harshavardhana** moved from **Thaneshwar** to **Kannauj**.

104.s: Which pair is NOT correctly matched?
104.x: Kitab-ul-Hind was written by Al-Biruni, not Firdausi. The other three source-author pairs are correctly matched.
104.tq: Find the swapped author in a list of medieval sources.
xs: **Kitab-ul-Hind — Firdausi** is wrong — so option **(2)** is the answer.
**Kitab-ul-Hind (Tahqiq-i-Hind)** was written in Arabic by **Al-Biruni**; **Firdausi** wrote the **Shahnama**.
The rest are correct: **Prithviraj Raso** by **Chand Bardai**, **Tabaqat-i-Nasiri** by **Minhaj-us-Siraj**, **Taj-ul-Maasir** by **Hasan Nizami**.
xa: ⚠ **Mahmud of Ghazni** patronised **Al-Biruni**, **Firdausi** and **Utbi** — all three, so they are easily mixed up.
**Utbi**, Mahmud's court historian, wrote **Kitab-ul-Yamini**.
⚠ **Prithviraj Raso** = Chand Bardai; **Prithviraja Vijaya** = **Jayanaka**.

104.s:
Consider the following statements regarding medieval Persian chronicles:
1. Taj-ul-Maasir was written by Hasan Nizami and relates to the early Sultanate.
2. Hasan Nizami was patronised by Qutbuddin Aibak.
3. Tabaqat-i-Nasiri was dedicated to Nasiruddin Mahmud.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
104.x: All three statements are correct. Hasan Nizami wrote Taj-ul-Maasir on the early Sultanate under the patronage of Qutbuddin Aibak, and Minhaj-us-Siraj dedicated Tabaqat-i-Nasiri to Nasiruddin Mahmud.
104.tq: Combine author, patron and dedication facts while checking whether all statements belong to the same source cluster.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is the answer.
1: **Taj-ul-Maasir** by **Hasan Nizami** covers the **early Sultanate**.
2: Hasan Nizami was patronised by **Qutbuddin Aibak**.
3: **Minhaj-us-Siraj** dedicated **Tabaqat-i-Nasiri** to **Nasiruddin Mahmud**.
xa: Tabaqat-i-Nasiri covers the **Ghurids** and early **Delhi Sultans**.
Chronological order: **Kitab-ul-Hind** → **Taj-ul-Maasir** → **Tabaqat-i-Nasiri** → **Futuh-us-Salatin** → **Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi**.

104.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi — Yahiya bin Ahmad Sarhindi
104.x: Tabaqat-i-Akbari was written by Nizamuddin Ahmad. Badauni’s own historical work was Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh.
104.tq: Find the wrong author–work pairing, especially where a neighbouring historian is substituted.
xs: **Tabaqat-i-Akbari — Badauni** is wrong — so option **(4)** is the answer.
**Tabaqat-i-Akbari** was written by **Nizamuddin Ahmad**; ⚠ some notes wrongly credit Badauni.
**Badauni's** own history is **Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh**.
The rest are correct: **Ziauddin Barani** wrote both **Fatawa-i-Jahandari** and **Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi**; **Sarhindi** wrote **Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi**.
xa: Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi is the main account of **Alauddin's market regulations**.
Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi was written under the **Sayyid** Sultan **Mubarak Shah**.

104.s: Fatawa-i-Jahandari is primarily a work on which subject?
o: The postal system of the Delhi Sultanate
104.x: Fatawa-i-Jahandari, written by Ziauddin Barani, deals with political theory and kingship.
104.tq: Identify the subject of a text rather than confusing it with the author’s historical chronicle.
xs: **Fatawa-i-Jahandari** deals with the **political theory of kingship** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Its author is **Ziauddin Barani**, who wrote from an **orthodox Sunni** viewpoint.
The postal system is in **Ibn Battuta's Rihla**; Golconda's conquest in **Khafi Khan's Muntakhab-ul-Lubab**; astronomy in **Al-Biruni**.
xa: Barani also wrote **Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi** (Balban to early Firoz Tughlaq).
Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi is the main account of **Alauddin's market regulations and ordinances**.

104.s:
Arrange the following works in chronological order of the periods they primarily cover:
A. Tabaqat-i-Akbari
B. Taj-ul-Maasir
C. Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi
D. Tabaqat-i-Nasiri
104.x: Taj-ul-Maasir belongs to the early Sultanate, followed by Tabaqat-i-Nasiri, Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi and finally Tabaqat-i-Akbari up to Akbar’s reign.
104.tq: Place the earliest and latest works first, then distinguish the two intervening Sultanate chronicles.
xs: The order is **B, D, C, A** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Taj-ul-Maasir** (early Sultanate, Aibak) → **Tabaqat-i-Nasiri** (Ghurids, early Sultans, Nasiruddin Mahmud).
→ **Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi** (Balban to early Firoz Tughlaq) → **Tabaqat-i-Akbari** (up to Akbar).
xa: The earliest work in the list is **Al-Biruni's Kitab-ul-Hind** (c. **1030** CE).
**Futuh-us-Salatin** (Isami, c. **1350**) sits between Tabaqat-i-Nasiri and Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi.
**Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi** (Sayyid period) comes just before Tabaqat-i-Akbari.

104.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding Amir Khusrau?
o: He wrote Kitab-ul-Yamini as court historian of Mahmud of Ghazni.
He wrote Rihla in Arabic after visiting Muhammad bin Tughlaq’s court.
He wrote Shahnama under the patronage of Akbar.
He wrote Khazain-ul-Futuh and accompanied Malik Kafur’s 1310 invasion of Warangal.
104.x: Amir Khusrau, court poet of Alauddin Khalji, wrote Khazain-ul-Futuh and accompanied Malik Kafur’s 1310 expedition to Warangal. Kitab-ul-Yamini was written by Utbi, Shahnama by Firdausi and Rihla by Ibn Battuta.
104.tq: Apply the author–ruler–work trap to distinguish famous medieval writers.
xs: Amir Khusrau **wrote Khazain-ul-Futuh and accompanied Malik Kafur's 1310 invasion of Warangal** — so option **(4)** is correct.
He was the **court poet of Alauddin Khalji**; Khazain-ul-Futuh describes 14th-century **Deccan** conditions.
**Kitab-ul-Yamini** is **Utbi's**, **Rihla** is **Ibn Battuta's**, **Shahnama** is **Firdausi's**.
xa: ⚠ As a court poet his history glorifies the patron — the **court bias** problem.
Muslim sources (**Amir Khusrau**, **Wassaf**) count **5** Warangal invasions; Telugu sources count **8**.

104.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Source)
A. Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi
B. Khazain-ul-Futuh
C. Futuh-us-Salatin

List-II (Author)
I. Isami
II. Amir Khusrau
III. Ziauddin Barani

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
104.x: Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi was written by Ziauddin Barani, Khazain-ul-Futuh by Amir Khusrau, and Futuh-us-Salatin by Isami.
104.tq: Start from the sure author–work pair and eliminate the remaining codes.
xs: The correct code is **A-III, B-II, C-I** — so option **(1)** is the answer.
**Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi** — **Ziauddin Barani**; **Khazain-ul-Futuh** — **Amir Khusrau**.
**Futuh-us-Salatin** — **Isami**, written at the **Bahmani court c. 1350**.
xa: Barani also wrote **Fatawa-i-Jahandari** on the theory of kingship.
Amir Khusrau went with **Malik Kafur's 1310** invasion of **Warangal**.

104.s: Madhura Vijayam provides information chiefly about which of the following?
o: Kampana’s conquest of Madurai and conditions under Tughlaq rule
The conquest of Golconda by Aurangzeb
The life of Pala king Ramapala
104.x: Madhura Vijayam, written by Gangadevi, describes Kampana’s conquest of Madurai and conditions under Tughlaq rule.
104.tq: Associate the regional biography with its protagonist, campaign and political context.
xs: **Madhura Vijayam** describes **Kampana's conquest of Madurai and conditions under Tughlaq rule** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was written by **Gangadevi**.
Golconda's conquest is in **Muntakhab-ul-Lubab**; Ramapala in **Ramacharitam**; Kashmir in **Rajatarangini**.
xa: **Kumara Ramana Charitam** (Kannada) covers **South India after the fall of Warangal**.
**Siddhesvara Charitam** (Telugu, **Kase Siddhappa**) covers **Kakatiya-era society and religion**.

104.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Tarikh-i-Firishta — Muhammad Qasim Firishta — Deccan history
Hadikat-us-Salatin — Ali bin Tahir Bustani — Qutb Shahis
Kumara Ramana Charitam — Kannada — South India after the fall of Warangal
104.x: Muntakhab-ul-Lubab was written by Khafi Khan and deals with Aurangzeb’s conquest of Golconda. Gangadevi wrote Madhura Vijayam.
104.tq: Detect the swapped author in a list of regional and Deccan sources.
xs: **Muntakhab-ul-Lubab — Gangadevi — conquest of Madurai** is wrong — so option **(3)** is the answer.
**Muntakhab-ul-Lubab** was written by **Khafi Khan** on **Aurangzeb's conquest of Golconda**.
**Gangadevi** wrote **Madhura Vijayam** on **Kampana's** conquest of Madurai.
The other three are correct: **Firishta** on the **Deccan**, **Bustani** on the **Qutb Shahis**, **Kumara Ramana Charitam** (Kannada) on post-Warangal South India.
xa: Other Qutb Shahi sources: **Tarikh Muhammad Qutb Shah** (anonymous, **1617**), **Basatin-us-Salatin** (**Mirza Ibrahim Zuberi**).
Modern work: **H.K. Sherwani's** History of the Qutb Shahi Dynasty.

104.s:
Consider the following statements about Muhammad Qasim Firishta and his work:
1. His Tarikh-i-Firishta is also known as Gulshan-i-Ibrahimi.
2. He dedicated his work to Ibrahim Qutb Shah of Golconda.
3. He was born at Astarabad in Iran in 1552.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
104.x: Statement 1 is correct: Tarikh-i-Firishta is also called Gulshan-i-Ibrahimi. Statement 2 is wrong: it was dedicated to Ibrahim Adil Shah of Bijapur, not a Qutb Shahi ruler. Statement 3 is correct: Firishta was born at Astarabad, Iran, in 1552. So '1 and 3 only' is right; options with 2 are wrong and '1 and 2 only' omits a true statement.
104.tq: Gulshan-i-IBRAHIMI = Ibrahim ADIL Shah of Bijapur; don't fall for the Qutb Shahi swap.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — so option **(2) 1 and 3 only** is the answer.
1 is correct: **Tarikh-i-Firishta** is also called **Gulshan-i-Ibrahimi**.
2 is wrong: it was dedicated to **Ibrahim Adil Shah of Bijapur**, not a Qutb Shahi.
3 is correct: Firishta was born at **Astarabad, Iran, in 1552**.
xa: Firishta calls **Telangana "Tilang"**.
⚠ His story of **Deva Raya kidnapping Nehal** is rejected by modern historians.
AP angle: **Isami** and **Firishta** → **Warangal**.

104.s: Which one of the following statements about Al-Biruni is correct?
o: He confined his study of India exclusively to military campaigns.
He wrote in Persian without learning any Indian language.
He was patronised by Deva Raya II of Vijayanagara.
He wrote in Arabic after learning Sanskrit and studied Indian religion, philosophy, astronomy and caste.
104.x: Al-Biruni learned Sanskrit and wrote in Arabic on Indian religion, philosophy, astronomy and the caste system. He was associated with Mahmud of Ghazni, not Vijayanagara.
104.tq: Use the language, subjects and patron together to identify the correct biographical statement.
xs: Al-Biruni **wrote in Arabic after learning Sanskrit** and studied **religion, philosophy, astronomy and caste** — so option **(4)** is correct.
His work is **Kitab-ul-Hind / Tahqiq-i-Hind** on **Indian sciences and society**, not just military campaigns.
His patron was **Mahmud of Ghazni**; **Deva Raya II** received **Abdur Razzaq**.
xa: He records **Diwali** on **Kartika Amavasya**.
He found Indians **unwilling to share learning with outsiders**.

104.s: According to Al-Biruni’s account, which of the following was observed on Kartika Amavasya?
o: The conquest of Madurai by Kampana
The coronation of Muhammad bin Tughlaq
The annual court of the Qutb Shahis
104.x: Al-Biruni recorded the celebration of Diwali on Kartika Amavasya.
104.tq: Match the festival and its calendrical occasion with the appropriate chronicler.
xs: Al-Biruni records **the celebration of Diwali** on **Kartika Amavasya** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Kampana's** Madurai conquest is in **Gangadevi's Madhura Vijayam**, not Al-Biruni.
xa: Vision PT365 cites **Al-Biruni**, **Nicolo Conti** and **Ain-i-Akbari** as early evidence of Diwali (UNESCO topic, **Apr 2026**).
**Nicolo Conti** described **"innumerable oil lamps"** at Diwali in Vijayanagara.

104.s: Al-Biruni, who came to India with Mahmud of Ghazni, was a native of:
104.x: Al-Biruni came from Khwarazm in Central Asia, in present Uzbekistan. Tangiers was Ibn Battuta's birthplace, Balkh was Mahmud Wali Balkhi's home, and Astarabad was Firishta's birthplace.
104.tq: Al-Biruni = Khwarazm (Uzbekistan)
xs: Al-Biruni was from **Khwarazm in Central Asia (present Uzbekistan)** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Tangiers (Morocco)** was **Ibn Battuta's** birthplace; **Balkh** was **Mahmud Wali Balkhi's** home; **Astarabad** was **Firishta's**.
xa: He came with **Mahmud of Ghazni** in the **11th century**.
Mahmud's other protégés: **Firdausi** and **Utbi**.

104.s: Rihla, the travel account of Ibn Battuta, was written in which language?
104.x: Ibn Battuta’s travel account, Rihla, was written in Arabic.
104.tq: Test the exact language of a source rather than its author’s place of origin.
xs: **Rihla** was written in **Arabic** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Ibn Battuta** was from **Morocco**, born at **Tangiers** in **1304**.
xa: He served **Muhammad bin Tughlaq**, who made him **qazi of Delhi** and sent him as **envoy to China**.
Rihla describes **espionage**, the **postal system**, **sati** and **slave markets**.
⚠ **Al-Biruni's Kitab-ul-Hind** is also in Arabic.

104.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Ibn Battuta — Morocco — Muhammad bin Tughlaq
Abdur Razzaq — Portugal — Deva Raya II
104.x: Ibn Battuta was from Morocco and visited the court of Muhammad bin Tughlaq. Marco Polo was from Venice, Abdur Razzaq from Persia and Duarte Barbosa from Portugal.
104.tq: Begin with the country–traveller pair and verify the ruler visited.
xs: **Ibn Battuta — Morocco — Muhammad bin Tughlaq** is correct — so option **(1)** is the answer.
**Marco Polo** was from **Venice (Italy)**, not France — **Tavernier** was French.
**Abdur Razzaq** was from **Persia**, a Timurid envoy of **Shah Rukh**.
xa: Other traveller-country pairs: **Afanasy Nikitin** — **Russia**; **Seydi Ali Reis** — **Turkey**; **Mahmud Wali Balkhi** — **Balkh (Afghanistan)**.
Ibn Battuta was made **qazi of Delhi** and sent as **envoy to China**.

104.s: Which traveller is associated with observations on espionage, the postal system, sati and slave markets in the Delhi Sultanate?
104.x: Ibn Battuta’s account of Muhammad bin Tughlaq’s reign contains observations on espionage, the postal system, sati and slave markets.
104.tq: Match the distinctive subject described with the traveller who recorded it.
xs: **Ibn Battuta**, in his **Rihla**, describes **espionage**, the **postal system**, **sati** and **slave markets** — so option **(3)** is correct.
He served **Muhammad bin Tughlaq** as **qazi of Delhi**.
**Tavernier** wrote on **Golconda diamonds**; **Nicolo Conti** on **Diwali lamps** in Vijayanagara.
xa: Rihla is in **Arabic**; Ibn Battuta was born at **Tangiers** in **1304**.
⚠ "Who mentioned sati" at Vijayanagara = **Abdur Razzaq**.

104.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Nicolo Conti was a traveller from Venice.
2. He described innumerable oil lamps at Diwali in Vijayanagara.
3. The APPSC-associated account places him at the court of Deva Raya II.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
104.x: All three statements are correct. Nicolo Conti was a Venetian who described the innumerable oil lamps at Diwali in Vijayanagara. Some sources place him at the end of Deva Raya I's reign, but the APPSC 2011 key placed this Italian traveller in Deva Raya II's reign.
104.tq: Combine origin, court and distinctive observation to identify one traveller precisely.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is the answer.
1: **Nicolo Conti** was from **Venice (Italy)**.
2: he described **"innumerable oil lamps"** at **Diwali** in Vijayanagara.
3: the **APPSC 2011** key places this Italian traveller in **Deva Raya II's** reign.
xa: ⚠ Notes place Conti at the end of **Deva Raya I's** reign — follow the key's version in APPSC.
⚠ Two Venetians: **Marco Polo** → Kakatiyas; **Nicolo Conti** → Vijayanagara.

104.s: Abdur Razzaq visited Vijayanagara in 1443–44 as an envoy sent by which ruler?
104.x: Abdur Razzaq was a Persian envoy of Shah Rukh and visited the court of Deva Raya II in 1443–44.
104.tq: Distinguish the envoy’s sending ruler from the ruler whose court he visited.
xs: **Abdur Razzaq** was the Timurid envoy of **Shah Rukh of Persia** — so option **(1)** is correct.
He visited **Deva Raya II** at Vijayanagara in **1443-44**.
**Ibrahim Adil Shah** was **Firishta's** patron; **Muhammad Qutb Shah** received **Mir Zainul Abidin** (**1614**).
xa: He called Vijayanagara among the **largest, richest cities**, with **diamonds sold in heaps**.
He mentions **sati** and **"300 ports"**.

104.s: Robert Sewell’s A Forgotten Empire is based principally on the accounts of which group?
o: Barbosa, Seydi Ali Reis and Mahmud Wali Balkhi
Marco Polo, Ibn Battuta and Tavernier
104.x: Robert Sewell’s A Forgotten Empire draws chiefly on the accounts of Paes, Nuniz and Abdur Razzaq.
104.tq: Recognise the specific cluster of sources associated with a modern historical reconstruction.
xs: Sewell's **A Forgotten Empire** is built on the accounts of **Paes, Nuniz and Abdur Razzaq** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It is a history of **Vijayanagara**, which all three described.
xa: **Abdur Razzaq** visited **Deva Raya II** in **1443-44**.
AP angle: **Abdur Razzaq** and **Barbosa** → **Vijayanagara**; **Tavernier** → **Golconda**.

104.s: Afanasy Nikitin, a horse merchant who visited India during the reign of Virupaksha Raya II, belonged to which country?
104.x: Afanasy Nikitin was a Russian traveller from Tver, situated on the Volga. He visited Vijayanagara during the reign of Virupaksha Raya II.
104.tq: Test the traveller’s nationality through the associated ruler and occupation.
xs: **Afanasy Nikitin** was from **Russia** (**Tver**, on the **Volga**) — so option **(3)** is correct.
He was a **horse merchant** at Vijayanagara under **Virupaksha Raya II**.
**Persia** = Abdur Razzaq, **Afghanistan (Balkh)** = Mahmud Wali Balkhi, **Turkey** = Seydi Ali Reis.
xa: **Nicolo Conti** and **Marco Polo** were both from **Venice**.
**Tavernier** was from **France**.

104.s: Which foreign traveller is associated with the mention of '300 ports'?
104.x: Abdur Razzaq, the Timurid envoy to Deva Raya II's Vijayanagara, is credited with mentioning '300 ports'. ⚠ The APPSC key said Barbosa, so recognise that answer if it appears in an APPSC paper. Nikitin was a Russian horse merchant, and Tavernier described the diamonds of Golconda.
104.tq: 300 ports = Barbosa; sati = Abdur Razzaq
xs: **Abdur Razzaq** is credited with mentioning **"300 ports"** — so option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ The **APPSC key** said **Barbosa** — know both answers.
**Afanasy Nikitin** was a Russian horse merchant; **Tavernier** wrote on **Golconda** diamonds.
xa: Abdur Razzaq also mentions **sati** and describes **diamonds sold in heaps**.
He visited **Deva Raya II** in **1443-44** as **Shah Rukh's** envoy.

104.s: The Nizami Mosque inscription at Golconda is significant because it dates Quli Qutb-ul-Mulk's independence to:
104.x: The Nizami Mosque inscription at Golconda dates the independence of Quli Qutb-ul-Mulk to 1518.
104.tq: Test the precise date attached to a political event in an inscription.
xs: The **Nizami Mosque** inscription at Golconda dates **Quli Qutb-ul-Mulk's** independence to **1518** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**1576** is the **Ghazinagar** inscription (Nalgonda, **Ibrahim Quli**, **1576-77**); **1595** is the **Daru-Shifa** inscription.
xa: **Badshahi Ashurkhana** inscription: **1592-96**.
These Qutb Shahi inscriptions are in **Persian**.

104.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Vilasa copper plate — Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka
Palam Baoli inscription — Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka
104.x: The Palam Baoli inscription is a Sanskrit record praising Balban and dates to 1276. The Vilasa copper plate is associated with Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka.
104.tq: Find the wrongly assigned person by checking the inscription–issuer relationship.
xs: **Palam Baoli inscription — Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka** is wrong — so option **(4)** is the answer.
The **Palam Baoli** inscription (**1276**) is bilingual and praises **Balban** in **Sanskrit**.
**Vilasa copper plate** — **Prolaya Nayaka** (c. **1330**); **Kaluvacheru** — **Anitalli**; **Warangal** — **Shitab Khan** (**1504-06**).
xa: The Telugu sources **Vilasa**, **Kaluvacheru** and **Pratapa Charitra** count **8** Warangal invasions.
Muslim sources count **5**.

104.s: Mahmud of Ghazni's Lahore dirhams are especially significant as medieval sources because they contain:
o: An Arabic legend and its Sanskrit translation in Sharada script
A Telugu inscription and an Arabic translation
A Sanskrit legend and its Persian translation in Devanagari script
Only a Persian inscription in Nastaliq script
104.x: The Lahore dirhams of Mahmud of Ghazni carry an Arabic legend along with a Sanskrit translation written in Sharada script.
104.tq: Use the script–language combination to distinguish bilingual numismatic evidence.
xs: Mahmud's **Lahore dirhams** carry **an Arabic legend and its Sanskrit translation in Sharada script** — so option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ Mahmud's coins = Arabic + **Sanskrit**; **Iltutmish's** coins = purely **Arabic**.
xa: Iltutmish issued the silver **tanka** and copper **jital**.
The **Palam Baoli** inscription (**1276**) is another bilingual record, praising **Balban** in Sanskrit.

104.s: The Palam Baoli inscription of 1276 praises which ruler in Sanskrit?
104.x: The Palam Baoli inscription, dated 1276, praises Balban in Sanskrit.
104.tq: Link the inscription's date with the ruler praised in it.
xs: The **Palam Baoli** inscription of **1276** praises **Balban** in Sanskrit — so option **(1)** is correct.
It is a **bilingual** record.
**Mahmud of Ghazni** is linked with bilingual **Lahore dirhams**; **Iltutmish's** coins are purely **Arabic**.
xa: ⚠ Iltutmish: silver **tanka** and copper **jital**.
**Barani's Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi** covers **Balban** to early Firoz Tughlaq.

104.s: The transition from trabeate to arcuate construction in Sultanate architecture is marked by the increasing use of:
o: Wooden pillars and flat roofs only
Timber frames and corbelled balconies only
True arches, domes and lime mortar
104.x: Sultanate buildings demonstrate the shift from trabeate construction to arcuate construction through the use of true arches, domes and lime mortar.
104.tq: Identify the architectural system from its characteristic structural elements.
xs: The **trabeate → arcuate** shift used **true arches, domes and lime mortar** — so option **(3)** is correct.
That change marks Sultanate buildings.
xa: **Naskh** script was used for Quranic verses, e.g. the **Jami Masjid mihrab**.
**Nastaliq** was used for **Persian** texts.

104.s:
With reference to Qutb Shahi calligraphy, consider the following statements:
1. Naskh was used for Quranic verses, including those in the Jami Masjid mihrab.
2. Nastaliq was used for Persian texts.
3. Naskh and Nastaliq were forms of architectural construction.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
104.x: Naskh was used for Quranic verses, while Nastaliq was used for Persian texts. They are calligraphic scripts, not forms of architectural construction.
104.tq: Separate the two related scripts from the unrelated architectural term.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — so option **(1) 1 and 2 only** is the answer.
1 is correct: **Naskh** was used for **Quranic verses** (e.g. **Jami Masjid mihrab**).
2 is correct: **Nastaliq** was used for **Persian texts**.
3 is wrong: both are **calligraphy** styles, not building methods.
xa: Architecture shifted from **trabeate** to **arcuate** (true arch, dome, lime mortar).
The **Golconda school** of painting was founded by **Mir Hashimi**.

104.s: Who founded the Golconda school of painting?
104.x: The Golconda school of painting was founded by Mir Hashimi.
104.tq: Test the founder of an artistic tradition against prominent literary figures.
xs: The Golconda school of painting was founded by **Mir Hashimi** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Amir Khusrau** was a court poet; **Abul Fazl** wrote the official history of **Akbar**.
xa: The **"Quliyat Quli"** manuscript has **14** miniatures.
Qutb Shahi calligraphy: **Naskh** (Quranic), **Nastaliq** (Persian).

104.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Ziauddin Barani?
o: He wrote from an orthodox Sunni viewpoint and theorised kingship.
He was a Persian ambassador to Vijayanagara and described its markets.
He founded the Golconda school of painting.
He composed the royal memoirs of Jahangir.
104.x: Ziauddin Barani wrote from an orthodox Sunni viewpoint and also theorised about kingship. The other descriptions belong to different figures or traditions.
104.tq: Use the writer's viewpoint and intellectual contribution to identify him.
xs: Barani **wrote from an orthodox Sunni viewpoint and theorised kingship** — so option **(1)** is correct.
His kingship theory is in **Fatawa-i-Jahandari**.
The Persian envoy to Vijayanagara was **Abdur Razzaq**; the Golconda school was founded by **Mir Hashimi**.
xa: Barani's **Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi** covers **Balban** to early **Firoz Tughlaq**.
It is the main account of **Alauddin's market regulations** and Sultanate attacks on **south Indian kingdoms**.

104.s: Telugu sources and Muslim sources differ in their accounts of the number of invasions of Warangal. Which statement is correct?
o: Telugu sources record 5 invasions, while Muslim sources record 8.
Telugu sources record 8 invasions, while Muslim sources record 5.
Both groups of sources record 8 invasions.
Both groups of sources record 5 invasions.
104.x: The Telugu sources Pratapa Charitra, Vilasa and Kaluvacheru record eight invasions of Warangal, whereas Muslim sources associated with Amir Khusrau and Wassaf record five.
104.tq: Compare conflicting numerical claims by source tradition.
xs: **Telugu sources record 8 invasions, while Muslim sources record 5** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Telugu: **Pratapa Charitra**, **Vilasa**, **Kaluvacheru** — **8**.
Muslim: **Amir Khusrau**, **Wassaf** — **5**.
xa: Amir Khusrau went with **Malik Kafur's 1310** invasion of Warangal.
**Isami's Futuh-us-Salatin** covers the **Tughlaq campaigns against Warangal**.

104.s: Which of the following statements regarding Firishta's account of Deva Raya is correct?
o: His story that Deva Raya kidnapped Nehal has been rejected by modern historians.
Modern historians regard Firishta as the author of the Ain-i-Akbari.
His story that Deva Raya kidnapped Nehal is accepted without reservation by modern historians.
Firishta did not write about Deva Raya.
104.x: Firishta's story that Deva Raya kidnapped Nehal is rejected by modern historians. This illustrates the need to critically evaluate chronicle narratives.
104.tq: Identify the historically qualified statement rather than accepting a dramatic anecdote.
xs: Firishta's story that **Deva Raya kidnapped Nehal** has been **rejected by modern historians** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It shows that chronicle stories must be checked, not accepted wholesale.
Firishta wrote **Tarikh-i-Firishta**, not the **Ain-i-Akbari**.
xa: Tarikh-i-Firishta (**Gulshan-i-Ibrahimi**) was dedicated to **Ibrahim Adil Shah** of Bijapur.
Firishta was born at **Astarabad, Iran, 1552**; he calls Telangana **"Tilang"**.

104.s: Foreign travellers' accounts of medieval India should generally be used by historians in which manner?
o: They should replace inscriptions and archaeological evidence.
They should be ignored because they were written outside India.
They should be accepted as accurate in every detail.
They should supplement Indian texts and be cross-verified with inscriptions and archaeology.
104.x: Foreign accounts supplement Indian textual evidence, but their statements must be cross-verified with inscriptions and archaeological evidence.
104.tq: Apply the principle of corroboration across different source types.
xs: Foreign accounts **supplement Indian texts** and must be **cross-verified with inscriptions and archaeology** — so option **(4)** is correct.
They neither replace other evidence nor are accurate in every detail; nor are they to be ignored.
xa: ⚠ Court histories have their own bias — they **glorify the patron**.
**Taj Mahal** case (**Jul 2026**): evidence that **Shah Jahan** built it includes **European travellers' accounts**.

104.s: Which of the following combinations correctly associates an AP-linked source with the place or polity described?
o: Marco Polo — Motupalli; Abdur Razzaq — Vijayanagara; Tavernier — Golconda
Marco Polo — Golconda; Abdur Razzaq — Warangal; Tavernier — Motupalli
Barbosa — Motupalli; Isami — Vijayanagara; Firishta — Golconda
Tavernier — Vijayanagara; Marco Polo — Warangal; Barbosa — Golconda
104.x: Marco Polo is associated with Motupalli, Abdur Razzaq and Barbosa with Vijayanagara, and Tavernier with Golconda. Isami and Firishta are associated with Warangal.
104.tq: Start with the sure place–traveller pair and complete the matching set.
xs: **Marco Polo — Motupalli; Abdur Razzaq — Vijayanagara; Tavernier — Golconda** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Isami** and **Firishta** are the sources asked for **Warangal**; **Barbosa** goes with **Vijayanagara**, not Motupalli or Golconda.
The other options shuffle these places.
xa: Marco Polo landed at **Motupalli** and visited Kakatiya **Rudramadevi** (**1289-93**).
Tavernier wrote on **Golconda diamonds** under **Abdullah Qutb Shah**.
Abdur Razzaq visited **Deva Raya II** in **1443-44**.

104.s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
 a. Taj-ul-Masir
 b. Rihla
 c. Fatwa-i-Jahandari
 d. Fawaid-ul-Fawad

List-II
 i. Ibn Battuta
 ii. Amir Hasan Sijzi
 iii. Hasan Nizami
 iv. Ziauddin Barani
104.x: Taj-ul-Masir is by Hasan Nizami, Rihla by Ibn Battuta, Fatwa-i-Jahandari by Ziauddin Barani and Fawaid-ul-Fawad by Amir Hasan Sijzi, giving a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.
104.tq: Recall the author of each Sultanate-period work.
n: Taj-ul-Masir was written by Hasan Nizami. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 40-45]
Fatwa-i-Jahandari was written by Ziauddin Barani. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 40-45]
Rihla was written by Ibn Battuta. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 40-45]
Fawaid-ul-Fawad was written by Amir Hasan Sijzi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 40-45]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Taj-ul-Masir** — **Hasan Nizami**; **Rihla** — **Ibn Battuta**.
**Fatwa-i-Jahandari** — **Ziauddin Barani**; **Fawaid-ul-Fawad** — **Amir Hasan Sijzi**.
xa: Hasan Nizami was patronised by **Qutbuddin Aibak**.
Fatwa-i-Jahandari is on the **political theory of kingship**.
**Tabaqat-i-Nasiri** — **Minhaj-us-Siraj**; **Khazain-ul-Futuh** — **Amir Khusrau**.

104.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Tabqat-i-Nasiri
(b) Khazain-ul-Futuh
(c) Tarikh-i-Firuzshahi
(d) Rihla

List-II
(i) Ibn Battuta
(ii) Shams-i-Siraj Afif
(iii) Minhaj-us-Siraj
(iv) Amir Khusrau
104.x: Tabqat-i-Nasiri is by Minhaj-us-Siraj, Khazain-ul-Futuh by Amir Khusrau, Tarikh-i-Firuzshahi (here) by Shams-i-Siraj Afif and Rihla by Ibn Battuta, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
104.tq: Discriminate Afif's Tarikh-i-Firuzshahi from Barani's.
n: Tabqat-i-Nasiri was written by Minhaj-us-Siraj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 40-45]
Khazain-ul-Futuh was written by Amir Khusrau. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 40-45]
Tarikh-i-Firuzshahi was written by Shams-i-Siraj Afif. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 40-45]
Rihla was written by Ibn Battuta. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 40-45]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Tabqat-i-Nasiri** — **Minhaj-us-Siraj**; **Khazain-ul-Futuh** — **Amir Khusrau**.
**Tarikh-i-Firuzshahi** — **Shams-i-Siraj Afif** (also Barani); **Rihla** — **Ibn Battuta**.
xa: Tabaqat-i-Nasiri covers **Bengal** and **Bakhtiyar Khalji**, dedicated to **Nasiruddin Mahmud**.
**Futuhat-i-Firuz Shahi** is a **royal account** by **Firuz Shah Tughluq**.
**Tarikh-i-Mubarakshahi** — **Yahya bin Ahmad Sarhindi**.
⚠ **Tabaqat-i-Akbari** = **Nizamuddin Ahmad**, not Badauni.

104.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Marco Polo
(b) Nicolo Conti
(c) Nuniz
(d) Tavernier

List-II
(i) Devaraya I of Vijayanagara
(ii) 17th century
(iii) Achyutadeva Raya of Vijayanagara
(iv) Kakatiya ruler Rudramadevi

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
104.x: Marco Polo came in Rudramadevi's reign, Nicolo Conti under Devaraya I, Nuniz under Achyutadeva Raya, and Tavernier in the 17th century, giving a-iv, b-i, c-iii, d-ii.
104.tq: Recall the period of each traveller.
n: Marco Polo visited Motupalli port during the Kakatiya period of Rudramadevi. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 32-33]
Nicolo Conti visited South India during the reign of Devaraya I of Vijayanagara. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 32-33]
Nuniz visited during the reign of Achyutadeva Raya of Vijayanagara. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 32-33]
Tavernier lived in the 17th century. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 32-33]
xs: The correct match is **a-iv, b-i, c-iii, d-ii** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Marco Polo** — Kakatiya ruler **Rudramadevi**; **Nicolo Conti** — **Devaraya I** of Vijayanagara.
**Nuniz** — **Achyutadeva Raya**; **Tavernier** — **17th century**.
xa: ⚠ APPSC **2011** key placed **Nicolo Conti** in **Deva Raya II's** reign.
**Abdur Razzaq** (Persia) visited **Deva Raya II** in **1443-44**.
**Robert Sewell's** **A Forgotten Empire** used Paes, Nuniz and Abdur Razzaq.

104.s:
Assertion (A): Tavernier visited Andhra mines for precious stones and diamonds.
Reason (R): Tavernier was a traveller of the 17th century.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
104.x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Tavernier, a 17th-century French jeweller, visited the Golconda-Andhra diamond mines for trade, which his period alone does not explain.
104.tq: Check whether R is the cause of A.
n: Tavernier lived in the 17th century. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 32-33]
Tavernier visited the Andhra mines for precious stones and diamonds. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 32-33]
xs: **Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A** — so option **(2)** is correct.
A: **Tavernier** went to the **Andhra mines** for **precious stones and diamonds**.
R: he was a **17th-century** traveller (from France) — his period does not explain his purpose.
xa: He visited **Golconda** under **Abdullah Qutb Shah**.
**Marco Polo** visited **Motupalli** under **Rudramadevi**.
**Mir Zainul Abidin** (Persia) visited Golconda under **Muhammad Qutb Shah** (**1614**).

104.s:
Assertion (A): Itsing is identified as a Chinese traveller.
Reason (R): He saw students by-hearting “Sushrullekha” in India.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
104.x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Itsing was a Chinese pilgrim, and seeing students memorise Nagarjuna's Suhrllekha does not explain his nationality.
104.tq: Check whether R is the cause of A.
n: Itsing was a Chinese traveller. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 32-33]
Itsing saw students by-hearting “Sushrullekha” in India. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 32-33]
xs: **Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A** — so option **(2)** is correct.
A: **Itsing** was a **Chinese** traveller of the **post-Satavahana** era.
R: he saw students **by-hearting "Sushrullekha"** — this does not explain his nationality.
xa: **Ibn Battuta** (Morocco) wrote the **Rihla** in Arabic.
**Mahmud Wali Balkhi** came from **Balkh (Afghanistan)**.
**Seydi Ali Reis** was a **Turkish** (Ottoman) admiral.

104.s:
How many of the following traveller–association pairs are correct?
I. Marco Polo — Motupalli port
II. Nicolo Conti — Devaraya I
III. Nuniz — Achyutadeva Raya
IV. Tavernier — Andhra mines for precious stones and diamonds
104.x: All four pairs are correct: Marco Polo with Motupalli, Nicolo Conti with Devaraya I, Nuniz with Achyutadeva Raya and Tavernier with the Andhra diamond mines.
104.tq: Check each pair separately.
n: Marco Polo visited Motupalli port during the Kakatiya period of Rudramadevi. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 32-33]
Nicolo Conti visited South India during the reign of Devaraya I of Vijayanagara. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 32-33]
Nuniz visited during the reign of Achyutadeva Raya of Vijayanagara. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 32-33]
Tavernier visited the Andhra mines for precious stones and diamonds. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 32-33]
xs: **All four** pairs are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Marco Polo** — **Motupalli port**; **Nicolo Conti** — **Devaraya I**.
**Nuniz** — **Achyutadeva Raya**; **Tavernier** — **Andhra mines** for diamonds.
xa: ⚠ Two Venetians: **Marco Polo** → Kakatiyas; **Nicolo Conti** → Vijayanagara.
Marco Polo praised the **Kakatiya army** and noted the **diamond trade**.
**Afanasy Nikitin** (Russia) was a **horse merchant**.

105.s: The term ‘Mamluk’ literally refers to:
105.x: Mamluk is an Arabic term meaning ‘owned’. In this context it denotes a military slave, distinct from a domestic slave.
105.tq: Test the precise meaning of a technical historical term.
xs: **Mamluk** is Arabic for "owned" — **an owned military slave** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It means a **military** slave as opposed to a **domestic** slave.
xa: The **Slave / Mamluk** dynasty ruled **1206-1290**.
Aibak was a slave of **Muhammad Ghori** (APPSC G1 **2004**).
Balban was captured by the Mongols and **bought by Iltutmish**.

105.s: Which one of the following is the correct chronological order of the major Delhi Sultanate dynasties?
105.x: The sequence was Mamluk (1206–1290), Khalji (1290–1320), Tughlaq (1320–1414), Sayyid (1414–1451) and Lodi (1451–1526).
105.tq: Use the dynasty transition sequence to eliminate reversals.
xs: The order is **Mamluk, Khalji, Tughlaq, Sayyid, Lodi** — so option **(1)** is correct.
xa: **Jalaluddin Firoz Khalji** crowned himself at **Kilokhari** in **1290**, ending Mamluk rule.
The Mamluks were the **first Muslim dynasty** to rule north India from Delhi.

105.s: Which of the following does NOT belong to the Mamluk dynasty?
105.x: Jalaluddin Khalji belonged to the Khalji dynasty. Alauddin Masud, Nasiruddin Mahmud and Ruknuddin Firuz were rulers of the Mamluk dynasty.
105.tq: Identify the outsider from a list of rulers belonging to one dynasty.
xs: **Jalaluddin Khalji** was not a Mamluk — so option **(4)** is the answer.
He founded the **Khalji** dynasty at **Kilokhari** in **1290**.
**Ruknuddin Firuz** (**1236**), **Alauddin Masud** (**1242-46**) and **Nasiruddin Mahmud** (**1246-66**) were Mamluks.
xa: ⚠ Odd one out: **Jalaluddin Khalji** and the **Tughlaqs** are NOT Mamluks.
The last Mamluks after Balban: grandson **Kaiqubad**, then infant **Kaimurs**.

105.s: Arrange the following Mamluk rulers in chronological order: 1. Razia  2. Balban  3. Iltutmish  4. Nasiruddin Mahmud
105.x: Iltutmish (1210-36) was followed, after Ruknuddin Firuz, by Razia (1236-40); after Bahram Shah and Alauddin Masud came Nasiruddin Mahmud (1246-66) and then Balban (1266-86). The other orders misplace Razia, Nasiruddin or Balban.
105.tq: Iltutmish - Razia - Nasiruddin - Balban
xs: The order is **3, 1, 4, 2** — Iltutmish, Razia, Nasiruddin Mahmud, Balban — so option **(1)** is correct.
