→ **Nasiruddin Mahmud (1246-66)** → **Balban (1266-86)**.
xa: Between them: **Ruknuddin Firuz** (**1236**), **Bahram Shah** (**1240-42**), **Alauddin Masud** (**1242-46**).
Before Iltutmish: **Aibak**, then **Aram Shah**.

105.s:
Consider the following statements about Qutbuddin Aibak:
1. He was born in Turkestan and was first sold to the Qazi of Nishapur.
2. His title 'Lakh Bakhsh' means 'shadow of God'.
3. He died in 1210 after falling from his horse while playing chaugan (polo).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
105.x: Statement 1 is correct: Aibak was born in Turkestan and first sold to the Qazi of Nishapur. Statement 2 is wrong: Lakh Bakhsh means 'giver of lakhs'; 'shadow of God' (Zil-i-Ilahi) is Balban's idea of the Sultan. Statement 3 is correct: he died in 1210 in a chaugan accident. Hence '1 and 3 only'; any option including 2 is wrong, and '1 and 2 only' drops a true statement.
105.tq: Lakh Bakhsh = giver of lakhs (Aibak); Zil-i-Ilahi = shadow of God (Balban).
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — so option **(2) 1 and 3 only** is the answer.
1 is correct: Aibak was born in **Turkestan** and first sold to the **Qazi of Nishapur**.
2 is wrong: **Lakh Bakhsh** means **"giver of lakhs"**; **Zil-i-Ilahi** ("shadow of God") is **Balban's** theory.
3 is correct: he died in **1210** falling from his horse playing **chaugan** (polo).
xa: He was then a slave of **Muhammad Ghori** and rose to **Amir-i-Akhur** (Master of Stables).
His son **Aram Shah** ruled only about **8** months.

105.s: Before becoming a general, Qutbuddin Aibak held the office of:
105.x: Aibak rose to the position of Amir-i-Akhur, or Master of Stables, and subsequently became a general.
105.tq: Test an earlier post through an official Persian title.
xs: Aibak rose to **Amir-i-Akhur** (**Master of Stables**) before becoming a general — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Diwan-i-Arz** is the military department later created by **Balban**, not an office of Aibak.
xa: After **Tarain II (1192)** Aibak was **Ghori's** representative in India.
He became Sultan on Ghori's death and ruled **1206-1210** from **Lahore**.

105.s: Which statement about the monuments associated with Qutbuddin Aibak is NOT correct?
o: The Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque was built using reused temple pillars.
Aibak completed the Qutb Minar during his own reign.
The Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque is regarded as the first mosque in India.
Aibak began the construction of the Qutb Minar.
105.x: Aibak began the Qutb Minar, but it was completed by Iltutmish. The Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque used reused temple pillars and is regarded as the first mosque in India.
105.tq: Find the wrong completion claim in a sequence of monument-related facts.
xs: "**Aibak completed the Qutb Minar**" is wrong — so option **(2)** is the answer.
Aibak **began** the Qutb Minar; **Iltutmish completed** it.
Quwwat-ul-Islam used **reused temple pillars** and is the **first mosque in India** — both true.
xa: The Qutb Minar is dedicated to **Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki**.
The **Qutb complex** is now a **UNESCO** site.

105.s: The Qutb Minar was dedicated to:
105.x: Qutbuddin Aibak began the Qutb Minar and dedicated it to Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki.
105.tq: Separate the dedicatee of a monument from other well-known Sufi figures.
xs: The Qutb Minar is dedicated to **Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki** — so option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ It is named after the saint **Bakhtiyar Kaki**, not after Aibak.
xa: It was **begun by Aibak** and **completed by Iltutmish**.
Iltutmish's **Sultan Ghari** tomb made him the **"Father of tomb building"**.

105.s:
Consider the following statements about Iltutmish:
1. He was an Ilbari Turk and the slave and son-in-law of Qutbuddin Aibak.
2. He moved the capital from Delhi to Lahore.
3. Before becoming Sultan he was iqtadar of Gwalior and governor of Baran and Badaun.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
105.x: Statement 1 is correct: Iltutmish was an Ilbari Turk, Aibak's slave and son-in-law. Statement 2 is wrong: he moved the capital the other way, from Lahore (Aibak's capital) to Delhi. Statement 3 is correct: he was iqtadar of Gwalior, then governor of Baran and Badaun. So '1 and 3 only'.
105.tq: Aibak = Lahore; Iltutmish shifted to Delhi. Reversed direction is the trap.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — so option **(2) 1 and 3 only** is the answer.
1 is correct: Iltutmish was an **Ilbari** Turk, **slave and son-in-law** of Aibak.
2 is wrong: he moved the capital from **Lahore to Delhi**, not the reverse.
3 is correct: he was **iqtadar of Gwalior**, then governor of **Baran** and **Badaun**.
xa: His title was **Shamsuddin**.
He received investiture (**"mansur"**) from the **Abbasid Caliph of Baghdad** in **1229**.

105.s:
Consider the following statements about the institutions of Iltutmish:
1. He received investiture (mansur) from the Abbasid Caliph of Baghdad in 1229.
2. Under the iqta system, officers (muqtis) were given revenue assignments instead of cash salaries.
3. The Turkan-i-Chahalgani was a body of Persian revenue clerks.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
105.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Abbasid Caliph's mansur came in 1229. Statement 2 is correct: iqtas were revenue assignments to muqtis in place of cash pay. Statement 3 is wrong: the Turkan-i-Chahalgani (the Forty) was the Turkish military elite. So '1 and 2 only'.
105.tq: Chahalgani = Forty TURKISH nobles; mansur 1229; iqta = revenue assignment, not cash.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — so option **(1) 1 and 2 only** is the answer.
1 is correct: investiture (**mansur**) from the **Abbasid Caliph of Baghdad** in **1229**.
2 is correct: **iqta** = revenue assignments to officers (**muqtis**) instead of cash salaries.
3 is wrong: **Turkan-i-Chahalgani** (the Forty / **Chalisa**) was the **Turkish military elite**.
xa: ⚠ Iltutmish **created** the Forty; **Balban broke** its power.
1229 is the **first Caliphal investiture** of a Delhi Sultan.

105.s: Which statement regarding Iltutmish and the Mongols is correct?
o: He sheltered Jalaluddin Mangbarni and invited Chengiz Khan to India.
He made Jalaluddin Mangbarni a member of the Forty.
He refused shelter to Jalaluddin Mangbarni, helping keep Chengiz Khan out of India.
He defeated Chengiz Khan at Tarain in 1216.
105.x: Iltutmish refused shelter to Jalaluddin Mangbarni of Khwarazm. This diplomatic decision helped prevent Chengiz Khan from entering India.
105.tq: Use the cause-and-effect relationship in a diplomatic episode.
xs: Iltutmish **refused shelter to Jalaluddin Mangbarni**, keeping **Chengiz Khan** out of India — so option **(3)** is correct.
Mangbarni was the prince of **Khwarazm**, fleeing the Mongols.
**1216** at Tarain was Iltutmish's victory over **Yildiz**, not Chengiz Khan.
xa: Balban later built **outposts and forts** against the **Mongols**.
Balban's son **Prince Muhammad** died fighting the Mongols (**1285**).

105.s: Which monument led to Iltutmish being called the ‘Father of tomb building’?
105.x: Iltutmish built the Sultan Ghari tomb and is consequently called the Father of tomb building. He also completed the Qutb Minar.
105.tq: Match an architectural work with the historical epithet associated with its builder.
xs: The **Sultan Ghari tomb** made Iltutmish the **"Father of tomb building"** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Arhai-din-ka-Jhonpra** at Ajmer was built by **Aibak** and is not a tomb.
xa: Iltutmish **completed** the **Qutb Minar** begun by Aibak.
Aibak's **Quwwat-ul-Islam** mosque, Delhi, is the **first mosque in India**.

105.s: Which of the following was a distinctive feature of Razia Sultan's rule?
o: She accepted the authority of Bahram Shah throughout her reign.
She maintained purdah and never appeared before the army.
She discarded purdah, wore male attire and led the army.
She ruled only through Balban as her regent.
105.x: Razia discarded purdah, wore male attire and personally led the army. Her conduct challenged the expectations of the Turkish nobles.
105.tq: Identify the correct application of a ruler's known social and military policy.
xs: Razia **discarded purdah, wore male attire and led the army** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Bahram Shah** was the noble's choice who replaced her; **Balban** was **naib** to Nasiruddin Mahmud, not her regent.
xa: Razia made Balban **Amir-i-Shikar**.
Turkish nobles resented her favour to **Yaqut** (Abyssinian).

105.s: The Turkish nobles opposed Razia primarily because she favoured:
105.x: The Turkish nobles resented Razia's favour towards Yaqut, an Abyssinian. Their opposition contributed to the revolt led by Altuniya.
105.tq: Use the person–identity association to resolve a confusable court-politics question.
xs: The nobles resented her favour to **Yaqut, an Abyssinian** — so option **(4)** is correct.
In **1240** **Altuniya**, governor of **Bhatinda (Sirhind)**, revolted; Yaqut was killed and Razia imprisoned.
**Minhaj-us-Siraj** and **Hasan Nizami** were chroniclers; **Yildiz** was Iltutmish's rival.
xa: The nobles then enthroned **Bahram Shah**.
Razia married Altuniya, marched on Delhi, and was **defeated and killed** (**1240**).

105.s: Which sequence correctly describes Balban's early rise?
o: Slave of Iltutmish → water-carrier → member of the Forty → Amir-i-Shikar
Water-carrier → slave of Aibak → Amir-i-Akhur → member of the Forty
Member of the Forty → slave of Iltutmish → water-carrier → governor of Bhatinda
105.x: Balban was captured by the Mongols, bought by Iltutmish, rose from water-carrier to the Forty, and was made Amir-i-Shikar by Razia.
105.tq: Arrange biographical stages rather than merely recalling an isolated title.
xs: **Slave of Iltutmish → water-carrier → member of the Forty → Amir-i-Shikar** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Balban was captured by the **Mongols** and **bought by Iltutmish**.
**Razia** made him **Amir-i-Shikar**; title **Ulugh Khan**.
xa: **Amir-i-Akhur** (Master of Stables) was **Aibak's** post, not Balban's.
Under Nasiruddin Mahmud he became **principal minister (naib)** and leader of the Forty.

105.s: During the reign of Nasiruddin Mahmud, Balban served as:
105.x: Balban was Nasiruddin Mahmud's principal minister, or naib, and leader of the Forty. He was briefly displaced by Imaduddin Raihan before returning to power.
105.tq: Test the exact office held by a powerful minister during a weak ruler's reign.
xs: Balban was Nasiruddin Mahmud's **principal minister and naib** — so option **(2)** is correct.
He was also **leader of the Forty**.
He was briefly displaced by **Imaduddin Raihan**, then returned.
xa: **Altuniya** was governor of **Bhatinda**; **Amir-i-Akhur** was **Aibak's** post.
Balban became Sultan in **1266**.

105.s:
Consider the following statements about Balban's theory of kingship:
1. He regarded the Sultan as Zil-i-Ilahi (shadow of God).
2. He required sijda (prostration) and paibos (kissing the feet) at court.
3. He abolished the Persian festival of Nauroz at court.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
105.x: Statement 1 is correct: Balban held the Sultan to be Zil-i-Ilahi. Statement 2 is correct: sijda and paibos were required. Statement 3 is wrong: Balban introduced the Persian Nauroz festival with strict court etiquette, he did not abolish it. So '1 and 2 only'; options with 3 are wrong and '1 only' is incomplete.
105.tq: Balban's court was Persian in style: Nauroz, sijda, paibos, Zil-i-Ilahi.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — so option **(1) 1 and 2 only** is the answer.
1 is correct: Balban saw the Sultan as **Zil-i-Ilahi** (shadow of God).
2 is correct: **sijda** (prostration) and **paibos** (kissing the feet) were required.
3 is wrong: Balban **adopted** the Persian **Nauroz** festival with strict court etiquette.
xa: ⚠ **Sijda** = prostration; **paibos** = kissing the feet.
He created the military department **Diwan-i-Arz**.

105.s:
Consider the following statements about Balban's 'blood and iron' policy:
1. He ruthlessly suppressed the Mewatis and rebellious villages.
2. He strengthened the Forty by promoting only senior Turks.
3. He broke the power of the Forty by promoting junior Turks.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
105.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Mewatis and rebel villages were ruthlessly suppressed. Statement 2 is wrong: he did not strengthen the Forty. Statement 3 is correct: he broke the Forty's power by promoting junior Turks. Hence '1 and 3 only'; any option with 2 is wrong.
105.tq: Balban ended the Chahalgani; he did not build it up.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — so option **(2) 1 and 3 only** is the answer.
1 is correct: **ruthless suppression** of the **Mewatis** and rebellious villages.
2 is wrong: he did not strengthen the Forty.
3 is correct: he **broke the power of the Forty** by promoting **junior Turks**.
xa: ⚠ Iltutmish **created** the Forty; Balban **broke** it.
UPPSC **2024**: Balban centralised authority AND guarded the north-west, but the second is not the reason for the first.

105.s: The military department reorganised by Balban was known as:
105.x: Balban reorganised the army and created the military department Diwan-i-Arz. He also built outposts and forts against the Mongols.
105.tq: Use the function of an institution to distinguish it from neighbouring departments.
xs: Balban created the military department **Diwan-i-Arz** — so option **(2)** is correct.
He reorganised the army and built **outposts and forts** against the **Mongols**.
xa: His son **Prince Muhammad** died fighting the Mongols (**1285**).
Diwan-i-Arz is one of the dynasty's **core institutions**, with iqta, the Forty and **tanka/jital**.

105.s: Which sequence correctly describes the end of Mamluk rule?
o: Balban → Kaiqubad → Kaimurs → Jalaluddin Firoz Khalji
Kaiqubad → Balban → Kaimurs → Jalaluddin Firoz Khalji
Balban → Kaimurs → Kaiqubad → Jalaluddin Firoz Khalji
Jalaluddin Firoz Khalji → Balban → Kaiqubad → Kaimurs
105.x: Balban died in 1286 and was followed by his grandson Kaiqubad, who was murdered. The infant Kaimurs succeeded him briefly before Jalaluddin Firoz Khalji ended Mamluk rule in 1290.
105.tq: Arrange succession events by fixing the transition from the last Mamluk ruler to the Khaljis.
xs: **Balban → Kaiqubad → Kaimurs → Jalaluddin Firoz Khalji** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Balban died in **1286**; grandson **Kaiqubad** was murdered (body thrown into the **Yamuna**).
Then the infant **Kaimurs**, until **Jalaluddin Firoz Khalji** took over in **1290**.
xa: Jalaluddin crowned himself at **Kilokhari**.
The **Khalji** dynasty ruled **1290-1320**.

105.s: Jalaluddin Firoz Khalji crowned himself at which place in 1290?
105.x: Jalaluddin Firoz Khalji crowned himself at Kilokhari in 1290, thereby ending Mamluk rule and beginning the Khalji dynasty.
105.tq: Match the accession event with its precise location and year.
xs: Jalaluddin Firoz Khalji crowned himself at **Kilokhari** in **1290** — so option **(2)** is correct.
That ended **Mamluk** rule.
**Bhatinda** is linked with **Altuniya**, **Badaun** with Iltutmish's governorship and **Lahore** with **Aibak's** capital.
xa: The last Mamluks were **Kaiqubad** and the infant **Kaimurs**.
The **Khalji** dynasty ruled **1290-1320**.

105.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the contributions of the Slave or Mamluk dynasty:
1. It created the iqta institution as a core institution of the Sultanate.
2. It developed the institution known as the Forty.
3. It introduced the tanka and jital as important Sultanate coins.
4. It established the Diwan-i-Arz as a core institution.
5. The Qutb complex associated with this dynasty is now a UNESCO site.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
105.x: All five statements are correct. The dynasty helped establish the iqta, Forty, tanka-jital and Diwan-i-Arz institutions, while the Qutb complex is now a UNESCO site.
105.tq: Check each institutional contribution separately before selecting the comprehensive combination.
xs: All five statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5** is the answer.
Core institutions: **iqta**, **the Forty**, **tanka/jital** and **Diwan-i-Arz**.
The **Qutb complex** is now a **UNESCO** site.
xa: **Iqta** and the **Forty** came from **Iltutmish**; **Diwan-i-Arz** from **Balban**.
**Iqta** = revenue assignments to **muqtis** instead of cash salaries.

106.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Jalaluddin Khalji's policy towards rebels and Hindus?
o: He imposed severe punishments on every rebel without exception.
He adopted a benevolent attitude and was lenient towards rebels such as Malik Chhajju.
He adopted a policy of complete exclusion of Hindus from administration.
He transferred the capital to Ranthambore to control Hindu chiefs.
106.x: Jalaluddin Khalji was the first Sultan described as having a benevolent attitude towards Hindus, and he was lenient towards rebels including Malik Chhajju.
106.tq: Identify the policy statement that combines the ruler's general approach with its specific example.
xs: Jalaluddin **adopted a benevolent attitude** and was **lenient towards rebels such as Malik Chhajju** — so option **(2)** is correct.
He was the **first Sultan** with a benevolent attitude to **Hindus**.
His attack on **Ranthambore** failed; he never moved his capital there.
xa: He crowned himself at **Kilokhari** in **1290**, aged about **70**.
He was a **Khalji** from **Turkestan** who had fought the Mongols.

106.s:
Consider the following statements about Jalaluddin Khalji:
1. He crowned himself at Kilokhari.
2. His attack on Ranthambore failed.
3. He was murdered at Kara by his nephew and son-in-law Alauddin.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
106.x: All three statements are correct. Jalaluddin crowned himself at Kilokhari, failed in his attack on Ranthambore, and was murdered at Kara by Alauddin in 1296.
106.tq: Check the event, outcome and place separately before selecting the combined option.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is the answer.
1: he crowned himself at **Kilokhari** (**1290**).
2: his attack on **Ranthambore** failed.
3: his nephew and son-in-law **Alauddin** murdered him at **Kara (1296)**.
xa: Before the murder Alauddin raided **Devagiri** (**1294-96**) — the **first Turkish invasion of the south**.
Jalaluddin was lenient to rebels like **Malik Chhajju**.

106.s:
Consider the following statements about Jalaluddin Khalji and the Mongols:
1. Mongols who converted and settled in the Sultanate were called 'New Mussalmans'.
2. He married his daughter to Ulugh Khan, a descendant of Chengiz Khan.
3. The first Mongol invasion of India came during his reign.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
106.x: Statement 1 is correct: settled converted Mongols were the New Mussalmans. Statement 2 is correct: Jalaluddin married his daughter to Ulugh Khan, a descendant of Chengiz Khan. Statement 3 is wrong: the first Mongol threat came under Iltutmish (Chengiz Khan, 1221). So '1 and 2 only'.
106.tq: 'First Mongol invasion under Jalaluddin' is a classic false statement: it was under Iltutmish.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — so option **(1) 1 and 2 only** is the answer.
1 is correct: converted, settled Mongols were the **"New Mussalmans"**.
2 is correct: he married his daughter to **Ulugh Khan**, a descendant of **Chengiz Khan**.
3 is wrong: the first Mongol threat came under **Iltutmish** (**1221**) (UPSC **2022**).
xa: **Hammir Deva** of **Ranthambore** later sheltered the New Mussalmans — the cause of the **1301** campaign.
Alauddin met a Mongol **siege of Delhi** by sheltering in **Siri** fort.

106.s: Which one of the following statements about Alauddin Khalji's defence against the Mongols is NOT correct?
o: He abandoned the north-western frontier and concentrated all forces in the Deccan.
He maintained a large standing army.
He built Siri as a new capital.
He repaired old forts and constructed new ones on the north-western frontier.
106.x: Alauddin did not abandon the north-western frontier. He repaired and built forts, maintained a large standing army, established Siri and appointed Ghazi Malik as governor of Punjab.
106.tq: Find the extreme reversal of a policy supported by several defensive measures.
xs: "He **abandoned the north-western frontier** and concentrated in the Deccan" is wrong — so option **(1)** is the answer.
He **repaired old forts and built new ones** on the north-west frontier, completing **Balban's** policy.
He kept a **large standing army** and built **Siri** as a new capital — both true.
xa: **Ghazi Malik** was made governor of **Punjab** to hold the frontier.
**Zafar Khan** was killed at the **Battle of Kili**.

106.s:
Consider the following statements about Alauddin Khalji's wars with the Mongols:
1. Zafar Khan was killed at the battle of Kili.
2. Ghazi Malik was made governor of Bengal to hold the frontier.
3. When the Mongols besieged Delhi, Alauddin sheltered in Siri fort.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
106.x: Statement 1 is correct: Zafar Khan died at Kili. Statement 2 is wrong: Ghazi Malik was made governor of Punjab, the north-west frontier province. Statement 3 is correct: Alauddin sheltered in Siri during the siege of Delhi. So '1 and 3 only'.
106.tq: Mongol frontier = north-west, so Ghazi Malik guarded Punjab, not Bengal.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — so option **(2) 1 and 3 only** is the answer.
1 is correct: **Zafar Khan** was killed at **Kili**.
2 is wrong: **Ghazi Malik** was made governor of **Punjab**, not Bengal.
3 is correct: during the Mongol **siege of Delhi**, Alauddin sheltered in **Siri** fort.
xa: Alauddin built **Siri** as his new capital and kept a **large standing army**.
Ghazi Malik later killed **Khusrau Khan** in **1320** and founded the **Tughlaq** dynasty.

106.s: Before becoming Sultan, Alauddin Khalji was known as:
106.x: Alauddin Khalji's earlier name was Ali Gurshasp.
106.tq: Test the ruler’s earlier name directly against names of contemporaries.
xs: Alauddin's earlier name was **Ali Gurshasp** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Khizr Khan** was his son; **Ghazi Malik** and **Ain-ul-Mulk Multani** were his nobles.
xa: Under Jalaluddin he was **Amir-i-Tuzuk** (master of ceremonies) and **Ariz-i-Mumalik** (army minister).
He wished to be **Sikandar-i-Sani** — a second Alexander.

106.s:
Consider the following statements about Alauddin Khalji's posts under Jalaluddin Khalji:
1. He was Amir-i-Tuzuk, the master of ceremonies.
2. As Ariz-i-Mumalik he was the minister of law.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
106.x: Statement 1 is correct: Alauddin was Amir-i-Tuzuk (master of ceremonies). Statement 2 is wrong: the Ariz-i-Mumalik was the army minister; 'minister of law' is a known misprint. So '1 only'.
106.tq: Ariz = army. Any statement calling it law is false.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — so option **(1) 1 only** is the answer.
1 is correct: **Amir-i-Tuzuk** = **master of ceremonies**.
2 is wrong: **Ariz-i-Mumalik** = **army minister**; ⚠ "minister of law" is a known misprint.
xa: **Sikandar-i-Sani** = second Alexander, his world-conqueror ambition.
His court poet was **Amir Khusrau**.

106.s:
Consider the following statements about Alauddin Khalji's ambitions:
1. He took the title Sikandar-i-Sani and wished to be a world conqueror like Alexander.
2. He also thought of founding a new religion.
3. Ala-ul-Mulk, who advised him against both plans, was Barani's father.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
106.x: Statement 1 is correct: Sikandar-i-Sani means the second Alexander. Statement 2 is correct: he also planned a new religion. Statement 3 is wrong: Ala-ul-Mulk, Kotwal of Delhi, was Barani's uncle, not his father. So '1 and 2 only'.
106.tq: Ala-ul-Mulk = Kotwal of Delhi = Barani's UNCLE.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — so option **(1) 1 and 2 only** is the answer.
1 is correct: **Sikandar-i-Sani** — a world conqueror like **Alexander**.
2 is correct: he also thought of founding a **new religion**.
3 is wrong: **Ala-ul-Mulk**, Kotwal of Delhi, was **Barani's uncle**, not father.
xa: Alauddin ruled **without the ulema**, acting in the state's interest.
His nobles: **Ulugh Khan**, **Nusrat Khan**, **Zafar Khan**, **Ain-ul-Mulk Multani**, **Malik Kafur**, **Ghazi Malik**.

106.s: Which pair of officials led Alauddin Khalji's Gujarat campaign of 1299?
o: Khwaja Haji and Malik Fakhruddin Juna
106.x: Ulugh Khan and Nusrat Khan commanded the Gujarat campaign of 1299. Rai Karan, also known as Karnadeva II, was defeated, and Queen Kamala Devi was captured.
106.tq: Use the commander–campaign association and reject swapped generals.
xs: **Ulugh Khan and Nusrat Khan** led the **1299** Gujarat campaign — so option **(3)** is correct.
They defeated **Rai Karan (Karnadeva II)** Vaghela; his queen **Kamala Devi** was captured.
**Malik Kafur** was acquired here; **Ain-ul-Mulk** led **Malwa** (**1305**).
xa: **1299** is the accepted date (APPSC **2023** key); older notes say **1297**.
**Nusrat Khan** was later killed at **Ranthambore** (**1301**).

106.s: Alauddin Khalji renamed Chittor as:
106.x: After the conquest of Chittor in 1303, Alauddin Khalji renamed it Khizrabad after his son Prince Khizr Khan.
106.tq: Test the conqueror–renaming relationship.
xs: Chittor was renamed **Khizrabad** after prince **Khizr Khan** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Alauddin took it in **1303** from **Rana Ratan Singh** of Mewar.
xa: **Rani Padmini's jauhar** is set at Chittor.
⚠ Prince **Khizr Khan** (set aside **1316**) ≠ Sayyid **Khizr Khan** (**1414-1421**).

106.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the distinction between Alauddin Khalji's northern and southern policy?
o: Northern kingdoms were generally annexed, whereas southern rulers retained their thrones and paid tribute.
Southern kingdoms were converted into provinces governed by Mongol chiefs.
Northern rulers paid tribute, whereas southern rulers were annexed directly.
Both northern and southern kingdoms retained their rulers and paid tribute.
106.x: Alauddin generally annexed conquered kingdoms in the north. In the south, rulers retained their thrones and accepted the obligation to pay tribute.
106.tq: Test the reversed-comparison trap between northern and southern policy.
xs: **Northern kingdoms were annexed**, while **southern rulers kept their thrones and paid tribute** — so option **(1)** is correct.
E.g. **Prataparudra II** of Warangal signed a **treaty and annual tribute** (**1309-10**).
xa: **Ramachandra** of Devagiri agreed to **tribute** (**1307-08**).
Kakatiya **tribute stopped after 1316**.

106.s: The story of Padmini is narrated in the work Padmavat, written by:
106.x: Padmavat was written by Malik Muhammad Jayasi. It presents the Padmini story, which some scholars regard as a legend.
106.tq: Match the literary work with its author and avoid the famous court-poet trap.
xs: **Padmavat** was written by **Malik Muhammad Jayasi** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was written in **1540** in **Awadhi**.
**Amir Khusrau** was Alauddin's court poet; **Barani** was Ala-ul-Mulk's nephew.
xa: Some scholars treat the **Padmini** motive as **legend**.
The story rests on a text written **two centuries later** than the events.

106.s: Padmavat was composed primarily in:
106.x: Malik Muhammad Jayasi composed Padmavat in Awadhi. Some descriptions place it within the broader Hindi literary tradition.
106.tq: Distinguish the precise literary language from the broader language classification.
xs: Padmavat was written in **Awadhi** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Malik Muhammad Jayasi** wrote it in **1540**; some notes call it **15th-century Hindi**.
xa: It tells of **Rani Padmini's jauhar** at **Chittor** (**1303**).
Some scholars treat the Padmini motive as **legend**.

106.s:
Consider the following statements about the Padmini narrative:
1. It is associated with Alauddin Khalji's conquest of Chittor.
2. It was recorded in Padmavat in 1540.
3. All scholars treat the story as an undisputed historical account.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
106.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because some scholars treat the Padmini motive as a legend rather than an undisputed historical account.
106.tq: Identify the absolute claim in a question involving a contested historical tradition.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — so option **(1) 1 and 2 only** is the answer.
1 is correct: it is linked to Alauddin's conquest of **Chittor** (**1303**).
2 is correct: **Padmavat** dates to **1540**.
3 is wrong: **some scholars treat the Padmini motive as legend**.
xa: Padmavat is by **Malik Muhammad Jayasi**, in **Awadhi**.
Chittor's king was **Rana Ratan Singh**.

106.s:
Arrange the following conquests of Alauddin Khalji in chronological order:
A. Chittor
B. Gujarat
C. Malwa
D. Ranthambhor

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
106.x: The sequence was Gujarat in 1299, Ranthambhor in 1301, Chittor in 1303 and Malwa in 1305.
106.tq: Fix the earliest and latest dates first, then place the middle conquests.
xs: The order is **B, D, A, C** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Gujarat 1299** → **Ranthambhor 1301**.
xa: Southern sequence: **Devagiri** → **Warangal** → **Dwarasamudra** → **Madurai**.
UPPSC **2022** order: Gujarat, Ranthambore, Chittor, Warangal.

106.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Gujarat — Rai Karan or Karnadeva II Vaghela
2. Chittor — Rana Ratan Singh
3. Warangal — Prataparudra II
4. Malwa — Ain-ul-Mulk Multani
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
106.x: All four pairs are correct. Gujarat was associated with Rai Karan, Chittor with Rana Ratan Singh, Warangal with Prataparudra II, and the Malwa campaign was led by Ain-ul-Mulk Multani.
106.tq: Verify several ruler–region associations before choosing the coded combination.
xs: All four pairs are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4** is the answer.
**Gujarat — Rai Karan (Karnadeva II)**; **Chittor — Rana Ratan Singh**.
**Warangal — Prataparudra II**; **Malwa — Ain-ul-Mulk Multani** (commander, **1305**).
xa: **Ranthambore** — **Hammir Deva**; **Devagiri** — **Ramachandra**; **Dwarasamudra** — **Vira Ballala III**.
Warangal ended in a **treaty and annual tribute** (**1309-10**).

106.s: Arrange Malik Kafur's southern campaigns in chronological order: 1. Warangal  2. Madurai  3. Devagiri  4. Dwarasamudra
106.x: Devagiri (Yadava Ramachandra, 1307-08), Warangal (Kakatiya Prataparudra II, 1309-10), Dwarasamudra (Hoysala Vira Ballala III, 1310-11) and Madurai (Pandya princes, 1311). The other orders put Warangal before Devagiri or Madurai before Dwarasamudra.
106.tq: Devagiri - Warangal - Dwarasamudra - Madurai
xs: The order is **3, 1, 4, 2** — Devagiri, Warangal, Dwarasamudra, Madurai — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Devagiri** (Ramachandra, **1307-08**) → **Warangal** (Prataparudra II, **1309-10**).
→ **Dwarasamudra** (Vira Ballala III, **1310-11**) → **Madurai** (Pandya princes, **1311**).
xa: Some notes give **1307 / 1309 / 1310 / 1311**; others: Yadavas **1308**, Kakatiyas **1310**, Hoysalas **1311**.
Kakatiya troops aided Malik Kafur against Madurai.

106.s: Which of the following events occurred immediately after the death of Alauddin Khalji in 1316?
o: Ghazi Malik founded the Tughlaq dynasty.
Malik Kafur set aside Khizr Khan and enthroned the minor Shihabuddin Umar.
Khusrau Khan subdued Warangal for the first time.
106.x: After Alauddin's death in 1316, Malik Kafur set aside Khizr Khan and placed the minor Shihabuddin Umar on the throne.
106.tq: Use the immediate-successor sequence to eliminate events belonging to other reigns.
xs: After Alauddin's death (**1316**), **Malik Kafur set aside Khizr Khan and enthroned the minor Shihabuddin Umar** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Kafur himself was then murdered.
**Ghazi Malik** founded the Tughlaqs only in **1320**; Khusrau Khan's Warangal campaign was the **3rd** (**1318**).
xa: Next Sultan: **Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah (1316-20)**.
⚠ This **Khizr Khan** ≠ the **Sayyid** Sultan Khizr Khan (**1414-1421**).

106.s: Khusrau Khan's campaign against Warangal during the reign of Mubarak Shah is regarded as which invasion of the Kakatiya kingdom?
106.x: Khusrau Khan subdued Warangal again in 1318, which is identified as the third invasion.
106.tq: Separate the ordinal number of the campaign from its date and commander.
xs: Khusrau Khan's campaign was the **third invasion in 1318** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It came under **Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah (1316-20)**.
**1309-10** was Malik Kafur's treaty; **1303** the Kakatiya defeat at **Upparapalli**.
xa: Khusrau Khan became **Nasiruddin Khusrau Shah** after murdering Mubarak.
Kakatiya tribute had stopped after **1316**.

106.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Jalaluddin Khalji was approximately seventy years old when he crowned himself.
2. Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah restored all of Alauddin Khalji's harsh regulations.
3. Ghazi Malik's victory over Khusrau Khan marked the end of Khalji rule.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
106.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is false because Mubarak Shah withdrew, rather than restored, Alauddin Khalji's harsh regulations and price controls.
106.tq: Find the reversed policy statement and retain the two correct succession facts.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — so option **(2) 1 and 3 only** is the answer.
1 is correct: Jalaluddin was about **70** at **Kilokhari** (**1290**).
2 is wrong: Mubarak Shah **withdrew** the harsh regulations and price controls.
3 is correct: **Ghazi Malik** killed **Khusrau Khan** in **1320**, ending the Khaljis.
xa: Ghazi Malik then founded the **Tughlaq** dynasty.
Ghazi Malik had been Alauddin's governor of **Punjab**.

106.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
106.x: Bahlol Lodi ruled from 1451 to 1489, not 1491. The other three reign periods are correctly matched.
106.tq: Find the altered terminal year in an otherwise familiar reign period.
xs: **Bahlol Lodi — 1451–1491** is wrong — so option **(4)** is the answer.
Bahlol Lodi ruled **1451-1489**.
**Khizr Khan 1414-1421**, **Jalaluddin 1290-1296** and **Alauddin 1296-1316** are correct.
xa: **Muhammad bin Tughlaq**: **1325-1351** (some keys print **1324**).
⚠ Sayyid **Khizr Khan** ≠ Alauddin's son Khizr Khan.

106.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Kakatiya–Delhi relations:
1. The Kakatiyas were defeated at Upparapalli in 1303.
2. Malik Kafur concluded a treaty with the Kakatiyas in 1309–10.
3. The Kakatiyas helped the Delhi forces against the Pandyas in 1311.
4. Kakatiya tribute to Delhi stopped after 1316.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
106.x: All four statements correctly describe the major stages of Kakatiya–Delhi relations: the defeat at Upparapalli, the treaty of 1309–10, assistance against the Pandyas in 1311, and the cessation of tribute after 1316.
106.tq: Verify each chronological stage before choosing the all-inclusive combination.
xs: All four statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4** is the answer.
1: defeat at **Upparapalli** (**1303**); 2: **Kafur's treaty** (**1309-10**).
3: Kakatiya help against the **Pandyas** (**1311**); 4: tribute **stopped after 1316**.
xa: Kafur's treaty with **Prataparudra II** set **annual tribute**.
⚠ Telugu sources count **8** invasions; Muslim sources **5**.
**Khusrau Khan's** campaign of **1318** was the **3rd invasion**.

106.s: Alauddin Khalji's raid on Devagiri is significant in the history of the Delhi Sultanate because it was:
o: The first expedition of the Tughlaqs into the south
The first Kakatiya invasion of Delhi
The first Turkish invasion of southern India
The first Mongol invasion of the Deccan
106.x: Alauddin Khalji's Devagiri raid of 1294–96 is described as the first Turkish invasion of the south.
106.tq: Use the FIRST/LAST marker to identify the historically defining event.
xs: Alauddin's Devagiri raid (**1294-96**) was **the first Turkish invasion of southern India** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was made under **Jalaluddin**, before Alauddin's accession — not by the Tughlaqs or Mongols.
xa: He later murdered Jalaluddin at **Kara (1296)**.
Devagiri (Yadava **Ramachandra**) was attacked again by **Malik Kafur** in **1307-08**.

106.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Mongols repeatedly invaded during Alauddin Khalji’s reign.
II. The Mongol invasions contributed to the creation of a large standing army.
III. The Mongol invasions contributed to military reforms.
IV. The Mongol invasions contributed to revenue reforms.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
106.x: All four are correct: repeated Mongol invasions under Alauddin Khalji led him to keep a large standing army and make military reforms, and his revenue and market reforms paid for it.
106.tq: Check each statement separately.
n: The Mongols repeatedly invaded during Alauddin Khalji’s reign. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 78-80]
The Mongol invasions contributed to the creation of a large standing army. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 78-80]
The Mongol invasions contributed to military reforms. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 78-80]
The Mongol invasions contributed to revenue reforms. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 78-80]
xs: All four — **I, II, III and IV** — are correct, so option **(2)** is correct.
**Repeated Mongol invasions** in **Alauddin Khalji's** reign led to a **large standing army**.
They also contributed to **military reforms** and **revenue reforms**.
xa: At the **Battle of Kili**, **Zafar Khan** was killed.
Alauddin built **Siri** as a new capital; **Ghazi Malik** was made governor of **Punjab**.
Ghazi Malik chased the Mongols **29 times**, later becoming **Ghiyasuddin Tughluq**.

106.s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Genghis Khan reached the Indus during Iltutmish's reign.
Statement B: Genghis Khan invaded India in 1398 CE.
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
106.x: A is true: Genghis Khan reached the Indus around 1221, under Iltutmish. B is false because the 1398 invasion was by Timur, not Genghis Khan.
106.tq: Discriminate Genghis Khan from Timur.
n: Genghis Khan reached the Indus during Iltutmish's reign. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #67 · pp 143-144]
Timur, also known as Taimur, invaded India in 1398 CE. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #67 · pp 143-144]
xs: **Statement A is true, Statement B is false** — so option **(3)** is correct.
A: **Genghis Khan** reached the **Indus** in **Iltutmish's reign** (**1221 CE**) — the first Mongol threat.
B is false: the **1398** invasion was by **Timur**, not Genghis Khan.
xa: Timur's invasion **severely weakened** the Sultanate, under **Nasiruddin Mahmud Tughlaq**.
⚠ "First Mongol invasion under **Jalaluddin**" is **false** (UPSC **2022**).
Jalaluddin settled converted Mongols as **"New Mussalmans"**.

107.s: Alauddin Khalji's policy towards the Ulema is best described by which one of the following statements?
o: He made their approval compulsory for every market transaction.
He transferred the entire revenue administration to them.
He accepted their guidance in all matters of state administration.
He refused their guidance and declared that he would act in the interest of the state.
107.x: Alauddin Khalji refused to be guided by the Ulema in state policy and declared that his actions would be governed by the interests of the state.
107.tq: Discriminate between religious guidance and the Sultan's assertion of state interest.
xs: Alauddin **refused the guidance of the ulema** and declared he would **act in the interest of the state** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Policy was decided by **state needs, not religious advice** — Barani's **"State interest over Shariat"** position.
So the ulema neither ran revenue nor approved market deals.
xa: He revived **Balban's** harsh, centralised rule, but without Balban's dependence on **religious sanction**.
He took the title **Sikandar-i-Sani** (second Alexander).

107.s: The office of Ariz-i-Mamalik under Alauddin Khalji was associated principally with which department?
107.x: Ariz-i-Mamalik was the head of the army department. It was not a ministerial office concerned with law or religious endowments.
107.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to an administrative title.
xs: **Ariz-i-Mamalik** headed the **army department** — so option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ Some notes call it "minister of law" — a trap.
Under Jalaluddin, Alauddin held this post along with **Amir-i-Tuzuk**.
xa: The Ariz-i-Mumalik **recruited the standing army**.
**Diwan-i-Riyasat** ran the markets; **Diwan-i-Mustakhraj** recovered revenue arrears.

107.s:
Assertion (A): Alauddin Khalji revived Balban’s harsh and centralised style of rule.
Reason (R): Alauddin depended on religious sanction to justify every major state policy.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
107.x: Alauddin did revive a harsh and centralised style of rule, but unlike Balban he did not depend on religious sanction for his policies. Therefore, the Assertion is true and the Reason is false.
107.tq: Test a true comparison against a reversed explanation involving religious authority.
xs: **A is true but R is false** — so option **(3)** is correct.
A is true: Alauddin **revived Balban's harsh, centralised rule**.
R is false: he did it **without Balban's dependence on religious sanction**, overriding the **ulema**.
xa: He declared he would act in the **state's interest** whatever the ulema advised.
Kotwal **Ala-ul-Mulk** talked him out of world conquest and a **new religion**.

107.s: Alauddin Khalji defeated the Mongols at which of the following places in 1298, 1299, 1305 and 1306 respectively?
107.x: The Mongol defeats associated with the four years were Jalandhar in 1298, Kili in 1299, Amroha in 1305 and Ravi in 1306.
107.tq: Match each year with its place and reject sequences with swapped battle sites.
xs: The victories were **Jalandhar, Kili, Amroha and Ravi** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Jalandhar 1298**, **Kili 1299**.
xa: During one invasion he took shelter in **Siri** fort.
He **repaired old frontier forts** and built new ones, completing Balban's frontier policy.

107.s: Who persuaded Alauddin Khalji to abandon both his plans for world conquest and a new religion?
107.x: Kotwal Ala-ul-Mulk talked Alauddin out of both the plan for world conquest and the proposal for a new religion.
107.tq: Identify the adviser associated with restraining a ruler’s ambitious proposal.
xs: **Kotwal Ala-ul-Mulk** talked Alauddin out of **world conquest** and a **new religion** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Alauddin's world-conqueror dream gave him the title **Sikandar-i-Sani**.
xa: ⚠ **Nusrat Khan** acquired **Malik Kafur**; **Barani** is the main source on the market control.
Alauddin openly overrode the **ulema** in state matters.

107.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes dagh from huliya or chehra?
o: Dagh was the cash payment of soldiers, whereas huliya was the recruitment of cavalry.
Dagh was a land-revenue assessment, whereas huliya recorded the wealth of nobles.
Dagh was the registration of peasants, whereas huliya was the measurement of land.
Dagh was the branding of horses, whereas huliya was the descriptive roll of soldiers.
107.x: Dagh referred to branding horses and huliya or chehra to the descriptive roll of each soldier. Neither was a land-revenue measure or an assessment of nobles’ wealth.
107.tq: Discriminate between two closely associated military terms.
xs: **Dagh** = **branding of horses**; **huliya / chehra** = **descriptive roll of each soldier** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Both stopped **fraud / false musters**.
⚠ Notes that call dagh a land-revenue measure, or huliya an assessment of nobles' wealth, are wrong.
xa: Alauddin was the **first Sultan** to keep a large **permanent standing army**, paid in **cash**.
The Bahmani minister **Mahmud Gawan** later brought in **dagh and chehra**.

107.s: Which ruler is associated with the creation of the first standing army paid in cash, along with the systems of dagh and huliya?
107.x: Alauddin Khalji created the first standing army paid in cash and introduced dagh and huliya in military administration.
107.tq: Link the military reform, payment method and identifying administrative terms to one ruler.
xs: **Alauddin Khalji** created the first standing army paid in **cash**, with **dagh** and **huliya** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was recruited by the **Ariz-i-Mumalik** (army minister).
xa: Ferishta puts its cavalry at about **4,75,000**.
Dagh = **branding of horses**; huliya = **descriptive roll** of soldiers.

107.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the markets regulated under Alauddin Khalji:

List-I (Market)

a. Mandi
b. Sarai Adl
c. Third market
d. Fourth market

List-II (Goods)

i. Miscellaneous goods
ii. Horses, slaves and cattle
iii. Food grains
iv. Cloth, sugar, dry fruits, butter and oil

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
107.x: Mandi dealt with food grains, Sarai Adl with cloth and other specified commodities, the third market with horses, slaves and cattle, and the fourth market with miscellaneous goods.
107.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes with a swapped market and commodity.
xs: The code is **a–iii, b–iv, c–ii, d–i** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Mandi** — **food grains**; **Sarai Adl** — **cloth, sugar, dry fruits, butter, oil**.
**Third market** — **horses, slaves, cattle**; **fourth market** — **miscellaneous goods**.
xa: ⚠ **Mandi** = grain; **Sarai Adl** = cloth and other goods.
Each market had a **Shahna-i-Mandi** (superintendent).

107.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the four-point framework of Alauddin Khalji's market regulations?
o: Rationing, abolition of markets, compulsory barter and withdrawal of officials
Price fixation, guaranteed supply, controlled distribution and abolition of monopolies
Price fixation, abolition of state granaries, free trade and reduction of taxation
Free pricing, private storage, unrestricted distribution and expansion of monopolies
107.x: The regulations sought to fix prices, guarantee supply, control distribution and end monopolistic practices through official supervision.
107.tq: Choose the option that combines the four linked policy components without reversing their purpose.
xs: The four points: **price fixation, guaranteed supply, controlled distribution and abolition of monopolies** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Supply was guaranteed through **state granaries**; enforcement through officials and a **separate administration**.
xa: Aim: keep a large army on **low, fixed salaries** (APPSC G2 **2017** key).
The granaries are called the **first public distribution system** of the Sultanate (BPSC **2020**).

107.s:
With reference to the administration of the regulated markets, consider the following statements:
1. The Shahna-i-Mandi was the superintendent of an individual market.
2. The entire market system functioned under the Diwan-i-Riyasat.
3. The Diwan-i-Riyasat functioned under the Naib-i-Riyasat.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: The Shahna-i-Mandi supervised each market, while the overall system was administered by the Diwan-i-Riyasat under the Naib-i-Riyasat.
107.tq: Check the administrative hierarchy from the market superintendent upward.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is the answer.
1: the **Shahna-i-Mandi** was superintendent of each market, helped by an intelligence officer.
2 and 3: the whole system ran under the **Diwan-i-Riyasat**, headed by the **Naib-i-Riyasat**.
xa: **Barids** (intelligence officers) and **munhiyan** (secret spies) sent daily reports.
⚠ **Diwan-i-Riyasat** = markets; **Diwan-i-Mustakhraj** = revenue arrears.

107.s:
Consider the following statements about Alauddin Khalji's market control:
1. Government granaries held stocks, and rationing was used in times of scarcity.
2. Barani is the main source for these measures.
3. Mubarak Shah tightened the price controls after Alauddin's death.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
107.x: Statement 1 is correct: state granaries held stocks and grain was rationed in scarcity. Statement 2 is correct: Barani is the main source. Statement 3 is wrong: Mubarak Shah abolished the controls; prices had stayed stable during Alauddin's reign. So '1 and 2 only'.
107.tq: Mubarak Shah (1316-20) undid Alauddin's controls; he did not tighten them.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — so option **(1) 1 and 2 only** is the answer.
1 is correct: **government granaries** held stocks, with **rationing** in scarcity.
2 is correct: **Barani** is the main source.
3 is wrong: **Mubarak Shah (1316-20)** **abolished** the price controls.
xa: UPPSC keys call the market control **"highly successful"**.
Prices stayed **stable** during Alauddin's reign.

107.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
107.x: The Shahna-i-Mandi supervised a market. Land-revenue arrears were recovered by the Diwan-i-Mustakhraj, whereas barids, munhiyans and slave boys helped monitor market compliance.
107.tq: Find the official assigned to a different department rather than confusing market surveillance with revenue administration.
xs: **Shahna-i-Mandi — collection of land-revenue arrears** is wrong — so option **(1)** is the answer.
The Shahna-i-Mandi was **superintendent of a market**; arrears were recovered by the **Diwan-i-Mustakhraj**.
The rest are correct: **slave boys** made **test purchases**; **munhiyans** were **secret spies**; **barids** sent intelligence reports.
xa: Cheating merchants were **punished**.
The market system ran under the **Diwan-i-Riyasat**.

107.s: The principal objective of Alauddin Khalji's market control regulations was to:
o: increase the profits of grain merchants in Delhi
maintain a large standing army on low, fixed salaries by keeping prices low
raise revenue for the construction of mosques and madrasas
promote free trade with Central Asian merchants
107.x: Prices of daily goods were lowered and fixed so that soldiers could live comfortably on low, fixed pay; military need shaped the economic policy. The regulations curbed merchants rather than enriching them, and they were not aimed at religious building or free trade.
107.tq: Cheap goods for a cheap army (APPSC G2 2017).
xs: The aim was to **maintain a large standing army on low, fixed salaries** by keeping prices low — so option **(2)** is correct.
Soldiers could live comfortably on low pay (APPSC G2 **2017** key); **military need shaped economic policy**.
The controls curbed merchants and **ended monopolies** — not merchant profit or free trade.
xa: Criticism: the controls may have been **confined to Delhi** and hurt **merchants and peasants**.
Mubarak Shah abolished them after **1316**.

107.s:
Consider the following statements about Alauddin Khalji's land revenue:
1. He was the first Sultan to measure land, with the biswa as the standard unit.
2. The state's share (kharaj) was fixed at one-third of the produce.
3. Revenue was assessed on the measured area and the yield.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
107.x: Statement 1 is correct: Alauddin first measured land, using the biswa. Statement 2 is wrong: the state share was one-half (50%) of the produce. Statement 3 is correct: assessment used measured area and yield. So '1 and 3 only'.
107.tq: Alauddin's kharaj = HALF the produce, the highest share of the Sultanate period.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — so option **(2) 1 and 3 only** is the answer.
1 is correct: the **first Sultan to measure land**, using the **biswa**.
2 is wrong: the state share (**kharaj**) was **half (50%)** (BPSC **2018**); some notes say one-fifth.
3 is correct: assessed on **measured area + yield**.
xa: New taxes: **ghari** (house) and **charai** (grazing); **jizya** continued.
Resumed **inam** and **waqf** grants enlarged the **khalisa**.

107.s: Which officer was associated with the recovery of arrears from revenue officials?
107.x: The Diwan-i-Mustakhraj was established to recover arrears from revenue officials. The Diwan-i-Riyasat was concerned with market administration.
107.tq: Separate the similarly named market and revenue departments by their functions.
xs: The **Diwan-i-Mustakhraj** recovered **arrears from revenue officials** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **Diwan-i-Riyasat** (under the **Naib-i-Riyasat**) ran the markets; the **Shahna-i-Mandi** supervised one market.
xa: ⚠ **Diwan-i-Riyasat** = markets; **Diwan-i-Mustakhraj** = revenue arrears.
**Malik Naib** (deputy) was the rank **Malik Kafur** rose to.

107.s:
With reference to the position of village intermediaries under Alauddin Khalji, consider the following statements:
1. Khuts, muqaddams and chaudharis had to pay taxes like other taxpayers.
2. The kismat-i-khuti, or headman's cess, was abolished.
3. The reform enabled rich peasants to transfer the entire tax burden to poorer peasants.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: Khuts, muqaddams and chaudharis were brought under taxation, and the headman's cess was abolished. The reform prevented rich peasants from passing the burden on to others, so statement 3 is false.
107.tq: Watch for the reversed effect in the final statement and test the reform's stated purpose.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — so option **(1) 1 and 2 only** is the answer.
1 is correct: **khuts, muqaddams and chaudharis** paid the same taxes as others.
2 is correct: the **kismat-i-khuti** (headman's cess) was abolished.
3 is wrong: the reform meant **rich peasants could not pass on the burden**.
xa: The state share (**kharaj**) was **half** of produce.
Land was measured in **biswa**.

107.s:
Barani attributed the possibility of revolts during Alauddin Khalji's reign to which combination of factors?
1. Wealth of the nobles
2. Marriages and social gatherings among nobles
3. Weakness of the spy system
4. Drinking

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
107.x: Barani identified noble wealth, noble intermarriage and gatherings, a weak intelligence system and drinking as four causes of revolt perceived by Alauddin.
107.tq: Treat the complete four-item list as the unit and check whether any listed cause is omitted.
xs: All four were causes — so option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4** is the answer.
Barani's causes: **nobles' wealth**, **intermarriage and social gatherings of nobles**.
Also a **weak spy system** and **drinking**.
xa: Answers: confiscated **inam, waqf**; reorganised **spies**; **prohibited liquor**, gambling; royal permission for feasts and marriages.
APPSC G1 **2018**: prohibition + market control + severe punishment = **Alauddin**.

107.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the measures included in Alauddin Khalji's ordinances?
o: Permission for nobles to form unrestricted marriage alliances
Confiscation of religious grants and free lands
107.x: Alauddin reorganised espionage, prohibited liquor and gambling, and confiscated religious grants and free lands. Noble marriages and gatherings required royal permission.
107.tq: Identify the option that reverses a restrictive ordinance into a permission.
xs: **Unrestricted marriage alliances** for nobles were not allowed — so option **(1)** is the answer.
Feasts, gatherings and **marriage alliances** needed **royal permission**.
The other three were real ordinances: confiscating **inam, waqf**; reorganising the **spy system**; **prohibiting liquor** and gambling.
xa: Offenders got **severe punishment**; rape was punished severely.
The causes come from **Barani**.

107.s: Prohibition of liquor and gambling, control of markets and severe punishment of offenders are associated with which Delhi Sultan?
107.x: All three measures belong to Alauddin Khalji: his ordinances prohibited liquor and gambling, he regulated the markets, and offenders were punished severely. Balban was harsh but did not control markets; Muhammad bin Tughlaq and Firoz did not impose these measures together.
107.tq: Prohibition + market control = Alauddin (APPSC G1 2018).
xs: Prohibition, market control and severe punishment = **Alauddin Khalji** (APPSC G1 **2018**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
His ordinances **prohibited liquor**, intoxicants and gambling.
His **market control** fixed prices for a cheap standing army.
xa: Barani's four causes of revolt: **wealth**, **intermarriage**, **weak spies**, **drinking**.
**Mubarak Shah** withdrew the harsh regulations after **1316**.

107.s:
Consider the following statements about Malik Kafur's second expedition against Warangal:
1. It took place in 1309–10.
2. Khwaja Haji accompanied Malik Kafur.
3. Prataparudra accepted a treaty and agreed to pay annual tribute.
4. The captured wealth was sent to Delhi on 1,000 camels.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: All four statements are correct. Malik Kafur and Khwaja Haji besieged Warangal, obtained Prataparudra's submission and sent the loot to Delhi on 1,000 camels.
107.tq: Test a campaign through its date, companion, settlement and numerical detail.
xs: All four statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4** is the answer.
1, 2: in **1309-10** **Kafur** and **Khwaja Haji** besieged Warangal.
3: **Prataparudra** accepted a **treaty** and **annual tribute**.
4: the loot went to Delhi on **1,000 camels**.
xa: By tradition the **Koh-i-Noor** was part of the Kakatiya treasure surrendered in **1310**.
**Amir Khusrau** went with the 1310 campaign.

107.s: What was the principal purpose of Alauddin Khalji's Deccan expeditions according to the policy described?
o: To obtain plunder and tribute for maintaining the army
To establish permanent provinces ruled by Delhi governors
To transfer the Delhi capital to Warangal
To spread a new religious order in the southern kingdoms
107.x: The Deccan expeditions were primarily financial ventures intended to secure plunder and tribute for paying the army, rather than to annex the southern states.
107.tq: Distinguish the stated economic objective from the stronger but incorrect claim of annexation.
xs: The aim was **plunder and tribute** to pay for the **army** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was **not annexation**: southern kings **kept their thrones** and paid tribute.
xa: **Ramachandra** of Devagiri and **Prataparudra II** of Warangal both agreed to tribute.
The **Pandya** kingdom of Madurai was **sacked** (**1311**).

107.s:
Consider the following statements about Amir Khusrau and the Warangal campaign:
1. Amir Khusrau went with Malik Kafur's 1310 campaign against Warangal.
2. His Khazain-ul-Futuh describes Warangal as a fort with a single mud wall and no moat.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
107.x: Statement 1 is correct: Amir Khusrau accompanied the 1310 Warangal campaign. Statement 2 is wrong: Khazain-ul-Futuh describes Warangal's double-walled fort, its moat and the diamond mines. So '1 only'.
107.tq: Khazain-ul-Futuh on Warangal = double walls + moat + diamond mines.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — so option **(1) 1 only** is the answer.
1 is correct: **Amir Khusrau** went with the **1310** campaign.
2 is wrong: **Khazain-ul-Futuh** describes Warangal's **double-walled fort**, **moat** and **diamond mines**.
xa: The **1309-10** siege by Kafur and **Khwaja Haji** made **Prataparudra** a tributary.
Traditionally the **Koh-i-Noor** was surrendered in **1310**.

107.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Deccan campaign)
A. Devagiri
B. Warangal
C. Dwarasamudra
D. Madurai

List-II (Ruler or outcome)
I. Vira Ballala III
II. Pandya kingdom sacked
III. Ramachandra
IV. Prataparudra II

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
107.x: Devagiri was ruled by Ramachandra, Warangal by Prataparudra II, Dwarasamudra by Vira Ballala III, and the Pandya kingdom of Madurai was sacked.
107.tq: Start with the distinctive outcome ‘Pandya kingdom sacked’ and complete the ruler pairs.
xs: The code is **A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Devagiri — Ramachandra**; **Warangal — Prataparudra II**.
**Dwarasamudra — Vira Ballala III**; **Madurai — Pandya kingdom sacked**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes call the Kakatiya king "**Prataparudradeva I**".

107.s: Which one of the following statements about Malik Kafur is correct?
o: He was a eunuch, later rose to Malik Naib, and participated in the Deccan campaigns.
He was a court historian who wrote Futuh-us-Salatin.
He was a hereditary Rajput commander who became governor of Kara.
He was the Kakatiya ruler who negotiated tribute with Delhi.
107.x: Malik Kafur was a eunuch purchased during the Gujarat campaign, later rose to Malik Naib and led important Deccan campaigns.
107.tq: Reject options that swap a commander’s identity with a ruler, historian or earlier officer.
xs: Malik Kafur **was a eunuch, rose to Malik Naib, and led the Deccan campaigns** — so option **(1)** is correct.
He was acquired by **Nusrat Khan** in the **1299** Gujarat campaign.
The Kakatiya ruler who paid tribute was **Prataparudra II**; Kara was **Alauddin's** governorship.
xa: He was called **"Hazar Dinari"** — bought for **1,000** dinars.
His campaigns aimed at **plunder and tribute**.

107.s: Which Sultan abolished Alauddin Khalji’s price controls, restored confiscated lands and withdrew harsh regulations after ascending the throne?
107.x: Mubarak Shah, who ruled from 1316 to 1320, abolished the price controls, restored confiscated lands and withdrew the harsh regulations.
107.tq: Link a ruler with the specific reversal of a predecessor’s measures.
xs: **Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah (1316-20)** reversed Alauddin's system — so option **(3)** is correct.
He **abolished price controls**, **restored confiscated lands** and **withdrew harsh regulations**.
xa: Alauddin died in **1316**; the dynasty fell soon after.
Under Alauddin **prices stayed stable** and the army beat the Mongols.

107.s: Which one of the following best explains the contradictory effects of Alauddin Khalji’s reforms?
o: They weakened the army but eliminated all opposition among the nobles.
They raised prices and ended the use of spies, but strengthened provincial autonomy.
They benefited merchants and peasants while weakening the central government.
They kept prices low and strengthened the army, but espionage and repression generated discontent.
107.x: The reforms helped maintain low prices and a strong army capable of resisting the Mongols, but repression and espionage created widespread discontent.
107.tq: Balance positive and negative consequences instead of selecting a one-sided claim.
xs: The reforms **kept prices low and strengthened the army, but espionage and repression bred discontent** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The army became strong enough to **beat the Mongols**.
**Rule by espionage + repression** hollowed out the state.
xa: The dynasty **fell soon after his death in 1316**.
Criticism: controls may have been **confined to Delhi**, and they hurt **merchants and peasants**.

107.s: Which one of the following pairs of Delhi Sultanate dynasties and their key contribution is NOT correctly matched?
o: Khaljis — Market control and taxation reforms
Tughlaqs — Token currency, transfer of capital and canals
Lodis — First Turkish dynasty and founding of Daulatabad
Tomaras — Delhi became an important commercial centre
107.x: The Lodis were the first Afghan dynasty and Agra was founded under them, so the third pair is wrong. The Khaljis are known for market control, the Tughlaqs for token currency, capital transfer and canals, and under the Tomaras Delhi became an important commercial centre.
107.tq: Lodis = first Afghan dynasty, Agra.
xs: **Lodis — first Turkish dynasty and Daulatabad** is wrong — so option **(3)** is the answer.
The **Lodis** were the **first Afghan** dynasty and **Agra** was founded under them.
The rest are correct: **Khaljis** — **market control**; **Tughlaqs** — **token currency, capital transfer, canals**; **Tomaras** — **Delhi** as a commercial centre.
xa: Khaljis' contribution also included **taxation reforms**.
Alauddin's reign = the **"imperial period"**.

107.s: The first attack on Warangal in 1303 ended in failure at Upparapalli. Which pair of Kakatiya commanders defeated Malik Fakhruddin Juna there?
o: Hamir Deva and Rana Ratan Singh
107.x: Potuganti Maili and Recherla Venna defeated Malik Fakhruddin Juna at Upparapalli during the failed 1303 attack on Warangal.
107.tq: Use the local commanders as the decisive clue in an Andhra-specific military question.
xs: **Potuganti Maili and Recherla Venna** beat **Malik Fakhruddin Juna** at **Upparapalli** (**1303**) — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Ramachandra** and **Vira Ballala III** were Yadava and Hoysala kings; **Hamir Deva** and **Ratan Singh** were Rajputs.
xa: The **1309-10** attack made **Prataparudra** a tributary.
⚠ **1303** = Delhi defeated; **1309-10** = treaty and **annual tribute**.

107.s: Which of the following is regarded as a major significance of Alauddin Khalji’s economic and revenue measures?
o: They made religious institutions solely responsible for land measurement.
They introduced paper currency and decentralised all revenue administration.
They introduced the first state-run price-control and rationing system in India and the first land measurement for revenue.
They abolished all forms of taxation and ended state supervision of markets.
107.x: Alauddin’s measures are regarded as the first state-run price-control and rationing system in India and the first land measurement system for revenue assessment.
107.tq: Select the option containing both linked historical significances without an exaggerated claim.
xs: They were the **first state-run price control and rationing system** in India and the **first land measurement for revenue** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Land was measured in **biswa**; granaries rationed grain in scarcity.
There was no paper currency and no end of taxation — taxes like **ghari** and **charai** were added.
xa: His reign = **"imperial period"** of the Sultanate.
Despotism and heavy spying hollowed out the state.

107.s: Which criticism is associated with Alauddin Khalji’s market controls?
o: They operated only in the Deccan and made the army prohibitively expensive.
They benefited merchants and peasants by removing all state interference.
They may have been confined to Delhi and imposed hardship on merchants and peasants to keep the army inexpensive.
They were limited to religious goods and had no relation to military expenditure.
107.x: The controls may have been confined to Delhi and were criticised for hurting merchants and peasants while helping maintain a cheap army.
107.tq: Combine the geographical qualification with the principal criticism of the policy.
xs: The controls **may have been confined to Delhi** and **hurt merchants and peasants** to keep the army cheap — so option **(3)** is correct.
They were meant for the **army**, not limited to religious goods or the Deccan.
xa: UPPSC keys still call the market control **"highly successful"**; **Barani** is the main source.
Effects: **stable prices** and an army strong enough to beat the Mongols.

107.s: Alauddin Khalji’s reign is often called the ‘imperial period’ of the Delhi Sultanate mainly because it was marked by:
o: the replacement of the Sultanate by the Bahmani kingdom
the exclusive supremacy of the ulema over state policy
extensive conquests, strong centralisation and imperial ambitions
the abandonment of expansion and the growth of provincial independence
107.x: Alauddin’s extensive conquests, centralised administration, strong army and imperial ambitions led his reign to be described as the imperial period of the Sultanate.
107.tq: Infer the historical label from the cluster of policies and achievements.
xs: The reign shows **extensive conquests, strong centralisation and imperial ambitions** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Alauddin dreamed of being **Sikandar-i-Sani** and ran **harsh, centralised** rule.
The **ulema** were overridden, not supreme.
xa: Firsts: **state-run price control**, **rationing**, **land measurement** for revenue.
Kafur's campaigns reached **Madurai** (**1311**).

107.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding Alauddin Khalji's revenue measures?
o: The privileges of Khutt, Mukaddam and Chaudhary were expanded to strengthen intermediaries.
His measures weakened the role of traditional intermediary tax collectors.
The traditional tax-collection privileges of Khutt, Mukaddam and Chaudhary were abolished.
Revenue was collected more directly by weakening intermediary tax collectors.
107.x: Option A is incorrect: Alauddin Khalji abolished, not expanded, the privileges of the Khuts, Muqaddams and Chaudharis. This weakened the intermediaries and let the state collect revenue more directly.
107.tq: Check what happened to the intermediaries' privileges.
n: Alauddin Khalji abolished the traditional tax-collection privileges of Khutts, Mukaddams, and Chaudharys. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
Alauddin Khalji collected revenue more directly after abolishing the privileges of Khutts, Mukaddams, and Chaudharys. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
Alauddin Khalji's policy weakened intermediary tax collectors. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
xs: The incorrect statement is that the privileges of **Khutt, Mukaddam and Chaudhary** were **expanded** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Alauddin Khalji** **abolished** their **traditional tax-collection privileges**, **weakening intermediary tax collectors**.
Revenue was thus **collected more directly** — options **(2)**, **(3)** and **(4)** are true.
xa: The intermediaries had to pay the **same taxes** as others; **Kismat-i-khuti** (headman's cess) was abolished.
He was the **first Sultan** linked with **systematic land measurement**; standard unit = **biswa**.
**Diwan-i-Mustakharaj** recovered **arrears** from revenue officials.

107.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Milq and Waqf lands
(b) Kharaj
(c) Ghari
(d) Charai

List-II
(i) House tax
(ii) Reclaimed for expansion of Khalisa land
(iii) Grazing tax on milch animals
(iv) 50% of yield as land tax
107.x: Alauddin reclaimed Milk and Waqf lands into Khalisa, fixed Kharaj at 50% of the yield, and levied Ghari as house tax and Charai as grazing tax on milch animals, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.
107.tq: Recall the meaning of each Khalji tax term.
n: Alauddin Khalji reclaimed Milq lands. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
Alauddin Khalji reclaimed Waqf lands. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
The reclamation of Milq and Waqf lands expanded Khalisa land. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
Kharaj was a land tax under Alauddin Khalji. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
Kharaj was fixed at 50% of the yield under Alauddin Khalji. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
Ghari was a house tax under Alauddin Khalji. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
Charai was a grazing tax on milch animals under Alauddin Khalji. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
xs: The correct match is **a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Milq and Waqf lands** were **reclaimed** to expand **Khalisa** land; **Kharaj** = land tax at **50%** of yield.
**Ghari** = **house tax**; **Charai** = **grazing tax** on **milch animals**.
xa: ⚠ **Ghari** = house; **Charai** = grazing.
**Khalisa** = crown land, grew as **inam, waqf** grants were resumed.
**Jizya** continued; ⚠ some notes give the state share as one-fifth.
State share of **half (50%)**: BPSC **2018**.

108.s:
Consider the following statements about Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq:
1. Earlier called Ghazi Malik, he was the son of a Turkish slave and a Rajput woman.
2. Under Alauddin Khalji he was governor of Punjab against the Mongols.
3. He became Sultan in 1320 after killing Khusrau Shah.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
108.x: Statement 1 is wrong: Ghazi Malik was the son of a Turkish slave and a Jat woman. Statement 2 is correct: he governed Punjab against the Mongols. Statement 3 is correct: he killed Khusrau Shah and became Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq Shah in 1320. So '2 and 3 only'.
108.tq: Ghazi Malik = Turkish father + JAT mother; Punjab governor; Sultan in 1320.
xs: Statements 2 and 3 are correct — so option **(3) 2 and 3 only** is the answer.
1 is wrong: **Ghazi Malik** was the son of a Turkish slave and a **Jat** woman, not a Rajput.
2 is correct: under Alauddin he was **governor of Punjab** against the Mongols.
3 is correct: he killed **Khusrau Shah** and became **Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq Shah in 1320**.
xa: He built the **Tughlaqabad** fort.
He was the **first Sultan to start irrigation/canal works**.

108.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq's agrarian policy?
o: Immediate and unlimited enhancement of land revenue
108.x: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq limited any increase in land revenue to about one-tenth and raised it gradually. He also resumed unlawful grants, granted drought remission and encouraged cultivation of waste land.
108.tq: Reject the extreme statement that reverses a cautious revenue policy.
xs: **Immediate and unlimited enhancement of land revenue** was not his policy — so option **(4)** is the answer.
He **limited the rise to about one-tenth**, raised gradually.
He did **take back unlawful grants**, give **remission in drought** and bring **waste land** under the plough.
xa: He was the **first Sultan to start canal works**; **Firoz** dug the most.
He improved the **postal system** with runners and horsemen.

108.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Warangal fell after a five-month siege.
B. Juna Khan first attacked Warangal.
C. Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq became Sultan.
D. Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq died at Afghanpur.
108.x: Ghiyasuddin became Sultan in 1320, Juna Khan attacked Warangal in 1321–22, Warangal fell in 1323, and Ghiyasuddin died in 1325.
108.tq: Fix the first and last dates, then place the Warangal events between them.
xs: The order is **C, B, A, D** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Ghiyasuddin became Sultan in **1320** → **Juna Khan** attacked Warangal in **1321-22**.
→ Warangal fell after a **5-month** siege in **1323** → he died at **Afghanpur** in **1325**.
xa: Juna Khan's first attack failed when **false news of the Sultan's death** caused a retreat.
⚠ **Ibn Battuta** suspects a plot by Juna Khan in the pavilion collapse.

108.s: Warangal was renamed Sultanpur after it was conquered during the reign of
108.x: Warangal fell in 1323 during Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq's reign and was renamed Sultanpur.
108.tq: Link the conquered place, its new name and the ruler responsible for the conquest.
xs: Warangal fell in **1323** under **Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq** and was renamed **Sultanpur** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The attack was led by Prince **Juna Khan** (later **Muhammad bin Tughlaq**).
xa: Andhra was then run by **Malik Burhanuddin** of Devagiri, assisted by **Malik Maqbul**.
**Prataparudra II** was taken towards Delhi and died in the **Narmada**.

108.s:
Consider the following statements about Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq:
1. He built the Tughlaqabad fort.
2. He had cordial relations with Nizamuddin Auliya.
3. He died in 1325 when a wooden pavilion collapsed at Afghanpur.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
108.x: Statement 1 is correct: Ghiyasuddin built Tughlaqabad. Statement 2 is wrong: his relations with Nizamuddin Auliya were strained. Statement 3 is correct: he died at Afghanpur in 1325 when a wooden pavilion collapsed (Ibn Battuta suspected Juna Khan). So '1 and 3 only'.
108.tq: Ghiyasuddin: Tughlaqabad, strained ties with Nizamuddin Auliya, Afghanpur pavilion death.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — so option **(2) 1 and 3 only** is the answer.
1 is correct: he built **Tughlaqabad** fort.
2 is wrong: his relations with **Nizamuddin Auliya** were **strained**.
3 is correct: a **wooden pavilion collapsed at Afghanpur** in **1325**.
xa: **Ibn Battuta** suspects a plot by **Juna Khan**.
Cities of Delhi: **Siri** — **Alauddin Khalji**; **Tughlaqabad** — **Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq**.

108.s:
Arrange the following experiments of Muhammad bin Tughlaq in chronological order:
A. Introduction of token currency
B. Transfer of the capital to Devagiri
C. Khurasan expedition
D. Qarachil expedition

Select the correct sequence.
108.x: The capital was transferred in 1327, token currency was introduced around 1329–30, and the Khurasan and Qarachil experiments followed.
108.tq: Fix the dated capital transfer and token currency first, then place the later expeditions.
xs: The order is **B, A, C, D** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Transfer of capital** to Devagiri (**1327**) → **token currency** (c. **1329-30**).
→ **Khurasan** expedition → **Qarachil** expedition.
xa: Khurasan: a huge army raised, then **disbanded unpaid / unused**.
Qarachil (**Kumaon** hills): **army destroyed in the hills**.

108.s: The token currency introduced by Muhammad bin Tughlaq around 1329–30 consisted of:
o: Gold and silver coins issued to overcome a gold shortage
Silver and copper coins issued exclusively for the army
Copper and brass coins intended to function as tokens
Lead and potin coins modelled on Satavahana currency
108.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq introduced token currency in copper and brass because of a shortage of silver. Widespread forgery led to its recall and redemption at heavy cost.
108.tq: Discriminate the metal composition and the economic purpose of the token currency.
xs: The token currency was of **copper and brass**, meant to function as tokens — so option **(3)** is correct.
Cause: a **silver shortage** and the idea of a token coin.
Result: **mass forgery**; the coins were **recalled and redeemed at heavy cost** to the treasury.
xa: It came c. **1329-30**, after the move to Daulatabad (**1327**).
Exam line: "token currency was **copper and brass**".

108.s:
Consider the following statements about Muhammad bin Tughlaq's taxation of the Doab:
1. The tax increase was intended to secure more revenue.
2. It coincided with a famine.
3. Peasants revolted and fled as a consequence.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
108.x: The higher Doab taxation aimed at increasing revenue, but it coincided with famine and led to peasant revolts and flight.
108.tq: Trace the complete aim–circumstance–consequence sequence.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is the answer.
1: the **Doab tax rise** aimed at **more revenue**.
2: it **coincided with a famine**.
3: **peasants revolted and fled**.
xa: During the famine the Sultan moved to the **Swarga-dwari** relief camp on the **Ganga** near **Kannauj**.
**Taqavi** (sondhar) loans for seed and wells came from MBT.

108.s:
Consider the following pairs of Muhammad bin Tughlaq's experiments and their aims:
1. Khurasan expedition - conquest in Central Asia
2. Qarachil expedition - securing the hill frontier
3. Transfer of capital to Devagiri - escaping the Doab famine
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
108.x: Pair 1 is correct: the Khurasan expedition aimed at conquest in Central Asia. Pair 2 is correct: the Qarachil expedition (Kumaon hills) aimed to secure the hill frontier. Pair 3 is wrong: the capital moved to Devagiri to have a central base to control the Deccan, not to escape famine. So '1 and 2 only'.
108.tq: Match each experiment to its aim: Khurasan = Central Asia, Qarachil = hills, Daulatabad = Deccan control.
