xs: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct — so option **(1) 1 and 2 only** is the answer.
1 is correct: **Khurasan** — **conquest in Central Asia**.
2 is correct: **Qarachil** (Kumaon hills) — **securing the hill frontier**.
3 is wrong: Devagiri was meant as a **central base to control the Deccan**, not a famine escape.
xa: Khurasan army: **disbanded unpaid / unused**; Qarachil army: **destroyed in the hills**.
Barani called MBT a **"mixture of opposites"**.

108.s: During the famine associated with Muhammad bin Tughlaq's reign, the relief and cultivation camp near Kannauj on the Ganga was called:
108.x: Swarga-dwari was a famine-relief camp on the Ganga near Kannauj, established for relief and cultivation.
108.tq: Use the place-name association to distinguish a famine-relief camp from Firoz Shah's institutions and towns.
xs: The relief camp was **Swarga-dwari** (Swargadwari), on the **Ganga near Kannauj** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It gave **relief and cultivation** during the **Doab famine**.
**Dar-ul-Shifa** (free hospital) and **Diwan-i-Khairat** (charity) are **Firoz's**; **Firozabad** is his town.
xa: The **Doab tax rise** coincided with the famine; peasants revolted and fled.
MBT gave **taqavi** loans for **seed + wells**.

108.s: The Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi established by Muhammad bin Tughlaq was primarily concerned with
108.x: Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi was an agriculture department intended to extend cultivation, especially by bringing waste land under the plough.
108.tq: Identify the administrative department from the function assigned to it.
xs: **Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi** was MBT's **agriculture** department to **bring waste land under cultivation** — so option **(4)** is correct (UKPSC **2025**; UPPSC **2017**).
It also pushed farmers towards **better crops**.
Horse branding (**dagh**) and **market control** were **Alauddin's**; **jizya on Brahmins** was **Firoz's**.
xa: ⚠ **Diwan-i-Amir-Kohi** = MBT; **Diwan-i-Khairat** and **Diwan-i-Bandagan** = Firoz.
**Taqavi** loans were later **written off by Firoz**.

108.s: Taqavi, or sondhar, loans during Muhammad bin Tughlaq's reign were provided mainly for
108.x: Taqavi or sondhar loans were agricultural advances intended to help cultivators purchase seed and dig wells.
108.tq: Match the specialised administrative term with its precise practical purpose.
xs: **Taqavi** (sondhar) loans were for **seeds and wells** — so option **(4)** is correct.
They were MBT's state loans to cultivators.
xa: **Firoz** later **wrote off** MBT's taqavi loans and all debts owed to the state.
MBT's **Diwan-i-Amir-Kohi** worked to **extend cultivation**.

108.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Ibn Battuta's association with Muhammad bin Tughlaq?
o: He served as governor of Punjab and led the Warangal campaign.
He was the Sultan's chief revenue officer in the Doab.
He served as Qazi of Delhi and was later sent as envoy to China in 1342.
He succeeded Muhammad bin Tughlaq as Sultan.
108.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq appointed Ibn Battuta Qazi of Delhi and later sent him as an envoy to China in 1342.
108.tq: Separate an observer's administrative and diplomatic roles from military and succession roles.
xs: Ibn Battuta **served as Qazi of Delhi** and was sent as **envoy to China in 1342** — so option **(3)** is correct.
He came in MBT's reign in **1333**.
The **governor of Punjab** was **Ghazi Malik**; MBT's successor was **Firoz Shah**.
xa: He was a **Moroccan**, born at **Tangiers**, **1304**; real name **Abu Abdullah Muhammad**.
His **Rihla (Kitab-ul-Rehla)** is in **Arabic**.

108.s: According to Ibn Battuta's description of the postal system, which of the following is correct?
o: The system used only foot couriers at one-mile intervals.
Horse couriers travelled every mile and foot couriers every four miles.
Horse couriers were posted every four miles and foot couriers had three stations to every mile.
Both horse and foot couriers travelled every four miles.
108.x: Ibn Battuta recorded horse couriers called uluq at intervals of four miles and foot couriers called dawa at three stations to every mile.
108.tq: Discriminate between closely related numerical intervals and their corresponding terms.
xs: **Horse couriers every four miles; foot couriers at three stations to every mile** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Horse couriers = **uluq**; foot couriers = **dawa** (Ibn Battuta).
xa: ⚠ **Uluq** = horse; **dawa** = foot.
Ghiyasuddin had already improved the post with **runners + horsemen**.

108.s: Which of the following observations is associated with Ibn Battuta's account of the Delhi Sultanate?
o: Sati was permitted only to members of the royal family.
Sati was completely prohibited throughout the Sultanate.
Sati was not recorded by any contemporary traveller.
108.x: Ibn Battuta recorded the practice of sati and stated that it required the Sultan's permission.
108.tq: Select the precise recorded condition rather than an absolute statement about the practice.
xs: Ibn Battuta records that **sati required the Sultan's permission** — so option **(4)** is correct.
He also recorded the **spy system** and the **postal system**.
xa: He found MBT **eccentric**, **severe in temper**, but **generous**.
He was the **first foreign traveller** to visit **Vijayanagara**, in **Harihara I's** reign (APPSC PYQ).

108.s: Who described Muhammad bin Tughlaq as a 'mixture of opposites'?
108.x: Barani described Muhammad bin Tughlaq as a 'mixture of opposites'. Ibn Battuta characterised him as eccentric, severe in temper and generous.
108.tq: Separate the judgements of the court chronicler, foreign traveller and other contemporary figures.
xs: **Barani** called MBT a **"mixture of opposites"** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Ibn Battuta** called him **eccentric**, **quick-tempered**, but **generous**.
**Badauni** commented on his **death at Thatta (1351)**.
xa: Barani's **Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi** is the main account of these reigns.
Verdict: experiments **sound in idea, poor in execution**.

108.s: Ibn Battuta is described as the first foreign traveller to visit Vijayanagara during the reign of
108.x: Ibn Battuta is identified in this context as the first foreign traveller to visit Vijayanagara during the reign of Harihara I.
108.tq: Distinguish the earliest associated ruler from the more famous later Vijayanagara monarchs.
xs: Ibn Battuta was the first foreign traveller to visit Vijayanagara, in **Harihara I's** reign (APPSC PYQ) — so option **(2)** is correct.
Vijayanagara was founded in **1336** by **Harihara and Bukka**.
xa: He came to India in **1333** and served MBT as **Qazi of Delhi**.
He was sent as **envoy to China** in **1342**.

108.s: Which of the following statements about Ibn Battuta’s Rihla is correct?
o: It was written in Arabic and describes conditions in the Sultanate and the Deccan.
It was written in Persian and deals only with Central Asia.
It was written in Hindavi and describes only Vijayanagara.
It was written in Sanskrit under the patronage of Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
108.x: Rihla, also called Kitab-ul-Rehla, was written in Arabic and describes conditions in the Sultanate and the Deccan.
108.tq: Use the language-and-content combination to reject swapped literary traditions.
xs: Rihla **was written in Arabic and describes the Sultanate and the Deccan** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It is also called **Kitab-ul-Rehla**.
It was not Persian, Hindavi or Sanskrit.
xa: It records **uluq** and **dawa** couriers, the **spy system** and **sati**.
Its author, **Abu Abdullah Muhammad**, was a Moroccan born in **1304**.

108.s: Ibn Battuta, who came to India in 1333 during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq, was a native of:
108.x: Ibn Battuta (Abu Abdullah Muhammad) was a Moroccan, born at Tangiers in 1304. He came to India in 1333, was made Qazi of Delhi and wrote the Rihla in Arabic. He was not from Persia, Egypt or Turkey.
108.tq: Ibn Battuta = Morocco, Tangiers 1304.
xs: Ibn Battuta was from **Morocco** — so option **(2)** is correct.
He was born at **Tangiers** in **1304**; real name **Abu Abdullah Muhammad**.
He came in **1333** and was made **Qazi of Delhi**.
xa: He was sent as **envoy to China** (**1342**).
He wrote the **Rihla** in **Arabic**.

108.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Madurai Sultanate — 1335
2. Vijayanagara — 1336
3. Bahmani Kingdom — 1347
4. Musunuri recapture of Warangal — 1325
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
108.x: The Madurai Sultanate, Vijayanagara and Bahmani Kingdom are correctly associated with 1335, 1336 and 1347 respectively. The Musunuri recapture of Warangal occurred in 1336, not 1325.
108.tq: Find the one reversed date before selecting the coded combination.
xs: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct — so option **(1) 1, 2 and 3 only** is the answer.
**Madurai Sultanate — 1335**; **Vijayanagara — 1336**; **Bahmani — 1347**.
4 is wrong: the Musunuri recapture of Warangal was in **1336**; **1325** is the **Reddi** liberation of coastal Andhra.
xa: Madurai Sultanate: **Jalaluddin Ahsan Shah**.
Bahmani founder: **Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah** (**Hasan Gangu**).

108.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Coastal Andhra liberation — Prolaya Vema Reddi
Musunuri recapture of Warangal — Kapaya Nayaka
108.x: The Bahmani kingdom was founded by Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah. Jalaluddin Ahsan Shah was associated with the Madurai Sultanate.
108.tq: Find the incorrectly assigned founder among otherwise familiar state–leader pairs.
xs: **Bahmani kingdom — Jalaluddin Ahsan Shah** is wrong — so option **(3)** is the answer.
The Bahmani founder was **Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah** (Hasan Gangu); **Jalaluddin Ahsan Shah** founded the **Madurai Sultanate**.
The rest are correct: **Harihara and Bukka**; **Prolaya Vema Reddi**; **Kapaya Nayaka**.
xa: Years: Madurai **1335**, Vijayanagara **1336**, Bahmani **1347**.
Reddis freed coastal Andhra around **1325**.

108.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Establishment of the Bahmani kingdom
B. Expulsion of Tughlaq forces from coastal Andhra by the Reddis
C. Establishment of the Madurai Sultanate
D. Establishment of Vijayanagara
108.x: The order is coastal Andhra liberation around 1325, Madurai Sultanate in 1335, Vijayanagara in 1336 and Bahmani kingdom in 1347.
108.tq: Fix the dated milestones first and then arrange them from the earliest to the latest.
xs: The order is **B, C, D, A** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Reddi** expulsion from coastal Andhra (c. **1325**) → **Madurai Sultanate** (**1335**).
→ **Vijayanagara** (**1336**) → **Bahmani** kingdom (**1347**).
xa: **Kapaya Nayaka** recaptured Warangal also in **1336**.
These break-aways followed MBT's **badly carried out** schemes.

108.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the relationship between the founding of Vijayanagara and Muhammad bin Tughlaq?
o: Muhammad bin Tughlaq personally founded Vijayanagara under the guidance of Hasan Gangu.
Vidyaranya founded Vijayanagara as a provincial capital of the Madurai Sultanate.
Harihara and Bukka founded Vijayanagara after being appointed governors by Firoz Shah Tughlaq.
Harihara and Bukka, who had been sent by Muhammad bin Tughlaq, founded Vijayanagara under Vidyaranya's guidance.
108.x: Harihara and Bukka had been sent by Muhammad bin Tughlaq and later founded Vijayanagara under the guidance of Vidyaranya.
108.tq: Test the sequence of association—Tughlaq service, Vidyaranya's guidance and Vijayanagara foundation.
xs: **Harihara and Bukka, sent by Muhammad bin Tughlaq, founded Vijayanagara under Vidyaranya's guidance** — so option **(4)** is correct.
They were of the **Sangama** family; the year was **1336**.
**Hasan Gangu** founded the **Bahmani** kingdom; **Firoz** did not appoint them.
xa: **Ibn Battuta** visited Vijayanagara in **Harihara I's** reign.
⚠ In **1336** Kapaya Nayaka also recaptured **Warangal**.

108.s: Firoz Shah Tughlaq was placed on the throne at Thatta in 1351 after the death of:
108.x: Firoz Shah succeeded Muhammad bin Tughlaq at Thatta in 1351 and ruled until 1388.
108.tq: Test succession through a direct ruler-event association.
xs: Firoz was enthroned at **Thatta** after **Muhammad bin Tughlaq** died there (**1351**) — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Jam Babaniya** of **Sind** only agreed to pay tribute; **Haji Iliyas** was Bengal's ruler.
xa: Firoz ruled **1351-88**.
Badauni: on MBT's death the Sultan was **freed from his people, and they from him**.

108.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Department or institution)
a. Diwan-i-Khairat
b. Diwan-i-Bandagan
c. Dar-ul-Shifa
d. Diwan-i-Istihqaq

List-II (Function)
i. Pensions and grants to deserving persons
ii. Free hospital
iii. Charity and assistance in marriages of poor Muslim girls
iv. Department of slaves

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
108.x: Diwan-i-Khairat dealt with charity, Diwan-i-Bandagan with slaves, Dar-ul-Shifa was a free hospital, and Diwan-i-Istihqaq provided pensions and grants.
108.tq: Start from the sure pair, especially the distinctive hospital and slave departments.
xs: The code is **a–iii, b–iv, c–ii, d–i** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Diwan-i-Khairat** — charity, marriages of poor Muslim girls; **Diwan-i-Bandagan** — slaves.
**Dar-ul-Shifa** — free hospital; **Diwan-i-Istihqaq** — pensions and grants.
xa: Diwan-i-Bandagan had about **1,80,000** slaves in the Sultan's service.
Firoz also ran an **employment bureau** and a **Public Works Department** (APPSC G2 **2017**).

108.s: Which of the following statements about Firoz Shah Tughlaq's canal policy is correct?
o: He built canals mainly to connect Bengal with Sind.
He abolished irrigation charges and prohibited the construction of canals.
He built the largest number of canals among the Delhi Sultans and levied haq-i-sharb.
His canals were drawn only from the Ganga and the Narmada.
108.x: Firoz Shah built more canals than any other Delhi Sultan and imposed an irrigation cess called haq-i-sharb.
108.tq: Use the superlative and the named levy together, while rejecting reversed policy statements.
xs: Firoz **built the largest number of canals** and levied **haq-i-sharb** — so option **(3)** is correct (BPSC **2019**).
His canals ran from the **Yamuna and Sutlej to Hisar**, not the Ganga and Narmada.
**Haq-i-sharb** was an irrigation cess of **one-tenth**.
xa: ⚠ **Ghiyasuddin** was the **first** to dig canals; **Firoz** dug the **most**.
His **Public Works Department** ran the building programme.

108.s:
Consider the following statements about Firoz Shah Tughlaq's canals:
1. His canals carried water from the Yamuna and the Sutlej to Hisar.
2. The irrigation cess haq-i-sharb was one-fifth of the produce.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
108.x: Statement 1 is correct: his canals ran from the Yamuna and Sutlej to Hisar. Statement 2 is wrong: haq-i-sharb was one-tenth. So '1 only'.
108.tq: Haq-i-sharb = one-tenth; canals Yamuna + Sutlej to Hisar.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — so option **(1) 1 only** is the answer.
1 is correct: canals from the **Yamuna and Sutlej to Hisar**.
2 is wrong: **haq-i-sharb** was **one-tenth**, not one-fifth.
xa: Firoz built **more canals than any other Sultan** (BPSC **2019**).
His towns include **Hisar Firoza** and **Fatehabad**.

108.s: Which one of the following is NOT a town associated with Firoz Shah Tughlaq?
108.x: Firozabad, Fatehabad and Hisar Firoza were associated with Firoz Shah. Daulatabad was the renamed capital under Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
108.tq: Find the odd location by separating Firoz Shah's town-building from Muhammad bin Tughlaq's capital transfer.
xs: **Daulatabad** is not a Firoz town — so option **(1)** is the answer.
Daulatabad was **Devagiri**, renamed by **Muhammad bin Tughlaq** (**1327**).
Firoz founded **Firozabad** (Firoz Shah Kotla), **Fatehabad**, **Hisar Firoza** and **Jaunpur**.
xa: He laid about **1,200** fruit gardens around Delhi.
He moved **Ashokan pillars** from **Topra** and **Meerut** to Delhi.

108.s: The Ashokan pillars brought to Delhi during the reign of Firoz Shah Tughlaq came from:
108.x: Firoz Shah transported Ashokan pillars from Topra in the Ambala region and from Meerut to Delhi.
108.tq: Test the pair of source locations and reject the nearby religious and inscriptional sites.
xs: The Ashokan pillars came from **Topra** (Ambala) **and Meerut** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Jwalamukhi** at **Nagarkot** is where he seized **Sanskrit texts**, not pillars.
xa: Firoz founded **Firozabad** (Firoz Shah Kotla).
He laid about **1,200** fruit gardens around Delhi.

108.s: Firoz Shah Tughlaq's wazir Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul is noted for:
o: Paying compensation to people who had suffered under Muhammad bin Tughlaq
Introducing token currency in copper and brass
Leading the Qarachil expedition into the Kumaon hills
108.x: Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul paid compensation to persons who had suffered during Muhammad bin Tughlaq's rule.
108.tq: Identify the responsible official by matching the administrative action with the correct office-holder.
xs: **Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul** **paid compensation to people who had suffered under Muhammad bin Tughlaq** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The Nagarkot texts were translated by **Azizuddin Khalid Khani**; **token currency** and **Qarachil** were **MBT's**.
xa: Maqbul was the Brahmin **Jagannatha Pandit**, converted to Islam.
He had assisted **Malik Burhanuddin** at **Warangal** before becoming Firoz's chief minister.

108.s: Which Delhi Sultan set up a separate Public Works Department to run his building programme?
108.x: Firoz Shah Tughlaq created a Public Works Department for his canals, towns and buildings. Alauddin is known for market control, Muhammad bin Tughlaq for his experiments and Diwan-i-Amir-Kohi, and Sikandar Lodi for founding Agra.
108.tq: PWD = Firoz (APPSC G2 2017).
xs: **Firoz Shah Tughlaq** set up a **Public Works Department** for his buildings (APPSC G2 **2017**) — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Alauddin** is known for **market control** and **dagh**; **MBT** for **token currency** and **Diwan-i-Amir-Kohi**.
xa: Firoz's other departments: **Diwan-i-Khairat**, **Diwan-i-Bandagan**, **Dar-ul-Shifa**, **Diwan-i-Istihqaq**.
**Sikandar Lodi** had a Sanskrit medical treatise translated into Persian.

108.s:
Consider the following statements about Firoz Shah Tughlaq's revenue measures:
1. He wrote off Muhammad bin Tughlaq's taqavi loans.
2. He fixed land revenue permanently.
3. He retained the four Islamic taxes of kharaj, jizya, khams and zakat.
4. He made iqtas hereditary.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
108.x: All four statements are correct. Firoz wrote off taqavi loans and state debts, fixed land revenue, retained the four Islamic taxes, and made iqtas hereditary.
108.tq: Check the complete fiscal package instead of treating each reform as an isolated measure.
xs: All four statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4** is the answer.
1, 2: he **wrote off taqavi loans** and **fixed land revenue permanently**.
3: he kept only **kharaj, jizya, khams, zakat**, abolishing about **24** taxes.
4: he **made iqtas hereditary**.
xa: He levied **jizya** even on **Brahmins**, for the first time.
Hereditary iqtas and the slave corps **weakened central control**.

108.s: Which statement correctly describes the jizya policy of Firoz Shah Tughlaq?
o: He replaced jizya with the irrigation cess haq-i-sharb.
He abolished jizya for all non-Muslims.
He made jizya a separate tax and extended it to Brahmins.
He levied jizya only on Muslim peasants.
108.x: Firoz Shah made jizya a separate tax and, following the advice of the ulema, extended it to Brahmins for the first time.
108.tq: Discriminate between jizya, a religious tax, and haq-i-sharb, an irrigation cess.
xs: Firoz **made jizya a separate tax and extended it to Brahmins** — so option **(3)** is correct.
He did this on the **ulema's** advice.
**Haq-i-sharb** was an irrigation cess, not a replacement for jizya.
xa: He kept the **four Islamic taxes**: kharaj, jizya, khams, zakat.
His welfare state **won back nobles and ulema**.

108.s: The autobiography of Firoz Shah Tughlaq is:
108.x: Futuhat-i-Firoz Shahi is the autobiography of Firoz Shah Tughlaq.
108.tq: Distinguish the ruler's autobiography from Barani's historical and political works.
xs: Firoz Shah's autobiography is **Futuhat-i-Firoz Shahi** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Dalail-i-Firozshahi** is the Persian translation of Sanskrit texts from **Nagarkot**, by **Azizuddin Khalid Khani**.
**Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi** and **Fatawa-i-Jahandari** were written by **Barani** under Firoz's patronage.
xa: **Ragadarpan**, a work on music, was also translated in his reign.
⚠ **Sikandar Lodi** had a Sanskrit medical treatise translated into Persian — a different Sultan.

108.s: Which one of the following military events is correctly associated with Firoz Shah Tughlaq?
o: He captured Daulatabad from Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
His two expeditions against Haji Iliyas in Bengal failed.
He conquered Central Asia during the Khurasan expedition.
He was defeated by Jam Babaniya, who refused to pay tribute.
108.x: Firoz Shah's two Bengal campaigns against Haji Iliyas failed. He captured Jajnagar and Nagarkot, while Jam Babaniya of Sind agreed to pay tribute.
108.tq: Use the ruler–military event trap by separating failed expeditions from successful conquests and tribute relationships.
xs: Firoz's **two expeditions against Haji Iliyas in Bengal failed** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The second was in **1359-60**.
**Jam Babaniya** of **Sind** **agreed to pay tribute**; **Daulatabad** and the **Khurasan** plan belong to **MBT**.
xa: Firoz did take **Jajnagar** and **Nagarkot**.
His military record is summed up as **mixed results**.

108.s: The Tughlaq period of the Delhi Sultanate is generally placed between
108.x: The Tughlaq period began with Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq in 1320 and ended when Khizr Khan took Delhi in 1414.
108.tq: Identify the dynasty's beginning and end points rather than confusing it with neighbouring dynasties.
xs: The Tughlaq period runs **1320 to 1414** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It began with **Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq Shah in 1320** and ended when **Khizr Khan** took Delhi in **1414**.
xa: Ghiyasuddin ruled **1320-25**; Firoz **1351-88**.
**Timur's invasion** came in **1398**.

108.s: Who was the Tughlaq Sultan on the throne of Delhi at the time of Timur's invasion in 1398?
108.x: Nasiruddin Mahmud Shah Tughlaq, the last Tughlaq, ruled during Timur's invasion of 1398. Firoz had died in 1388, and Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq II and Abu Bakr were earlier weak successors who fought each other.
108.tq: Timur 1398 = Nasiruddin Mahmud, last Tughlaq.
xs: **Nasiruddin Mahmud Shah Tughlaq** was on the throne during **Timur's invasion (1398)** — so option **(3)** is correct.
He was the **last Tughlaq**; some notes call him "Nasiruddin Muhammad Tughlaq".
**Firoz** had ruled to **1388**; **Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq II** and **Abu Bakr** were weak successors who fought each other.
xa: After Sultan Mahmud's death **Daulat Khan Lodi** was briefly recognised.
**Khizr Khan** took Delhi in **1414**.

108.s: Which of the following was NOT associated with Balban?
o: The doctrine of blood and iron
108.x: Branding of horses, or dagh, was a measure of Alauddin Khalji. Balban was associated with Sijda, paibos, the Zil-i-Ilahi theory and the policy of blood and iron.
108.tq: Find the one measure belonging to a neighbouring Sultan rather than the ruler named.
xs: **Branding of horses** (**dagh**) was not Balban's — so option **(4)** is the answer.
Dagh belongs to **Alauddin Khalji** (APPSC-G2 **2023** match key).
Balban's: **Zil-i-Ilahi** theory, **sijda and paibos**, **blood and iron**.
xa: Alauddin's other measures: **huliya**, **market control**, **land measurement**.
Balban also created **Diwan-i-Arz** and ended the **Chahalgani**.

108.s: Which of the following pairs is incorrectly matched?
o: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq — Revenue increase limited to about one-tenth
108.x: The Zil-i-Ilahi theory was associated with Balban, not Iltutmish. Muhammad bin Tughlaq, Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq and Firoz Tughlaq are correctly matched with the measures given.
108.tq: Use the swapped ruler–reform trap to identify the incorrectly matched pair.
xs: **Iltutmish — Zil-i-Ilahi theory** is wrong — so option **(2)** is the answer.
**Zil-i-Ilahi** was **Balban's** theory; Iltutmish's were the **iqta**, **tanka/jital** and **Chahalgani**.
The rest are correct: **Firoz** — hereditary iqtas; **MBT** — token currency; **Ghiyasuddin** — revenue capped at **one-tenth**.
xa: MBT also set up **Diwan-i-Amir-Kohi** and moved to **Daulatabad**.
Firoz: **canals**, **Diwan-i-Khairat**, **Public Works Department**, **jizya on Brahmins**.

108.s: Which one of the following pairs of a city of Delhi and its founder is correctly matched?
108.x: Siri was founded by Alauddin Khalji and Tughlaqabad by Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq. Firoz Shah founded Firozabad, not Tughlaqabad; Balban did not found Siri; Muhammad bin Tughlaq is linked with Daulatabad.
108.tq: Siri = Alauddin; Tughlaqabad = Ghiyasuddin.
xs: **Siri — Alauddin Khalji** is correct — so option **(1)** is the answer.
**Tughlaqabad** was founded by **Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq**, not Firoz or MBT.
**Balban** did not found Siri.
xa: Firoz founded **Firozabad** (Firoz Shah Kotla).
MBT renamed **Devagiri** as **Daulatabad**.

108.s: Which one of the following statements about Malik Maqbul is correct?
o: He established the Bahmani kingdom under the title Hasan Gangu.
He was the founder of the Madurai Sultanate and was known as Ahsan Shah.
He founded Vijayanagara jointly with Harihara and Bukka.
He was originally a captured Brahmin named Jagannatha Pandit and later became Firoz Shah's wazir.
108.x: Malik Maqbul was originally the captured Brahmin Jagannatha Pandit, who converted to Islam and later became Firoz Shah's wazir, Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul.
108.tq: Trace a historical personality through a name change, conversion and later office.
xs: Malik Maqbul **was the captured Brahmin Jagannatha Pandit who became Firoz Shah's wazir** — so option **(4)** is correct.
He converted to Islam and became **Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul**.
**Hasan Gangu** founded the **Bahmani** kingdom; **Jalaluddin Ahsan Shah** the **Madurai Sultanate**; **Harihara and Bukka** Vijayanagara.
xa: After **1323** he assisted **Malik Burhanuddin** of Devagiri at **Warangal**.
As wazir he **paid compensation** to those who had suffered under MBT.

108.s: The Vilasa copper plate of Prolaya Nayaka and Gangadevi's Madhura Vijayam are important for understanding:
o: The conditions under Tughlaq rule in the southern regions
The revenue system of the Bahmani kingdom
The maritime trade policy of the Madurai Sultanate
The succession disputes among the Mughal emperors
108.x: The Vilasa copper plate and Madhura Vijayam describe the conditions prevailing under Tughlaq rule in the southern regions.
108.tq: Associate each source with the historical situation it records, not with a later administrative theme.
xs: They describe **conditions under Tughlaq rule in the southern regions** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Vilasa copper plate** is **Prolaya Nayaka's**; **Madhura Vijayam** is **Gangadevi's**.
xa: Prolaya Nayaka led the fight to free Andhra (**Vilasa** grant, c. **1330**).
**Kapaya Nayaka** then **recaptured Warangal in 1336**.

108.s: Which of the following correctly expresses the distinction between Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq and Firoz Shah Tughlaq regarding canals?
o: Ghiyasuddin was the first Sultan of Delhi to dig canals, whereas Firoz Shah dug the largest number of canals.
Firoz Shah was the first Sultan to dig canals, whereas Ghiyasuddin merely repaired existing canals.
Both Sultans began canal construction simultaneously and undertook the same number of projects.
Neither Sultan undertook canal construction; irrigation was left entirely to provincial rulers.
108.x: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq is regarded as the first Sultan of Delhi to initiate canal digging, while Firoz Shah undertook canal construction on a much larger scale.
108.tq: Separate the FIRST achievement from the larger later expansion instead of treating both claims as identical.
xs: **Ghiyasuddin was the first Sultan to dig canals; Firoz dug the largest number** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Firoz built **more canals than any other Sultan** (BPSC **2019**).
xa: Firoz's canals ran from the **Yamuna and Sutlej to Hisar**, with **haq-i-sharb** (one-tenth).
Ghiyasuddin also capped revenue rises at **one-tenth** and improved the **postal system**.

108.s: Which one of the following best represents the contrasting consequences of the policies of Muhammad bin Tughlaq and Firoz Shah Tughlaq?
o: Muhammad strengthened hereditary iqtas, while Firoz abolished the slave corps and restored direct central administration.
Firoz's welfare measures caused the southern provinces to break away, while Muhammad permanently won the support of the nobles.
Muhammad's experiments contributed to the breakaway of southern provinces, while Firoz's welfare measures won nobles and ulema but weakened central control.
Both rulers followed identical policies and faced no significant provincial revolts.
108.x: Muhammad's poorly executed schemes were followed by the breakaway of southern provinces. Firoz gained the support of nobles and ulema through welfare measures, but hereditary iqtas and the slave corps weakened central control.
108.tq: Compare the paired effects of two rulers and reject the reversed consequence.
xs: **MBT's experiments led to the breakaway of southern provinces; Firoz's welfare won nobles and ulema but weakened central control** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Firoz's weakness came from **hereditary iqtas** and the **slave corps**.
So Firoz **created**, not abolished, the hereditary iqtas and slave department.
xa: Break-aways: **Madurai** (**1335**), **Vijayanagara** (**1336**), **Bahmani** (**1347**).
Firoz's **Diwan-i-Bandagan** held about **1,80,000** slaves.

108.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Rajabwah
(b) Yamuna–Hisar canal
(c) Sirmur Hills canal
(d) Ghaggar–Firozabad canal
List-II
(i) Ended at Hansi
(ii) Sutlej to Ghaggar
(iii) Approximately 150 miles
(iv) Irrigation and public works at Firozabad
108.x: Rajabwah ran from the Sutlej to the Ghaggar, the Yamuna–Hisar canal was about 150 miles long, the Sirmur Hills canal ran to Hansi, and the Ghaggar–Firozabad canal served irrigation and public works, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv.
108.tq: Recall the route or length of each canal.
n: The canal from the Sutlej to the Ghaggar was associated with Firoz Shah Tughlaq. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #88 · pp 170-171]
The canal from the Yamuna to Hisar was approximately 150 miles long. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #88 · pp 170-171]
The canal from the Sirmur Hills to Hansi was an irrigation canal. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #88 · pp 170-171]
The canal from the Ghaggar to Firozabad was used for irrigation and public works. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #88 · pp 170-171]
xs: The correct match is **a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Rajabwah** — **Sutlej** to **Ghaggar** (about **96 miles**); **Yamuna–Hisar** canal — about **150 miles**, the longest.
**Sirmur Hills** canal — ended at **Hansi**; **Ghaggar–Firozabad** — irrigation and public works.
xa: Firoz built **more canals than any other Sultan** (BPSC **2019**).
Irrigation cess = **haq-i-sharb** (**one-tenth**).
**Shahab (Shihab) Canal** of **Akbar's period** restored the **Rajabwah**.
⚠ Other notes say the canals ran from the **Yamuna and Sutlej to Hisar**.

108.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Firoz Shah Tughlaq was associated with Rajabwah.
II. Firoz Shah Tughlaq was associated with the Yamuna–Hisar canal.
III. The Shahab or Shihab Canal belongs to Akbar’s period.
IV. The Shahab or Shihab Canal was associated with the Sutlej–Ghaggar route.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
108.x: I, II and III are correct: Firuz Tughlaq built Rajabwah and the Yamuna–Hisar canal, and the Shahab Canal belongs to Akbar's period. IV is false because the Sutlej–Ghaggar route was Rajabwah's.
108.tq: Check each canal statement separately.
n: Rajabwah was associated with Firoz Shah Tughlaq. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #88 · pp 170-171]
The canal from the Sutlej to the Ghaggar was associated with Firoz Shah Tughlaq. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #88 · pp 170-171]
The canal from the Yamuna to Hisar was associated with Firoz Shah Tughlaq. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #88 · pp 170-171]
The Shahab Canal belonged to Akbar’s period. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #88 · pp 170-171]
xs: Statements **I, II and III only** are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Firoz Shah Tughlaq** is linked with **Rajabwah** and the **Yamuna–Hisar** canal.
The **Shahab / Shihab Canal** belongs to **Akbar's period** — it restored Firoz's **Rajabwah**.
IV is wrong: the **Sutlej–Ghaggar** route is **Rajabwah's** own course.
xa: **Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq** was the **first Sultan to start canal works**; Firoz dug the most.
Firoz's towns: **Firozabad**, **Fatehabad**, **Hisar Firoza**, **Jaunpur**.
He moved **Ashokan pillars** to Delhi from **Topra** and **Meerut**.

108.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Sanskrit texts were translated into Persian by various scholars under Firuz Tughlaq.
II. About 1,300 Sanskrit manuscripts were obtained from the Jawalamukhi library.
III. Azizuddin Khan is associated with the translation of those manuscripts.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
108.x: All three are correct: under Firuz Tughlaq about 1,300 Sanskrit manuscripts from the Jawalamukhi temple library at Nagarkot were obtained, and Azizuddin Khalid Khani translated some into Persian.
108.tq: Check each statement separately.
n: Various scholars translated Sanskrit texts into Persian during Firuz Tughlaq’s rule. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23-2 · pp 84-85]
Approximately 1,300 Sanskrit manuscripts were associated with the Jawalamukhi library. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23-2 · pp 84-85]
Azizuddin Khan translated the Sanskrit manuscripts from the Jawalamukhi library into Persian. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23-2 · pp 84-85]
xs: All three — **I, II and III** — are correct, so option **(1)** is correct.
Under **Firuz Tughlaq**, **Sanskrit texts** were **translated into Persian** by various scholars.
About **1,300 Sanskrit manuscripts** came from the **Jawalamukhi library** (**Nagarkot**); **Azizuddin Khan** translated them.
xa: The translation was **Dalail-i-Firozshahi** by **Aizuddin (Azizuddin) Khalid Khani** (UPPSC **2023**).
**Ragadarpan**, on music, was also translated in his reign.
Firoz's autobiography: **Futuhat-i-Firoz Shahi**.
Firoz took **Jajnagar** and **Nagarkot**.

108.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Alauddin Khalji
(b) Balban
(c) Muhammad bin Tughlaq
(d) Firoz Shah Tughlaq

List-II
(i) Canals, irrigation and public works
(ii) Blood and Iron policy
(iii) Market and price control
(iv) Token currency and capital transfer
108.x: Alauddin Khalji brought in market and price control, Balban followed Blood and Iron, Muhammad bin Tughlaq issued token currency and moved the capital, and Firoz Shah Tughlaq built canals, giving a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
108.tq: Recall the policy of each sultan.
n: Alauddin Khalji is associated with market and price control. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Balban is associated with the Blood and Iron policy. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Muhammad bin Tughlaq is associated with token currency. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Muhammad bin Tughlaq is associated with capital transfer. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Firoz Shah Tughlaq is associated with canals. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Firoz Shah Tughlaq is associated with irrigation. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Firoz Shah Tughlaq is associated with public works. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Alauddin Khalji** — **market and price control**; **Balban** — **Blood and Iron policy**.
**Muhammad bin Tughlaq** — **token currency** and **capital transfer**; **Firoz Shah Tughlaq** — **canals, irrigation, public works**.
xa: Alauddin is also matched with **branding of horses (dagh)** (APPSC-G2 **2023**).
**Sher Shah Suri** — **roads, currency, administrative reforms**.
MBT's **Diwan-i-Amir-Kohi** = **agriculture** department.

108.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Akbar is associated with Din-i-Ilahi and Mansabdari.
II. Abul Fazl wrote Akbarnama and Ain-i-Akbari.
III. Todar Mal is associated with the Dahsala system.
IV. Aurangzeb is associated with Sulh-i-kul.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
108.x: I, II and III are correct: Akbar is linked with Din-i-Ilahi and Mansabdari, Abul Fazl wrote Akbarnama and Ain-i-Akbari, and Todar Mal devised the Dahsala. IV is false because Sulh-i-kul was Akbar's policy; Aurangzeb reimposed Jizya.
108.tq: Spot the policy attached to the wrong Mughal ruler.
n: Akbar is associated with Din-i-Ilahi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Akbar is associated with Mansabdari. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Akbar is associated with Sulh-i-kul. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Abul Fazl is associated with Akbarnama. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Abul Fazl is associated with Ain-i-Akbari. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Todar Mal is associated with the Dahsala system. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Aurangzeb is associated with Jizya. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Aurangzeb is associated with Zinda Pir. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Aurangzeb is associated with Deccan policy. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Abul Fazl is associated with Akbar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Todar Mal is associated with revenue reforms. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
xs: Statements **I, II and III only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
I: **Akbar** — **Din-i-Ilahi**, **Mansabdari**; II: **Abul Fazl** — **Akbarnama**, **Ain-i-Akbari**.
III: **Todar Mal** — **revenue reforms**, the **Dahsala system**.
IV is wrong: **Sulh-i-kul** is **Akbar's**; **Aurangzeb** is linked with **Jizya**, **Zinda Pir**, **Deccan policy**.
xa: Akbar also: **Rajput policy**.
**Shah Jahan** — **Taj Mahal**, Mughal architecture.
**Shivaji** — title **Chhatrapati**, **Ashtapradhan**.

108.s: Who shifted the capital from Delhi to Daulatabad and then back to Delhi?
108.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq moved the capital from Delhi to Daulatabad (Devagiri) in 1327 and later back to Delhi. Harshavardhana moved to Kannauj and Udayin to Pataliputra.
108.tq: Recall which ruler made each capital shift.
xs: **Muhammad bin Tughlaq** shifted the capital from Delhi to **Devagiri**, renamed **Daulatabad** (**1327**) — so option **(4)** is correct.
The aim was a central base to control the **Deccan**; mass migration and hardship followed and the court **returned to Delhi**.
xa: Other experiments: **token currency** of **copper and brass**, **Doab** tax rise, **Khurasan** and **Qarachil** expeditions.
The Doab tax rise **coincided with a famine**.
MBT died at **Thatta** (**1351**).

109.s: Which was the route followed by Timur during his invasion of India?
o: Indus – Punjab, through Multan and Bhatnair – Delhi
109.x: Timur crossed the Indus, passed through Punjab via Multan and Bhatnair, and sacked Delhi in December 1398.
109.tq: Reconstruct the route from the first crossing to the final target.
xs: Timur's route was **Indus – Punjab (through Multan and Bhatnair) – Delhi** — so option **(2)** is correct.
He crossed the **Indus**, passed through **Multan** and **Bhatnair** in Punjab, and sacked **Delhi** in **December 1398**.
xa: Effects: Delhi **plundered** and its people **massacred**; the **Tughlaq** state broke up into regional kingdoms (**Jaunpur**, **Malwa**, **Gujarat**).
Timur's nominee **Khizr Khan** later founded the **Sayyid dynasty** (**1414**).
**Babur** descended from **Timur** on his father's side and **Chengiz Khan** on his mother's side.

109.s: Which of the following was NOT an effect of Timur’s invasion of India?
o: Khizr Khan later founded the Sayyid dynasty as Timur’s nominee.
The Tughlaq state broke up into regional kingdoms.
Delhi was plundered and its people were massacred.
The Mughal Empire was immediately established in Delhi.
109.x: The Mughal Empire was established much later by Babur in 1526. Timur’s invasion led to the plunder and massacre at Delhi, the fragmentation of the Tughlaq state and the later rise of Khizr Khan.
109.tq: Separate immediate consequences from a later dynastic development.
xs: The **Mughal Empire was NOT immediately established** after Timur's invasion — so option **(4)** is the answer.
The Mughal Empire began only after **Babur** won the **First Battle of Panipat** in **1526**.
Options (1), (2) and (3) are real effects: **Khizr Khan** as Timur's nominee, the **Tughlaq** state's break-up, and the **plunder and massacre** at Delhi.
xa: Timur sacked **Delhi** in **December 1398**, after crossing the **Indus** and passing **Multan** and **Bhatnair**.
Regional kingdoms that emerged: **Jaunpur**, **Malwa**, **Gujarat**.
Khizr Khan founded the **Sayyid dynasty (1414-51)**.

109.s:
Consider the following statements about Khizr Khan:
1. He was Timur’s viceroy.
2. He took Delhi in 1414 after arresting Daulat Khan Lodi.
3. He ruled as Timur’s deputy without assuming the title of Sultan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
109.x: All three statements are correct. Khizr Khan, Timur’s viceroy, arrested Daulat Khan Lodi, captured Delhi in 1414 and ruled as Timur’s deputy without using the title Sultan.
109.tq: Check the linked facts about office, capture of Delhi and formal title.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Khizr Khan (1414-21)** was **Timur's viceroy**.
Statement 2 is correct: he **arrested Daulat Khan Lodi** and took **Delhi** in **1414**.
Statement 3 is correct: he ruled as **Timur's deputy without the title of Sultan** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: He founded the **Sayyid dynasty (1414-51)**.
Sayyid order: **Khizr Khan – Mubarak Shah (1421-34) – Muhammad Shah (1434-45) – Alauddin Alam Shah**.
⚠ **Khizr Khan** ruled without the title of Sultan; **Bahlol Lodi** got the throne from **Alam Shah** without a battle.

109.s:
Arrange the following Sayyid rulers in chronological order:
A. Muhammad Shah
B. Khizr Khan
C. Alauddin Alam Shah
D. Mubarak Shah
109.x: The correct order is Khizr Khan, Mubarak Shah, Muhammad Shah and Alauddin Alam Shah.
109.tq: Start with the founder and then follow the stated reign sequence.
xs: The order is **Khizr Khan – Mubarak Shah – Muhammad Shah – Alauddin Alam Shah** (**B, D, A, C**) — option **(1)**.
Reigns: **Khizr Khan (1414-21)**, **Mubarak Shah (1421-34)**, **Muhammad Shah (1434-45)**, then **Alam Shah** till **1451**.
xa: **UPPSC 2023** asked this same order.
**Alam Shah** voluntarily gave up the throne to **Bahlol Lodi** in **1451**.
**Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi** (by **Yahiya bin Ahmad Sarhindi**) was written in **Mubarak Shah's** reign.

109.s: Which feature was associated with the tomb of Mubarak Shah?
o: A tower decorated with red sandstone screens
Blue enamelled tiles and guldasta motifs
A marble dome and pietra dura work
A bronze gateway and granite pillars
109.x: Mubarak Shah’s octagonal tomb is noted for blue enamelled tiles and guldasta motifs.
109.tq: Distinguish architectural features attached to a specific ruler’s monument.
xs: Mubarak Shah's **octagonal tomb** is noted for **blue enamelled tiles and guldasta motifs** — option **(2)**.
Mubarak Shah was the **second Sayyid** ruler (**1421-34**), after **Khizr Khan**.
xa: Mubarak Shah failed against the **Khokhars**.
**Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi** by **Yahiya bin Ahmad Sarhindi** was written in his reign.
**Sikandar Lodi** built the **Moth ki Masjid** and the royal tombs of the **Lodi Gardens**.

109.s: Alauddin Alam Shah ended the Sayyid dynasty by:
o: Voluntarily giving up the throne to Bahlol Lodi in 1451
Being defeated and killed by Babur
109.x: Alauddin Alam Shah voluntarily gave up the throne to Bahlol Lodi in 1451.
109.tq: Test the unusual voluntary-succession detail rather than a battlefield transfer.
xs: **Alauddin Alam Shah** voluntarily **gave up the throne to Bahlol Lodi in 1451** — option **(1)**.
**Babur** killed **Ibrahim Lodi**, not a Sayyid, at **Panipat (1526)**; **Mubarak Shah** ruled before Alam Shah.
xa: ⚠ Bahlol got the throne **without a battle**.
**Bahlol Lodi** had been **Governor of Punjab**; he ruled **1451-1489** and conquered **Jaunpur**.
The **Sayyid dynasty** lasted **1414-51**.

109.s: Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi, written by Yahiya bin Ahmad Sarhindi, belongs to the reign of which Sayyid ruler?
109.x: Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi was written by Yahiya bin Ahmad Sarhindi in the reign of Mubarak Shah (1421-34). Khizr Khan was the founder, and Muhammad Shah and Alam Shah were the later Sayyid rulers.
109.tq: Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi = Mubarak Shah's reign.
xs: **Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi** was written in the reign of **Mubarak Shah (1421-34)** — option **(2)**.
**Khizr Khan** was the founder; **Muhammad Shah** and **Alam Shah** were the later Sayyid rulers.
xa: Author: **Yahiya bin Ahmad Sarhindi**.
Mubarak Shah's **octagonal tomb**: **blue enamelled tiles** + **guldasta motifs**.
Militarily he **failed against the Khokhars**.

109.s:
Consider the following statements about Bahlol Lodi:
1. He had served as the governor of Punjab.
2. He received the throne of Delhi from Khizr Khan.
3. He ruled the longest among the three Lodi rulers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
109.x: Statement 1 is correct: Bahlol was governor of Punjab. Statement 2 is wrong: he received the throne from Alam Shah, the last Sayyid, not Khizr Khan (founder of the Sayyids). Statement 3 is correct: he ruled 1451-1489. So C; A omits 3, B and D include the false statement 2.
109.tq: Khizr Khan began the Sayyid line; Alam Shah ended it by handing over to Bahlol.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Bahlol Lodi** was **Governor of Punjab**.
Statement 2 is wrong: he received the throne from **Alam Shah**, the last Sayyid, not **Khizr Khan** (the founder).
Statement 3 is correct: he ruled **1451-1489**, the longest of the three Lodis (**BPSC 2025**) — so **1 and 3 only**, option **(3)**.
xa: Bahlol conquered **Jaunpur**.
**Sikandar Lodi** ruled **1489-1517**; **Ibrahim Lodi** **1517-1526**.
Lodi kingship: the king was "**first among equals**" among the Afghan nobles.

109.s: In the political conception of the Lodis, the Sultan was regarded as:
o: A ceremonial head chosen by village councils
An absolute monarch above all Afghan nobles
First among equals among the Afghan nobles
A religious representative appointed by the Abbasid Caliph
109.x: The Lodis regarded the king as first among equals among the Afghan nobles.
109.tq: Test the constitutional relationship between the ruler and the nobility.
xs: The Lodis regarded the king as "**first among equals**" among the **Afghan nobles** — option **(3)**.
He was neither an **absolute monarch** above them nor a ceremonial head; the nobles shared power with him.
xa: **Ibrahim Lodi's arrogance** to the nobles broke this tradition and alienated them.
The nobles plotted to enthrone his brother **Jalal Khan**.
The Lodis were the **first Afghan dynasty** of the Delhi Sultanate.

109.s: Sikandar Lodi shifted the capital of the Delhi Sultanate from Delhi to which city?
109.x: Sikandar Lodi founded Agra in 1504 and shifted the capital there from Delhi.
109.tq: Use the founder–city association to distinguish Sikandar Lodi from other Lodi rulers.
xs: **Sikandar Lodi** founded **Agra** in **1504** and moved the capital there from Delhi — option **(2)**.
**Jaunpur** he only subdued; **Gwalior** was seized later by **Ibrahim Lodi**.
xa: Asked in **CGPSC 2018**.
**Gaz-i-Sikandari** = yard used to measure land.
He wrote Persian poetry under the pen name **Gulrukhi**.
After **Panipat**, **Babur** captured **Delhi and Agra** with the Lodi treasure.

109.s:
Consider the following statements about the administration of Sikandar Lodi:
1. The Gaz-i-Sikandari was a yard used to measure land.
2. He imposed new taxes and trade restrictions, making necessities costlier.
3. He kept control through systematic audits and a spy network.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
109.x: Statement 1 is correct: Gaz-i-Sikandari was the yard for measuring land. Statement 2 is wrong: he abolished several taxes and trade restrictions, making necessities cheaper. Statement 3 is correct: he used systematic audits and spies. So '1 and 3 only' (C); A misses 3, B wrongly includes 2, D includes the false statement 2.
109.tq: Remember Sikandar Lodi for tax remissions, not new taxes.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Gaz-i-Sikandari** was a **yard used to measure land**.
Statement 2 is wrong: he **abolished several taxes and trade restrictions**, making necessities **cheaper**.
Statement 3 is correct: control through **systematic audits** and a **spy network** — so **1 and 3 only**, option **(3)**.
xa: **Sikandar Lodi** reigned **1489-1517** and founded **Agra (1504)**.
Pen name: **Gulrukhi** (Persian poetry).
Buildings: **Moth ki Masjid** and the royal tombs of the **Lodi Gardens**.

109.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the rule of Sikandar Lodi:
1. He extended his rule from Punjab to Bihar.
2. He subdued the ruler of Jaunpur.
3. He defeated Bengal rulers and Rajput chiefs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
109.x: Sikandar Lodi extended his authority from Punjab to Bihar, subdued Jaunpur and defeated Bengal rulers and Rajput chiefs.
109.tq: Combine territorial expansion statements and verify each geographical claim.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: his rule ran **from Punjab to Bihar**.
Statement 2 is correct: he **subdued the ruler of Jaunpur**.
Statement 3 is correct: he **defeated Bengal rulers and Rajput chiefs** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: **Bahlol Lodi** had earlier conquered **Jaunpur**.
Sikandar moved the capital to **Agra** (founded **1504**).
**Vasco da Gama** arrived in **1498** during Sikandar's reign.

109.s: Which one of the following combinations correctly represents the religious policy and cultural activity of Sikandar Lodi?
o: He adopted Buddhism and commissioned translations into Pali.
He patronised only Persian religious works and permitted no temple destruction.
He destroyed temples and imposed jizya, but also had a Sanskrit medical work translated into Persian.
He abolished jizya and prohibited the translation of Sanskrit works.
109.x: Sikandar Lodi was religiously intolerant in several actions, including destruction of images and temples and imposition of jizya, yet he had a Sanskrit medical treatise translated into Persian.
109.tq: Handle a seemingly contradictory ruler profile by separating religious policy from cultural patronage.
xs: Sikandar Lodi **destroyed temples and imposed jizya**, yet had a **Sanskrit medical treatise translated into Persian** — option **(3)**.
He destroyed **Jwalamukhi (Nagarkot)** images and **Mathura** temples, so "no temple destruction" (2) is wrong; he **imposed** jizya, so (4) is wrong.
xa: Pen name **Gulrukhi** for his **Persian poetry**.
Built **Moth ki Masjid** and the royal tombs of the **Lodi Gardens**.
Abolished several **taxes and trade restrictions** → necessities cheaper.

109.s: Which of the following monuments is associated with Sikandar Lodi?
o: Adhai Din ka Jhonpra and Alai Darwaza
Moth ki Masjid and the royal tombs of the Lodi Gardens
109.x: Sikandar Lodi built Moth ki Masjid and royal tombs in the Lodi Gardens.
109.tq: Use the ruler–monument association while rejecting monuments from neighbouring periods.
xs: **Moth ki Masjid** and the royal tombs of the **Lodi Gardens** are linked to **Sikandar Lodi** — option **(3)**.
Sikandar Lodi reigned **1489-1517**, the second Lodi after **Bahlol**.
xa: **Mubarak Shah's** octagonal tomb: **blue enamelled tiles** + **guldasta motifs**.
Sikandar founded **Agra (1504)**.
**Gaz-i-Sikandari** = his yard for measuring land.

109.s: Which Delhi Sultan wrote Persian poetry under the pen name 'Gulrukhi'?
109.x: Sikandar Lodi wrote Persian poetry under the pen name Gulrukhi. Bahlol and Ibrahim Lodi are not known for this, and Firoz Shah's own work was his autobiography Futuhat-i-Firoz Shahi.
109.tq: Gulrukhi = Sikandar Lodi.
xs: **Sikandar Lodi** wrote Persian poetry under the pen name **Gulrukhi** — option **(2)**.
**Bahlol** is noted for conquering **Jaunpur**, and **Ibrahim** for his arrogance to the nobles, not for poetry.
xa: Sikandar reigned **1489-1517**.
He had a **Sanskrit medical treatise** translated into **Persian**.
**Gaz-i-Sikandari** = yard to measure land.

109.s: Which of the following was NOT a contemporary of Ibrahim Lodi?
109.x: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq belonged to an earlier period. Krishnadevaraya, Sultan Quli Qutb-ul-Mulk and Rana Sanga were contemporaries of Ibrahim Lodi.
109.tq: Use the period filter to identify the ruler separated from the contemporary group.
xs: **Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq** was **NOT** a contemporary of **Ibrahim Lodi (1517-26)** — option **(2)**.
Contemporaries of Ibrahim: **Krishnadevaraya** (Vijayanagara), **Sultan Quli Qutb-ul-Mulk** (Golconda) and **Rana Sanga** (Mewar).
xa: **Golconda** became independent in **1518** under Sultan Quli Qutb-ul-Mulk.
**Rana Sanga** defeated Ibrahim at **Khatauli (1517-18)**.
The **Deccan** was then split into **five Sultanates**.

109.s: Babur was descended from which two conquerors through his paternal and maternal lines respectively?
o: Mahmud of Ghazni and Muhammad Ghori
109.x: Babur was descended from Timur on his father’s side and from Chengiz Khan on his mother’s side.
109.tq: Keep the two genealogical lines in the correct paternal–maternal order.
xs: Babur descended from **Timur** (father's side) and **Chengiz Khan** (mother's side) — option **(1)**.
Option (3) reverses the two lines.
xa: **Timur** invaded India in **1398** and sacked **Delhi**.
Babur, with about **12,000** men, defeated **Ibrahim Lodi** (about **1,00,000**) at **Panipat** in **1526**.
He was invited by **Daulat Khan Lodi**, Governor of Punjab.

109.s:
Consider the following statements about Ibrahim Lodi:
1. His nobles plotted to place his brother Jalal Khan on the throne.
2. He seized Gwalior, which had sheltered Jalal Khan, and made its ruler Vikramajit a vassal.
3. He defeated Rana Sanga of Mewar at Khatauli (1517-18).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
109.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the nobles backed Jalal Khan, and Ibrahim seized Gwalior and made Vikramajit a vassal. Statement 3 is wrong: at Khatauli Ibrahim was defeated by Rana Sanga. So '1 and 2 only' (B); A omits 2, C and D include the false statement 3.
109.tq: Khatauli was Rana Sanga's victory over Ibrahim.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: nobles plotted to enthrone his brother **Jalal Khan**.
Statement 2 is correct: he seized **Gwalior**, which had sheltered Jalal Khan, and made **Vikramajit** a vassal.
Statement 3 is wrong: at **Khatauli (1517-18)** Ibrahim was **defeated by Rana Sanga** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: ⚠ **Khatauli** = Ibrahim defeated by **Rana Sanga**; **Panipat** = Ibrahim killed by **Babur**.
Ibrahim reigned **1517-1526**.
He is the only Delhi Sultan to **die on the battlefield**.

109.s: Daulat Khan Lodi and Alam Khan Lodi are remembered in the context of Babur's invasion because they:
o: commanded Ibrahim Lodi's artillery at Panipat
invited or sought Babur's help against Ibrahim Lodi
founded the Sayyid dynasty after Timur's departure
109.x: Daulat Khan Lodi, governor of Punjab, and Alam Khan, Ibrahim's uncle, invited or sought Babur's help against Ibrahim Lodi; Rana Sanga too offered to join him, according to Babur. They did not run Ibrahim's guns, Khizr Khan founded the Sayyid dynasty, and Khatauli was Rana Sanga's victory over Ibrahim.
109.tq: Inviters of Babur: Daulat Khan, Alam Khan, Rana Sanga.
xs: **Daulat Khan Lodi** (Governor of Punjab) and **Alam Khan Lodi** (Ibrahim's uncle) **invited or sought Babur's help** against Ibrahim — option **(2)**.
Babur's gunners were **Ustad Ali** and **Mustafa**; **Khizr Khan** founded the Sayyids; **Khatauli** was **Rana Sanga's** win over Ibrahim.
xa: Babur says **Rana Sanga** also offered to join against Ibrahim.
**Khizr Khan** had arrested **Daulat Khan Lodi** in **1414** — a different, earlier Daulat Khan.
Babur won at **Panipat** on **21 April 1526**.

109.s:
Consider the following statements about the First Battle of Panipat (1526):
1. Tulughma was a flanking manoeuvre used by Babur.
2. Babur chained Araba carts together as a defensive line, a 'Rumi' (Ottoman) device.
3. Babur's army outnumbered that of Ibrahim Lodi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
109.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Tulughma was a flanking manoeuvre and Araba carts were chained as a defensive line (Rumi device). Statement 3 is wrong: Babur had about 12,000 men against Ibrahim's about 1,00,000. So B; A omits 2, C and D include the false statement 3.
109.tq: Babur won with a small army through tactics and artillery, not numbers.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Tulughma** was a **flanking manoeuvre**.
Statement 2 is correct: **Araba** carts were chained as a defensive line, a "**Rumi**" (Ottoman) device.
Statement 3 is wrong: Babur had about **12,000** against Ibrahim's about **1,00,000** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Field **artillery** and **muskets** were the decisive factor.
Gunners: **Ustad Ali** and **Mustafa**.
Date: **21 April 1526**; older notes say **20 April**.

109.s: Which military technology was described as the decisive factor in Babur’s victory at the First Battle of Panipat?
109.x: Babur’s field artillery and muskets were decisive factors in the victory at Panipat.
109.tq: Identify the decisive technology instead of a general feature of medieval warfare.
xs: Babur's **field artillery and muskets** were the decisive factor at Panipat — option **(3)**.
They let Babur's small army beat a far larger one on **21 April 1526**.
xa: Tactics also included the **Tulughma** flanking manoeuvre and **Araba** carts chained as a defensive line.
Gunners: **Ustad Ali** and **Mustafa**.
Babur (about **12,000**) defeated **Ibrahim Lodi** (about **1,00,000**).

109.s: Ibrahim Lodi occupies a unique position among the Delhi Sultans because he was the only one who:
o: Founded a new capital at Agra
109.x: Ibrahim Lodi was the only Delhi Sultan to die on the battlefield.
109.tq: Use the unique-exception clue to identify the ruler associated with a rare outcome.
xs: **Ibrahim Lodi** was the only Delhi Sultan to **die on the battlefield** — option **(3)**.
**Gaz-i-Sikandari** and **Agra** belong to **Sikandar Lodi**; **Khizr Khan** ruled as Timur's deputy.
xa: He died at the **First Battle of Panipat** (**21 April 1526**).
Ibrahim Lodi = the **last Delhi Sultan**.
Babur then captured **Delhi and Agra** and the Lodi treasure.

109.s: The First Battle of Panipat is considered a turning point because it:
o: Ended the Delhi Sultanate and began the Mughal Empire.
Ended the Vijayanagara Empire and began the Lodi dynasty.
Restored the Tughlaq state and ended Afghan rule in Bengal.
Established Rajput rule over Delhi and Agra.
109.x: Babur’s victory ended the Delhi Sultanate and marked the beginning of the Mughal Empire.
109.tq: Connect a battle outcome with its larger dynastic consequence.
xs: Panipat **ended the Delhi Sultanate and began the Mughal Empire** — option **(1)**.
**Ibrahim Lodi**, the last Delhi Sultan, died on the battlefield against **Babur** (**1526**).
xa: Babur captured **Delhi and Agra** and the **Lodi treasure**.
Next: **Kanwah (1527)** against **Rana Sanga** broke Rajput power, then **Chanderi (1528)**.
**21 April 2026** = **500th anniversary** of the battle.

109.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Lodi dynasty and Ibrahim Lodi:
1. The Lodis were the first Afghan dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate.
2. The Lodis were the last dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate.
3. Ibrahim Lodi was the last Delhi Sultan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
109.x: All three statements are correct. The Lodis constituted the first Afghan dynasty and the final ruling dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate, while Ibrahim Lodi was its last Delhi Sultan.
109.tq: Check whether the statements refer separately to the dynasty’s origin, position in sequence and final ruler.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **Lodis** were the **first Afghan dynasty**.
Statement 2 is correct: they were the **last dynasty** of the Sultanate.
Statement 3 is correct: **Ibrahim Lodi** was the **last Delhi Sultan** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: Lodi dynasty: **1451-1526** (**Bahlol – Sikandar – Ibrahim**).
Preceded by the **Sayyid dynasty (1414-51)**.
Lodi king = "**first among equals**" among Afghan nobles.

109.s: When Vasco da Gama reached India in 1498, who was on the throne of Delhi?
109.x: Sikandar Lodi was the Delhi Sultan when Vasco da Gama arrived in 1498.
109.tq: 1498: Sikandar ruled when the sea route opened.
xs: **Sikandar Lodi (1489-1517)** was on the throne when **Vasco da Gama** arrived in **1498** — option **(3)**.
**Bahlol** ruled till **1489**, **Ibrahim** from **1517**, and **Khizr Khan** in **1414-21**.
xa: Sikandar founded **Agra (1504)** and moved the capital there.
**Gaz-i-Sikandari** = land-measuring yard.
Pen name: **Gulrukhi**.

110.s: Which dynasty had the shortest period of rule among the five major dynasties of the Delhi Sultanate?
110.x: The Khalji dynasty ruled for about 30 years, from 1290 to 1320, making it the shortest-ruling dynasty among the five.
110.tq: Compare duration rather than merely arranging dynasties by order.
xs: The **Khalji** dynasty had the shortest rule — **30 years** (**1290-1320**) — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **Tughlaqs** ruled longest (**94 years**, **1320-1414**); the **Mamluks** ruled **1206-1290** and the **Sayyids** **1414-1451**.
xa: Khalji founder: **Jalaluddin Khalji**, crowned at **Kilokhari**; reign **1290-96**.
Khalji order: **Jalaluddin → Alauddin → Shihabuddin** (a child set up by **Malik Kafur**) **→ Mubarak Shah**.
Last Khalji **Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah (1316-20)** was killed by the usurper **Khusrau Khan**.

110.s: Which dynasty ruled the Delhi Sultanate for the longest period among the five dynasties listed?
110.x: The Tughlaq dynasty ruled for 94 years, from 1320 to 1414, the longest period among the five.
110.tq: Calculate and compare the spans of neighbouring dynastic periods.
xs: The **Tughlaq** dynasty ruled longest — **94 years** (**1320-1414**) — option **(1)**.
**Mamluks** ruled **1206-1290**, **Lodis** **1451-1526**, and **Khaljis** only **30 years** (**1290-1320**), the shortest.
xa: Founder: **Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq** (**Ghazi Malik**) — father a **Turkish slave**, mother a **Jat**.
Last Tughlaq: **Nasiruddin Mahmud**, under whom **Timur** invaded in **1398**.
⚠ Two **Nasiruddin Mahmuds**: one in the Slave line (before **Balban**), one the last Tughlaq.

**Ghiyasuddin Tughluq** — **Tughluq** (**1320-1414**); **Bahlul Lodi** — **Lodi** (**1451-1526**).
xa: **Khizr Khan** founded the **Sayyid** dynasty (**1414-1451**) as **Timur's viceroy**.
Ghiyasuddin was also known as **Ghazi Malik**; Bahlol was the **first Afghan** Sultan.
Slave sub-phases: **Qutbi**, **First Ilbari** (Iltutmish), **Second Ilbari** (Balban).

110.s:
Arrange the following Delhi Sultanate dynasties in their correct successive order:
A. Lodi
B. Slave/Mamluk
C. Sayyid
D. Khalji
110.x: The Delhi Sultanate dynasties ran Slave/Mamluk (1206), Khalji (1290), Tughluq (1320), Sayyid (1414) and Lodi (1451). Leaving out the Tughluqs, the order is B, D, C, A.
110.tq: Arrange the Sultanate dynasties by their starting years.
n: The Slave or Mamluk dynasty was the first major dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
The Khalji dynasty was the second major dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
The Tughluq dynasty was the third major dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
The Sayyid dynasty was the fourth major dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
The Lodi dynasty was the fifth major dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
xs: The order is **B, D, C, A** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **Tughlaqs** (**1320-1414**) came between Khalji and Sayyid but are not listed.
xa: **Longest dynasty**: **Tughlaq** (**94 years**); **shortest**: **Khalji** (**30 years**).
The Sultanate began with **Tarain** (**1192**) and ended at **Panipat** (**1526**).
**Longest reign**: **Bahlol Lodi** (**38 years**).

110.s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Qutbuddin Aybak was known as Malik and did not assume the title Sultan.
Statement B: Qutbuddin Aybak was known as Quran Khwan for his melodious Quran recitation.
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
110.x: Both are true: Aybak ruled with the titles Malik and Sipahsalar and never took the title Sultan, and he was called Quran Khwan for reciting the Quran melodiously.
110.tq: Check each statement separately.
n: Qutbuddin Aybak was titled Malik. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 53-55]
Qutbuddin Aybak did not assume the title Sultan. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 53-55]
Qutbuddin Aybak was called Quran Khwan. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 53-55]
Qutbuddin Aybak was known for melodious Quran recitation. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 53-55]
The recall association for Aybak's Malik title is Malik. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 53-55]
The recall association for Aybak's Quran Khwan title is Quran Khwan. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 53-55]
xs: **Both Statement A and Statement B are true** — so option **(1)** is correct.
A: **Qutbuddin Aybak** was known as **Malik** and did **not assume** the **title Sultan**.
B: he was called **Quran Khwan** for **melodious Quran recitation**.
xa: He was also **Sipahasalaar** (military commander) and **Lakh Baksh**.
⚠ Other notes say Aibak took the title of Sultan when Ghori died in **1206**.
**Iltutmish** used **Sultan** / **Sultan-i-Azam**, a sovereign title.

110.s:
Consider the following statements:

I. Iltutmish held the title Sultan.
II. Iltutmish held the title Sultan-i-Azam.
III. Sultan-i-Azam was a sovereign title.
IV. Balban was known as Zil-i-Ilahi.
V. Zil-i-Ilahi means shadow of God.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: I, II, III, IV and V
110.x: All five are correct: Iltutmish used the titles Sultan and Sultan-i-Azam, a sovereign title, and Balban called himself Zil-i-Ilahi, the Shadow of God, to raise royal prestige.
110.tq: Check each statement separately.
n: Iltutmish was titled Sultan or Sultan-i-Azam. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 53-55]
Sultan-i-Azam was a sovereign title. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 53-55]
Balban was titled Zil-i-Ilahi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 53-55]
Zil-i-Ilahi means Shadow of God. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 53-55]
Balban was associated with divine kingship. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 53-55]
xs: All five — **I, II, III, IV and V** — are correct, so option **(4)** is correct.
**Iltutmish** held the titles **Sultan** and **Sultan-i-Azam**, a **sovereign title**.
**Balban** was **Zil-i-Ilahi** (**Zillillah**) — **Shadow of God**, divine kingship.
xa: Balban was also **Niyabat-i-Khudai** — **God's representative**.
**Alauddin Khalji** = **Sikandar-i-Sani** (Second Alexander).
**Mubarak Shah** Khalji = **Al-Imam**, **Khilafatullah**.

110.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Qutbuddin Aibak
(b) Iltutmish
(c) Balban
(d) Alauddin Khalji

List-II
(i) Strong monarchy
(ii) Founded the Slave dynasty; began Qutub Minar
(iii) Market and military reforms; southern expeditions
(iv) Consolidated the Sultanate; Tanka and Jital; completed Qutub Minar
110.x: Aibak founded the Slave dynasty and began the Qutub Minar, Iltutmish consolidated the Sultanate, issued the tanka and jital and completed the Minar, Balban built a strong monarchy, and Alauddin made market and military reforms, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.
110.tq: Link each Sultan to his main achievement.
n: Qutbuddin Aibak founded the Slave dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Qutbuddin Aibak began the construction of the Qutub Minar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Iltutmish consolidated the Sultanate. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Iltutmish introduced the Tanka. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Iltutmish introduced the Jital. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Iltutmish completed the Qutub Minar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Balban established a strong monarchy. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Alauddin Khalji introduced market reforms. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Alauddin Khalji introduced military reforms. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Alauddin Khalji undertook southern expeditions. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
xs: The correct match is **a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Qutbuddin Aibak** — founded the **Slave dynasty**, began the **Qutub Minar**; **Iltutmish** — **Tanka** and **Jital**, completed the Minar.
**Balban** — **strong monarchy**; **Alauddin Khalji** — **market and military reforms**, **southern expeditions**.
xa: Aibak also built the **Quwwat-ul-Islam** (**1206–1210**).
**Razia** (**1236–1240**) was the **first and only woman ruler**.
**Firoz Shah Tughluq** — **canals**, **public works**, **Ashokan pillars**.

110.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Razia was the first and only woman ruler of the Delhi Sultanate.
Firoz Shah Tughluq is associated with canals, public works and Ashokan pillars.
Muhammad bin Tughluq introduced token currency and transferred the capital to Daulatabad.
110.x: Option C is incorrect: Sikandar Lodi founded Agra in 1504, not Delhi. Razia as the only woman Sultan, Firoz Shah's canals and Muhammad bin Tughluq's token currency are right.
110.tq: Recall the city Sikandar Lodi founded.
n: Razia was the first woman ruler of the Delhi Sultanate. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Razia was the only woman ruler of the Delhi Sultanate. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Muhammad bin Tughluq introduced token currency. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Muhammad bin Tughluq transferred the capital to Daulatabad. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Firoz Shah Tughluq constructed canals. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Firoz Shah Tughluq undertook public works. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Firoz Shah Tughluq was associated with Ashokan pillars. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Sikandar Lodi founded Agra. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
xs: The incorrect statement is **"Sikandar Lodi founded Delhi"** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Sikandar Lodi** (**1489–1517**) **founded Agra**, not Delhi.
**Razia**, **Firoz Shah's canals** and **MBT's token currency** statements are correct.
xa: **Muhammad bin Tughluq** (**1325–1351**) moved the capital to **Daulatabad**.
**Iltutmish** (**1211–1236**) consolidated the Sultanate.
Vasco da Gama reached Calicut (**17 May 1498**) under **Sikandar Lodi**.

110.s: Who was the first and only woman ruler of the Delhi Sultanate?
110.x: Razia, daughter of Iltutmish, ruled 1236–1240 and was the first and only woman ruler of the Delhi Sultanate. Chand Bibi, Nur Jahan and Durgavati were not Sultans of Delhi.
110.tq: Recall the only woman ruler of Delhi.
n: Razia was the first woman ruler of the Delhi Sultanate. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Razia was the only woman ruler of the Delhi Sultanate. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Razia's period was 1236–1240. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
xs: **Razia** was the **first and only woman ruler** of the **Delhi Sultanate** — so option **(1)** is correct.
xa: Slave succession: Iltutmish → **Ruknuddin Firoz** → **Razia** → **Bahram Shah**.
⚠ Two **Nasiruddin Mahmuds**: one in the Slave line (before **Balban**), one the last Tughlaq.
First Afghan ruler: **Bahlol**; first Sultan: **Aibak**.

110.s:
How many of the following are associated with Muhammad bin Tughluq?

1. Token currency
2. Capital transfer to Daulatabad
3. Strong monarchy
4. Foundation of Agra
110.x: Two are linked with Muhammad bin Tughluq: token currency and moving the capital to Daulatabad. Strong monarchy belongs to Balban and the founding of Agra to Sikandar Lodi.
110.tq: Check each item against the ruler.
n: Balban established a strong monarchy. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Muhammad bin Tughluq introduced token currency. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Muhammad bin Tughluq transferred the capital to Daulatabad. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Sikandar Lodi founded Agra. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
xs: **Only two** — **token currency** and **capital transfer to Daulatabad** — belong to **Muhammad bin Tughluq**, so option **(2)** is correct.
**Strong monarchy** belongs to **Balban**; **foundation of Agra** to **Sikandar Lodi**.
xa: MBT reigned **1325–1351**.
**Firoz Shah Tughluq** (**1351–1388**) — canals, public works.
**Timur** invaded in **1398** under **Nasiruddin Mahmud**, not MBT.

111.s: Under whose theory of kingship was the Sultan described as Zil-i-Ilahi, or the Shadow of God?
111.x: Balban propounded the concept of the Sultan as Zil-i-Ilahi, or Shadow of God, along with Niyabat-i-Khudai, or divine deputyship.
111.tq: Match the distinctive political doctrine with its proponent.
xs: The theory of kingship of **Balban** called the Sultan **Zil-i-Ilahi** (Shadow of God) — option **(4)**.
He paired it with **Niyabat-i-Khudai** (divine deputyship), **sijda and paibos**, **Nauroz** and a "**blood and iron**" policy.
**Iltutmish** sought legitimacy through **caliphal investiture**; **Alauddin** put state interest above the ulema; **MBT** followed **rationalist absolutism**.
xa: Balban allowed **no low-born men** in office.
Balban, himself one of the **Forty**, destroyed the **Chalisa**.
He set up the **Diwan-i-Arz** (army department) — **RPSC 2018**.

111.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Alauddin Khalji — Kingship knows no kinship
Muhammad bin Tughlaq — Exclusion of non-Turks from high office
111.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq followed rationalist absolutism and appointed non-Turks and low-born persons. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
111.tq: Look for the reversed policy statement, especially where a ruler's inclusionary policy is made exclusionary.
xs: **MBT – exclusion of non-Turks** is wrong: MBT **appointed non-Turks and low-born men** — option **(4)**.
The rest are correct: **Alauddin** – "kingship knows no kinship"; **Balban** – "blood and iron"; **Iltutmish** – created the **Turkan-i-Chahalgani** (the Forty).
xa: MBT's theory: **rationalist absolutism**.
MBT sought investiture from the Abbasid Caliph in **Egypt**.
MBT set up the **Diwan-i-Kohi** (agriculture).

111.s:
Consider the following statements about the theory of kingship:
1. Alauddin Khalji placed the interests of the state above the authority of the ulema and religious law.
2. Alauddin Khalji used the title Sikandar-i-Sani.
3. Balban permitted low-born men to occupy high offices as a central feature of his theory of kingship.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
111.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Balban excluded low-born men from high office, whereas the appointment of non-Turks and low-born men is associated with Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
111.tq: Use the contrast between the social policies of Balban and Muhammad bin Tughlaq to identify the false statement.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Alauddin** put **state interest above the ulema** and law.
Statement 2 is correct: Alauddin took the title **Sikandar-i-Sani** (some notes: Sikander-i-Azam).
Statement 3 is wrong: **Balban** allowed **no low-born men** in office; appointing them was **MBT's** policy — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Alauddin's maxim: "**kingship knows no kinship**".
Alauddin took **Yamin-ul-Khilafat Nasir-i-Amir-ul-Mominin** but did **not** seek investiture (**UPPSC 2023**).
Balban's titles: **Zil-i-Ilahi** and **Niyabat-i-Khudai**.

111.s:
Consider the following statements about the Sultan in the Delhi Sultanate:
1. The Sultan was supreme in military, legal and political matters and was the highest court of appeal.
2. There was a fixed rule of succession by which the eldest son always succeeded.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
111.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Sultan was supreme in military, legal and political matters and the highest court of appeal. Statement 2 is wrong: there was no fixed rule; succession rested on acceptance by nobles and ulema or on military strength. So A; B and C accept the false statement 2, D rejects the true statement 1.
111.tq: No fixed succession rule in the Sultanate.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the Sultan was supreme in **military, legal and political** matters and the **highest court of appeal**.
Statement 2 is wrong: there was **no fixed rule of succession** — it rested on backing of **nobles, ulema and army**, or military strength — so **1 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Sultans saw themselves as the **Caliph's representatives**.
The state was essentially a **military, centralised** state.
**Barids** formed the intelligence network.

111.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Delhi Sultans and the Caliphate is correct?
o: The Caliph directly appointed all provincial governors in India.
Every Sultan obtained investiture before occupying the throne.
The Sultans saw themselves as representatives of the Caliph.
The Sultans generally regarded themselves as independent successors of the Caliphs.
111.x: The Sultans generally saw themselves as representatives of the Caliph. There was no rule that every Sultan obtained investiture, and the Caliph did not directly appoint all provincial governors.
111.tq: Reject absolute statements such as “every” and identify the general constitutional relationship.
xs: The Sultans **saw themselves as the Caliph's representatives** — option **(3)**.
Not every Sultan sought investiture: **Alauddin** did not, and **Mubarak Shah Khalji** proclaimed himself Caliph.
xa: **Iltutmish** got investiture from **Baghdad (c.1229)**; **MBT** sought it from **Egypt**.
**Firoz** respected the Caliph.
The Caliph's **nominal authority** was a **Perso-Arabic** element of the state.

111.s: Who among the following proclaimed himself the Caliph?
111.x: Mubarak Shah Khalji proclaimed himself Caliph. This was distinct from Iltutmish's receipt of investiture and Alauddin's adoption of Caliphal titles without seeking investiture.
111.tq: Distinguish a self-proclaimed Caliph from a Sultan who merely received investiture or adopted titles.
xs: **Mubarak Shah Khalji** **proclaimed himself Caliph** — option **(1)**.
