**Iltutmish** received investiture from Baghdad; **Firoz** respected the Caliph; Balban is given "**Nasir-amir-ul-momin**" in some notes.
xa: **Alauddin Khalji** took caliphal titles but **did not seek investiture**.
**MBT** sought investiture from the Caliph in **Egypt**.
⚠ **Baghdad** = Iltutmish; **Egypt** = MBT.

111.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the position of Muhammad bin Tughlaq in relation to the Abbasid Caliphate?
o: He proclaimed himself the only Caliph of India.
He received investiture from the Caliph of Baghdad in 1229.
He sought investiture from the Abbasid Caliph in Egypt.
He rejected every form of association with the Caliphate.
111.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq sought investiture from the Abbasid Caliph in Egypt. The 1229 investiture from the Abbasid Caliph of Baghdad was received by Iltutmish.
111.tq: Separate the similar investiture episodes of Iltutmish and Muhammad bin Tughlaq by place and event.
xs: **MBT** **sought investiture from the Abbasid Caliph in Egypt** — option **(3)**.
The **1229** investiture from **Baghdad** was **Iltutmish's**; **Mubarak Shah Khalji** proclaimed himself Caliph.
xa: MBT's theory: **rationalist absolutism**; he appointed **non-Turks and low-born men**.
MBT promoted **foreigners** in the nobility.
**Firoz** respected the Caliph.

111.s: Which Delhi Sultan took the titles 'Yamin-ul-Khilafat Nasir-i-Amir-ul-Mominin' without seeking investiture from the Caliph?
111.x: Alauddin Khalji took these titles but did not seek investiture. Iltutmish received investiture from the Caliph of Baghdad (c.1229), Mubarak Shah Khalji proclaimed himself Caliph, and Muhammad bin Tughlaq sought investiture from the Caliph in Egypt.
111.tq: Yamin-ul-Khilafat = Alauddin (UPPSC 2023).
xs: **Alauddin Khalji** took **Yamin-ul-Khilafat Nasir-i-Amir-ul-Mominin** without seeking investiture — option **(2)** (**UPPSC 2023** key).
**Iltutmish** received investiture (**c.1229**); **Mubarak Shah Khalji** proclaimed himself Caliph; **MBT** sought investiture from **Egypt**.
xa: Alauddin put **state interest above the ulema** and law.
His title: **Sikandar-i-Sani**.
He set up **Diwan-i-Mustakhraj** and **Diwan-i-Riyasat**.

111.s: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between sharia and zawabit in the Delhi Sultanate?
o: Zawabit replaced sharia in all civil and criminal matters.
Sharia governed all criminal matters, while zawabit governed only Hindu personal law.
Sharia applied only to the Sultan and his nobles, whereas zawabit applied to the general population.
Sharia covered Muslims’ civil matters, while royal decrees called zawabit supplemented it.
111.x: Sharia covered the civil matters of Muslims, while royal decrees or zawabit supplemented the legal order. Criminal law followed the Sultan’s rules, and Hindus retained their personal law.
111.tq: Separate civil law, personal law, criminal rules and royal decrees rather than treating them as one system.
xs: **Sharia** covered **Muslims' civil matters**, and royal decrees called **zawabit** supplemented it — option **(4)**.
**Criminal law** followed the **Sultans' rules**, and **Hindus** kept their own personal law — so (1), (2) and (3) are wrong.
xa: The state was a **composite of Perso-Arabic, Turko-Mongol and Indian** elements (**JPSC 2021**).
The Sultan was the **highest court of appeal**.
**Qazi-ul-Quzat** = chief justice.

111.s:
Consider the following statements about the composite nature of the Delhi Sultanate state:
1. The title Sultan and Persian court rituals such as sijda, paibos and Nauroz were Perso-Arabic elements.
2. An army organised in decimal units with mounted archers was an Indian element.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
111.x: Statement 1 is correct: the title Sultan and sijda, paibos and Nauroz were Perso-Arabic. Statement 2 is wrong: decimal army units and horse warfare with mounted archers were Turko-Mongol elements. So A; B and C accept the false statement 2, D rejects the true statement 1.
111.tq: Decimal army + mounted archers = Turko-Mongol.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the title **Sultan** and **sijda, paibos, Nauroz** were **Perso-Arabic**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **decimal army units** and **mounted archers** were **Turko-Mongol**, not Indian — so **1 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Decimal ranks: **khan, malik, amir, sipahsalar**.
The state was a composite of **Perso-Arabic, Turko-Mongol and Indian** elements (**JPSC 2021**).
Sijda and paibos were part of **Balban's** court ritual.

111.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Diwan-i-Wizarat dealt with finance and revenue.
2. Diwan-i-Insha handled royal correspondence and drafting of decrees.
3. Diwan-i-Qaza was concerned with justice.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
111.x: All three statements are correct. Diwan-i-Wizarat dealt with finance and revenue, Diwan-i-Insha with royal correspondence and decrees, and Diwan-i-Qaza with justice.
111.tq: Verify each department against its distinct administrative function before selecting the combined code.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Diwan-i-Wizarat** (under the **Wazir**) = **finance and revenue**.
Statement 2 is correct: **Diwan-i-Insha** (under the **Dabir-i-Khas**) = **royal correspondence** and decrees.
Statement 3 is correct: **Diwan-i-Qaza** = **justice** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: The Wazir was assisted by the **Auditor-General** and **Accountant-General**.
**Qazi-ul-Quzat** = chief justice.
**Diwan-i-Risalat** under the **Sadr-us-Sudur** = religious affairs.

111.s: Which Sultan is associated with the establishment of Diwan-i-Arz?
111.x: Diwan-i-Arz, the department dealing with army recruitment and inspection, was set up by Balban.
111.tq: Separate the founder of a department from later rulers who expanded military administration.
xs: **Balban** set up the **Diwan-i-Arz** — option **(2)** (**RPSC 2018**).
⚠ "Alauddin first set up a separate Ariz's department" is **false** (**UPSC 2002**).
xa: Alauddin set up **Diwan-i-Mustakhraj** and **Diwan-i-Riyasat**.
**Firoz**: **Diwan-i-Bandagan** and **Diwan-i-Khairat**.
Head of Diwan-i-Arz: **Ariz-i-Mumalik**.

111.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
111.x: Diwan-i-Bandagan, the department dealing with slaves, was established by Firoz Tughlaq, not Balban. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
111.tq: Find the single founder swapped with a neighbouring Sultan.
xs: **Diwan-i-Bandagan – Balban** is wrong: the department of **slaves** was set up by **Firoz** (**UPSC 2002**) — option **(4)**.
The rest are correct: **Kohi** = **MBT**; **Mustakhraj** and **Riyasat** = **Alauddin**.
xa: **Mustakhraj** recovered arrears from revenue officials.
**Kohi** aimed at extending cultivation.
Firoz also set up **Diwan-i-Khairat**.

111.s: The Sadr-us-Sudur in the Delhi Sultanate was primarily associated with which of the following functions?
111.x: The Sadr-us-Sudur supervised religious affairs and endowments; the Chief Sadr was also the Chief Qazi.
111.tq: Discriminate between officials whose functions belonged to religion, intelligence and court administration.
xs: The **Sadr-us-Sudur** headed the **Diwan-i-Risalat**: **religious affairs and endowments** — option **(4)**.
News and intelligence = **Barid-i-Mumalik**; despatch of decrees = **Khareetadar**; court decorum and household = **Wakil-i-Dar**.
xa: The Chief Sadr was also the **Chief Qazi**.
Risalat made grants to **mosques and madrasas**.
Older notes call Diwan-i-Risalat the **foreign ministry**; learn the religious-affairs meaning first.

111.s:
Consider the following statements about the central administration of the Delhi Sultanate:
1. The Naib ranked next to the Sultan and in practice could control all departments.
2. The wizarat reached its heyday under Balban.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
111.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Naib ranked next to the Sultan and in practice controlled all departments. Statement 2 is wrong: the wizarat's heyday was under Firoz Tughlaq, when Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul ran the government. So '1 only' (A); B and C accept the false statement 2, D rejects the true statement 1.
111.tq: Heyday of wazir = Firoz Tughlaq with Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **Naib** ranked next to the Sultan and in practice **controlled all departments**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the wizarat's heyday was under **Firoz Tughlaq**, not Balban — so **1 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: **Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul** ran Firoz's government as **wazir**.
**Malik Kafur** was **Naib Malik** of Alauddin.
The Wazir headed the **Diwan-i-Wizarat** (finance and revenue).

111.s:
With reference to the central officials of the Delhi Sultanate, consider the following statements:
1. Qazi-ul-Quzat was the Chief Justice.
2. Barid-i-Mumalik headed the news and intelligence system.
3. Wakil-i-Dar was responsible for court decorum and the royal household.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
111.x: All three statements are correct. Qazi-ul-Quzat was the Chief Justice, Barid-i-Mumalik headed intelligence, and Wakil-i-Dar supervised the court and royal household.
111.tq: Use the official-function pairings and check all three statements independently.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Qazi-ul-Quzat** = **chief justice**.
Statement 2 is correct: **Barid-i-Mumalik** = head of **news and intelligence**.
Statement 3 is correct: **Wakil-i-Dar** = **court decorum** and **royal household** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: **Amir-i-Hajib** = master of ceremonies.
**Khareetadar** = despatcher of royal decrees.
**Naib** = second only to the Sultan.

111.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Imad-ul-Mulk — Balban
2. Malik Kafur — Alauddin Khalji
3. Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul — Firoz Tughlaq
4. Nizam-ul-Mulk Junaidi — Muhammad bin Tughlaq
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
111.x: Imad-ul-Mulk served Balban, Malik Kafur was the Naib Malik of Alauddin Khalji, and Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul was the wazir of Firoz Tughlaq. Nizam-ul-Mulk Junaidi served Iltutmish, not Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
111.tq: Split the options by identifying the swapped Sultan in the fourth pair.
xs: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct: **Imad-ul-Mulk – Balban**, **Malik Kafur – Alauddin**, **Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul – Firoz** — option **(2)**.
Pair 4 is wrong: **Nizam-ul-Mulk Junaidi** was **Iltutmish's** wazir (**APPSC-GS 2023**).
xa: Malik Kafur was Alauddin's **Naib Malik**.
**Ain-ul-Mulk Multani** conquered **Malwa** in **1305** for Alauddin.
Imad-ul-Mulk headed Balban's **army department**.

111.s:
Which of the following practices were introduced by Balban to enhance the dignity of the Sultan?
1. Sijda
2. Paibos
3. Nauroz
4. Turkan-i-Chahalgani
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
111.x: Balban introduced sijda, paibos and the Persian festival Nauroz. Turkan-i-Chahalgani, the Forty, was created by Iltutmish.
111.tq: Separate the practices of Balban from the institution created by Iltutmish.
xs: **Sijda**, **paibos** and **Nauroz** were Balban's court practices — **1, 2 and 3 only**, option **(2)**.
The **Turkan-i-Chahalgani** ("The Forty") was created by **Iltutmish**; Balban **destroyed** it.
xa: Balban's theory: **Zil-i-Ilahi** + **Niyabat-i-Khudai**.
These rituals were **Perso-Arabic** elements of the state.
Balban's policy: "**blood and iron**".

111.s:
Consider the following statements about the Turkan-i-Chahalgani:
1. It was created by Iltutmish.
2. It consisted of forty Turkish slave-nobles.
3. Balban ultimately destroyed its political influence.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
111.x: Iltutmish created the Turkan-i-Chahalgani, or the Forty, of Turkish slave-nobles. They influenced the succession after him, but Balban destroyed their power.
111.tq: Check the institution through its founder, composition and later fate.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Iltutmish** created the **Turkan-i-Chahalgani**.
Statement 2 is correct: it was "**The Forty**" Turkish **slave-nobles**.
Statement 3 is correct: **Balban**, himself one of the Forty, **destroyed it** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: The Forty made and unmade Sultans after Iltutmish, including over **Razia**.
⚠ **Iltutmish** created the Forty; **Balban** destroyed it.
After Balban, nobles set aside his nominee **Kai Khusrau** and raised **Kaiqubad**.

111.s: Which development is associated with the Khalji Revolution of 1290?
o: The Sultan was reduced to a ceremonial position.
All nobles were made hereditary landholders.
High offices were opened to non-Turks and Indian Muslims.
High offices were restricted to Turkish slave-nobles.
111.x: The Khalji Revolution opened high office to non-Turks and Indian Muslims, breaking the earlier Turkish monopoly.
111.tq: Use the date and institutional change together to identify the correct development.
xs: The **Khalji revolution (1290)** **opened high office to non-Turks and Indian Muslims** — option **(3)**.
It ended the earlier **Turkish monopoly** of the Slave nobility, so (4) is the opposite.
xa: **Alauddin** crushed the **Balbani and Jalali** nobles.
He **banned noble gatherings** and **spied** on the nobility.
**Jalaluddin Khalji** took power in **1290**.

111.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched with the policy concerning nobility?
o: Muhammad bin Tughluq — Promoted foreigners and low-born men
Alauddin Khalji — Crushed the Balbani and Jalali nobles
Lodi Sultans — Treated Afghan nobles as subordinate officials without tribal equality
111.x: Lodi rulers dealt with an Afghan tribal nobility that treated the Sultan as first among equals. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
111.tq: Detect the reversed description in a dynasty-wise comparison of nobility.
xs: **Lodis – nobles as subordinate officials** is wrong: the **Afghan tribal nobility** treated the Sultan as "**first among equals**" — option **(4)**.
The rest are correct: **Firoz** made iqtas **hereditary**; **MBT** promoted **foreigners and low-born men**; **Alauddin** crushed **Balbani and Jalali** nobles.
xa: Khalji revolution (**1290**) opened office to **non-Turks** and **Indian Muslims**.
Slave dynasty nobility = **Turkish monopoly**.

111.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Muqti or wali — Governor of an iqta
Amil — Revenue officer of a pargana
111.x: A Khut was a hereditary rural landholder. The despatcher of royal decrees was the Khareetadar.
111.tq: Identify the official whose role has been replaced by a central court function.
xs: **Khut – despatcher of royal decrees** is wrong: the khut was a **hereditary rural landholder** — option **(4)**.
The despatcher of royal decrees was the **Khareetadar**; the other three pairs are correct.
xa: **Alauddin** abolished the **khut's cess**.
**Shiqdar** = in charge of a **shiq** (division/district).
**Muqaddam / Chaudhari** = village headman (**BPSC 2022**).

111.s:
With reference to rural officials of the Delhi Sultanate, consider the following statements:
1. Muqaddam or Chaudhari was the village headman.
2. The Chaudhari was regarded as the chief rural land-revenue official.
3. Alauddin Khalji abolished the cess of the khut.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
111.x: All three statements are correct. The muqaddam or chaudhari headed the village, the chaudhari had a major rural revenue role, and Alauddin abolished the khut’s cess.
111.tq: Combine the village hierarchy with the specific revenue measure associated with Alauddin.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Muqaddam / Chaudhari** = **village headman** (**BPSC 2022**).
Statement 2 is correct: the **UPSC 2004** key made the chaudhari the **chief rural land-revenue official**.
Statement 3 is correct: **Alauddin** abolished the **khut's cess** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: **Patwari** = village accountant.
**Amil** = revenue officer of a **pargana** (**UPSC 2019**).

111.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
111.x: A pargana, comprising a group of villages, was placed under an amil for revenue collection. A province was under a muqti or wali, a shiq under a shiqdar, and a village under a muqaddam or chaudhari.
111.tq: Match each territorial unit with its corresponding officer.
xs: **Pargana – Amil** is correct: the amil was **in charge of revenue collection** in a pargana — option **(3)** (**UPSC 2019**).
A province (iqta) was under a **muqti / wali**, a shiq under a **shiqdar**, a village under a **muqaddam / chaudhari**.
xa: A **pargana** = group of villages.
**Patwari** = village accountant.
**Khut** = hereditary rural landholder.

111.s: Which one of the following offices did NOT exist under the Delhi Sultans?
111.x: Mir Bakshi was a Mughal office and did not exist under the Delhi Sultans. The other offices belonged to the Sultanate administrative or military structure.
111.tq: Use the dynasty-specific office trap.
xs: The office of **Mir Bakshi** did **not** exist under the Sultans; it is **Mughal** — option **(4)** (**UPSC 2019**).
**Shiqdar** (shiq), **Ariz-i-Mumalik** (Diwan-i-Arz) and **Muqti** (iqta) were Sultanate offices.
xa: Sultanate diwans prefigured the Mughal **Diwan**, **Mir Bakshi** and **Sadr-us-Sudur**.
The Ariz-i-Mumalik's department was set up by **Balban**.

111.s:
Consider the following statements about Qutb Shahi administration:
1. The Peshwa functioned as the Prime Minister.
2. Under Tana Shah, the title Peshwa was renamed Diwan.
3. Madanna was the last holder of the Peshwa office.
4. Majumdar was an auditor and was mostly drawn from Hindus.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
111.x: All four statements are correct. The Peshwa was the Prime Minister, was renamed Diwan under Tana Shah, was last held by Madanna, and the Majumdar served as auditor, mostly from the Hindu community.
111.tq: Check the office, renaming, last holder and community detail separately.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: Qutb Shahi **Peshwa** = **PM**, renamed **Diwan** under **Tana Shah**, last held by **Madanna**.
Statement 4 is correct: **Majumdar** = **auditor**, mostly **Hindus** — so **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(4)**.
xa: Qutb Shahi **Mir Jumla** = finance; **Ain-ul-Mulk** = army.
**Dabir** = Diwan-i-Insha.
Bahmani PM = **Wakil-us-Saltanat**.

111.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Mahmud Ghazni's silver coins had Arabic on one side and Sanskrit in Devanagari on the other.
II. Muhammad Ghori's coins had Goddess Lakshmi on one side and the Kalma in Arabic on the other.
III. Iltutmish placed the Caliph's name on coins after Caliph's recognition.
IV. Alauddin Khalji used the title Sikandar-i-Sani on coins.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
111.x: I, II, III and IV are all correct: Mahmud Ghazni's bilingual silver coins used Arabic and Devanagari Sanskrit, Ghori's coins showed Lakshmi, Iltutmish added the Caliph's name after recognition, and Alauddin styled himself Sikandar-i-Sani.
111.tq: Check each statement separately.
n: Mahmud Ghazni issued silver coins with Arabic on one side. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
Mahmud Ghazni's silver coins had Sanskrit on the other side. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
The Sanskrit script on Mahmud Ghazni's coins was Devanagari. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
Muhammad Ghori's coins had Goddess Lakshmi on one side. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
Muhammad Ghori's coins had the Kalma in Arabic on the other side. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
Iltutmish placed the Caliph's name on coins after recognition by the Caliph. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
Alauddin Khalji used the title Sikandar-i-Sani. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
Alauddin Khalji inscribed the title Sikandar-i-Sani on coins. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
xs: All four — **I, II, III and IV** — are correct, so option **(1)** is correct.
I: **Mahmud Ghazni's** **silver coins**: **Arabic** on one side, **Sanskrit** in **Devanagari** on the other.
II: **Muhammad Ghori's** coins: **Goddess Lakshmi** and the **Kalma** in Arabic.
III: **Iltutmish** put the **Caliph's name** on coins after recognition; IV: **Alauddin** inscribed **Sikandar-i-Sani** on coins.
xa: Iltutmish got investiture (**mansur**) from the **Abbasid Caliph of Baghdad** in c. **1229**.
**MBT's** coin legend: **"Al Sultan Zilli Allah"**; he sought investiture from the Caliph in **Egypt**.
**Mubarak Shah Khalji** **proclaimed himself Caliph**.
**Balban's** **Garhmukteshwar** inscription calls him **"Helper of a Caliph"**.

112.s: Which statement regarding the development of the iqta system is correct?
o: Firoz Tughluq abolished the iqta system completely.
Iltutmish built the iqta into a systematic administrative institution.
Alauddin Khalji converted every iqta into private property.
Qutbuddin Aibak first introduced it as a hereditary system in India.
112.x: Iltutmish developed the iqta into a system. Under the Sultanate, it remained a revenue assignment rather than private ownership.
112.tq: Identify the ruler associated with institutional consolidation, not later modification.
xs: **Iltutmish** built the iqta into a **systematic institution** — option **(2)** (**UPPSC 2010** key: Iltutmish).
**Firoz** did not abolish iqtas — he made them **hereditary**; iqtas were **not ownership of land**, so (3) is wrong.
**Aibak** received the **first iqta** (**Hansi**) from **Ghori**, but it was **transferable**, not hereditary.
xa: Holder = **iqtadar / muqti** (or **wali** for a province).
Iqta = a **Turkish, non-indigenous** institution (**UPSC 2019**).
Some notes credit **Aibak** with introducing it.

112.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the responsibilities of a muqti:
1. He maintained troops.
2. He collected revenue.
3. He sent the surplus revenue to the central government.
4. He was exempt from maintaining law and order.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
112.x: A muqti maintained troops, collected revenue, preserved law and order, and remitted the surplus to the centre. Therefore, statement 4 is false.
112.tq: Find the statement that reverses a duty of the office-holder.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: the muqti **kept troops**, **collected revenue** and sent the **surplus (fawazil)** to the centre.
Statement 4 is wrong: he also **kept law and order** — so **1, 2 and 3 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: The muqti held an **iqta**, a revenue assignment, **not ownership of land**.
Iqtas were **transferable**; muqtis moved periodically until **Firoz** made them hereditary.
**Alauddin** tightened the **audit** of muqtis.

112.s: Which one of the following statements about the nature of the iqta system is correct?
o: It was an ancient indigenous Indian institution.
It was exclusively a religious endowment system.
It was introduced only in the Mughal period.
It was a Turkish, non-indigenous institution.
112.x: The iqta was a Turkish institution and was not an ancient indigenous Indian institution.
112.tq: Discriminate between a foreign administrative institution and an indigenous one.
xs: The iqta was a **Turkish, non-indigenous** institution — option **(4)**.
⚠ Trap: "ancient indigenous institution" is **false** (**UPSC 2019**).
It began under **Ghori** (**Hansi** to **Aibak**), long before the Mughals, and was a revenue assignment, not a religious endowment.
xa: **Iltutmish** institutionalised it.
Iqta = ancestor of the Mughal **jagir/mansab** system.

112.s: The first iqta grant in India, of Hansi, is credited to:
o: Muhammad Ghori, granted to Qutbuddin Aibak
Alauddin Khalji, granted to Malik Kafur
112.x: Muhammad Ghori granted Hansi (some sources say Kuhram) to Qutbuddin Aibak, the first iqta. Iltutmish later built the iqta into a system; Balban and Alauddin are not linked with the first grant.
112.tq: First iqta: Hansi, Ghori to Aibak.
xs: The first iqta, **Hansi**, was granted by **Muhammad Ghori** to **Qutbuddin Aibak** — option **(2)**.
Some notes say **Kuhram** instead of Hansi.
xa: **Iltutmish** later built the iqta into a system (**UPPSC 2010**).
Some notes credit **Aibak** with introducing it.
Iqta = a **Turkish, non-indigenous** institution.

112.s:
Consider the following statements about changes in the iqta system:
1. Balban appointed khwajas (auditors) to check the muqtis' accounts.
2. Alauddin Khalji paid the standing army in cash and enlarged the khalisa.
3. Ghiyasuddin Tughluq made the iqtas hereditary.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
112.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Balban appointed khwajas, and Alauddin paid the army in cash and enlarged the khalisa. Statement 3 is wrong: Firoz Tughlaq made iqtas hereditary; Ghiyasuddin held an inquiry into grants and seized unlawful ones. So B; A omits 2, C and D include the false statement 3.
112.tq: Hereditary iqtas = Firoz Tughlaq only.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Balban** appointed **khwajas** (auditors) to check muqtis' accounts.
Statement 2 is correct: **Alauddin** paid a **standing army in cash** and enlarged the **khalisa**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Firoz** made iqtas **hereditary**; **Ghiyasuddin** held an **inquiry into grants** and seized unlawful ones — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: ⚠ **Alauddin** = cash pay; **Firoz** = hereditary iqtas.
**Balban** tried to resume the iqtas of **old soldiers**.

112.s: With reference to the iqta system, which of the following statements is NOT correct?
o: Firoz Tughlaq abolished the jagir system to improve army efficiency.
Ghiyasuddin Tughluq ordered an inquiry into grants and jagirs.
Unlawful grants were seized during the reign of Ghiyasuddin Tughluq.
112.x: Firoz Tughlaq revived the jagir system and made iqtas hereditary. This revival adversely affected army efficiency; he did not abolish the system.
112.tq: Find the option that reverses the stated policy and its consequence.
xs: "**Firoz abolished the jagir system**" is NOT correct: he **revived** the jagir and made iqtas **hereditary** — option **(2)**.
That revival **hurt army efficiency**, as nobles controlled recruitment, promotion and discipline.
Statements (3) and (4) are correct: **Ghiyasuddin Tughluq** inquired into **grants/jagirs** and seized **unlawful grants**.
xa: Before Firoz, iqtas were **transferable**.
⚠ **Alauddin** = cash pay; **Firoz** = back to assignments.

112.s:
Arrange the following developments in the iqta system in chronological order:
A. Iqtas were made hereditary under Firoz Tughlaq.
B. Iltutmish organised the iqta system.
C. Balban appointed khwajas to audit muqtis' accounts.
D. Alauddin Khalji enlarged the khalisa and paid the standing army in cash.
112.x: The correct sequence is Iltutmish, Balban, Alauddin Khalji and Firoz Tughlaq.
112.tq: Use the rulers' chronological order to arrange administrative changes.
xs: Order: **Iltutmish** organises the iqta → **Balban** appoints **khwajas** → **Alauddin** pays cash and enlarges **khalisa** → **Firoz** makes iqtas **hereditary** (**B, C, D, A**) — option **(1)**.
Each change is tied to the Sultan's own reign, so the dynastic order fixes the sequence.
xa: **Ghiyasuddin Tughluq** (between Alauddin and Firoz) inquired into grants.
**Ghori** made the first iqta grant (**Hansi**) to **Aibak**.
⚠ **Alauddin** = cash pay; **Firoz** = hereditary iqtas.

112.s: What was the position of iqtas before the policy of Firoz Tughlaq?
o: They were permanently owned by the muqtis.
They were administered exclusively as khalisa lands.
They were granted only to religious leaders.
They were periodically transferable between muqtis.
112.x: Before Firoz Tughlaq made iqtas hereditary, muqtis were transferred periodically from one iqta to another.
112.tq: Distinguish a transferable assignment from a hereditary one.
xs: Before Firoz, iqtas were **transferable** and muqtis were **moved periodically** — option **(4)**.
Iqtas were **not ownership of land**; **khalisa** was the separate crown land; grants to religious men were **inam**.
xa: **Firoz Tughlaq** made iqtas **hereditary**.
Iqta = **land revenue** assigned instead of a **cash salary**.
Muqti sent the **fawazil** (surplus) to the treasury.

112.s:
Consider the following statements regarding army pay:
1. Iltutmish and Balban used iqtas for paying officers and troopers.
2. Alauddin Khalji paid his standing army in cash.
3. Firoz Tughlaq restored assignment-based payment through the revival of the jagir system.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
112.x: Iltutmish and Balban used iqtas for payment, Alauddin Khalji introduced large-scale cash payment, and Firoz Tughlaq returned to assignment-based payment through the jagir revival.
112.tq: Compare payment systems across successive rulers.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Iltutmish** and **Balban** gave **iqtas to officers and troopers**.
Statement 2 is correct: **Alauddin** paid his **standing army in cash**.
Statement 3 is correct: **Firoz** went back to assignments through the **jagir** revival — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: Firoz also made iqtas **hereditary**.
Alauddin enlarged the **khalisa** to fund cash pay.

112.s: Who introduced the branding of horses and the descriptive roll of soldiers in the Delhi Sultanate?
112.x: Alauddin Khalji introduced dagh, the branding of horses, and huliya, the descriptive roll of each soldier. Sher Shah later revived dagh.
112.tq: Match paired military controls with the ruler who introduced them.
xs: **Alauddin Khalji** introduced **dagh** (branding of horses) and **huliya** (descriptive roll) — option **(3)**.
**Sher Shah** only **revived** the dagh later.
⚠ "**Balban** introduced the branding of horses" is **false** (**UPSC 2002**).
xa: Purpose: stop **substandard horses** or **proxies** at the muster.
The army was run by the **Ariz-i-Mumalik**.

112.s: The primary purpose of dagh and huliya was to
o: Record the revenue of each iqta
Determine the hereditary rights of military officers
Prevent the presentation of substandard horses and substitute soldiers at muster
Classify villages according to agricultural production
112.x: Branding horses and maintaining descriptive rolls helped prevent soldiers from bringing inferior horses or sending proxies in their place during inspection.
112.tq: Infer the administrative purpose from the control mechanism.
xs: Dagh and huliya stopped **substandard horses** and **proxy soldiers** at the muster — option **(3)**.
**Dagh** = branding of horses; **huliya** = descriptive roll of each soldier.
xa: Introduced by **Alauddin Khalji**; dagh revived by **Sher Shah**.
The **Ariz's department** recruited, inspected and paid the army.

112.s: Which one of the following sequences correctly represents the Sultanate military hierarchy from the lowest listed rank to the highest?
112.x: The order was sar-i-khail, sipah-salar, amir, malik and khan. Khan was the highest listed rank.
112.tq: Arrange a graded hierarchy by its internal sequence.
xs: Lowest to highest: **Sar-i-khail → Sipah-salar → Amir → Malik → Khan** — option **(1)**.
A **Sar-i-khail** commanded **10 horsemen**; each higher rank commanded **10** of the rank below; **Khan** was highest.
xa: Ranks followed a **decimal** pattern — a **Turko-Mongol** feature.
Cavalry = **core arm**; also infantry and elephants.

112.s:
Which combination of military innovations is associated with the Turks in medieval India?
1. Horse-based warfare
2. Mounted archery
3. Iron stirrup
4. Stronger fortifications
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
112.x: The Turks introduced or strengthened horse-based warfare, mounted archery, the iron stirrup, armour and stronger fortifications. Therefore, all four statements are correct.
112.tq: Identify the complete set of related military features before eliminating partial combinations.
xs: Turkish innovations: **horse-based warfare**, **mounted archers**, the **iron stirrup**, **armour** and **stronger fortification** — **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(4)**.
So every listed item — horse-based warfare, mounted archery, iron stirrup and stronger fortifications — is a **Turkish** innovation.
xa: The **horse** became a key military and economic resource, **imported from West Asia**.
**War elephants** = a royal preserve.

112.s: Alauddin Khalji received daily market reports from
112.x: Alauddin Khalji obtained daily market reports from barids and munhiyans, the latter functioning as secret spies.
112.tq: Match information sources with the ruler who used them.
xs: Alauddin got daily market reports from **barids and munhiyans** (secret spies) — option **(3)**.
**Barids** were news-reporters and intelligence agents under the **barid-i-mumalik**.
xa: **Khwajas** were **Balban's** auditors; **amils** were pargana revenue officers.
Alauddin's **market control** kept the army's cash pay adequate.

112.s: Who improved the postal system by using runners and horsemen?
112.x: Ghiyasuddin Tughluq improved the postal system by employing both runners and horsemen.
112.tq: Associate a communication reform with the correct Sultan.
xs: **Ghiyasuddin Tughluq** improved the post with **runners and horsemen** — option **(1)**.
**Sher Shah** later set up the **dak chowki**.
xa: **Ibn Battuta** described two relays: **ulaq** (horse) and **dawa** (foot).
⚠ **Ulaq** = horse; **dawa** = foot.
Ghiyasuddin also held an **inquiry into grants/jagirs**.

112.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the Sultanate postal system?
o: The horse post, ulaq, was used to bring Khorasan fruit to Delhi.
The ulaq was a system of village revenue collection.
The foot post, dawa, was exclusively used for military recruitment.
The dawa was the department responsible for horse branding.
112.x: The horse post, called ulaq, was used to bring fruit from Khorasan to Delhi. Dawa referred to the foot post.
112.tq: Apply the functional distinction between the two postal relays.
xs: The horse post **ulaq** brought **Khorasan fruit** to Delhi — option **(1)** (**APPSC-G1 2017**).
**Dawa** was the **foot post**, not recruitment or branding; ulaq was a relay, not revenue collection.
xa: Both relays are from **Ibn Battuta's** account.
⚠ **Ulaq** = horse; **dawa** = foot.
**Sher Shah's dak chowki** = precursor of the modern post.

112.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Iqta — Delhi Sultanate
2. Jagir — Mughal Empire
3. Amaram — Vijayanagara Empire
4. Mokasa — Bahmani and later Deccan
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
112.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Iqta, jagir, amaram and mokasa belonged respectively to the Delhi Sultanate, Mughal Empire, Vijayanagara and Bahmani-later Deccan contexts.
112.tq: Compare the four revenue assignments by both region and administrative nature.
xs: All four pairs are correct: **Iqta – Sultanate**, **Jagir – Mughal**, **Amaram – Vijayanagara**, **Mokasa – Bahmani and later Deccan** — option **(4)**.
So **1, 2, 3 and 4** are all correctly matched.
xa: The **jagir** also appears in **Bahmani** and **Qutb Shahi** usage.
Bahmanis used **iqta** as a synonym for **jagir**.
**Amaram** holders paid **kappam**.

112.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
112.x: Mahrousa meant a protected town. Khalisa referred to land under state administration, shiq to a portion or division, and iqta to a revenue assignment.
112.tq: Start with the sure terminological pair and eliminate the swapped meanings.
xs: **Mahrousa – protected town** is correct — option **(1)** (**UPPSC 2023**).
**Khalisa** = land under **direct state administration**; **Shiq** = "**a portion**", a division; **Iqta** = assignment of **land revenue**.
xa: A shiq was under a **shiqdar**.
**Inam** = land granted to religious leaders/institutions.

112.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Land category)
 a. Khalisa
 b. Iqta
 c. Inam
List-II (Meaning)
 i. Land assigned to officials in place of salary
 ii. Land granted to religious men and institutions
 iii. Crown land whose revenue supported the court and royal household

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
112.x: Khalisa was crown land, iqta was assigned to officials in place of salary, and inam was granted to religious men and institutions.
112.tq: Start from the sure meaning of Khalisa and then distinguish official assignments from religious grants.
xs: **Khalisa** = crown land (iii), **Iqta** = land in place of salary (i), **Inam** = religious grants (ii) — option **(1)**.
Khalisa revenue went to the **royal treasury, court and household**; inam went to **religious leaders/institutions**.
xa: **UPPSC 2025**: Sultanate territory broadly **Khalisa and Iqta**.
Bahmani khalisa **paid the central army**.
**Alauddin** enlarged the **khalisa**.

112.s:
Assertion (A): The territory of the Delhi Sultanate was broadly divided into Khalisa and Iqta lands.
Reason (R): The territory of the Delhi Sultanate was broadly divided into Khalsa and Jagirs.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
112.x: A is true: Sultanate land was broadly khalisa (crown land) and iqta (revenue assignments). R is false: the jagir belongs to the Bahmani, Qutb Shahi and Mughal systems, not the Sultanate's basic division. So A is true and R is false, as in the UPPSC 2025 key.
112.tq: Sultanate = Khalisa + Iqta; jagir is Mughal/Deccan.
xs: **A is true**: Sultanate territory was broadly **Khalisa and Iqta**.
**R is false**: "**Khalsa and Jagirs**" is wrong; the **jagir** belongs to **Bahmani, Qutb Shahi and Mughal** usage — so option **(3)**, as in the **UPPSC 2025** key.
xa: Khalisa revenue went to the **royal treasury, court and household**.
The **Mughal jagir** was tied to **mansab** rank.

112.s:
Assertion (A): The iqta system helped the Delhi Sultanate finance its army.
Reason (R): Revenue assignments under the system linked military obligations with the administration of distant territories.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
112.x: Both statements are correct. The iqta system provided the financial basis for maintaining troops while also connecting military service with the administration of assigned territories.
112.tq: Check whether the reason explains the administrative and military function stated in the assertion.
xs: **A is true**: the **iqta** financed the army.
**Both A and R are true**, and **R is the correct explanation** of A: revenue assignments linked **military service** with **integrating distant provinces** — option **(1)**.
xa: The muqti **kept troops** and sent the **fawazil** to the centre.
The iqta is the ancestor of the Mughal **jagir/mansab** system.

112.s: The iqta system is regarded as the ancestor of which later Mughal arrangement?
o: Amara Nayankara and Siddha Sainyam system
112.x: The iqta system is considered the ancestor of the Mughal jagir and mansab system. The other combinations belong to different administrative or military contexts.
112.tq: Discriminate between related administrative and military institutions of different periods.
xs: The iqta is the ancestor of the Mughal **jagir and mansab** system — option **(1)**.
**Amara Nayankara** and **Siddha Sainyam** belong to **Vijayanagara**.
xa: The Mughal jagir was tied to **mansab** rank and was **transferable**.
The iqta financed the army and integrated **distant provinces**.

112.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Military feature)
A. Vijayanagara
B. Qutb Shahis
C. Kakatiyas
D. Shivaji

List-II (Associated feature)
I. Lenkas as royal bodyguards
II. Standing army paid in cash
III. Siddha Sainyam and Amara Nayankara army
IV. Siddha Sainyam and Jagirdar Sainyam

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
112.x: Vijayanagara had the Siddha Sainyam and Amara Nayankara army; the Qutb Shahis had the Siddha Sainyam and Jagirdar Sainyam; Kakatiya royal bodyguards were Lenkas; and Shivaji maintained a cash-paid standing army.
112.tq: Start from the sure institutional pairs and eliminate codes with a swapped military feature.
xs: **Vijayanagara – Siddha Sainyam + Amara Nayankara** (III); **Qutb Shahis – Siddha + Jagirdar Sainyam** (IV) — option **(1)**.
**Kakatiyas – Lenkas** (I); **Shivaji – standing army paid in cash** (II).
xa: Kakatiya posts: **Gajasahini**, **Ashwasahini**.
Shivaji set up **Sindhudurg** and **Vijaydurg** naval bases.

112.s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Chauth was an important Maratha revenue claim.
Statement B: Sardeshmukhi was an important Maratha revenue claim.
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
112.x: Both are true: Chauth (one-fourth) and Sardeshmukhi (one-tenth) were the main Maratha revenue claims on neighbouring territory.
112.tq: Check each statement separately.
n: Chauth was an important Maratha revenue claim. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
Sardeshmukhi was an important Maratha revenue claim. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
xs: **Both Statement A and Statement B are true** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Chauth** — a **Maratha levy**, generally **one-fourth**, an important revenue claim.
**Sardeshmukhi** — a **Maratha levy**, generally **10%**, also an important claim.
xa: **Jizya** = tax on **non-Muslims**; **Zakat** = religious tax on **Muslims**.
**Hundi** = a **credit / bill-of-exchange** instrument.
**Zabt** = a **Mughal land-revenue assessment** system.

112.s:
How many of the following were recipients of Madad-i-Mash grants?
I. Saints
II. Religious institutions
III. Mashaikhs
IV. Mansabdars, in lieu of salary
112.x: Three are right: Madad-i-Mash revenue-free grants went to saints, religious institutions and mashaikhs. Mansabdars were paid through jagirs or cash, not Madad-i-Mash.
112.tq: Separate charitable revenue-free grants from salary assignments to officers.
n: Madad-i-Mash was associated with saints. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
Madad-i-Mash was associated with religious institutions. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
Madad-i-Mash was associated with mashaikhs. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
xs: **Only three** — **saints**, **religious institutions** and **mashaikhs** — received **Madad-i-Mash**, so option **(3)** is correct.
**Madad-i-Mash** = a **revenue-free land grant** to **learned, pious and worthy persons**.
**Mansabdars** were paid through a **jagir**, a revenue assignment — not Madad-i-Mash.
xa: **Maal** = land revenue under the **Mughals**.
**Inam** = land granted to religious leaders/institutions.
**Jagir** = revenue assignment to a **Mansabdar or Jagirdar**.

112.s:
How many of the following are associated with taxes or levies?
1. Jizya
2. Zakat
3. Chauth
4. Tanka
112.x: Three are taxes: Jizya on non-Muslims, Zakat on Muslims, and the Maratha Chauth. Tanka was a silver coin introduced by Iltutmish.
112.tq: Separate the taxes from the coin.
n: Jizya was a tax imposed on non-Muslims. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #83 · pp 165-166]
Zakat was a religious tax on Muslims. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #83 · pp 165-166]
Chauth was a Maratha levy generally amounting to one-fourth. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #83 · pp 165-166]
Tanka was a silver coin introduced by Iltutmish. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #83 · pp 165-166]
xs: **Only three** — **Jizya**, **Zakat** and **Chauth** — are taxes or levies, so option **(3)** is correct.
**Jizya** = tax on **non-Muslims**; **Zakat** = religious tax on **Muslims**; **Chauth** = **Maratha levy** of about **one-fourth**.
xa: **Sardeshmukhi** = Maratha levy of about **10%**.
**Madad-i-Mash** = revenue-free grant under the Mughals.
**Dagh** = branding of horses in Sultanate military administration.

112.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Iqta was a revenue assignment in the Delhi Sultanate.
II. Khalisa referred to land under direct state control.
III. Jagir was a revenue assignment to a Mansabdar or Jagirdar.
IV. Dagh was a Mughal land-revenue assessment system.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
112.x: I, II and III are correct: Iqta was a Sultanate revenue assignment, Khalisa land was under direct state control, and Jagir was a Mughal assignment. IV is false because Dagh was the branding of horses; Zabt was the Mughal revenue system.
112.tq: Check each term separately.
n: Iqta was a revenue assignment in the Delhi Sultanate. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #83 · pp 165-166]
Khalisa was land under direct state control. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #83 · pp 165-166]
Jagir was a revenue assignment to a Mansabdar or Jagirdar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #83 · pp 165-166]
Zabt was a Mughal land-revenue assessment system. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #83 · pp 165-166]
Dagh was the branding of horses in Sultanate military administration. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #83 · pp 165-166]
xs: Statements **I, II and III only** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Iqta** = revenue assignment in the **Delhi Sultanate**; **Khalisa** = land under **direct state control**.
**Jagir** = revenue assignment to a **Mansabdar or Jagirdar**.
IV is wrong: **Dagh** = **branding of horses**; **Zabt** was the **Mughal land-revenue assessment system**.
xa: **Mahrousa** = **protected town/territory** (UPPSC **2023**).
**Shiq** = division of a province under a **shiqdar**.
UPPSC **2025**: Sultanate territory = **Khalisa and Iqta**, not "Khalsa and Jagirs".
**Amaram** = Vijayanagara land to **Amaranayakas**, paying **kappam**.

113.s:
Consider the following statements about taxes in the Delhi Sultanate:
1. Firoz Tughlaq extended jizya to Brahmins.
2. Ushr was a land tax of one-half of the produce on Muslim-held land.
3. Kharaj was a land tax, usually one-third of the produce, paid by non-Muslim cultivators.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
113.x: Statement 3 is correct: kharaj was a land tax usually assessed at one-third of the produce (varying from one-tenth to one-half), paid mainly by non-Muslim cultivators. Statement 2 is wrong: ushr was levied at one-tenth, not one-half, on Muslim-held land. Statement 1 is correct: Firoz Tughlaq extended jizya to Brahmins. So '3 only' misses statement 1, and options with statement 2 are wrong.
113.tq: Kharaj = 1/3 (non-Muslims); Ushr = 1/10 (Muslims); Firoz = jizya on Brahmins.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Firoz Tughlaq** extended **jizya** to **Brahmins**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Ushr** was levied at **1/10** on Muslim-held land, not one-half.
Statement 3 is correct: **Kharaj** was a land tax, usually **1/3** of produce, paid by **non-Muslim cultivators**.
xa: **Zakat** = religious tax of about **2.5%** of wealth, on **Muslims** only.
**Khams** = **one-fifth (1/5)** of war booty (APPSC-G1 **2012**).
**Alauddin and MBT** took **4/5** of booty; **Firoz** restored **1/5**.
⚠ **Kharaj** = non-Muslims' land tax; **Ushr** = Muslims' land tax.

113.s:
With reference to taxation during the Sultanate period, consider the following statements:
1. Jizya was imposed on non-Muslims as a poll or protection tax.
2. Zakat was a religious tax payable only by Muslims.
3. Khams represented one-fifth of war booty and treasure-troves due to the state.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
113.x: All three statements are correct. Jizya was a protection tax on non-Muslims, zakat was payable by Muslims, and khams was the state’s one-fifth share of booty and treasure-troves.
113.tq: Match each tax with both its payer and its nature before selecting the coded combination.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Jizya** = poll or "**protection**" tax on **non-Muslims**.
Statement 2 is correct: **Zakat** (about **2.5%** of wealth) was paid by **Muslims only**.
Statement 3 is correct: **Khams** = **one-fifth (1/5)** of war booty and treasure-troves — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: "Khams = 1/5 of war booty" and "Zakat = tax on Muslims only" are the **standard traps**.
**APPSC-G1 2012** asked khams as the state's share of booty.
**Firoz** extended jizya to **Brahmins**.

113.s: Which of the following statements regarding booty distribution is correct?
o: All the Sultans uniformly retained one-half of the booty.
Alauddin Khalji and Muhammad bin Tughlaq took four-fifths, while Firoz Tughlaq restored the one-fifth share.
Alauddin Khalji and Firoz Tughlaq took four-fifths, while Muhammad bin Tughlaq restored the one-fifth share.
Firoz Tughlaq took four-fifths, while Alauddin Khalji restored the one-fifth share.
113.x: Although the sharia rule assigned one-fifth to the state, Alauddin Khalji and Muhammad bin Tughlaq took four-fifths. Firoz Tughlaq restored the one-fifth share.
113.tq: Track the ruler associated with the deviation and restoration of the standard rate.
xs: **Alauddin and MBT** took **4/5** of booty; **Firoz** restored the **1/5** share — option **(2)**.
Under sharia, the state got **1/5** and the soldiers **4/5**.
xa: **Khams** also covered **treasure-troves**.
Firoz abolished many **illegal cesses**.
Asked in **APPSC-G1 2012**.

113.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Ghari — House tax
2. Charai — Grazing tax
3. Haq-i-sharb — Irrigation tax
4. Khams — Customs duty
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
113.x: Ghari was a house tax, charai was a grazing tax, and haq-i-sharb was an irrigation tax. Khams was the state’s one-fifth share of booty, not a customs duty.
113.tq: Find the wrongly assigned nature of a levy before choosing the matching set.
xs: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct: **Ghari** = house tax, **Charai** = grazing tax, **Haq-i-sharb** = irrigation tax — option **(2)**.
Pair 4 is wrong: **Khams** = **1/5 of war booty**, not customs; customs and **octroi** were separate levies.
xa: Ghari and Charai: **Alauddin Khalji**; Haq-i-sharb: **Firoz Tughlaq**.
Charai was on **milch cattle** (cattle and sheep).
Haq-i-sharb ≈ **1/10** of produce on **canal-watered** land.

113.s: Which one of the following sets consists only of the four Sharia taxes retained by Firoz Tughlaq?
113.x: Firoz Tughlaq abolished the many illegal cesses and kept only the four Sharia taxes: kharaj, jizya, zakat and khams. The other sets include non-Sharia items such as ghari, charai, haq-i-sharb (cesses), taccavi (loans) and iqta or inam (land assignments).
113.tq: Separate the standard Sharia taxes from additional cesses, loans and land assignments.
xs: Firoz kept only the four sharia taxes: **kharaj, jizya, zakat and khams** — option **(3)**.
**Ghari, Charai, Haq-i-sharb** are cesses; **taccavi** is a loan; **iqta** and **inam** are land categories.
xa: Firoz **abolished many illegal cesses**.
He restored the **1/5** khams share.
He extended **jizya** to **Brahmins**.

113.s: Alauddin Khalji’s enhancement of land revenue resulted in the land tax being raised to approximately:
113.x: Peasants generally paid one-third of the produce as land revenue, but Alauddin Khalji raised the demand to one-half.
113.tq: Compare the normal assessment with the exceptional rate associated with a specific ruler.
xs: **Alauddin** raised land revenue to **one-half (1/2)** of produce — option **(3)**.
Peasants normally paid **one-third (1/3)**, sometimes **one-half**.
xa: Alauddin also introduced **Ghari** (house tax) and **Charai** (grazing tax).
**Sher Shah's** revenue: **1/4 to 1/3** of produce, based on survey.
Alauddin's **price-control** markets show military needs shaping economic policy.

113.s: Which Sultan introduced Ghari and Charai as additional cesses?
113.x: Alauddin Khalji introduced Ghari, the house tax, and Charai, the grazing tax on milch cattle.
113.tq: Use the ruler–measure association rather than confusing the tax with its later reform.
xs: **Alauddin Khalji** introduced **Ghari** (house tax) and **Charai** (grazing tax) — option **(3)**.
**Haq-i-sharb** (irrigation tax) was **Firoz Tughlaq's**.
xa: Charai fell on **milch cattle** (cattle and sheep).
Alauddin raised land revenue to **1/2**.
Other levies: **octroi** and **customs duties**.

113.s: An iqta in the Sultanate administrative system was:
o: A grant to religious institutions only
Land assigned to officials in place of salary
Crown land reserved for the royal household
113.x: An iqta was a land assignment made to officials instead of paying them a direct salary.
113.tq: Separate the official land assignment from Khalisa and religious inam grants.
xs: An **iqta** was land **assigned to officials in place of salary** — option **(2)**.
Grants to religious men and institutions were **inam**.
xa: **Maagani** (irrigated) and **Metta** (rain-fed) were **Kakatiya** land types.
Kakatiya land tax = **Ari**.
Nobles **held iqtas**.

113.s: Which one of the following crops was NOT grown in India during the 13th–14th centuries?
113.x: Maize was not grown in India during the 13th–14th centuries. It was introduced later by the Portuguese.
113.tq: Find the crop associated with later European introduction rather than the established medieval crops.
xs: **Maize** was **not grown** in the 13th-14th centuries (**UPPSC 2011**) — option **(3)**.
Maize and **tobacco** came later with the **Portuguese / Europeans**; **gram**, **barley** and **wheat** were grown.
xa: Other crops: **rice**, **sugarcane**, **cotton**, **oilseeds**.
**Ibn Battuta** saw two harvests a year: **rabi** and **kharif**.
Rice was sown **three times** a year.

113.s: Which irrigation device was popularised by the Turks in medieval India?
113.x: The Turks popularised the Persian wheel, known as saqiya, for irrigation.
113.tq: Separate the specific Persian wheel from other irrigation and revenue terms.
xs: The Turks popularised the **Persian wheel (saqiya)** — option **(4)**.
**Araghatta** was an existing water-wheel; **taccavi** was a loan; **Samudrams** were **Kakatiya** tanks.
xa: Paper and the Persian wheel = **lasting gains**.
Other Turkish technologies: **paper-making**, **glass-making**, **spinning wheel**.

113.s:
Consider the following statements about irrigation and agriculture under the Tughlaqs:
1. Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq granted remission in droughts and brought wasteland under the plough.
2. Muhammad bin Tughlaq built the largest number of canals.
3. Firoz Tughlaq's longest canal ran from the Yamuna to Hisar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
113.x: Statement 1 is correct: Ghiyasuddin gave drought remission and extended cultivation to wasteland. Statement 2 is wrong: Firoz Tughlaq built the most canals; MBT is known for the Diwan-i-Kohi and taccavi loans. Statement 3 is correct: Firoz's longest canal ran Yamuna to Hisar. So C; A omits 3, B and D include the false statement 2.
113.tq: First canal-builder = Ghiyasuddin; most canals = Firoz.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Ghiyasuddin** gave **drought remission** and brought **wasteland** under the plough.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Firoz** built the most canals; **MBT** is known for **Diwan-i-Kohi** and **taccavi** loans.
Statement 3 is correct: Firoz's longest canal ran **Yamuna → Hisar** — so **1 and 3 only**, option **(3)**.
xa: ⚠ **First** canal-builder of the 14th century = **Ghiyasuddin** (**UPPSC 2017**).
Firoz's irrigation cess = **haq-i-sharb**.

113.s: Who is regarded as the first canal-builder of the fourteenth century?
113.x: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq is regarded as the first canal-builder of the fourteenth century, while Firoz Tughlaq later built the largest number of canals.
113.tq: Distinguish the pioneer canal-builder from the ruler credited with building the most canals.
xs: **Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq** was the **first canal-builder** of the 14th century — option **(3)** (**UPPSC 2017**).
⚠ **Firoz Tughlaq** built the **most** canals, not the first.
xa: Firoz's longest canal: **Yamuna → Hisar**.
Ghiyasuddin gave **remission in droughts**.
**MBT** gave **taccavi (sondhar)** loans.

113.s: Taccavi, also called sondhar, referred to:
o: Loans given to cultivators to extend cultivation
113.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq gave taccavi or sondhar loans to cultivators for extending cultivation.
113.tq: Distinguish an agricultural loan from the several Sultanate cesses and grants.
xs: **Taccavi (sondhar)** were **loans to cultivators to extend cultivation** — option **(4)**.
Given by **Muhammad bin Tughlaq**, along with the **Diwan-i-Kohi**.
The canal tax was **haq-i-sharb**; the grazing tax **Charai**; religious grants **inam**.
xa: Diwan-i-Kohi is also called **Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi**.
**MBT and Firoz** both pushed irrigation and "**superior crops**".

113.s: Paper-making was particularly significant for the Sultanate administration because it:
113.x: The availability of paper strengthened bureaucratic record-keeping in the Sultanate administration.
113.tq: Link a technological development to its administrative consequence.
xs: Paper-making **strengthened bureaucratic record-keeping** — option **(2)**.
It did not replace coinage: the **tanka** (silver) and **jital** (copper) remained the basic coins.
xa: Paper and the **Persian wheel** were lasting gains.
Other Turkish technologies: **glass-making**, **spinning wheel**, better **looms**.
Superior **mortar** for **arches and domes**.

113.s: Which combination correctly represents crafts that flourished during the Sultanate period?
o: Automobile manufacture, glass fibre and cement
Tea processing, rubber and petroleum refining
113.x: Leather work, metal-work and carpet-weaving flourished during the Sultanate period, along with textiles and other crafts.
113.tq: Select the historically appropriate craft cluster and reject anachronistic industries.
xs: **Leather, metal-work and carpet-weaving** flourished — option **(2)**.
**Textiles** also flourished; the other options list modern industries.
xa: Royal **karkhanas** made luxury goods; **Firoz** ran about **36**.
**Sericulture** reduced the need to import raw silk.

113.s: Which Delhi Sultan is known to have run about 36 royal karkhanas producing goods for the court?
113.x: Royal karkhanas made luxury goods for the court, and Firoz Shah Tughlaq ran about 36 of them. Iltutmish, Alauddin and Sikandar Lodi are not credited with this figure.
113.tq: 36 karkhanas = Firoz.
xs: **Firoz Shah Tughlaq** ran about **36 royal karkhanas** — option **(3)**.
Karkhanas made **luxury goods** for the court.
xa: Firoz also had a separate **department for slaves**.
Firoz founded **Hisar, Firozabad, Fatehabad, Jaunpur**.

113.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below.

List-I (City or fort)
a. Siri
b. Tughlaqabad
c. Jahanpanah
d. Agra

List-II (Founder)
i. Sikandar Lodi
ii. Muhammad bin Tughlaq
iii. Alauddin Khalji
iv. Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq
113.x: Alauddin Khalji founded Siri, Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq founded Tughlaqabad, Muhammad bin Tughlaq founded Jahanpanah and Sikandar Lodi founded Agra.
113.tq: Begin with the well-known Agra–Sikandar Lodi pair and eliminate the remaining codes.
xs: **Siri – Alauddin Khalji**, **Tughlaqabad – Ghiyasuddin Tughluq**, **Jahanpanah – MBT**, **Agra – Sikandar Lodi** — option **(1)**.
So a–iii, b–iv, c–ii, d–i.
xa: **Firoz** founded **Hisar (Hisar Firoza), Firozabad, Fatehabad, Jaunpur**.
Sikandar Lodi founded Agra in **1504** and moved the capital there.

113.s: Which one of the following was NOT founded by Firoz Shah Tughlaq?
113.x: Siri was founded by Alauddin Khalji. Firoz Shah Tughlaq founded Firozabad, Fatehabad, Hisar-Firoza and Jaunpur.
113.tq: Find the odd city-founder association within the same historical period.
xs: **Siri** was NOT founded by Firoz; it was **Alauddin Khalji's** — option **(4)**.
Firoz founded **Firozabad**, **Hisar Firoza**, **Fatehabad** and **Jaunpur**.
xa: **Tughlaqabad** = Ghiyasuddin; **Jahanpanah** = MBT.
**Agra (1504)** = Sikandar Lodi.

113.s:
Consider the following statements about trade in the Sultanate period:
1. The overland route ran from Khorasan through Kabul to Multan and Lahore.
2. Coastal trade used the Gujarat ports of Cambay and Broach.
3. Silk and porcelain were imported from West Asia.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
113.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the overland route was Khorasan-Kabul-Multan/Lahore and coastal trade used Cambay and Broach. Statement 3 is wrong: silk and porcelain came from China; West Asia supplied textiles, glassware and horses. So B; A omits 2, C and D include the false statement 3.
113.tq: Silk and porcelain = China; horses = West Asia.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the overland route ran **Khorasan → Kabul → Multan and Lahore**.
Statement 2 is correct: coastal trade used Gujarat ports **Cambay and Broach**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **silk and porcelain** came from **China**; West Asia sent **textiles, glassware, horses** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: India was tied into the **Islamic world economy**.
Caravans used **roads and sarais**.

113.s: Khorasan fruit was brought to Delhi by which mode of transport?
113.x: Khorasan fruit was brought to Delhi through the horse-post system.
113.tq: Recall the specific commodity–transport association rather than the general role of caravans.
xs: **Khorasan fruit** came to Delhi by the **horse-post system** — option **(4)** (**APPSC-G1 2017** key).
The horse post (**uluq/ulaq**) had **royal horses** about every **4 miles**.
xa: The foot post (**dawa**) had **three stations** to every mile.
**Banjaras** carried bulk grain on oxen.

113.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Multanis and Khurasanis — Overseas trade and financing
2. Gujarati, Marwari and Muslim Bohra merchants — Inland trade
3. Banjaras — Bulk carriage of grain using oxen
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
113.x: Multanis and Khurasanis controlled overseas trade and financing; Gujarati, Marwari and Muslim Bohra merchants dominated inland trade; and Banjaras carried bulk goods such as grain using oxen.
113.tq: Start with the distinctive Banjaras association and verify the remaining trading groups.
xs: All three pairs are correct: **Multanis and Khurasanis** – overseas trade; **Gujarati, Marwari, Bohra** – inland trade; **Banjaras** – bulk grain on oxen — option **(4)**.
So **1, 2 and 3** are all correctly matched.
xa: Gujarati merchants included **Hindus, Jains and Muslims**.
⚠ **Multanis and Khurasanis** = overseas; **Gujarati, Marwari, Bohra** = inland.
Banjaras moved goods over **long distances**.

113.s: Before the Delhi Sultanate, which coin was minted at Delhi by the Tomaras and Chauhans?
113.x: The dehliwal was minted at Delhi before the Sultanate under the Tomaras and Chauhans.
113.tq: Separate pre-Sultanate coinage from Sultanate coinage.
xs: The **dehliwal** was minted at Delhi under the **Tomaras and Chauhans** — option **(2)**.
The **tanka** and **jital** came later under **Iltutmish**; **Bahloli** coins were **Bahlol Lodi's**.
xa: Tanka = ancestor of the **rupee**.
Iltutmish's coins were standard **Arabic** coinage.

113.s: Gold dinars became popular under Alauddin Khalji mainly after:
o: The introduction of token currency in Delhi
The establishment of the horse-post system
113.x: Gold dinars became popular under Alauddin Khalji after his South Indian conquests.
113.tq: Link the monetary development to the event that generated the relevant wealth.
xs: Gold dinars became popular under **Alauddin** after his **South Indian conquests** — option **(3)**.
**Token currency** was **MBT's**, later.
xa: Copper coins were then **fewer and undated**.
Alauddin raised land revenue to **1/2**.

113.s:
Consider the following statements about the token currency of Muhammad bin Tughlaq:
1. Brass and copper coins were issued at par with the silver tanka (c. 1329-30).
2. It failed because of widespread forgery and was withdrawn.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
113.x: Statement 1 is correct: brass/copper tokens were made equal in value to the silver tanka around 1329-30. Statement 2 is correct: widespread forgery led to its failure and withdrawal. So 'Both 1 and 2' (C); A and B each omit a true statement, D rejects both.
113.tq: Token currency: brass/copper at par with silver; killed by forgery.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **brass/copper** tokens were issued **at par with the silver tanka** (**c. 1329-30**).
Statement 2 is correct: **widespread forgery** made it fail and it was **withdrawn** — so **Both 1 and 2**, option **(3)**.
xa: It was **Muhammad bin Tughlaq's** token currency.
MBT also set up the **Diwan-i-Kohi** and gave **taccavi** loans.

113.s:
Consider the following statements about Sultanate coinage:
1. The tanka was a silver coin associated with Iltutmish.
2. The tanka weighed 175 grains.
3. The jital was a copper coin associated with Iltutmish.
4. The shashgani was a silver-based coin worth six jitals.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
113.x: All four statements are correct. The tanka was silver, associated with Iltutmish and weighed 175 grains; the jital was copper; and the shashgani was worth six jitals.
113.tq: Verify each coin through its metal, ruler association, weight or relative value before selecting the complete combination.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the **tanka** was **silver**, from **Iltutmish**, weighing **175 grains**.
Statement 3 is correct: the **jital** was **copper**, from Iltutmish.
Statement 4 is correct: **Shashgani** = silver-based coin worth **6 jitals** — so **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(4)**.
xa: ⚠ Sources differ on **Shashgani**: listed under **Firoz's** small coins and under **MBT**.
**Bahloli** coins were **copper** (Bahlol Lodi).

113.s:
Consider the following statements about Sultanate society:
1. Turkish nobles, and later Indian Muslim and Afghan nobles, held iqtas.
2. The ulema were the custodians of religious law.
3. Peasants bore the burden of revenue collection through khuts and muqaddams.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
113.x: All three statements are correct. Nobles held iqtas, the ulema interpreted religious law, and khuts and muqaddams were involved in collecting revenue from peasants.
113.tq: Verify each social group against its distinct administrative or economic role.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **nobles** — Turkish, later Indian Muslim and Afghan — **held iqtas**.
Statement 2 is correct: the **ulema** were keepers of **religious law**.
Statement 3 is correct: **peasants** bore the revenue burden, collected through **khuts and muqaddams** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: **Slaves** were traded in slave markets (**Ibn Battuta**).
Hindu society: caste order kept; **sati** and **purdah** spread.

113.s: Which statement regarding slaves during the Sultanate period is correct?
o: Slaves were employed only in agriculture and not traded
Ibn Battuta mentioned slave markets, and Firoz Tughlaq maintained a separate department for slaves
Slaves were absent from urban markets
Firoz Tughlaq abolished all forms of slavery
113.x: Ibn Battuta referred to slave markets, and Firoz Tughlaq maintained a separate department for slaves.
113.tq: Reject absolute statements and combine the two documented features of slavery.
xs: **Ibn Battuta** mentioned **slave markets**, and **Firoz** had a **separate department** for slaves — option **(2)**.
Firoz did not abolish slavery; slaves were traded in markets.
xa: Firoz's slave department = **Diwan-i-Bandagan**.
Firoz also ran about **36 karkhanas**.

113.s: Which social developments are associated with medieval Hindu society during the Sultanate period?
o: The disappearance of caste distinctions and purdah
The abolition of sati and caste by royal decree
The replacement of caste by iqta administration
The continuation of caste order and the spread of sati and purdah
113.x: Hindu society retained its caste order, while sati and purdah spread during this period.
113.tq: Identify the option that preserves both social features rather than reversing them.
xs: Hindu society kept its **caste order**, while **sati and purdah spread** — option **(4)**.
So caste did not disappear and sati was not abolished.
xa: **Nobles** held iqtas; **ulema** kept religious law.
**Peasants** bore the revenue burden.

113.s: Alauddin Khalji's price-control markets primarily demonstrate that:
o: Trade was restricted to religious institutions
Military needs could shape economic policy
Agriculture had no connection with state policy
Economic policy was independent of military requirements
113.x: Alauddin Khalji's price controls were designed in the context of maintaining the army, showing how military needs shaped economic policy.
113.tq: Infer the broader administrative significance from a specific economic measure.
xs: Alauddin's **price-control markets** show **military needs shaping economic policy** — option **(2)**.
They kept his army's **cash pay** adequate.
xa: Alauddin got daily market reports from **barids** and **munhiyans**.
He raised land revenue to **1/2**.

113.s:
Consider the following statements about land and revenue in the Deccan:
1. Kakatiya land was classed as Maagani (irrigated) and Metta (rain-fed).
2. Kakatiya big tanks (Samudrams) were linked in chains.
3. Bahmani kharaj was normally one-half of the produce.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
113.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Maagani = irrigated, Metta = rain-fed, and Samudrams were linked in chains. Statement 3 is wrong: Bahmani kharaj was normally one-third. So B; A omits 2, C and D include the false statement 3.
113.tq: Bahmani kharaj = 1/3, the usual Sultanate share.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: Kakatiya land was **Maagani** (irrigated) or **Metta** (rain-fed).
Statement 2 is correct: big tanks (**Samudrams**) were **linked in chains**.
Statement 3 is wrong: Bahmani kharaj was normally **1/3**, not one-half — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Kakatiya land tax = **Ari**.
Sultanate **kharaj** was also usually **1/3**, varying from **1/10 to 1/2**.
**Alauddin** raised land revenue to **1/2**.

113.s: Sher Shah's revenue system served as a model for the later:
113.x: Sher Shah's surveyed revenue system became the model for Todar Mal's bandobast.
113.tq: Match the earlier revenue system with the later administrative adaptation.
xs: **Sher Shah's** survey-based revenue was the model for **Todar Mal's bandobast** — option **(4)**.
Sher Shah took **1/4 to 1/3** of produce, **based on survey**.
The **canal** work was **Ghiyasuddin's** and **Firoz's**; the **karkhanas** were Firoz's; the iqta was organised by **Iltutmish**.
xa: Sultanate peasants paid **1/3**, sometimes **1/2**.
Sher Shah also set up the **dak chowki**.

113.s: According to Amir Khusrau, the wealth and diamonds of Kakatiya Warangal attracted:
113.x: Amir Khusrau's account of Warangal's diamonds and wealth helps explain why it attracted invasions from Delhi.
113.tq: Link the reported source observation with its historical consequence.
xs: Warangal's **diamonds and wealth**, noted by **Amir Khusrau**, drew **the Delhi invasions** — option **(1)**.
**Warangal** was the **Kakatiya** capital.
xa: Kakatiya land: **Maagani** (irrigated) vs **Metta** (rain-fed); land tax **Ari**.
Kakatiya **Samudrams** were linked in chains.
**Ibn Battuta** described the **Malabar pepper trade** with **China and Persia**.

113.s: Which Muslim ruler's coins bore the image of Lakshmi?
113.x: Muhammad Ghori issued gold coins showing the goddess Lakshmi, copying the earlier Gahadavala type. Kanishka and Chandragupta II were not Muslim rulers.
113.tq: Recall which Muslim ruler copied Hindu coin designs.
n: Muhammad Ghori issued Muslim ruler’s coins bearing Lakshmi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 55-57]
xs: **Muhammad Ghori's** coins bore **Goddess Lakshmi** with the **Arabic Kalma** — so option **(3)** is correct.
He is the **Muslim ruler** whose coins carried Lakshmi.
**Iltutmish's** coins were **purely Arabic**, bearing the **Khalifa's name**.
xa: Pre-Sultanate Delhi minted the **dehliwal** under the **Tomaras** and **Chauhans**.
Iltutmish introduced the **Tanka** (silver) and **Jital** (copper) — the two basic Sultanate coins.
Tanka = ancestor of the **rupee**.

113.s:
Assertion (A): Iltutmish's coins bore the Khalifa's name after his recognition by the Abbasid Caliph.
Reason (R): Recognition by the Abbasid Caliph preceded the appearance of the Khalifa's name on Iltutmish's coins.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
113.x: Both are true and R explains A: Iltutmish received recognition from the Abbasid Caliph in 1229, and after that he put the Caliph's name on his coins.
113.tq: Check whether R is the cause of A.
n: Iltutmish placed the Khalifa’s name on his coins after recognition by the Abbasid Caliph. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 55-57]
xs: **Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Iltutmish** placed the **Khalifa's name** on his coins **after recognition** by the **Abbasid Caliph**.
The recognition came first and led to the Caliph's name on coins — R explains A.
xa: Iltutmish **introduced regular Sultanate coinage** in **silver** and **copper**.
His silver tanka weighed **175 grains** (⚠ some notes print **175 grams**).
⚠ **Muhammad Ghori's** coins showed **Lakshmi**; Iltutmish's were **purely Arabic**.

113.s:
Assertion (A): Sher Shah's currency consisted of pure gold, silver and copper.
Reason (R): Pure silver in the Rupiya weighed 173 grains.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
113.x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Sher Shah issued coins in pure gold, silver and copper, and his Rupiya held 173 grains of pure silver. R describes one coin, not the whole currency.
113.tq: Check whether R is the cause of A.
n: Sher Shah currency consisted of pure gold, silver, and copper. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 101-102]
The Rupiya contained 173 grains of pure silver. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 101-102]
xs: **Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A** — so option **(2)** is correct.
A: **Sher Shah's currency** was in **pure gold, silver and copper**.
R: the **Rupiya** (**178 grains**) held **173 grains** of **pure silver** — a fact about one coin, not the reason for A.
xa: **Copper Daam** weighed **380 grains**.
Exchange ratio **Rupiya : Daam** = **1:64**.
Sher Shah's revenue = **1/4 to 1/3** of produce, a model for **Todar Mal's** bandobast.

113.s: What was the ratio of the Rupiya to the Daam?
113.x: One Rupiya of Sher Shah was worth 64 copper Daams, a ratio of 1 : 64.
113.tq: Recall the exchange rate of Rupiya and Daam.
n: The exchange ratio of the Rupiya to the Daam was 1:64. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 101-102]
xs: **One Rupiya** = **64 Daams**, a ratio of **1 : 64** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **Sher Shah Rupiya** weighed **178 grains** (**173 grains** of pure silver); the **copper Daam** **380 grains**.
xa: Sher Shah's currency: **pure gold, silver and copper**.
**Iltutmish's** **Tanka** = silver, **Jital** = copper.
**Bahloli** coins of **Bahlol Lodi** were **copper**.

113.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Fatehpur Sikri is associated with Akbar, Buland Darwaza and Ibadat Khana.
II. Daulatabad or Devagiri is associated with Muhammad bin Tughlaq’s capital transfer.
III. Nagarkot is associated with about 1300 Sanskrit manuscripts from the Jawalamukhi library.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
113.x: All three are correct: Akbar built Fatehpur Sikri with the Buland Darwaza and Ibadat Khana, Muhammad bin Tughlaq shifted his capital to Daulatabad (Devagiri), and Firuz Tughlaq took about 1,300 Sanskrit manuscripts from the Jawalamukhi temple library at Nagarkot.
113.tq: Check each place with its ruler.
n: Fatehpur Sikri was associated with Akbar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
Fatehpur Sikri had the Buland Darwaza. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
Fatehpur Sikri had the Ibadat Khana. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
Daulatabad was also known as Devagiri. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
Muhammad bin Tughlaq was associated with Daulatabad. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
Daulatabad was associated with the transfer of the capital. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
Nagarkot was associated with Firuz Tughlaq. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
The Jawalamukhi library had approximately 1,300 Sanskrit manuscripts. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
Nagarkot was associated with approximately 1,300 Sanskrit manuscripts from the Jawalamukhi library. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
xs: All three — **I, II and III** — are correct, so option **(4)** is correct.
I: **Fatehpur Sikri** is linked with **Akbar**, the **Buland Darwaza** and the **Ibadat Khana**.
II: **Daulatabad / Devagiri** — **Muhammad bin Tughlaq's** **transfer of the capital**.
III: **Nagarkot** — **Firuz Tughlaq** took about **1,300 Sanskrit manuscripts** from the **Jawalamukhi library**.
xa: **Allahabad (Prayagraj)** — **Akbar's fort**.
**Hampi** — the **Vijayanagara Empire**.
**Jahanpanah** was founded by **Muhammad bin Tughlaq**.

113.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Agra was a Mughal imperial centre.
II. Delhi was especially a Mughal imperial capital under Shah Jahan.
III. Lahore was a Mughal political and architectural centre.
IV. Allahabad is associated with Akbar's fort and Mughal administration.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
113.x: All four are correct: Agra, Delhi (Shahjahanabad under Shah Jahan) and Lahore were Mughal imperial centres, and Akbar built the fort at Allahabad (Prayagraj) as a provincial seat.
113.tq: Check each city's Mughal role.
n: Agra was a Mughal imperial centre. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
Delhi was a Mughal imperial capital, especially under Shah Jahan. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
Lahore was a Mughal political and architectural centre. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
Allahabad was associated with Akbar's fort. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
Allahabad was associated with Mughal administration. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
Allahabad was also known as Prayagraj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
Delhi was a Mughal political centre. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
xs: All four — **I, II, III and IV** — are correct, so option **(4)** is correct.
**Agra** — a **Mughal imperial centre**; **Delhi** — Mughal imperial capital, especially under **Shah Jahan**.
**Lahore** — **Mughal political and architectural centre**; **Allahabad** — **Akbar's fort**, **Mughal administration**.
xa: **Agra** was founded by **Sikandar Lodi** (**1504**).
**Firoz Tughlaq** founded **Hisar Firoza, Firozabad, Fatehabad, Jaunpur**.
**Siri** — **Alauddin Khalji**; **Tughlaqabad** — **Ghiyasuddin Tughluq**.

113.s:
Assertion (A): Haqq-e-Sharb was an irrigation tax under Firuz Tughlaq.
Reason (R): Haqq-e-Sharb amounted to 10% of the crop yield.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
113.x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Firuz Tughlaq's Haqq-i-Sharb was an irrigation tax, fixed at 10% of the yield. R gives the rate, not the reason it was an irrigation tax.
113.tq: Check whether R is the cause of A.
n: Firuz Tughlaq imposed Haqq-e-Sharb as an irrigation tax. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 104-105]
