**Ibn Battuta** wrote the **Rihla** (Arabic).
Khusrau's ragas: **Aiman (Yaman), Zilaf, Sazgiri**.

117.s: Which ruler unified Bengal in 1342 and made Pandua his capital?
117.x: Haji Ilyas, who assumed the title Shamsuddin Ilyas Shah, unified Bengal in 1342 and established Pandua as his capital.
117.tq: Distinguish the unifier of Bengal from the rulers connected with its monuments and later dynasty.
xs: **Haji Ilyas (Shamsuddin Ilyas Shah)** unified Bengal in **1342** with **Pandua** as capital — option **(1)**.
He founded the **Ilyas Shahi** line; **Alauddin Hussain Shah** founded the later **Hussain Shahi** line.
**Sikandar Shah** built the **Adina Mosque**; **Jalaluddin Muhammad Shah** lies in the **Eklakhi Tomb**.
xa: ⚠ **1342** Bengal (Ilyas) – **1347** Bahmani – **1394** Sharqi – **1401** Malwa – **1407** Gujarat.
Akbar annexed **Bengal** in **1576**.
Bengal chronicle: **Riyaz-us-Salatin**.

117.s:
Consider the following statements about Ilyas Shahi monuments at Pandua:
1. The Adina Mosque was built by Sikandar Shah.
2. The Adina Mosque is one of the largest mosques in India.
3. The Eklakhi Tomb, prototype for Bengal buildings, is the tomb of Alauddin Hussain Shah.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
117.x: Statement 1 is correct: Sikandar Shah built the Adina Mosque (1373-75). Statement 2 is correct: it is one of India's largest mosques. Statement 3 is wrong: the Eklakhi Tomb is that of Jalaluddin Muhammad Shah (1414-31); Alauddin Hussain Shah founded the later Hussain Shahi dynasty. So 1 and 2 only.
117.tq: Adina = Sikandar Shah; Eklakhi = Jalaluddin Muhammad Shah.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **Sikandar Shah** built the **Adina Mosque** (**1373-75**) — correct.
Statement 2: it is one of **India's largest** mosques — correct.
Statement 3: wrong — the **Eklakhi Tomb** is of **Jalaluddin Muhammad Shah** (**1414-31**).
xa: The Eklakhi Tomb was the **prototype for Bengal buildings**.
Hussain Shahi works: **Chhota Sona Masjid** (**1510**), mosque at **Bagerhat**.

117.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Hussain Shah and his son Nusrat Shah of Bengal patronised Bengali translations of the Mahabharata.
2. Sikandar of Kashmir, called Butshikan, abolished jizya and called back the Brahmins.
3. Chaitanya lived during the reign of Hussain Shah.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
117.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: the Hussain Shahis patronised Bengali Mahabharata translations, and Chaitanya lived in Hussain Shah's reign. Statement 2 is wrong: Sikandar 'Butshikan' destroyed temples, imposed jizya and drove out Brahmins; it was Zain-ul-Abidin (Bud Shah) who abolished jizya and called the Brahmins back. Hence 1 and 3 only.
117.tq: Butshikan = Sikandar (jizya imposed); Bud Shah = Zain-ul-Abidin (jizya abolished).
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1: **Hussain Shah** and **Nusrat Shah** patronised **Bengali translations** of the **Mahabharata**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Sikandar "Butshikan"** imposed jizya and drove out Brahmins; **Zain-ul-Abidin** abolished jizya and called them back.
Statement 3: **Chaitanya** lived in **Hussain Shah's** reign.
xa: ⚠ **Butshikan** = Sikandar; **Bud Shah** = Zain-ul-Abidin, the **"Akbar of Kashmir"**.
Zain-ul-Abidin had the **Mahabharata** and **Rajatarangini** translated into Persian.
He built the **Zaina Kadal** bridge in Srinagar.

117.s:
Consider the following statements about the end of the provincial kingdoms:
1. Akbar annexed Gujarat in 1572.
2. Baz Bahadur, the last Sultan of Malwa, was defeated by Akbar.
3. Akbar annexed Bengal in 1567.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
117.x: Statement 1 is correct: Gujarat was annexed in 1572. Statement 3 is wrong: Bengal was annexed in 1576, after Gujarat. Statement 2 is correct: Baz Bahadur, last Sultan of Malwa, was defeated by Akbar. Hence 1 and 2 only.
117.tq: Akbar: Gujarat 1572 then Bengal 1576.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1: **Akbar** annexed **Gujarat** in **1572**.
Statement 2: **Baz Bahadur**, last Sultan of **Malwa**, was defeated by **Akbar**.
Statement 3 is wrong: Akbar annexed **Bengal** in **1576**, after Gujarat.
xa: **Jaunpur** fell to **Bahlul Lodi** in **1479**.
The **Bahmani** kingdom ended in **1527** under **Kalimullah**.
⚠ Akbar: Gujarat **1572** → Bengal **1576**.

117.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the Bahmani Sultanate is correct?
1. It was the first independent Muslim kingdom of the Deccan.
2. Gulbarga was its initial capital.
3. Its last Sultan was Kalimullah.
4. The kingdom ended in 1527.
117.x: All four statements are correct. The Bahmani kingdom was founded in the Deccan, initially ruled from Gulbarga, and ended in 1527 under its last Sultan, Kalimullah.
117.tq: Check every statement against the kingdom’s identity, capital, last ruler and terminal date.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
The Bahmani kingdom (**1347**) was the **first independent Muslim kingdom of the Deccan**, capital **Gulbarga**.
Its last Sultan was **Kalimullah**; it ended in **1527**.
xa: **Ahmad Shah I** shifted the capital to **Bidar**.
**Golconda (Qutb Shahi)** grew out of the Bahmani break-up.
Main conflict with Vijayanagara: the **Raichur Doab**.

117.s:
Which of the following were also disputed zones in the Bahmani–Vijayanagara conflicts?
1. Krishna-Godavari delta
2. Marathwada
3. Mewar
4. Khandesh
117.x: The Krishna-Godavari delta and Marathwada were other disputed zones. Mewar and Khandesh are associated with other regional kingdoms in the period.
117.tq: Distinguish secondary disputed regions from territories belonging to other kingdoms.
xs: **Krishna-Godavari delta** and **Marathwada** were Bahmani conflict zones — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
The main zone was the **Raichur Doab**.
**Mewar** was the **Sisodias'** kingdom and **Khandesh** the **Faruqis'** — not Bahmani-Vijayanagara zones.
xa: Exam angle: "main cause of conflict" = **Raichur Doab**.
AP angle: **Telangana revolts** against the Bahmanis, quelled by Mahmud Gawan with **Velama** help.

117.s: The Bahmani Sultanate was founded in 1347 by:
117.x: Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah, also called Hasan Gangu, founded the Bahmani Sultanate in 1347 with Gulbarga as capital. Muhammad Shah I built the Gulbarga Jama Masjid, Ahmad Shah I shifted the capital to Bidar, and Firuz Shah was the scholar-king.
117.tq: Bahman Shah = Hasan Gangu, 1347, Gulbarga.
xs: The Bahmani Sultanate was founded in **1347** by **Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah (Hasan Gangu)** — option **(3)**.
**Muhammad Shah I** built the Gulbarga Jama Masjid; **Ahmad Shah I** shifted to **Bidar**; **Firuz Shah** was the scholar-king.
xa: Capital: **Gulbarga**; first independent Muslim kingdom of the **Deccan**.
**Kalaburagi (Gulbarga) Fort** is his fort, flagged by the PM for neglect.

117.s:
Consider the following statements about the Bahmani Sultanate:
1. Control of the Raichur Doab was the main cause of its conflict with Vijayanagara.
2. Muhammad Shah I shifted the capital from Gulbarga to Bidar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
117.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Raichur Doab was the main bone of contention with Vijayanagara. Statement 2 is wrong: Ahmad Shah I shifted the capital to Bidar; Muhammad Shah I built the Gulbarga Jama Masjid. So 1 only.
117.tq: Doab = conflict; Ahmad Shah I = Bidar.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1: the **Raichur Doab** was the main cause of conflict with **Vijayanagara** — correct.
Statement 2: wrong — **Ahmad Shah I** shifted the capital to **Bidar**; **Muhammad Shah I** built the Gulbarga Jama Masjid.
xa: Other conflict zones: **Krishna-Godavari delta**, **Marathwada**.
Bahmani end: last Sultan **Kalimullah**, **1527**.

117.s:
Consider the following statements about Mahmud Gawan:
1. He was a Persian Afaqi who served as wazir of Muhammad Shah III.
2. The Bahmani kingdom reached its greatest extent under him.
3. He quelled the Telangana revolts with the help of the Reddis.
4. The Bahmanis took Goa in 1472.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
117.x: Statement 1 is correct: Mahmud Gawan, a Persian Afaqi, was wazir of Muhammad Shah III. Statement 2 is correct: the kingdom reached its greatest extent under him. Statement 3 is wrong: he quelled the Telangana revolts with Velama help, not the Reddis. Statement 4 is correct: the Bahmanis took Goa in 1472. So 1, 2 and 4 only.
117.tq: Telangana revolts put down with Velama help; Goa 1472.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct — option **(2) 1, 2 and 4 only**.
Statements 1 and 2: Mahmud Gawan, a Persian **Afaqi**, was **wazir** of **Muhammad Shah III**; kingdom at **greatest extent** under him.
Statement 3: wrong — he quelled the **Telangana revolts** (**1453** onward) with **Velama** help, not the Reddis.
Statement 4: the Bahmanis took **Goa** in **1472** — correct.
xa: His letters: **Riyaz-ul-Insha**.
Framed by rival nobles and **executed in 1481** → break-up of the kingdom.

117.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the administrative reforms of Mahmud Gawan:
1. He strengthened the central authority.
2. He reduced the power of provincial nobles.
3. He divided the four tarafs into eight provinces.
4. He placed forts under central commanders.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
117.x: All four statements are correct. Mahmud Gawan strengthened the centre, curtailed provincial nobles, divided the four tarafs into eight and placed forts under central commanders.
117.tq: Check each administrative measure separately before selecting the comprehensive combination.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
Mahmud Gawan **strengthened the centre** and **cut the power of provincial nobles**.
He split the **4 tarafs into 8** and put **forts under central commanders**.
xa: **Crown (khalisa) land** was reserved in each taraf.

117.s:
Which of the following features was associated with Mahmud Gawan's madrasa at Bidar?
1. Three-storeyed structure
2. Glazed tiles
3. A large library
4. A model based on Cordoba
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
117.x: Mahmud Gawan's madrasa at Bidar was three storeys high, decorated with glazed tiles and had a huge library. Item 4 is wrong: it followed a Persian (Herat/Samarkand) model; the Cordoba comparison belongs to the Gulbarga Jama Masjid. So 1, 2 and 3 only.
117.tq: Find the misplaced architectural feature before selecting the coded combination.
xs: Items 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
The **Bidar madrasa** had **three storeys**, **glazed tiles** and a **huge library**.
Item 4 is wrong: it followed a **Persian model (Herat/Samarkand)**; **Cordoba** is the model of the **Gulbarga Jama Masjid**.
xa: **Bidriware** of Bidar: **14th century** under the Bahmanis; GI tag **2006**.
Mahmud Gawan's letters: **Riyaz-ul-Insha**.

117.s: Mahmud Gawan's fall was directly associated with which of the following developments?
o: His voluntary retirement after the conquest of Bengal
His defeat at Talikota and the annexation of Berar
His appointment as governor of Gujarat by Akbar
His execution after being framed by rival nobles, followed by the break-up of the Bahmani Kingdom
117.x: Mahmud Gawan was framed by rival nobles and executed, traditionally dated to 1481; his fall contributed to the break-up of the Bahmani Kingdom.
117.tq: Link the cause, event and consequence instead of isolating the execution from its political result.
xs: Mahmud Gawan was **framed by rival nobles** and **executed**, followed by the **break-up of the Bahmani kingdom** — option **(4)**.
Executed in **1481** (some notes say **1482**).
xa: Under him the kingdom had reached its **greatest extent**; Bahmanis took **Goa (1472)**.
Last Sultan **Kalimullah**; kingdom ended **1527**.
**Golconda (Qutb Shahi)** grew out of the Bahmani break-up.

117.s: Zain-ul-Abidin of Kashmir was popularly known by which of the following titles?
o: Bud Shah and the Akbar of Kashmir
Butshikan and Lord of the East
117.x: Zain-ul-Abidin was called “Bud Shah”, meaning Great King, and the “Akbar of Kashmir”.
117.tq: Match the ruler with his distinctive epithets, avoiding famous but unrelated titles.
xs: **Zain-ul-Abidin** was called **"Bud Shah" (Great King)** and the **"Akbar of Kashmir"** — option **(1)**.
**Butshikan** was **Sikandar's** epithet; **Lord of the East** (Malik-us-Sharq) was **Malik Sarwar's** title; **Shiraz-i-Hind** = Jaunpur.
xa: Original name: **Shahi Khan**; ruled **1420-1470**.
He **abolished jizya**, rebuilt temples and recalled Brahmins.

117.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the religious policy of Zain-ul-Abidin:
1. He abolished jizya.
2. He permitted the rebuilding of temples.
3. He called back Brahmins who had fled Kashmir.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
117.x: All three statements correctly describe the conciliatory religious policy of Zain-ul-Abidin.
117.tq: Recognise a cluster of measures belonging to the same ruler.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Zain-ul-Abidin** **abolished jizya**, had **temples rebuilt** and **called back fled Brahmins**.
xa: This reversed the policy of **Sikandar Butshikan**, who imposed jizya.
He had the **Mahabharata** and **Rajatarangini** translated into Persian.
Works: **Zaina Kadal** bridge (Srinagar), **Zaina Lank** island (Wular lake).

117.s:
Which of the following works were translated into Persian during the reign of Zain-ul-Abidin?
1. Mahabharata
2. Rajatarangini
3. Mirat-i-Sikandari
4. Riyaz-us-Salatin
117.x: Zain-ul-Abidin had the Mahabharata and Kalhana's Rajatarangini translated into Persian. Mirat-i-Sikandari is a Persian history of the Gujarat Sultanate by Sikandar bin Muhammad, and Riyaz-us-Salatin is a chronicle of Bengal; neither was a translation under him.
117.tq: Eliminate works belonging to other regional chronicles.
xs: The **Mahabharata** and **Kalhana's Rajatarangini** were put into Persian — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
**Mirat-i-Sikandari** is a Persian history of **Gujarat** by Sikandar bin Muhammad.
**Riyaz-us-Salatin** is a **Bengal** chronicle — neither was translated under him.
xa: **Jonaraja** continued the Rajatarangini.
Zain-ul-Abidin = "**Akbar of Kashmir**".

117.s: Who founded the Sharqi dynasty of Jaunpur in 1394?
o: Malik Sarwar, also known as Khwaja Jahan
117.x: Malik Sarwar, known as Khwaja Jahan, founded the Sharqi dynasty in 1394 after receiving the title Malik-us-Sharq.
117.tq: Distinguish the founder of the dynasty from the founder of the city and its last ruler.
xs: The **Sharqi** dynasty (**1394**) was founded by **Malik Sarwar (Khwaja Jahan)** — option **(4)**.
His title was **Malik-us-Sharq** ("**Lord of the East**").
**Firoz Shah Tughlaq** founded the **city** of Jaunpur; **Bahlul Lodi** conquered it in **1479**.
xa: Jaunpur = "**Shiraz of India**" (Shiraz-i-Hind), a centre of learning.
**Jaunpur school** of architecture dated **1394-1479**.

117.s: Jaunpur acquired the title “Shiraz-i-Hind” primarily because it was:
o: The capital of the Bahmani kingdom
117.x: Jaunpur was called Shiraz-i-Hind because it developed as a centre of learning.
117.tq: Link an honorific geographical title with the reason for its use.
xs: Jaunpur was called **"Shiraz-i-Hind"** because it was a **centre of learning** — option **(3)**.
It was the **Sharqi** capital, not the Bahmani capital.
xa: Sharqi founder: **Malik Sarwar** (**1394**); city founded by **Firoz Shah Tughlaq**.
The Sharqi court patronised **Khyal**.
Jaunpur fell to **Bahlul Lodi** in **1479**.

117.s:
Consider the following statements about music at the Sharqi court of Jaunpur:
1. The Sharqi court patronised Khyal.
2. The Sufi musician Pir Bodhan flourished under Ibrahim Shah Sharqi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
117.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Sharqi court patronised Khyal. Statement 2 is wrong: Pir Bodhan, a Sufi musician, flourished under Husain Shah Sharqi; Ibrahim Shah Sharqi is the builder of the Atala Masjid. So 1 only.
117.tq: Music = Husain Shah Sharqi; buildings = Ibrahim Shah Sharqi.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1: the **Sharqi court patronised Khyal** — correct.
Statement 2: wrong — **Pir Bodhan** was at the court of **Husain Shah Sharqi**; **Ibrahim Shah Sharqi** built the **Atala Masjid**.
xa: Pir Bodhan was asked in **UPSC**.
Jaunpur = **Shiraz-i-Hind**, centre of learning.

117.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Atala Masjid — Ibrahim Shah Sharqi
2. Jama Masjid, Jaunpur — Ibrahim Shah Sharqi
3. Lal Darwaza Mosque — Bibi Raje
4. Ashrafi Mahal — Ibrahim Shah Sharqi
117.x: Atala Masjid and Jama Masjid were associated with Ibrahim Shah Sharqi, while Lal Darwaza Mosque was built by Bibi Raje. Ashrafi Mahal belongs to Mandu, not Jaunpur.
117.tq: Use the monument–builder table and reject a monument shifted from another kingdom.
xs: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
**Atala Masjid** and **Jama Masjid, Jaunpur** — **Ibrahim Shah Sharqi**; **Lal Darwaza Mosque** — queen **Bibi Raje**.
Pair 4 is wrong: **Ashrafi Mahal** is at **Mandu**, late Malwa period.
xa: Atala Masjid: **three-storey facade**, **blue tiles** (UPSC).
⚠ **Lal Darwaza** = a queen (**Bibi Raje**, JPSC 2023 key); **Atala** = **Ibrahim Shah Sharqi**.

117.s:
Consider the following statements about the rulers of Malwa:
1. Dilawar Khan Ghuri broke away from Delhi in 1401.
2. Mahmud Khalji moved the capital from Dhar to Mandu.
3. The Khalji line of Malwa was founded by Mahmud Khalji.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
117.x: Statement 1 is correct: Dilawar Khan Ghuri broke away from Delhi in 1401. Statement 2 is wrong: Hoshang Shah moved the capital from Dhar to Mandu. Statement 3 is correct: Mahmud Khalji founded the Khalji line. So 1 and 3 only.
117.tq: Dhar to Mandu = Hoshang Shah.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(3) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1: **Dilawar Khan Ghuri** broke away from Delhi in **1401** — correct.
Statement 2: wrong — **Hoshang Shah** moved the capital from **Dhar to Mandu**.
Statement 3: the **Khalji** line was founded by **Mahmud Khalji** — correct.
xa: Hoshang Shah's Tomb = **India's first marble tomb**.
Last Sultan **Baz Bahadur** was defeated by **Akbar**.

117.s: Hoshang Shah’s Tomb at Mandu is significant because it is regarded as:
o: The first fort built by Akbar
The first covered courtyard mosque in the Deccan
117.x: Hoshang Shah’s Tomb is regarded as India’s first marble tomb.
117.tq: Match the monument with its distinguishing architectural feature.
xs: **Hoshang Shah's Tomb** at Mandu is **India's first marble tomb** — option **(4)** (UPSC).
The first covered-courtyard mosque in the Deccan is not it — that feature belongs to **Gulbarga Jama Masjid**.
xa: Hoshang Shah moved Malwa's capital from **Dhar → Mandu**.
He began the **Jami Masjid**, Mandu, completed by **Mahmud Khalji**.

117.s:
Consider the following statements regarding monuments at Mandu:
1. Hoshang Shah began the Jami Masjid.
2. Mahmud Khalji completed the Jami Masjid.
3. Ghiyasuddin Khalji built the Hindola Mahal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
117.x: Hoshang Shah began the Jami Masjid, Mahmud Khalji completed it, and Ghiyasuddin Khalji built the Hindola Mahal.
117.tq: Break a monument’s construction history into builder and completer roles.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Hoshang Shah** began the **Jami Masjid**, Mandu; **Mahmud Khalji** completed it.
**Ghiyasuddin Khalji** built the **Hindola Mahal**.
xa: ⚠ **Jahaz Mahal** and **Hindola Mahal** = **Ghiyasuddin Khalji**, not Hoshang Shah (JPSC 2023 key).
Late Malwa: **Baz Bahadur's Palace**, **Rupmati's pavilion**, **Ashrafi Mahal**.

117.s: The Jahaz Mahal at Mandu was built by:
117.x: The Jahaz Mahal at Mandu was built by Ghiyasuddin Khalji (JPSC 2023 key), who also built the Hindola Mahal. Hoshang Shah is known for his marble tomb and for beginning the Jami Masjid, Baz Bahadur for his palace of the late Malwa period, and Dilawar Khan Ghuri for breaking away from Delhi in 1401.
117.tq: Ghiyasuddin Khalji: Jahaz + Hindola Mahals.
xs: The **Jahaz Mahal** at Mandu was built by **Ghiyasuddin Khalji** — option **(2)** (JPSC 2023 key).
He also built the **Hindola Mahal** — **not Hoshang Shah**.
**Hoshang Shah** = first marble tomb; **Baz Bahadur** = late Malwa palace; **Dilawar Khan Ghuri** = broke from Delhi (**1401**).
xa: Jami Masjid, Mandu: begun by **Hoshang Shah**, completed by **Mahmud Khalji**.
Late Malwa: **Baz Bahadur's Palace**, **Rupmati's pavilion**, **Ashrafi Mahal**.

117.s: Which ruler of Gujarat founded Ahmedabad in 1411 on the banks of the Sabarmati?
117.x: Ahmad Shah I founded Ahmedabad in 1411 on the Sabarmati River.
117.tq: Use the ruler–city–date association.
xs: **Ahmad Shah I** of Gujarat founded **Ahmedabad** (**1411**) on the **Sabarmati** — option **(1)**.
**Zafar Khan** (Muzaffar Shah I) founded the Gujarat Sultanate (**1407**).
**Mahmud Begarha** took Girnar and Champaner; **Bahadur Shah** died at Diu.
xa: ⚠ Bahmani **Ahmad Shah I** is a different ruler — he shifted the capital to **Bidar**.
Gujarat style: **Jama Masjid, Ahmedabad**.

117.s: Mahmud Begarha’s name is associated with the capture of which two forts?
117.x: Mahmud Begarha captured Girnar in Junagadh and Champaner, the two forts associated with his name.
117.tq: Test the ruler–two-forts association using nearby regional monuments as distractors.
xs: **Mahmud Begarha** took **Girnar (Junagadh) and Champaner**, the "two forts" of his name — option **(1)**.
**Chittor/Kumbhalgarh** are Mewar; **Asirgarh** is Khandesh; **Raichur/Gulbarga** are Bahmani.
xa: He ruled **1458-1511**; joined **Egypt** against the Portuguese (**Chaul 1508**, lost at **Diu 1509**).
**Mirat-i-Sikandari** describes his prosperity and administration (UPPSC 2023).

117.s: Who authored the Persian history of the Gujarat Sultanate titled Mirat-i-Sikandari?
117.x: Mirat-i-Sikandari was written by Sikandar bin Muhammad as a Persian history of the Gujarat Sultanate.
117.tq: Distinguish an author’s name from a similarly named ruler or chronicle.
xs: **Mirat-i-Sikandari** was written by **Sikandar bin Muhammad** — option **(3)**.
It is a **Persian history of the Gujarat Sultanate**.
**Jonaraja** continued the Rajatarangini; **Sikandar Butshikan** was a Kashmir Sultan; **Riyaz-us-Salatin** is a Bengal chronicle.
xa: It describes **Mahmud Begada's** prosperity and administration (UPPSC 2023).
**Burhan-i-Maasir** = Ahmadnagar (Nizam Shahis).

117.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Chronicle)
 a. Mirat-i-Sikandari
 b. Burhan-i-Maasir
 c. Riyaz-us-Salatin
 d. Riyaz-ul-Insha

List-II (Subject)
 i. Bengal
 ii. Mahmud Gawan’s letters
 iii. Gujarat
 iv. Ahmadnagar
117.x: Mirat-i-Sikandari concerns Gujarat, Burhan-i-Maasir concerns Ahmadnagar, Riyaz-us-Salatin concerns Bengal, and Riyaz-ul-Insha contains Mahmud Gawan’s letters.
117.tq: Start with the sure chronicle–region pair and complete the one-to-one matching.
xs: **a–iii, b–iv, c–i, d–ii** — option **(1)**.
**Mirat-i-Sikandari — Gujarat**; **Burhan-i-Maasir — Ahmadnagar**.
**Riyaz-us-Salatin — Bengal**; **Riyaz-ul-Insha — Mahmud Gawan's letters**.
xa: ⚠ **Riyaz-us-Salatin** = Bengal; **Riyaz-ul-Insha** = Mahmud Gawan's letters.
Burhan-i-Maasir concerns the **Nizam Shahis**.

117.s:
With reference to the Mirat-i-Sikandari, consider the following statements:
1. It describes the prosperity of Mahmud Begada's kingdom.
2. It describes the administrative arrangements of Mahmud Begada.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
117.x: Both statements are correct (UPPSC 2023). The Mirat-i-Sikandari, a Persian history of the Gujarat Sultanate by Sikandar bin Muhammad, describes both the prosperity of Mahmud Begada's kingdom and his administrative arrangements. So options A, B and D are wrong.
117.tq: Mirat-i-Sikandari = Gujarat; Begada's prosperity + administration.
xs: Both statements are correct — option **(3) Both 1 and 2** (UPPSC 2023).
The **Mirat-i-Sikandari** describes the **prosperity** of **Mahmud Begada's** kingdom and his **administrative arrangements**.
xa: Author: **Sikandar bin Muhammad**; a Persian history of the **Gujarat Sultanate**.
Mahmud Begarha took **Girnar** and **Champaner**.

117.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Sisodias — Mewar
2. Rathores — Marwar
3. Faruqis — Khandesh
4. Sisodias — Tapti valley
117.x: Sisodias were associated with Mewar, Rathores with Marwar and Faruqis with Khandesh. The Tapti valley was associated with Khandesh, not the Sisodias.
117.tq: Use region-based elimination to distinguish neighbouring Rajput and Deccan kingdoms.
xs: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
**Sisodias — Mewar**; **Rathores — Marwar**; **Faruqis — Khandesh**.
Pair 4 is wrong: the **Tapti valley** is **Khandesh** (Faruqis), not the Sisodias.
xa: **Rao Jodha** founded **Jodhpur** (**1459**); **Rao Bika** founded Bikaner.
**Rana Sanga** lost at **Khanwa** (**1527**).

117.s:
Consider the following statements about the historical significance of the Bahmani and successor states:
1. The Bahmani-Vijayanagara wars involved control over the Doab.
2. Telangana witnessed revolts against the Bahmani rulers.
3. Golconda, associated with the Qutb Shahis, emerged from the break-up of the Bahmani Kingdom.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
117.x: All three statements are correct. The Doab was contested in Bahmani-Vijayanagara wars, Telangana saw revolts, and the Qutb Shahi state of Golconda emerged from the Bahmani break-up.
117.tq: Group related regional consequences while checking that each statement belongs to the same political context.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: the **Bahmani-Vijayanagara wars** were fought over the **Doab** — correct.
Statement 2: **Telangana** saw **revolts** against the Bahmanis — correct.
Statement 3: **Golconda (Qutb Shahi)** grew out of the **Bahmani break-up** — correct.
xa: "Main cause of conflict" = the **Raichur Doab**; other zones: **Krishna-Godavari delta**, **Marathwada**.
**Mahmud Gawan** quelled the Telangana revolts (**1453** onward) with **Velama** help.
The break-up followed Mahmud Gawan's **execution in 1481**; the kingdom ended in **1527**.

117.s:
Bidriware is correctly described by which of the following statements?
1. It developed in the fourteenth century under the Bahmanis.
2. It is associated with Bidar.
3. It received a Geographical Indication tag in 2006.
4. It was among the diplomatic gifts presented by the Prime Minister on 22 May 2026.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
117.x: All four statements are correct. Bidriware developed under the Bahmanis in the fourteenth century, is linked to Bidar, received a GI tag in 2006 and was included among the Prime Minister’s diplomatic gifts on 22 May 2026.
117.tq: Combine historical origin, geographical association, legal recognition and current relevance in one coded question.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Bidriware** of **Bidar** developed in the **14th century** under the **Bahmanis** — statements 1 and 2.
It got a **GI tag** in **2006** and was among the **PM's diplomatic gifts** — statements 3 and 4.
xa: **Ahmad Shah I** shifted the Bahmani capital from **Gulbarga → Bidar**.
Bidar also has **Mahmud Gawan's madrasa**: three storeys, **glazed tiles**, huge library.

117.s: Malik Sarwar is associated with the foundation of which dynasty?
117.x: Malik Sarwar, a Tughluq noble titled Malik-us-Sharq, founded the Sharqi dynasty of Jaunpur. The Lodi, Sayyid and Tughluq dynasties had other founders.
117.tq: Link the title Malik-us-Sharq to the Sharqi dynasty.
xs: **Malik Sarwar** (Khwaja Jahan) founded the **Sharqi dynasty** of Jaunpur — so option **(4)** is correct.
His title was **Malik-us-Sharq** ("Lord of the East"); the dynasty was founded in **1394**.
xa: The city of **Jaunpur** was founded by **Firoz Shah Tughlaq**.
Jaunpur = **"Shiraz of India"**, a centre of learning.
**Atala Masjid** — **Ibrahim Shah Sharqi**; **Lal Darwaza Mosque** — **Bibi Raje**.

118.s:
Arrange the following successor states of the Bahmani Kingdom in the order in which they broke away:
A. Golconda
B. Ahmadnagar
C. Bijapur
D. Berar
118.x: Bijapur broke away first in 1489, followed by Ahmadnagar and Berar in 1490, while Golconda became independent last in 1518.
118.tq: Fix the first and last breakaways, then place the two states that emerged in 1490.
xs: Order: **Bijapur (1489) → Ahmadnagar (1490) → Berar (1490) → Golconda (1518)** — option **(1) C, B, D, A**.
**Yusuf Adil Shah's Bijapur** was the **first to break away**; **Golconda** under Sultan Quli was the **last**.
xa: ⚠ Golconda = last to break away (**1518**) and last to fall (**1687**).
**Bidar** (Barid Shahi) was founded by **Qasim Barid**.
Ahmadnagar founder: **Malik Ahmad (Ahmad Nizam Shah)**; Berar founder: **Fathullah Imad-ul-Mulk**.

118.s:
Consider the following statements about Berar:
1. It emerged as a successor state of the Bahmani Kingdom.
2. Its founder was Fathullah Imad-ul-Mulk.
3. Ellichpur or Achalpur was its capital.
4. It was annexed by Ahmadnagar in 1574.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
118.x: All four statements are correct. Berar was founded by Fathullah Imad-ul-Mulk, had its capital at Ellichpur or Achalpur and was annexed by Ahmadnagar in 1574.
118.tq: Combine political origin, capital and later fate without confusing Berar with Ahmadnagar or Bidar.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Berar** (Imad Shahi) was a Bahmani successor founded by **Fathullah Imad-ul-Mulk** in **1490**.
Its capital was **Ellichpur/Achalpur**; it was annexed by **Ahmadnagar** in **1574**.
xa: Exam angle: "Berar was founded by" = **Imad Shahis** (APPSC G2 2005).
At **Talikota (1565)** four of the five combined — **all except Berar**.

118.s: Amir Ali Barid, known as the ‘cunning fox of the Deccan’, was associated with which successor state?
118.x: Amir Ali Barid was associated with the Barid Shahi state of Bidar and was referred to as the ‘cunning fox of the Deccan’.
118.tq: Use the sobriquet as the clue for identifying the correct successor state.
xs: **Amir Ali Barid**, "**cunning fox of the Deccan**", belonged to **Bidar** (Barid Shahi) — option **(3)**.
**Bijapur** = Adil Shahi; **Golconda** = Qutb Shahi; **Berar** = Imad Shahi.
xa: Barid Shahi founder: **Qasim Barid**.
Bidar was absorbed by **Bijapur** in **1619**.
Jamsheed of Golconda won the **Battle of Koulan** over Bidar (**1544**).

118.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Deccan Sultanates and Talikota is correct?
o: Only Bijapur and Golconda participated in the battle of Talikota.
The battle of Talikota occurred in 1518, immediately after Golconda became independent.
Four of the five successor states, excluding Berar, combined against Vijayanagara at Talikota in 1565.
All five successor states jointly defeated Vijayanagara at Talikota.
118.x: Four of the five successor states, all except Berar, combined to defeat Vijayanagara at Talikota in 1565.
118.tq: Test the exception in the coalition and reject the extreme claim that all five participated.
xs: **Four of the five** successor states, **all except Berar**, combined against Vijayanagara at **Talikota in 1565** — option **(3)** (UPSC).
So "all five" and "only Bijapur and Golconda" are wrong; **1518** is Golconda's independence, not Talikota.
xa: **Ibrahim Qutb Shah** led the Qutb Shahi part in the Talikota alliance.
**Chand Bibi's** marriage to **Ali Adil Shah** sealed the anti-Vijayanagara alliance.
After 1565, Ibrahim gained **Kondavidu** and **Machilipatnam**.

118.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Dynasty)
a. Adil Shahi
b. Nizam Shahi
c. Imad Shahi
d. Barid Shahi

List-II (Capital)
i. Bidar
ii. Berar
iii. Bijapur
iv. Ahmadnagar

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
118.x: Adil Shahi was centred at Bijapur, Nizam Shahi at Ahmadnagar, Imad Shahi at Berar and Barid Shahi at Bidar.
118.tq: Start from the sure dynasty–capital pairs and eliminate codes.
xs: **a–iii, b–iv, c–ii, d–i** — option **(1)**.
**Adil Shahi — Bijapur**; **Nizam Shahi — Ahmadnagar**.
**Imad Shahi — Berar**; **Barid Shahi — Bidar**.
xa: **Qutb Shahi — Golconda**, later **Hyderabad**.
⚠ **Bijapur** first to break away (**1489**); **Golconda** last (**1518**).

118.s:
Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
1. Adil Shahi — Ended by Aurangzeb in 1686
2. Nizam Shahi — Ended by Shah Jahan in 1633
3. Imad Shahi — Ended by Ahmadnagar in 1574
4. Qutb Shahi — Ended by Shah Jahan in 1633
118.x: The Qutb Shahi dynasty ended under Aurangzeb in 1687, not under Shah Jahan in 1633. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
118.tq: Find the swapped conqueror and end-date in a dynasty table.
xs: **Qutb Shahi — Shah Jahan, 1633** is wrong — option **(4)**; Golconda fell to **Aurangzeb** in **1687**.
The rest are right: **Adil Shahi** — Aurangzeb **1686**; **Nizam Shahi** — Shah Jahan **1633**; **Imad Shahi** — Ahmadnagar **1574**.
xa: ⚠ **1633** Nizam Shahis – **1686** Bijapur – **1687** Golconda.
In **1636** Golconda only signed an **ahdnama** (Inqiyad Nama) accepting Mughal suzerainty.

118.s:
Consider the following statements about Ibrahim Adil Shah II:
1. He wrote Kitab-i-Nauras in Dakhni.
2. He invoked Saraswati as his muse.
3. Firishta dedicated Tarikh-i-Firishta to him.
4. He married Chand Sultana, the sister of Muhammad Quli.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
118.x: All four statements are correct. Ibrahim Adil Shah II was a Dakhni author, invoked Saraswati, received Firishta’s dedication, and married Chand Sultana, Muhammad Quli’s sister.
118.tq: Test several biographical details in a single coded combination.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Ibrahim Adil Shah II** wrote **Kitab-i-Nauras** in **Dakhni**, invoking **Saraswati** as muse.
**Firishta** dedicated **Tarikh-i-Firishta** to him; he married **Chand Sultana**, Muhammad Quli's sister.
xa: His tomb is the **Ibrahim Rauza** (UPSC).
⚠ **Chand Sultana** (his wife) ≠ **Chand Bibi** (wife of Ali Adil Shah).

118.s:
Which of the following statements about Gol Gumbaz is correct?
1. It is the tomb of Muhammad Adil Shah.
2. It has a whispering gallery.
3. It is among the world’s largest domes.
4. There are arches and structures around it.
Select the correct answer using the code below.
118.x: All four statements correctly describe Gol Gumbaz. It is not an isolated dome without surrounding arches and structures.
118.tq: Reject an absolute architectural claim by checking the complete monument description.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Gol Gumbaz** = tomb of **Muhammad Adil Shah**, with a **whispering gallery**, among the **world's largest domes**.
There are **arches and structures** around it (APPSC G2 2003; UPSC).
xa: **Malik-e-Maidan** cannon is also at Bijapur.
**Ibrahim Rauza** = tomb of Ibrahim Adil Shah II.

118.s:
Consider the following statements about the Bijapur style:
1. It is marked by three-arched facades, bulbous domes and cornices.
2. The Malik-e-Maidan associated with Bijapur is a famous gateway.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
118.x: Statement 1 is correct: three-arched facades, bulbous domes and cornices mark the Bijapur style. Statement 2 is wrong: the Malik-e-Maidan is a cannon, not a gateway. So 1 only (A); B and C accept the wrong statement, D rejects the correct one.
118.tq: Malik-e-Maidan = the great cannon of Bijapur.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1: **3-arched facades**, **bulbous domes** and **cornices** mark the Bijapur style — correct.
Statement 2: wrong — **Malik-e-Maidan** is a **cannon**, not a gateway (UPSC).
xa: **Gol Gumbaz** (Muhammad Adil Shah) has a **whispering gallery**.
**Ibrahim Rauza** = tomb of **Ibrahim Adil Shah II**.

118.s:
Consider the following statements about Chand Bibi:
1. She was the daughter of Hussain Nizam Shah I.
2. Her marriage to Ali Adil Shah of Bijapur sealed the anti-Vijayanagara alliance.
3. She defended Ahmadnagar against Shah Jahan in 1633.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
118.x: Statement 1 is correct: she was the daughter of Hussain Nizam Shah I. Statement 2 is correct: her marriage to Ali Adil Shah sealed the anti-Vijayanagara alliance. Statement 3 is wrong: she defended Ahmadnagar against the Mughals in 1595-96 and died when it fell in 1600; 1633 is when Shah Jahan ended the Nizam Shahis. So 1 and 2 only (A); B, C and D include statement 3.
118.tq: Chand Bibi = Akbar-era siege (1595-96); 1633 belongs to Shah Jahan ending the Nizam Shahis.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **Chand Bibi** was the daughter of **Hussain Nizam Shah I** — correct.
Statement 2: her marriage to **Ali Adil Shah** sealed the **anti-Vijayanagara alliance** — correct.
Statement 3: wrong — she defended Ahmadnagar against the Mughals in **1595-96** and died at its fall in **1600**; **1633** is the Nizam Shahi end.
xa: ⚠ **Chand Bibi** ≠ **Chand Sultana** (Muhammad Quli's sister).
**Akbar** took **Ahmadnagar city** in **1600**.

118.s: Who was the Abyssinian regent of the Nizam Shahis who resisted Jahangir?
118.x: Malik Ambar was an Abyssinian regent of the Nizam Shahis and resisted the Mughal emperor Jahangir.
118.tq: Match the distinctive identity and political role with the correct Deccan administrator.
xs: **Malik Ambar** was the **Abyssinian regent** of the Nizam Shahis who resisted **Jahangir** — option **(4)**.
**Fath Khan** was his son; **Abul Razak Lari** defended Golconda; **Abdullah Khan Pani** betrayed Golconda.
xa: He revived land revenue on **Todar Mal's lines**.
He founded **Khirki** → later **Aurangabad**.

118.s:
Which of the following features belonged to Malik Ambar’s revenue system?
1. Survey of land
2. Fixed assessment
3. Absence of revenue farming
4. Use of Maratha guerrilla cavalry
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
118.x: Malik Ambar revived revenue administration on Todar Mal’s lines through survey and fixed assessment, avoided revenue farming and used Maratha guerrilla cavalry.
118.tq: Test whether administrative and military innovations are both included in the same reform profile.
xs: All four features are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
Malik Ambar revived revenue on **Todar Mal's lines**: **survey**, **fixed assessment**, **no revenue farming**.
He also used **Maratha guerrilla cavalry**.
xa: He founded **Khirki**, later **Aurangabad**.
His son **Fath Khan** made peace with the Mughals.

118.s: Malik Ambar founded Khirki, which later came to be known as
118.x: Malik Ambar founded Khirki, which was later known as Aurangabad.
118.tq: Distinguish the original and later names of the city from nearby Deccan centres.
xs: Malik Ambar's **Khirki** later became **Aurangabad** — option **(2)**.
**Daulatabad** is where **Abul Hasan Tana Shah** was imprisoned; **Bidar** was the Barid Shahi capital.
xa: Malik Ambar resisted **Jahangir**.
Revenue system on **Todar Mal's lines**.

118.s:
Consider the following statements about the Qutb Shahi dynasty of Golconda:
1. Its rulers belonged to the Shia sect of Islam.
2. They were Qara Qoyunlu (Black Sheep) Turkmen from Hamadan.
3. Telugu was the official language of the Qutb Shahi court.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
118.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Qutb Shahis were Shia. Statement 2 is correct: they were Qara Qoyunlu (Black Sheep) Turkmen from Hamadan. Statement 3 is wrong: the official language was Persian; Telugu and Dakhni received patronage but were not the court language. So 1 and 2 only (B); A misses statement 2, C and D wrongly include statement 3.
118.tq: Shia + Black Sheep Turkmen + Persian court: patronage of Telugu is not the same as official language.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: the Qutb Shahis were **Shia** — correct.
Statement 2: they were **Qara Qoyunlu (Black Sheep)** Turkmen from **Hamadan** — correct.
Statement 3: wrong — the official language was **Persian**.
xa: The dynasty had **7 rulers** (**1518-1687**).
Hindus held high office (**Murari Rao**, **Jagadeva Rao**, **Madanna**).

118.s: Which of the following statements about Sultan Quli Qutb-ul-Mulk is NOT correct?
o: He gave the dynasty its name through the title Qutb-ul-Mulk.
He was killed by his son Jamsheed.
118.x: Hyderabad was founded in 1591 by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah, not by Sultan Quli Qutb-ul-Mulk. The other three statements describe Sultan Quli.
118.tq: Find the wrong ruler-contribution pairing.
xs: "**He founded Hyderabad in 1591**" is NOT true of Sultan Quli — option **(4)**; **Muhammad Quli** founded it.
True of Sultan Quli: title **Qutb-ul-Mulk** named the dynasty; he **strengthened Golconda fort**; he was **killed by son Jamsheed**.
xa: He was defeated by **Krishnadevaraya at Goni** (**1517**).
He built the **Golconda Jama Masjid** and the new city of **Muhammad Nagar**.

118.s:
Consider the following statements about Ibrahim Qutb Shah:
1. He was known as Malkibharama or Malkibharamudu.
2. He led the Qutb Shahi participation in the Talikota alliance.
3. Hussain Sagar and the Ibrahimpatnam tank are associated with his reign.
4. He introduced the first Qutb Shahi coins.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
118.x: All four statements are correct. Ibrahim was associated with the title Malkibharama, the Talikota alliance of 1565, the two tanks, and the first Qutb Shahi coins.
118.tq: Check a cluster of contributions belonging to one ruler.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
Ibrahim was **Malkibharama / Malkibharamudu** and led the **Talikota (1565)** alliance.
**Hussain Sagar** and the **Ibrahimpatnam tank** date from his reign; he issued the **first Qutb Shahi coins**.
xa: Hussain Sagar was built by **Hussain Shah Wali** — UNWTO "**Heart of the World**" (**2012**).
He was the chief patron of Telugu poets, e.g. **Addanki Gangadhara**.

118.s:
Consider the following statements about Dakhni/Urdu literature under the Qutb Shahis:
1. Urdu literature is said to have reached its peak under Abdullah Qutb Shah.
2. Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah wrote Dakhni poetry under the pen name 'Maani', collected as the Kulliyat-e-Quli Qutb Shah.
3. 'Zillullah' was the pen name of Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
118.x: Statement 2 is correct: Muhammad Quli wrote Dakhni/Urdu poetry as 'Maani' (Kulliyat-e-Quli Qutb Shah). Statement 1 is correct: Urdu literature peaked under Abdullah Qutb Shah. Statement 3 is wrong: Zillullah was the pen name of Muhammad Qutb Shah (1612-26), Muhammad Quli's nephew and son-in-law. Hence 1 and 2 only.
118.tq: Maani = Muhammad Quli; Zillullah = Muhammad Qutb Shah.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1: **Urdu literature peaked** under **Abdullah Qutb Shah**.
Statement 2: **Muhammad Quli** wrote Dakhni poetry as **"Maani"** (**Kulliyat-e-Quli Qutb Shah**).
Statement 3 is wrong: **Zillullah** was the pen name of **Muhammad Qutb Shah** (**1612-26**), Muhammad Quli's nephew.
xa: ⚠ Pen names: **Maani** = Muhammad Quli; **Zillullah** = Muhammad Qutb Shah.
Some notes call **Ibrahim** the **"Chaucer of Urdu"**.
Muhammad Quli **founded Hyderabad** (**1591**) and built the **Charminar**.

118.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Muhammad Qutb Shah — Zillullah
2. Abdullah Qutb Shah — Kshetrayya
3. Abul Hasan Tana Shah — 1677 pact with Shivaji
4. Ibrahim Qutb Shah — 1636 Inqiyad Nama
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
118.x: Muhammad Qutb Shah used Zillullah as his pen-name, Abdullah patronised Kshetrayya, and Abul Hasan made the pact with Shivaji in 1677. The Inqiyad Nama was signed by Abdullah, not Ibrahim.
118.tq: Identify one swapped ruler-document association among otherwise correct pairs.
xs: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(1) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
**Muhammad Qutb Shah — Zillullah**; **Abdullah — Kshetrayya**; **Abul Hasan — Shivaji pact (1677)**.
Pair 4 is wrong: the **1636 Inqiyad Nama** was signed by **Abdullah**, not Ibrahim.
xa: Abdullah also issued the **Bangaru Farmana** (**1636**) to the English.
**Tavernier** visited in **Abdullah's** reign.

118.s: The Inqiyad Nama of 1636 signified which development?
o: Acceptance of Mughal suzerainty by Abdullah Qutb Shah
The declaration of independence from the Bahmani kingdom
The formation of the Talikota alliance
The treaty between Abul Hasan and Shivaji
118.x: Through the Inqiyad Nama of 1636, Abdullah Qutb Shah accepted Mughal suzerainty.
118.tq: Match a document with its political consequence.
xs: The **Inqiyad Nama (1636)** = **Abdullah Qutb Shah's acceptance of Mughal suzerainty** — option **(1)**.
It was a **deed of submission** to **Shah Jahan**.
Independence was declared in **1518**; Talikota was **1565**; the Shivaji treaty was **1677**.
xa: In **1636** both **Bijapur and Golconda** signed **ahdnamas** — suzerainty + indemnity.
The same year Abdullah issued the **Bangaru Farmana** to the English.

118.s: What was the Bangaru Farmana issued by Abdullah Qutb Shah in 1636 associated with?
o: Accepting the Shia faith as the state religion
Granting trading privileges to the English
Beginning construction of the Mecca Masjid
118.x: The Bangaru Farmana of 1636 was issued to the English and is associated with their trading privileges.
118.tq: Distinguish two documents issued in the same year by their purpose.
xs: The **Bangaru Farmana** (**1636**) was issued to the **English** — option **(2)**, trading privileges.
The **Mecca Masjid** was begun by Muhammad Qutb Shah; **Madanna** became Diwan under Abul Hasan.
xa: The English first came to **Machilipatnam** in **1611** (Captain **Hippon**, ship **Globe**).
In the same year Abdullah signed the **Inqiyad Nama**.

118.s:
Which of the following constructions are associated with Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah?
1. Charminar
2. Dar-ul-Shifa
3. Mecca Masjid
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
118.x: Muhammad Quli founded Hyderabad (1591) and built the Charminar and the Dar-ul-Shifa (1595). The Mecca Masjid was begun in 1614 by his successor Muhammad Qutb Shah, so statement 3 is wrong. So 1 and 2 only.
118.tq: Muhammad Quli = Charminar + Dar-ul-Shifa; Muhammad Qutb Shah = Mecca Masjid.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
**Muhammad Quli** built the **Charminar** and the **Dar-ul-Shifa** (**1595**).
The **Mecca Masjid** was begun in **1614** by **Muhammad Qutb Shah**.
xa: Muhammad Quli also built the **Jama Masjid** (**1598**).
⚠ Mecca Masjid completed by **Aurangzeb**; Charminar = **Muhammad Quli**.

118.s: Which of the following places was NOT among the territories conquered by Sultan Quli?
118.x: Sultan Quli conquered Rachakonda, Devarakonda and Rajahmundry, among other places. Kondavidu was gained by Ibrahim after 1565.
118.tq: Find the place associated with Ibrahim’s later coastal expansion rather than Sultan Quli’s conquests.
xs: **Kondavidu** was NOT conquered by Sultan Quli — option **(4)**; **Ibrahim** gained it after **1565**.
Sultan Quli took **Rachakonda**, **Devarakonda**, **Warangal**, **Rajahmundry**, **Eluru**, Kovilakonda.
xa: Ibrahim also gained **Machilipatnam** and annexed coastal Andhra (**1570-78**).
Warangal was taken from **Shitab Khan**.

118.s: Ponnaganti Telaganarya’s Yayati Charitra is notable as
o: the first Telugu work on revenue administration
the first Telugu poem written under Abul Hasan
the first kavya in pure Telugu
118.x: Yayati Charitra is identified as the first kavya in pure Telugu. Its dedication is attributed to Amir Khan in one account and to Ibrahim in another.
118.tq: Distinguish the work’s literary distinction from its disputed dedication.
xs: **Yayati Charitra** is the **first kavya in pure Telugu** — option **(4)**.
The **first Telugu Yakshagana** is **Sugriva Vijayam** (Rudrakavi).
xa: It was dedicated to **Amir Khan**, Ibrahim's governor of **Patancheru** (some notes: to Ibrahim).
⚠ FIRSTs: **Tapati Samvaranopakhyanam** = dedicated to a Muslim ruler; **Yayati Charitra** = pure Telugu.

118.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
118.x: Movva padams are associated with Kshetrayya. Akkanna was a military official, not the composer associated with those padams.
118.tq: Find the mismatched person–work association among closely related Golconda personalities.
xs: **Akkanna — Movva padams** is wrong — option **(4)**; Movva padams are **Kshetrayya's**.
Akkanna was **Sar Lashkar** (army chief).
Others are right: **Rudrakavi — Rentachintala agraharam**; **Bhakta Ramadasu = Kancherla Gopanna**.
xa: Kshetrayya flourished under **Abdullah**; Ramadasu under **Abul Hasan**.
Ramadasu was **Tahsildar of Palvancha/Bhadrachalam** and a nephew of Madanna and Akkanna.

118.s: The Qutb Shahis are credited with uniting the Telugu lands for the:
o: First time, after the Mauryas and Satavahanas
Second time, after the Cholas and Kakatiyas
Third time, after the Satavahanas and Kakatiyas
Fourth time, after the Vijayanagara and Bahmani kingdoms
118.x: The Qutb Shahis united the Telugu lands for the third time, following the earlier unifications under the Satavahanas and Kakatiyas.
118.tq: Use the stated sequence of earlier unifying powers to identify the correct ordinal position.
xs: The Qutb Shahis united the Telugu lands for the **third time**, after the **Satavahanas and Kakatiyas** — option **(3)**.
**Sultan Quli** took Telangana forts; **Ibrahim** annexed **coastal Andhra** (**1570-78**).
xa: Ibrahim gained **Kondavidu** and **Machilipatnam** after **1565**.
Muharram was celebrated as **Peerla Panduga**.

118.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Poet)
a. Addanki Gangadhara
b. Ponnaganti Telaganarya
c. Kandukuri Rudrakavi
List-II (Work)
i. Sugriva Vijayam
ii. Yayati Charitra
iii. Tapati Samvaranopakhyanamu
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
118.x: Addanki Gangadhara wrote Tapati Samvaranopakhyanamu, Ponnaganti Telaganarya wrote Yayati Charitra, and Kandukuri Rudrakavi wrote Sugriva Vijayam.
118.tq: Start from the sure poet–work pair and complete the remaining matches by elimination.
xs: **a–iii, b–ii, c–i** — option **(2)**.
**Addanki Gangadhara — Tapati Samvaranopakhyanamu**; **Ponnaganti Telaganarya — Yayati Charitra**.
**Kandukuri Rudrakavi — Sugriva Vijayam**.
xa: Rudrakavi also wrote **Nirankusopakhyanam** and **Janardanashtakam**.
⚠ Firsts: Muslim dedication / pure Telugu / **Yakshagana**.

118.s: A Tarafdar in the Qutb Shahi administration was primarily responsible for which combination of functions?
o: Judicial administration at the village level
Customs collection at a port only
Law and order, revenue and troops in a province
118.x: The Tarafdar was the governor of a Taraf and was responsible for law and order, revenue and troops.
118.tq: Apply the office’s territorial level to its functions.
xs: The **Tarafdar** governed a **Taraf** (province): **law and order, revenue and troops** — option **(4)**.
Port customs = **Shahbandar**; auditing = **Majumdar / Dabir**.
xa: ⚠ **Taraf – Sarkar – Pargana** = **Tarafdar – Fauzdar – Tahsildar**; **6 – 37 – 517**.
**Abdullah** had **6 Tarafs**.

118.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Majumdar or Dabir — Auditor-general or secretary
118.x: Kayasthas served as scribes. The chief port officer was the Shahbandar; the other three pairs are correctly matched.
118.tq: Find the wrongly assigned official function.
xs: **Kayastha — Chief port officer** is wrong — option **(3)**; **Kayasthas** were **scribes** (APPSC G2 2012).
The chief port officer was the **Shahbandar**.
Others correct: **Ain-ul-Mulk** — military; **Majumdar/Dabir** — auditor/secretary; **Peshwa/Wakil** — prime minister.
xa: **Kotwal** = city police chief who also ran the **mint**.
**Mahasibs** supervised **public morals**.

118.s: Under Abul Hasan, the office of Peshwa was renamed as which office, held by Madanna?
118.x: Under Abul Hasan, the Peshwa or Wakil was renamed Diwan, and the office was held by Madanna.
118.tq: Test an institutional name change and its office-holder together.
xs: Under Abul Hasan the **Peshwa / Wakil** was renamed **Diwan**, held by **Madanna** — option **(4)**.
**Kotwal** = city police; **Shahbandar** = port; **Jumlat-ul-Mulk** = Mir Jumla (finance).
xa: Madanna's titles: **Surya Prakasa Rao** and **Alampana**; **Akkanna** was **Sar Lashkar**.
Madanna and Akkanna were **murdered in 1686**.

118.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Mir Jumla — Finance minister
2. Kotwal — City police chief and mint administration
3. Havaldar — Treasuries and horse or elephant stables
4. Tahsildar — Chief port officer
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
118.x: Mir Jumla was the finance minister, the Kotwal headed city policing and also ran the mint, and the Havaldar was associated with treasuries and stables. The Tahsildar headed a Pargana, not port administration.
118.tq: Use one administrative-unit mismatch to eliminate the incorrect combination.
xs: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
**Mir Jumla** (Jumlat-ul-Mulk) = **finance** minister; **Kotwal** = city police chief who also ran the **mint**.
**Havaldar** = **treasuries and horse/elephant stables** (one account; another says ports and coastal trade).
Pair 4 is wrong: the **Tahsildar** headed a **Pargana**; the chief port officer was the **Shahbandar**.
xa: ⚠ One block calls Mir Jumla **war and foreign affairs** — the standard view is finance.
**Kotwal** sometimes also **judged cases**.

118.s: The Qutb Shahi system of justice was organised in which order from the Sultan downward?
o: Sultan – Qazi – Shariat Panch – Pargana Majlis
Sultan – Shariat Panch – Qazi – Pargana Majlis
Sultan – Pargana Majlis – Qazi – Shariat Panch
118.x: The judicial hierarchy was Sultan, Shariat Panch as chief justice, Qazi, and Pargana Majlis.
118.tq: Arrange judicial authorities by hierarchical order.
xs: Justice ran **Sultan → Shariat Panch → Qazi → Pargana Majlis** — option **(2)**.
The **Shariat Panch** was the **chief justice**, above the Qazi.
**Kotwal** and **Faujdar** were police/district officers, not the judicial chain.
xa: The **Kotwal** sometimes **judged cases** besides policing.
**Mahasibs / Mustasibs** supervised **public morals**, like the Mughal **Muhtasib**.

118.s:
Which of the following correctly matches the administrative unit with its head?
1. Sarkar — Faujdar
2. Pargana — Tahsildar or Deshmukh
3. Village — Mukaddam and Kulkarni
4. Village — Shahbandar
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
118.x: A Sarkar was headed by a Faujdar, a Pargana by a Tahsildar or Deshmukh, and the village had the Mukaddam as head and Kulkarni as accountant. The Shahbandar was a port officer.
118.tq: Match each territorial unit with its proper local officer.
xs: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
**Sarkar — Faujdar**; **Pargana — Tahsildar / Deshmukh**; **Village — Mukaddam / Kulkarni** (head / accountant).
Pair 4 is wrong: the **Shahbandar** was the **chief port officer**.
xa: **Tarafdar** governed a **Taraf**: law and order, revenue, troops.
Under **Abul Hasan**: **37 Sarkars**, **517 Parganas**.

118.s: Which of the following statements about Qutb Shahi revenue administration is correct?
o: Land revenue was abolished and the state depended exclusively on port customs.
Revenue was collected only from professional groups and courtesans.
Land revenue was collected mainly through tax farming, with rights auctioned to the highest bidder.
Tax-farming rights were reserved exclusively for Muslim nobles.
118.x: Land revenue was the main source and was collected through tax farming, in which collection rights were auctioned to the highest bidder. The tax farmers, called Mustajirs, were mostly Hindus, and the arrangement could produce exploitation.
118.tq: Apply the revenue mechanism and avoid extreme words such as ‘exclusively’ and ‘only’.
xs: Land revenue was collected mainly by **tax farming**, rights going to the **highest bidder** — option **(3)**.
The bidders, **Mustajirs**, were **mostly Hindus** — so option 4 is wrong; the system led to **exploitation**.
**Land revenue** was the **chief source**, not abolished.
xa: Example: **Machilipatnam** leased for **1,80,000 pagodas** a year.
**Dasabandhu** lands paid only **1/10**.

118.s:
Apart from land revenue, which of the following formed part of the Qutb Shahi revenue base?
1. Trade taxes
2. Port customs
3. Taxes on courtesans and professions
4. Compulsory military service in place of all taxes
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
118.x: Trade taxes, port customs, and taxes on courtesans and professions were additional revenue sources. Compulsory military service did not replace all taxes.
118.tq: Separate listed revenue sources from an absolute and unsupported substitution.
xs: Items 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
Besides land revenue: **trade taxes**, **port customs**, and **taxes on courtesans and professions**.
Compulsory military service in place of taxes is not in the revenue system.
xa: **State monopolies**: **salt**, **betel leaf**, **tobacco**.
Some notes call the **leased diamond mines** the highest single source.

118.s:
Consider the following pairs relating to Qutb Shahi revenue:
1. Haveli — crown lands
2. Mustajirs — highest bidders who bought revenue-collection rights
3. Dasabandhu lands — paid one-fifth of the produce
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
118.x: Pair 1 is correct: Haveli meant crown lands (Zamindari being the other land type). Pair 3 is wrong: Dasabandhu lands paid only one-tenth. Pair 2 is correct: Mustajirs, mostly Hindus, were the highest bidders in tax farming. Hence 1 and 2 only.
118.tq: Dasabandhu = 1/10; Mustajir = tax farmer.
xs: Pairs **1 and 2 only** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Pair 1: **Haveli** = **crown lands**; pair 2: **Mustajirs** = **highest bidders** buying revenue rights in **tax farming**.
Pair 3 is wrong: **Dasabandhu** lands paid only **1/10**.
xa: Chief source of revenue: **land revenue**; some notes call the leased **diamond mines** the highest single source.
**Machilipatnam** was leased for **1,80,000 pagodas** a year.
State monopolies: **salt, betel leaf, tobacco**.

118.s: Which of the following commodities were state monopolies?
118.x: Salt, betel leaf and tobacco were state monopolies.
118.tq: Select the complete commodity group rather than a partially correct combination.
xs: **Salt, betel leaf and tobacco** were **state monopolies** — option **(4)**.
Diamonds came from **leased mines**, traded at **Moti Darwaza**.
xa: Other sources: **trade taxes**, **port customs**, taxes on courtesans and professions.
Chief source: **land revenue**.

118.s:
Consider the following statements about Akkanna and Madanna:
1. They were Pingali Brahmin brothers from Hanamkonda.
2. Madanna served as Mir Jumla or Diwan.
3. Akkanna served as Sar Lashkar.
4. Madanna held the titles Surya Prakasa Rao and Alampana.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
118.x: All four statements are correct. Madanna was the Diwan or prime minister, while Akkanna was the Sar Lashkar or army chief.
118.tq: Check the family, offices and titles together, while avoiding the documented reversal of their roles.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Madanna and Akkanna** were **Pingali Brahmin** brothers from **Hanamkonda**.
**Madanna** = **Mir Jumla / Diwan**, titles **Surya Prakasa Rao** + **Alampana**; **Akkanna** = **Sar Lashkar**.
xa: ⚠ Trap: some notes (Block 03) **reverse** their roles.
They made an alliance with **Shivaji** (**1677**); were **murdered in 1686**.

118.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding the nephews of Akkanna and Madanna?
o: Podili Linganna — governor of the Karnatak; Gopanna — tahsildar of Palvancha
Podili Linganna — tahsildar of Palvancha; Gopanna — governor of the Karnatak
Podili Linganna — Sar Lashkar; Gopanna — Mir Jumla
Podili Linganna — governor of Golconda; Gopanna — commander of the Karnatak
118.x: Podili Linganna was the governor of the Karnatak, while Kancherla Gopanna was the tahsildar of Palvancha.
118.tq: Match each nephew with his office, using the distinct administrative locations as clues.
xs: **Podili Linganna** = **governor of the Karnatak**; **Kancherla Gopanna** = **Tahsildar of Palvancha** — option **(1)**.
Option (2) swaps them; **Sar Lashkar** and **Mir Jumla** were Akkanna and Madanna themselves.
xa: Gopanna is **Bhakta Ramadasu** (Palvancha/**Bhadrachalam**), under **Abul Hasan**.
Madanna's titles: **Surya Prakasa Rao**, **Alampana**.

118.s: The murder of Akkanna and Madanna in 1686 weakened Golconda because it occurred
o: before the Qutb Shahis acquired coastal Andhra
during the establishment of the Nizam Shahi dynasty
immediately after the founding of Khirki
just before the Mughal fall of Golconda
118.x: The brothers were murdered in 1686, shortly before Golconda fell to Aurangzeb in 1687, thereby weakening the state’s administration and defence.
118.tq: Connect the event’s timing with its political consequence rather than treating it as an isolated date.
xs: The brothers were **murdered in 1686**, **just before the Mughal fall of Golconda** — option **(4)**.
**Aurangzeb** took Golconda on **21 September 1687**.
xa: Aurangzeb annexed **Bijapur** the same year (**1686**).
⚠ **1633** Nizam Shahis – **1686** Bijapur – **1687** Golconda.

118.s: The city of Hyderabad was planned by which official?
118.x: Peshwa Mir Momin Astarabadi planned Hyderabad after its foundation by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah.
118.tq: Use the official–institution or official–project association.
xs: Hyderabad was planned by Peshwa **Mir Momin Astarabadi** — option **(2)**.
**Hussain Shah Wali** built Hussain Sagar; **Mir Jumla** gave the Kohinoor to Shah Jahan; **Firishta** was a historian.
xa: Capital shifted from **Golconda** in **1592**.
Original name **Bhagyanagar**; founded by **Muhammad Quli** in **1591**.

118.s:
Match List-I (Monument) with List-II (Feature):
List-I
a. Charminar
b. Golconda fort
c. Qutb Shahi tombs at Ibrahim Bagh
List-II
i. Four Char Kaman gateways
ii. Acoustics: a handclap at the gate carries to the Bala Hisar
iii. Onion domes on square bases with charbagh gardens
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
118.x: Charminar is linked with the four Char Kaman gateways, Golconda fort is famous for its acoustics (handclap at the gate heard at the Bala Hisar), and the Qutb Shahi tombs at Ibrahim Bagh have onion domes on square bases with charbagh gardens. So A. B swaps Charminar and Golconda; C swaps Charminar and the tombs; D swaps the fort and the tombs.
118.tq: Fix the unique one first: the handclap acoustics belong only to Golconda fort.
xs: **a-i, b-ii, c-iii** — option **(1)**.
**Charminar — four Char Kaman gateways**; **Golconda fort — acoustics** (handclap heard at **Bala Hisar**).
**Qutb Shahi tombs (Ibrahim Bagh) — onion domes on square bases**, charbagh gardens.
xa: Golconda fort also had **piped water**; old name **Mangalavaram/Mankal**.
**Ibrahim** built Golconda's **high walls**.

118.s:
Consider the following statements about the early names associated with Hyderabad and Golconda:
1. Hyderabad was originally known as Bhagyanagar.
2. Golconda was also known by the name Mankal.
3. Mangalavaram is another name associated with old Golconda.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
118.x: Bhagyanagar is identified as the original name of Hyderabad, while Mankal and Mangalavaram are names associated with old Golconda.
118.tq: Combine closely related alternative names and test all listed associations.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Hyderabad's original name was **Bhagyanagar**.
Golconda fort's old name was **Mangalavaram / Mankal**.
xa: Golconda was the Qutb Shahi capital from **Sultan Quli**, who renamed it **Muhammadnagar**.
Capital moved to Hyderabad in **1592**.

118.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the construction of the Mecca Masjid?
o: It was begun in 1591 and completed in 1614 by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah.
It was begun in 1614 by Muhammad Qutb Shah and completed by Aurangzeb in 1692–93.
It was begun by Aurangzeb in 1692 and completed by Muhammad Qutb Shah.
It was built in 1562 by Hussain Shah Wali.
118.x: Muhammad Qutb Shah began the Mecca Masjid in 1614, and Aurangzeb completed it in 1692–93.
118.tq: Separate the initiator, successor and completion date in a long construction history.
xs: Begun in **1614** by **Muhammad Qutb Shah**, completed by **Aurangzeb** in **1692-93** — option **(2)**.
Option (3) reverses the two; **1591** is the Charminar; **1562** is Hussain Sagar.
xa: **Tavernier** saw **4,000** workers on it.
Muhammad Qutb Shah's pen name: **Zillullah**.

118.s:
Consider the following statements about monuments associated with Hyderabad:
1. Golconda Fort was the Qutb Shahi capital from the time of Sultan Quli.
2. Ibrahim Qutb Shah built the high walls of Golconda Fort.
3. Hussain Sagar was built in 1562 during Ibrahim’s reign.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
118.x: All three statements are correct. Golconda served as the Qutb Shahi capital from Sultan Quli, Ibrahim built its high walls, and Hussain Sagar was built by Hussain Shah Wali in 1562 during Ibrahim’s reign.
118.tq: Check ruler, monument and date together instead of treating them as isolated facts.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Golconda fort** was the Qutb Shahi capital from **Sultan Quli**; **Ibrahim** built its **high walls**.
**Hussain Sagar** was built by **Hussain Shah Wali** in **1562**, in Ibrahim's reign.
xa: Golconda fort: **acoustics** (handclap heard at **Bala Hisar**) and **piped water**.
Hussain Sagar date: **1562** / **1563** — notes differ.

118.s: Tavernier visited the Andhra diamond mines during the reign of:
118.x: Tavernier visited the mines during the reign of Abdullah Qutb Shah.
118.tq: Apply the traveller–ruler association while avoiding a neighbouring ruler trap.
xs: **Tavernier** visited the Andhra diamond mines in **Abdullah Qutb Shah's** reign — option **(1)** (APPSC G2 2019).
He was a **French jeweller / diamond merchant** (**17th century**) and wrote **Six Travels**.
xa: He recorded the **Kohinoor** and saw **4,000** workers at the Mecca Masjid.
Mines: **Kollur** (Guntur), **Paritala** (Krishna), **Ramallakota** (Kurnool), **Vajrakarur** (Anantapur).

118.s:
Consider the following statements about the Kohinoor diamond:
1. It came from the Kollur mines on the Krishna.
2. It is stated to have been found in 1656.
3. Tavernier presented it to Shah Jahan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
118.x:
Statement 1 is correct: the Kohinoor came from the Kollur mines (Guntur district, on the Krishna). Statement 2 is correct: it was found in 1656. Statement 3 is wrong: Tavernier only recorded it; Mir Jumla presented it to Shah Jahan. So 1 and 2 only (A); B, C and D include the wrong statement 3.
⚠ Sources differ: the Kohinoor's origin is uncertain; exam texts give the Kollur mine / Mir Jumla 1656 tradition. This key follows the standard view.
118.tq: Tavernier recorded, Mir Jumla presented: separate the chronicler from the giver.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: the **Kohinoor** came from the **Kollur mines** (Guntur, on the Krishna) — correct (APPSC G2 2011).
Statement 2: found in **1656** — correct.
Statement 3: wrong — **Tavernier** only recorded it; **Mir Jumla** presented it to Shah Jahan.
xa: It is now in the **British crown**, in British hands since **1849**.
Pakistan's **1976** claim was recalled in the news.

118.s:
Consider the following pairs concerning European factories at Machilipatnam:
1. Dutch — 1605
2. English — 1611
3. Captain Hippon — Ship Globe
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
118.x: The Dutch factory dates to 1605, the English factory to 1611, and Captain Hippon arrived in the ship Globe. All three pairs are correct.
118.tq: Start with the sure company–year pair and verify the associated agent and vessel.
xs: All three pairs are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Dutch** factory at Machilipatnam **1605**; **English** **1611**.
The English came under **Captain Hippon** in the ship **Globe**.
xa: The Dutch factory was the **first European factory in Andhra**.
The English came with **Muhammad Quli's** permission.

118.s: The English obtained permission to establish their presence at Machilipatnam from:
118.x: The English came to Machilipatnam with the permission of Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah. The attribution to Ibrahim Qutb Shah is chronologically inconsistent because he died in 1580.
118.tq: Use chronology to reject a ruler who could not have granted the permission.
xs: The English came to Machilipatnam with **Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah's** permission — option **(1)**.
APPSC 2025 accepted "**Quli Qutub Shah**".
xa: ⚠ Trap: the **APPSC G2 2008** key gave **Ibrahim Qutb Shah**, though he died in **1580** — choose him only if Muhammad Quli is absent.
The English factory dates to **1611** (Captain **Hippon**, ship **Globe**).

118.s: Machilipatnam was particularly famous for the manufacture and trade of:
118.x: Machilipatnam was famed for muslin and Kalamkari, in addition to its importance as a trading centre.
118.tq: Identify the characteristic goods associated with a historic port.
xs: **Machilipatnam** was famed for **muslin** and **Kalamkari** — option **(1)**.
Diamonds came from the **Kollur** and other mines, traded at **Moti Darwaza**.
xa: It was leased for **1,80,000 pagodas** a year.
Port works revive the old **Gilakaladindi** port.

118.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Annexation of Bijapur by Aurangzeb
B. Ahmadnagar city captured by Akbar
C. Golconda annexed as the 21st Mughal Suba
D. Nizam Shahi dynasty ended by Shah Jahan
118.x: The correct order is Ahmadnagar’s capture in 1600, the end of the Nizam Shahis in 1633, Bijapur’s annexation in 1686 and Golconda’s annexation in 1687.
118.tq: Place the events by their dates before comparing the middle positions.
xs: Order: **Ahmadnagar captured (1600) → Nizam Shahis ended (1633) → Bijapur annexed (1686) → Golconda annexed (1687)** — option **(1) B, D, A, C**.
Golconda became the Mughals' **21st Suba**.
xa: In **1636** Bijapur and Golconda signed **ahdnamas** under Shah Jahan.
Aurangzeb first attacked Golconda in **1656** as Deccan subedar.

118.s: Who opened the gates of Golconda Fort to Aurangzeb on 21 September 1687?
118.x: The gates were opened by the traitor Abdullah Khan Pani, also referred to as Abdullah Phani in the accounts.
118.tq: Use the person–deed trap by associating the gate-opening with the named traitor rather than the defender.
xs: The traitor **Abdullah Khan Pani** (Abdullah Phani) opened the gates on **21 September 1687** — option **(4)**.
**Abul Razak Lari** was honoured for **defending** Golconda; **Fath Khan** was Malik Ambar's son.
xa: Golconda became the Mughals' **21st Suba**.
Last ruler **Abul Hasan Tana Shah** was imprisoned at Bidar, then **Daulatabad**.

118.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Hussain Sagar:
1. It was named after Hussain Shah Wali.
2. It was built under Ibrahim.
3. It was declared the UNWTO ‘Heart of the World’ in 2012.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
118.x: Hussain Sagar was named after Hussain Shah Wali, built under Ibrahim, and received the UNWTO designation ‘Heart of the World’ in 2012.
118.tq: Check each statement independently, especially the name, patron, and recognition-year details.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Hussain Sagar** is named after **Hussain Shah Wali** and was built under **Ibrahim**.
It was declared the UNWTO "**Heart of the World**" (**2012**).
xa: Date given as **1562** / **1563** — notes differ.
The **Ibrahimpatnam** tank also dates from Ibrahim's reign.

118.s:
Consider the following statements about the Bonalu festival of Telangana:
1. It began at the Jagadamba Mahankali temple inside Golconda fort.
2. Its roots are traced to the Vijayanagara and Mughal periods.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
118.x: Statement 1 is correct: Bonalu began at the Jagadamba Mahankali temple inside Golconda fort. Statement 2 is wrong: its roots go back to the Kakatiya and Qutb Shahi periods, not Vijayanagara and Mughal. So 1 only (A); B and C accept the wrong period, D rejects the correct temple link.
118.tq: Bonalu: Golconda fort temple, Kakatiya + Qutb Shahi roots - both Telangana-centred.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1: **Bonalu** began at the **Jagadamba Mahankali temple inside Golconda fort** — correct.
Statement 2: wrong — it goes back to the **Kakatiya + Qutb Shahi** periods.
xa: Muharram was celebrated as **Peerla Panduga**.
Golconda fort's old name: **Mangalavaram / Mankal**.

118.s: Which of the following sets consists entirely of Hindus who held high office under the Qutb Shahis?
o: Murari Rao, Jagadeva Rao and Madanna
Hussain Shah Wali, Ibrahim and Madanna
Murari Rao, Abul Hasan and Jagadeva Rao
Madanna, Muhammad Quli and Jagadeva Rao
118.x: Murari Rao, Jagadeva Rao and Madanna are identified as Hindus who held high office under the Qutb Shahis.
118.tq: Eliminate options containing rulers or other non-matching personalities and retain the complete administrative trio.
xs: **Murari Rao**, **Jagadeva Rao** and **Madanna** were Hindus in high office — option **(1)**.
**Hussain Shah Wali**, **Ibrahim**, **Abul Hasan** and **Muhammad Quli** were Muslims.
xa: Madanna was **Mir Jumla / Diwan**; his brother **Akkanna** was **Sar Lashkar**.
**Mustajirs** (tax farmers) were also **mostly Hindus**.

118.s: During the Qutb Shahi period, Muharram came to be celebrated in Andhra as:
118.x: Muharram came to be celebrated as Peerla Panduga during the Qutb Shahi period.
118.tq: Separate closely associated regional festival names by linking the specific festival with its religious occasion.
xs: **Muharram** was celebrated as **Peerla Panduga** — option **(2)**.
**Bonalu** is a separate Telangana festival begun at Golconda fort.
xa: Hindus held high office (**Murari Rao**, **Jagadeva Rao**, **Madanna**).
The Qutb Shahis united the Telugu lands for the **third time**.

118.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Malik Ahmad
(b) Yusuf Adil Shah
(c) Fatehullah Imad Shah
(d) Quli Qutb Shah

List-II
i. Qutbshahi
 ii. Nizamshahi
 iii. Imadshahi
 iv. Adilshahi
118.x: Malik Ahmad founded the Nizamshahi, Yusuf Adil Shah the Adilshahi, Fatehullah Imad Shah the Imadshahi and Quli Qutb Shah the Qutbshahi dynasty, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
118.tq: Link each Bahmani successor founder to his dynasty by name.

o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false

n: Golconda was the capital of the Qutbshahi dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
Amir Ali Barid founded the Baridshahi dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]

119.s: The Kakatiya-service theory regarding Harihara and Bukka holds that they had served under:
119.x: The Kakatiya theory states that Harihara and Bukka served Prataparudra of Warangal before being taken to Delhi after 1323.
119.tq: Apply the ruler–regional power association without confusing it with the Kampili or Hoysala theories.
xs: The Kakatiya-service theory says they served **Prataparudra of Warangal** — option **(1)**.
After **1323** they were taken to **Delhi** and converted.
Service under **Veera Ballala III** is the **Kannada/Hoysala** theory; service to **Muhammad bin Tughlaq** is the Delhi version.
xa: **APPSC G2 2005** key: Sangama was "**a Kakatiya chief**".
There are **7 theories** of origin; **Sewell** records **seven** local traditions.

119.s:
Consider the following statements about the versions of Harihara and Bukka's early career:
1. In the Kampili version, they governed Kampili, were captured by Muhammad bin Tughlaq, converted in Delhi and sent back as Sultanate governors.
2. In the Delhi-service version, Muhammad bin Tughlaq sent them to crush Deccan rebels such as Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka and Prolaya Vema.
3. In the Kampili version, they were officers of Veera Ballala III.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: Statement 1 is correct: this is the Kampili version. Statement 2 is correct: the Delhi-service version has Tughlaq sending them against Deccan rebels (Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka, Prolaya Vema). Statement 3 is wrong: service under Veera Ballala III is the Kannada/Hoysala theory, not the Kampili version. So 1 and 2 only (A); B, C and D include statement 3.
119.tq: Keep each theory to its patron: Kampili/Tughlaq, Kakatiya/Prataparudra, Hoysala/Ballala III.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **Kampili** version — governed Kampili, captured by **Muhammad bin Tughlaq**, converted, sent back as governors — correct.
Statement 2: **Delhi-service** version — sent against **Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka** and **Prolaya Vema** — correct.
Statement 3: wrong — service under **Veera Ballala III** is the **Kannada/Hoysala** theory.
xa: After defeat they met **Vidyaranya** near **Pampa** and returned to Hinduism.
They founded **Anegondi** in the name of **Virupaksha**.

119.s:
Consider the following statements about the theories concerning the origin of the Vijayanagara founders:
1. The Kannada or Hoysala theory associates them with Veera Ballala III.
2. The Andhra theory is associated with scholars such as N. Venkataramanaiah, Sewell and Nilakanta Sastri.
3. Robert Sewell recorded seven local founding traditions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: All three statements are correct. The Kannada/Hoysala theory links them with Veera Ballala III, the Andhra theory has the listed scholarly supporters, and Sewell recorded seven local traditions.
119.tq: Test several competing origin theories together rather than relying on one familiar association.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Kannada/Hoysala** theory: officers of **Veera Ballala III** — correct.
**Andhra** theory: **N. Venkataramanaiah, Sewell, Nilakanta Sastri** — correct; **Sewell** recorded **seven** traditions — correct.
xa: ⚠ **Sewell** appears twice: records the seven traditions + backs the **Andhra** theory.
Kannada theory backers: **Father Heras**, **Rice**, **S.K. Ayyangar**, **H. Krishna Sastri**, **P.B. Desai**.

119.s: Who among the following is associated with the Kannada or Hoysala theory of the origin of Harihara and Bukka?
119.x: Father Heras, Rice, S. K. Ayyangar, H. Krishna Sastri and P. B. Desai supported the Kannada or Hoysala theory.
119.tq: Separate the scholars supporting the Kannada/Hoysala theory from those associated with the Andhra theory.
xs: **Father Heras** backs the **Kannada/Hoysala** theory — option **(2)**.
**N. Venkataramanaiah**, **Nilakanta Sastri** and **Sewell** back the **Andhra** theory.
xa: Other Kannada-theory backers: **Rice**, **S.K. Ayyangar**, **H. Krishna Sastri**, **P.B. Desai**.
The theory makes them officers of **Veera Ballala III**.
Heras also wrote **The Aravidu Dynasty of Vijayanagara**.

119.s: The first inscription to call Harihara I a king was the:
