119.x: The Nellore inscription is regarded as the first inscription to call Harihara I a king; it dates his reign to 1336–1355.
119.tq: Match the inscription with the precise historical claim associated with it.
xs: The first record to call Harihara I king is the **Nellore inscription** — option **(3)**.
It dates his reign **1336-1355**.
xa: First seat of the kingdom: **Anegondi**.
Harihara I was crowned on **18 April 1336** at the **Virupaksha** temple.
The city was completed by **1343** (some notes: entered **1344**).

119.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the founding location of Vijayanagara?
o: It was founded on the northern bank of the Tungabhadra in 1323.
It was founded on the southern bank of the Godavari in 1346.
It was founded on the northern bank of the Krishna near Warangal.
It was founded on the southern bank of the Tungabhadra in 1336.
119.x: The Vijayanagara kingdom was founded in 1336 on the southern bank of the Tungabhadra.
119.tq: Use the river-bank and year together to reject reversed-location options.
xs: Vijayanagara was founded in **1336** on the **southern bank of the Tungabhadra** — option **(4)**.
**1323** is the fall of Warangal; **1346** is the Sringeri visit after the Hoysala victory.
xa: ⚠ **1336** = founding + coronation (**18 April**); **1343** = city completed; **1346** = Sringeri visit.
It was built as a **Giri Durga** on **Ramadurga** hill; ruins at **Hampi**.

119.s: Vidyaranya, who is associated with the reconversion of Harihara and Bukka, was the head of the:
119.x: Vidyaranya headed the Sringeri Shankara Math and is associated with the brothers' return to Hinduism.
119.tq: Match the religious institution with its associated spiritual leader.
xs: **Vidyaranya** headed the **Sringeri Shankara Math** — option **(4)**.
He **reconverted** the brothers to Hinduism before the **1336** coronation.
xa: The brothers visited **Sringeri** in **1346** after the **Hoysala** victory.
He wrote the **Vidyaranya Kalajnana**; his brother **Sayana** was minister of Harihara II.
⚠ **Madhava-Vidyaranya** (Advaita head) ≠ **Madhava** the minister who took **Goa**.

119.s: Which of the following correctly represents the sequence in the founding legend?
o: Fall of Warangal → conversion in Delhi → dispatch against Deccan rebels → meeting with Vidyaranya → return to Hinduism
Meeting with Vidyaranya → fall of Warangal → conversion in Delhi → foundation of Anegondi
Conversion in Delhi → fall of Warangal → visit to Sringeri → appointment by Prataparudra
Foundation of Anegondi → conversion in Delhi → fall of Warangal → meeting with Vidyaranya
119.x: The legend proceeds from the fall of Warangal and conversion in Delhi to the Deccan campaign, meeting Vidyaranya, and return to Hinduism.
119.tq: Arrange the narrative by identifying the first event and following the linked sequence.
xs: Sequence: **fall of Warangal → conversion in Delhi → sent against Deccan rebels → met Vidyaranya → return to Hinduism** — option **(1)**.
Then they founded **Anegondi** in the name of **Virupaksha**.
xa: The meeting took place near **Pampa**.
Harihara I was crowned **18 April 1336**.

119.s: Anegondi is significant in the early history of Vijayanagara because it was:
o: The site of the Sringeri Shankara Math
The place where Saluva Narasimha began the first usurpation
The first seat of the kingdom, established in the name of Sri Virupaksha
The final capital of the Aravidu dynasty
119.x: Anegondi was the first seat of the kingdom, and it was set up in the name of Sri Virupaksha.
119.tq: Distinguish the founders' first seat from later dynastic capitals and religious centres.
xs: **Anegondi** was the **first seat** of the kingdom, set up "**in the name of Sri Virupaksha**" — option **(3)**.
**Harihara I** later moved the capital from Anegondi to **Vijayanagara**.
**Saluva Narasimha** was lord of **Chandragiri**; the Aravidu capitals were **Penukonda, Chandragiri, Vellore**.
xa: Vidyaranya headed **Sringeri**, not Anegondi.
City completed by **1343**.

119.s: After the battle of Talikota, the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire was shifted in which sequence?
119.x: After Talikota, the capital moved from Hampi to Penukonda and subsequently to Chandragiri; both later capitals were in present-day Andhra Pradesh.
119.tq: Follow the first and second capital shifts in sequence.
xs: After Talikota: **Hampi → Penukonda → Chandragiri** — option **(2)**.
Both **Penukonda** and **Chandragiri** are in **AP**.
xa: The **Aravidu** capitals were **Penukonda, Chandragiri, Vellore**.
**Talikota (1565)**: Deccan sultanates defeated **Rama Raya**.

119.s: The name 'Vijayanagara', the capital built by Harihara and Bukka on the south bank of the Tungabhadra, means:
119.x: Vijayanagara means 'City of Victory'; it was built on the south bank of the Tungabhadra and its ruins lie at Hampi. 'City of Learning', 'City of Gold' and 'City of the Boar' are not meanings of the name (the boar, Varaha, was the royal emblem, not the city's name).
119.tq: Vijaya = victory, nagara = city.
xs: **Vijayanagara** means "**City of Victory**" — option **(1)**.
The **boar (Varaha)** was the royal **emblem**, not the city's name.
xa: Built on the **south bank of the Tungabhadra**; ruins at **Hampi**.
**7 stone ramparts**; completed by **1343**.

119.s: The first usurpation in the history of the Vijayanagara Empire is associated with:
o: Saluva Narasimha and the Saluva dynasty
Harihara I and the Sangama dynasty
Tirumala Raya and the Aravidu dynasty
Vira Narasimha and the Tuluva dynasty
119.x: Saluva Narasimha ended the Sangama line and established the Saluva dynasty, an event described as the first usurpation.
119.tq: Match the political event ‘first usurpation’ with its ruler and dynasty.
xs: The **first usurpation** = **Saluva Narasimha**, founding the **Saluva** dynasty — option **(1)**.
In **1485** he expelled **Praudha Raya** with **Tuluva Narasa Nayaka's** help.
xa: He was lord of **Chandragiri**; clan from **Kalyana**.
**Annamacharya** (**1408-1503**) was his contemporary.

119.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Tuluva dynasty is correct?
o: Tirumala Raya founded the Tuluva dynasty at Chandragiri.
Krishnadevaraya founded the Tuluva dynasty in 1570.
Vira Narasimha was crowned in 1505 after executing Immadi Narasimha.
Tuluva Narasa Nayaka was crowned in 1485 after defeating Saluva Narasimha.
119.x: The APPSC-associated account identifies Vira Narasimha as the founder; he was crowned in 1505 after executing Immadi Narasimha. Tuluva Narasa Nayaka was his father and is also called the dynasty founder in another historiographical usage.
119.tq: Separate the formal APPSC founder attribution from the alternative genealogical description of Tuluva Narasa Nayaka.
xs: **Vira Narasimha** was crowned in **1505** after executing **Immadi Narasimha** — option **(3)**.
**Tirumala Raya** founded the **Aravidu**; **Krishnadevaraya** reigned **1509-29**; **1485** is Saluva Narasimha's usurpation.
xa: ⚠ APPSC key names **Veera Narasimha** as Tuluva founder; some notes give his father **Tuluva Narasa Nayaka**.

119.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the Aravidu dynasty?
o: Founder—Tirumala Raya; capitals—Penukonda, Chandragiri and Vellore
119.x: Tirumala Raya founded the Aravidu dynasty, whose capitals included Penukonda, Chandragiri and Vellore.
119.tq: Check both the founder and the capital list before selecting the complete pair.
xs: **Aravidu**: founder **Tirumala Raya**; capitals **Penukonda, Chandragiri, Vellore** — option **(1)**.
**Saluva Narasimha** founded the Saluva; **Vira Narasimha** the Tuluva; **Bukka I** co-founded the Sangama.
xa: Aravidu origin: **Andhra** (**Araviti**, Kurnool).
Span **1570-1680** in one source.

119.s: Which dynasty of Vijayanagara ruled for the longest period and had Devaraya II as its greatest ruler and Praudha Raya as its last ruler?
119.x: The Sangama dynasty was the longest-ruling dynasty; Devaraya II was regarded as its greatest ruler and Praudha Raya as its last ruler.
119.tq: Combine the duration, greatest ruler and last ruler to identify the dynasty.
xs: The **Sangama** dynasty ruled longest; greatest king **Devaraya II**, last **Praudha Raya** — option **(3)**.
xa: ⚠ **Harihara II** = longest-reigning Sangama king; **Sangama** = longest-ruling dynasty.
Praudha Raya was expelled by **Saluva Narasimha** in **1485**.

119.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the religious affiliation and emblem of the Vijayanagara dynasties:
1. The emblem was the Varaha or boar.
2. The Sangamas were Shaiva.
3. The later three dynasties were Vaishnava.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: The Vijayanagara emblem was the Varaha. The Sangama rulers were Shaiva, while the Saluva, Tuluva and Aravidu dynasties were associated with Vaishnavism.
119.tq: Test the common emblem separately from the Shaiva–Vaishnava dynastic distinction.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
The emblem was the **Varaha** (boar); the **Sangamas** were **Shaiva**; the later **three** dynasties were **Vaishnava**.
xa: **Devaraya I's** coronation copper plates (Apr **2025**) carry a **Vamana** seal instead of the usual **Varaha**.
The family deity was **Virupaksha**.

119.s: Which ruler shifted the capital of the Vijayanagara kingdom from Anegondi to Vijayanagara?
119.x: Harihara I shifted the capital from Anegondi to Vijayanagara.
119.tq: Direct ruler–achievement recall.
xs: **Harihara I** moved the capital from **Anegondi** to **Vijayanagara** — option **(1)**.
**Bukka I** completed the city; **Devaraya I** built the dam.
xa: Harihara I annexed the **Hoysala** kingdom (**1346**) and the **Kadambas** (**1347**).
Title: **Purva-Paschima Samudradhipati**.

119.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Harihara I:
1. He annexed the Hoysala kingdom in 1346.
2. He annexed the Kadamba territory in 1347.
3. He took Udayagiri himself in 1343.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: Harihara I annexed the Hoysala kingdom in 1346 and the Kadambas in 1347. Udayagiri was taken by Bukka, not Harihara I, in 1343.
119.tq: Separate the ruler from the achievement attributed to his associate.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Harihara I annexed the **Hoysala** kingdom (**1346**) and the **Kadambas** (**1347**).
Statement 3 is wrong: **Bukka** took **Udayagiri** (**1343**).
xa: **Ibn Battuta** visited in Harihara I's reign — the first foreign traveller.
Title: **Purva-Paschima Samudradhipati**.

119.s:
Consider the following pairs (title — Sangama ruler):
1. Rajavyasa and Rajavalmiki — Devaraya I
2. Purva-Paschima Samudradhipati — Harihara I
3. Vedamarga Pratishthapaka — Bukka I
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
119.x: Pair 2 is correct: Harihara I took the title Purva-Paschima Samudradhipati. Pair 3 is correct: Bukka I was Vedamarga Pratishthapaka. Pair 1 is wrong: Rajavyasa and Rajavalmiki were titles of Harihara II, not Devaraya I. Hence 2 and 3 only.
119.tq: Harihara I = Purva-Paschima Samudradhipati; Bukka I = Vedamarga Pratishthapaka; Harihara II = Rajavyasa.
xs: Pairs **2 and 3 only** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Pair 2: **Purva-Paschima Samudradhipati** — **Harihara I**; pair 3: **Vedamarga Pratishthapaka** — **Bukka I**.
Pair 1 is wrong: **Rajavyasa** and **Rajavalmiki** were titles of **Harihara II**.
xa: ⚠ **Gajabetekara** = **Devaraya II**; **Dakshina Samudradhipati** = **Lakkanna Dandanayaka**.
**Harihara II** = **longest-reigning** Sangama king; **first to attack Sri Lanka**.
**Devaraya I** built a **dam on the Tungabhadra**.

119.s:
Bukka I is associated with which combination of achievements?
1. Completion of the city of Vijayanagara
2. Conquest of Madurai
3. Reconciliation of Jains and Vaishnavas
4. Construction of the Ganigitti Jain temple
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
119.x: Bukka I completed the city, conquered Madurai and reconciled Jains and Vaishnavas. The Ganigitti Jain temple was built by Irugappa, minister of Harihara II.
119.tq: Identify the one achievement shifted from one Sangama ruler to another.
xs: Items 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(1) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
**Bukka I** **completed the city**, conquered **Madurai** and **reconciled Jains and Vaishnavas** (Shravanabelagola inscription).
Item 4 is wrong: the **Ganigitti Jain temple** was built by **Irugappa**, minister of Harihara II.
xa: Bukka sent an **embassy to Ming China (1374)**.
He took **Srisailam** and **Dupadu**.

119.s:
Consider the following statements about Harihara II:
1. He was the longest-reigning Sangama king.
2. He bore the titles Rajavyasa and Rajavalmiki.
3. He bore the title Gajabetekara.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: Statement 1 is correct: Harihara II (1377-1404) had the longest Sangama reign. Statement 2 is correct: Rajavyasa and Rajavalmiki were his titles. Statement 3 is wrong: Gajabetekara (elephant hunter) was the title of Devaraya II. So 1 and 2 only (A); B, C and D include statement 3.
119.tq: Literary titles (Vyasa, Valmiki) = Harihara II; elephant hunter = Devaraya II.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
**Harihara II** (**1377-1404**) was the **longest-reigning** Sangama king, titled **Rajavyasa** and **Rajavalmiki**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Gajabetekara** was **Devaraya II's** title.
xa: He was the **first to attack Sri Lanka**.
His minister was **Sayana**.

119.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Devaraya I — Dam across the Tungabhadra
2. Devaraya I — War with Firuz Shah
3. Devaraya I — First recruitment of Muslims into the army
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
119.x: Devaraya I built a dam and canals, fought Firuz Shah and is recorded as the first Sangama ruler to recruit Muslims into the army.
119.tq: Combine several achievements of one ruler before selecting the code.
xs: All three pairs are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Devaraya I** built the **Tungabhadra dam**, fought **Firuz Shah** (Mudgal), and one source calls him **first to recruit Muslims**.
xa: He gave his daughter to **Firoz Shah Bahmani** with **Bankapur** as dowry — "**War of the Goldsmith's Daughter**".
**Devaraya II** enrolled **10,000 Muslim soldiers**.

119.s: Who led the conquest of Madurai during the reign of Bukka I?
119.x: Kumara Kampana, son of Bukka I, overthrew Sambhuvaraya in 1366 and destroyed the Madurai Sultanate.
119.tq: Direct identification of the commander in a dynastic conquest.
xs: **Kumara Kampana**, Bukka I's son, led the **Madurai** conquest — option **(1)**.
He overthrew **Sambhuvaraya** (**1366**) and destroyed the **Madurai Sultanate**.
xa: General **Saluva Mangu** killed the Sultan — title "**Parapakshi Saluva**".
Kampana's wife **Gangadevi** wrote **Madhura Vijayam**.

119.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Kumara Kampana overthrew Sambhuvaraya in 1366.
2. Saluva Mangu killed the Sultan of Madurai.
3. Saluva Mangu received the title ‘Parapakshi Saluva’.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: All three statements are correct. Kampana led the conquest, while General Saluva Mangu killed the Sultan and received the title ‘Parapakshi Saluva’.
119.tq: Test a conquest through its date, commander and associated title.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Kumara Kampana** overthrew **Sambhuvaraya** in **1366**.
**Saluva Mangu** killed the **Sultan of Madurai** and got the title "**Parapakshi Saluva**".
xa: Saluva Mangu was an **ancestor of Saluva Narasimha**.
The campaign is told in **Madhura Vijayam** by **Gangadevi**.

119.s: Bukka I sent an embassy to the Ming emperor of China in which year?
119.x: Bukka I sent an embassy to the Ming emperor in 1374.
119.tq: Direct year recall using four distinct chronological values.
xs: **Bukka I** sent an embassy to the **Ming emperor of China** in **1374** — option **(2)**.
**1366** = Kampana overthrew Sambhuvaraya; **1424** = Kondaveedu annexed; **1443** = Abdur Razzaq's visit.
xa: Bukka's title: **Vedamarga Pratishthapaka**.
He patronised **Nachana Somana**.

119.s:
Match List-I (Author) with List-II (Work):
List-I
a. Sayana
b. Vidyaranya
c. Nachana Somana
List-II
i. Uttara Harivamsam
ii. Vedartha Prakasha
iii. Vidyaranya Kalajnana
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
119.x: Sayana (brother of Vidyaranya, minister of Harihara II) wrote the Vedic commentary Vedartha Prakasha; Vidyaranya wrote the Vidyaranya Kalajnana; Nachana Somana, patronised by the first two Sangama kings, wrote Uttara Harivamsam. So A. B swaps Sayana and Vidyaranya; C and D give the Telugu Uttara Harivamsam to the wrong author.
119.tq: Vedic commentary = Sayana; the Kalajnana carries Vidyaranya's own name; Uttara Harivamsam is the Telugu work.
xs: **a-ii, b-iii, c-i** — option **(1)**.
**Sayana — Vedartha Prakasha**; **Vidyaranya — Vidyaranya Kalajnana**; **Nachana Somana — Uttara Harivamsam**.
xa: Sayana was **Vidyaranya's brother** and **minister of Harihara II**.
Nachana Somana was patronised by the **first two** Sangama kings.

119.s:
With reference to the Vedic commentaries associated with the early Vijayanagara rulers, consider the following statements:
1. The work was initiated under Bukka Raya I.
2. The work continued under Harihara II.
3. Sayana served as a minister of Harihara II.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: The Vedic commentaries were produced under Bukka Raya I and continued under Harihara II, during whose reign Sayana served as minister.
119.tq: Combine the ruler, continuation and minister facts before selecting the coded option.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Sayana + Madhava's** Vedic commentaries began **under Bukka Raya I** (APPSC G2 2008 key) and continued under **Harihara II**.
**Sayana** was **minister of Harihara II**.
xa: Sayana's commentary: **Vedartha Prakasha**.
Bukka's title **Vedamarga Pratishthapaka** fits this Vedic patronage.

119.s: Madhava, the minister and general associated with the conquest of Goa, was known by which title?
119.x: Madhava was known by the title Bhuvanaikavira in connection with his military achievement and conquest of Goa.
119.tq: Test the title–person association rather than the broader event.
xs: **Madhava**, minister/general who conquered **Goa**, was titled **"Bhuvanaikavira"** — option **(1)**.
He is distinct from **Madhava-Vidyaranya**, Advaita head of Sringeri; some notes merge the two.
xa: Goa was taken in **1366** and lost to the Bahmanis in **1472**.
Sayana and Madhava wrote **Vedic commentaries**.

119.s:
Consider the following statements about Gangadevi and Madhura Vijayam:
1. Gangadevi wrote Madhura Vijayam in Sanskrit.
2. Gangadevi was the wife of Bukka I.
3. Madhura Vijayam describes Kumara Kampana's southern campaign, including the defeat of Champaraya of Tondaimandalam and the conquest of Madurai.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: Statement 1 is correct: Madhura Vijayam is a Sanskrit work by Gangadevi. Statement 2 is wrong: she was the wife of Kumara Kampana and the daughter-in-law of Bukka I. Statement 3 is correct: the work narrates Kampana's campaign, the defeat of Champaraya of Tondaimandalam, the advance to Kanchi and the conquest of Madurai. So 1 and 3 only (C); A, B and D include statement 2.
119.tq: Gangadevi = Kampana's wife, Bukka's daughter-in-law: the relation is the usual trap.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(3) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1: **Gangadevi** wrote **Madhura Vijayam** in **Sanskrit** — correct.
Statement 2: wrong — she was the wife of **Kumara Kampana**, **daughter-in-law** of Bukka I.
Statement 3: it narrates Kampana's campaign, defeat of **Champaraya of Tondaimandalam** and conquest of **Madurai** — correct.
xa: She was a **disciple of Agastya**.
Kampana overthrew **Sambhuvaraya** in **1366**.

119.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Devaraya II’s military policy is correct?
1. He enrolled 10,000 Muslim soldiers.
2. Muslims received jagirs and a mosque.
3. He kept a Quran near his throne.
4. He improved cavalry and archery.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
119.x: All four statements describe Devaraya II’s army reforms and accommodation of Muslim soldiers.
119.tq: Use the complete military-policy cluster rather than an isolated reform.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Devaraya II** enrolled **10,000 Muslim soldiers** (APPSC G2 2011 key), gave them **jagirs** and a **mosque**.
He kept a **Quran** near his throne and improved **cavalry and archery**.
xa: Titles: **Gajabetekara**, **Praudha Devaraya**, **Ilanti Raikonda**.
He was the **greatest** Sangama ruler (**1422-46**).

119.s:
Which of the following observations is associated with Abdur Razzaq’s account of Vijayanagara?
1. Open diamond bazaars
2. Three hundred ports
3. Taxation of prostitution
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
119.x: Abdur Razzaq described the open diamond bazaars, the large number of ports and the taxation of prostitution.
119.tq: Cluster the distinctive details of one foreign traveller’s account.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Abdur Razzaq** noted **open diamond bazaars**, **300 ports** and **taxed prostitution**.
xa: He was the Persian envoy of **Shah Rukh**, **1443**, in **Devaraya II's** reign.
**Paes** and **Barbosa** came under **Krishnadevaraya**; **Nuniz** under **Achyutaraya**.

119.s: Which of the following titles was NOT associated with Devaraya II?
119.x: Purva-Paschima Samudradhipati was the title of Harihara I. Devaraya II was known as Gajabetekara, Praudha Devaraya and Ilanti Raikonda.
119.tq: Find the title belonging to a different ruler.
xs: **Purva-Paschima Samudradhipati** is NOT Devaraya II's — option **(2)**; it was **Harihara I's**.
Devaraya II's titles: **Gajabetekara** (elephant hunter), **Praudha Devaraya**, **Ilanti Raikonda**.
xa: ⚠ **Dakshina Samudradhipati** = **Lakkanna Dandanayaka**.
Devaraya II wrote **Mahanataka Sudhanidhi**.

119.s:
Which of the following achievements is associated with Devaraya II?
1. Annexation of Kondaveedu in 1424
2. Collection of tribute from Sri Lanka through Lakkanna Dandanayaka
3. Repulsion of the Gajapatis, recorded in the Draksharama inscription of 1444
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
119.x: Devaraya II annexed Kondaveedu, received Sri Lankan tribute through Lakkanna Dandanayaka and repelled the Gajapatis, as recorded at Draksharama.
119.tq: Link ruler, date, inscription and military achievement.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Devaraya II** annexed **Kondaveedu (1424)** and got **Sri Lankan** tribute via **Lakkanna Dandanayaka**.
He repelled the **Gajapatis**, sending **Mallappa Odayar** to Rajahmundry (**Draksharama inscription, 1444**).
xa: He honoured **Srinatha** with a **kanakabhishekam** after he beat **Gauda Dindima**.
**Vinukonda Vallabharaya** (Kridabhiramam) was his governor of **Vinukonda**.

119.s:
Consider the following statements about culture under Devaraya II:
1. Srinatha received kanakabhishekam after defeating Gauda Dindima.
2. Devaraya II wrote the Navaratnamala.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
119.x: Statement 1 is correct: Srinatha was honoured with kanakabhishekam after beating Gauda Dindima. Statement 2 is wrong: Devaraya II's own work is Mahanataka Sudhanidhi; Navaratnamala was written by Irugappa, minister of Harihara II. So 1 only (A); B and C accept the wrong statement, D rejects the correct one.
119.tq: Devaraya II wrote Mahanataka Sudhanidhi; Navaratnamala belongs to Irugappa.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct, so option **(1) 1 only** is the answer.
Statement 1 is correct: **Srinatha** received the **kanakabhishekam** after defeating **Gauda Dindima**, under the patronage of **Devaraya II**.
Statement 2 is wrong: Devaraya II's own work is **Mahanataka Sudhanidhi**; the **Navaratnamala** was written by **Irugappa**, minister of **Harihara II**.
xa: **Vinukonda Vallabharaya**, author of **Kridabhiramam**, was governor of **Vinukonda** under Devaraya II.
Devaraya II's titles: **Gajabetekara** (elephant hunter), **Praudha Devaraya**, **Ilanti Raikonda**.
Irugappa also built the **Ganigitti Jain temple**.

119.s: Abdur Razzaq, who visited Vijayanagara in 1443 during the reign of Devaraya II, came as the envoy of:
119.x: Abdur Razzaq was the Persian envoy of Shah Rukh and visited in 1443 under Devaraya II. Firuz Shah Bahmani fought Devaraya I; the Ming emperor received Bukka I's embassy (1374); the Portuguese came later, under the Tuluvas.
119.tq: Razzaq - Persia - Shah Rukh - 1443 - Devaraya II.
xs: **Abdur Razzaq** came as the Persian envoy of **Shah Rukh** in **1443** — option **(1)**.
**Firuz Shah Bahmani** fought **Devaraya I** (War of the Goldsmith's Daughter), not Devaraya II.
The **Ming emperor of China** received **Bukka I's** embassy of **1374**.
xa: Abdur Razzaq described open **diamond bazaars**, **300 ports**, and a tax on prostitution.
Travellers by reign: **Paes** and **Barbosa** (Portugal) → **Krishnadevaraya**; **Nuniz** → **Achyutaraya**; **Cesare Federici** (Italy) → **Sadasivaraya**.
⚠ **Nicolo Conti**: APPSC G2 **2011** key places him under **Devaraya II**; some notes date his visit **1420-21** under **Devaraya I**.

119.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Devaraya I:
1. He fought the Kandukuru Reddis and made them feudatories.
2. He allied with the Velamas and Kataya Vema.
3. He captured Srisailam and Dupadu near Markapur.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because the capture of Srisailam and Dupadu is attributed to Bukka I.
119.tq: Find the wrong ruler–achievement pairing before selecting the coded combination.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: **Devaraya I** fought the **Kandukuru Reddis** and made them **feudatories**.
Statement 2 is correct: he allied with the **Velamas** and **Kataya Vema**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Srisailam** and **Dupadu** (near **Markapur**) were captured by **Bukka I**.
xa: Devaraya I took southern **Kondaveedu**, including **Motupalli**, recorded in his **Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam**.
Devaraya I built a **dam on the Tungabhadra** with canals to carry water to the city.
**Nicolo Conti** visited in his reign; CDX calls him the first to recruit Muslims.

119.s: Devaraya I’s capture of southern Kondaveedu, including Motupalli, is recorded in which inscription?
119.x: Devaraya I’s capture of southern Kondaveedu, including Motupalli, is recorded in the Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam.
119.tq: Match the specific inscription with the ruler’s territorial achievement.
xs: Devaraya I's capture of southern **Kondaveedu**, including **Motupalli**, is recorded in the **Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam** — option **(1)**.
The **Draksharama inscription** (**1444**) belongs to **Devaraya II**, recording help sent to **Rajahmundry** against the Gajapatis.
xa: Devaraya I also fought the **Kandukuru Reddis** and allied with the **Velamas** and **Kataya Vema**.
**Devaraya II** annexed **Kondaveedu** fully in **1424**.
Devaraya I gave his daughter to **Firoz Shah Bahmani** with **Bankapur** as dowry.

119.s: Who among the following was the author of Kridabhiramam and served as governor of Vinukonda under Devaraya II?
119.x: Vinukonda Vallabharaya wrote Kridabhiramam and was the governor of Vinukonda under Devaraya II.
119.tq: Link the author, work and office rather than confusing the poet with a military officer or ally.
xs: **Vinukonda Vallabharaya** wrote **Kridabhiramam** and was governor of **Vinukonda** under **Devaraya II** — option **(1)**.
**Srinatha** was the poet honoured with **kanakabhishekam**; **Mallappa Odayar** was sent to help **Rajahmundry**.
**Kataya Vema** was an ally of **Devaraya I**, not a governor-poet.
xa: Srinatha's kanakabhishekam followed his victory over **Gauda Dindima**.
Devaraya II's own work: **Mahanataka Sudhanidhi**.
⚠ **Gajabetekara** = Devaraya II; **Purva-Paschima Samudradhipati** = **Harihara I**.

119.s: The principal bone of contention between the Vijayanagara and Bahmani kingdoms was the Raichur Doab, situated between which two rivers?
119.x: The Raichur Doab, or Raichur Antarvedi, lies between the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers and was the main cause of the recurring wars.
119.tq: Test the geographical boundaries of a disputed region.
xs: The **Raichur Doab** lies between the **Krishna and Tungabhadra** — option **(1)**.
Also called the **Raichur Antarvedi**, it was the main cause of the Vijayanagara-Bahmani wars (APPSC G2 **2000**, **2003**; PYQ **2017**).
xa: The two kingdoms also fought over the **Krishna-Godavari delta** and **Marathwada**.
Key contested points: **Mudgal** and **Raichur**.
**Krishnadevaraya** retook Raichur in the **Gobburi/Raichur war (1520)** with Portuguese help.

119.s:
With reference to the conflict at Mudgal in 1358, consider the following statements:
1. Bukka I took Mudgal.
2. It was regarded as the first Indian war involving artillery.
3. A truce was concluded to spare civilians.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: The 1358 Mudgal conflict occurred under Bukka I, who took Mudgal; it is noted as the first Indian war involving artillery, followed by a truce intended to spare civilians.
119.tq: Verify the date, military innovation and stated consequence as a single event cluster.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **Bukka I** took **Mudgal** in **1358**.
Statement 2: it is called the **first Indian war with artillery**, used by the **Bahmanis**.
Statement 3: a **truce** was concluded to spare civilians.
xa: In **1347**, the Bahmani general **Mubarak Khan** took land west of Raichur.
Under **Devaraya I**, the **"War of the Goldsmith's Daughter"** (Nehal of Mudgal) was fought against **Firuz Shah**.
**Devaraya II** fought two wars over **Mudgal**, **Raichur** and **Bijapur**.

119.s:
Consider the following statements about the 'War of the Goldsmith's Daughter':
1. It was fought between Devaraya I and Firuz Shah Bahmani.
2. After his defeat, Devaraya I gave his daughter and Bankapur as dowry.
3. Bankapur was never regained by Vijayanagara.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: Statement 1 is correct: the war (over Nehal of Mudgal) was between Devaraya I and Firuz Shah. Statement 2 is correct: the defeated Devaraya I gave his daughter and Bankapur as dowry. Statement 3 is wrong: Bankapur was later regained. So 1 and 2 only (A); B, C and D include statement 3.
119.tq: Goldsmith's daughter = Devaraya I vs Firuz Shah; Bankapur lost as dowry, later regained.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: the war, over **Nehal of Mudgal**, was between **Devaraya I** and **Firuz Shah** Bahmani.
Statement 2 is correct: the defeated Devaraya I gave his **daughter** and **Bankapur** as dowry.
Statement 3 is wrong: Bankapur was **later regained** (CDX).
xa: The **Mudgal (1358)** war under **Bukka I** was the **first Indian war with artillery**.
Main bone of contention: the **Raichur Doab** between the **Krishna and Tungabhadra**.
**Nicolo Conti** visited Vijayanagara under Devaraya I (per some notes, **1420-21**).

119.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Krishnadevaraya’s campaigns:
1. He retook Raichur in the Gobburi or Raichur war of 1520.
2. Portuguese assistance was received in that campaign.
3. He took Gulbarga in 1523.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: Krishnadevaraya retook Raichur in 1520 with Portuguese help and took Gulbarga in 1523.
119.tq: Combine the campaign, foreign assistance and successive dates before choosing the code.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Krishnadevaraya** retook **Raichur** in the **Gobburi/Raichur war (1520)**, with **Portuguese** help.
He then took **Gulbarga** in **1523**.
xa: Krishnadevaraya (**1509-29**, Tuluva) marked the empire's **zenith**.
**Paes** and **Barbosa** (Portugal) visited during his reign.
The conflict ended at **Talikota (1565)**, where the Deccan sultanates defeated **Rama Raya**.

119.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Krishnadevaraya took Gulbarga.
B. Bukka I took Mudgal.
C. Goa was lost to the Bahmanis.
D. The Battle of Talikota was fought.
119.x: The correct sequence is Mudgal in 1358, Goa’s loss in 1472, the capture of Gulbarga in 1523, and Talikota in 1565.
119.tq: Place the dated events first and then compare the middle positions.
xs: The order is **B, C, A, D** — option **(1)**.
**B**: **Bukka I** took **Mudgal** in **1358**; **C**: **Goa** lost to the Bahmanis in **1472**.
**A**: **Krishnadevaraya** took **Gulbarga** in **1523**; **D**: **Talikota** in **1565**.
xa: Goa had been taken in **1366** by minister **Madhava**.
**Raichur** was retaken in the **Gobburi war (1520)**, three years before Gulbarga.
In **1347**, the Bahmani general **Mubarak Khan** took land west of Raichur.

119.s:
Consider the following statements about Saluva Narasimha:
1. He was originally the lord of Chandragiri.
2. He seized the throne in 1485 with the help of Tuluva Narasa Nayaka.
3. He expelled Devaraya II to seize the throne.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: Statement 1 is correct: Saluva Narasimha was lord of Chandragiri. Statement 2 is correct: in 1485 he seized the throne with Tuluva Narasa Nayaka's help (the First Usurpation). Statement 3 is wrong: he expelled Praudha Raya, the last Sangama ruler, not Devaraya II. So 1 and 2 only (A); B, C and D include statement 3.
119.tq: First Usurpation 1485: Chandragiri lord + Tuluva Narasa Nayaka against Praudha Raya.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: **Saluva Narasimha** was lord of **Chandragiri**.
Statement 2 is correct: in **1485** he seized the throne with **Tuluva Narasa Nayaka's** help — the **First Usurpation**.
Statement 3 is wrong: he expelled **Praudha Raya**, the last Sangama ruler, not Devaraya II.
xa: His clan came from **Kalyana**; ancestor **Saluva Mangu** served **Kumara Kampana**.
He took the **Machilipatnam** area and repelled a **Bahmani raid on Kanchi (1481)**.
The **Saluva** dynasty ruled **1485-1505**.

119.s: Annamacharya, born in 1408 and deceased in 1503, was a contemporary of which ruler?
119.x: Annamacharya (1408–1503) was a contemporary of Saluva Narasimha and is also placed in his court.
119.tq: Use overlapping life dates to identify the contemporary ruler.
xs: **Annamacharya (1408-1503)** was a contemporary of **Saluva Narasimha** — option **(3)**.
Some notes even place him in Saluva Narasimha's **court** (PYQ **2011**).
xa: Saluva Narasimha seized the throne in **1485** from **Praudha Raya** — the **First Usurpation**.
He repelled a **Bahmani raid on Kanchi (1481)** and took the **Machilipatnam** area.
**Jaimini Bharatam** by **Pillalamarri Pinaveerabhadra** was dedicated to him.

119.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
119.x: Jaimini Bharatam was written by Pillalamarri Pinaveerabhadra and dedicated to Saluva Narasimha. Gangadevi wrote Madhura Vijayam.
119.tq: Detect the swapped author–work pair.
xs: **Gangadevi — Jaimini Bharatam** is wrongly matched — option **(1)**.
**Jaimini Bharatam** is by **Pillalamarri Pinaveerabhadra**, dedicated to **Saluva Narasimha**.
**Saluvabhyudayam** is by **Rajanatha Dindima**, from Saluva Narasimha's court.
**Gangadevi** wrote **Madhura Vijayam** (Sanskrit).
xa: Gangadevi was wife of **Kumara Kampana** and daughter-in-law of **Bukka I**; a **disciple of Agastya**.
Madhura Vijayam's theme: Kampana's defeat of **Champaraya of Tondaimandalam**, advance to **Kanchi** and conquest of **Madurai**.
**Annamacharya (1408-1503)** was Saluva Narasimha's contemporary.

119.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: The Aravidu Dynasty of Vijayanagara — Father H. Heras
Peasant State and Society in Medieval South India — Burton Stein
Social and Political Life in the Vijayanagara Empire — B.A. Saletore
119.x: Kampili and Vijayanagara was written by Nelaturi Venkataramanaiah, not Robert Sewell. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
119.tq: Find the swapped author–title pair among closely related historical works.
xs: **Kampili and Vijayanagara — Robert Sewell** is wrong — option **(4)**; it was written by **Nelaturi Venkataramanaiah**.
The other pairs are correct: **Father H. Heras** (The Aravidu Dynasty), **Burton Stein** (Peasant State and Society), **B.A. Saletore** (Social and Political Life).
xa: Robert Sewell wrote **A Forgotten Empire**, translating **Paes** and **Nuniz** (APPSC G2 **2011**, **2017**).
Burton Stein called Vijayanagara a **"segmentary state"**.
⚠ **Sewell** backs the **Andhra theory**; **Heras** backs the **Kannada** theory of origin.

119.s: A Forgotten Empire: Vijayanagar is best described as which of the following?
o: A Sanskrit poem describing the conquest of Madurai
A Telugu account of the twelve Sangama kings
A Persian chronicle presenting the Bahmani view of the wars
An English translation of the accounts of Domingo Paes and Fernao Nuniz
119.x: Robert Sewell’s A Forgotten Empire: Vijayanagar is an English translation of the Portuguese accounts of Domingo Paes and Fernao Nuniz.
119.tq: Distinguish the nature and source-language tradition of the work from other historical sources.
xs: **A Forgotten Empire** is **Robert Sewell's** English translation of the accounts of **Domingo Paes and Fernao Nuniz** — option **(4)**.
The Sanskrit poem on Madurai's conquest is **Madhura Vijayam** by **Gangadevi**.
The list of **12 Sangama kings** is in **Virupakshaya Kalajnana**; the Bahmani view comes from **Ferishta**.
xa: Asked in APPSC G2 **2011** and **2017**.
**Paes** visited under **Krishnadevaraya**; **Nuniz** under **Achyutaraya**.
Sewell also records the **seven** founding traditions of Vijayanagara.

119.s:
Consider the following statements about sources for Vijayanagara history:
1. Rayavachakam is associated with Sthanapati.
2. Virupakshaya Kalajnana lists the kings of the Aravidu dynasty.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
119.x: Statement 1 is correct: Rayavachakam is by Sthanapati. Statement 2 is wrong: Virupakshaya Kalajnana lists 12 Sangama kings, not the Aravidu kings. So 1 only (A); B and C accept the wrong statement, D rejects the correct one.
119.tq: Virupakshaya Kalajnana = 12 Sangama kings; Rayavachakam = Sthanapati.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: **Rayavachakam** is by **Sthanapati**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Virupakshaya Kalajnana** lists **12 Sangama kings**, not Aravidu kings.
xa: Other sources: **Kaifiyats** and foreign travellers; **Ferishta** gives the Bahmani view.
**Vidyaranya** wrote the **Vidyaranya Kalajnana**.
**The Aravidu Dynasty of Vijayanagara** is by **Father H. Heras**.

119.s: Cesare Federici, the Italian traveller, was associated with the reign of which Vijayanagara ruler?
119.x: Cesare Federici visited Vijayanagara during the reign of Sadasivaraya.
119.tq: Use nationality and reign as a paired identification clue.
xs: **Cesare Federici** (Italy) visited in the reign of **Sadasivaraya** — option **(2)**.
**Devaraya II** received **Abdur Razzaq**; **Achyutaraya** received **Nuniz**; **Devaraya I** is linked in some notes to **Nicolo Conti**.
xa: Sadasivaraya (Tuluva) ruled with **Rama Raya** as regent; **Talikota (1565)** fell in his reign.
**Paes** and **Barbosa** came under **Krishnadevaraya**.
Order of dynasties: **Sangama – Saluva – Tuluva – Aravidu**.

119.s: Which symbol appears on the seal of the copper plates connected with Devaraya I’s coronation?
119.x: The copper plates carry a Vamana seal, rather than the usual Varaha seal.
119.tq: Focus on the exceptional symbol and avoid reversing the unusual seal with the customary one.
xs: The plates carry a **Vamana** seal — option **(1)**.
This replaces the usual **Varaha** (boar), the Vijayanagara emblem.
xa: The plates record Devaraya I's coronation and grant **Gudipalli**, renamed **Devarayapura-Agrahara**.
Sangamas were **Shaiva**; the later three dynasties were **Vaishnava**.
Harihara I's coronation was at the **Virupaksha** temple, **18 April 1336**.

119.s: Which ruler is identified as the first Vijayanagara ruler to attack Sri Lanka?
119.x: Harihara II is identified as the first Vijayanagara ruler to attack Sri Lanka.
119.tq: Separate the first external attack from the foreign-traveller association and Andhra campaigns.
xs: **Harihara II** was the **first to attack Sri Lanka** — option **(1)**.
**Harihara I** was visited by **Ibn Battuta**; **Bukka I** sent the embassy to **Ming China (1374)**; **Devaraya II** received tribute from Sri Lanka via **Lakkanna Dandanayaka**.
xa: Harihara II (**1377-1404**) was the **longest-reigning** Sangama king; titles **Rajavyasa**, **Rajavalmiki**.
His minister **Sayana** wrote **Vedartha Prakasha**.
Last Sangama ruler: **Praudha Raya**.

119.s:
With reference to the dynastic and geographical features of the Vijayanagara Empire, consider the following statements:
1. Sangama and Aravidu are described as two dynasties of Andhra origin.
2. Penukonda and Chandragiri served as later capitals and are located in Andhra Pradesh.
3. All four Vijayanagara dynasties are described as Andhra in origin.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because only two of the four dynasties, Sangama and Aravidu, are described as Andhra in origin.
119.tq: Reject the extreme claim that extends a correct two-dynasty classification to all four dynasties.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: **Sangama** and **Aravidu** are called Andhra in origin.
Statement 2 is correct: later capitals **Penukonda** and **Chandragiri** are in AP.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Saluva** (Kalyani) and **Tuluva** are of **Karnataka** origin.
xa: Aravidu origin: **Araviti**, Kurnool; capitals Penukonda, Chandragiri, **Vellore**.
Founders' origin theories: **7**; the APPSC key says Sangama was **"a Kakatiya chief"** (G2 **2005**).
⚠ Order **S-S-T-A** = Sangama – Saluva – Tuluva – Aravidu.

119.s: Which foreign traveller is noted as the first to visit Vijayanagara, during the reign of Harihara I?
119.x: Ibn Battuta is listed as the first foreign traveller, in Harihara I's reign. Nicolo Conti came under Devaraya I/II, Abdur Razzaq under Devaraya II (1443) and Domingo Paes under Krishnadevaraya.
119.tq: Firsts: traveller Ibn Battuta (Harihara I); attack on Sri Lanka Harihara II.
xs: **Ibn Battuta** was the first foreign traveller, in **Harihara I's** reign — option **(2)**.
**Nicolo Conti** came under Devaraya I/II, **Abdur Razzaq** under **Devaraya II** (**1443**), **Domingo Paes** under **Krishnadevaraya**.
xa: Harihara I moved the capital from **Anegondi** to **Vijayanagara**; title **Purva-Paschima Samudradhipati**.
He annexed the **Hoysala** kingdom (**1346**) and the **Kadambas** (**1347**).
Vijayanagara was founded in **1336** on the **southern bank of the Tungabhadra**.

119.s:
Consider the following statements about the Vijayanagara Empire:
I. Harihara I and Bukka I established the empire in 1336 AD.
II. The Sangama dynasty was the first of its four successive dynasties.
III. The Tuluva dynasty was followed by the Saluva dynasty.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
119.x: I and II are correct: Harihara I and Bukka I founded Vijayanagara in 1336, and the Sangama was its first dynasty. III is false because the order was Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva and Aravidu, so the Saluva came before the Tuluva.
119.tq: Recall the order of the four Vijayanagara dynasties.
n: Harihara I and Bukka I established the Vijayanagara Empire in 1336 AD. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
The Sangama dynasty was the first dynasty of the Vijayanagara Empire. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
The Vijayanagara Empire was ruled successively by the Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva, and Aravidu dynasties. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
xs: Statements **I and II only** are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
I: **Harihara I** and **Bukka I** founded the empire in **1336 AD**; II: **Sangama** was the **first** of four dynasties.
III is wrong: the order was **Sangama – Saluva – Tuluva – Aravidu**, so **Saluva** came before **Tuluva**.
xa: **Sangama** and **Aravidu** = Andhra origin (CDX).
The **Sangama** dynasty ruled longest; greatest king **Devaraya II**.

119.s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Sangama
(b) Saluva
(c) Tuluva
(d) Aravidu

List-II
i. Vira Narasimha
ii. Harihara I and Bukka I
iii. Tirumala Deva Raya
iv. Narasimha Saluva
119.x: Harihara I and Bukka I began the Sangama line, Narasimha Saluva the Saluva, Vira Narasimha the Tuluva, and Tirumala Deva Raya, brother of Aliya Rama Raya, founded the Aravidu dynasty after Talikota, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.
119.tq: Link each Vijayanagara dynasty to its first ruler.
n: Harihara I belonged to the Sangama dynasty of Vijayanagara. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
Bukka I belonged to the Sangama dynasty of Vijayanagara. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
Harihara I and Bukka I belonged to the Sangama dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
Narasimha Saluva belonged to the Saluva dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
Vira Narasimha belonged to the Tuluva dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
The Aravidu dynasty was associated with the Aravidu line. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
xs: The correct match is **a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Sangama** — **Harihara I and Bukka I**; **Saluva** — **Narasimha Saluva**.
**Tuluva** — **Vira Narasimha** (APPSC G2 **2002** key); **Aravidu** — **Tirumala Raya** at Penukonda.
xa: ⚠ Some notes call **Tuluva Narasa Nayaka** the Tuluva founder; APPSC key says **Veera Narasimha**.
Aravidu capitals: **Penukonda, Chandragiri, Vellore**.
Saluva Narasimha's seizure (**1485**) = the **"first usurpation"**.

119.s: Who immediately succeeded Prauda Deva Raya?
119.x: Narasimha Saluva ended Sangama rule in 1485 by taking the throne from Prauda Deva Raya, the last Sangama king, and began the Saluva dynasty.
119.tq: Recall who ended the Sangama line.
n: The immediate successor of Prauda Deva Raya was Narasimha Saluva. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 94-95]
xs: **Narasimha Saluva** immediately succeeded **Praudha Raya** — so option **(2)** is correct.
In **1485** he expelled Praudha Raya, the **last Sangama** ruler, with **Tuluva Narasa Nayaka's** help — the **First Usurpation**.
**Vira Narasimha** came later (**1505**, Tuluva); **Krishnadevaraya** ruled **1509-29**; **Achyutaraya** was also Tuluva.
xa: Saluva Narasimha was lord of **Chandragiri**; clan from **Kalyana**.
**Annamacharya** (**1408-1503**) was his contemporary.
**Jaimini Bharatam** by **Pillalamarri Pinaveerabhadra** was dedicated to him.

119.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Harihara-II’s campaign:

I. It was part of the Vijayanagara–Bahamani conflict.
II. It extended into Kanara.
III. It extended into Mysore.
IV. It extended into Kanchi.
V. It extended into Trichinapalli.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
o: I, II, III, IV and V
I, III, IV and V only
119.x: All five are correct: Harihara II's campaigns were part of the Vijayanagara–Bahmani struggle and extended his rule over Kanara, Mysore, Kanchi and Trichinopoly.
119.tq: Check each statement separately.
n: Harihara-II’s campaign was part of the Vijayanagara–Bahamani conflict. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 76-78]
Harihara-II expanded into Kanara. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 76-78]
Harihara-II expanded into Mysore. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 76-78]
Harihara-II expanded into Kanchi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 76-78]
Harihara-II expanded into Trichinapalli. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 76-78]
xs: All five — **I, II, III, IV and V** — are correct, so option **(2)** is correct.
**Harihara-II** took **Goa** and **Belgaum** from the **Bahamani** in **1380** — part of the **Vijayanagara–Bahamani conflict**.
He **expanded** into **Kanara**, **Mysore**, **Kanchi** and **Trichinapalli**.
xa: Bone of contention: **Raichur Doab** between the **Krishna and Tungabhadra**.
⚠ Other notes say Goa was taken in **1366** by minister **Madhava**; lost in **1472**.
**Mudgal (1358)** under **Bukka I** = **first Indian war with artillery**.

119.s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Pataliputra
(b) Vijayanagara
(c) Tughluqabad
(d) Nauraspur

List-II
(i) Harihara and Bukka
(ii) Ajatashatru
(iii) Ghiyasuddin Tughluq
(iv) Ibrahim Adil Shah II
119.x: Ajatashatru fortified Pataliputra, Harihara and Bukka founded Vijayanagara in 1336, Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq built Tughlaqabad, and Ibrahim Adil Shah II founded Nauraspur, giving a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv.
119.tq: Recall the founder of each city.
n: Ajatashatru established Pataliputra as a fortified settlement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 144-145]
Harihara and Bukka founded Vijayanagara in 1336 CE. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 144-145]
Ghiyasuddin Tughluq established Tughluqabad as a city in Delhi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 144-145]
Ibrahim Adil Shah II established Nauraspur as a new township. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 144-145]
xs: The correct match is **a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Pataliputra** — **Ajatashatru**; **Vijayanagara** — **Harihara and Bukka** (**1336**).
**Tughluqabad** — **Ghiyasuddin Tughluq**; **Nauraspur** — **Ibrahim Adil Shah II**.
xa: Nauraspur was known as a **musical city**.
**Udayin** shifted the capital from **Rajagriha** to **Pataliputra**.
**Nagalapuram** — **Krishnadeva Raya**, for his mother **Nagala Devi**.

119.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Ajatashatru established Pataliputra as a fortified settlement.
II. Udayin shifted the capital from Rajagriha to Pataliputra.
III. Ghiyasuddin Tughluq established Tughluqabad as a city in Delhi.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: All three are correct: Ajatashatru fortified Pataliputra, his successor Udayin shifted the capital there from Rajagriha, and Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq built Tughlaqabad in Delhi.
119.tq: Check each statement separately.
n: Ajatashatru established Pataliputra as a fortified settlement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 144-145]
Udayin shifted the capital from Rajagriha to Pataliputra. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 144-145]
Ghiyasuddin Tughluq established Tughluqabad as a city in Delhi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 144-145]
xs: All three — **I, II and III** — are correct, so option **(3)** is correct.
I: **Ajatashatru** established **Pataliputra** as a **fortified settlement**.
II: **Udayin** shifted the capital from **Rajagriha** to **Pataliputra**; III: **Ghiyasuddin Tughluq** established **Tughluqabad** in **Delhi**.
xa: **Nauraspur** — **Ibrahim Adil Shah II**, a musical township.
**Nagalapuram** — **Krishnadeva Raya**.
**Vijayanagara** — **Harihara and Bukka**, on the **Tungabhadra**.

119.s: What was the name of Krishnadeva Raya’s mother in whose honour Nagalapuram was founded?
119.x: Krishnadeva Raya founded Nagalapuram near Hampi in honour of his mother, Nagala Devi. Tirumala Devi and Chinna Devi were his queens.
119.tq: Recall the name behind Nagalapuram.
n: Krishnadeva Raya founded Nagalapuram in honour or memory of his mother, Nagala Devi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 144-145]
xs: **Krishnadeva Raya** founded **Nagalapuram** in honour of his mother **Nagala Devi** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Nauraspur** is a township of **Ibrahim Adil Shah II**, not a person's name.
xa: Krishnadevaraya (**1509-29**) marked the empire's **zenith**.
**Paes** and **Barbosa** visited in his reign.
He retook **Raichur** (**1520**) and took **Gulbarga** (**1523**).

119.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Marco Polo
(b) Nicolo Conti
(c) Nuniz
(d) Abdul Razzaq

List-II
(i) Court of Devaraya II
(ii) Motupalli port
(iii) Vijayanagara under Achyutadeva Raya
(iv) Vijayanagara under Devaraya I
119.x: Marco Polo visited Motupalli port under Rudramadevi, Nicolo Conti came under Devaraya I, Nuniz described Vijayanagara under Achyutadeva Raya, and Abdul Razzaq came as envoy to Devaraya II's court, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
119.tq: Place each traveller by the ruler in whose reign he came.
n: Marco Polo visited Motupalli port in Andhra Desa during Rudramadevi’s rule. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 39-40]
Nicolo Conti visited South India during the reign of Devaraya I of the Vijayanagara Empire. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 39-40]
Nuniz visited the Vijayanagara Empire during the rule of Achyutadeva Raya. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 39-40]
Abdul Razzaq visited the court of Devaraya II. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 39-40]
xs: The correct match is **a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Marco Polo** — **Motupalli port** (Rudramadevi); **Nicolo Conti** — **Devaraya I**.
**Nuniz** — **Achyutadeva Raya**; **Abdul Razzaq** — **court of Devaraya II**.
xa: Abdur Razzaq was envoy of **Shah Rukh**, **1443**; noted **300 ports**.
⚠ Other notes say **Nuniz** was from **Portugal**.
**Cesare Federici** (Italy) visited under **Sadasivaraya**.
**Robert Sewell's** **A Forgotten Empire** used **Paes and Nuniz**.

120.s: Which statement regarding the rulers preceding Saluva Narasimha is correct?
o: Praudha Raya was the general who seized the throne for Saluva Narasimha.
Virupaksha II was described as a drunkard, while Praudha Raya was considered worthless.
Virupaksha II founded the Saluva dynasty, while Praudha Raya ruled from Chandragiri.
Both rulers successfully repelled the Gajapati and Bahmani invasions.
120.x: Nuniz described Virupaksha II as a drunkard, while Praudha Raya was considered worthless; their weakness contributed to the crisis of the kingdom.
120.tq: Match the correct description with each of two neighbouring rulers.
xs: **Virupaksha II** was described (by **Nuniz**) as a **drunkard**, and **Praudha Raya** as **worthless** — option **(2)**.
The general who seized the throne for Saluva Narasimha was **Tuluva Narasa Nayaka**, not Praudha Raya.
Their weakness let **Gajapati** and **Bahmani** invasions eat into the kingdom — they did not repel them.
xa: Saluva Narasimha, lord of **Chandragiri**, took the throne in **1485** — the **first usurpation**.
Saluva rule (**1485-91**) moved the capital from **Kalyanapuram** to **Chandragiri**.
Praudha Raya was the **last Sangama ruler**.

120.s:
Consider the following statements about Saluva Narasimha:
1. He took Honnavar, Bhatkal and Mangalore.
2. He brought Arab horses from Ormuz and introduced Samugaris (gunmen).
3. He won Udayagiri from Gajapati Purushottama.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
120.x: Statement 1 is correct: he took Honnavar, Bhatkal and Mangalore. Statement 2 is correct: he brought Arab horses from Ormuz and introduced Samugaris. Statement 3 is wrong: he lost Udayagiri to Gajapati Purushottama. Hence 1 and 2 only.
120.tq: Saluva Narasimha LOST Udayagiri; Krishnadevaraya later won it back.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: he took **Honnavar, Bhatkal and Mangalore**.
Statement 2 is correct: he brought **Arab horses** (Ormuz) with Arab cavalry and introduced **Samugaris (gunmen)**.
Statement 3 is wrong: he **lost Udayagiri** to Gajapati **Purushottama**.
xa: Udayagiri was later retaken by **Krishnadevaraya** (**1513-14**) after an **18-month siege**.
Saluva capital: **Kalyanapuram** → **Chandragiri**.
Court poet: **Rajanatha Dindima** (**Saluvabhyudayam**).

120.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
120.x: Rajanatha Dindima, court poet of Saluva Narasimha, wrote Saluvabhyudayam. Gangadevi wrote Madhura Vijayam, not Saluvabhyudayam; Dhurjati wrote Sri Kalahasteeswara Mahatyam and Satakam, not Madhura Vijayam; Ramabhyudayamu is by Ayyalaraju Ramabhadrudu, while Tirumalamba wrote Varadambika Parinayam.
120.tq: Use a sure author–work pair to eliminate literary-name swaps.
xs: **Rajanatha Dindima — Saluvabhyudayam** is correct — option **(1)**; he was Saluva Narasimha's court poet.
**Dhurjati** wrote **Sri Kalahasteeswara Mahatyam** and **Satakam**, not Madhura Vijayam.
**Ramabhyudayamu** is by **Ayyalaraju Ramabhadrudu**; **Tirumalamba** wrote **Varadambika Parinayam**.
xa: Dhurjati was the **Shaiva** poet of **Kalahasti**, one of the **Ashtadiggajas**.
Ayyalaraju Ramabhadrudu's Ramabhyudayamu is the **Ramayana in Telugu**.
**Annamacharya** was Saluva Narasimha's contemporary.

120.s: Annamacharya was a contemporary of:
120.x: Annamacharya was a contemporary of Saluva Narasimha.
120.tq: Connect a major saint-poet with the correct contemporary ruler.
xs: **Annamacharya** was a contemporary of **Saluva Narasimha** — option **(2)** (APPSC G2 **2011**).
He composed **32,000 kirtanas** to **Venkateswara**.
xa: In this period **Tirupati** became the leading **Vaishnava** centre.
Saluva Narasimha seized the throne in **1485** (first usurpation); Saluva rule lasted **1485-91**.
**Gajapati Purushottama** took **Udayagiri** from Saluva Narasimha.

120.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Tuluva dynasty:
1. Timmaraju was regarded as its progenitor.
2. Kannada was the mother tongue of its ruling family.
3. Telugu was not favoured in its court.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
120.x: Timmaraju was the progenitor, and Kannada was the mother tongue. Telugu was favoured, so statement 3 is false.
120.tq: Find the statement that reverses a language-related fact.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: **Timmaraju** was the **progenitor**.
Statement 2 is correct: their mother tongue was **Kannada**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Telugu was favoured**.
xa: The name comes from **Tulunadu** (Mysore region), conquered by Harihara in **1342**.
Krishnadevaraya's reign (**1509-1529**) was the **golden age of Telugu literature**, the **Prabandha era**.
⚠ Founder in the key = **Vira Narasimha**, not **Tuluva Narasa Nayaka**.

120.s: Who was the real ruler under Immadi Narasimha?
120.x: Tuluva Narasa Nayaka, a Saluva general, was the real ruler under Immadi Narasimha.
120.tq: Match the ruler with the political role actually held.
xs: **Tuluva Narasa Nayaka**, a Saluva general, was the real ruler under **Immadi Narasimha** — option **(3)**.
He died in **1503**; his son **Vira Narasimha** then killed Immadi Narasimha at **Penugonda** in **1505**.
xa: ⚠ Narasa Nayaka helped both usurpations: general in **1485**, father of the usurper in **1505**.
The APPSC key names **Vira Narasimha** the Tuluva founder (G2 **2002**).
**Saluva Narasimha** ruled **1485-91**.

120.s: Who was the Prime Minister of Krishnadevaraya, also known as Appaji?
120.x: Saluva Timmarusu, popularly known as Appaji, served as the Prime Minister of Krishnadevaraya.
120.tq: Apply the person–office association rather than the ruler–enemy association.
xs: Krishnadevaraya's PM was **Saluva Timmarusu (Appaji)** — option **(1)**.
**Ismail Adil Shah** was routed at **Raichur (1520)**; **Prataparudra Gajapati** was the Kalinga foe; **Ali Barid** held **Sultan Mahmud Shah**.
xa: Timmarusu helped take **Kondaveedu** by splitting **Veerabhadra Gajapati's** army.
Krishnadevaraya was crowned on **8 Aug 1509** (Hampi inscription).
The Kalinga campaign ran **1513-1519**.

120.s: Which campaign resulted in the defeat of Yusuf Adil Khan?
120.x: During the Diwani or Kovilkonda campaign of 1509–10, the Bahmani jihad was crushed and Yusuf Adil Khan was killed.
120.tq: Match the military result with the correct campaign.
xs: **Yusuf Adil Khan** was killed in the **Diwani / Kovilkonda** campaign (**1509-10**) — option **(1)**; the Bahmani "jihad" was crushed.
**Udayagiri**, **Kondaveedu** and **Simhachalam** belong to the **Kalinga campaign (1513-1519)** against the Gajapatis.
xa: ⚠ **Yusuf Adil Khan** killed at Kovilkonda; **Ismail Adil Shah** routed at **Raichur (1520)**.
**Raichur Doab (1510)**: Raichur taken; freed **Sultan Mahmud Shah** from **Ali Barid**.
Ummattur / Sivasamudram (**1512-13**): **Gangaraja** defeated.

120.s: The title “Yavanarajya Sthapanacharya” was associated with Krishnadevaraya’s:
120.x: After taking Raichur and freeing Sultan Mahmud Shah from Ali Barid, Krishnadevaraya acquired the title Yavanarajya Sthapanacharya.
120.tq: Link an honorific title with the event that produced it.
xs: The title came from the **Raichur and Bidar** campaign (**1510**) — option **(4)**: he freed **Sultan Mahmud Shah** from **Ali Barid**.
**Ummattur** defeated **Gangaraja**; **Udayagiri** and the **Kalinga campaign** were against the Gajapatis.
xa: The title **Yavana Rajya Sthapanacharya** is celebrated in **Manucharitra**.
Other titles: **Andhra Bhoja**, **Sahiti Samarangana Sarvabhauma**, **Kannada Rajya Rama Ramana**, **Gajapati Gajakuta Pakaveni**.
Raichur was again won in **1520**, routing **Ismail Adil Shah** with **Portuguese** help.

120.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the Ummattur campaign?
o: Gangaraja was defeated and a new province was established at Srirangapatna.
Yusuf Adil Khan was killed and the Bahmani jihad was crushed.
The Balakrishna idol was brought to Hampi.
Victory pillars were erected at Potnuru and Simhachalam.
120.x: In the Ummattur or Sivasamudram campaign of 1512–13, Gangaraja was defeated and a new province was established at Srirangapatna.
120.tq: Match a campaign with its distinctive result while rejecting results from other campaigns.
xs: In the **Ummattur / Sivasamudram** campaign (**1512-13**), **Gangaraja was defeated** and a new province set up at **Srirangapatna** — option **(1)**.
**Yusuf Adil Khan** was killed at **Kovilkonda**; the **Balakrishna idol** came from **Udayagiri**; victory pillars stood at **Potnuru** and **Simhachalam**.
xa: Campaign order: **Kovilkonda (1509-10)** → **Raichur Doab (1510)** → **Ummattur (1512-13)** → **Kalinga (1513-1519)** → **Raichur (1520)**.
**Gulbarga** was taken in **1523**.

120.s:
Consider the following statements about Krishnadevaraya's Kalinga campaign:
1. The campaign ran from 1513 to 1519.
2. Udayagiri fell after a siege of about 12 months.
3. Krishnadevaraya reached Cuttack in 1518.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
120.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Kalinga campaign ran 1513-1519. Statement 2 is wrong: Udayagiri fell after an 18-month siege. Statement 3 is correct: Cuttack was reached in 1518. Hence 1 and 3 only.
120.tq: Udayagiri = 18-month siege; Cuttack = 1518; campaign 1513-19.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: the Kalinga campaign ran **1513-1519**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Udayagiri** fell after an **18-month siege**.
Statement 3 is correct: **Cuttack** was reached in **1518**; the Gajapati sued for peace.
xa: Aim: win back **Tirandhra** and **Telangana** from **Prataparudra Gajapati**.
Telangana forts taken: **Devarakonda, Nalgonda, Kambhamettu, Jallipalli and Warangal**.
Victory pillars: **Potnuru** and **Simhachalam**.

120.s: After the conquest of Udayagiri, which idol was taken to Hampi?
120.x: Krishnadevaraya brought the Balakrishna idol from Udayagiri to Hampi, where the Krishna temple was built for it.
120.tq: Use the deity–campaign association to separate three Narasimha-related locations.
xs: The **Balakrishna idol** was taken from **Udayagiri** to **Hampi** — option **(3)**, for the **Krishna temple**.
**Varaha Narasimha** (Simhachalam) got a **diamond necklace**; **Lakshmi Narasimha** (Mangalagiri) got land.
xa: Udayagiri (**1513-14**) fell after an **18-month siege**.
Udayagiri had earlier been lost by **Saluva Narasimha** to Gajapati **Purushottama**.
After **Kondaveedu**, the king performed **Talapurusha Danam** at **Amaravati**.

120.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Ummattur — Balakrishna idol taken to Hampi
120.x: After the conquest of Kondaveedu, Krishnadevaraya performed Talapurusha Danam at Amaravati. The other pairs associate results with the wrong campaigns.
120.tq: Start from the sure campaign–event pair and eliminate swapped results.
xs: **Kondaveedu — Talapurusha Danam at Amaravati** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Udayagiri** = **Balakrishna idol** to Hampi; the **Potnuru** pillar marked the conquest of coastal Andhra.
**Srirangapatna** province came from **Ummattur**, not Raichur.
xa: Kondaveedu was taken with **Saluva Timmarusu's** help, who split **Veerabhadra Gajapati's** army.
At **Kondapalli and Bejawada**, **Praharajeshwara** and Prataparudra's forces were beaten.
PYQ **2025**: pillar marking the conquest of coastal Andhra = **Potnuru**.

120.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the locations of Krishnadevaraya’s victory pillars?
120.x: Victory pillars were erected at Potnuru and Simhachalam after the Kalinga campaign. The pillar at Potnuru marked the conquest of coastal Andhra.
120.tq: Use location-based discrimination among campaign and religious centres.
xs: Victory pillars stood at **Potnuru and Simhachalam** — option **(3)**.
PYQ **2025**: the pillar marking the conquest of coastal Andhra = **Potnuru**.
**Amaravati** saw **Talapurusha Danam**; **Mangalagiri** got a land grant; **Udayagiri** and **Kondaveedu** were forts taken.
xa: **Simhachalam**: a **diamond necklace** to **Varaha Narasimha**.
The Kalinga campaign ran **1513-1519**; **Cuttack** reached in **1518**.
AP angle: **Udayagiri, Kondaveedu, Kondapalli** forts of the campaign lie in AP.

120.s:
Consider the following statements about the Raichur campaign of 1520:
1. Ismail Adil Shah was routed.
2. The Portuguese assisted Krishnadevaraya.
3. Gulbarga was taken in 1523.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
120.x: All three statements are correct: Ismail Adil Shah was defeated in 1520 with Portuguese help, and Gulbarga was taken in 1523.
120.tq: Check the campaign, foreign assistance and later territorial result separately.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Ismail Adil Shah** was routed at **Raichur (1520)** with **Portuguese** help.
**Gulbarga** was taken in **1523**.
xa: ⚠ **Yusuf Adil Khan** was killed earlier, at **Kovilkonda (1509-10)**.
Raichur had first been taken in **1510**, when **Sultan Mahmud Shah** was freed from **Ali Barid**.
In **1510** Krishnadevaraya backed **Albuquerque's** capture of **Goa** through envoy **Luis**.

120.s:
Consider the following statements about the settlement after Krishnadevaraya's Kalinga campaign:
1. Gajapati Prataparudra gave his daughter in marriage to Krishnadevaraya.
2. Lands south of the Krishna were returned to the Gajapati.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
120.x: Statement 1 is correct: Prataparudra Gajapati gave his daughter to Krishnadevaraya. Statement 2 is wrong: it was the lands north of the Krishna that went back to the Gajapati. Hence 1 only.
120.tq: Marriage alliance + lands NORTH of the Krishna back to the Gajapati.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: **Gajapati Prataparudra** gave his **daughter** to Krishnadevaraya.
Statement 2 is wrong: lands **north of the Krishna** went back to the Gajapati.
xa: Her name: **Annapurnadevi** (some notes) vs **Bhadradevi (Tukka / Jaganmohini)**.
The campaign reached **Cuttack** in **1518**, when the Gajapati sued for peace.
Aim: win back **Tirandhra** and **Telangana**.

120.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Simhachalam — diamond necklace to Varaha Narasimha
Potnuru — pillar marking the conquest of coastal Andhra
Mangalagiri — land grant to Lakshmi Narasimha
Udayagiri — land grant to Lakshmi Narasimha
120.x: Udayagiri is associated with the capture of the Balakrishna idol. The land grant to Lakshmi Narasimha was made at Mangalagiri.
120.tq: Find the location whose associated religious act has been deliberately swapped.
xs: **Udayagiri — land grant to Lakshmi Narasimha** is wrong — option **(4)**.
The land grant to **Lakshmi Narasimha** was at **Mangalagiri**; Udayagiri gave the **Balakrishna idol** taken to Hampi.
**Simhachalam** (diamond necklace) and **Potnuru** (coastal Andhra pillar) are correctly matched.
xa: The **Mangalagiri** temple renovation (**₹6 crore**) includes restoring the **Sri Krishna Devaraya Mandapam**.
Udayagiri fell after an **18-month siege** (**1513-14**).
PYQ **2025**: **Potnuru** pillar.

120.s: Vira Narasimha entered into an alliance with which Portuguese Viceroy for securing horses and military training?
120.x: Vira Narasimha allied with Viceroy Francisco de Almeida for horses and military training.
120.tq: Identify the person directly associated with the stated diplomatic and military arrangement.
xs: **Vira Narasimha** allied with Viceroy **Francisco de Almeida** for **horses** and **military training** — option **(2)**.
**Albuquerque** was backed by **Krishnadevaraya** in taking **Goa (1510)**; **Joao de Castro** made peace with Sadasiva/Rama Raya; **Duarte Barbosa** was a visitor.
xa: ⚠ **Almeida** = Vira Narasimha; **Albuquerque** = Krishnadevaraya.
In return for Goa, the Portuguese supplied **horses** and were allowed a fort at **Bhatkal**.
Portuguese help counted at **Raichur (1520)**.

120.s: Which one of the following was NOT a consequence of Krishnadevaraya's support to Albuquerque in the capture of Goa?
o: Permission to build a fort at Bhatkal
Transfer of Raichur to the Portuguese
120.x: Krishnadevaraya received horses and training and permitted the Portuguese to build a fort at Bhatkal. Transfer of Raichur to the Portuguese was not a stated consequence.
120.tq: Find the option that changes a military and commercial arrangement into an unsupported territorial transfer.
xs: **Transfer of Raichur to the Portuguese** was not a consequence — option **(4)**.
In return for Goa, Krishnadevaraya got a steady **supply of horses** and **military training**, and let the Portuguese build a fort at **Bhatkal**.
Raichur stayed with Vijayanagara: **Ismail Adil Shah** was routed there in **1520** with Portuguese help.
xa: Goa was captured by **Albuquerque** from **Bijapur** in **1510**, through envoy **Luis**.
Bhatkal had earlier been taken by **Saluva Narasimha**.

120.s: Who made peace after Sadasiva and Rama Raya defeated Governor Martin de Souza for damaging temples?
120.x: João de Castro made peace after the defeat of Martin de Souza, whose actions had included damaging temples.
120.tq: Apply the wrong-person-with-the-deed trap to distinguish Portuguese governors and peace-makers.
xs: **Joao de Castro** made peace — option **(4)**.
**Sadasiva / Rama Raya** had defeated Governor **Martin de Souza** for damaging temples.
**Almeida** allied with **Vira Narasimha**; **Albuquerque** took Goa in **1510**; **Duarte Barbosa** visited Krishnadevaraya's court.
xa: **Aliya Rama Raya**, Krishnadevaraya's son-in-law of the **Aravidu** family, made **Sadasiva** a figurehead.
He killed **Salakam Tirumala** in **1543**.
His **divide and rule** policy united the Sultanates against him → **Talikota (1565)**.

120.s: Which pair is correctly matched?
120.x: Nagalapuram was named after Krishnadevaraya's mother Nagalamba.
120.tq: Match a foundation name with its namesake, avoiding queen–mother confusion.
xs: **Nagalapuram — Nagalamba** is correct — option **(3)**; it is named after his mother.
**Hospet** is named after his queen **Tirumaladevi**, not Nagalamba.
**Gangadevi** was the author of Madhura Vijayam, not linked to Hospet.
xa: Hospet is also called **Tirumaladevipattana**.
⚠ **Nagalapuram** = mother; **Hospet** = queen.
Titles: **Andhra Bhoja**, **Sahiti Samarangana Sarvabhauma**.

120.s: Which one of the following was NOT a title of Krishnadevaraya?
120.x: Andhra Bhoja, Sahiti Samarangana Sarvabhauma and Kannada Rajya Rama Ramana were titles of Krishnadevaraya. Gajabetekara (elephant hunter) was the title of the Sangama ruler Devaraya II.
120.tq: Gajabetekara = Devaraya II; Andhra Bhoja = Krishnadevaraya.
xs: **Gajabetekara** was not Krishnadevaraya's title — option **(4)**; it means "elephant hunter" and belongs to **Devaraya II**.
**Andhra Bhoja**, **Sahiti Samarangana Sarvabhauma** and **Kannada Rajya Rama Ramana** are his titles.
xa: **Yavana Rajya Sthapanacharya**: for restoring the Bahmani Sultan; celebrated in **Manucharitra**.
Others: **Gajapati Gajakuta Pakaveni**, **Dakshinapatha Swami**, **Mururaya Raganda**, **Paribhuta Suratrana**.

120.s: The title “Amuktamalyada” literally means:
o: One who wears the garland of victory
One who offers the garland she has worn
One who conquers the garlanded city
One who worships Vishnu with flowers
120.x: Amuktamalyada means “one who offers the garland she has worn,” referring to the devotional story associated with Goda Devi or Andal.
120.tq: Test the exact meaning of a title rather than its broad theme.
xs: Amuktamalyada means **"one who offers the garland she has worn"** — option **(2)**.
It tells the story of **Goda Devi (Andal)** and her marriage to **Sri Ranganatha**.
xa: Also called **Vishnuchittiyam**; written in **Telugu**.
It is the **first Telugu work named after its heroine**.
One of the **Telugu Pancha Kavyas**.

120.s:
Consider the following statements about Krishnadevaraya's Amuktamalyada:
1. According to legend, Andhra Mahavishnu of Srikakulam commanded the king in a dream to write it.
2. It was written during the Raichur campaign.
3. It is dedicated to Lord Venkateswara.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
120.x: Statement 1 is correct: Andhra Mahavishnu of Srikakulam commanded him in a dream. Statement 2 is wrong: it was written during the Kalinga campaign, not the Raichur campaign. Statement 3 is correct: it is dedicated to Lord Venkateswara. Hence 1 and 3 only; options with 2 are wrong and '1 only' misses 3.
120.tq: Dream deity = Srikakulam Andhra Mahavishnu; campaign = Kalinga; dedication = Venkateswara.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: **Andhra Mahavishnu of Srikakulam** commanded the king in a **dream** to write it.
Statement 2 is wrong: it was written during the **Kalinga campaign**, not Raichur.
Statement 3 is correct: it is dedicated to **Lord Venkateswara**.
xa: Its subject: **Goda Devi (Andal)** and her marriage to **Sri Ranganatha**.
It describes **Villiputtur** and **Madhura**.
AP angle: **Srikakulam** (Krishna district) is linked to the work.

120.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Amuktamalyada:
1. It deals with Goda Devi and her marriage to Ranganatha.
2. It contains the stories of Yamunacharya and Maladasari.
3. It describes the invasions of Krishnadevaraya in detail.
4. It contains political advice relating to kingship and administration.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
120.x: The work deals with Goda Devi’s marriage to Ranganatha, includes Yamunacharya Charitra and Maladasari Katha, and gives political advice. It does not describe Krishnadevaraya’s invasions.
120.tq: Find the one negative statement that reverses the known scope of the work.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct — option **(1) 1, 2 and 4 only**.
1: it deals with **Goda Devi** and her marriage to **Ranganatha**; 2: it includes **Yamunacharya Charitra** and **Maladasari Katha**.
4: it gives practical advice on **statecraft, kingship and administration**.
3 is wrong: PYQ (APPSC G2 **2003**) — it does **not** describe Krishnadevaraya's **invasions**.
xa: It also gives the **genealogy from Bukka to Krishnadevaraya**.
It records social, religious and economic life of the period.

120.s: The phrase “Desa Bhashalandu Telugu Lessa” occurs in which work?
120.x: The famous expression praising Telugu among regional languages occurs in the preface to Amuktamalyada.
120.tq: Match a famous quotation with its exact literary source.
xs: **"Desa Bhashalandu Telugu Lessa"** is in the preface of **Amuktamalyada** — option **(1)**.
It means **"Telugu is the best of the regional languages"**.
**Jambavati Kalyanam** and **Madalasa Charita** are Krishnadevaraya's **Sanskrit** works; **Madhura Vijayam** is Gangadevi's.
xa: Amuktamalyada is **Telugu**, one of the **Telugu Pancha Kavyas**.
⚠ Only **Amuktamalyada** is Telugu among his works.

120.s:
Consider the following statements about Amuktamalyada:
1. It is one of the Telugu Pancha Kavyas.
2. It is the first Telugu work named after its author.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
120.x: Statement 1 is correct: it is one of the Telugu Pancha Kavyas. Statement 2 is wrong: it is the first Telugu work named after its heroine (Goda Devi), not its author. Hence 1 only.
120.tq: Remember 'heroine' - Amuktamalyada = the one who offers the garland she wore (Goda).
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: it is one of the **Telugu Pancha Kavyas**.
Statement 2 is wrong: it is the first Telugu work named after its **heroine** (**Goda Devi**), not its author.
xa: Its title means **"one who offers the garland she has worn"**.
Also called **Vishnuchittiyam**; dedicated to **Lord Venkateswara**.

120.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
120.x: Usha Parinayam is among the Sanskrit works attributed to Krishnadevaraya. Amuktamalyada is Telugu, while Jambavati Kalyanam and Rasamanjari are Sanskrit.
120.tq: Use language-based elimination among closely related literary works.
xs: **Usha Parinayam — Sanskrit** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Amuktamalyada** is **Telugu**; **Jambavati Kalyanam** and **Rasamanjari** are **Sanskrit**.
xa: **Jambavati Kalyanam** is a Sanskrit **drama** (APPSC G2 **2019**) mentioning **Virupaksha** and the **Vasantotsavams**.
Other Sanskrit works: **Madalasa Charita**, **Jnana Chintamani**, **Satyavadhu Parinayam**.
⚠ Only **Amuktamalyada** is Telugu.

120.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Madalasa Charita — Sanskrit
2. Rasamanjari — Sanskrit
3. Jnana Chintamani — Sanskrit
4. Satyavadhu Parinayam — Telugu
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
120.x: Madalasa Charita, Rasamanjari and Jnana Chintamani are Sanskrit works of Krishnadevaraya, so pairs 1-3 are correct. Pair 4 is wrong: Satyavadhu Parinayam is also a Sanskrit work, not Telugu; his only Telugu work is Amuktamalyada. So 1, 2 and 3 only.
120.tq: Spot the language reversal in a list of literary works.
xs: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(1) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
**Madalasa Charita**, **Rasamanjari** and **Jnana Chintamani** are **Sanskrit**.
Pair 4 is wrong: **Satyavadhu Parinayam** is also **Sanskrit**; his only Telugu work is **Amuktamalyada**.
xa: **Jambavati Kalyanam** is a Sanskrit drama (PYQ **2019**).
Court poets (**Ashtadiggajas**) wrote in **Telugu**.
**Sakala Katha Sara Sangrahamu** is also listed as Sanskrit.

120.s: Krishnadevaraya's drama Jambavati Kalyanam, which mentions Virupaksha and the Vasantotsavams, was written in:
120.x: Jambavati Kalyanam is a Sanskrit drama (APPSC G2 2019). Telugu is wrong - his Telugu work is Amuktamalyada. Kannada and Tamil are wrong - none of his listed works are in these languages.
120.tq: Only Amuktamalyada is Telugu; the rest of KDR's works are Sanskrit.
xs: **Jambavati Kalyanam** is a drama in **Sanskrit** — option **(2)** (APPSC G2 **2019**).
**Telugu** is wrong: Krishnadevaraya's only Telugu work is **Amuktamalyada**.
