Statement 3: in **1557-63** he backed **Bijapur** and **razed Ahmadnagar**.
This was his policy of **playing the Sultans against each other**.
xa: This **divide-and-rule** diplomacy is listed as a cause that **united the Sultans** against him.
Rama Raya had earlier served under **Golconda** and the **Bahmanis**.
He also sheltered **Jagadeva Rao**, a rebel from Golconda.

126.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Vijayanagara side in the Battle of Talikota:
1. Sadasiva Raya was the Tuluva king.
2. Aliya Rama Raya acted as his regent.
3. Tirumala and Venkatadri fought alongside Rama Raya.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
126.x: Sadasiva Raya was the nominal Tuluva king, while Rama Raya was his regent; Rama Raya's brothers Tirumala and Venkatadri fought with him.
126.tq: Combine the nominal ruler, regent and military associates in one statement set.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
Statements 1 and 2: **Sadasiva Raya** was the Tuluva king; **Aliya Rama Raya** was his regent and the de-facto ruler.
Statement 3: Rama Raya's brothers **Tirumala and Venkatadri** fought alongside him.
xa: Rama Raya was **captured and killed**; **Venkatadri** was also killed.
**Sadashiva and Tirumala** fled to **Penukonda**.
Last Tuluva ruler = **Sadasiva**; first Aravidu = **Tirumala**.

126.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Sultanate)
A. Bijapur
B. Ahmadnagar
C. Golconda
D. Bidar

List-II (Ruler)
1. Ali Barid Shah
2. Ibrahim Qutb Shah
3. Ali Adil Shah
4. Hussain Nizam Shah

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
126.x: Bijapur was ruled by Ali Adil Shah, Ahmadnagar by Hussain Nizam Shah, Golconda by Ibrahim Qutb Shah and Bidar by Ali Barid Shah.
126.tq: Start from the sure ruler–Sultanate pairs and eliminate the codes.
xs: **A-3, B-4, C-2, D-1** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Bijapur — Ali Adil Shah**; **Ahmadnagar — Hussain Nizam Shah**.
**Golconda — Ibrahim Qutb Shah**; **Bidar — Ali Barid Shah**.
xa: **Ibrahim Qutb Shah** was the key organiser of the alliance.
**Hussain Nizam Shah** beheaded Rama Raya.
**Berar** (Imad Shahi) stayed out.

126.s:
Consider the following statements about the Battle of Talikota (1565):
1. Aliya Rama Raya was beheaded by Ali Adil Shah of Bijapur.
2. Ibrahim Qutb Shah of Golconda was a key organiser of the Sultanates' alliance.
3. H.K. Sherwani called the battle 'Bannihatti'.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
126.x: Statement 2 is correct: Ibrahim Qutb Shah was the key organiser (CDX says he led the coalition). Statement 1 is wrong: Rama Raya was beheaded by Hussain Nizam Shah of Ahmadnagar, not Ali Adil Shah. Statement 3 is correct: Sherwani used the name Bannihatti (Sewell: Talikota; Heras and Nilakanta Sastri: Rakshasi-Tangadi). Hence 2 and 3 only.
126.tq: Organiser = Ibrahim Qutb Shah; executioner = Hussain Nizam Shah; Bannihatti = Sherwani.
xs: Statements **2 and 3 only** are correct — option **(3)**.
Statement 1 is wrong: **Rama Raya** was beheaded by **Hussain Nizam Shah** of **Ahmadnagar**, not Ali Adil Shah.
Statement 2 is correct: **Ibrahim Qutb Shah** of Golconda was the **key organiser** of the alliance.
Statement 3 is correct: **H.K. Sherwani** called it **Bannihatti**.
xa: **Robert Sewell** called it **Talikota**; **Fr. Heras** and **Nilakanta Sastri** called it **Rakshasi-Tangadi**.
Date: **23 January 1565**; some notes give **26 January**.
**Ali Adil Shah** ruled **Bijapur**; **Ali Barid Shah** ruled **Bidar**.
⚠ **Berar** (Imad Shahi) stayed out of the battle.

126.s: Which one of the following Deccan Sultanates did NOT participate in the alliance against Vijayanagara at Talikota?
126.x: Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda and Bidar formed the alliance; Berar, ruled by the Imad Shahi dynasty, stayed out.
126.tq: Find the excluded member by separating the four participating Sultanates from Berar.
xs: **Berar** (Imad Shahi) did not take part — so option **(1)** is the answer.
The alliance: **Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda and Bidar**.
⚠ Some notes add Berar's **Burhan Imad-ul-Mulk** to the "Pancha Padushas"; others (incl. **Sherwani**) exclude Berar.
xa: **Ibrahim Qutb Shah** of Golconda organised the alliance.
Vijayanagara faced the **Deccan Sultanates**, not the Bahmani kingdom (G1 **2018**).

126.s: In the Battle of Talikota (1565), the Vijayanagara Empire fought against
o: A confederacy of the Deccan Sultanates
126.x: Vijayanagara under Aliya Rama Raya fought the confederacy of the Deccan Sultanates (Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda, Bidar). The Bahmani kingdom had already broken up into these Sultanates, so 'Bahmani' is a common trap. The Mughals and the Gajapatis were not parties to the battle.
126.tq: 1565 = Deccan Sultanates, not Bahmanis
xs: At Talikota, Vijayanagara fought **a confederacy of the Deccan Sultanates** — so option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ Trap: it was **NOT the Bahmani kingdom** (G1 **2018**; UPPSC **2014**).
Members: **Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda, Bidar**.
xa: Vijayanagara's de-facto ruler was **Aliya Rama Raya**, regent of **Sadasiva Raya**.
Date: **23 January 1565**.
After victory, the Sultanates **went back to fighting each other**.

126.s: Which one of the following was NOT a principal cause contributing to the formation of the Deccan coalition against Vijayanagara?
o: Rama Raya's policy of playing the Sultans against one another
Rama Raya's interference in the affairs of the Sultanates
Rama Raya's sheltering of Jagadeva Rao, a rebel from Golconda
The permanent military union created by the Bahmani emperor
126.x: The coalition is attributed to Rama Raya's diplomacy, interference, earlier attacks and sheltering of Jagadeva Rao; no Bahmani emperor created the coalition.
126.tq: Find the historically unrelated cause among closely connected political factors.
xs: No **Bahmani emperor** created a military union — so option **(4)** is the answer.
Real causes: Rama Raya's **divide-and-rule** diplomacy, **interference** in the Sultanates' affairs and sheltering **Jagadeva Rao**.
⚠ The enemy was the **Deccan Sultanates**, not the Bahmani kingdom.
xa: Marriage links: **Bibi Jamal** married Ibrahim; **Chand Bibi** married Ali Adil.
**Ferishta** also alleges religious insults.
Rama Raya **sacked Ahmadnagar** in **1557-63**.

126.s:
Consider the following statements about the causes of the Battle of Talikota:
1. Rama Raya sacked Ahmadnagar during 1557-63.
2. Bibi Jamal married Ali Adil, while Chand Bibi married Ibrahim.
3. Ferishta also alleges religious insults as a cause.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
126.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 reverses the marriages: Bibi Jamal married Ibrahim and Chand Bibi married Ali Adil. So A; B, C and D include the false statement 2.
126.tq: Marriage links: Bibi Jamal-Ibrahim, Chand Bibi-Ali Adil; watch for swaps.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: Rama Raya sacked **Ahmadnagar** in **1557-63**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Bibi Jamal** married **Ibrahim**, and **Chand Bibi** married **Ali Adil**.
Statement 3 is correct: **Ferishta** also alleges **religious insults**.
xa: Rama Raya sheltered **Jagadeva Rao**, a rebel from Golconda.
In **1546-47** he took the **Raichur doab**.

126.s: Which sequence best represents the principal course of the Battle of Talikota?
o: Surprise attack, Vijayanagara success, peace talks, capture of Rama Raya
Vijayanagara successes, deceptive peace talks, surprise attack, withdrawal of Muslim contingents
Peace treaty, Vijayanagara retreat, Sultanate division, capture of Rama Raya
Withdrawal of Muslim contingents, Vijayanagara successes, peace talks, Sultanate attack
126.x: The battle initially saw Vijayanagara successes, followed by deceptive peace talks, a surprise attack and the withdrawal of Muslim contingents from the Vijayanagara army.
126.tq: Arrange the stages of the battle by identifying the first and final developments.
xs: **Vijayanagara successes → deceptive peace talks → surprise attack → withdrawal of Muslim contingents** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The Muslim contingents in Vijayanagara's army **withdrew/deserted**.
**Rama Raya** was then **captured and killed**; **Venkatadri** too.
xa: **Hussain Nizam Shah** beheaded Rama Raya.
Hampi was looted for about **six months**.
Sadashiva and Tirumala fled to **Penukonda**.

126.s:
Consider the following statements about the consequences of the Battle of Talikota:
1. Hampi was looted for about six months.
2. The damage to the capital was severe but not total.
3. The Nayakas became autonomous and later developed into zamindars and poligars.
4. The Deccan Sultanates permanently stopped fighting one another after their victory.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
126.x: Hampi was looted for about six months, the destruction was severe but not total, and the Nayakas became autonomous. The Sultanates resumed fighting among themselves after the victory.
126.tq: Reject the extreme claim that a temporary alliance became permanent.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statements 1 and 2: **Hampi** was looted for about **six months**; damage was **severe but not total**.
Statement 3: the **Nayakas** became autonomous → later **zamindars and poligars**.
Statement 4 is wrong: the Sultanates **went back to fighting each other**.
xa: Sewell's **"graveyard"** account may exaggerate.
Golconda gained **Kondavidu and Machilipatnam** + coastal tracts.
Sadashiva and Tirumala fled to **Penukonda**.

126.s:
Consider the following statements about the results of the Battle of Talikota:
1. Golconda gained Kondavidu and Machilipatnam along with coastal tracts.
2. Sadasiva and Tirumala fled to Chandragiri after the defeat.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
126.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Sadasiva and Tirumala fled to Penukonda (Chandragiri became a capital later, under Venkata II). So 1 only (A); B, C and D misjudge the statements.
126.tq: First refuge after 1565 = Penukonda.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Golconda** gained **Kondavidu and Machilipatnam** with coastal tracts.
Statement 2 is wrong: Sadasiva and Tirumala fled to **Penukonda**; **Chandragiri** became capital later, under **Venkata II**.
xa: Capital order: **Penukonda (1570) → Chandragiri → Vellore (1600)**.
After **1565**, the empire's centre moved into AP.
**Sriranga Raya I** later lost **Kondaveedu** to Ibrahim Qutb Shah.

126.s: The Aravidu dynasty of Vijayanagara derived its name from which place?
126.x: The dynasty was named after Araviti, also called Aravidu, a village in Kurnool district.
126.tq: Use the place-name clue to distinguish the dynasty from similarly named ruling houses.
xs: The Aravidu dynasty is named after **Araviti (Aravidu) village, Kurnool district** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Penukonda** was its first capital (**1570**), not its namesake.
**Gandikota** is where **Mir Jumla** melted temple idols into cannon (**1657**).
xa: Aravidus ruled **1570-1680**, with **7** rulers.
Founder: **Tirumala Raya**, crowned at **Penukonda** at about age **90**.
Last ruler: **Sriranga III**, died **1680**.

126.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Aravidu dynasty:
1. It ruled the Vijayanagara Empire from 1570 to 1680.
2. It had seven rulers.
3. It was the first dynasty to rule Vijayanagara.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
126.x: The Aravidu dynasty ruled from 1570 to 1680 and had seven rulers. Statement 3 is false because it was the fourth ruling dynasty of Vijayanagara.
126.tq: Split the statements and reject the extreme historical claim about being the first dynasty.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: the Aravidus ruled **1570-1680**.
Statement 2 is correct: there were **7** rulers.
Statement 3 is wrong: they came after the **Tuluvas** (last Tuluva = **Sadasiva**), so they were not the first dynasty.
xa: Some notes date the empire's end to **1646**.
Founder **Tirumala** shifted the capital to **Penukonda** in **1570**.
Greatest ruler: **Venkatapati Raya II** (**1585-1614**).

126.s: Who founded the Aravidu dynasty and was crowned at Penukonda in 1570?
126.x: Tirumala Raya founded the Aravidu dynasty and was crowned at Penukonda in 1570.
126.tq: Match the founder with his accession place and year.
xs: **Tirumala Raya** founded the Aravidu dynasty and was crowned at **Penukonda** in **1570** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Sriranga Raya I** (**1572-85**) succeeded him; **Venkatapati Raya II** (**1585-1614**) was the greatest.
**Ramadeva** (**1616-30**) fought the **Battle of Toppur**.
xa: Tirumala was crowned at the age of **90**.
He wrote a commentary on the **Gita Govinda**; **Vasucharitra** was dedicated to him.
⚠ **Tirumala Raya** = Aravidu founder; **Tirumala Nayaka** = Madurai.

126.s: The Vilapakam inscription of 1601 is important primarily because it provides information about the genealogy of which dynasties?
126.x: The Vilapakam inscription of 1601 gives the genealogy of the Tuluva and Aravidu dynasties.
126.tq: Identify the inscription through its specific genealogical content.
xs: The **Vilapaka(m) inscription (1601)** gives the genealogy of the **Tuluva and Aravidu** dynasties — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is an inscription of **Venkatapati Raya II**.
xa: ⚠ Vilapaka = Venkatapati II's (**1601**); **Siddhavatam** fort inscription = Venkatapati II's (**1605**).
The Siddhavatam inscription says **Matli Ananta** built the fort walls.
His Penukonda inscription records villages given to the saint **Babanathu**.

126.s:
Consider the following statements about the Battle of Toppur:
1. It was fought in 1616 and is called the 'second Talikota'.
2. Mir Jumla was killed in this battle.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
126.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Jagga Raya was killed at Toppur; Mir Jumla later defeated Sriranga III at Vandavasi (1642). So 1 only (A).
126.tq: Toppur 1616: Jagga Raya killed.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Toppur (1616)** is called the **"second Talikota"**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Jagga Raya** was killed at Toppur; **Mir Jumla** later defeated **Sriranga III** at **Vandavasi (1642)**.
xa: Toppur was won by **Velugoti Yachama Nayaka** and **Raghunatha of Tanjore**.
It was fought in **Ramadeva**'s reign (**1616-30**).
Jagga Raya had killed **Sriranga II** (**1614**).

126.s:
Consider the following statements about Sriranga Raya III:
1. He was the last ruler of the Aravidu dynasty.
2. He was defeated at Vandavasi (1642) by Ibrahim Qutb Shah.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
126.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: he was defeated at Vandavasi by Mir Jumla of Golconda. So 1 only (A).
126.tq: Vandavasi 1642 = Mir Jumla.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Sriranga Raya III** (**1643-80**) was the **last** Aravidu ruler.
Statement 2 is wrong: he was defeated at **Vandavasi (1642)** by **Mir Jumla** of Golconda, not Ibrahim Qutb Shah.
xa: He later held **Penukonda** as a chieftain; his death in **1680** ended the empire.
Mir Jumla also melted temple idols into cannon at **Gandikota** (**1657**).
**Ibrahim Qutb Shah** organised the Talikota alliance.

126.s:
Consider the following statements about Venkatapati Raya II:
1. He allowed Jesuit churches to be built at Nellore and Chandragiri.
2. He permitted the Dutch to trade at Pulicat.
3. He allied with Spain and Portugal.
4. He accepted Akbar's suzerainty.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
126.x: Venkatapati Raya II permitted Jesuit churches and Dutch trade, and allied with Spain and Portugal. He rejected, rather than accepted, Akbar's suzerainty.
126.tq: Use the reversed-meaning trap in the statement about accepting suzerainty.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3 only** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1: he allowed **Jesuit** churches at **Chandragiri and Nellore** (APPSC-G1 **2022** key).
Statements 2 and 3: he let the **Dutch** trade at **Pulicat** and had ties with the **Portuguese and Philip II of Spain**.
Statement 4 is wrong: he **rejected Akbar's** demand for submission.
xa: His coins bore **"Om Venkateshwaraya Namah"**.
He gave villages to the Muslim saint **Babanathu**.

126.s:
Which of the following statements about Venkatapati Raya II is correct?
1. He was called the Second Andhra Bhoja.
2. Appayya Dikshita was associated with his court.
3. His coins bore the inscription ‘Om Venkateshwaraya Namah’.
4. He defeated Veerappa Nayaka of Madurai at Vallankota.
126.x: All four are correct: Venkatapati Raya II was called the 'Second Andhra Bhoja' (and 'Second Krishnadevaraya'), Appayya Dikshita (Shaivarka Mani Dipika) was at his court, his coins bore 'Om Venkateshwaraya Namah', and he defeated Veerappa Nayaka of Madurai at Vallankota.
126.tq: Check each closely connected biographical detail before choosing the complete combination.
xs: All four statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
Statements 1 and 2: he was called **"Second Andhra Bhoja"**; **Appayya Dikshita** (**Shaivarka Mani Dipika**) was at his court.
Statement 3: his coins bore **"Om Venkateshwaraya Namah"**.
Statement 4: he defeated **Veerappa Nayaka** of Madurai at **Vallankota**.
xa: He is also called the **"Second Krishnadevaraya"**.

126.s:
Consider the following statements about the grant of Madras:
1. Damarla Venkatadri Nayaka granted it in 1639 to Francis Day of the English East India Company's Machilipatnam council.
2. It was made during the reign of Venkatapati Raya III.
3. The name Chennapatnam came from Chennappa, father of Damarla Venkatadri Nayaka.
4. Fort St David was built following the grant.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
126.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: the grant came in Venkatapati Raya III's reign, from the local Nayaka Damarla Venkatadri to Francis Day of the Machilipatnam council in 1639, and Madras/Chennapatnam was named after Damarla's father Chennappa. Statement 4 is wrong: the grant was followed by Fort St George (1641 in some notes), not Fort St David. Hence 1, 2 and 3 only.
126.tq: Madras 1639: Venkatapati III - Damarla Venkatadri - Francis Day - Fort St George.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: **Damarla Venkatadri Nayaka** granted it in **1639** to **Francis Day** of the EIC's **Machilipatnam** council.
Statement 2: it came in the reign of **Venkatapati Raya III**.
Statement 3: **Chennapatnam** is named after Damarla's father **Chennappa**.
Statement 4 is wrong: the grant was followed by **Fort St George** (**1641**, per some notes), not Fort St David.
xa: Damarla Venkatadri Nayaka was the **Kalahasti-Wandiwash** chief.
⚠ Some notes give the grant date as **1630**.
**Sriranga Raya III** (1643-80) was the **last** Aravidu ruler.

126.s: After the weakening of the Vijayanagara Empire, the amara-nayakas developed into which group?
o: Hereditary Palegars and the forerunners of zamindars
126.x: The amara-nayakas became hereditary Palegars, who were forerunners of the zamindars.
126.tq: Trace the institutional transformation after imperial decline.
xs: The amara-nayakas became hereditary **Palegars**, the **forerunners of the zamindars** — so option **(4)** is correct.
This followed the **Nayankara / Amaranayaka** system after **1565**.
xa: After Talikota, the **Nayakas** became autonomous → later **zamindars and poligars**.
Local Nayaka **Damarla Venkatadri Nayaka** granted **Madras** to the English.
**Velugoti Yachama Nayaka** won the Battle of **Toppur (1616)**.

126.s: Which pair of leaders won the Battle of Toppur in 1616?
o: Velugoti Yachama Nayaka and Raghunatha of Tanjore
Mir Jumla and Sriranga Raya III
Damarla Venkatadri Nayaka and Veerappa Nayaka
126.x: Velugoti Yachama Nayaka and Raghunatha of Tanjore won the Battle of Toppur in 1616.
126.tq: Start with the battle year and match the associated victorious commanders.
xs: **Velugoti Yachama Nayaka** and **Raghunatha of Tanjore** won **Toppur (1616)** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Jagga Raya** was killed there; it is called the **"second Talikota"**.
**Mir Jumla** defeated **Sriranga III** at **Vandavasi (1642)**, a different battle.
xa: Toppur came in **Ramadeva**'s reign (**1616-30**).
Jagga Raya had killed **Sriranga II** in **1614**.
**Tanjore** was founded by **Sevappa Nayaka**.

126.s: At Gandikota in 1657, who is recorded as having melted temple idols into cannon?
126.x: Mir Jumla of Golconda is recorded as having melted temple idols into cannon at Gandikota in 1657.
126.tq: Link the place and year with the named military commander.
xs: **Mir Jumla of Golconda** melted temple idols into cannon at **Gandikota** in **1657** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Jagga Raya** was killed at **Toppur**; **Damarla Venkatadri Nayaka** granted **Madras**; **Raghunatha of Tanjore** won Toppur.
xa: Mir Jumla defeated **Sriranga III** at **Vandavasi (1642)**.
Sriranga III died in **1680**, ending the empire.
Gandikota was a Vijayanagara fort.

126.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Nayaka kingdom)
A. Madurai
B. Tanjore
C. Gingee
D. Mysore

List-II (Founder)
1. Raja Wodeyar

**Gingee — Krishnappa Nayaka**; **Mysore — Raja Wodeyar**.

126.s:
Consider the following statements about the Madurai Nayakas:
1. Vishwanatha Nayaka was granted Madurai after capturing his rebel father Nagama.
2. Tirumala Nayaka made Madurai independent around 1565.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
126.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Vishwanatha's son Krishnappa Nayaka made Madurai independent c. 1565; Tirumala Nayaka ruled 1623-59. So 1 only (A).
126.tq: Vishwanatha founded, Krishnappa made independent, Tirumala built the Mahal.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Vishwanatha Nayaka** got Madurai after capturing his rebel father **Nagama**.
Statement 2 is wrong: his son **Krishnappa** made Madurai independent c. **1565**; **Tirumala Nayaka** ruled **1623-59**.

126.s:

2. Tirumala Nayaka built the Tirumala Rayala Mahal.
3. Madurai fell to Chanda Sahib in 1757.

126.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Madurai fell to Chanda Sahib in 1739. So A; B, C and D include the false statement 3.
126.tq: Madurai's fall to Chanda Sahib = 1739.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Tirumala Nayaka** ruled Madurai **1623-59** and allied with **Golconda** against Vijayanagara.
Statement 2 is correct: he built the **Tirumala Rayala Mahal**.
Statement 3 is wrong: Madurai fell to **Chanda Sahib** in **1739**, not 1757.
xa: ⚠ **Tirumala Raya** = Aravidu founder (Penukonda); **Tirumala Nayaka** = Madurai.
**Krishnappa** made Madurai independent c. **1565**.

126.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
126.x: Chowdappa Nayaka is identified as the founder or key ruler of Ikkeri (Keladi), founded around 1500.

xs: **Ikkeri (Keladi) — Chowdappa Nayaka** is correctly matched — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Raja Wodeyar** belongs to **Mysore**.
**Gingee** is linked to **Krishnappa Nayaka**; **Tanjore** to **Sevappa Nayaka**.

Raja Wodeyar took **Srirangapatna** in **1610**.

126.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Classical Telugu literature reached its zenith under Krishnadevaraya.
2. Shaivarka Mani Dipika was written by Appayya Dikshita.
3. Vasucharitra was associated with Ramaraja Bhushanudu.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
126.x: All three statements are correct. Krishnadevaraya’s reign marked the zenith of classical Telugu, while Appayya Dikshita and Ramaraja Bhushanudu are linked with the two named works.
126.tq: Verify each author–work and period association before selecting the combined option.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
Statement 1: classical Telugu reached its **zenith under Krishnadevaraya**.
Statement 2: **Shaivarka Mani Dipika** was written by **Appayya Dikshita** (Aravidu era).
Statement 3: **Vasucharitra** was written by **Ramaraja Bhushanudu** (Aravidu era).
xa: Appayya Dikshita was at **Venkatapati Raya II**'s court.
**Vasucharitra** was dedicated to **Tirumala Raya**, the Aravidu founder.
**A Forgotten Empire** (**1900**) by **Robert Sewell** brought Vijayanagara to wide notice.

126.s: Who surveyed and mapped the ruins of Hampi in 1800?
126.x: Colin Mackenzie surveyed and mapped the Hampi ruins in 1800 and later became the first Surveyor General of India.
126.tq: Associate the survey date with the correct investigator.
xs: **Colin Mackenzie** surveyed and mapped the Hampi ruins in **1800** — so option **(3)** is correct.
He later became the first **Surveyor General of India**.
**Robert Sewell** wrote **A Forgotten Empire** (**1900**); **Caesar Frederick** visited in **1567**; **Mir Jumla** was a Golconda general.
xa: Caesar Frederick was a **Venetian merchant** who saw the ruined capital.
Sewell's **"graveyard"** account of the sack may exaggerate.

126.s: Which European visitor left an eyewitness account of the ruined Vijayanagara capital in 1567?
126.x: Caesar Frederick, a Venetian merchant, visited Vijayanagara in 1567 and left an eyewitness account of the ruined capital.
126.tq: Use the visitor–description–year association to separate similar foreign accounts.
xs: **Caesar Frederick**, a **Venetian merchant**, visited in **1567** and left an eyewitness account of the ruined capital — so option **(2)** is correct.
The visit came two years after **Talikota** (**1565**).
xa: **Colin Mackenzie** mapped Hampi's ruins in **1800**.
**Robert Sewell**'s **A Forgotten Empire** came out in **1900**.
Hampi was looted for about **six months** after Talikota.

126.s:
With reference to the post-Talikota phase of Vijayanagara history, consider the following statements:
1. The empire’s centre of gravity shifted towards the Telugu country.
2. Penukonda and Chandragiri became important centres in this phase.
3. The Aravidu rulers originated from Kurnool.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
126.x: All three statements are correct. After Talikota, the political centre shifted towards the Telugu country, particularly Penukonda and Chandragiri, while the Aravidus were associated with Kurnool.
126.tq: Test a regional shift through multiple connected consequences rather than a single place-name.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
Statements 1 and 2: after Talikota, the centre of gravity shifted to the **Telugu country** — **Penukonda, Chandragiri**.
Statement 3: the **Aravidus** came from **Kurnool** (Araviti village).
xa: The **Madras** grant came from a **Chandragiri-era Nayaka**.
Capital order: **Penukonda (1570) → Chandragiri → Vellore (1600)**.
After **1565**, the empire's centre moved into AP.

126.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Caesar Frederick — Founder of the Aravidu dynasty
126.x: Caesar Frederick was a Venetian merchant who recorded an eyewitness account in 1567; Tirumala, not Caesar Frederick, founded the Aravidu line.
126.tq: Find the wrong person–achievement pairing by checking founders against visitors.
xs: **Caesar Frederick — Founder of the Aravidu dynasty** is wrongly matched — so option **(3)** is the answer.
Caesar Frederick was a **Venetian merchant** who saw the ruined capital in **1567**.
The other pairs are correct: **Tirumala** = first Aravidu, **Sriranga III** = last Aravidu, **Sadasiva** = last Tuluva.
xa: Tirumala founded the line in **1570** and moved the capital to **Penukonda**.
Sriranga III died in **1680**, ending the empire.

126.s: Which of the following statements regarding interpretations of the aftermath of Talikota is correct?
o: The sack is universally accepted as having caused the complete disappearance of Vijayanagara culture.
Sewell denied that the Vijayanagara capital suffered any destruction.
Sewell described the sack as a “graveyard”, but this description may be exaggerated.
The description of the sack was written by Tirumala in 1570.
126.x: Sewell used the expression “graveyard” for the sack, although that assessment may be exaggerated. The other statements do not reflect the stated historical interpretation.
126.tq: Distinguish a historian’s vivid interpretation from an absolute claim about historical consequences.
xs: **Sewell** called the sack a **"graveyard"**, but this **may be exaggerated** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Hampi was looted for about **six months**: damage was **severe but not total**.
So the sack neither ended Vijayanagara culture completely, nor did Sewell deny destruction.
xa: Sewell wrote **A Forgotten Empire** (**1900**).
**Caesar Frederick** gave an eyewitness account in **1567**.
Nayaka courts later spread **Raya gopurams** and **kalyana mandapas** across Andhra.

127.s: Babur’s descent was traced to which of the following combinations?
o: Timur on his father’s side and Chingiz Khan on his mother’s side
Chingiz Khan on his father’s side and Timur on his mother’s side
Sher Shah on his father’s side and Timur on his mother’s side
Ibrahim Lodi on his father’s side and Chingiz Khan on his mother’s side
127.x: Babur was descended from Timur through his father and from Chingiz Khan through his mother.
127.tq: Check the direction of descent carefully; the two ancestors are deliberately placed in opposite sides.
xs: Babur descended from **Timur on his father's side** and **Chingiz Khan on his mother's side** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Option (2) reverses the two lines.
xa: Born **1483**, **Farghana**.
His coins were silver **Shahrukhi** in **Timurid** style.
He wrote the **Tuzuk-i-Baburi** in **Chagatai Turki**.

127.s:
Consider the following statements about those who invited Babur to India:
1. Daulat Khan Lodi, Governor of Punjab, invited him.
2. Alam Khan, Ibrahim Lodi's uncle, invited him.
3. Bahadur Shah of Gujarat invited him.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
127.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the third inviter was Rana Sanga of Mewar, not Bahadur Shah. So A; B, C and D include the false statement 3.
127.tq: Inviters: Daulat Khan Lodi, Alam Khan, Rana Sanga.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Daulat Khan Lodi**, Governor of **Punjab**, invited him.
Statement 2 is correct: **Alam Khan**, Ibrahim's uncle, invited him.
Statement 3 is wrong: the third inviter was **Rana Sanga** of **Mewar**; **Bahadur Shah** united **Gujarat-Malwa**.
xa: Rana Sanga later fought Babur at **Khanwa (1527)**.
Babur's first raid: **1519**.

127.s:
Consider the following statements about Babur's military methods:
1. Tulughma, of Uzbek origin, had flanking units wheel round to encircle the enemy.
2. The Rumi method used war elephants chained together as a barrier.
3. Babur's artillery was commanded by the Ottoman gunners Ustad Ali and Mustafa.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
127.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Rumi method (araba) chained carts as a barrier for matchlockmen and guns; the elephant version is a known error. So A; B, C and D include the false statement 2.
127.tq: Tulughma = Uzbek; Rumi = Ottoman carts, never elephants.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Tulughma**, of **Uzbek** origin, had flanking units wheel round to encircle the enemy.
Statement 2 is wrong: the **Rumi method (araba)** chained **carts** as a barrier for matchlockmen and guns; ⚠ the elephant version is a known error.
Statement 3 is correct: Ottoman gunners **Ustad Ali** and **Mustafa** commanded his artillery.
xa: The Rumi method is an **Ottoman** field-defence system.
Panipat = first large-scale use of **field artillery** in North Indian warfare.

127.s: Which statement regarding Babur’s use of artillery at Panipat is correct?
o: It was commanded by Ibrahim Lodi’s Ottoman officers.
It was used exclusively against cavalry and not infantry.
It marked the first large-scale use of field artillery in North Indian warfare.
It was the first use of any firearm ever known in India.
127.x: Panipat marked the first large-scale use of field artillery in North Indian warfare. Firearms were not wholly unknown in India before Babur.
127.tq: Avoid the extreme claim that a first large-scale use means the first knowledge of firearms.
xs: Panipat was the **first large-scale use of field artillery in North Indian warfare** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Firearms were **not wholly unknown** in India before Babur — so option (4) is wrong.
The guns were Babur's, under Ottoman gunners **Ustad Ali** and **Mustafa**, not Ibrahim Lodi's.
xa: The **Rumi method / araba**: carts chained as a barrier for matchlockmen and guns.
Artillery was decisive again at **Khanwa** (**1527**).

127.s:
Consider the following statements about Babur after Panipat:
1. The victory gave Babur Delhi and Agra along with the treasure of the Lodis.
2. His lavish sharing of the treasure earned him the nickname 'Ghazi'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
127.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: lavish distribution earned him the nickname 'Qalandar'; 'Ghazi' was the title he took after Khanwa. So 1 only (A).
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: Panipat gave Babur **Delhi and Agra** + the **treasure of the Lodis** (APPSC-GS **2023**).
Statement 2 is wrong: lavish sharing earned him **"Qalandar"**; **"Ghazi"** was his title after **Khanwa**.
xa: The lavish sharing left the treasury **depleted for Humayun**.
The **Kabuli Bagh mosque** at Panipat commemorates the **1526** victory.

127.s: At the Battle of Khanwa, the Rajput confederacy led by Rana Sanga was joined by
o: Daulat Khan Lodi and Medini Rai
Mahmud Lodi and Hasan Khan Mewati
127.x: Rana Sanga’s coalition included the Afghan Mahmud Lodi and Hasan Khan Mewati.
127.tq: Identify the members of the coalition rather than confusing them with Babur’s earlier opponents.
xs: Rana Sanga's Rajput confederacy was joined by **Mahmud Lodi** and **Hasan Khan Mewati** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Daulat Khan Lodi** had invited Babur; **Ibrahim Lodi** was already defeated at Panipat (**1526**).
xa: Babur used **trenches and barricades** against Sanga's **elephants**.
Before Khanwa he declared a **jihad**, renounced wine and remitted the **tamgha**.
Khanwa **broke Rajput power**; Babur took the title **"Ghazi"**.

127.s:
Consider the following statements about the Battle of Khanwa:
1. Before the battle Babur declared a jihad and renounced wine.
2. He remitted the tamgha for Muslims.
3. After the victory he took the title 'Padshah'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
127.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: after Khanwa Babur took the title 'Ghazi'. So A; B, C and D include the false statement 3.
127.tq: Khanwa: jihad, wine renounced, tamgha remitted, title Ghazi.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: before Khanwa, Babur declared a **jihad** and **renounced wine**.
Statement 2 is correct: he remitted the **tamgha** for Muslims.
Statement 3 is wrong: after victory he took the title **"Ghazi"**.
xa: ⚠ **"Qalandar"** = for sharing the Lodi treasure; **"Ghazi"** = after Khanwa.
Rana Sanga was wounded and retreated.

127.s: Babur used trenches and barricades at Khanwa primarily to counter
127.x: Babur used trenches and barricades against the elephants of Rana Sanga. His artillery also played a decisive role in the battle.
127.tq: Infer the defensive measure from the battlefield threat it was designed to neutralise.
xs: Babur's **trenches and barricades** at Khanwa countered **Rana Sanga's elephants** — so option **(2)** is correct.
His **artillery** was decisive again; Sanga was **wounded** and retreated.
xa: Sanga's allies: **Mahmud Lodi** and **Hasan Khan Mewati**.
Khanwa (**1527**) broke **Rajput power**.
Babur then took the title **"Ghazi"**.

127.s: Which of the following best describes the extent of Babur’s dominions at the time of his death?
o: From Kabul and Badakhshan through Punjab, Delhi and Agra to the borders of Bihar
Only Kabul, Punjab and Delhi, without Agra
From Gujarat and Malwa to Bengal and the Deccan
From Afghanistan to the entire Indian subcontinent
127.x: At his death, Babur’s dominions extended from Kabul and Badakhshan through Punjab, Delhi and Agra to the borders of Bihar.
127.tq: Reject both the exaggerated all-India claim and the underestimation of the actual extent.
xs: At his death, Babur's empire ran from **Kabul and Badakhshan** through **Punjab, Delhi and Agra** to the **borders of Bihar** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Bengal** stayed unconquered and **Gujarat-Malwa** was under **Bahadur Shah**, so options (3) and (4) are wrong.
xa: The Bihar border was reached after **Ghaghra**.
He died in **1530** at Agra; **Humayun** took the throne on **29 Dec 1530**.
Mughal authority had **shallow roots**.

127.s: Which one of the following was NOT a limitation of Babur’s rule in India?
o: The Afghans continued to claim Delhi
Gujarat and Malwa were united under Bahadur Shah
A fully developed administrative system was established
127.x: D is the answer because Babur set up no administrative system at all (his rule had shallow roots and the treasury was empty), so 'a fully developed administrative system' was not one of his limitations. A, B and C are listed limits: the Afghans still claimed Delhi, Bengal stayed unconquered, and Gujarat-Malwa was united under Bahadur Shah.
127.tq: Find the option that reverses a stated weakness of Babur’s administration.
xs: **A fully developed administrative system** was not something Babur had — so option **(4)** is the answer.
He left **no administrative system** and an **empty treasury**.
The others are real limits: **Afghans** still claimed Delhi, **Bengal** unconquered, **Gujarat-Malwa** under **Bahadur Shah**.
xa: Mughal authority had **shallow roots** in his **4-year** rule.
⚠ The **Mansabdari system** is **Akbar's**, not Babur's.

127.s:
Consider the following statements about the foundations of Mughal rule under Babur:
1. Babur’s victory at Panipat I displaced the Lodis.
2. The victory at Khanwa weakened Rajput power.
3. Babur introduced the Mansabdari system during his four-year rule.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
127.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Mansabdari system was introduced under Akbar, not Babur.
127.tq: Use the ruler–institution trap to identify the statement assigning Akbar’s system to Babur.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Panipat I (1526)** displaced the **Lodis**.
Statement 2 is correct: **Khanwa** broke **Rajput power**.
Statement 3 is wrong: ⚠ the **Mansabdari system** is **Akbar's**.
xa: Babur left no administrative system; the treasury was empty.
Panipat ended the **Delhi Sultanate**.

127.s: Tuzuk-i-Baburi, also known as Baburnama, was written in
127.x: Baburnama was written in Chagatai Turki. Persian, rather than Turki, was the language of the Mughal court.
127.tq: Distinguish the language of the autobiography from the language of the Mughal court.
xs: The **Tuzuk-i-Baburi (Baburnama)** was written in **Chagatai Turki** — so option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ The Mughal **court language** was **Persian**, not Turki (UPPSC **2025**: A true, R false).
xa: English translators: **Leyden and Erskine** (**1826**); **Annette Beveridge**.
It counts **five Muslim and two Hindu powers** in India.
It praises **Krishnadevaraya** as the most powerful ruler.

127.s:
Consider the following statements about Babur's account of India:
1. He counted five Muslim and two Hindu powers, the Hindu ones being Vijayanagara and Mewar.
2. He praised Rana Sanga as the most powerful ruler in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
127.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Babur praised Krishnadevaraya as the most powerful ruler. So 1 only (A).
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: Babur counted **five Muslim and two Hindu powers** — **Vijayanagara and Mewar**.
Statement 2 is wrong: he praised **Krishnadevaraya**, not Rana Sanga, as the most powerful.
xa: Babur was a contemporary of **Krishnadevaraya** and Golconda's **Sultan Quli**.
The Baburnama is in **Chagatai Turki**; translated by **Leyden and Erskine** (**1826**).

127.s: The first Mughal garden is generally identified as
o: Ram Bagh or Aram Bagh at Agra
127.x: Ram Bagh, also called Aram Bagh, at Agra was the first Mughal garden. It reflected the charbagh, or four-quartered, design.
127.tq: Match the garden with its location and historical distinction.
xs: **Ram Bagh (Aram Bagh)** at **Agra** was the first Mughal garden — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Bagh-e-Babur** at Kabul is Babur's **burial place**.
xa: Babur also built the **Kabuli Bagh mosque** at **Panipat**, for the **1526** victory.
He built a mosque at **Agra** too.
His coins: silver **Shahrukhi**, Timurid style.

127.s: Which of the following statements about Babur’s architectural and monetary contributions is correct?
o: He introduced the Mansabdari system and issued gold dinars in the Ottoman style.
He built only forts and issued copper coins in the Rajput style.
He introduced the charbagh and issued silver Shahrukhi coins in the Timurid style.
He introduced Persian as the language of Baburnama and issued silver rupees in the Safavid style.
127.x: Babur introduced the charbagh garden and issued silver Shahrukhi coins in the Timurid style.
127.tq: Select the option that combines two independently correct contributions without importing later institutions.
xs: Babur's garden and silver **Shahrukhi** coins in **Timurid** style — option **(3)** — is correct.
His garden **Ram Bagh (Aram Bagh)** at **Agra** was the **first Mughal garden**.
⚠ The **Mansabdari system** is **Akbar's**; the Baburnama is in **Chagatai Turki**, not Persian.
xa: He built the **Kabuli Bagh mosque** at Panipat and a mosque at **Agra**.
His paternal descent was from **Timur**.

127.s: Which of the following statements about Babur’s relations with the Deccan is correct?
o: Babur made Golconda his provincial capital.
Babur defeated Sultan Quli of Golconda at Ghaghra.
The Mughals did not interfere in the Deccan during Babur’s time.
Babur conquered the Deccan before the Battle of Khanwa.
127.x: The Mughals did not interfere in the Deccan during Babur’s time. Babur was a contemporary of Krishnadevaraya and Golconda’s Sultan Quli.
127.tq: Reject the exaggerated conquest claim and retain the stated scope of Babur’s activity.
xs: The **Mughals did not interfere in the Deccan** in Babur's time — so option **(3)** is correct.
Babur's empire reached only the **borders of Bihar**.
xa: Babur was a contemporary of **Krishnadevaraya** and Golconda's **Sultan Quli**.
In the Baburnama he praised **Krishnadevaraya** as the most powerful ruler.
His two Hindu powers: **Vijayanagara and Mewar**.

127.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Ibrahim Lodi was the last Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate.
2. Panipat I was the first major field-artillery battle in North India.
3. Babur’s victory at Panipat immediately created a fully consolidated Mughal administrative system.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
127.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Ibrahim Lodi was the last Delhi Sultan, and Panipat I was the first major field-artillery battle in North India. Statement 3 is false: Babur's authority had shallow roots and he left no administrative system, so Panipat did not create a consolidated Mughal administration.
127.tq: Combine two significance statements with a deliberately overstated administrative conclusion.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Ibrahim Lodi** was the **last Delhi Sultan**.
Statement 2 is correct: **Panipat I** was the first major **field-artillery** battle in North India.
Statement 3 is wrong: Babur's authority had **shallow roots** and he left **no administrative system**.
xa: His treasury was **empty**, depleted by lavish gifts that earned him the nickname **"Qalandar"**.
⚠ The Mansabdari system is **Akbar's**.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about Babur:
1. He was born in Farghana and descended from Timur on his father's side and Genghis Khan on his mother's side.
2. He had held Samarkand and Kabul.
3. After Panipat he occupied Lahore and Kabul.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: after Panipat Babur occupied Delhi and Agra. So A; B, C and D include the false statement 3.
128.tq: Panipat gains = Delhi and Agra.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: Babur was born in **Farghana**, descended from **Timur** (father) and **Genghis Khan** (mother).
Statement 2 is correct: he had held **Samarkand** and **Kabul**.
Statement 3 is wrong: after Panipat he occupied **Delhi and Agra** (APPSC **2023**).
xa: His memoir **Tuzuk-i-Baburi** is in **Chaghatai Turkish** and praises **Krishnadevaraya**.
Panipat was the first large-scale use of **gunpowder artillery** in Indian warfare.
Babur's battles in order: **Panipat I → Khanwa → Chanderi → Ghaghra** (UKPSC **2024**).

128.s:
Consider the following statements about the Tuzuk-i-Baburi:
1. It was written in Persian.
2. It praises Krishnadevaraya.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the Baburnama was written in Chaghatai Turkish (Persian was the Mughal court language). Statement 2 is correct. So 2 only (B).
128.tq: Baburnama = Chaghatai Turkish, not Persian.
xs: Only statement **2** is correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is wrong: the **Tuzuk-i-Baburi** was written in **Chaghatai Turkish**, not Persian.
Statement 2 is correct: it **praises Krishnadevaraya**.
xa: Babur's tactics: **Tulughma** (cavalry flanking) and the **Rumi (Ottoman) method**.
After Panipat he occupied **Delhi and Agra**.
**Sultan Quli Qutb Shah** of Golconda (**1518-43**) was Babur's contemporary.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about Babur's tactics:
1. Tulughma was rapid cavalry flanking and encircling.
2. The Rumi method linked carts into a barrier sheltering matchlockmen and artillery.
3. The Rumi method was of Uzbek origin.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Rumi method was Ottoman. So A; B, C and D include the false statement 3.
128.tq: Rumi = Rome/Ottoman.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Tulughma** = rapid cavalry **flanking and encircling**.
Statement 2 is correct: the **Rumi method** linked **carts** into a barrier sheltering matchlockmen and artillery.
Statement 3 is wrong: the Rumi method was **Ottoman**, not Uzbek.
xa: Panipat I (**21 Apr 1526**): Babur beat **Ibrahim Lodi**; artillery decisive.
These tactics were tested in a PMF IAS practice item (**Apr 2026**).
**Kabuli Bagh Mosque** at Panipat marks **1526**.

128.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with Babur’s architectural or garden works?
o: Charbagh — a system of horse branding
128.x: Babur built the Kabuli Bagh Mosque at Panipat to commemorate the events of 1526. He also introduced the Charbagh and built Ram Bagh at Agra.
128.tq: Start with the sure monument–place pair and eliminate shifted locations or meanings.
xs: **Kabuli Bagh Mosque — Panipat** is correctly matched — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Ram Bagh** is at **Agra**, not Delhi; it is the **first Mughal garden**.
The **Charbagh** is a garden plan Babur introduced; horse branding is **dagh**.
**Sasaram** has **Sher Shah's tomb**, not the Kabuli Bagh Mosque.
xa: The mosque marks the **1526** victory at Panipat.
After Panipat Babur occupied **Delhi and Agra**.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about Humayun's early reign:
1. His initial problems included his rival brothers Kamran, Askari and Hindal, and Bahadur Shah of Gujarat-Malwa.
2. At Dourah (Devara) in 1532 he defeated the Afghans and drove Mahmud Lodi from Jaunpur.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x: Statement 1 is correct: brothers, Afghans, Bahadur Shah and an empty treasury were his problems. Statement 2 is correct: Dourah (1532) on the Gomati drove Mahmud Lodi from Jaunpur. So both.
128.tq: Dourah 1532 = Humayun's win over the Afghans.
xs: **Both 1 and 2** are correct — option **(3)**.
Statement 1: his problems were brothers **Kamran, Askari, Hindal**, the Afghans, **Bahadur Shah** of Gujarat-Malwa and an empty treasury.
Statement 2: at **Dourah (Devara)** in **1532**, on the **Gomati**, he defeated the Afghans and drove **Mahmud Lodi** from **Jaunpur**.
xa: Humayun acceded on **29 Dec 1530**, three days after Babur's death.
At Dourah he also lifted the siege of **Kalinjar**.
**Chausa (1539)** and **Kannauj/Bilgram (1540)** were Sher Shah's victories over Humayun.

128.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Gujarat, 1535 — Bahadur Shah allowed the Portuguese to fortify Diu
128.x: When pressed by Humayun in Gujarat in 1535, Bahadur Shah allowed the Portuguese to fortify Diu. Humayun was defeated at Chausa and Kannauj, while he defeated Sikandar Sur at Sirhind.
128.tq: Separate victories from defeats by checking the result attached to each event.
xs: **Gujarat, 1535 — Bahadur Shah let the Portuguese fortify Diu** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
At **Chausa (1539)** and **Kannauj (1540)**, **Sher Khan** defeated Humayun, not the reverse.
At **Sirhind (1555)**, **Humayun** defeated **Sikandar Sur**.
xa: After Kannauj, Humayun went into **exile**.
He returned in **July 1555**, retaking **Delhi and Agra**.
⚠ "Jahangir - Chausa" is a planted wrong pair (APPSC G2 **2025**).

128.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding Samugarh?
o: It was fought in 1539 between Babur and Mahmud Lodi.
It was fought in 1540 between Humayun and Sher Khan.
It was fought in 1555 between Humayun and Hemu.
It was fought in 1658 between Aurangzeb and Dara Shikoh.
128.x: The Battle of Samugarh was fought in 1658 between Aurangzeb and Dara Shikoh. It was not a battle of Humayun's return in 1555.
128.tq: Discriminate between closely placed Mughal dates and similarly named battles.
xs: **Samugarh** was fought in **1658** between **Aurangzeb and Dara** — so option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ Some notes wrongly list a "Battle of Samugarh (**1555**) Humayun vs Hemu".
**1540** was **Kannauj/Bilgram** (Humayun vs Sher Khan); **1555** was **Sirhind** (Humayun vs Sikandar Sur).
xa: **Hemu** fought Akbar/Bairam Khan at **Second Panipat** (**5 Nov 1556**).
**Panipat III (1761)**: Marathas vs **Ahmad Shah Abdali**.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about Sher Shah's early life:
1. He was born Farid, of the Afghan Sur tribe.
2. Babur gave him the title 'Sher Khan' for slaying a tiger.
3. He served Babur and later became the de facto ruler of Bihar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the title 'Sher Khan' was given by Bahar Khan of Bihar. So A; B, C and D include the false statement 2.
128.tq: Sher Khan title = Bahar Khan of Bihar.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: he was born **Farid**, of the Afghan **Sur** tribe.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Bahar Khan** of Bihar gave him the title **"Sher Khan"** for slaying a tiger.
Statement 3 is correct: he served Babur and became **deputy regent (de facto ruler)** of Bihar.
xa: He studied at **Jaunpur** and managed his father's jagir from **1511**.
⚠ **"Sher Shah"** was assumed after **Chausa (1539)**.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about Sher Shah's rise:
1. Surajgarh was the turning point, after which he took Gaur (1538).
2. He assumed the title 'Sher Shah' after the Battle of Kannauj (1540).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: he took the title Sher Shah after Chausa (1539); after Kannauj (1540) he took the throne. So 1 only (A).
128.tq: Chausa = title; Kannauj = throne.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Surajgarh** was the turning point; he took **Gaur** (**1538**).
Statement 2 is wrong: he became **"Sher Shah"** after **Chausa (1539)**; after **Kannauj (1540)** he **took the throne**.
xa: ⚠ **"Sher Khan"** = from **Bahar Khan** (tiger).
Sher Shah's reign: **1540-45**.
He died in **1545** during the siege of **Kalinjar**.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about Sher Shah's conquests:
1. He took Raisen from Puran Mal.
2. Kandahar was among his conquests.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x: Statement 1 is correct: Raisen was taken from Puran Mal. Statement 2 is wrong: his conquests were Malwa, Raisen and Marwar; Kandahar is linked with Humayun's recovery with Safavid help. So 1 only.
128.tq: Sher Shah: Malwa, Raisen, Marwar.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: Sher Shah took **Raisen** from **Puran Mal**.
Statement 2 is wrong: his conquests were **Malwa**, **Raisen** and **Marwar**; **Kandahar** was retaken by **Humayun** with **Shah Tahmasp**'s help.
xa: At **Samel (1544)** Sher Shah fought **Maldeo of Marwar**.
He died in **1545** in a gunpowder explosion during the siege of **Kalinjar**.
⚠ Title **"Sher Khan"** came from **Bahar Khan**; **"Sher Shah"** was assumed after **Chausa (1539)**.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about Sher Shah's war with Marwar:
1. After the battle of Samel (1544) against Maldeo, Sher Shah said he had nearly lost Hindustan 'for a handful of bajra'.
2. Jaita and Kumpa were generals of Bahadur Shah of Gujarat.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x: Statement 2 is wrong: Jaita and Kumpa were the generals of Maldeo of Marwar. Statement 1 is correct: the remark refers to the hard-fought battle of Samel (Giri-Sumel). So 1 only.
128.tq: Samel 1544: Maldeo's Jaita and Kumpa.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: after **Samel (1544)** against **Maldeo**, Sher Shah said he nearly lost Hindustan **"for a handful of bajra"**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Jaita and Kumpa** were generals of **Maldeo of Marwar**, not Bahadur Shah.
xa: Samel is also called **Sammel / Giri-Sumel**.
**Bahadur Shah** of Gujarat let the **Portuguese** fortify **Diu** (**1535**).
Sher Shah's other conquests: **Malwa** and **Raisen** (Puran Mal).

128.s: Sher Shah died in 1545 in a gunpowder explosion during the siege of
128.x: Sher Shah died in 1545 in a gunpowder explosion during the siege of Kalinjar.
128.tq: Associate the ruler's death with the exact military operation rather than merely the year.
xs: Sher Shah died in **1545** in a gunpowder explosion during the siege of **Kalinjar** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Raisen** was taken from Puran Mal; **Gaur** was taken in **1538**.
xa: Humayun had earlier lifted a siege of **Kalinjar** after **Dourah**.
Successor: **Islam Shah** (**Jalal Khan**, **1545-53**).
Sher Shah's tomb is at **Sasaram** (Bihar), an **octagonal tomb in a tank**.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about Humayun's exile:
1. He married Hamida Banu Begum.
2. Akbar was born at Amarkot in 1542.
3. Bahadur Shah of Gujarat helped him retake Kandahar and Kabul.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Safavid Shah Tahmasp of Persia helped him retake Kandahar and Kabul. So A; B, C and D include the false statement 3.
128.tq: Exile help came from Persia (Shah Tahmasp).
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: Humayun married **Hamida Banu Begum**.
Statement 2 is correct: **Akbar** was born at **Amarkot** (**1542**).
Statement 3 is wrong: Safavid **Shah Tahmasp** of Persia helped him retake **Kandahar and Kabul**; Bahadur Shah was an enemy.
xa: Humayun went to **Persia**, forming an alliance with the **Safavids**.
He returned in **July 1555**.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about Humayun's return and death:
1. He returned in July 1555, exploiting quarrels among Sher Shah's successors.
2. He defeated Sikandar Sur at Machhiwara and Sirhind and then took Delhi and Agra.
3. He died in January 1556 after falling from the stairs of the library in Agra Fort.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: he fell from the stairs of the Sher Mandal library in the Purana Qila, Delhi. So A; B, C and D include the false statement 3.
128.tq: Humayun's fatal fall = Sher Mandal, Purana Qila.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: he returned in **July 1555**, exploiting quarrels among Sher Shah's successors.
Statement 2 is correct: he beat **Sikandar Sur** at **Machhiwara and Sirhind**, then took **Delhi and Agra**.
Statement 3 is wrong: he fell from the stairs of the **Sher Mandal** library in the **Purana Qila**, Delhi (**January 1556**).
xa: The **Purana Qila** was begun by Humayun and rebuilt by Sher Shah.
**Humayun-nama** was written by his sister **Gulbadan Begum**.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about the Sur successors:
1. Hemu, Muhammad Adil Shah's Hindu minister-general, seized Agra and Delhi and took the title Vikramaditya.
2. Islam Shah (Jalal Khan) succeeded Sher Shah.
3. Muhammad Adil Shah was the ruler of Marwar who resisted Sher Shah.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
128.x: Statement 2 is correct: Islam Shah ruled 1545-53. Statement 1 is correct: Hemu took the title Vikramaditya in 1556. Statement 3 is wrong: Adil Shah ruled in the east and fought Sikandar Sur; Maldeo was the ruler of Marwar. So 1 and 2 only.
128.tq: Hemu = Adil Shah's general, 'Vikramaditya'.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: **Hemu**, **Adil Shah**'s Hindu minister-general, seized **Agra and Delhi** (1556) and took the title **"Vikramaditya"**.
Statement 2: **Islam Shah** (**Jalal Khan**, **1545-53**) succeeded Sher Shah.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Muhammad Adil Shah** ruled in the east; **Maldeo** was the ruler of **Marwar**.
xa: Hemu lost **Panipat II (5 Nov 1556)**: an arrow struck his eye; Afghan power ended.
**Sikandar Sur** was Adil Shah's rival; Humayun defeated him at **Machhiwara and Sirhind**.
The Surs were the **last Afghan dynasty** to rule Delhi.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about the Second Battle of Panipat:
1. It was fought on 5 November 1556.
2. Hemu was struck in the eye by an arrow and captured.
3. It marked the end of Afghan power in the relevant political context.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
128.x: All three statements are correct. The defeat and capture of Hemu at the battle helped end Afghan power in north India.
128.tq: Combine the date, battlefield incident and political consequence in one statement set.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
Statement 1: **Panipat II** was fought on **5 Nov 1556**.
Statement 2: an **arrow struck Hemu's eye**; he was captured.
Statement 3: it marked the **end of Afghan power**.
xa: The Mughal side was led by **Akbar/Bairam Khan**.
⚠ "Tipu vs Marathas" is **not** Panipat II.
**Panipat III (1761)**: Marathas vs **Ahmad Shah Abdali**.

128.s: The Humayun-nama was written by
128.x: The Humayun-nama was written by Humayun's sister Gulbadan Begum. Hamida Banu Begum was Humayun's wife and Akbar's mother; Abul Fazl wrote the Akbarnama; Babur wrote the Tuzuk-i-Baburi.
128.tq: Gulbadan = Humayun's sister = Humayun-nama
xs: The **Humayun-nama** was written by Humayun's sister **Gulbadan Begum** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Hamida Banu Begum** was Humayun's wife and **Akbar's** mother.
**Babur** wrote the **Tuzuk-i-Baburi**.
xa: Akbar was born at **Amarkot** (**1542**).
Humayun died in **January 1556** at the **Sher Mandal** library, **Purana Qila**.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about Sur administration:
1. Maktabs were opened with stipends for students.
2. Hindus held high posts in the army.
3. Officers held their posts for life to give stability.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
128.x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is correct. Statement 3 is wrong: officers were frequently transferred so that they did not build local interests. So 1 and 2 only.
128.tq: Sur officers = frequent transfers.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: **maktabs** were opened with scholarships/stipends.
Statement 2: the army was regular and directly recruited; **Hindus held high posts**.
Statement 3 is wrong: officers were **frequently transferred**.
xa: **dagh** = horse branding; **chehra/huliya** = descriptive roll of soldiers — both against fraud.
Sarkar level: **Chief Shiqdar** (law and order) and **Chief Munsif** (revenue/civil).
Pargana: **Shiqdar**, **Amin**, treasurer (**fotedar**) and **Hindi and Persian writers** (karkuns).

128.s:
Consider the following statements about Sur sarkar administration:
1. The Chief Shiqdar (shiqdar-i-shiqdaran) looked after law and order in a sarkar.
2. The Chief Munsif (munsif-i-munsifan) was the treasurer of a pargana.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Chief Munsif was the sarkar-level revenue/civil officer; the pargana treasurer was the fotedar. So 1 only (A).
128.tq: Sarkar: Chief Shiqdar + Chief Munsif; pargana treasurer = fotedar.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: the **Chief Shiqdar** (shiqdar-i-shiqdaran) handled **law and order** in a sarkar.
Statement 2 is wrong: the **Chief Munsif** (munsif-i-munsifan) was the sarkar's **revenue/civil** officer; the pargana treasurer was the **fotedar**.
xa: Pargana officers: **Shiqdar**, **Amin** (munsif), **fotedar**, **Hindi and Persian writers** (karkuns).
Officers were **frequently transferred**.

128.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the officers of a Sur-era pargana:
1. The Shiqdar was an officer of the pargana.
2. The Fotedar functioned as treasurer.
3. Karkuns included Hindi and Persian writers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
128.x: All three statements are correct. The pargana had a Shiqdar, Amin, Fotedar and Hindi and Persian-writing Karkuns.
128.tq: Check each statement against the composition of the pargana administration.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
Statement 1: the **Shiqdar** was a pargana officer.
Statement 2: the **fotedar** was the treasurer.
Statement 3: **karkuns** were **Hindi and Persian writers**.
xa: The pargana also had an **Amin** (munsif).
Sarkar level: **Chief Shiqdar** (law and order) and **Chief Munsif** (revenue/civil).

128.s:
Consider the following statements about the Sur army:
1. It was a regular army, directly recruited and strictly disciplined.
2. 'Dagh' meant the descriptive roll of soldiers, while 'chehra' meant the branding of horses.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 reverses the terms: dagh was horse branding and chehra/huliya the descriptive roll of soldiers. So 1 only (A).
128.tq: Dagh = horse brand; chehra = face/description of soldier.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: the army was **regular**, **directly recruited** and **strictly disciplined**.
Statement 2 is wrong — it reverses the terms: **dagh** = **horse branding**; **chehra/huliya** = **descriptive roll** of soldiers.
xa: Both measures were aimed **against fraud**.
**Hindus** held high army posts.

128.s: Which statement about policing under the Sur administration is correct?
o: Public morals were regulated only by village accountants.
Local headmen were made responsible for detecting crime.
Crime detection was entrusted exclusively to the central army.
The Sur rulers had no organised espionage system.
128.x: Local headmen were held responsible for detecting crime. The system also included censors of public morals and an efficient espionage network.
128.tq: Test the responsible authority and reject the exclusive or negative claims.
xs: **Local headmen** were made responsible for **detecting crime** — so option **(2)** is correct.
There were **censors of public morals** and an efficient **espionage** system — so options (1) and (4) are wrong.
xa: Justice was **uniform** and **harsh**.
Sarkar law and order lay with the **Chief Shiqdar**.
Officers were **frequently transferred**.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about Sher Shah's land survey:
1. Land was measured uniformly with the gaz-i-Sikandari.
2. Land was classified as wet, dry and irrigated.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x: Statement 1 is correct: the sikandari gaz and the jarib were used. Statement 2 is wrong: land was classified by produce into good, middling and bad. So 1 only.
128.tq: Sher Shah: 3 classes; Akbar: 4 classes.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: land was measured under a **uniform system** with the **gaz-i-Sikandari** and the **jarib**.
Statement 2 is wrong: land was classified into **three categories** — **good, middling, bad** — by produce.
xa: State share: **one-third** of average produce, paid in **cash or grain**.
⚠ APPSC-G1 **2024** key: "one-fourth" is false.
**Patta** = title deed given to the cultivator; **Qabuliyat** = deed of acceptance signed by the peasant.
The system became the model for **Todar Mal's Bandobast**.

128.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with Sher Shah's revenue administration?
o: Qanungo — command of the royal cavalry
128.x: The amin made the revenue assessment in Sher Shah's system. The shiqdar, qanungo and patwari were also revenue/local officials; none of them prepared manuscripts, commanded the cavalry or minted coins, so B, C and D are false pairs.
128.tq: Use the 'who would do this job?' method to identify the official function.
xs: **Amin — assessment of revenue** is correctly matched — so option **(1)** is correct.
The Amin assessed revenue together with the **shiqdar, qanungo and patwari** — all revenue/local officials.
None of them prepared manuscripts, commanded cavalry or minted coins.
xa: **Jaribana** = surveyor's fee; **Muhasilana** = collector's fee.
**Patta** = title deed; **Qabuliyat** = peasant's deed of acceptance.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about Sher Shah's land revenue system:
1. His direct settlement with cultivators removed illegal demands and recognised tenant rights.
2. It became the model for Todar Mal's Bandobast.
3. The state's share was fixed at one-fourth of the average produce.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the state share was one-third of average produce (APPSC-G1 2024 key marks 'one-fourth' false). So A; B, C and D include the false statement 3.
128.tq: Sher Shah's share = one-third; 'one-fourth' is the trap.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: the **direct settlement** with cultivators removed illegal demands and recognised **tenant rights**.
Statement 2 is correct: it was the model for **Todar Mal's Bandobast**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the share was **one-third**; APPSC-G1 **2024** key marks "one-fourth" false.
xa: ⚠ Some notes say "one-fourth to one-third".
Some notes call Sher Shah the first to introduce a **ryotwari**-type system.

128.s: In Sher Shah's revenue system, the Qabuliyat was
o: the title deed given to the peasant stating his revenue dues
the deed of agreement signed by the peasant accepting the revenue demand
the fee paid to the surveyor
the fee paid to the revenue collector
128.x: The Qabuliyat was the peasant's deed of acceptance of the revenue demand, signed by him. The Patta was the title deed given to the cultivator. Jaribana was the surveyor's fee and muhasilana the collector's fee.
128.tq: Patta given to peasant; Qabuliyat signed by peasant
xs: The **Qabuliyat** was the peasant's **deed of agreement** accepting the revenue demand, **signed by him** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **Patta** was the **title deed** given to the cultivator.
**Jaribana** = surveyor's fee; **Muhasilana** = collector's fee.
xa: ⚠ **Patta** = given by the state; **Qabuliyat** = signed by the peasant.
Assessment was by the **Amin**, with shiqdar, qanungo and patwari.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about Sher Shah's currency:
1. His coinage disappeared with the end of the Sur dynasty.
2. The rupiya was silver, the dam copper and the mohur gold.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: he minted pure gold and silver coins, and the reform outlived the Surs; the rupiya stayed standard for centuries. So 2 only.
128.tq: Rupiya = silver, from Sher Shah.
xs: Only statement **2** is correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 2: **Rupiya** was **silver**, **Dam** **copper**, and the **Mohur** **gold**.
Statement 1 is wrong: his currency reform **outlived the Sur dynasty**; the rupiya remained standard for centuries.
xa: The rupiya weighed about **178 grains** and was introduced **1540-45**.
Sher Shah minted **pure** gold and silver coins.
He restored the **Grand Trunk Road** (Sadak-e-Azam) from **Sonargaon** to the **Indus**.

128.s: The Sadak-e-Azam constructed or restored by Sher Shah connected
o: Sonargaon in Bengal with the Indus
128.x: The major road, also called the Grand Trunk Road, ran from Sonargaon in Bengal to the Indus.
128.tq: Distinguish the principal imperial highway from the other roads associated with Sher Shah.
xs: The **Sadak-e-Azam (Grand Trunk Road)** ran from **Sonargaon (Bengal) to the Indus** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Lahore-Multan** and **Agra-Burhanpur** were his other, shorter roads.
xa: APPSC-G1 **2022** answer: "Indus to Sonargaon"; APPSC-GS **2018**: he **restored** it.
⚠ Some notes say **Chittagong-Kabul**, about **1,500 miles**.
Another road: **Agra-Jodhpur-Chittor**.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about Sher Shah's sarais:
1. They were built along roads, with shady trees planted for travellers.
2. They gave common lodging with no separate arrangement for Hindus and Muslims.
3. They served as dak-chowkis for relaying news and mail.
4. Market towns grew around them.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the sarais had separate lodging for Hindus and Muslims. So A; B, C and D include the false statement 2.
128.tq: Sarais: roads + trees, separate lodging, dak-chowki, market towns.
xs: Statements **1, 3 and 4 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: sarais stood along roads, with **shady trees**.
Statement 2 is wrong: there was **separate lodging for Hindus and Muslims**.
Statements 3 and 4 are correct: they served as **dak-chowkis** and **market towns** grew around them.
xa: Dak-chowkis were post stations relaying news and mail, with **horses**.
The **Grand Trunk Road** ran from **Sonargaon** to the **Indus**.

128.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:

List-I (Road)
a. Sadak-e-Azam
b. Agra–Burhanpur
c. Agra–Jodhpur–Chittor
d. Lahore–Multan

List-II (Association)
i. Major road from Bengal to the Indus
ii. Road linking Lahore and Multan
iii. Road linking Agra and Burhanpur
iv. Road linking Agra, Jodhpur and Chittor
128.x: Sadak-e-Azam was the Bengal–Indus highway; the remaining pairs reproduce the three other routes correctly.
128.tq: Start from the sure route pair and eliminate codes that repeat or misplace the roads.
xs: **a–i, b–iii, c–iv, d–ii** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Sadak-e-Azam** = the Bengal-to-Indus highway (**Sonargaon to the Indus**).
The other three roads link exactly the places named: **Agra-Burhanpur**, **Agra-Jodhpur-Chittor**, **Lahore-Multan**.
xa: The Grand Trunk Road still exists.
Sarais along the roads doubled as **dak-chowkis**.

128.s: Sher Shah's tomb at Sasaram is notable for being
o: a four-domed marble mausoleum in Agra
an octagonal tomb set in a tank
a circular tomb built inside the Purana Qila
128.x: The tomb at Sasaram is an octagonal monument surrounded by water in a tank.
128.tq: Use the distinctive architectural feature to distinguish the monument from other Sur structures.
xs: **Sher Shah's tomb** at **Sasaram** (Bihar) is an **octagonal tomb in a tank** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Rohtas fort** is in present-day **Pakistan**; the **Purana Qila** is in **Delhi**.
xa: Sher Shah rebuilt the **Purana Qila** (Dinpanah), begun by **Humayun**.
He built the **Qila-i-Kuhna mosque** inside it.
**Humayun's Tomb** is the first **garden tomb**, with a **double dome**.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about Rohtas fort:
1. It is located at Sasaram in Bihar.
2. It is known for its angled walls and bastions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x: Statement 1 is wrong: Rohtas fort is in present-day Pakistan; Sasaram has Sher Shah's tomb. Statement 2 is correct. So 2 only (B); A, C and D misjudge the statements.
128.tq: Sasaram = tomb in a tank; Rohtas = Pakistan fort.
xs: Only statement **2** is correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is wrong: **Rohtas fort** is in present-day **Pakistan**; **Sasaram** has **Sher Shah's tomb**.
Statement 2 is correct: Rohtas has **angled walls and bastions**.
xa: Sasaram tomb: **octagonal**, set in a **tank**.
**Qila-i-Kuhna mosque** stands inside the **Purana Qila**, Delhi.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about tombs:
1. Sikandar Lodi's tomb in Delhi was built by his son Ibrahim Lodi.
2. Balban's Tomb, with the first true arch in India, is at Sasaram.
3. Humayun's Tomb is the first garden tomb of the subcontinent and has a double dome.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
128.x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Balban's Tomb is at Mehrauli, Delhi; Sasaram has Sher Shah's octagonal tomb. Statement 1 is correct. So 1 and 3 only.
128.tq: Balban's tomb = Mehrauli, first true arch.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct — option **(3)**.
Statement 1: **Sikandar Lodi's Tomb** in Delhi was built by his son **Ibrahim Lodi**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Balban's Tomb** is at **Mehrauli, Delhi**; **Sasaram** has **Sher Shah's tomb**.
Statement 3: **Humayun's Tomb** is the first **garden tomb** with a **double dome**.
xa: Balban's Tomb is the first in India in a **purely Indo-Islamic style**, with the **first true arch**.
Sher Shah's octagonal tomb in a tank at Sasaram was **completed** by **Islam Shah**.
Humayun's Tomb uses **red sandstone + white marble**.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about Babur's battles:
1. At Chanderi (1528) Babur fought Medini Rai.
2. Ghaghra (1529), fought against the Afghans under Mahmud Lodi, was Babur's last battle.
3. Babur's battles in order were Panipat I, Chanderi, Khanwa and Ghaghra.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the order is Panipat I (1526), Khanwa (1527), Chanderi (1528), Ghaghra (1529). So A; B, C and D include the false statement 3.
128.tq: Babur's order: Panipat-Khanwa-Chanderi-Ghaghra (1526-29).
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: at **Chanderi (1528)** Babur fought **Medini Rai**.
Statement 2 is correct: **Ghaghra (1529)**, against the Afghans of Bihar-Bengal (**Mahmud Lodi**), was Babur's **last battle**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the order is **Panipat I (1526) → Khanwa (1527) → Chanderi (1528) → Ghaghra (1529)** (UKPSC **2024**).
xa: Panipat I (**21 Apr 1526**): Babur beat **Ibrahim Lodi**; Mughal Empire founded.
**Khanwa** broke **Rajput** power (Babur vs **Rana Sanga**).

128.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Panipat II — Akbar and Sher Shah
128.x: Panipat II was fought in 1556 between Akbar, represented by Bairam Khan, and Hemu. Sher Shah was the opponent of Humayun at Kannauj.
128.tq: Find the wrong ruler–opponent pairing by checking the battle chronology.
xs: **Panipat II — Akbar and Sher Shah** is wrongly matched — so option **(4)** is the answer.
**Panipat II (5 Nov 1556)** was **Akbar/Bairam Khan vs Hemu**; Sher Shah had died in **1545**.
The others are correct: **Haldighati** (Akbar's general **Man Singh** vs **Maharana Pratap**), **Chausa** and **Kannauj** (Humayun vs **Sher Khan**).
xa: Panipat II ended **Afghan power**.
⚠ "Tipu vs Marathas" is not Panipat II.
Kannauj is also called **Bilgram** (**1540**).

128.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
128.x: Chausa (1539) was fought by Humayun against Sher Khan, so 'Chausa - Jahangir' is the wrong pair (APPSC G2 2025). Babur fought Rana Sanga at Khanwa (1527), Humayun beat Sikandar Sur at Sirhind (1555), and the Marathas fought Ahmad Shah Abdali at Panipat III (1761).
128.tq: Chausa = Humayun vs Sher Khan, never Jahangir
xs: **Chausa - Jahangir** is the wrong pair — so option **(1)** is the answer (APPSC G2 **2025**).
**Chausa (1539)** was **Humayun vs Sher Khan**.
Correct pairs: **Khanwa — Babur** (**1527**), **Sirhind — Humayun** (**1555**), **Panipat III — Ahmad Shah Abdali** (**1761**).
xa: At Sirhind Humayun beat **Sikandar Sur** and retook Delhi and Agra.
After **Chausa**, Sher Khan assumed the title **Sher Shah**.
⚠ "Wrong pair" questions: Jahangir-Chausa is the planted mismatch.

128.s:
Consider the following statements about Sher Shah and the Surs:
1. The Surs were the last Afghan dynasty to rule Delhi.
2. Sher Shah's short reign set the pattern for Mughal land revenue, coinage and roads.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x: Statement 2 is correct: via Todar Mal (revenue), the rupee and the roads. Statement 1 is correct. So both.
128.tq: Sher Shah = template for Akbar.
xs: **Both 1 and 2** are correct — option **(3)**.
Statement 1: the **Surs** were the **last Afghan dynasty** to rule Delhi.
Statement 2: Sher Shah's short reign (**1540-45**) set the pattern for Mughal land revenue (via **Todar Mal**), coinage (the **rupee**) and roads.
xa: Sher Shah took **1/3** of average produce with **three** land classes.
Akbar-Todar Mal kept **1/3** but used **ten-year averages** and **four** classes (**polaj, parauti, chachar, banjar**).
The **Rupiya** began with Sher Shah.

128.s:
Which statement correctly compares the revenue systems of Sher Shah and Akbar under Todar Mal?
1. Sher Shah assessed revenue at one-third of average produce.
2. Sher Shah classified land into three categories.
3. Akbar-Todar Mal retained the one-third share but used ten-year averages.
4. Akbar-Todar Mal used four land classes: polaj, parauti, chachar and banjar.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
128.x: All four statements are correct. Sher Shah used three land classes and a one-third rate, while Akbar’s system used ten-year averages and four classes while retaining the one-third share.
