128.tq: Compare the systems across both the rate and the classification method.
xs: All four statements are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
Statements 1 and 2: **Sher Shah** = **1/3** of average produce + **three** land classes.
Statements 3 and 4: **Akbar-Todar Mal** kept **1/3** but used **ten-year averages** + **four** classes — **polaj, parauti, chachar, banjar**.
xa: Sher Shah's classes: **good, middling, bad**.
His system was the model for **Todar Mal's Bandobast**.
⚠ APPSC-G1 **2024**: "one-fourth" for Sher Shah's share is false.

128.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Sultan Quli Qutb Shah of Golconda was contemporary with Babur, Humayun and Sher Shah.
2. The Mughal rulers did not interfere in the Deccan during this period.
3. Sultan Quli Qutb Shah ruled Golconda from 1518 to 1543.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
128.x: All three statements are correct. Sultan Quli Qutb Shah ruled Golconda from 1518 to 1543 and was contemporary with the early Mughals and Sher Shah, while Mughal interference in the Deccan had not yet begun.
128.tq: Combine chronology, contemporary rulers and regional-policy facts in one check.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
Statements 1 and 3: **Sultan Quli Qutb Shah** of Golconda (**1518-43**) was contemporary with **Babur, Humayun and Sher Shah**.
Statement 2: the **Mughals did not interfere in the Deccan** then.
xa: Babur's **Tuzuk-i-Baburi** praises **Krishnadevaraya**.
Sher Shah's reign: **1540-45**.
Humayun acceded on **29 Dec 1530**.

128.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Battle of Kannauj:
I. The Battle of Kannauj is also called the Battle of Bilgram.
II. The battle took place in 1540.
III. Humayun fought against Sher Shah in the battle.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x: All three are correct: Kannauj is also called Bilgram, it was fought in 1540, and Sher Shah defeated Humayun there.
128.tq: Check each statement separately.
n: The Battle of Kannauj is also called the Battle of Bilgram. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
The Battle of Kannauj or Bilgram was fought in 1540. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
The Battle of Kannauj or Bilgram was fought between Humayun and Sher Shah. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
xs: **I, II and III** are all correct — option **(3)**.
The **Battle of Kannauj** is also called the **Battle of Bilgram**, fought in **1540**.
**Sher Shah defeated Humayun** there; Humayun lost control of **North India** and went into exile.
xa: **Chausa** (**26 June 1539**) preceded Bilgram.
⚠ Some notes wrongly list "Bilgram (1540)" as a Humayun victory.
Humayun reoccupied Delhi after **Sirhind** (**1555**).

128.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
 a. Chunar Fort
 b. Kalinjar Fort
 c. Purana Qila
 d. Bhatkal Fort

List-II
 i. Portuguese allowed to build a fort by Krishnadeva Raya
 ii. Qila-e-Kuhna Mosque built inside it by Sher Shah
 iii. Sher Shah Suri died during its siege in 1545
 iv. Sher Khan submitted to Humayun after a siege
128.x: Sher Khan submitted to Humayun after the siege of Chunar, Sher Shah died besieging Kalinjar, Sher Shah built the Qila-e-Kuhna Mosque inside Purana Qila, and Krishnadeva Raya let the Portuguese build at Bhatkal, giving a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i.
128.tq: Link each fort to the event that made it famous.
n: Chunar Fort is associated with Humayun. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 137-138]
Chunar Fort is associated with Sher Khan. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 137-138]
Kalinjar Fort is associated with Sher Shah Suri. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 137-138]
Raisina Fort is associated with Humayun. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 137-138]
Bhatkal Fort is associated with Krishnadeva Raya. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 137-138]
xs: The correct match is **a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i** — option **(1)**.
**Chunar Fort**: **Sher Khan** accepted Humayun's supremacy after a **four-month siege**.
**Kalinjar Fort**: Sher Shah died in a gunpowder explosion during its siege in **1545**.
**Purana Qila**: Sher Shah built the **Qila-e-Kuhna Mosque** inside it; **Bhatkal Fort**: **Krishnadeva Raya** permitted the **Portuguese** to build it.
xa: Humayun first invaded **Chunar** in **1532**.
Sher Shah built the Qila-e-Kuhna Mosque in **1541**.
Purana Qila (**Dinpanah**) was begun by **Humayun** and rebuilt by **Sher Shah**.

128.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Sher Khan accepted Humayun's supremacy after the siege of Chunar Fort.
B. Sher Shah defeated Humayun at the Battle of Chausa.
C. Sher Shah built the Qila-e-Kuhna Mosque inside Purana Qila.
D. Sher Shah Suri died during the siege of Kalinjar Fort.
128.x: The siege of Chunar ended with Sher Khan's submission in 1532, Chausa was fought in 1539, the Qila-e-Kuhna Mosque dates to 1541 and Sher Shah died at Kalinjar in 1545. The order is A, B, C, D.
128.tq: Fix the Humayun–Sher Shah rivalry milestones on a timeline.
n: Sher Shah Suri invaded Kalinjar in 1531. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 137-138]
Humayun first invaded Chunar in 1532. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 137-138]
Humayun annexed Raisina Fort in 1535. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 137-138]
Sher Shah built the Qila-e-Kuhna Mosque inside Purana Qila in 1541. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 137-138]
Purana Qila is associated with Sher Shah Suri. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 137-138]
xs: The order is **A, B, C, D** — option **(2)**.
A: **Chunar** siege — Humayun invaded in **1532**; Sher Khan submitted.
B: **Chausa** — Sher Shah defeated Humayun on **26 June 1539**.
C: **Qila-e-Kuhna Mosque** in Purana Qila — **1541**; D: Sher Shah died at **Kalinjar** — **1545**.
xa: **Kannauj/Bilgram** (**1540**) fell between B and C.
Humayun died in **January 1556** after a fall from the **Sher Mandal** library in the **Purana Qila**.
**Raisina Fort** was annexed by Humayun in **1535**.

128.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
 a. Warangal Fort
 b. Kondaveedu Fort
 c. Purana Qila / Old Fort
 d. Bhatkal Fort

List-II
 i. Qila-e-Kuhna Mosque built inside it
 ii. Portuguese permitted to construct a fort
 iii. Old Kakatiya capital later taken by the Qutb Shahis
 iv. Old Reddy kingdom stronghold later taken by the Qutb Shahis
128.x: Warangal was the Kakatiya capital and Kondaveedu the Reddy stronghold, both later taken in the Qutb Shahi expansion; the Qila-e-Kuhna Mosque stands inside Purana Qila, and Bhatkal is where the Portuguese were allowed a fort, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
128.tq: Recall each fort's earlier dynasty to separate the two Andhra forts.
n: Quli Qutb Shah captured Warangal Fort during the Qutb Shahi expansion. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 137-138]
Quli Qutb Shah captured Kondaveedu Fort during the Qutb Shahi expansion. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 137-138]
Sher Shah built the Qila-e-Kuhna Mosque inside Purana Qila in 1541. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 137-138]
Krishnadeva Raya permitted the Portuguese to construct a fort at Bhatkal. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 137-138]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii** — option **(4)**.
**Warangal** and **Kondaveedu** forts were both captured by **Quli Qutb Shah** in the **Qutb Shahi expansion**.
**Purana Qila** holds the **Qila-e-Kuhna Mosque**; at **Bhatkal**, **Krishnadeva Raya** let the **Portuguese** build a fort.
xa: Sher Shah gave Purana Qila its **present form**.
**Sultan Quli Qutb Shah** of Golconda (**1518-43**) was contemporary with Babur, Humayun and Sher Shah.
The Qila-e-Kuhna Mosque dates to **1541**.

128.s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Rao Jaitsi defeated Kamran Mirza in the Bikaner conflict.
Statement B: Rao Jaitsi was the ruler of Bikaner.
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
128.x: Both are true: Rao Jaitsi, ruler of Bikaner, defeated Babur's son Kamran Mirza in 1534.
128.tq: Check each statement separately.
n: Rao Jaitsi defeated Kamran Mirza in the Bikaner conflict. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 74-76]
Rao Jaitsi was the ruler of Bikaner. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 74-76]
xs: **Both Statement A and Statement B are true** — option **(1)**.
**Rao Jaitsi** was the **ruler of Bikaner**.
He **defeated Kamran Mirza** in the **Bikaner conflict**.
xa: **Kamran, Askari and Hindal** were Humayun's rival brothers.
Humayun acceded on **29 Dec 1530**.
Humayun's sister **Gulbadan Begum** wrote the **Humayun-nama**.

129.s:
Consider the following statements about Bairam Khan:
1. He was Akbar's regent from 1556 to 1560.
2. He was dismissed in 1560 and killed on the way to Mecca in 1561.
3. Akbar gave him the title 'Khan-i-Khanan' as part of his appointment as wazir.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
129.x: Statement 1 is correct: Bairam Khan's regency lasted 1556-60. Statement 2 is correct: he was dismissed in 1560 and killed on the way to Mecca in 1561. Statement 3 is wrong: Akbar did give him the title Khan-i-Khanan, but it was not tied to his appointment as wazir (UPPSC 2024). So '1 only' is incomplete and options with 3 are wrong.
129.tq: Regency 1556-60, dismissed 1560, killed 1561; petticoat government 1560-64 follows.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Bairam Khan's regency** lasted **1556-60**.
Statement 2 is correct: he was **dismissed in 1560** and **killed on the way to Mecca** in **1561**.
Statement 3 is wrong: Akbar gave him the title **"Khan-i-Khanan"**, but it was **not tied to his appointment as wazir** (UPPSC **2024**).
xa: Bairam Khan enthroned Akbar at **Kalanaur**.
His son **Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khanan** translated the **Baburnama** into Persian.

129.s: The expression 'petticoat government' in Akbar's early reign refers to the dominance of:
o: Ruqaiya Sultan Begum and Man Singh I
Hamida Banu Begum and Salima Sultan Begum
Maham Anaga and her son Adham Khan
129.x: The term refers to the period from 1560 to 1564 when Maham Anaga and her son Adham Khan exercised considerable influence.
129.tq: Match the political expression with the persons and period it denotes.
xs: **Petticoat government** (**1560-64**) was the dominance of **Maham Anaga** and her son **Adham Khan** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It followed **Bairam Khan's regency** (**1556-60**).
xa: Bairam Khan was dismissed in **1560** and killed in **1561**.
**Man Singh I** was a Kachhwaha general; **Todar Mal** was the revenue minister.
Akbar married the daughter of **Raja Bharmal of Amber** in **1562**.

129.s: The Second Battle of Panipat (5 November 1556), which ended Afghan power, was fought between Akbar's forces and:
129.x: At Panipat II (1556) Hemu was hit in the eye by an arrow and captured, ending Afghan power. Daud Khan Karrani opposed Akbar in Bengal (1576), Baz Bahadur in Malwa (1561), and Ibrahim Lodi lost the First Battle of Panipat (1526) to Babur.
129.tq: Panipat II = 1556 = Hemu (arrow in the eye).
xs: At **Panipat II (5 Nov 1556)**, Akbar's forces fought **Hemu** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Hemu was **hit in the eye by an arrow** and captured; **Afghan power ended**.
**Daud Khan Karrani** opposed Akbar in **Bengal** (**1576**); **Baz Bahadur** in **Malwa** (**1561**).
xa: Akbar was then **14**, under **Bairam Khan**.
Malwa (**1561**) was Akbar's first listed conquest.

129.s:
Match the following conquests of Akbar with the rulers opposed:

List-I (Region)
 a. Malwa
 b. Gondwana
 c. Chittor
 d. Ranthambore

List-II (Ruler)
 i. Rani Durgavati
 ii. Surjan Rai
 iii. Baz Bahadur
 iv. Rana Udai Singh

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
129.x: Baz Bahadur opposed Akbar in Malwa, Rani Durgavati in Gondwana, Rana Udai Singh at Chittor, and Surjan Rai at Ranthambore.
129.tq: Begin with a known ruler–region pair and check the remaining regional matches.
xs: **a–iii, b–i, c–iv, d–ii** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Malwa** (**1561**) — **Baz Bahadur**; **Gondwana** (**1564**) — **Rani Durgavati**.
**Chittor** (**1568**) — **Rana Udai Singh**; **Ranthambore** (**1569**) — **Surjan Rai** (Hada).
xa: ⚠ Women who resisted: **Rani Durgavati** (Gondwana) and **Chand Bibi** (Ahmednagar).
In **Marwar**, **Rao Chandrasena** resisted.
Last campaign: **Asirgarh (1601)**.

129.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
129.x: Akbar conquered Gujarat in 1572–73, opposing Muzaffar Shah III. Daud Khan Karrani was associated with Bengal, Mirza Hakim with Kabul, and Chand Bibi with Ahmednagar.
129.tq: Use the region–year–ruler triple and reject swapped opponents.
xs: **Gujarat — 1572–73 — Muzaffar Shah III** is correctly matched — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Bengal** (**1576**) was taken from **Daud Khan Karrani**, not Mirza Hakim.
**Kabul** (**1581**) was taken from **Mirza Hakim**, not Daud Khan.
**Kashmir** (**1586**) was **Yusuf Shah Chak**'s; **Chand Bibi** defended **Ahmednagar** (**1600**).
xa: **Buland Darwaza** commemorates the Gujarat conquest.
The Bengal campaign ran **1574-76**.

129.s: Akbar's last campaign was associated with the conquest of:
o: Gujarat, where Buland Darwaza was built
Khandesh, including the capture of Asirgarh fort
129.x: Akbar's last campaign was the conquest of Khandesh in 1601, during which the Asirgarh fort was taken from Miran Bahadur.
129.tq: Identify the last event in a sequence of conquests rather than the most famous one.
xs: Akbar's **last campaign** was **Khandesh**, taking **Asirgarh** fort (**1601**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was taken from **Miran Bahadur**.
**Gujarat** (Buland Darwaza), **Bengal** and **Kashmir** were earlier conquests.
xa: **Ahmednagar** fell in **1600**, resisted by **Chand Bibi**.
Akbar's empire reached the **Godavari** in the south.

129.s: Which one of the following statements about the extent of Akbar's empire is correct?
o: It extended from the Indus to the Narmada and from Gujarat to Bengal.
It extended from Kabul to Tamil Nadu and from Gujarat to Assam.
It extended from Bengal to Afghanistan and from Kashmir to the Godavari.
It was confined to northern India and did not reach the Deccan.
129.x: The extent of Akbar's empire is described as stretching from Bengal to Afghanistan and from Kashmir to the Godavari.
129.tq: Test a geographical extent through both of its stated boundaries.
xs: Akbar's empire ran from **Bengal to Afghanistan** and from **Kashmir to the Godavari** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It did reach the Deccan: **Ahmednagar** (**1600**) and **Khandesh** (**1601**).
xa: **Kashmir** was taken in **1586** from Yusuf Shah Chak.
**Kabul** was taken in **1581** from Mirza Hakim.
Golconda's **Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah** kept friendly relations with Akbar.

129.s: The Battle of Haldighati formed part of Akbar's campaign against:
129.x: The Battle of Haldighati was part of Akbar's Mewar campaign. It was fought between the Mughal forces led by Man Singh and Maharana Pratap.
129.tq: Distinguish the broader campaign from nearby Rajput regions.
xs: **Haldighati** was part of Akbar's campaign against **Mewar** — so option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ Some notes wrongly place it in the **Gujarat** campaign.
In **Marwar** it was **Rao Chandrasena** who resisted; **Khandesh** and **Malwa** were separate campaigns.
xa: Haldighati (**1576**): **Maharana Pratap** vs Mughals under **Man Singh**; not decisive.
Mewar submitted only under **Jahangir** (**Amar Singh**).
The siege of **Chittor** (**1568**) was against **Rana Udai Singh**.

129.s: In 1562, Akbar entered into a matrimonial alliance with the daughter of:
129.x: In 1562, Akbar married the daughter of Raja Bharmal of Amber, a Kachhwaha ruler.
129.tq: Test the exact person and state connected with the matrimonial alliance.
xs: In **1562** Akbar married the daughter of **Raja Bharmal of Amber** (Kachhwaha) — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Miran Bahadur** lost Asirgarh; **Rao Chandrasena** resisted in Marwar; **Rana Udai Singh** defended Chittor.
xa: **Man Singh** and **Bhagwan Das** were top mansabdars.
**Man Singh I**, Kachhwaha of Amber, led the Mughals at **Haldighati**.

129.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Akbar's Rajput policy:
1. Rajputs were appointed to high posts.
2. Matrimonial alliances formed part of the policy.
3. Religious toleration helped secure lasting Rajput loyalty.
4. Every Rajput state was immediately deprived of its autonomy after submission.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
129.x: Akbar appointed Rajputs to high posts, formed matrimonial alliances and followed religious toleration. Submission could be followed by restoration of autonomy and honour, so statement 4 is false.
129.tq: Reject the absolute statement that conflicts with the conquest-plus-conciliation approach.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3 only** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statements 1 and 2: Rajputs got **high posts** and **matrimonial alliances**.
Statement 3: **religious toleration** and equal treatment won **lasting loyalty**.
Statement 4 is wrong: after submission, **autonomy and honour were returned**.
xa: The policy was **conquest and conciliation**.
Prominent Rajputs: **Raja Man Singh**, **Raja Todarmal**, **Raja Birbal**.

129.s:
Consider the following statements about the Rajput holdouts against Akbar:
1. Mewar submitted to Akbar soon after the Battle of Haldighati.
2. Rao Chandrasen resisted Akbar in Marwar.
3. Mewar submitted only under Jahangir, through Amar Singh, whose son Karan Singh became a mansabdar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
129.x: Statement 1 is wrong: Mewar never submitted under Akbar; Rana Pratap fought on after Haldighati (1576). Statement 2 is correct: Rao Chandrasen resisted in Marwar. Statement 3 is correct: Mewar submitted under Jahangir (Amar Singh; son Karan Singh made a mansabdar). Hence only '2 and 3 only' fits; '1 and 2 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement, and '3 only' misses statement 2.
129.tq: Mewar = never under Akbar; submitted under Jahangir. Marwar holdout = Rao Chandrasen.
xs: Statements **2 and 3 only** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is wrong: **Mewar never submitted** under Akbar; **Rana Pratap** fought on after **Haldighati (1576)**.
Statement 2 is correct: **Rao Chandrasen** resisted in **Marwar**.
Statement 3 is correct: Mewar submitted under **Jahangir** (**Amar Singh**); his son **Karan Singh** became a mansabdar.
xa: Haldighati was **not decisive**.
Haldighati is a UPPSC **2023** question.

129.s: The Zabti or Dahsala system was designed by
129.x: Raja Todar Mal designed the Zabti, also called Bandobast or Dahsala, revenue system.
129.tq: Test the administrator–revenue-system association.
xs: **Raja Todar Mal** designed the **Zabti / Bandobast / Dahsala** system — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Abul Fazl** wrote the **Akbarnama**; **Man Singh** was a general; **Birbal** a wit and adviser.
xa: It was modelled on **Sher Shah's** survey-based system.
Land was measured with the bamboo **Gaz-i-Ilahi** (about **82** cm).
Revenue = **one-third** of average produce of the last **10** years.

129.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Batai — crop-sharing
2. Kankut — estimation of standing crop
3. Nasaq — rough assessment based on past payments
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
129.x: Batai involved division of the harvested crop, Kankut estimated the standing crop, and Nasaq relied roughly on the peasant's past payments.
129.tq: Match each revenue term with its defining assessment method.
xs: All three pairs are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Batai / Ghallabakshi** = **crop-sharing** between state and peasant.
**Kankut** = revenue by **estimation** of the standing crop; **Nasaq** = rough assessment from **past payments**.
xa: **Zabti** used measurement and **10**-year averages, paid in cash.
Relief came through **Taccavi** loans.

129.s: Which statement regarding Raja Todar Mal is correct?
o: He served Aurangzeb and had earlier served Murshid Quli Khan.
He served only the Qutb Shahis and introduced the Pargana system.
He was a provincial Qazi who designed the Mansabdari system.
He served Akbar and had earlier served Sher Shah.
129.x: Todar Mal was Akbar's revenue minister and had earlier served Sher Shah. His system was modelled on Sher Shah's survey-based arrangements.
129.tq: Use the predecessor-service link to distinguish Todar Mal from other administrative figures.
xs: **Todar Mal** served **Akbar** and had earlier served **Sher Shah** — so option **(4)** is correct.
His Zabti was modelled on **Sher Shah's survey-based system**.
xa: He designed the **Zabti / Bandobast (dahsala)** in **1580**.
He is listed among the prominent Rajputs with **Man Singh** and **Birbal**.
He died in **1589**.

129.s: Under Akbar's Zabti system, land that had been left fallow for three to four years was classified as:
129.x: Chachar was land fallow for 3-4 years. Polaj was cultivated every year, Parauti was fallow for 1-2 years, and Banjar was uncultivated for 5 years or more.
129.tq: Polaj (every year) -> Parauti (1-2) -> Chachar (3-4) -> Banjar (5+).
xs: Land fallow for **3-4 years** was **Chachar** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Polaj** = cultivated every year; **Parauti** = fallow **1-2** years; **Banjar** = uncultivated **5** years or more.
xa: Sher Shah had only **three** land classes.
Akbar-Todar Mal used **four** classes and **ten-year averages**.

129.s: Abul Fazl was murdered in 1602 by:
o: Man Singh I at Akbar's instance
Adham Khan at Bairam Khan's instance
Bir Singh Bundela at Salim's instance
129.x: Abul Fazl was murdered in 1602 by Bir Singh Bundela at the instance of Prince Salim.
129.tq: Use the wrong-person and wrong-instigator trap in a court event.
xs: **Abul Fazl** was murdered in **1602** by **Bir Singh Bundela** at **Salim's** instance — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Adham Khan** belongs to the **petticoat government**; **Hemu** died at **Panipat II**.
xa: Abul Fazl wrote the **Akbarnama** and **Ain-i-Akbari**.
He was the chief exponent of **Din-i-Ilahi**.
Order of deaths: **Sheikh Mubarak → Faizi → Abul Fazl → Prince Daniyal** (UPPSC **2024**).

129.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Person)
a. Faizi
b. Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khanan (son of Bairam Khan)
c. Badauni
d. Nizamuddin Ahmad
List-II (Work)
i. Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh
ii. Tabaqat-i-Akbari
iii. Persian translation of Lilavati
iv. Persian translation of the Baburnama
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
129.x: Faizi, the poet laureate, made the Persian Lilavati (a–iii); Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khanan, son of Bairam Khan, translated the Baburnama into Persian (b–iv); Badauni wrote the Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh (c–i); Nizamuddin Ahmad wrote the Tabaqat-i-Akbari (d–ii). The second option swaps Faizi and Rahim, the third credits Tabaqat-i-Akbari to Badauni (the common trap), and the fourth gives Faizi Badauni's work.
129.tq: Trap: Tabaqat-i-Akbari is Nizamuddin's, not Badauni's.
xs: **a–iii, b–iv, c–i, d–ii** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Faizi** — Persian **Lilavati**; **Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khanan** — Persian **Baburnama**.
**Badauni** — **Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh**; **Nizamuddin Ahmad** — **Tabaqat-i-Akbari**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes wrongly credit **Tabaqat-i-Akbari** to Badauni.
Faizi was **poet laureate** and Abul Fazl's brother.
The **Razmnama** is the translation of the **Mahabharata**.

129.s:
Arrange the following persons in the order of their deaths:
A. Faizi
B. Prince Daniyal
C. Sheikh Mubarak
D. Abul Fazl
129.x: The order of deaths was Sheikh Mubarak, Faizi, Abul Fazl and Prince Daniyal.
129.tq: Identify the earliest and latest deaths first, then place the two middle figures.
xs: **C, A, D, B** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Sheikh Mubarak → Faizi (1595) → Abul Fazl (1602) → Prince Daniyal** (UPPSC **2024**).
xa: Abul Fazl was murdered by **Bir Singh Bundela** at Salim's instance.
**Shaikh Mubarak** drafted the **Mahzar** (**1579**).
Abul Fazl, Faizi and Shaikh Mubarak were members of **Din-i-Ilahi**.

129.s: Which one of Akbar's court figures, originally named Ramtanu Pandey, is associated with the ragas Miyan ki Malhar and Miyan ki Todi?
129.x: Tansen (Ramtanu Pandey) was the court musician credited with Miyan ki Malhar and Miyan ki Todi. Faizi was the poet laureate, Birbal (Mahesh Das) the wit and adviser, and Abdur Rahim a poet known for Hindi dohas.
129.tq: 'Miyan ki' ragas = Miyan Tansen.
xs: **Tansen** (Ramtanu Pandey) is linked to **Miyan ki Malhar** and **Miyan ki Todi** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Faizi** was the **poet laureate**; **Birbal** (Mahesh Das) the wit and adviser; **Abdur Rahim** a poet of Hindi **dohas**.
xa: Tansen is credited with a **gharana** tradition and linked to **Gwalior**.
**Man Singh I** led the Mughals at Haldighati.

129.s: Which one of the following pairs regarding Akbar's religious measures is correctly matched?
129.x: The pilgrimage tax was abolished in 1563 and jizya was abolished in 1564 according to the commonly used chronology. Some accounts place both abolitions in 1564.
129.tq: Use the numerical comparison and distinguish two closely dated measures.
xs: **Pilgrimage tax — 1563; Jizya — 1564** — so option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ Some older notes give **1564** for both.
xa: **Aurangzeb** reimposed jizya in **1679**.
**Shah Jahan** abolished the pilgrim tax at **Banaras and Allahabad** after **Kavindracharya**'s deputation.

129.s:
Consider the following statements about Akbar's Ibadat Khana:
1. It was built at Fatehpur Sikri in 1575 for interfaith debates.
2. Its debates were opened to Hindus, Jains, Christians and Zoroastrians.
3. It was built in 1582, the year Din-i-Ilahi was proclaimed.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
129.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Ibadat Khana was built at Fatehpur Sikri in 1575 as a forum for interfaith debate. Statement 2 is correct: it was opened to Hindus, Jains, Christians and Zoroastrians. Statement 3 is wrong: 1582 is the year of Din-i-Ilahi, not of the Ibadat Khana. So '1 only' is incomplete and options with 3 are wrong.
129.tq: Sequence: 1575 Ibadat Khana -> 1579 Mahzar -> 1582 Din-i-Ilahi.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: the **Ibadat Khana** was built at **Fatehpur Sikri** in **1575** for interfaith debate.
Statement 2 is correct: it was opened to **Hindus, Jains, Christians and Zoroastrians**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **1582** is the year of **Din-i-Ilahi**.
xa: **1579**: the **Mahzar** made Akbar supreme arbiter.
Guiding principle: **Sulh-i-Kul**.

129.s:
With reference to the Mahzar of 1579, consider the following statements:
1. It made Akbar the supreme arbiter in religious disputes.
2. It was drafted by Shaikh Mubarak.
3. It transferred the Mughal capital to Fatehpur Sikri.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
129.x: The Mahzar of 1579 made Akbar the supreme arbiter in religious disputes and was drafted by Shaikh Mubarak. It had no connection with transferring the capital.
129.tq: Separate the constitutional-religious effect of a decree from an unrelated administrative change.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: the **Mahzar (1579)** made Akbar **supreme arbiter** in religious disputes.
Statement 2 is correct: it was drafted by **Shaikh Mubarak**.
Statement 3 is wrong: it had nothing to do with the capital; the **Ibadat Khana** was at **Fatehpur Sikri**.
xa: It is also called the so-called **Infallibility Decree**.
**Din-i-Ilahi** followed in **1582**.

129.s: Which one of the following represents the central meaning of Sulh-i-Kul?
o: Compulsory conversion to a single faith
129.x: Sulh-i-Kul means universal peace or peace with all and served as a guiding principle of Akbar's policy.
129.tq: Discriminate the exact meaning of a Persian administrative-religious term.
xs: **Sulh-i-Kul** means **"peace with all"** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was the **guiding principle** of Akbar's religious policy.
**Din-i-Ilahi** was **never forced** on anyone, so compulsory conversion is wrong.
xa: Measures: abolition of **jizya** (**1564**) and **pilgrimage tax** (**1563**), **Ibadat Khana**, **Mahzar**.
Shaikh Ahmad **Sirhindi** attacked Sulh-i-kul and Din-i-Ilahi.
Akbar's coins showed **Rama and Sita** with the legend **'Rama-Siya'**.

129.s:
Match the following taxes with their descriptions.
List-I
(a) Zakat
(b) Ushr
(c) Khums
(d) Jizya
List-II
(i) Poll tax on non-Muslims
(ii) Alms tax on Muslims
(iii) Land tax on Muslims
(iv) One-fifth of war booty
Choose the correct answer using the code given below.
129.x: Zakat was an alms tax on Muslims, ushr was a land tax on Muslims, khums represented one-fifth of war booty, and jizya was imposed on non-Muslims.
129.tq: Start with the sure jizya pair and complete the tax classifications.
xs: **a–ii, b–iii, c–iv, d–i** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Zakat** = alms tax on Muslims; **Ushr** = land tax on Muslims.
**Khums** = one-fifth of war booty; **Jizya** = poll tax on non-Muslims.
xa: Jizya: abolished by Akbar (**1564**), reimposed by Aurangzeb (**1679**).
Pilgrim tax: abolished by Akbar in **1563**.

129.s:
Arrange the following measures in chronological order:
A. Mahzar
B. Abolition of jizya
C. Construction of Ibadat Khana
D. Proclamation of Din-i-Ilahi
129.x: The sequence is abolition of jizya in 1564, construction of the Ibadat Khana in 1575, Mahzar in 1579 and Din-i-Ilahi in 1582.
129.tq: Fix the first and last events, then arrange the middle dates.
xs: **B, C, A, D** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Jizya abolished (1564)** → **Ibadat Khana (1575)**.
xa: The **pilgrimage tax** went in **1563**.
The Mahzar was drafted by **Shaikh Mubarak**.
Jizya was reimposed in **1679** by **Aurangzeb**.

129.s: Which Mughal emperor issued coins bearing figures of Rama and Sita with the Devanagari legend 'Rama-Siya'?
129.x: Akbar, in keeping with Sulh-i-Kul, issued coins with Rama and Sita and the legend 'Rama-Siya' (UPPSC 2011). Babur was an orthodox Sunni who took the title Ghazi, Jahangir is known for his own portrait/zodiac coinage, and Aurangzeb reversed tolerance.
129.tq: Rama-Siya coins = Akbar's Sulh-i-Kul.
xs: **Akbar** issued coins with **Rama and Sita** and the Devanagari legend **'Rama-Siya'** (UPPSC **2011**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Babur** was an orthodox Sunni who took the title **Ghazi**; **Aurangzeb** reversed tolerance.
xa: The coins reflect **Sulh-i-Kul** ("peace with all").
**Jahangir** broadly continued Akbar's tolerance.
Akbar was the **unlettered** emperor, yet a great patron.

129.s: The first Jesuit mission to Akbar's court in 1580 was led by:
o: Dastur Meherji Rana and Guru Ram Das
Jerome Xavier and Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi
129.x: The first Jesuit mission from Goa in 1580 was led by Rudolf Acquaviva and Antonio Monserrate.
129.tq: Match the mission year with its correct representatives.
xs: The **first** Jesuit mission (**1580**) was led by **Rudolf Acquaviva** and **Antonio Monserrate** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Dastur Meherji Rana** (Parsi) and **Guru Ram Das** (Sikh) got land grants.
**Hiravijaya Suri** and **Jinachandra Suri** were Jains; **Jerome Xavier** led the **third** mission.
xa: The second mission came in **1591**.
The missions came from **Goa**.

129.s: The third Jesuit mission to Akbar's court in 1595 was conducted under the leadership of:
129.x: The third Jesuit mission, sent in 1595, was under Jerome Xavier.
129.tq: Distinguish the leader of the later mission from those of the first mission.
xs: The **third** Jesuit mission (**1595**) was led by **Jerome Xavier** (CGPSC **2022**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Rudolf Acquaviva** and **Antonio Monserrate** led the **first** (**1580**).
**Dastur Meherji Rana** was a **Parsi** leader.
xa: The second mission came in **1591**.
The Ibadat Khana was opened to **Christians** among others.

129.s:
Consider the following statements about Akbar's contacts with religious leaders:
1. The Jain scholar Hiravijaya Suri was given the title 'Jagat Guru'.
2. Jinachandra Suri was also given the title 'Jagat Guru'.
3. Akbar granted land to the Parsi leader Dastur Meherji Rana.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
129.x: Statement 1 is correct: Hiravijaya Suri was 'Jagat Guru'. Statement 2 is wrong: Jinachandra Suri was given the title 'Yuga Pradhan'. Statement 3 is correct: Akbar granted land to Dastur Meherji Rana. So '1 only' misses statement 3, and options with 2 are wrong.
129.tq: Hiravijaya = Jagat Guru; Jinachandra = Yuga Pradhan.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Hiravijaya Suri** got the title **"Jagat Guru"** (CGPSC **2024**).
Statement 2 is wrong: **Jinachandra Suri** got **"Yuga Pradhan"**.
Statement 3 is correct: Akbar gave land to Parsi **Dastur Meherji Rana**.
xa: ⚠ "Jagat Guru" = Hiravijaya Suri; "Yuga Pradhan" = Jinachandra Suri.
Land to **Guru Ram Das** → growth of **Amritsar**.

129.s: Akbar's grant of land to Guru Ram Das is associated with the growth of:
129.x: Land granted to Guru Ram Das became associated with the growth of Amritsar.
129.tq: Link the religious leader with the place connected to the grant.
xs: Akbar's land grant to **Guru Ram Das** is where **Amritsar** grew — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Fatehpur Sikri** housed the **Ibadat Khana**.
xa: **Guru Arjan Dev** built the **Golden Temple (Harmandir)** at Amritsar.
Guru Arjan Dev was **executed by Jahangir (1606)**.
Akbar also gave land to Parsi **Dastur Meherji Rana**.

129.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature associated with Din-i-Ilahi?
o: Reverence for the sun and fire
129.x: Din-i-Ilahi included belief in one God, reverence for the sun and fire, and avoidance of meat-eating. It was never forcibly imposed on anyone.
129.tq: Reject the extreme compulsory feature that contradicts the voluntary character of the order.
xs: **Compulsory conversion of all subjects** was not a feature — Din-i-Ilahi was **never forced on anyone** — so option **(1)** is the answer.
Its features included **one God**, **reverence for sun and fire** and **avoiding meat**.
xa: Other features: greeting **"Allah-hu-Akbar"**, readiness to sacrifice wealth, high character.
Proclaimed in **1582**.
Orthodox critics: **Badauni** and Naqshbandi **Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi**.

129.s: Who was the only Hindu member of Din-i-Ilahi?
129.x: Birbal was the only Hindu member of Din-i-Ilahi. The circle of members was small, numbering about 18 according to the cited account.
129.tq: Distinguish the sole Hindu member from other prominent Hindu officials at Akbar's court.
xs: **Birbal** was the **only Hindu** disciple of Din-i-Ilahi — so option **(3)** is correct.
The circle was small — about **18** members.
xa: Other members: **Abul Fazl, Faizi and Shaikh Mubarak**.
Birbal (Mahesh Das) was killed in **1586** fighting the **Yusufzai**.
**Man Singh** and **Todar Mal** are not listed as members.

129.s:
Assertion (A): Din-i-Ilahi did not become a mass religion in Akbar's empire.
Reason (R): It was never forced on anyone and attracted only a small circle of members.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
129.x: Both statements are true, and the voluntary nature and small membership of Din-i-Ilahi explain why it did not become a mass religion.
129.tq: Check whether the reason directly accounts for the limited spread of the doctrine.
xs: Both **A and R are true**, and R is the **correct explanation** of A — so option **(1)** is correct.
Din-i-Ilahi was **never forced on anyone** and drew only a **small circle** (about **18**).
Only a handful joined, and it **lapsed with Akbar**.
xa: Debate: new religion or a **discipleship order**?
**Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi** (**Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani**) attacked it and propounded **Wahdat-ul-Shuhud**.
The **Naqshbandi** order, founded by **Baha-ud-din Naqshband**, came to India with **Babur**.

129.s: Who among the following criticised Din-i-Ilahi and Sulh-i-Kul from an orthodox Islamic standpoint?
129.x: Badauni and the Naqshbandi scholar Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi criticised Akbar's religious innovations, including Din-i-Ilahi and Sulh-i-Kul.
129.tq: Match the criticism with the correct orthodox scholars rather than with supporters or foreign visitors.
xs: Orthodox criticism of Akbar's religious innovations came from **Badauni** and the Naqshbandi **Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Sirhindi** (**Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani**) attacked Akbar's **Sulh-i-kul** and **Din-i-Ilahi**.
**Faizi** and **Abul Fazl** were members of Din-i-Ilahi; **Abul Fazl** was its chief exponent.
**Hiravijaya Suri** and **Jinachandra Suri** were Jain monks honoured by Akbar; **Acquaviva** and **Jerome Xavier** led Jesuit missions from Goa.
xa: **Naqshbandi** order: founded by **Baha-ud-din Naqshband**; came to India with **Babur**; stressed strict **Sharia**.
Sirhindi propounded **Wahdat-ul-Shuhud** (Unity of Appearance) against **Wahdat-ul-Wujud**.
**Badauni** wrote the **Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh**.
Din-i-Ilahi (**1582**) had about **18** members; **Birbal** was the only Hindu disciple.

129.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi was known as Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani.
2. Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi propounded Wahdat-ul-Wujud.
3. Shah Waliullah and Shah Abdul Aziz were later scholars of the Naqshbandi tradition.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
129.x: Statement 1 is correct: Sirhindi was Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani. Statement 2 is wrong: he propounded Wahdat-ul-Shuhud (Unity of Appearance) against Wahdat-ul-Wujud, which was the Qadiri stand followed by Dara Shikoh. Statement 3 is correct. So '1 only' misses 3, and options with 2 are wrong.
129.tq: Naqshbandi/Sirhindi = Shuhud; Qadiri/Dara Shikoh = Wujud.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi** was known as **Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani**.
Statement 2 wrong: he propounded **Wahdat-ul-Shuhud** (Unity of Appearance), opposing **Wahdat-ul-Wujud**.
Statement 3 correct: **Shah Waliullah** and **Shah Abdul Aziz** were later scholars of the tradition.
xa: **Wahdat-ul-Wujud** was the stand of the **Qadiri** order; **Dara Shikoh** followed it.
Sirhindi attacked Akbar's **Sulh-i-kul** and **Din-i-Ilahi**.
The **Naqshbandi** order was founded by **Baha-ud-din Naqshband** and came to India with **Babur**.

129.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Order)
a. Qadiri
b. Naqshbandi

List-II (Feature)
i. Founded by Baha-ud-din Naqshband
ii. Associated with Abdul Qadir Jilani
iii. Orthodox orientation and Wahdat-ul-Shuhud
iv. Dara Shikoh was a follower

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
129.x: The Qadiri order is associated with Abdul Qadir Jilani and Dara Shikoh, while the Naqshbandi order was founded by Baha-ud-din Naqshband and had an orthodox Wahdat-ul-Shuhud orientation.
129.tq: Start from the distinctive founder and follower pairs.
xs: **Qadiri: a–ii, iv; Naqshbandi: b–i, iii** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Qadiri** order: founder **Abdul Qadir Jilani**; stand **Wahdat-ul-Wujud**; **Dara Shikoh** a follower.
**Naqshbandi** order: founder **Baha-ud-din Naqshband**; orthodox, **Wahdat-ul-Shuhud**.
xa: The Naqshbandi order came to India with **Babur** and stressed strict **Sharia**.
**Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi** (**Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani**), a Naqshbandi, criticised **Sulh-i-kul** and **Din-i-Ilahi**.
Later Naqshbandi scholars: **Shah Waliullah** and **Shah Abdul Aziz**.

129.s: Who among the following Mughal emperors was unlettered but became a great patron of learning and culture?
129.x: Akbar was unlettered, yet he was a great patron of learning, literature and culture.
129.tq: Use the distinctive contrast between personal literacy and cultural patronage.
xs: **Akbar** was the **unlettered** (illiterate) Mughal emperor, yet a great patron — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Babur** wrote his memoirs (**Tuzuk-i-Baburi**) in **Turki**; **Humayun** was learned in Persian, Arabic, Turkish, mathematics and **astronomy**.
**Jahangir** wrote his memoir, the **Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri**.
xa: Akbar's court produced the **Razmnama** (Persian translation of the **Mahabharata**); the **Atharvaveda** was also translated.
**Abul Fazl** wrote the **Akbarnama** and **Ain-i-Akbari**.
Akbar broadened the curriculum to include ethics, arithmetic, agriculture, geometry, astronomy, medicine, logic and history.
**Aurangzeb** was learned in Arabic and Persian and played the **veena**.

129.s: Which of the following statements about the Mughal emperors is correct?
o: Babur adopted the title Zinda Pir.
Shah Jahan received the title 'Shah Jahan' from Jahangir.
Aurangzeb was known as Nur-ud-din Muhammad Jahangir.
129.x: Jahangir gave Prince Khurram the title 'Shah Jahan'. Alamgir and Zinda Pir were associated with Aurangzeb, while Nur-ud-din Muhammad Jahangir was Jahangir's title.
129.tq: Use swapped royal titles as the principal trap.
xs: **Shah Jahan** received the title **"Shah Jahan" from Jahangir** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Zinda Pir** was a name of **Aurangzeb**, not Babur.
**Nur-ud-din Muhammad Jahangir** was Jahangir's coronation name; **Alamgir** was Aurangzeb's title.
xa: **Babur** took the title **Padshah** and, at **Khanwa**, the title **Ghazi**.
Aurangzeb was also called **Darvesh**; he was learned in Arabic and Persian.
**Akbar** was the **unlettered** emperor; **Humayun** was learned in **astronomy** and mathematics.

129.s:
Consider the following statements about translations made under Akbar:
1. The Mahabharata was translated as the Razmnama.
2. The Atharvaveda was also translated.
3. The Razmnama was Jahangir's memoir.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
129.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Mahabharata was rendered as the Razmnama and the Atharvaveda was also translated. Statement 3 is wrong: Jahangir's memoir is the Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri. So '1 only' leaves out a true statement, and every option containing 3 is wrong.
129.tq: Razmnama = Mahabharata; 'Tuzuk' = memoir (Baburi / Jahangiri).
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: the **Mahabharata** was translated as the **Razmnama**.
Statement 2 correct: the **Atharvaveda** was also translated.
Statement 3 wrong: the Razmnama is a translation; Jahangir's memoir is the **Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri**.
xa: **Faizi** (Abul Fazl's brother) made the Persian **Lilavati**.
**Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khanan** made a Persian translation of the **Baburnama**.
**Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh** — **Badauni**; **Tabaqat-i-Akbari** — **Nizamuddin Ahmad**.

129.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Emperor)
 a. Babur
 b. Humayun
 c. Jahangir
 d. Aurangzeb

List-II (Description)
 i. Learned in Persian, Arabic, Turkish, mathematics and astronomy
 ii. Memoir titled Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri
 iii. Autobiography in Chaghatai Turkish
 iv. Known as Alamgir and Zinda Pir

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
129.x: Babur wrote in Chaghatai Turkish, Humayun learned the listed subjects, Jahangir wrote the Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri, and Aurangzeb was known as Alamgir and Zinda Pir.
129.tq: Start from the sure memoir pair and eliminate the remaining mismatches.
xs: **a–iii, b–i, c–ii, d–iv** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Babur** — autobiography in **Chaghatai Turkish** (Tuzuk-i-Baburi); **Humayun** — learned in Persian, Arabic, Turkish, mathematics, **astronomy**.
**Jahangir** — **Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri**; **Aurangzeb** — **Alamgir**, **Zinda Pir**.
xa: **Akbar** was the **unlettered** emperor.
**Shah Jahan** got his title from **Jahangir**.
Jahangir was crowned as **Nur-ud-din Muhammad Jahangir**; Aurangzeb played the **veena**.

129.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Guru Hargobind — compilation of Adi Granth
129.x: Guru Hargobind built the Akal Takht, was imprisoned at Gwalior and fought at Kartarpur. The Adi Granth was compiled by Guru Arjan Dev.
129.tq: Find the deed assigned to the wrong Sikh Guru.
xs: **Guru Hargobind — compilation of Adi Granth** is wrongly matched — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **Adi Granth (1604)** was compiled by **Guru Arjan Dev**.
Guru Hargobind did build the **Akal Takht**, was imprisoned at **Gwalior** and fought the Battle of **Kartarpur**.
xa: Guru Hargobind (**6th** Guru) **militarised** the Sikhs.
**Guru Tegh Bahadur**, the 9th Guru, was Guru Hargobind's son.
Guru Arjan Dev was **executed by Jahangir (1606)** for supporting **Khusrau**.

129.s:
Consider the following statements about Guru Tegh Bahadur:
1. He was the ninth Sikh Guru, born Tyag Mal at Amritsar in 1621, and was Guru from 1665 to 1675.
2. He founded Anandpur Sahib (Chak Nanki) and has 116 hymns in the Guru Granth Sahib.
3. He was executed by Jahangir in 1606 for supporting the rebel prince Khusrau.
4. He was called 'Hind-di-Chadar' for shielding Kashmiri Pandits from forced conversion.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
129.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct: ninth Guru, born Tyag Mal (1621), Guru 1665-75; founder of Anandpur Sahib with 116 hymns in the Guru Granth Sahib; 'Hind-di-Chadar'. Statement 3 is wrong: it describes Guru Arjan Dev; Tegh Bahadur was executed on Aurangzeb's orders at Chandni Chowk, Delhi, in 1675. So '1 and 2 only' misses 4, and options with 3 are wrong.
129.tq: Arjan Dev - Jahangir - 1606; Tegh Bahadur - Aurangzeb - 1675.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 4** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **9th** Guru, born **Tyag Mal** at Amritsar in **1621**; Guru **1665-75**.
Statement 2 correct: founded **Anandpur Sahib** (Chak Nanki); **116 hymns** in the Guru Granth Sahib.
Statement 3 wrong: that is **Guru Arjan Dev**; Tegh Bahadur was beheaded at **Chandni Chowk** on **Aurangzeb's** orders, **24 Nov 1675**.
Statement 4 correct: **"Hind-di-Chadar"** for shielding **Kashmiri Pandits**.
xa: ⚠ **Sis Ganj Sahib** = execution site; **Rakab Ganj Sahib** = cremation site.
His martyrdom is observed as **Shaheedi Divas, 24 November**.
He was the son of **Guru Hargobind**.

129.s: Guru Tegh Bahadur was executed by Aurangzeb at Chandni Chowk, Delhi, in
129.x: Guru Tegh Bahadur was executed at Chandni Chowk in Delhi in 1675 by order of Aurangzeb.
129.tq: Match the execution site and ruler with the correct year.
xs: Guru Tegh Bahadur was executed at **Chandni Chowk, Delhi** in **1675** — so option **(2)** is correct.
He was beheaded on **24 Nov 1675** on **Aurangzeb's** orders.
xa: **Gurudwara Sis Ganj Sahib** marks the execution site; **Rakab Ganj Sahib** the cremation site.
Called **"Hind-di-Chadar"** for shielding **Kashmiri Brahmins** from forced conversion.
**1699**: his son **Guru Gobind Singh** founded the **Khalsa** on Baisakhi.
Aurangzeb reimposed **jizya** in **1679**.

129.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Sis Ganj — Cremation place of Guru Tegh Bahadur
Rakab Ganj — Execution place of Guru Tegh Bahadur
Sis Ganj — Execution place of Guru Tegh Bahadur
Muktsar — Execution place of Guru Tegh Bahadur
129.x: Sis Ganj marks the execution place of Guru Tegh Bahadur, while Rakab Ganj marks his cremation place.
129.tq: Discriminate between two closely associated sacred places.
xs: **Sis Ganj — execution place** of Guru Tegh Bahadur — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Rakab Ganj** is the **cremation** site, not the execution site (and Sis Ganj is not the cremation site).
**Muktsar** is the battle where the **Chali Mukte** died defending **Guru Gobind Singh**.
xa: Execution: **Chandni Chowk, Delhi**, **24 Nov 1675**, on **Aurangzeb's** orders.
**Shaheedi Divas: 24 November** marks his martyrdom.
He founded **Anandpur Sahib** (Chak Nanki) and has **116 hymns** in the Guru Granth Sahib.

129.s: Which statement best describes Guru Gobind Singh's conflict with Aurangzeb?
o: He fought the British and authored the Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri.
He never engaged in military conflict and only compiled scriptures.
He fought one war and accepted Mughal sovereignty through the Adi Granth.
He fought 14 wars and authored the Zafarnama.
129.x: Guru Gobind Singh fought 14 wars against Aurangzeb's forces and wrote the Zafarnama, which advocated using the sword only when all other avenues failed.
129.tq: Reject exaggerated or historically misplaced ruler-and-work combinations.
xs: **Guru Gobind Singh** fought **14 wars** against Aurangzeb and wrote the **Zafarnama** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **Zafarnama** says the **sword only when all avenues fail**.
The **Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri** is Jahangir's memoir; the **Adi Granth** was compiled by **Guru Arjan Dev**.
xa: He founded the **Khalsa** on **13 April 1699** (Baisakhi) at **Takht Keshgarh Sahib** with the **Panj Pyaras**.
His **four Sahibzade** were martyred.
**Battle of Muktsar**: the **Chali Mukte** (40 liberated ones) died defending him — commemorated as **Maghi**.

129.s: The Chali Mukte are associated with which event?
o: The release of Guru Hargobind from Gwalior Fort
The founding of the Khalsa at Anandpur
The compilation of the Adi Granth at Amritsar
The defence of Guru Gobind Singh at Muktsar
129.x: The Chali Mukte, or 40 liberated ones, died defending Guru Gobind Singh at Muktsar; the event is commemorated as Maghi.
129.tq: Identify the event linked to a distinctive commemorative name.
xs: The **Chali Mukte** died **defending Guru Gobind Singh at Muktsar** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Chali Mukte** = the **40 liberated ones**; the event is commemorated as **Maghi**.
Guru Hargobind was imprisoned at **Gwalior**; the **Adi Granth** was compiled by **Guru Arjan Dev**.
xa: The **Khalsa** was founded on **13 April 1699** (Baisakhi) at **Takht Keshgarh Sahib**.
Guru Gobind Singh fought **14 wars** with Aurangzeb and wrote the **Zafarnama**.
His disciple **Banda Singh Bahadur** conquered **Sirhind (1710)** to avenge the Guru's younger sons.

129.s: The Adi Granth was compiled in 1604 by:
129.x: Guru Arjan compiled the Adi Granth in 1604.
129.tq: Use the specific contribution and year to distinguish the Gurus.
xs: The **Adi Granth** was compiled in **1604** by **Guru Arjan** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Guru Arjan Dev was the **5th** Guru; he also built the **Golden Temple** (Harmandir), Amritsar.
**Guru Tegh Bahadur** (9th) founded **Anandpur Sahib**; **Guru Gobind Singh** (10th) founded the **Khalsa**.
xa: Guru Arjan Dev was **executed by Jahangir (1606)** for supporting rebel prince **Khusrau**.
**Guru Tegh Bahadur** has **116 hymns** in the Guru Granth Sahib.
Akbar granted land to **Guru Ram Das**, where **Amritsar** grew.

129.s: The Khalsa was founded by Guru Gobind Singh on Baisakhi day in the year:
129.x: Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa on 13 April 1699 (Baisakhi) with the Panj Pyaras. 1675 is Guru Tegh Bahadur's martyrdom, and 1710 is Banda Singh Bahadur's conquest of Sirhind; 1704 is not the Khalsa's date.
129.tq: Khalsa = Baisakhi, 13 April 1699.
xs: The **Khalsa** was founded on **13 April 1699** (Baisakhi) — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was founded at **Takht Keshgarh Sahib** with the **Panj Pyaras**.
**1675** = Guru Tegh Bahadur's martyrdom; **1710** = Banda Singh Bahadur's conquest of **Sirhind**.
xa: **Baisakhi** is recalled as Khalsa foundation day.
Guru Gobind Singh fought **14 wars** with Aurangzeb and wrote the **Zafarnama**.
⚠ **Sirhind Fateh Diwas (12-14 May)** marks Banda Singh's **1710** conquest — not Baisakhi.

129.s:
Consider the following statements about Banda Singh Bahadur:
1. Originally Lachhman Dev, he was a disciple of Guru Gobind Singh.
2. After taking Samana (1709), he defeated Wazir Khan at Chappar Chiri and conquered Sirhind in 1710.
3. His sovereign Sikh state had its capital at Anandpur Sahib.
4. He abolished zamindari, issued coins in the Gurus' names and was executed in Delhi in 1716 by Farrukhsiyar.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
129.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the capital of the first sovereign Sikh state was Lohgarh; Anandpur Sahib was founded by Guru Tegh Bahadur. So '1 and 2 only' misses 4, and options with 3 are wrong.
129.tq: Banda: Lachhman Dev, Sirhind 1710 (Wazir Khan), capital Lohgarh, executed 1716.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 4** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: born **Lachhman Dev**, a disciple of **Guru Gobind Singh**.
Statement 2 correct: took **Samana (1709)**, defeated **Wazir Khan** at **Chappar Chiri** and conquered **Sirhind (1710)**.
Statement 3 wrong: the capital was **Lohgarh**; **Anandpur Sahib** was founded by Guru Tegh Bahadur.
Statement 4 correct: abolished **zamindari**, struck coins in the Gurus' names; executed by **Farrukhsiyar** in **1716**.
xa: He founded the **first sovereign Sikh state**.
Sirhind was conquered to avenge the Guru's **younger sons**.
**Sirhind Fateh Diwas (12-14 May)** commemorates the **1710** conquest.

129.s:
Consider the following statements about the religious and social composition of the Mughal nobility:
1. Shah Jahan retained a high number of Hindu nobles despite being more orthodox.
2. Aurangzeb had the highest number of Hindu nobles and generals in absolute terms.
3. Many of Aurangzeb's Hindu nobles were Marathas and Rajputs recruited during the Deccan wars.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
129.x: All three statements are correct. Shah Jahan retained many Hindu nobles, and Aurangzeb had the highest absolute number, including Marathas and Rajputs recruited during the Deccan wars.
129.tq: Handle the counter-intuitive comparison by checking absolute number rather than presumed religious orientation.
xs: All three statements — **1, 2 and 3** — are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
Statement 1: **Shah Jahan**, though slightly more orthodox, **retained a high number of Hindu nobles**.
Statement 2: **Aurangzeb** had the **highest number of Hindu nobles/generals** in absolute terms (UPPSC **2000** key).
Statement 3: they were largely **Marathas and Rajputs** taken in during the **Deccan wars**.
xa: This is the counter-intuitive tested fact, since Aurangzeb **reversed tolerance** (jizya **1679**).
Aurangzeb also banned **Navroz** and patronised the **Fatawa-i-Alamgiri**.
Shah Jahan destroyed some **newly built temples**.

129.s: Which one of the following statements best describes Jahangir's religious policy?
o: He broadly continued Akbar's tolerance, though Guru Arjan Dev was executed for political reasons.
He entirely abandoned Akbar's policy of tolerance.
129.x: Jahangir broadly continued Akbar's tolerant approach, but Guru Arjan Dev was executed for political reasons related to support for rebel prince Khusrau.
129.tq: Avoid the extreme claim and retain the ruler-specific qualification.
xs: **Jahangir** broadly **continued Akbar's tolerance**; Guru Arjan Dev's execution was **for political reasons** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **Khalsa (1699)** was founded by **Guru Gobind Singh**.
**Jizya** was reimposed in **1679** by **Aurangzeb**.
xa: **Guru Arjan Dev** was executed in **1606** for supporting rebel prince **Khusrau**.
Jahangir imprisoned **Guru Hargobind** at **Gwalior**.
Jahangir gave Prince Khurram the title **"Shah Jahan"**.

129.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Shah Jahan's religious policy:
1. It was slightly more orthodox than Akbar's policy.
2. Some newly built temples were destroyed during his reign.
3. Hindu nobles were completely excluded from his administration.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
129.x: Shah Jahan was slightly more orthodox and destroyed some newly built temples, but he continued to employ many Hindu nobles. Therefore, statement 3 is false.
129.tq: Reject the absolute exclusion claim while retaining the qualified policy description.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **Shah Jahan** was **slightly more orthodox** than Akbar.
Statement 2 correct: he **destroyed some newly built temples**.
Statement 3 wrong: he **retained a high number of Hindu nobles**.
xa: Shah Jahan abolished the **pilgrim tax at Banaras and Allahabad** after a deputation led by **Kavindracharya**.
**Aurangzeb** had the highest number of Hindu nobles in absolute terms.
Shah Jahan got his title from **Jahangir**.

129.s:
Consider the following statements about Aurangzeb's religious policy:
1. He reimposed jizya in 1679 and banned festivals such as Navroz.
2. He patronised the Fatawa-i-Alamgiri and was called 'Zinda Pir'.
3. He executed Guru Arjan Dev.
4. His reversal of tolerance alienated the Rajputs, Marathas and Sikhs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
129.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Guru Arjan Dev was executed by Jahangir; Aurangzeb executed Guru Tegh Bahadur. So '1 and 2 only' misses 4, and options with 3 are wrong.
129.tq: Match Guru to emperor: Arjan Dev - Jahangir; Tegh Bahadur - Aurangzeb.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 4** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **Aurangzeb** reimposed **jizya in 1679** and banned **Navroz**.
Statement 2 correct: he patronised the **Fatawa-i-Alamgiri** and was called **"Zinda Pir"**.
Statement 3 wrong: **Guru Arjan Dev** was executed by **Jahangir**; Aurangzeb executed **Guru Tegh Bahadur**.
Statement 4 correct: the reversal **alienated Rajputs, Marathas and Sikhs**.
xa: The reversal is cited among the **causes of decline**.
Akbar had abolished jizya in **1564**.
⚠ Aurangzeb still had the **highest number of Hindu nobles** in absolute terms.

129.s: Which development most directly helped transform the Mughal state from a conquest state into a durable empire?
o: The withdrawal from Rajput affairs and restriction of Hindu participation
The exclusive use of Persian in local administration
The abolition of the mansabdari system
The combination of Sulh-i-Kul with partnership with the Rajputs
129.x: Sulh-i-Kul and the Rajput partnership broadened support and helped turn the conquest state into a durable empire.
129.tq: Link the stated policy with its institutional and political consequence.
xs: **Sulh-i-Kul** combined with the **Rajput partnership** turned a conquest state into a durable empire — so option **(4)** is correct.
It underpinned **Rajput and Hindu support**; Rajputs got high posts, matrimonial alliances and autonomy.
Akbar did not withdraw from Rajput affairs, and **mansabdari** was a core of governance, not abolished.
xa: **1562**: Akbar married the daughter of **Raja Bharmal of Amber** (Kachhwaha).
Top Rajput mansabdars: **Man Singh** and **Bhagwan Das**.
**Mewar** never submitted under Akbar; it submitted under **Jahangir** (**Amar Singh**).
Aurangzeb's reversal (jizya **1679**) alienated Rajputs, Marathas and Sikhs.

129.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Din-i-Ilahi has been debated as either a new religion or a discipleship order.
2. Only a handful of people joined it.
3. It continued as a major institution after Akbar’s death.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
129.x: The first two statements are correct. Din-i-Ilahi lapsed with Akbar and did not continue as a major institution after his reign.
129.tq: Reject the overstatement about the size and continuity of a short-lived institution.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: debated as a **new religion or a discipleship order**.
Statement 2 correct: only a **handful** joined (about **18**).
Statement 3 wrong: Din-i-Ilahi **lapsed with Akbar**.
xa: Proclaimed **1582**; features: one God, greeting **"Allah-hu-Akbar"**, avoiding meat, reverence for **sun and fire**.
Members included **Abul Fazl**, **Faizi** and **Shaikh Mubarak**; **Birbal** was the only Hindu.
It was never forced on anyone.

129.s: What condition is described as the jagirdari crisis under Aurangzeb?
o: Too many jagirdars competing for too few jagirs, placing pressure on the peasantry
The complete abolition of jagirs by Akbar
The transfer of all jagirs to Rajput rulers
Too few mansabdars controlling an excessive number of jagirs
129.x: The jagirdari crisis arose because too many mansabdars chased too few jagirs, which increased pressure on the peasantry.
129.tq: Translate the economic consequence into an administrative scenario.
xs: The **jagirdari crisis**: **too many mansabdars chased too few jagirs**, pressing the peasantry — so option **(1)** is correct.
It arose under **Aurangzeb**, not Akbar; jagirs were not abolished or handed to Rajput rulers.
xa: **Mansabdari-jagirdari** and **Zabti** were the core of Mughal governance for **150 years**.
Aurangzeb's reversal of tolerance (jizya **1679**) is also cited among **causes of decline**.
Many of Aurangzeb's Hindu nobles were **Marathas and Rajputs** taken in during the **Deccan wars**.

129.s:
Consider the following statements about Golconda (AP angle):
1. Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah kept friendly relations with Akbar, who sent Masud Beg with gifts.
2. Abul Hasan Tana Shah followed religious tolerance and appointed Madanna and Akkanna to high office.
3. Bhakta Ramadasu was the son of Madanna.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
129.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Bhakta Ramadasu was the nephew of Madanna and Akkanna, not a son. So '1 only' misses 2, and options with 3 are wrong.
129.tq: Ramadasu = nephew of Madanna-Akkanna.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah** kept friendly ties with Akbar, who sent **Masud Beg** with gifts.
Statement 2 correct: **Abul Hasan Tana Shah** was tolerant and appointed **Madanna and Akkanna**.
Statement 3 wrong: **Bhakta Ramadasu** was their **nephew**, not Madanna's son.
xa: Akbar's southern limit reached the **Godavari**.
**Ahmednagar (1600)**: Akbar's forces opposed **Chand Bibi**.
Akbar's **last campaign**: **Asirgarh (1601)** in Khandesh.

129.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Baisakhi — Banda Singh Bahadur’s conquest of Sirhind
Baisakhi — foundation day of the Khalsa
Shaheedi Divas — martyrdom of Guru Tegh Bahadur
Sirhind Fateh Diwas — Banda Singh Bahadur’s conquest of Sirhind
129.x: Baisakhi is associated with the foundation of the Khalsa, not Banda Singh Bahadur’s conquest of Sirhind. The conquest is commemorated by Sirhind Fateh Diwas.
129.tq: Find the event–observance swap among related Sikh commemorations.
xs: **Baisakhi — conquest of Sirhind** is wrongly matched — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Baisakhi** is the Khalsa foundation day (**13 April 1699**).
Banda Singh Bahadur's **1710** conquest of Sirhind is marked by **Sirhind Fateh Diwas (12-14 May)**.
**Shaheedi Divas (24 Nov)** marks Guru Tegh Bahadur's martyrdom.
xa: Banda took Sirhind after defeating **Wazir Khan** at **Chappar Chiri**.
Guru Tegh Bahadur was beheaded at **Chandni Chowk** in **1675**; **Sis Ganj** marks the site.
The **Chali Mukte** at **Muktsar** are commemorated as **Maghi**.

129.s: In which year did Aurangzeb reimpose jizya?
129.x: Aurangzeb reimposed jizya in 1679, reversing Akbar's abolition. 1582 is Din-i-Ilahi, 1579 the Mahzar and 1675 the execution of Guru Tegh Bahadur.
129.tq: Recall the year of each event.
n: Aurangzeb reimposed jizya in 1679. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
xs: Aurangzeb reimposed **jizya** in **1679** — option **(1)**.
**Akbar** had abolished jizya in **1564**.
xa: The **pilgrimage tax** was abolished in **1563** (some notes say **1564**).
**Ibadat Khana**: established **1575**, opened to different religions in **1578**.
**Zakat** = alms tax on Muslims; **Ushr** = land tax on Muslims; **Khums** = one-fifth of war booty.

129.s: Which of the following statements regarding Aurangzeb is incorrect?
o: His second coronation followed victories at Khajwa and Deorai.
His second coronation took place on June 5, 1659.
His first coronation followed his victory over Dara Shikoh at Deorai.
129.x: Option C is incorrect: Aurangzeb's first coronation was on July 21, 1658 at Delhi, months before he beat Dara at Deorai in March 1659. The Khajwa and Deorai victories preceded his second coronation on June 5, 1659.
129.tq: Place each battle before or after each coronation date.
n: Aurangzeb’s first coronation took place on July 21, 1658. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 73-74]
Aurangzeb’s first coronation took place in Delhi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 73-74]
Aurangzeb was coronated twice. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 73-74]
Aurangzeb’s second coronation took place on June 5, 1659. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 73-74]
Aurangzeb’s second coronation followed his victories at Khajwa and Deorai. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 73-74]
xs: The incorrect statement is that his **first coronation followed Deorai** — option **(3)**.
His **first coronation** was on **July 21, 1658** in **Delhi**.
His **second coronation** was on **June 5, 1659**, after victories at **Khajwa** and **Deorai** — so options 1, 2 and 4 are true.
xa: **Akbar** was coronated on **February 14, 1556** at **Kalanaur**.
**Shivaji** was formally crowned in **1674** at **Raigarh**.
**Krishnadeva Raya** was enthroned in **1509**.

129.s:
Assertion (A): Shivaji assumed the title Chhatrapati in 1674.
Reason (R): Gaga Bhatta, also known as Vishweshwar, performed Shivaji's formal coronation.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
129.x: Both are true and R explains A: at the 1674 coronation at Raigarh, performed by Gaga Bhatta (Vishweshwar) of Varanasi, Shivaji was crowned and took the title Chhatrapati.
129.tq: Check whether R is the cause of A.
n: Shivaji was coronated in 1674. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 73-74]
Shivaji underwent a formal coronation. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 73-74]
Shivaji assumed the title Chhatrapati. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 73-74]
Gaga Bhatta, also known as Vishweshwar, performed Shivaji’s coronation. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 73-74]
xs: **Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A** — option **(1)**.
A: **Shivaji** assumed the title **Chhatrapati** at his **1674** coronation at **Raigarh**.
R: the coronation was performed by **Gaga Bhatta** (**Vishweshwar**), who declared Shivaji a **Kshatriya**.
xa: **Shivaji-II** was placed on the throne in **1689** by **Tarabai** after **Rajaram's death**.
**Aurangzeb** was coronated twice: **1658** and **1659**.
**Iltutmish** acceded in **1211**, supported by **Turkish nobles**.

129.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Iltutmish
(b) Akbar
(c) Shivaji
(d) Ashoka

List-II
(i) Was under 14 years of age at coronation
(ii) Worshipped Buddha’s birthplace at Lumbini
(iii) Succession was supported or approved by Turkish nobles
(iv) Was coronated at Raigarh
129.x: Turkish nobles backed Iltutmish after Aibak, Akbar was only 13 when crowned, Shivaji was crowned at Raigarh, and Ashoka worshipped at Buddha's birthplace, Lumbini, giving a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.
129.tq: Link each ruler to his accession detail.
n: Turkish nobles supported or approved Iltutmish’s succession after Qutbuddin Aibak. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 73-74]
Akbar was under 14 years of age at his coronation. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 73-74]
Shivaji was coronated at Raigarh. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 73-74]
Ashoka worshipped Buddha’s birthplace at Lumbini. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 73-74]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii** — option **(3)**.
**Iltutmish**: succession approved by **Turkish nobles** after **Qutbuddin Aibak**.
**Akbar**: **under 14 years** at coronation; **Shivaji**: crowned at **Raigarh**.
**Ashoka**: worshipped **Buddha's birthplace** at **Lumbini** (Rummindei).
xa: Ashoka visited Lumbini in the **twentieth year** after coronation, exempted it from **Bali tax** and cut land revenue to **one-eighth**.
Iltutmish acceded in **1211**; Akbar on **February 14, 1556** at **Kalanaur**.
⚠ Sources differ: some notes say Akbar was aged **14**.

129.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Iltutmish declared himself Sultan at Delhi.
Aurangzeb’s first coronation took place at Kalanaur.
Akbar was enthroned at Kalanaur, Gurdaspur, Punjab.
129.x: Option C is incorrect: Aurangzeb's first coronation was at Delhi, not Kalanaur; Kalanaur is where Akbar was enthroned. Iltutmish at Delhi, Shivaji at Raigarh and Akbar at Kalanaur are right.
129.tq: Match each coronation with its place.
xs: The incorrect statement: **Aurangzeb's first coronation** was **not at Kalanaur** — option **(3)**.
His first coronation was on **July 21, 1658** in **Delhi**.
**Kalanaur** (Gurdaspur, Punjab) is where **Akbar** was enthroned.
**Iltutmish** declared himself Sultan at **Delhi**; **Shivaji** was crowned at **Raigarh** — both true.
xa: Aurangzeb's second coronation was on **June 5, 1659**.
**Bairam Khan** was associated with Akbar's accession.
**Rajaraja-I** acceded in **985**, beginning the Chola golden era.

129.s: On which date was Akbar enthroned?
129.x: Akbar was enthroned at Kalanaur on February 14, 1556, after Humayun's death. The 1658 and 1659 dates are Aurangzeb's two coronations.
129.tq: Match each coronation date with its ruler.
xs: Akbar was enthroned on **February 14, 1556** — option **(3)**.
He was crowned at **Kalanaur** in **Gurdaspur, Punjab**, by **Bairam Khan**.
**July 21, 1658** and **June 5, 1659** are **Aurangzeb's** two coronations.
xa: **Bairam Khan's regency**: **1556-60**; dismissed **1560**, killed on the way to Mecca **1561**.
**Petticoat government** (**1560-64**): **Maham Anaga** and **Adham Khan**.
Akbar gave Bairam Khan the title **"Khan-i-Khanan"**.

129.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Humayun
(b) Akbar
(c) Jahangir
(d) Shah Jahan

List-II
(i) Mughal architectural zenith and Taj Mahal
(ii) Foundation of Mughal painting
(iii) Imperial expansion, administrative reforms and religious policy
(iv) Zenith of Mughal painting
129.x: Humayun laid the foundation of Mughal painting, Akbar expanded the empire with reforms, Jahangir's reign was the peak of painting and Shah Jahan's the peak of architecture, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
129.tq: Link each Mughal emperor to his main achievement.
n: Humayun was associated with the foundation of Mughal painting. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Akbar undertook imperial expansion. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Akbar introduced administrative reforms. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Akbar pursued a religious policy. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Jahangir's reign marked the zenith of Mughal painting. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Shah Jahan's reign marked the architectural zenith of the Mughal Empire. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]

130.s: The 'Bandobast' system of land revenue under Akbar is another name for:
130.x: The Bandobast system is the Dahsala (Zabti) reform of Todar Mal, introduced in 1580 (JPSC 2013). Batai (ghalla-bakhshi) was crop-sharing, Nasaq a rough assessment from past records mainly in Bengal, and Iqta the Sultanate revenue assignment.
xs: The **Bandobast** system is another name for the **Dahsala** system — so option **(1)** is correct (JPSC **2013** key).
**Batai** was crop-sharing; **Nasaq** a rough assessment from past records, mainly in **Bengal**.
xa: Some notes use "**Zabti or Bandobast**" for the same **Todar Mal** reform.
Dahsala (**1580**) fixed revenue on the average produce and prices of the **last ten years**.
**Kankut** estimated yield on the **standing crop**.

130.s:
Consider the following statements about Mughal revenue terms:
1. Madad-i-maash was a revenue-free grant to scholars, holy men and the needy.
2. Suyurghal was crown land whose revenue went straight to the imperial treasury.
3. Maal (mal), the land revenue, was the principal state income.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
130.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Suyurghal was another name for charitable revenue-free grants like madad-i-maash; crown land whose revenue went to the treasury was khalisa. So '1 only' misses 3, and options with 2 are wrong.
130.tq: Madad-i-maash = Suyurghal (charity); Khalisa = crown land; Maal = land revenue.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **Madad-i-maash** was a revenue-free grant to scholars, holy men and the needy.
Statement 2 wrong: **Suyurghal** is another name for such charitable grants; crown land was **khalisa**.
Statement 3 correct: **Maal (mal)**, land revenue, was the **principal state income**.
xa: **Khalisa** revenue went straight to the imperial treasury; cash (**naqd**) salaries were paid from it.
A **jagir** was a right to collect revenue in lieu of salary — not ownership.
Khalisa expanded in Golconda under **Abdullah** and **Tana Shah**.

130.s: A jagir under the Mughal system represented:
o: A direct cash payment from the khalisa treasury
The right to collect revenue in lieu of salary, without ownership
A permanent revenue-free grant to scholars
130.x: A jagir was an assignment of the right to collect revenue in lieu of salary; it did not confer ownership of the land.
130.tq: Apply the distinction between revenue-collection rights and ownership.
xs: A **jagir** was the **right to collect revenue in lieu of salary**, not ownership — so option **(3)** is correct.
Direct cash salaries came from **khalisa** revenue (**naqd**); revenue-free grants to scholars were **madad-i-maash**.
xa: Mansabdars held **non-hereditary**, combined civil-military ranks **paid by jagir**.
⚠ British **ICS** = purely civil, fixed salary from the treasury.
**Suyurghal** = another name for charitable revenue-free grants.

130.s:
Which of the following officials were associated with a Suba?
1. Subedar
2. Diwan
3. Bakhshi
4. Sadr
5. Qazi
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
130.x: The officials associated with a Suba included the Subedar, Diwan, Bakhshi, Sadr and Qazi.
130.tq: Check the complete composition of the provincial administrative group.
xs: All five — **Subedar, Diwan, Bakhshi, Sadr and Qazi** — served at suba level — so option **(4)** is correct.
The notes list these five officials for the **Suba**.
xa: **Sarkar**: **Faujdar** (law and order) and **amalguzar** (revenue).
**Pargana**: **Shiqdar**, amil, qanungo.

130.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Unit)
a. Sarkar
b. Pargana
c. Town
d. Village
List-II (Officials)
i. Kotwal
ii. Muqaddam, patwari, chowkidar
iii. Faujdar, amalguzar
iv. Shiqdar, amil, qanungo
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
130.x: Sarkar had the faujdar (law and order) and amalguzar (revenue) (a–iii); pargana had the shiqdar, amil and qanungo (b–iv); the town had the kotwal for police and municipal order (c–i); the village had the muqaddam, patwari and chowkidar (d–ii). The second option swaps sarkar and pargana, the third swaps town and village, and the fourth puts the kotwal at sarkar level.
130.tq: Faujdar = sarkar; shiqdar = pargana; kotwal = town; muqaddam = village.
xs: **a–iii, b–iv, c–i, d–ii** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Sarkar** — **Faujdar**, amalguzar; **Pargana** — **Shiqdar**, amil, qanungo.
**Town** — **Kotwal**; **Village** — **Muqaddam**, patwari, chowkidar.
xa: The **Faujdar** handled law and order; the **amalguzar** handled revenue.
The **Kotwal** looked after police and municipal order.
**Suba** officials: Subedar, diwan, bakhshi, sadr, qazi.

130.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Faujdar — military and law-and-order duties at the sarkar level
Subahdar — governor responsible for law and order
Provincial Diwan — revenue administration and an independent check on the governor
Kotwal — maintenance of pargana land and revenue records
130.x: The Kotwal was responsible for law and order in the city. Maintenance of land and revenue records at the pargana level was the duty of the Qanungo.
130.tq: Locate the wrong administrative level attached to the official.
xs: **Kotwal — pargana land and revenue records** is wrongly matched — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **Kotwal** was a **town** official for **police and municipal order**.
Pargana-level officials were the **Shiqdar**, **amil** and **qanungo**.
The **Faujdar** handled **law and order** at the **sarkar** level; the **Subedar** and **diwan** were suba officials.
xa: Sarkar revenue was handled by the **amalguzar**.
Village: **muqaddam** (headman), **patwari**, **chowkidar**.

130.s: Which one of the following best expresses the combined significance of the Mughal mansabdari and zabti-dahsala systems?
o: They provided a salaried and transferable nobility along with predictable cash revenue.
They created a hereditary nobility supported by tribute from autonomous chiefs.
They replaced military service with purely religious endowments.
They abolished all intermediaries and made every village directly taxable in kind.
130.x: The mansabdari and zabti-dahsala arrangements together provided the Mughal state with a salaried, transferable nobility and a predictable stream of cash revenue.
130.tq: Select the option that combines the institutional and fiscal outcomes without adding an unsupported claim.
xs: Together, **mansabdari** and **zabti-dahsala** gave a **salaried, transferable nobility** and **predictable cash revenue** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Mansabdar ranks were **non-hereditary** and paid by **jagir**, so not a hereditary nobility.
xa: ⚠ Mughal mansabdars combined **civil-military** roles; the British **ICS** was purely civil with a fixed salary.
Dahsala (**1580**) fixed cash revenue on the average of the **last ten years**.
State share: **one-third**, paid in **dam**.

130.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes Mughal mansabdars from the British Indian Civil Service (ICS)?
o: Mughal mansabdars were appointed only from hereditary zamindar families, whereas the ICS was recruited from Rajput chiefs.
Mughal mansabdars held combined civil-military, non-hereditary ranks paid by jagir, whereas the ICS was purely civil and paid a fixed salary from the treasury.
Mughal mansabdars were purely civil officials paid fixed salaries, whereas the ICS held military ranks paid by jagirs.
Both Mughal mansabdars and the ICS were hereditary services paid through land assignments.
130.x: Mughal mansabdars combined civil and military functions, held non-hereditary ranks and were paid through jagirs. The British ICS was purely civil and received a fixed salary from the treasury.
130.tq: Split the comparison into functions, hereditary character and mode of payment before choosing the complete distinction.
xs: Mansabdars held **combined civil-military, non-hereditary ranks paid by jagir**; the **ICS** was **purely civil**, paid a **fixed salary from the treasury** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Mansabdars were therefore not purely civil, not hereditary, and not paid fixed treasury salaries.
xa: A **jagir** was the right to collect revenue, **not ownership**.
Cash (**naqd**) salaries were paid against **khalisa** land.
Mansabdari + **zabti-dahsala** gave a salaried, **transferable** nobility.

130.s:
Consider the following statements about land revenue in Qutb Shahi Golconda:
1. Land was classified as wet, dry, garden and waste.
2. The state generally took one-half of the produce.
