4. Urban society consisted exclusively of merchants and soldiers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
136.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Urban society was not exclusively composed of merchants and soldiers.
136.tq: Reject the exclusive statement while retaining the occupational details.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statements 1 and 2: artisans were often in **guilds**, working in state **karkhanas** or **private** enterprises.
Statement 3: **professional groups** were physicians (**hakims**), teachers, lawyers, painters and musicians.
Statement 4 wrong: urban society also had **merchants** (Nagarseths, Marwaris, Bohras, Chettis), artisans and professionals.
xa: Merchants and artisans = **middle and lower urban strata**.
**Pelsaert** contrasted nobles' luxury with the **misery of servants and workmen**.
**Bernier**: no real middle class in **Delhi**.

136.s: Bernier’s observation about the urban society of Delhi was that it
o: had no real middle class, with people tending to be either very rich or very poor
was dominated by peasants who had migrated from villages
had a large and prosperous middle class between the rich and poor
consisted entirely of artisans employed by the state
136.x: Bernier found no real middle class in Delhi and described a sharp contrast between the very rich and the very poor.
136.tq: Recall the traveller’s distinctive social observation.
xs: **Bernier** found **no real middle class** in Delhi — people were **very rich or very poor** — option **(1)**.
He also recorded **Sati**, **child marriage** and **polygamy**.
xa: His "bleak India" view reflects **European bias**, though he still conceded a **prosperous merchant class**.
**Pelsaert** contrasted **nobles' luxury** with the **misery of servants and workmen**.
Travellers' accounts = main source for Mughal social history, read against **Persian chronicles**.

136.s: Firangi Mahal at Lucknow was noted for being a madrasa of
136.x: Firangi Mahal in Lucknow was a madrasa associated with Muslim jurisprudence.
xs: **Firangi Mahal (Lucknow)** was a madrasa of **Muslim jurisprudence** — option **(2)**.
This was the UPPSC **2016** key.
xa: **Nauroz** = **Persian New Year**, adopted from the **Zoroastrians** (UPPSC **2001** key).
**Tuladan** = weighing the emperor against gold and goods on his birthday — a **Hindu** custom adopted by Akbar.

136.s: In 1562, Akbar took which significant measure concerning slavery?
o: He abolished all domestic service in noble households.
He prohibited the employment of servants in royal karkhanas.
He stopped the enslavement of prisoners of war.
He made every slave a mansabdar.
136.x: Akbar stopped the enslavement of prisoners of war in 1562, although slaves and large domestic staffs continued to exist in noble households.
136.tq: Link a precise year with the reform actually introduced.
xs: In **1562** Akbar **stopped the enslavement of prisoners of war** — option **(3)**.
Domestic service did not end: **noble households** were still full of **slaves** and large domestic staffs.
xa: Akbar also tried to stop **forced sati**.
Akbar began **Jharokha darshan** and introduced **sijda / paibos**.
Akbar added **Rajputs** and **Hindustanis** to the nobility.

136.s:
Consider the following statements about Nur Jahan:
1. She married Jahangir in 1611.
2. She held the title Padshah Begum.
3. Her name appeared on coins and farmans.
4. She built the tomb of Itimad-ud-Daula.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
136.x: All four statements are correct. Nur Jahan married Jahangir in 1611, became Padshah Begum, had her name inscribed on coins and farmans, and built Itimad-ud-Daula’s tomb.
136.tq: Test a royal woman through date, title, symbols of authority and architecture.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)**.
Nur Jahan married **Jahangir** in **1611** and was **Padshah Begum**.
Her name appeared on **coins** and **farmans**, and she built **Itimad-ud-Daula's tomb**.
xa: ⚠ Pen name **Makhfi**: some notes give it for Nur Jahan, but it is best known as **Zeb-un-Nissa**'s.
**Jahanara** (Shah Jahan's daughter) was also **Padshah Begum**.
**Gulbadan Begum**, Babur's daughter, wrote the **Humayun-nama**.

136.s: Which of the following works is associated with Jahanara?
o: Jama Masjid at Agra and a sarai at Chandni Chowk
136.x: Jahanara, Shah Jahan’s daughter and Padshah Begum, built the Jama Masjid at Agra and a sarai at Chandni Chowk.
136.tq: Match a royal woman with her architectural contributions.
xs: **Jahanara** built the **Jama Masjid at Agra** and a **sarai at Chandni Chowk** — option **(2)**.
**Six Voyages** is Tavernier's; the **Humayun-nama** is Gulbadan Begum's; **Itimad-ud-Daula's tomb** was built by Nur Jahan.
xa: Jahanara was **Shah Jahan's daughter** and **Padshah Begum**.
⚠ **Jahanara** = Jama Masjid, **Agra**; **Shah Jahan** = Jama Masjid, **Delhi**.
**Nur Jahan** married Jahangir in **1611**.

136.s: Which of the following statements correctly reflects the account of purdah in Mughal-period society?
o: Muslim women were generally strictly veiled and travelled in covered palanquins, whereas Hindu women were described as moving more freely.
Purdah was confined exclusively to royal women of both communities.
Only Hindu women followed strict purdah, while Muslim women moved freely.
Both Muslim and Hindu women were universally confined to covered palanquins.
136.x: Muslim women were described as strictly veiled and transported in covered palanquins, while Hindu women were reported as moving more freely. John Fryer discussed this contrast in A New Account of East India and Persia concerning the Deccan.
136.tq: Compare social practices by community without overlooking the source attribution.
xs: **Muslim women** were **strictly veiled** and carried in **covered palanquins**, while **Hindu women moved freely** — option **(1)**.
**John Fryer**, in **A New Account of East India and Persia**, noted on the Deccan that Hindu women moved freely.
xa: Social evils recorded: **Sati**, **child marriage**, **polygamy** (Bernier, Tavernier).
⚠ Property: **Mehr** = Muslim women; **stridhana** = Hindu women.
Akbar tried to stop **forced** sati.

136.s: Which of the following social practices prevailed during the Mughal period according to the accounts of Bernier and Tavernier?
o: Universal female property ownership and prohibition of polygamy
Female suffrage, widow remarriage and monogamy
Compulsory education for women and abolition of sati
136.x: Bernier and Tavernier referred to the prevalence of sati, child marriage and polygamy. Akbar nevertheless attempted to stop forced sati.
136.tq: Select the historically recorded cluster of social practices.
xs: **Bernier** and **Tavernier** recorded **sati, child marriage and polygamy** — option **(4)**.
Akbar only **tried to stop forced sati**; sati was not abolished.
xa: Muslim women had **inheritance shares** + **mehr** under sharia; Hindu women controlled **stridhana**.
**Purdah**: Muslim women strictly veiled; Hindu women moved freely (**John Fryer**).
Bernier's "bleak India" view is criticised as reflecting **European bias**.

136.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the property rights of women?
o: Muslim women — stridhana; Hindu women — mehr under sharia
Muslim women — inheritance shares and mehr under sharia; Hindu women — control of stridhana
Muslim women — no inheritance rights; Hindu women — no control over stridhana
Muslim women — only communal property; Hindu women — inheritance prohibited in every case
136.x: Muslim women had inheritance shares and mehr under sharia, while Hindu women controlled stridhana.
136.tq: Avoid reversing the distinct property concepts of the two communities.
xs: **Muslim women** had **inheritance shares and mehr under sharia**; **Hindu women** controlled **stridhana** — option **(2)**.
Option 1 swaps the terms: **mehr** belongs to Muslim women, **stridhana** to Hindu women.
xa: ⚠ **Mehr** = Muslim women; **stridhana** = Hindu women.
**Nur Jahan** held the title **Padshah Begum**; her name appeared on **coins** and **farmans**.
Social evils: **Sati**, **child marriage**, **polygamy** (Bernier, Tavernier).

136.s:
With reference to Mughal court customs, consider the following statements:
1. Nauroz was a Persian New Year festival adopted from the Zoroastrians.
2. Jharokha darshan was begun by Akbar and ended by Aurangzeb.
3. Tuladan involved weighing the emperor against gold and goods on his birthday.
4. Sijda and paibos were introduced by Shah Jahan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
136.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Sijda and paibos were introduced by Akbar, not Shah Jahan.
136.tq: Find the wrong ruler attached to a court custom.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: **Nauroz** = **Persian New Year** adopted from the **Zoroastrians**.
Statement 2: **Jharokha darshan** begun by **Akbar**, ended by **Aurangzeb**; statement 3: **Tuladan** = weighing the emperor against gold and goods on his birthday.
Statement 4 wrong: **sijda / paibos** were introduced by **Akbar**, not Shah Jahan.
xa: Tuladan was a **Hindu** custom adopted by Akbar; the goods were given to the poor.
Nauroz was **stopped by Aurangzeb** (UPPSC **2001** key for Zoroastrian origin).
**Qutb Shahi Golconda** also celebrated **Nauroz**.

136.s: Which approach is most appropriate while using foreign travellers’ accounts for reconstructing Mughal social history?
o: Use only their descriptions of court ceremonies and disregard society.
Use them as a major source but read them critically alongside Persian chronicles.
Treat every observation as completely objective and ignore Persian chronicles.
Reject them entirely because foreign observers never recorded social conditions.
136.x: Travellers’ accounts are a major source for Mughal social history, but their observations should be read critically alongside Persian chronicles.
136.tq: Apply source criticism rather than accepting or rejecting an entire source category.
xs: Travellers' accounts are the **main source** for Mughal social history but must be **read against Persian chronicles** — option **(2)**.
Bernier's "**no private property**" and "**bleak India**" view reflects **European bias**, so they cannot be taken as fully objective.
Yet they do record society: **Sati**, **child marriage**, **polygamy**, purdah, Delhi's class gap.
xa: Bernier still conceded a **prosperous merchant class**.
**Pelsaert** contrasted nobles' luxury with the misery of servants and workmen.
**John Fryer**: Hindu women in the Deccan **moved freely**.

136.s:
Consider the following statements about the Qutb Shahi kingdom of Golconda:
1. Muharram was popularly known as Peerla Panduga.
2. Fourteen national festivals were observed under Abdullah Qutb Shah.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
136.x: Statement 1 is correct: Muharram was known as Peerla Panduga in Golconda. Statement 2 is wrong: the 14 national festivals are associated with Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah, not Abdullah Qutb Shah. Hence '1 only'; '2 only', 'Both' and 'Neither' are wrong.
136.tq: Check the ruler's name: 14 festivals = Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: **Muharram** was known as **Peerla Panduga** in Golconda.
Statement 2 wrong: the **14 national festivals** belong to **Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah**, not Abdullah Qutb Shah.
xa: **Abdullah Qutb Shah**'s Hyderabad had **20,000** registered prostitutes (Tavernier).
Golconda also shared the Mughal **Nauroz**.

137.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Tomb of Salim Chishti — Fatehpur Sikri
137.x: The Taj Mahal is situated at Agra, not Delhi. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
137.tq: Find the wrong location among familiar monument–place pairs.
xs: **Taj Mahal — Delhi** is wrongly matched; the Taj is at **Agra** — option **(4)**.
**Akbar's Tomb** — **Sikandra** near Agra; **Salim Chishti's tomb** — **Fatehpur Sikri**; **Char Minar** — **Hyderabad**: all correct.
xa: APPSC G1 **2018** pairs: Charminar - **Hyderabad**; Akbar's Tomb - **Sikandara**; Humayun's Tomb - **Delhi**; Taj Mahal - **Agra**.
⚠ **Char Minar** (**1591**) is **Qutb Shahi**, not Mughal — a common distractor.
Jahangir's tomb is at **Shahdara, Lahore**; Aurangzeb's at **Khuldabad**.

137.s: Char Minar at Hyderabad was built by:
137.x: Char Minar was built at Hyderabad in 1591 by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah of the Qutb Shahi dynasty. It is not a Mughal monument.
137.tq: Discriminate between rulers of the Qutb Shahi dynasty and Mughal builders.
xs: **Char Minar** at Hyderabad was built by **Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah** in **1591** — option **(4)**.
It is a **Qutb Shahi**, not a Mughal, monument; it marked the **end of a plague**.
xa: Style: **Persian arches** + **Deccani stucco**.
**Golconda Fort**: acoustic warning system, piped water.
**Qutb Shahi tombs** at **Ibrahim Bagh**: onion domes on square bases, in gardens.

137.s:
Which of the following monuments were built during the reign of Akbar?
1. Humayun's tomb, Delhi
2. Buland Darwaza, Fatehpur Sikri
3. Tomb of Itimad-ud-Daula, Agra
4. Tomb of Salim Chishti, Fatehpur Sikri
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
137.x: Humayun's tomb (c.1565-72, commissioned by Haji Begum in Akbar's reign), Buland Darwaza (c.1575, for the Gujarat victory) and Salim Chishti's tomb (c.1580-81) all belong to Akbar's reign. Itimad-ud-Daula's tomb was built by Nur Jahan in 1622-28, in Jahangir's reign. Option A leaves out the Salim Chishti tomb; options C and D wrongly include Itimad-ud-Daula.
137.tq: Humayun's tomb is Akbar-era; Buland Darwaza is Akbar's, never Shah Jahan's.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 4** are correct — option **(2)**.
**Humayun's tomb** (c. **1565-72**) and **Buland Darwaza** (c. **1575**) belong to Akbar's reign.
**Salim Chishti's tomb** (c. **1580-81**) was built by **Akbar**.
**Itimad-ud-Daula** (**1622-1628**) was built by **Nur Jahan** — not Akbar's reign.
xa: APPSC-G1 **2024**: Salim Chishti's tomb, Buland Darwaza, Humayun's tomb and Jami Masjid (Fatehpur Sikri) — all Akbar's reign.
⚠ "Not built by Shah Jahan" = **Buland Darwaza** (APPSC GS **2019**).

137.s: Which one of the following features is associated with Humayun’s tomb?
o: It was built entirely of black basalt without a dome.
It was the first garden tomb in the subcontinent and used red sandstone with white marble inlay.
It introduced the first rock-cut chaitya design in Delhi.
It was constructed only of timber and glazed tiles.
137.x: Humayun’s tomb was the first garden tomb in the subcontinent, introduced the double dome and used red sandstone with white marble inlay.
137.tq: Select the option combining the distinctive architectural features stated for the monument.
xs: Humayun's tomb was the **first garden tomb in the subcontinent** and used **red sandstone with white marble inlay** — option **(2)**.
It also introduced the **double dome** (inner and outer shells).
xa: Its **jali (lattice)** work is a hallmark.
It inspired the **Taj Mahal** (garden tomb, double dome).
UNESCO World Heritage Site, inscribed **1993**.

137.s: Which development is associated with the Sayyid-Lodi tomb tradition?
o: Introduction of Hindu-style gates and facades
Construction of the first double dome
Exclusive use of white marble and pietra dura
137.x: Sayyid-Lodi tombs incorporated Hindu elements such as Hindu-style gates and facades, plaster ornament and drip-stones.
137.tq: Identify the distinctive architectural contribution rather than the later Mughal features.
xs: **Sayyid-Lodi** tombs show **Hindu-style gates and facades** — option **(1)**.
They also used **plaster ornament** and **drip-stones**.
The **double dome** came at **Humayun's tomb**; **mirror work** is in the **Sheesh Mahal**.
xa: Evolution: Sayyid-Lodi → **Sher Shah's tomb** (Sur transition) → **Itimad-ud-Daula** → **Taj Mahal** (climax) → **Bibi ka Maqbara** (late imitation).
White marble with **pietra dura** first appeared at **Itimad-ud-Daula**.

137.s: Which monument marked the transition from the Lodi tradition to the Mughal architectural tradition under the Sur rulers?
137.x: Sher Shah's tomb at Sasaram marks the Sur transition in the evolution of Indo-Islamic tomb architecture.
137.tq: Use the historical transition clue to connect the monument with the correct dynasty.
xs: **Sher Shah's tomb** marks the **Sur transition** — option **(1)**.
It is at **Sasaram**, Bihar, set in a tank; finished under **Islam Shah**.
The **Taj Mahal** is the climax and **Bibi ka Maqbara** the late imitation of the tradition.
xa: Sayyid-Lodi tombs: **Hindu-style gates**, plaster ornament, drip-stones.
**Itimad-ud-Daula** = first Mughal tomb in **white marble** with **pietra dura**.

137.s: Fatehpur Sikri was built in honour of which Sufi saint, after whom Prince Salim was named?
137.x: Fatehpur Sikri was built in honour of Sheikh Salim Chishti, after whom Prince Salim was named.
137.tq: Use the direct saint–monument association.
xs: Fatehpur Sikri was built in honour of **Sheikh Salim Chishti** — option **(2)**.
**Akbar** planned it as his capital, **1571-1585**.
xa: Salim Chishti's white-marble tomb lies in the **Jami Masjid** courtyard.
Main material: **red sandstone**; UNESCO site since **1986**.
Style: blend of **Persian, Indian and Central Asian**.

137.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched with Fatehpur Sikri?
137.x: Panch Mahal, the Jama Masjid and Jodha Bai's palace are at Fatehpur Sikri. The Moti Masjids are in Agra Fort (Shah Jahan) and the Red Fort, Delhi (Aurangzeb), not at Fatehpur Sikri.
137.tq: Find the structure that does not belong to the monument group.
xs: **Moti Masjid** is not at Fatehpur Sikri — option **(4)**.
The Moti Masjids are in **Agra Fort** (**Shah Jahan**) and the **Red Fort** (**Aurangzeb**).
**Panch Mahal**, **Jama Masjid** and **Jodha Bai's palace** are all at Fatehpur Sikri.
xa: Other Fatehpur Sikri buildings: **Buland Darwaza**, **Ibadat Khana**, **Diwan-i-Khas**, Salim Chishti's tomb.
⚠ Moti Masjid: **Red Fort** = Aurangzeb; **Agra Fort** = Shah Jahan.

137.s: Which building at Fatehpur Sikri served as a house of worship where scholars of different religions held philosophical debates?
137.x: The Ibadat Khana was the House of Worship used for philosophical debates among scholars of various religions.
137.tq: Match the building with its precise institutional purpose.
xs: The **Ibadat Khana** was the **House of Worship** for debates among scholars of various religions — option **(2)**.
It was built in **1575** and was part of the religious core of Fatehpur Sikri.
**Jodha Bai's palace** = trabeate + arcuate; **Diwan-i-Khas** = private audience; **Panch Mahal** = five-storeyed pavilion.
xa: The religious core also had the **Jama Masjid** and **Salim Chishti's tomb**.
**Buland Darwaza** was also built c. **1575**.

137.s: Jodha Bai's palace at Fatehpur Sikri illustrates the combination of:
o: Hindu trabeate and Islamic arcuate styles
Buddhist stupa and Jain temple styles
Persian dome and Turkish minaret styles only
137.x: Jodha Bai's palace combines Hindu trabeate construction, based on beams and lintels, with Islamic arcuate construction, based on arches and domes.
137.tq: Distinguish trabeate and arcuate systems by their structural elements.
xs: Jodha Bai's palace blends **Hindu trabeate** and **Islamic arcuate** styles — option **(1)**.
**Trabeate** = **beam and lintel** (Hindu); **arcuate** = **arch and dome** (Islamic).
xa: The **Persian-Indian synthesis**: arch and dome + trabeate, **chhatris**, **Hindu motifs** (Fatehpur Sikri, Akbar's tomb).
**Panch Mahal** shows **Persian wind tower** influence.

137.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Fatehpur Sikri:
1. It was planned as Akbar's capital during 1571–1585.
2. Its buildings show Persian, Indian and Central Asian influences.
3. Akbar introduced the Tudor or four-centred arch in his buildings.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
137.x: All three statements are correct. Fatehpur Sikri was Akbar's planned capital during 1571–1585 and reflects multiple architectural influences, including the Tudor arch introduced by Akbar.
137.tq: Test chronology, stylistic synthesis and a specific architectural innovation together.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
Statement 1: Fatehpur Sikri was **Akbar's** planned capital, **1571-1585**.
Statement 2: its style blends **Persian, Indian and Central Asian** elements.
Statement 3: it introduced the **Tudor (four-centred) arch**.
xa: Built in honour of **Sheikh Salim Chishti**, mainly in **red sandstone**.
**Jahangir Mahal at Orchha** (MP) continues Akbar's style.
UNESCO World Heritage Site (**1986**).

137.s: Who is identified as the chief architect of the Taj Mahal?
137.x: Ustad Ahmad Lahori is identified as the chief architect of the Taj Mahal.
137.tq: Test the specific architect associated with the monument rather than a general Mughal architect.
xs: The chief architect of the Taj Mahal was **Ustad Ahmad Lahori** — option **(2)**.
The Taj was built by **Shah Jahan** at **Agra**, **1632-1648**.
xa: Its marble came from **Makrana** (Rajasthan) (APPSC GS **2016**).
It is the mausoleum of **Mumtaz Mahal (Arjumand Banu Begum)**.
**V.A. Smith**: combination of **European and Asiatic genius**.

137.s: The design of the Taj Mahal was particularly inspired by which earlier Mughal monument?
137.x: Humayun's Tomb provided an important design ancestry for the Taj Mahal, particularly through the garden-tomb form and use of a double dome.
137.tq: Trace architectural influence from an earlier monument rather than selecting a later or contemporary structure.
xs: **Humayun's Tomb** inspired the Taj Mahal's design — option **(1)**.
It gave the **garden tomb**, **double dome** and red sandstone with marble.
xa: Humayun's tomb = **first garden tomb** in the subcontinent.
The Taj stands at the **river end** of its **charbagh**, not the centre.
The Taj = **climax** of the tomb tradition; Bibi ka Maqbara = late imitation.

137.s: Which one of the following statements about the Taj Mahal is NOT correct?
o: It was built entirely of red sandstone.
It is associated with the mausoleum of Mumtaz Mahal.
It was built at Agra by Shah Jahan.
It represents a high point of pietra dura and symmetry.
137.x: The Taj Mahal is principally constructed of white marble, not entirely of red sandstone. It is the mausoleum of Mumtaz Mahal and is noted for pietra dura and symmetry.
137.tq: Reject the material-based reversal between the Taj Mahal and earlier red-sandstone Mughal monuments.
xs: "**Built entirely of red sandstone**" is wrong — the Taj is in **white marble** — option **(1)**.
It is the mausoleum of **Mumtaz Mahal**, built at **Agra** by **Shah Jahan**.
It is the **pinnacle of pietra dura** and **symmetry**.
xa: Marble source: **Makrana** (Rajasthan).
UNESCO **1983**; among the **New Seven Wonders** (**2007**).

137.s: The Taj Trapezium Zone (TTZ) rulings concerning protection of the Taj Mahal are associated with the case of:
137.x: The Supreme Court's Taj Trapezium Zone rulings, including those concerning industrial pollution, were associated with the M.C. Mehta case in 1996.
137.tq: Match an environmental protection measure with the relevant legal case.
xs: The **TTZ** rulings came in the **M.C. Mehta** case — option **(1)**.
The Supreme Court ruled in **1996** against pollution threatening the Taj.
xa: Threat: **marble cancer**, yellowing from **sulphur dioxide** (Mathura refinery, industries, traffic).
The Taj is a UNESCO site since **1983**.

137.s: The white marble used in the construction of the Taj Mahal was obtained mainly from
137.x: The Taj Mahal's marble came from Makrana in Rajasthan. Sasaram is the site of Sher Shah's tomb, Fatehpur Sikri was built mainly of red sandstone, and Kollur is known for diamond mines (the Koh-i-Noor).
137.tq: Taj marble = Makrana (Rajasthan).
xs: The Taj's marble came from **Makrana in Rajasthan** — option **(1)**.
This was the APPSC GS **2016** key.
**Sasaram** = Sher Shah's tomb; **Fatehpur Sikri** = red sandstone.
xa: Taj features: **pietra dura**, symmetry, white marble.
Architect: **Ustad Ahmad Lahori**.

137.s: Which historian described the Taj Mahal as the product of a combination of European and Asiatic genius?
137.x: V.A. Smith saw the Taj Mahal as a combination of European and Asiatic genius (APPSC-G1 2022 key). Fergusson and Percy Brown treated it as a product of the Indo-Persian tradition, and R.C. Majumdar is a distractor here.
137.tq: European + Asiatic genius = V.A. Smith.
xs: **V.A. Smith** saw the Taj as a combination of **European and Asiatic genius** — option **(3)**.
This is the APPSC-G1 **2022** key.
**James Fergusson** and **Percy Brown** saw it as a product of the **Indo-Persian tradition**.
xa: Chief architect: **Ustad Ahmad Lahori**; marble from **Makrana**.
Built **1632-1648** for **Mumtaz Mahal**.

137.s: Which one of the following statements about the Diwan-i-Khas of the Red Fort is correct?
o: It was the residence of the royal women and was called the Palace of Colours.
It housed the Peacock Throne, which was taken by Nadir Shah in 1739.
It was built by Aurangzeb as the Moti Masjid.
It was the public audience hall of Shah Jahan.
137.x: The Diwan-i-Khas was the private audience hall and housed the Peacock Throne, which was taken by Nadir Shah in 1739.
137.tq: Use the famous object-event association while distinguishing the two audience halls.
xs: The Red Fort's **Diwan-i-Khas** housed the **Peacock Throne**, taken by **Nadir Shah** in **1739** — option **(2)**.
It was the **hall of private audience**.
**Rang Mahal** = Palace of Colours for royal women; **Diwan-i-Am** = public audience.
xa: The Red Fort's **Moti Masjid** was built by **Aurangzeb**.
**Sheesh Mahal** = mirror-work chambers.

137.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes the two Mughal structures named Moti Masjid?
o: The Moti Masjid in the Red Fort was built by Aurangzeb, whereas the Moti Masjid in Agra Fort was built by Shah Jahan.
The Red Fort Moti Masjid was built by Shah Jahan, whereas the Agra Fort Moti Masjid was built by Aurangzeb.
Both Moti Masjids were built by Akbar in Agra Fort.
Both Moti Masjids were built by Aurangzeb in Delhi.
137.x: Aurangzeb built the Moti Masjid in the Red Fort, while Shah Jahan built the Moti Masjid in Agra Fort.
137.tq: Resolve the look-alike monument pair by comparing location and builder.
xs: **Red Fort** Moti Masjid = **Aurangzeb**; **Agra Fort** Moti Masjid = **Shah Jahan** — option **(1)**.
Options 2–4 swap or merge the builders; neither Moti Masjid is **Akbar's**.
xa: Shah Jahan also built the **Red Fort** and **Jama Masjid, Delhi**.
Red Fort uses **red sandstone** for structure + **marble** for decoration.

137.s:
Consider the following statements about forts associated with the Mughal rulers:
1. Agra Fort was begun by Akbar in 1565.
2. Allahabad Fort was built by Akbar in 1583.
3. Lahore Fort was rebuilt by Akbar.
4. The Red Fort at Delhi was built by Shah Jahan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
137.x: All four statements are correct. Agra Fort was begun in 1565, Allahabad Fort was built in 1583, Lahore Fort was rebuilt by Akbar and the Red Fort at Delhi was built by Shah Jahan.
137.tq: Check the ruler, date and location of each fort before selecting the complete code.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**Agra Fort**: Akbar, begun **1565**; **Allahabad Fort**: Akbar, **1583**.
**Lahore Fort** rebuilt by **Akbar**; **Red Fort, Delhi** built by **Shah Jahan**.
xa: Agra Fort: **red sandstone**, on the **Yamuna**; has Diwan-i-Am and Diwan-i-Khas.
Agra Fort and Taj Mahal: UNESCO **1983**.

137.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Pietra dura — inlay of semi-precious stones
Double dome — inner and outer shells
137.x: Jali refers to lattice work. Mirror-work chambers are associated with the Sheesh Mahal.
137.tq: Separate related decorative terms by their exact meanings and locations.
xs: **Jali — mirror-work chambers** is wrong — option **(1)**.
**Jali** = **lattice** work (Humayun's tomb); mirror work is in the **Sheesh Mahal**.
**Pietra dura** = semi-precious stone inlay; **charbagh** = four-quartered garden; **double dome** = inner and outer shells — all correct.
xa: Other hallmarks: **calligraphy**, **arabesque**.
Double dome introduced at **Humayun's tomb**.

137.s: The charbagh garden tradition in Mughal architecture was introduced by:
137.x: Babur introduced the charbagh, or four-quartered garden, tradition; Ram Bagh at Agra is an example.
137.tq: Match the architectural innovation with the earliest Mughal ruler associated with it.
xs: **Babur** introduced the **charbagh** (four-quartered garden) — option **(4)**.
Example: **Ram Bagh**, Agra (c. **1528**), the **first Mughal garden**.
xa: Shalimar: **Srinagar** = **Jahangir**; **Lahore** = **Shah Jahan**.
**Nishat Bagh** (Srinagar) was built by **Asaf Khan**, Nur Jahan's brother.
**Pinjore garden** (Haryana): Fidai Khan, under Aurangzeb.

137.s: Which of the following correctly describes the development of pietra dura in Mughal architecture?
o: It began under Jahangir, appeared on a large scale at Itimad-ud-Daula and reached its peak at the Taj Mahal.
It began under Babur and reached its peak at Sher Shah's tomb.
It began under Akbar and was confined to red sandstone buildings.
It began under Aurangzeb and reached its peak at Bibi ka Maqbara.
137.x: Pietra dura began during Jahangir's reign, was first used on a large scale at Itimad-ud-Daula and reached its peak at the Taj Mahal.
137.tq: Arrange the beginning, large-scale use and culmination of a style in sequence.
xs: Pietra dura **began under Jahangir**, appeared on a large scale at **Itimad-ud-Daula** and peaked at the **Taj Mahal** — option **(1)**.
**Pietra dura** = inlay of **semi-precious stones**.
xa: Itimad-ud-Daula ("**Baby Taj**") = first Mughal tomb in white marble with pietra dura.
White marble: transition under **Jahangir**, dominant under **Shah Jahan**.

137.s: Which comparison between the architectural phases of Akbar and Shah Jahan is correct?
o: Akbar is associated mainly with red sandstone, whereas Shah Jahan is associated mainly with white marble.
Akbar is associated mainly with white marble, whereas Shah Jahan is associated mainly with red sandstone.
Both rulers used only white marble.
Both rulers used only red sandstone.
137.x: Akbar's phase is represented by red-sandstone structures such as Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri, while Shah Jahan's phase is dominated by white marble, as in the Taj Mahal.
137.tq: Use the material contrast to distinguish the architectural phases of the two rulers.
xs: **Akbar** = mainly **red sandstone**; **Shah Jahan** = mainly **white marble** — option **(1)**.
Red sandstone: **Agra Fort**, **Fatehpur Sikri**; white marble: **Taj Mahal**.
The transition came under **Jahangir** (**Itimad-ud-Daula**).
xa: The **Red Fort** combines red sandstone structure with marble decoration.
Humayun's tomb: **red sandstone with white marble inlay**.

137.s: Shalimar Gardens at Lahore were built under which Mughal ruler?
137.x: The Shalimar Gardens at Lahore were built under Shah Jahan. The Shalimar Bagh at Srinagar is associated with Jahangir.
137.tq: Separate the similarly named Shalimar gardens by location and builder.
xs: The **Shalimar Gardens at Lahore** were built under **Shah Jahan** — option **(4)**.
The **Shalimar Bagh at Srinagar** is **Jahangir's**.
xa: ⚠ Shalimar: **Srinagar** = Jahangir; **Lahore** = Shah Jahan.
**Nishat Bagh** (Srinagar, Dal Lake) = **Asaf Khan**.
**Charbagh** introduced by **Babur** (Ram Bagh, Agra).

137.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
137.x: Ram Bagh was built by Babur at Agra, not Lahore. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
137.tq: Find the wrong location while keeping the builder association in view.
xs: **Ram Bagh — Lahore — Babur** is wrong: Ram Bagh is at **Agra** — option **(3)**.
**Nishat Bagh** — Srinagar — **Asaf Khan**; **Pinjore** — Haryana — **Fidai Khan**; **Shalimar Bagh** — Srinagar — **Jahangir**: all correct.
xa: Ram Bagh (c. **1528**) = **first Mughal garden**.
Lahore has Shah Jahan's **Shalimar Gardens** and **Jahangir's tomb** (Shahdara).

137.s: Babur's final tomb is located at:
137.x: Babur's tomb is at Bagh-e-Babur in Kabul, although he was first buried at Agra.
137.tq: Watch the distinction between the first burial place and the final tomb location.
xs: Babur's final tomb is at **Kabul** (**Bagh-e-Babur**) — option **(1)**.
He was **first buried at Agra**.
xa: Humayun — **Delhi**; Akbar — **Sikandra**; Jahangir — **Shahdara, Lahore**.
Shah Jahan — **Taj Mahal, Agra**; Aurangzeb — **Khuldabad**.

137.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
137.x: Shah Jahan is buried in the Taj Mahal at Agra beside Mumtaz Mahal. Sikandra near Agra is associated with Akbar's tomb.
137.tq: Find the wrongly shifted emperor-location pair among otherwise familiar tomb sites.
xs: **Shah Jahan — Sikandra** is wrong — option **(4)**.
Shah Jahan lies in the **Taj Mahal, Agra**, beside **Mumtaz Mahal**; **Sikandra** is **Akbar's** tomb.
Aurangzeb — **Khuldabad**; Jahangir — **Shahdara, Lahore**; Humayun — **Delhi**: correct.
xa: Babur — **Kabul** (Bagh-e-Babur), first buried at Agra.
Akbar's tomb was begun by Akbar and **completed by Jahangir**.

137.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Monument)
a. Charminar
b. Akbar's Tomb
c. Humayun's Tomb
d. Taj Mahal
List-II (Place)
i. Agra
ii. Delhi
iii. Sikandara
iv. Hyderabad
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
137.x: Charminar is in Hyderabad, Akbar's Tomb at Sikandara, Humayun's Tomb in Delhi and the Taj Mahal at Agra.
137.tq: Akbar rests at Sikandara near Agra, not in Agra itself.
xs: Correct code **a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i** — option **(4)**.
**Charminar** — **Hyderabad**; **Akbar's Tomb** — **Sikandara**.
**Humayun's Tomb** — **Delhi**; **Taj Mahal** — **Agra**.
xa: This is the APPSC G1 **2018** pairs question.
⚠ Charminar (**1591**) is **Qutb Shahi** — **Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah**.

137.s: Which of the following combinations correctly represents UNESCO inscription years of Mughal sites in India?
o: Agra Fort and Taj Mahal—1993; Fatehpur Sikri—2007; Humayun's Tomb—1983; Red Fort Complex—1986
Agra Fort and Taj Mahal—1986; Fatehpur Sikri—1983; Humayun's Tomb—2007; Red Fort Complex—1993
Agra Fort and Taj Mahal—1983; Fatehpur Sikri—1986; Humayun's Tomb—1993; Red Fort Complex—2007
Agra Fort and Taj Mahal—2007; Fatehpur Sikri—1993; Humayun's Tomb—1986; Red Fort Complex—1983
137.x: Agra Fort and the Taj Mahal were inscribed in 1983, Fatehpur Sikri in 1986, Humayun's Tomb in 1993 and the Red Fort Complex in 2007.
137.tq: Anchor the sequence using the four distinct inscription years.
xs: **Agra Fort and Taj Mahal—1983; Fatehpur Sikri—1986; Humayun's Tomb—1993; Red Fort Complex—2007** — option **(3)**.
The order follows the sequence **1983 → 1986 → 1993 → 2007**.
xa: The Taj was also named among the **New Seven Wonders** in **2007**.
Fatehpur Sikri: Akbar's capital, **1571-1585**.

137.s: Which one of the following is NOT included in the listed UNESCO Mughal sites in India?
137.x: Golconda Fort is a Qutb Shahi monument and is not included in the listed UNESCO Mughal sites. Humayun's Tomb, the Red Fort Complex and Fatehpur Sikri are included.
137.tq: Use the dynasty distinction to eliminate the non-Mughal monument.
xs: **Golconda Fort** is not among the listed UNESCO Mughal sites — option **(4)**.
It is a **Qutb Shahi** fort, known for its **acoustic warning system** and **piped water**.
**Humayun's Tomb** (**1993**), **Red Fort Complex** (**2007**) and **Fatehpur Sikri** (**1986**) are listed.
xa: Agra Fort and Taj Mahal were inscribed in **1983**.
**Qutb Shahi tombs** at Ibrahim Bagh: onion domes on square bases.

137.s: The architectural synthesis represented by Mughal monuments primarily blended which traditions?
137.x: Mughal architecture blended Persian, Timurid and Indian architectural elements.
137.tq: Test the exact components of a cultural synthesis without confusing them with general influences.
xs: Mughal architecture blended **Persian, Timurid and Indian** traditions — option **(3)**.
It is the **zenith of Indo-Islamic architecture**.
xa: **Persian-Indian synthesis**: arch and dome + trabeate, **chhatris**, Hindu motifs (Fatehpur Sikri, Akbar's tomb).
Fatehpur Sikri: **Persian, Indian and Central Asian** blend.

137.s: Which of the following is regarded as the last major imitation in the Mughal garden-tomb tradition?
137.x: Bibi ka Maqbara is regarded as the last major imitation in the Mughal garden-tomb tradition.
137.tq: Distinguish the terminal example from the first example in an architectural sequence.
xs: **Bibi ka Maqbara** is the **last major imitation** — option **(4)**.
It is the "**Taj of the Deccan**" at Aurangabad, built by **Azam Shah**.
**Ram Bagh** = first Mughal garden; **Humayun's Tomb** = first garden tomb.
xa: FIRST/LAST: first Mughal garden = **Ram Bagh**; pietra dura first under **Jahangir**.
⚠ "**Baby Taj**" = Itimad-ud-Daula; "**Taj of the Deccan**" = Bibi ka Maqbara.

137.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Bahmani Jama Masjid at Gulbarga from Mughal open-court mosques?
o: It follows a charbagh garden plan, unlike Mughal tombs
It is built entirely of white marble, unlike all Mughal mosques
It has no domes, unlike every Mughal mosque
It has a fully covered courtyard, unlike the open-court pattern of Mughal mosques
137.x: The Bahmani Jama Masjid at Gulbarga is notable for its fully covered courtyard, whereas Mughal mosques generally followed an open-court arrangement.
137.tq: Focus on the precise structural contrast rather than broad stylistic similarities.
xs: The **Bahmani Jama Masjid at Gulbarga** has a **fully covered courtyard**, unlike the **open-court** Mughal mosques — option **(4)**.
**Charbagh** plans belong to garden tombs, not mosques; the notes give no basis for the "white marble" or "no domes" claims.
xa: Shah Jahan's **Jama Masjid, Delhi** (**1650-1656**) is part of Shahjahanabad.
Akbar's **Jami Masjid, Fatehpur Sikri** (c. **1571-74**) has Buland Darwaza as its southern entrance.

137.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Qutb Shahi tombs — onion domes on square bases in gardens
Golconda Fort — acoustic warning system and piped water
Charminar — Persian arches with Deccani stucco
137.x: Charminar is not a fully covered courtyard mosque; that feature is associated with the Bahmani Jama Masjid at Gulbarga. The other pairs are correctly matched.
137.tq: Reject the option that imports a distinctive feature from a different monument.
xs: **Charminar — fully covered courtyard mosque** is wrong — option **(1)**.
The fully covered courtyard belongs to the **Bahmani Jama Masjid at Gulbarga**.
**Qutb Shahi tombs** (onion domes), **Golconda Fort** (acoustic warning, piped water) and **Charminar** (Persian arches + Deccani stucco) are correct.
xa: Charminar (**1591**), by **Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah**, marked the **end of a plague**.
Qutb Shahi tombs are at **Ibrahim Bagh**.

137.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Bahmani Kingdom initially had Gulbarga as its capital and later shifted it to Bidar.
II. Vijayanagara was situated on the Tungabhadra River.
III. Pune became the centre of Peshwa power.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
137.x: I, II and III are correct: the Bahmanis moved from Gulbarga to Bidar, Vijayanagara stood on the Tungabhadra, and Pune was the seat of the Peshwas.
137.tq: Check each statement separately.
n: The initial Bahmani capital was Gulbarga. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 51-53]
The Bahmani capital was later shifted to Bidar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 51-53]
Vijayanagara was situated on the Tungabhadra River. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 51-53]
The Peshwas had Pune as their centre of power. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 51-53]
Peshwa power was centred at Pune. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 51-53]
xs: All three, **I, II and III**, are correct — option **(2)**.
I: the **Bahmanis** had **Gulbarga** as capital first, then shifted to **Bidar**.
II: **Vijayanagara** (Hampi) stood on the **Tungabhadra River**.
III: **Pune** was the centre of **Peshwa power**.
xa: **Delhi** was the main political centre of the **Delhi Sultanate**.
Shivaji's Marathas had their capital at **Raigad**.
Akbar used **Agra**, **Fatehpur Sikri** and **Lahore**; Shah Jahan moved to **Shahjahanabad** (Delhi).

137.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Chandela
(b) Sena
(c) Delhi Sultanate
(d) Mughal

List-II
(i) Delhi
(ii) Khajuraho region
(iii) Nadia / Nabadwip
(iv) Agra / Delhi and other imperial centres
137.x: The Chandelas ruled from the Khajuraho region, the Senas from Nadia/Nabadwip, the Delhi Sultanate from Delhi and the Mughals from Agra, Delhi and other centres, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv.
137.tq: Recall the capital of each dynasty.
n: The Chandela capital was in the Khajuraho region. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 51-53]
Khajuraho was an important centre of the Chandela kingdom. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 51-53]
The Sena capital was Nadia. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 51-53]
Nadia was also called Nabadwip. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 51-53]
Lakshmanasena had Nadia as his capital. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 51-53]
Delhi was the capital of the Delhi Sultanate. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 51-53]
Delhi was the main political centre of the Delhi Sultanate. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 51-53]
The Mughal Empire had Agra as an imperial centre. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 51-53]
The Mughal Empire had Delhi as an imperial centre. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 51-53]
The Mughal Empire had other imperial centres. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 51-53]
xs: The correct match is **a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv** — option **(1)**.
**Chandela** — **Khajuraho region**; **Sena** — **Nadia / Nabadwip**.
**Delhi Sultanate** — **Delhi**; **Mughal** — **Agra / Delhi** and other imperial centres.
xa: **Khajuraho** is associated with **Chandela architecture**.
Under **Shah Jahan** the Mughal capital was **Shahjahanabad**, Delhi.
The **Bahmanis** moved from **Gulbarga** to **Bidar**.

137.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Raigad was associated with Shivaji.
II. Pune was associated with Peshwa power.
III. Raigad was the seat of Peshwa power.
IV. Pune was associated with Shivaji.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
137.x: I and II are correct: Shivaji made Raigad his capital, and Pune was the centre of Peshwa power. III and IV are false because they swap Raigad and Pune.
137.tq: Discriminate Shivaji's capital from the Peshwas' seat.
n: Shivaji had Raigad as his capital. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 51-53]
The Maratha capital under Shivaji was Raigad. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 51-53]
The Peshwas had Pune as their centre of power. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 51-53]
Peshwa power was centred at Pune. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 51-53]
xs: Statements **I and II only** are correct — option **(2)**.
I: **Raigad** was the capital of the Marathas under **Shivaji**.
II: **Pune** was the centre of **Peshwa power**.
III and IV swap the two places, so both are wrong.
xa: **Vijayanagara** was on the **Tungabhadra River**, linked with **Hampi**.
Bahmani capital: **Gulbarga**, later **Bidar**.
Mughal centres: **Agra**, **Delhi**, **Fatehpur Sikri**, **Lahore**.

137.s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Bibi Ka Maqbara
(b) Tomb of Akbar, Sikandra
(c) Jama Masjid, Delhi

Statement 3 is wrong: Basawan belongs to Akbar's reign; Jahangir's painters included Manohar, Bishandas and Mansur. Option A leaves out statement 2; options C and D include the false statement 3.
138.tq: Jahangir = golden age; Abul Hasan Nadir-uz-Zaman, Mansur Nadir-ul-Asr; Basawan is Akbar's.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: Jahangir's reign = **golden period** of Mughal painting.
Statement 2: **Abul Hasan** was titled **Nadir-uz-Zaman**.
Statement 3 wrong: **Basawan** belongs to **Akbar's** reign.
xa: Jahangir's painters: **Manohar, Bishandas and Mansur** (UKPSC **2025**).
Jahangir introduced the **halo (nimbus)**.

138.s:
With reference to the Pahari school of painting, consider the following statements:
1. It flourished mainly between the seventeenth and nineteenth centuries.
2. It was associated with the Sub-Himalayan region.
3. It originated in the Bahmani court.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
138.x: The Pahari school flourished in the seventeenth to nineteenth centuries in the Sub-Himalayan region. Its association with the Bahmani court belongs to Deccani painting, not Pahari painting.
138.tq: Find the statement carrying the wrong school-origin association.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
The **Pahari** school belongs to the **Sub-Himalayan** belt (Himachal, Jammu, Almora, Garhwal), **17th-19th c.**
Statement 3 wrong: the **Bahmani** court origin belongs to the **Deccani** school.
xa: Pahari painting grew from painters dispersed after **Aurangzeb** withdrew patronage.
Deccani school: **heavy use of gold**.

138.s: The Deccani school of painting began in the court of the
138.x: Deccani painting began in the Bahmani court and continued in the successor states of the Bahmani kingdom.
138.tq: Identify the institutional origin of the school.
xs: Deccani painting began in the court of the **Bahmanis** — option **(3)**.
It continued in the **successor states**; at **Golconda** the founder was **Mir Hashim**.
xa: Deccani painting made **heavy use of gold**.
Qutb Shahi Deccani painting was **independent of Mughal style**.

138.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes Mughal painting from Rajput painting?
o: Mughal painting was indigenous and decorative, whereas Rajput painting was cosmopolitan and naturalistic.
Rajput painting alone reflected European influence and a cosmopolitan outlook.
Mughal painting generally used muted naturalistic colours, perspective and shading, whereas Rajput painting was vivid and decorative.
Both schools used identical styles and differed only in the language of captions.
138.x: Mughal painting generally displayed muted naturalistic colours, perspective, shading and a cosmopolitan outlook, while Rajput painting was indigenous, vivid and decorative.
138.tq: Read both sides of the reversed comparison carefully.
xs: Mughal = **muted, naturalistic colour**, **perspective and shading**; Rajput = **vivid and decorative** — option **(3)**.
Mughal painting was **cosmopolitan** with **European influence**; Rajput was **indigenous** — option 1 reverses this.
xa: Rajput: **bold colours**, flat **2-D**, Hindu epics.
Pahari school: Sub-Himalayan, **17th-19th c.**

138.s: Tansen, who became one of the Navaratnas of Akbar, was originally known as
138.x: Tansen's original name was Ramtanu Pande. He first served at the court of Raja Ramchandra of Rewa before joining Akbar's court.
138.tq: Use the exact-name distinction to reject the look-alike personal name.
xs: Tansen's original name was **Ramtanu Pande** — option **(2)**.
**Makaranda Pande** is the APPSC-G2 **2011** distractor.
xa: He was a disciple of **Swami Haridas**, first at Raja Ramchandra of **Rewa**'s court.
Title **Mian**; ragas **Mian ki Todi**, **Mian ki Malhar**, **Darbari Kanada**.

138.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Tansen:
1. He first served in the court of Raja Ramchandra of Rewa.
2. He was given the title ‘Mian’.
3. He was one of Akbar’s Navaratnas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
138.x: All three statements are correct. Tansen moved from Raja Ramchandra of Rewa's court to Akbar's court and was honoured with the title ‘Mian’.
138.tq: Test the whole biographical chain rather than relying on a single association.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
Tansen first served **Raja Ramchandra of Rewa**, then became one of **Akbar's Navaratnas**.
He held the title **Mian**.
xa: Original name: **Ramtanu Pande**; from **Gwalior**, disciple of **Swami Haridas**.
**Dhrupad** style; ragas **Mian ki Todi**, **Darbari Kanada**.

138.s: Which one of the following musical forms is correctly matched with its Mughal-era patronage?
o: Tappa — Raja Man Singh Tomar of Gwalior
138.x: Khayal flourished at the court of Muhammad Shah ‘Rangeela’, particularly through Sadarang and Adarang. Dhrupad was associated with Raja Man Singh Tomar, while Tappa was refined by Shori Miyan.
138.tq: Start from the sure form–court association and eliminate the swapped pairs.
xs: **Khayal — Muhammad Shah 'Rangeela'** is correct — option **(2)**.
It flourished there with **Sadarang** and **Adarang**.
**Dhrupad** = **Raja Man Singh Tomar**, Gwalior; **Tappa** = refined by **Shori Miyan**.
xa: Tappa was refined at Muhammad Shah's court (UPPSC **2023**).
**Tansen** and **Baiju** were masters of dhrupad.

138.s:
Consider the following statements about music under Aurangzeb:
1. Aurangzeb ended court music.
2. His reign witnessed the production of several Persian works on classical music.
3. Aurangzeb himself played the veena.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
138.x: All three statements are correct. Although Aurangzeb ended court music, Persian treatises on classical music were produced during his reign, and he played the veena.
138.tq: Recognise the apparent contradiction between royal policy and developments during the same reign.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**Aurangzeb** ended (banned) **court music**.
Yet many **Persian works and treatises on classical music** date from his reign, and he played the **veena**.
xa: He also **withdrew patronage** from painting.
FIRST/LAST: Aurangzeb withdrew patronage from **painting and music**.

138.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the languages of the Sultanate period:
1. Persian became the language of administration, diplomacy and high culture.
2. Persian replaced Sanskrit and Arabic in these official and elite functions.
3. Hindavi developed in camps and bazaars through interaction between Perso-Arabic and indigenous linguistic elements.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
138.x: All three statements are correct. Persian acquired elite official status, while Hindavi developed through the interaction of Perso-Arabic script and indigenous grammar and vocabulary.
138.tq: Check whether each statement describes a separate stage or feature of linguistic development.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**Persian** replaced **Sanskrit and Arabic** as the language of **administration, diplomacy and high culture**.
**Hindavi** (→ Urdu) grew out of **military camps and bazaars**, mixing Perso-Arabic and indigenous elements.
xa: Persian linked Delhi with **Isfahan** and **Central Asia**.
Urdu = **Perso-Arabic script** + **indigenous grammar**.

138.s:
With reference to Dakhni Urdu, consider the following statements:
1. It became a lingua franca of Deccan camps and bazaars.
2. It developed as a literary medium under the Qutb Shahis.
3. Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah is associated with the first Urdu poetic diwan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
138.x: Dakhni Urdu served as the common language of Deccan camps and bazaars, became a literary medium under the Qutb Shahis, and Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah is known for the first Urdu poetic diwan.
138.tq: Combine the language’s social role, literary role and associated poet.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**Dakhni Urdu** was the **lingua franca of Deccan camps and bazaars** and a literary medium under the **Qutb Shahis**.
**Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah** = **first Urdu poet with a diwan**.
xa: **Mulla Khiali** = first Deccani poetry in Telangana.
**Abdullah Qutb Shah**'s era = **Golden Age of Urdu**.

138.s: Urdu developed historically through the stages represented by which sequence?
138.x: The development is described as Hindavi followed by Rekhta, Lashkari and Urdu. Urdu grew in military camps and bazaars.
138.tq: Arrange the successive names of the language in the stated historical sequence.
xs: **Hindavi → Rekhta → Lashkari → Urdu** — option **(2)**.
Urdu grew out of **military camps and bazaars**.
xa: Mix = **Persian, Arabic, Turkic**, local **Prakrits**, **Braj**.
Script: **Perso-Arabic**; grammar: **indigenous**.

138.s: Who was the first writer of Deccani poetry in Telangana?
138.x: Mulla Khiali was the first to write Deccani poetry in Telangana.
138.tq: Identify the pioneer rather than the later court poet associated with the same tradition.
xs: **Mulla Khiali** wrote the **first Deccani poetry in Telangana** — option **(2)**.
**Ghavvasi** was a later court poet (**Tuti Nama**, **1657**); **Keshavdas** was a Hindi poet of **Orchha**; **Sadarang** a Khayal musician.
xa: **Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah** = first Urdu poet with a **diwan**.
**Abdullah Qutb Shah**'s era = **Golden Age of Urdu**.

138.s: The Golden Age of Urdu is associated with the reign of
138.x: The era of Abdullah Qutb Shah is described as the Golden Age of Urdu.
138.tq: Distinguish Deccani Urdu’s regional golden age from North Indian Mughal patronage.
xs: The **Golden Age of Urdu** was the era of **Abdullah Qutb Shah** — option **(2)**.
Court poet **Ghavvasi** wrote the **Tuti Nama** (**1657**) in that era.
xa: **Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah** = first Urdu poet with a diwan.
Under the Qutb Shahis, **Persian** was official and **Telugu** the people's language.

138.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Akbarnama is correct?
o: It was written by Khafi Khan during Aurangzeb's reign.
It consists of three volumes, the third being the Ain-i-Akbari.
It is a critical account of Akbar's religious policy by Badauni.
It was written by Jahangir as his autobiography.
138.x: The Akbarnama was written by Abul Fazl in three volumes, with the third volume known as the Ain-i-Akbari.
138.tq: Use the volume relationship to distinguish closely related Mughal works and authors.
xs: The **Akbarnama** has **three volumes**, the third being the **Ain-i-Akbari** — option **(2)**.
Its author is **Abul Fazl** (APPSC GS **2023**).
**Khafi Khan** wrote the Muntakhab-ul-Lubab; **Badauni** the critical **Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh**; **Jahangir** the **Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri**.
xa: Ain-i-Akbari (**1590**) = detailed **administrative report**.
**Tabaqat-i-Akbari** = **Nizamuddin Ahmad**.

138.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Work)
a. Tabaqat-i-Akbari
b. Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh
c. Padshahnama
d. Alamgirnama

List-II (Author)
i. Abdul Hamid Lahori
ii. Mirza Muhammad Kazim
iii. Nizamuddin Ahmad
iv. Abdul Qadir Badauni

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
138.x: Tabaqat-i-Akbari was written by Nizamuddin Ahmad; Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh by Badauni; Padshahnama by Abdul Hamid Lahori; and Alamgirnama by Mirza Muhammad Kazim.
138.tq: Start with the sure chronicle–author pair and eliminate codes with swapped Mughal writers.
xs: Correct code **a–iii, b–iv, c–i, d–ii** — option **(1)**.
**Tabaqat-i-Akbari** — **Nizamuddin Ahmad**; **Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh** — **Badauni**.
**Padshahnama** — **Abdul Hamid Lahori**; **Alamgirnama** — **Mirza Muhammad Kazim**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes wrongly credit Tabaqat-i-Akbari to **Badauni**.
Sultanate-era **Tabaqat-i-Nasiri** = **Minhaj-us-Siraj**.

138.s:
Consider the following statements about Mughal literary works:
1. The Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri is an autobiography.
2. Jahangir patronised the dictionary Farhang-i-Jahangiri.
3. The Muntakhab-ul-Lubab was written by Khafi Khan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
138.x: All three statements are correct. Jahangir wrote the Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri, patronised Farhang-i-Jahangiri, and Khafi Khan wrote the Muntakhab-ul-Lubab.
138.tq: Combine related literary facts while checking that each author and work belongs to the correct period.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri** = Jahangir's **autobiography**; he patronised the **Farhang-i-Jahangiri** dictionary.
**Muntakhab-ul-Lubab** = **Khafi Khan**.
xa: ⚠ Babur's Tuzuk (**Turki** memoir) ≠ Jahangir's Tuzuk.
**Futuhat-i-Alamgiri** = **Ishwardas Nagar**.

138.s: Akbar’s translation department at Fatehpur Sikri was known as
138.x: Maktab Khana was Akbar’s translation department at Fatehpur Sikri.
138.tq: Distinguish an administrative-cultural institution from a religious assembly hall.
xs: Akbar's translation bureau was the **Maktab Khana** at **Fatehpur Sikri** — option **(3)**.
**Ibadat Khana** was the house of worship for religious debates.
xa: Purpose: **cross-cultural understanding** among the nobility.
Its output included the **Razmnama** (Mahabharata).
Earlier precedent: **Panchatantra** → **Kalila wa Dimna**.

138.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
138.x: Lilavati was translated by Faizi. Maulana Shah Muhammad Shahabadi was associated with the translation of Rajatarangini.
138.tq: Find the swapped translator by checking the less familiar pair.
xs: **Lilavati — Shahabadi** is wrong: **Faizi** translated Lilavati — option **(4)**.
**Maulana Shah Muhammad Shahabadi** translated the **Rajatarangini**.
**Atharvaveda — Haji Ibrahim Sirhindi**, **Mahabharata — Razmnama** and **Ramayana — Badauni** are correct.
xa: **Lilavati** = **Bhaskaracharya**'s mathematics.
⚠ **Razmnama** = Mahabharata; **Sirr-i-Akbar** = Upanishads.

138.s:
Who among the following were associated with the Persian translation of the Mahabharata known as Razmnama?
1. Badauni
2. Naqib Khan
3. Haji Ibrahim Sirhindi
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
138.x: Badauni and Naqib Khan, along with others, were associated with the translation of the Mahabharata as Razmnama. Haji Ibrahim Sirhindi translated the Atharvaveda.
138.tq: Separate translators of different Sanskrit works.
xs: **Badauni** and **Naqib Khan** (**1 and 2 only**) — option **(2)**.
**Haji Ibrahim Sirhindi** translated the **Atharvaveda**, not the Mahabharata.
xa: Badauni also translated the **Valmiki Ramayana**.
**Daswant** illustrated the **Razmnama**.

138.s: Lilavati, translated into Persian during Akbar’s reign, was originally a work on
138.x: Lilavati was Bhaskaracharya's mathematical work, translated into Persian by Faizi during Akbar's reign.
138.tq: Use the original-text subject to distinguish translated works with similar religious associations.
xs: **Lilavati** was a work on **mathematics by Bhaskaracharya** — option **(2)**.
**Faizi** translated it into Persian in **Akbar's** reign.
xa: Faizi was a **Persian poet** with **Sufi themes** in Akbar's literary circle.
Akbar's **Maktab Khana** at Fatehpur Sikri was the translation bureau.
Vedanta link = **Dara Shikoh**'s **Majma-ul-Bahrain** and **Sirr-i-Akbar**.

138.s: Dara Shikoh was associated with which Sufi order?
138.x: Dara Shikoh followed the Qadiri order and was associated with Miyan Mir and Muhibullah Shah.
138.tq: Distinguish closely related Sufi orders by their associated personalities.
xs: Dara Shikoh was a **Qadiri** Sufi — option **(2)**.
He was linked with **Miyan Mir** and **Muhibullah Shah**.
xa: Dara was **Shah Jahan's eldest son**.
**Majma-ul-Bahrain** = "Mingling of the Two Oceans" — **Sufism and Vedanta**.
**Manucci** served in **Dara's artillery**.

138.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Sirr-i-Akbar — Persian translation of the Upanishads
Majma-ul-Bahrain — Persian translation of the Ramayana
Razmnama — Persian translation of the Atharvaveda
Lilavati — Persian translation of the Rajatarangini
138.x: Sirr-i-Akbar, meaning ‘The Great Secret’, was Dara Shikoh’s Persian translation of the Upanishads.
138.tq: Start with the sure work–subject pair and eliminate swapped titles.
xs: **Sirr-i-Akbar** = Persian translation of the **Upanishads** — option **(1)**.
It is **Dara Shikoh's** "**the Great Secret**" (**1657**), covering **52 Upanishads**.
**Majma-ul-Bahrain** is on **Sufism and Vedanta**; **Razmnama** = **Mahabharata**; **Lilavati** = mathematics.
xa: Its **Latin** version by **Anquetil-Duperron** took the Upanishads to Europe.
**Rajatarangini** → **Maulana Shah Muhammad Shahabadi**.

138.s: Majma-ul-Bahrain, written by Dara Shikoh, deals primarily with the
o: development of Urdu in Mughal cantonments
common ground between Sufism and Vedanta
military campaigns of Shah Jahan in Central Asia
administrative systems of the Mughals and Safavids
138.x: Majma-ul-Bahrain, meaning ‘Mingling of the Two Oceans’, explores the common ground between Sufism and Vedanta.
138.tq: Use the title’s conceptual meaning to identify the subject of the work.
xs: **Majma-ul-Bahrain** deals with the **common ground between Sufism and Vedanta** — option **(2)**.
The title means "**Mingling of the Two Oceans**".
xa: Dara Shikoh was a **Qadiri** Sufi, Shah Jahan's eldest son.
His **Sirr-i-Akbar** (**1657**) translated **52 Upanishads**.

138.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
138.x: Pair A is wrong: Keshavdas of the Orchha court wrote Ramchandrika, Kavipriya, Rasikpriya and Ratan Bavani, not Ram Rasayan (the MPPSC 2025 trap). Tulsidas wrote Ramcharitmanas, Surdas Sur Sagar and Kavindracharya Saraswati Kavindra-kalpalata.
138.tq: Use the single false title among a cluster of genuine poet–work pairs.
xs: **Keshavdas — Ram Rasayan** is wrong — option **(1)**.
Keshavdas wrote **Ramchandrika**, **Kavipriya**, **Rasikpriya**, **Ratan Bavani** — **not Ram Rasayan** (MPPSC **2025**).
**Tulsidas — Ramcharitmanas**, **Surdas — Sur Sagar**, **Kavindracharya — Kavindra-kalpalata** are correct.
xa: Keshavdas belonged to the **Bundela court of Orchha**.
**Akbar's tolerance** led to a surge in Hindi literature.

138.s: Kavindracharya Saraswati is associated with which one of the following achievements?
o: Persuading Shah Jahan to remit the pilgrim tax at Banaras and Prayag
Writing the Persian translation of the Baburnama
138.x: Kavindracharya Saraswati obtained Shah Jahan's remission of the pilgrim tax at Banaras and Prayag and wrote Kavindra-kalpalata in Hindi.
138.tq: Identify the patronage-related achievement rather than confusing it with translation work.
xs: **Kavindracharya Saraswati** got **Shah Jahan to remit the pilgrim tax at Banaras and Prayag** — option **(2)**.
He wrote the Hindi **Kavindra-kalpalata**.
**Atharvaveda** = Haji Ibrahim Sirhindi; **Baburnama** translation = Abdur Rahim; **Tappa** = Shori Miyan.
xa: **Keshavdas** = Bundela court of **Orchha**.
**Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khana** was one of **Akbar's Navaratnas**.

138.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Hindi literary figures of the Mughal age is correct?
1. Tulsidas wrote Ramcharitmanas.
2. Tulsidas was a court poet of Akbar.
3. Surdas wrote Sur Sagar.
4. Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khana composed Hindi dohas.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
138.x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Tulsidas belonged to Akbar's age but was not a court poet of Akbar.
138.tq: Separate a poet’s period from formal court membership.
xs: Statements **1, 3 and 4** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: **Tulsidas** wrote **Ramcharitmanas**; statement 3: **Surdas** wrote **Sur Sagar**.
Statement 2 wrong: Tulsidas lived in **Akbar's age** but was **not a court poet**.
Statement 4: **Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khana** composed Hindi **dohas**.
xa: Akbar's literary circle: **Birbal**, **Faizi** (Persian poet), **Mulla Do-Piyaza** (court wit).
**Akbar's tolerance** led to a surge in Hindi literature.

138.s: Which of the following was a major consequence of Aurangzeb's Deccan wars?
o: They ended all Maratha resistance by 1689.
They drained the treasury because Aurangzeb spent about his last twenty-seven years campaigning in the Deccan.
They strengthened the Mughal treasury through uninterrupted revenue collection.
They led to the immediate abolition of the jagirdari system.
138.x: Aurangzeb spent approximately the last twenty-seven years of his reign campaigning in the Deccan against the Marathas, which drained the Mughal treasury.
138.tq: Connect prolonged military expenditure with financial decline.
xs: Aurangzeb's last ~**27 years** in the Deccan **drained the treasury** — option **(2)**.
He camped there against the **Marathas**; resistance did not end in **1689** — after **Sambhaji**'s execution came **Rajaram** at Jinji and **Tarabai**.
xa: **Jizya** (**1679**) alienated Rajputs, Marathas and Sikhs.
**Be-jagiri**: too many mansabdars for too few revenue-yielding jagirs.

138.s: Aurangzeb's reimposition of jizya in 1679 particularly alienated the
138.x: The religious policy, including the reimposition of jizya in 1679, alienated important groups such as the Rajputs, Marathas and Sikhs.
138.tq: Link the dated policy with the affected social and political groups.
xs: **Jizya** (**1679**) alienated the **Rajputs, Marathas and Sikhs** — option **(1)**.
It was part of Aurangzeb's **religious policy**, a cause of Mughal decline.
xa: Other causes: **Deccan wars**, **jagirdari crisis**, **Sayyid brothers**.
**Kavindracharya** had earlier got Shah Jahan to remit the **pilgrim tax** at Banaras and Prayag.

138.s:
Consider the following statements about the Sayyid brothers:
1. They were Abdullah Khan and Husain Ali Khan.
2. They controlled Jahandar Shah and Farrukhsiyar, deposed Farrukhsiyar in 1719 and installed puppet successors.
3. They were overthrown with the help of Murshid Quli Khan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
138.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Sayyid brothers were Abdullah Khan and Husain Ali Khan. Statement 2 is correct: they acted as kingmakers, controlling Jahandar Shah and Farrukhsiyar and deposing Farrukhsiyar in 1719. Statement 3 is wrong: they were overthrown with the help of Nizam-ul-Mulk, not Murshid Quli Khan. Hence '1 only' is incomplete, '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 3; the answer is 1 and 2 only.
138.tq: Sayyids fell to Muhammad Shah with Nizam-ul-Mulk's help; Murshid Quli Khan is the Bengal distractor.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: the Sayyid brothers were **Abdullah Khan** and **Husain Ali Khan**.
Statement 2: they controlled **Jahandar Shah** and **Farrukhsiyar**, deposed Farrukhsiyar (**1719**), then installed puppets.
Statement 3 wrong: they were overthrown with **Nizam-ul-Mulk's** help.
xa: They are called the **kingmakers**.
**Nizam-ul-Mulk** also took part in the siege of **Golconda**.

138.s: The translation movement, Persian-Indian painting and the development of Hindavi and Urdu together contributed to the growth of which cultural formation?
138.x: The interaction of translation, painting and Hindavi-Urdu literature helped create a composite Indo-Persian culture.
138.tq: Identify the broad cultural consequence of several connected developments.
xs: Together they created **a composite Indo-Persian culture** — option **(3)**.
Translation movement + **Persian-Indian painting** + **Hindavi/Urdu**.
xa: Mughal dispersal of painters → **Rajput and Pahari** schools.
Akbar's **Maktab Khana** promoted **cross-cultural understanding**.

138.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with reference to the development of culture under the Qutb Shahis?
o: Kuchipudi — growth associated with Siddhendra Yogi
Deccani Urdu — language prohibited in the Qutb Shahi court
Telugu — official language of the Qutb Shahi kingdom
Persian — language used only by village communities
138.x: The growth of Kuchipudi is associated with Siddhendra Yogi. Persian was the official language, Telugu was the people's language, and Deccani Urdu flourished rather than being prohibited.
138.tq: Use the correctly matched person and cultural development to eliminate reversed language claims.
xs: **Kuchipudi** grew under **Siddhendra Yogi** — option **(1)**.
Under the Qutb Shahis **Persian** was **official** and **Telugu** the **people's language** — options 3 and 4 reverse this.
**Deccani Urdu flourished**, it was not prohibited.
xa: **Abul Hasan Tana Shah** granted **Kuchipudi village** to its dancers.
Qutb Shahi Deccani painting (**Mir Hashim**) was independent of Mughal style.

138.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
138.x: Tabaqat-i-Nasiri was written by Minhaj-us-Siraj, whereas Tabaqat-i-Akbari is associated with Nizamuddin Ahmad.
138.tq: Separate two similarly titled historical works by matching each with its correct author.
xs: **Tabaqat-i-Nasiri — Minhaj-us-Siraj** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Tabaqat-i-Akbari** is by **Nizamuddin Ahmad**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes wrongly credit **Tabaqat-i-Akbari** to **Badauni**, who wrote the **Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh**.
Tabaqat-i-Nasiri is **Sultanate-era**.

138.s: Which Golconda ruler granted the village of Kuchipudi to its dancers?
138.x: Abul Hasan Tana Shah granted Kuchipudi village to the dancers of the form that grew under Siddhendra Yogi. Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah built the Char Minar and was the first Urdu poet with a diwan; Abdullah Qutb Shah's era is called the Golden Age of Urdu; Ibrahim Quli Qutb Shah is a distractor.
138.tq: Kuchipudi: Siddhendra Yogi (growth), Tana Shah (village grant).
xs: **Abul Hasan Tana Shah** granted **Kuchipudi** village to its dancers — option **(1)**.
Kuchipudi grew under **Siddhendra Yogi**.
**Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah** = first Urdu poet with a diwan; **Abdullah Qutb Shah**'s era = Golden Age of Urdu.
xa: Golconda was annexed by **Aurangzeb** in **1687**.

**Baburnama** is **Babur**'s memoir.
**Akbarnama** was extensively illustrated under Akbar.

138.s:
Assertion (A): Razmnama is associated with Akbar.
Reason (R): Razmnama is the Persian translation of the Mahabharata.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
138.x: Both are true but R does not explain A: the Razmnama is the Persian Mahabharata, but it is linked to Akbar because he commissioned it, not because of its content.
138.tq: Check whether R is the cause of A.
n: Razmnama is associated with Akbar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #85 · pp 167-168]
Razmnama is a Persian translation of the Mahabharata. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #85 · pp 167-168]
Mahabharata in Persian is associated with Akbar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #85 · pp 167-168]
xs: **Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A** — option **(2)**.
A: the **Razmnama** is associated with **Akbar**.
R: it is the **Persian translation** of the **Mahabharata**.
xa: Translators: **Naqib Khan**, **Badauni** and others of Akbar's **Maktab Khana**.
⚠ **Razmnama** = Mahabharata; **Sirr-i-Akbar** = Upanishads.
The **Ramayana in Persian** was by **Badauni**.

138.s:
Match List-I with List-II.

(b) Akbarnama
(c) Razmnama
(d) Padshahnama

(iii) Humayun
(iv) Akbar and Abul Fazl
138.x: Hamzanama goes with Humayun, Akbarnama with Akbar and its author Abul Fazl, Razmnama with the translators of Akbar's Maktab Khana, and Padshahnama with Shah Jahan, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
138.tq: Separate the history written by Abul Fazl from the translation made in the Maktab Khana.
n: Dastan-i-Amir Hamza is associated with Humayun. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #85 · pp 167-168]
Akbarnama is associated with Akbar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #85 · pp 167-168]
Abul Fazl is associated with Akbarnama. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #85 · pp 167-168]
Razmnama is associated with Akbar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #85 · pp 167-168]
Padshahnama is associated with Shah Jahan. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #85 · pp 167-168]
Mahabharata in Persian is associated with Akbar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #85 · pp 167-168]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i** — option **(4)**.
**Dastan-i-Amir Hamza** — **Humayun**; **Akbarnama** — **Akbar and Abul Fazl**.
**Razmnama** — Akbar's **Maktab Khana**; **Padshahnama** — **Shah Jahan**.
xa: The Hamzanama had about **1,400 paintings** by about **100 artists**.
**Tarikh-i-Alfi** is an Akbar-era historical work.
The Akbarnama's third volume is the **Ain-i-Akbari**.

138.s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Baburnama
(b) Akbarnama
(c) Tarikh-i-Alfi
(d) Padshahnama

(i) Official illustrated chronicle of Shah Jahan's reign

138.x: Baburnama is Babur's memoir in Chagatai Turkish, Akbarnama Abul Fazl's history of Akbar, Tarikh-i-Alfi a history of Islam's first millennium, and Padshahnama the chronicle of Shah Jahan, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
138.tq: Link each work to its author or subject period.
n: Baburnama is a Mughal memoir. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #85 · pp 167-168]
Baburnama consists of illustrated manuscripts. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #85 · pp 167-168]
