Padshahnama is a major Mughal illustrated manuscript. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #85 · pp 167-168]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i** — option **(2)**.
**Baburnama** — memoir in **Chagatai Turkish**; **Akbarnama** — **Abul Fazl's** history of Akbar.
**Tarikh-i-Alfi** — history of the **first thousand years of Islam**; **Padshahnama** — chronicle of **Shah Jahan**.
xa: Baburnama is also called the **Tuzuk-i-Baburi**.
**Padshahnama** is by **Abdul Hamid Lahori**.
**Humayun-nama** is by **Gulbadan Begum**.

138.s:
How many of the following are illustrated manuscripts produced at the Mughal court?
1. Dastan-i-Amir Hamza
2. Razmnama
3. Padshahnama
4. Ramcharitmanas
138.x: Three are illustrated Mughal court manuscripts: Dastan-i-Amir Hamza, Razmnama and Padshahnama. Ramcharitmanas is an Awadhi devotional poem by Tulsidas, not a Mughal court manuscript.
138.tq: Remove the one work composed outside the Mughal court.
n: Dastan-i-Amir Hamza is an early Mughal illustrated manuscript. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #85 · pp 167-168]
Razmnama is illustrated. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #85 · pp 167-168]
Padshahnama is a major Mughal illustrated manuscript. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #85 · pp 167-168]
Ramcharitmanas belongs to the Awadhi literary tradition. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #85 · pp 167-168]
xs: **Only three** are Mughal illustrated manuscripts — option **(3)**.
**Dastan-i-Amir Hamza**, **Razmnama** and **Padshahnama** were produced at the Mughal court.
**Ramcharitmanas** is **Tulsidas**'s work of Akbar's age; Tulsidas was **not a court poet**.
xa: **Akbarnama** and **Tarikh-i-Alfi** were also illustrated.
**Surdas** wrote the **Sur Sagar** in Akbar's age.
**Keshavdas** served the Bundela court of **Orchha**.

138.s:
How many of the following are associated with Persian translation or Persian literary tradition?
1. Razmnama
2. Ramayana in Persian
3. Mahabharata in Persian
4. Molla Ramayanam
138.x: Three are Persian translations made under Akbar: the Razmnama, the Persian Ramayana and the Persian Mahabharata, which is the Razmnama under another name. Molla Ramayanam is a Telugu work.
138.tq: Separate Persian translations from regional works.
n: Razmnama is a Persian translation of the Mahabharata. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #85 · pp 167-168]
Ramayana in Persian is a Persian translation. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #85 · pp 167-168]
Mahabharata in Persian is also known as Razmnama. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #85 · pp 167-168]
Mahabharata in Persian involves translation and illustration. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #85 · pp 167-168]
Molla Ramayanam belongs to the Telugu literary tradition. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #85 · pp 167-168]
xs: **Only three** — option **(3)**.
**Razmnama**, the **Ramayana in Persian** and the **Mahabharata in Persian** belong to the Persian translation tradition.
The **Razmnama** is itself the **Mahabharata in Persian**.
**Molla Ramayanam** is not part of this Persian tradition.
xa: The Persian Ramayana was translated by **Badauni**.
The **Atharvaveda** was translated by **Haji Ibrahim Sirhindi**.
**Faizi** translated **Lilavati**.

138.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Nashurullah translated the Panchatantra into Kalila-wa-Dimnah.
Abul Fazl translated the Panchatantra into Ayar-i-Danish.
Nizamuddin Panipati translated the Panchatantra into Yogavasistha.
Mulla Husain Waaiz Kashifi translated the Panchatantra into Anwar-i-Suheli.
138.x: Option C is incorrect: Nizamuddin Panipati translated the Yogavasistha into Persian, not the Panchatantra. Nasrullah, Abul Fazl and Kashifi did make Panchatantra versions.
138.tq: Check the work in each statement.
n: Nashurullah Munshi Shiraji translated the Panchatantra as Kalila-wa-Dimnah. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23-2 · pp 84-85]
Mulla Husain Waaiz Kashifi translated the Panchatantra as Anwar-i-Suheli. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23-2 · pp 84-85]
Abul Fazl translated the Panchatantra as Ayar-i-Danish. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23-2 · pp 84-85]
Nizamuddin Panipati translated Yogavasistha into Persian. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23-2 · pp 84-85]
xs: The incorrect statement: **Nizamuddin Panipati** translated the **Panchatantra** — option **(3)**.
Nizamuddin Panipati translated the **Yogavasistha** into **Persian**.
**Nashurullah** — **Kalila-wa-Dimnah**; **Abul Fazl** — **Ayar-i-Danish**; **Mulla Husain Waaiz Kashifi** — **Anwar-i-Suheli** — all Panchatantra versions.
xa: The Persian Yogavasistha (**Jog Bashisht**) was made for **Prince Salim**, and again under **Dara Shikoh**.
**Taj-ul-Din Maliki** translated the **Hitopadesha**.
**Faizi** supervised Akbar's Translation Department.

139.s:
Arrange the following Later Mughal rulers in chronological order of accession:
A. Farrukhsiyar
B. Bahadur Shah I
C. Shah Alam II
D. Jahandar Shah
139.x: The correct order is Bahadur Shah I, Jahandar Shah, Farrukhsiyar and Shah Alam II.
139.tq: Fix the first and last rulers before arranging the middle reigns.
xs: Correct order **B, D, A, C** — option **(1)**.
xa: APPSC-G1 **2024** order: Bahadur Shah I > Jahandar Shah > Farrukh Siyar > **Muhammad Shah** > Shah Alam II.
Between them: **Muhammad Shah** (**1719-1748**), **Ahmad Shah** (1748-54), **Alamgir II** (1754-59).
Last emperor: **Bahadur Shah Zafar** (**1837-1857**).

139.s: Which Later Mughal ruler released Shahu?
139.x: Bahadur Shah I, who reigned from 1707 to 1712, released Shahu.
139.tq: Associate the ruler with the specific administrative event.
xs: **Bahadur Shah I** (Muazzam, **1707-1712**) released **Shahu** from Mughal captivity — option **(4)**.
**Farrukhsiyar** was the Sayyids' puppet; **Muhammad Shah** faced Nadir Shah; **Jahandar Shah** was backed by Zulfiqar Khan.
xa: Bahadur Shah I was called "**Shah-i-Bekhabar**".
The **1719** grant gave **chauth and sardeshmukhi** of six Deccan subas to Shahu's agent **Balaji Vishwanath**.

139.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Farrukhsiyar is correct?
o: He ruled from 1719 to 1748 and faced Nadir Shah's invasion.
He was a puppet of the Sayyid brothers and gave the English duty-free trade in Bengal.
He was the last Mughal emperor and ruled from 1837 to 1857.
He released Shahu immediately after Aurangzeb's death.
139.x: Farrukhsiyar ruled from 1713 to 1719, was controlled by the Sayyid brothers, executed Banda Singh Bahadur in 1716, and granted the English duty-free trade in Bengal.
139.tq: Reject options that attach another Later Mughal's event to Farrukhsiyar.
xs: Farrukhsiyar was a **puppet of the Sayyid brothers** and gave the **English duty-free trade in Bengal** — option **(2)**.
He ruled **1713-1719**; his **1717 farman** is called the Company's "**Magna Carta**".
**1719-1748** and Nadir Shah = **Muhammad Shah**; **1837-1857** = **Bahadur Shah Zafar**; Shahu's release = **Bahadur Shah I**.
xa: He executed **Banda Singh Bahadur** (**1716**).
He was **blinded, deposed and killed** by the Sayyids, **1719**.
He gave Chin Qilich Khan the title **Nizam-ul-Mulk**.

139.s:
Consider the following statements about the fate of Later Mughal rulers:
1. Jahandar Shah was deposed and killed by Farrukh Siyar and the Sayyids.
2. Farrukh Siyar was blinded, deposed and killed by the Sayyids in 1719.
3. Ahmad Shah was blinded by Ghulam Qadir Rohilla in 1788.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
139.x: Statement 1 is correct: Jahandar Shah was deposed and killed by Farrukh Siyar and the Sayyids. Statement 2 is correct: the Sayyids blinded, deposed and killed Farrukh Siyar in 1719. Statement 3 is wrong: Ahmad Shah was blinded and deposed by Imad-ul-Mulk; it was Shah Alam II who was blinded by Ghulam Qadir Rohilla in 1788. So '1 only' is incomplete, while '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' wrongly include statement 3.
139.tq: Imad-ul-Mulk blinded Ahmad Shah and murdered Alamgir II; Ghulam Qadir Rohilla blinded Shah Alam II.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: **Jahandar Shah** was deposed and killed by **Farrukh Siyar and the Sayyids**.
Statement 2: **Farrukh Siyar** was **blinded, deposed and killed** by the Sayyids in **1719**.
Statement 3 wrong: **Ahmad Shah** was blinded by **Imad-ul-Mulk**; **Shah Alam II** was blinded by **Ghulam Qadir Rohilla** (**1788**).
xa: **Alamgir II** was murdered by **Imad-ul-Mulk**.
**Bahadur Shah Zafar** was exiled to **Rangoon**, died **1862**.

139.s: Who among the following was popularly known as ‘Rangeela’?
139.x: Muhammad Shah, who ruled from 1719 to 1748, was known as Rangeela.
139.tq: Directly identify the ruler associated with a well-known epithet.
xs: **Muhammad Shah** (**1719-1748**) was called "**Rangeela**" — option **(2)**.
**Nadir Shah** invaded in his reign (**1739**).
xa: He got rid of the Sayyids with **Nizam-ul-Mulk**'s help.
He gave Nizam-ul-Mulk the title **Asaf Jah** (**1725**).
Abdali's **first raid** came in **1748**.

139.s:
Consider the following statements about Muhammad Shah:
1. He got rid of the Sayyid brothers with the help of Nizam-ul-Mulk.
2. Nizam-ul-Mulk, Saadat Khan and Murshid Quli Khan became autonomous during his reign.
3. Nadir Shah invaded India during his reign.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: All three statements are correct. Muhammad Shah eliminated the Sayyid influence with Nizam-ul-Mulk’s help, witnessed the autonomy of major provincial rulers and faced Nadir Shah’s invasion in 1739.
139.tq: Check a ruler’s reign through political, provincial and invasion-related facts.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
Muhammad Shah got rid of the **Sayyids** with **Nizam-ul-Mulk**'s help.
**Nizam** (Deccan), **Saadat Khan** (Awadh) and **Murshid Quli Khan** (Bengal) became autonomous.
**Nadir Shah** invaded in **1739**, defeating him at **Karnal**.
xa: Husain Ali was killed in **1720**.
Abdali's **first raid**: **1748**.

139.s: Which of the following developments took place during the reign of Alamgir II?
o: The Battle of Plassey was fought in 1757 and Abdali invasions continued.
Ram Mohan Roy received the title Raja.
The Third Battle of Panipat was fought and Buxar was won.
The Company granted pension to the first Mughal pensioner.
139.x: Repeated invasions by Ahmad Shah Abdali and the Battle of Plassey in 1757 occurred during Alamgir II’s reign.
139.tq: Associate events with the correct reign instead of relying only on chronology.
xs: Under **Alamgir II**: **Plassey (1757)** and repeated **Abdali** invasions — option **(1)**.
Ram Mohan Roy's title "Raja" came from **Akbar II**; **Third Panipat** and **Buxar** fell under **Shah Alam II**.
Shah Alam II was the **first Mughal pensioner**.
xa: Alamgir II (**1754-59**) was **murdered by Imad-ul-Mulk**.
**Third Battle of Panipat**: **14 January 1761**.

139.s: With reference to Shah Alam II, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: He was the first Mughal ruler to release Shahu.
He became the first Mughal pensioner of the Company.
He was killed by the Sayyid brothers in 1719.
He gave Raja title to Ram Mohan Roy.
139.x: Shah Alam II became the first Mughal pensioner of the East India Company. He witnessed the Third Battle of Panipat and the Battle of Buxar during his reign.
139.tq: Separate the defining political position of Shah Alam II from facts belonging to other rulers.
xs: **Shah Alam II** was the **first Mughal pensioner of the Company** — option **(2)**.
**Shahu**'s release = **Bahadur Shah I**; killed by Sayyids in **1719** = **Farrukhsiyar**; Raja title = **Akbar II**.
xa: **Third Panipat (1761)** and **Buxar (1764)** came in his reign.
**Treaty of Allahabad (1765)**: he granted the **Diwani** of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.
Blinded by **Ghulam Qadir Rohilla**, **1788**.

139.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Bahadur Shah II — Exiled to Rangoon after 1857
Shah Alam II — Blinded by Ghulam Qadir Rohilla
Akbar II — Gave Ram Mohan Roy the title ‘Raja’
Muhammad Shah — Exiled to Rangoon after 1857
139.x: Muhammad Shah was not exiled to Rangoon. Bahadur Shah II was exiled to Rangoon after the Revolt of 1857; Shah Alam II was blinded by Ghulam Qadir Rohilla.
139.tq: Find the mismatched ruler and fate by eliminating well-known correct associations.
xs: **Muhammad Shah — exiled to Rangoon** is wrong — option **(4)**.
**Bahadur Shah II (Zafar)** was exiled to **Rangoon** after **1857**.
**Shah Alam II** — blinded by **Ghulam Qadir Rohilla**; **Akbar II** — gave **Ram Mohan Roy** the title "Raja": correct.
xa: Muhammad Shah faced **Nadir Shah** at **Karnal** (**1739**).
Akbar II (**1806-37**) was a **British pensioner**.

139.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Shah Alam II returned to Delhi under the protection of Mahadji Scindia.
2. He returned to Delhi in 1771–72.
3. Before returning, he lived at Allahabad under Company protection.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: All three statements are correct. Shah Alam II lived at Allahabad under Company protection and returned to Delhi in 1771–72 under Mahadji Scindia’s protection.
139.tq: Test a sequence of political circumstances rather than a single isolated date.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
After **Buxar**, Shah Alam II lived at **Allahabad** under **Company protection**.
He returned to Delhi in **1771-72** under **Mahadji Scindia**'s protection.
xa: This was in **Madhav Rao I**'s time.
From **1772** **Warren Hastings** stopped his annual grant.

139.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Sayyid brothers is NOT correct?
o: Husain Ali Khan was the Mir Bakhshi.
They were eliminated during the reign of Farrukh Siyar in 1713.
They dominated Mughal politics from 1713 to 1720.
139.x: The Sayyid brothers were eliminated under Muhammad Shah; Husain Ali Khan was killed in 1720. They did not meet this fate during Farrukh Siyar’s reign in 1713.
139.tq: Use the NOT format to separate the period of their dominance from the period of their elimination.
xs: "**Eliminated during Farrukh Siyar's reign in 1713**" is wrong — option **(2)**.
They were **eliminated under Muhammad Shah**; **Husain Ali** was killed in **1720**.
**Husain Ali Khan** = **mir bakhshi**; **Abdullah Khan** = **wazir**; king-makers **1713 to 1720**: correct.
xa: They were overthrown with **Nizam-ul-Mulk's** help.
They made **Farrukh Siyar** emperor, then deposed and killed him (**1719**).

139.s: Which one of the following correctly states the consequence of Ahmad Shah Abdali’s invasions?
o: Bengal and Bihar were ceded to him after the Battle of Karnal.
Punjab and Multan were ceded to him, and he repeatedly invaded during Alamgir II’s reign.
He established the autonomous state of Hyderabad with Puran Chand as Diwan.
He carried away the Peacock Throne after defeating Muhammad Shah at Karnal.
139.x: Punjab and Multan were ceded to Ahmad Shah Abdali, and his repeated invasions occurred during the reign of Alamgir II. The other options describe Nadir Shah’s actions or Hyderabad’s administration.
139.tq: Distinguish the consequences and identities of Nadir Shah and Ahmad Shah Abdali.
xs: **Punjab and Multan** were ceded to Abdali, and he **raided repeatedly under Alamgir II** — option **(2)**.
Karnal and the **Peacock Throne** belong to **Nadir Shah**; **Puran Chand** was **Nizam-ul-Mulk**'s Diwan.
xa: Abdali raided from **1748** (first raid) to **1767**.
He defeated the Marathas at **Third Panipat** (**14 January 1761**).
Punjab and Multan were ceded under **Ahmad Shah**.

139.s: The Farman of 1717 issued by Farrukh Siyar is significant because it:
o: Granted chauth and sardeshmukhi to Shahu's agent
Exempted the English Company from customs duties in Bengal
Granted the Company Diwani rights in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa
Transferred Kora and Allahabad to the Company
139.x: The Farman of 1717 exempted the Company from customs duties in Bengal and was called the Company's Magna Carta.
139.tq: Distinguish the 1717 Farman from the 1765 Treaty of Allahabad.
xs: The **1717 farman** **exempted the Company from customs duties in Bengal** — option **(2)**.
It was called the Company's "**Magna Carta**".
Chauth to Shahu's agent = **1719**; Diwani = **1765**.
xa: ⚠ **1717** = customs exemption; **1719** = Marathas' chauth; **1765** = Company's Diwani.
It was issued by **Farrukh Siyar** (**1713-1719**).

139.s: The Mughal grant of 1719, issued through the Sayyids, granted to Balaji Vishwanath, as Shahu's agent:
o: Diwani rights in Bengal and Bihar
Kora and Allahabad with an annual payment
Chauth and sardeshmukhi of the six Deccan subas
139.x: The 1719 grant recognised Shahu's claim to chauth and sardeshmukhi from the six Deccan subas through his agent Balaji Vishwanath.
139.tq: Separate the content of the 1719 grant from the later Company concessions.
xs: The **1719** grant gave **chauth and sardeshmukhi of the six Deccan subas** — option **(3)**.
It went to Shahu's agent **Balaji Vishwanath**, issued through the **Sayyids**.
Diwani = **1765**; customs exemption = **1717**.
xa: **Shahu** had been released by **Bahadur Shah I**.
⚠ **1717** = Company; **1719** = Marathas; **1765** = Diwani.

139.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Treaty of Allahabad of 1765?
o: The Sayyids granted the Company chauth of the Deccan subas.
Shah Alam II granted the Company the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.
Farrukh Siyar exempted the Company from customs duties in Bengal.
Akbar II granted the Company the title of Raja.
139.x: Under the Treaty of Allahabad, Shah Alam II granted the Company the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa. The emperor received Kora and Allahabad and an annual payment of Rs 26 lakh.
139.tq: Identify the correct grantor and the precise territorial content of the treaty.
xs: At the **Treaty of Allahabad (1765)** **Shah Alam II** granted the **Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa** — option **(2)**.
Chauth = Sayyids (**1719**); customs exemption = **Farrukh Siyar** (**1717**); "Raja" title = **Akbar II** to Ram Mohan Roy.
xa: The emperor got **Kora and Allahabad** and **Rs 26 lakh** a year.
Diwani (**1765**) = the Company's **legal foothold**.

139.s:
With reference to the Treaty of Allahabad, consider the following statements:
1. Shah Alam II received Kora and Allahabad.
2. The emperor was entitled to an annual payment of Rs 26 lakh.
3. Warren Hastings continued this annual payment without interruption after 1772.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. From 1772 Warren Hastings stopped the annual grant and sold Kora and Allahabad to the Nawab of Awadh.
139.tq: Use the date-based exception to identify the false continuation claim.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Shah Alam II got **Kora and Allahabad** and an annual **Rs 26 lakh**.
Statement 3 wrong: from **1772** **Warren Hastings** **stopped** the grant and sold Kora and Allahabad to the **Nawab of Awadh**.
xa: The treaty gave the Company the **Diwani** of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.
Shah Alam II returned to Delhi in **1771-72** under **Mahadji Scindia**.

139.s: Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah held which Mughal offices before establishing the Asaf Jahi state?
o: Subedar of the Deccan and Wazir
Nawab of Carnatic and Mir Bakshi
Subedar of Bengal and Diwan of Awadh
Diwan of Bengal and Subedar of Gujarat
139.x: Nizam-ul-Mulk was Subedar of the Deccan and also served as Wazir in the Mughal administration.
139.tq: Distinguish the founder's Mughal offices from those of other successor-state founders.
xs: Nizam-ul-Mulk was **Subedar of the Deccan** and later **Wazir** — option **(1)**.
**Farrukh Siyar** made him Mughal Governor of the Deccan.
xa: Titles: **Chin Qilich Khan** (Aurangzeb), **Nizam-ul-Mulk** (Farrukh Siyar), **Asaf Jah** (Muhammad Shah, **1725**).
Bengal's **Murshid Quli Khan** was Diwan, then Nazim.

139.s: The founder of the Carnatic state of Arcot was
139.x: Saadatullah Khan, also rendered as Saadullah Khan, founded the Carnatic state of Arcot and named his nephew Dost Ali as successor.
139.tq: Use the founder-name and regional-state association.
xs: **Saadatullah Khan** founded the **Carnatic (Arcot)** — option **(1)**.
He was **Nawab under the Nizam** and named his nephew **Dost Ali** successor without the Nizam's approval.
**Daud Khan** governed the Deccan for Zulfiqar Khan; **Safdar Jung** = Awadh; **Puran Chand** = Nizam's Diwan.
xa: ⚠ **Saadat Khan** = Awadh; **Saadatullah Khan** = Carnatic.
The Nizam himself was **Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah**, Subedar of the **Deccan**.

139.s: Murshid Quli Khan held which offices in Bengal?
139.x: Murshid Quli Khan first served as Diwan and later became Nazim of Bengal. He ruled Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.
139.tq: Test the exact office held by a regional founder rather than merely the state associated with him.
xs: **Murshid Quli Khan** was **Diwan, then Nazim** of Bengal — option **(4)**.
He ruled **Bengal, Bihar and Orissa**.
xa: He became autonomous under **Muhammad Shah**.
APPSC-G1 **2024** match: Murshid Quli Khan — **Bengal**.

139.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

List-I (Person)
a. Husain Ali Khan
b. Murshid Quli Khan
c. Chin Qilich Khan
d. Safdar Jung

List-II (Association)
i. Awadh
ii. Bengal
iii. Sayyid brother
iv. Nizam of Hyderabad

Which of the following is the correct code?
139.x: Husain Ali Khan was a Sayyid brother, Murshid Quli Khan was associated with Bengal, Chin Qilich Khan was the Nizam of Hyderabad and Safdar Jung was associated with Awadh.
139.tq: Start with the sure pair and eliminate codes that repeat the wrong regional association.
xs: Correct code **a–iii, b–ii, c–iv, d–i** — option **(1)**.
**Husain Ali Khan** — **Sayyid brother**; **Murshid Quli Khan** — **Bengal**.
**Chin Qilich Khan** — **Nizam of Hyderabad**; **Safdar Jung** — **Awadh**.
xa: This is the APPSC-G1 **2024** match.
Husain Ali Khan was **mir bakhshi**, killed in **1720**.

139.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Awadh succession:
1. Safdar Jung was the nephew and son-in-law of Saadat Khan.
2. Safdar Jung became Nawab of Awadh and Wazir.
3. Shuja-ud-Daula, who came later, fought at the Battle of Buxar.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: All three statements are correct. Safdar Jung, Saadat Khan's nephew and son-in-law, succeeded him as Nawab of Awadh and also became Wazir; his successor Shuja-ud-Daula fought at Buxar.
139.tq: Test succession through relationship, office and a later military event.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**Safdar Jung** was Saadat Khan's **nephew and son-in-law**.
He became **Nawab of Awadh and Wazir**; later **Shuja-ud-Daula** fought at **Buxar**.
xa: **Saadat Khan Burhan-ul-Mulk** became Subedar of Awadh in **1722**.
**Buxar** (**1764**) came in **Shah Alam II**'s reign.

139.s:
Consider the following statements about Saadat Khan Burhan-ul-Mulk:
1. He founded the independent state of Awadh.
2. He joined the conspiracy against the Sayyid brothers.
3. He was the founder of the Carnatic state of Arcot.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
139.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Saadat Khan founded independent Awadh and took part in the conspiracy against the Sayyids (UPPSC 2023). Statement 3 is wrong: the Carnatic (Arcot) was founded by Saadatullah Khan, a similar-sounding name. Option A leaves out statement 2; options C and D include the false statement 3.
139.tq: Saadat Khan = Awadh; Saadatullah Khan = Carnatic.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
**Saadat Khan** founded **independent Awadh** and joined the **conspiracy against the Sayyids** (UPPSC **2023**).
Statement 3 wrong: the **Carnatic** was founded by **Saadatullah Khan**.
xa: ⚠ **Saadat Khan** = Awadh; **Saadatullah Khan** = Carnatic.
Successor: **Safdar Jung**.

139.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding Nizam-ul-Mulk's role in the decline of Mughal central authority?
o: He helped the Sayyid brothers retain power and appointed Murshid Quli Khan as Diwan.
He helped overthrow the Sayyid brothers and appointed Puran Chand as Diwan.
He founded Awadh after defeating Saadat Khan.
He was appointed Diwan of Bengal by Farrukhsiyar.
139.x: Nizam-ul-Mulk helped overthrow the Sayyid brothers and appointed Puran Chand as Diwan.
139.tq: Identify the correct political alliance and appointment.
xs: Nizam-ul-Mulk **helped overthrow the Sayyid brothers** and **appointed Puran Chand as Diwan** — option **(2)**.
He ran a tolerant, Mughal-type **jagirdari** administration.
**Murshid Quli Khan** was **Diwan of Bengal**; **Awadh** was founded by **Saadat Khan**.
xa: He kept the **Marathas** out in his lifetime; after his death (**1748**) Hyderabad was vulnerable.
He defeated **Mubariz Khan** at **Shakar Kheda** (**1724**).

139.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
139.x: Aurangzeb conferred the title Chin Qilich Khan, Farrukh Siyar conferred Nizam-ul-Mulk, and Muhammad Shah conferred Asaf Jah in 1725.
139.tq: Start from the sure title-giver pair and eliminate the swapped authorities.
xs: **Asaf Jah — Muhammad Shah** (**1725**) is correct — option **(3)**.
**Chin Qilich Khan** was conferred by **Aurangzeb**; **Nizam-ul-Mulk** by **Farrukh Siyar**.
xa: ⚠ Chin Qilich Khan – Nizam-ul-Mulk – Asaf Jah = **Aurangzeb – Farrukh Siyar – Muhammad Shah**.
His name: **Mir Qamar-ud-din Siddiqi**, the **first Nizam**.

139.s: Which one of the following statements about the first Nizam is correct?
o: He accepted the Subsidiary Alliance in 1798.
He kept the Marathas out of Hyderabad during his lifetime.
He was defeated at Shakar Kheda by Mubariz Khan.
139.x: The first Nizam kept the Marathas out during his lifetime. He died in 1748; the Subsidiary Alliance was accepted much later by Nizam Ali Khan.
139.tq: Separate the founder's achievements from those of the later Nizam Ali Khan.
xs: The first Nizam **kept the Marathas out of Hyderabad during his lifetime** — option **(3)**.
The **Subsidiary Alliance** (**1798**) was accepted by **Nizam Ali Khan**; Nizam Ali ruled until **1803**.
At **Shakar Kheda** he **defeated** Mubariz Khan.
xa: After his death (**1748**) Hyderabad became vulnerable.
**Puran Chand** was his Diwan.

139.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Asaf Jahi dynasty is correct?
o: Hyderabad State was integrated into the Indian Union through Operation Polo in 1948.
Mir Osman Ali Khan ruled from 1869 to 1911.
The dynasty continued as the ruling power after 1948.
Nizam Ali Khan was the last Nizam of Hyderabad.
139.x: Operation Polo integrated Hyderabad State into the Indian Union in 1948. Mir Osman Ali Khan was the last Nizam.
139.tq: Distinguish the end of the dynasty from the end of individual rulers.
xs: **Operation Polo** integrated **Hyderabad State into the Indian Union** in **1948** — option **(1)**.
**Mir Osman Ali Khan** ruled **1911-48**, not 1869-1911 (that was **Mir Mahbub Ali Khan**).
The last Nizam was **Mir Osman Ali Khan**, not Nizam Ali Khan.
xa: The dynasty ruled until **1948**.
First Nizam: **Asaf Jah I** (**1724-48**).

139.s: Who founded the Asaf Jahi state of Hyderabad in 1724?
139.x: Mir Qamar-ud-din Khan Siddiqi founded the Asaf Jahi state and became its first Nizam.
139.tq: Identify the founder directly and distinguish him from the early successors.
xs: **Mir Qamar-ud-din Khan Siddiqi** founded the Asaf Jahi state — option **(1)**.
He was the **first Nizam** (APPSC **2018**, **2022**).
**Mubariz Khan** was the rival he defeated at **Shakar Kheda** (**1724**); **Nasir Jung** and **Nizam Ali Khan** were later Nizams.
xa: Titles: **Chin Qilich Khan**, **Nizam-ul-Mulk**, **Asaf Jah**.
**Puran Chand** was his Diwan.

139.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the establishment of the Asaf Jahi state:
1. Farrukh Siyar appointed Mir Qamar-ud-din Khan as Mughal Governor of the Deccan.
2. He defeated Mubariz Khan at Shakar Kheda.
3. The independent Asaf Jahi state was established in 1748.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The state was established in 1724, not 1748; 1748 was the year of the founder's death.
139.tq: Find the changed date in the statement set.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: **Farrukh Siyar** made him **Governor of the Deccan**; statement 2: he defeated **Mubariz Khan** at **Shakar Kheda**.
Statement 3 wrong: the state dates from **1724**; **1748** was the founder's death.
xa: After **1748** Hyderabad became vulnerable to the **Marathas**.
**Muhammad Shah** gave him the title **Asaf Jah** (**1725**).

139.s: Which one of the following was NOT a major cause of the decline of the Mughal Empire?
o: The invasions of Nadir Shah and Ahmad Shah Abdali
The long Deccan wars and the resulting drain on the treasury
The strengthening of central authority by independent nobles
139.x: Independent nobles weakened, rather than strengthened, central authority. The Deccan wars, Maratha rise and invasions were among the major causes of decline.
139.tq: Find the reversed effect in a cause-of-decline option.
xs: "**Strengthening of central authority by independent nobles**" is not a cause — option **(4)**.
Nobles **acted independently** and their rivalries **broke central authority**.
**Nadir Shah** and **Abdali**'s invasions, the **Maratha rise** and the long **Deccan wars** were real causes.
xa: **Jagirdari and agrarian crises** → peasant and zamindar revolts.
**European companies** also contributed.

139.s: At its greatest extent under Aurangzeb, the Mughal Empire extended approximately from:
o: Kashmir to Jinji and the Hindukush to Chittagong
Kabul to Bijapur and Sindh to Assam
Punjab to Madurai and the Arabian Sea to the Bay of Bengal
Delhi to the Narmada and Gujarat to Bengal
139.x: Under Aurangzeb the empire reached from Kashmir to Jinji and from the Hindukush to Chittagong.
139.tq: Recall both geographical limits together instead of relying on one directional clue.
xs: The empire reached from **Kashmir to Jinji** and the **Hindukush to Chittagong** — option **(1)**.
This was its **greatest extent** under **Aurangzeb**.
xa: His intolerant policies and long **Deccan wars** weakened its foundations and drained the treasury.
Golconda became the **21st Mughal suba** after **1687**.

139.s:
Consider the following statements about the causes of Mughal decline:
1. Aurangzeb's long Deccan wars weakened the foundations of the empire and drained the treasury.
2. The Sayyids' control contributed to corruption and mismanagement.
3. Peasant and zamindar revolts followed the jagirdari and agrarian crises.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: All three statements are correct. Religious policies, prolonged warfare, factional noble politics, fiscal crisis and agrarian unrest combined to weaken the empire.
139.tq: Test cumulative causation by checking each internal cause separately.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
Statement 1: Aurangzeb's long **Deccan wars** weakened foundations and **drained the treasury**.
Statement 2: the **Sayyids'** control bred **corruption and mismanagement**.
Statement 3: **jagirdari and agrarian crises** shrank the fiscal base → **peasant and zamindar revolts**.
xa: ⚠ **Irfan Habib** = **agrarian crisis**; **Satish Chandra** = **jagirdari crisis**.
Revisionist view: the 18th century = **regional growth**, not collapse.

139.s: Who wrote both History of Aurangzeb and Fall of the Mughal Empire?
139.x: Jadunath Sarkar authored both History of Aurangzeb and Fall of the Mughal Empire.
139.tq: Match the historian with the distinctive pair of works.
xs: **Jadunath Sarkar** wrote **History of Aurangzeb** and **Fall of the Mughal Empire** — option **(2)**.
He blamed Aurangzeb's **religious policy**, personal failings and **weak successors**.
**Irfan Habib** = **Agrarian System of Mughal India** (**1963**); **Satish Chandra** = **Parties and Politics at the Mughal Court**; **Moreland** = **India at the Death of Akbar**.
xa: **M. Athar Ali** (Mughal Nobility under Aurangzeb): enlarged nobility worsened the **jagir shortage**.
**Bernier**: no private property in land, so no incentive to improve.

139.s: The agrarian-crisis interpretation of Mughal decline, emphasising the over-exploitation of peasants and the resulting revolts, is associated with:
139.x: Irfan Habib explained the decline through an agrarian crisis in The Agrarian System of Mughal India (1963), arguing that over-exploitation of peasants provoked revolts.
139.tq: Link the interpretation to the historian rather than merely recalling the book title.
xs: The **agrarian-crisis** view is **Irfan Habib**'s — option **(4)**.
In **The Agrarian System of Mughal India** (**1963**) he argued that **over-exploitation of peasants** set off revolts.
**Jadunath Sarkar** blamed Aurangzeb's **religious policy**; **Athar Ali** the enlarged nobility; **Bernier** the absence of **private property in land**.
xa: ⚠ **Irfan Habib** = **agrarian crisis**; **Satish Chandra** = **jagirdari crisis**.
Jagirdari and agrarian crises shrank the **fiscal base** → **peasant and zamindar revolts**.

139.s: M. Athar Ali attributed the worsening of the jagir shortage primarily to:
o: The transfer of all jagirs to European companies
The enlargement of the nobility through the inclusion of Deccanis and Marathas
The abolition of the mansabdari system by Farrukh Siyar
The decline of agriculture caused by Nadir Shah's raid
139.x: Athar Ali argued that the enlarged nobility, including Deccanis and Marathas, intensified the shortage of jagirs.
139.tq: Apply the historian's specific causal argument rather than choosing a general cause of decline.
xs: Athar Ali blamed **the enlargement of the nobility** through **Deccanis and Marathas** — option **(2)**.
This worsened the **jagir shortage**.
xa: **Satish Chandra** = the **jagirdari crisis**: too few jagirs for too many nobles.
Nadir Shah's raid came in **1739**, well after the jagir crisis began.

139.s: François Bernier's explanation of Mughal decline emphasised that:
o: The empire collapsed mainly because of the Maratha naval power.
The jagirdari crisis resulted from too few nobles in the imperial service.
The absence of private property in land reduced the incentive for improvement and led towards ruin.
Aurangzeb's religious policy alone caused the complete collapse of agriculture.
139.x: Bernier associated the absence of private property in land with a lack of incentive to improve it and predicted ruin.
139.tq: Identify the precise argument attached to the named historian.
xs: Bernier held that the **absence of private property in land** removed the **incentive to improve** and led to **ruin** — option **(3)**.
The **jagirdari crisis** was about **too many nobles**, not too few — option 2 is wrong.
xa: Bernier's work: **Travels in the Mogul Empire**.
**Jadunath Sarkar** blamed Aurangzeb's **religious policy** and **weak successors**.

139.s: The revisionist interpretation of the eighteenth century views it chiefly as a period of:
o: Exclusive European control over the peasant surplus
Regional growth, with successor states controlling economic and law-and-order systems
Uninterrupted Mughal centralisation under weak successors
139.x: The revisionist view treats the eighteenth century as a period of regional growth. The new states managed their own economic and law-and-order systems and controlled peasant surplus.
139.tq: Contrast the revisionist regional-growth interpretation with the older collapse narrative.
xs: Revisionists see the 18th century as **regional growth**, with successor states running **economic and law-and-order systems** — option **(3)**.
The new states **controlled the peasant surplus** — not "complete collapse".
xa: Successor states: **Hyderabad**, **Bengal**, **Awadh**, **Carnatic**, **Rohilkhand**, **Farrukhabad**.
The decline's vacuum was filled by regional states, the **Marathas** and the **East India Company**.

139.s: The decline of the Mughal Empire created a power vacuum that was successively filled by:
o: Regional states, the Marathas and finally the East India Company
The Rajputs, the Sikhs and the Portuguese
The Mughals, the Marathas and the Ottoman Empire
The Sayyids, the Afghans and the French alone
139.x: The decline opened space for regional successor states, the Marathas and ultimately the East India Company.
139.tq: Recall the broad political sequence following imperial decline.
xs: The vacuum was filled by **regional states, the Marathas and finally the East India Company** — option **(1)**.
**Diwani (1765)** gave the Company its **legal foothold**.
xa: Post-decline Hyderabad (**Asaf Jahi**) grew out of the **Mughal Deccan**.
Revisionist view: **regional growth**, not collapse.

139.s: The Diwani granted in 1765 is regarded as the East India Company's:
o: First exemption from customs duties in Bengal
139.x: The Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa, obtained in 1765, provided the Company's legal foothold for territorial and fiscal power in India.
139.tq: Link the constitutional-financial concession with its wider historical significance.
xs: The **1765 Diwani** was the Company's **legal foothold** — option **(1)**.
Granted by **Shah Alam II** at the **Treaty of Allahabad**: Diwani of **Bengal, Bihar and Orissa**.
The customs exemption came in **1717** (Farrukh Siyar); the Raja title was **Akbar II**'s gift to Ram Mohan Roy.
xa: ⚠ **1717** = customs exemption; **1719** = Marathas' chauth; **1765** = Diwani.
The emperor got **Kora and Allahabad** and **Rs 26 lakh** a year.

139.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes the raids of Nadir Shah and Ahmad Shah Abdali?
o: Nadir Shah took Punjab, whereas Abdali took the Koh-i-Noor and Peacock Throne.
Nadir Shah's raid occurred in 1739, while Abdali's raids began from 1748.
Nadir Shah's raids began in 1748, while Abdali invaded in 1739.
Both raids began in 1761 and ended with the Battle of Panipat.
139.x: Nadir Shah raided India in 1739, taking the Koh-i-Noor and Peacock Throne. Abdali's raids began from 1748, took Punjab and culminated in Panipat in 1761.
139.tq: Separate the two invaders by starting date and the distinctive result of each raid.
xs: **Nadir Shah**'s raid was in **1739**; **Abdali**'s raids began from **1748** — option **(2)**.
Nadir Shah took the **Koh-i-Noor** and **Peacock Throne**; Abdali took **Punjab** — option 1 reverses them.
xa: Abdali's raids ended with **Panipat (1761)**.
Nadir Shah defeated **Muhammad Shah** at **Karnal**.
**Abdali** had been **Nadir Shah's general**.

139.s: Who was the first ruler stated to have invaded parts of India?
139.x: Darius I of Persia (Achaemenid) was the first foreign ruler to invade parts of north-west India, around 518 BCE, before Alexander.
139.tq: Recall the earliest invader.
n: Darius I is listed first among the invaders and groups. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #141 · pp 244-246]
Darius I was the first ruler stated to have invaded parts of India. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #141 · pp 244-246]
Darius I's invasion was the first Persian invasion. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #141 · pp 244-246]
xs: **Darius I** is the first ruler stated to have invaded parts of India — option **(1)**.
He led the **first Persian invasion** of **northwestern India**, approximately **522–486 BCE**.
**Alexander** came later (approximately **326 BCE**); **Muhammad bin Qasim** in **712 CE**; **Mahmud Ghazni** made **17 attacks** later still.
xa: Alexander **defeated Porus** at the **Jhelum**.
The **Sakas** (Scythians) targeted **western India** and were later defeated by **Chandragupta II**.
The **Kushanas** (approximately **1st century CE**) are linked with **Kanishka**.

139.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Alexander defeated Porus at the Jhelum.
Skandagupta defeated the first Huna invasion.
Muhammad bin Qasim conquered North India.
The Sakas were later defeated by Chandragupta II.
139.x: Option C is incorrect: Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh in 712 CE, not North India. Alexander beat Porus at the Jhelum, Skandagupta repelled the Hunas and Chandragupta II defeated the Sakas.
139.tq: Check the region in each statement.
n: Alexander defeated Porus at the Jhelum. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #141 · pp 244-246]
Chandragupta II later defeated the Sakas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #141 · pp 244-246]
Skandagupta defeated the first Huna invasion. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #141 · pp 244-246]
Muhammad bin Qasim targeted Sindh. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #141 · pp 244-246]
Muhammad bin Qasim's invasion resulted in the Arab conquest of Sindh. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #141 · pp 244-246]
xs: The incorrect statement: **Muhammad bin Qasim conquered North India** — option **(3)**.
Muhammad bin Qasim made the **Arab conquest** of **Sindh** in **712 CE**, opposing **Dahir**.
**Alexander** defeated **Porus** at the **Jhelum**; **Skandagupta** defeated the **first Huna invasion**; the **Sakas** were defeated by **Chandragupta II** — all true.
xa: **Toramana** led the **second Huna attack**; **Yashodharman** defeated **Mihirakula**.
**Mahmud Ghazni** made **17 attacks** on northern India for plunder.
**Darius I** led the **first Persian invasion**.

139.s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Darius I
(b) Alexander
(c) Sakas
(d) Hunas

List-II
(i) Gupta Empire
(ii) Porus
(iii) NW India
(iv) Western India
139.x: Darius I invaded NW India, Alexander fought Porus, the Sakas ruled western India and the Hunas attacked the Gupta Empire, giving a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
139.tq: Recall the target of each invader.
n: Darius I targeted northwestern India. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #141 · pp 244-246]
Alexander opposed Porus. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #141 · pp 244-246]
The Sakas targeted western India. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #141 · pp 244-246]
The Hunas targeted the Gupta Empire. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #141 · pp 244-246]
The Sakas targeted western India. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #141 · pp 244-246]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i** — option **(3)**.
**Darius I** — **northwestern India**; **Alexander** — opposed **Porus**.
**Sakas** — **western India**; **Hunas** — the **Gupta Empire**.
xa: The Hunas came approximately in the **5th century CE**, the **Gupta period**.
**Skandagupta** defeated the first Huna invasion.
Alexander came approximately **326 BCE** and defeated Porus at the **Jhelum**.

139.s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Muhammad bin Qasim
(b) Mahmud Ghazni
(c) Muhammad Ghori
(d) Timur

List-II
(i) 1398 invasion of Delhi
(ii) Arab conquest of Sindh
(iii) 17 attacks and plunder
(iv) Tarain and Chandawar
139.x: Muhammad bin Qasim made the Arab conquest of Sindh, Mahmud Ghazni made 17 raids, Muhammad Ghori fought at Tarain and Chandawar, and Timur invaded Delhi in 1398, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
139.tq: Recall the event linked to each invader.
n: Muhammad bin Qasim targeted Sindh. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #141 · pp 244-246]
Muhammad bin Qasim's invasion resulted in the Arab conquest of Sindh. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #141 · pp 244-246]
Mahmud Ghazni made 17 attacks. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #141 · pp 244-246]
Mahmud Ghazni's attacks involved plunder. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #141 · pp 244-246]
Muhammad Ghori fought at Tarain. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #141 · pp 244-246]
Muhammad Ghori fought at Chandawar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #141 · pp 244-246]
Timur invaded Delhi in 1398. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #141 · pp 244-246]
xs: The correct match is **a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i** — option **(1)**.
**Muhammad bin Qasim** — **Arab conquest of Sindh**; **Mahmud Ghazni** — **17 attacks** and plunder.
**Muhammad Ghori** — **Tarain** and **Chandawar**; **Timur** — invasion of **Delhi** in **1398**.
xa: Ghori opposed **Prithviraj** and **Jayachandra**; his campaigns began approximately **1175 CE**.
Timur invaded in the reign of **Nasiruddin Mahmud Shah**.
Ghori **contributed** to the foundation of **Turkish power**.

139.s:
Arrange the following invaders or groups in chronological order:
A. Hunas
B. Arabs under Muhammad bin Qasim
C. Kushanas
D. Greeks under Alexander
139.x: Alexander came in 326 BCE, the Kushanas in the 1st century CE, the Hunas in the 5th century CE and Muhammad bin Qasim in 712 CE, giving D, C, A, B.
139.tq: Arrange the invasions by century.
n: Alexander invaded in approximately 326 BCE. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #141 · pp 244-246]
The Kushanas invaded during approximately the 1st century CE. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #141 · pp 244-246]
The Hunas invaded during approximately the 5th century CE. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #141 · pp 244-246]
Muhammad bin Qasim invaded in 712 CE. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #141 · pp 244-246]
xs: The order is **D, C, A, B** — option **(4)**.
D: **Alexander** — approximately **326 BCE**; C: **Kushanas** — approximately the **1st century CE**.
A: **Hunas** — approximately the **5th century CE**; B: **Muhammad bin Qasim** — **712 CE**.
xa: **Darius I** (approximately **522–486 BCE**) came before Alexander.
The **Sakas** came approximately in the **1st century BCE**.
**Mahmud Ghazni** and **Muhammad Ghori** came after the Arabs.

139.s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Babur
(b) Nadir Shah
(c) Ahmad Shah Abdali
(d) Timur

List-II
(i) Delhi, 1398
(ii) Panipat, 1526
(iii) Karnal, 1739
(iv) Panipat, 1761
139.x: Babur won at Panipat in 1526, Nadir Shah at Karnal in 1739, Ahmad Shah Abdali at Panipat in 1761 and Timur sacked Delhi in 1398, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
139.tq: Recall the place and year of each invasion.
n: Timur targeted Delhi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #141 · pp 244-246]
Timur invaded Delhi in 1398. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #141 · pp 244-246]
Babur's invasion resulted in the Battle of Panipat in 1526. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #141 · pp 244-246]
Nadir Shah fought at Karnal in 1739. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #141 · pp 244-246]
Ahmad Shah Abdali fought at Panipat in 1761. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #141 · pp 244-246]
Ahmad Shah Abdali was associated with the Third Battle of Panipat in 1761. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #141 · pp 244-246]
xs: The correct match is **a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i** — option **(3)**.
**Babur** — **Panipat, 1526**; **Nadir Shah** — **Karnal, 1739**.
**Ahmad Shah Abdali** — **Panipat, 1761**; **Timur** — **Delhi, 1398**.

o: 1670 — Defeat of Afzal Khan at Pratapgad
1663 — Night raid on Shaista Khan at Pune
140.x: In 1663, Shivaji conducted a night raid on Shaista Khan at Pune, during which Khan lost his fingers and retreated.
140.tq: Use the year-event pairing and reject swapped dates.
xs: **1663 — night raid on Shaista Khan at Pune** is correctly matched — option **(4)**.
In the raid the Khan **lost his fingers** and retreated.
Afzal Khan was killed in **1659**, Purandar was **1665**, and Surat was sacked in **1664** and **1670**.
xa: **Shaista Khan** was a Mughal noble, **Aurangzeb's maternal uncle**.
**1660**: Siege of **Panhala** — Shivaji broke out after months.

140.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the episode involving Afzal Khan in 1659?
o: Afzal Khan signed the Treaty of Purandar at Pune.
Afzal Khan was killed with a wagh nakh at the foot of Pratapgad.
Afzal Khan lost his fingers during a night raid.
Afzal Khan was defeated at the siege of Panhala after several months.
140.x: Shivaji killed the Bijapur general Afzal Khan with a wagh nakh at the foot of Pratapgad in 1659.
140.tq: Match the opponent with the distinctive event rather than with a nearby conflict.
xs: **Afzal Khan**, the **Bijapur** general, was killed with a **wagh nakh** at the foot of **Pratapgad** in **1659** — option **(2)**.
Losing **fingers** in a night raid was **Shaista Khan (1663)**; Purandar (**1665**) was with **Jai Singh**.
**Panhala (1660)** was a siege Shivaji broke out of, not Afzal Khan's defeat.
xa: **Pratapgad** later served as a base for defence and expansion.
Wars with Bijapur began with seizing hill forts, starting with **Torna (1646)**.

140.s: Under the treaty between Shivaji and Abul Hasan Tana Shah, Golconda agreed to provide money for the southern conquests and
o: send Sambhaji to the Mughal court
140.x: The agreement provided financial support from Golconda for the southern conquests, with the spoils to be shared.
140.tq: Identify the reciprocal terms of the alliance instead of confusing them with Purandar conditions.
xs: Golconda was to give money and **share the spoils** with Shivaji — option **(4)**.
The **1677** treaty with **Abul Hasan Tana Shah** was for aid in the southern campaign.
Sending **Sambhaji** to the Mughal court was a **Purandar** term, not a Golconda one.
xa: Shivaji afterwards **refused to share the spoils**.
Conquests: **Ballari, Gingee (Jinji), Vellore**.
Envoys to Golconda: **Niraj Pant** and **Prahlad Pant**.

140.s: Which one of the following statements about Shivaji's southern campaign is NOT correct?
o: The treaty with Golconda was made through Akkanna and Madanna.
He took Gingee but left Vellore and Ballari untouched.
He refused to share the spoils of the campaign.
He took Gingee, Vellore and Ballari.
140.x: Shivaji took Gingee, Vellore and Ballari and refused to share the spoils. Therefore, the statement that he left Vellore and Ballari untouched is incorrect.
140.tq: Spot the reversed action in a list of campaign achievements.
xs: Statement **(2)** is NOT correct: Shivaji did **not** leave Vellore and Ballari untouched.
In **1677** he took **Ballari, Gingee (Jinji) and Vellore**.
The treaty was made through **Akkanna and Madanna**, and he **refused to share the spoils** — both correct.
xa: **Vellore** was taken from step-brother **Venkoji/Ekoji**.
**1672** attack on Golconda took **2 lakh Honnu**.

140.s:
Consider the following pairs relating to Golconda's ties with Shivaji:
1. Akkanna — Sar Lashkar
2. Madanna — Mir Jumla
3. Venkoji (Ekoji) — Golconda's envoy to Shivaji
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
140.x: Pair 1 is correct: Akkanna was the Sar Lashkar of Golconda. Pair 2 is correct: Madanna was the Mir Jumla. Pair 3 is wrong: Venkoji (Ekoji) was Shivaji's step-brother from whom he took Vellore; Shivaji's envoys were Niraj Pant and Prahlad Pant. Hence 1 and 2 only.
140.tq: Akkanna = Sar Lashkar, Madanna = Mir Jumla; the brothers brokered the 1677 Golconda treaty.
xs: Pairs **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
**Akkanna** was **Sar Lashkar** and **Madanna** was **Mir Jumla** of Golconda.
Pair 3 is wrong: **Venkoji/Ekoji** was Shivaji's **step-brother**, who lost Vellore; the envoys were **Niraj Pant** and **Prahlad Pant**.
xa: The **1677** treaty with **Abul Hasan Tana Shah** was made through Akkanna and Madanna.
Shivaji visited **Hyderabad** on **7 March 1677**.

140.s: Who officiated at Shivaji's coronation with Vedic rites?
o: Gaga Bhatt of Banaras or Varanasi
140.x: Gaga Bhatt, a learned Brahmin from Banaras or Varanasi, officiated at the coronation with Vedic rites.
140.tq: Test the person-place association rather than the event date.
xs: **Gaga Bhatt of Banaras (Varanasi)** officiated at the coronation — option **(2)**.
The coronation was at **Raigad** in **1674** with **Vedic rites**.
**Annaji Datto** did the **Kathi** survey; **Ramachandrapant Amatya** wrote the **Adnyapatra**; **Balaji Vishwanath** was Shahu's Peshwa.
xa: Title taken: **"Shri Raja Shiva Chhatrapati"**.
The **Rajyabhisheka shaka** asserted sovereignty against the Mughals and Sultanates.

140.s:
Consider the following statements about Shivaji's coronation:
1. He adopted the title "Shri Raja Shiva Chhatrapati".
2. He was also styled "Hindavi Sultan".
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
140.x: Statement 1 is correct: the coronation title was "Shri Raja Shiva Chhatrapati". Statement 2 is wrong: he was also styled Haindava Dharmoddharak, not Hindavi Sultan. Hence 1 only.
140.tq: Title = Shri Raja Shiva Chhatrapati; style = Haindava Dharmoddharak.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: the title was **"Shri Raja Shiva Chhatrapati"**.
Statement 2 is wrong: he was also styled **Haindava Dharmoddharak**, not "Hindavi Sultan".
xa: Coronation: **Raigad, 6 June 1674**, by **Gaga Bhatt**.
The new era: **Rajyabhisheka shaka**.

140.s: The era started by Shivaji to assert sovereignty against the Mughals and the Sultanates was known as the
140.x: Shivaji began the Rajabhisheka Shaka after his coronation to assert sovereign status.
140.tq: Match the political purpose with the precise name of the era.
xs: Shivaji's era was the **Rajabhisheka Shaka** (Rajyabhisheka shaka) — option **(3)**.
It began with the **1674** coronation and asserted **sovereignty** against the Mughals and Sultanates.
**Warna** is a **1731** treaty settling Tarabai's line at Kolhapur, not an era.
xa: Coronation title: **"Shri Raja Shiva Chhatrapati"**.
Priest: **Gaga Bhatt** of Banaras.

140.s:
Consider the following pairs (minister — portfolio) in Shivaji's Ashtapradhan:
1. Amatya — Treasury, accounts audit and revenue
2. Panditrao — Religious affairs and charitable grants
3. Nyayadhish — Intelligence and the king's diary
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
140.x: Pair 1 is correct: the Amatya handled finance. Pair 2 is correct: the Panditrao handled religious affairs and charitable grants. Pair 3 is wrong: the Nyayadhish was the chief justice; intelligence and the king's diary belonged to the Mantri. Hence 1 and 2 only.
140.tq: Nyayadhish = nyaya = justice; Mantri = intelligence/diary.
xs: Pairs **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
**Amatya** (Majumdar) = **finance**: treasury, accounts audit, revenue; **Panditrao** = **religious affairs and charitable grants**.
Pair 3 is wrong: **Nyayadhish** = **justice**; intelligence and the king's diary belonged to the **Mantri**.
xa: ⚠ **Sachiv** = correspondence; **Sumant** = foreign affairs; **Mantri** = intelligence.
BPSC **2024**: Sachiv-correspondence, Peshwa-PM, Sumant-foreign, Amatya-finance.

140.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Shivaji's Ashtapradhan is correct?
o: Every minister reported directly to the Chhatrapati.
All posts were hereditary and could not be transferred.
The council was modelled on the Mughal mansabdari system.
The ministers were appointed for life and could not be dismissed.
140.x: Each minister reported directly to the Chhatrapati. The posts were not hereditary, and ministers could be transferred or dismissed at the king's will.
140.tq: Identify the precise administrative feature while rejecting absolute claims.
xs: **Every minister reported directly to the Chhatrapati** — option **(1)**.
Posts were **not hereditary**; ministers could be **transferred or dismissed** at the king's will.
The council was modelled on the **Deccan Sultanates**, not Mughal mansabdari.
xa: All except **Panditrao and Nyayadhish** had to lead military campaigns.
Later the Peshwa post became **hereditary and supreme**.
Ashtapradhan was **advisory**, whereas the Mughal wazir system was hierarchical.

140.s: Which one of the following statements about the Peshwa post is NOT correct?
o: The post was hereditary and supreme from the beginning of Shivaji's Ashtapradhan.
The post was associated with general administration.
The post became hereditary and supreme under the later Peshwas.
Initially, the Peshwa was the Prime Minister of Shivaji.
140.x: The Peshwa post became hereditary and supreme only later, under the Peshwas; it was not hereditary and supreme from the beginning of Shivaji's administration.
140.tq: Reject the statement that extends a later development back to the original system.
xs: Statement **(1)** is NOT correct: the Peshwa post was **not hereditary and supreme from the beginning**.
Under Shivaji the Peshwa (**Mukhya Pradhan**) was the **Prime Minister**, in charge of general administration.
It became **hereditary and supreme** only under the **later Peshwas**.
xa: **Balaji Vishwanath** became Peshwa in **1713**, appointed by **Shahu**.
From **1713**, real power moved from the Chhatrapati at **Satara** to the Peshwa.

140.s: In Shivaji's Ashtapradhan, the minister known as the Dabir was responsible for
o: foreign affairs, acting as master of ceremonies who received envoys
the treasury and audit of accounts
140.x: The Dabir was the Sumant, in charge of foreign affairs and the master of ceremonies who received envoys (APPSC-G1 2024). Royal correspondence was the Sachiv (Shurnavis); religious affairs and grants the Panditrao (Danadhyaksha); treasury and accounts the Amatya (Majumdar).
140.tq: Dabir = Sumant = foreign affairs + master of ceremonies.
xs: The **Dabir** (Sumant) handled **foreign affairs** as **master of ceremonies who received envoys** — option **(2)**.
Correspondence and records = **Sachiv (Shurnavis)**; religious grants = **Panditrao**; treasury = **Amatya (Majumdar)**.
xa: PYQ: **Dabir = master of ceremonies** (APPSC-G1 **2024**).
⚠ **Sachiv** = correspondence; **Sumant** = foreign affairs; **Mantri** = intelligence.

140.s:
Match List-I (title in Shivaji's Ashtapradhan) with List-II (portfolio):
List-I: A. Sar-i-Naubat  B. Shurnavis  C. Waqia-navis  D. Dabir
List-II: 1. Intelligence and the king's diary  2. Foreign affairs  3. Military commander  4. Royal correspondence and records
Select the correct answer:
140.x: Sar-i-Naubat was the Senapati, the military commander (APPSC-G2 2023); Shurnavis (Surnis) was the Sachiv, in charge of royal correspondence and records; Waqia-navis was the Mantri, in charge of intelligence and the king's diary; Dabir was the Sumant, in charge of foreign affairs. The other codes swap these titles.
140.tq: Sar-i-Naubat = Senapati; Shurnavis = Sachiv; Waqia-navis = Mantri; Dabir = Sumant.
xs: The match is **A-3, B-4, C-1, D-2** — option **(1)**.
**Sar-i-Naubat** (Senapati) = **military commander**; **Shurnavis** (Sachiv) = **royal correspondence and records**.
**Waqia-navis** (Mantri) = **intelligence and the king's diary**; **Dabir** (Sumant) = **foreign affairs**.
xa: PYQ: **Sar-i-Naubat = military commander** (APPSC-G2 **2023**).
**Majumdar** = Amatya (finance); **Danadhyaksha** = Panditrao.

140.s: Which one of the following statements about Shivaji's revenue administration is NOT correct?
o: The state dealt directly with the cultivator in a ryotwari-type settlement.
Officials were generally paid in cash rather than through jagirs.
Peasant property was routinely seized whenever revenue could not be paid.
Hereditary deshmukhs and deshpandes were bypassed or regulated.
140.x: Peasant property was not seized as a normal revenue measure. Shivaji preferred cash payment of officials and direct settlement with cultivators.
140.tq: Find the one statement that reverses the stated protection given to peasant property.
xs: Statement **(3)** is NOT correct: **peasant property was not seized**.
Relief measures: **remission in famine**, illegal cesses abolished, peasant property not seized.
The state dealt **directly with the cultivator**, paid officials in **cash**, and **regulated deshmukhs**.
xa: State share: **33%, later 40%** of gross produce.
Assessment was on **area cultivated and crop**.

140.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Shivaji, jagirs were abolished and officials were paid in cash.
2. Saranjam (service land grants) never returned after Shivaji's time.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
140.x: Statement 1 is correct: Shivaji abolished jagirs and paid officials in cash. Statement 2 is wrong: saranjam grants came back under Shahu and the Peshwas. Hence 1 only.
140.tq: Shivaji = cash; Shahu and Peshwas = saranjam back.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: **jagirs abolished**; officials paid in **cash**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Saranjam** service grants **returned under Shahu and the Peshwas**.
xa: The army too was **paid in cash**, so loyalty went directly to the state.
Comparison: Mughal mansabdari rested on **jagirs**.

140.s:
Which of the following combinations is correctly matched?
1. Kathi — measuring rod
2. Jirayat — dry land
3. Bagayat — irrigated land
4. Rajvyavahar Kosh — naval manual
Select the correct answer.
140.x: Kathi was a measuring rod, Jirayat denoted dry land and Bagayat denoted irrigated land. The Rajvyavahar Kosh concerned official terminology, not naval matters.
140.tq: Find the single mismatched association and select the code containing the three correct terms.
xs: Pairs **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
**Kathi** = measuring rod; **Jirayat** = dry land; **Bagayat** = irrigated land.
Pair 4 is wrong: **Rajvyavahar Kosh** replaced **Persian official terms with Sanskrit** ones.
xa: **Saranjam** = service land grants.
**Modi script** = cursive script for Marathi records.

140.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Administrative unit)
A. Prant
B. Pargana and Tarf
C. Mauza

List-II (Official)
1. Patil and Kulkarni
2. Subedar or Sarsubedar
3. Deshmukh and Deshpande

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
140.x: A Prant was administered by a Subedar or Sarsubedar; Pargana and Tarf were associated with Deshmukh and Deshpande; Mauza had the Patil and Kulkarni.
140.tq: Start from the sure province and village pairings, then place the intermediate unit.
xs: The match is **A-2, B-3, C-1** — option **(1)**.
**Prant** — **Subedar / Sarsubedar**; **Pargana, Tarf** — **Deshmukh, Deshpande**; **Mauza** — **Patil** (head) and **Kulkarni** (accountant).
xa: The kingdom was divided into **prants**.
Hereditary **deshmukhs and deshpandes** had their rights curbed and resisted.

140.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The big deshmukhs opposed Shivaji.
Reason (R): The deshmukhs did not back the creation of an independent Maratha state, which curbed their hereditary rights.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
140.x: Both are true and R explains A (UPPSC 2024). Shivaji bypassed or regulated the hereditary deshmukhs and deshpandes and curbed their rights, so the big deshmukhs, who did not support an independent Maratha state, resisted him. Options B, C and D misstate this link.
140.tq: Shivaji curbed watandar deshmukhs, so they opposed him: A and R true, R explains A.
xs: **Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A** — option **(1)** (UPPSC **2024**).
Shivaji **bypassed or regulated** the hereditary deshmukhs and deshpandes and curbed their rights.
The big deshmukhs **did not back** an independent Maratha state, so they resisted him.
xa: **Jagirs abolished**; officials paid in **cash**.
**Sardeshmukhi** was claimed as the king's hereditary right as **Sardeshmukh** of the Deccan.

140.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes chauth from sardeshmukhi?
o: Chauth was a hereditary right, whereas sardeshmukhi was protection money.
Chauth was generally 25 per cent protection money, whereas sardeshmukhi was an additional 10 per cent claimed as the king's hereditary right.
Chauth was a religious grant, whereas sardeshmukhi was a military salary.
Both were identical levies collected only within the Maratha heartland.
140.x: Chauth was generally one-fourth of land revenue, justified as protection against invasion or Maratha raids. Sardeshmukhi was an additional 10 per cent claimed as the king's hereditary right as Sardeshmukh.
140.tq: Compare rate, justification and nature rather than relying on the names alone.
xs: **Chauth** was **25%** protection money; **sardeshmukhi** an additional **10%** hereditary-right claim — option **(2)**.
Chauth: protection against third-party invasion, or to be **spared Maratha raids**.
Sardeshmukhi: the king's **hereditary right as Sardeshmukh** (chief headman) of the Deccan.
xa: Both were collected from lands **outside the Maratha realm**.
Mughals formally conceded them in **1719** (Farrukhsiyar, six Deccan subas).
Exam angle: "Maratha revenue claim for protection" = **Chauth** (UPPSC **2018**).

140.s: Chauth was collected primarily from
o: territories under direct Maratha administration only
the personal estates of the Ashtapradhan ministers
140.x: Chauth was levied on territories outside direct Maratha rule, including Mughal and Deccan Sultanate territories.
140.tq: Apply the rule about the geographical scope of an external levy.
xs: Chauth was levied on **territories outside direct Maratha rule** — option **(4)**.
Chiefly **Mughal and Deccan Sultanate** territory.
It financed expansion **without the cost of direct governance**.
xa: Chauth = **25%** of land revenue.
Recognised by the **Nizam at Palkhed**; Nizam paid again after the **1795** war.
In **Rajputana** the Marathas took tribute and chauth but annexed no Rajput state.

140.s: The combined effect of chauth and sardeshmukhi was to
o: finance military expansion and establish political hegemony without the cost of direct governance
confine Maratha authority to the fort of Raigad
replace the Ashtapradhan with a hereditary Mughal bureaucracy
end Maratha military expansion by restricting revenue collection
140.x: Together, the levies financed military expansion and extended political hegemony without requiring the Marathas to administer every territory directly.
140.tq: Infer the administrative consequence from the stated revenue mechanism.
xs: Chauth and sardeshmukhi **financed military expansion** and **political hegemony without the cost of direct governance** — option **(1)**.
They were collected from lands **outside the Maratha realm** — Mughal and Deccan Sultanate territory.
This let a **regional state become a pan-Indian power** without direct administration.
xa: ⚠ **Chauth = 25%** (protection); **Sardeshmukhi = 10%** (hereditary right).
Mughals formally conceded them in **1719**.
Peak extent later: **Attock to Cuttack**.

140.s:
Consider the following statements about the recognition of Maratha claims to chauth and sardeshmukhi:
1. The Mughals formally conceded them in 1719.
2. The Nizam conceded them at Palkhed.
3. After the 1795 war the Nizam was freed from paying chauth.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
140.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Mughals conceded the rights in 1719. Statement 2 is correct: the Nizam conceded them at Palkhed. Statement 3 is wrong: after the 1795 war the Nizam was forced to pay chauth again. Hence 1 and 2 only.
140.tq: 1719 Mughals, Palkhed Nizam, 1795 Nizam pays again.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
The **Mughals** conceded the claims in **1719**; the **Nizam** at **Palkhed**.
Statement 3 is wrong: after the **1795** war the Nizam was **forced to pay chauth again**.
xa: The **1719** grants came from **Farrukhsiyar**: chauth and sardeshmukhi of the **six Deccan subas**.
The 1795 defeat pushed the Nizam toward the **British Subsidiary Alliance (1798)**.

140.s: The Rajvyavahar Kosh was associated with the replacement of
o: Persian official terms by Sanskrit terms
140.x: The Rajvyavahar Kosh replaced Persian official terminology with Sanskrit terminology.
140.tq: Test the direction of replacement in a language-policy reform.
xs: The **Rajvyavahar Kosh** replaced **Persian official terms by Sanskrit** ones — option **(1)**.
**Marathi and Sanskrit** replaced **Persian** as official languages.
xa: **Modi script** = cursive script for Marathi administrative records.
**Hindavi Swarajya** promoted Marathi and Sanskrit in administration over Persian.

140.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies Shivaji’s coins?
140.x: Shivaji issued the gold Hon and the copper Shivrai.
140.tq: Discriminate between the names and metals of the two coins.
xs: Shivaji's coins were the **gold Hon** ("Shivrai hon") and the **copper Shivrai** — option **(1)**.
**Rupaya** and **Taka** were listed as silver, not gold or copper.
xa: ⚠ **Ruka** was the coin **not silver** (UPPSC **2016** key); Rupaya, Lari, Taka listed as silver.
**1672** attack on Golconda took **2 lakh Honnu**.

140.s: Which one of the following statements about official language and records under Shivaji is correct?
o: Persian alone continued as the official language and Modi was used for military signals.
Marathi and Sanskrit replaced Persian in official usage, while Modi was used for Marathi administrative records.
Sanskrit replaced Marathi and Modi was used only for religious manuscripts.
Marathi replaced Sanskrit and Persian in all diplomatic correspondence with Golconda.
140.x: Marathi and Sanskrit were promoted in official usage over Persian, and the cursive Modi script was used for Marathi administrative records.
140.tq: Combine the language change with the precise function of Modi script.
xs: **Marathi and Sanskrit replaced Persian**, and **Modi** was used for **Marathi administrative records** — option **(2)**.
Modi was a **cursive script**, not for military signals or religious manuscripts.
xa: **Rajvyavahar Kosh** replaced Persian official terms with Sanskrit ones.
**Ganimi Kava** = guerrilla hit-and-run warfare in the Sahyadri terrain.

140.s: Which of the following groups contains only forts classified as Giri Durg?
140.x: Raigad, Pratapgad, Torna and Sinhagad are hill forts, or Giri Durg. Vishalgad is a land fort, while the others in the distractors include sea forts.
140.tq: Classify each example by fort type and eliminate groups containing a land or sea fort.
xs: **Raigad, Pratapgad, Torna and Sinhagad** are all **Giri Durg** (hill forts) — option **(1)**.
**Vishalgad** is a **Bhu Durg** (land fort); **Sindhudurg, Vijaydurg, Khanderi, Suvarnadurg** are **Jal Durg** (sea forts).
xa: **Rajgad** and **Panhala** are also Giri Durg.
Shivaji held over **300 forts**.
**Kolaba** was also a sea base guarding the Konkan.

140.s: Each fort under Shivaji was placed under the charge of three officers of equal rank. Which set correctly identifies them?
140.x: The three officers were the Havaldar, Sabnis and Sarnobat. The Sabnis handled records, while the Havaldar and Sarnobat had garrison and military responsibilities.
140.tq: Distinguish the fort command structure from the Ashtapradhan and army categories.
xs: The three equal-rank fort officers were the **Havaldar, Sabnis and Sarnobat** — option **(2)**.
**Havaldar** = garrison commander; **Sabnis** = records; **Sarnobat** = military officer.
**Bargir, Shiledar, Mavali** are army troops; **Peshwa, Amatya, Dabir** belong to the Ashtapradhan.
xa: **Adnyapatra** of Ramachandrapant Amatya: "**forts are the core of the state**".
The army's smallest unit was led by a **havildar**.

140.s:
Consider the following statements about Maratha cavalry:
1. Bargirs were provided horses and equipment by the state.
2. Shiledars maintained their own horses.
3. Both terms referred to categories of cavalry.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
140.x: Bargirs were state-equipped cavalrymen, whereas Shiledars supplied their own horses; both were cavalry categories.
140.tq: Compare the two confusable cavalry categories before selecting the complete combination.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**Bargirs** were **state-equipped**; **shiledars** kept their **own horses**; both were **cavalry**.
xa: The standing army was **paid in cash**, no jagirs — loyalty direct to the state.
**Mavali** infantry were the hill troops.
**Battle of Salher (1672)**: Mughals beaten in open battle.

140.s:
Consider the following statements about Shivaji's navy:
1. He built a navy with sea forts such as Sindhudurg, Kolaba and Vijaydurg.
2. These sea forts guarded the Malabar coast.
3. He is called the Father of the Indian Navy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
140.x: Statement 1 is correct: Shivaji built a navy with sea forts such as Sindhudurg, Kolaba and Vijaydurg. Statement 2 is wrong: they guarded the Konkan coast. Statement 3 is correct: he is called the Father of the Indian Navy. Hence 1 and 3 only.
140.tq: Shivaji's sea forts = Konkan coast.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(3)**.
Shivaji built a navy with sea bases **Sindhudurg, Kolaba and Vijaydurg**; he is called **Father of the Indian Navy**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the sea forts guarded the **Konkan**, not Malabar.
xa: Other Jal Durg: **Khanderi**, **Suvarnadurg**.
The "Father of the Indian Navy" title is a **Feb 2026** current-affairs row.

140.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Shivaji's military organisation is NOT correct?
o: The Battle of Salher in 1672 saw the Mughals defeated in open battle.
Jagirs were the regular means of paying the standing army and securing its loyalty.
The standing army was organised without jagir-based payment.
He maintained a standing army paid in cash.
140.x: Shivaji's standing army was paid in cash rather than jagirs so that loyalty remained directly attached to the state. The Marathas defeated the Mughals in open battle at Salher in 1672.
140.tq: Reject the statement that reverses the cash-payment principle and use the related battle fact as confirmation.
xs: Statement **(2)** is NOT correct: **jagirs** were **not** used to pay the army.
The standing army was **paid in cash**, so loyalty went **directly to the state**.
The Mughals were beaten in open battle at **Salher (1672)**.
xa: Officials too were paid in cash — **jagirs abolished**.
Contrast: Mughal **mansabdari** rested on jagirs.

140.s:
Arrange the following rulers in chronological order of their succession in the Maratha polity:
A. Shahu
B. Sambhaji
C. Tarabai
D. Rajaram
140.x: The sequence was Sambhaji, Rajaram, Tarabai as regent for Shivaji II, and Shahu.
140.tq: Fix the first and last rulers, then place Rajaram and Tarabai between them.
xs: The order is **B, D, C, A** — option **(1)**.
xa: Exam angle: order **Sambhaji - Rajaram - Shivaji II - Shahu** (UPPSC **2005**).
"Maratha woman who fought the Mughals from **1700**" = **Tarabai**.

140.s:
Consider the following statements about Rajaram:
1. He moved to Gingee (Jinji), directed resistance from there and drew Aurangzeb south.
2. He created the post of Pratinidhi.
3. He was the elder son of Shivaji and succeeded him directly in 1680.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
140.x: Statement 1 is correct: Rajaram directed resistance from Gingee and drew Aurangzeb south. Statement 2 is correct: he created the post of Pratinidhi. Statement 3 is wrong: Rajaram was the younger son and ruled 1689-1700, after Sambhaji (1680-89). Hence 1 and 2 only.
140.tq: Rajaram = younger son, Jinji, Pratinidhi.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
**Rajaram** moved to **Gingee (Jinji)**, directed resistance and **drew Aurangzeb south**; he created the post of **Pratinidhi**.
Statement 3 is wrong: he was the **younger son**, ruling **1689-1700** after **Sambhaji (1680-89)**.
xa: His widow **Tarabai** became regent for **Shivaji II**.
Gingee was among Shivaji's **1677** conquests.

140.s:
Consider the following statements about Tarabai:
1. She acted as regent for her young son after Rajaram's death.
2. She led massive raids into Mughal territory.
3. Her line was later settled at Kolhapur under the Treaty of Warna.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
140.x: All three statements are correct. Tarabai governed as regent, raided Mughal territory, and her line was later settled at Kolhapur under the Treaty of Warna.
140.tq: Check all three connected facts about a ruler before selecting the complete combination.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**Tarabai**, Rajaram's widow, was **regent** for her young son **Shivaji II** and led **massive raids** into Mughal territory.
The **Treaty of Warna (1731)** settled her line at **Kolhapur**.
xa: She led the Marathas at **Aurangzeb's death (1707)**.
**Shahu** beat Tarabai's forces at **Khed (1707)**.
Tarabai's raids especially **broke Mughal finances**.

140.s: Which of the following statements regarding Shahu is correct?
o: He was released by Bahadur Shah I, defeated Tarabai's forces at Khed, and ruled from Satara.
He moved to Gingee and created the post of Pratinidhi.
He was captured and executed by Aurangzeb in 1689.
He led the Marathas at Aurangzeb's death as Rajaram's widow.
140.x: Shahu was released by Bahadur Shah I in 1707, defeated Tarabai at Khed, and ruled from Satara.
140.tq: Use the ruler-deed association and reject actions belonging to Rajaram, Sambhaji or Tarabai.
xs: **Shahu** was **released by Bahadur Shah I**, beat **Tarabai at Khed** and ruled from **Satara** — option **(1)**.
**Gingee and Pratinidhi** = **Rajaram**; executed in **1689** = **Sambhaji**; Rajaram's widow = **Tarabai**.
xa: Shahu ruled **1707-1749** and appointed **Balaji Vishwanath** Peshwa in **1713**.
The **1719** grants recognised Shahu.

140.s:
Consider the following statements about Balaji Vishwanath:
1. He was Peshwa from 1713 to 1720, appointed by Shahu.
2. From 1713, real power moved from the Peshwa to the Chhatrapati at Satara.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
140.x: Statement 1 is correct: Balaji Vishwanath was Peshwa 1713-20, appointed by Shahu. Statement 2 is wrong: the shift was the other way, from the Chhatrapati at Satara to the Peshwa. Hence 1 only.
140.tq: 1713: power flows Satara (Chhatrapati) -> Peshwa.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Balaji Vishwanath** was Peshwa **1713-20**, appointed by **Shahu**.
Statement 2 is reversed: power moved **from the Chhatrapati at Satara to the Peshwa**.
xa: He **backed Shahu in the civil war** and rallied chiefs to him.
Under the later Peshwas the post became **hereditary and supreme**.

140.s:
Which of the following were included in the Mughal grants of 1719?
1. Recognition of Shahu
2. Swarajya lands
3. Chauth and sardeshmukhi of the six Deccan subas
4. Direct Mughal administration of Raigad
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
140.x: The grants recognised Shahu, confirmed Swarajya lands, and granted chauth and sardeshmukhi in six Deccan subas. They did not establish direct Mughal administration of Raigad.
140.tq: Reject the extra condition that is not part of the grant.
xs: Items **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
The **1719** grants gave **recognition of Shahu**, **Swarajya lands** and **chauth and sardeshmukhi of the six Deccan subas**.
There was no direct Mughal administration of **Raigad**.
xa: Granted by **Farrukhsiyar**; obtained by **Balaji Vishwanath**.
**Treaty of Warna (1731)**: Tarabai's line settled at **Kolhapur**.

140.s: Which combination best describes the distinctive character of Shivaji’s state?
o: Mughal-style, mansab-based and paid only through jagirs
Decentralised, hereditary and entirely land-grant based
140.x: Shivaji built a centralised and non-hereditary state in which officials and forces were paid in cash.
140.tq: Compare the three defining features instead of selecting a single administrative characteristic.
xs: Shivaji's state was **centralised, non-hereditary and cash-paid** — option **(1)**.
**Jagirs abolished**; officials and army paid in **cash**; ministers could be **transferred or dismissed**.
xa: Mughal **mansabdari** rested on jagirs.
The **Ashtapradhan** was advisory, unlike the hierarchical Mughal wazir system.

140.s:
Consider the following statements comparing Shivaji's system with the Mughal system:
1. Mughal mansabdari rested on jagirs, whereas Shivaji paid in cash.
2. The Ashtapradhan was hierarchical, whereas the Mughal wazir system was advisory.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
140.x: Statement 1 is correct: mansabdari rested on jagirs while Shivaji paid in cash. Statement 2 is wrong: it is reversed; the Ashtapradhan was advisory and the Mughal wazir system hierarchical. Hence 1 only.
140.tq: Shivaji: cash + advisory council; Mughals: jagir + hierarchical wazir.
