155.x: The sequence is 1693, 1697, 1761 and 1763: Dutch capture, Treaty of Ryswick restoration, British capture and Treaty of Paris restoration.
155.tq: Use the four dates as anchors and preserve the two capture-restoration pairs.
xs: Order: **Dutch capture (1693)**, **Ryswick (1697)**, **British capture (1761)**, **Paris (1763)** — **1, 2, 3, 4**, option **(1)**.
The British took it after **Wandiwash**.
xa: After the Treaty of Paris the French kept only **trading enclaves**.
Pondicherry was founded in **1674**.
It merged with India de facto **1954**, de jure **1962**.

155.s: Who was the first French governor and the builder of Pondicherry?
155.x: François Martin was the first French governor and built Pondicherry. He died on 31 December 1706.
155.tq: Link the earliest governor with the foundational development at Pondicherry.
xs: **François Martin** was the **first French governor** and built **Pondicherry** — option **(2)**.
He died on **31 Dec 1706**.
**Dumas** (**1735-41**) and **Dupleix** (**1742-54**) came later; **Godeheu** replaced Dupleix.
xa: He got the land from **Sher Khan Lodi** in **1673**.
He had been director at **Masulipatnam**.
Fort at Pondicherry: **Fort St. Louis**.

155.s:
Consider the following statements about the later French governors:
1. Dupleix served as governor from 1742 to 1754.
2. Godeheu replaced Dupleix.
3. Godeheu was recalled at the beginning of the Third Carnatic War.
4. Count de Lally was defeated at Wandiwash by Eyre Coote.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
155.x: All four statements are correct. Dupleix served from 1742 to 1754, Godeheu replaced him and was recalled at the start of the Third Carnatic War, while Lally lost at Wandiwash to Eyre Coote.
155.tq: Combine tenure, succession, recall and military defeat to test the full governor sequence.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Dupleix** governed **1742-54** — the peak of French power.
**Godeheu (1754)** replaced him and was recalled at the start of the **Third Carnatic War**.
**Count de Lally** lost at **Wandiwash (1760)** to **Eyre Coote**.
xa: **Treaty of Pondicherry (1754)** → Dupleix recalled.
Dupleix's title: **Nawab** of Mughal territory south of the **Krishna**; jagir **Valapadu**.
**Dumas (1735-41)** came before Dupleix.

155.s: After the death of Nizam-ul-Mulk in 1748, Dupleix exploited which succession disputes?
155.x: Dupleix intervened in the Hyderabad succession between Nasir Jang and Muzaffar Jang and in the Carnatic succession between Anwaruddin and Chanda Sahib.
155.tq: Identify the two linked succession struggles used by Dupleix for intervention.
xs: Dupleix exploited the **Hyderabad and Carnatic** successions — option **(1)**.
**Hyderabad:** after **Nizam-ul-Mulk's** death (**1748**) — **Nasir Jang** vs **Muzaffar Jang**.
**Carnatic:** **Anwaruddin** vs **Chanda Sahib**.
xa: **Ambur (1749):** Dupleix + Muzaffar Jang + Chanda Sahib killed **Anwaruddin**.
**Bussy** escorted **Muzaffar Jang**.
Turning point: Clive's **siege of Arcot (1751)**.

155.s: The Battle of Ambur in 1749 resulted in which of the following outcomes?
o: Anwaruddin was killed, Muzaffar Jang became Subedar and Chanda Sahib became Nawab
Chanda Sahib was killed and Nasir Jang became Nawab of the Carnatic
Salabat Jang became Nizam and Dupleix was recalled
Muzaffar Jang was killed, Anwaruddin became Subedar and Chanda Sahib was imprisoned
155.x: At Ambur, Anwaruddin was killed; Muzaffar Jang was made Subedar and Chanda Sahib became Nawab.
155.tq: Trace the consequence of the alliance instead of recalling only the battle name.
xs: At **Ambur (1749)** **Anwaruddin** was killed; **Muzaffar Jang** became **Subedar** and **Chanda Sahib** **Nawab** — option **(1)**.
The winning alliance was **Dupleix + Muzaffar Jang + Chanda Sahib**.
xa: Muzaffar Jang was later murdered at **Rayachoti**; **Salabat Jang** made Subedar.
Clive's **Arcot** siege (**1751**) turned the tide.
**Dupleix** was recalled after the **Treaty of Pondicherry (1754)**.

155.s: Which treaty provided that the French and the English should not interfere in the quarrels of Indian princes and led to the recall of Dupleix?
155.x: The Treaty of Pondicherry was concluded in 1754. It required both sides not to meddle in the quarrels of Indian princes, and Dupleix was recalled.
155.tq: Match the non-intervention clause with the treaty that ended Dupleix’s tenure.
xs: The **Treaty of Pondicherry (1754)** barred meddling in princes' quarrels and led to **Dupleix's recall** — option **(2)**.
**Ryswick (1697)** and **Paris (1763)** restored Pondicherry.
xa: **Godeheu (1754)** replaced Dupleix.
Clive's **Arcot** siege (**1751**) held **53** days.
Dupleix governed **1742-54**.

155.s: After the murder of Muzaffar Jang at Rayachoti, whom did Bussy help establish as Subedar of the Deccan?
155.x: Following Muzaffar Jang’s murder at Rayachoti, Bussy helped establish Salabat Jang as Subedar of the Deccan.
155.tq: Apply the succession sequence and distinguish Salabat Jang from the rival claimants.
xs: After **Muzaffar Jang's** murder at **Rayachoti**, **Bussy** made **Salabat Jang** Subedar — option **(1)**.
Bussy guarded him in **Hyderabad** for seven years.
**Nasir Jang** was Muzaffar's rival; **Chanda Sahib** and **Anwaruddin** were Carnatic rivals.
xa: **1753:** Salabat Jang gave the French the **Northern Circars** to pay Bussy's troops.
**1758-59:** Salabat Jang switched to the **British**.
Bussy helped **Vijayaramaraju** at **Bobbili (1757)**.

155.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the Northern Circars granted by Salabat Jang to meet the expenses of the French army?
155.x: The Northern Circars granted in 1753 comprised Mustafanagar or Kondapalli, Eluru, Rajahmundry and Chicacole or Srikakulam. Nellore was not included in this list.
155.tq: Recall the complete four-part list and identify the outside district.
xs: **Nellore** was NOT among the Circars — option **(4)**.
The **1753** grant: **Mustafanagar (Kondapalli), Eluru, Rajahmundry** and **Chicacole (Srikakulam)**.
xa: It paid for **Bussy's** troops — **peak** of French power in the region.
**1759** treaty gave the British **Machilipatnam, Nizampatnam, Vakal Mannar** and part of Kondapalli.
Other Circars British in **1768**; **Guntur** in **1788**.

155.s:
Consider the following statements about the Battle of Bobbili:
1. It was fought on 24 January 1757.
2. Vijayaramaraju of Vizianagaram received French assistance under Bussy.
3. Ranga Rao of Bobbili was killed in the battle.
4. Vijayaramaraju was later killed by Tandra Papayya.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
155.x: All four statements are correct. The battle took place on 24 January 1757; French forces under Bussy supported Vijayaramaraju, Ranga Rao was killed, and Vijayaramaraju was later killed by Ranga Rao’s brother-in-law Tandra Papayya.
155.tq: Build the answer from the date, alliance, casualty and subsequent retaliation in the same episode.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Bobbili** was fought on **24 Jan 1757**.
**Vijayaramaraju** of Vizianagaram had **French (Bussy)** help; **Ranga Rao** of Bobbili was killed.
Vijayaramaraju was later killed by Ranga Rao's brother-in-law **Tandra Papayya**.
xa: APPSC G2 **2019**: Vijayaramaraju took **French** help.
**Tumnapalem (1756):** Bussy + Vijayaramaraju vs **Jafar Ali**.
Bobbili is a key AP-linked French event.

155.s: The grant of the Northern Circars to the French in 1753 was primarily intended to
o: establish a French capital at Guntur
finance the troops maintained by Bussy
compensate the British for the fall of Machilipatnam
secure French control over the port of Surat
155.x: Salabat Jang granted the Northern Circars to the French to pay for Bussy's troops. The grant represented the high point of French influence in the region.
155.tq: Identify the purpose behind a political-territorial arrangement rather than merely recalling its date.
xs: The **1753** grant was **to pay for Bussy's troops** — option **(2)**.
Granted by **Salabat Jang**; it marked the **peak** of French power in the region.
**Guntur** was never a French capital; it became British in **1788**.
xa: Circars: **Mustafanagar (Kondapalli), Eluru, Rajahmundry, Chicacole**.
Lost after **Chendurthi** and the fall of **Machilipatnam (1759)**.
The **1759** treaty = **first British-Hyderabad agreement**.

155.s:
Consider the following statements about the merger of French enclaves with India:
1. Yanam was transferred de facto in 1954 and de jure in 1962.
2. Pondicherry, Karaikal and Mahe were transferred de jure in 1954.
3. Chandernagore joined India through a plebiscite in 1950.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
155.x: Statement 3 is correct: Chandernagore joined by plebiscite in 1950. Statement 1 is correct: Yanam passed de facto in 1954 and de jure in 1962. Statement 2 is wrong: the four enclaves (Pondicherry, Karaikal, Mahe, Yanam) passed de facto in 1954 and de jure only in 1962. So options with statement 2 are wrong.
155.tq: Chandernagore 1950 (plebiscite); other four 1954 de facto, 1962 de jure.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: **Yanam** passed **de facto** in **1954** and **de jure** in **1962**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Pondicherry, Karaikal, Mahe** (with Yanam) passed de jure only in **1962**.
Statement 3: **Chandernagore** joined by **plebiscite** in **1950**.
xa: The four now form the UT of **Puducherry**.
French enclaves remained after **Wandiwash** and the **Treaty of Paris** (**1763**).
**Yanam** (**1723**) was the only French territory in Andhra.

155.s: After the Battle of Wandiwash and the Treaty of Paris, which of the following best describes the territorial position of the French in India?
o: They transferred all settlements immediately to the British
They retained the entire Northern Circars but lost Pondicherry
They retained only trading enclaves at Pondicherry, Karaikal, Mahe, Yanam and Chandernagore
They retained all their former territorial possessions under direct rule
155.x: After Wandiwash and the Treaty of Paris of 1763, the French retained only the trading enclaves of Pondicherry, Karaikal, Mahe, Yanam and Chandernagore.
155.tq: Contrast retained enclaves with the wider territorial ambitions of the earlier period.
xs: After **Wandiwash** and the **Treaty of Paris (1763)** the French kept only **trading enclaves** — option **(3)**.
The five: **Pondicherry, Karaikal, Mahe, Yanam, Chandernagore**.
They had already lost the Northern Circars (**1759**).
xa: Chandernagore → India by **plebiscite (1950)**.
The other four: de facto **1954**, de jure **1962**.
**Lally** lost Wandiwash (**1760**) to **Eyre Coote**.

155.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. It ended French power south of the Krishna, except in Guntur.
2. Salabat Jang then gave Machilipatnam, Nizampatnam, Vakal Mannar and part of Kondapalli to the British.
3. The 1759 treaty was the first British-Hyderabad agreement.
4. Colonel Forde took Machilipatnam from the French in 1759.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
155.x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct: Forde took Machilipatnam in 1759, Salabat Jang then gave Machilipatnam, Nizampatnam, Vakal Mannar and part of Kondapalli to the British, and the treaty was the first British-Hyderabad agreement. Statement 1 is wrong: it ended French power north of the Krishna, except in Guntur. So '2 and 4 only' misses statement 3, and options with statement 1 are wrong.
155.tq: 1759 = first British-Hyderabad treaty; French out north of the Krishna.
xs: Statements **2, 3 and 4 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 4: **Colonel Forde** took **Machilipatnam** in **1759**.
Statement 2: **Salabat Jang** then gave **Machilipatnam, Nizampatnam, Vakal Mannar** and part of **Kondapalli** to the British.
Statement 3: the **1759** treaty was the **first British-Hyderabad agreement**; statement 1 is wrong — it ended French power **north** of the Krishna, except **Guntur**.
xa: In **1753** Salabat Jang had given the French the **Northern Circars** for **Bussy's** troops.
Other Circars went to the British in **1768**; **Guntur** in **1788**.
The defeat at **Chendurthi** preceded the fall of Machilipatnam.

155.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The other Northern Circars became British in 1768.
2. Guntur became British in 1788.
3. Guntur became British before the other Circars.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
155.x: The other Circars became British in 1768, while Guntur followed in 1788. Therefore, the statement that Guntur became British earlier is false.
155.tq: Catch the reversed chronological comparison between the general transfer and the later exception.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: the **other Circars** became British in **1768**.
Statement 2 correct: **Guntur** became British in **1788**.
Statement 3 wrong: Guntur came **after** the other Circars.
xa: **1759** treaty ended French power north of the Krishna except **Guntur**.
Circars granted to the French in **1753**: **Mustafanagar, Eluru, Rajahmundry, Chicacole**.
**Colonel Forde** took Machilipatnam (**1759**).

155.s: The French were the only serious European rival to the British in India, but ultimately lost mainly because of:
o: Their refusal to intervene in Indian succession disputes
Lack of commercial settlements and absence of Indian allies
The immediate surrender of Pondicherry without resistance
Lack of naval supremacy and steady state support
155.x: The French challenge weakened because they lacked naval supremacy and consistent state support.
155.tq: Identify the paired structural causes instead of focusing only on an individual battle.
xs: The French lost for want of **naval supremacy** and **steady state support** — option **(4)**.
They did intervene in successions (**Dupleix**) and had allies and settlements, so the other options are wrong.
xa: French = **only serious European rival** to the British.
The company was **state-owned**, **dependent on subsidies**.
Decisive defeat: **Wandiwash (1760)**.

156.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the order of arrival of the European powers in India?
156.x: The Portuguese were the first among these powers to arrive, followed by the Dutch, British, Danish and French. The French arrived last in 1664.
156.tq: Use the first-and-last positions before fixing the middle sequence.
xs: Order of arrival: **Portuguese → Dutch → British → Danish → French** — option **(1)**.
The **French** came **last (1664)**; the Portuguese first (**1498**).
xa: ⚠ The order **in Andhra** is different: the **Dutch** set up the first factory (**Machilipatnam**); the French were **third**.
Danish East India Company: **1616**.
Portuguese were the last to leave (**1961**); Danes left **1845**.

156.s: Which European power was the third to arrive in Andhra?
156.x: The French were the third European power to arrive in Andhra, although the general order of arrival in India placed them last among the listed powers.
156.tq: Distinguish the regional order in Andhra from the broader Indian order.
xs: The **French** were the **third** Europeans to arrive in **Andhra** — option **(4)**.
⚠ In India overall they were **last (1664)** — the Andhra order is different.
xa: The **Dutch** were first to set up a factory in Andhra (**Machilipatnam**).
All-India order: **Portuguese → Dutch → British → Danish → French**.
**Pondicherry (1673-74)** was the French HQ.

156.s: Which one of the following pairs (settlement - European power) is correctly matched?
156.x: Sadras was Dutch. Tranquebar and Serampore were Danish, and Chandernagore was French.
xs: **Sadras — Dutch** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Tranquebar** and **Serampore** were **Danish**; **Chandernagore** was **French**.
xa: UPPSC **2016** match: Pondicherry-French, Goa-Portuguese, Tranquebar-Danish, Sadras-Dutch.
**Chinsura** was also Dutch.
**Goa, Daman, Diu** were Portuguese.

156.s:
Consider the following statements about the Danes in India:
1. The Danish East India Company was founded in 1616.
2. Their first settlement, Tranquebar, lies on the Malabar coast.
3. Tranquebar was set up in 1620.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
156.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Danish East India Company was founded in 1616. Statement 2 is wrong: Tranquebar lies near Tanjore on the south-eastern Coromandel coast, not Malabar. Statement 3 is correct: Tranquebar was set up in 1620. So '1 only' misses statement 3, and options with statement 2 are wrong.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: the **Danish East India Company** was founded in **1616**.
Statement 2 wrong: **Tranquebar** is near **Tanjore** on the south-eastern **Coromandel** coast, not Malabar.
Statement 3 correct: Tranquebar was set up in **1620**.
xa: Second major settlement: **Serampore (1699)** near Calcutta.
Tranquebar = **Tharangambadi**, in **Tamil Nadu**.
Danes sold both to the British in **1845**.

156.s: Which one of the following was the second major Danish settlement in India and the centre of Danish activity in Bengal?
156.x: Serampore, established in 1699 near Calcutta, became the second major Danish settlement and the focus of Danish activity in Bengal.
156.tq: Link the settlement with both its date and regional role.
xs: **Serampore (1699)**, near **Calcutta**, was the second major Danish settlement and focus of **Bengal** activity — option **(1)**.
**Chinsura** was **Dutch**; **Covelong** was an **Ostend Company** post near Madras.
xa: Serampore = **Srirampur**, West Bengal.
The **Serampore Trio** worked from Danish Serampore.
**Serampore College** founded **1818**.

156.s: Which of the following best describes the principal historical importance of the Danish settlements in India?
o: Their extensive military conquest of the Deccan
Their Protestant missionary, educational and linguistic work
Their establishment of the first British administrative capital
Their dominant share in Indian maritime commerce
156.x: The commercial impact of the Danish settlements was negligible, but their Protestant missionary, educational and linguistic work was historically important.
156.tq: Choose the option that captures the stated long-term significance rather than commercial size.
xs: The Danes mattered mainly for **Protestant missionary**, educational and linguistic work — option **(2)**.
Their **commercial impact was negligible**.
xa: Legacy: **printing**, **vernacular Bible**, **Serampore College**.
**Danish-Halle Mission (1706)** — earliest sustained Protestant mission in South India.
AP angle: start of **printed Telugu prose**.

156.s: The sale of the Danish settlements in India in 1845 took place under Governor-General:
156.x: The sale of Serampore and Tranquebar to the British in 1845 took place under Governor-General Hardinge I.
156.tq: Use the office-holder trap by distinguishing the Governor-General connected with the transaction.
xs: The **1845** sale took place under Governor-General **Hardinge I** — option **(2)**.
Denmark, in **financial difficulty**, sold **Serampore and Tranquebar** to the British.
xa: It ended the Danish presence in India.
Price: some notes **Rs 1,20,000**, others "Rs **120** lakhs" — learn the **year + buyer**.
The Danes had come in **1616**.

156.s: The Danish-Halle Mission at Tranquebar was founded in 1706 as the earliest sustained Protestant mission in:
156.x: Founded in 1706, the Danish-Halle Mission at Tranquebar was the earliest sustained Protestant mission in South India.
156.tq: Associate the mission’s foundation date with its regional field of activity.
xs: The **Danish-Halle Mission (1706)** at Tranquebar was the earliest sustained **Protestant** mission in **South India** — option **(3)**.
It was founded by **Ziegenbalg** (Danish-German).
xa: Ziegenbalg translated the New Testament into **Tamil**.
**Benjamin Schulz** of the same mission did the first **Telugu** Bible.
⚠ Some notes say "the Dutch" propagated religion from Tranquebar — it was the **Danes**.

156.s: Bartholomaeus Ziegenbalg, associated with the Tranquebar Mission, was a:
o: Danish naval commander working in Telugu
156.x: Ziegenbalg was a German pietist who worked in Tamil at the Tranquebar Mission. He lived from 1682 to 1719.
156.tq: Distinguish the missionary’s nationality, religious background and language from those of later workers.
xs: **Ziegenbalg (1682-1719)** was a **German pietist** working in **Tamil** — option **(2)**.
He founded the **Danish-Halle Mission** and translated the Bible (New Testament) into Tamil.
xa: His method: learn the language, vernacular Bible, schools.
That method became a **template for later missions in Andhra**.
The mission was founded in **1706**.

156.s:
Consider the following statements about Benjamin Schulz:
1. He was the first to translate the Bible into Telugu, completed and published in 1746-47 at Halle.
2. He began the Telugu translation in 1727.
3. He prepared a Tamil grammar and dictionary.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
156.x: Statement 1 is correct: Schulz of the Danish-Halle Mission was the first to translate the Bible into Telugu, completed/published in 1746-47 at Halle (APPSC G2 2019). Statement 2 is correct: he began the translation in 1727. Statement 3 is wrong: he prepared a Telugu grammar and dictionary; it was Ziegenbalg who worked in Tamil. So '1 only' misses statement 2, and options with statement 3 are wrong.
156.tq: Schulz = Telugu (1727 begun, 1746-47 Halle); Ziegenbalg = Tamil.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: **Schulz** made the **first Telugu Bible**, published **1746-47** at **Halle** (APPSC G2 **2019**).
Statement 2 correct: he began the translation in **1727**.
Statement 3 wrong: he prepared a **Telugu** grammar and dictionary; **Ziegenbalg** worked in Tamil.
xa: Schulz learnt Telugu from **1719** at **Madras, Cuddalore, Pulicat**.
His grammar was a landmark in early **Telugu prose**.
**Subbarayudu (Anandarao)** helped with the Telugu Bible.

156.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes the Danish and Dutch roles at Tranquebar?
o: The Dutch founded the Danish-Halle Mission at Tranquebar.
The Danes established the Ostend Company at Tranquebar.
The Dutch founded Serampore College at Tranquebar.
The Danes founded the Danish-Halle Mission at Tranquebar.
156.x: The Danish-Halle Mission at Tranquebar was founded by the Danes in 1706. The attribution of this missionary work to the Dutch is incorrect.
156.tq: Resolve the look-alike European-power confusion by matching the mission to its actual sponsor.
xs: The **Danes** founded the **Danish-Halle Mission** at Tranquebar — option **(4)**.
⚠ Some notes say "the Dutch" propagated religion from Tranquebar — it was the **Danes**.
The **Ostend Company** was Austrian; **Serampore College** was in Serampore, not Tranquebar.
xa: The mission was founded in **1706** by **Ziegenbalg**.
Earliest sustained **Protestant** mission in South India.
⚠ The Serampore press too is wrongly called "Dutch" in some notes — it was **Danish** Serampore.

o: William Carey, Joshua Marshman and William Ward
William Carey, Benjamin Schulz and Bartholomaeus Ziegenbalg
Joshua Marshman, Francois Martin and William Ward
William Ward, Subbarayudu and Benjamin Schulz
156.x: The Serampore Trio consisted of the Baptist missionaries William Carey, Joshua Marshman and William Ward.
156.tq: Match all three names as a missionary group instead of mixing members from the Tranquebar mission.
xs: The **Serampore Trio**: **William Carey, Joshua Marshman, William Ward** — option **(1)**.
They were **Baptists**; **Schulz** and **Ziegenbalg** were of the **Danish-Halle Mission**.
xa: They worked from Danish Serampore to bypass **EIC bans** on missionaries.
Founded **Serampore College (1818)**.
Ran the **Serampore Mission Press**.

156.s: The Serampore Trio worked from Danish Serampore primarily in order to:
o: bypass the early East India Company bans on missionaries
replace Tamil with Persian in missionary education
establish a Dutch trading monopoly in Bengal
156.x: Carey, Marshman and Ward operated from Danish Serampore to bypass the early bans imposed by the East India Company on missionary activity.
156.tq: Identify the cause-and-effect link between the location and missionary activity.
xs: They worked from **Danish Serampore** to **bypass early EIC bans on missionaries** — option **(2)**.
The **Ostend Company** was Austrian; Serampore was Danish, not Dutch.
xa: They translated the Bible into many **vernaculars**.
They led early **social reform + education**.
**Serampore College (1818)**.

156.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Benjamin Schulz's Telugu Bible was completed and published at Serampore in 1746-47.
2. Serampore College was founded by the Serampore Trio in 1818.
3. The first Telugu Bible printed in India came from the Serampore press in 1807-1810.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
156.x: Statement 2 is correct: Serampore College was founded in 1818. Statement 3 is correct: the Serampore press printed the first Telugu Bible in India in 1807-1810. Statement 1 is wrong: Schulz's Telugu Bible was completed/published at Halle in 1746-47, not at Serampore. So '2 only' misses statement 3, and options with statement 1 are wrong.
156.tq: Schulz = Halle 1746-47; Serampore = printed in India 1807-10.
xs: Statements **2 and 3 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 2: **Serampore College** was founded by the **Serampore Trio** in **1818**.
Statement 3: the **first Telugu Bible printed in India** came from the **Serampore** press, **1807-1810**.
Statement 1 is wrong: **Schulz's** Telugu Bible was completed/published at **Halle**, **1746-47**.
xa: Schulz learnt Telugu from **1719** and began the translation in **1727**.
**Ziegenbalg** founded the **Danish-Halle Mission** in **1706**; translated the Bible into **Tamil**.
Serampore Trio: **William Carey, Joshua Marshman, William Ward**.

156.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Swedish East India Company — founded in 1616
Danish East India Company — chartered in 1731
156.x: The Ostend Company of the Austrian Netherlands was chartered in 1722. The Swedish East India Company dates from 1731, the Danish East India Company from 1616, and the Danish-Halle Mission from 1706.
156.tq: Match the organisation with its correct date while rejecting swapped dates from nearby institutions.
xs: **Ostend Company — 1722** is correct — option **(1)**.
The **Swedish** company dates from **1731**; the **Danish** from **1616**; the **Danish-Halle Mission** from **1706**.
xa: Ostend Company was of the **Austrian Netherlands**.
Its posts: **Banquibazar** (Bengal) and **Covelong** near Madras.
**1845** is the Danish sale.

156.s:
With regard to the Swedish East India Company, consider the following statements:
1. It was established in 1731.
2. It traded mainly with China.
3. It had a negligible presence in India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
156.x: All three statements are correct. The Swedish East India Company was established in 1731, focused mainly on trade with China, and had only a negligible presence in India.
156.tq: Combine the organisation’s date, principal trading area and Indian significance.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.

156.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Portuguese, Danish and French presence in India is correct?

The French arrived in 1498 and were the last to leave in 1961.

156.s: Following the Tranquebar methods, which Protestant missions became associated with Guntur and Ongole respectively in Andhra?

157.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the order of establishment of the four European factories at Machilipatnam?

the headquarters of the Dutch in India

Statement 2: about **930** French defeated about **10,000** of **Anwaruddin's** army.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Captain Paradis** led the French; **Mahfuz Khan**, Anwaruddin's son, led the Nawab's army.
xa: Lesson: small disciplined European infantry + artillery beat far larger Indian cavalry armies.
⚠ Anwaruddin died later, at **Ambur (1749)**.
A French fleet from **Mauritius** captured Madras in **1746**.

159.s: The Battle of St. Thome is historically significant because it demonstrated that:
o: The Nawab of Carnatic had established French supremacy in India
Naval power had become irrelevant on the Coromandel coast
A small disciplined European force could defeat a much larger Indian army
Indian cavalry could defeat European artillery in open battle
159.x: The battle showed the superiority of disciplined European infantry over a much larger Indian army and opened the way for European interference in Indian politics.
159.tq: Infer the broader historical significance from the unequal force sizes and result.
xs: St. Thome showed a **small disciplined European force** could beat a **much larger Indian army** — option **(3)**.
About **930** French beat about **10,000**; it **opened the door to European interference**.
⚠ The war also showed **naval power** was decisive — so naval power was not irrelevant.
xa: St. Thome = Battle of **Adyar (1746)**.
It first showed Indian rulers' **military weakness** against European-trained troops.
French led by **Captain Paradis**; Nawab's army by **Mahfuz Khan**.

159.s: Anwaruddin became Nawab of Arcot in 1744 after:
o: Being elected by the French East India Company
Killing Syed Ali, the minor Nawab whom he had been appointed to guard
Receiving the office directly from the English East India Company
159.x: Nizam-ul-Mulk sent Anwaruddin as guardian of the minor Nawab Syed Ali. Anwaruddin killed Syed Ali and made himself Nawab of Arcot in 1744.
159.tq: Track the succession event and distinguish appointment as guardian from assumption of power.
xs: **Anwaruddin** **killed Syed Ali**, the minor Nawab he was to guard, and became **Nawab of Arcot (1744)** — option **(3)**.
He had been sent as guardian by **Nizam-ul-Mulk**.
**St. Thome (1746)** came later, and his army **lost** there.
xa: He asked both Companies **not to fight in his territory**.
He marched to support the **English** against the French.
He was killed at **Ambur (1749)** in the Second War.

159.s:
Consider the following statements about Anwaruddin:
1. He asked both the English and French Companies not to fight in his territory.
2. He marched to support the English against the French.
3. His army was defeated at St. Thome.
4. He was killed at Ambur in 1749.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
159.x: All four statements are correct. Anwaruddin opposed fighting in his territory, supported the English, suffered defeat at St. Thome, and was later killed at Ambur in 1749 during the Second Carnatic War.
159.tq: Verify the sequence of Anwaruddin’s policy, military action and later fate.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Anwaruddin** asked both Companies not to fight in his territory and **marched to support the English**.
His army (under **Mahfuz Khan**) lost at **St. Thome (1746)**; he was killed at **Ambur (1749)**.
xa: He became **Nawab of Arcot** in **1744** after killing **Syed Ali**.
He had been sent by **Nizam-ul-Mulk** as guardian.
**930** French beat about **10,000** at St. Thome.

159.s: Under the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle, which territory was given to France in exchange for the restoration of Madras to the English?
o: Fort St. David on the Coromandel coast
159.x: Madras was restored to the English in exchange for Louisbourg in North America, which was given back to the French.
159.tq: Use the territorial-exchange pair rather than recalling only the treaty’s name.
xs: **Louisbourg** in **North America** went to the French in exchange for **Madras** — option **(2)**.
The treaty was **Aix-la-Chapelle (1748)**.
**Mauritius** was where the French fleet came from in **1746**.
xa: Madras had been captured by the French in **1746**.
The treaty restored the **pre-war position**.
UPPSC **2020/2025** keyed "English got back Madras" as correct.

159.s:
Consider the following statements about the results of the First Carnatic War:
1. It ended French political power in India.
2. It showed that naval power decided the Anglo-French contest on the Coromandel coast.
3. Its political result was nil despite Dupleix's victories.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
159.x: Statement 2 is correct: naval power proved decisive. Statement 3 is correct: the political result was nil, though both sides now eyed Indian politics. Statement 1 is wrong: Aix-la-Chapelle (1748) restored the pre-war position; French political power ended only with the Treaty of Paris (1763). So options with statement 1 are wrong.
159.tq: First war = status quo (Madras for Louisbourg); Paris 1763 ended French power.
xs: Statements **2 and 3 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 2: **naval power** decided the Anglo-French contest on the **Coromandel coast**.
Statement 3: the **political result was nil** despite Dupleix's victories.
Statement 1 is wrong: **Aix-la-Chapelle (1748)** restored the pre-war position; French political power ended with **Paris (1763)**.
xa: The Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle was signed on **18 September 1748**.
**Madras** went back to the English in exchange for **Louisbourg** (North America).
The war was a direct extension of the **War of Austrian Succession**.

159.s: Which comparison between the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle and the Treaty of Paris is correct?
o: Aix-la-Chapelle restored the pre-war position, whereas Paris ended French political power in India
Aix-la-Chapelle ended the Seven Years’ War, whereas Paris restored Madras to the English
Aix-la-Chapelle transferred Madras to France, whereas Paris transferred Louisbourg to England
Both treaties permanently ended French political power in India
159.x: The Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle restored the pre-war position, while the Treaty of Paris in 1763 marked the end of French political power in India.
159.tq: Compare the limited settlement of 1748 with the decisive settlement of 1763.
xs: **Aix-la-Chapelle** restored the **pre-war position**, while **Paris (1763)** **ended French political power** — option **(1)**.
Aix-la-Chapelle returned **Madras** to the English and **Louisbourg** to the French.
xa: Aix-la-Chapelle signed **18 September 1748**.
It also ended the **War of Austrian Succession**.
Political result of the First War: **nil**.

160.s:
The succession disputes that led to the Second Carnatic War were triggered by which combination of events?
1. Death of Nizam-ul-Mulk in 1748
2. Release of Chanda Sahib from Maratha captivity
3. Outbreak of a European war before the Indian succession disputes
Which of the statements given above are correct?
160.x: The disputes were triggered by the death of Nizam-ul-Mulk in 1748 and the release of Chanda Sahib, who had earlier been held by the Marathas. They were not initially caused by a European war.
160.tq: Separate the actual triggers from the tempting but false European-war explanation.
xs: The trigger was the **death of Nizam-ul-Mulk (1748)** plus the **release of Chanda Sahib** by the Marathas: statements **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
Statement 1 is correct: **Nizam-ul-Mulk's death in 1748** opened the Hyderabad succession.
Statement 2 is correct: **Chanda Sahib**, son-in-law of **Dost Ali**, was released by the **Marathas** and claimed the Carnatic.
Statement 3 is wrong: **no European war** lay behind the Second Carnatic War.
xa: It was the **first war fought over Indian politics**, not a European war.
Lesson both companies learnt: backing **Indian claimants** brought **territory + revenue**.
Thrones in dispute: **Hyderabad** (Deccan subahdari) and the **Carnatic (Arcot)**.

160.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the rival claims in Hyderabad and the Carnatic:
1. Nasir Jang was the son of Nizam-ul-Mulk.
2. Muzaffar Jang was the daughter's son of Nizam-ul-Mulk.
3. Chanda Sahib was the English-backed claimant to the Carnatic.
4. Muhammad Ali succeeded Anwaruddin as the French-backed claimant.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
160.x: Nasir Jang was Nizam-ul-Mulk's son and Muzaffar Jang was his daughter's son. Chanda Sahib was French-backed, while Muhammad Ali was supported by the English after Anwaruddin.
160.tq: Check family relationships first, then identify the company supporting each claimant.
xs: Only statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: **Nasir Jang** was **Nizam-ul-Mulk's son** (English-backed).
Statement 2 correct: **Muzaffar Jang** was Nizam-ul-Mulk's **daughter's son** (French-backed).
Statement 3 wrong: **Chanda Sahib** was the **French**-backed claimant to the Carnatic.
Statement 4 wrong: **Muhammad Ali** succeeded Anwaruddin as the **English**-backed claimant.
xa: **Nasir Jang** first **captured Muzaffar Jang**; he was later murdered by **Himmat Khan**, Nawab of Kurnool.
**Muhammad Ali** became **Nawab of Carnatic** after the relief of Trichinopoly in **June 1752**.
⚠ Trap: Dupleix **won the Deccan** (Hyderabad) but **lost the Carnatic** (Arcot, Trichinopoly).

160.s:
Consider the following statements about the Battle of Ambur:
1. Muhammad Ali fled to Trichinopoly after the battle.
2. It was fought in 1752.
3. Anwaruddin was killed and Chanda Sahib became Nawab of the Carnatic.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
160.x: Statement 2 is wrong: Ambur was fought in 1749 (1752 is Chanda Sahib's surrender at Trichinopoly). Statement 3 is correct: Anwaruddin was killed and Chanda Sahib became Nawab. Statement 1 is correct: Muhammad Ali fled to Trichinopoly. So only 2 and 3.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: **Muhammad Ali** fled to **Tiruchirappalli (Trichinopoly)**.
Statement 3: **Anwaruddin** was killed; **Chanda Sahib** became **Nawab of Carnatic**.
Statement 2 is wrong: Ambur was fought in **1749**; **June 1752** is Chanda Sahib's surrender.
xa: At Ambur **Dupleix + Muzaffar Jang + Chanda Sahib** were allied.
**Rayachoti** (**1751**): Muzaffar Jang killed; **Bussy** installed **Salabat Jang**.
**Clive** held **Arcot** for **53 days** (**1751**).

160.s: Nasir Jang, the English-backed claimant to Hyderabad, was murdered in a plot arranged by Dupleix by which ruler?
o: The Nawab of Kurnool, Himmat Khan
160.x: Nasir Jang was murdered by Himmat Khan, the Nawab of Kurnool, in a plot arranged by Dupleix.
160.tq: Use the wrong-ruler trap by distinguishing Himmat Khan from other regional chiefs.
xs: **Nasir Jang** was killed by the **Nawab of Kurnool, Himmat Khan** — option **(1)**.
The plot was **arranged by Dupleix**; it freed **Muzaffar Jang**, who became Subahdar.
**Raja Sahib** was Chanda Sahib's son who besieged **Arcot**; **Salabat Jang** was installed by **Bussy**.
The **Nawab of Kadapa** was among those who killed **Muzaffar Jang** at **Rayachoti**, not Nasir Jang.
xa: **Nasir Jang** was **Nizam-ul-Mulk's son**, backed by the **English**.
**Rayachoti (1751)**: Muzaffar Jang killed by Nawabs of **Kadapa, Kurnool, Nayanur**.
⚠ Kurnool appears twice: **Himmat Khan** killed Nasir Jang; Kurnool's Nawab also joined at **Rayachoti**.

160.s: Who was installed by Bussy immediately after the death of Muzaffar Jang?
160.x: Bussy immediately installed Salabat Jang, the fourth son of Nizam-ul-Mulk, after Muzaffar Jang was killed.
160.tq: Distinguish the replacement ruler from the earlier rival claimants.
xs: **Bussy** at once installed **Salabat Jang** after Muzaffar Jang's death — option **(4)**.
**Salabat Jang** was **Nizam-ul-Mulk's 4th son**.
**Nasir Jang** was already murdered; **Chanda Sahib** and **Muhammad Ali** were Carnatic (Arcot) claimants, not Hyderabad.
xa: **Muzaffar Jang** was killed at **Rayachoti (1751)** by the Nawabs of **Kadapa, Kurnool, Nayanur**.
**Bussy** was French; **Dupleix** was the architect of the **policy of interference**.
Comparative note: Dupleix **won the Deccan (Hyderabad)** but lost the Carnatic.

160.s: Which of the following was granted to Dupleix by Muzaffar Jang?
o: The governorship of Mauritius and Fort St. David
The governorship of Mughal territory south of the Krishna and Valapadu as a jagir
The whole of Bengal and the port of Calcutta
160.x: Dupleix was declared Governor or Nawab of Mughal territory south of the Krishna and received Valapadu as a jagir.
160.tq: Use the exact territorial grant and jagir association.
xs: Dupleix was made **governor (Nawab) of Mughal territory south of the Krishna** and got **Valapadu** as a **jagir** — option **(2)**.
This reward is an **APPSC 2021** question.
The other options name places (Mauritius, Bengal, Madras, Louisburg) that the notes do not list among Dupleix's rewards.
xa: Territories near **Pondicherry**: **Villianur, Bahur, Valapadu**.
On the **Andhra coast**: **Diviseema and Machilipatnam**.
Dupleix was **recalled in 1754**; successor **Godeheu**.

160.s: Why did Robert Clive propose an attack on Arcot during the siege of Trichinopoly?
o: To install Salabat Jang as Nawab of the Carnatic
To capture the French headquarters at Pondicherry
To recover Machilipatnam from the French
To create a diversion and relieve Muhammad Ali by drawing away Chanda Sahib's forces
160.x: Chanda Sahib and the French were besieging Muhammad Ali at Trichinopoly. Clive proposed attacking Arcot, the Carnatic capital, as a diversionary measure.
160.tq: Identify the strategic purpose of the operation rather than its later political result.
xs: Clive proposed attacking **Arcot** as a **diversion** to relieve **Muhammad Ali** by drawing away **Chanda Sahib's forces** — option **(4)**.
**Chanda Sahib + the French** were besieging Muhammad Ali at **Trichinopoly**; **Arcot** was the **Carnatic capital**.
**Salabat Jang** was installed at Hyderabad by **Bussy**, not by Clive.
xa: Clive took Arcot with **210 men** (UPSC); some notes say **200 English + 300 sepoys**.
He held it against **Raja Sahib** for **53 days** (some notes say 50).
Clive then beat Raja Sahib at **Arni** and **Kaveripak**.

160.s:
Consider the following statements about Robert Clive's capture and defence of Arcot (1751):
1. Clive took Arcot with a small force of about 210 men.
2. He held Arcot for about 53 days against Raja Sahib, the son of Chanda Sahib.
3. After the siege, he defeated Raja Sahib at Ambur and Rayachoti.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
160.x: Statement 1 is correct: Clive took Arcot with about 210 men. Statement 2 is correct: he held it for 53 days against Raja Sahib. Statement 3 is wrong: Clive then beat Raja Sahib at Arni and Kaveripak; Ambur (1749) was where Anwaruddin was killed and Rayachoti (1751) where Muzaffar Jang was killed. So only 1 and 2 (A); B, C and D all include the false statement 3.
160.tq: Arcot = 210 men, 53 days, then Arni + Kaveripak.
xs: Only statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: Clive took **Arcot** with about **210 men** (UPSC).
Statement 2 correct: he held it **53 days** against **Raja Sahib**, Chanda Sahib's son.
Statement 3 wrong: he beat Raja Sahib at **Arni** and **Kaveripak**; **Ambur (1749)** killed Anwaruddin and **Rayachoti (1751)** killed Muzaffar Jang.
xa: Some notes give Clive's force as **200 English + 300 sepoys** and the siege as **50** days.
**Clive and Stringer Lawrence** then relieved **Trichinopoly** (**June 1752**).
French commander **Law** surrendered; **Chanda Sahib** surrendered and was **executed**.

160.s:
Which of the following groups joined the English during Clive's campaign in the Carnatic?
1. Mysore
2. Tanjore
3. The Maratha chief Morari Rao
4. The Nawab of Kurnool
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
160.x: Mysore, Tanjore and the Maratha chief Morari Rao joined the English. The Nawab of Kurnool was associated with the plot against Nasir Jang, not with this English alliance.
160.tq: Separate the campaign allies from a regional figure associated with a different event.
xs: **Mysore**, **Tanjore** and the Maratha chief **Morari Rao** joined the English — **1, 2 and 3 only**, option **(1)**.
The **Nawab of Kurnool**, **Himmat Khan**, murdered **Nasir Jang** in a plot arranged by **Dupleix** — not an English ally.
xa: **Clive and Stringer Lawrence** relieved **Trichinopoly**.
French commander **Law** surrendered at Trichinopoly; **Muhammad Ali** became **Nawab of Carnatic**.
**Raja Sahib** (Chanda Sahib's son) fought on the **French side**.

160.s: Who jointly relieved Trichinopoly, leading to the surrender of the French commander Law?
160.x: Robert Clive and Stringer Lawrence relieved Trichinopoly. The French commander Law surrendered during this operation.
160.tq: Match the two English commanders with the relief operation and avoid swapping them with French leaders.
xs: **Robert Clive and Stringer Lawrence** relieved Trichinopoly — option **(4)**.
The French commander **Law** surrendered; **Chanda Sahib** surrendered and was **executed** (**June 1752**).
**Bussy and Dupleix** were French leaders; **Chanda Sahib and Raja Sahib** were on the French side.
xa: **Muhammad Ali** then became **Nawab of Carnatic**.
The defeat at **Trichinopoly** was a reason for **Dupleix's recall (1754)**.
Allies of the English: **Morari Rao**, **Mysore**, **Tanjore**.

160.s:
Which sequence correctly represents the concluding events of the Trichinopoly campaign?
A. Law surrendered
B. Chanda Sahib surrendered
C. Chanda Sahib was executed
D. Muhammad Ali became Nawab of the Carnatic
160.x: Law first surrendered; Chanda Sahib surrendered in June 1752, was executed, and Muhammad Ali subsequently became Nawab of the Carnatic.
160.tq: Follow the surrender–execution–succession sequence to eliminate reversals.
xs: The order is **A, B, C, D** — option **(1)**.
**Law surrendered** first at Trichinopoly; then **Chanda Sahib surrendered** (**June 1752**) and was **executed**.
Finally **Muhammad Ali became Nawab of Carnatic**.
xa: Trichinopoly was relieved by **Clive and Stringer Lawrence**.
Before this, Clive's **Siege of Arcot (1751)** lasted **53 days**.
⚠ **Ambur = 1749**; **Rayachoti = 1751**; Chanda Sahib's surrender = **June 1752**.

160.s: The French Company recalled Dupleix in 1754 primarily because of which reason?
o: His grant of the Northern Circars to Salabat Jang
The heavy cost and failures of his policy of intervention in Indian politics, including defeat at Trichinopoly
His appointment as Nawab of the Carnatic
His refusal to negotiate with the English after the Treaty of Pondicherry
160.x: The French Company became alarmed by the heavy expense and failures of Dupleix's interventionist policy, particularly the defeat at Trichinopoly, and recalled him in 1754.
160.tq: Identify the administrative reason for recall rather than a later treaty or territorial event.
xs: The French Company was alarmed at the **heavy cost** and **failures of the interference policy**, including defeat at **Trichinopoly** — option **(2)**.
Dupleix was recalled in **1754**.
He was never **Nawab of the Carnatic**: his title was governor (Nawab) of Mughal territory **south of the Krishna**.
xa: His successor **Godeheu** **made peace with the English**.
Rewards to the French: jagir of **Valapadu**; **Diviseema and Machilipatnam** on the Andhra coast.
Comparative note: Dupleix **won the Deccan** but **lost the Carnatic**.

160.s: Who succeeded Dupleix as the French Governor in India and made peace with the English?
160.x: Godeheu succeeded Dupleix in 1754 and made peace with the English.
160.tq: Use the successor–policy association to distinguish Godeheu from military commanders.
xs: **Godeheu** succeeded Dupleix and **made peace with the English** — option **(4)**.
**Law** was the French commander who **surrendered at Trichinopoly**; **Bussy** installed **Salabat Jang**.
**Salabat Jang** was Nizam-ul-Mulk's **4th son**, not a French governor.
xa: Dupleix was **recalled in 1754**.
Reasons: **heavy cost** + failures of the **interference policy**; defeat at **Trichinopoly**.

160.s:
Which of the following statements best explains the significance of the Second Carnatic War?
1. It was the first war fought over Indian political succession rather than a European conflict.
2. It taught both companies that support to Indian claimants could yield territory and revenue.
3. The Andhra coast was the principal area of French territorial gain in this war.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
160.x: All three statements are correct. The war centred on Indian political disputes, demonstrated the territorial and revenue advantages of backing claimants, and brought major French gains on the Andhra coast.
160.tq: Check whether each statement captures a separate aspect of the war's significance.
xs: All three statements are correct — **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
Statement 1: it was the **first war fought over Indian politics**, not a European war.
Statement 2: the lesson was that **backing Indian claimants** brought **territory + revenue**.
Statement 3: the **Andhra coast** (Machilipatnam, Diviseema, **Northern Circars**) was the main **French territorial gain**.
xa: Trigger: death of **Nizam-ul-Mulk (1748)** + release of **Chanda Sahib** by the Marathas.
Dupleix **won the Deccan (Hyderabad)** but **lost the Carnatic** (Arcot, Trichinopoly).

160.s: Which one of the following correctly compares Dupleix's fortunes in the Deccan and the Carnatic?
o: He won the Deccan but lost the Carnatic
He lost both the Deccan and the Carnatic
He lost the Deccan but won the Carnatic
He won both the Deccan and the Carnatic
160.x: Dupleix succeeded in the Deccan, particularly through influence at Hyderabad, but lost the Carnatic struggle at Arcot and Trichinopoly.
160.tq: Use the paired regional comparison to avoid reversing the Deccan and Carnatic outcomes.
xs: Dupleix **won the Deccan** (Hyderabad) but **lost the Carnatic** (Arcot, Trichinopoly) — option **(1)**.
In the Deccan, **Bussy** installed **Salabat Jang** after Muzaffar Jang's death.
In the Carnatic, Clive's **Arcot** siege and the relief of **Trichinopoly** made **Muhammad Ali** Nawab.
xa: The defeat at **Trichinopoly** led to **Dupleix's recall (1754)**.
Successor **Godeheu** made peace with the English.

161.s: The Third Carnatic War in India formed the Indian theatre of which wider conflict?
161.x: The Third Carnatic War was the Indian theatre of the Seven Years' War, fought from 1756 to 1763.
161.tq: Connect the regional conflict with its wider international war and dates.
xs: The Third Carnatic War was the Indian theatre of the **Seven Years' War (1756-63)** — option **(1)**.
The **Treaty of Paris (1763)** ended both the **Seven Years' War** and the Third Carnatic War.
xa: By **1758** Clive had won **Plassey (1757)** and taken French **Chandernagore**; Bengal revenue paid for the Carnatic campaign.
Decisive battle: **Wandiwash**, **22 January 1760** — **Eyre Coote** routed **Count de Lally**.
"Third Carnatic War concluded by the Treaty of ___ in 1763" — **Paris** (**APPSC 2025**).

161.s: Which development enabled the English to finance the Carnatic campaign from Bengal?
o: Clive's victory at Plassey and the resulting availability of Bengal revenue
The French conquest of Chandernagore after Plassey
The surrender of Madras to Salabat Jang
The transfer of Pondicherry revenue to Calcutta
161.x: After Clive's victory at Plassey in 1757 and the capture of French Chandernagore, Bengal revenue helped finance the English Carnatic campaign.
161.tq: Trace the resource link between an earlier victory and a later campaign.
xs: **Clive's victory at Plassey (1757)** made **Bengal revenue** available to pay for the Carnatic campaign — option **(1)**.
Chandernagore was a **French** settlement **taken by Clive**, not a French conquest — option (2) inverts it.
**Pondicherry** was the only French base; its revenue was never transferred to Calcutta.
xa: English advantage: **Bengal's wealth and men after Plassey**; the French suffered a **chronic shortage of funds** and **unpaid troops**.
**UPPSC 2016**: both "Bengal wealth and manpower" and "**naval superiority**" are correct reasons for English success.
Clive sent **Colonel Forde** from Bengal, who won **Chandurti**.

161.s:
Consider the following statements about the Andhra theatre of the Third Carnatic War:
1. The Battle of Chandurti (Condore) was fought on 7 December 1758 near Rajahmundry.
2. The English took Machilipatnam in April 1759.
3. The Bobbili battle was fought on 24 January 1760.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
161.x: Statement 1 is correct: Chandurti was fought on 7 December 1758 near Rajahmundry. Statement 2 is correct: Machilipatnam was taken in April 1759. Statement 3 is wrong: the Bobbili battle was on 24 January 1757 (1760 is the year of Wandiwash). So A; B, C and D include the false statement 3.
161.tq: Andhra sequence: Tumnapalem 1756 - Bobbili 1757 - Chandurti 1758 - Machilipatnam 1759.
xs: Only statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: **Chandurti** was fought on **7 December 1758** near **Rajahmundry**.
Statement 2 correct: **Machilipatnam** was taken in **April 1759**.
Statement 3 wrong: the **Bobbili battle** was on **24 Jan 1757**; **22 January 1760** is **Wandiwash**.
xa: At Chandurti, the **English + Vizianagaram army** defeated the French under **Conflans**.
**Tumnapalem (1756)**: Bussy aided by Vizianagaram ruler **Vijayaramaraju**.
Malleson on Chandurti: "**small battle, great results**".

161.s:
With reference to the Battle of Chandurti, consider the following statements:
1. Colonel Forde was sent by Clive from Bengal.
2. Forde fought alongside the Vizianagaram army of Ananda Gajapati.
3. The French force was commanded by Conflans.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
161.x: All three statements are correct. Forde came from Bengal, joined Ananda Gajapati's Vizianagaram force, and defeated the French under Conflans.
161.tq: Confirm the commander, ally and opponent as a single battlefield combination.
xs: All three statements are correct — **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
Statement 1: **Colonel Forde** was **sent by Clive from Bengal**.
Statement 2: Forde fought with the **Vizianagaram** army of **Ananda Gajapati**.
Statement 3: the French were commanded by **Conflans**.
xa: Result: the French were **driven out of the Northern Circars**.
**Ananda Gajapati** also beat Peddapuram's **Jagapati Raju** at **Konduru**; he died of **smallpox** in **1760**.
Comparative note: **Chandurti (1758)** = foundation of British rule in **Andhra**, as **Plassey (1757)** is for India.

161.s: The immediate significance of the English victory at Chandurti was that it:
o: ended the rule of Salabat Jang in Hyderabad
drove the French out of the Northern Circars
gave the French control over Bengal
161.x: The victory at Chandurti drove the French out of the Northern Circars and was later described as a small battle with great results.
161.tq: Identify the regional consequence rather than the later treaty settlement.
xs: Chandurti **drove the French out of the Northern Circars** — option **(3)**.
**Salabat Jang** was not removed; after Machilipatnam fell (**April 1759**) he **changed sides** to the English.
**Pondicherry** fell to the English in **1761**; France never controlled Bengal.
xa: Chandurti: **7 December 1758**, near **Rajahmundry**; English + Vizianagaram army beat **Conflans**.
Malleson: "**small battle, great results**".
AP angle: Chandurti and Machilipatnam gave the English their **first foothold in the Northern Circars**.

161.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Bobbili battle — 24 January 1757; led by Pocock
Machilipatnam — 1761; transferred by the Treaty of Paris
161.x: In 1756 at Tumnapalem, Bussy was aided by the Vizianagaram ruler Vijayaramaraju. The other pairs wrongly associate dates, commanders or causes.
161.tq: Check each date and person against the Andhra sequence before selecting the complete pair.
xs: **Tumnapalem (1756)** — **Bussy** aided by the Vizianagaram ruler **Vijayaramaraju** — is correctly matched, option **(1)**.
**Pocock** was the English **admiral**, not linked to the Bobbili battle (**24 Jan 1757**).
**Chandurti** was **7 December 1758**, an **English** victory with **Forde** over the French under **Conflans**.
**Machilipatnam** was taken in **April 1759** and given by **Salabat Jang**, not by the Treaty of Paris.
xa: **Vijayaramaraju** aided the French; later **Ananda Gajapati** of Vizianagaram fought with the **English** at Chandurti.
⚠ Vizianagaram switched sides between **Tumnapalem (1756)** and **Chandurti (1758)**.

161.s: After the fall of Machilipatnam in 1759, Salabat Jang changed sides and gave the English Machilipatnam, Nizampatnam, Vakal Mannar and part of Kondapalli. This arrangement is significant because it was the:
o: first agreement between the British and Hyderabad
Treaty of Paris settlement of the Carnatic
first Subsidiary Alliance signed by the Nizam
Treaty of Masulipatnam leasing the Northern Circars
161.x: The 1759 grant by Salabat Jang was the first British-Hyderabad agreement. The Treaty of Paris came in 1763, the first Subsidiary Alliance with Hyderabad in 1798, and the Treaty of Masulipatnam in 1768.
161.tq: 1759 Salabat Jang grant = first British-Hyderabad agreement
xs: **Salabat Jang**'s grant after Machilipatnam fell (**April 1759**) was the **first British-Hyderabad agreement** — option **(1)**.
He gave the English **Machilipatnam, Nizampatnam, Vakal Mannar and part of Kondapalli**.
The **Treaty of Paris** came in **1763** and dealt with the Seven Years' War, not Hyderabad.
xa: This followed **Chandurti (7 December 1758)**, which drove the French out of the **Northern Circars**.
AP angle: this gave the English their **first foothold in the Northern Circars**; **Yanam** stayed French.

161.s: Who was the English admiral during the Third Carnatic War?
161.x: Pocock was the English admiral. D'Ache was the French admiral (some sources wrongly call the English admiral 'D'Eveche'), La Bourdonnais was the French Governor of Mauritius in the First war, and Conflans was the French commander beaten at Chandurti.
161.tq: English admiral = Pocock; French admiral = d'Ache
xs: The English admiral was **Pocock** — option **(2)**.
**d'Ache** commanded the **French** fleet, which was beaten.
**Conflans** was the **French** commander defeated at **Chandurti**.
xa: ⚠ Trap: some notes name the English admiral "**D'Eveche**" – wrong; he was **Pocock**.
English **naval superiority** let them supply troops and cut off the French; **Lally** was left **without sea support**.
Lally failed before **Madras (1758)** for lack of **money + naval support**.

161.s: Which of the following correctly states the immediate military outcome at Wandiwash?
o: Count de Lally routed Eyre Coote and captured Madras.
Eyre Coote routed Count de Lally and Bussy was taken prisoner.
Francis Forde defeated d'Ache and captured Pondicherry.
Bussy defeated Coote and occupied Bengal.
161.x: Eyre Coote led the English victory over Count de Lally at Wandiwash, where Bussy was taken prisoner.
161.tq: Apply the wrong-person-with-the-deed trap to commanders and outcomes.
xs: At Wandiwash, **Eyre Coote routed Count de Lally** and **Bussy was taken prisoner** — option **(2)**.
**Lally** did not take Madras — he **failed before Madras (1758)** for lack of money and naval support.
**Forde** won **Chandurti**, not Pondicherry; **d'Ache** was the French admiral.
xa: ⚠ Trap: **Lally** was captured at **Pondicherry (1761)**, not at Wandiwash.
Lally held Pondicherry **eight months** before surrendering on **16 January 1761**; **Jinji + Mahe** also fell.

161.s: The Battle of Wandiwash is regarded as a turning point in Indian history mainly because it:
o: brought the Seven Years' War to an end in Europe
established French control over the Northern Circars
removed the last major European rival to British political power in India
ended the Mughal Empire in India
161.x: The English victory at Wandiwash, along with Plassey, removed the last serious European rival to British political supremacy in India.
161.tq: Move from the battle result to its wider political consequence.
xs: Wandiwash, with **Plassey**, **removed the last European rival** to British power in India — option **(3)**.
It **ended French political power in India** (BPSC 2020, UPPSC 2015).
The **Seven Years' War** ended with the **Treaty of Paris (1763)**, not Wandiwash.
The **Northern Circars** went to the **English**, not the French, after **Chandurti**.
xa: Wandiwash: **22 January 1760**, **Eyre Coote** vs **Count de Lally**; **Bussy taken prisoner**.
After 1763 the French stayed **as traders only**.

161.s: The Treaty of Paris of 1763 provided that the French factories and settlements in India would be:
o: Placed under the joint control of France and Hyderabad
Restored to France but retained only as trading posts without fortifications
Transferred permanently to the English East India Company
161.x: The French settlements were restored, but they could function only as trading posts and could not be fortified.
161.tq: Test the legally significant qualification attached to territorial restoration.
xs: Under the **Treaty of Paris (1763)**, French settlements were **restored** only as **trading posts** that **could not be fortified** — option **(2)**.
They were **demilitarised**, not transferred to the English or made into states.
xa: Retained enclaves: **Pondicherry, Karaikal, Mahe, Yanam** + **Chandernagore**.
⚠ Some notes list only "**Pondicherry, Yanam, Mahe**" – incomplete.
The treaty ended the **Seven Years' War** + Third Carnatic War (**APPSC 2025**).

161.s: Which of the following was NOT retained by the French as an enclave under the Treaty of Paris, 1763?
161.x: Pondicherry, Karaikal, Mahe, Yanam and Chandernagore were retained as French enclaves. Machilipatnam was transferred to the English through the Hyderabad agreement.
161.tq: Eliminate the recognised French enclaves and identify the Andhra territory transferred to the English.
xs: **Machilipatnam** was not a French enclave — option **(2)**.
It went to the English in **April 1759**, when **Salabat Jang** changed sides (first **British-Hyderabad agreement**).
Retained French enclaves: **Pondicherry, Karaikal, Mahe, Yanam** + **Chandernagore**.
xa: Enclaves were restored only as **trading posts** that **could not be fortified**.
AP angle: **Yanam** stayed French though the English held the **Northern Circars**.

161.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the fate of Lally from that of Bussy?
o: Lally was captured at Wandiwash, whereas Bussy surrendered Pondicherry.
Lally surrendered at Pondicherry in 1761, whereas Bussy was taken prisoner at Wandiwash.
161.x: Lally surrendered at Pondicherry on 16 January 1761. Bussy was the French commander taken prisoner at Wandiwash.
161.tq: Directly separate two frequently confused French commanders and locations.
xs: **Lally** surrendered at **Pondicherry (1761)**, while **Bussy** was **taken prisoner at Wandiwash** — option **(2)**.
Wandiwash (**22 January 1760**): **Eyre Coote** routed **Count de Lally**.
Pondicherry fell on **16 January 1761** after **eight months**.
xa: Earlier, Bussy had been aided by **Vijayaramaraju** at **Tumnapalem (1756)**.
Lally had taken **Fort St. David** (Cuddalore) in **1758**.

161.s: The Third Carnatic War was concluded by the Treaty of ___ in 1763.
161.x: The Treaty of Paris (1763) ended the Seven Years' War and the Third Carnatic War. Aix-la-Chapelle (1748) ended the First war, Pondicherry (1754) the Second, and Allahabad (1765) followed Buxar.
161.tq: 1763 = Paris (APPSC 2025)
xs: The Third Carnatic War ended with the **Treaty of Paris** (**1763**) — option **(3)**.
It also ended the **Seven Years' War (1756-63)** (**APPSC 2025**).
xa: Terms: French settlements **restored** as trading posts that **could not be fortified**.
Retained: **Pondicherry, Karaikal, Mahe, Yanam** + **Chandernagore**.
Significance: settled the **Anglo-French contest**; French stayed **as traders only**.

161.s: Which feature distinguished the English East India Company from the French company during the struggle for supremacy in India?
o: The English company was a private company with a board elected yearly, enabling quicker decisions.
The English company was state-controlled and dependent on royal subsidy.
The English company operated from Pondicherry alone.
The English company was primarily concerned with European wars rather than trade.
161.x: The English company was privately organised, with a yearly elected board and relatively quicker decision-making. The French company was state-controlled and bureaucratic.
161.tq: Compare organisational structure rather than battlefield performance.
xs: The English company was a **private company** with a **board elected yearly**, giving **quick decisions** — option **(1)**.
The **French** company was **state-controlled**, dependent on **royal subsidy** and **bureaucratic** — option (2).
The English had bases at **Calcutta, Bombay, Madras**; the French had **only Pondicherry**.
English home priority was **trade and colonies**; France was busy with **wars in Europe**.
xa: English **naval superiority**; the French fleet (**d'Ache**) was beaten.
English leadership: **Clive, Lawrence, Coote**; French: Lally quarrelled, **Dupleix recalled**.

161.s:
Consider the following statements about the reasons for English success in the Carnatic struggle:
1. English naval superiority enabled the supply of troops and the cutting off of French support.
2. Bengal's wealth and manpower strengthened the English position.
3. The French possessed several equally strong bases at Calcutta, Bombay and Madras.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
161.x: Naval superiority and Bengal's wealth and manpower were English advantages. Calcutta, Bombay and Madras were English bases, whereas the French had only Pondicherry.
161.tq: Use the comparison table and reject the reversed bases statement.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: **naval superiority** let the English supply troops and cut off the French.
Statement 2 correct: **Bengal's wealth and men after Plassey** (UPPSC 2016 lists both 1 and 2).
Statement 3 wrong: **Calcutta, Bombay, Madras** were **English** bases; the French had **only Pondicherry**.
xa: French company: **state-controlled**, dependent on **royal subsidy**; **chronic shortage of funds**.
**Lally** was left **without sea support**.

161.s: Which one of the following was a weakness of French leadership during the struggle for supremacy?
o: Coote abandoned the English naval bases.
Lally quarrelled with his officers and failed to understand Indian conditions.
Clive refused to cooperate with Indian rulers.
Lawrence was recalled by the French Crown.
161.x: Lally's quarrels with his officers and inadequate understanding of Indian conditions weakened the French effort. Dupleix was also recalled.
161.tq: Identify the correct leader–weakness association while rejecting swapped names.
xs: **Lally quarrelled with his officers** and **did not understand Indian conditions** — option **(2)**.
**Coote**, **Clive** and **Lawrence** were the **English** leaders — a strength, not a French weakness.
xa: The French also lost **Dupleix**, who had been **recalled**.
Lally lost **Wandiwash (1760)** and **surrendered Pondicherry (1761)**.
French company: **bureaucratic**, **state-controlled**.

161.s: Which one of the following statements about the Andhra theatre is correct?
o: The Andhra theatre had no bearing on French power north of the Krishna.
Chandurti gave the French their first foothold in Bengal, while Yanam became English.
Machilipatnam remained French under the Treaty of Paris, while Pondicherry became English.
Chandurti and Machilipatnam gave the English their first foothold in the Northern Circars, while Yanam remained French.
161.x: The victories at Chandurti and Machilipatnam gave the English their first foothold in the Northern Circars. Yanam remained a French possession.
161.tq: Compare the territories gained by the English with the French enclave that remained.
xs: **Chandurti and Machilipatnam** gave the English their **first foothold in the Northern Circars**, while **Yanam** stayed French — option **(4)**.
Chandurti **drove the French out of the Northern Circars** — so option (1) is wrong.
**Machilipatnam** went to the English (**1759**); **Pondicherry** was restored to France in 1763.
xa: Chandurti: **7 December 1758**, near **Rajahmundry**.
Salabat Jang's grant: **Machilipatnam, Nizampatnam, Vakal Mannar, part of Kondapalli**.

161.s: Chandurti is to the foundation of British rule in Andhra as which of the following is to the foundation of British rule in India?
161.x: Chandurti is described as the foundation of British rule in Andhra, in a parallel often drawn with Plassey as the foundation of British rule in India.
161.tq: Recognise the historical analogy rather than a military sequence.
xs: **Chandurti (1758)** is the foundation of British rule in Andhra, as **Plassey (1757)** is for India — option **(2)**.
**Wandiwash** removed the last European rival; **Bobbili** was the **24 Jan 1757** battle.
xa: Malleson: Chandurti was a "**small battle, great results**".
Chandurti was won by **Colonel Forde** with **Ananda Gajapati**'s Vizianagaram army.

161.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The First Carnatic War was fought from 1746 to 1748.
The Second Carnatic War was fought from 1750 to 1755.
The Battle of Wandiwash was fought in 1760.
The Third Carnatic War was fought from 1758 to 1763.
161.x: Option B is incorrect: the Second Carnatic War lasted from 1749 to 1754. The First (1746–48), Wandiwash (1760) and the Third (1758–63) are dated correctly.
161.tq: Recall the years of each Carnatic War.
n: The First Carnatic War was fought from 1746 to 1748. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
The Second Carnatic War was fought from 1749 to 1754. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
The Battle of Wandiwash was fought in 1760. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
The Third Carnatic War was fought from 1758 to 1763. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
xs: The incorrect statement: the **Second Carnatic War** was fought **1750 to 1755** — option **(2)**.
The Second Carnatic War lasted **1749 to 1754**.
**First war** (**1746 to 1748**), **Wandiwash** (**1760**) and **Third war** (**1758 to 1763**) are correctly dated.
xa: The Second war was **inconclusive**.
**Ambur** (**1749**) was part of the Second war.
⚠ Some notes date the Third war with the **Seven Years' War (1756-63)**.

161.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) First Carnatic War
(b) Result concerning Madras
(c) Treaty associated with the First Carnatic War
(d) Year of the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle

List-II
i. British regained Madras
ii. English fought against the French
iii. Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle
iv. 1748
161.x: The First Carnatic War was English against French, Madras went back to the British, by the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle, signed in 1748, giving a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv.
161.tq: Match each attribute of the First Carnatic War.
n: The First Carnatic War was fought from 1746 to 1748. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
The First Carnatic War was fought between the English and the French. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
The British regained Madras in the First Carnatic War. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
The Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle was signed in 1748. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
xs: The correct match is **a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv** — option **(3)**.
**First Carnatic War** — the **English** against the **French**.
**Madras** — the **British regained** it; treaty — **Aix-la-Chapelle**, signed in **1748**.
xa: The French captured Madras in **1746**.
The war ended both the **War of Austrian Succession** and the First Carnatic War.
**Anwaruddin** had asked both Companies not to fight in his territory.

161.s:
Assertion (A): The Second Carnatic War was inconclusive.
Reason (R): English- and French-backed Indian factions fought in the Second Carnatic War.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
161.x: Both are true but R does not explain A: English- and French-backed rivals fought over the Carnatic and Hyderabad, but that alone does not explain why the war ended inconclusively.
161.tq: Check whether R is the cause of A.
n: The Second Carnatic War involved English- and French-backed Indian factions. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
The Second Carnatic War was inconclusive. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
xs: **Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A** — option **(2)**.
A: the **Second Carnatic War** (**1749 to 1754**) was **inconclusive**.
R: it was fought between **English-** and **French-backed Indian factions**.
xa: Hyderabad: French backed **Muzaffar Jang**; English backed **Nasir Jang**.
Carnatic: French backed **Chanda Sahib**; English backed **Anwaruddin**, then **Muhammad Ali**.
**Dupleix** was recalled in **1754**; his successor **Godeheu** made peace.

161.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Third Carnatic War
(b) Count Lally
(c) British victory in the Third Carnatic War
(d) Treaty of Paris

List-II
(i) British fought against the French
(ii) Led the French side
(iii) French power in India ended
(iv) Concluded in 1763 and associated with the Third Carnatic War
161.x: The Third Carnatic War was British against French, Count Lally led the French, the British victory ended French power in India, and the Treaty of Paris came in 1763, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
161.tq: Match each attribute of the Third Carnatic War.
n: The Third Carnatic War was fought from 1758 to 1763. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
The Third Carnatic War was fought between the British and the French. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
Count Lally led the French in the Third Carnatic War. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
The British defeated the French in the Third Carnatic War. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
The Third Carnatic War ended French power in India. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
The Treaty of Paris was signed in 1763. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
xs: The correct match is **a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv** — option **(3)**.
**Third Carnatic War** — the **British** against the **French**; **Count Lally** — **led the French**.
**British victory** — **ended French power** in India; **Treaty of Paris** — concluded in **1763**.
xa: **Wandiwash** (**22 January 1760**): **Eyre Coote** routed Lally; **Bussy taken prisoner**.
**Pondicherry** fell on **16 January 1761**.
⚠ Lally was captured at **Pondicherry**, not at Wandiwash.

162.s:
Consider the following statements about the Treaty of Pondicherry of 1754:
1. The two companies agreed not to interfere in the quarrels of Indian princes.
2. Each company retained its existing possessions.
3. The treaty resulted in an immediate and complete French victory in the Carnatic.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
162.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: under the Treaty of Pondicherry (1754) both companies agreed not to interfere in Indian princes' quarrels and each kept its existing possessions. Statement 3 is wrong: the treaty was inconclusive, not a French victory, and Dupleix was recalled.
162.tq: Reject the extreme claim of complete victory while retaining the treaty's two stated terms.
xs: Only statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: both companies agreed **not to interfere in the quarrels of Indian princes**.
Statement 2 correct: **each kept its existing possessions**.
Statement 3 wrong: the Second war was **inconclusive**, and **Dupleix was recalled**.
xa: **Godeheu**, Dupleix's successor, made this peace.
Failure: the **Seven Years' War** broke out before England + France **ratified** it.
⚠ The Second war was **not** ended by the **Treaty of Yandabo** (First Anglo-Burmese War, **1826**).

162.s: Which development occurred before England and France ratified the Treaty of Pondicherry?
o: The Seven Years' War broke out, leading to the Third Carnatic War
Dupleix was appointed Governor of Mughal territory
162.x: The Seven Years' War broke out before the treaty was ratified by England and France, thereby beginning the Third Carnatic War.
162.tq: Place the outbreak of the Seven Years' War between the treaty and its ratification.
xs: The **Seven Years' War** broke out before ratification, starting the **Third Carnatic War** — option **(2)**.
So the Third war began **before the Treaty of Pondicherry could be ratified**.
**Forde** took Machilipatnam only in **1759**, years later.
xa: Third war: **1756-63** (UPSC gives **1758-63**), ended by the **Treaty of Paris (1763)**.
Treaty of Pondicherry terms: **non-interference** in Indian princes' quarrels; existing possessions kept.

162.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Treaty of Paris
B. Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle
C. Treaty of Pondicherry
D. Capture of Madras
162.x: Madras was captured in 1746, the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle was signed in 1748, the Treaty of Pondicherry followed in 1754, and the Treaty of Paris was concluded in 1763.
162.tq: Fix the earliest event first and then arrange the treaties by date.
xs: The order is **D, B, C, A** — option **(1)**.
D: capture of **Madras (1746)** by La Bourdonnais's fleet.
B: **Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle** (**18 Sep 1748**); C: **Treaty of Pondicherry (1754)**; A: **Treaty of Paris (1763)**.
xa: Aix-la-Chapelle returned **Madras to the English** in exchange for **Louisburg** (North America).
Treaty of Paris also ended the **Seven Years' War**.

162.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Third Carnatic War — decisive British victory
First Carnatic War — permanent British political supremacy in India
162.x: The First Carnatic War was politically inconclusive and did not establish permanent British political supremacy. The other three pairs correctly state the results of the respective wars.
162.tq: Reject the exaggerated finality attached to the result of the First Carnatic War.
xs: "**First Carnatic War — permanent British political supremacy**" is NOT correctly matched — option **(3)**.
The First war ended with **Madras restored to the English** in exchange for **Louisburg** — a return to the old position, not supremacy.
Correct pairs: Second war — **Dupleix recalled**; Third war — **decisive British victory** (Treaty of Paris).
xa: First war: **1746-48**, an extension of the **War of Austrian Succession**.
First war participants: **British vs French**, with Nawab **Anwaruddin** on the English side.

162.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Carnatic War)
 a. First Carnatic War
 b. Second Carnatic War
 c. Third Carnatic War
List-II (Period)
 i. 1756–1763
 ii. 1746–1748
 iii. 1749–1754

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
162.x: The First, Second and Third Carnatic Wars respectively occurred during 1746–48, 1749–54 and 1756–63.
162.tq: Start from the sure period-war pair and eliminate the remaining codes.
xs: Treaties: **Aix-la-Chapelle (1748)**, **Pondicherry (1754)**, **Paris (1763)**.
xa: Third war dates: UPSC gives **1758-63**.
European context: First = **War of Austrian Succession**; Third = **Seven Years' War**; Second = none.

162.s: The First Carnatic War was primarily
o: an extension of the Seven Years’ War
an extension of the War of Austrian Succession in Europe
