165.tq: Test the contrast between humanitarian response and continued fiscal extraction.
xs: The Company gave **little or no relief** and **revenue collection continued** — option **(1)**.
Revenue was **squeezed even as famine spread**.
xa: This **hurt the Company's reputation** + **increased local opposition**.
Deaths: about **10 million** (UPSC notes); "**about two million lives**" (APP); textbook: about **one-third**.

165.s: The Bengal Famine of 1770 is directly linked, as cause and effect, with which arrangement?
165.x: The famine came under the Dual Government (1765-72), when the Company held revenue power without responsibility and kept squeezing revenue as the famine spread. The Permanent Settlement (1793), Subsidiary Alliance (1798) and Ryotwari came later.
165.tq: 1770 famine <-> Dual Government
xs: The **1770** famine is a direct **cause-effect** of the **Dual Government** — option **(3)**.
The Dual Government (**1765-72**) gave "**power without responsibility**"; revenue was **squeezed** as famine spread.
xa: Verdict on the Dual Government: "**a sham**" → economic ruin of Bengal.
Governor at the time: **John Cartier**.

165.s:
Consider the following statements about the steps taken by Warren Hastings after abolishing the Dual Government in 1772:
1. The treasury was shifted from Murshidabad to Calcutta.
2. The annual payment of ₹26 lakh to Shah Alam II was continued.
3. Allahabad and Kora were taken back from Shah Alam II and sold to the Nawab of Awadh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
165.x: Statement 1 is correct: the treasury moved from Murshidabad to Calcutta. Statement 2 is wrong: Hastings stopped the ₹26 lakh payment to Shah Alam II. Statement 3 is correct: Allahabad and Kora were taken back and sold to the Nawab of Awadh. So only 1 and 3 are correct; options with 2 are wrong.
165.tq: Hastings 'tore the mask' of Mughal sovereignty, so anything that keeps paying the Emperor is the false statement.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: the treasury moved **Murshidabad → Calcutta**.
Statement 2 wrong: Hastings **stopped** the **₹26 lakh** payment to **Shah Alam II**.
Statement 3 correct: **Allahabad** and **Kora** were taken back and **sold to the Nawab of Awadh**.
xa: Revenue was now collected **directly through Company servants**.
Hastings = **last Governor of Bengal (1772-73)**, **first Governor-General (1773)**.

165.s: Which combination correctly identifies the principal causes of the Sanyasi-Fakir Revolt?
o: The famine of 1770, Company insensitivity and restrictions on pilgrims
The Subsidiary Alliance, the Doctrine of Lapse and missionary education
The Carnatic Wars, salt taxation and the Ilbert Bill
The Permanent Settlement, the Revolt of 1857 and railway construction
165.x: The revolt was caused by the famine of 1770, Company insensitivity and restrictions on pilgrims visiting holy places.
165.tq: Group the causes of a revolt and reject causes belonging to later periods.
xs: Causes: the **famine of 1770**, **Company insensitivity** and **restrictions on pilgrims** — option **(1)**.
The other options list later policies unrelated to this revolt in the notes.
xa: **Sanyasi (Fakir) Revolt** = **1763-1800**.
Leaders: **Majnum Shah, Bhawani Pathak, Devi Chaudhurani**.

165.s: Which one of the following was NOT associated with the leadership of the Sanyasi-Fakir Revolt?
165.x: Majnum Shah, Bhawani Pathak and Devi Chaudhurani were associated with the revolt; Shah Alam II was not a leader of it.
165.tq: Find the unrelated historical figure among the revolt’s named leaders.
xs: **Shah Alam II** was not a leader of the revolt — option **(4)**.
He was the **Mughal Emperor** who granted the **Diwani (1765)**.
Leaders: **Majnum Shah, Bhawani Pathak, Devi Chaudhurani**.
xa: Revolt period: **1763-1800**.
Shah Alam II lost the **₹26 lakh** payment in **1772**.

165.s:
Consider the following statements about Anandamath:
1. It was written by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay and published in 1882.
2. It is set against the background of the Revolt of 1857.
3. It contains the song Vande Mataram.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
165.x: Statement 1 is correct: Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay, 1882. Statement 2 is wrong: the novel is set against the Bengal Famine of 1770 and the Sanyasi revolt, not 1857. Statement 3 is correct: it contains Vande Mataram. So 1 and 3 only.
165.tq: Anandamath = Sanyasis + 1770 famine; 1857 is the classic distractor.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: **Anandamath** by **Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay**, **1882**.
Statement 2 wrong: it is set against the **1770 famine + Sanyasi revolt**, not 1857.
Statement 3: it contains **Vande Mataram**.
xa: Sanyasi revolt leaders include **Bhawani Pathak** and **Devi Chaudhurani**.
Revolt period: **1763-1800**.

165.s:
Assertion (A): The origins of the drain of wealth and deindustrialisation in India are traced by scholars to the Dual Government.
Reason (R): The Dual Government marked the first formal Company control of revenue in India.

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
165.x: Both statements are true, and the Company's formal control over revenue provides the basis for tracing the drain of wealth and deindustrialisation to the arrangement.
165.tq: Test whether the stated revenue-control feature explains the broader economic consequence.
xs: **Both A and R are true** and **R is the correct explanation of A** — option **(1)**.
R: the Dual Government was the **first formal Company control of revenue** in India.
A: scholars trace the **drain of wealth** + **deindustrialisation** to it.
xa: Wealth drain = R.P. Dutt's **Mercantilist phase (1757-1813)**.
**Weavers** forced to sell cheap → **handicrafts declined**.

165.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the famines mentioned in relation to Bengal and Andhra:
1. The Guntur or Dokkala famine occurred in 1832–33 and caused about two lakh deaths.
2. The Kurnool famine occurred in 1866.
3. Both these Andhra famines were the same event as the Bengal Famine of 1770.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
165.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the Guntur famine of 1832–33 and the Kurnool famine of 1866 were separate Andhra famines, distinct from the Bengal Famine of 1770.
165.tq: Use dates and location to separate similar famine references and reject the conflation of distinct events.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: **Guntur (Dokkala) famine 1832-33** — about **2 lakh** deaths.
Statement 2: **Kurnool famine of 1866**.
Statement 3 wrong: Andhra famines were **separate** from the **1770** Bengal famine.
xa: The 1770 famine hit **Bengal and Bihar** (lower Gangetic plain).
Governor in 1770: **John Cartier**.

165.s: Which of the following correctly describes Warren Hastings in relation to Bengal administration?
o: He was the first Governor of Bengal in 1773 and the last Governor-General in 1774.
He was the first Governor of Bengal in 1758 and the last Governor in 1772–73.
He was the first Governor-General of Bengal in 1758 and the first Viceroy in 1773.
He was the last Governor of Bengal in 1772–73 and the first Governor-General of Bengal in 1773.
165.x: Warren Hastings was the last Governor of Bengal from 1772 to 1773 and became the first Governor-General of Bengal in 1773.
165.tq: Discriminate between closely related offices and dates by tracking the change from Governor to Governor-General.
xs: **Warren Hastings** was the **last Governor of Bengal (1772-73)** and **first Governor-General of Bengal (1773)** — option **(4)**.
The **first Governor of Bengal** was **Clive** (**1758**).
xa: Hastings **abolished** the Dual Government in **1772**.
⚠ **Clive** enforced (**1765**); **Hastings** abolished (**1772**).

166.s:
Consider the following statements about the rise of Haidar Ali:
1. He rose to prominence under the Wodeyar kingdom of Mysore.
2. He became Faujdar of Dindigul in 1755 under the minister Nanjaraja.
3. He became the de facto ruler of Mysore in 1782.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
166.x: Statement 1 is correct: he rose under the Wodeyars. Statement 2 is correct: Faujdar of Dindigul in 1755 under Nanjaraja. Statement 3 is wrong: he became de facto ruler in 1761, not 1782. So 1 and 2 only; '1 only' misses statement 2, and options with 3 are wrong.
166.tq: Haidar's timeline: 1755 Dindigul, 1761 de facto ruler.
xs: Only statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: **Haidar Ali** rose under the **Wodeyar** kingdom of Mysore.
Statement 2: he became **Faujdar of Dindigul in 1755** under minister **Nanjaraja**.
Statement 3 wrong: he became **de facto ruler** in **1761**, not 1782.
xa: He adopted **Western techniques** and set up a **modern arsenal at Dindigul** with French help.
In the 1st war he **won over the Marathas** and **detached the Nizam** from the British.

166.s: Which development at Dindigul is associated with Haidar Ali?
o: A naval dockyard was established under British supervision.
A modern arsenal was established with French help.
The Ryotwari system was first introduced by Read and Munro.
A Jacobin Club was established with Maratha help.
166.x: Haidar Ali adopted Western military techniques and established a modern arsenal at Dindigul with French help.
166.tq: Use the military institution and foreign assistance as the identifying pair.
xs: Haidar Ali set up a **modern arsenal at Dindigul** with **French help** — option **(2)**.
**Ryotwari** began in the **Bara Mahal** (Read and Munro); the **Jacobin Club** was Tipu's, at **Seringapatam (1797)**.
xa: Haidar was **Faujdar of Dindigul in 1755**.
⚠ **Dindigul** arsenal = Haidar; **French embassy + navy + Jacobin Club** = Tipu.

166.s: During the First Anglo-Mysore War, Haidar Ali weakened the British position by
o: winning over the Marathas and detaching the Nizam from the British
restoring the Wodeyar dynasty to the Madras Presidency
forming a permanent alliance with Lord Cornwallis
166.x: Haidar Ali used diplomacy to win over the Marathas and detach the Nizam from the British during the First Anglo-Mysore War.
166.tq: Identify the diplomatic combination that changed the balance of the war.
xs: Haidar **won over the Marathas** and **detached the Nizam** from the British — option **(2)**.
The **Wodeyar** restoration came in **1799**; **Cornwallis** belongs to the **Third** war.
xa: The Nizam had first **joined the British**, and the Marathas had **joined against Haidar** (UPSC).
The war ended with the **Treaty of Madras (1769)** with Haidar.

166.s: Which ruler of Sivaganga took Haidar Ali's help to recover her kingdom and is called the first queen to wage war against the British?
166.x: Velu Nachiyar of Sivaganga recovered her kingdom with Haidar Ali's help and is called the first queen to wage war against the British (APPSC-G1 2022). Chennamma (Kittur) and Lakshmibai (Jhansi) fought later, and Durgavati fought the Mughals.
166.tq: Velu Nachiyar + Haidar Ali
xs: **Velu Nachiyar** of **Sivaganga** took Haidar Ali's help to recover her kingdom — option **(2)**.
She is called the **first queen to wage war against the British** (**APPSC-G1 2022** key).
xa: Haidar Ali was **de facto ruler** of Mysore from **1761**.
Haidar's allies-and-diplomacy also turned the **Marathas** and **Nizam** in the 1st war.

166.s:
Consider the following statements about Tipu Sultan's association with the Jacobin Club:
1. It was established at Seringapatam in 1797.
2. Tipu Sultan became a member of the club.
3. Tipu Sultan called himself ‘Citizen Tipu’.
4. A Tree of Liberty was planted there.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
166.x: All four statements are correct. Tipu Sultan supported the Jacobin Club at Seringapatam, became a member, used the title ‘Citizen Tipu’ and planted a Tree of Liberty.
166.tq: Confirm the complete cluster of associated details before selecting the inclusive option.
xs: All four statements are correct — **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(4)**.
Tipu helped French soldiers set up a **Jacobin Club at Seringapatam (1797)** and **became a member**.
He called himself **"Citizen Tipu"** and planted a **Tree of Liberty**.
xa: Other titles: **"Tiger of Mysore"**, **Padshah**.
He sent ambassadors to **France** and built a **navy**.

166.s: Which one of the following statements about Tipu Sultan is NOT correct?
o: He supported the establishment of a Jacobin Club at Seringapatam.
He sent envoys to Turkey, Afghanistan and Mauritius.
He discontinued the use of war rockets in military operations.
166.x: Tipu Sultan used war rockets; he did not discontinue their use. The other three statements are correct.
166.tq: Find the statement that reverses a documented military or administrative measure.
xs: "He **discontinued** the use of **war rockets**" is NOT correct — Tipu **used** war rockets — option **(3)**.
The rest are true: **Jacobin Club** at Seringapatam; envoys to **Turkey, Afghanistan, Mauritius**; **sericulture**.
xa: He also brought a **new calendar**, **coinage**, **weights and measures**.
He was killed on **4 May 1799** defending Seringapatam.

166.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
166.x: Tipu Sultan was associated with the titles ‘Tiger of Mysore’, ‘Citizen Tipu’ and ‘Padshah’. ‘Lion of Mysore’ is not among the stated titles.
166.tq: Find the look-alike title that does not belong to the stated set.
xs: "**Lion of Mysore — Tipu Sultan**" is NOT correctly matched — option **(1)**.
Tipu's titles: **"Tiger of Mysore"**, **"Citizen Tipu"** and **Padshah**.
xa: "Citizen Tipu" came from the **Jacobin Club at Seringapatam (1797)**.
His **Gumbaz** at Srirangapatna is the **mausoleum of Haidar and Tipu**.

166.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding monuments at Srirangapatna:

List-I (Monument)
 a. Daria Daulat Bagh
 b. Gumbaz
 c. Jamia Masjid

List-II (Description)
 i. Masjid-e-Ala
 ii. Mausoleum of Haidar Ali and Tipu Sultan
 iii. Summer palace containing war murals

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
166.x: Daria Daulat Bagh was a summer palace with war murals, the Gumbaz is the mausoleum of Haidar Ali and Tipu Sultan, and Jamia Masjid is also known as Masjid-e-Ala.
166.tq: Begin with the distinctive monument–description pair and use elimination for the remaining pairs.
xs: **a–iii, b–ii, c–i** — option **(1)**.
**Daria Daulat Bagh** — **summer palace with war murals**.
**Gumbaz** — **mausoleum of Haidar and Tipu**; **Jamia Masjid** — **Masjid-e-Ala**.
xa: Srirangapatna = **Seringapatam**, Tipu's capital.
Tipu was killed there on **4 May 1799**.

166.s: Which Mysore ruler sent ambassadors to France for European technology and used it to build a navy?
166.x: Tipu Sultan sent ambassadors to France and built a navy (APPSC-G1 2018 key). Statement questions on the 'French embassy + navy' point to Tipu, not Haidar Ali or the Wodeyars.
166.tq: French embassy + navy = Tipu
xs: **Tipu Sultan** sent ambassadors to **France** and built a **navy** — option **(3)**.
This is the **APPSC-G1 2018** key; "French embassy + navy" points to Tipu, **not Haidar or the Wodeyars**.
xa: **Haidar**'s French link was the **arsenal at Dindigul**.
**Krishnaraja Wodeyar III** was the **boy ruler** restored in **1799**.

166.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Pollilur — Eyre Coote defeated Haidar Ali
Porto Novo — Haidar Ali and Tipu defeated Colonel Baillie
166.x: Cornwallis's coalition won at Seringapatam in 1792 and Tipu sued for peace. A and B swap the battles: Pollilur (1780) was Haidar and Tipu's defeat of Baillie, Porto Novo (1781) was Eyre Coote's win over Haidar; D is wrong because the British won in 1799 and Tipu was killed.
166.tq: Check the victor first, then verify the year and war.
xs: **Seringapatam (1792)** — **Cornwallis's coalition won** — option **(3)**.
**Pollilur (1780)**: Haidar and Tipu beat **Col. Baillie**; **Porto Novo (1781)**: **Eyre Coote** beat Haidar — options (1) and (2) swap them.
**Seringapatam (1799)**: the **British won** and Tipu was killed.
xa: After 1792 Tipu **sued for peace** — Treaty of Seringapatam.
Pollilur and Porto Novo were **2nd war** battles.

166.s: In 1790, Tipu Sultan defeated the British army commanded by
166.x: In 1790, Tipu Sultan defeated the British army under General Meadows during the Third Anglo-Mysore War.
166.tq: Avoid swapping commanders from different battles and years.
xs: In **1790** Tipu defeated the British army under **General Meadows** — option **(1)**.
**Col. Baillie** was beaten at **Pollilur (1780)**; **Hector Munro** and **Sir Eyre Coote** were early-wars commanders.
xa: In **1791** **Cornwallis** took **Bangalore (March 1791)** via **Ambur** and **Vellore**.
The 3rd war ended with Cornwallis's coalition win at **Seringapatam (1792)**.

166.s:
Which of the following statements about British commanders in the early Anglo-Mysore Wars is correct?
1. Hector Munro was among the British commanders.
2. Sir Eyre Coote was among the British commanders.
3. Thomas Munro served under both Hector Munro and Sir Eyre Coote.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
166.x: Hector Munro and Sir Eyre Coote were British commanders in the early wars, and Thomas Munro served under both of them.
166.tq: Verify each person’s role before choosing the comprehensive combination.
xs: All three statements are correct — **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
**Hector Munro** and **Sir Eyre Coote** were early-wars commanders.
**Thomas Munro** **served under both**.
xa: ⚠ Don't confuse **Hector Munro** (commander) with **Thomas Munro**.
**Eyre Coote** defeated Haidar at **Porto Novo (1781)**.

166.s: Under the Treaty of Seringapatam of 1792, Tipu Sultan was required to
o: transfer his capital to Bangalore and join the Maratha confederacy
surrender the whole of Mysore and abdicate permanently
cede about half his territory, pay ₹3 crore and give two sons as hostages
cede Dindigul alone and pay no indemnity
166.x: Tipu Sultan ceded about half his territory, paid a war indemnity of ₹3 crore and gave two sons as hostages under the Treaty of Seringapatam.
166.tq: Combine the territorial, financial and hostage terms of the treaty.
xs: Tipu ceded about **half his territory**, paid **₹3 crore** and gave **two sons as hostages** — option **(3)**.
**Half the indemnity** was paid at once; the sons returned after the rest was paid.
xa: **Nizam** gained from the **Krishna to beyond the Pennar**; **Marathas** around the **Tungabhadra**.
**British** gained **Malabar, Coorg, Dindigul and the Bara Mahal**.

166.s:
Match the gainers under the Treaty of Seringapatam (1792) with their shares:
List-I (Gainer)
a. Nizam
b. Marathas
c. British
List-II (Share)
i. Malabar, Coorg (as protectorate), Dindigul and the Bara Mahal
ii. Areas from the Krishna to beyond the Pennar
iii. Areas around the Tungabhadra and its tributaries
Select the correct code:
166.x: The Nizam got the areas from the Krishna to beyond the Pennar (ii), the Marathas got the areas around the Tungabhadra (iii), and the British got Malabar, Coorg, Dindigul and the Bara Mahal (i). Option 2 swaps the Nizam and the Marathas; options 3 and 4 give the British share to an Indian ally.
166.tq: Nizam = Krishna-Pennar (Rayalaseema), Marathas = Tungabhadra, British = coast and Bara Mahal.
xs: **a–ii, b–iii, c–i** — option **(1)**.
**Nizam** — **Krishna to beyond the Pennar**; **Marathas** — around the **Tungabhadra** and tributaries.
**British** — **Malabar, Coorg (protectorate), Dindigul, Bara Mahal**.
xa: The Nizam's share included half of **Rayalaseema**: **Bellary, Gurramkonda, Gandikota, Kambham, Kadapa**.
**Bara Mahal** (Salem region) is where **Read and Munro** began **Ryotwari**.

166.s: The Bara Mahal, obtained by the British after the Treaty of Seringapatam, is associated with the beginning of the Ryotwari system by
166.x: The Bara Mahal, identified with the Salem region, was where Read and Thomas Munro began the Ryotwari system.
166.tq: Match the administrative experiment with the place and officials associated with it.
xs: **Read and Munro** began the **Ryotwari** system in the **Bara Mahal** — option **(4)**.
Bara Mahal = **Salem region**, gained by the **British** in **1792**.
xa: **Arthur Wellesley** served in the **1799** campaign; **Cornwallis** won the **3rd war**.
British share in 1792 also included **Malabar**, **Coorg** and **Dindigul**.

166.s: On which date was Tipu Sultan killed while defending Seringapatam?
166.x: Tipu Sultan was killed on 4 May 1799 while defending Seringapatam during the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War.
166.tq: Distinguish the exact date of the event from the year of the earlier treaty.
xs: Tipu was killed on **4 May 1799** defending **Seringapatam** — option **(3)**.
**1792** was the **Treaty of Seringapatam**; **1800** the **Ceded Districts**.
xa: This was the **4th war**; the **British won**.
**Arthur Wellesley** (later **Duke of Wellington**) served in this campaign.

166.s:
Which statement correctly describes the settlement of Mysore after the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War?
1. Mysore was partitioned.
2. The Hindu Wodeyar dynasty was restored.
3. Krishnaraja Wodeyar III was placed on the throne as a boy ruler.
4. Mysore was brought under a Subsidiary Alliance.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
166.x: After the Fourth War, Mysore was partitioned, the Hindu Wodeyar dynasty was restored, the boy ruler Krishnaraja Wodeyar III was installed, and the state was placed under a Subsidiary Alliance.
166.tq: Treat the post-war settlement as a linked set of political consequences.
xs: All four are correct — **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(4)**.
Mysore was **partitioned**; the Hindu **Wodeyar** dynasty was **restored**.
Boy ruler **Krishnaraja Wodeyar III** was placed under a **Subsidiary Alliance**.
xa: The Nizam's share → handed to the Company in **1800** as the **Ceded Districts**.
The 4th war **removed the French-backed threat**.

166.s: The Nizam's share of Mysore lands after the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War later became known as the
166.x: The Nizam's share of Mysore lands became known as the Ceded Districts.
166.tq: Identify the later administrative name given to the territorial transfer.
xs: The Nizam's share of Mysore lands became the **Ceded Districts** — option **(2)**.
**Bara Mahal** was a **British** gain of **1792**.
xa: They were handed to the Company in **1800** to pay for the **subsidiary force**.
Ceded Districts: **Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur, Bellary**.

166.s: Which one of the following best describes the position of the Nizam during the Second Anglo-Mysore War?
o: He supported Haidar Ali without interruption until the Treaty of Salbai.
He was part of an anti-British confederacy but was later bought off.
He remained a subsidiary ally of the British from 1798.
He formed a grand alliance with the British throughout the war.
166.x: During the Second Anglo-Mysore War, the Nizam was associated with an anti-British confederacy but was later bought off.
166.tq: Use the specific alliance description to distinguish the Second War from the other Anglo-Mysore Wars.
xs: In the 2nd war the Nizam was in an **anti-British confederacy**, later **bought off** — option **(2)**.
He became a **subsidiary ally** only **since 1798** (4th war); the **grand alliance** was the **3rd** war.
xa: The **Marathas** made peace with the British at **Salbai 1782**.
2nd war battles: **Pollilur (1780)**, **Porto Novo (1781)**; ended by **Mangalore (1784)**.

166.s: During which Anglo-Mysore War did both the Nizam and the Marathas join the British in a grand alliance?
166.x: Both the Nizam and the Marathas were with the British in the Third Anglo-Mysore War, forming part of the grand alliance.
166.tq: Use the common position of two powers to distinguish the Third War from the other wars.
xs: Both the Nizam and the Marathas were **with the British** in the **Third** war (grand alliance) — option **(1)**.
⚠ Only the **Third** war had both on the British side.
xa: The 3rd war **ended Tipu's supremacy in the south**.
It closed with the **Treaty of Seringapatam (1792)**.

166.s:
Consider the following statements about the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War:
1. The Nizam was a subsidiary ally of the British from 1798.
2. The Marathas were recorded as neutral in the war.
3. Both the Nizam and the Marathas formed a grand alliance with the British in this war.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
166.x: The Nizam was a British subsidiary ally from 1798 and the Marathas were neutral. The statement that both formed a grand alliance in the Fourth War is incorrect.
166.tq: Reject the statement that transfers the Third War alliance pattern to the Fourth War.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: the Nizam was a **subsidiary ally since 1798**.
Statement 2: the Marathas were **neutral** (UPSC notes say they "supported" the British).
Statement 3 wrong: the **grand alliance** of both was in the **Third** war.
xa: The 4th war ended with Tipu killed on **4 May 1799**.
Mysore was **partitioned** and put under a **Subsidiary Alliance**.

166.s: The Third Anglo-Mysore War is significant because it
o: made the Marathas neutral in all subsequent wars.
ended Tipu Sultan's supremacy in southern India.
brought the Ceded Districts directly under the British in 1800.
established the French-backed threat in Mysore.
166.x: The Third Anglo-Mysore War ended Tipu Sultan's supremacy in the south. The Ceded Districts came to the British in 1800 as a consequence of the Mysore wars, not as the stated significance of the Third War alone.
166.tq: Separate the significance of the Third War from consequences associated with the Fourth War and 1800 settlement.
xs: The **Third war** **ended Tipu's supremacy in the south** — option **(2)**.
The **Ceded Districts (1800)** and removal of the **French-backed threat** belong to the **Fourth** war.
xa: Tipu ceded about **half his territory** in **1792**.
Cornwallis took **Bangalore (March 1791)**.

166.s: The Fourth Anglo-Mysore War had which one of the following broader consequences?
o: It ended all British relations with the Nizam.
It restored Tipu Sultan's supremacy in southern India.
It transferred Mysore and Andhra to the Marathas.
It removed the French-backed threat and brought Mysore and Andhra under Company control.
166.x: The Fourth Anglo-Mysore War removed the French-backed threat and brought Mysore and Andhra, through the Ceded Districts, under the Company.
166.tq: Link the war with its two stated strategic consequences instead of focusing on only one region.
xs: The Fourth war **removed the French-backed threat** and brought **Mysore + Andhra** under the Company — option **(4)**.
Andhra came via the **Ceded Districts**; the Nizam stayed a **British ally**.
xa: Tipu was killed on **4 May 1799**; **Wodeyar** rule restored.
Ceded Districts: **Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur, Bellary** (**1800**).

166.s: Which of the following districts constituted the Ceded Districts that came to the British in 1800 as a direct result of the Mysore Wars?
o: Chittoor, East Godavari, West Godavari and Visakhapatnam
166.x: The Ceded Districts were Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur and Bellary. They came to the British in 1800 as a direct result of the Mysore Wars.
166.tq: Test the complete district list and avoid substituting neighbouring Andhra or Telangana districts.
xs: The **Ceded Districts** were **Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur, Bellary** — option **(2)**.
They came to the British in **1800** as a **direct result of the Mysore wars**.
xa: They were the Nizam's share of Mysore lands, handed over to pay for the **subsidiary force**.
In **1792** the Nizam's share had included **Bellary, Gurramkonda, Gandikota, Kambham, Kadapa**.

166.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Treaties associated with the Anglo-Mysore Wars:
1. The Treaty of Madras was concluded in 1769.
2. The Treaty of Mangalore was concluded in 1784.
3. The Treaty of Madras was made with Tipu Sultan, whereas the Treaty of Mangalore was made with Haidar Ali.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
166.x: The Treaty of Madras was concluded in 1769 and the Treaty of Mangalore in 1784. Statement 3 reverses the parties: the former was made with Haidar Ali and the latter with Tipu Sultan.
166.tq: Separate the two similarly named treaties by checking both their years and the ruler associated with each.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: **Treaty of Madras (1769)**; Statement 2: **Treaty of Mangalore (1784)**.
Statement 3 wrong: Madras was **with Haidar**, Mangalore **with Tipu**.
xa: 3rd war → **Treaty of Seringapatam (1792)**.
⚠ Trap: **Madras (1769)** = Haidar vs **Mangalore (1784)** = Tipu.

166.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the First Anglo-Mysore War:
I. Haidar Ali led Mysore in the war.
II. Haidar Ali was victorious in the war.
III. The Treaty of Madras was concluded in 1769.
IV. The Treaty of Madras was associated with the First Anglo-Mysore War.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
166.x: All four are correct: Haidar Ali led Mysore, came out on top near Madras, and the war ended with the Treaty of Madras in 1769.
166.tq: Check each statement separately.
n: Haidar Ali led Mysore in the First Anglo-Mysore War. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
Haidar Ali was victorious in the First Anglo-Mysore War. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
The Treaty of Madras was concluded in 1769. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
xs: All four, **I, II, III and IV**, are correct — option **(3)**.
**Haidar Ali** led Mysore in the **First Anglo-Mysore War** (**1767 to 1769**) and was **victorious**.
It ended with the **Treaty of Madras** in **1769**.
xa: ⚠ **Treaty of Madras (1769)** = with Haidar; **Treaty of Mangalore (1784)** = with Tipu.
Haidar won over the **Marathas** and detached the **Nizam** from the British.
Haidar became **de facto ruler** in **1761**.

166.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Battle of Pollilur:
Statement A: Haidar Ali and Tipu Sultan fought against Colonel Baillie.
Statement B: Haidar Ali and Tipu Sultan defeated Colonel Baillie.
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
166.x: Both are true: at Pollilur (1780) Haidar Ali and Tipu Sultan fought and routed Colonel Baillie's force.
166.tq: Check each statement separately.
n: The Battle of Pollilur was fought between Haidar Ali and Tipu Sultan on one side and Colonel Baillie on the other. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
Colonel Baillie was defeated in the Battle of Pollilur. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
xs: **Both Statement A and Statement B are true** — option **(1)**.
At **Pollilur** (**10 September 1780**) **Haidar Ali** and **Tipu Sultan** fought **Colonel Baillie**.
They **defeated** him — a **major British defeat**.
xa: Pollilur was part of the **Second Anglo-Mysore War** (**1780 to 1784**).
**Porto Novo** (**July 1781**) reversed it: **Eyre Coote** defeated Haidar.
Tipu was called the **"Tiger of Mysore"**.

166.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Second Anglo-Mysore War:
I. It took place from 1780 to 1784.
II. The British fought against Mysore.
III. Haidar Ali and Tipu Sultan were associated with the war.
IV. It was a major Anglo-Mysore conflict.
V. Haidar Ali allied with the Nizam during the war.
VI. Haidar Ali allied with the Marathas during the war.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
o: I, II, III and IV only
I, II, III, IV, V and VI
II, III, IV, V and VI only
I, II, IV, V and VI only
166.x: All six are correct: the Second Anglo-Mysore War (1780–84) was a major British–Mysore conflict under Haidar Ali and Tipu, begun with Haidar allied to the Nizam and the Marathas.
166.tq: Check each statement separately.
n: The Second Anglo-Mysore War was fought from 1780 to 1784. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
The Second Anglo-Mysore War was fought between the British and Mysore. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
Haidar Ali and Tipu Sultan were associated with the Second Anglo-Mysore War. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
The Second Anglo-Mysore War was a major Anglo-Mysore conflict. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
Haidar Ali allied with the Nizam and the Marathas during the Second Anglo-Mysore War. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
xs: All six, **I, II, III, IV, V and VI**, are correct — option **(2)**.
The **Second Anglo-Mysore War** (**1780 to 1784**) was a **major** conflict between the **British** and **Mysore**.
It involved **Haidar Ali** and **Tipu Sultan**.
**Haidar Ali allied** with the **Nizam** and the **Marathas**.
xa: ⚠ Sources differ: other notes say the Nizam was later bought off and the Marathas made peace with the British at **Salbai 1782**.
**Pollilur** (**1780**) and **Porto Novo** (**1781**) were its battles.
It ended with the **Treaty of Mangalore** (**1784**).

166.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Battle of Porto Novo:
I. It took place in July 1781.
II. Haidar Ali fought against Sir Eyre Coote.
III. Sir Eyre Coote led the British side.
IV. The British achieved victory.
V. It was part of the Second Anglo-Mysore War.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
o: I, II, III, IV and V
I, III, IV and V only
166.x: All five are correct: at Porto Novo (July 1781) Sir Eyre Coote led the British to victory over Haidar Ali in the Second Anglo-Mysore War.
166.tq: Check each statement separately.
n: The Battle of Porto Novo was fought in July 1781. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
The Battle of Porto Novo was fought between Sir Eyre Coote and Haidar Ali. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
Sir Eyre Coote led the British side in the Battle of Porto Novo. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
The British won the Battle of Porto Novo. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
The Battle of Porto Novo was part of the Second Anglo-Mysore War. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
xs: All five, **I, II, III, IV and V**, are correct — option **(2)**.
**Porto Novo** was fought in **July 1781**.
**Sir Eyre Coote** led the British and **defeated Haidar Ali** — a British victory.
It was part of the **Second Anglo-Mysore War**.
xa: It reversed the British defeat at **Pollilur** (**1780**).
Coote later won **Wandiwash** against the French.
**Thomas Munro** served under both **Hector Munro** and **Eyre Coote**.

166.s:
Assertion (A): The Battle of Porto Novo reversed the result of the Battle of Pollilur.
Reason (R): Sir Eyre Coote defeated Haidar Ali in the Battle of Porto Novo.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
166.x: Both are true and R explains A: Coote's defeat of Haidar Ali at Porto Novo (1781) is exactly what reversed the British disaster at Pollilur (1780).
166.tq: Check whether R is the cause of A.
n: Sir Eyre Coote defeated Haidar Ali in the Battle of Porto Novo. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 74-76]
The Battle of Porto Novo reversed the result of the Battle of Pollilur. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 74-76]
xs: **Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A** — option **(1)**.
R: **Sir Eyre Coote** **defeated Haidar Ali** at **Porto Novo** (**July 1781**).
A: that victory **reversed** the British defeat at **Pollilur** (**1780**).
xa: At Pollilur Haidar and Tipu had defeated **Colonel Baillie**.
Both battles belong to the **Second Anglo-Mysore War**.
Third war: Tipu defeated **General Meadows** (**1790**); **Cornwallis** took **Bangalore** (**March 1791**).

167.s: Which event most directly explains why Lord Wellesley compelled Nizam Ali Khan to accept the Subsidiary Alliance in 1798?
o: The Nizam's alliance with Holkar during the Second Maratha War
The Nizam's refusal to lease the Northern Circars in 1766
The Nizam's defeat by the Marathas at Kharda and his reliance on French troops under Raymond
The Nizam's annexation of Mysore after the Fourth Mysore War
167.x: After the defeat at Kharda in 1795, Nizam Ali Khan blamed Sir John Shore's neutrality, dismissed his British battalions and relied on French troops under Raymond. Wellesley used this situation to force the alliance.
167.tq: Link the political cause, foreign military influence and British response.
xs: After defeat by the Marathas at **Kharda (1795)**, the Nizam relied on **French troops under Raymond** — option **(3)**.
He blamed **Sir John Shore's neutrality** and **dismissed the British battalions**.
Resident **Kirkpatrick** reported the French battalions → **Wellesley** forced the **1798** alliance.
xa: The Subsidiary Alliance aimed to **keep the French out**.
**Holkar** resisted the system longest; the Nizam did not ally with him.

167.s:
Under the Subsidiary Alliance, the British Resident at Hyderabad primarily:
1. Controlled the Nizam's foreign relations.
2. Supervised the subsidiary force.
3. Exercised direct hereditary succession to the Nizam's throne.
Select the correct answer using the code below.
167.x: The Resident controlled the Nizam's foreign relations and supervised the subsidiary force. The Resident did not possess hereditary succession to the Nizam's throne.
167.tq: Identify the actual functions of the British Resident and reject an extreme unrelated power.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
The **British Resident** at Hyderabad **controlled the Nizam's foreign relations** and **supervised the subsidiary force**.
Statement 3 wrong: the Resident had no claim to the Nizam's throne.
xa: Resident **Kirkpatrick** built the Residency building, the **"Koti"**.
On **17 July 1857**, **Turrebaz Khan** attacked the Residency.

167.s: Which British Resident reported the presence of French battalions in the Nizam's forces during the 1790s and pressed him into the 1798 alliance?
167.x: Resident James Kirkpatrick reported the Nizam's French battalions in the 1790s and pushed him into the Subsidiary Alliance of 1798.
167.tq: Use the person–action association and distinguish the Resident from the military officer who repulsed the later attack.
xs: **(James) Kirkpatrick** reported the Nizam's French battalions in the **1790s** — option **(3)**.
**Wellesley** then forced the **1798** alliance on the Nizam.
**Calliaud** signed the **1766** treaty; **Davidson** repulsed the **1857** Residency attack.
xa: Kirkpatrick built the Residency, the **"Koti"**.
The French troops were commanded by **Raymond**.

167.s: Nizam Ali Khan (Asaf Jah II) shifted the capital of the Nizam's dominions in 1763 from:
167.x: Nizam Ali Khan moved the capital from Aurangabad to Hyderabad in 1763. Golconda and Bidar were earlier Deccan sultanate seats, and the move was towards Hyderabad, not away from it.
167.tq: 1763: Aurangabad -> Hyderabad
xs: Nizam Ali Khan moved the capital from **Aurangabad to Hyderabad** (**1763**) — option **(2)**.
Option (4) reverses the direction.
xa: **Secunderabad** cantonment is named after **Sikandar Jah** (Asaf Jah III).

167.s: The Treaty of Hyderabad of 1766 provided for the leasing of the Northern Circars to the British in return for
o: lands between the Krishna and the Pennar
a yearly payment of ₹9 lakh or military aid
a yearly payment of ₹7 lakh and the surrender of Guntur
the cession of Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur and Bellary
167.x: Under the 1766 Treaty of Hyderabad, the Northern Circars were leased to the British for military aid or an annual payment of ₹9 lakh.
167.tq: Separate the terms of the 1766 treaty from later territorial cessions.
xs: The **1766 Treaty of Hyderabad** leased the **Northern Circars** for **military aid or ₹9 lakh a year** — option **(2)**.
**₹7 lakh** was the **Guntur (1788)** figure; **Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur, Bellary** were ceded in **1800**.
xa: Envoy **Calliaud** signed it; **Kandregula Jogipanthulu** mediated.
⚠ **₹15 lakh** = proposed lease; **₹9 lakh** = **1766/1768**; **₹7 lakh** = Guntur.

167.s: Who granted the Northern Circars to the East India Company through a Mughal firman in 1765?
167.x: The Mughal firman granting the Circars to the East India Company was issued by Shah Alam II in 1765, though some sources date it to 1766.
167.tq: Identify the issuing authority directly, while distinguishing it from the later Nizam agreement.
xs: The **Farman of Shah Alam II** (**1765**), received by **Clive**, granted the Circars to the EIC — option **(3)**.
Some notes date the firman to **1766**.
xa: **Nizam Ali refused to accept it at first**.
Some notes put the firman payment at **₹20 lakh** a year.

167.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the transfer of the Northern Circars is correct?
o: Nizam Ali initially refused to accept the Mughal firman but agreed to lease the Circars in 1766.
The Nizam transferred the Circars only after the Battle of Padmanabham.
The Circars were leased by Salabat Jung in 1768 after the Treaty of Masulipatnam.
Nizam Ali accepted the Mughal firman immediately in 1765.
167.x: Nizam Ali initially refused to accept Shah Alam II's firman and agreed to lease the Circars in 1766.
167.tq: Separate the Mughal grant of 1765 from the Nizam's acceptance and lease arrangement of 1766.
xs: **Nizam Ali** at first **refused** the Mughal firman, then agreed to **lease the Circars** in **1766** — option **(1)**.
**Padmanabham** was **1794**; **Masulipatnam (1768)** only **confirmed** the arrangement.
**Salabat Jang**'s grant was in **1759** (Machilipatnam, Nizampatnam, Vakal Mannar).
xa: Circars handed over: **Mustafanagar (Kondapalli), Eluru, Rajamahendravaram, Srikakulam**.
CDX dates the acquisition to **1768**.

167.s:
Consider the following events:
A. Treaty of Masulipatnam confirmed the arrangement
B. Salabat Jung gave Machilipatnam and other territories to the British
C. Nizam Ali agreed to lease the Circars
D. Guntur was handed over after the death of Basalat Jung
Which one of the following is the correct chronological order?
167.x: The correct sequence is 1759, 1766, 1768 and 1788: B, C, A, D.
167.tq: Fix the earliest territorial grant first and then arrange the lease, confirmation and Guntur transfer.
xs: The order is **B, C, A, D** — option **(1)**.
**1759**: Salabat Jang's grant → **1766**: Nizam Ali leased the Circars.
**1768**: **Masulipatnam** confirmed it → **1788**: **Guntur** handed over.
xa: **Basalat Jung** died in **1782**; Guntur came after **6 years of talks**.
Guntur's handover completed the **Northern Circars**.

167.s:
Consider the following statements about Kandregula Jogipantulu, the Andhra negotiator of the Circar lease:
1. He used the pay mutiny of the Nizam's army at Gollapudi to propose leasing the Circars at ₹15 lakh a year.
2. The final 1766 treaty kept the amount at ₹15 lakh a year.
3. Nizam Ali made him Majumdar of Rajamahendravaram, and the British gave him the title 'Raja Bahadur'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
167.x: Statement 1 is correct: he used the Gollapudi pay mutiny to propose ₹15 lakh. Statement 2 is wrong: the final 1766 treaty fixed ₹9 lakh. Statement 3 is correct: Majumdar of Rajamahendravaram (from the Nizam) and 'Raja Bahadur' (from the British). So 1 and 3 only.
167.tq: Proposal 15 lakh, final 9 lakh; Nizam gave the post, British gave the title.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: he used the **pay mutiny** at **Gollapudi** to propose **₹15 lakh** a year.
Statement 2 wrong: the final **1766** treaty fixed **₹9 lakh**.
Statement 3: **Majumdar of Rajamahendravaram** (Nizam Ali) and **"Raja Bahadur"** (British).
xa: This is the **APPSC G2 2019** key.
⚠ **₹15 lakh** proposed; **₹9 lakh** final; **₹7 lakh** = Guntur (**1788**).

167.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the Circars handed over in 1766?
167.x: Mustafanagar, Eluru, Rajamahendravaram and Srikakulam were among the Circars handed over in 1766. Kurnool formed part of the Ceded Districts transferred in 1800.
167.tq: Find the item belonging to the later Ceded Districts transfer rather than the 1766 Circars.
xs: **Kurnool** was not one of the 1766 Circars — option **(1)**.
The **1766** Circars: **Mustafanagar (Kondapalli), Eluru, Rajamahendravaram, Srikakulam**.
Kurnool was one of the **Ceded Districts** (**1800**).
xa: The 1766 lease was for **military aid or ₹9 lakh** a year.
**Guntur** (**Kondaveedu / Murtazanagar**) was the **5th Circar**, handed over in **1788**.

167.s: Which Circar became the principal area of conflict between Nizam Ali and the British?
167.x: Guntur Circar was the area of conflict because it was held by Nizam Ali's brother, Basalat Jung. It was the fifth Circar and was also called Kondaveedu or Murtazanagar.
167.tq: Apply the specific conflict clue instead of choosing the broader regional term Northern Circars.
xs: The **Guntur Circar** was the area of conflict — option **(1)**.
It was held by the Nizam's brother **Basalat Jung** (APHQ 2011).
Exam angle: the answer is **Guntur Circar**, not the Northern Circars as a whole.
xa: Guntur = **5th Circar**, also **Kondaveedu** / **Murtazanagar**.
Handed over on **18 September 1788** for **₹7 lakh**.

167.s: Which combination correctly describes the final transfer of Guntur to the Company?
o: Basalat Jung died in 1782; the transfer followed payment of 7 lakh rupees on 18 September 1788.
Basalat Jung died in 1788; the transfer followed payment of 9 lakh rupees in 1798.
Basalat Jung died in 1766; the transfer followed payment of 15 lakh rupees in 1768.
Basalat Jung died in 1800; the transfer followed the Cession Treaty.
167.x: Basalat Jung died in 1782. Nizam Ali received 7 lakh rupees and handed Guntur over on 18 September 1788.
167.tq: Match the two dates and the payment figure as a single transfer sequence.
xs: **Basalat Jung** died in **1782**; Guntur was handed over for **7 lakh rupees** on **18 September 1788** — option **(1)**.
The handover came after **6 years of talks** and completed the **Northern Circars**.
xa: **₹9 lakh** was the **1766/1768** Circars figure; **₹15 lakh** the proposed lease.
The **Ceded Districts** came separately in **1800**.

167.s: The Subsidiary Alliance system introduced by Lord Wellesley in 1798 was primarily intended to
o: provide direct British administration at the lowest possible cost
restore the authority of Mughal provincial governors
promote free trade between Indian states and European powers
counter French influence and establish British paramountcy without direct administration
167.x: Wellesley designed the system to counter French influence and establish British paramountcy without assuming the cost of direct administration.
167.tq: Identify the stated aim rather than confusing political control with direct annexation.
xs: The aim was to **counter French influence** and **establish British paramountcy** without the cost of **direct administration** — option **(4)**.
Option (1) is the opposite: the system avoided direct administration.
Another aim: maintain a large army **at the Indian states' cost**.
xa: Introduced by **Lord Wellesley**, **1798**.
First state: **Hyderabad (1798)**.

167.s: Under the Subsidiary Alliance system, which one of the following was NOT a condition imposed on the Indian ruler?
o: Surrender of control over foreign affairs
Permission to employ other Europeans without British approval
Acceptance of a British Resident at the court
Maintenance of a permanent British subsidiary force
167.x: The ruler could not employ other Europeans without the consent of the Company. Acceptance of a Resident, surrender of foreign affairs and maintenance of the subsidiary force were terms of the alliance.
167.tq: Find the reversed condition in a NOT question.
xs: The ruler could **not employ other Europeans** without British consent — so option **(2)** was NOT a condition.
Real terms: **foreign policy** surrendered, a **British Resident** at court, a **permanent subsidiary force**.
xa: The ruler **paid for its upkeep**, in cash or by **ceding territory**.
In return the Company **protected the state's borders**.

167.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the financial obligation under the Subsidiary Alliance:
1. The ruler had to pay for the upkeep of the British subsidiary force.
2. Payment could be made in cash or by ceding territory.
3. If payment was delayed, the British were required to withdraw the subsidiary force.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
167.x: The ruler paid for the force in cash or through territorial cession. Failure to pay led to territorial cession, not withdrawal of the force.
167.tq: Spot the statement that reverses the consequence of non-payment.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: the ruler **paid for the force's upkeep**.
Statement 2: in **cash** or by **ceding territory**.
Statement 3 wrong: late payment meant **ceded territory in lieu of cash**, not withdrawal.
xa: Example: the Nizam's **Ceded Districts** (**1800**).
Finances were **drained by the subsidy**.

167.s:
Which of the following was a consequence of the Subsidiary Alliance for the Indian states?
1. Loss of control over foreign policy
2. Drain through the subsidy
3. Territorial cessions when subsidies were unpaid
4. Increased dependence of the rulers on the Company
167.x: The alliance reduced sovereignty, imposed financial burdens, caused territorial cessions such as the Nizam's Ceded Districts and increased dependence on the Company.
167.tq: Combine political, financial and administrative effects in a coded statement question.
xs: All four were consequences — **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(4)**.
Loss of **sovereignty + foreign policy**; finances **drained by the subsidy**.
**Territorial cessions** (e.g. Nizam's **Ceded Districts**); rulers grew **dependent**.
xa: Neglected government became a later **pretext for annexation**.
**Disbanded soldiers** were left without work.

167.s:
Arrange the following states in the chronological order in which they accepted the Subsidiary Alliance under Wellesley's system:
A. Awadh
B. Hyderabad
C. Scindia of Gwalior
D. Peshwa
167.x: Hyderabad accepted in 1798, Awadh in 1801, the Peshwa in 1802 and Scindia in 1804.
167.tq: Fix the earliest and latest entries first, then place the intermediate treaties by year.
xs: The order is **B, A, D, C** — option **(1)**.
**Hyderabad (Sep 1798)** → **Awadh (Nov 1801)** → **Peshwa (31 Dec 1802; UPSC notes say Dec 1801)** → **Scindia (Feb 1804)**.
xa: **Mysore** (**1799**) and **Tanjore** (**Oct 1799**) came between Hyderabad and Awadh.
The Peshwa's treaty was the **Treaty of Bassein**.

167.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
167.x: Mysore accepted the Subsidiary Alliance in 1799. Tanjore accepted in 1799, Bhonsle in 1803 and the Rajput states in 1818.
167.tq: Use the year-state pairing and reject the near-year substitutions.
xs: **Mysore — 1799** is correctly matched — option **(1)**.
**Tanjore** accepted in **Oct 1799**, not 1803.
**Bhonsle (Nagpur)** accepted in **Dec 1803**; **Rajput states** in **1818**.
xa: Mysore's restored **Wodeyars** accepted it after Tipu's fall.
**Hyderabad** was first (**Sep 1798**).

167.s:
Consider the following statements regarding resistance to the Subsidiary Alliance:
1. Tipu Sultan refused it, which led to the Fourth Mysore War.
2. Holkar accepted it readily in 1798 and was the first Maratha power to sign it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
167.x: Statement 1 is correct: Tipu's refusal led to the Fourth Mysore War. Statement 2 is wrong: Holkar resisted longest, fought on in the Second Maratha War and signed only in 1818 as the last Maratha power; the first state (1798) was Hyderabad. So 1 only.
167.tq: First to sign = Hyderabad (1798); last Maratha = Holkar (1818); refused outright = Tipu.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: **Tipu Sultan refused** → **4th Mysore War**.
Statement 2 wrong: **Holkar resisted longest**, fought on in the **2nd Maratha War**, and came in only in **1818**.
xa: The first state was **Hyderabad (1798)** (APPSC-G1 2004).
Holkar was **the last Maratha** power to accept.

167.s: Which one of the following groups entered into the Subsidiary Alliance in 1818?
o: Holkar, Bharatpur, Jodhpur, Jaipur and Bundi
Mysore, Tanjore, Awadh, Peshwa and Scindia
Punjab, Awadh, Holkar, Tanjore and Jaitpur
Hyderabad, Berar, Satara, Jhansi and Nagpur
167.x: Holkar, Bharatpur, Jodhpur, Jaipur and Bundi entered into the arrangement in 1818. Holkar was the last Maratha power to sign it.
167.tq: Recognise the final group in the alliance chronology and avoid mixing it with earlier signatories.
xs: **Holkar, Bharatpur, Jodhpur, Jaipur and Bundi** came in **1818** — option **(1)**.
**Mysore, Tanjore, Awadh, Peshwa, Scindia** came in **1799-1804**.
xa: The **1818** Rajput treaties were negotiated by **Charles Metcalfe** under **Lord Hastings**.
Aim: protect them from the **Marathas and Pindaris**.

167.s: The territories ceded by the Nizam to the British came to be known as:
167.x: The ceded territories of Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur and Bellary were known as Dattamandalalu, or the Ceded Districts.
167.tq: Distinguish the regional label for the ceded inland districts from the coastal Northern Circars.
xs: The ceded lands were called **Dattamandalalu**, the **Ceded Districts** — option **(3)**.
The **Northern Circars** were a separate, earlier transfer (**1766-1788**).
xa: **Rayalaseema** was proposed by **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao** in **1928**.
It was approved at the **Andhra Mahasabha, Nandyal**.

167.s: The proposal to rename Dattamandalalu as Rayalaseema was approved at the Andhra Mahasabha held at Nandyal under the presidency of:
167.x: The Andhra Mahasabha at Nandyal, presided over by Dr S. Radhakrishnan, approved the name Rayalaseema proposed by Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao.
167.tq: Use the role distinction between the proposer and the presiding authority.
xs: The Nandyal **Andhra Mahasabha** was presided over by **Dr S. Radhakrishnan** — option **(4)**.
**Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao** **proposed** the name **Rayalaseema** (**1928**), but did not preside.
xa: Earlier name: **Dattamandalalu** (Ceded Districts).
Districts: **Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur, Bellary**.

167.s:
Which of the following statements about the territorial integration of Andhra under the Company is correct?
1. Nellore and Chittoor were annexed from the Carnatic Nawab in 1801.
2. By 1801, the whole Andhra region was under the Company.
3. Wellesley merged the region into the Madras Presidency.
4. Tamil leaders dominated the Madras Presidency in this arrangement.
Select the correct answer using the code below.
167.x: All four statements are correct. The 1801 acquisition of Nellore and Chittoor completed Company control over the Andhra region, which Wellesley merged into the Madras Presidency.
167.tq: Trace the final territorial step and its administrative consequence before selecting the full code.
xs: All four are correct — **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(4)**.
**1801**: **Nellore and Chittoor** taken from the **Carnatic Nawab**; by **1801** whole Andhra was under the Company.
**Wellesley merged it into the Madras Presidency**, where **Tamil leaders dominated**.
xa: **1794**: **Battle of Padmanabham** — Chinna Vijayaramaraju of Vizianagaram defeated.
**Telangana** stayed under the Nizam.

167.s: The Battle of Padmanabham (1794) is associated with:
o: the defeat of Chinna Vijayaramaraju of Vizianagaram by the Company
the cession of the Ceded Districts by the Nizam
the transfer of Guntur Circar to the Company
167.x: At Padmanabham (10 July 1794) the Company defeated Chinna Vijayaramaraju of Vizianagaram. The Ceded Districts came in 1800, Conflans was beaten at Chandurti (1758), and Guntur was handed over in 1788.
167.tq: Padmanabham 1794 = Vizianagaram defeated
xs: At **Padmanabham (1794)**, **Chinna Vijayaramaraju** of **Vizianagaram** was defeated — option **(1)**.
The **Ceded Districts** came in **1800**; **Guntur** in **1788**.
xa: The battle was fought on **10 July**.
By **1801** the whole Andhra region was under the Company.

167.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Sikandar Jah — Secunderabad cantonment named after him
Nasir-ud-Daula — title Star of India for loyalty during 1857
Mir Mahbub Ali Khan — Wahabi conspiracy of 1839
167.x: The Secunderabad cantonment was named after Sikandar Jah. The Wahabi conspiracy occurred during Nasir-ud-Daula's reign, the title Star of India was associated with Afzal-ud-Daula, and Mir Mahbub Ali Khan ruled later.
167.tq: Reject swapped ruler-event associations among successive Nizams.
xs: **Sikandar Jah** — **Secunderabad cantonment** named after him — option **(1)**.
"**Star of India**" was **Afzal-ud-Daula**; the **Berar Treaty 1853** and **Wahabi conspiracy 1839** were under **Nasir-ud-Daula**.
xa: Sikandar Jah = **Asaf Jah III** (**1803-29**).
⚠ **Afzal-ud-Daula** = 1857 + "Star of India"; **Mahbub Ali Khan** = youngest Asaf Jahi.

167.s: The Berar Treaty of 1853, concluded during the reign of Nasir-ud-Daula, transferred which territories to the British?
167.x: The Berar Treaty of 1853 gave Berar, Raichur and Osmanabad, also known as Dharashiv, to the British.
167.tq: Test the treaty-territory association against nearby Hyderabad territorial cessions.
xs: The **Berar Treaty 1853** gave **Berar, Raichur and Osmanabad/Dharashiv** to the British — option **(2)**.
It was signed under **Dalhousie**, in **Nasir-ud-Daula**'s reign.
**Kadapa, Kurnool, Bellary** were **Ceded Districts** of **1800**.
xa: **Salar Jung I** became **Diwan** in **1853**.
Nasir-ud-Daula's reign also saw the **Wahabi conspiracy 1839**.

167.s: Which Nizam ruled Hyderabad during the Revolt of 1857 and was given the title “Star of India” for his loyalty?
167.x: Afzal-ud-Daula, or Asaf Jah V, ruled from 1857 to 1869, was the Nizam during the Revolt of 1857 and received the title “Star of India” for his loyalty.
167.tq: Combine the reign period with the associated political event and honour.
xs: **Afzal-ud-Daula (Asaf Jah V)** was Nizam during the **Revolt of 1857** and got "**Star of India**" — option **(1)**.
He ruled **1857-69**; asked in **APPSC G2 2001**.
**Nasir-ud-Daula** died on **16 May 1857**, before the revolt reached Hyderabad.
xa: **17 July 1857**: **Turrebaz Khan** attacked the Residency to free **Chida Khan**.
The attack was **repulsed by Davidson**.

167.s: Which one of the following statements about Mir Mahbub Ali Khan is correct?
o: He ruled from 1829 to 1857 and was associated with the Berar Treaty.
He ruled during the Fourth Mysore War as an adult monarch.
He was the youngest Asaf Jahi ruler and became Nizam as an infant.
He was the first Nizam to move the capital to Hyderabad.
167.x: Mir Mahbub Ali Khan, or Asaf Jah VI, was the youngest Asaf Jahi ruler and became Nizam as an infant. He ruled from 1869 to 1911.
167.tq: Use the distinctive biographical clue to distinguish successive Nizams.
xs: **Mir Mahbub Ali Khan** was the **youngest Asaf Jahi ruler**, Nizam **as an infant** — option **(3)**.
This is the **APPSC-GS 2022** key.
**1829-57** and the **Berar Treaty** belong to **Nasir-ud-Daula**; the capital shift to Hyderabad (**1763**) was **Nizam Ali Khan**'s.
xa: He was **Asaf Jah VI** (**1869-1911**).
**Salar Jung I** served as **regent**.

167.s: Salar Jung I served under which of the following three Nizams?
o: Nasir-ud-Daula, Afzal-ud-Daula and Mir Mahbub Ali Khan
Nizam Ali Khan, Sikandar Jah and Nasir-ud-Daula
Sikandar Jah, Afzal-ud-Daula and the last Nizam
Afzal-ud-Daula, Mir Mahbub Ali Khan and Nizam Ali Khan
167.x: Salar Jung I served Nasir-ud-Daula, Afzal-ud-Daula and Mir Mahbub Ali Khan, dying in 1883 during the period of the latter's reign.
167.tq: Use the overlapping reign sequence to identify all three associated rulers.
xs: **Salar Jung I** served **Nasir-ud-Daula, Afzal-ud-Daula and Mahbub Ali Khan** — option **(1)**.
He served until his death in **1883**.
xa: **Mir Turab Ali Khan** was made **Diwan** on **31 May 1853**, after **Siraj-ul-Mulk**'s death.
He took the title **Salar Jung I**.

167.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the attack on the Hyderabad Residency:
1. It took place on 17 July 1857.
2. Turrebaz Khan led the attack.
3. The objective was to free Chida Khan.
4. The attack was repulsed by Davidson.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
167.x: All four statements are correct. Turrebaz Khan attacked the Residency on 17 July 1857 in an attempt to free Chida Khan, but Davidson repulsed the attack.
167.tq: Check the date, leader, objective and outcome together to identify the complete event description.
xs: All four statements are correct — **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(4)**.
On **17 July 1857**, **Turrebaz Khan** attacked the **Residency** to free **Chida Khan**.
The attack was **repulsed by Davidson**.
xa: The Nizam then was **Afzal-ud-Daula**, given "**Star of India**" for loyalty.
The Residency building was called the **"Koti"**.

167.s:
The British intervened in the internal affairs of princely states primarily on which of the following grounds?
1. Giving effect to their international commitments
2. Succession disputes
3. Misgovernment
167.x: The British claimed intervention to fulfil international commitments and also intervened in succession disputes and cases of misgovernment.
167.tq: Identify all recognised grounds instead of treating paramountcy as unrestricted annexation.
xs: All three grounds — **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
The British intervened **to give effect to their international commitments** (**APPSC-G2 2017**).
They also intervened over **succession disputes** + **misgovernment**.
xa: States ran internal affairs but had **no external or international life**.
**Awadh (1856)** was annexed for **misgovernment**.

167.s: The expression “breakwaters to the storm” was used in relation to the princes under the policy of
167.x: After 1858, the princes were described as “breakwaters to the storm” under the policy of subordinate union.
167.tq: Match the distinctive phrase with the later policy rather than the earlier annexation policies.
xs: After **1858**, under **subordinate union**, the princes were called the "**breakwaters to the storm**" — so option **(4)** is correct.
Subordinate union came through the **Crown** (**Queen's Proclamation**): annexation stopped, the **right of adoption** was recognised and borders were guaranteed.
**Doctrine of Lapse** was **Dalhousie's** (1848) and **Ring-fence** was **Warren Hastings'** — both belong to the Company era, before 1858.
xa: Policy sequence: **Ring-fence** (Warren Hastings) → **Subsidiary Alliance** (Wellesley, **1798**) → **Subordinate isolation** (Lord Hastings, **1813-23**) → **Doctrine of Lapse** (Dalhousie, **1848**) → **Subordinate union** (Crown, after 1858).
Lapse annexations and the Awadh takeover turned rulers, **taluqdars** and sepoys against the Company → policy abandoned after **1857**.
⚠ **Warren Hastings** = ring-fence; **Lord Hastings** = subordinate isolation.

167.s: Who negotiated the treaties concluded with Jodhpur, Jaipur, Bundi and other Rajput states in 1818?
167.x: Charles Metcalfe negotiated the treaties with the Rajput states in 1818 under Lord Hastings.
167.tq: Separate the negotiator from the Governor-General under whom the treaties were concluded.
xs: **Charles Metcalfe** negotiated the **1818** treaties with **Jodhpur, Jaipur, Bundi** and other Rajput states — so option **(3)** is correct.
The treaties were made under **Lord Hastings**, as part of his policy of **subordinate isolation**.
**Wajid Ali Shah** was the Nawab of **Awadh** dispossessed in **1856**; **Raymond** commanded the **Nizam's French troops**.
xa: Aims of the Rajput treaties: protect the states from the **Marathas and Pindaris**, bring them under **British paramountcy**, and isolate them from the Maratha powers.
**Holkar**, the last Maratha, also came into the alliance system in **1818**, along with **Bharatpur**.
Subordinate isolation: each state bound **separately** to the paramount Company and cut off from the others.

167.s: The Rajput states entered into subordinate alliances in 1818 primarily to
o: Secure independence from all external powers
Restore French influence in western India
Obtain protection from the Marathas and Pindaris and accept British paramountcy
167.x: The alliances aimed to protect the Rajput states from the Marathas and Pindaris, bring them under British paramountcy and isolate them from Maratha powers.
167.tq: Select the option containing the combined strategic aims rather than one isolated purpose.
xs: The Rajput states accepted the **1818** alliances to get **protection from the Marathas and Pindaris** and came under **British paramountcy** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The treaties also aimed to **isolate** them from the Maratha powers — the opposite of independence from all external powers.
Keeping the **French out** was an aim of Wellesley's **Subsidiary Alliance** (1798), not of the 1818 treaties; **Awadh** was annexed only in **1856**.
xa: States: **Jodhpur, Jaipur, Bundi** + other Rajput states; negotiator **Charles Metcalfe**, under **Lord Hastings** (**1813-23**).
Under paramountcy, states ran internal affairs but had **no external or international life**.
The British stepped in **to give effect to their international commitments** (**APPSC-G2 2017**), and also over succession disputes and misgovernment.

167.s: The Ring-fence policy of Warren Hastings was intended to
o: Protect the Company's frontiers by defending neighbouring states
Annex every state without a natural male heir
Transfer Indian territories to the French
End all relations with princely states
167.x: The Ring-fence policy sought to guard the Company's own frontiers by defending the borders of neighbouring states.
167.tq: Infer the policy objective from the frontier-protection scenario.
xs: **Warren Hastings'** **Ring-fence** policy aimed to **protect the Company's frontiers by defending the borders of neighbouring states** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Annexing states without a natural heir was **Dalhousie's** **Doctrine of Lapse** (**1848**), a different policy.
xa: **Awadh** was the classic buffer: set up after **Buxar (1764)**; it shielded **Bengal** from the **Marathas** and the **Afghans**.
Hastings sold **Kora and Allahabad** to the Nawab of Awadh to keep the buffer strong.
⚠ **Warren Hastings** = ring-fence; **Lord Hastings** = subordinate isolation (**1813-23**).

167.s: Awadh served as a classic buffer state because it
o: Blocked the advance of the Burmese into Assam
Shielded Bengal from the Marathas and Afghans
Separated Bombay from the Portuguese territories
Protected Madras from French naval attacks
167.x: Awadh acted as a buffer protecting Bengal from the Marathas and Afghans.
167.tq: Match the buffer state with the frontier threat it was meant to contain.
xs: **Awadh** was the classic buffer state because it **shielded Bengal from the Marathas and Afghans** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was set up as a buffer after **Buxar (1764)** under Warren Hastings' **Ring-fence** policy.
xa: **Warren Hastings** sold **Kora and Allahabad** to the Nawab of Awadh.
Awadh was a Company-protected buffer from **1764-65**; some notes treat the **Treaty of Allahabad (1765)** as the first subsidiary-type treaty — **Shuja-ud-Daulah** accepted a subsidiary force.
Awadh accepted Wellesley's Subsidiary Alliance in **Nov 1801**, and was annexed by Dalhousie in **1856** for misgovernment.

167.s:
Arrange the following states annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse in chronological order:
A. Nagpur
B. Satara
C. Jhansi
D. Sambalpur
167.x: The correct sequence is Satara (1848), Sambalpur (1849), Jhansi (1853) and Nagpur (1854).
167.tq: Fix the earliest and latest items first, then place the middle dates.
xs: Order: **Satara (1848)** → **Sambalpur (1849)** → **Jhansi (1853)** → **Nagpur (1854)** = **B, D, C, A** — option **(1)**.
**Satara** was the **first** state taken under the Doctrine of Lapse.
**Nagpur** lapsed when the Bhonsle Raja **Raghuji III** died heirless.
xa: Other lapse cases: **Jaitpur (1849)**, **Baghat (1850)**, **Udaipur (1852)** — the Chhattisgarh Udaipur, not Mewar.
⚠ Some notes print "Jaipur" for **1849** — the state was **Jaitpur**.
**APPSC-G1 2024** key: of Awadh, Jhansi, Satara, Nagpur, Sindh → only **Jhansi, Satara, Nagpur** by lapse.

167.s: Which of the following groups consists entirely of states annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse?
167.x: Satara, Jaitpur, Sambalpur and Jhansi were all annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse.
167.tq: Separate the lapse cases from conquest, misgovernment and revenue-related cases.
xs: **Satara, Jaitpur, Sambalpur, Jhansi** were all taken by **lapse** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Punjab** and **Lower Burma** were taken by **conquest**, and **Berar** from the Nizam for **arrears** — option 1 fails.
**Awadh** was annexed for **misgovernment**; for **Tanjore** and the **Carnatic** only titles and pensions were abolished — option 2 fails.
**Sindh (1843)** and **Punjab (1849)** were **conquests** — option 4 fails.
xa: Lapse dates: **Satara 1848**, **Jaitpur 1849**, **Sambalpur 1849**, **Baghat 1850**, **Udaipur 1852**, **Jhansi 1853**, **Nagpur 1854**.
**UPPSC 2025** key: **Karnataka (Carnatic)** was not a lapse case.

167.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
167.x: Lower Burma, also called Pegu, was annexed by conquest in 1852. Berar was taken from the Nizam for arrears, Awadh for misgovernment, and Sindh by conquest in 1843.
167.tq: Check both the ground and the year instead of accepting a familiar territory name.
xs: **Lower Burma (Pegu)** was annexed by **conquest** in **1852** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Berar (1853)** was taken from the Nizam for **arrears**, not misgovernment.
**Awadh** was annexed in **1856** for **misgovernment**, not conquest in 1843.
**Sindh** was annexed by **conquest** under **Ellenborough** in **1843**, not by lapse in 1848.
xa: **Satara (1848)** was the first lapse annexation.
**Punjab (1849)** was also a conquest, after the **Second Anglo-Sikh War**; **Duleep Singh** was deposed.

167.s: Which of the following states was annexed on the ground of maladministration, rather than under the Doctrine of Lapse?
167.x: Awadh was annexed in 1856 on the ground of maladministration, based on Outram's reports. Nagpur, Jhansi and Sambalpur were annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse.
167.tq: Find the exception by separating policy-based annexations from administrative grounds.
xs: **Awadh** was annexed in **1856** for **maladministration** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The ground rested on reports by Residents **Sleeman** and **Outram**; the ruler dispossessed was **Wajid Ali Shah**.
**Sambalpur (1849)**, **Jhansi (1853)** and **Nagpur (1854)** were all **lapse** annexations.
xa: Other non-lapse cases: **Punjab** and **Lower Burma** by conquest; titles and pensions abolished for **Tanjore** and the **Carnatic**.
The Awadh takeover turned **taluqdars** and sepoys against the Company before **1857**.
Earlier, Awadh was Warren Hastings' classic **buffer** state, shielding Bengal.

167.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Sindh was annexed after conquest under Ellenborough.
2. Punjab was annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse.
3. Awadh was annexed in 1856 on the ground of maladministration.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
167.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is false because Punjab was annexed by conquest after the Second Anglo-Sikh War, not under the Doctrine of Lapse.
167.tq: Test each statement against the specific ground of annexation.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **Sindh** was annexed by **conquest** under **Ellenborough** in **1843**.
Statement 2 wrong: **Punjab (1849)** was taken by **conquest** after the **Second Anglo-Sikh War**, not by lapse.
Statement 3 correct: **Awadh** was annexed in **1856** for **maladministration**.
xa: Punjab's ruler **Duleep Singh** was deposed.
**Punjab annexed 1849** (**APPSC-GS 2012**; the key there was blank, but 1849 is correct).
Awadh's annexation rested on reports by **Sleeman** and **Outram**; **Wajid Ali Shah** lost his throne.

167.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Awadh — 1856 — annexation due to absence of a natural heir
Satara — 1848 — first annexation under the Doctrine of Lapse
Punjab — 1849 — annexation under the Doctrine of Lapse
Berar — 1853 — annexation after the Second Anglo-Sikh War
167.x: Satara was annexed in 1848 and was the first state annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse. Punjab was conquered after the Second Anglo-Sikh War, Awadh for misgovernment, and Berar was taken for subsidy arrears.
167.tq: Check both the ground and the year instead of accepting a partially familiar pair.
xs: **Satara — 1848** was the **first annexation under the Doctrine of Lapse** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Awadh (1856)** was annexed for **misgovernment**, not for want of an heir.
**Punjab (1849)** was a **conquest** after the **Second Anglo-Sikh War**, not lapse.
**Berar (1853)** was taken from the Nizam for **arrears**.
xa: Dalhousie's policy of annexing heirless states = **Doctrine of Lapse** (**APPSC-GS 2018** key).
**Sindh (1843)** came before Dalhousie — a conquest under **Ellenborough**.

167.s: Subordinate isolation is associated with the administration of
167.x: Lord Hastings pursued subordinate isolation during 1813–1823, binding each princely state separately to the paramount Company.
167.tq: Discriminate between the similarly named Hastings and the other policy-makers.
xs: **Subordinate isolation** belongs to **Lord Hastings** (**1813-23**) — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Warren Hastings** = **Ring-fence**; **Lord Wellesley** = **Subsidiary Alliance (1798)**; **Lord Dalhousie** = **Doctrine of Lapse (1848)**.
xa: Under subordinate isolation each state was bound **separately** to the paramount Company and cut off from the others.
Its showpiece: the **1818** treaties with **Jodhpur, Jaipur, Bundi**, negotiated by **Charles Metcalfe**.
⚠ **Warren Hastings** and **Lord Hastings** are different men — a frequent trap.

167.s: Lord Dalhousie's policy of annexing states whose rulers died without a natural heir is known as the:
167.x: Dalhousie's annexation policy (from 1848) is the Doctrine of Lapse (APPSC-GS 2018 key). Ring-fence was Warren Hastings', the Subsidiary Alliance Wellesley's (1798), and subordinate isolation Lord Hastings'.
167.tq: Dalhousie = Doctrine of Lapse
xs: Annexing states whose rulers died without a natural heir = **Doctrine of Lapse** (Dalhousie, **1848**) — so option **(3)** is correct (**APPSC-GS 2018** key).
**Ring-fence** = **Warren Hastings**; **Subsidiary Alliance** = **Wellesley (1798)**; **Subordinate isolation** = **Lord Hastings**.
xa: Lapse states: **Satara, Jaitpur, Udaipur, Sambalpur, Nagpur, Baghat, Jhansi**.
Not lapse: **Punjab** and **Lower Burma** (conquest), **Awadh** (misgovernment), **Berar** (arrears).
**APPSC-G1 2024**: of Awadh, Jhansi, Satara, Nagpur, Sindh → only **Jhansi, Satara, Nagpur** by lapse.

167.s: Which region remained under the Nizam, while the Northern Circars and Ceded Districts formed the main territorial basis of present-day Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema?
167.x: Telangana remained under the Nizam, whereas the Northern Circars and Ceded Districts together broadly correspond to Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema.
167.tq: Use a regional contrast to distinguish Nizam-held territory from ceded Andhra regions.
xs: **Telangana** stayed under the **Nizam** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **Northern Circars** and **Ceded Districts** became almost all of **Coastal Andhra** and **Rayalaseema**.
xa: Circars handed over (**1766**): **Mustafanagar (Kondapalli), Eluru, Rajamahendravaram, Srikakulam**; **Guntur** followed in **1788**.
Ceded Districts = **Dattamandalalu**; the name **Rayalaseema** was proposed by **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao** in **1928**.
**Nellore and Chittoor** were taken from the Carnatic Nawab in **1801**.

167.s: The lapse annexations and the takeover of Awadh contributed to the Revolt of 1857 because they alienated
167.x: The annexations and Awadh takeover turned rulers, taluqdars and sepoys against the Company, contributing to the revolt.
167.tq: Connect a political policy with its stated social and military reaction.
xs: The **lapse** annexations and the **Awadh** takeover turned **rulers, taluqdars and sepoys** against the Company — so option **(2)** is correct.
As a result the policy was **abandoned after 1857**.
xa: After **1858**, annexation stopped and the **right of adoption** was recognised (subordinate union).
**Awadh (1856)** was annexed for **misgovernment**; its Nawab **Wajid Ali Shah** was dispossessed.
At **Hyderabad** in **1857**, **Turrebaz Khan** attacked the Residency on **17 July** to free **Chida Khan**; repulsed by **Davidson**.

167.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Market / Price Control Policy aimed to control prices.
The policy was associated with Alauddin Khalji.
The policy aimed to establish buffer states to protect Company territories.
The policy was intended to maintain a large army at lower cost.
167.x: Option C is incorrect: creating buffer states to protect Company land was the Ring Fence Policy. Alauddin Khalji's price control aimed to keep a large army at low cost.
167.tq: Discriminate the aim of each policy.
n: Market/Price Control Policy aimed to control prices. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #91 · pp 173-174]
Market/Price Control Policy is associated with Alauddin Khalji. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #91 · pp 173-174]
Ring Fence Policy aimed to create buffer states. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #91 · pp 173-174]
Ring Fence Policy aimed to protect Company territories. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #91 · pp 173-174]
Alauddin Khalji used Market/Price Control Policy to maintain a large army at lower cost. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #91 · pp 173-174]
xs: The incorrect statement: the policy aimed to **establish buffer states** — option **(3)**.
**Buffer states** to protect Company territories was the **Ring Fence Policy** of **Warren Hastings**.
**Alauddin Khalji**'s **Market/Price Control Policy** aimed to **control prices** and **maintain a large army** at **lower cost**.
xa: **Awadh** was the classic buffer, shielding Bengal from the **Marathas** and **Afghans**.
**Blood and Iron Policy** = **Balban**, to establish a **strong monarchy**.
**Dhamma Policy** = **Ashoka**, for moral and social harmony.

167.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Dhamma Policy
(b) Market / Price Control Policy
(c) Blood and Iron Policy
(d) Ring Fence Policy

List-II
(i) Balban
(ii) Warren Hastings
(iii) Ashoka
(iv) Alauddin Khalji
167.x: Dhamma belongs to Ashoka, Market Control to Alauddin Khalji, Blood and Iron to Balban, and the Ring Fence to Warren Hastings, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
167.tq: Recall the ruler of each policy.
n: Dhamma Policy is associated with Ashoka. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #91 · pp 173-174]
Market/Price Control Policy is associated with Alauddin Khalji. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #91 · pp 173-174]
Blood and Iron Policy is associated with Balban. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #91 · pp 173-174]
