177.x: The Lyall Commission assessed the causes of famine and recommended measures to prevent or mitigate future famines.
177.tq: Distinguish the commission’s function from its associated famine year.
xs: The **Lyall Commission** assessed the **causes** and recommended measures against **future famines** — option **(3)**.
It followed the **1896-97** famine under **Elgin II**.
**MacDonnell** stressed **early relief + more irrigation**; **Campbell** was the first (Orissa); **Woodhead** the last (Bengal **1943**).
xa: MacDonnell: **1901**, Curzon.
The **Famine Code (1883)** was framed on the **Strachey** Commission's recommendations.

177.s: What was the principal emphasis of the MacDonnell Commission?
177.x: The MacDonnell Commission stressed early relief and greater irrigation as measures against famine.
177.tq: Identify the policy recommendation rather than the commission’s name or date.
xs: The **MacDonnell Commission** stressed **early relief and more irrigation** — option **(1)**.
It came in **1901** under **Curzon**.
xa: R.C. Dutt wrote **"Open Letters to Lord Curzon"** (**1900**).
**Lyall** assessed causes and measures against future famines.

177.s: The Famine Code of 1883 was framed primarily on the recommendations of which commission?
177.x: The Famine Code of 1883 was framed on the recommendations of the Strachey Commission of 1880.
177.tq: Link a policy code to the commission whose recommendations formed its basis.
xs: The **Famine Code, 1883** was framed on the **Strachey Commission (1880)** recommendations — option **(1)**.
**Campbell** (**1866**) came earlier; **Lyall** and **Woodhead** came later.
xa: Provisions: stages of scarcity and famine, **relief works**, **gratuitous relief**, revenue suspension or remission.
A **Famine Relief and Insurance Fund** was also set up.

177.s:
Consider the following provisions of the Famine Code:
1. Classification of stages of scarcity and famine
2. Relief works for the able-bodied
3. Gratuitous relief for the old and infirm
4. Suspension or remission of revenue
Which of the above were provisions of the Code?
177.x: The Famine Code provided for stages of scarcity and famine, relief works for able-bodied persons, gratuitous relief for the old and infirm, and suspension or remission of revenue.
177.tq: Recognise a complete set of administrative provisions rather than one isolated relief measure.
xs: All four were provisions — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Stages of scarcity and famine**; **relief works** for the able-bodied.
**Gratuitous relief** for the old and infirm; **suspension or remission of revenue**.
xa: ⚠ **Relief works** = able-bodied; **gratuitous relief** = old and infirm.
It also created a **Famine Relief and Insurance Fund**.
The Code dates to **1883**, on the **Strachey** report.

177.s: Which statement regarding famine policy during the Company period is correct?
o: The government adopted a comprehensive famine code and provided extensive relief.
The government never adopted a famine code and gave minimal relief.
The government suspended revenue in every famine without exception.
The government transferred all famine relief to village councils.
177.x: During the Company period, the government never adopted a famine code and provided only minimal relief.
177.tq: Watch for absolute claims about uniform revenue suspension or comprehensive relief.
xs: In the Company period the government **never adopted a famine code** and gave **minimal relief** — option **(2)**.
In the **1770** Bengal famine the Company **kept collecting revenue**.
xa: The first Famine Code came only in **1883**.
Nationalists blamed **rigid revenue collection in drought** for famines.

177.s: The Temple wage during the Madras famine of 1877 consisted approximately of which ration?
o: About 1 pound of grain a day on relief works
About 5 pounds of grain a day on relief works
One rupee a day without grain
A weekly ration of ten pounds of rice
177.x: The Temple wage provided about 1 pound of grain per day on relief works and was criticised as a starvation wage.
177.tq: Distinguish the exact quantitative ration from plausible but exaggerated alternatives.
xs: The **Temple wage** was **about 1 pound (1 lb) of grain a day** on relief works — option **(1)**.
**Sir Richard Temple** fixed it in the **1877 Madras famine**.
xa: It was criticised as a **starvation wage**.
Relief works gave employment on **roads and canals**.

177.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the causes of famines under colonial rule:
1. Rigid revenue collection aggravated the impact of drought.
2. Export of food grains contributed to famine conditions.
3. Famines were caused exclusively by failure of the monsoon.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
177.x: Rigid revenue collection and export of food grains were identified as important causes of famines. The nationalist critique rejected the view that famines resulted exclusively from monsoon failure.
177.tq: Identify the statement using the extreme word ‘exclusively’ and separate structural causes from a single natural cause.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **rigid revenue collection in drought** aggravated famines.
Statement 2 correct: the **export of food grains** contributed.
Statement 3 wrong: famines were **not just monsoon failure**.
xa: Aggravators: **commercialisation** (cotton in **Ganjam**) + **laissez-faire** relief.
**Naoroji & R.C. Dutt** linked famines to **high land revenue and the drain**.

177.s: Who among the following linked Indian famines with high land revenue and the drain of wealth?
o: Dadabhai Naoroji and Sir Arthur Cotton
177.x: Dadabhai Naoroji and R.C. Dutt connected famines with the burden of high land revenue and the drain of wealth.
177.tq: Use the thinker–argument association and reject combinations that mix a critic with an administrator or engineer.
xs: **Dadabhai Naoroji and R.C. Dutt** linked famines to **high land revenue and the drain** — option **(2)**.
**Arthur Cotton** was an irrigation engineer; **Curzon** was the Viceroy R.C. Dutt wrote to.
xa: R.C. Dutt wrote **"Open Letters to Lord Curzon"** (**1900**).
Nationalists blamed **export of food grains** too.

177.s: With reference to R.C. Dutt, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: He wrote Open Letters to Lord Curzon in 1900.
He chaired the Woodhead Commission in 1944.
He led the construction of the Godavari anicut in 1833.
He introduced the IPC food-insecurity scale in 2025.
177.x: R.C. Dutt’s work titled Open Letters to Lord Curzon was associated with the year 1900. The other options incorrectly associate him with a famine commission, a modern food-security scale or an irrigation project.
177.tq: Match the historical personality with the precise work and year; the wrong options swap roles across different subjects.
xs: **R.C. Dutt** wrote **"Open Letters to Lord Curzon"** in **1900** — option **(1)**.
He did not chair **Woodhead (1944)**, build the Godavari anicut (that was **Cotton**), or devise the **IPC** scale.
xa: With **Naoroji** he linked famines to **high land revenue and the drain**.
The **MacDonnell Commission (1901)** came under **Curzon**.

177.s: Which one of the following correctly presents the sequence of the Godavari anicut project at Dowleswaram?
o: Report in 1844, sanction in 1846, work begun in 1847, main structure finished in April 1852
Report in 1846, sanction in 1847, work begun in 1852, main structure finished in 1855
Report in 1847, sanction in 1852, work begun in 1844, main structure finished in 1860
Report in 1852, sanction in 1844, work begun in 1846, main structure finished in 1872
177.x: Arthur Cotton’s Godavari anicut project was reported in 1844, sanctioned in 1846, begun in 1847 and had its main structure completed in April 1852.
177.tq: Arrange the project milestones in sequence, keeping the report before sanction and construction.
xs: **Report 1844 → sanction 1846 → work began 1847 → main structure finished April 1852** — option **(1)**.
⚠ **APPSC-G2 2012** keyed **1855** for the Dhavaleswaram Dam — in APPSC MCQs choose **1855**; the notes say built **1847-52**.
xa: Cost only **Rs 1,50,000**.
Revenue rose from **Rs 20.38 lakh (1853-54)** to **Rs 55.18 lakh (1894-95)**.
**Veenam Veeranna** helped Cotton build it.

177.s: Which of the following pairs relating to irrigation works is correctly matched?
o: Krishna anicut — Bezwada — proposed by Henry Atlock Lake
Godavari anicut — Bezwada — supervised by Charles Orr
177.x: The Krishna anicut at Bezwada was proposed by Colonel Henry Atlock Lake. The Penna anicut was at Nellore, while the K.C. Canal began from Sunkesula on the Tungabhadra.
177.tq: Use location and responsible engineer together to reject swapped irrigation projects.
xs: **Krishna anicut — Bezwada — proposed by Henry Atlock Lake** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Penna** anicut is at **Nellore** (**1860**); **K.C. Canal** is from **Sunkesula** (**1872**).
The **Godavari** anicut is at **Dowleswaram**; **Charles Orr** supervised the **Krishna** anicut.
xa: Krishna anicut: begun **1853**, finished by end-**1854**.
⚠ **Godavari** = Dowleswaram; **Krishna** = Bezwada; **Penna** = Nellore.

177.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: K.C. Canal — Sunkesula on the Tungabhadra — 1872
177.x: The Godavari anicut was at Dowleswaram, not Nellore. The Penna anicut was at Nellore in 1860, and the K.C. Canal dates from 1872 at Sunkesula on the Tungabhadra.
177.tq: Find the wrong location in a list of otherwise correctly matched irrigation projects.
xs: **Godavari anicut — Nellore — 1860** is wrongly matched — option **(3)**.
The Godavari anicut is at **Dowleswaram**, built **1847-52**; **Nellore 1860** is the **Penna** anicut.
**K.C. Canal** (Sunkesula, **1872**) and **Krishna** anicut (Bezwada, **1853**-54) are correct.
xa: Penna anicut was built on **Cotton's plan**.
⚠ **Godavari** = Dowleswaram; **Krishna** = Bezwada; **Penna** = Nellore.

177.s: Which Andhra official assisted Sir Arthur Cotton in building the Godavari anicut at Dowleswaram?
177.x: Veenam Veeranna was the Andhra official who helped Cotton build the Godavari dam (APPSC-G2 2019 key). Charles Orr supervised the Krishna anicut at Bezwada, Budda Vengalareddy fed people in the 1866 Kurnool famine and K.S. Gupta formed a relief committee in the 1945 famine.
177.tq: Cotton's Godavari helper = Veenam Veeranna.
xs: **Veenam Veeranna** helped Cotton build the Godavari dam — option **(2)** (APPSC-G2 **2019** key).
**Charles Orr** supervised the **Krishna** anicut; **Budda Vengalareddy** fed people in the Kurnool famine; **K.S. Gupta** led **1945** relief.
xa: Cotton was born **15 May 1803**.
The Guntur famine convinced the Company irrigation was needed.

177.s: The IPC food-insecurity scale places the following phases in which correct order from least severe to most severe?
177.x: The five phases progress from Phase 1 Minimal through Phase 2 Stressed, Phase 3 Crisis and Phase 4 Emergency to Phase 5 Catastrophe/Famine.
177.tq: Arrange the stages by increasing severity, beginning with the least severe and ending with famine.
xs: The IPC scale runs **Phase 1 Minimal, 2 Stressed, 3 Crisis, 4 Emergency, 5 Catastrophe/Famine** — option **(1)**.
It is a current-relevance point (**Jun 2025**).
xa: Modern food security = **availability, accessibility and affordability** through the **PDS**.
⚠ **IPC** here is the food-insecurity scale, not the Indian Penal Code.

177.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Kurnool famine — 1833; impetus to Cotton’s Godavari anicut
Guntur famine — 1833; impetus to Cotton’s Godavari anicut
Ganjam famine — 1833; impetus to Cotton’s Godavari anicut
Guntur famine — 1944; impetus to Cotton’s Godavari anicut
177.x: The Guntur famine of 1833 led to the construction of Cotton’s Godavari anicut. The other options assign the event to the wrong famine or year.
177.tq: Discriminate between the closely associated Andhra famine names and their years.
xs: **Guntur famine — 1833; impetus to Cotton's Godavari anicut** is correct — option **(2)**.
**Kurnool** was **1866**, **Ganjam** **1865-66**; **1944** is the **Woodhead** Commission.
xa: Guntur famine = **Dokkala Karuvu** (**1832-33**), worst in the south.
Ganjam (**1865-66**) and Kurnool (**1866**) are favourite Andhra famine MCQs.

177.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the first and the last famine commissions of the colonial period mentioned in the context of British India?
o: Campbell Commission in 1866 and Woodhead Commission in 1944
Woodhead Commission in 1866 and Campbell Commission in 1944
Lyall Commission in 1866 and Hunter Commission in 1944
Campbell Commission in 1833 and Woodhead Commission in 1865–66
177.x: The Campbell Commission of 1866 was the first famine commission, while the Woodhead Commission of 1944 was the last colonial famine commission.
177.tq: Use the first–last comparison and verify both the commission names and their years.
xs: First famine commission = **Campbell (1866)**; last colonial one = **Woodhead (1944)** — option **(1)**.
Campbell followed the **Orissa** famine; Woodhead followed the **Bengal Famine 1943**.
xa: Campbell: Viceroy **John Lawrence**; Woodhead: **Wavell**.
In between: **Strachey (1880)**, **Lyall**, **MacDonnell (1901)**.

178.s: Fort William College at Calcutta was established in 1800 by:
178.x: Lord Richard Wellesley established Fort William College in Calcutta in 1800 to train Company civil servants.
178.tq: Use the precise first name to avoid the Wellesley-name trap.
xs: **Fort William College (1800)** was founded by **Lord Richard Wellesley** — option **(3)**.
⚠ Trap: it was **Richard**, not **Arthur**, Wellesley.
**Dalhousie** is linked to the **1853** Minute and Wood's Despatch; **Bentinck** to the **1835** English Education Act.
xa: It trained **Company civil servants**.
It was replaced by the East India College, **Haileybury** (England), by **1806**.

178.s:
Arrange the following institutions in chronological order of their foundation:
A. Calcutta Madrasa
B. Asiatic Society of Bengal
C. Sanskrit College, Benaras
D. Fort William College
178.x: The institutions were founded in the order Calcutta Madrasa (1781), Asiatic Society of Bengal (1784), Sanskrit College, Benaras (1791), and Fort William College (1800).
178.tq: Arrange institutions by their foundation years and verify the first and last entries.
xs: Order: **Calcutta Madrasa (1781)** → **Asiatic Society (1784)** → **Sanskrit College, Benares (1791)** → **Fort William College (1800)** — option **(1) A, B, C, D**.
The Calcutta Madrasa was the **first educational institution** set up by the Company.
xa: After these: **Hindu College (1817)** and **Vedanta College (1825)**.
Founders: **Warren Hastings**, **William Jones**, **Jonathan Duncan**, **Richard Wellesley**.

178.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. Charter Act
B. General Committee of Public Instruction
C. English Education Act
D. Wood's Despatch
178.x: The Charter Act was passed in 1813, the General Committee was established in 1823, the English Education Act followed in 1835, and Wood's Despatch was issued in 1854.
178.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the two intermediate measures.
xs: Order: **Charter Act (1813)** → **General Committee of Public Instruction (1823)** → **English Education Act (1835)** → **Wood's Despatch (1854)** — option **(1) A, B, C, D**.
The Committee managed the **1813** grant; the **1835** Act settled its Orientalist-Anglicist split in favour of English.
xa: **Dalhousie's Minute (1853)** came just before Wood's Despatch.
⚠ English Education Act **1835** = **Bentinck + Macaulay**; Wood's Despatch **1854** = **Charles Wood + Dalhousie**.

178.s:
Consider the following statements about the Charter Act of 1813:
1. It earmarked Rs 1 lakh a year for the revival of Indian literature and the promotion of science.
2. The earmarked sum was released immediately from 1813 onwards.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
178.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Act provided Rs 1 lakh a year for literature and science. Statement 2 is wrong: the money was actually released only in the 1830s. So '1 only'; '2 only', 'Both' and 'Neither' are therefore wrong.
178.tq: 1813 = Rs 1 lakh promised, paid only in the 1830s.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1 correct: the **1813** Act gave **Rs 1 lakh** a year for **revival of Indian literature** and **promotion of science**.
Statement 2 wrong: the money was **actually released only in the 1830s**.
xa: The same Act ended the Company's **trade monopoly** (except **tea and China** trade).
It also **admitted missionaries**.
The grant was managed by the **General Committee of Public Instruction (1823)**.

178.s:
Consider the following statements about the General Committee of Public Instruction:
1. It managed the education grant.
2. It split into Orientalist and Anglicist camps.
3. It was created by the Charter Act of 1813.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
178.x: Statement 1 is correct: the GCPI (1823) managed the education grant. Statement 2 is correct: it split into Orientalist and Anglicist camps. Statement 3 is wrong: it was set up in 1823, ten years after the Charter Act of 1813. Hence '1 and 2 only'; the other options either miss 2 or include 3.
178.tq: GCPI = 1823, not 1813; it was the arena of the Orientalist-Anglicist debate.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: it **managed the education grant**.
Statement 2 correct: it **split into Orientalist and Anglicist camps**.
Statement 3 wrong: it came in **1823**, not by the **1813** Act.
xa: The debate ended with the **English Education Act 1835** (Bentinck, on **Macaulay's Minute**).
English became the medium of **higher education**.

178.s:
Consider the following statements about the English Education Act of 1835:
1. It made English the medium of higher education.
2. It was passed under Lord Dalhousie on the basis of Wood's recommendations.
3. It dealt a fatal blow to the district and tahsildari vernacular schools of Madras.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
178.x: Statement 1 is correct: English became the medium of higher education. Statement 2 is wrong: the Act was passed under Bentinck on the basis of Macaulay's Minute; Dalhousie and Wood belong to 1853-54. Statement 3 is correct: the 1835 resolution was a fatal blow to Madras district/tahsildari vernacular schools. Hence '1 and 3 only'.
178.tq: 1835 = Bentinck + Macaulay; 1854 = Dalhousie + Wood.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 correct: it made **English the medium of higher education**.
Statement 2 wrong: it was passed under **Bentinck**, on **Macaulay's Minute** — not Dalhousie or Wood.
Statement 3 correct: it dealt a **fatal blow** to Madras **district/tahsildari vernacular schools**.
xa: **Dalhousie's Minute (1853)** later backed vernacular education.
Critics say its **downward filtration** neglected mass literacy.

178.s:
Consider the following statements about Wood's Despatch of 1854:
1. It was drafted by Sir Charles Wood as President of the Board of Control.
2. It was issued under Governor-General Lord William Bentinck.
3. It proposed universities in the presidency towns on the model of London University.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
178.x: Statement 1 is correct: Wood drafted it as President of the Board of Control. Statement 2 is wrong: it was issued under Dalhousie, not Bentinck. Statement 3 is correct: Calcutta, Bombay and Madras universities (1857) followed the London University model. So '1 and 3 only'; '1 only' misses 3, and the options with 2 are wrong.
178.tq: Wood's Despatch = Wood (Board of Control) + Dalhousie + London model; Bentinck belongs to 1835.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 correct: drafted by **Sir Charles Wood**, President of the **Board of Control**.
Statement 2 wrong: it came under **Dalhousie**, not **Bentinck**.
Statement 3 correct: universities in presidency towns on the **London University** model.
xa: The universities: **Calcutta, Bombay, Madras (1857)**.
Epithet: **"Magna Carta of English Education in India"**.

178.s: Which of the following represents the graded educational hierarchy envisaged by Wood's Despatch?
o: Universities → affiliated colleges → Anglo-vernacular schools → vernacular primary schools
Vernacular primary schools → Anglo-vernacular high schools → affiliated colleges → universities
Anglo-vernacular schools → universities → primary schools → affiliated colleges
Affiliated colleges → vernacular primary schools → universities → high schools
178.x: The Despatch proposed a hierarchy beginning with vernacular primary schools and progressing through Anglo-vernacular high schools and affiliated colleges to universities.
178.tq: Read the educational structure from its base upward.
xs: **Vernacular primary schools → Anglo-vernacular high schools → affiliated colleges → universities** — option **(2)**.
Primary schools were at the **base** of Wood's graded hierarchy.
xa: It also brought **grants-in-aid** for private (largely missionary) enterprise.
English for **higher**, vernacular for **lower** education.

178.s: Which one of the following was a provision of Wood's Despatch of 1854?
o: Replacement of English by Persian in higher education
Exclusive state control over every school
Introduction of grants-in-aid to encourage private educational enterprise
Abolition of all vernacular primary schools
178.x: Wood's Despatch introduced a grants-in-aid system to encourage private, largely missionary, educational enterprise.
178.tq: Identify the positive institutional provision among reversed policy statements.
xs: Wood's Despatch introduced **grants-in-aid** to encourage **private educational enterprise** — option **(3)**.
Much of that enterprise was **missionary**.
It did not replace English with Persian or abolish vernacular schools — it kept them at the base.
xa: Result-based grants-in-aid to primary schools came from **1877-78** in Andhra.
It also called for **training of teachers**.

178.s:
With reference to Wood's Despatch, consider the following statements:
1. It recommended government supervision of vernacular education.
2. It provided for the training of teachers.
3. It prescribed English for higher education and vernacular languages for lower education.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
178.x: Wood's Despatch recommended supervision of vernacular education, teacher training, and a differentiated language policy using English at higher levels and vernacular languages at lower levels.
178.tq: Test the provisions together and watch for the language-level distinction.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Wood's Despatch provided **government supervision of vernacular education** and **training of teachers**.
It prescribed **English for higher** and **vernacular for lower** education.
xa: It set up universities on the **London University** model: **Calcutta, Bombay, Madras (1857)**.
It is the **"Magna Carta of English Education in India"**.

178.s: Which document is called the 'Magna Carta of English Education in India'?
178.x: Wood's Despatch (1854), drafted by Sir Charles Wood under Dalhousie, is called the Magna Carta of English Education in India. Macaulay's Minute (1835) led to the English Education Act, the Hunter Commission (1882) dealt with primary and secondary education, and the Charter Act (1813) sanctioned Rs 1 lakh for education.
178.tq: Magna Carta of English education = Wood's Despatch 1854.
xs: **Wood's Despatch, 1854** is called the **"Magna Carta of English Education in India"** — option **(2)**.
**Macaulay's Minute** led to the **1835** English Education Act; the **Hunter** Commission came in **1882**.
xa: It was drafted by **Sir Charles Wood** under **Dalhousie**.
**Madras University** followed on **5 September 1857**.

178.s:
Consider the following statements about the Hunter Commission:
1. It recommended that schools be handed over to local boards and municipalities.
2. It gave attention to the education of backward classes, especially Muslims, and of women.
3. It was appointed in 1882 during the Viceroyalty of Lord Curzon.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
178.x: Statement 1 is correct: Hunter recommended handing schools to local boards and municipalities. Statement 2 is correct: it stressed education of backward classes (esp. Muslims) and women. Statement 3 is wrong: the 1882 Hunter Commission was under Ripon; Curzon is linked with the 1902 Universities Commission. Hence '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' leaves out 2, and options with 3 are wrong.
178.tq: Hunter 1882 = Ripon; Curzon = 1902 Universities Commission.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: schools went to **local boards and municipalities**.
Statement 2 correct: it stressed **backward classes (esp. Muslims) and women**.
Statement 3 wrong: Hunter (**1882**) was under **Ripon**, not Curzon.
xa: ⚠ **Hunter 1882** = Ripon; **Universities Commission 1902** = Curzon.
It also wanted **qualified Indians** in the education department.

178.s: The Indian Universities Commission of 1902 led to the:
178.x: The 1902 Indian Universities Commission led to the Indian Universities Act of 1904, which increased government control over universities.
178.tq: Link the commission to its immediate legislative outcome.
xs: The **Indian Universities Commission (1902)** led to the **Indian Universities Act 1904** — option **(4)**.
The Act brought **tighter government control of universities**.
xa: It was under **Curzon**.
The **1913** Resolution came next, under **Hardinge II**.

178.s:
Consider the following statements about the Resolution on Education Policy, 1913:
1. It was a response to Gopal Krishna Gokhale's demand for compulsory primary education.
2. It led to the Indian Universities Act, 1904.
3. It was issued during the Viceroyalty of Lord Hardinge II.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
178.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: the 1913 Resolution came under Hardinge II and answered Gokhale's demand for compulsory primary education, with funding for primary education. Statement 2 is wrong: the Indian Universities Act, 1904 followed Curzon's Universities Commission of 1902, nine years before the Resolution. So '3 only' is incomplete and the options with 3 are wrong.
178.tq: 1913 = Hardinge II + Gokhale's primary-education demand; 1904 Act = Curzon.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
1 is correct: the **1913 Resolution** responded to **Gokhale's** demand for **compulsory primary education**.
2 is wrong: the **Indian Universities Act 1904** followed **Curzon's** Universities Commission of **1902**.
3 is correct: it came under **Hardinge II**.
xa: The **Hartog Committee (1929)** under **Irwin** studied primary education **wastage and stagnation**.
The **Sadler Commission** (**1917-19**) under **Chelmsford** examined **Calcutta University**.
The **Sargent Plan (1944)** under **Wavell** proposed universal free compulsory education for **6-14** years.

178.s: Which educational sequence was recommended by the Sadler Commission?
o: Twelve-year school course followed directly by a four-year degree
Twelve-year school course, an intermediate stage and a three-year degree
Ten-year school course followed directly by a two-year degree
Eight-year school course followed by a five-year degree
178.x: The Sadler Commission recommended a 12-year school course, an intermediate stage, and a three-year degree.
178.tq: Compare the duration and intermediate stage instead of relying only on the commission name.
xs: Sadler recommended a **12-year school course**, an **intermediate stage**, then a **3-year degree** — option **(2)**.
It dealt with **university education** (**Calcutta University**).
xa: Sadler sat in **1917-19** under **Chelmsford**.
**Hartog (1929)** returned to primary-education **wastage and stagnation**.

178.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
178.x: The Hartog Committee of 1929 was associated with Lord Irwin, not Lord Wavell. Wavell was the Viceroy associated with the Sargent Plan of 1944.
178.tq: Locate the swapped Viceroy in a multi-column factual match.
xs: **Hartog Committee — 1929 — Wavell** is wrongly matched — option **(4)**; Hartog was under **Irwin**.
**Wavell** goes with the **Sargent Plan (1944)**.
Sadler–**Chelmsford**, Hunter–**Ripon** and Universities Commission–**Curzon** are correct.
xa: The **1913** Resolution came under **Hardinge II**.
⚠ **Hunter 1882** = Ripon; **Universities Commission 1902** = Curzon.

178.s:
Consider the following statements about the Sargent Plan:
1. It was formulated in 1944.
2. It envisaged universal free and compulsory education for children aged 6-14 years.
3. It was drawn up during the Viceroyalty of Lord Irwin.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
178.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Sargent Plan (1944) proposed universal free compulsory education for 6-14 years. Statement 3 is wrong: it came under Wavell; Irwin was the Viceroy of the Hartog Committee (1929). Hence '1 only' and '2 only' are incomplete and '1, 2 and 3' is wrong.
178.tq: Sargent 1944 = Wavell, 6-14 years; Hartog 1929 = Irwin.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
1 and 2 are correct: the **Sargent Plan (1944)** proposed **universal free compulsory education** for **6-14** years.
3 is wrong: it came under **Wavell**; **Irwin** was Viceroy at the time of the **Hartog Committee (1929)**.
xa: **Hartog Committee**: **Philip Hartog**; continued priority to vernacular education.
**Hunter Commission (1882)**: appointed by **Lord Ripon**.
The **1913 Resolution** (Hardinge II) gave funding for primary education.

178.s: The result-based grants-in-aid to primary schools in Andhra were introduced from:
178.x: In Andhra, result-based grants-in-aid to primary schools began from 1877-78.
178.tq: Distinguish the Andhra follow-up date from the dates of the main education policies.
xs: Result-based **grants-in-aid** to primary schools came from **1877-78** — option **(2)**.
It was a **Wood's Despatch** follow-up.
**1883-84** is when **Hunter**'s recommendations took effect.
xa: Wood's Despatch (**1854**) began grants-in-aid for private, largely **missionary**, enterprise.
**Hindu College, Visakhapatnam** was set up in **1878**.

178.s: Which missionary organisation was the first missionary body to spread Western education in Andhra?
178.x: The London Missionary Society was the first missionary body associated with the spread of Western education in Andhra. It began its work in 1805.
178.tq: Directly identify the earliest organisation from a group of closely related missionary bodies.
xs: The **London Missionary Society** was the first missionary body (**1805**) — option **(4)**.
**Kadapa** became its centre in **1824**.
xa: **North German Society**: Rajahmundry and Eluru (**1843**).
**Church Missionary Society**: **Machilipatnam** (**Rev. Robert Noble**).
**American Baptists**: Rayalaseema, **Ongole** and **Nellore**.

178.s: The institution at Machilipatnam founded by Reverend Robert Noble is presently known as
178.x: The Machilipatnam institution founded by Reverend Robert Noble and upgraded in 1864 is now known as Noble College.
178.tq: Discriminate among similarly named colleges by linking the institution to its founder and location.
xs: Rev. Robert Noble's Machilipatnam institution is today **Noble College** — option **(1)**.
He founded the school in **1843** for the **Church Missionary Society**; it became a college in **1864**.
**Mrs A.V.N. College** is the old Hindu College, Visakhapatnam; **Khallikota College** is in **Berhampur**.
xa: Some notes say **1813** or **1841**, or credit the **LMS**.
⚠ **Noble** = Machilipatnam (**1843**); **G.N. Taylor** = Narsapur (**1852**).

178.s: The Central Collegiate Institute at Madras, established in 1841, was the forerunner of which institution?
178.x: The Central Collegiate Institute, Madras, established in 1841, was the forerunner of Presidency College.
178.tq: Match the predecessor institution with the later college it developed into.
xs: The **Central Collegiate Institute, Madras (1841)** was the forerunner of **Presidency College** — option **(1)**.
**Noble College** is at Machilipatnam; **Hindu College** at Visakhapatnam (**1878**); **Khallikota** at Berhampur (**1879**).
xa: **Madras University** came on **5 September 1857**.
**1841** is also when the **CMS** began work in Krishna-Godavari.

178.s:
Arrange the following developments in Rajahmundry in chronological order:
A. Establishment of the Government second-grade college
B. Elphinstone's scheme
C. Establishment of the regional school
D. Conversion into a degree college
178.x: Elphinstone's scheme dates to 1839, the regional school to 1854, the second-grade college to 1873 and the degree college to 1877.
178.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the two intervening institutional stages by year.
xs: Order: **Elphinstone's scheme (1839)** → regional school (**1854**) → second-grade college (**1873**) → degree college (**1877**) — option **(1) B, C, A, D**.
Elphinstone's scheme produced **only one** regional school, at **Rajahmundry**.
xa: Rajahmundry was the base of **Veeresalingam**'s reform journalism.
AP angle: **Noble (1843)**, **G.N. Taylor (Narsapur 1852)** and **Rajahmundry (1854/1873)**.

178.s:
The Anglo-Vernacular School established at Narsapur in 1852 had branches at which of the following places?
1. Palakollu
2. Penugonda
3. Achanta
4. Eluru
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
178.x: The Narsapur Anglo-Vernacular School had branches at Palakollu, Penugonda and Achanta. Eluru was associated with the North German Society, not listed as a branch of this school.
178.tq: Separate the places directly linked with one institution from a nearby missionary centre.
xs: The Narsapur school had branches at **Palakollu, Penugonda, Achanta** — option **(1) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
**Eluru** was a **North German Society** centre, not a branch.
xa: The school was set up in **1852** by **G.N. Taylor**.
Taylor drafted the **1854 Godavari District Education Scheme**.

178.s: Who drafted the 1854 Godavari District Education Scheme?
178.x: G.N. Taylor drafted the Godavari District Education Scheme in 1854 while serving as Sub-Collector of Godavari.
178.tq: Avoid the founder-substitution trap by associating the scheme with the official who prepared it.
xs: **G.N. Taylor** drafted the **1854 Godavari District Education Scheme** — option **(3)**.
**Rev. Robert Noble** founded the Machilipatnam school; **Father Heyer** led Lutherans in **Guntur**; **Elphinstone**'s scheme (**1839**) gave Rajahmundry its school.
xa: Taylor was **Sub-Collector** of Godavari.
He founded the **Anglo-Vernacular School, Narsapur (1852)**.

178.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Mrs A.V.N. College — former Hindu College, Visakhapatnam
178.x: Noble College is located at Machilipatnam, not Rajahmundry. Hindu College was established at Visakhapatnam and is now known as Mrs A.V.N. College, while Khallikota College is at Berhampur.
178.tq: Find the wrong location by checking each institution-place pairing.
xs: **Noble College — Rajahmundry** is wrongly matched — option **(2)**; Noble College is at **Machilipatnam**.
**Mrs A.V.N. College** = former **Hindu College, Visakhapatnam** (**1878**); **Khallikota College** = **Berhampur** (**1879**).
xa: Noble's school (**1843**) became a college in **1864**.
Rajahmundry got a government second-grade college in **1873**.

178.s:
Match List-I (Mission) with List-II (Area of work in Andhra):
List-I
a. North German Society
b. Lutherans under Father Heyer
c. American Baptists
d. London Missionary Society
List-II
i. Guntur
ii. Rajahmundry and Eluru
iii. Rayalaseema, Ongole and Nellore
iv. Kadapa
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
178.x: Correct: North German Society - Rajahmundry and Eluru (1843); Lutherans under Father Heyer - Guntur; American Baptists - Rayalaseema, Ongole and Nellore; London Missionary Society - Kadapa (centre in 1824). Option B swaps the German Society and the Lutherans; option C swaps the Lutherans and the Baptists; option D swaps the German Society and the LMS.
178.tq: Father Heyer = Guntur; Baptists = Ongole/Nellore; Germans = Rajahmundry/Eluru.
xs: **North German–Rajahmundry and Eluru; Lutherans (Heyer)–Guntur; American Baptists–Rayalaseema, Ongole, Nellore; LMS–Kadapa** — option **(1) a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv**.
The North German Society came to Rajahmundry and Eluru in **1843**.
xa: The **LMS** was the first missionary body (**1805**); Kadapa centre in **1824**.
The **Church Missionary Society** worked at **Machilipatnam**.
Mission schools admitted **Sudras and Panchamas**.

178.s: The Machilipatnam National College became notable as a centre of Home Rule protests in:
178.x: The Machilipatnam National College was a centre of Home Rule protests in 1917.
178.tq: Discriminate among close years associated with a political institution.
xs: The **Machilipatnam National College** was a centre of **Home Rule** protests in **1917** — option **(3)**.
It grew from Rev. **Robert Noble**'s **1843** school.
xa: Noble's school became a college in **1864**.
Noble worked for the **Church Missionary Society**.

178.s: Rajahmundry was an important base for the reform journalism of:
178.x: Rajahmundry served as the base of Kandukuri Veeresalingam’s reform journalism.
178.tq: Identify the reformer associated with the place and activity.
xs: Rajahmundry was the base of **Kandukuri Veeresalingam**'s reform journalism — option **(2)**.
English education created the **reformist middle class** of coastal Andhra, e.g. Veeresalingam.
xa: Rajahmundry: regional school **1854**, second-grade college **1873**, degree college **1877**.
The **North German Society** worked in Rajahmundry and Eluru (**1843**).

178.s: Which of the following sequences is in the correct chronological order?
o: Madras University — Central Collegiate Institute — Noble School — grants-in-aid system
Central Collegiate Institute — Noble School — Madras University — grants-in-aid system
Noble School — Central Collegiate Institute — grants-in-aid system — Madras University
Central Collegiate Institute — Madras University — Noble School — grants-in-aid system
178.x: The correct order is Central Collegiate Institute (1841), Noble School (1843), Madras University (1857), and the grants-in-aid system linked to results (1877–78).
178.tq: Place the earliest and latest items first, then resolve the middle dates.
xs: Order: **Central Collegiate Institute (1841)** → **Noble School (1843)** → **Madras University (1857)** → **grants-in-aid (1877-78)** — option **(2)**.
The result-based **grants-in-aid system** was a **Wood's Despatch** follow-up, hence after the university.
xa: Noble's school became a college in **1864**.
**Hindu College, Visakhapatnam** followed in **1878**.

178.s: Who contributed most to the early spread of Western education in Andhra?
178.x: Western education in Andhra was first spread by Christian missionaries (APPSC key), beginning with the London Missionary Society in 1805 and followed by the CMS, North German, Lutheran and American Baptist missions. Zamindars, the Mahajana Sabha and karanams were not the pioneers.
178.tq: Western education in Andhra = missionaries first (LMS 1805).
xs: Western education in Andhra was first spread by **Christian missionaries** — option **(2)** (APPSC key for "who contributed most").
The **London Missionary Society (1805)** was the first missionary body.
xa: Mission schools admitted **Sudras and Panchamas**.
Wood's **grants-in-aid** encouraged largely **missionary** enterprise.

178.s: Which of the following correctly describes a significance of English education in coastal Andhra?
o: It eliminated the need for primary education among the masses
It prevented the emergence of a pan-Indian educated elite

179.tq: Start from the sure founder–newspaper pairs and eliminate codes.
xs: Correct pairs: **a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Amrita Bazar Patrika** = **Sisir Kumar and Motilal Ghosh**; **The Hindu** = **G. Subramania Iyer, M. Veeraraghavachariar**.
**The Bengalee** = **Surendranath Banerjea**; **Kesari** = **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** (**1881**).
xa: The Hindu: **Madras, 1878**, English.
Amrita Bazar Patrika became an **English** paper overnight (**1878**) to escape the **VPA**.
**Sambad Kaumudi** = **Ram Mohan Roy**; **Andhra Prakasika** = **A.P. Parthasarathy Naidu**.

179.s: India's first newspaper, the Bengal Gazette (Calcutta General Advertiser) of 1780, was started by:
179.x: James Augustus Hicky started the Bengal Gazette on 29 January 1780, India's first newspaper. Ram Mohan Roy ran Sambad Kaumudi, Surendranath Banerjea The Bengalee, and Sisir Kumar Ghosh (with Motilal Ghosh) the Amrita Bazar Patrika.
179.tq: First newspaper = Hicky's Bengal Gazette, 1780.
xs: **James Augustus Hicky** started the **Bengal Gazette**, India's first newspaper, on **29 January 1780** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Ram Mohan Roy** ran **Sambad Kaumudi**; **Surendranath Banerjea** ran **The Bengalee**; **Sisir Kumar Ghosh** (with Motilal) ran **Amrita Bazar Patrika**.
xa: It was also called the **Calcutta General Advertiser**.
⚠ First printing press = **Goa (1556)**, by **Portuguese Jesuits**.
First political magazine of Andhra = **Andhra Prakasika**.

179.s:
Consider the following statements about early Indian journals:
1. Sir Syed Ahmad Khan's Tahzeeb-ul-Akhlaq (1870) was published in Urdu.
2. His Mirat-ul-Akhbar (1822) was published in Urdu.
3. Raja Ram Mohan Roy's Sambad Kaumudi (1821) was published in Bengali.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
179.x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Mirat-ul-Akhbar was in Persian. Statement 1 is correct. So 1 and 3 only.
179.tq: Mirat-ul-Akhbar = Persian.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
1 is correct: **Sir Syed Ahmad Khan**'s **Tahzeeb-ul-Akhlaq** (**1870**) was in **Urdu**.
2 is wrong: **Mirat-ul-Akhbar** (**1822**) was **Raja Ram Mohan Roy**'s, published in **Persian**.
3 is correct: Roy's **Sambad Kaumudi** (**1821**) was in **Bengali**.
xa: Roy shut **Mirat-ul-Akhbar** in protest against the **Licensing Regulations** of **1823**.
The first newspaper was **Hicky's Bengal Gazette** (**29 January 1780**).
**Samachar Chandrika** (**Bhavani Charan Bandyopadhyay**) opposed Rammohan Roy.

179.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
179.x: Satyaduta dates to 1835; it was not the journal published from Masulipatnam in 1848. Hitavadi was associated with Masulipatnam and J. Edmund Sharky.
179.tq: Find the single swapped date-and-place association.
xs: **Satyaduta — Masulipatnam 1848** is wrongly matched — so option **(4)** is the answer.
**Satyaduta** dates to **1835**; the **1848 Masulipatnam** journal was **Hitavadi** of **J. Edmund Sharky**.
The other pairs are right: **Dinavartamani** criticised the **1857** revolt; **Vartamana Tarangini (1842)** = **Sayyad Rahamtulla**.
xa: **Vrittanti** came from **Madras, 1837-38**.
Dinavartamani ran **1855-72**.
**Veeresalingam's** first journal: **Vivekavardhini (1874)**.

179.s: Which of the following was NOT among the journals associated with Kandukuri Veeresalingam?
179.x: Andhra Kesari was associated with Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao. Veeresalingam was associated with Vivekavardhini, Hasyasanjivani and Sati Hitabodhini, among others.
179.tq: Use the odd association within a list of publications.
xs: **Andhra Kesari** was not Veeresalingam's — it was **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao's** — so option **(4)** is the answer.
Veeresalingam ran **Vivekavardhini (1874)**, **Hasyasanjivani (1876)** and **Sati Hitabodhini (1883)**.
xa: His other journals: **Satyasamvardhini (1891)** and **Zenana Patrika (1894)**.
Gadicherla's others: **Navayugam**, **Matru Seva**, **Panchayati Rajyam**.
**Chilakamarti** = **Desamata**.

179.s:
Consider the following statements about the Telugu press:
1. Desamata of Chilakamarti supported the Home Rule movement, along with Andhra Patrika and Krishna Patrika.
2. The series 'Telugu Prajala Prasthuta Paristhiti' in The Hindu was written by Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
179.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the series was by Sitarama Sastri of Guntur; Gadicherla ran Andhra Kesari, Navayugam and others. So 1 only.
179.tq: Sitarama Sastri wrote in The Hindu.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
1 is correct: **Desamata** (**Chilakamarti**), **Andhra Patrika** and **Krishna Patrika** supported the Home Rule movement.
2 is wrong: the series **"Telugu Prajala Prasthuta Paristhiti"** in **The Hindu** was by **Sitarama Sastri (Guntur)**.
xa: **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao** ran **Andhra Kesari**, **Navayugam**, **Matru Seva**, **Panchayati Rajyam**.
**Andhra Prakasika** (**A.P. Parthasarathy Naidu**) was the **first political magazine of Andhra**.
**Hitavadi** (**1848**, **Masulipatnam**) was founded by **J. Edmund Sharky**.

179.s:
Arrange the following press laws in chronological order:
A. Registration Act
B. Licensing Regulations
C. Press Act of Metcalfe
D. Censorship of Press Act
179.x: The sequence is Censorship of Press Act (1799), Licensing Regulations (1823), Metcalfe’s Press Act (1835), and Registration Act (1867).
179.tq: Arrange by the years first, then verify the middle two laws.
xs: Order **D, B, C, A** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Censorship of Press Act (1799)** → **Licensing Regulations (1823)** → **Metcalfe's Press Act (1835)** → **Registration Act (1867)**.
xa: Then came **Sedition, Sec. 124A (1870)** and the **Vernacular Press Act (1878)**.
Later: **Newspapers Act 1908** and **Indian Press Act 1910**, both under **Minto II**.
⚠ **Metcalfe** = "liberator" (**1835**); **Lytton** = gag (**1878**); **Ripon** = repeal (**1882**).

179.s:
Consider the following statements about the Licensing Regulations of 1823:
1. They were issued under John Adams, the acting Governor-General.
2. Printing without a licence was penalised.
3. They freed the Indian press and earned their author the title 'liberator of the Indian press'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
179.x: Statement 1 is correct: the 1823 rules were issued by acting G-G John Adams. Statement 2 is correct: printing without a licence was penalised. Statement 3 is wrong: it was Metcalfe's Act of 1835 that repealed the 1823 rules and earned him the title 'liberator of the Indian press'. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
179.tq: 1823 Adams = gag; 1835 Metcalfe = liberator.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: the **1823** rules were issued by **John Adams** (acting Governor-General).
Statement 2 correct: a **licence** was needed; printing without one was penalised.
Statement 3 wrong: **Metcalfe's Act (1835)** repealed the 1823 rules and earned him the title **"liberator of the Indian press"**.
xa: **Ram Mohan Roy** shut **Mirat-ul-Akhbar** in protest.
Earlier: **Censorship of Press Act (1799)**, **Wellesley**.

179.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Registration Act was enacted in 1867.
2. It dealt with the registration of printers and presses.
3. It was associated with John Lawrence.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
179.x: All three statements are correct. The 1867 Registration Act, formally linked with the Press and Registration of Books framework, concerned registration of printers and presses under John Lawrence.
179.tq: Test year, authority and provision together.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
The **Registration Act (1867)**, under **John Lawrence**, covered **registration of printers and presses** (Press and Registration of Books Act).
xa: It was replaced by the **Press and Registration of Periodicals Act, 2023**, w.e.f. **1 March 2024**.
The RNI is now the **Press Registrar General of India**.
John Lawrence also opened telegraph links with **Europe (1864-69)**.

179.s:
Consider the following statements about colonial press laws:
1. The Newspapers (Incitement to Offences) Act, 1908, under Minto II, let magistrates seize the presses of papers inciting violence.
2. The Indian Press Act, 1910, revived features of the Vernacular Press Act with heavy security deposits.
3. Sedition under Section 124A IPC ('exciting disaffection') was introduced under Ripon.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
179.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Section 124A dates from 1870, under Mayo; Ripon repealed the VPA in 1882. So 1 and 2 only.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
1 is correct: the **Newspapers (Incitement to Offences) Act, 1908** (**Minto II**) let magistrates seize presses of papers inciting violence.
2 is correct: the **Indian Press Act 1910** revived VPA features with heavy **security deposits**.
3 is wrong: **Section 124A** (sedition) dates from **1870** under **Mayo**; **Ripon** repealed the VPA in **1882**.
xa: **Metcalfe** (**1835**) is the **"liberator of the Indian press"**.
**Licensing Regulations 1823** under **John Adams** (acting).
Annie Besant's **New India** had to deposit **Rs 2,000**, then **Rs 10,000** under the Press Act.

179.s: Which sequence correctly represents the broad development of press policy in colonial India?
o: Freedom after Metcalfe — gag of 1878 — repeal in 1882 — repression in 1908 and 1910
Gag of 1878 — freedom after Metcalfe — repeal in 1882 — repression in 1908 and 1910
Repression in 1908 — repeal in 1882 — gag of 1878 — freedom after Metcalfe
Repeal in 1882 — gag of 1878 — freedom after Metcalfe — repression in 1910
179.x: Metcalfe’s 1835 measure brought relative freedom, the 1878 Act imposed restrictions, it was repealed in 1882, and repression returned through the 1908 and 1910 measures.
179.tq: Trace the policy trend rather than merely ordering isolated dates.
xs: Sequence: **freedom after Metcalfe (1835)** → **gag of 1878** → **repeal in 1882** → **repression in 1908 and 1910** — so option **(1)** is correct.
After the **1882** repeal came about **25 years** of relative freedom, until the post-**Swadeshi** laws.
xa: **Metcalfe** = "liberator of the Indian press".
**Lytton's** VPA = "**Gagging Act**"; **Ripon** repealed it.
**1908** = Newspapers (Incitement to Offences) Act; **1910** = Indian Press Act.

179.s: The Vernacular Press Act of 1878 was introduced in the background of:
o: The Swadeshi movement and the First Factory Act
The famine of 1876–77 and the lavish Delhi Durbar of 1877
The Revolt of 1857 and the Ilbert Bill controversy
The Permanent Settlement and the Regulating Act
179.x: The Act was passed by Lord Lytton amid public anger over the 1876–77 famine and the lavish Delhi Durbar held in 1877.
179.tq: Connect a law with its immediate political and economic context.
xs: The VPA came amid anger over the **1876-77 famine** and the lavish **Delhi Durbar (1877)** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was passed by **Lord Lytton**.
xa: It was nicknamed the **"Gagging Act"**.
It applied only to **Indian-language** papers, not English ones.
Repealed in **1882** by **Ripon**.

179.s:
Consider the following statements about the Vernacular Press Act, 1878:
1. District magistrates could make printers and publishers of vernacular papers sign bonds not to publish seditious matter.
2. A paper could obtain exemption by submitting proofs to a government censor before publication.
3. An appeal against the magistrate's action lay to the High Court.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
179.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: magistrates could demand bonds, and exemption was available by submitting proofs to a government censor. Statement 3 is wrong: there was no appeal to a court of law. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
179.tq: VPA: bonds, deposits, seizure, NO appeal; exemption only via pre-censorship.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **district magistrates** could make printers/publishers sign **bonds** not to publish seditious matter.
Statement 2 correct: exemption only by **submitting proofs to a government censor**.
Statement 3 wrong: there was **no appeal to a court of law**.
xa: Magistrates could also demand forfeitable **security deposits** and **seize presses** for repeat offences.
Targets: **Som Prakash, Bharat Mihir, Dacca Prakash, Samachar**.

179.s: Which of the following was NOT a provision of the Vernacular Press Act, 1878?
o: Security deposits could be demanded and forfeited
There was no appeal to a court of law
Presses could be seized for repeated offences
English-language newspapers were subjected to the same restrictions
179.x: The Act was discriminatory: it applied to Indian-language papers and not to English-language newspapers. The other three were provisions of the Act.
179.tq: Find the exception by testing the discriminatory scope of the law.
xs: The VPA did **not** cover **English-language newspapers** — so option **(4)** is the answer.
It was **discriminatory**: it applied only to **Indian-language** papers.
**Security deposits**, **no appeal** and **seizure of presses** were all real provisions.
xa: **Amrita Bazar Patrika** turned **English** overnight to escape it.
Passed by **Lytton** (**1878**); repealed by **Ripon** (**1882**).

179.s:
Consider the following statements about the Vernacular Press Act, 1878:
1. Som Prakash was among the papers it targeted.
2. To escape it, The Hindu turned itself into an English paper overnight.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
179.x: Statement 1 is correct: targets included Som Prakash, Bharat Mihir, Dacca Prakash and Samachar. Statement 2 is wrong: it was Amrita Bazar Patrika that became English overnight; The Hindu was already in English. So 1 only.
179.tq: Amrita Bazar Patrika dodged the VPA by going English.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
1 is correct: VPA targets were **Som Prakash**, **Bharat Mihir**, **Dacca Prakash**, **Samachar**.
2 is wrong: it was **Amrita Bazar Patrika** that turned into an **English** paper overnight (**1878**).
xa: The VPA was **Lord Lytton**'s **"Gagging Act"**, passed amid anger over the **1876-77 famine** and the **Delhi Durbar (1877)**.
It applied to Indian-language papers, **not English ones**; **no appeal** to a court of law.
**Som Prakash** was associated with **Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar**.

179.s:
Consider the following statements about the repeal of the Vernacular Press Act:
1. After the repeal, the pre-censorship clause was dropped and a press commissioner was appointed.
2. It was repealed in 1882 by Lord Lytton.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
179.x: Statement 2 is wrong: Lytton passed the Act in 1878; Ripon repealed it in 1882. Statement 1 is correct. So 1 only.
179.tq: Lytton gagged (1878), Ripon freed (1882).
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
1 is correct: after repeal the **pre-censorship clause** was dropped and a **press commissioner** appointed.
2 is wrong: the VPA was passed by **Lytton** (**1878**) and repealed in **1882** by **Lord Ripon**.
xa: Under the VPA, **district magistrates** could demand **bonds** and **security deposits** and **seize presses**.
After the repeal came about **25 years** of relative freedom, until the **1908** and **1910** Acts.

179.s:
Consider the following statements about T.B. Macaulay:
1. He led the Anglicist group.
2. He wrote his Minute as Law Member and President of the General Committee of Public Instruction.
3. His Minute was approved by Lord Dalhousie.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
179.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Minute of 1835 was approved by Lord William Bentinck. So 1 and 2 only.
179.tq: Macaulay's Minute 1835 = Bentinck.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
1 is correct: **T.B. Macaulay** led the **Anglicists**.
2 is correct: he wrote the Minute (**1835**) as **Law Member** and **President of the General Committee of Public Instruction**.
3 is wrong: the Minute was approved by **Lord William Bentinck**, not Dalhousie.
xa: Bentinck is called the **"Father of Modern Western Education in India"**.
Orientalists: **H.T. Colebrooke**, **H.H. Wilson**; in Madras **Thomas Munro** backed vernacular schooling.
**Munro's Survey of Indigenous Education (1826)** found a wide network of village schools.

179.s: Which of the following was associated with the Orientalist group?
179.x: H.T. Colebrooke was an Orientalist. H.H. Wilson was another prominent Orientalist, whereas Macaulay, Bentinck and Trevelyan were associated with the Anglicist side.
179.tq: Identify the camp affiliation of a named protagonist.
xs: **H.T. Colebrooke** was an **Orientalist** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Macaulay** (leader), **Bentinck** and **Charles Trevelyan** were **Anglicists**.
xa: **H.H. Wilson** was another Orientalist; in Madras **Thomas Munro** backed vernacular schooling.
**Munro's Survey (1826)** found a wide network of vernacular village schools.
**Bentinck** = "Father of Modern Western Education in India".

179.s: Thomas Munro's Survey of Indigenous Education in 1826 found:
o: No organised system of village education in Madras
A complete absence of pathashalas in rural areas
Only English-medium colleges in the presidency towns
A wide network of vernacular village schools in the Madras Presidency
179.x: Munro's 1826 survey found a wide network of vernacular village schools in the Madras Presidency.
179.tq: Use the survey's empirical finding to reject absolute claims about indigenous education.
xs: **Munro's Survey of Indigenous Education (1826)** found a **wide network of vernacular village schools** in the **Madras Presidency** — so option **(4)** is correct.
So options claiming no system or no pathashalas are wrong; Munro himself **backed pathashalas and vernacular schooling**.
xa: Munro is counted on the **Orientalist** side, in Madras.
Munro's collectorate and tahsildari schools (**2** in Kadapa, **1** Nellore, **2** Vizag by **1830**) were closed in **1836**.
The **1835 Resolution** banned regional-language instruction in Madras district schools.

179.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Thomas Munro — English-only education in Madras
179.x: Thomas Munro supported pathashalas and vernacular schooling, not English-only education in Madras. Colebrooke and Wilson were Orientalists, while Trevelyan was an Anglicist.
179.tq: Find the reversed position of a regional education-policy protagonist.
xs: **Thomas Munro — English-only education** is wrongly matched — so option **(3)** is the answer.
Munro **backed pathashalas and vernacular schooling** in Madras.
The rest are right: **H.H. Wilson** and **H.T. Colebrooke** = **Orientalists**; **Charles Trevelyan** = **Anglicist**.
xa: Anglicist leader: **T.B. Macaulay**, with **Bentinck**.
**Munro's Survey (1826)** found a wide network of vernacular village schools.
Orientalists favoured **Sanskrit, Arabic, Persian**; Anglicists **Western science + English literature**.

179.s:
Consider the following statements about Macaulay's Minute (1835):
1. It aimed at a class 'English in blood and colour, but Indian in taste, in opinions, in morals and in intellect'.
2. It recommended that education funds be spent only on English-medium teaching of Western science and literature.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
179.x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: it is reversed; the class was to be 'Indian in blood and colour, but English in taste, in opinions, in morals, and in intellect'. So 2 only.
179.tq: Indian in blood, English in taste.
xs: Only statement **2** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
2 is correct: the Minute wanted education funds **exclusively** for **English-medium** teaching of Western science and literature.
1 is wrong: it is reversed — the class was to be "**Indian in blood and colour, but English in taste**, in opinions, in morals, and in intellect".
xa: Famous remark: "a **single shelf** of a good European library was worth the whole native literature of India and Arabia" (APPSC-G2 **2025**).
**Downward Filtration Theory**: educate a few upper-class Indians → knowledge filters to the masses.
The **1835** Resolution banned regional-language instruction in Madras district schools.

179.s: Which of the following best describes the Downward Filtration Theory?
o: A small upper class should first be educated so that learning would filter down to the masses
Education should begin with village schools and move upward to universities
Traditional learning should filter into English institutions through translation
Primary education should be universal before higher education is introduced
179.x: The theory proposed educating a small upper class first, expecting knowledge to descend or filter down to the wider population.
179.tq: Translate the policy theory into its practical educational sequence.
xs: **Downward Filtration**: educate a **few upper-class Indians** so knowledge **filters down to the masses** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Starting from village schools upward is the reverse — that was the ladder of **Wood's Despatch**, which **rejected** downward filtration.
xa: The theory relates to **education** (**APPSC-G2 2024**).
Wood's Despatch asked the Company to take up **mass instruction**.
It grew from **Macaulay's Minute (1835)**.

179.s: Which statement correctly reflects Macaulay's view expressed in the Minute?
o: European literature should be excluded from Indian education.
A single shelf of a good European library was worth the whole native literature of India and Arabia.
Arabic and Sanskrit literature alone should receive public funds.
The whole native literature of India and Arabia was superior to European literature.
179.x: Macaulay made the well-known comparison that a single shelf of a good European library was worth the whole native literature of India and Arabia.
179.tq: Recognise the exact author–remark association and avoid reversing the comparison.
xs: Macaulay wrote that **"a single shelf of a good European library was worth the whole native literature of India and Arabia"** — so option **(2)** is correct.
He wanted funds **exclusively** for English-medium Western learning, the opposite of options 1, 3 and 4.
xa: The remark was asked in **APPSC-G2 2025**.
Macaulay led the **Anglicists**; **H.T. Colebrooke** and **H.H. Wilson** were Orientalists.
The Minute was approved by **Bentinck** in **1835**.

179.s:
Consider the following statements about Wood's Despatch:
1. It recommended grants-in-aid.
2. It asked the Company to take up mass instruction.
3. It supported the downward filtration of education from a few upper-class Indians.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
179.x: Wood's Despatch recommended grants-in-aid and mass instruction. It rejected, rather than supported, the downward filtration approach.
179.tq: Spot the reversed policy position in the statement about downward filtration.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: Wood's Despatch recommended **grants-in-aid**.
Statement 2 correct: it asked the Company to take up **mass instruction**.
Statement 3 wrong: it **rejected downward filtration**.
xa: Called the **"Magna Carta of English Education in India"**; dated **1854**, under **Dalhousie**.
Ladder: **vernacular primary** → **Anglo-vernacular high school** → **university**.
Universities of **Calcutta, Bombay, Madras** followed in **1857**.

179.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the Anglicists from the Orientalists?
o: Anglicists favoured Persian learning, whereas Orientalists favoured English literature
Anglicists favoured Western science and English literature, whereas Orientalists favoured classical Sanskrit, Arabic and Persian learning
Both groups rejected Western science and English education
Both groups demanded only vernacular primary education
179.x: Anglicists supported Western science and English literature, while Orientalists supported Sanskrit, Arabic and Persian learning.
179.tq: Use the reversed-comparison trap to distinguish two rival educational positions.
xs: **Anglicists** favoured **Western science and English literature**; **Orientalists** favoured **Sanskrit, Arabic and Persian** learning — so option **(2)** is correct.
Option 1 reverses the two camps.
xa: Orientalists: **H.T. Colebrooke**, **H.H. Wilson**; in Madras **Thomas Munro**.
Anglicists: **T.B. Macaulay** (leader), **Bentinck**, **Charles Trevelyan**.
Macaulay's Minute (**1835**) settled the debate for English.

179.s: Which of the following statements about the 1835 educational resolution is correct?
o: It transferred Madras schools to municipalities
It introduced regional-language instruction in all Madras district schools
It established the first universities in India
It banned regional-language instruction in Madras district schools
179.x: The 1835 resolution banned regional-language instruction in Madras district schools.
179.tq: Test the exact policy direction and avoid replacing a ban with an introduction.
xs: The **1835 Resolution** **banned regional-language instruction** in **Madras district schools** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The first universities came later, in **1857**, after **Wood's Despatch**.
xa: Munro's collectorate and tahsildari schools were closed in **1836**.
By **1830** these schools were **2** in Kadapa, **1** in Nellore, **2** in Vizag.
The resolution followed **Macaulay's Minute**, approved by **Bentinck**.

179.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Charter Act of 1813 provided not less than Rs 1 lakh a year for literature and science.
2. The money under the 1813 Act was released only in the 1830s.
3. The General Committee of Public Instruction (1823) was set up mainly to train teachers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
179.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the 1813 Act set aside at least Rs 1 lakh a year, but the money was released only in the 1830s. Statement 3 is wrong: the GCPI managed education funds; it was not a teacher-training body. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
179.tq: GCPI = manager of the education fund.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: the **Charter Act 1813** set aside not less than **Rs 1 lakh** a year for literature and science.
Statement 2 correct: the money was released only in the **1830s**.
Statement 3 wrong: the **General Committee of Public Instruction (1823)** **managed education funds**.
xa: The 1813 Act also **allowed missionaries**.
**Macaulay** was later President of the General Committee of Public Instruction.

179.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Wood's Despatch (1854) is called the 'Magna Carta of English Education in India'.
2. Following it, universities were set up at Calcutta, Bombay and Madras in 1857.
3. The Hunter Commission on education is usually dated 1854.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
179.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Hunter Commission is usually dated 1882 (some say appointed 1880). So only two.
179.tq: 1854 Wood, 1857 universities, 1882 Hunter.
xs: **Only two** statements (1 and 2) are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
1 is correct: **Wood's Despatch (1854)** = **"Magna Carta of English Education in India"**.
2 is correct: universities at **Calcutta, Bombay, Madras** followed in **1857**.
3 is wrong: the **Hunter Commission** is usually dated **1882** (some notes: appointed **1880**).
xa: Wood's Despatch introduced **grants-in-aid** and a vernacular primary → Anglo-vernacular → university ladder.

179.s:

179.x: I, II and III are correct: faster movement, communication and troop movement were official reasons. IV is false because the colonial aim was to bring British goods into Indian markets, not to expand markets for Indian goods.
179.tq: Separate official reasons from the colonial economic aim.
n: Railway development officially aimed to enable faster movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #135 · pp 238-239]
Railway development officially aimed to improve communication. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #135 · pp 238-239]
Railway development officially aimed to facilitate troop movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #135 · pp 238-239]
The colonial economic purpose of railway development was to transport British goods to Indian markets. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #135 · pp 238-239]
xs: Statements **I, II and III** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Official aims: **faster movement**, **improved communication**, **support for administration** and **troop movement**.
IV is wrong: the colonial purpose was to carry **British goods to Indian markets**, not Indian goods.
xa: Colonial economic purpose: **raw materials to ports**, **British goods** inland.
Guarantee system: **5%** return from Indian revenues.
Railways also moved grain for **famine relief**.

179.s: Which of the following correctly expresses the colonial economic purpose of railway development?
o: Indian goods to ports and raw materials to British markets
Raw materials to ports and British goods to Indian markets
British goods to ports and Indian goods to British markets
Troops to markets and raw materials to administrative centres
179.x: The colonial economic aim was to carry raw materials to the ports for export and to carry British goods into Indian markets. The other options reverse or confuse this flow.

n: The colonial economic purpose of railway development was to transport raw materials to ports. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #135 · pp 238-239]

xs: The colonial purpose was to carry **raw materials to ports and British goods to Indian markets** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The other options reverse or confuse this flow of **raw materials** out and **British manufactures** in.
xa: Officially railways were meant for **faster movement**, **communication**, **administration** and **troop movement**.
Guaranteed interest on railways was counted in the **"drain"** of wealth.
Unintended effect: an integrated **national market**.

180.s: Which one of the following best describes the principal features associated with Lord Cornwallis's civil service reforms in India?
o: A military service based on hereditary succession and private trade
A merit-based covenanted service, prohibition of private trade and gifts, and promotion by seniority
A wholly Indian civil service recruited through provincial elections
A service recruited exclusively through examinations conducted in India
180.x: Cornwallis established a merit-based covenanted civil service, prohibited private trade and acceptance of gifts, and introduced promotion substantially based on seniority.

xs: Cornwallis built a **merit-based covenanted** service, **banned private trade and gifts**, and gave **seniority promotions** — so option **(2)** is correct.
His service was **dominated by Europeans**, so a "wholly Indian" service is wrong; exams in India came only from **1922**.

Immediate parity between Indians and Europeans in all covenanted posts
Limited Indian entry, mainly into uncovenanted posts, subject to conditions including residence and language examination

xs: The **Indian Civil Services Act 1861** allowed **limited Indian entry**, mainly to **uncovenanted** posts — so option **(4)** is correct.

Consider the following statements about the Aitchison (Public Service) Commission:

180.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Aitchison (1886, Dufferin) replaced covenanted/uncovenanted with Imperial, Provincial and Subordinate services. Statement 3 is wrong: 50:50 parity was the Lee Commission's (1923-24) proposal. Hence '1 and 2 only'.

xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **Aitchison Commission**, **1886**, under **Dufferin**.
Statement 2 correct: it replaced covenanted/uncovenanted with **Imperial, Provincial, Subordinate** services.
Statement 3 wrong: **50:50** parity within **15** years was the **Lee Commission's** proposal.

**Islington (1912-15)** = Indianisation of higher posts.

180.s:
Consider the following statements:

xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Islington (1912-15)** = **Indianisation** of higher posts; **Lee** = **50:50** parity in **15** years; a **PSC** came on **1 October 1926**.

180.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the relevant civil service provisions of the Government of India Act, 1919?
o: It established the Federal Public Service Commission in place of all provincial services.
It abolished the ICS and created the IAS with immediate effect.
It provided for a separate ICS examination in India, enabling simultaneous examinations with England from 1922.

180.x: The Government of India Act, 1919, provided for a separate ICS examination in India; simultaneous examinations were held from 1922, alongside the London examination.
180.tq: Distinguish the enabling legal provision from the later date of actual examination and from post-independence reforms.
xs: The **GoI Act 1919** provided a **separate ICS examination in India**, held from **1922** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **Federal PSC** came with the **GoI Act 1935**; the ICS became the **IAS** in **1947**.
xa: Exams were held at **Allahabad, later Delhi**, alongside London.
This was an INC demand from its first session (**1885**).

180.s: Who described the Indian Civil Service as the 'Steel Frame' of India?

**Cornwallis** is the "Father of Civil Services"; **Ram Mohan Roy** first demanded Indians in higher posts (**1832**).

180.s: Who established the district Diwani and Faujdari Adalats in 1772?

xs: **Warren Hastings** set up district **diwani** (civil) and **faujdari** (criminal) adalats in **1772** — so option **(2)** is correct.

180.s:
With reference to Cornwallis's judicial administration, consider the following statements:

3. Provincial courts of appeal were established at Calcutta, Dacca, Murshidabad and Patna.

180.tq: Test a reform cluster through a coded combination of correct statements.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
Under the **Cornwallis Code (1793)** the **Collector lost judicial powers** and a **District Judge** post was created.
**Provincial courts of appeal** were set up at **Calcutta, Dacca, Murshidabad, Patna**.

180.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly associated with Bentinck's judicial reforms?
o: Abolition of Cornwallis's provincial courts of appeal
Creation of provincial courts of appeal at Dacca and Patna
Transfer of circuit courts' work to Commissioners
Establishment of separate Sadar courts at Allahabad
180.x: The creation of provincial courts of appeal at Dacca and Patna was associated with Cornwallis. Bentinck abolished the provincial courts of appeal and circuit courts, transferred their work to Commissioners, and established separate Sadar courts at Allahabad.

xs: **Creating provincial courts of appeal at Dacca and Patna** was **Cornwallis's**, not Bentinck's — so option **(2)** is the answer.
**Bentinck** **abolished** those courts and circuit courts, gave their work to **Commissioners**, and set up separate Sadar courts at **Allahabad**.
xa: Bentinck also replaced **Persian** with vernacular/English in courts.

180.s: The Supreme Court at Calcutta, set up in 1774 under the Regulating Act of 1773, had as its first Chief Justice:

180.tq: 1773 Act, Supreme Court 1774, CJ Impey.
xs: The first Chief Justice of the **Supreme Court at Calcutta (1774)** was **Sir Elijah Impey** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**C.P. Ilbert** was the Law Member behind the **Ilbert Bill (1883)**; **Macaulay** headed the **Law Commission** (Charter Act **1833**).
xa: The Court was set up under the **Regulating Act 1773**.
The **Indian High Courts Act 1861** later replaced the Supreme Courts and Sadar Adalats.

180.s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of Cornwallis's police reorganisation?
o: The Royal Irish Constabulary model was adopted.
Indian darogas were placed in charge of thanas.
Zamindars were relieved of police duties.

180.s: The principal aim of the Ilbert Bill was to empower Indian:

Till then Europeans were tried **only by European judges**.

180.s: Which of the following correctly describes the outcome of the Ilbert Bill controversy?

The Bill was withdrawn and no compromise was made.
European subjects were placed under village courts.
The Bill was passed without modification.

xs: Ripon **watered the Bill down**: a European tried by an Indian judge could claim a **jury of which at least half were Europeans** — so option **(1)** is correct.
So it was neither withdrawn without compromise nor passed unchanged.
xa: The compromise came in **1884**.
The European protest was the **"White Mutiny"**.
It showed **racial discrimination** persisted.

180.s: The European agitation against the Ilbert Bill is commonly described as the:

xs: The fierce European agitation was called the **"White Mutiny"** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It opposed Indian judges trying **European British subjects**.
xa: Ripon **diluted** the Bill: jury at least **half European** (**1884**).
It showed Indians the value of **organised agitation**.

3. The Indian Association supported the Bill against European agitation.

180.x: All three statements are correct. The controversy revealed British racism, encouraged organised Indian political action and saw the Indian Association support the Bill.

The controversy **exposed British racism** and showed Indians the value of **organised agitation**.
The **Indian Association** **backed** the Bill against the European agitation.
xa: ⚠ Trap: some notes wrongly say the Indian Association "opposed" it.
Bill: **1883**, **Ripon**, Law Member **C.P. Ilbert**.

B. Lord Ripon's Resolution on local self-government

xs: Order **D, B, C, A** — so option **(1)** is correct.
