With reference to the administrative legacy of British rule in India, consider the following statements:
1. Cornwallis, Wellesley and Macaulay contributed to building the administrative ‘steel frame’.
2. The UPSC, CAG and Election Commission can trace their institutional roots to British-era bodies.
3. The administrative legacy was confined exclusively to the police and did not extend to constitutional institutions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
180.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the legacy also extended to institutions whose successors include the UPSC, CAG and Election Commission.
180.tq: Reject the extreme word ‘exclusively’ when the institutional legacy spans several branches of administration.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Cornwallis, Wellesley and Macaulay** built the "steel frame"; **UPSC, CAG and Election Commission** trace roots to British-era bodies.
Statement 3 wrong: the legacy spread well beyond the police.
xa: ICS, codified laws, the **1861** police model and Ripon's local bodies are direct ancestors of today's systems.
**Sardar Patel** called the ICS the **"Steel Frame"**.

180.s:
Assertion (A): The High Courts replaced both the Supreme Courts and the Sadar Adalats.
Reason (R): The Indian High Courts Act of 1861 provided the foundation for the High Court system.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
180.x: Both are true and R explains A: the Indian High Courts Act of 1861 empowered the Crown to set up High Courts and abolished the Supreme Courts and Sadar Adalats, so the High Courts replaced both under that Act.
180.tq: Ask whether the Reason names the law that brought about the Assertion.
n: The Indian High Courts Act was enacted in 1861. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #134 · pp 237-238]
The Indian High Courts Act of 1861 laid the foundation of the High Court system. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #134 · pp 237-238]
The High Courts replaced the Supreme Courts. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #134 · pp 237-238]
The High Courts replaced the Sadar Adalats. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #134 · pp 237-238]
The 1861 Act led to the establishment of the 1862 Courts. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #134 · pp 237-238]
xs: **Both A and R are true**, and R is the **correct explanation** of A — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Indian High Courts Act** (**1861**) laid the **foundation** of the **High Court system**.
Under it the **High Courts replaced** the **Supreme Courts** and the **Sadar Adalats**.
xa: The first High Courts: **Calcutta, Bombay, Madras** (**1862**); **Allahabad** **1866**.
The High Courts were established through **Letters Patent** issued under **Crown authority**.
The **Federal Court** came under the **GoI Act 1935**.

180.s:
Assertion (A): The High Courts were established through Letters Patent.
Reason (R): The Letters Patent were issued under Crown authority.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
180.x: Both are true and R explains A: the High Courts were set up by Letters Patent, which were instruments issued under the authority of the Crown.
180.tq: Check whether R is the cause of A.
n: Letters Patent were the instruments of establishment of the High Courts. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #134 · pp 237-238]
The Letters Patent were issued under Crown authority. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #134 · pp 237-238]
xs: **Both A and R are true**, and R is the **correct explanation** of A — so option **(1)** is correct.
The High Courts were established by **Letters Patent** — the **instruments** of establishment.
The Letters Patent were **issued under Crown authority**.
xa: The **Indian High Courts Act 1861** laid the foundation of the system.
**Calcutta, Bombay, Madras** — first set, **1862**.
Codes under **Canning**: **CPC 1859**, **IPC 1860**, **CrPC 1861**.

180.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Calcutta High Court belonged to the first set of High Courts.
II. Bombay High Court belonged to the first set of High Courts.
III. Madras High Court belonged to the first set of High Courts.
IV. Allahabad High Court belonged to the first set of High Courts.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
180.x: I, II and III are correct: Calcutta, Bombay and Madras High Courts were the first set, set up in 1862. IV is false because the Allahabad High Court came later, in 1866.
180.tq: Recall which High Courts were set up in 1862.
n: The Calcutta High Court was part of the first set of High Courts. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #134 · pp 237-238]
The Bombay High Court was part of the first set of High Courts. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #134 · pp 237-238]
The Madras High Court was part of the first set of High Courts. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #134 · pp 237-238]
The Allahabad High Court was established in 1866. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #134 · pp 237-238]
xs: Statements **I, II and III** are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Calcutta**, **Bombay** and **Madras** High Courts were the **first set**, formally established in **1862**.
IV is wrong: **Allahabad** High Court came in **1866**.
xa: They were set up under the **Indian High Courts Act 1861**.
They replaced the **Supreme Courts** and **Sadar Adalats**.
The **Supreme Court at Calcutta** dated from **1774** (Regulating Act **1773**).

180.s: Which sequence correctly represents the early development of the High Court system?
o: 1861 Act → 1866 Calcutta, Bombay and Madras → 1862 Allahabad
1862 Act → 1861 Calcutta, Bombay and Madras → 1866 Allahabad
1866 Act → 1862 Calcutta, Bombay and Madras → 1861 Allahabad
1861 Act → 1862 Calcutta, Bombay and Madras → 1866 Allahabad
180.x: The Indian High Courts Act came in 1861, Calcutta, Bombay and Madras High Courts were set up in 1862, and Allahabad followed in 1866. The other options mix up these years.
180.tq: Arrange the Act and the courts by year.
n: The Indian High Courts Act was enacted in 1861. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #134 · pp 237-238]
Calcutta, Bombay and Madras were the first High Courts. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #134 · pp 237-238]
The Calcutta High Court was established in 1862. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #134 · pp 237-238]
The Bombay High Court was established in 1862. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #134 · pp 237-238]
The Madras High Court was established in 1862. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #134 · pp 237-238]
The Allahabad High Court was established in 1866. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #134 · pp 237-238]
The 1861 Act led to the establishment of the 1862 Courts. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #134 · pp 237-238]
xs: **1861 Act → 1862 Calcutta, Bombay and Madras → 1866 Allahabad** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **Indian High Courts Act** came in **1861**; the first three High Courts in **1862**; **Allahabad** followed in **1866**.
xa: The High Courts were set up by **Letters Patent** under Crown authority.
**Bentinck** had set up separate Sadar courts at **Allahabad** earlier.
**IPC** **1860**, **CrPC** **1861** — both under **Canning**.

180.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Macaulay Committee
(b) Aitchison Commission
(c) Lee Commission
(d) Federal and Provincial PSCs

List-II
(i) 1935
(ii) 1924

n: The Macaulay Committee was formed in 1854. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #107 · pp 199-200]
The Aitchison Commission was formed in 1886/87. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #107 · pp 199-200]
The Lee Commission was formed in 1924. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #107 · pp 199-200]
Federal and Provincial Public Service Commissions existed in 1935. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #107 · pp 199-200]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Macaulay Committee** **1854**; **Aitchison Commission** **1886/87**; **Lee Commission** **1924**; **Federal and Provincial PSCs** **1935**.
xa: Aitchison created **Imperial, Provincial, Subordinate** services.
Lee recommended **50:50** Indian-European parity and a PSC (set up **1 October 1926**).
**Islington** Commission (**1912-15**) — Indianisation of higher posts.

180.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. Public Service Commission established
B. Government of India Act provided for civil service examination in India
C. Examination held in India and England
D. Lee Commission associated with Public Service Commission
180.x: The 1919 Act provided for an examination in India, the examination was held in India and England in 1922, the Lee Commission came in 1924, and the Public Service Commission was set up in 1926, giving B, C, D, A.
180.tq: Arrange the events by year.
n: The Government of India Act of 1919 provided for the Civil Service examination in India. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #107 · pp 199-200]
The Civil Service examination was held in India and England in 1922. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #107 · pp 199-200]
The Lee Commission was formed in 1924. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #107 · pp 199-200]
The Public Service Commission was established in 1926. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #107 · pp 199-200]
xs: The correct order is **B, C, D, A** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**GoI Act 1919** provided for an exam in India → exam held in India and England in **1922**.
**Lee Commission** (**1924**) → **Public Service Commission** established in **1926**.
xa: The exam in India was held at **Allahabad**, later **Delhi**.
The **INC** had demanded **simultaneous examinations** from its first session (**1885**).
In **1941** the ICS had **617** Indians and **585** Europeans.

181.s: Which one of the following was NOT a condition of the Subsidiary Alliance devised by Lord Wellesley?
o: The ruler had to maintain a British subsidiary force at his own cost
The ruler had to accept a British Resident
The ruler had to exclude other Europeans from his service
The ruler could freely conduct an independent foreign policy
181.x: A subsidiary ally had to surrender independent foreign-policy control. The other conditions were part of the system devised by Wellesley.
181.tq: Spot the option that reverses the central consequence of the alliance.
xs: A subsidiary ally could **not** run an **independent foreign policy** — so option **(4)** is the answer.
Real terms: keep a **British subsidiary force** at his cost, accept a **British Resident**, no other **Europeans** in service.
xa: The ruler also had to **disband his own army**; unpaid subsidy → **ceding territory**.
Devised by **Lord Wellesley, 1798**.
First to accept: **Nizam of Hyderabad** (**September 1798**).

181.s:
Arrange the following Subsidiary Alliance acceptances in chronological order:
A. Bhonsle of Berar
B. Awadh
C. Scindia
D. Peshwa
181.x: Awadh accepted the alliance in November 1801, the Peshwa in December 1802 (Treaty of Bassein), Bhonsle of Berar in December 1803 and Scindia in February 1804.
181.tq: Place Awadh (1801) and the Peshwa (1802) first, then distinguish the 1803 and 1804 agreements.
xs: Order **B, D, A, C** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Awadh (November 1801)** → **Peshwa (December 1802**, Treaty of Bassein) → **Bhonsle of Berar (December 1803)** → **Scindia (February 1804)**.
xa: Earlier: **Hyderabad (September 1798)**, **Mysore (1799)**, **Tanjore (October 1799)**.
Last Maratha to sign: **Holkar (1818)**.

181.s: The 1800 treaty involving the Nizam resulted in the cession of the Rayalaseema districts, which came to be known as the
181.x: The Nizam ceded the Rayalaseema districts in 1800 to meet the cost of the subsidiary force; these became known as the Ceded Districts.
181.tq: Link the treaty, territorial transfer and historical regional name.
xs: The Rayalaseema districts ceded in **1800** became the **"Ceded Districts"** — so option **(4)** is correct.
They paid for the **subsidiary force** kept for the Nizam.
xa: The Nizam was the **first** subsidiary ally (**September 1798**), again **1800**.
AP angle: asked in **APPSC G2 2002, 2008**.

181.s: The first Indian ruler to accept Wellesley's Subsidiary Alliance (September 1798) was the:
181.x: The Nizam of Hyderabad was first, in September 1798 (and again in 1800). Mysore followed in 1799, Awadh in November 1801, and the Peshwa signed through the Treaty of Bassein.
181.tq: First subsidiary ally = Nizam, 1798.
xs: The **Nizam of Hyderabad** was first, in **September 1798** (again **1800**) — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Mysore** followed in **1799**, **Awadh** in **November 1801**, the **Peshwa** in **December 1802** (Treaty of Bassein).
xa: AP angle: asked in **APPSC G2 2002, 2008**.
The **1800** treaty created the **"Ceded Districts"** (Rayalaseema).

181.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Doctrine of Lapse:
1. It was associated with Lord Dalhousie.
2. An adopted son could inherit the ruler's private property.
3. An adopted son could automatically inherit the throne of the dependent state.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
181.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Under the policy, an adopted son could inherit private property but not the throne.
181.tq: Separate private-property succession from succession to political sovereignty.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: it was **Dalhousie's** policy.
Statement 2 correct: adoption was allowed only for **private property**.
Statement 3 wrong: an adopted son **could not inherit the throne**.
xa: Withdrawn by **Queen Victoria's Proclamation** (**1 November 1858**), which **recognised adoption**.
**APPSC-GS 2018** called it "the policy of annexation devised by the EIC".

181.s: Lord Dalhousie announced the Doctrine of Lapse in
181.x: Lord Dalhousie formulated and applied the Doctrine of Lapse from 1848.
181.tq: Use the earliest date in the sequence of Dalhousie’s annexations and policies.
xs: Dalhousie applied the **Doctrine of Lapse** from **1848** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**1853** = **Jhansi** lapsed; **1856** = **Awadh** annexed for misgovernment.
xa: First lapse annexation: **Satara (1848)**.
Dalhousie's term: **1848-56**.

181.s: The policy of annexation under the Doctrine of Lapse was formally abandoned after the Revolt of 1857 through
181.x: Queen Victoria’s Proclamation, read by Canning at the Allahabad Durbar on 1 November 1858, abolished the policy and recognised adoption.
181.tq: Connect the policy change with the correct proclamation, date and official occasion.
xs: **Queen Victoria's Proclamation** (**1 November 1858**) abandoned annexation — so option **(4)** is correct.
It was read by **Canning** at the **Allahabad Durbar**; the Treaty of Bassein was the Peshwa's subsidiary alliance.
xa: It **recognised adoption**.
Canning called the princes **"breakwaters to the storm"**.
After **1858** the Crown guaranteed princely states in return for **paramountcy**.

181.s: Which of the following grievances was associated with Nana Saheb?
o: Denial of the pension of his adoptive father, Baji Rao II
Refusal to recognise his adopted son as ruler of Jhansi
Removal from the Red Fort and loss of the imperial title
181.x: Nana Saheb, the adopted son of Peshwa Baji Rao II, was denied the pension of his adoptive father.
181.tq: Match the leader with his personal political grievance, avoiding swapped revolutionary leaders.
xs: **Nana Saheb** was denied the pension of his adoptive father **Baji Rao II** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Jhansi** throne = **Rani Lakshmibai**; **Jagdishpur** estates = **Kunwar Singh**; Red Fort/title = **Bahadur Shah Zafar**.
xa: Baji Rao II was the **last Peshwa**.
Nana Saheb led the revolt at **Kanpur**.

181.s: Dalhousie announced that the successors of Bahadur Shah would have to leave the
o: Red Fort and move to the Qutub at Mehrauli
Qutub at Mehrauli and move to Calcutta
Agra Fort and move to Delhi
Allahabad Fort and move to Lucknow
181.x: Dalhousie declared that Bahadur Shah’s successors would have to leave the Red Fort and move to the Qutub at Mehrauli.
181.tq: Use the place pair—Red Fort and Qutub, Mehrauli—to avoid confusing Mughal centres.
xs: **Dalhousie** said Bahadur Shah's successors must **leave the Red Fort** and move to the **Qutub, Mehrauli** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The move was from the **Red Fort** to the **Qutub**, not the reverse; Calcutta, Agra and Allahabad play no part.
xa: ⚠ **Dalhousie** = leave the **Red Fort**; **Canning (1856)** = lose the **imperial title**.
Bahadur Shah Zafar's grievance: loss of **title and Red Fort** for his successors.

181.s: What did Canning announce in 1856 regarding the successors of Bahadur Shah Zafar?
o: They would receive pensions equal to those of the Peshwas
They would lose the imperial title and become mere princes
They would be recognised as governors of Awadh
They would inherit the imperial title and the Red Fort
181.x: Canning announced that after Bahadur Shah Zafar, his successors would lose the imperial title and would be treated merely as princes.
181.tq: Distinguish Canning’s announcement about imperial status from Dalhousie’s order about residence.
xs: **Canning (1856)** announced the successors would **lose the imperial title** and be **mere princes** — so option **(2)** is correct.
This would apply after **Bahadur Shah Zafar**; they would not inherit the title or the Red Fort.
xa: ⚠ **Dalhousie** had said they must **leave the Red Fort** for the **Qutub, Mehrauli**.
Bahadur Shah Zafar led the revolt at **Delhi**.

181.s: Which of the following titles were abolished in 1855?
o: The titles of the Nizam and the Peshwa
The titles of the Raja of Satara and the ruler of Jhansi
The titles of the Mughal emperor and the Nawab of Awadh
The titles of the Carnatic Nawab and the Tanjore Raja
181.x: The titles of the Carnatic Nawab and the Tanjore Raja were abolished in 1855.
181.tq: Match the year with the two specific titles rather than with rulers affected by the Doctrine of Lapse.
xs: In **1855** the titles of the **Carnatic Nawab** and the **Tanjore Raja** were abolished — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **Mughal** title was only threatened for Bahadur Shah's successors (Canning, **1856**), and **Awadh** was annexed in **1856** for misgovernment.
xa: **Nana Saheb** was denied his father's pension.
**Pindaris and irregular troops** were disbanded, adding to unemployment.
Mughal successors were to lose the **Red Fort** (Dalhousie) and the **imperial title** (Canning).

181.s: Who among the following was deposed and exiled to Calcutta after the annexation of Awadh?
181.x: Nawab Wajid Ali Shah was deposed after Awadh was annexed and was exiled to Calcutta.
181.tq: Use the ruler–territory association to avoid swapping rulers of different annexed states.
xs: Nawab **Wajid Ali Shah** was deposed and exiled to **Calcutta** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Birjis Qadr** was **Begum Hazrat Mahal's** son, proclaimed ruler in **1857**; **Bahadur Shah Zafar** was at Delhi.
xa: Awadh was annexed in **1856** for **"misgovernment"**.
The **Summary Revenue Settlement (1856)** dispossessed the **taluqdars**.

181.s:
With reference to the Summary Revenue Settlement introduced in Awadh in 1856, consider the following statements:
1. The settlement was made directly with village proprietors.
2. Taluqdars were dispossessed of their estates.
3. Taluqdars were allowed to retain their arms and forts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
181.x: The settlement was made directly with village proprietors, while taluqdars lost their estates, were disarmed and had their forts demolished. Statement 3 is false.
181.tq: Find the false statement by checking the reversal of a specific administrative consequence.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: settlement was made **directly with village proprietors**.
Statement 2 correct: **taluqdars were dispossessed** of their estates.
Statement 3 wrong: taluqdars were **disarmed** and their **forts demolished** (UPSC **2026** key).
xa: It "deeply alienated the **sepoys** and the **landed aristocracy**".
The Bengal Army drew heavily from **Awadh**.

181.s: The annexation of Awadh particularly alienated the Bengal Army sepoys because
o: most Bengal Army sepoys were recruited from Punjab alone
their families in Awadh were affected by the new revenue burden
their own regiments were immediately disbanded
they were denied promotion to the rank of Resident
181.x: The Bengal Army drew heavily from Awadh, and the new revenue burden directly affected the families of its sepoys.
181.tq: Link the social base of recruitment with the direct effect of annexation on soldiers’ families.
xs: The **Bengal Army** drew heavily from **Awadh**, and sepoys' **families bore the new revenue burden** — so option **(2)** is correct.
So the sepoys were **hurt directly** by the annexation; Awadh, not Punjab, was the recruiting ground.
xa: The Nawab's **lords, officials, retainers and soldiers** were thrown out of work.
Awadh became a **centre of unrest**.
Settlement: **Summary Revenue Settlement (1856)**.

181.s: Begum Hazrat Mahal’s political grievance during the Revolt of 1857 was primarily connected with
o: the loss of the Red Fort by Mughal successors
the annexation of Awadh and the proclamation of her son Birjis Qadr as ruler
the confiscation of Kunwar Singh’s estates
the denial of Baji Rao II’s pension
181.x: Begum Hazrat Mahal opposed the annexation of Awadh and had her son Birjis Qadr proclaimed ruler.
181.tq: Match the leader with the specific grievance and associated claimant.
xs: **Begum Hazrat Mahal** (Lucknow) resented the **annexation of Awadh**; her son **Birjis Qadr** was proclaimed ruler — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **Red Fort** grievance was **Bahadur Shah Zafar's**; the **pension** grievance **Nana Saheb's**.
xa: ⚠ **Kanpur** = Nana Saheb; **Lucknow** = Begum Hazrat Mahal; **Jagdishpur** = Kunwar Singh; **Bareilly** = Khan Bahadur Khan.
Awadh's Nawab **Wajid Ali Shah** was exiled to Calcutta.

181.s: Which of the following states was annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse in spite of the presence of an adopted heir whose succession was refused?
181.x: Rani Lakshmibai’s adopted son, Damodar Rao, was not recognised as heir and Jhansi was annexed in 1853.
181.tq: Pair the adopted heir with the correct state rather than with another annexed territory.
xs: **Jhansi** lapsed (**1853**) after Rani Lakshmibai's **adopted son was denied the throne** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Awadh** was annexed for **misgovernment**, not lapse.
xa: First lapse annexation: **Satara (1848)**.
Lapse withdrawn by **Queen Victoria's Proclamation (1858)**, which **recognised adoption**.

181.s: The fear of annexation among the princes contributed to the Revolt of 1857 by
o: turning a sepoy mutiny into a wider revolt
preventing the participation of Awadh’s landed aristocracy
making the revolt exclusively a movement of zamindars
181.x: Fear of further annexations encouraged princely and aristocratic participation and helped transform the sepoy mutiny into a wider revolt.
181.tq: Apply the political cause to the broader character and spread of the revolt.
xs: The princes' **fear of annexation** turned a **sepoy mutiny into a wider revolt** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Awadh's **landed aristocracy** was deeply alienated, not kept out.
xa: After **1858** the Crown guaranteed princely states in return for **paramountcy**.
**P.E. Roberts** called it "just a sepoy mutiny".

181.s: After 1858, the British Crown guaranteed the princely states in return for their acceptance of
181.x: After 1858, princely states were guaranteed in return for accepting British paramountcy.
181.tq: Distinguish a guarantee under paramountcy from restoration of full sovereignty.
xs: After **1858** the Crown guaranteed princely states in return for **paramountcy** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **Doctrine of Lapse** itself was **abolished** in **1858**, and adoption recognised.
xa: Canning called the princes **"breakwaters to the storm"**.
Proclamation read at the **Allahabad Durbar**, **1 November 1858**.

181.s: The first state annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse (1848) was:
181.x: Satara (1848) was the first state annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse. Jhansi lapsed in 1853 and Nagpur later. Awadh (1856) was annexed for misgovernment, not under lapse.
181.tq: Lapse: Satara first (1848); Awadh was NOT lapse.
xs: **Satara (1848)** was the first state annexed under lapse — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Jhansi** lapsed in **1853**; **Awadh (1856)** was annexed for **misgovernment**, not lapse.
xa: ⚠ First subsidiary ally = **Hyderabad (1798)**; last Maratha to sign = **Holkar (1818)**.
Lapse = ruler dying **without a natural male heir**; adopted son could not inherit the throne.

181.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

(b) Kanpur

181.x: In 1857 Bahadur Shah II led at Delhi, Nana Sahib at Kanpur, Begum Hazrat Mahal at Lucknow and Kunwar Singh at Jagdishpur, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.

**Lucknow** — **Begum Hazrat Mahal**; **Jagdishpur** (Bihar) — **Kunwar Singh**.

181.s: The Revolt of 1857 began at which place?
181.x: The Revolt of 1857 began at Meerut on 10 May 1857, when sepoys rose and marched to Delhi.
181.tq: Recall where the 1857 revolt broke out.
n: Meerut was associated with the beginning of the Revolt of 1857. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
xs: The Revolt of **1857** began at **Meerut** — so option **(4)** is correct.

181.s:
Consider the following statements:

I. Jagdishpur was located in Bihar.
II. Bareilly was associated with Khan Bahadur Khan during the Revolt of 1857.
III. Jagdishpur was associated with Khan Bahadur Khan during the Revolt of 1857.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
181.x: I and II are correct: Jagdishpur is in Bihar, and Khan Bahadur Khan led the 1857 revolt at Bareilly. III is false because Jagdishpur was led by Kunwar Singh.
181.tq: Check each 1857 leader against his centre.
n: Jagdishpur was located in Bihar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
Bareilly was associated with Khan Bahadur Khan during 1857. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
xs: Statements **I and II** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
I is correct: **Jagdishpur** was located in **Bihar**.
II is correct: **Bareilly** was led by **Khan Bahadur Khan**, a **Rohilla** chief who proclaimed himself **Nawab Nizam**.
III is wrong: **Jagdishpur** was led by **Kunwar Singh**.
xa: Kunwar Singh was a zamindar ruined by loss of his estates.
**Faizabad** — **Maulavi Ahmadullah Shah**.
⚠ **Kanpur** = Nana Saheb; **Lucknow** = Begum Hazrat Mahal; **Jagdishpur** = Kunwar Singh; **Bareilly** = Khan Bahadur Khan.

181.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Officer)
a. John Nicholson
b. Hugh Rose
c. Colin Campbell
d. Henry Lawrence

List-II (Role)
i. Relieved and later recaptured Lucknow
ii. Defeated the rebels at Jhansi
iii. Led the assault that recaptured Delhi
iv. Killed while defending the Lucknow Residency
181.x: John Nicholson led the assault on Delhi, Hugh Rose took Jhansi, Colin Campbell relieved and then recaptured Lucknow, and Henry Lawrence died defending the Lucknow Residency in July 1857, giving a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv.
181.tq: Recall each officer's centre and pair repeats in order.
n: John Nicholson was associated with Delhi during the 1857 Revolt. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #121 · pp 221-223]
Hugh Rose was associated with Jhansi and Rani Lakshmibai during the 1857 Revolt. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #121 · pp 221-223]
Colin Campbell was associated with Lucknow during the 1857 Revolt. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #121 · pp 221-223]
Henry Lawrence was associated with Lucknow during the 1857 Revolt. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #121 · pp 221-223]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**John Nicholson** was the British opponent at **Delhi**; **Hugh Rose** was **Rani Lakshmibai**'s opponent at **Jhansi**.
**Colin Campbell** and **Henry Lawrence** were British opponents at **Lucknow** and **Oudh**.
xa: Other British names at Lucknow: **Havelock** and **Neil**.
Lucknow's rebel leader was **Begum Hazrat Mahal**, who proclaimed her son **Birjis Qadr** ruler.
Jhansi had **lapsed** in **1853** when the Rani's adopted son was denied the throne.

181.s: Who was the military commander who fought on behalf of Nana Sahib at Kanpur during the Revolt of 1857?
181.x: Tatya Tope was the military commander at Kanpur, fighting for Nana Sahib, who was the political leader there. Khan Bahadur Khan led at Bareilly and Kunwar Singh in Bihar.
181.tq: Discriminate the commander from the leader at Kanpur.
n: Tatya Tope was the commander at Kanpur. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #121 · pp 221-223]
xs: **Tatya Tope** was the **commander** at **Kanpur** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Nana Sahib** was the leader at Kanpur; **Khan Bahadur Khan** led at **Bareilly**; **Kunwar Singh** in **Bihar**.
xa: Tatya Tope also led in **Central India**.
Nana Sahib was the adopted son of **Peshwa Baji Rao II** and was denied his pension.
**Rani Lakshmibai** led at **Jhansi**.

181.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Centre)
a. Bareilly
b. Bihar/Jagdishpur
c. Faizabad
d. Central India

List-II (Leader)
i. Tatya Tope
ii. Khan Bahadur Khan
iii. Kunwar Singh
iv. Maulavi Ahmadullah Shah
181.x: Khan Bahadur Khan led at Bareilly, Kunwar Singh at Jagdishpur in Bihar, Maulavi Ahmadullah Shah at Faizabad, and Tatya Tope in Central India, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
181.tq: Recall the leader at each centre.
n: The 1857 Revolt was centred at Bareilly under Khan Bahadur Khan. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #121 · pp 221-223]
Khan Bahadur Khan was the leader at Bareilly during the 1857 Revolt. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #121 · pp 221-223]
The 1857 Revolt was centred at Bihar and Jagdishpur under Kunwar Singh. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #121 · pp 221-223]
Kunwar Singh was the leader at Bihar and Jagdishpur during the 1857 Revolt. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #121 · pp 221-223]
The 1857 Revolt was centred at Faizabad under Maulavi Ahmadullah Shah. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #121 · pp 221-223]
Maulavi Ahmadullah Shah was the leader at Faizabad during the 1857 Revolt. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #121 · pp 221-223]
The 1857 Revolt was centred in Central India under Tatya Tope. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #121 · pp 221-223]
Tatya Tope was the leader in Central India during the 1857 Revolt. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #121 · pp 221-223]
xs: The correct match is **a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Bareilly** — **Khan Bahadur Khan**; **Bihar/Jagdishpur** — **Kunwar Singh**.
**Faizabad** — **Maulavi Ahmadullah Shah**; **Central India** — **Tatya Tope**.
xa: **Assam** — **Maniram Dutt**.
Khan Bahadur Khan was a **Rohilla** chief.
**Delhi** — **Bahadur Shah Zafar**, opposed by **John Nicholson**.

181.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Year of the Bihar episode
(b) Opponents in the Bihar episode
(c) Leader associated with the Bihar episode
(d) Significance of Bihar

List-II
(i) Kunwar Singh
(ii) Rebels and the British
(iii) Major centre of the Revolt of 1857
(iv) 1857
181.x: The Bihar rising came in 1857, it pitted rebels against the British, Kunwar Singh of Jagdishpur led it, and Bihar was a major centre of the revolt, giving a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii.
181.tq: Match each attribute of the Bihar rising.
n: The Revolt of 1857 was fought between rebels and the British. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
Kunwar Singh was a leader in Bihar during the Revolt of 1857. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
Bihar was a major centre of the Revolt of 1857. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
xs: The correct match is **a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The Bihar episode was in **1857**, fought between **rebels and the British**.
Its leader was **Kunwar Singh** of **Jagdishpur**; Bihar was a **major centre of the Revolt of 1857**.
xa: Kunwar Singh was a zamindar ruined by loss of his estates.
Other major centres: **Delhi**, **Kanpur**, **Lucknow**, **Jhansi**, **Bareilly**.
The revolt began at **Meerut**.

182.s: Which of the following was an administrative cause of resentment before the Revolt of 1857?
o: Exclusion of Indians from high civil and military posts
Rapid and inexpensive justice for all social groups
Abolition of corruption in lower courts
Admission of Indians to all high civil and military posts
182.x: Indians were excluded from high civil and military posts, producing resentment against the colonial administrative structure.
182.tq: Identify the discriminatory administrative practice.
xs: Indians were **excluded from high civil and military posts** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Justice was in fact **slow and costly**, and **corruption** was rampant in lower courts, so options 2 and 3 are wrong.
xa: Corruption was rampant in **lower courts and police**; justice **favoured the rich**.
Annexations threw thousands of **officials, retainers and soldiers** of princely courts out of work.
In the army an Indian could rise **no higher than Subedar**.

182.s:
Consider the following statements about the lower courts and police before 1857:
1. Corruption was rampant.
2. Justice was slow and costly.
3. The system generally favoured the poor over the rich.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
182.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The judicial system was slow, costly and generally favoured the rich, making statement 3 incorrect.
182.tq: Use the reversed comparison trap in the third statement.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **corruption** was rampant in **lower courts and police**.
Statement 2 correct: justice was **slow and costly**.
Statement 3 wrong: it **favoured the rich**, not the poor.
xa: The administration was also **inefficient and prejudiced**.
Indians were **shut out of high administrative posts**.

182.s: The annexation of princely states adversely affected the colonial administration because it—
o: ended the drain of wealth to Britain
created employment for thousands of court officials and soldiers
restored the authority of all displaced rulers
threw officials, retainers and soldiers of princely courts out of work
182.x: Annexations displaced thousands of officials, retainers and soldiers who had depended on princely courts for employment and patronage.
182.tq: Trace the administrative consequence of annexation.
xs: Annexations **threw officials, retainers and soldiers of princely courts out of work** — so option **(4)** is correct.
They did the opposite of creating jobs; and Company rule kept the **drain of wealth** going.
xa: In Awadh (**1856**), the deposition of **Wajid Ali Shah** cost lords, officials, retainers and soldiers their livelihoods.
**Pindaris and irregular soldiers** were also disbanded.
Annexations also ended **princely/court patronage** of artisans.

182.s:
Which of the following territories were annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse before the Revolt of 1857?
1. Satara
2. Jhansi
3. Nagpur
4. Awadh
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
182.x: Satara, Jhansi and Nagpur were annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse. Awadh was annexed separately in 1856 on the ground of misgovernance.
182.tq: Separate the territories taken under the Doctrine of Lapse from Awadh, which was annexed on a different ground.
xs: **Satara, Jhansi and Nagpur** were taken under lapse — so option **(1) 1, 2 and 3 only** is correct.
**Awadh (1856)** was annexed on grounds of **"misgovernance"**, not lapse.
xa: **Rani Lakshmibai's** adopted son was refused the throne of Jhansi.
**Nana Saheb** was denied his pension.
Awadh's Nawab **Wajid Ali Shah** was deposed.

182.s:
Consider the following statements about the annexation of Awadh:
1. Awadh was annexed in 1856 under the Doctrine of Lapse.
2. Wajid Ali Shah was deposed.
3. Lords, officials, retainers and soldiers lost their livelihoods.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
182.x: Statement 1 is wrong: Awadh was annexed in 1856 on the ground of misgovernance, not the Doctrine of Lapse (which took Satara, Jhansi, Nagpur). Statements 2 and 3 are correct. So B; A, C and D include the false statement 1.
182.tq: Awadh = misgovernance, not lapse.
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 wrong: Awadh (**1856**) was annexed for **"misgovernance"**, not lapse.
Statement 2 correct: **Wajid Ali Shah** was deposed.
Statement 3 correct: **lords, officials, retainers, soldiers** lost their livelihoods.
xa: Awadh was the **"nursery of the Bengal Army"**, so its annexation angered high-caste sepoys.
About **21,000** taluqdars lost estates under the **Summary Settlement of 1856**.

182.s: What was a major consequence of the high and rigid land revenue demand on peasants?
o: They became independent of moneylenders and traders
They were driven into debt and lost land to moneylenders and traders
They were exempted from commercial cultivation
182.x: The heavy revenue burden pushed peasants into debt, often resulting in the loss of their land to moneylenders and traders.
182.tq: Follow the economic cause to its immediate social consequence.
xs: **Heavy, rigid land revenue** drove peasants into **debt**, and they **lost land to moneylenders and traders** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Revenue was collected rigidly under **Permanent/Zamindari**, **Ryotwari** and **Mahalwari** settlements.
xa: **Commercialisation** forced **cash crops** under high taxes.
Sepoys were **"peasants in uniform"** — they carried these rural grievances into the army.
Company rule was seen as **absentee sovereignty** + **drain of wealth**.

182.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The taluqdars of Awadh lost their estates under the 1856 summary settlement.
2. The Inam Commission was set up in Madras in 1852.
3. The Inam Commission confiscated some 20,000 estates whose owners could not show title.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
182.x: Statement 1 is correct: Awadh taluqdars lost estates under the 1856 summary settlement. Statement 2 is wrong: the Inam Commission (1852) was in Bombay, not Madras. Statement 3 is correct: it confiscated about 20,000 estates lacking title. So B; A, C and D include the false statement 2.
182.tq: Inam Commission = Bombay, 1852, ~20,000 estates.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **Awadh taluqdars** lost estates under the **1856 Summary Settlement**.
Statement 2 wrong: the **Inam Commission (1852)** was in **Bombay**, not Madras.
Statement 3 correct: it confiscated some **20,000** estates whose owners could not show title.
xa: ⚠ **21,000** = taluqdars of Awadh (**1856**); **20,000** = Inam Commission estates (**1852**).
Result: a **fiercely anti-British landed class**.

182.s: Which of the following best explains the ruin of Indian artisans and handicrafts before 1857?
o: The Industrial Revolution reduced the supply of British textiles
Indian handicrafts received increased princely patronage after annexations
British machine-made goods entered duty-free, while Indian goods faced heavy tariffs
British goods were excluded from Indian markets
182.x: After the Industrial Revolution, cheap British machine-made goods, especially textiles, entered India duty-free while Indian goods faced heavy tariffs, causing deindustrialisation. A and D reverse this, and B is wrong because annexations ended princely patronage.
182.tq: Compare unequal trade treatment rather than focusing on only one factor.
xs: **British machine-made goods entered duty-free**, while **Indian goods faced heavy tariffs** — so option **(3)** is correct.
This caused **deindustrialisation**; the Industrial Revolution **increased** cheap British goods, esp. **textiles**.
Annexations **ended** princely patronage, so option 2 is wrong.
xa: **Artisans were ruined** by cheap British goods.
Company rule was seen as **absentee sovereignty** draining wealth to Britain.

182.s: The terms ‘absentee sovereignty’ and ‘drain of wealth’ in the context of the causes of 1857 refer primarily to—
o: the movement of peasants from villages to princely courts
the transfer of religious authority from temples to courts
the transfer of economic resources from India to Britain
the migration of British officials to Indian villages
182.x: Company rule was seen as 'absentee sovereignty', rule from distant Britain, under which India's wealth was drained to Britain. Both terms describe resources being transferred from India to Britain.
182.tq: Distinguish an economic concept from unrelated administrative or religious processes.
xs: Both terms describe **economic resources transferred from India to Britain** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Company rule was seen as **absentee sovereignty** (rule from distant Britain) plus a **drain of wealth** to Britain.
xa: Peasants faced **heavy land revenue** and lost land to **moneylenders**.
Artisans were ruined by **duty-free** British goods.

182.s:
Consider the following statements about the abolition of Sati:
1. It was carried out in 1829 under Lord Dalhousie.
2. Orthodox sections resented it as interference in custom.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
182.x: Statement 1 is wrong: Sati was abolished in 1829 under Lord William Bentinck, not Dalhousie. Statement 2 is correct: it was resented as interference in custom. So B; A and C accept the false statement 1, D rejects the true statement 2.
182.tq: Sati 1829 = Bentinck.
xs: Only statement **2** is correct — so option **(2) 2 only** is correct.
Statement 1 wrong: **Sati** was abolished in **1829** by **Bentinck**, not Dalhousie.
Statement 2 correct: it was resented as **interference in custom**.
xa: **Lex Loci Act (1850)**: converts could **inherit ancestral property**.
**Hindu Widow Remarriage Act (1856)** challenged orthodox norms.

182.s:
Consider the following statements about the Lex Loci Act (Religious / Caste Disabilities Act):
1. It was enacted in 1856.
2. It allowed converts to Christianity to inherit ancestral property.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
182.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the Act is of 1850 (1856 is the trap date of the Widow Remarriage Act). Statement 2 is correct: converts could inherit ancestral property, seen as an incentive to convert. So B; A and C accept the false date, D rejects the true statement 2.
182.tq: Lex Loci = 1850; Widow Remarriage = 1856.
xs: Only statement **2** is correct — so option **(2) 2 only** is correct.
Statement 1 wrong: the **Lex Loci / Caste Disabilities Removal Act** is of **1850**; **1856** is the trap date.
Statement 2 correct: converts to Christianity could **inherit ancestral property**, seen as a state **incentive to convert**.
xa: **1856** = **Hindu Widow Remarriage Act**.
**1829** = abolition of **Sati** (Bentinck).

182.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Christian missionaries preached under police protection.
2. Missionaries criticised Hindu and Islamic practices.
3. Western education, railways and the telegraph generated fears of mass conversion.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
182.x: All three statements are correct. Missionary activity under official protection and the spread of Western institutions created apprehensions about religious conversion and the loss of caste identity.
182.tq: Test a cluster of related causes through an all-inclusive option.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
Missionaries **preached under police protection** and **attacked Hindu and Islamic practice**.
**Western education, railways and telegraph** seemed to threaten caste and religion → **fears of mass conversion**.
xa: Other grievances: **taxation of temple and mosque lands**; **racial arrogance** of officials.
After **1858** the Crown promised **religious neutrality** and withdrew state patronage from missionary work.

182.s: Which of the following social measures, resented by orthodox opinion before 1857, was enacted in 1856?
182.x: The Hindu Widow Remarriage Act was passed in 1856 and challenged orthodox norms. Sati was abolished in 1829, the Caste Disabilities Removal (Lex Loci) Act dates to 1850 (1856 is a trap date for it), and the Charter Act grant was 1813.
182.tq: 1829 Sati, 1850 Lex Loci, 1856 Widow Remarriage.
xs: The **Hindu Widow Remarriage Act** was passed in **1856** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Sati** was abolished in **1829**; the **Caste Disabilities Removal Act** is of **1850** (**1856** is the trap date).
xa: ⚠ Some notes date the Religious Disabilities Act to **1856**; the Act is of **1850**.
**1856** also = **General Service Enlistment Act** and the annexation of **Awadh**.

182.s:
Consider the following statements about the General Service Enlistment Act, 1856:
1. It was passed under Lord Canning.
2. It required new recruits to serve only within India.
3. Orthodox Hindu sepoys feared that crossing the sea would mean loss of caste.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
182.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Act was Canning's (1856). Statement 2 is wrong: it required recruits to serve anywhere, including overseas. Statement 3 is correct: sea crossing meant loss of caste for orthodox Hindus. Hence B; A and C include the false statement 2, D includes it too.
182.tq: GSEA = Canning, 1856, service ANYWHERE incl. overseas -> caste fear.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: the **General Service Enlistment Act 1856** was **Canning's**.
Statement 2 wrong: recruits had to serve **anywhere, including overseas**.
Statement 3 correct: **crossing the sea** meant **loss of caste** for orthodox Hindus.
xa: The order to travel by ship **was** a cause (BPSC key).
Earlier: **Barrackpore 1824** — refusal to go to **Burma by sea**.

182.s:
Consider the following statements about bhatta before 1857:
1. Bhatta was a foreign service allowance.
2. It was withdrawn for service in Awadh and Bengal after these became British territory.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
182.x: Statement 1 is correct: bhatta was the foreign service allowance. Statement 2 is wrong: it was withdrawn for service in Sindh and Punjab, not Awadh and Bengal. So A; B, C and D are wrong because statement 2 is false and statement 1 is true.
182.tq: Bhatta = foreign service allowance; withdrawn for Sindh and Punjab.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — so option **(1) 1 only** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **bhatta** was a **foreign service allowance**.
Statement 2 wrong: it was withdrawn for service in **Sindh and Punjab**, now British territory.
xa: **Bhatta mutinies** of the **1840s**: **34th NI 1844**, **66th NI 1849-50**.
Stopping of bhatta **was** a cause (BPSC **2018** key).

182.s: Which of the following was NOT a military grievance of the Indian sepoys mentioned in relation to the Revolt of 1857?
o: The ceiling of promotion at the rank of Subedar
182.x: Inefficiency of officers was identified as not being a cause of sepoy anger. Lower pay, racial contempt and the Subedar ceiling were genuine grievances.
182.tq: Find the one item expressly excluded from the list of grievances.
xs: **Inefficiency of officers** was **not** a cause — so option **(3)** is the answer (**BPSC 2018** key).
**Lower pay** than British soldiers, **racial contempt** and the **Subedar** ceiling were real grievances.
xa: **APPSC-GS 2023**: Subedar ceiling + greased cartridges both correct.
Missionary pressure, the order to travel by ship and stopping of **bhatta** **were** causes.

182.s: An Indian sepoy in the pre-1857 army could ordinarily rise no higher than:
182.x: Racial discrimination restricted the highest rank ordinarily attainable by an Indian soldier to Subedar.
182.tq: Test the exact promotion ceiling rather than general discrimination.
xs: An Indian could rise **no higher than Subedar** — so option **(2)** is correct.
This was part of the **racial discrimination** in pay and promotion.
xa: **APPSC-GS 2023** keyed the Subedar ceiling as correct.
Sepoys got **lower pay** than British soldiers and faced **racial contempt**.
Indians were also shut out of **high civil and military posts**.

182.s: On the eve of the Revolt of 1857, the approximate ratio of Indian sepoys to European soldiers in India was:
182.x: There were about 2.3 lakh Indian sepoys and 45,000 European soldiers, giving an approximate ratio of 5:1.
182.tq: Convert the supplied troop figures into the approximate ratio.
xs: About **2.3 lakh sepoys to 45,000 Europeans** — roughly **5:1** — so option **(4)** is correct.
So sepoys far outnumbered Europeans; ratios like **2:1** or **3:1** understate the gap.
xa: Europeans had been drawn off for the **Crimean and Persian wars**.
**Awadh** was the **"nursery of the Bengal Army"**.

182.s: The expression “peasants in uniform” referred to the fact that the sepoys:
o: Were recruited only from European farming communities
Were trained exclusively in agricultural work
Received land grants instead of salaries
Carried rural and village grievances into the army
182.x: The sepoys were largely drawn from rural communities, so their grievances reflected those of the villages from which they came.
182.tq: Translate a descriptive phrase into its historical implication.
xs: **"Peasants in uniform"**: sepoys **carried rural and village grievances into the army** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Their grievances **mirrored the village's**.
xa: Peasants suffered **heavy land revenue**, **debt** and loss of land to **moneylenders**.
**Awadh** = **"nursery of the Bengal Army"**.

182.s: The Vellore mutiny of 1806 was chiefly triggered by which of the following measures?
o: Introduction of a new dress code and prohibition of caste marks and earrings
Refusal to cross the sea to Burma
Refusal to use the new rifle cartridges
182.x: The new dress code, including a turban with a leather cockade and restrictions on caste marks and earrings, caused resentment among the sepoys at Vellore.
182.tq: Distinguish the cause attached to a specific mutiny.
xs: **Vellore (July 1806)** was triggered by a **new dress code** — turban with **leather cockade**, ban on **caste marks and earrings** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Burma by sea** = **Barrackpore 1824**; **bhatta** = **1840s**; cartridges = **1857**.
xa: **Tipu's sons** were lodged in the Vellore fort.
UPPSC match key: **Vellore = July 1806**; **Barrackpur = Nov 1824**; **Santhal = 1855-56**.

182.s: The Barrackpore mutiny of November 1824 was caused by the sepoys’ refusal to—
182.x: The 47th Native Infantry at Barrackpore refused to go to Burma by sea during the First Anglo-Burmese War.
182.tq: Apply the who–cause–event linkage.
xs: The **47th NI** at Barrackpore (**November 1824**) refused to **go to Burma by sea** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It came during the **First Anglo-Burmese War**.
xa: ⚠ **Barrackpore 1824** (47th NI, Burma) ≠ **Barrackpore 1857** (**Mangal Pandey**, 34th Bengal NI).
**38th NI (1852)** also refused to go to **Burma**.

182.s: The Santhal revolt of 1855–56 is distinguished from the mutinies listed in the context of the 1857 uprising because it was—
o: the first mutiny of the 34th Native Infantry
a civil revolt rather than a sepoy revolt
an uprising caused by the new cartridges
a military revolt over sea service
182.x: The Santhal revolt of 1855–56 was a civil revolt and not a sepoy mutiny.
182.tq: Separate a civil revolt from a military mutiny.
xs: The **Santhal revolt (1855-56)** was a **civil revolt, not a sepoy revolt** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It had nothing to do with cartridges or sea service; those drove the sepoy outbreaks of **1824** and **1857**.
xa: UPPSC key: **Santhal revolt = 1855-56**; **Vellore = July 1806**; **Barrackpur = Nov 1824**.
Bhatta mutinies: **34th NI 1844**, **66th NI 1849-50**.

182.s: Why did the cartridges of the new Enfield rifle offend both Hindu and Muslim sepoys?
o: They were believed to contain cow and pig fat, and had to be bitten open.
They required sepoys to cross the sea before use.
They were made exclusively from animal skin.
They were distributed only to European soldiers.
182.x: The greased-paper cartridges were believed to contain cow fat, offensive to Hindus, and pig fat, offensive to Muslims. Sepoys had to bite them open before loading.
182.tq: Identify the religious implication of the practical loading procedure.
xs: The cartridges were believed to contain **cow and pig fat** and had to be **bitten** open — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Cow** fat offended **Hindus**; **pig** fat offended **Muslims**.
xa: They were read as proof of a **colonial-missionary plot** to force conversion.
Rumours also spoke of **bone dust** in Company flour.

182.s:
Consider the following statements about the rumours that spread before the Revolt of 1857:
1. Bone dust was said to be mixed in the flour supplied by the Company.
2. Mysterious chapatis were passed from village to village across South India in early 1857.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
182.x: Statement 1 is correct: the rumour was that bone dust was mixed in Company flour. Statement 2 is wrong: the chapatis passed village to village across North India, not South India. So '1 only' (A) is right; B, C and D wrongly accept statement 2 or reject statement 1.
182.tq: Rumours = bone dust in flour + chapatis across NORTH India.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — so option **(1) 1 only** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **bone dust** was said to be mixed in **Company flour**.
Statement 2 wrong: the **chapatis** passed across **North India**, not South India.
xa: The **Enfield** cartridges were believed greased with **cow and pig fat**.
All read as a plot to **force conversion**.

182.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the early refusals and outbreaks connected with the Revolt of 1857:
1. The 19th Native Infantry refused at Berhampur in February 1857.
2. Mangal Pandey's action occurred at Barrackpore on 29 March 1857.
3. The Meerut rising began on 10 May 1857.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
182.x: All three statements are correct: the 19th Native Infantry acted at Berhampur in February, Mangal Pandey acted at Barrackpore on 29 March, and the Meerut rising began on 10 May 1857.
182.tq: Link the three events through their locations and dates.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
**19th NI** at **Berhampur** (**February 1857**); **Mangal Pandey** at **Barrackpore** (**29 March 1857**); **Meerut rising** (**10 May 1857**).
xa: Mangal Pandey was hanged on **8 April 1857**.
**9 May**: **85** sepoys of the **3rd Cavalry** sentenced to **10 years**.
**11-12 May**: rebels reach **Delhi**.

182.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Barrackpore mutiny of the 47th Native Infantry
B. Vellore mutiny
C. Berhampur refusal of the new cartridges
D. Mangal Pandey’s attack at Barrackpore
182.x: The correct sequence is Vellore mutiny in July 1806, Barrackpore mutiny in November 1824, Berhampur in February 1857 and Mangal Pandey’s attack on 29 March 1857.
182.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the intervening events.
xs: Order **B, A, C, D** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Vellore (July 1806)** → **Barrackpore 47th NI (November 1824)** → **Berhampur (February 1857)** → **Mangal Pandey (29 March 1857)**.
xa: Then **Meerut** (**10 May 1857**) and **Delhi** (**11-12 May**).
**Santhal revolt (1855-56)** was a civil revolt.

182.s: What immediately preceded the Meerut rising of 10 May 1857?
o: The proclamation of Bahadur Shah II as Shahenshah-e-Hindustan
The sentencing of 85 sepoys of the 3rd Native Cavalry to ten years’ imprisonment
The disbandment of Mangal Pandey’s regiment
The refusal of the 19th Native Infantry to use the rifle
182.x: On 9 May 1857, 85 sepoys of the 3rd Native Cavalry at Meerut were sentenced to ten years. The rising followed on 10 May, when officers were shot and imprisoned comrades were freed.
182.tq: Identify the immediately preceding event rather than the later consequence.
xs: On **9 May 1857**, **85** sepoys of the **3rd Native Cavalry** were sentenced to **10 years** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The rising followed on **10 May**: officers shot, comrades freed, **"Delhi Chalo"**.
**Bahadur Shah II** was proclaimed only after it (**11-12 May**); the other events were earlier.
xa: Mangal Pandey's regiment was disbanded on **8 April 1857**.
**19th NI** refused the cartridges at **Berhampur** in **February 1857**.

182.s: The rebels who reached Delhi on 11–12 May 1857 proclaimed whom as Shahenshah-e-Hindustan?
182.x: After reaching Delhi, the rebels proclaimed Bahadur Shah II as Shahenshah-e-Hindustan on 11–12 May 1857.
182.tq: Match the political title with the associated leader.
xs: Rebels reaching Delhi (**11-12 May 1857**) proclaimed **Bahadur Shah II** **Shahenshah-e-Hindustan** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Kunwar Singh** was at Jagdishpur; **Wajid Ali Shah** had been deposed in **1856**; **Nana Sahib** was at Kanpur.
xa: They came from the **Meerut rising** (**10 May**) with the cry **"Delhi Chalo"**.
Bahadur Shah Zafar's successors were to lose the **Red Fort** and **royal title**.

182.s: P.E. Roberts described the Revolt of 1857 as:
o: A religious war against the British
The First War of Indian Independence
182.x: P.E. Roberts characterized the revolt as “just a sepoy mutiny,” particularly in connection with the cartridge issue.
182.tq: Separate the British interpretive label from the nationalist interpretation.
xs: **P.E. Roberts** called it **"just a sepoy mutiny"** over the greased cartridges — so option **(2)** is correct.
**"First War of Independence"** is **V.D. Savarkar's** view.
xa: Savarkar: **The Indian War of Independence, 1857** (**1909**).
The revolt in fact combined **peasant, princely and sepoy** grievances.
**S.N. Sen**: **Eighteen Fifty-Seven** (**1957**, centenary volume).

182.s: Who wrote *Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind* on the causes of the Indian Revolt?
182.x: Sir Syed Ahmed Khan wrote *Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind*, meaning “The Causes of the Indian Revolt.”
182.tq: Match the author with the exact title of the work.
xs: **Sir Syed Ahmed Khan** wrote **Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind** ("The Causes of the Indian Revolt", **1859**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**S.N. Sen** wrote **Eighteen Fifty-Seven**; **Vishnubhat Godse** wrote **Majha Pravas**; **Savarkar** wrote **The Indian War of Independence**.
xa: It was the **first Indian-language** work on the causes of 1857 (UPPSC **2009**).
He blamed lack of Indian representation in the **Legislative Council** and misunderstanding of Indian customs.
⚠ **The Great Rebellion** = **Ashok Mehta**; **The Great Mutiny** = **Christopher Hibbert**.

182.s:
According to Sir Syed Ahmed Khan, which of the following contributed to the outbreak of the Revolt of 1857?
1. Lack of Indian representation in the Legislative Council
2. Misunderstanding of Indian customs
3. Complete equality between Indian and British soldiers
Which of the statements given above are correct?
182.x: Sir Syed Ahmed Khan blamed the lack of Indian representation in the Legislative Council and the misunderstanding of Indian customs. Complete equality between Indian and British soldiers was not a cause identified by him.
182.tq: Use the contradiction in the third statement to isolate the two supported causes.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Sir Syed Ahmed Khan** blamed **lack of Indian representation in the Legislative Council** and **misunderstanding of Indian customs**.
Statement 3 wrong: sepoys in fact had **lower pay** than British soldiers and could rise **no higher than Subedar**.
xa: His **Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind** = "The Causes of the Indian Revolt" (**1859**).
He was the **first Indian** to write on the causes of 1857 in an **Indian language** (UPPSC **2009**).

182.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Book)
A. Civil Rebellion in the Indian Mutinies
B. The Great Rebellion
C. The Peasant and the Raj
D. Awadh in Revolt 1857-58

List-II (Author)
1. Eric Stokes
2. Ashok Mehta
3. Rudrangshu Mukherjee
4. S.B. Chaudhuri
182.x: Civil Rebellion in the Indian Mutinies was written by S.B. Chaudhuri; The Great Rebellion by Ashok Mehta; The Peasant and the Raj by Eric Stokes; and Awadh in Revolt 1857-58 by Rudrangshu Mukherjee.
182.tq: Start from the sure book-author pair and eliminate the codes.
xs: Correct pairs: **A-4, B-2, C-1, D-3** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**S.B. Chaudhuri** = **Civil Rebellion in the Indian Mutinies**; **Ashok Mehta** = **The Great Rebellion**.
**Eric Stokes** = **The Peasant and the Raj**; **Rudrangshu Mukherjee** = **Awadh in Revolt 1857-58**.
xa: Eric Stokes also wrote **The Peasant Armed**.
**UPPSC 2017** key: Savarkar → Indian War of Independence; S.B. Chaudhuri → Civil Rebellion; The Great Rebellion → Ashok Mehta.
⚠ **The Great Mutiny** = **Christopher Hibbert**.

182.s: The Revolt of 1857 is described as combining the grievances of
o: rulers, peasants, soldiers and common people
urban merchants and British officials alone
missionaries, taluqdars and European soldiers only
182.x: The revolt brought together the grievances of rulers, peasants, soldiers and common people. It therefore had participation and causes extending beyond the sepoy ranks.
182.tq: Choose the complete social composition rather than the narrower sepoy-only interpretation.
xs: 1857 brought together the grievances of **rulers, peasants, soldiers and common people** — so option **(2)** is correct.
So it was more than a sepoy affair; option 1's "only" is too narrow.
xa: Princes' fear of annexation helped turn a **sepoy mutiny** into a wider revolt.
Debate: **"sepoy mutiny"** (**Roberts**) vs **"first war of independence"** (**Savarkar**).
Sepoys were **"peasants in uniform"**.

182.s: Who is regarded as the first martyr of the Revolt of 1857?
182.x: Mangal Pandey is identified as the first martyr of the Revolt of 1857.
182.tq: Test a first-in-sequence fact directly, while using other prominent figures as nearby distractors.
xs: **Mangal Pandey** is the **first martyr of 1857** — so option **(4)** is correct.
He attacked **Lt Baugh** and **Sergeant-Major Hewson** at **Barrackpore** on **29 March 1857**.
xa: He was hanged on **8 April 1857**; his regiment (**34th Bengal NI**) was disbanded.
On **21 July 2026** the PM paid tribute on his birth anniversary (born **19 July 1827**).
**Bahadur Shah II** was proclaimed **Shahenshah-e-Hindustan** on **11-12 May 1857**.

182.s:
With reference to the post-1857 policy of the British Crown, consider the following statements:
1. The Crown promised religious neutrality.
2. State patronage of missionary work was withdrawn.
3. The policy formally expanded state support for missionary activities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
182.x: After 1858, the Crown promised religious neutrality and withdrew state patronage from missionary work. Statement 3 reverses this policy.
182.tq: Identify the reversed policy statement in a post-revolt administrative change.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
After **1858** the Crown promised **religious neutrality** (Queen's Proclamation) and **withdrew state patronage from missionary work**.
Statement 3 reverses this policy.
xa: Before 1857, missionaries **preached under police protection** and attacked Hindu and Islamic practice.
The **Lex Loci Act (1850)** let converts **inherit ancestral property**, seen as an incentive to convert.

n: Hind Swaraj was written by M.K. Gandhi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 40-45]
My Experiments with Truth was written by M.K. Gandhi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 40-45]

183.s: The incident involving Mangal Pandey at Barrackpore occurred on:
183.x: Mangal Pandey attacked British officers at Barrackpore on 29 March 1857.
183.tq: Distinguish the date of the Barrackpore incident from the date of execution and the Meerut rising.
xs: **Mangal Pandey's** attack at **Barrackpore** came on **29 March 1857** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**8 April 1857** = his hanging; **10 May** = **Meerut**; **11 May** = rebels reach **Delhi**.
xa: He was of the **34th Bengal Native Infantry** and attacked **Lt Baugh** and **Sgt-Major Hewson**.
⚠ Some notes date the incident to **April**.
⚠ **Barrackpore** = first outbreak; **Meerut** = real **start** of the revolt.

183.s:
Consider the following statements about the Meerut rising of 10 May 1857:
1. It followed the jailing of 85 sepoys of the 3rd (Light) Cavalry for refusing the cartridges.
2. The rebels shot their officers, freed the prisoners and marched to Delhi.
3. The slogan of the march was 'Inquilab Zindabad'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
183.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the slogan was 'Dilli Chalo' (Delhi Chalo). So B; A omits the true statement 2, C and D include the false statement 3.
183.tq: Meerut: 85 sepoys, 3rd Cavalry, 'Dilli Chalo'.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **85** sepoys of the **3rd (Light) Cavalry** were jailed for refusing cartridges.
Statement 2 correct: comrades **shot officers, freed prisoners, marched to Delhi**.
Statement 3 wrong: the slogan was **"Dilli Chalo" / "Delhi Chalo"**.
xa: **Meerut (10 May 1857)** = the **real start** of the revolt.
**APPSC-GS 2024** key: revolt began at **Meerut**, was widespread but failed.

183.s: Which of the following statements regarding the events at Delhi is correct?
o: The rebels retained the existing British administration without change.
The rebels reached Delhi before the Meerut rising.
The rebels appointed Lord Canning as their emperor.
The rebels killed Commissioner Simon Fraser after entering the Red Fort.
183.x: After reaching Delhi, the rebels entered the Red Fort and killed Commissioner Simon Fraser. The other statements are incorrect.
183.tq: Reject options that reverse the sequence or wrongly assign titles and actions.
xs: In Delhi the rebels took the **Red Fort** and killed Commissioner **Simon Fraser** — so option **(4)** is correct.
They reached Delhi **after** Meerut (**11 May 1857**) and proclaimed **Bahadur Shah II**, not Canning, as emperor.
xa: ⚠ Some notes write "**Simon Ripley**".
Bahadur Shah II was proclaimed **"Shahenshah-e-Hindustan"**.
Some notes say Delhi was seized on **12 May**.

183.s:
Consider the following statements about General Bakht Khan:
1. He was the real military leader at Delhi while Bahadur Shah Zafar was the nominal leader.
2. He led a 10-member 'Court of Soldiers' at Delhi.
3. He came to Delhi from Lucknow.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
183.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Bakht Khan came from Bareilly and reached Delhi on 3 July 1857. So A; B, C and D include the false statement 3.
183.tq: Bakht Khan: Bareilly -> Delhi, Court of Soldiers.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **Bakht Khan** was the **real** leader; **Bahadur Shah Zafar** the **nominal** one.
Statement 2 correct: he led a **10-member "Court of Soldiers"**.
Statement 3 wrong: he came from **Bareilly**, reaching Delhi on **3 July 1857**.
xa: **Delhi was recaptured** in **Sep 1857**.
Bareilly's own leader was **Khan Bahadur Khan**.

183.s: The revolt at Bareilly was led by Khan Bahadur Khan, who proclaimed himself:
183.x: Khan Bahadur Khan proclaimed himself Nawab Nizam at Bareilly and commanded an army of about 40,000.
183.tq: Test the exact title adopted by a regional leader.
xs: **Khan Bahadur Khan** proclaimed himself **Nawab Nizam** at Bareilly — so option **(3)** is correct.
**"Shahenshah-e-Hindustan"** was **Bahadur Shah II's** title.
xa: He led an army of **40,000** in **Rohilkhand**.
Bareilly rose in **May 1857** and was recaptured in **May 1858**.

183.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Jhalkari Bai — Jhansi
2. Uda Devi — Sikandar Bagh, Lucknow
3. Azizun — Kanpur
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
183.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. Jhalkari Bai was associated with Jhansi, Uda Devi fought at Sikandar Bagh in Lucknow, and Azizun supported the sepoys at Kanpur.
183.tq: Check each leader against the associated centre before selecting the coded combination.
xs: All three pairs are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
**Jhalkari Bai** = **Jhansi** (Lakshmibai's lookalike); **Uda Devi** = **Sikandar Bagh**, Lucknow; **Azizun** = **Kanpur**.
xa: Uda Devi was a **Pasi** woman; Azizun was a courtesan who **armed and rode with the sepoys**.
Jhalkari Bai commanded the Rani's **women's wing**.
**Shah Mal** mobilised the **chaurasee des (84 villages)** of Baraut.

183.s:
Consider the following statements about Bahadur Shah Zafar:
1. He wrote to princely states seeking support.
2. Most princely states responded positively to his appeal.
3. He was captured after Delhi fell, tried and exiled to Rangoon.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
183.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Most princes ignored his appeals rather than responding positively to them.
183.tq: Use the negative statement to distinguish the appeal from its limited response.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: he **wrote to princely states** seeking support.
Statement 2 wrong: his appeals were **mostly ignored**, though they spread the rising.
Statement 3 correct: captured after Delhi fell (**Sep 1857**), tried, **exiled to Rangoon**.
xa: He died in **1862**.
Big states like **Hyderabad, Mysore**, **Scindia** and **Holkar** stayed loyal.

183.s: Who among the following was the correspondent of The Times who reported on the Revolt of 1857 and British reprisals?
183.x: W. H. Russell, correspondent of The Times, reported on the revolt and British reprisals in My Diary in India.
183.tq: Distinguish the contemporary reporter from political advisers and military officers.
xs: **W.H. Russell**, correspondent of **The Times**, reported on the revolt and British reprisals — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Azimullah Khan** was **Nana Saheb's adviser**; **Afzal-ud-Daula** was the **Nizam**; **Captain Wilson** crushed **Dandasena**.
xa: Russell's account: **My Diary in India**.
Azimullah Khan went to **London** to plead Nana Saheb's **pension** case.

183.s: Azimullah Khan went to London primarily to plead which case?
o: The restoration of the Nizam’s authority
The pension case of Nana Saheb
The forest-produce rights of Savara chiefs
183.x: Azimullah Khan, Nana Saheb’s adviser, went to London to plead Nana Saheb’s pension case.
183.tq: Connect the adviser with the specific political mission he undertook.
xs: **Azimullah Khan** went to London to plead **Nana Saheb's pension** case — so option **(2)** is correct.
He was **Nana Saheb's adviser**.
xa: At **Kanpur** Nana Saheb led with **Tantia Tope** and **Azimullah Khan**.
Kanpur rose on **5 June 1857**; **Colin Campbell** retook it in **Dec 1857**.

183.s: Shah Mal mobilised the headmen and cultivators of which area during the Revolt of 1857?
o: The chaurasee des of 84 villages in Baraut
183.x: Shah Mal mobilised the chaurasee des, meaning the area of 84 villages, in the Baraut region of Uttar Pradesh.
183.tq: Identify the distinctive local organisation and its numerical extent.
xs: **Shah Mal** mobilised headmen and cultivators of the **chaurasee des (84 villages)** of **Baraut** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Jagdishpur** belongs to **Kunwar Singh**; **Rohilkhand** to **Khan Bahadur Khan**.
xa: Asked as the **APPSC-GS 2021** key.
Baraut is a pargana in **UP**.

183.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the revolt at Lucknow:
1. Begum Hazrat Mahal led the revolt.
2. She declared her son Birjis Qadr the ruler of Awadh.
3. Hindus and Muslims shared offices under the arrangement established there.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
183.x: All three statements are correct. Begum Hazrat Mahal led at Lucknow, proclaimed Birjis Qadr ruler of Awadh, and the administration included both Hindus and Muslims in offices.
183.tq: Check whether all details associated with one centre are simultaneously correct.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
**Begum Hazrat Mahal** led at **Lucknow**, declared son **Birjis Qadr** ruler of **Awadh**, and **Hindus and Muslims shared offices**.
xa: Lucknow rose on **4 June 1857** and was recaptured in **Mar 1858**.
**Uda Devi** fought at **Sikandar Bagh**, Lucknow.

183.s:
Match the leaders of 1857 with their centres:
a. Kunwar Singh  b. Begum Hazrat Mahal  c. Nana Saheb  d. Bahadur Shah Zafar
1. Delhi  2. Kanpur  3. Lucknow  4. Arrah
183.x: Kunwar Singh led at Arrah (Bihar), Begum Hazrat Mahal at Lucknow, Nana Saheb at Kanpur and Bahadur Shah Zafar at Delhi (APPSC-G2 2025). Option B swaps Kunwar Singh and Hazrat Mahal, C swaps Hazrat Mahal and Nana Saheb, and D puts Kunwar Singh at Kanpur and Nana Saheb at Arrah.
183.tq: Arrah-Kunwar Singh, Lucknow-Hazrat Mahal, Kanpur-Nana, Delhi-Zafar.
xs: Correct pairs: **a-4, b-3, c-2, d-1** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Kunwar Singh** = **Arrah**; **Begum Hazrat Mahal** = **Lucknow**; **Nana Saheb** = **Kanpur**; **Bahadur Shah** = **Delhi**.
xa: This was the **APPSC-G2 2025** match.
Kunwar Singh led a **fresh rising in Bihar** in **Apr 1858**.
**Jhansi** = **Rani Lakshmibai**; **Faizabad** = **Maulvi Ahmadullah**.

183.s: Which one of the following was NOT a leader of the Revolt of 1857?
183.x: Bhagat Singh belongs to the later freedom movement and only drew on 1857's legacy (APPSC 2019 odd one out). Maulvi Ahmadullah led at Faizabad, Khan Bahadur Khan at Bareilly, and Maulvi Liyakat Ali at Allahabad and Banaras.
183.tq: Bhagat Singh = odd one out for 1857.
xs: **Bhagat Singh** was not part of 1857 — so option **(3)** is the answer.
He only **drew on its legacy** later (**APPSC 2019** odd one out).
**Maulvi Ahmadullah** = **Faizabad**; **Khan Bahadur Khan** = **Bareilly**; **Maulvi Liyakat Ali** = **Allahabad and Banaras**.
xa: 1857 heroes were invoked in the **Quit India** and **INA** phases.
⚠ At **Delhi**, **Bahadur Shah** was nominal leader; **Bakht Khan** the real one.

183.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Gwalior and Jhansi witnessed major rebel activity
B. Delhi was recaptured
C. Kanpur was retaken by Colin Campbell
D. Lucknow was recaptured
183.x: The sequence was Gwalior and Jhansi in June 1857, Delhi recaptured in September 1857, Kanpur retaken in December 1857, and Lucknow recaptured in March 1858.
183.tq: Anchor the sequence using the month in which each centre was recaptured or occupied.
xs: Order **A, B, C, D** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Gwalior, Jhansi (June 1857)** → **Delhi recaptured (Sep 1857)** → **Kanpur retaken (Dec 1857)** → **Lucknow recaptured (Mar 1858)**.
xa: **Apr 1858**: **Jhansi recaptured**; **May 1858**: **Bareilly** recaptured.
Kanpur was retaken by **Colin Campbell**.

183.s:
Which of the following statements about the spread and suppression of the revolt is correct?
1. Jhansi was recaptured in April 1858.
2. Kunwar Singh led a fresh rising in Bihar in April 1858.
3. Bareilly was recaptured in May 1858.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
183.x: All three statements are correct. Jhansi was recaptured and Kunwar Singh led a fresh rising in Bihar in April 1858, while Bareilly was recaptured in May 1858.
183.tq: Combine several late-stage developments and verify their months independently.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
**Apr 1858**: **Jhansi recaptured** and **Kunwar Singh's** fresh rising in **Bihar**; **May 1858**: **Bareilly** recaptured.
xa: **Mar 1858**: **Lucknow** recaptured.
Kunwar Singh is linked with **Arrah**.

183.s: The correct chronological order of the beginning of the rising at the following centres is: Barrackpore, Delhi, Lucknow and Kanpur
183.x: The rising began at Barrackpore on 29 March, Delhi on 11 May, Lucknow on 4 June and Kanpur on 5 June 1857.
183.tq: Place the earliest event first and distinguish the successive May and June dates.
xs: Order **Barrackpore, Delhi, Lucknow, Kanpur** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Barrackpore (29 March)** → **Delhi (11 May)** → **Lucknow (4 June)** → **Kanpur (5 June 1857)**.
xa: **Meerut** rose on **10 May 1857**.
**Kolhapur area** rose in **October 1857**.

183.s: Which of the following regions formed the main zone of the Revolt of 1857?
o: The Doab, Awadh, Rohilkhand, Bihar, Bundelkhand and Central India
Eastern, western and southern coastal India
183.x: The main zone included the Doab, Awadh, Rohilkhand, Bihar, Bundelkhand and Central India.
183.tq: Select the complete geographical cluster instead of a partial region.
xs: The main zone was the **Doab, Awadh, Rohilkhand, Bihar, Bundelkhand and Central India** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Bengal, Punjab** and **eastern, western and southern India** were largely unaffected.
xa: The zone ran from near **Patna** to the **Rajasthan border**.
**Hyderabad** and **Mysore** stayed loyal.

183.s: Which of the following regions was largely unaffected by the Revolt of 1857?
o: Bengal, Punjab, eastern, western and southern India
183.x: Bengal, Punjab, and eastern, western and southern India were largely unaffected; British forces for suppression came from several of these regions.
183.tq: Locate the unaffected regions by eliminating the principal revolt zone.
xs: **Bengal, Punjab, eastern, western and southern India** were largely unaffected — so option **(4)** is correct.
British power stayed intact there, and **suppression forces came from here**.
The other options list parts of the **main zone**.
xa: The revolt's **narrow territorial and social base** was a cause of failure.
**Martial groups of the north** mostly backed the British.

183.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Nizam of Hyderabad remained loyal to the British.
2. Scindia of Gwalior remained loyal, but his troops went over to the Rani and he fled to Agra.
3. The rulers of Tonk and Bhopal remained loyal even though their troops rebelled.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
183.x: All three statements are correct. Hyderabad's Nizam and Scindia were loyal, while Scindia's troops defected and the troops of Tonk and Bhopal rebelled despite their rulers' loyalty.
183.tq: Separate the conduct of rulers from that of their troops.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
The **Nizam** was loyal; **Scindia** was loyal but his **troops went over to the Rani** and he **fled to Agra**.
**Tonk** and **Bhopal** rulers stayed loyal though their **troops rebelled**.
xa: The Nizam's loyalty **kept the Deccan quiet**.
**Mysore** and **Holkar** were also loyal.

183.s:
Arrange the following British recapture operations in chronological order:
A. Hugh Rose recaptured Jhansi
B. Colin Campbell recaptured Kanpur
C. Colin Campbell recaptured Lucknow
D. Hugh Rose recaptured Gwalior
183.x: Colin Campbell recaptured Kanpur in December 1857, Lucknow in March 1858, Hugh Rose recaptured Jhansi in April 1858 and Gwalior in June 1858.
183.tq: Anchor the sequence using the year change and then order the 1858 operations by month.
xs: Order **B, C, A, D** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Kanpur (Dec 1857)** → **Lucknow (Mar 1858)** → **Jhansi (Apr 1858)** → **Gwalior** last.
