**Workers and Peasants Party** — make the **Congress more revolutionary**; **Bhoodan Movement** — **distribute land** to **landless farmers**.
**Non-Cooperation** — **non-violent non-cooperation**; **Civil Disobedience** — **violate unjust colonial laws**.
xa: **Satyashodhak Samaj** — uplift **backward classes**.
**Radhasoami Satsang** — one God, the **Guru** and **Satsang**.
**Prarthana Samaj** — **reform marriage customs**.

190.x: Dayananda Saraswati’s original name was Mool Shankar Tiwari.
190.tq: Discriminate between the original names of Arya Samaj personalities.
xs: Dayananda Saraswati was born as **Mool Shankar Tiwari** — so option **(3)** is correct.
He was born at **Tankara** in **Kathiawar, Gujarat**, and lived **1824-1883**.
xa: His guru was **Swami Virajananda** (Virjanand) of **Mathura**.
He died at **Ajmer** in **1883**.
Titles: **"Martin Luther of India"** (given by **Lala Lajpat Rai**) and **"Grandfather of the Indian Nation"**.

190.s:
Consider the following statements about Dayananda Saraswati:
1. His guru was Swami Virajananda of Mathura.
2. He lived from 1824 to 1883.
3. He died at Lahore, where the Arya Samaj later shifted its headquarters.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
190.x: Statement 3 is wrong: he died at Ajmer in 1883; Lahore was only the later headquarters of the Arya Samaj. The other two are correct: his guru was Swami Virajananda of Mathura and he lived 1824-1883. So '1 and 2 only' is right; every other option either includes statement 3 or leaves out a correct statement.
190.tq: Born Tankara, guru at Mathura, died at Ajmer.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: his guru was **Swami Virajananda** of **Mathura**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: he lived **1824-1883**.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: he died at **Ajmer** in **1883**; **Lahore** was only where the Arya Samaj later shifted its HQ.
So **1 and 2 only** — option **(1)** is correct.
xa: His original name was **Mool Shankar** (Tiwari), born at **Tankara**, Kathiawar, **Gujarat**.
He founded the **Arya Samaj** at **Bombay** in **1875**; its strongest base became **Punjab**.
⚠ Trap: Arya Samaj was founded in **Bombay**, not Calcutta or Lahore.

190.s:
Consider the following statements about Dayananda Saraswati:
1. He gave the slogan 'India for the Indians'.
2. Bal Gangadhar Tilak called him the 'Martin Luther of India'.
3. He is credited as the first to use the term Swaraj.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
190.x: Statement 2 is wrong: it was Lala Lajpat Rai who called him the 'Martin Luther of India'. The other two are correct: he gave the slogan 'India for the Indians' and is credited as the first to use the term Swaraj. So '1 and 3 only' is right; every other option either includes statement 2 or leaves out a correct statement.
190.tq: Martin Luther of India - said by Lala Lajpat Rai.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: he gave the slogan **"India for the Indians"**.
Statement 2 is **wrong**: it was **Lala Lajpat Rai**, not Tilak, who called him the **"Martin Luther of India"**.
Statement 3 is **correct**: he is credited as the first to use the term **Swaraj**.
So **1 and 3 only** — option **(3)** is correct.
xa: His other title: **"Grandfather of the Indian Nation"**.
His other slogan: **"Back to the Vedas"** ("Go Back to the Vedas").
He wrote his main work, **Satyarth Prakash**, in **Hindi**.

190.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Dayananda Saraswati’s contribution to language policy?
o: He wrote his main work in Hindi and promoted Hindi as a link language.
He confined his writings to Telugu and Tamil.
He promoted English as the sole link language.
He wrote exclusively in Persian and opposed vernacular languages.
190.x: Dayananda wrote his main work in Hindi and promoted Hindi as a link language.
190.tq: Select the complete and precise language-related statement.
xs: Dayananda **wrote his main work in Hindi** and **promoted Hindi as a link language** — so option **(1)** is correct.
His main work, **Satyarth Prakash** (**1875**), was written in **Hindi** — not Telugu, Tamil, English or Persian.
xa: **Satyarth Prakash** means **"The Light of Truth"** (also "The True Exposition").
It critiqued Hindu orthodoxy: **idolatry**, **caste by birth**, **child marriage**.
His slogans: **"India for the Indians"** and **"Back to the Vedas"**.

190.s: Arya Samaj was founded at which place in 1875?
190.x: Arya Samaj was founded by Swami Dayananda Saraswati at Bombay in 1875. Its headquarters were later shifted to Lahore.
190.tq: Distinguish the place of founding from the later headquarters.
xs: The Arya Samaj was founded at **Bombay** in **1875** (April) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Lahore** became its HQ only later; **Calcutta** is a classic trap.
xa: Founding date: some notes give **7 April 1875**; many texts give **10 April 1875**.
Founder: **Swami Dayananda Saraswati**; name means **"Society of Nobles"**.
Strongest base: **Punjab**; also strong in **Rajasthan** and **United Provinces**.
⚠ Statement traps: "founded in Calcutta" (wrong) and "promotes idol worship" (wrong; it rejects it).

190.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Arya Samaj:
1. Its name means ‘Society of Nobles’.
2. Its strongest base became Punjab.
3. Its headquarters were originally established at Lahore.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
190.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Arya Samaj was founded at Bombay, while its headquarters were later shifted to Lahore.
190.tq: Find the wrong location by separating the founding place from the later headquarters.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: Arya Samaj means **"Society of Nobles"**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: its strongest base was **Punjab**.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: it was founded at **Bombay** (**1875**); the HQ was **later** shifted to **Lahore**.
So **1 and 2 only** — option **(1)** is correct.
xa: It was also strong in **Rajasthan** and the **United Provinces**.
**Ten Principles** drafted by Dayananda: truth, rational thought, moral action, well-being of all.
Called a **"nursery of militant nationalists"** — **Lala Lajpat Rai**, **Swami Shraddhanand**, Bhagat Singh's family.

190.s:
The Ten Principles of Arya Samaj, drafted by Dayananda Saraswati, emphasised which of the following?
1. Truth and rational thought
2. Moral action
3. Welfare of all
4. Caste by birth
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
190.x: The Ten Principles emphasised truth, rational thought, moral conduct and the well-being of all. Arya Samaj rejected caste based on birth.
190.tq: Reject the swapped reform principle involving caste by birth.
xs: The Ten Principles stressed **truth and rational thought**, **moral action** and **well-being of all** — so **1, 2 and 3 only**, option **(1)**.
**Caste by birth** was **rejected** by the Arya Samaj, so item 4 is wrong.
xa: The **Ten Principles** were drafted by **Dayananda Saraswati** himself.
The Samaj also rejected **idol worship**, **polytheism** and **ritualism**.
It supported **widow remarriage**, **inter-caste marriage** and **women's education**.

190.s:
The Arya Samaj came to be regarded as a ‘nursery of militant nationalists’ mainly because it influenced personalities and groups such as:
1. Lala Lajpat Rai
2. Swami Shraddhanand
3. Bhagat Singh’s family
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
190.x: Arya Samaj influenced Lala Lajpat Rai, Swami Shraddhanand and the family of Bhagat Singh, contributing to militant nationalist attitudes.
190.tq: Recognise the combined list of nationalist associations.
xs: The Samaj influenced **Lala Lajpat Rai**, **Swami Shraddhanand** and **Bhagat Singh's family** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
Hence it is called the **"nursery of militant nationalists"**.
xa: **Lala Lajpat Rai** called Dayananda the **"Martin Luther of India"**.
**Swami Shraddhanand** led the 1920s **Shuddhi** campaign via the **Bharatiya Hindu Shuddhi Sabha (1923)**; assassinated in **1926**.
Significance: revivalism + reform; built **Hindu self-confidence**; fed **militant nationalism**.

190.s: The slogan ‘Back to the Vedas’ implied that Dayananda Saraswati regarded the Vedas as:
o: Political documents of the colonial state
Texts limited exclusively to ritual practices
Infallible and the primordial word of God
190.x: The slogan expressed the belief that the four Vedas were infallible and constituted the primordial word of God.
190.tq: Infer the doctrine from the exact meaning of the slogan.
xs: "Back to the Vedas" held the four Vedas **infallible** — the **primordial word of God** — so option **(4)** is correct.
He **rejected** later **Puranic** accretions (myths, rituals, idol worship), so option (2) is the opposite.
xa: He claimed the Vedas contained **all true knowledge, including science**.
This countered the colonial idea of **Western intellectual superiority**.
The slogan is set out in **Satyarth Prakash** (**1875**, **Hindi**).

190.s: The title ‘Satyarth Prakash’ is generally translated as:
190.x: Satyarth Prakash means ‘The Light of Truth’; it is also rendered as ‘The True Exposition’.
190.tq: Choose the precise translation of the title.
xs: **Satyarth Prakash** means **"The Light of Truth"** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It is also rendered as **"The True Exposition"**.
xa: Author: **Dayananda Saraswati**, **1875**, in **Hindi**.
It set out his religious and social philosophy and critiqued **Hindu orthodoxy** and other religions.
Its core idea: **"Back to the Vedas"** — Vedas infallible, Puranic accretions rejected.

190.s: Which of the following subjects was NOT a theme of Satyarth Prakash?
o: Critique of idolatry and caste by birth
Religious and social philosophy of Dayananda
190.x: Satyarth Prakash presented Dayananda’s religious and social philosophy and criticised Hindu orthodoxy, idolatry, caste by birth and child marriage.
190.tq: Use the reversal trap involving orthodoxy and reform.
xs: **Advocacy of unquestioned Hindu orthodoxy** was NOT a theme — the book **critiqued** orthodoxy — so option **(4)** is correct.
It did set out his **religious and social philosophy** and attacked **idolatry**, **caste by birth** and **child marriage** — options (1)-(3).
xa: It also critiqued **other religions**.
Written in **Hindi** in **1875**; title means **"The Light of Truth"**.
It rejected the **Puranas'** later accretions — myths, rituals, idol worship.

190.s:
With reference to the Shuddhi movement, consider the following statements:
1. It aimed to reconvert persons who had converted to Islam or Christianity.
2. It also sought to admit outsiders into the Hindu fold.
3. It was initiated by the Brahmo Samaj.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
190.x: Shuddhi was started by Arya Samaj to reconvert converts and admit outsiders into the Hindu fold. It was not initiated by the Brahmo Samaj.
190.tq: Identify the wrong organisation associated with the movement.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: Shuddhi aimed to **reconvert** those who had converted to **Islam or Christianity**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: it also admitted **outsiders** into the Hindu fold.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: Shuddhi was started by the **Arya Samaj**, not the Brahmo Samaj.
So **1 and 2 only** — option **(1)** is correct.
xa: ⚠ "Shuddhi was started by ___" → **Arya Samaj** (not Brahmo Samaj, Satyashodhak Samaj or Ramakrishna Mission).
Later leader: **Swami Shraddhanand**, via the **Bharatiya Hindu Shuddhi Sabha (1923)**.
Impact: contributed to the **communalisation** of social life.

190.s: Who led the Shuddhi campaign of the 1920s through the Bharatiya Hindu Shuddhi Sabha?
190.x: Swami Shraddhanand led the Shuddhi campaign of the 1920s through the Bharatiya Hindu Shuddhi Sabha, formed in 1923.
190.tq: Match the later leader with the specific organisation and campaign.
xs: **Swami Shraddhanand** led the 1920s Shuddhi campaign through the **Bharatiya Hindu Shuddhi Sabha** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The Sabha was formed in **1923**; Shraddhanand was **assassinated in 1926**.
xa: Shuddhi was started by the **Arya Samaj** — ritual "purification" to reconvert converts to **Islam or Christianity**.
Shraddhanand is among the **"militant nationalists"** the Samaj nurtured, with **Lala Lajpat Rai**.
Impact: Shuddhi fed **communal political consciousness**.

190.s: The Arya Samaj satyagraha in Hyderabad State during 1938–39 was directed against:
o: The Nizam’s curbs on religious and civil rights
The educational policies of the Government of India
The abolition of zamindari in coastal Andhra
190.x: In 1938–39, Arya Samaj conducted a satyagraha in Hyderabad State against the Nizam’s restrictions on religious and civil rights.
190.tq: Link the movement, region, period and immediate grievance.
xs: The **1938-39** Hyderabad satyagraha opposed **the Nizam's curbs on religious and civil rights** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was led by the **Arya Samaj** in **Hyderabad State**.
xa: It ran alongside the **Hyderabad State Congress** satyagraha.
Impact: built **political awakening against Nizam rule** in the **Telangana** region.
AP angle: Arya Samaj had great influence on **women's upliftment in Andhra**.

190.s: Which development associated with Arya Samaj was criticised for sharpening communal divisions?
o: Shuddhi and aggressive attacks on other faiths
190.x: Shuddhi and aggressive attacks on other faiths were criticised for sharpening communal divides.
190.tq: Separate reform measures from activities linked to communal tension.
xs: **Shuddhi and aggressive attacks on other faiths** were criticised for sharpening **communal divides** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Women's education, widow remarriage and rational thought were part of its **reform** programme, not the criticism.
xa: Shuddhi: reconversion of those converted to **Islam or Christianity**, started by the **Arya Samaj**.
**Swami Shraddhanand** led it via the **Bharatiya Hindu Shuddhi Sabha (1923)**.
It contributed to the **communalisation of social life**.

191.s: Ramakrishna Paramahansa was associated as a mystic and priest with the:
191.x: Ramakrishna Paramahansa served as a mystic and priest at the Dakshineswar Kali Temple near Calcutta.
191.tq: Identify the religious figure through his principal place of association.
xs: Ramakrishna Paramahansa was a mystic and priest of the **Kali Temple at Dakshineswar**, near Calcutta — so option **(4)** is correct.
xa: Original name: **Gadadhar Chattopadhyaya**; wife: **Sarada Devi**.
Gurus: **Bhairavi Brahmani** (Tantra) and **Totapuri** (Advaita).
His saying **"as many faiths, so many paths"** — all religions lead to the same truth.

191.s:
Consider the following statements about the teachings of Ramakrishna Paramahansa:
1. His saying 'as many faiths, so many paths' expresses the belief that all religions lead to the same truth.
2. He held that salvation could be pursued through devotion, meditation and renunciation.
3. He held that salvation was possible only through renunciation and never through devotion.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
191.x: Statement 1 is correct: 'as many faiths, so many paths' means all religions lead to the same truth. Statement 2 is correct: he named devotion, meditation and renunciation as paths to salvation. Statement 3 is wrong: devotion was itself one of the paths, not excluded. So '1 only' misses 2, while '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' wrongly include 3.
191.tq: Ramakrishna = universalism; words like 'only' or 'never' clash with 'as many faiths, so many paths'.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **"as many faiths, so many paths"** means all religions lead to the **same truth**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: salvation through **devotion, meditation, renunciation**.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: **devotion** was itself one of the paths.
So **1 and 2 only** — option **(3)** is correct.
xa: Vivekananda's **Practical Vedanta**: serving the poor = serving God (**"Daridra Narayana"**).
RKM motto: **"Atmano Mokshartham Jagat Hitaya Cha"** — for one's own liberation and the welfare of the world.

191.s:
Consider the following statements about Swami Vivekananda:
1. His original name was Narendranath Datta.
2. He was born in Calcutta on 12 January 1863.
3. He was the chief disciple of Ramakrishna Paramahamsa.
4. He was born as Gadadhar Chattopadhyaya.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
191.x: Vivekananda was born Narendranath Datta in Calcutta on 12 January 1863 and became Ramakrishna’s chief disciple. Gadadhar Chattopadhyaya was the birth name of Ramakrishna, not Vivekananda.
191.tq: Use the look-alike personal-name trap to separate the disciple’s name from the guru’s birth name.
xs: Statements 1, 2, 3 are **correct**: born **Narendranath Datta**, **Calcutta**, **12 January 1863**; chief disciple of **Ramakrishna**.
Statement 4 is **wrong**: **Gadadhar Chattopadhyaya** was Ramakrishna's birth name.
So **1, 2 and 3 only** — option **(1)** is correct.
xa: Vivekananda died in **1902**.
His birthday, **12 January**, is **National Youth Day**.
Titles: **"Prophet of Indian Nationalism"**, **"Maker of Modern India"**.

191.s: Swami Vivekananda’s birthday is observed in India as:
191.x: 12 January, the birthday of Swami Vivekananda, is observed as National Youth Day.
191.tq: Link the precise date-based observance with the correct national day.
xs: Vivekananda's birthday, **12 January**, is observed as **National Youth Day** — so option **(2)** is correct.
He was born **Narendranath Datta** in **Calcutta** in **1863**.
xa: His ideas stressed **strength, self-confidence, youth** for national regeneration.
Titles: **"Prophet of Indian Nationalism"** and **"Maker of Modern India"**.
He died in **1902**.

191.s:
Swami Vivekananda is described by which of the following titles?
1. Prophet of Indian Nationalism
2. Maker of Modern India
3. Father of the Indian Constitution
4. Grand Old Man of India
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
191.x: Vivekananda is described as the ‘Prophet of Indian Nationalism’ and the ‘Maker of Modern India’. The other titles refer to different personalities.
191.tq: Separate attributed titles from famous titles belonging to other national figures.
xs: Vivekananda is called the **"Prophet of Indian Nationalism"** and **"Maker of Modern India"** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
The other two titles belong to other personalities, not Vivekananda.
xa: His Western disciple: **Margaret Noble (Sister Nivedita)**.
He set up **Vedanta Societies** in the **USA and Britain** — **Vedanta Society of New York (1894)**.
He made **humanitarian relief** a monastic duty.

191.s:
Match the participants at the Chicago Parliament of Religions with their affiliations.
List-I (Participant)
a. P.C. Mozoomdar
b. Virchand Gandhi
c. Anagarika Dharmapala
 d. Swami Vivekananda
List-II (Affiliation)
i. Buddhism, Ceylon
ii. Hinduism
iii. Jainism
iv. Brahmo Samaj
Options:
191.x: P.C. Mozoomdar was associated with the Brahmo Samaj, Virchand Gandhi with Jainism, Anagarika Dharmapala with Buddhism from Ceylon, and Vivekananda with Hinduism.
191.tq: Begin with the distinctive Ceylon–Buddhism pair and then match the remaining religious affiliations.
xs: Correct match: **a–iv, b–iii, c–i, d–ii** — option **(1)**.
**P.C. Mozoomdar** – **Brahmo Samaj**; **Virchand Gandhi** – **Jain**; **Anagarika Dharmapala** – **Buddhist, Ceylon**; **Vivekananda** – **Hinduism**.
xa: The event: **World's Parliament of Religions, Chicago, 1893**.
Vivekananda opened with **"Sisters and Brothers of America"** on **11 Sep 1893**.
Before Chicago he meditated on the **Kanyakumari** rock (**Dec 1892**).

191.s: Swami Vivekananda’s opening words at the Chicago Parliament of Religions were:
191.x: Vivekananda began his address with ‘Sisters and Brothers of America’, which received wide acclaim.
191.tq: Recall the exact famous opening phrase instead of a synonymous greeting.
xs: His opening words were **"Sisters and Brothers of America"** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Delivered at the **World's Parliament of Religions, Chicago**, on **11 Sep 1893**; it won wide acclaim.
xa: He represented **Hinduism** there.
Other participants: **P.C. Mozoomdar** (Brahmo Samaj), **Virchand Gandhi** (Jain), **Anagarika Dharmapala** (Buddhist, Ceylon).
In **Feb 1893** he spoke at **Mahboob College, Secunderabad**.

191.s: Swami Vivekananda established Vedanta Societies in:
191.x: Vivekananda established Vedanta Societies in the United States of America and Britain.
191.tq: Recall the two-country institutional association given for the reformer.
xs: Vivekananda set up Vedanta Societies in **the USA and Britain** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The first was the **Vedanta Society of New York** (**1894**).
xa: He spoke at **Chicago** in **1893**, representing **Hinduism**.
His Western disciple: **Margaret Noble (Sister Nivedita)**.
On return he founded the **Ramakrishna Mission** (**1897**).

191.s:
Arrange the following events associated with Swami Vivekananda in chronological order:
A. Meditation on the Kanyakumari rock
B. Address at the World’s Parliament of Religions
C. Speech at Mahboob College, Secunderabad
D. Return through Colombo, Ramnad and Madras
191.x: Vivekananda meditated at Kanyakumari in December 1892, spoke at Secunderabad in February 1893, addressed the Chicago Parliament in 1893, and returned through the southern route in 1897.
191.tq: Fix the first and last events, then arrange the two intervening 1893 events.
xs: Order: **A, C, B, D** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Kanyakumari** rock (**Dec 1892**) → **Mahboob College, Secunderabad** (**Feb 1893**) → **Chicago** (**11 Sep 1893**) → return via **Colombo, Ramnad, Madras** (**1897**).
xa: The return speeches form **Lectures from Colombo to Almora**.
**Ramakrishna Mission** founded **1 May 1897**, soon after the return.

191.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
191.x: My Master was written by Swami Vivekananda. Annie Besant is not its author.
191.tq: Find the swapped author among otherwise correctly matched books and authors.
xs: **My Master — Annie Besant** is wrongly matched; **My Master** is by **Vivekananda** — so option **(4)** is the answer.
**The Secret Doctrine** is by **Blavatsky**; **Karma Yoga** and **Raja Yoga** are by **Vivekananda** — correctly matched.
xa: Vivekananda also wrote **Jnana Yoga** and **Lectures from Colombo to Almora**.
Besant's papers: **New India** and **Commonweal**.
Blavatsky's other book: **Isis Unveiled**; Krishnamurti wrote **At the Feet of the Master** (**1910**).

191.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the social ideas of Swami Vivekananda:
1. He condemned caste-based discrimination.
2. He regarded humanitarian relief as a monastic duty.
3. He supported empty ritual as the basis of national regeneration.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
191.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Vivekananda condemned empty ritual, so statement 3 is false.
191.tq: Split the options by testing the reformer's positive and negative positions separately.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: Vivekananda **condemned caste**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: he made **humanitarian relief a monastic duty**.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: he **condemned empty ritual**.
So **1 and 2 only** — option **(1)** is correct.
xa: He stressed **strength, self-confidence, youth** for national regeneration.
**Practical Vedanta**: serving the poor = serving God (**"Daridra Narayana"**).

191.s: Who among the following was the Western disciple of Swami Vivekananda known as Sister Nivedita?
191.x: Margaret Noble became the well-known Western disciple of Vivekananda under the name Sister Nivedita.
191.tq: Match the adopted religious name with the original personal name.
xs: **Margaret Noble** was Vivekananda's Western disciple, known as **Sister Nivedita** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Blavatsky** co-founded the Theosophical Society; **Annie Besant** led it; **Sarada Devi** was Ramakrishna's wife.
xa: Vivekananda set up **Vedanta Societies** in the **USA and Britain** (New York, **1894**).
Titles: **"Prophet of Indian Nationalism"**, **"Maker of Modern India"**.
Born **Narendranath Datta** (**1863**); died **1902**.

191.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the two journals associated with the Ramakrishna movement?
o: Prabuddha Bharata was in English and Udbodhan was in Bengali
Prabuddha Bharata was in Bengali and Udbodhan was in English
Both Prabuddha Bharata and Udbodhan were in English
Both Prabuddha Bharata and Udbodhan were in Bengali
191.x: Prabuddha Bharata was an English journal, whereas Udbodhan was published in Bengali.
191.tq: Discriminate between two similar entries by pairing each with its language.
xs: **Prabuddha Bharata** was in **English** and **Udbodhan** in **Bengali** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Both journals are associated with **Vivekananda**.
xa: ⚠ Classic swap trap: **Prabuddha Bharata = English**; **Udbodhan = Bengali**.
Vivekananda's books: **Karma Yoga**, **Raja Yoga**, **Jnana Yoga**, **My Master**.
Besant's papers, by contrast: **New India** and **Commonweal**.

191.s: Lectures from Colombo to Almora is associated with speeches delivered by Swami Vivekananda after his return in 1897 through:
191.x: The work is based on speeches delivered after Vivekananda’s 1897 return through Colombo, Ramnad and Madras.
191.tq: Identify the correct travel route attached to a published work.
xs: **Lectures from Colombo to Almora** are speeches after his **1897** return via **Colombo, Ramnad and Madras** — so option **(3)** is correct.
He had been in the West since the **Chicago** Parliament of **1893**.
xa: Soon after this return he founded the **Ramakrishna Mission** (**1 May 1897**).
His journals: **Prabuddha Bharata** (English) and **Udbodhan** (Bengali).
Other works: **Karma Yoga**, **Raja Yoga**, **Jnana Yoga**, **My Master**.

191.s: Ramakrishna Mission has its headquarters at which of the following places?
o: Belur Math on the Hooghly near Howrah
191.x: The headquarters of the Ramakrishna Mission is at Belur Math, situated on the Hooghly near Howrah.
191.tq: Use the location clue to distinguish the headquarters from the founder’s temple and other reform institutions.
xs: The RKM headquarters is **Belur Math on the Hooghly near Howrah** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Adyar** is the Theosophical Society's Indian HQ; **Dakshineswar** was Ramakrishna's temple; the **Central Hindu College** was Besant's.
xa: **Belur Math** was established in **1898**; permanent HQ of the **Ramakrishna Order**.
Its architecture blends **Hindu, Islamic and Christian** motifs → unity of religions.
**Ramakrishna Mission** founded **1 May 1897** at **Belur (Howrah)**.

191.s: The motto of the Ramakrishna Mission, ‘Atmano Mokshartham Jagat Hitaya Cha’, signifies:
o: For one’s own liberation and the welfare of the world
191.x: The motto means ‘for one’s own liberation and the welfare of the world’.
191.tq: Test the exact meaning of a distinctive institutional motto rather than its general theme.
xs: **"Atmano Mokshartham Jagat Hitaya Cha"** means **for one's own liberation and the welfare of the world** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Universal brotherhood** and comparative religion were **Theosophical** aims, not this motto.
xa: RKM's **Practical Vedanta**: **"Service to mankind is service to God"**.
**Daridra narayana** = God in the poor.
⚠ **"Back to the Vedas"** = Arya Samaj slogan, not RKM.

191.s:
Which of the following activities is associated with the practical work of the Ramakrishna Mission?
1. Running schools and colleges
2. Operating hospitals and orphanages
3. Providing famine and disaster relief
4. Promoting exclusively ritualistic worship
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
191.x: The Mission runs educational and medical institutions, orphanages and relief programmes. Its work is not exclusively ritualistic.
191.tq: Find the one extreme and incompatible statement among several practical-service activities.
xs: The Mission runs **schools and colleges**, **hospitals and orphanages**, and **famine and disaster relief** — so **1, 2 and 3 only**, option **(1)**.
It is not exclusively ritualistic: it combines **renunciation** with **practical spirituality**.
xa: Two wings: a **monastic order** and **lay disciples** doing preaching, philanthropy, humanitarian work.
Vivekananda made **humanitarian relief** a monastic duty.
Current: RKM's **Vivekananda Human Excellence Centre**, **Vijayawada** (**₹8.5 crore**), inaugurated **1 Feb 2026**.

191.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the two broad components of the Ramakrishna Mission’s work?
o: A political party and a constitutional body engaged in legislative reform
A literary society and an educational department of the colonial government
A missionary organisation devoted exclusively to conversion and a trading corporation
A monastic order devoted to renunciation and practical spirituality, and lay disciples engaged in preaching and humanitarian work
191.x: The Mission combines a monastic order devoted to renunciation and practical spirituality with lay work involving preaching, philanthropy and humanitarian service.
191.tq: Compare the two institutional components and reject options that impose an exclusive or unrelated purpose.
xs: The Mission has **a monastic order devoted to renunciation and practical spirituality** and **lay disciples** doing **preaching and humanitarian work** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Lay disciples also carry out **philanthropy**.
xa: Works: **schools, colleges, hospitals, orphanages**; **famine and disaster relief**.
Motto: **"Atmano Mokshartham Jagat Hitaya Cha"**.
Comparative: **RKM = service and universalism**; Arya Samaj = revivalist; Theosophy = foreign-founded Hindu revival.

191.s: The expression ‘daridra narayana’, associated with the practical Vedanta of the Ramakrishna Mission, refers to:
191.x: ‘Daridra narayana’ expresses the idea that service to the poor is service to God.
191.tq: Discriminate between a service-oriented expression and the philosophical doctrines of the Theosophical Society.
xs: **Daridra narayana** means **God manifest in the poor** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It underlies **Practical Vedanta**: **"Service to mankind is service to God"**.
xa: Vivekananda: serving the poor = **serving God**.
⚠ **Rebirth** and **study of ancient religions** are Theosophical beliefs, not this idea.
RKM motto: **"for one's own liberation and the welfare of the world"**.

191.s: In which year did Swami Vivekananda found the Ramakrishna Mission?
191.x: Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission on 1 May 1897, soon after returning from the West, and named it after his guru. 1879 is a common wrong version of 1897; 1875 is the founding year of the Arya Samaj and the Theosophical Society; 1902 is the year Vivekananda died.
191.tq: RKM = 1 May 1897, not 1879; Belur Math HQ came in 1898.
xs: Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission in **1897** (**1 May 1897**) — so option **(3)** is correct.
**1879** is the classic wrong version; **1875** = Arya Samaj and Theosophical Society; **1902** = Vivekananda's death.
xa: He founded it soon after returning from the West and **named it after his guru**.
Place: **Belur (Howrah)**; **Belur Math** followed in **1898**.
⚠ "Founded the Ramakrishna Mission in **1879**" is a WRONG statement.

191.s:
With reference to the Theosophical Society, consider the following statements:
1. Its Indian headquarters is at Adyar.
2. The headquarters was shifted to Adyar in 1882.
3. Its original headquarters was established at Madras in 1875.
4. Its major beliefs included karma and reincarnation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
191.x: Adyar became the Indian headquarters in 1882, and karma and reincarnation were among the Society’s beliefs. The Society was originally founded at New York, not Madras.
191.tq: Spot the location reversal between the original foundation and the later Indian headquarters.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are **correct**: Indian HQ at **Adyar**, Madras, moved in **1882**.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: it was founded at **New York** in **1875**, not Madras.
Statement 4 is **correct**: it believed in **karma and reincarnation**.
So **1, 2 and 4 only** — option **(2)** is correct.
xa: Founders: **Madame H.P. Blavatsky** (Russian) and **Col. H.S. Olcott** (American).
⚠ **1875** twice: **Arya Samaj (Bombay)** and **Theosophical Society (New York)**.

191.s:
With reference to the Theosophical Society, consider the following statements:
1. It drew upon the Upanishads, Samkhya, Yoga and Vedanta.
2. It condemned child marriage and worked for the uplift of outcastes and widows.
3. It rejected the doctrines of karma and reincarnation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
191.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Society drew on the Upanishads, Samkhya, Yoga and Vedanta. Statement 2 is correct: it condemned child marriage and worked for outcastes and widows. Statement 3 is wrong: karma and reincarnation were among its core beliefs. So '1 only' misses statement 2, '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' wrongly include statement 3.
191.tq: Theosophy = Hindu revival: it accepted karma and rebirth, so any statement that it rejected them is false.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: it drew on the **Upanishads, Samkhya, Yoga and Vedanta**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: it condemned **child marriage** and worked for **outcastes and widows**.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: **karma and reincarnation** were core beliefs.
So **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)** is correct.
xa: Aims: **universal brotherhood**; comparative religion.
Theosophy led straight into **Home Rule** politics.

191.s: The Telugu name of the Theosophical Society is:
191.x: The Theosophical Society is known in Telugu as Divya Gnana Samajam.
191.tq: Test the exact regional-language equivalent of a well-known organisation.
xs: The Theosophical Society's Telugu name is **Divya Gnana Samajam** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Its Indian HQ at **Adyar (Madras)** put Andhra in the Society's **core area**.
xa: **Krishna Divyajnana Lodge** set up the first public library in **Guntur** district (**1882**).
**Madanapalle** = Theosophy's Andhra centre (**BT College**, **1916**).
**Veeresalingam** set up the **first Theosophical High School** in Andhra.

191.s: The Theosophical Society was founded in 1875 by:
o: Madame H.P. Blavatsky and Col. H.S. Olcott
Annie Besant and Madan Mohan Malaviya
Swami Dayanand Saraswati and Col. H.S. Olcott
191.x: The Theosophical Society was founded at New York in 1875 by the Russian Madame H.P. Blavatsky and the American Col. H.S. Olcott. Annie Besant joined only in 1889 and became President in 1907; Malaviya worked with her on the Central Hindu College; Jiddu Krishnamurti was her adopted son; Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj.
191.tq: Theosophy founders = Blavatsky (Russian) + Olcott (American), New York 1875.
xs: The Theosophical Society was founded by **Madame H.P. Blavatsky** (Russian) and **Col. H.S. Olcott** (American) — option **(1)**.
It was founded at **New York** in **1875**.
**Annie Besant** joined in **1889**; **Malaviya** worked with her on BHU; **Krishnamurti** was her adopted son; **Dayanand** founded the Arya Samaj.
xa: Indian HQ moved to **Adyar, Madras** in **1882**.
Besant became President after Olcott's death (**1907**).
Blavatsky's books: **Isis Unveiled**, **The Secret Doctrine**.

191.s: Which of the following statements about the Besant Theosophical College is correct?
o: It was founded at Lahore in 1886 and its first Principal was Hansraj.
It was founded at Haridwar in 1902 and its first Principal was Swami Shraddhanand.
It was founded at Adyar in 1882 and its first Principal was H.S. Olcott.
It was founded at Madanapalle in 1916 and its first Principal was H.J. Cousins.
191.x: The Besant Theosophical College was founded by Annie Besant at Madanapalle in 1916; H.J. Cousins was its first Principal.
191.tq: Use the founder, location, year and first office-holder together to defeat swapped institutional details.
xs: **BT College** was founded at **Madanapalle** in **1916**; first Principal **H.J. Cousins** — option **(4)**.
**Lahore 1886** = first **DAV School**; **Haridwar 1902** = **Gurukul Kangri**; **Adyar 1882** = Theosophical HQ.
xa: Founder: **Annie Besant**; also called **Besant Theosophical (National) College**.
There **Rabindranath Tagore** translated **Jana Gana Mana** as **"Morning Song of India"** at Cousins' request.
**Madanapalle** = Theosophy's Andhra centre.

191.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Annie Besant is correct?
o: She came to India in 1882 and became President in 1893.
She joined the Society in 1907 and became President in 1916.
She founded the Society at New York in 1875 and became President in 1882.
She came to India in 1893 and became President of the Theosophical Society in 1907.
191.x: Annie Besant came to India in 1893 and became President of the Theosophical Society in 1907 after the death of Olcott.
191.tq: Separate the dates of joining, arrival in India and assumption of the presidency.
xs: Annie Besant **came to India in 1893** and **became President in 1907** — so option **(4)** is correct.
She **joined** the Society in **1889**; became President after **Olcott's** death.
xa: ⚠ **1889** joined; **1893** came to India; **1907** President; **1916** Home Rule League; **1917** INC President.
**1882** = HQ moved to **Adyar**; **1875** = founding at **New York** by Blavatsky and Olcott.

191.s:
Which of the following statements about Annie Besant is correct?
1. She became the first woman President of the Indian National Congress at Calcutta in 1917.
2. She launched the Home Rule movement in 1916.
3. She was associated with the papers New India and Commonweal.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
191.x: All three statements are correct. Annie Besant was associated with Home Rule in 1916, the papers New India and Commonweal, and the 1917 Calcutta Congress presidency.
191.tq: Combine a leader’s political role, publications and organisational activity.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: first woman **INC President**, **Calcutta 1917**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: **Home Rule League (1916)** (one note says 1915).
Statement 3 is **correct**: papers **New India** and **Commonweal**.
So **1, 2 and 3** — option **(4)** is correct.
xa: Andhra Home Rule workers: **Konda Venkatappayya**, **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**, **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao** (Secretary).
She founded **Central Hindu College** (**1898**) and **BT College, Madanapalle** (**1916**).

191.s: Who, along with Madan Mohan Malaviya, is regarded as a founder of the Central Hindu College at Benaras?
191.x: Annie Besant founded the Central Hindu College at Benaras in 1898; with Madan Mohan Malaviya it became the nucleus of Banaras Hindu University (1916). Olcott co-founded the Theosophical Society, Sister Nivedita was Vivekananda's disciple, and Shraddhanand led the Gurukul party of the Arya Samaj.
191.tq: Benaras Hindu College + Malaviya -> Annie Besant (APPSC-GS 2025).
xs: **Annie Besant** founded the **Central Hindu College** (**1898**), which with **Malaviya** became BHU — option **(1)**.
**Olcott** co-founded the Theosophical Society; **Sister Nivedita** was Vivekananda's disciple; **Shraddhanand** led the Gurukul party.
xa: APPSC-GS **2025** asked exactly this: answer **Annie Besant**.
Besant's adopted son: **Jiddu Krishnamurti** (**At the Feet of the Master**, **1910**).

191.s: Jiddu Krishnamurti, the adopted son of Annie Besant, wrote:
o: At the Feet of the Master
191.x: Jiddu Krishnamurti, adopted by Annie Besant, wrote At the Feet of the Master (1910). Isis Unveiled and The Secret Doctrine are by H.P. Blavatsky; My Master is by Swami Vivekananda.
191.tq: Krishnamurti = At the Feet of the Master; Blavatsky = Isis Unveiled, Secret Doctrine.
xs: **Jiddu Krishnamurti** wrote **At the Feet of the Master** (**1910**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Isis Unveiled** and **The Secret Doctrine** are by **Blavatsky**; **My Master** is by **Vivekananda**.
xa: Krishnamurti was **Annie Besant's adopted son**.
Besant's papers: **New India**, **Commonweal**.
Vivekananda's journals: **Prabuddha Bharata** (English), **Udbodhan** (Bengali).

191.s: At Madanapalle, Rabindranath Tagore translated ‘Jana Gana Mana’ into English under which title?

**1875** = Society founded at New York; **1893** = Besant came to India; **1916** = BT College / Home Rule League.

xs: **DAV party**: **Lala Hansraj** and **Lala Lajpat Rai**; **Gurukul party**: **Swami Shraddhanand** and **Pandit Lekh Ram** — option **(1)**.

191.s:
Consider the following statements about the split in the Arya Samaj:
1. It took place in 1893, after the death of Dayanand Saraswati.
2. It arose over Western versus Vedic education and the question of diet.
3. It took place during Dayanand Saraswati's lifetime, in 1875.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
191.x: Statement 1 is correct: the split came in 1893, after Dayanand's death. Statement 2 is correct: the issues were Western versus Vedic education and diet. Statement 3 is wrong: 1875 is the founding year of the Arya Samaj at Bombay, and the split came after Dayanand died. So '2 only' misses statement 1, and the options with statement 3 are wrong.
191.tq: 1875 = Arya Samaj founded; 1893 = split (DAV vs Gurukul) after Dayanand's death.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: the split came in **1893**, after **Dayanand's death**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: the cause was **Western vs Vedic education** and **diet**.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: **1875** is the year the Arya Samaj was **founded** at Bombay, not the split.
So **1 and 2 only** — option **(1)** is correct.
xa: **DAV party**: **Mahatma Hansraj**, **Lala Lajpat Rai** — **First DAV School, Lahore, 1886**.
**Gurukul party**: **Swami Shraddhanand** (Munshi Ram), **Pandit Lekh Ram** — **Gurukul Kangri, Haridwar (1902)**.

191.s:
Consider the following statements about Gurukul Kangri:
1. It was established at Haridwar in 1902.
2. It followed a traditional Vedic curriculum.
3. It was the institution of the College (DAV) party led by Lala Lajpat Rai and Mahatma Hansraj.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
191.x: Statement 1 is correct: Gurukul Kangri was set up at Haridwar in 1902. Statement 2 is correct: it followed a traditional Vedic curriculum. Statement 3 is wrong: it belonged to the Gurukul party of Swami Shraddhanand and Pandit Lekh Ram; the DAV party of Hansraj and Lajpat Rai had the first DAV School, Lahore (1886). So '1 only' misses 2, and the options with 3 are wrong.
191.tq: Gurukul party = Shraddhanand (Munshi Ram) + Lekh Ram, Haridwar 1902; DAV party = Hansraj + Lajpat Rai, Lahore 1886.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **Gurukul Kangri** was set up at **Haridwar** in **1902**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: it followed a **traditional Vedic curriculum**.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: it belonged to the **Gurukul party** of **Shraddhanand** and **Lekh Ram**, not the DAV party.
So **1 and 2 only** — option **(3)** is correct.
xa: The DAV party's institution: **First DAV School, Lahore, 1886**.
⚠ **Swami Shraddhanand** = **Munshi Ram**.

191.s:
Consider the following statements about the Arya Samaj:
1. It opposed caste based on birth.
2. It supported widow remarriage and women’s education.
3. It held idol worship to be useful and essential.
4. It maintained that all people could read the Vedas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
191.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. The Arya Samaj considered idol worship useless, making statement 3 false.
191.tq: Find the single doctrinal reversal among several reform principles.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are **correct**: against **caste by birth**; for **widow remarriage** and **women's education**; **all may read the Vedas**.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: the Samaj held **idol worship useless**.
So **1, 2 and 4 only** — option **(1)** is correct.
xa: It believed in **One God** and opposed **child marriage**.
Its **Shuddhi** movement aimed at **reconversion** to Hinduism.
Text: **Satyarth Prakash**; slogan: **"Back to the Vedas"**.

191.s: Which organisation launched the Shuddhi Movement?
191.x: The Shuddhi Movement was launched by the Arya Samaj.
191.tq: Identify the organisation from a movement–organisation association.
xs: The **Shuddhi Movement** was launched by the **Arya Samaj** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Its purpose: **reconversion** to Hinduism and **admission of outsiders**.
xa: The **Brahmo Samaj** (**1828**) was Rammohan Roy's; the **Theosophical Society** (**1875**) Blavatsky and Olcott's; the **RKM** (**1897**) Vivekananda's.
**Keshavdev Gnaneshi**, a disciple of **Shraddhanand**, carried Shuddhi to **Guntur**.
Secretary of the **Andhra Shuddhi Samajam** (**1934**): **Upputuru Venkata Punnarao**.

191.s: The cultural role of these reform movements in the growth of Indian nationalism was primarily to:
o: Strengthen the colonial claim of Indian inferiority
Create cultural confidence and provide ground for the national movement
End all political activity in India
191.x: By generating cultural confidence against the colonial narrative of Indian inferiority, the reform movements helped prepare the ground for the national movement.
191.tq: Apply the cause-and-effect link between cultural reform and nationalism.
xs: The movements **created cultural confidence** and **provided ground for the national movement** — so option **(2)** is correct.
They countered the colonial **"inferiority"** narrative, not strengthened it.
xa: **Theosophy** led straight into **Home Rule**.
Common features: **rationalism**, **education**, **women's emancipation**, attack on caste.
Significance: Theosophy + Ramakrishna movement restored **Indian cultural self-confidence**.

191.s: Which statement best describes the political significance of Theosophy in the Indian context?
o: It supported the colonial narrative of racial superiority
It remained completely separate from political activity
It opposed all forms of education
It led directly into the Home Rule movement
191.x: Theosophy led directly into Home Rule, particularly through Annie Besant’s activities and publications.
191.tq: Identify the direct political consequence of an intellectual movement.
xs: Theosophy **led directly into the Home Rule movement** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Annie Besant** started the **Home Rule League (1916)** and ran **New India** and **Commonweal**.
xa: Besant became first woman **INC President**, **Calcutta 1917**.
Her **Madras Home Rule League** reached Andhra; Secretary among Andhra workers: **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao**.
Theosophy = **foreign-founded Hindu revival**.

**Calcutta** = Brahmo Samaj; **Aligarh** = MAO College; **Kerala** = SNDP Yogam.
xa: Founders: **Madame H.P. Blavatsky** (Russian) and **Col. H.S. Olcott** (American).
Indian HQ moved to **Adyar, Madras** in **1882**.
Telugu name: **Divya Gnana Samajam**.

191.s: Match the bodies with their founding years: a. Arya Samaj  b. Prarthana Samaj  c. MAO College, Aligarh  d. SNDP Yogam ; i. 1867  ii. 1875  iii. 1877  iv. 1903
191.x: Arya Samaj was founded at Bombay in 1875, Prarthana Samaj at Bombay in 1867, MAO College at Aligarh in 1877 and SNDP Yogam in Kerala in 1903. The other codes swap 1875 with 1867 or 1877.
191.tq: 1867 Prarthana, 1875 Arya, 1877 MAO, 1903 SNDP (APPSC 2023-24).
xs: Correct match: **a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv** — option **(1)**.
**Arya Samaj 1875**; **Prarthana Samaj 1867**; **MAO College, Aligarh 1877**; **SNDP Yogam 1903**.

**Brahmo Samaj**: **Calcutta**, **1828**; **Ramakrishna Mission**: **1897**.

191.s:
Which one of the following correctly represents the comparative orientation of the three movements?
1. Arya Samaj — revivalist and associated with ‘Back to the Vedas’
2. Ramakrishna Mission — service and universalism
3. Theosophy — foreign-founded Hindu revival
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
191.x: All three comparisons are correct. Arya Samaj followed a revivalist ‘Back to the Vedas’ approach, the Ramakrishna Mission emphasised service and universalism, and Theosophy represented a foreign-founded Hindu revival.
191.tq: Compare the defining orientation of each movement instead of treating them as identical reform organisations.
xs: All three are **correct**: **Arya Samaj** = revivalist ("Back to the Vedas"); **RKM** = service and universalism; **Theosophy** = foreign-founded Hindu revival.

xa: Theosophy + Ramakrishna movement restored **Indian cultural self-confidence** against colonial claims.
Theosophy was founded at **New York** (**1875**) by **Blavatsky** and **Olcott**.
RKM motto: **"for one's own liberation and the welfare of the world"**.

Vinoba Bhave is listed as the founder/key person of Sarvodaya Samaj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #116 · pp 211-212]
xs: Statements **I, II and III** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
I: **Jyotiba Phule** — **Satyashodhak Samaj**; II: **Vinoba Bhave** — **Sarvodaya Samaj**.

**Radha Swami Satsang** — **Shivdayal Sahab**.

191.x: I, II and III are correct: the Theosophical Society stood for spiritual reform, the Satyashodhak Samaj for caste equality and Seva Sadan for women's welfare. IV is false because modern education among Muslims was the aim of the Aligarh Movement, not the Dev Samaj.
191.tq: Check the aim given in each statement.
n: The Theosophical Society was associated with spiritual reform. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #126 · pp 229-230]
The Theosophical Society was associated with religious reform. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #126 · pp 229-230]
Satyashodhak Samaj was associated with opposition to the caste system. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #126 · pp 229-230]
Satyashodhak Samaj was associated with social equality. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #126 · pp 229-230]
Seva Sadan was associated with women’s welfare. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #126 · pp 229-230]
Seva Sadan was associated with women’s education. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #126 · pp 229-230]
The Aligarh Movement was associated with modern education among Muslims. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #126 · pp 229-230]
xs: Statements **I, II and III** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
I: **Theosophical Society** — **spiritual and religious reform**; II: **Satyashodhak Samaj** — opposition to **caste discrimination**, **social equality**.

xa: Seva Sadan is linked with **Ramabai Ranade**.
Theosophical Society promoted the **universal brotherhood** of humanity.
Aligarh Movement was led by **Sir Syed Ahmad Khan**.

Brahmo Samaj promoted universal worship of one God. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #127 · pp 230-231]

n: Banaras Hindu University was the first Central University among the given options. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 60-64]
xs: **Banaras Hindu University** was the **first Central University** among the given options — so option **(3)** is correct.
BHU was established in **1916** at **Varanasi** through **Madan Mohan Malviya**'s efforts.

192.s:
Consider the following statements about the Wahabi Movement in India:
1. It was named after Abdul Wahab of Arabia.
2. It first fought the Sikhs in Punjab and then the British.
3. It was suppressed by 1857 and never faced British trials.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
192.x: Statement 1 is correct: the name comes from Abdul Wahab of Arabia, though the Indian founder was Syed Ahmad Barelvi. Statement 2 is correct: it fought the Sikhs in Punjab and then the British. Statement 3 is wrong: the British crushed it through the Ambala (1864) and Patna (1865) trials, and it was suppressed only by 1870. So '1 only' misses 2, and the options with 3 are wrong.
192.tq: Wahabi: Sikhs first, then British; Ambala 1864 + Patna 1865 trials; suppressed by 1870.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: named after **Abdul Wahab** of **Arabia**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: it fought the **Sikhs** in Punjab, then the **British**.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: the British held the **Ambala (1864)** and **Patna (1865)** trials; it was suppressed **by 1870**.
So **1 and 2 only** — option **(4)** is correct.
xa: Indian founder: **Syed Ahmad Barelvi**, inspired by **Shah Waliullah**.
Chief centre: **Patna**; aim: restore **Muslim power**.

192.s: Mubariz-ud-Daula, associated with Wahabi activity in Hyderabad, was:
o: A Parsi reformer who edited Rast Goftar
A brother of the Nizam who resisted British influence in the Deccan
A principal of the Aligarh college
A Sikh mahant who controlled gurdwaras in Punjab
192.x: Mubariz-ud-Daula was the Nizam’s brother. Influenced by Syed Ahmad Barelvi, he attempted to organise resistance to British influence in the Deccan and died in prison after his arrest.
192.tq: Match the regional leader with his family position and political activity.
xs: **Mubariz-ud-Daula** was **a brother of the Nizam** who tried to organise **resistance to British influence in the Deccan** — option **(2)**.
Influenced by **Syed Ahmad Barelvi**, he was arrested under British pressure (**1839**) and **died in prison**.
xa: The **Nawab of Kurnool** was also implicated.
This was **Wahabi** activity in **Hyderabad State** (APPSC G2 **2002**).
Wahabi trials later: **Ambala (1864)**, **Patna (1865)**.

192.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Wahabi movement in India?
o: A loyalist movement centred at Aligarh
An anti-British movement with its chief centre at Patna
A Parsi reform movement centred at Bombay
A peasant movement against indigo planters centred at Faridpur
192.x: The Indian Wahabi movement of Syed Ahmad Barelvi was anti-British in character, and its chief centre was Patna. Aligarh was the loyalist Aligarh Movement, Bombay the centre of Parsi reform, and Faridpur the Faraizi base of Dudu Miyan's peasant movement.
192.tq: Wahabi = anti-British, centre Patna (APPSC G2 2011).
xs: The Indian Wahabi movement was **anti-British**, with its **chief centre at Patna** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Aligarh** was loyalist; **Faridpur** was the **Faraizi** base, whose **Dudu Miyan** led peasants against indigo planters.
xa: Founder in India: **Syed Ahmad Barelvi** (Rae Bareli).
It fought the **Sikhs** in Punjab, then the **British**.
Suppressed **by 1870** after the **Ambala** and **Patna** trials.

192.s: The Faraizi Movement, founded in East Bengal, primarily aimed at:
o: Enforcing the religious duties known as faraiz and purging un-Islamic practices
192.x: The Faraizi Movement sought to enforce religious duties, or faraiz, and remove un-Islamic practices. It was founded by Haji Shariatullah in East Bengal.
192.tq: Identify the movement from its distinctive objective and religious terminology.
xs: The Faraizi movement sought to **purge un-Islamic practices** and **enforce religious duties (faraiz)** — option **(3)**.
Founder: **Haji Shariatullah**, **East Bengal (Faridpur)**, **1818**.
xa: His son **Dudu Miyan** turned it into a peasant movement against **zamindars** and **indigo planters**.
APPSC-GS **2019** paired **"Faraizi - Haji Shariatullah"**.
⚠ **Promoting Western education** among Muslims was the **Aligarh** / **Ahmadiya** aim.

192.s: Who founded the Faraizi Movement in East Bengal in 1818?
192.x: Haji Shariatullah founded the Faraizi Movement in East Bengal in 1818. Dudu Miyan, his son, later led the movement.
192.tq: Separate the founder from the later leader while retaining the date.
xs: **Haji Shariatullah** founded the Faraizi movement in **East Bengal**, **1818** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Dudu Miyan** was his **son and successor**; **Syed Ahmad Barelvi** led the Wahabis; **Mirza Ghulam Ahmad** founded the **Ahmadiya**.
xa: Base: **Faridpur**.
Aim: enforce **faraiz** (religious duties), purge un-Islamic practices.
APPSC-GS **2019** asked this pair.

192.s: Dudu Miyan transformed the Faraizi Movement into a movement primarily directed against:
o: British missionary institutions and Parsi reformers
192.x: Dudu Miyan, the son of Haji Shariatullah, converted the Faraizi Movement into a peasant movement against zamindars and indigo planters.
192.tq: Apply the movement’s social base and immediate opponents to a rural conflict.
xs: **Dudu Miyan** turned the Faraizi movement against **zamindars and indigo planters** — so option **(2)** is correct.
He was the **son and successor** of **Haji Shariatullah**.
xa: Faraizi founded in **East Bengal (Faridpur)**, **1818**.
Original aim: enforce **religious duties (faraiz)**.
⚠ Removing corrupt **mahants** was the Sikh **Akali** movement, not Faraizi.

192.s: The MAO Defence Association, formed in 1893, was primarily associated with which of the following positions?
o: Loyalism and opposition to the Congress
192.x: The MAO Defence Association, associated with Sayyid Ahmad Khan and Theodore Beck, was loyalist and anti-Congress in outlook.
192.tq: Identify the organisation's political stance rather than its educational association.
xs: The **MAO Defence Association** (**1893**) stood for **loyalism** and **opposition to the Congress** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It was formed by **Sayyid Ahmad Khan** with **Theodore Beck**.
xa: Earlier, in **1888**, he formed the **United Indian Patriotic Association** to counter the Congress.
**Deoband** issued a **fatwa (1888)** against his associations.
Beck was MAO principal (**1883-99**), followed by **Theodore Morison**.

192.s: Which of the following was the journal associated with Sayyid Ahmad Khan's reformist thought?
192.x: Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq was the journal associated with Sayyid Ahmad Khan's reformist and rational interpretation of Islam.
192.tq: Distinguish a journal from books and publications associated with other reformers.
xs: Sayyid Ahmad Khan's journal was **Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**The Indian Musalmans** is a **1871** book by **W.W. Hunter**, not a journal of Sayyid Ahmad.
xa: His book: **Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind** (**1859**) on the causes of **1857**.
He promoted **Urdu** as a unifying language of Muslims.
Aim: modernisation via **English education** + **rational reading of Islam**.

192.s:
Consider the following statements about Sayyid Ahmad Khan:
1. He lived from 1817 to 1898.
2. After 1857, he promoted the modernisation of Muslims through English education.
3. He advocated a rational reading of Islam.
4. He consistently maintained the same political view throughout his life and never spoke of Hindu-Muslim unity.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
192.x: Sayyid Ahmad Khan lived from 1817 to 1898 and promoted English education and rational religious interpretation after 1857. The fourth statement is false because his earlier thought included advocacy of Hindu-Muslim unity.
192.tq: Reject the absolute word 'never' by separating an earlier view from a later political position.
xs: Statements 1-3 are **correct**: he lived **1817-1898**; promoted **English education** after **1857**; advocated a **rational reading of Islam**.
Statement 4 is **wrong**: early on he called Hindus and Muslims India's **"two eyes"** and spoke for **Hindu-Muslim unity**.
So **1, 2 and 3 only** — option **(1)** is correct.
xa: His turn came after the **Hindi-Urdu controversy (1867)**.
He then formed the **United Indian Patriotic Association (1888)** to counter Congress.
Criticism: his later **political conservatism** sowed seeds of communal division.

192.s: The change in Sayyid Ahmad Khan's political outlook, from an earlier emphasis on Hindu-Muslim unity to separate political paths, was associated with the
192.x: The Hindi-Urdu controversy of 1867 contributed to the change in Sayyid Ahmad Khan's political outlook.
192.tq: Link the change in political outlook to the specific earlier controversy, not to later nationalist movements.
xs: His shift followed the **Hindi-Urdu controversy of 1867** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Earlier he called India a bride with Hindus and Muslims as **"her two eyes"**.
xa: Later he held that Hindus and Muslims needed **separate political paths**.
**United Indian Patriotic Association (1888)**; **MAO Defence Association (1893)**.
⚠ **1866** = Deoband; **1867** = Hindi-Urdu controversy.

192.s: Which of the following best describes Sayyid Ahmad Khan's political position towards the Indian National Congress?
o: He supported the Congress as the sole organisation representing both communities.
He founded the Congress and presided over its first session.
He asked Muslims to stay away from it and formed the United Indian Patriotic Association in 1888.
He joined the Congress through the Deoband fatwa of 1888.
192.x: Sayyid Ahmad Khan advised Muslims to remain away from the Congress and formed the United Indian Patriotic Association in 1888 to counter it.
192.tq: Use the organisation formed and its date to confirm the political position.
xs: He **asked Muslims to stay away** from the Congress and formed the **United Indian Patriotic Association in 1888** — option **(3)**.
The **Deoband fatwa (1888)** was **against** his association, not a way to join Congress.
xa: ⚠ **1888** twice: his **United Indian Patriotic Association** and Deoband's **fatwa** against it.
**MAO Defence Association** (**1893**, with **Theodore Beck**): loyalist, anti-Congress.
Comparative: **Aligarh** opposed Congress; **Deoband** welcomed it.

192.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Scientific Society associated with Sayyid Ahmad Khan:
1. It was founded at Ghazipur in 1864.
2. It translated Western science, history and philosophy into Urdu.
3. It was later shifted to Lucknow.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
192.x: The Scientific Society was founded at Ghazipur in 1864 and translated Western knowledge into Urdu. It was later shifted to Aligarh, not Lucknow.
192.tq: Split the statements by checking the institution's original and later locations.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: founded at **Ghazipur** in **1864**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: it translated **Western science, history and philosophy** into **Urdu**.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: it shifted to **Aligarh**, not Lucknow.
So **1 and 2 only** — option **(1)** is correct.
xa: Some notes give **1863** and Aligarh; **1864 at Ghazipur** is better supported.
⚠ **1863** = **Mohammadan Literary Society** (Calcutta, **Nawab Abdul Latif**).

192.s:
With reference to the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental institution, consider the following statements:
1. The school stage began at Aligarh in 1875.
2. It was elevated into a college in 1877.
3. It was founded by Theodore Beck.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
192.x: The MAO institution began as a school in 1875 and became a college in 1877 under Sayyid Ahmad Khan. Theodore Beck later served as its principal, but was not its founder.
192.tq: Distinguish the founder from a later principal and separate the school and college dates.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: the **MAO school** began at **Aligarh** in **1875**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: **college** classes began in **1877**.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: the founder was **Sir Syed Ahmad Khan**; **Theodore Beck** was a later **principal**.
So **1 and 2 only** — option **(1)** is correct.
xa: Modelled on **Oxford and Cambridge**; became **AMU in 1920**.
Beck (**1883-99**), then **Theodore Morison**, were MAO principals.

192.s: Which sequence correctly represents the institutional development of the Aligarh educational initiative?
o: College classes in 1877 — school in 1875 — AMU in 1920
School in 1875 — college classes in 1877 — AMU in 1920
AMU in 1920 — school in 1875 — college classes in 1877
School in 1877 — college classes in 1920 — AMU in 1875
192.x: The Aligarh institution began as a school in 1875, college classes started in 1877, and it became Aligarh Muslim University in 1920.
192.tq: Arrange the institutional stages by first identifying the earliest year.
xs: The sequence is **school in 1875 — college classes in 1877 — AMU in 1920** — option **(2)**.
The MAO College was founded by **Sir Syed Ahmad Khan** at **Aligarh**.
xa: It was modelled on **Oxford and Cambridge**.
The **Scientific Society** (**1864**) also later shifted to **Aligarh**.
Aligarh built the **modern educated Muslim middle class**.

192.s: The Deoband Movement began at Darul Uloom in 1866 under the leadership of
o: Mirza Ghulam Ahmad and Shibli Numani
Qasim Nanotavi and Rashid Ahmad Gangohi
Sayyid Ahmad Khan and Theodore Beck
192.x: Qasim Nanotavi and Rashid Ahmad Gangohi led the establishment of the Deoband movement at Darul Uloom in 1866.
192.tq: Use the paired-founder clue and avoid mixing Deoband leaders with Aligarh or Ahmadiya figures.
xs: Deoband (Darul Uloom, **1866**) was led by **Qasim Nanotavi** and **Rashid Ahmad Gangohi** — option **(3)**.
**Shariatullah / Dudu Miyan** = Faraizi; **Mirza Ghulam Ahmad** = Ahmadiya; **Sayyid Ahmad / Beck** = Aligarh.
xa: Location: **Deoband, Saharanpur (UP)** — APPSC-GS **2019**: "Darul Uloom Deoband is in" → **Uttar Pradesh**.
Lifespans: **Nanotavi 1832-80**; **Gangohi 1828-1905**.
⚠ Gangohi belongs to **Deoband**, not the **Taiyuni** movement.

192.s:
Consider the following statements about the Deoband Movement:
1. It began in Deoband in Saharanpur district of the United Provinces.
2. It was led by orthodox ulema.
3. Its principal aim was to promote loyalty to British rule.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
192.x: The movement began at Deoband in Saharanpur district and was led by orthodox ulema. It opposed foreign rule rather than promoting loyalty to the British.
192.tq: Test the location and leadership separately from the reversed political stance.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **Deoband**, **Saharanpur** district, United Provinces.
Statement 2 is **correct**: led by **orthodox ulema** (Nanotavi, Gangohi).
Statement 3 is **wrong**: it kept alive **jihad against foreign rulers** — **anti-British**.
So **1 and 2 only** — option **(1)** is correct.
xa: Founded **1866**; nature: orthodox **revivalist**.
It **welcomed the Congress**.

192.s: Which of the following was NOT an objective of the Deoband Movement?
o: To keep alive the spirit of jihad against foreign rulers
To replace traditional Islamic learning with exclusively Western education
To spread the pure teachings of the Quran and Hadith
192.x: The Deoband Movement aimed at religious revival, training religious leaders and resistance to foreign rule; replacing Islamic learning with exclusively Western education was not its objective.
192.tq: Find the option that reverses the movement's traditionalist educational character.
xs: **Replacing traditional Islamic learning with exclusively Western education** was NOT a Deoband aim — option **(3)**.
Deoband aims: spread pure **Koran and Hadis** teachings, keep alive **jihad against foreign rulers**, **train religious leaders**.
xa: Nature: **orthodox revivalist**; traditional Islamic learning, **anti-British**.
⚠ Deoband kept **jihad** alive; **Ahmadiya opposed jihad**.
**Western education** was the **Aligarh** approach.

192.s: The Deoband leadership's position towards the Indian National Congress was that it
o: remained permanently neutral towards all political organisations
welcomed the Congress and issued a fatwa against the anti-Congress associations of Sayyid Ahmad Khan
rejected the Congress and established the United Indian Patriotic Association
supported the MAO Defence Association against the Congress
192.x: The Deoband movement welcomed the Congress. In 1888, it issued a fatwa against Sayyid Ahmad Khan's United Indian Patriotic Association and MAO Association.
192.tq: Contrast the Congress-friendly Deoband position with the anti-Congress Aligarh position.
xs: Deoband **welcomed the Congress** and issued a **fatwa** against Sayyid Ahmad's anti-Congress associations — option **(2)**.
The **fatwa (1888)** targeted his **United Patriotic Association** and **MAO Association**.
xa: ⚠ **1888** twice: the **Association** and the **fatwa** against it.
Critics: Deoband backed the Congress more **to oppose Sir Syed** than from a positive creed.
**Mahmud-ul-Hasan** gave Deoband political content → **Jamiat-ul-Ulema**.

192.s:
Consider the following statements about later developments in the Deoband school:
1. Mahmud-ul-Hasan gave the Deoband movement political content, which led to the Jamiat-ul-Ulema.
2. Shibli Numani founded the Nadwat al-Ulama at Lucknow.
3. Shibli Numani opposed the teaching of English and European science.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
192.x: Statement 1 is correct: Mahmud-ul-Hasan gave Deoband political content, leading to the Jamiat-ul-Ulema. Statement 2 is correct: Shibli Numani founded the Nadwat al-Ulama at Lucknow (1894-96). Statement 3 is wrong: Shibli wanted English and European science to be taught. So '1 only' misses 2, while '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' wrongly include 3.
192.tq: Mahmud-ul-Hasan = politics (Jamiat-ul-Ulema); Shibli = Nadwa, Lucknow, open to English and science.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **Mahmud-ul-Hasan** gave Deoband political content → **Jamiat-ul-Ulema**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: **Shibli Numani** founded the **Nadwat al-Ulama**, **Lucknow** (**1894-96**).
Statement 3 is **wrong**: Shibli **wanted English and European science taught**.
So **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)** is correct.
xa: Shibli **backed Deoband**.
**Nadwatul Ulama**: Maulana **Muhammad Ali Mungeri**; Shibli prominent; Lucknow, **1894**.

192.s: Which one of the following is NOT a belief or feature associated with the Ahmadiya Movement?
o: A liberal and universal conception of religion
Unqualified acceptance of orthodox Muslim objections to its founder’s claims
Promotion of Western liberal education among Muslims
192.x: B is the odd one out: orthodox Muslims rejected Mirza Ghulam Ahmad's claim to be a messiah, so the movement never accepted their objections. A liberal and universal religion, opposition to jihad and Western liberal education among Muslims were all Ahmadiya features.
192.tq: Identify the statement that reverses the movement’s relationship with orthodox criticism.
xs: **Unqualified acceptance of orthodox objections** was NOT an Ahmadiya feature — orthodox Muslims **rejected** its founder — option **(2)**.
**Mirza Ghulam Ahmad** claimed to be a **messiah**; orthodox Muslims rejected the claim.
Ahmadiya features: **liberal and universal religion**, **opposed jihad**, **Western liberal education** among Muslims.
xa: Founded at **Qadian (Gurdaspur, Punjab)**, **1889**.
⚠ **Deoband** kept jihad alive; **Ahmadiya** opposed it.

192.s: The Muhammadan Literary Society (1863) founded by Nawab Abdul Latif was established at:
192.x: Nawab Abdul Latif founded the Muhammadan Literary Society at Calcutta in 1863. Aligarh was Sayyid Ahmad Khan's centre, Lucknow the seat of the Nadwatul Ulama, and Patna the chief centre of the Wahabis.
192.tq: Literary Society = Abdul Latif = Calcutta.
xs: **Nawab Abdul Latif's** Muhammadan Literary Society (**1863**) was set up at **Calcutta** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Aligarh** = Sayyid Ahmad Khan; **Lucknow** = **Nadwatul Ulama**; **Patna** = Wahabi centre.
xa: One APPSC key gives **1863**, another **1862** — the place is **Calcutta** in both.
⚠ **1863/1864** = Literary Society / **Scientific Society** (Ghazipur).

192.s: Who wrote The Indian Musalmans, published in 1871?
192.x: The Indian Musalmans was written by W.W. Hunter and published in 1871.
192.tq: Match a work with its author and publication year.
xs: **The Indian Musalmans** (**1871**) was written by **W.W. Hunter** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It came a year after the Wahabis were **suppressed by 1870**.
xa: Sayyid Ahmad Khan's book: **Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind** (**1859**).
His journal: **Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq**.
⚠ Don't confuse Hunter's book (**1871**) with Sayyid Ahmad's works.

192.s: Nasaraiah, who was popular among the Madigas, preached:
o: The superiority of zamindars over peasants
The necessity of armed jihad against all Western education
One God and opposition to idol worship
The establishment of Sikh gurdwara committees
192.x: Nasaraiah, a Sayyid Muslim who died in 1825, preached belief in one God and opposed idol worship. He was associated with the Vinukonda–Narasaraopet region of Guntur.
192.tq: Connect the regional reformer with his central religious teaching.
xs: **Nasaraiah** preached **one God** and opposed **idol worship** — so option **(3)** is correct.
He was a **Sayyid Muslim** (d. **1825**), popular with **Madigas**.
xa: Region: **Vinukonda-Narasaraopet** (**Guntur**).
Other AP Muslim figure: **Mubariz-ud-Daula** — Wahabi activity in Hyderabad.
**Osmania University (1918)**, Hyderabad, taught in **Urdu**.

192.s: Which one of the following statements about Osmania University is correct?
o: It was established at Bombay in 1851 and taught through Gujarati.
It was established at Qadian in 1889 and taught through Punjabi.
It was established at Aligarh in 1920 and taught only through Persian.
It was established at Hyderabad in 1918 and taught through Urdu.
192.x: Osmania University was established at Hyderabad in 1918 and taught in Urdu. It conferred an honorary D.Litt. on B.R. Ambedkar in 1953.
192.tq: Combine the institution’s place, year and medium of instruction.
xs: **Osmania University** was set up at **Hyderabad** in **1918** and taught through **Urdu** — option **(4)**.
**Qadian 1889** = Ahmadiya; **Aligarh 1920** = AMU.
xa: It gave **Ambedkar** an honorary **D.Litt in 1953**.
Sayyid Ahmad Khan promoted **Urdu** as a unifying language of Muslims.
**AMU** grew out of the **MAO College** (**1877**).

192.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Movement)
a. Nirankari
b. Namdhari or Kuka
c. Singh Sabha
d. Akali

List-II (Leader or feature)
i. Removal of corrupt mahants from gurdwaras
ii. Baba Dayal Das and belief in Nirankar
iii. Baba Ram Singh and Bhaini
a. Gurmukhi and Punjabi literature
192.x: Nirankari was associated with Baba Dayal Das and the formless God; Namdhari with Baba Ram Singh and Bhaini; Singh Sabha with Gurmukhi and Punjabi literature; and Akali with removal of corrupt mahants.
192.tq: Start from the distinctive Nirankar and mahant associations to secure the code.
xs: Correct match: **a–ii, b–iii, c–iv, d–i** — option **(1)**.
**Nirankari** – **Baba Dayal Das** (God as Nirankar); **Namdhari** – **Baba Ram Singh**, **Bhaini**; **Singh Sabha** – **Gurmukhi/Punjabi** literature; **Akali** – removal of corrupt **mahants**.
xa: **Akali Movement**: **1920**; it grew out of the **Singh Sabha**.
**Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925** put gurdwaras under the **SGPC**.
**Ram Singh Kuka** was exiled to **Rangoon** after the **1872 Malerkotla** clash.

192.s: Which statement best describes the significance of Ram Singh Kuka in the Sikh reform tradition?
o: He was the first to use non-cooperation and boycott of British goods.
He founded the Ahmadiya Movement at Qadian.
He introduced Urdu as the language of Osmania University.
He founded the Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha in Bombay.
192.x: Ram Singh Kuka is noted as the first to use non-cooperation and boycott of British goods. He was later exiled to Rangoon after the 1872 Malerkotla clash.
192.tq: Identify the distinctive method associated with the correct Sikh leader.
xs: **Ram Singh Kuka** was the **first to use non-cooperation and boycott of British goods** — option **(1)** (APPSC-GS **2025**).
He was exiled to **Rangoon** after the **1872 Malerkotla** clash.
xa: He led the **Namdhari (Kuka)** movement from **Bhaini, Ludhiana**.
Namdharis wore **white clothes** and gave up meat.
Namdharis were among the **earliest** movements to resist British rule in Punjab.

192.s: The Akali movement grew out of the:
192.x: The Akali movement grew out of the Singh Sabha movement and later developed into the Akali Dal as a political party.
192.tq: Trace institutional succession among closely related Sikh movements.
xs: The Akali movement **grew out of** the **Singh Sabha movement** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **Nirankari** movement was **Baba Dayal Das's**, centred on God as **Nirankar**.
xa: **Akali Movement (1920)** removed corrupt **mahants** and became a **political party**.
Its success: **Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925** → gurdwaras under the **SGPC**.
Singh Sabha promoted **Gurmukhi/Punjabi** literature.

192.s: The Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925 placed the gurdwaras under the control of the:
192.x: The Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925 placed the gurdwaras under the SGPC. The Akali movement later became the political party known as the Akali Dal.
192.tq: Distinguish the statutory administrative body from the later political party.
xs: The **Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925** put gurdwaras under the **SGPC** (**Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee**) — option **(3)**.
This was the **Akali movement's** success; it had **removed corrupt mahants**.
xa: The Akali movement (**1920**) grew out of the **Singh Sabha** and became a political party.
Sikh **Anand Marriage Act, 1909**, amended **2012** to allow registration.
Parsi marriages: **Parsi Marriage and Divorce Act, 1936**.

192.s:
Arrange the following movements in chronological order of their establishment:
A. Faraizi Movement
B. Deoband Movement
C. Ahmadiya Movement
D. Nadwatul Ulama
192.x: The Faraizi Movement dates from 1818, Deoband from 1866, Ahmadiya from 1889 and Nadwatul Ulama from 1894.
192.tq: Fix the earliest and latest items first, then place the two nineteenth-century movements between them.
xs: Order: **A, B, C, D** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Faraizi 1818** → **Deoband 1866** → **Ahmadiya 1889** → **Nadwatul Ulama 1894**.
xa: Faraizi: **Haji Shariatullah**, East Bengal.
Deoband: **Nanotavi** and **Gangohi**, Saharanpur.
Ahmadiya: **Mirza Ghulam Ahmad**, Qadian; Nadwatul Ulama: **Lucknow**, Shibli prominent.

192.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Aligarh and Deoband approaches?
o: Aligarh emphasised Western education and loyalty to the British, whereas Deoband emphasised traditional Islamic learning and opposed foreign rule.
Aligarh opposed Western education, whereas Deoband promoted exclusive Western education.
Both movements opposed the Congress and supported loyalty to the British.
Both movements rejected religious education and concentrated only on political agitation.
192.x: The Aligarh approach promoted Western education and loyalty to the British, while Deoband upheld traditional Islamic learning and adopted an anti-foreign-rule orientation.
192.tq: Compare both columns together, especially education policy and political attitude.
xs: **Aligarh**: **Western education** and **loyalty to the British**; **Deoband**: **traditional Islamic learning**, **anti-British** — option **(1)**.
Aligarh **opposed Congress**; Deoband **welcomed** it — so option (3) is wrong.
xa: Deoband's **fatwa (1888)** targeted Sayyid Ahmad's anti-Congress associations.
Aligarh built the **modern educated Muslim middle class**; Deoband kept the **anti-colonial** strand alive.
Critics: Deoband backed Congress more to **oppose Sir Syed**.

192.s:
Arrange the following developments associated with Sayyid Ahmad Khan in chronological order:
A. Establishment of the Scientific Society at Ghazipur
B. Beginning of the MAO school at Aligarh
C. Establishment of the Muhammadan Educational Conference
D. Formation of the United Indian Patriotic Association
192.x: The Scientific Society began in 1864, the MAO school in 1875, the Muhammadan Educational Conference in 1886, and the United Indian Patriotic Association in 1888.
192.tq: Place the dated milestones in ascending order and use the 1886–1888 pair as the final check.
xs: Order: **A, B, C, D** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Scientific Society, Ghazipur 1864** → **MAO school 1875** → **Muhammadan Educational Conference 1886** → **United Indian Patriotic Association 1888**.
xa: MAO **college** classes began in **1877**; it became **AMU in 1920**.
