194.tq: Distinguish the founder of the mission from founders of other anti-caste organisations.
xs: **V.R. Shinde** founded the **Depressed Classes Mission** at **Bombay** in **1906** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Phule** founded the **Satyashodhak Samaj** (**1873**); **Ambedkar** the **BHS** (**1924**); **Gandhi** the **Anti-Untouchability League** (**1932**).
xa: **1906** also = **Jagan Mitra Mandali** (Bhagya Reddy Varma).
**All India Depressed Classes Association** = **M.C. Rajah**.
⚠ Gandhi's own body = **Anti-Untouchability League / Harijan Sevak Sangh**.

194.s: The All India Anti-Untouchability League, founded in September 1932, was renamed the Harijan Sevak Sangh in:
194.x: The League was founded in September 1932 and renamed the Harijan Sevak Sangh in 1933.
194.tq: Distinguish an organisation's founding year from its renaming year.
xs: The **Anti-Untouchability League** (Sept **1932**) was renamed **Harijan Sevak Sangh** in **1933** — option **(2)**.
Some notes date the Sangh to **1932** (the League's founding).
xa: Founder **Gandhi**; president **G.D. Birla**; secretary **A.V. Thakkar**.
Gandhi's weekly **Harijan** also began in **1933**.
⚠ Gandhi did not found the "All India Depressed Class Association" — that was **M.C. Rajah**.

194.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: All India Depressed Classes Association — M.C. Rajah
194.x: M.C. Rajah was associated with the All India Depressed Classes Association. The Scheduled Castes Federation was established in 1942, the Independent Labour Party in 1936, and Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha was founded by Ambedkar.
194.tq: Use a sure leader–organisation pair to eliminate swapped dates and founders.
xs: **All India Depressed Classes Association — M.C. Rajah** is correctly matched — option **(3)**.
**SCF** = **1942**; **ILP** = **1936** (options 1 and 2 swap the years); **BHS** = **Ambedkar**, not Gandhi.
xa: Gandhi's body: **Anti-Untouchability League** (**1932**) → **Harijan Sevak Sangh** (**1933**).
⚠ "Gandhi founded the All India Depressed Class Association" is a trap.

194.s: Consider the following pairs: 1. Satyashodhak Samaj - 1873  2. Veda Samaj - 1864  3. SNDP Yogam - 1906. Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
194.x: Pair 1 is correct: the Satyashodhak Samaj dates from 1873. Pair 2 is correct: Veda Samaj, 1864. Pair 3 is wrong: SNDP Yogam was founded in 1903 (1906 is the Depressed Classes Mission). So '1 only' misses pair 2, and the options with pair 3 are wrong.
194.tq: 1864 Veda Samaj, 1873 Satyashodhak, 1903 SNDP (APPSC-GS 2023).
xs: Pair 1 is **correct**: **Satyashodhak Samaj – 1873**.
Pair 2 is **correct**: **Veda Samaj – 1864**.
Pair 3 is **wrong**: **SNDP Yogam** was founded in **1903**; **1906** = **Depressed Classes Mission**.
So **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)** is correct.
xa: This was the APPSC-GS **2023** year match.
SNDP: **Ezhavas**, Kerala, **Sree Narayana Guru**.

194.s: Who founded the journal Vital-Vidhvansak in 1888?
194.x: Vital-Vidhvansak was founded in 1888 by Gopal Baba Walangkar.
194.tq: Match a journal with its founder rather than with a related social reformer.
xs: **Gopal Baba Walangkar** founded **Vital-Vidhvansak** in **1888** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Din Bandhu** (**1877**) was **Krishnarao Bhalekar's**, later **N.M. Lokhande's**; **V.R. Shinde** founded the **Depressed Classes Mission**.
xa: Walangkar also founded the **Anarya Dosh Pariharak Mandali** (**Mahars**).
⚠ **1888** also = Phule's title **"Mahatma"**.
**Mooknayak** (**1920**) = **Ambedkar**.

194.s: Mooknayak and Bahishkrit Bharat were founded by whom?
194.x: Mooknayak and Bahishkrit Bharat were journals founded by B.R. Ambedkar.
194.tq: Group two journals under their common founder.
xs: **Mooknayak** and **Bahishkrit Bharat** were founded by **B.R. Ambedkar** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Gandhi** = **Harijan**; **Jala Rangaswamy** = **Jai Bheem**, **Veera Bharati**; **Walangkar** = **Vital-Vidhvansak**.
xa: **Mooknayak** = "Leader of the Silent" (**1920**); **Bahishkrit Bharat** **1927**.
Ambedkar's third journal: **Janata**.
⚠ **Mooknayak** = Ambedkar; **Kudi Arasu** = Periyar.

194.s: The weekly Harijan, started in 1933, was founded by:
194.x: Gandhi founded the weekly Harijan in 1933. Ambedkar founded Mooknayak and Bahishkrit Bharat, Periyar Kudi Arasu, and Walangkar Vital-Vidhvansak.
194.tq: Harijan (1933) = Gandhi; Mooknayak = Ambedkar; Kudi Arasu = Periyar.
xs: **Gandhi** founded the weekly **Harijan** in **1933** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Ambedkar** = **Mooknayak**, **Bahishkrit Bharat**; **Periyar** = **Kudi Arasu**; **Walangkar** = **Vital-Vidhvansak**.
xa: **1933** also = League renamed **Harijan Sevak Sangh**.
Gandhi used the term "**Harijan**"; saw untouchability as a **corruption**.
Gandhi's **1932-33** Andhra tour collected **Harijana Bhiksha**.

194.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
194.x: The Orion was written by Bal Gangadhar Tilak, not B.R. Ambedkar. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
194.tq: Use the wrong-author trap with books of closely associated reformers.
xs: **The Orion — B.R. Ambedkar** is wrongly matched; **The Orion** is by **Tilak** — option **(1)**.
**Nimna Jatula Charitra – Jala Rangaswamy**, **Annihilation of Caste – Ambedkar**, **Gulamgiri – Phule** are correct.
xa: **Annihilation of Caste** (**1936**) also rebukes **Gandhi's** approach.
**Gulamgiri** = Slavery, **1873**.
⚠ "The Evils/Devils of Caste" in some notes = standard **Annihilation of Caste**.

194.s: Who among the following is associated with the works Paleru, Gudiselu Kalipotunnai, Pilli Shatakam and Paleru Nundi Padmasri Daka?
194.x: These works are associated with Boyi Bhimanna.
194.tq: Start from a distinctive work-title cluster and identify its author.
xs: **Paleru**, **Gudiselu Kalipotunnai**, **Pilli Shatakam**, **Paleru Nundi Padmasri Daka** are linked to **Boyi Bhimanna** — option **(2)**.
**Jala Rangaswamy** wrote **Nimna Jatula Charitra**; **Tripuraneni** wrote **Sambuka Vadha**; **Vaddipati Niranjanasastri** ran **Prabhodini**.
xa: Tripuraneni's other works: **Kurukshetra Sangramam**, **Suta Puranam**.
**Gora** wrote **Positive Atheism**.
Prabhodini (**1907**) was the **Viswa Brahmana Sangham** journal.

194.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Annihilation of Caste was written by B.R. Ambedkar.
2. Who Were the Shudras? and The Untouchables were also written by B.R. Ambedkar.
3. Nimna Jatula Charitra was written by Ambedkar.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
194.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Nimna Jatula Charitra was written by Jala Rangaswamy, not B.R. Ambedkar.
194.tq: Catch the wrong author assigned to a similar anti-caste title.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **Annihilation of Caste** (**1936**) is **Ambedkar's**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: **Who Were the Shudras?** and **The Untouchables** are Ambedkar's.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: **Nimna Jatula Charitra** is by **Jala Rangaswamy**.
So **1 and 2 only** — option **(1)** is correct.
xa: Ambedkar also wrote **The Problem of the Rupee**.
APPSC-GS **2019** asked **Who Were the Shudras?** → Ambedkar.

194.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. First Provincial Panchama Mahajana Sabha at Vijayawada
B. Jagan Mitra Mandali
C. First Adi-Andhra Sadassu at Amalapuram
D. All India Adi Hindu Conference at Lucknow
194.x: Jagan Mitra Mandali was established in 1906, the first Adi-Andhra session was held in 1917, the Amalapuram Sadassu in 1921, and the Lucknow conference in 1930.
194.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the middle events by year.
xs: Order: **B, A, C, D** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Jagan Mitra Mandali 1906** → **Panchama Mahajana Sabha, Vijayawada 1917** → **Amalapuram Sadassu 1921** → **Adi Hindu Conference, Lucknow 1930**.
xa: **Machilipatnam** conference: **1919**.
**Vizianagaram** Mahasabha: **1936** (**Kusuma Dharmanna**).
**Lucknow 1930** chose **Ambedkar** for the Round Table Conferences.

194.s:
Which of the following chronological sequences is correct?
A. Satyashodhak Samaj
B. SNDP Yogam
C. Justice Party
D. Self-Respect Movement
194.x: The organisations were established in 1873, 1903, 1916 and 1925 respectively.
194.tq: Arrange organisations by their establishment years.
xs: Order: **A, B, C, D** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Satyashodhak 1873** → **SNDP 1903** → **Justice Party 1916** → **Self-Respect 1925**.
xa: **Vaikom** and **BHS**: **1924**.

194.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: First Panchama Mahajana Sabha at Vijayawada — 1917
194.x: The Madras Communal G.O. was issued in 1921, not 1937. The other pairs are correctly matched.
194.tq: Locate the incorrect year among a sequence of reform milestones.
xs: **Communal G.O. — 1937** is wrongly matched; the G.O. was issued in **1921** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**BHS 1924**, **Jagan Mitra Mandali 1906**, **Panchama Mahajana Sabha 1917** are correct.
xa: **1937** = Justice Party's defeat and the **anti-Hindi agitation**.
Communal G.O. = root of South Indian **reservation** policy.
CDX dates it **Dec 1921**.

194.s:
Consider the following statements about the Justice Party:
1. It won reservations for non-Brahmins by the 1920s.
2. It formed the government four times from 1920.
3. It declined by 1937.
4. Its communal representation policy had no connection with non-Brahmin interests.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
194.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because safeguarding non-Brahmin interests and communal representation were central to the Justice Party's politics.
194.tq: Reject the statement that reverses the organisation's stated social and political purpose.
xs: Statements 1-3 are **correct**: it **won reservations** by the **1920s**, formed government **four times** from **1920**, and **declined by 1937**.
Statement 4 is **wrong**: protecting **non-Brahmin** interests through communal representation was its core aim.
So **1, 2 and 3 only** — option **(1)** is correct.
xa: Source: The Hindu (**16 Jun 2026**).
Non-Brahmin reservations began in **1920** → shaped Tamil politics.

194.s: Which of the following was a major criticism of the Justice Party?
o: It was anti-British, peasant-led and dominant among Andhra masses
It opposed all forms of reservation for non-Brahmins
It was pro-British, landlord-led and weak among Andhra masses
It was exclusively led by Dalit organisations
194.x: The Justice Party was criticised for being pro-British and landlord-led, and for having a weak base among the Andhra masses.
194.tq: Select the option containing the historically precise combination of criticisms.
xs: The Justice Party was criticised as **pro-British**, **landlord-led** and **weak among Andhra masses** — option **(3)**.
It **won reservations** for non-Brahmins, so option (2) is wrong.
xa: British backed it partly to **weaken Home Rule**.
It **opposed the freedom struggle and the Andhra movement**.
**Natesa Mudaliar** attacked its neglect of the **poor and Harijans**.

194.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the comparative approaches of Gandhi and Ambedkar:
1. Gandhi viewed varna as a division of labour.
2. Gandhi regarded untouchability as a corruption.
3. Ambedkar sought the annihilation of caste and legal rights.
4. Ambedkar’s approach included the demand for separate electorates.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
194.x: All four statements accurately describe the contrast: Gandhi defended varna as division of labour while opposing untouchability, whereas Ambedkar sought caste annihilation, legal rights and separate electorates.
194.tq: Compare reform within the varna framework with the demand for annihilation of caste.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are **correct**: Gandhi saw **varna as division of labour** and **untouchability as a corruption**.
Statements 3 and 4 are **correct**: Ambedkar sought caste's **annihilation**, **legal rights** and **separate electorates**.
So **1, 2, 3 and 4** — option **(1)** is correct.
xa: **Annihilation of Caste** (**1936**) rebukes **Gandhi's** approach.
**Poona Pact** (**1932**): reserved seats in **joint electorates** replaced separate electorates.

194.s: Which one of the following correctly contrasts Periyar’s movement with the Andhra non-Brahmin movement?
o: Periyar’s movement was anti-religious, whereas Andhra’s was largely reformist and education-led
Periyar’s movement was education-led, whereas Andhra’s was exclusively anti-religious
Both movements were exclusively religious reform movements
Both movements rejected education as a means of social change
194.x: Periyar’s movement was strongly anti-religious, while the Andhra movement was mostly reformist and education-led.
194.tq: Identify the reversed comparison by carefully separating the characteristic of each regional movement.
xs: **Periyar's** movement was **anti-religious**; Andhra's was mostly **reformist and education-led** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Option (2) reverses the two.
xa: Periyar's movement **inspired the Adi-Andhra leaders**.
Self-Respect/DK stream **separated religion and caste from politics**.
Non-Brahmin politics helped **Reddys, Kammas and Kapus** rise.

194.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Satyashodhak Samaj was founded by Jyotiba Phule.
Deenbandhu spread the Satyashodhak movement in remote parts of Maharashtra.
Satyashodhak Samaj aimed at the upliftment of Arya-Brahmins.
Savitribai Phule headed the women's section of Satyashodhak Samaj.
194.x: Option C is incorrect: the Satyashodhak Samaj worked for backward classes, especially Shudras and Ati-Shudras, against exploitation by Arya-Brahmins. Phule founded it, Deenbandhu spread it and Savitribai led its women's section.
194.tq: Check the aim given in each statement.
n: Jyotiba Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
Deenbandhu spread the Satyashodhak movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
Deenbandhu spread the Satyashodhak movement to remote parts of Maharashtra. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
Satyashodhak Samaj worked for the upliftment of backward classes. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
Shudras and Ati-Shudras were the main beneficiaries of the Satyashodhak movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
The Satyashodhak movement opposed exploitation by Arya-Brahmins. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
Opposition to Arya-Brahmin exploitation was a Satyashodhak objective. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
Savitribai Phule headed the women's section of the Satyashodhak Samaj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
Jyotiba Phule worked for lower-caste upliftment. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
xs: The incorrect statement is "**Satyashodhak Samaj aimed at the upliftment of Arya-Brahmins**" — so option **(3)** is the answer.
It worked for **backward classes** — **Shudras** and **Ati-Shudras** — and **opposed exploitation** by **Arya-Brahmins**.
**Jyotiba Phule** founded it; **Deenbandhu** spread it; **Savitribai Phule** headed its women's section.
xa: It was founded at **Pune in 1873**.
Phule's symbol was **King Bali** against the Brahmanical symbol of Rama.
**Satyashodhak marriages**: inter-caste marriages **without priests**.

194.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Satyashodhak Samaj was founded by Jyotiba Phule.
II. Its main beneficiaries were Shudras and Ati-Shudras.
III. Its objective included liberation from exploitation.
IV. Deenbandhu headed the women's section of the organisation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
194.x: I, II and III are correct: Phule founded the Samaj for Shudras and Ati-Shudras and their freedom from exploitation. IV is false because Savitribai Phule, not Deenbandhu, headed its women's section.
194.tq: Check the person named in each statement.
n: Jyotiba Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
Shudras and Ati-Shudras were the main beneficiaries of the Satyashodhak movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
The Satyashodhak movement sought liberation from exploitation. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
Savitribai Phule headed the women's section of the Satyashodhak Samaj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
xs: Statements **I, II and III** are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
I: **Jyotiba Phule** founded the **Satyashodhak Samaj**; II: main beneficiaries — **Shudras** and **Ati-Shudras**.
III: it sought **liberation from exploitation**.
IV is wrong: **Savitribai Phule** headed the women's section; **Deenbandhu** spread the movement in remote Maharashtra.
xa: Phule (**1827-1890**) belonged to the **Mali community**.
Phule's girls' school in **Pune**: **1848**; home for upper-caste widows: **1854**.
Title "Mahatma" given by **Vithalrao Krishnaji Vandekar** (**1888**).

194.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Gulamgiri
(b) Sarvjanik Satyadharm Pustak

List-II
i. 1873 book comparing caste oppression with slavery
ii. Posthumous work (1891) setting out a universal religion of truth

a. a-i, b-ii
b. a-ii, b-i
c. a-i, b-i
d. a-ii, b-ii
194.x: Phule's Gulamgiri (1873) compared caste oppression with slavery, while Sarvajanik Satyadharma Pustak, published after his death in 1891, set out a universal religion of truth, giving a-i, b-ii.
194.tq: Recall Gulamgiri as the slavery book and the other as Phule's last work.
n: Gulamgiri was a work by Jyotiba Phule. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
Gulamgiri criticized Brahmanical domination. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
Sarvjanik Satyadharm Pustak was a work by Jyotiba Phule. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
Sarvjanik Satyadharm Pustak advanced anti-caste thought. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
Jyotiba Phule worked for lower-caste upliftment. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
xs: The correct match is **a-i, b-ii** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Gulamgiri** (**1873**) compared lower castes' condition to **slavery** and **criticized Brahmanical domination**.
**Sarvjanik Satyadharm Pustak** **advanced anti-caste thought** — a universal religion of truth.
xa: Other Phule works: **Shetkaryacha Asud**, **Tritiya Ratna**, **Brahmananche Kasab**.
**Who Were the Shudras?** and **Annihilation of Caste** (**1936**) are by **B.R. Ambedkar**.
⚠ **The Orion** (**Tilak**) is a regular distractor.

194.s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Jyotiba Phule belonged to the Mali community.
Statement B: The Satyashodhak Samaj was founded for the upliftment of backward classes.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
194.x: Both are true: Jyotiba Phule belonged to the Mali community, and he founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873 to uplift the backward classes.
194.tq: Check each statement separately.
n: Jyotiba Phule belonged to the Mali community. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
Satyashodhak Samaj worked for the upliftment of backward classes. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
Jyotiba Phule worked for lower-caste upliftment. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
xs: **Both Statement A and Statement B are true** — so option **(1)** is correct.
A: **Jyotiba Phule** belonged to the **Mali community**.
B: the **Satyashodhak Samaj** worked for the **upliftment of backward classes**.
xa: Satyashodhak Samaj = "**Society of Truth Seekers**", founded at **Pune** in **1873**.
Phule is called the "**Father of Indian Social Revolution**".
**Savitribai** was India's first woman teacher (Pune, **1848**).

195.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Brahmo movement in Andhra:
1. Its period of greatest influence was approximately from 1870 to 1935.
2. Rajahmundry and Kakinada were its principal centres in Andhra.
3. The movement was based on monotheism and opposition to idol worship.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
195.x: All three statements are correct. The Brahmo movement in Andhra reached its peak during 1870–1935, with Rajahmundry and Kakinada as its main centres, and upheld monotheism without idol worship.
195.tq: Test the time span, centres and defining principle together.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** **1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1 is correct: Andhra reform peaked in **1870-1935**.
Statement 2 is correct: its main centres were **Rajahmundry** and **Kakinada**; Machilipatnam, Bapatla and Guntur followed.
Statement 3 is correct: the parent **Brahmo Samaj** (**Raja Ram Mohan Roy**, **1828**, Calcutta) stood for **monotheism** and **no idol worship**.
xa: **Trinity of Brahmo Samaj** in Andhra: **Veeresalingam**, **Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu**, **Desiraju Peda Bapayya**.
Samaj timeline: **Machilipatnam 1882**, **Rajahmundry 1887**, **Kakinada 1888**, **Guntur 1898**.
⚠ **1878** = **Prarthana Samaj**, Rajahmundry; **1887** = **Brahmo Samaj**, Rajahmundry.
The movement declined through splits after Venkataratnam Naidu joined the **Justice Party**.

195.s: The earliest phase of Andhra social reform was led mainly by which social group?
195.x: The reform movement began in Rajahmundry under the leadership of the English-educated middle class. It was not an exclusive movement of rulers, soldiers or European missionaries.
195.tq: Identify the social base of a movement rather than its geographical location.
xs: Andhra reform began at **Rajahmundry** under the **English-educated middle class** — option **(4)**.
It was not the work of princely families, a military aristocracy or missionaries alone; zamindari patrons such as the **Pithapuram Raja** only funded later work.
Its first guru was **Atmuri Lakshmi Narasimham**.
xa: Rajahmundry (**Godavari district**, today East Godavari) = Andhra's **first Renaissance centre**.
Peak period: **1870-1935**; other main centre **Kakinada**.
Veeresalingam used the **press, not politics**, for reform; by **1905** about **20** Telugu journals were in print.
Reform became institutional — **samajs, homes, journals** — and so outlived its founders.

195.s: Who is identified as the first guru associated with the early social reform movement in Andhra?
195.x: Atmuri Lakshmi Narasimham is identified as the first guru of the early Andhra social reform movement.
195.tq: Recall the specific title-holder among several reform-era personalities.
xs: **Atmuri Lakshmi Narasimham** is named the **first guru** of Andhra social reform — option **(1)**.
**Gidugu Ramamurthy** led the **vyavaharika** (spoken Telugu) movement; **Gurajada Apparao** wrote **Kanyasulkam**.
**Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary** was the rationalist poet called **Kavi Raju**.
xa: The early reform was led by the **English-educated middle class** of **Rajahmundry**.
Peak: **1870-1935**; main centres **Rajahmundry** and **Kakinada**.
First organised reform body: **Rajahmundry Social Reform Association** (Veeresalingam).

195.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with the place and year mentioned in the context of Andhra reform activity?
o: Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam — Hyderabad, 1898
195.x: The Kavi Club was at Kumudavalli (West Godavari) in 1897. The traps: the 1882 Brahmo Samaj was at Machilipatnam (Guntur's Samaj came in 1898), the Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam at Hyderabad dates to 1901, and the Kakinada Samaj was at Kakinada in 1888.
195.tq: Check both components of a place–year pair instead of accepting a familiar institution name.
xs: The **Kavi Club** was at **Kumudavalli** (West Godavari) in **1897** — option **(3)** is correctly matched.
The **1882** Brahmo Samaj was at **Machilipatnam**, not Guntur; the **Guntur Samaj** came in **1898**.
**Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam** (Hyderabad) dates to **1901**, not 1898.
The **Kakinada Samaj** was at Kakinada in **1888**, not Rajahmundry in 1898.
xa: Kakinada Samaj founders: **Tayi Surya Prakasarao Naidu**, Duggirala Surya Prakasarao; Guntur Samaj: **Pillarisetty Sitaramayya**.
The Bhasha Nilayam was founded by **Komarraju Lakshmana Rao** with Ravichettu Ranga Rao and Nayani Venkata Ranga Rao.
**Bapatla** is linked with **Desiraju** (Peda Bapayya).

195.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Pennsylvania Synod — Guntur, Prattipadu and Nallapadu
195.x: The Church Mission Society operated in the Krishna-Godavari region and had a school at Machilipatnam; it was not confined to Palnadu.
195.tq: Reject the option that narrows a mission’s area incorrectly.
xs: "**Church Mission Society — Palnadu only**" is wrong — option **(4)**; the CMS worked in **Krishna-Godavari** from **1841**.
Palnadu had schools of the **American Baptist** mission.
The other pairs are correct: **LMS — Jammalamadugu**, **Pennsylvania Synod — Guntur, Prattipadu, Nallapadu**, **North German Mission — Godavari**.
xa: CMS's **Machilipatnam school** (**1841**) became a college in **1864**.
⚠ **London Missionary Society** = **Jammalamadugu 1805**; **Church Mission Society** = Krishna-Godavari **1841**.
American Baptists: **Rayalaseema 1835**; schools in Guntur, Gurazala, Palnadu, Ongole, Nellore.

195.s: Which of the following statements about Christian mission schools in Andhra is correct?
o: They admitted only members of the upper castes.
They excluded children from socially disadvantaged communities.
They admitted only converts from Europe.
195.x: Christian mission schools admitted Sudras and Panchamas, thereby extending education beyond the traditional upper-caste groups.
195.tq: Test the social composition of institutional beneficiaries.
xs: Christian mission schools **admitted Sudras and Panchamas** — option **(3)**.
So they neither restricted entry to upper castes nor excluded disadvantaged children.
xa: **London Missionary Society**: **Jammalamadugu, 1805**.
**American Baptists**: Rayalaseema **1835**; schools in Guntur, Gurazala, Palnadu, **Ongole**, Nellore.
**Church Mission Society**: Krishna-Godavari from **1841**; Machilipatnam school became a college in **1864**.
The **Bellary Christian Mission** issued the first Telugu journal, **Satyaduta** (**1835**).

195.s: The London Missionary Society began its work in Andhra in 1805 at:
195.x: The London Missionary Society is associated with Jammalamadugu in Cuddapah, where it began work in Andhra in 1805.
195.tq: Apply the place-and-year pair rather than relying on the organisation alone.
xs: The **London Missionary Society** began at **Jammalamadugu** (Cuddapah) in **1805** — option **(3)**.
**Machilipatnam** was a **Church Mission Society** centre (from **1841**).
**Rajahmundry** was the social-reform base, not an LMS centre.
xa: LMS also worked in **Cuddapah, Kurnool and Bellary**.
⚠ **LMS** = Jammalamadugu **1805**; **CMS** = Krishna-Godavari **1841**.
**North German Mission** = Godavari; **Pennsylvania Synod** = Guntur, Prattipadu, Nallapadu.

195.s: Which one of the following was the first organised social reform body in Andhra?
195.x: The Rajahmundry Social Reform Association was regarded as the first organised reform body in Andhra.
195.tq: Distinguish the earliest organisation from later reform bodies by its specific description.
xs: The **Rajahmundry Social Reform Association** was the **first organised reform body** in Andhra — option **(2)**.
Its aim was **widow remarriage** — shelter, legal defence and money for widows.
The **Prarthana Samaj** (**1878**), **Widow Remarriage Association** (**1880**) and **Hitakarini Samajam** (**1905**) came later.
xa: ⚠ Its date varies: **1871** (RPSC key), **1875** (CDX), **1878** (some notes) — learn all three.
Hitakarini Samajam managed all his institutions; he gave it **all his property** (**Rs 50,000**).
Also Veeresalingam's: Andhra's **first night school** and **first Theosophical High School**.

195.s: The widow homes established by Kandukuri Veeresalingam were located at:
195.x: Veeresalingam established a widow home at Madras in 1897 and another at Rajahmundry in 1905. The Rajahmundry home was called Vitantu Saranalayam.
195.tq: Use the paired-place and year sequence to eliminate reversed locations.
xs: Veeresalingam's widow homes were at **Madras (1897)** and **Rajahmundry (1905)** — option **(4)**.
The Rajahmundry home, opened **16 Jan 1905**, was the **Sri Victoria Widow Asylum** = **Vitantu Saranalayam**.
Option (1) reverses the places; 1880 and 1909 are the years of the Widow Remarriage Association and the Ram Mohan Roy School.
xa: **Hitakarini Samajam** (**1905**; some notes **1906**) managed all his institutions.
He gave **all his property** (**Rs 50,000**) to it for women's homes and schools.
His wife **Rajyalakshmamma** sheltered widows and couples of the remarriage movement.

195.s: Which institution was managed through the entire property donated by Kandukuri Veeresalingam?
195.x: Veeresalingam donated his entire property, valued at Rs. 50,000, to Hitakarini Samajam, which managed all his institutions.
195.tq: Link the distinctive donation detail with the institution it supported.
xs: Veeresalingam gave **all his property** (**Rs 50,000**) to the **Hitakarini Samajam**, which managed all his institutions — option **(2)**.
It was founded in **1905** (some notes **1906**).
The **Social Reform Association**, **Widow Remarriage Association** (**1880**) and **Prarthana Samaj** (**1878**) were earlier bodies with narrower aims.
xa: The money went to **women's homes and schools**.
**Sri Victoria Widow Asylum** (Vitantu Saranalayam), Rajahmundry, opened **16 Jan 1905**.
Titles: **Andhra Rammohan Roy**, **Gadya Tikkana**, **Yuga Karta**.

195.s:
Arrange the following institutions associated with Andhra social reform in chronological order of establishment:
A. Hitakarini Samajam
B. Rajahmundry Social Reform Association
C. Widow Remarriage Association
D. Prarthana Samaj at Rajahmundry
195.x: The correct order is Rajahmundry Social Reform Association (1875), Prarthana Samaj (1878), Widow Remarriage Association (1880), and Hitakarini Samajam (1905).
195.tq: Arrange the organisations by their establishment years, beginning with the earliest reform body.
xs: Correct order: **Social Reform Association → Prarthana Samaj → Widow Remarriage Association → Hitakarini Samajam** — option **(1)** **B, D, C, A**.
**Rajahmundry Social Reform Association**: **1871** / **1875** (key dates).
**Prarthana Samaj, Rajahmundry**: **1878**; **Widow Remarriage Association**: **1880**; **Hitakarini Samajam**: **1905**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes date the Social Reform Association to **1878** — still the first organised reform body.
First girls' school: **1874**, Dowlaiswaram; second at **Innispeta**, **1881**.
Widow homes: **Madras 1897**; **Rajahmundry 1905**.

195.s: Andhra's first girls' school, started by Kandukuri Veeresalingam in 1874, was located at:
195.x: Veeresalingam opened the first girls' school in Andhra at Dowlaiswaram, near Rajahmundry, in 1874 (some keys say simply 'at Rajahmundry'). Innispeta in Rajahmundry got his second girls' school in 1881. Kakinada and Machilipatnam were later reform centres, not the site of the first school.
195.tq: 1874 Dowlaiswaram first; 1881 Innispeta second.
xs: Andhra's **first girls' school** (**1874**) was at **Dowlaiswaram** near Rajahmundry — option **(2)**.
**Innispeta** (Rajahmundry) had his **second** girls' school, **1881**.
**Kakinada** and **Machilipatnam** were later reform centres.
xa: ⚠ CDX and APP say **Dowlaiswaram**; APHQ and CDI say "**at Rajahmundry**".
Veeresalingam was the first in Andhra to promote **co-education**.
His **Satihitabodhini** (**1883**) was a monthly for women's education.

195.s: On 3 August 1879, Kandukuri Veeresalingam delivered a public lecture at Rajahmundry declaring that widow remarriage was
o: a matter solely for colonial courts
195.x: On 3 August 1879, Veeresalingam publicly argued at Rajahmundry that widow remarriage was sanctioned by Hindu scripture. He was attacked and was protected by his students.
195.tq: Test the precise claim made in a reform lecture rather than the later marriage event.
xs: On **3 Aug 1879** Veeresalingam declared widow remarriage **scripturally valid** — option **(1)**.
He was attacked at the meeting and **saved by his students**.
xa: The first remarriage followed on **11 Dec 1881** at Rajahmundry.
**Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856** (Act XV) — Vidyasagar's campaign, under **Lord Canning**.
**Vedam Venkataraya Sastri** replied with **Stree Punarvivaha Durvada Nirvaranam** (**1883**), the first major anti-remarriage book.

195.s:
Consider the following statements about the first widow remarriage in Andhra:

1. It took place on 11 December 1881.
2. It was held at Ananda Udyana Mandapam behind Veeresalingam's house at Rajahmundry.
3. The groom was Gogulapati Sriramulu and the bride was Seethamma, originally known as Gauramma.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
195.x: All three statements correctly describe the first widow remarriage in Andhra on 11 December 1881.
195.tq: Test date, venue and participants together, requiring complete identification of the event.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** **1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: Andhra's first widow remarriage was on **11 Dec 1881**.
Statement 2: it was held at **Ananda Udyana Mandapam** behind Veeresalingam's house, **Rajahmundry**.
Statement 3: groom **Gogulapati Sriramulu**; bride **Seethamma** (Sitamma), originally **Gauramma**.
xa: Second remarriage: **15 Dec 1881** (Racharla Ramachandrayya - Ratnamma).
Totals differ: **20** by **1892**; about **53** in all; **61** by **1904**.
At **Kakinada**, **Paidah Ramakrishnayya** funded remarriages and built houses for grooms.

195.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

A. Paidah Ramakrishnayya — Kakinada Widow Remarriage Association
B. Vedam Venkataraya Sastri — Stree Punarvivaha Durvada Nirvaranam
C. Kasibhatta Brahmayya Sastri — Aryananda Brundavani Sabha
D. All of the above
195.x: All three pairs are correct. Paidah Ramakrishnayya supported remarriages at Kakinada, Vedam Venkataraya Sastri wrote the anti-remarriage work, and Kasibhatta Brahmayya Sastri was associated with Aryananda Brundavani Sabha.
195.tq: Start from the sure associations and verify all three reform-related pairings.
xs: All three pairs are correct — option **(4)** **A, B and C**.
**Paidah Ramakrishnayya**, Kakinada municipal president, funded remarriages → **Kakinada Widow Remarriage Association**.
**Vedam Venkataraya Sastri** wrote **Stree Punarvivaha Durvada Nirvaranam** (**1883**), the first major anti-remarriage book.
**Kasibhatta Brahmayya Sastri** ran the **Aryananda Brundavani Sabha**, Kakinada.
xa: Kasibhatta's **Arya Mata Bodhini** drew Veeresalingam's reply **Satyavahini** (**1905**).
Kasibhatta also called **Rajasekhara Charitra** a mere translation.
**Kalpavalli** (Machilipatnam) was another anti-remarriage paper.

195.s: The first major anti-widow-remarriage book mentioned in connection with Andhra was
195.x: Vedam Venkataraya Sastri wrote Stree Punarvivaha Durvada Nirvaranam in 1883, described as the first major anti-remarriage book.
195.tq: Identify the exact title of a polemical work instead of a reformist literary work.
xs: **Stree Punarvivaha Durvada Nirvaranam** (**1883**), by **Vedam Venkataraya Sastri**, was the first major anti-remarriage book — option **(4)**.
**Abala Sachcharitra Ratnamala** is **Bhandaru Acchamamba**'s women's biography series.
**Satyaraju Purvadesayatralu** (from Gulliver's Travels) and **Brahma Vivaham** (satire) are Veeresalingam's pro-reform works.
xa: Other opponents: **Kalpavalli** paper (Machilipatnam) and **Kasibhatta Brahmayya Sastri** (Aryananda Brundavani Sabha).
**Kokkonda Venkataratnam** of Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevini also opposed reform and women's education.
The first remarriage the book opposed took place on **11 Dec 1881**.

195.s: The Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, which inspired the widow-remarriage campaign in Andhra, was passed in which year and under which Governor-General?
195.x: The Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act (Act XV of 1856) came out of Vidyasagar's campaign and was passed under Lord Canning. 1829 under Bentinck is the Sati Regulation. 1872 is the Native Marriage Act. 1891 under Lansdowne is the Age of Consent Act.
195.tq: Act 1856 (Canning); Andhra's first remarriage 1881.
xs: The **Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act** (Act XV) was passed in **1856** under **Lord Canning** — option **(2)**.
It came out of **Vidyasagar**'s campaign.
**1829** is the year of the **Sati ban**, not the remarriage Act.
xa: Bengal's first remarriage: **7 Dec 1856**; Andhra's: **11 Dec 1881**.
Exam angle: the year (**1881**) and the Act (**1856**) are asked directly.
Ram Mohan Roy timeline: **Atmiya Sabha 1814**, **Brahmo Sabha 1828**, Sati ban **1829**.

195.s: Which of the following was NOT among the social evils against which reform activities in Andhra were directed?
195.x: Expansion of scientific education was a reform objective, not a social evil. The listed evils included child marriage, nautch or Bhogam and official corruption, among others.
195.tq: Find the item that is a reform measure rather than a social evil.
xs: **Expansion of scientific education** was not a social evil — option **(1)**.
The evils targeted: ban on widow remarriage, **child marriage**, **dowry**, **caste**, bride-price, superstition, **nautch/Bhogam** and **official corruption**.
xa: Methods: **journals and satire**, public lectures, **schools and co-education**, remarriages at his own cost, widow homes.
**Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu** led the **anti-nautch** (Devadasi) campaign.
**Gurajada**'s **Kanyasulkam** attacked **bride-price** and child marriage.

195.s: Which one of the following was NOT a method used in the social reform campaigns associated with Veeresalingam?
o: Conducting public lectures and establishing schools
Performing remarriages at his own cost and maintaining widow homes
195.x: Veeresalingam's reform methods included journals, satire, public lectures, schools, co-education, remarriages at his own expense and widow homes. Prarthana Samaj worship was conducted without idols.
195.tq: Reject the reversed religious practice while retaining the practical reform methods.
xs: **Promoting worship exclusively through idols** was not his method — option **(3)**; **Prarthana Samaj** worship was **without idols**.
His real methods: **journals and satire**, **public lectures**, **schools and co-education**, **remarriages at his own cost**, **widow homes**.
xa: He founded the **Prarthana Samaj, Rajahmundry** (**1878**), the first in Andhra.
⚠ Prarthana Samaj did not reject idol worship or caste outright, unlike the **Brahmo Samaj**.
He used the **press, not politics**; own printing press from **1876**.

195.s: Which of the following social evils was directly associated with the term 'Bhogam' in reform discussions in Andhra?
195.x: Nautch, or the Bhogam system, was one of the social evils targeted by reformers in Andhra.
195.tq: Discriminate between a named social practice and other evils in the same reform list.
xs: **Bhogam** refers to the **nautch** (Devadasi) custom — option **(2)**.
**Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu** began the **anti-nautch (Devadasi)** movement in Madras and was the main force behind ending the **Bhogam caste** custom.
xa: APPSC **2019**: Venkataratnam Naidu = main factor in eliminating the **'Bhogam' caste**.
**Desiraju Peda Bapayya**'s **Temperance and Social Purity Sangham** led a boycott of Bhogam melas.
**Devadasi bill**: **Dr. Muthulakshmi Reddy** + Chodagam Ammannaraja — bill **1937**, passed **1947**.
Venkataratnam Naidu's **People's Friend** was an anti-Devadasi journal.

195.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Telugu journals:
1. Vivekavardhini attacked corruption and superstition.
2. Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevani supported women's education.
3. Satyasamvardhini printed a biography of Raja Rammohan Roy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
195.x: Vivekavardhini attacked corruption and superstition, while Satyasamvardhini printed a biography of Raja Rammohan Roy. Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevani was orthodox and opposed women's education.
195.tq: Find the statement that reverses the reformist and orthodox positions of two rival journals.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2)** **1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: **Vivekavardhini** (**1874**) attacked **corruption and superstition**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevini** (Kokkonda Venkataratnam) was **orthodox** and **opposed women's education**.
Statement 3 is correct: **Satyasamvardhini** (**1891**) printed a **biography of Rammohan Roy**.
xa: Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevini is credited with the **first editorial column**.
Satyasamvardhini was edited by **Rayasam Venkata Siva** for the Rajahmundry Prarthana Samaj.
⚠ APPSC G2 2025 key names **D. Rangacharyulu** as Vivekavardhini's founder; all notes credit **Veeresalingam**.

195.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Journal)
(a) Satyaduta
(b) Satyasamvardhini
(c) Janana Patrika
(d) Chintamani

List-II (Association or feature)
(i) First Telugu political journal
(ii) Bellary Christian Mission
(iii) Women's education
(iv) Rajahmundry Prarthana Samaj

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
195.x: Satyaduta was issued by the Bellary Christian Mission; Satyasamvardhini was associated with the Rajahmundry Prarthana Samaj; Janana Patrika concerned women's education; and Chintamani was the first Telugu political journal.
195.tq: Start with the sure pair and eliminate codes that disturb the journal's distinctive association.
xs: Correct match: **a–ii, b–iv, c–iii, d–i** — option **(1)**.
**Satyaduta** → **Bellary Christian Mission** (**1835**); **Satyasamvardhini** → **Rajahmundry Prarthana Samaj** (**1891**).
**Janana Patrika** → **women's education**; **Chintamani** → **first Telugu political journal** (**1891**).
xa: Janana/Zenana Patrika: **1893/1894**; Venkata Siva, later Veeresalingam.
Chintamani was jointly edited by **Veeresalingam** and **Nyapati Subbarao**.
⚠ APPSC 2019 key marks "Telugu Janana - Veeresalingam" as the **wrong pair**.

195.s: Which one of the following journals was started as a satirical reply to Kokkonda Venkataratnam's Hasyavardhini?
195.x: Veeresalingam's Hasyasanjeevani, started in 1876, was a satirical reply to Kokkonda Venkataratnam's Hasyavardhini.
195.tq: Discriminate between similarly named journals by identifying the direction of the rivalry.
xs: **Hasyasanjeevani** (**1876**), Veeresalingam's satire, replied to Kokkonda's **Hasyavardhini** — option **(4)**.
**Satyasamvardhini** was the Prarthana Samaj monthly; **Satyaduta** the first Telugu journal; **Satihitabodhini** a women's monthly.
xa: It mocked Kokkonda as "**Ko.Ko.Ko...kkonda**".
**Kokkonda Venkataratnam** also edited the orthodox **Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevini**.
The rivalry began with Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevini vs **Purushartha Pradayini** (Machilipatnam), where Veeresalingam first wrote.

195.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The monthly Telugu was associated with Gidugu in 1919.
2. Janavani was associated with Tapi Dharma Rao.
3. The Andhra Sahitya Parishad magazine was associated with Jayanti Ramaiah Pantulu.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
195.x: All three statements are correct. Telugu was associated with Gidugu in 1919, Janavani with Tapi Dharma Rao, and the Andhra Sahitya Parishad magazine with Jayanti Ramaiah Pantulu.
195.tq: Check each journal-editor association independently before selecting the combined code.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** **1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: the monthly **Telugu** (**1919**) was **Gidugu**'s, for the language movement.
Statement 2: **Janavani** was **Tapi Dharma Rao**'s — first magazine to popularise vyavaharika.
Statement 3: the **Andhra Sahitya Parishad magazine** was **Jayanti Ramaiah Pantulu**'s (APPSC **2019** correct pair).
xa: ⚠ Jayanti Ramaiah Pantulu led the **classical (granthika)** side; Gidugu and Tapi Dharma Rao backed **vyavaharika**.
**Andhra Patrika** = **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** (PYQ **2019**).
Gidugu founded the **Vyavaharika Bhashodyama Samstha** (**1910**).

195.s: Who among the following represented the orthodox opposition to the reform of Telugu prose?
o: Gidugu Ramamurthy, editor of *Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevini*
Gurajada Apparao, editor of *Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevini*
Tapi Dharma Rao, editor of *Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevini*
Kokkonda Venkataratnam, editor of *Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevini*
195.x: Kokkonda Venkataratnam was an orthodox editor of *Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevini* and opposed the reform towards spoken Telugu.
195.tq: Use the editor–journal association to identify the opponent of reform.
xs: **Kokkonda Venkataratnam**, orthodox editor of **Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevini**, opposed reform — option **(4)**.
**Gidugu**, **Gurajada** and **Tapi Dharma Rao** were **supporters** of vyavaharika (spoken Telugu), not editors of Sanjeevini.
xa: Kokkonda also opposed **women's education**; his **Hasyavardhini** attacked Vivekavardhini.
**Jayanti Ramaiah Pantulu** led the classical side through the **Andhra Sahitya Parishad**.
Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevini is credited with the **first editorial column**.

195.s: Chintamani (1891), regarded as the first Telugu political journal, was jointly edited by:
o: Rayasam Venkata Siva and A.C. Parthasarathi Naidu
195.x: Chintamani (1891) was jointly edited by Veeresalingam and Nyapati Subbarao. Kokkonda was an orthodox editor, and Umaranga Nayakulu ran Purushartha Pradayini. Gidugu and Gurajada led the language movement. Rayasam Venkata Siva edited Satyasamvardhini, and Parthasarathi Naidu is linked with Andhra Prakasika.
195.tq: Chintamani 1891 = Veeresalingam + Nyapati Subbarao.
xs: **Chintamani** (**1891**) was jointly edited by **Veeresalingam** and **Nyapati Subbarao** — option **(3)**.
**Kokkonda** was an orthodox editor; **Umaranga Nayakulu** ran **Purushartha Pradayini**.
**Gidugu** and **Gurajada** led the language movement; **Rayasam Venkata Siva** edited Satyasamvardhini; **Parthasarathi Naidu** is linked with Andhra Prakasika.
xa: ⚠ First political **journal** = **Chintamani**; first political **weekly** (CDX) = **Andhra Prakasika** (**1885**).
First social-reform journal = **Vivekavardhini** (**1874**).
First Telugu journal = **Satyaduta** (**1835**).

195.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched in relation to the works of Kandukuri Veeresalingam?
o: Brahma Vivaham — Historical chronicle of the Rajahmundry Prarthana Samaj
Satyaraju Purvadesayatralu — Based on Gulliver's Travels
195.x: Brahma Vivaham was a satire, not a historical chronicle of the Rajahmundry Prarthana Samaj. The other three pairs correctly state the significance or inspiration of the works.
195.tq: Identify the option that assigns the wrong genre or description to a known work.
xs: **Brahma Vivaham** is a **satire on opponents of reform**, not a chronicle of the Prarthana Samaj — option **(2)** is the wrong pair.
His **Autobiography** = **first Telugu autobiography**; **Rajasekhara Charitra** = **first Telugu novel**.
**Satyaraju Purvadesayatralu** is based on Swift's **Gulliver's Travels**.
xa: Rajasekhara Charitra (**1878**) was modelled on Goldsmith's **The Vicar of Wakefield**.
**Vyavahara Dharmabodhini**: play satirising lawyers.
First to render classical Sanskrit drama into Telugu: **Abhijnana Sakuntalam**, **Malavikagnimitram**, **Ratnavali**.

195.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: The Vicar of Wakefield — Satyaraju Purvadesayatralu
195.x: Satyaraju Purvadesayatralu was based on Gulliver’s Travels, not The Vicar of Wakefield. The Vicar of Wakefield was the basis for Veeresalingam’s Rajasekhara Charitramu.
195.tq: Spot the swapped source-work relationship among otherwise familiar literary pairs.
xs: "**The Vicar of Wakefield — Satyaraju Purvadesayatralu**" is wrong — option **(1)**.
Satyaraju Purvadesayatralu is based on Swift's **Gulliver's Travels**; The Vicar of Wakefield inspired **Rajasekhara Charitra**.
The rest are correct: Satyaraju and **Brahma Vivaham** are **Veeresalingam**'s; **Mutyala Saralu** is **Gurajada**'s.
xa: ⚠ Rajasekhara Charitra ← **Goldsmith**; Satyaraju Purvadesayatralu ← **Swift**.
**Mutyala Saralu** introduced a new lyrical **metre** of the same name.
Rajasekhara Charitra (**1878**) = **first Telugu novel**.

195.s:
Which of the following works were translations through which Veeresalingam became the first to render classical Sanskrit drama into Telugu?

1. Abhijnana Sakuntalam
2. Malavikagnimitram
3. Ratnavali

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
195.x: Abhijnana Sakuntalam, Malavikagnimitram and Ratnavali were among the translations through which Veeresalingam rendered classical Sanskrit drama into Telugu for the first time.
195.tq: Test completeness of a named literary list through coded options.
xs: All three — **Abhijnana Sakuntalam**, **Malavikagnimitram**, **Ratnavali** — are his translations — option **(4)** **1, 2 and 3**.
Through them Veeresalingam became the **first to render classical Sanskrit drama into Telugu**.
xa: **Rajasekhara Charitra** (**1878**) = first Telugu novel.
**Satyaraju Purvadesayatralu** ← Swift's **Gulliver's Travels**.
Titles: **Gadya Tikkana**, Gadya Vajmaya Brahma.

195.s: Who authored *Kasiyatra Charitra*, regarded as an important early modern Telugu travelogue?
195.x: *Kasiyatra Charitra* was written by Enugula Veeraswamayya.
195.tq: Use author–work pairing for an early prose text.
xs: **Kasiyatra Charitra**, a travelogue, was written by **Enugula Veeraswamayya** — option **(1)** (APPSC-GS **2022**).
**Veeresalingam** wrote the first Telugu novel and autobiography; **Gurajada** wrote **Kanyasulkam**.
**C.P. Brown** compiled Telugu-English dictionaries.
xa: **Stree Punarvivaha Durvada Nirvaranam** (**1883**) — Vedam Venkataraya Sastri.
Telugu **Brahma Dharmam** — **Chembeti Sridharulu Naidu** (**1875**), published by Mannava Buchayya Pantulu (**1886**).
**Satyaraju Purvadesayatralu** (Veeresalingam) is based on Gulliver's Travels.

195.s: C. P. Brown is particularly associated with which contribution to Telugu studies?
o: Preparing the first Telugu-English dictionaries and editing Vemana’s verses
195.x: C. P. Brown, Collector of Cuddapah, prepared the first Telugu-English dictionaries and edited Vemana’s verses.
195.tq: Combine two distinctive contributions of the same personality.
xs: **C.P. Brown**, Collector of **Cuddapah**, made the **first Telugu-English dictionaries** and edited **Vemana**'s verses — option **(1)**.
**Mutyala Saralu** is **Gurajada**'s; the **first Telugu autobiography** is Veeresalingam's.
The **Navya Sahitya Parishat** was a youth body spreading **Gidugu**'s vyavaharika cause.
xa: **Kasiyatra Charitra** (travelogue) — **Enugula Veeraswamayya**.
Cuddapah also had the **London Missionary Society** (Jammalamadugu, **1805**).
First Telugu journal: **Satyaduta** (**1835**), Bellary.

195.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Chembeti Sridharulu Naidu — Prarthana Samaj, Rajahmundry, 1888
195.x: Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu founded the Brahmo Samaj at Machilipatnam in 1882. The Kakinada Samaj (1888) was founded by Tayi Surya Prakasarao Naidu, the Guntur Samaj (1898) by Pillarisetty Sitaramayya, and the Rajahmundry Prarthana Samaj (1878) by Veeresalingam.
195.tq: Check the organiser, location and year as a three-part match.
xs: **Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu** founded the **Brahmo Samaj, Machilipatnam** in **1882** — option **(2)**.
The **Kakinada** Samaj (**1888**) was founded by **Tayi Surya Prakasarao Naidu** and Duggirala Surya Prakasarao.
The **Guntur** Samaj (**1898**) was **Pillarisetty Sitaramayya**'s; the Rajahmundry **Prarthana Samaj** (**1878**) was **Veeresalingam**'s.
xa: **Chembeti Sridharulu Naidu** renamed the Madras **Veda Samajam** as **Dakshina Bharata Brahmo Samaj**.
Brahmo Samaj, **Rajahmundry**: **1887**.
Venkataratnam Naidu was inspired to join the Brahmo Samaj by **Pandit Sivanath Sastri**.

195.s:
Arrange the following Andhra Brahmo-related developments in chronological order:
A. Veeresalingam's Prarthana Samaj at Rajahmundry
B. Venkataratnam Naidu's Brahmo Samaj at Machilipatnam
C. Brahmo Samaj at Kakinada
D. Brahmo Samaj at Guntur
195.x: The correct sequence is Rajahmundry in 1878, Machilipatnam in 1882, Kakinada in 1888 and Guntur in 1898.
195.tq: Fix the earliest and latest dates first, then place the two middle developments.
xs: Order: **Rajahmundry 1878 → Machilipatnam 1882 → Kakinada 1888 → Guntur 1898** — option **(1)** **A, B, C, D**.
A = **Prarthana Samaj** (Veeresalingam); B = **Brahmo Samaj** (Venkataratnam Naidu); C = Tayi Surya Prakasarao Naidu; D = **Pillarisetty Sitaramayya**.
xa: ⚠ Brahmo Samaj at **Rajahmundry** itself came in **1887**.
Peak of Andhra reform: **1870-1935**.
Decline: splits after Venkataratnam Naidu joined the **Justice Party**.

195.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the Brahmo Trinity of Andhra?
o: Mannava Buchayya Pantulu, M.G. Ranade and R.G. Bhandarkar
Chembeti Sridharulu Naidu, Balshastri Jambhekar and Gopal Hari Deshmukh
Henry Vivian Derozio, Veeresalingam and Karsandas Mulji
Veeresalingam, Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu and Desiraju Peda Bapaiah
195.x: The Brahmo Trinity of Andhra comprised Veeresalingam, Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu and Desiraju Peda Bapaiah.
195.tq: Separate a regional collective title from individual founders and leaders of other reform movements.
xs: Andhra's **Brahmo Trinity**: **Veeresalingam**, **Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu** and **Desiraju Peda Bapaiah** — option **(4)**.
**Chembeti Sridharulu Naidu** renamed the Madras Veda Samajam; **Mannava Buchayya Pantulu** published the Telugu **Brahma Dharmam** (**1886**) — neither is in the Trinity.
xa: Desiraju Peda Bapayya (**Bapatla**) = **first practising (Anushtanika) Brahmo** in Andhra; discarded the sacred thread.
Comparison: Veeresalingam (**Prarthana Samaj**, widow remarriage) vs Venkataratnam Naidu (**Brahmo Samaj**, anti-nautch, social purity).
Venkataratnam Naidu's **Social Purity Association**: **1891**.

195.s: Who among the following was the first practising Brahmo in Andhra and later founded the Temperance and Social Purity Sangham at Rajahmundry?
195.x: Desiraju Peda Bapayya of Bapatla was the first practising, or Anushtanika, Brahmo in Andhra. He discarded the sacred thread and founded the Temperance and Social Purity Sangham at Rajahmundry.
195.tq: Identify the reformer through two distinctive institutional and personal clues.
xs: **Desiraju Peda Bapayya** of **Bapatla** was the **first practising (Anushtanika) Brahmo** in Andhra — option **(1)**.
He discarded the sacred thread and founded the **Temperance and Social Purity Sangham**, Rajahmundry.
**Pillarisetty Sitaramayya** founded the Guntur Samaj; **Venkataratnam Naidu** founded the **Social Purity Association** (**1891**), a different body.
xa: His Sangham led the **boycott of Bhogam melas**.
He is one of the Andhra **Brahmo Trinity** with Veeresalingam and Venkataratnam Naidu.
⚠ **Temperance and Social Purity Sangham** = Bapayya; **Samajika Shuddhi Samajam** = Venkataratnam Naidu.

195.s: The Brahmo movement in Andhra declined mainly because of splits that followed:
o: Veeresalingam's founding of the Prarthana Samaj at Rajahmundry
Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu joining the Justice Party
the passing of the Vernacular Press Act
the death of Desiraju Pedda Bapayya at Bapatla
195.x: The movement split and declined after Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu joined the Justice Party. The Rajahmundry Prarthana Samaj (1878) came at the start of the movement, not its decline. The Vernacular Press Act concerned the press. Bapayya's death is not given as the cause.
195.tq: Decline = Venkataratnam Naidu to the Justice Party.
xs: The Andhra Brahmo movement split and declined after **Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu joined the Justice Party** — option **(2)**.
The Rajahmundry **Prarthana Samaj** (**1878**) marked the movement's start, not its decline.
xa: Brahmo Trinity: **Veeresalingam**, **Venkataratnam Naidu**, **Desiraju Peda Bapayya**.
Reform became institutional (samajs, homes, journals) and so **outlived its founders**.
Venkataratnam Naidu was the **first Andhra Vice-Chancellor of Madras University**.

195.s: Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu was inspired to join the Brahmo Samaj by whom?
195.x: Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu joined the Brahmo Samaj under the inspiration of Pandit Sivanath Sastri.
195.tq: Test the reformer–influence association directly.
xs: Venkataratnam Naidu joined the Brahmo Samaj inspired by **Pandit Sivanath Sastri** — option **(4)**.
**Debendranath Tagore** wrote **Brahma Dharmam**, which Chembeti Sridharulu Naidu translated into Telugu.
xa: He founded the **Brahmo Samaj, Machilipatnam** (**1882**).
His centre was **Kakinada**; he took reform to **North Coastal Andhra**.
Bodies: **Brahmopasana Mandiram**, **Andhra Brahma Dharma Pracharak Nidhi**, **Karunalayam** (with the Pithapuram Maharaja).

195.s:
Consider the following statements about Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu:
1. He founded the Samajika Shuddhi Samajam in 1891.
2. He was associated with the anti-nautch movement in Madras.
3. He founded the Temperance and Social Purity Sangham at Rajahmundry.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
195.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Temperance and Social Purity Sangham at Rajahmundry was associated with Desiraju Peda Bapayya.
195.tq: Separate the reformer's own organisations from those founded by another reformer.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1)** **1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: he founded the **Samajika Shuddhi Samajam** in **1891**.
Statement 2 is correct: he began the **anti-nautch (Devadasi)** movement in **Madras**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **Temperance and Social Purity Sangham**, Rajahmundry, was **Desiraju Peda Bapayya**'s.
xa: The Social Purity Association was his **most important** body.
⚠ Similar names: **Social Purity Association** (Venkataratnam Naidu) vs **Temperance and Social Purity Sangham** (Bapayya).
His anti-Devadasi journal: **People's Friend**.

195.s: Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu received a knighthood in 1924 and was the first person of which category to receive it?
195.x: He was the first non-official educator to receive a knighthood, in 1924.
195.tq: Use the precise description rather than the associated titles.
xs: Venkataratnam Naidu's **knighthood** (**1924**) made him the **first non-official educator** knighted — option **(3)**.
He was principal of **Pithapuram Raja's College** (**1905-18**) and first Andhra VC of **Madras University**.
xa: His students called him **Brahmarshi** (**1932**).
Other titles: **Rao Bahadur**, **Diwan Bahadur**, **Kulapati**, **Abhinava Socrates**.
⚠ **Rao Bahadur** = Veeresalingam (**1893**) and Venkataratnam Naidu; **Rao Saheb** = Gidugu.

195.s: Karunalayam, established by the Pithapuram Raja, was described as:
o: The first Brahmo Samaj in Andhra
The first girls' school in Andhra
195.x: Karunalayam was described as the only orphanage in Andhra and also provided vocational education.
195.tq: Test the distinctive numerical or superlative description.
xs: **Karunalayam** (**1909**), of the **Pithapuram Raja**, was the **only orphanage in Andhra** — option **(1)**.
The first Samaj in Andhra was the **Prarthana Samaj, Rajahmundry** (**1878**); the first girls' school was at **Dowlaiswaram** (**1874**).
xa: Pithapuram Raja: **Rao Venkatakumara Mahipati Suryarao** (**1885-1964**).
He also ran **orphan and vocational schools**; gave **Rs 1 lakh** to the Brahma Dharma Prachara Nidhi.
Karunalayam at **Kakinada** was set up with **Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu**.

195.s:
With reference to women reformers of Andhra, consider the following statements:

1. Bhandaru Acchamamba founded Stree Samajam at Brundavanapuram in Machilipatnam in 1902.
2. Hindu Sundari was associated with Mosalikanti Ramabai and Vempati Shantabai.
3. Rajyalakshmamma sheltered widows and conducted widow and inter-caste marriages at her home.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
195.x: All three statements are correct. Acchamamba founded Stree Samajam in 1902, Hindu Sundari was associated with Ramabai and Shantabai, and Rajyalakshmamma provided shelter and organised marriages.
195.tq: Test several women reformers through a coded combination of organisations and activities.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** **1, 2 and 3**.
**Bhandaru Acchamamba** founded **Stree Samajam**, Brundavanapuram (**Machilipatnam**), **1902**.
**Hindu Sundari** was run by **Mosalikanti Ramabai** and **Vempati Shantabai**.
**Rajyalakshmamma** sheltered widows and held widow and inter-caste marriages at home.
xa: ⚠ **1902** = both Stree Samajam (Machilipatnam) and Hindu Sundari (**Kakinada**).
Acchamamba's women's biography series: **Abala Sachcharitra Ratnamala**.
Devadasi bill: **Dr. Muthulakshmi Reddy** + Chodagam Ammannaraja (**1937** → passed **1947**).

195.s: Hindu Sundari, associated with the reform activities of Mosalikanti Ramabai and Vempati Shantabai, was published from
195.x: Hindu Sundari was associated with Mosalikanti Ramabai and Vempati Shantabai and was published from Kakinada in 1902.
195.tq: Test a journal-place association using nearby Andhra reform centres as distractors.
xs: **Hindu Sundari** (**1902**) was published from **Kakinada** — option **(3)**.
**Machilipatnam** was the seat of **Acchamamba's Stree Samajam** (also **1902**) — the trap.
xa: Editors: **Mosalikanti Ramabai** + **Vempati Shantabai**.
⚠ **1902** = Stree Samajam (Machilipatnam) and Hindu Sundari (Kakinada).
Kakinada also had the Samaj (**1888**) and **Karunalayam**.

195.s: The Devadasi Bill associated with Dr. Muthulakshmi Reddy and Chodagam Ammannaraja was passed in
195.x: The Devadasi Bill campaign was associated with Dr. Muthulakshmi Reddy and Chodagam Ammannaraja; the Bill was passed in 1947.
195.tq: Distinguish the year of the reform initiative from the year in which the legislation was passed.
xs: The **Devadasi bill** of **Dr. Muthulakshmi Reddy** and **Chodagam Ammannaraja** was passed in **1947** — option **(3)**.
**1937** is the year the bill was introduced, not passed.
xa: The anti-nautch (Devadasi) movement in Madras was begun by **Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu**.
**Desiraju Peda Bapayya** led the **boycott of Bhogam melas**.
Venkataratnam Naidu's anti-Devadasi journal: **People's Friend**.

195.s:
Which of the following statements regarding reform bodies in the Madras Presidency is correct?
1. The Madras Native Association was formed in 1852.
2. Gajula Lakshmi Narasu Chetty was associated with the Madras Native Association.
3. The Madras Mahajana Sabha was formed in 1884.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
195.x: All three statements are correct. The Madras Native Association dates to 1852 and was associated with Gajula Lakshmi Narasu Chetty; the Madras Mahajana Sabha was formed in 1884.
195.tq: Combine dates and an associated personality in a coded statement question.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** **1, 2 and 3**.
The **Madras Native Association** was formed in **1852** by **Gajula Lakshmi Narasu Chetty**.
The **Madras Mahajana Sabha** was formed in **1884**.
xa: **Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam** (Hyderabad): **1901**, **Komarraju Lakshmana Rao**.
**Social Purity Association**: **1891**, Venkataratnam Naidu.
**Andhra Desa Library Association**: **1914**.

195.s: Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam was established at Hyderabad in 1901 with the association of which group?
o: Komarraju Lakshmana Rao, Ravichettu Ranga Rao and Nayani Venkata Ranga Rao
Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu, Desiraju Peda Bapayya and Tayi Surya Prakasarao
Gajula Lakshmi Narasu Chetty, Paidah Ramakrishnayya and Atmuri Lakshmi Narasimham
Veeresalingam, Gurajada Apparao and Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy
195.x: Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam at Hyderabad was established in 1901 with Komarraju Lakshmana Rao, Ravichettu Ranga Rao and Nayani Venkata Ranga Rao.
195.tq: Identify the correct founding group from closely related reform-era names.
xs: The **Bhasha Nilayam** (Hyderabad, **1901**) was set up by **Komarraju Lakshmana Rao**, **Ravichettu Ranga Rao** and **Nayani Venkata Ranga Rao** — option **(1)**.
The other groups mix reformers of the Brahmo, remarriage and language movements.
xa: **Varthamana Vyavaharikandhra Bhasha Parivartaka Samaj** — **Gidugu Ramamurthy** (APPSC **2017**).
**Andhra Desa Library Association** (**1914**) — **Iyyanki Venkata Ramanaiah**, leader of the **Library movement**.
⚠ APPSC-GS 2024: "Kanyasulkam written by **Kommaraju Lakshmana Rao**" is **false** — it is **Gurajada**'s.

195.s: Who among the following founded the Andhra Desa Library Association in 1914?
195.x: Iyyanki Venkata Ramanaiah founded the Andhra Desa Library Association in 1914.
195.tq: Distinguish the founder of the library movement from leaders of the spoken-Telugu movement.
xs: **Iyyanki Venkata Ramanaiah** founded the **Andhra Desa Library Association** (**1914**) — option **(2)**.
He led the **Library movement**.
**Gidugu** led the vyavaharika movement; **Acchamamba** founded Stree Samajam; **Gurajada** wrote Kanyasulkam.
xa: **Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam**: Hyderabad, **1901**.
**Kavi Club, Kumudavalli** (West Godavari): **1897**.
**Madras Native Association**: **1852**.

195.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Association)
 a. Social Purity Association
 b. Widow Remarriage Association
 c. Temperance and Social Purity Sangham
 d. Varthamana Vyavaharikandhra Bhasha Parivartaka Samaj

List-II (Founder)
 i. Gidugu Ramamurthy
 ii. Desiraju Peda Bapayya
 iii. R. Venkataratnam Naidu
 iv. Kandukuri Veeresalingam

195.x: The correct associations are Social Purity Association–R. Venkataratnam Naidu; Widow Remarriage Association–Veeresalingam; Temperance and Social Purity Sangham–Desiraju Peda Bapayya; and Varthamana Vyavaharikandhra Bhasha Parivartaka Samaj–Gidugu Ramamurthy.
195.tq: Start from the sure founder–association pairs.
xs: Correct match: **a–iii, b–iv, c–ii, d–i** — option **(1)**.
**Social Purity Association** (**1891**) → **R. Venkataratnam Naidu**; **Widow Remarriage Association** (**1880**) → **Veeresalingam**.
**Temperance and Social Purity Sangham** → **Desiraju Peda Bapayya**; **Varthamana Vyavaharikandhra Bhasha Parivartaka Samaj** → **Gidugu Ramamurthy**.
xa: Gidugu also founded the **Vyavaharika Bhashodyama Samstha** (**1910**).
Bapayya's Sangham led the **boycott of Bhogam melas**.
Widow Remarriage Association co-founders: **Challapalli Bapayya**, **Basavaraju Gavarraju**.

195.s: ‘Desamante matti kadoyi, desamante manushuloyi’ conveys the idea that:
o: A country is determined by its religious institutions.
A country is its people, not merely its soil.
A country is defined exclusively by its territory.
A country is identified primarily with its rulers.
195.x: Gurajada's line means that a country is its people, not merely its soil. ⚠ Sources differ on the poem it comes from: Desamunu Preminchumanna / Desabhakti in most notes, while the APPSC 2025 key says Kanyaka.
195.tq: Interpret the central idea of the quoted line rather than relying only on author recall.
xs: "**Desamante matti kadoyi, desamante manushuloyi**" means a country is **its people, not merely its soil** — option **(2)**.
It is **Gurajada**'s line.
xa: ⚠ Source differs: patriotic song **"Desamunu Preminchumanna"** / poem Desabhakti; APPSC **2025** key says **Kanyaka**.
Gurajada's **Mutyala Saralu** introduced a new lyrical metre.
⚠ **Purnamma** (girl married off for money) vs **Kanyaka** — both Gurajada poems.

195.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding Gurajada Appa Rao?

1. Kanyasulkam — Attack on bride-price and child marriage
2. Mutyala Saralu — New metre
3. Desamunu Preminchumanna — Patriotic song

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
195.x: All three pairs are correct. Kanyasulkam attacked bride-price and child marriage, Mutyala Saralu introduced a new metre, and Desamunu Preminchumanna is a patriotic song associated with Gurajada Appa Rao.
195.tq: Combine closely related literary facts and test whether all the pairings are correctly identified.
xs: All three pairs are correct — option **(4)** **1, 2 and 3**.
**Kanyasulkam** attacks **bride-price** and **child marriage**.
**Mutyala Saralu** introduced a new lyrical **metre** of the same name.
**Desamunu Preminchumanna** is Gurajada's **patriotic song**.
xa: **Diddubatu** = first modern Telugu **short story**.
**Saranga Dhara** (**1883**) = English poem, with brother Shyamala Rao.
Other works: **Kalinga Desa Charitra**, Neelagiri Paatalu, Gramina Sabda Vicharam.

195.s: Gurajada Appa Rao worked with which reformer in promoting literary and cultural renaissance in Andhra?
195.x: Gurajada Appa Rao worked alongside Kandukuri Veeresalingam's reform activities, contributing to literary and cultural renaissance.
195.tq: Use the associated-person trap by distinguishing collaborators from other reformers.
xs: Gurajada worked alongside **Kandukuri Veeresalingam**'s reform, focusing on **literary and cultural renaissance** — option **(3)**.
**Vedam Venkataraya Sastri** was an **opponent** of widow remarriage; **Iyyanki Venkata Ramanaiah** led the Library movement.
xa: His literature attacked **bride-price** and the exploitation of widows.
With **Gidugu**, he championed **vyavaharika** (spoken) Telugu.

195.s: Who among the following, along with Gurajada Appa Rao, championed the use of vyavaharika or spoken Telugu?
195.x: Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy and Gurajada Appa Rao were prominent champions of vyavaharika, or spoken, Telugu.
195.tq: Separate leaders of the spoken-Telugu movement from leaders of library and widow-remarriage movements.
xs: **Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy** and Gurajada championed **vyavaharika** (spoken) Telugu — option **(2)**.
Gidugu supplied the **theory and education** side; Gurajada the **literature**.
**Kasibhatta Brahmayya Sastri** was an orthodox opponent of reform; **Paidah Ramakrishnayya** funded remarriages.
xa: Gidugu = "**Father of the Vyavaharika Bhashodyamam**"; founded the **Vyavaharika Bhashodyama Samstha** (**1910**).
Opponents: **Kokkonda Venkataratnam**, **Jayanti Ramaiah Pantulu**.
**Telugu Language Day** = **29 August**, Gidugu's birthday.

195.s: The second edition of Kanyasulkam published in 1909 was dedicated to:
195.x: The second edition of Kanyasulkam, published in 1909, was dedicated to Ananda Gajapati.
195.tq: Test the work–dedication association.
xs: Kanyasulkam's **2nd edition** (**1909**) was dedicated to **Ananda Gajapati** — option **(1)**.
Gurajada served the **Vizianagaram** court of Ananda Gajapati.
xa: **Saranga Dhara** (**1883**) was written with brother **Shyamala Rao**.
Kanyasulkam was first staged on **13 Aug 1892** by the **Jagannatha Vilasa Nataka Sangham**.
**1909** is also the year of **Karunalayam** (Pithapuram Raja).

195.s: The first staging of Kanyasulkam was associated with which troupe and place?
195.x: Kanyasulkam was first staged by the Jagannatha Vilasa Nataka Sangham of Vizianagaram.
195.tq: Match the literary work with its first staging institution and place.
xs: Kanyasulkam was first staged by the **Jagannatha Vilasa Nataka Sangham**, **Vizianagaram** — option **(1)**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes date the first staging to **1893**.
Characters: **Madhuravani** (reformed courtesan), **Girisham** (educated fraud), **Buchamma** (widow), **Soujanya Rao** (reformer).
Dialect: **Srikakulam dialect**.

195.s: Which one of the following is the correct publication and staging sequence for Kanyasulkam?
o: Written in 1890, first staged in 1892, published in 1897
Written in 1892, first staged in 1897, published in 1909
Written in 1897, first staged in 1890, published in 1892
Written in 1909, first staged in 1892, published in 1897
195.x: Kanyasulkam was written in 1890, first staged on 13 August 1892, and published in 1897 by Vavilla.
195.tq: Arrange the work’s composition, performance and publication stages.
xs: Kanyasulkam: **written 1890 → first staged 1892 → published 1897** — option **(1)**.
First staging: **13 Aug 1892**, Vizianagaram; publication by **Vavilla**.
xa: 2nd edition **1909**, dedicated to **Ananda Gajapati**.
First **vyavaharika** play.
Exam angle (APPSC-GS 2024): a **satirical play on social evils** — true.

195.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Saranga Dhara — Telugu novel — Rural social reform
Purnamma — Poem — Girl married off for money
Mutyala Saralu — Poetry — New lyrical metre
195.x: Saranga Dhara is an English poem written with Shyamala Rao and published in Indian Leisure Hour; it is not a Telugu novel.
195.tq: Use the genre-swapping trap among closely related literary works.
xs: "**Saranga Dhara — Telugu novel**" is wrong — option **(1)**; it is an **English poem** (**1883**) with brother **Shyamala Rao**, published in **Indian Leisure Hour**.
The rest are correct: **Purnamma** — girl married off for money; **Diddubatu** — short story on social reform; **Mutyala Saralu** — new metre.
xa: Diddubatu is regarded as the **first modern Telugu short story**.
The **first Telugu novel** is Veeresalingam's **Rajasekhara Charitra** (**1878**).
Gurajada's other works: **Kalinga Desa Charitra**, Neelagiri Paatalu.

195.s: Diddubatu is regarded as:
o: The first modern Telugu short story
195.x: Diddubatu is regarded as the first modern Telugu short story and deals with social reform.
195.tq: Test the literary milestone and genre together.
xs: **Diddubatu** is regarded as the **first modern Telugu short story** — option **(1)**.
The **first Telugu social play** in vyavaharika is **Kanyasulkam**; Gurajada's English poem is **Saranga Dhara**.
xa: Diddubatu has a **social reform** theme.
First Telugu **novel**: **Rajasekhara Charitra** (**1878**); first Telugu **autobiography**: Veeresalingam's.
**Mutyala Saralu** introduced a new metre.

195.s: Which of the following characters in Kanyasulkam is correctly matched with the description?
195.x: Madhuravani is portrayed as a reformed courtesan. Girisham is an educated fraud, Ramappa Pantulu is a hypocrite and Buchamma is a widow.
195.tq: Match characters with their precise roles and avoid swapped descriptions.
xs: **Madhuravani** is the **reformed courtesan** of Kanyasulkam — option **(3)**.
**Girisham** is the **educated fraud**, not a reformer; **Ramappa Pantulu** is a **hypocrite**.
**Buchamma** is the **widow**; the reformer is **Soujanya Rao**.
xa: Kanyasulkam is written in the **Srikakulam dialect** of **vyavaharika** Telugu.
It attacks **bride-price**, child marriage and the plight of widows.
First staged **13 Aug 1892** by the Jagannatha Vilasa Nataka Sangham, **Vizianagaram**.

195.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Kanyasulkam is correct?
1. It uses the Srikakulam dialect.
2. Soujanya Rao is portrayed as a reformer.
3. Ramappa Pantulu is portrayed as a hypocrite.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
195.x: All three statements are correct. Kanyasulkam uses the Srikakulam dialect, presents Soujanya Rao as a reformer and Ramappa Pantulu as a hypocrite.
195.tq: Combine language, character and social-role clues in a literary text.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** **1, 2 and 3**.

Statement 2: **Soujanya Rao** is the **reformer**.

195.s:
Assertion (A): Kanyasulkam is a satirical social play attacking bride-price and the plight of widows.
Reason (R): Kanyasulkam was written by Komarraju Lakshmana Rao.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A

xs: **A is true, R is false** — option **(3)**.
A: Kanyasulkam is a **satirical social play** attacking **bride-price**, child marriage and the plight of widows.
R is false: Kanyasulkam was written by **Gurajada Apparao**.
**Komarraju Lakshmana Rao** founded the **Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam** (Hyderabad, **1901**).
xa: This was asked as an assertion-reason item in **APPSC-GS 2024**.
Kanyasulkam's 2nd edition (**1909**) was dedicated to **Ananda Gajapati**.
It was published in **1897** by **Vavilla**.

195.s: Telugu Language Day is observed on 29 August in recognition of the contribution of
195.x: 29 August is observed as Telugu Language Day in recognition of Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy, a major champion of vyavaharika Telugu.
195.tq: Link a commemorative date with the correct movement leader rather than a general reformer.
xs: **Telugu Language Day** (**29 August**) is **Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy**'s birthday — option **(3)**.
He is the only Indian whose birthday is a state language day.
xa: It is called **Telugu Bhasha Dinotsavam**.
Gidugu = "**Father of the Vyavaharika Bhashodyamam**".

195.s: Gidugu Ramamurthy was born on 29 August 1863 at which place?
195.x: Gidugu Ramamurthy was born on 29 August 1863 at Ponduru in the Srikakulam region.
195.tq: Use the birthplace and date together to identify the correct personality detail.
xs: Gidugu was born on **29 Aug 1863** at **Ponduru (Srikakulam)** — option **(4)**.
**Parlakimidi** is where he worked as a **Telugu teacher**; he worked mostly from **Vizianagaram**.
xa: He died on **22 Jan 1940**.
**Visakhapatnam** hosted the **1910** meeting that led to his Vyavaharika Bhashodyama Samstha.

195.s: Which of the following was NOT one of Gidugu Ramamurthy’s contributions to Savara studies?
o: Preparing a Savara-Telugu and Telugu-Savara dictionary
195.x: Gidugu created a script, prepared bilingual dictionaries and wrote *A Manual of Savara Language*. The Andhra Sahitya Parishad was associated with the classical side of the language debate.
195.tq: Separate the individual’s documented linguistic work from an association linked to the opposing camp.
xs: **Establishing the Andhra Sahitya Parishad** was not Gidugu's — option **(3)**; through it **Jayanti Ramaiah Pantulu** led the **classical** side.
Gidugu's Savara work: a **script**, a **Savara-Telugu / Telugu-Savara dictionary** and **A Manual of Savara Language**.

**Sri Sri** called him "**our recent inspiration**".

195.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with Gidugu Ramamurthy?
o: A Memorandum of Modern Telugu Prose — Gidugu Ramamurthy
The Vicar of Wakefield — Gidugu Ramamurthy
