195.tq: Identify the correct author–work pair from nearby literary associations.
xs: **A Memorandum of Modern Telugu Prose** is **Gidugu**'s work — option **(2)**.
**Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevini** was **Kokkonda Venkataratnam**'s orthodox journal.
**The Vicar of Wakefield** (Goldsmith) was the model for **Rajasekhara Charitra**; **Desabhakti** is linked with **Gurajada**.
xa: Gidugu's other works: **Bala Kavi Saranyam**, **Andhra Pandita Bhishakkula Bhasha Beshajam**.
He also wrote **A Manual of Savara Language**.
His monthly: **Telugu** (**1919**).

195.s:
Which of the following sets contains only titles or honours associated with Gidugu Ramamurthy?
1. Vyavaharika Bhashodyama Pitamaha
2. Abhinava Vaganushasanudu
3. Kaisar-e-Hind
4. Andhra Kesari
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
195.x: Gidugu was known as Vyavaharika Bhashodyama Pitamaha and Abhinava Vaganushasanudu, and received the titles Rao Saheb and Kaisar-e-Hind. Andhra Kesari is not among the titles listed for him.
195.tq: Eliminate the unrelated title from a personality-based list.
xs: Gidugu's titles: **Vyavaharika Bhashodyama Pitamaha**, **Abhinava Vaganushasanudu**, **Kaisar-e-Hind** — option **(1)** **1, 2 and 3 only**.
**Andhra Kesari** is not among the titles listed for Gidugu.
xa: He was also **Rao Saheb**; Kaisar-e-Hind came in **1934**.
⚠ **Rao Saheb** = Gidugu; **Rao Bahadur** = Veeresalingam (**1893**) and Venkataratnam Naidu.
**Andhra Ratna** = **Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya**.

195.s: In which year did Telugu receive classical language status from the Government of India?
195.x: Telugu was granted classical language status by the Government of India in 2008.
195.tq: Test the exact year using closely spaced numerical distractors.
xs: Telugu got **classical language status** in **2008** from the **Government of India** — option **(3)**.
The notes give only **2008**; the other years are distractors.
xa: ⚠ Some notes wrongly say "Government of **Uttar Pradesh**" — a slip.
**Telugu Language Day** = **29 August**, Gidugu's birthday.
Gidugu's monthly **Telugu**: **1919**.

195.s: Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy led a movement against which literary style in Telugu?
195.x: Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy led the movement for Vyavaharika Bhasha, opposing the Sanskritised grandhika style. He was allied with Gurajada Apparao.
195.tq: Distinguish the spoken-language movement from unrelated literary and religious styles.
xs: Gidugu led the **vyavaharika** movement against the **Sanskritised grandhika** style — option **(2)**.
Granthika = Sanskritised classical Telugu with **archaic grammar**, claimed as the only "pure" literary medium.
xa: Vyavaharika = spoken Telugu (also **Gramya / Janapada bhasha**).
His ally in literature: **Gurajada Apparao**.
Outcome: the **Andhra Mahasabha** endorsed colloquial Telugu for literature, education and administration.

195.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the objectives of the Vyavaharika language movement:
1. Granthika supporters claimed that it was the only pure literary medium.
2. Vyavaharika supporters sought to reduce the gap between written and spoken Telugu.
3. Orthodox pandits generally led the movement for spoken Telugu.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
195.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because orthodox pandits supported Granthika Telugu, while Gidugu and Gurajada led the Vyavaharika cause.
195.tq: Find the swapped leadership statement among the comparison-based propositions.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1)** **1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: **granthika** supporters claimed it was the only **"pure" literary medium**.
Statement 2 is correct: **vyavaharika** sought to **close the gap between written and spoken Telugu**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **orthodox pandits** led the **granthika** side; **Gidugu** and **Gurajada** led vyavaharika.
xa: Opponents: **Kokkonda Venkataratnam**, **Jayanti Ramaiah Pantulu** (Andhra Sahitya Parishad).
Supporters: **Tapi Dharma Rao**, **Navya Sahitya Parishat**.

195.s: Who inspired the Vyavaharika Telugu movement?
195.x: J. A. Yates inspired the movement for the use of Vyavaharika Telugu.
195.tq: Discriminate among the individuals associated with different roles in the language movement.
xs: **J.A. Yates** inspired the vyavaharika movement — option **(3)**.
**P.T. Srinivasa Ayyangar** wrote **Life or Death: A Plea for Vernaculars**.
**Jayanti Ramaiah Pantulu** and **Kokkonda Venkataratnam** were **opponents**.
xa: Grammars for vyavaharika: **Malladi Suryanarayana Sastri** (Andhra Bhashanusasanam), **Vadlamudi Gopalakrishnayya** (Vyavaharika Bhasha Vyakaranam).
**Vajjala Venkateswarlu**: Aadhunikapramanikandhra Vyakaranam.
Leaders: **Gidugu** (theory, education), **Gurajada** (literature).

195.s: Who wrote the work titled *Life or Death: A Plea for Vernaculars*?
195.x: P. T. Srinivasa Ayyangar wrote *Life or Death: A Plea for Vernaculars* in support of vernacular language use.
195.tq: Match the distinctive title with its author.
xs: **Life or Death: A Plea for Vernaculars** was written by **P.T. Srinivasa Ayyangar** — option **(2)**.
**J.A. Yates** inspired the movement; **Tapi Dharma Rao** ran **Janavani**.
xa: Gidugu's own manifesto-type work: **A Memorandum of Modern Telugu Prose**.
**Malladi Suryanarayana Sastri**: **Andhra Bhashanusasanam**.
Vyavaharika aim: close the gap between **written and spoken** Telugu.

195.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
195.x: *Kasiyatra Charitra* was authored by Enugula Veeraswamayya, not C. P. Brown. The other three grammar–author pairs are correctly matched.
195.tq: Find the wrong author–work pairing among closely related language texts.
xs: "**Kasiyatra Charitra — C.P. Brown**" is wrong — option **(4)**; it is **Enugula Veeraswamayya**'s travelogue.
C.P. Brown made the **first Telugu-English dictionaries** and edited **Vemana**.
The grammar pairs are correct: **Vajjala Venkateswarlu**, **Malladi Suryanarayana Sastri**, **Vadlamudi Gopalakrishnayya**.
xa: Kasiyatra Charitra was asked in **APPSC-GS 2022**.
C.P. Brown was **Collector of Cuddapah**.
**P.T. Srinivasa Ayyangar**: Life or Death: A Plea for Vernaculars.

195.s: The classical side in the Telugu language controversy was led through which organisation by Jayanti Ramaiah Pantulu?
195.x: Jayanti Ramaiah Pantulu led the classical side through the Andhra Sahitya Parishad.
195.tq: Match the leader with the organisation representing his position.
xs: **Jayanti Ramaiah Pantulu** led the classical side through the **Andhra Sahitya Parishad** — option **(4)**.
The **Navya Sahitya Parishat** and **Vyavaharika Bhashodyama Samstha** backed **spoken** Telugu; the **Andhra Mahasabha** finally endorsed it.
xa: **Andhra Sahitya Parishad magazine** — Jayanti Ramaiah Pantulu (correct pair, APPSC **2019**).
The other orthodox opponent: **Kokkonda Venkataratnam** (Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevini).
⚠ **Parishad** (classical) vs **Parishat** (Navya Sahitya, vyavaharika).

195.s: Who among the following was known as the ‘Gadya Tikkana’ and ‘Andhra Vaitalikudu’?
195.x: Kandukuri Veeresalingam was known by several titles, including Gadya Tikkana and Andhra Vaitalikudu.
195.tq: Discriminate among reformers by matching multiple honorific titles to one person.
xs: **Gadya Tikkana** and **Andhra Vaitalikudu** are titles of **Kandukuri Veeresalingam** — option **(1)**.
**Kavi Raju** = **Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary**; **Brahmarshi** = **Venkataratnam Naidu**.
xa: Other titles: **Gadya Vajmaya Brahma**, **Yuga Karta**, **Andhra Rammohan Roy**.
He was the **Father of the Andhra Renaissance**.
**Rao Bahadur** (**1893**, British government).

195.s: The title ‘Vidyasagar of South India’ was conferred on Kandukuri Veeresalingam by:
195.x: M. G. Ranade called Veeresalingam the ‘Vidyasagar of South India’ in 1898, when Veeresalingam presided over the Indian Social Reform Congress at Madras.
195.tq: Pair the title with the person who bestowed it, not with the reformer’s own title.
xs: **M.G. Ranade** called Veeresalingam the "**Vidyasagar of South India**" — option **(1)**.
This was in **1898**, when Veeresalingam presided over the **Indian Social Reform Congress, Madras** (PYQ **2019**).
xa: Veeresalingam : Andhra :: **Vidyasagar** : Bengal — widow remarriage, girls' schools.
Bengal's first remarriage **7 Dec 1856**; Andhra's **11 Dec 1881**.
⚠ **Mrs Manning** (willed **50 pounds** to his association) is used as a distractor.

195.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
195.x: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya was known as Andhra Ratna. The title Brahma Rishi was associated with Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu.
195.tq: Find the swapped title–person pair among closely related reform personalities.
xs: "**Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya — Brahma Rishi**" is wrong — option **(4)**; he was **Andhra Ratna**.
**Brahma Rishi** (**1932**) was **Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu**'s, from his students.
The rest are correct: **Kavi Raju** — Tripuraneni; **Rao Bahadur, 1893** — Veeresalingam.
xa: Venkataratnam Naidu's **knighthood** (**1924**): first non-official educator knighted.
**Father of Andhra Drama** = **Dharmavaram Krishnamacharyulu**.
**Rao Saheb** = **Gidugu**.

195.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Dharmavaram Krishnamacharyulu — Father of Andhra Drama
Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu — Father of Andhra Drama
195.x: Dharmavaram Krishnamacharyulu was known as the Father of Andhra Drama. Andhra Ratna was the title of Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya, while Kavi Raju was associated with Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary.
195.tq: Use title-based elimination, especially where neighbouring personalities have similar reform credentials.
xs: **Dharmavaram Krishnamacharyulu** = **Father of Andhra Drama** — option **(1)**.
**Andhra Ratna** = **Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya**; **Kavi Raju** = **Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary**.
**Venkataratnam Naidu** was **Brahmarshi**, not Father of Andhra Drama.
xa: Veeresalingam = **Andhra Rammohan Roy**, **Gadya Tikkana**.
Gidugu = **Vyavaharika Bhashodyama Pitamaha**.
Tripuraneni was a **rationalist poet**.

195.s: Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary's song 'Veeragandhamu techinaramu' is associated with which movement?
195.x: The song 'Veeragandhamu techinaramu' is associated with the Civil Disobedience Movement.
195.tq: Link a literary work with the correct phase of the national movement.
xs: Tripuraneni's song "**Veeragandhamu techinaramu**" is linked to the **Civil Disobedience Movement** — option **(1)** (PYQ **2012**).
The notes link the song to no other movement.
xa: Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary = **Kavi Raju**, a **rationalist poet**.
⚠ **Kavi Raju** (Tripuraneni) vs **Andhra Ratna** (Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya).

195.s: Kandukuri Veeresalingam is popularly known as:
195.x: Veeresalingam is called Andhra Rammohan Roy (Raja Ram Mohan Roy of Andhra) and the father of the Andhra renaissance. Andhra Kesari was Tanguturi Prakasam. Andhra Ratna was Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya, and Kavi Raju was Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary.
195.tq: Andhra Rammohan Roy = Veeresalingam; Andhra Ratna = Duggirala.
xs: Veeresalingam is called **Andhra Rammohan Roy** (Raja Ram Mohan Roy of Andhra) — option **(4)**.
**Andhra Ratna** = **Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya**; **Kavi Raju** = **Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary**.
xa: He is also the **Father of the Andhra Renaissance** and of the Social Reform Movement in Andhra.
Other titles: **Gadya Tikkana**, **Yuga Karta**, **Andhra Vaitalikudu**.
"**Vidyasagar of South India**" — **M.G. Ranade** (**1898**).

195.s: Which one of the following places became the centre of Telugu social reform, modern prose, journalism and the novel during the nineteenth century?
195.x: Rajahmundry emerged as the centre of Telugu social reform and the development of modern prose, journalism and the novel.
195.tq: Use the significance-based location clue and distinguish the reform centre from other Andhra places.
xs: **Rajahmundry** was the centre of Telugu **social reform, modern prose, journalism and the novel** — option **(4)**.
**Vizianagaram** was a cradle of the **language movement**; **Madanapalle** is the **Theosophy** link; **Kakinada** was the other reform centre.
xa: Rajahmundry (Godavari district) = Andhra's **first Renaissance centre**.
Firsts there: **Prarthana Samaj** (**1878**), first widow remarriage (**11 Dec 1881**).
Dowlaiswaram near it had the **first girls' school** (**1874**).

195.s: Who described Kandukuri Veeresalingam's Rajasekhara Charitra as a mere translation?
195.x: Kasibhatta Brahmayya Sastri criticised Rajasekhara Charitra by calling it a mere translation.
195.tq: Apply the author-versus-critic discrimination trap in literary history.
xs: **Kasibhatta Brahmayya Sastri** called **Rajasekhara Charitra** a mere translation — option **(3)**.
**Kokkonda Venkataratnam** was a different orthodox critic (Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevini, Hasyavardhini).
xa: Kasibhatta ran the **Aryananda Brundavani Sabha**, Kakinada; his **Arya Mata Bodhini** drew Veeresalingam's **Satyavahini** (**1905**).
Rajasekhara Charitra (**1878**) was modelled on Goldsmith's **The Vicar of Wakefield**.
It is the **first Telugu novel**.

195.s: Which of the following best explains the principal method adopted by Kandukuri Veeresalingam for advancing social reform?
o: Organising armed resistance against colonial rule
Using the press rather than direct political activity
Rejecting all forms of public education
Working exclusively through princely state administrations
195.x: Veeresalingam primarily used the press as an instrument of social reform rather than pursuing reform through direct political activity.
195.tq: Identify the means of reform from the contrast between press activism and political action.
xs: Veeresalingam used the **press, not politics**, for reform — option **(2)**.
He set up his own **printing press in 1876**; by **1905** about **20** Telugu journals were in print.
xa: His journals: **Vivekavardhini** (**1874**), **Hasyasanjeevani** (**1876**), **Satihitabodhini** (**1883**).
Other methods: public lectures, **schools and co-education**, remarriages at his own cost, widow homes.
He created the Telugu **reading public** and modern prose.

195.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the Prarthana Samaj from the Brahmo Samaj?
o: The Prarthana Samaj rejected idol worship and caste more completely than the Brahmo Samaj.
The Brahmo Samaj was chiefly concerned with anti-nautch reform, while the Prarthana Samaj dealt only with education.
The Prarthana Samaj did not reject idol worship or caste outright, unlike the Brahmo Samaj.
Both organisations adopted identical positions on idol worship and caste.
195.x: The Prarthana Samaj did not reject idol worship or caste outright, whereas the Brahmo Samaj took a more categorical position against them.
195.tq: Separate the two similarly named reform organisations by testing their doctrinal difference.
xs: The **Prarthana Samaj did not reject idol worship or caste outright**, unlike the **Brahmo Samaj** — option **(3)**.
Option 1 reverses this; the Brahmo Samaj stood for **monotheism, no idol worship**.
**Anti-nautch** was Venkataratnam Naidu's cause, not the Brahmo Samaj's only concern.
xa: First Prarthana Samaj in Andhra: **Rajahmundry, 1878** (Veeresalingam).
Brahmo Samaj: **Raja Ram Mohan Roy**, **1828**, Calcutta.
Prarthana Samaj worship was held **without idols**.

195.s: The principal geographical region associated with the cradle of the Telugu language movement was:
o: South Coastal Andhra, especially Nellore and Ongole
North Coastal Andhra, especially Vizianagaram, Srikakulam and Parlakimidi
195.x: The language movement had its cradle in North Coastal Andhra, particularly Vizianagaram, Srikakulam and Parlakimidi.
195.tq: Use the region-and-example pairing to avoid confusing the cultural zones of Andhra.
xs: The cradle of the language movement was **North Coastal Andhra** — **Vizianagaram**, **Srikakulam**, **Parlakimidi** — option **(2)**.
⚠ The **Rajahmundry-Kakinada** belt was the cradle of social **reform**, not of the language movement.
xa: Gidugu was born at **Ponduru (Srikakulam)** and taught at **Parlakimidi**.
Kanyasulkam uses the **Srikakulam dialect** and was staged at **Vizianagaram** (**1892**).
The Samstha's founding meeting was at **Visakhapatnam** (**1910**).

195.s: Which of the following was the first Telugu journal?
195.x: Satya Doota, started in 1835 by the Christian Association of Bellary, was the first Telugu journal. Andhra Prakasika was the first political journal, and Vivekavardhini came later in 1874.
195.tq: Discriminate the first journal from the first political journal.
n: Vivekavardhini is a journal. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 20-22]
Satya Doota is the first Telugu journal. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 20-22]
Andhra Prakasika is the first political journal. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 20-22]
Hasyavardhani is a journal. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 20-22]
Satya Doota was started by the Christian Association of Bellary. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 20-22]
Satya Doota was published from Bellary. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 20-22]
xs: **Satya Doota** (**Satyadoota**) was the **first Telugu journal** (**1835**) — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was published from **Bellary** by the **Christian Association of Bellary**.
**Andhra Prakasika** was the **first political journal** (**1885**); **Vivekavardhini** and **Hasyavardhani** came in **1874**.
xa: ⚠ First Telugu social-reform journal = **Vivekavardhini**; first Telugu political journal (other notes) = **Chintamani** (**1891**).
**Satihita Bodhini** (**1883**) was Veeresalingam's monthly for women.
By **1905** about **20** Telugu journals were in print.

o: Vivekavardhini was a journal started by Kandukuri Veeresalingam in 1874.

Vivekavardhini was started in 1874. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 20-22]
Satyasamvardhini is a journal. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 20-22]
Satyasamvardhini was written by Kandukuri Veeresalingam. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 20-22]
Satyasamvardhini was started in 1891. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 20-22]
Satihita Bodhini is a journal. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 20-22]
Satihita Bodhini is a monthly magazine. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 20-22]
Satihita Bodhini was written by Kandukuri Veeresalingam. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 20-22]
Satihita Bodhini was started in 1883. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 20-22]
Brahma Prakasika is a journal. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 20-22]
Brahma Prakasika was edited by Ragupati Venkataratnam Naidu. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 20-22]

xs: The incorrect statement is about **Satihita Bodhini** — so option **(2)** is the answer.
**Satihita Bodhini** was a **monthly magazine** started by **Kandukuri Veeresalingam** in **1883**, not **1886**.
**Vivekavardhini** (**1874**), **Satyasamvardhini** (**1891**) and **Brahma Prakasika** (**1886**, **Ragupati Venkataratnam Naidu**) are correct.
xa: Satihita Bodhini was for **women's education** (APHQ).

195.s:

o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A

**William Carey** of the **Serampore Mission** produced the complete Telugu Bible.

196.s:
Consider the following statements about early printing in Telugu:
1. Benjamin Schultze belonged to the Danish-Halle Mission.
2. William Carey's complete Telugu Bible came from Serampore (1812-19).
3. Schultze's Telugu books were printed at Serampore in 1812.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
196.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Schultze's four Telugu books were printed at Halle, Germany, in 1747. Statement 2 is correct. So 1 and 2 only.
196.tq: Schultze = Halle 1747; Carey = Serampore.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
1 is correct: **Benjamin Schultze** was a German Lutheran of the **Danish-Halle Mission**.
2 is correct: **William Carey**'s complete Telugu Bible came from **Serampore** (NT **1812**, full **1818-19**).
3 is wrong: Schultze printed **4 Telugu books** at **Halle** in **1747**.
xa: Schultze came in **1719** and returned in **1743**.
Carey also made **Telugu typefaces**.
**A.D. Campbell** wrote the first systematic Telugu Grammar (**1816**).

196.s: Which colonial scholar kept Telugu as an administrative language?
196.x: Thomas Munro kept Telugu as an administrative language.
196.tq: Match the administrative policy with the appropriate colonial official.
xs: **Thomas Munro** kept Telugu as an **administrative language** — option **(4)**.
**C.P. Brown** made dictionaries; **Mackenzie** collected Kaifiyats; **A.D. Campbell** wrote the 1816 grammar.
xa: Campbell's grammar (**1816**) was the first systematic one.
Brown's dictionaries: **1853**.
Mackenzie: first **Surveyor General** (**1815**).

196.s: The C.P. Brown Memorial Trust Library is located at:
196.x: The C.P. Brown Memorial Trust Library is at Kadapa (Cuddapah), where Brown served as Collector (APPSC G2 2001 and 2005 keys). Rajahmundry was Veeresalingam's reform base. Machilipatnam and Bellary were missionary and press centres.
196.tq: Brown = Collector of Cuddapah; library at Kadapa.
xs: The **C.P. Brown Memorial Trust Library** is at **Kadapa** — option **(1)** (APPSC G2 **2001**, **2005** keys).
Brown was **Collector of Cuddapah** (Kadapa).
**Rajahmundry** was Veeresalingam's base; **Machilipatnam** and **Bellary** were press centres.
xa: Brown (**1798-1884**) learnt Telugu from **Kodandarama Pantulu**.
Dictionaries **1853**; Grammar **1840**.
He called Telugu the "**Italian of the East**".

196.s: The Adams Regulation of 1823, the Vernacular Press Act of 1878, and the Press Acts of 1908 and 1910 are associated with which aspect of colonial rule?
o: Regulation and curbs on the press
196.x: These measures were press regulations or Press Acts used to impose curbs on the press during colonial rule.
196.tq: Identify the common administrative purpose linking a sequence of laws.
xs: These were **curbs on the press** — option **(1)**.
**Adams Regulation 1823**, **Vernacular Press Act 1878**, Press Acts **1908** and **1910**.
xa: Early presses: **Bellary** (Satyaduta **1835**), **Madras** (Vrittanti, Dinavartamani), **Masulipatnam** (Hitavadi **1848**).
Veeresalingam used the press for reform from **1874** (Vivekavardhini).

196.s: Which one of the following statements regarding education in Andhra during the early period of missionary activity is correct?
o: The Adams Regulation of 1823 established missionary schools throughout Andhra.
Christian missionaries were prohibited from undertaking educational work in Andhra.
Christian missionaries made the major contribution to education in Andhra.
Education in Andhra was developed mainly through the Press Acts of 1908 and 1910.
196.x: Christian missionaries made the major contribution to education in Andhra. The Press Acts and Adams Regulation related to press control, not the establishment of missionary schools.
196.tq: Distinguish the educational contribution of missionaries from press-control legislation.
xs: **Christian missionaries** did most of the education in Andhra — option **(3)** (APPSC G2 **2011** key).
The **Adams Regulation** (**1823**) and **Press Acts** (**1908**, **1910**) were **press curbs**, not education measures.
xa: **Benjamin Schultze** (Danish-Halle Mission) printed the first Telugu books.
**William Carey** (Serampore) gave the complete Telugu Bible and Telugu typefaces.
**A.D. Campbell**'s 1816 grammar served missionaries and Telugu scholars.

196.s: According to the APPSC Group 2 (2011) key, the first Telugu magazine published from Bellary was:
196.x: The 2011 key names Tatvabodhini (1864-70) as the first Telugu magazine from Bellary, although Satyaduta (1835) is also called the first Telugu journal. Hitavadi (1848) was from Masulipatnam. Vrittanti and Dinavartamani were Madras papers.
196.tq: Bellary question in the APPSC key: Tatvabodhini.
xs: The APPSC G2 **2011** key names **Tatvabodhini** (1864-70) the first Telugu magazine from **Bellary** — option **(3)**.
**Hitavadi** (**1848**) was from **Masulipatnam**; **Vrittanti** and **Dinavartamani** were **Madras** papers.
xa: ⚠ Notes call **Satyaduta** (**1835**, Bellary) the first Telugu journal — answer the Bellary question with **Tatvabodhini**, as the key does.
Second Telugu journal: **Vartamana Tarangini** (**1842**).
Hitavadi was run by **J. Edmund Sharky**.

196.s: The author of Asamardhuni Jeevayatra is:
196.x: Asamardhuni Jeevayatra was written by Tripuraneni Gopichand.
196.tq: Directly match a modern Telugu work with its author.
xs: **Asamardhuni Jeevayatra** is by **Tripuraneni Gopichand** — option **(2)** (APPSC G2 **2017** key).
**Gurajada** wrote **Musalamma Maranamu**; **Gurram Jashuva** wrote **Gabbilam**; **Viswanatha Satyanarayana** wrote **Veyi Padagalu**.
xa: Gabbilam (**1941**): a bat carries a Dalit's prayer to God.
⚠ **Tripuraneni Gopichand** (novelist) — don't confuse with Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary.

196.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
196.x: Musalamma Maranamu was written by Gurajada Apparao, not Tripuraneni Gopichand. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
196.tq: Find the single swapped author in a list of familiar work–author pairs.
xs: "**Musalamma Maranamu — Tripuraneni Gopichand**" is wrong — option **(4)**; it is **Gurajada Apparao**'s.
The rest are correct: **Veyi Padagalu** — Viswanatha Satyanarayana; **Gabbilam** — Gurram Jashuva; **Kanyasulkam** — Gurajada.
xa: Gopichand wrote **Asamardhuni Jeevayatra**.
Gabbilam was published in **1941**.
Veeresalingam = "**Father of the Telugu Renaissance**".

196.s: What is the distinctive theme associated with Gurram Jashuva’s Gabbilam?
o: A bat carrying a Dalit’s prayer to God
A reformer’s criticism of child marriage
A king’s political struggle against colonial rule
196.x: Gabbilam, published in 1941, presents a bat carrying a Dalit’s prayer to God.
196.tq: Use the work’s distinctive thematic image to identify it without relying only on the author.
xs: In **Gurram Jashuva**'s **Gabbilam** (**1941**), **a bat carries a Dalit's prayer to God** — option **(1)**.
Gabbilam is about a **Dalit**'s prayer — not about child marriage, a pilgrimage or a king's struggle.
xa: **Asamardhuni Jeevayatra** — Tripuraneni Gopichand.
**Veyi Padagalu** — Viswanatha Satyanarayana.
**Musalamma Maranamu** — Gurajada Apparao.

196.s: Which statement about Kandukuri Veeresalingam is correct?
o: He first rendered Kalidasa’s Shakuntalam and Malavikagnimitram into Telugu.
He founded the Vijnana Chandrika Mandali in 1905.
He collected Mackenzie’s Kaifiyats as Surveyor General.
196.x: Veeresalingam was the first to render Kalidasa’s Shakuntalam and Malavikagnimitram into Telugu. The other statements refer to different persons or works.
196.tq: Use the author’s distinctive literary achievement to reject swapped contributions.
xs: Veeresalingam first rendered Kalidasa's **Shakuntalam** and **Malavikagnimitram** into Telugu — option **(1)**.
**Veyi Padagalu** is **Viswanatha Satyanarayana**'s; **1941** is **Gabbilam**'s year.
The **Kaifiyats** were collected by **Colin Mackenzie**, the Surveyor General.
xa: He is the "**Father of the Telugu Renaissance**".
His **Vivekavardhini** began in **1874**.
First Telugu novel: **Rajasekhara Charitram** (**1878**).

196.s: Jonnavittula Gurunatham was associated with the:
196.x: Jonnavittula Gurunatham belonged to the Young Men’s Literary Association and helped promote the Andhra idea through the press.
196.tq: Distinguish the literary association from similarly named cultural institutions.
xs: **Jonnavittula Gurunatham** belonged to the **Young Men's Literary Association** — option **(3)**.
He helped **sow the Andhra idea in the press**.
xa: The **Young Men's Association, Rajahmundry**, was active in **Bipin Chandra Pal**'s Rajahmundry visit.
**Brown's College** members: Pattam Parabrahma Sastri, Ravipati Gurumurti Sastri, Juluri Appayya.
**Andhra Sahitya Parishat**: Madras, **1911**.

196.s:
Consider the following statements about the Andhra Sahitya Parishat:
1. Its 1912 and 1913 sessions at Rajahmundry were presided over by Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao.
2. It was founded at Madras in 1911 and later based at Kakinada.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
196.x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Rajahmundry sessions (23 Apr 1912, 22 Apr 1913) were presided over by Kokkonda Venkataratnam. So 2 only.
196.tq: Parishat: Madras 1911 -> Kakinada; sessions under Kokkonda.
xs: Only statement **2** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
2 is correct: the **Andhra Sahitya Parishat** was founded at **Madras** in **1911** and later based at **Kakinada**.
1 is wrong: the **Rajahmundry** sessions (**23 Apr 1912**, **22 Apr 1913**) were presided over by **Kokkonda Venkataratnam**.
xa: Kokkonda was the first Andhra scholar made **Mahamahopadhyaya (1907)** — "**Andhra Bhasha Johnson**".
The **Young Men's Association, Rajahmundry** was active in **Bipin Chandra Pal's** visit.
Rajahmundry has been a cultural capital since **Eastern Chalukya** days.

196.s: Which of the following correctly describes Rajahmundry’s cultural significance?
o: It was the headquarters of the Danish-Halle Mission.
It served as Veeresalingam’s reform base and has been a cultural capital since Eastern Chalukya times.
It was only a centre of missionary printing during the nineteenth century.
It became a cultural centre only after the founding of the Andhra Sahitya Parishat in Kakinada.
196.x: Rajahmundry was Veeresalingam’s reform base, associated with Vivekavardhini, and has been regarded as a cultural capital since the Eastern Chalukya period.
196.tq: Choose the option that combines both historical dimensions without an absolute or limiting claim.
xs: **Rajahmundry** was **Veeresalingam's reform base** and a **cultural capital since Eastern Chalukya days** — option **(2)**.
The **Danish-Halle Mission** printed at **Halle**; the Parishat was later based at **Kakinada**.
xa: Parishat sessions at Rajahmundry: **23 Apr 1912** and **22 Apr 1913**.
**Young Men's Association, Rajahmundry**: Bipin Chandra Pal's visit.
**Vivekavardhini** (from **1874**) was Veeresalingam's journal.

196.s: The Young Men's Association of Rajahmundry played an active role in which event?
o: The first widow remarriage in Andhra
Bipin Chandra Pal's visit to Rajahmundry
The founding of the Andhra Sahitya Parishat
196.x: The Young Men's Association, Rajahmundry, played an active role in Bipin Chandra Pal's Rajahmundry visit (APPSC G2 2017 key). The first widow remarriage (1881) and Vivekavardhini (1874) were Veeresalingam's work. The Andhra Sahitya Parishat was founded at Madras in 1911.
196.tq: Rajahmundry Young Men's Association: Bipin Chandra Pal.
xs: The **Young Men's Association, Rajahmundry**, was active in **Bipin Chandra Pal's** Rajahmundry visit — option **(2)** (APPSC G2 **2017** key).
**Vivekavardhini** (**1874**) was Veeresalingam's; the **Andhra Sahitya Parishat** was founded at **Madras** (**1911**).
xa: **Jonnavittula Gurunatham** of the Young Men's Literary Association sowed the Andhra idea in the press.
Rajahmundry: cultural capital since **Eastern Chalukya** days.
Parishat sessions at Rajahmundry: **1912-13**.

196.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Telugu Language Day:
1. It is observed on 29 August.
2. Telugu Language Awards are associated with the observance.
3. It commemorates the birth anniversary of Gidugu.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
196.x: All three statements are correct: Telugu Language Day falls on 29 August, marks Gidugu's birth anniversary, and is associated with Telugu Language Awards.
196.tq: Test the date, commemorative basis and associated programme separately.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** **1, 2 and 3**.
**Telugu Language Day** falls on **29 August**, **Gidugu**'s birth anniversary, with **Telugu Language Awards**.
xa: Telugu: **Classical Language** in **2008**.
AP re-introduced **Vemana Suktulu** lessons in schools (Mar **2026**).
A **Telugu Bhavan** is planned in **Mumbai** (Jun **2026**).

196.s: The principal kshetra of Goddess Vasavi is located at—
196.x: Penugonda is the principal kshetra of Goddess Vasavi.
196.tq: Associate the religious figure with the specific Andhra place.
xs: The main kshetra of Goddess **Vasavi** is **Penugonda** — option **(4)** (APPSC G2 **2019** key).
**Halle** is in Germany (Schultze's press); **Masulipatnam** had **Hitavadi** (**1848**).
xa: Last Ikshvaku ruler (same key): **Rudra Purushadatta**.
Telugu declared a **Classical Language** in **2008**.

196.s: According to the APPSC Group 2 (2019) key, the last ruler of the Ikshvaku dynasty was:
196.x: The 2019 key names Rudra Purushadatta as the last Ikshvaku ruler. Vasishthiputra Chamtamula founded the line. Virapurushadatta and Ehuvala Chamtamula were earlier rulers who came before him.
196.tq: Last Ikshvaku = Rudra Purushadatta.
xs: The APPSC G2 **2019** key names **Rudra Purushadatta** as the **last Ikshvaku ruler** — option **(4)**.
The notes name no other Ikshvaku ruler, so the other options are distractors.
xa: The same key gives **Penugonda** as the main kshetra of Goddess **Vasavi**.
Telugu: **Classical Language** status **2008**.

196.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Saint Ramanuja's Bhakti movement stressed devotion to Shiva along with social equality.
2. Prolaya Nayaka led the confederacy of the post-Kakatiya liberation movement.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
196.x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Ramanuja's movement stressed devotion to Vishnu. So 2 only.
196.tq: Ramanuja = Vishnu.
xs: Only statement **2** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
1 is wrong: **Saint Ramanuja**'s Bhakti movement emphasized **devotion to Vishnu** and **social equality**.
2 is correct: **Prolaya Nayaka** led the **confederacy** in the **post-Kakatiya Liberation Movement**.
xa: **Kandukuri Veeresalingam** — father of the **Telugu Renaissance Movement**.
**Konda Venkatappaiah** — father of the **Andhra State Movement**.
**Sidugu Rama Murthy** — father of the **People's Dialect Movement**.

196.s:
How many of the following movements had a person specifically identified as its ‘Father’?

1. Telugu Renaissance Movement
2. People’s Dialect Movement
3. Andhra State Movement
4. Kisan / Agrarian Movement
196.x: Three have a named father: Kandukuri Veeresalingam for the Telugu Renaissance, Gidugu Rama Murthy for the People's Dialect Movement and Konda Venkatappaiah for the Andhra State Movement. N.G. Ranga is called its leader.
196.tq: Count the movements with a named father.
n: N.G. Ranga led the Kisan or Agrarian Movement in Andhra. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 35-37]
Kandukuri Veeresalingam was the father of the Telugu Renaissance Movement. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 35-37]
Sidugu Rama Murthy was the father of the People’s Dialect Movement in Telugu. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 35-37]
Konda Venkatappaiah was the father of the Andhra State Movement. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 35-37]
xs: **Only three** of the movements have a named "Father" — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Telugu Renaissance Movement** — **Kandukuri Veeresalingam**; **People's Dialect Movement** — **Sidugu Rama Murthy**.
**Andhra State Movement** — **Konda Venkatappaiah**; the notes name no "Father" for the **Kisan / Agrarian Movement**.
xa: Veeresalingam was the first to render **Shakuntalam** and **Malavikagnimitram** into Telugu.
**Prolaya Nayaka** led the **post-Kakatiya** confederacy.
Telugu was declared a **Classical Language in 2008**.

197.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Sati Regulation of 1829:
1. It was associated with William Bentinck.
2. It made sati illegal.
3. Sati was treated as culpable homicide under the Regulation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
197.x: All three statements are correct. Regulation XVII of 1829, associated with William Bentinck, prohibited sati and treated participation in it as culpable homicide.
197.tq: Check each statement against the Act’s year, authority and legal consequence.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** **1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: the **Bengal Sati Regulation (Regulation XVII), 1829** came under **William Bentinck**.
Statement 2: it made **sati illegal**.
Statement 3: sati became punishable as **culpable homicide**.
xa: It followed the campaign of **Raja Rammohan Roy**.
Other Bentinck-era steps: **thuggee** suppressed by **Colonel William Sleeman** (**1830s**); **English Education Act, 1835** (Macaulay's Minute).
Exam angle: "Sati was abolished by" → **Bentinck**.

197.s: Who led the suppression of thuggee in the 1830s?
197.x: Colonel William Sleeman led the suppression of thuggee in the 1830s.
197.tq: Use the officer–operation association to avoid confusing administrators and legislators.
xs: **Colonel William Sleeman** suppressed **thuggee** in the **1830s** — option **(1)**.
**Macaulay** is linked with the **English Education Act, 1835**; **Ellenborough** with **Act V of 1843** (slavery); **Irwin** with the **Sarda Act** (**1929**).
xa: Thuggee suppression was part of the **Bentinck-era** reforms.
Bentinck also passed the **Sati Regulation, 1829**.

197.s: Which of the following correctly describes Bengal Regulations XXI of 1795 and III of 1804?
o: They abolished sati throughout British India.
They made the slave trade an offence.
They prohibited child marriage by fixing marriageable ages.
They declared female infanticide to be murder.
197.x: Bengal Regulations XXI of 1795 and III of 1804 declared infanticide, including female infanticide, to be murder.
197.tq: Match the regulation numbers with their precise social reform subject.
xs: **Bengal Regulations XXI of 1795 and III of 1804** declared **infanticide murder** — option **(4)**.
**Sati** was banned in **1829**; the **slave trade** became an offence under the **IPC 1860**; marriage ages came with the **1872** Act.
xa: **Anti-Infanticide Act, 1802** (**Wellesley**): ban on child sacrifice at **Sagar Island**.
**Female Infanticide Prevention Act, 1870** under **Mayo**.
⚠ Some notes wrongly say **1856** under Dalhousie for the infanticide Act.

197.s: The Female Infanticide Prevention Act was enacted in:
197.x: The Female Infanticide Prevention Act was enacted in 1870. The 1802 reference concerns the ban on child sacrifice at Sagar Island under Wellesley, not this Act.
197.tq: Separate the exact Act year from nearby regulations and the Sagar Island measure.
xs: The **Female Infanticide Prevention Act** came in **1870**, under **Mayo** — option **(4)**.
**1795** = Bengal Regulation XXI; **1802** = Sagar Island ban (**Wellesley**).
⚠ **1856** under **Dalhousie**, given in some notes, is wrong.
xa: It curbed the **killing of female infants**.
**1856** is the **Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act**.
Regulations **1795** and **1804** had declared infanticide murder.

197.s: Which of the following correctly explains the relationship among the measures concerning abolition of slavery in British India?
o: The Charter Act of 1833 directed abolition, Act V of 1843 made slavery illegal, and the IPC of 1860 made slave trade an offence.
Act V of 1843 directed abolition, while the Charter Act of 1833 made slave trade an offence.
The Charter Act of 1833 abolished slavery immediately and the IPC of 1860 restored it.
The Native Marriage Act of 1872 abolished slavery and the IPC of 1860 regulated it.
197.x: The Charter Act of 1833 directed abolition, Act V of 1843 under Ellenborough made slavery illegal, and the IPC of 1860 made the slave trade an offence.
197.tq: Track the progressive legal stages instead of treating direction, abolition and offence as the same provision.
xs: **Charter Act 1833** directed abolition → **Act V of 1843** made slavery illegal → **IPC 1860** made slave trade an offence — option **(1)**.
Act V of 1843 came under **Ellenborough**.
The **1872** Act concerned **marriage**, not slavery.
xa: The IPC of **1860** also set the age of consent at **10**.
Exam angle: **Act-year-Governor-General** matching.

197.s:
Consider the following statements about the Lex Loci Act (Caste Disabilities Removal Act), 1850:
1. It was passed under Lord Dalhousie.
2. It let a Hindu who converted to another religion still inherit ancestral property.
3. Orthodox Hindus saw it as an incentive to conversion, and it became a grievance behind 1857.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
197.x: All three statements are correct. The Act was passed under Dalhousie and protected converts' right to inherit ancestral property (APPSC-G2 2025). Orthodox opinion read it as a state incentive to conversion, which fed the grievances of 1857. Every option that leaves out a statement is wrong.
197.tq: Lex Loci 1850 = convert's inheritance, Dalhousie.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** **1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: the **Lex Loci Act 1850** came under **Dalhousie**.
Statement 2: Hindu converts could still **inherit ancestral property** (APPSC-G2 **2025**).
Statement 3: orthodox Hindus saw it as a state **incentive to conversion** → a grievance behind **1857**.
xa: Also called the **Caste Disabilities Removal Act** and **Religious Disabilities Act**.
⚠ It did **not** deal with sati, widows or child marriage.
The **Widow Remarriage Act** was also drafted under Dalhousie.

197.s: Which statement most accurately describes the legislative history of the Hindu Widows’ Remarriage Act of 1856?
o: It was drafted under Mayo and enacted in 1872 under Irwin.
It was drafted under Bentinck and enacted in 1856 under Lansdowne.
It was drafted under Dalhousie and enacted in July 1856 under Canning.
It was drafted under Canning and enacted in 1850 under Dalhousie.
197.x: The bill was prepared during Dalhousie’s tenure but the Act was enacted in July 1856 under Lord Canning. The Act legalised widow remarriage and legitimised the children of such marriages.
197.tq: Resolve the close Governor-General distinction by separating drafting from enactment.
xs: The **Widow Remarriage Act** was **drafted under Dalhousie** and **enacted in July 1856 under Canning** — option **(3)**.
Dalhousie left in **Feb 1856**, before it was passed.
**Mayo**, **Irwin**, **Bentinck** and **Lansdowne** are linked with the **1870**, **1929**, **1829** and **1891** measures.
xa: It was **Act XV of 1856**, from **Vidyasagar**'s campaign.
It also **legitimised children** of such marriages.
⚠ Some tables list it under Dalhousie — read the options carefully.

197.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar:
1. He campaigned against child marriage.
2. He opposed polygamy.
3. His social reform activities were confined to widow remarriage.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
197.x: Vidyasagar campaigned against both child marriage and polygamy. His activities were not confined to widow remarriage.
197.tq: Find the single over-restrictive statement containing ‘confined’.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1)** **1 and 2 only**.
Statements 1 and 2: Vidyasagar **opposed child marriage and polygamy**.
Statement 3 is wrong: he also worked for **women's education** — the Bethune School (**1849**) and many girls' schools in Bengal.
xa: His petitions led to the **Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act (Act XV of 1856)**.
He performed Bengal's **first widow remarriage** on **7 Dec 1856**.
He sent support for **Veeresalingam**'s third remarriage.

197.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Indian Spectator — Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar’s Sanskrit grammar
Notes on Infant Marriage — Vidyasagar’s autobiography
197.x: Barnaparichay was a Bengali alphabet primer written by Vidyasagar. The other works or journals are wrongly attributed or misdescribed.
197.tq: Start from the sure author–work pair and reject swapped authorship or genre.
xs: **Barnaparichay** is Vidyasagar's **Bengali alphabet primer** — option **(1)**.
**Indian Spectator** was **Behramji Malabari**'s journal; **Kesari** was **Tilak**'s.
**Notes on Infant Marriage and Enforced Widowhood** (**1884**) is Malabari's, not an autobiography of Vidyasagar.
xa: Vidyasagar **modernised Bengali prose**.
He founded the **Metropolitan Institution**.
Title "**Vidyasagar**" = Ocean of Learning.

197.s: The Bethune School was established with the support of Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar and:
197.x: Vidyasagar helped J.E.D. Bethune establish the Bethune School in 1849, one of the earliest girls’ schools in India.
197.tq: Use the founder–institution association and distinguish it from later women’s education figures.
xs: Vidyasagar helped **J.E.D. Bethune** set up the **Bethune School** (**1849**) — option **(2)**; one of India's earliest girls' schools.
**D.K. Karve** founded the Indian Women's University; **Meherbai Tata** and **Cornelia Sorabji** the National Council of Women (**1925**).
xa: Vidyasagar opened many **girls' schools** in Bengal.
Savitribai Phule taught at the first girls' school in **Pune** (**1848**).
Vidyasagar opposed **child marriage and polygamy**.

197.s: The first widow remarriage in Bengal is associated with which date?
197.x: Vidyasagar performed the first widow remarriage in Bengal on 7 December 1856. 11 December 1881 is the date of Andhra's first widow remarriage at Rajahmundry, so the options mix the two events' dates.
197.tq: Separate closely related regional dates by matching each date with its correct region.
xs: Bengal's first lawful widow remarriage was on **7 December 1856** — option **(3)**, performed by **Vidyasagar**.
**11 Dec 1881** is **Andhra**'s first, at **Rajahmundry** — the options mix the two.
xa: Andhra couple: **Gogulapati Sriramulu** and **Seethamma**/Gauramma.
The **Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act** was enacted in **July 1856**.
**M.G. Ranade** called Veeresalingam the "**South Indian Vidyasagar**".

197.s: The Native (Civil) Marriage Act of 1872 was chiefly associated with the campaign of:
197.x: The Native or Brahmo Marriage Act of 1872 was a product of Keshab Chandra Sen’s campaign. It also barred polygamy and permitted inter-caste marriage.
197.tq: Match the reform legislation with the reformer who campaigned for it.
xs: The **Native (Civil) Marriage Act, 1872** came at **Keshab Chandra Sen**'s urging, for **Brahmo marriages** — option **(3)**.
**Rammohan Roy** = sati campaign (**1829**); **Har Bilas Sarda** = **1929** Act; **Vidyasagar** = **1856** Act.
xa: It set **14 for girls, 18 for boys** (APPSC-GS **2025**), allowed **inter-caste** marriage, barred **polygamy**.
Also called the "**Brahmo Marriage Act**".
⚠ Keshab broke it in **1878** by marrying his minor daughter to the **Cooch Behar** prince.

197.s:
Consider the following statements about the Native Marriage Act of 1872:
1. It allowed inter-caste marriage.
2. It barred polygamy.
3. It fixed the minimum marriage age at 14 years for girls and 18 years for boys.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
197.x: All three statements are correct. The Act permitted inter-caste marriage, prohibited polygamy and prescribed minimum ages of 14 for girls and 18 for boys.
197.tq: Check whether all legal features belong to the same enactment.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** **1, 2 and 3**.
The **1872** Act allowed **inter-caste** marriage, barred **polygamy**, and set **14 for girls, 18 for boys**.
xa: It was **Act III of 1872**, a product of **Keshab Chandra Sen**'s campaign.
Some notes list it as "Brahma Act (**Anti-Child Marriage Act**)".
⚠ **1891** Act = age of **consent 12**, not a marriage age.

197.s: The Brahmo Samaj split in 1878 because Keshab Chandra Sen:
o: opposed the Native Marriage Act of 1872
married his minor daughter to the prince of Cooch Behar, breaking the 1872 Act
joined the Prarthana Samaj at Bombay
supported Tilak's opposition to the Age of Consent Bill
197.x: Keshab broke the Native Marriage Act he had himself campaigned for by marrying his minor daughter to the Cooch Behar prince, and this split the Samaj in 1878. He did not oppose the 1872 Act; it came from his own campaign. He did not join the Prarthana Samaj. The Age of Consent debate came in 1891.
197.tq: 1878 split = Cooch Behar marriage.
xs: The **1878** Brahmo split came when Keshab **married his minor daughter to the Cooch Behar prince**, breaking the **1872** Act — option **(2)**.
He did not oppose the 1872 Act — it came from his own campaign.
The **Age of Consent** debate (Tilak) came in **1891**.
xa: The 1872 Act set **14 (girls)** / **18 (boys)**.
It allowed **inter-caste** marriage and barred **polygamy**.

197.s: Who advocated the enactment of the Age of Consent Act of 1891?
197.x: Behramji Malabari, a Parsi reformer from Bombay, advocated the Age of Consent law. The Act was enacted during Lord Lansdowne’s tenure.
197.tq: Use the reformer–Act association rather than the Governor-General association.
xs: **Behramji Malabari** (Parsi reformer) campaigned for the **Age of Consent Act 1891** — option **(1)**.
**Vishnu Shastri Pandit** led the widow-remarriage campaign in **Maharashtra**; **Ramabai Ranade** co-founded the **Poona Seva Sadan**.
xa: Malabari wrote **Notes on Infant Marriage and Enforced Widowhood** (**1884**).
He edited the **Indian Spectator**.
The Act came under **Lansdowne**.

197.s: Which journal was edited by Behramji Malabari?
197.x: Behramji Malabari edited the Indian Spectator. Kesari was associated with Tilak, while the other titles are not the journal identified here as his.
197.tq: Apply the editor–journal association and avoid substituting a journal linked with another reformer.
xs: **Behramji Malabari** edited the **Indian Spectator** — option **(1)**.
**Kesari** was **Tilak**'s; **Sati Hita Bodhini** (**1883**) was **Veeresalingam**'s women's journal.
xa: Malabari's book: **Notes on Infant Marriage and Enforced Widowhood** (**1884**).
His campaign led to the **Age of Consent Act 1891**.
⚠ The APPSC key pairs **Seva Sadan — Malabari**.

197.s: Which one of the following best describes the Rakhmabai case?
o: A husband’s suit for restitution of conjugal rights after a child marriage
A case concerning the abolition of sati
A dispute over admission to the Bethune School
A petition against the licensing of women doctors
197.x: Rakhmabai’s husband, Dadaji, sued for restitution of conjugal rights after their child marriage. The case raised questions concerning age of consent and conjugal rights.
197.tq: Identify the legal issue rather than choosing a broader but unrelated social-reform theme.
xs: The **Rakhmabai case** (**1884-88**) was husband **Dadaji**'s suit for **restitution of conjugal rights** after a child marriage — option **(1)**.
It raised the **age of consent** and conjugal-rights issues (UPSC PYQ **2020**).
xa: Rakhmabai refused to live with the husband she was married to as a child.
She later became one of India's first practising **women doctors**.
The **Phulmoni Dasi** case (**1889-90**) pushed the **1891** Act through.

197.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Age of Consent Act, 1891:
1. It raised the age of consent for girls from 10 to 12.
2. It regulated consummation rather than directly fixing the minimum age of marriage.
3. It was enacted during Lord Lansdowne’s tenure.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
197.x: All three statements are correct. The 1891 Act raised the age of consent from 10 to 12, dealt with consummation rather than directly regulating marriage, and was enacted during Lord Lansdowne’s tenure.
197.tq: Check each statement separately, especially the distinction between consent and marriage.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** **1, 2 and 3**.
The **1891** Act raised the age of consent from **10 to 12**.
It regulated **consummation, not marriage**.
It was passed under **Lansdowne**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes say it "prohibited marriage below 12" — loosely worded.
**Tilak** opposed it in **Kesari**; the **Moderates** supported it.
Campaigner: **Behramji Malabari**.

197.s: Who among the following opposed the Age of Consent Bill on the ground that it represented foreign interference in Hindu custom?
197.x: Bal Gangadhar Tilak opposed the Bill, including through Kesari, on the ground that it was foreign interference in Hindu custom. The Moderates supported the Bill.
197.tq: Use the reformer–position contrast, particularly the opposition of Tilak versus the support of the Moderates.
xs: **B.G. Tilak** opposed the Bill in **Kesari** as **foreign interference in Hindu custom** — option **(1)**.
**Behramji Malabari** campaigned **for** it; the **Moderates** supported it.
xa: The Act raised the age of consent to **12** (**1891**, Lansdowne).
The **Phulmoni Dasi** case (**1889-90**) pushed it through.
The **Rakhmabai** case (**1884-88**) sparked the debate.

197.s:
Arrange the following developments concerning the age of consent in chronological order:
A. Age of consent raised to 16 through an amendment to the Indian Penal Code
B. Age of consent raised to 18
C. Age of Consent Act raised the age from 10 to 12
D. Age of consent raised to 14
197.x: The sequence is 1891: 10 to 12; 1925: 14; 1949: 16; and 2012: 18 under POCSO.
197.tq: Anchor the sequence with the 1891 Act and the latest 2012 milestone, then place the intermediate amendments.
xs: The **18** came with **POCSO 2012**.
xa: ⚠ Age of consent (**18**, POCSO/BNS) ≠ minimum marriage age (**18/21**, **PCMA 2006**).
The **1925** step was an IPC amendment.

197.s: The death of which child bride after forced cohabitation by her adult husband helped push the Age of Consent Act of 1891 through?
197.x: Phulmoni Dasi, a child bride of about 10-11, died after forced cohabitation (1889-90), and her case pushed the 1891 Act through. Rakhmabai refused to live with her husband in the restitution-of-conjugal-rights case. Anandibai Joshi was the first Indian woman with a degree in Western medicine, and Tarabai Shinde wrote Stri Purush Tulana.
197.tq: Phulmoni = 1891 Act; Rakhmabai = conjugal rights.
xs: **Phulmoni Dasi** (**1889-90**), a child bride of about **10-11**, died after forced cohabitation — option **(3)**; this pushed the **1891** Act through.
**Rakhmabai** refused to live with her husband (restitution of conjugal rights case).
**Anandibai Joshi** = first Indian woman with a Western medical degree; **Tarabai Shinde** wrote **Stri Purush Tulana**.
xa: The Act raised the age of consent from **10 to 12**.
It was passed under **Lansdowne**.

197.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Pandita Ramabai — The High-Caste Hindu Woman
197.x: Stri Purush Tulana was written by Tarabai Shinde. Anandibai Joshi was associated with letters on women's education and was the first Indian woman to obtain a degree in Western medicine.
197.tq: Find the swapped author–work pair.
xs: "**Anandibai Joshi — Stri Purush Tulana**" is wrong — option **(1)**; that book (**1882**) is **Tarabai Shinde**'s.
Anandibai Joshi wrote **letters on women's education** and was the first Indian woman with a **Western medicine** degree.
The rest are correct: **Savitribai** — poems and articles; **Pandita Ramabai** — **The High-Caste Hindu Woman**.
xa: ⚠ **1882** = Ramabai's Arya Mahila Samaj and Tarabai Shinde's Stri Purush Tulana.
Tarabai Shinde (**1850-1910**): early feminist critique of patriarchy.
Anandibai Joshi: **1865-1887**.

197.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Reformer)
a. D.K. Karve
b. Pandita Ramabai
c. Jyotiba and Savitribai Phule

List-II (Institution or initiative)
i. Girls' school for untouchables
 ii. Widow Marriage Association
 iii. Arya Mahila Samaj

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
197.x: D.K. Karve founded the Widow Marriage Association, Pandita Ramabai founded the Arya Mahila Samaj, and Jyotiba and Savitribai Phule established a girls' school for untouchables.
197.tq: Start from the sure institution–reformer pair and eliminate codes.
xs: Correct match: **a-ii, b-iii, c-i** — option **(1)**.
**D.K. Karve** → **Widow Marriage Association** (**1893**); **Pandita Ramabai** → **Arya Mahila Samaj** (**1882**).
**Jyotiba and Savitribai Phule** → **girls' school for untouchables**.
xa: Karve also founded the **Hindu Widows' Home, Poona (1896)** and the **Indian Women's University (1916, now SNDT)**.
The Phules also opened a **home for upper-caste widows** (**1854**).
Karve praised **Veeresalingam**'s work.

197.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
o: Pandita Ramabai — Mukti Mission at Poona, 1882
D.K. Karve — Hindu Widows' Home at Poona, 1896
197.x: D.K. Karve established the Hindu Widows' Home at Poona in 1896. Mukti Mission was at Kedgaon, Sharada Sadan was associated with Pandita Ramabai, and the Widow Marriage Association was founded by Karve.
197.tq: Check both the institution and its location or date in each pair.
xs: **D.K. Karve — Hindu Widows' Home, Poona, 1896** is correct — option **(2)**.
**Mukti Mission** was at **Kedgaon** (**1898**), not Poona 1882.
**Sharada Sadan** (**1889**) was **Pandita Ramabai**'s; the **Widow Marriage Association** (**1893**) was **Karve**'s.
xa: The Widows' Home was at **Hingne**.
Karve: **Bharat Ratna 1958**.
**1882** = Ramabai's **Arya Mahila Samaj**.

197.s:
Consider the following statements about the educational work associated with Jyotiba and Savitribai Phule:
1. A girls’ school was opened at Pune in 1848.
2. Savitribai Phule is regarded as India’s first woman teacher.
3. A home for upper-caste widows was established in 1854.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
197.x: The Phules opened a girls’ school at Pune in 1848, Savitribai is regarded as India’s first woman teacher, and a home for upper-caste widows was established in 1854.
197.tq: Link the reformers with distinct educational and social-service initiatives and their dates.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** **1, 2 and 3**.
The Phules opened a **girls' school at Pune** in **1848**; **Savitribai** was **India's first woman teacher**.
They set up a **home for upper-caste widows** in **1854**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes date the first girls' school to **1851**.
Savitribai (**1831-1897**) was born at **Naigaon, Satara**.
Also a **Home for the Prevention of Infanticide** (**1863**).

197.s:
Consider the following statements about Pandita Ramabai:
1. She founded Arya Mahila Samaj in Poona.
2. Arya Mahila Samaj was founded in 1882.
3. She founded Sarada Niketan in Guntur in 1922.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
197.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Sarada Niketan in Guntur was founded by Unnava Lakshminarayana with his wife Lakshmibayamma.
197.tq: Catch the founder swap between institutions associated with women’s education.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1)** **1 and 2 only**.
Statements 1 and 2: **Pandita Ramabai** founded the **Arya Mahila Samaj** in **1882**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Sarada Niketan** (Guntur, **1922**) was founded by **Unnava Lakshminarayana** with wife **Lakshmibayamma**.
xa: Ramabai's **Sharada Sadan** (Bombay **1889**, later Poona) was a home for widows.
⚠ **Sharada Sadan** (Ramabai) vs **Sarada Niketan** (Unnava, Guntur).
Lakshmibayamma's widow asylum at **Guntur** (**1902**) later merged into Sarada Niketan.

197.s: Poona Seva Sadan was founded by:
o: Shiv Narayan Agnihotri and Hriday Nath Kunzru
197.x: Poona Seva Sadan was founded by Ramabai Ranade and G.K. Devadhar in 1909.
197.tq: Discriminate between institutions with the common name ‘Seva Sadan’.
xs: **Poona Seva Sadan** (**1909**) was founded by **Ramabai Ranade** and **G.K. Devadhar** — option **(2)**.
**Hriday Nath Kunzru** founded the **Seva Samiti**; **Unnava Lakshminarayana** and Lakshmibayamma founded **Sarada Niketan**.
xa: Seva Sadan cared for exploited and abandoned women **across castes** — education, medical help, welfare.
Ramabai Ranade also led the **Ladies' Social Conference** (**1904**, Bombay).
⚠ The APPSC-G2 **2023** key pairs **Seva Sadan — Malabari**.

197.s: Sarada Niketan, described as a women’s gurukulam, was established at Guntur in 1922 by:
197.x: Sarada Niketan was established at Guntur in 1922 by Unnava Lakshminarayana with his wife Lakshmibayamma.
197.tq: Test the Andhra-specific institution, place, year and founder together.
xs: **Sarada Niketan** (women's gurukulam, Guntur, **1922**) was founded by **Unnava Lakshminarayana** with **Lakshmibayamma** — option **(1)**.
**Ramabai Ranade** and **G.K. Devadhar** founded the **Poona Seva Sadan**; **N.M. Joshi** the **Social Service League**.
xa: Lakshmibayamma's widow asylum at **Guntur (1902)** later merged into it.
She ran the monthly **Sri Sarada Niketanam**.
Other Andhra bodies: **Vysya Seva Sadanam** (Rajahmundry, **1920**), **Indira Saranalayam** (Vijayawada, **1927**).

197.s: The Ladies’ Social Conference, also known as Bharat Mahila Parishad, was associated with:
197.x: The Ladies’ Social Conference, also called Bharat Mahila Parishad, was associated with Ramabai Ranade in Bombay in 1904 and functioned under the National Social Conference.
197.tq: Use the full organisation name, founder and location to avoid confusing similarly themed bodies.
xs: The **Ladies' Social Conference** (Bharat Mahila Parishad) was **Ramabai Ranade**'s, **Bombay**, **1904** — option **(1)**.
It worked under the **National Social Conference**.
**Sarala Devi Chaudhurani** and **Allahabad, 1910** = **Bharat Stree Mahamandal**; **Pandita Ramabai** and **1882** = **Arya Mahila Samaj**.
xa: **National Council of Women in India** (**1925**): **Meherbai Tata**, **Cornelia Sorabji**.
Ramabai Ranade also co-founded the **Poona Seva Sadan** (**1909**).

197.s: Which of the following statements regarding Bharat Stree Mahamandal is correct?
o: It was founded in 1927 by Margaret Cousins at Bombay.
It was founded in 1904 by Ramabai Ranade at Poona.
It was founded in 1917 by Annie Besant at Madras.
It was founded in 1910 by Sarala Devi Chaudhurani at Allahabad.
197.x: Bharat Stree Mahamandal was founded in 1910 by Sarala Devi Chaudhurani at Allahabad. It is regarded as the first major all-India women’s body founded by a woman.
197.tq: Use the founder–place–year triad and reject swapped details from other organisations.
xs: **Bharat Stree Mahamandal** was founded in **1910** by **Sarala Devi Chaudhurani** at **Allahabad** — option **(4)**.
It was the **first major all-India women's body founded by a woman**.
**1904** / **Ramabai Ranade** = Ladies' Social Conference.
xa: ⚠ Some notes credit it to **D.K. Karve** — the standard answer is Sarala Devi.
**AIWC** pressed for the **Sarda Act (1929)** and the **Hindu Women's Right to Property Act (1937)**.
**National Council of Women in India**: **1925**.

197.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Institution)
a. Deva Samaj
b. Seva Samiti
c. Social Service League
d. Sharada Sadan

List-II (Founder)
i. Pandita Ramabai
ii. N.M. Joshi
iii. Shiv Narayan Agnihotri
iv. Hriday Nath Kunzru

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
197.x: Deva Samaj — Shiv Narayan Agnihotri; Seva Samiti — Hriday Nath Kunzru (Allahabad, 1914); Social Service League — N.M. Joshi (Bombay, 1911); Sharada Sadan — Pandita Ramabai (1889). Note the APPSC-G2 2023 key paired Deva Samaj with Radhakant Deb, though standard texts give it to Agnihotri.
197.tq: Start from the sure institution–founder pairs and eliminate the remaining codes.
xs: Correct match: **a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i** — option **(1)**.
**Deva Samaj** → **Shiv Narayan Agnihotri** (standard texts); **Seva Samiti** → **Hriday Nath Kunzru** (Allahabad, **1914**).
**Social Service League** → **N.M. Joshi** (Bombay, **1911**); **Sharada Sadan** → **Pandita Ramabai** (**1889**).
xa: ⚠ The APPSC-G2 **2023** key paired **Deva Samaj — Radhakant Deb**; standard texts say **Agnihotri**.
**Poona Seva Sadan** (**1909**): **Ramabai Ranade** and **G.K. Devadhar**.
**Sarada Niketan** (Guntur, **1922**): **Unnava Lakshminarayana** with Lakshmibayamma.

197.s: The All India Women's Conference pressed for which of the following laws?
o: The Age of Consent Act, 1891 and the Native Marriage Act, 1872
The Sarda Act, 1929 and the Hindu Women's Right to Property Act, 1937
The Widow Remarriage Act, 1856 and the Lex Loci Act, 1850
The Vernacular Press Act, 1878 and the Arms Act, 1878
197.x: The AIWC pressed for the Sarda Act (1929) and the Hindu Women's Right to Property Act (1937). The 1872 and 1891 Acts were driven by Keshab Chandra Sen and Malabari. The 1850 and 1856 Acts were passed under Dalhousie and Canning. The 1878 Acts were Lytton's repressive measures.
197.tq: AIWC: Sarda Act + 1937 property Act.
xs: The **AIWC** pressed for the **Sarda Act (1929)** and the **Hindu Women's Right to Property Act (1937)** — option **(2)**.
The **1872** and **1891** Acts came from **Keshab Chandra Sen** and **Behramji Malabari**'s campaigns.
The **1850** and **1856** Acts were passed under **Dalhousie** and **Canning**.
xa: The Sarda Act set **girls 14, boys 18**; moved by **Harbilas Sarda** under **Irwin**.
Other women's bodies: **Bharat Stree Mahamandal** (**1910**), **National Council of Women in India** (**1925**).
The **Vernacular Press Act 1878** was a press curb, not a women's law.

197.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Veeresalingam's educational activities is correct?

1. He founded the first girls' school associated with his reform work in 1874.
2. A second girls' school was established at Innispeta, Rajahmundry, in 1881.
3. He was the first in Andhra to promote co-education.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
197.x: All three statements are correct. Veeresalingam's first girls' school dates to 1874, the Innispeta school to 1881, and he was the first in Andhra to promote co-education.
197.tq: Combine dates and a distinction to test the complete educational reform profile.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** **1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: his first girls' school dates to **1874** (**Dowlaiswaram**).
Statement 2: a second school opened at **Innispeta**, Rajahmundry, in **1881**.
Statement 3: he was the **first in Andhra to promote co-education**.
xa: ⚠ APPSC **2025** key: "first girls' school at **Rajahmundry**".
His women's journal: **Satihita Bodhini** (**1883**).
**M.G. Ranade** called him the "**South Indian Vidyasagar**".

197.s: Kandukuri Rajyalakshmamma, the wife of Veeresalingam, is particularly associated with:
o: Sheltering widows and destitute women and hosting widow and inter-caste marriages
Establishing the Mukti Mission at Kedgaon
197.x: Kandukuri Rajyalakshmamma hosted widow remarriages and inter-caste marriages at her home, which also became a shelter for widows and destitute women.
197.tq: Identify the reformer's distinctive social role rather than assigning her another reformer's institution.
xs: **Kandukuri Rajyalakshmamma** hosted **widow remarriages and inter-caste marriages** at her home and **sheltered widows and destitute women** — option **(1)**.
The **Indian Women's University** was **D.K. Karve**'s; **Stri Purush Tulana** is **Tarabai Shinde**'s; the **Mukti Mission** (Kedgaon) is **Pandita Ramabai**'s.
xa: She married Veeresalingam in **1860**.
Andhra's first widow remarriage: **11 Dec 1881**, Rajahmundry.
Veeresalingam's widow homes: **Madras** (**1897**) and **Rajahmundry** (**1905**).

197.s: Bandaru Achamamba is remembered as an early Telugu woman historian and short-story writer. Which of the following was her work?
197.x: Bandaru Achamamba wrote Abala Sachcharitra Ratnamala, dealing with the lives of notable women.
197.tq: Use the exact title to distinguish literary works of women reformers.
xs: **Bandaru Achamamba** wrote **Abala Sachcharitra Ratnamala**, lives of notable women — option **(3)**.
**Sri Sarada Niketanam** was **Unnava Lakshmibayamma**'s monthly; **The High-Caste Hindu Woman** is **Pandita Ramabai**'s; **Sati Hita Bodhini** is **Veeresalingam**'s.
xa: Achamamba was an early Telugu woman **historian** and **short-story writer**.
Lakshmibayamma's widow asylum at **Guntur (1902)** later merged into **Sarada Niketan**.
**Tripura Sundari Samajam** was at **Bapatla**.

197.s: Which of the following pairs relating to Veeresalingam's activities is correctly matched?
197.x: Veeresalingam established the Widow Remarriage Association in 1880. The Innispeta school dates to 1881, Satihita Bodhini to 1883, and the Rajahmundry widow home to 1905.
197.tq: Separate similar reform activities by matching each institution with its correct year.
xs: **Widow Remarriage Association — 1880** is correct — option **(1)**.
The **Innispeta** school is **1881**, not 1874; **Satihita Bodhini** is **1883**, not 1897.
The **Rajahmundry** widow home is **1905**, not 1881.
xa: **1874** = first girls' school (Dowlaiswaram); **1897** = Madras widow home.
**53** remarriages in all (some notes **20** by **1892**).
The Association was inspired by the **1856** Act.

197.s: Who moved the Child Marriage Restraint Bill that became the Sarda Act?
197.x: The Sarda Act was moved by Har Bilas Sarda during the period of Lord Irwin.
197.tq: Match the legislation with its mover, not with another contemporary reform advocate.
xs: The **Sarda Act** was moved by **Har Bilas Sarda**, under **Irwin** — option **(4)**.
**Keshab Chandra Sen** = **1872** Act; **Behramji Malabari** = **1891** Act; **D.K. Karve** = widows' home and women's university.
xa: Passed **1929**; in force from **1 April 1930**.
Minimum age: **girls 14, boys 18**.
Amended **1978**: **18 (girls) / 21 (boys)**.

197.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the legal age of marriage:
1. The 1978 amendment raised the minimum age to 18 years for girls and 21 years for boys.
2. The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 prescribes 18 years for women and 21 years for men.
3. A Union Cabinet proposal in 2021 to raise the women's age to 21 years had become law by January 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
197.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The 2021 proposal to raise the women's age to 21 had not become law by January 2026, when the legal age remained 18.
197.tq: Test the difference between an enacted provision and a proposal that has not become law.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1)** **1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: the **1978** amendment set **18 (girls) / 21 (boys)**.
Statement 2: the **Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006** = **18 for women, 21 for men**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **2021** proposal to raise women's age to **21** has **not become law** — still **18**.
xa: The original **Sarda Act (1929)** set **14 / 18**.
⚠ Age of consent (**18**, POCSO/BNS) ≠ marriage age (**18/21**, PCMA 2006).

197.s: The Child Marriage Restraint Act (Sarda Act), 1929, passed under Lord Irwin, fixed the minimum marriage age at:
197.x: The Sarda Act fixed 14 for girls and 18 for boys, the same ages as the 1872 Native Marriage Act. 12 was the age of consent set in 1891, not a marriage age. 18 and 21 came only with the 1978 amendment and are now in the PCMA 2006. 16 and 18 is not a pair any of these Acts used.
xs: The **Sarda Act, 1929** set **14 for girls and 18 for boys** — option **(2)**.
**12** was the **1891** age of **consent**, not a marriage age.
**18 and 21** came with the **1978** amendment and the **PCMA 2006**.
xa: ⚠ **14/18** = both the **1872** Act and the **1929** Sarda Act.
In force from **1 April 1930**.
The **AIWC** pressed for the Sarda Act.

197.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Age of Consent Act, 1891 — Lord Irwin
197.x: The Female Infanticide Act of 1870 was associated with Lord Mayo. Lansdowne was associated with the Age of Consent Act, Irwin with the Sarda Act, and the 1872 Native Marriage Act had no Governor-General specified in the table.
197.tq: Eliminate swapped Governor-General and Act combinations.
xs: **Female Infanticide Act, 1870 — Lord Mayo** is correct — option **(2)**.
**Age of Consent Act 1891** = **Lansdowne**; **Sarda Act 1929** = **Irwin**.
**Canning** passed the **1856** Widow Remarriage Act; the notes name no Governor-General for the **1872** Act.
xa: ⚠ Some notes wrongly say the infanticide Act was **1856** under Dalhousie.
Exam angle: **Act-year-Governor-General** matching.

197.s:
Arrange the following enactments in chronological order:
A. Age of Consent Act
B. Caste Disabilities Removal Act
C. Hindu Widows’ Remarriage Act
D. Child Marriage Restraint Act
197.x: The correct sequence is the Caste Disabilities Removal Act of 1850, Hindu Widows’ Remarriage Act of 1856, Age of Consent Act of 1891, and Child Marriage Restraint Act of 1929.
197.tq: Anchor the sequence with the earliest 1850 Act and the latest 1929 Act.
xs: Order: **Caste Disabilities Removal Act 1850 → Widow Remarriage Act 1856 → Age of Consent Act 1891 → Sarda Act 1929** — option **(1)** **B, C, A, D**.
Governors-General: **Dalhousie**, **Canning**, **Lansdowne**, **Irwin**.
xa: The **1856** Act was drafted under Dalhousie.
Movers: **Vidyasagar** (1856), **Malabari** (1891), **Har Bilas Sarda** (1929).

197.s:
Which of the following statements about the Caste Disabilities Removal Act of 1850 is correct?
1. It is also known as the Lex Loci Act.
2. It protected the inheritance rights of a person who converted to Christianity.
3. It dealt primarily with the abolition of sati.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
197.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Lex Loci Act protected the right of a convert to inherit ancestral property; abolition of sati was dealt with by the 1829 Sati Regulation.
197.tq: Reject the statement that assigns the subject of one reform Act to another.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2)** **1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: the Caste Disabilities Removal Act is the **Lex Loci Act**.
Statement 2: a convert (e.g. to **Christianity**) kept the right to **inherit ancestral property**.
Statement 3 is wrong: it did not deal with sati — that was the **1829** Sati Regulation.
xa: Also called the **Religious Disabilities Act**; passed under **Dalhousie**.
It became a grievance behind **1857**.

197.s: Which one of the following correctly states the distinction between the age of consent and the minimum age of marriage in India?
o: The age of consent is 18 years under POCSO/BNS, while the minimum age of marriage is 18 years for women and 21 years for men under the PCMA, 2006.
The age of consent is 21 years, while the minimum age of marriage is 18 years for both men and women.
The age of consent is 18 years, while the minimum age of marriage is 18 years for women and 21 years for men.
Both the age of consent and the minimum age of marriage are uniformly fixed at 21 years under the PCMA, 2006.
197.x: The age of consent is 18 under POCSO/BNS, while the minimum marriage age under the PCMA 2006 is 18 for women and 21 for men. Option C states the same figures but omits the laws; A is the complete statement of the distinction and is the key.
197.tq: Split the two legally related but distinct concepts before comparing their age limits.
xs: Age of consent = **18 years** under **POCSO/BNS**; minimum marriage age = **18 years for women and 21 years for men** under **PCMA, 2006** — option **(1)**.
Option 3 gives the same figures but omits the laws; option 1 is the complete statement.

197.s: Which of the following statements best expresses the historical significance of the widow-remarriage reform movement in India?
o: Indian reformers used the colonial legislature to challenge orthodox practices, showing that the reform was not merely a British gift.
The movement was initiated exclusively by Christian missionaries and opposed by Indian reformers.
The movement dealt only with education and had no connection with social customs.
It was implemented entirely through indigenous customary law without legislative intervention.
197.x: Indian reformers used colonial legislation as an instrument to challenge orthodoxy. Therefore, the reform cannot be described as merely a British gift.
197.tq: Choose the option that captures both the institutional method and the agency of Indian reformers.
xs: Indian reformers **used the colonial legislature against orthodoxy** — reform was "**not merely a British gift**" — option **(1)**.
Example: **Vidyasagar**'s petitions → **Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act (Act XV of 1856)**.
xa: Andhra's **Veeresalingam**, inspired by the 1856 Act, held the first remarriage on **11 Dec 1881**.
Bengal's first remarriage: **7 Dec 1856**.
**Malabari**'s campaign → **Age of Consent Act 1891**.

197.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
 a. Founder of the first Women's University in India
 b. Present location of that university (SNDT)
 c. Location of Karve's Home for Widows
 d. Year the Home for Widows was established

List-II
 i. D.K. Karve
 ii. Bombay
 iii. Poona
 iv. 1896
197.x: D.K. Karve founded the first Women's University (1916), now SNDT University in Bombay, and his Home for Widows was set up at Hingne near Poona in 1896. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
197.tq: Separate Karve's two institutions by city.
n: The First Women's University was associated with D.K. Karve. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 60-64]
The First Women's University was located in Bombay. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 60-64]
D.K. Karve established the Home for Widow. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 60-64]
The Home for Widow was located in Poona. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 60-64]
The Home for Widow was established in 1896. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 60-64]
xs: The correct match is **a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**D.K. Karve** founded the **First Women's University**, located in **Bombay** (now **SNDT**).
He set up the **Home for Widows** at **Poona** in **1896**.
xa: Karve's **Indian Women's University** dates from **1916**; he got the **Bharat Ratna** in **1958**.
He also founded the **Widow Marriage Association (1893)**.
**Pandita Ramabai**'s **Sharada Sadan (1889, Bombay)** — a **home for widows**.

198.s: Which of the following was NOT an unintended result of British rule that helped the growth of Indian nationalism?
o: Uniform laws and English as a link language
Development of railways, telegraph and postal communication
Complete economic prosperity of Indian artisans
198.x: British rule produced political, administrative and economic integration through railways, telegraph, post and uniform laws, but economic exploitation ruined many artisans rather than bringing them prosperity.
198.tq: Reject the extreme economic claim that reverses the nationalist critique.
xs: **Complete economic prosperity of Indian artisans** was not a result — option **(4)**; **economic exploitation** caused the **ruin of artisans**.
British rule did unify India **politically, administratively and economically** — railways, telegraph, post, uniform laws — and made **English** a link language.
xa: Other unintended results: **Western liberal ideas** and a **new educated middle class** (lawyers, journalists, teachers).
Reactions that fed nationalism: **drain**, **racial arrogance** (Lytton, **Ilbert Bill**), foreign inspiration.
**History-writing** — rediscovery of India's past — gave **self-confidence**.

198.s:
Which combination best explains the contribution of Western education to the growth of Indian nationalism?
1. It introduced Indians to Western liberal ideas.
2. It helped English function as a link language.
3. It created a new educated middle class of lawyers, journalists and teachers.
4. It ended all racial discrimination in administration.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
198.x: Western education spread liberal ideas, promoted English as a link language and produced an educated middle class. It did not end racial discrimination.
