201.x: The Krishna District Association was formed on the lines suggested at the first session of the INC.
201.tq: Link an institutional development with the earlier national event that inspired it.
xs: The **Krishna District Association** was formed on lines suggested at the **first session of the INC** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was formed in **1892**, the first in the **Madras Presidency** (APPSC-GS 2021).
xa: Its first meeting was at **Machilipatnam** (APPSC 2012 key).
Its conference, presided by **Nyapathi Subbarao**, drew ~**223** delegates.
It led to other district bodies — **Vizag** **1893**, **Anantapur** **1907**, **Nellore** **1908**.

201.s:
Arrange the following district associations in chronological order of their formation:
A. Vizag District Association
B. Nellore District Association
C. Krishna District Association
D. Kurnool District Association
201.x: The order is Krishna (1892), Vizag (1893), Nellore (1908) and Kurnool (1914).
201.tq: Fix the earliest and latest associations first, then place the intermediate years.
xs: The order is **C, A, B, D** — so option **(1)** is correct.
xa: **Anantapur** came in **1907**; **Chittoor** and **Kadapa** in **1916**.
Krishna was the **first** in the **Madras Presidency** (APPSC-GS 2021).
Its first meeting was at **Machilipatnam** (APPSC 2012 key).

201.s:
Consider the following statements about the Krishna District Association:
1. Formed in 1892, it was the first district association in the Madras Presidency.
2. According to the APPSC key, its first meeting was held at Machilipatnam.
3. It was formed after the Vizag District Association.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
201.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Krishna District Association (1892) was the first in the Madras Presidency (APPSC-GS 2021). Statement 2 is correct: the APPSC 2012 key places its first meeting at Machilipatnam (some sources say Guntur - use the key). Statement 3 is wrong: Vizag followed in 1893. So '1 only' is incomplete and options with 3 are wrong.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: formed in **1892**, it was the first in the **Madras Presidency** (APPSC-GS 2021).
Statement 2 is correct: the APPSC 2012 key puts its first meeting at **Machilipatnam**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Vizag** followed in **1893** — so option **(2)**, **1 and 2 only**, is correct.
xa: ⚠ Some notes say **Ramaswamy Gupta** held the first conference at **Guntur (Jul 1892)** — use the key.
It was formed on lines suggested at the **first INC**.
**Nyapathi Subbarao** presided over its ~**223**-delegate conference.

201.s: Andhra Prakasika is correctly associated with which person?
201.x: The pairing of Andhra Prakasika with P. Anandacharyulu is accepted as correct.
201.tq: Discriminate between closely associated newspaper editors and founders.
xs: **Andhra Prakasika** is paired with **P. Anandacharyulu** — accepted as correct in APPSC 2019 — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Nyapathi Subbarao** ran **Vyjayanti** and **People's Magazine**.
xa: Andhra Prakasika was the **first political magazine** in Andhra (APPSC 2012).
⚠ First Telugu journal = **Satyadoota**; first political magazine = **Andhra Prakasika**.
By **1905** there were about **20** Telugu journals, among them **Deshabhimani** and **Sasilekha**.

201.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Andhra Prakasika — first political magazine in Andhra
Satyadoota — first political magazine in Andhra
Andhra Prakasika — first Telugu journal, run by the Bellary Christian mission
201.x: Andhra Prakasika was the first political magazine in Andhra (APPSC 2012). Satyadoota, run by the Bellary Christian mission, was the first Telugu journal, not a political magazine. Vyjayanti was Nyapathi Subbarao's monthly.
201.tq: First political = Andhra Prakasika; first Telugu journal = Satyadoota
xs: **Andhra Prakasika — first political magazine in Andhra** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct (APPSC 2012).
**Satyadoota**, run by the **Bellary Christian mission**, was the **first Telugu journal**, not a political magazine.
**Vyjayanti** was **Nyapathi Subbarao**'s monthly.
xa: ⚠ First Telugu journal = **Satyadoota**; first political magazine = **Andhra Prakasika**.
Andhra Prakasika's pairing with **P. Anandacharyulu** was accepted as correct (APPSC 2019).
**Krishna Patrika** is part of **Krishna** district's lead.

201.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. First session of the Indian National Congress
B. Formation of the Madras Mahajana Sabha
C. Formation of the Krishna District Association
D. Publication of Krishna Patrika
201.x: The order is B, A, C, D: the Madras Mahajana Sabha was founded in 1884, the first INC session met in 1885, the Krishna District Association was formed in 1892 and Krishna Patrika appeared in 1902. Option B puts the INC session before the Sabha, which is wrong.
201.tq: Place the dated institutional and press developments from earliest to latest.
xs: The order is **B, A, C, D** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **first INC session** met in **1885**; the **Krishna District Association** followed in **1892**.
**Krishna Patrika** is the last of the four.
xa: The Krishna District Association was formed on lines suggested at the **first INC**.
**Krishna** district led Andhra — first district association and **Krishna Patrika**.
**Vizag**'s association followed in **1893**.

201.s: In which year did a Telugu leader first become President of the Indian National Congress?
201.x: The first Telugu President of the INC held office in 1891, a year before the first district association in Andhra (1892).
xs: A Telugu leader first became INC President in **1891** — so option **(3)** is correct.
That was **Anandacharlu**, at Nagpur.
**1892** is the first district association; **1885** the first INC session; **1905** the Moderate-Extremist divide.
xa: Andhra FIRSTs: first district association **1892**; first political magazine **Andhra Prakasika**.
Anandacharlu was an Andhra **spokesman** in the early INC.
First Telugu journal: **Satyadoota**.

201.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Bala Bharathi Samiti
(b) Krishna District Association
(c) Comrades Association
(d) Young Indian Association

List-II
(i) Born after the arrest of Annie Besant
(ii) Founded in 1940 at Hyderabad
(iii) Founded in 1892 to fight British rule on social issues
(iv) Youth of Rajahmundry; February 1907, during Swadeshi

Select the correct code:
201.x: Bala Bharathi Samiti was formed by the youth of Rajahmundry in February 1907 during Swadeshi, the Krishna District Association in 1892, the Comrades Association at Hyderabad in 1940, and the Young Indian Association after Annie Besant's arrest, giving a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i.
201.tq: Recall the year and origin of each association.
n: Bala Bharathi Samiti was associated with the youth of Rajahmundry. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 44-45]
Bala Bharathi Samiti was founded in February 1907. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 44-45]
Bala Bharathi Samiti was associated with the Swadeshi movement. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 44-45]
Krishna District Association was founded in 1892. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 44-45]
Krishna District Association aimed to fight British rule on social issues. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 44-45]
Comrades Association was established in 1940. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 44-45]
Comrades Association was established in Hyderabad. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 44-45]
Young Indian Association was formed after the arrest of Annie Besant. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 44-45]
xs: The correct code is **a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i** — option **(2)**.
**Bala Bharathi Samiti** — **youth of Rajahmundry**, **February 1907**, Swadeshi; **Krishna District Association** — **1892**, to fight British rule on social issues.
**Comrades Association** — **1940**, **Hyderabad**; **Young Indian Association** — formed after the **arrest** of **Annie Besant**.
xa: The Krishna District Association was the **first** in the **Madras Presidency** (**APPSC-GS 2021**).
**Andhra Jana Sangam**: first meeting **14 February 1922**, **Hyderabad**.
District bodies followed: **Vizag 1893**, **Anantapur 1907**, **Nellore 1908**, **Kurnool 1914**.

201.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Christian Association of Bellary
(b) Krishna District Congress Association
(c) Madras Native Association
(d) Young Indian Association

List-II
(i) First meeting held in Guntur
(ii) Founded by Gajula Lakshminarasu Chetty
(iii) Publisher of the first Telugu journal
(iv) Born after the arrest of Annie Besant
201.x: The Christian Association of Bellary published the first Telugu journal, the Krishna District Congress Association first met at Guntur, Gajula Lakshminarasu Chetty founded the Madras Native Association, and the Young Indian Association arose after Annie Besant's arrest, giving a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv.
201.tq: Recall one key fact about each association.
n: Madras Native Association was associated with Gajula Lakshminarasu Chetty. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 44-45]
Young Indian Association was formed after the arrest of Annie Besant. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 44-45]
Christian Association of Bellary published the first Telugu journal. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 44-45]
The first meeting of the Krishna District Congress Association was held in Guntur. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 44-45]
xs: The correct code is **a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv** — option **(4)**.
**Christian Association of Bellary** — published the **first Telugu journal** (**Satyadoota**); **Krishna District Congress Association** — first meeting at **Guntur**.
**Madras Native Association** — **Gajula Lakshminarasu Chetty**; **Young Indian Association** — after **Annie Besant**'s arrest.
xa: ⚠ Other notes give the first meeting at **Machilipatnam** (**APPSC 2012** key).
⚠ First Telugu journal = **Satyadoota**; first political magazine = **Andhra Prakasika**.
The Krishna conference was presided by **Nyapathi Subbarao** with ~**223** delegates.

202.s:
With reference to the partition of Bengal, consider the following statements:
1. Administrative convenience was given as its official justification.
2. One of its political effects was to make Bengalis a minority in their own province.
3. Its underlying objective was to strengthen Bengali nationalism by uniting Hindus and Muslims.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
202.x: Administrative convenience was the stated reason, while the actual policy sought to weaken Bengali nationalism and divide Hindus and Muslims. The third statement is therefore false.
202.tq: Separate the stated administrative justification from the political motive behind the measure.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the stated motive was **administrative convenience**.
Statement 2 is correct: in the rest of Bengal, **18 million** Bengalis were outnumbered by **36 million** Biharis and Oriyas.
Statement 3 is wrong: the real motive was to **divide Bengali Hindus from Muslims** and **weaken** Bengali nationalism — so option **(1)**, **1 and 2 only**, is correct.
xa: **H.H. Risley**: "Bengal united is a power; Bengal divided will pull in several different ways".
**Curzon**: "Bengal is the nerve centre of Indian nationalism".
The partition was annulled on **12 Dec 1911** at the **Delhi Durbar**.

202.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Moderate campaign against the partition of Bengal during 1903–1905?
o: It was led by Lord Curzon and relied mainly on official proclamations and military action.
It was led by Hardinge II and relied mainly on revolutionary violence and secret societies.
It was led by King George V and relied mainly on the boycott of constitutional institutions.
It was led by S.N. Banerjee, K.K. Mitra and Prithwishchandra Ray and relied mainly on petitions and meetings.
202.x: The Moderates’ campaign from 1903 to 1905 was associated with S.N. Banerjee, K.K. Mitra and Prithwishchandra Ray, and used petitions and meetings. The campaign failed to prevent the partition.
202.tq: Match the leaders with the characteristic constitutional methods rather than the later militant methods.
xs: The Moderate campaign (**1903-05**) was led by **S.N. Banerjee, K.K. Mitra and Prithwishchandra Ray** and used **petitions and meetings** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It **failed** to stop the partition.
**Curzon** made the partition; **Hardinge II** and **King George V** belong to its annulment in **1911**.
xa: **K.K. Mitra** first advocated boycott in **Sanjibani** (July 1905).
**S.N. Banerjee** and **A.M. Bose** raised **Rs 50,000** for funds.
The **Extremists** took control from **1906**.

202.s: On 16 October 1905, the day on which the partition of Bengal came into effect, which of the following combinations was associated with the popular protest?
o: Industrial strike, salt march, individual satyagraha and underground revolt
Day of mourning, hartal, bathing in the Ganga and Rakhi-bandhan
National education, constitutional reform, separate electorates and provincial autonomy
Day of celebration, military parade, temple entry and public feasting
202.x: The day was observed as a day of mourning and hartal; people took a bath in the Ganga and observed Rakhi-bandhan as a symbol of unity.
202.tq: Identify the cluster of contemporaneous protest rituals linked to the effective date.
xs: On **16 October 1905** people observed a **day of mourning, hartal, bathing in the Ganga and Rakhi-bandhan** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was also the day of the mass **Swadeshi vow**.
xa: The boycott resolution came earlier, on **7 Aug 1905**, at **Calcutta Town Hall**.
⚠ Trap: answer **7 Aug** for "launched/proclaimed"; **16 Oct** is when the partition took effect.
The partition was announced on **19/20 July 1905**.

202.s: The annulment of the partition of Bengal was announced at which event, and what important administrative change accompanied it?
o: The Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress in 1906; the capital was shifted from Delhi to Calcutta.
The Delhi Durbar of King George V in 1911; the capital was shifted from Calcutta to Delhi.
The Simla Conference of 1911; the capital was shifted from Delhi to Calcutta.
The Delhi Durbar of Edward VII in 1903; the capital was shifted from Calcutta to Bombay.
202.x: The partition was annulled on 12 December 1911 at the Delhi Durbar of King George V. The capital was simultaneously transferred from Calcutta to Delhi.
202.tq: Link the annulment event with its accompanying capital-transfer decision.
xs: The partition was annulled at the **Delhi Durbar of King George V** in **1911**, and the **capital moved from Calcutta to Delhi** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The date was **12 Dec 1911**; the Viceroy was **Hardinge II**.
The **1903** Durbar celebrated **Edward VII**'s coronation — not the annulment.
xa: ⚠ **1903** Durbar = Edward VII's coronation; **1911** Durbar = annulment (George V).
APPSC 2022 A-R: 1911 Durbar true; Edward VII's coronation is not its explanation.
**1916** brought the **Home Rule Leagues** and the **Lucknow Pact**.

202.s: Who described Bengal as “the nerve centre of Indian nationalism” in the context of the partition of Bengal?
202.x: Lord Curzon described Bengal as “the nerve centre of Indian nationalism,” reflecting the political significance he attached to the province.
202.tq: Discriminate between the Viceroy, the Home Secretary and the monarch associated with the episode.
xs: **Lord Curzon** called Bengal **"the nerve centre of Indian nationalism"** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**H.H. Risley** said "Bengal united is a power"; **King George V** and **Hardinge II** are linked to the **1911** annulment.
xa: Curzon announced the partition on **19/20 July 1905**.
Its real motive: divide **Hindus from Muslims**.
Eastern Bengal and Assam had **31 million** people.

202.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: King George V — Viceroy who announced the partition of Bengal
Lord Hardinge II — Viceroy at the time of annulment
H.H. Risley — “Bengal united is a power”
202.x: King George V was the monarch at whose Delhi Durbar the annulment was announced; he was not the Viceroy who announced the partition. Lord Curzon announced the partition, while Lord Hardinge II was Viceroy at the time of its annulment.
202.tq: Find the wrong authority by separating the monarch from the Viceroy who exercised executive authority.
xs: **King George V — Viceroy who announced the partition** is wrong — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Lord Curzon** announced the partition; **George V** was the King at whose **1911** Durbar it was annulled.
**Hardinge II** was Viceroy at the annulment; **Risley** said "Bengal united is a power".
xa: The annulment came on **12 Dec 1911**, with the capital moved to **Delhi**.
Risley was **Home Secretary**.
⚠ **1903** Durbar = Edward VII's coronation; **1911** Durbar = annulment.

202.s: Which event occurred on 7 August 1905?
o: The partition of Bengal was annulled and the capital shifted to Delhi
The partition of Bengal formally took effect as a day of mourning
The boycott resolution was passed at Calcutta Town Hall and Swadeshi was formally proclaimed
The National Council of Education was established
202.x: On 7 August 1905, the boycott resolution was passed at Calcutta Town Hall and Swadeshi was formally proclaimed.
202.tq: Distinguish the formal proclamation date from the later date on which the partition took effect.
xs: On **7 August 1905**, the **boycott resolution** was passed at **Calcutta Town Hall** and **Swadeshi was formally proclaimed** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The partition took effect on **16 Oct 1905**; the **National Council of Education** came on **15 Aug 1906**; the annulment on **12 Dec 1911**.
xa: ⚠ Trap: answer **7 Aug** for "launched/proclaimed".
**National Handloom Day** is observed on **7 August** (APPSC 2019).
**K.K. Mitra** had first advocated boycott in **Sanjibani** (July 1905).

202.s: National Handloom Day has been observed on 7 August since:
202.x: National Handloom Day has been observed on 7 August since 2015, commemorating the Swadeshi proclamation at Calcutta Town Hall.
202.tq: Separate the historical date commemorated from the modern year in which the observance began.
xs: **National Handloom Day** has been observed on **7 August** since **2015** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The date recalls the Swadeshi proclamation at **Calcutta Town Hall** on **7 Aug 1905** (APPSC 2019).
xa: The mass **Swadeshi vow** was taken on **16 Oct 1905**.
Handloom revival was part of Swadeshi, alongside **Mohini Mills**.
**Munagala Raja**'s textile unit at **Vijayawada** (**June 1906**) was the first in the Madras Presidency.

202.s: Which of the following was NOT a principal target of the boycott programme during the Swadeshi Movement?
202.x: The boycott targeted foreign cloth, salt and sugar; indigenous handloom products were encouraged through the Swadeshi programme.
202.tq: Find the option that reverses the central boycott–Swadeshi distinction.
xs: **Indigenous handloom products** were promoted, not boycotted — so option **(1)** is correct.
The boycott targeted **foreign cloth, salt and sugar**, with **bonfires** of cloth.
xa: Boycott extended to **courts, schools, government service**.
Priests refused rituals and marriages using **foreign goods**.
**Swadeshi / Atmashakti** stood for self-reliance.

202.s:
Consider the following statements about the Swadesh Bandhab Samiti:
1. It was led by Ashwini Kumar Dutt at Barisal.
2. It used magic-lantern shows, social work and arbitration courts.
3. It first advocated the boycott of foreign goods in Sanjibani in July 1905.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
202.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Samiti was Ashwini Kumar Dutt's, at Barisal. Statement 2 is correct: it used magic lanterns, social work and arbitration courts. Statement 3 is wrong: boycott was first advocated by K.K. (Krishna Kumar) Mitra in Sanjibani (July 1905). Hence '1 and 2 only'; the options with 3 are wrong.
202.tq: Barisal = Ashwini Kumar Dutt; Sanjibani = K.K. Mitra.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **Swadesh Bandhab Samiti** was **Ashwini Kumar Dutt**'s, at **Barisal**.
Statement 2 is correct: it used **magic lanterns**, **social work** and **arbitration courts**.
Statement 3 is wrong: boycott was first advocated by **K.K. Mitra** in **Sanjibani** — so option **(1)**, **1 and 2 only**, is correct.
xa: ⚠ Boycott first advocated = **K.K. Mitra**; funds raised = **S.N. Banerjee** + **A.M. Bose**.
Ashwini Kumar Dutt is listed among the **Bengal** Extremist leaders.
Mass mobilisation used **jatras**, **folk songs**, **melas** and **volunteer corps**.

202.s:
Which of the following formed part of the mass mobilisation methods of the Swadeshi Movement?
1. Jatras and folk songs
2. Melas and volunteer corps
3. Physical-training clubs, akharas and lathi clubs
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
202.x: Jatras, folk songs, melas, volunteer corps and physical-training institutions such as akharas and lathi clubs were all used for mobilisation.
202.tq: Treat each listed mobilisation method as an independent statement before choosing the complete combination.
xs: All three were mobilisation methods: **jatras and folk songs**, **melas and volunteer corps**, and **akharas and lathi clubs** — so option **(4)**, **1, 2 and 3**, is correct.
**Physical-training clubs** were part of mass mobilisation.
xa: **Samitis** like the **Swadesh Bandhab Samiti** used magic lanterns and arbitration courts.
**Tilak** started **Ganeshotsav** (**1893**) and the **Shivaji festival** (**1895**).
The movement is called the **first mass movement** (UPSC 2016).

202.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the transition in leadership during the Swadeshi Movement?
o: Leadership remained exclusively with the Moderates until 1911
Leadership passed from the Extremists to the Moderates in 1905
Leadership passed from the Moderates to the Extremists in 1906
Leadership passed directly from the Congress to the Muslim League in 1906
202.x: The leadership of the movement passed from the Moderates to the Extremists in 1906.
202.tq: Use the date and direction of transfer to avoid reversing the Moderate–Extremist relationship.
xs: Leadership **passed from the Moderates to the Extremists in 1906** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The Moderate phase was led by **S.N. Banerjea**, **K.K. Mitra** and **Prithwishchandra Ray**, using **petitions**.
xa: Extremist methods: **boycott**, **Swadeshi**, **national education**, **passive resistance**.
The **Surat Split** came in **Dec 1907**.
The movement faded by **1908** under repression and the Surat Split.

202.s: Who founded Bengal Chemicals during the Swadeshi Movement?
202.x: Bengal Chemicals was founded by Acharya P.C. Ray as a Swadeshi enterprise.
202.tq: Use the founder–enterprise association and distinguish it from leaders of the movement.
xs: **Bengal Chemicals** was founded by **Acharya P.C. Ray** — so option **(2)** is correct.

**V.O. Chidambaram Pillai** founded the **Swadeshi Steam Navigation Co.**; **Aurobindo Ghosh** was first principal of **Bengal National College**; **Ashwini Kumar Dutt** led the **Swadesh Bandhab Samiti**.
xa: P.C. Ray and **J.C. Bose** represented **Indian scientific achievement**.
**Banga Lakshmi Cotton Mills** came in **1906**.
Swadeshi banks: **Bank of India 1906**, **Indian Bank 1907**.

202.s: The Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company was associated with which of the following persons and places?
202.x: V.O. Chidambaram Pillai established the Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company at Tuticorin in 1906.
202.tq: Link the entrepreneur with both the enterprise and its regional centre.
xs: The **Swadeshi Steam Navigation Co.** was **V.O. Chidambaram Pillai**'s, at **Tuticorin** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was founded in **1906**.
**Munagala Raja** ran a textile unit at **Vijayawada**; **P.C. Ray** founded **Bengal Chemicals**; **Guneswara Rao** backed the **Bala Bharati Samiti**.
xa: Chidambaram Pillai led the movement in **Madras**.
The **Swarajya case** (**1908**) arose from an article praising Chidambaram Pillai.
Andhra youths were sent to **Japan** for industrial training.

202.s: Who was the first principal of Bengal National College?
202.x: Aurobindo Ghosh served as the first principal of Bengal National College.
202.tq: Distinguish an institutional office from general political leadership.
xs: **Aurobindo Ghosh** was the first principal of **Bengal National College** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**S.N. Banerjee** led the Moderates; **Bipin Chandra Pal** toured Andhra in **1907**.
xa: The **National Council of Education** came on **15 August 1906** (later **Jadavpur University**).
Aurobindo was tried in the **Alipore case**, acquitted, and retired to **Pondicherry**.
Aurobindo is linked with **Bande Mataram**.

202.s: The National Council of Education was established on:
202.x: The National Council of Education was established on 15 August 1906 and later became associated with Jadavpur University.
202.tq: Use the middle-date trap among the closely spaced Swadeshi milestones.
xs: The **National Council of Education** was set up on **15 August 1906** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It later became **Jadavpur University**.
**16 Oct 1905** = partition took effect; **7 Aug 1905** = Swadeshi proclaimed; **12 Dec 1911** = annulment.
xa: **Aurobindo Ghosh** was first principal of **Bengal National College**.
**National education** was one of the Extremist methods.
**Dec 1906**: **Muslim League** founded at **Dacca**; Calcutta INC adopted **Swaraj**.

202.s: Who wrote the song ‘Amar Sonar Bangla’, which later became the national anthem of Bangladesh?
202.x: Rabindranath Tagore wrote ‘Amar Sonar Bangla’, which later became Bangladesh’s national anthem.
202.tq: Separate the two Tagore-associated cultural contributions by matching the work with its creator.
xs: **Rabindranath Tagore** wrote **Amar Sonar Bangla**, now **Bangladesh's anthem** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Bankim Chandra Chatterjee** wrote **Bande Mataram**; **Abanindranath Tagore** painted **Bharat Mata**; **Chilakamarti** was a Telugu poet.
xa: ⚠ **Amar Sonar Bangla** = Tagore; **Bande Mataram** = Bankim (**Anandamath**).
Tagore also wrote **Jana Gana Mana**, India's anthem.
Tagore was profiled for his role in the **1905** movement (**10 Aug 2026**).

202.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
202.x: Bankim Chandra Chatterjee wrote ‘Bande Mataram’, which became the anthem of the Swadeshi movement. ‘Desher Katha’ was written by S.G. Deuskar.
202.tq: Use the author–work trap involving closely associated nationalist writers.
xs: **Bankim Chandra Chatterjee — Bande Mataram** is correctly matched — so option **(1)** is correct.
It came from **Anandamath** and became the movement's **anthem**.
**Desher Katha** is **S.G. Deuskar**'s; **Amar Sonar Bangla** is Tagore's; **Hindu Desa Daridryam** is **Attili Suryanarayana Rao**'s.
xa: **Nandalal Bose** is linked with **nationalist art**.
⚠ **Amar Sonar Bangla** = Tagore; **Bande Mataram** = Bankim.
Desher Katha warned of the British **"hypnotic conquest of the mind"** (UPSC 2020).

202.s: ‘Desher Katha’ was written by S.G. Deuskar primarily to warn Indians against:
o: the use of Indian languages in administration
the decline of Sanskrit education under the Mughals
the division of Bengal into linguistic provinces
the British ‘hypnotic conquest of the mind’
202.x: S.G. Deuskar’s ‘Desher Katha’ warned against the British ‘hypnotic conquest of the mind’.
202.tq: Read the distinctive phrase as the identifying clue for the work.
xs: **Desher Katha** warned against the British **'hypnotic conquest of the mind'** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It was written by **S.G. Deuskar** (UPSC 2020).
xa: **Abanindranath Tagore** painted **Bharat Mata** and broke with **Victorian naturalism**.
**Sumit Sarkar** wrote **The Swadeshi Movement in Bengal**.
Telugu: **Attili Suryanarayana Rao** wrote **Hindu Desa Daridryam**.

202.s: Who was described as the ‘First Telugu national poet’?
202.x: Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham was described as the ‘First Telugu national poet’.
202.tq: Use the distinctive title to identify the correct Telugu literary figure.
xs: **Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham** is called the **"First Telugu national poet"** (CDX) — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Dasu Narayana Rao** ran **"Jatiya Nataka Rangam"** theatre; **Attili Suryanarayana Rao** wrote **Hindu Desa Daridryam**; **C.Y. Chintamani** was a **Vizag** leader.
xa: Chilakamarti's poem **"Bharata khandambu chakkani paadi yaavu"** is tied to Pal's **Rajahmundry** visit.
Chilakamarti ran the paper **Desamata**.
He is listed as an Andhra leader at **Rajahmundry**.

202.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Hindu Desa Daridryam — Attili Suryanarayana Rao
Jatiya Nataka Rangam — Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham
Amar Sonar Bangla — Dasu Narayana Rao
202.x: ‘Hindu Desa Daridryam’ was associated with Attili Suryanarayana Rao. Dasu Narayana Rao was associated with the theatre work ‘Jatiya Nataka Rangam’.
202.tq: Begin with the sure author–title pair and reject swapped literary associations.
xs: **Hindu Desa Daridryam — Attili Suryanarayana Rao** is correctly matched — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Jatiya Nataka Rangam** was **Dasu Narayana Rao**'s; **Amar Sonar Bangla** was **Rabindranath Tagore**'s; **Bharat Mata** was **Abanindranath Tagore**'s.
xa: **Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham** = **"First Telugu national poet"**.
Andhra papers: **Krishna Patrika** (**1902**), **Swarajya**, **Desamata**, **Andhra Kesari**.
**Bande Mataram** came from Bankim's **Anandamath**.

202.s: Which one of the following regional associations is correctly matched?
o: Bengal — Aurobindo Ghosh, Bipin Chandra Pal and Ashwini Kumar Dutt
Punjab — V.O. Chidambaram Pillai and Ajit Singh
Madras — Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Syed Haider Raza
Delhi — Konda Venkatappayya and C.Y. Chintamani
202.x: Aurobindo Ghosh, Bipin Chandra Pal and Ashwini Kumar Dutt were associated with Bengal. The other options combine leaders from different regions.
202.tq: Start with the complete regional cluster and reject cross-regional substitutions.
xs: **Bengal — Aurobindo Ghosh, Bipin Chandra Pal and Ashwini Kumar Dutt** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
**V.O. Chidambaram Pillai** = **Madras**; **Tilak** = **Bombay / Poona**; **Syed Haider Raza** = **Delhi**.
**Konda Venkatappayya** (**Guntur**) and **C.Y. Chintamani** (**Vizag**) were Andhra leaders.
xa: APPSC 2023 match: Maharashtra – **Tilak**; Bengal – **B.C. Pal**; Punjab – **Lajpat Rai**.
Lajpat Rai = **"Punjab Kesari"**.
Andhra: **Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao** (**Vijayawada**), **Gadicherla** (**Bandar**).

202.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with Andhra?
202.x: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao was associated with Vijayawada. Gadicherla was associated with Bandar, Konda Venkatappayya with Guntur, and C.Y. Chintamani with Vizag.
202.tq: Use the place–leader pairs to catch the deliberate swapping of Andhra centres.
xs: **Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao — Vijayawada** is correctly matched — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Gadicherla** was at **Bandar**, **Konda Venkatappayya** at **Guntur**, **C.Y. Chintamani** at **Vizag**.
**Chilakamarti** was the **Rajahmundry** leader.
xa: Gadicherla was called **"Andhra Tilak"**.
Gadicherla ran **Swarajya**; Chilakamarti ran **Desamata**.
The Andhra phase ran **1905-1911**.

202.s: Bal Gangadhar Tilak was imprisoned for six years at which place?
202.x: Bal Gangadhar Tilak served a six-year imprisonment at Mandalay.
202.tq: Discriminate between the imprisonment and exile locations of extremist leaders.
xs: **Tilak** spent **6 years** in **Mandalay** — so option **(1)** is correct.
He was sent there in **1908**.
**Pondicherry** is where **Aurobindo** retired; **Alipore** was Aurobindo's case; the **Muslim League** was founded at **Dacca**.
xa: Tilak = **"Lokmanya"**; **Valentine Chirol** called him **"Father of Indian Unrest"**.
He ran **Kesari** and **Mahratta** (**1881**).
Slogan: **"Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it"**.

202.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Bipin Chandra Pal is correct?
o: He presided over the Surat session of 1907.
He was deported to the USA in 1907 and later retired to Pondicherry.
He undertook an Andhra tour in 1907 and was arrested.
He founded the Muslim League at Dacca in 1906.
202.x: Bipin Chandra Pal undertook an Andhra tour in 1907 and was subsequently arrested.
202.tq: Identify the correct leader–activity pair while rejecting swapped biographies.
xs: **Bipin Chandra Pal** made an **Andhra tour in 1907** and was **arrested** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Lajpat Rai** was **deported** in **1907** and later went to the **USA**; **Aurobindo** retired to **Pondicherry**.
The **Muslim League** was founded at **Dacca** in **Dec 1906**, not by Pal.
xa: The tour (**16-27 Apr 1907**) was arranged by **Mutnuri Krishna Rao** (**Krishna Patrika**).
At **Kakinada** he gave the line **"Swaraj the goal, boycott the weapon"**.
⚠ The APPSC 2025 key paired Pal's tour with **July 1907** — learn the key's pairing for that match.

202.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Extremist concept of Swaraj:
1. It meant complete freedom.
2. It meant colonial self-government within the British Empire.
3. Boycott, Swadeshi, national education and passive resistance were among its associated methods.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
202.x: Extremist Swaraj meant complete freedom, not colonial self-government. Boycott, Swadeshi, national education and passive resistance were its associated methods.
202.tq: Reject the reversed comparison between complete freedom and colonial self-government.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: Extremist **Swaraj** meant **complete freedom**.
Statement 2 is wrong: it was **not colonial self-government**.
Statement 3 is correct: methods were **boycott, Swadeshi, national education, passive resistance** — so option **(2)**, **1 and 3 only**, is correct.
xa: Tilak: **"Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it"**.
The **Calcutta 1906** INC under **Naoroji** adopted Swaraj.
⚠ **Banaras 1905** = Gokhale (Swadeshi); **Calcutta 1906** = Naoroji (Swaraj).

202.s: The British journalist Valentine Chirol called which leader the Father of Indian Unrest?
202.x: Chirol called Bal Gangadhar Tilak (Lokmanya, of Maharashtra) the Father of Indian Unrest. Pal led in Bengal, Lajpat Rai in Punjab (Punjab Kesari), and Aurobindo edited Bande Mataram.
202.tq: Chirol -> Tilak = Father of Indian Unrest
xs: **Valentine Chirol** called **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** the **"Father of Indian Unrest"** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Pal** led in Bengal; **Lajpat Rai** in Punjab; **Aurobindo** is linked with **Bande Mataram** and the **Alipore case**.
xa: Tilak = **"Lokmanya"**, of **Maharashtra**.
He spent **6 years** in **Mandalay**.
He was born **23 Jul 1856** at **Ratnagiri**.

202.s:
Consider the following statements about the Madras Beach students' meeting that marked the beginning of the Swadeshi movement in Andhra:
1. It was held in September 1905.
2. It was presided over by Mutnuri Krishna Rao.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
202.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Madras Beach students' meeting was held in September 1905. Statement 2 is wrong: it was presided over by G. Subramania Iyer; Mutnuri Krishna Rao (Krishna Patrika) arranged Bipin Chandra Pal's tour in 1907. Hence '1 only'; '2 only', 'Both' and 'Neither' are wrong.
202.tq: Madras Beach = Sep 1905 + G. Subramania Iyer; Mutnuri = Pal's tour.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **Madras Beach students' meeting** was held in **Sep 1905**.
Statement 2 is wrong: it was presided over by **G. Subramania Iyer**, not Mutnuri Krishna Rao — so option **(1)**, **1 only**, is correct.
**Mutnuri Krishna Rao** (**Krishna Patrika**) arranged **Pal's tour** in **1907**.
xa: The meeting featured **Subramania Bharati**'s songs.
The Andhra phase is placed in **1905-1911**.
S.N. Banerjee's arrest (**1906**) triggered protests with the slogan **"Vandemataram - Manade Rajyam"**.

202.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched regarding the Bala Bharati Samiti?
202.x: The Bala Bharati Samiti was formed at Rajahmundry in February 1907 by local youths and was supported by Karanam Guneswara Rao. Mutnuri Krishna Rao was associated with organising Bipin Chandra Pal’s tour.
202.tq: Use the wrong-person-with-the-deed trap to separate organisers of two related activities.
xs: **Mutnuri Krishna Rao — Founder** is wrong — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Bala Bharati Samiti** was founded at **Rajahmundry** in **Feb 1907** by youths such as **Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao**; **Karanam Guneswara Rao** backed it.
Mutnuri Krishna Rao arranged **Bipin Chandra Pal's tour**.
xa: Other founders: **Ganti Lakshmanna**, **Tanguturi Sriramulu**, **Kanchumarthi Ramachandra Rao**.
**Tanguturi Prakasam** was a member.
Guneswara Rao gave **Rs 1,000** at Rajahmundry for a national school.

202.s:
Consider the following statements about Bipin Chandra Pal's visit to Kakinada on 17 April 1907:
1. He delivered two lectures, on Vedanta and on Swaraj.
2. The lectures were presided over by Kompalle Hanumantha Rao.
3. The formulation "Swaraj the goal, boycott the weapon" is associated with this visit.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
202.x: Statement 1 is correct: Pal gave two lectures at Kakinada, on Vedanta and Swaraj. Statement 2 is wrong: the Kakinada lectures were presided over by Kattiventi Perraju; Kompalle Hanumantha Rao was the host at Machilipatnam. Statement 3 is correct: 'Swaraj the goal, boycott the weapon' is tied to Kakinada. So '1 and 3 only'; the options containing 2 are wrong.
202.tq: Kakinada = Perraju presides; Machilipatnam = Kompalle hosts.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: at **Kakinada** Pal gave **two lectures**, on **Vedanta** and **Swaraj**.
Statement 2 is wrong: they were presided by **Kattiventi Perraju**; **Kompalle Hanumantha Rao** hosted Pal at **Machilipatnam**.
Statement 3 is correct: **"Swaraj the goal, boycott the weapon"** is tied to Kakinada — so option **(2)**, **1 and 3 only**, is correct.
xa: At **Vizianagaram** and **Visakhapatnam** (**16 Apr**) the response was poor.
At **Rajahmundry** (**19-24 Apr**) he gave **five lectures**.
The tour was arranged by **Mutnuri Krishna Rao**.

202.s:
Which of the following events occurred during Bipin Chandra Pal’s visit to Rajahmundry?

1. Five lectures were delivered.
2. Godavari Swadeshi Stores was opened.
3. A contribution of Rs 1,000 was made for a national school.
4. Chilakamarti’s poem “Bharata khandambu chakkani paadi yaavu” was associated with the visit.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
202.x: All four events were associated with Pal’s Rajahmundry visit from 19 to 24 April 1907.
202.tq: Test several details belonging to one event cluster through a complete coded combination.
xs: All four happened at **Rajahmundry** (**19-24 Apr**) — so option **(4)**, **1, 2, 3 and 4**, is correct.
Pal gave **five lectures** and opened the **Godavari Swadeshi Stores**.
**Guneswara Rao** gave **Rs 1,000** for a national school; **Chilakamarti**'s poem **"Bharata khandambu chakkani paadi yaavu"** marked the visit.
xa: Rajahmundry host: **Young Men's Association** (APPSC 2017 key), vs **Bala Bharati Samiti** in other notes.
The next stop was **Machilipatnam** (**27 Apr**).
Kakinada lectures were presided by **Kattiventi Perraju**.

202.s: Which development was associated with Bipin Chandra Pal’s visit to Machilipatnam on 27 April 1907?
o: Formation of the Swadeshi League and Industrial Association
Formation of the Young Men’s Swarajya Samithi and foundation of a national college
Establishment of the Bala Bharati Samiti
Opening of the Godavari Swadeshi Stores
202.x: The Young Men’s Swarajya Samithi was formed and the foundation for a national college was laid at Machilipatnam during Pal’s visit.
202.tq: Match the final stop of a tour with the institutional developments recorded there.
xs: At **Machilipatnam** (**27 Apr**) the **Young Men's Swarajya Samithi** was formed and the foundation of a **national college** was laid — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **Godavari Swadeshi Stores** was opened at **Rajahmundry**; the **Bala Bharati Samiti** was formed at Rajahmundry in **Feb 1907**.
xa: Host: **Kompalle Hanumantha Rao** (APPSC 2008 key); some notes say **Ramadasu Naidu**.
The tour ran **16-27 Apr 1907**.
Tour arranged by **Mutnuri Krishna Rao** of **Krishna Patrika**.

202.s: The textile unit established by Munagala Raja at Vijayawada in June 1906 was significant because it was:
o: the first handloom centre established after 1911
the first such unit in the Madras Presidency
the first national college in the Madras Presidency
the first Swadeshi bank in Andhra
202.x: Munagala Raja’s textile unit at Vijayawada, established in June 1906, was the first of its kind in the Madras Presidency.
202.tq: Identify the significance attached to a precise date, place and institution.
xs: **Munagala Raja**'s textile unit at **Vijayawada** (**June 1906**) was **the first such unit in the Madras Presidency** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was part of the Swadeshi revival of **handlooms** and industry.
xa: Japan's influence: Munagala Raja named his sons **Togo** and **Nogi**.
Andhra youths went to **Japan** for training: **Malladi Venkata Subbarao** (pencils), **S. Ramarao** (glass and clocks).
**Banga Lakshmi Cotton Mills** also date from **1906**.

202.s: In Andhra, protests at Rajahmundry, Kakinada, Vizianagaram and Gooty, with the slogan Vandemataram - Manade Rajyam, were triggered by
o: the arrest of S.N. Banerjee in 1906
the annulment of the partition of Bengal in 1911
the formation of the Bala Bharati Samiti in 1907
the Madras Beach students' meeting of 1905
202.x: S.N. Banerjee's arrest in 1906 set off protests at Rajahmundry, Kakinada, Vizianagaram and Gooty under the slogan 'Vandemataram - Manade Rajyam'. The Madras Beach meeting (Sep 1905) began the movement, the Bala Bharati Samiti came in Feb 1907, and the partition was annulled in 1911.
202.tq: Trigger in Andhra = S.N. Banerjee's arrest, 1906
xs: The protests were triggered by **the arrest of S.N. Banerjee in 1906** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The slogan was **"Vandemataram - Manade Rajyam"**.
The **Madras Beach** meeting (**Sep 1905**) began the movement; the **Bala Bharati Samiti** came in **Feb 1907**; the annulment in **1911**.
xa: The Madras Beach meeting was presided over by **G. Subramania Iyer**.
The Andhra phase: **1905-1911**.

202.s:
Consider the following statements about the Rajahmundry College incident of 1907:
1. Principal Mark Hunter banned Vandemataram badges for Government College students.
2. 138 of 222 students were suspended.
3. Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao was expelled but was later allowed to enter government service.
4. It marked the start of student participation in the movement in Andhra.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
202.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct: Mark Hunter banned Vandemataram badges, 138 of 222 students were suspended, and the incident began student participation in Andhra. Statement 3 is wrong: Gadicherla was expelled and barred from government jobs. Hence '1, 2 and 4 only'; '1 and 2 only' omits 4, and the options with 3 are wrong.
202.tq: Gadicherla was expelled AND barred from government jobs.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Principal **Mark Hunter** banned **Vandemataram badges**; **138 of 222** students were suspended.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Gadicherla** was expelled and **barred from government jobs**.
Statement 4 is correct: it marked the **start of student participation** in Andhra — so option **(2)**, **1, 2 and 4 only**, is correct.
xa: The ban dates from **19 Mar 1907**.
**J. Ramachandra Rao** defied the ban with Gadicherla.
Gadicherla was later arrested in the **Swarajya case** (**18 July 1908**).

202.s: The first criminal case of the Swadeshi movement in Andhra arose from the:
202.x: The Kakinada Riot Case of 31 May 1907 was described as the first criminal case of the movement in Andhra.
202.tq: Use the distinction between connected incidents to identify the first legal case.
xs: The **Kakinada Riot Case** (**31 May 1907**) was the **first criminal case** of the movement in Andhra — so option **(3)** is correct (APPSC 2019 key).
**Dr Kemp** beat the boy **Kompelli Krishna Rao** for shouting Vande Mataram → the **European Club** was attacked.
The **Rajahmundry College** incident began **student participation**; **Kotappakonda** and **Tenali** came in **1909**.
xa: The defence was led by **Nyapati Subbarao**.
The **Swarajya case** produced the first **Telugu political prisoners**.
**Chinnappa Reddy** (Kotappakonda) got the **only death sentence** in India during the movement.

202.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Kakinada Riot Case of 31 May 1907?
o: A police clash occurred during Shivaratri celebrations near Narasaraopet.
Students were suspended for wearing Vandemataram badges at Rajahmundry College.
A bomb was thrown at the Howrah Express and Chukkapalli Ramayya was arrested.
A European club was attacked after Dr Kemp beat Kompelli Krishna Rao for shouting Vande Mataram.
202.x: The Kakinada case followed the assault of Kompelli Krishna Rao by Dr Kemp after the boy shouted Vande Mataram, after which the European Club was attacked.
202.tq: Separate similar incidents by matching the place, date and immediate trigger.
xs: In the **Kakinada Riot Case** (**31 May 1907**) the **European Club was attacked** after **Dr Kemp** beat **Kompelli Krishna Rao** for shouting Vande Mataram — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **Shivaratri** clash near **Narasaraopet** was **Kotappakonda**; the badge ban was the **Rajahmundry College** incident; the Howrah express bomb was the **Tenali Bomb Case**.
xa: It was the **first criminal case** of the movement in Andhra (APPSC 2019 key).
**Nyapati Subbarao** defended the accused.
⚠ The APPSC 2025 key paired the Kakinada riots case with **April 1907** — learn the key's pairing for that match.

202.s:
Consider the following statements about the Swarajya case:
1. Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao and Bodi Narayana Rao were arrested on 18 July 1908 for an article praising Chidambaram Pillai.
2. They were the first Telugu political prisoners.
3. Gadicherla came to be known as "Andhra Kesari".
Which of the statements given above are correct?
202.x: Statement 1 is correct: both were arrested on 18 July 1908 for an article praising Chidambaram Pillai. Statement 2 is correct: they were the first Telugu political prisoners. Statement 3 is wrong: Gadicherla was called 'Andhra Tilak', not 'Andhra Kesari'. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses 2 and the options with 3 are wrong.
202.tq: Gadicherla = Andhra Tilak; first Telugu political prisoners, 1908.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Gadicherla** and **Bodi Narayana Rao** were arrested on **18 July 1908** for an article praising **Chidambaram Pillai**.
Statement 2 is correct: they were the **first Telugu political prisoners**.
Statement 3 is wrong: Gadicherla was called **"Andhra Tilak"** — so option **(2)**, **1 and 2 only**, is correct.
xa: Gadicherla ran the paper **Swarajya**.
He had earlier been expelled after the **Rajahmundry College incident** (**1907**) and barred from government jobs.
**Andhra Kesari** is listed as a separate Andhra paper.

202.s: Which statement regarding the Kotappakonda incident is correct?
o: It occurred at Rajahmundry and Gadicherla was expelled.
It occurred near Machilipatnam and resulted in the arrest of Chukkapalli Ramayya.
It occurred near Narasaraopet and Chinnappa Reddy was hanged.
It occurred at Kakinada and Nyapati Subbarao defended the accused.
202.x: The Kotappakonda police clash occurred near Narasaraopet; Chinnappa Reddy was hanged and the incident was associated with the only death sentence in India during the movement.
202.tq: Match the place, person and consequence to distinguish neighbouring cases.
xs: **Kotappakonda** occurred **near Narasaraopet** and **Chinnappa Reddy was hanged** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The police clash came on **18 Feb 1909**, at **Shivaratri**.
Gadicherla's expulsion was at **Rajahmundry**; **Chukkapalli Ramayya** was in the **Tenali** case; **Nyapati Subbarao** defended the **Kakinada** accused.
xa: Chinnappa Reddy's was the **only death sentence** in India during the movement.
The **Tenali Bomb Case** followed on **6 Apr 1909**.
The Andhra phase ran **1905-1911**.

202.s:
Consider the following statements about the Tenali Bomb Case (6 April 1909):
1. The bomb was aimed at the Howrah express.
2. The accused were defended by Nyapati Subbarao.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
202.x: Statement 1 is correct: the bomb was aimed at the Howrah express. Statement 2 is wrong: the accused (Chukkapalli Ramayya and others) were defended by Prakasam; Nyapati Subbarao defended the accused in the Kakinada Riot Case. Hence '1 only'.
202.tq: Tenali = Prakasam; Kakinada riot = Nyapati Subbarao.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **Tenali** bomb was aimed at the **Howrah express**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the accused were defended by **Prakasam** — so option **(1)**, **1 only**, is correct.
**Nyapati Subbarao** defended the accused in the **Kakinada Riot Case**.
xa: **Chukkapalli Ramayya** and others were accused.
**Prakasam** was a member of the **Bala Bharati Samiti**.
**Kotappakonda** (**18 Feb 1909**) came shortly before.

202.s:
Consider the following statements about the Vandemataram movement at Osmania University:
1. It took place in 1938, when students were expelled for singing Vande Mataram in the hostels.
2. P.V. Narasimha Rao was among the students involved.
3. The students were punished for wearing Vandemataram badges, as at Rajahmundry.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
202.x: Statement 1 is correct: in 1938 students were expelled for singing Vande Mataram in hostels. Statement 2 is correct: P.V. Narasimha Rao was among them. Statement 3 is wrong: the badge ban belongs to the Rajahmundry College incident of 1907, not Osmania. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
202.tq: Osmania 1938 = singing in hostels, PVNR; Rajahmundry 1907 = badges.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: in **1938** students were expelled for singing **Vande Mataram** in **Osmania University** hostels.
Statement 2 is correct: **P.V. Narasimha Rao** was among them.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **badge** ban belongs to the **Rajahmundry College** incident (**1907**) — so option **(2)**, **1 and 2 only**, is correct.
xa: At Rajahmundry, Principal **Mark Hunter** suspended **138 of 222** students.
The Rajahmundry incident marked the **start of student participation** in Andhra.
Osmania 1938 is a **later echo** of the Vandemataram movement.

202.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. National Council of Education was established
B. Partition of Bengal took effect
C. Boycott resolution at Calcutta Town Hall
D. Partition of Bengal was annulled
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
202.x: The sequence is 7 August 1905, 16 October 1905, 15 August 1906 and 12 December 1911.
202.tq: Fix the earliest and latest dates first, then place the two 1905 events correctly.
xs: The order is **C, B, A, D** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Boycott resolution** **7 Aug 1905** → partition took effect **16 Oct 1905** → **National Council of Education** **15 Aug 1906** → annulment **12 Dec 1911**.
xa: The partition was announced on **19/20 Jul 1905**.
**Dec 1905**: the **Banaras** INC under **Gokhale** backed Swadeshi.
**Dec 1907**: the **Surat Split**.

202.s: Which of the following correctly describes the events of December 1906?
o: The National Council of Education was established and Home Rule Leagues began
The Surat Split occurred and Tilak was sent to Mandalay
The partition took effect and the Swadeshi vow was taken
The Muslim League was formed at Dacca and the Calcutta Congress adopted Swaraj
202.x: In December 1906, the Muslim League was formed at Dacca and the Calcutta Congress under Dadabhai Naoroji adopted Swaraj.
202.tq: Pair events sharing the same month while rejecting events from neighbouring years.
xs: In **Dec 1906** the **Muslim League** was formed at **Dacca** and the **Calcutta Congress** adopted **Swaraj** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The Calcutta session was presided over by **Naoroji**.
The **National Council of Education** was **15 Aug 1906**; **Home Rule Leagues** **1916**; **Surat Split** **Dec 1907**; Tilak to **Mandalay** **1908**.
xa: ⚠ **Banaras 1905** = Gokhale (Swadeshi); **Calcutta 1906** = Naoroji (Swaraj).
**1908** also saw the **Muzaffarpur bomb**, the **Alipore case** and the **Newspapers Act**.
The partition took effect on **16 Oct 1905**.

202.s: Which of the following newspapers was associated with Chilakamarti during the Swadeshi movement in Andhra?
202.x: Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham edited Desamata at Rajahmundry. Swarajya was Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao's paper and Krishna Patrika was Mutnuri Krishna Rao's, so neither was Chilakamarti's.
202.tq: Discriminate among closely related nationalist newspapers by their associated personalities.
xs: **Chilakamarti** was associated with **Desamata** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Swarajya** was **Gadicherla**'s; **Krishna Patrika** (**1902**) was the paper of **Mutnuri Krishna Rao**, who arranged Pal's tour.
xa: Chilakamarti is called the **"First Telugu national poet"** (CDX).
He is the **Rajahmundry** leader in the Andhra list.
His poem **"Bharata khandambu chakkani paadi yaavu"** is tied to Pal's Rajahmundry visit.

202.s: According to the historical interpretation associated with Sumit Sarkar’s work, which of the following helped intensify anger against the partition of Bengal?
o: The formation of the Muslim League in 1909
202.x: Japan’s victory over Russia in 1904–05 inspired Asian and Indian nationalist sentiment and contributed to anger against the partition.
202.tq: Reject the reversed comparison in a cause-and-effect statement.

Option (1) reverses the winner; the **Lucknow** reunion came in **1916**; the **Muslim League** was formed in **1906**, not **1909**.
xa: Japan's influence in Andhra: **Munagala Raja** named his sons **Togo** and **Nogi**.
Andhra youths went to **Japan** for industrial training.
Sarkar used **plays, novels and pamphlets** as sources.

o: Munagala Raja — named his sons Togo and Nogi
Adipudi Somanatha Rao — named his sons Togo and Nogi
Adipudi Somanatha Rao — presided over the Surat session
202.x: Munagala Raja named his sons Togo and Nogi, reflecting the influence of Japan’s victory over Russia. Adipudi Somanatha Rao wrote Japan Charitra.

xs: **Munagala Raja — named his sons Togo and Nogi** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.

202.s:
Which of the following statements best describes the historical significance of the Swadeshi movement of 1905?
1. It was regarded as the first mass movement.
2. It marked the birth of mass nationalism.
3. It introduced boycott and Swadeshi as important methods of struggle.
4. It introduced national education as a method of nationalist mobilisation.
Select the correct answer.
202.x: The movement was regarded as the first mass movement, fostered mass nationalism and popularised boycott, Swadeshi and national education as methods of struggle.
202.tq: Use the complete significance cluster rather than selecting only one feature.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: it was the **first mass movement**.
Statement 2 is correct: it marked the **birth of mass nationalism** (UPSC 2016).
Statements 3 and 4 are correct: it gave **boycott**, **Swadeshi** and **national education** as methods — so option **(4)**, **1, 2, 3 and 4**, is correct.
xa: Its limits: **limited peasant and Muslim participation**.
It faded by **1908** under **repression** and the **Surat Split**.
The **National Council of Education** came on **15 Aug 1906**.

202.s: Which one of the following was a major limitation of the Swadeshi movement?
o: It continued unaffected by repression after 1908.
It rejected all forms of national education.
It had no support among intellectuals or urban groups.
It received limited participation from peasants and Muslims.
202.x: Peasant and Muslim participation in the movement was limited. The movement also faded by 1908 under repression and after the Surat Split.
202.tq: Find the accurately stated limitation while rejecting extreme generalisations.
xs: The movement had **limited participation from peasants and Muslims** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It did not continue unaffected — it **faded by 1908**; and it **promoted** national education.
xa: It is still called the **first mass movement** (UPSC 2016).
The **Muslim League** was formed at **Dacca** in **Dec 1906**.
The **real motive** of partition was to divide **Bengali Hindus from Muslims**.

202.s: What was the principal feature of the Swadeshi and Boycott movement during the period of the Partition of Bengal?
o: Boycott foreign goods and promote indigenous goods and national education
Accept the Nehru Report and begin a mass movement
Adopt Complete Independence as the Congress goal
Draft a constitutional framework for India
202.x: The Swadeshi and Boycott movement against the 1905 Partition of Bengal boycotted foreign goods and promoted Indian goods and national education. Complete Independence and the Nehru Report came in the late 1920s.
202.tq: Link the movement to the Partition of Bengal.
n: The Swadeshi and Boycott movement occurred during the period of the Partition of Bengal. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #111 · pp 205-207]
The Swadeshi and Boycott movement was associated with the Congress and the nationalist movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #111 · pp 205-207]
The Swadeshi and Boycott movement promoted the boycott of foreign goods. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #111 · pp 205-207]
The Swadeshi and Boycott movement promoted indigenous goods. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #111 · pp 205-207]
The Swadeshi and Boycott movement promoted national education. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #111 · pp 205-207]
xs: The movement's feature was to **boycott foreign goods** and **promote indigenous goods** and **national education** — option **(1)**.
It occurred during the **Partition** of **Bengal**, which nationalists saw as **"Divide and Rule"**.
Boycott covered **foreign cloth**, **salt** and **sugar**, with **bonfires** of cloth, extending to courts, schools and government service.
xa: Formal proclamation: **7 Aug 1905**, boycott resolution at **Calcutta Town Hall**.
**National Council of Education**: **15 August 1906** (later **Jadavpur University**).
**National Handloom Day** is **7 August**, observed since **2015**.

202.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Partition of Bengal was announced in 1905.
The partition became effective on 15 October 1905.
Lord Curzon was the Viceroy associated with the partition.
202.x: Option B is incorrect: the Partition of Bengal took effect on 16 October 1905, not 15 October. It was announced in 1905 under Lord Curzon and annulled in 1911.
202.tq: Check the exact date in each statement.
n: The Partition of Bengal was announced in 1905. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #128 · pp 231-232]
Lord Curzon was the Viceroy during the Partition of Bengal. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #128 · pp 231-232]
The Partition of Bengal became effective on 16 October 1905. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #128 · pp 231-232]
The Partition of Bengal was annulled in 1911. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #128 · pp 231-232]
xs: The incorrect statement is that the partition took effect on **15 October 1905** — option **(2)**.
It became effective on **16 October 1905** — a day of mourning, hartal, Ganga bath and **Rakhi-bandhan**.
It was announced in **1905** by **Viceroy Lord Curzon** and **annulled** in **1911**.
xa: Announcement: **19/20 July 1905**.
Annulled on **12 Dec 1911** at the **Delhi Durbar** of **King George V** (Viceroy **Hardinge II**).
⚠ **1903** Durbar = Edward VII's coronation; **1911** Durbar = annulment.

**Western Bengal** — capital **Calcutta**; capital after **1911** — **Delhi**.

202.s:

202.x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Swaraj was the general Extremist aim, but that does not explain why Tilak in particular gave the slogan "Swaraj is my birthright".
202.tq: Check whether R is the cause of A.
n: The main objective of the Extremists was Swaraj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Bal Gangadhar Tilak gave the Swaraj slogan, “Swaraj is my birthright…”. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Bal Gangadhar Tilak was associated with Swaraj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]

xa: Tilak published **Kesari** and **Mahratta** (**1881**) and wrote **Gita Rahasya**.

Pal's line in Andhra: **"Swaraj the goal, boycott the weapon"**.
