204.s: Which one of the following leaders belonged to the militant (Extremist) school of nationalism?
204.x: Tilak was the militant leader (APPSC-GS 2018 key). Ranade, Gokhale and G.V. Joshi were Moderates - the trap is to mark any of them as militant.
204.tq: Militant = Tilak; Ranade, Gokhale, Joshi = Moderates
xs: **B.G. Tilak** belonged to the militant (Extremist) school — so option **(4)** is correct (APPSC-GS 2018).
⚠ Trap: **Ranade**, **Gokhale** and **G.V. Joshi** were **not** militant.
xa: Other Extremists: **Lajpat Rai**, **Pal**, **Aurobindo**.
The Extremist phase is dated **1905-1916**.
Tilak led the Extremists at **Surat 1907** against **Gokhale**.

204.s: Which one of the following was NOT a method associated with extremist nationalism?
204.x: The Extremists had no faith in British generosity. Their methods included passive resistance, mass agitation, boycott, Swadeshi, national education and self-sacrifice.
204.tq: Find the option that contradicts the underlying political attitude.
xs: **Dependence on British generosity** was not an Extremist method — they had **no faith in British generosity** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Their methods: **passive resistance**, **mass agitation**, **boycott**, **Swadeshi**, **national education**, **self-sacrifice**.
xa: Self-reliance (**Atmashakti**) meant constructive work such as **cooperatives**.
The Moderates had **faith in British justice**.
⚠ **3 Ps** = Moderates; **3 Ss** = Extremists.

204.s: The concept of spiritual nationalism viewed the nation primarily as:
204.x: Spiritual nationalism represented the nation as a mother goddess, an idea expressed through symbols such as Bande Mataram and Bhavani Mandir.
204.tq: Identify the defining symbol of an ideological concept.
xs: **Spiritual nationalism** saw the nation as **a mother goddess** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Its symbols were **Bande Mataram** and **Bhavani Mandir**.
xa: It used **Hindu festivals** for mass contact and took **pride in India's past**.
**Bhavani Mandir** was written by **Aurobindo**.
Criticism: religious symbolism **alienated Muslims**.

204.s: Atmashakti, in the context of extremist ideology, referred to:
204.x: Atmashakti meant self-reliance. It was connected with constructive work such as the establishment of cooperatives.
204.tq: Match the indigenous term with its precise ideological meaning.
xs: **Atmashakti** meant **self-reliance** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was expressed through constructive work such as **cooperatives**.
xa: The Extremists' **3 Ss**: **self-reliance, self-sacrifice, strong will**.
Other methods: **boycott**, **Swadeshi**, **national education**.
Extremist base: **students, women, workers, peasants**.

204.s: Which one of the following pairs of public festivals and years is correctly matched with Tilak?
204.x: Tilak transformed Ganesh Utsav into a public festival in 1893 and Shivaji Jayanti in 1895.
204.tq: Keep the two similar festival dates in their correct sequence.
xs: **Ganesh Utsav — 1893**; **Shivaji Jayanti — 1895** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Option (2) swaps the years.
xa: Extremists used **Hindu festivals** for mass contact.
Tilak's papers **Kesari** and **Mahratta** began in **1881**.
Tilak joined the INC in **1890**.

204.s: Which one of the following correctly represents Tilak’s sedition-trial and imprisonment sequence?
204.x: Tilak received 18 months in the 1897 sedition trial, six years in Mandalay in 1908, and was acquitted in the 1916 case.
204.tq: Match each year with the correct legal consequence and punishment.
xs: Tilak's sequence: **1897** — **18 months**; **1908** — **6 years in Mandalay**; **1916** — **acquitted** — so option **(1)** is correct.
He was released on **16 June 1914**.
xa: In Mandalay he wrote **Gita Rahasya**.
⚠ Abroad: Lajpat Rai = **USA**; Pal = **England**; Aurobindo = **Pondicherry**; Tilak = **Mandalay**.
The **Newspapers Act 1908** came the same year as his jailing.

204.s: Which of the following statements about Tilak’s political career is correct?
o: He joined the Indian National Congress in 1890 and founded the Home Rule League on 28 April 1916.
He joined the Congress in 1905 and founded the Home Rule League in 1914.
He joined the Congress in 1885 and founded the Home Rule League in September 1916.
He joined the Congress in 1897 and founded the Home Rule League in December 1916.
204.x: Tilak joined the Congress in 1890 and founded his Home Rule League on 28 April 1916.
204.tq: Pair two dates from the same leader’s political career and reject shifted years.
xs: Tilak **joined the INC in 1890** and founded the **Home Rule League on 28 April 1916** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Besant**'s League came in **Sept 1916**; the **Lucknow Pact** in **Dec 1916**.
xa: President of Tilak's League: **Joseph Baptista**; secretary **N.C. Kelkar**.
**52** Home Rule branches existed in Andhra by **1917**.
Tilak was released from Mandalay on **16 June 1914**.

204.s:
Consider the following statements about Lala Lajpat Rai:
1. He went to the USA after 1908 and set up the Indian Home Rule League of America in 1917.
2. He wrote biographies of Mazzini, Garibaldi and Shivaji.
3. The book Unhappy India was written by Bipin Chandra Pal, not by him.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
204.x: Statement 1 is correct: Lajpat Rai went to the USA after 1908 and founded the Indian Home Rule League of America (1917). Statement 2 is correct: he wrote biographies of Mazzini, Garibaldi and Shivaji. Statement 3 is wrong: Unhappy India is Lajpat Rai's own work; Pal wrote The Soul of India. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
204.tq: Lajpat Rai: USA, Mazzini-Garibaldi-Shivaji, Unhappy India.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Lajpat Rai** went to the **USA** after **1908** and set up the **Indian Home Rule League of America** (**1917**).
Statement 2 is correct: he wrote biographies of **Mazzini**, **Garibaldi** and **Shivaji**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Unhappy India** is Lajpat Rai's own; **Pal** wrote **The Soul of India** — so option **(2)**, **1 and 2 only**, is correct.
xa: Lajpat Rai (**1865-1928**) was an **Arya Samaj** leader.
He also wrote **Young India** and ran **The Punjabee**.
He died after the **lathi-charge** during the **Simon Commission** protest (**1928**).

204.s:
Consider the following statements about Aurobindo:
1. He was acquitted in the Alipore case in 1909.
2. He retired to Pondicherry in 1910.
3. His retirement to Pondicherry preceded the Alipore case.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
204.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because Aurobindo retired to Pondicherry in 1910, after his acquittal in the Alipore case in 1909.
204.tq: Check the sequence of the legal case and subsequent retirement.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Aurobindo** was **acquitted** in the **Alipore case** in **1909**.
Statement 2 is correct: he retired to **Pondicherry** in **1910**.
Statement 3 is wrong: Pondicherry came **after** the acquittal — so option **(1)**, **1 and 2 only**, is correct.
xa: Aurobindo was the **first principal** of **Bengal National College**.
**By 1910**: Tilak jailed, Aurobindo retired, Pal arrested, Lajpat Rai left → **Moderates dominated**.
His works: **Savitri**, **The Divine Life**, **Bhavani Mandir**.

204.s: Which one of the following newspapers was published by Bal Gangadhar Tilak in Marathi?
204.x: Tilak published Kesari in Marathi and Mahratta in English; both newspapers began in 1881.
204.tq: Distinguish paired newspapers by language and leader.
xs: Tilak's **Marathi** paper was **Kesari** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Mahratta** was his **English** paper; both began in **1881**.
**New India** was **Pal**'s / **Besant**'s; **Bande Mataram** was **Pal** and **Aurobindo**'s.
xa: Tilak wrote **Gita Rahasya** and **The Arctic Home in the Vedas**.
His slogan: **"Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it"**.
The PM's tribute (**23 Jul 2026**) recalled Tilak.

204.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Bipin Chandra Pal — The Arctic Home in the Vedas
204.x: Lala Lajpat Rai was associated with The Punjabee. The Arctic Home in the Vedas was written by Tilak, Unhappy India by Lajpat Rai and The Soul of India by Pal.
204.tq: Avoid the swapped-author trap among books and newspapers.
xs: **Lala Lajpat Rai — The Punjabee** is correctly matched — so option **(1)** is correct.
**The Arctic Home in the Vedas** is **Tilak**'s; **Unhappy India** is **Lajpat Rai**'s; **The Soul of India** is **Pal**'s.
xa: Lajpat Rai also wrote **Young India**.
**Aurobindo** wrote **New Lamps for Old**.
Lajpat Rai's slogan: **"Go back Simon"**.

204.s: Which of the following statements about extremist newspapers and writings is correct?
o: Annie Besant edited Mahratta and wrote Gita Rahasya.
Aurobindo Ghosh edited Bande Mataram and wrote New Lamps for Old.
Lajpat Rai edited Kesari and wrote Bhavani Mandir.
Tilak edited Bande Mataram and wrote Unhappy India.
204.x: Aurobindo Ghosh was the editor of Bande Mataram and wrote New Lamps for Old. The other options interchange the works or newspapers of different leaders.
204.tq: Use the author-editor association and reject swapped names.
xs: **Aurobindo Ghosh** edited **Bande Mataram** and wrote **New Lamps for Old** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Mahratta**, **Kesari** and **Gita Rahasya** are **Tilak**'s; **Unhappy India** is **Lajpat Rai**'s; **Bhavani Mandir** is **Aurobindo**'s.
xa: **New Lamps for Old** (**1893-94**) appeared in **Indu Prakash** (some notes say **Bangadarshan**).
Aurobindo also wrote **Savitri** and **The Divine Life**.
**Besant** ran **New India** and **Commonweal**.

204.s: Who co-edited Bande Mataram with Aurobindo Ghosh according to the standard association?
204.x: Bipin Chandra Pal is commonly identified with Aurobindo Ghosh as a co-editor of Bande Mataram.
204.tq: Test the standard collaborator rather than a leader from the same movement.
xs: **Bipin Chandra Pal** co-edited **Bande Mataram** with **Aurobindo** — so option **(2)** is correct.
That is the standard answer; UPSC adds **"and Tilak"**.
xa: Pal was arrested (**1907**) for refusing to testify in the **Bande Mataram case**.
Pal also started **New India** (**1901**).
**Besant** ran a separate **New India** — the renamed **Madras Standard**.

204.s: Which one of the following slogans is associated with Lala Lajpat Rai?
o: Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it
204.x: Lala Lajpat Rai is associated with the slogan ‘Go back Simon’. Tilak’s slogan was ‘Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it’.
204.tq: Separate slogans of closely associated Extremist leaders.
xs: **"Go back Simon"** is linked with **Lala Lajpat Rai** — so option **(2)** is correct (APPSC-GS 2018).
**"Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it"** was **Tilak**'s slogan.
xa: Lajpat Rai died after the **lathi-charge** during the **Simon Commission** protest (**1928**).
He is called **Punjab Kesari / Lion of Punjab**.
He ran **The Punjabee**.

204.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Gita Rahasya — written by Tilak in Mandalay
The Soul of India — Aurobindo Ghosh
204.x: Tilak wrote Gita Rahasya while imprisoned in Mandalay. New India (the renamed Madras Standard) was Annie Besant's paper, The Punjabee was Lajpat Rai's, and The Soul of India was written by Bipin Chandra Pal.
204.tq: Gita Rahasya = Tilak in Mandalay
xs: **Gita Rahasya — written by Tilak in Mandalay** is correctly matched — so option **(1)** is correct.
**New India** was **Besant**'s (and **Pal**'s, **1901**); **The Punjabee** was **Lajpat Rai**'s; **The Soul of India** was **Pal**'s.
xa: Tilak was released from Mandalay on **16 June 1914**.
⚠ Abroad: Lajpat Rai = **USA**; Pal = **England**; Aurobindo = **Pondicherry**; Tilak = **Mandalay**.
Government demanded **Rs 2,000** security from **Commonweal/New India**, then **Rs 10,000** more; Besant paid.

204.s: Which of the following sets of resolutions was associated with the Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress in 1906?
o: Swaraj, Swadeshi, Boycott and National Education
Separate electorates, provincial autonomy, adult franchise and federation
Non-Cooperation, Civil Disobedience, Quit India and Khilafat
Council entry, constitutional reform, Home Rule and communal award
204.x: The Calcutta session of 1906 passed resolutions on Swaraj, Swadeshi, Boycott and National Education as a compromise between Moderates and Extremists.
204.tq: Recognise the distinctive four-resolution combination.
xs: **Calcutta 1906** passed **Swaraj, Swadeshi, Boycott and National Education** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Under **Naoroji**, the split was **averted by compromise**.
xa: "Swaraj" was left **undefined**.
At **Surat 1907** the Moderates wanted these resolutions **dropped**.
⚠ **Calcutta 1906** = Naoroji; **Surat 1907** = Rash Behari Ghosh.

204.s: The immediate cause of the Surat Split of 1907 was chiefly the dispute between Moderates and Extremists over:
o: the annulment of the partition of Bengal
the formation of the Muslim League
the four resolutions adopted at Calcutta
204.x: The Surat clash centred on the four resolutions passed at Calcutta in 1906 (Swaraj, Swadeshi, Boycott, National Education): the Extremists wanted them kept and the boycott extended to all India, while the Moderates wanted them dropped. Separate electorates, the annulment of partition (1911) and the Muslim League were not the issue.
204.tq: Identify the specific issue behind an organisational split rather than its later consequences.
xs: The Surat Split centred on **the four resolutions adopted at Calcutta** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Extremists wanted them kept and **boycott extended to all of India**; Moderates wanted them **dropped** and the movement kept to **Bengal**.
The partition was annulled only in **1911**.
xa: UPSC 2016 key: the Extremists' **lack of faith in the Moderates' capacity to negotiate**.
Extremists wanted **Lajpat Rai or Tilak** as president.
The Moderates' choice, **Rash Behari Ghosh**, presided.

204.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched in relation to the Surat Split of 1907?
o: Moderates — Gokhale and Mehta; Extremists — Tilak
Moderates — Aga Khan; Extremists — Nawab Salimullah
204.x: Gopal Krishna Gokhale and Pherozeshah Mehta represented the Moderates, while Bal Gangadhar Tilak represented the Extremists in the Surat conflict.
204.tq: Start with the sure leader–group pair and eliminate swapped affiliations.
xs: At Surat, the **Moderates** were led by **Gokhale and Mehta**, the **Extremists** by **Tilak** — so option **(2)** is correct (UPSC).
Option (1) swaps them; **Aurobindo** was an Extremist and **Naoroji** a Moderate.
xa: The session was presided over by **Rash Behari Ghosh**.
Outcome: the Moderates pushed the Extremists out; a **scuffle** suspended the session.
The split **healed at Lucknow in 1916**.

204.s: The Surat session of the Indian National Congress in 1907 was presided over by:
204.x: Rash Behari Ghosh was the president of the Surat session of 1907.
204.tq: Distinguish the president of Surat from the president of Calcutta.
xs: **Rash Behari Ghosh** presided at **Surat 1907** — so option **(1)** is correct.
He was the **Moderates' choice**; the Extremists wanted **Lajpat Rai or Tilak**.
**Naoroji** presided at **Calcutta 1906**.
xa: ⚠ **Calcutta 1906** = Naoroji; **Surat 1907** = Rash Behari Ghosh.
**Gokhale** led the Moderates and **Tilak** the Extremists.
The session was **suspended** after a scuffle.

204.s:
Which of the following developments formed part of the aftermath of the Surat Split?
1. Repression by the colonial government
2. Newspapers Act of 1908
3. Imprisonment of Tilak
4. Immediate reunion of Moderates and Extremists in 1908
Select the correct answer.
204.x: Repression, the Newspapers Act of 1908 and Tilak’s imprisonment followed the split. The reunion occurred at Lucknow in 1916, not in 1908.
204.tq: Find the false chronology hidden among otherwise related consequences.
xs: Items 1, 2 and 3 are correct: **repression**, the **Newspapers Act 1908** and **Tilak jailed**.
Item 4 is wrong: the reunion came only at **Lucknow in 1916** — so option **(1)**, **1, 2 and 3 only**, is correct.
xa: Other 1908 Acts: **Criminal Law Amendment Act** and **Explosive Substances Act**.
Bengal leaders **Ashwini Kumar Dutt** and **K.K. Mitra** were deported in **1908**.
**Gadicherla** was jailed in **1908** in Andhra.

204.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the immediate outcome of the Surat session of 1907?
o: The Extremists secured the presidency and adopted a national boycott.
The session adopted the Lucknow Pact unanimously.
The Moderates pushed the Extremists out, and the session was suspended after a scuffle.
The Congress reunited under Tilak’s leadership.
204.x: The Moderates, being in a majority, pushed out the Extremists; a scuffle followed and the session was suspended.
204.tq: Test the actual consequence rather than the causes of a famous split.
xs: The **Moderates pushed the Extremists out**, and the session was **suspended after a scuffle** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The Moderates had the **majority**; their choice **Rash Behari Ghosh** presided.
xa: Aftermath: repression, **Newspapers Act 1908**, **Tilak jailed**.
**By 1910** the Moderates dominated.
The **Lucknow Pact** and reunion came in **Dec 1916**.

204.s: According to the UPSC 2016 key, a basic cause of the Surat Split of 1907 was
o: the Extremists' lack of faith in the Moderates' capacity to negotiate with the British
the annulment of the partition of Bengal
the founding of the Home Rule Leagues
204.x: The UPSC 2016 key gives the Extremists' lack of faith in the Moderates' capacity to negotiate as the cause, along with the dispute over the four 1906 resolutions. Separate electorates were not the issue at Surat; the partition was annulled in 1911 and the Home Rule Leagues came in 1916, both after the split.
204.tq: Surat: no faith in Moderate negotiation + four resolutions
xs: The UPSC 2016 key gives the **Extremists' lack of faith in the Moderates' capacity to negotiate** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The other cause was the dispute over the **four resolutions** of **1906**.
The annulment (**1911**) and the **Home Rule Leagues** (**1916**) came after the split.
xa: ⚠ Order check: **INC 1885 → Bengal partition 1905 → Muslim League 1906 → Surat 1907**.
The printed key "b, d, a, c" was a trap; true order = **d-b-a-c**.
The split healed at **Lucknow in 1916**.

204.s: Which one of the following Acts was enacted in 1908 to deal with incitement to offences through newspapers?
204.x: The Newspapers (Incitement to Offences) Act was enacted in 1908. The Indian Press Act followed in 1910.
204.tq: Distinguish similarly named press and security laws by their exact titles and years.
xs: The **Newspapers (Incitement to Offences) Act** was passed in **1908** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Explosive Substances Act** was also **1908** but aimed at explosives; the **Seditious Meetings Act** was **1907**; the **Indian Press Act** **1910**.
xa: The **Criminal Law Amendment Act** came in **1908** too.
Tilak was sent to **Mandalay** in **1908**.
**Gadicherla** was jailed in **1908**.

204.s: The Indian Press Act mentioned in the context of extremist repression was enacted in:
204.x: The Indian Press Act was enacted in 1910.
204.tq: Separate the later press law from the cluster of repressive Acts enacted in 1908.
xs: The **Indian Press Act** was enacted in **1910** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**1907** = **Seditious Meetings Act**; **1908** = **Newspapers**, **Criminal Law Amendment** and **Explosive Substances** Acts.
xa: **By 1910** the Extremist leadership was out of action and the **Moderates dominated**.
Aurobindo retired to **Pondicherry** in **1910**.
Under the Press Act, **Besant** was asked for **Rs 2,000** security, then **Rs 10,000** more.

204.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Bipin Chandra Pal — deported to Mandalay in 1907
Ashwini Kumar Dutt and K.K. Mitra — Bengal leaders deported in 1908
Bal Gangadhar Tilak — sent to Mandalay in 1908
Lajpat Rai and Ajit Singh — deported in 1907
204.x: Bipin Chandra Pal was arrested in 1907 for refusing to testify in the Bande Mataram case; he was not deported to Mandalay. Lajpat Rai and Ajit Singh were deported in 1907, while Tilak and the mentioned Bengal leaders faced repression in 1908.
204.tq: Find the swapped person–punishment association among closely related repression measures.
xs: **Bipin Chandra Pal — deported to Mandalay in 1907** is wrong — so option **(1)** is correct.
Pal was **arrested** in **1907** for refusing to testify in the **Bande Mataram case**; he lived in **England** **1908-1911**.
The other pairs are right: **Lajpat Rai** and **Ajit Singh** — **1907**; **Tilak** — Mandalay **1908**; **Ashwini Kumar Dutt** and **K.K. Mitra** — **1908**.
xa: ⚠ Abroad: Lajpat Rai = **USA**; Pal = **England**; Aurobindo = **Pondicherry**; Tilak = **Mandalay**.
**Gadicherla** was jailed in **1908**.
The **Seditious Meetings Act** dates from **1907**.

204.s: Which sequence correctly describes the position of the leading Extremists by 1910?
o: Tilak was in jail; Aurobindo had retired; Pal was arrested; Lajpat Rai had left
Tilak had left; Aurobindo was in jail; Pal had retired; Lajpat Rai led Congress
Tilak was in England; Aurobindo led Congress; Pal was deported; Lajpat Rai was in Mandalay
Tilak was in Pondicherry; Aurobindo was in Mandalay; Pal led Congress; Lajpat Rai was arrested
204.x: By 1910, Tilak was in jail, Aurobindo had retired to Pondicherry, Pal had been arrested and Lajpat Rai had left. This enabled the Moderates to dominate the Congress.
204.tq: Use a multi-person status snapshot and eliminate options with swapped locations or actions.
xs: By **1910**, **Tilak was in jail**, **Aurobindo had retired**, **Pal was arrested** and **Lajpat Rai had left** — so option **(1)** is correct.
With the leading Extremists out of the field, the **Moderates dominated** the Congress.
Tilak was in **Mandalay (Burma)**, not England or Pondicherry; **Pondicherry** was where **Aurobindo** retired (**1910**) after the **Alipore case**.
None of the four "led Congress" — that is why options (2), (3) and (4) fail.
xa: Tilak's **1908** sedition sentence: **6 years in Mandalay**; released **16 June 1914**.
Lajpat Rai went to the **USA** after **1908**; Pal lived in **England 1908-1911**.
⚠ Abroad trap: Lajpat Rai = **USA**; Pal = **England**; Aurobindo = **Pondicherry**; Tilak = **Mandalay**.
Repression laws of the period: **Seditious Meetings Act 1907**, **Newspapers (Incitement to Offences) Act 1908**, **Indian Press Act 1910**.

204.s: Which one of the following events took place in 1911?
o: The Partition of Bengal was annulled
The Tilak Home Rule League was founded
204.x: The Partition of Bengal was annulled in 1911. Tilak was released in 1914, the Lucknow Pact was concluded in 1916, and the Tilak Home Rule League began in 1916.
204.tq: Discriminate among closely spaced chronological milestones.
xs: In **1911** the **Partition of Bengal was annulled** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Lucknow Pact** came in **December 1916**.
**Tilak's Home Rule League** was founded on **28 Apr 1916**.
**Tilak was released** from Mandalay on **16 June 1914**.
xa: The Partition itself and the **Swadeshi Movement (7 Aug)** date from **1905**.
**1908**: Tilak to Mandalay and the **Newspapers Act**.
**Besant's Home Rule League** followed in **September 1916**.
The Congress **reunion** at **Lucknow (1916)** healed the **Surat Split** of **1907**.

204.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Tilak's Home Rule League was founded on 28 April 1916.
2. Annie Besant's Home Rule League was founded in September 1916.
3. The Congress reunion and Lucknow Pact took place in December 1916.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
204.x: All three statements are correct. Tilak began his league on 28 April 1916, Besant’s in September, and the reunion and Lucknow Pact occurred in December.
204.tq: Check dates within the same year instead of treating all Home Rule events as simultaneous.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Statement 1** is correct: **Tilak's Home Rule League** was founded on **28 Apr 1916**.
**Statement 2** is correct: **Besant's** league followed in **September 1916**.
**Statement 3** is correct: the **Lucknow Pact** and **Congress reunion** came in **December 1916**.
xa: Tilak's league: president **Joseph Baptista**, secretary **N.C. Kelkar**.
**52 Home Rule branches** existed in **Andhra by 1917**.
Besant ran **New India** (the renamed **Madras Standard**) and **Commonweal (Jan 1914)**.
Under the Press Act Besant paid **Rs 2,000** security, then **Rs 10,000** more, to keep publishing.

204.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Surat Split
B. Lucknow Pact
C. Swadeshi Movement
D. Morley-Minto Reforms
204.x: The sequence is Swadeshi Movement in 1905, Surat Split in 1907, Morley-Minto Reforms in 1909 and Lucknow Pact in 1916.
204.tq: Place the events by their years before comparing the middle items.
xs: The order is **C, A, D, B** — option **(1)**.
**C:** **Swadeshi Movement**, launched **7 Aug 1905**.
**D:** **Morley-Minto Reforms** come next in the keyed order, before **B:** the **Lucknow Pact** of **December 1916**.
xa: Surat **1907** president: **Rash Behari Ghosh**; Calcutta **1906** president: **Naoroji**.
The split was **healed at Lucknow in 1916**.
**Tilak's Home Rule League (28 Apr 1916)** and **Besant's (Sept 1916)** both preceded the Lucknow Pact.
Between Surat and Lucknow: **Partition annulled (1911)**, **Tilak released (1914)**.

204.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
a. Partition of Bengal
b. Formation of the Muslim League
c. Surat Split
d. Founding of the Indian National Congress
204.x: INC 1885 (d), partition of Bengal 1905 (a), Muslim League 1906 (b), Surat Split 1907 (c), so d, a, b, c. The trap is the printed key 'b, d, a, c' (option D), which wrongly puts the Muslim League before the founding of the INC.
204.tq: 1885 INC -> 1905 partition -> 1906 League -> 1907 Surat
xs: The correct order is **d, a, b, c** — option **(1)**.
**d:** **Indian National Congress** founded **1885**; **a:** **Partition of Bengal 1905**.
**b:** **Muslim League** formed **1906**; **c:** **Surat Split 1907**.
Option (4) **b, d, a, c** puts the Muslim League before the INC's founding — wrong.
xa: ⚠ Trap: a printed key "**b, d, a, c**" exists; the true order is **d-a-b-c** (INC first).
Moderate phase: **1885-1905**; Extremist phase: **1905-1916**.
Surat **1907**: Moderates under **Gokhale** (and Mehta) vs Extremists under **Tilak**.
The **Swadeshi Movement** began on **7 Aug 1905**, the year of the partition.

204.s: The Extremists contributed to the national movement by:
o: turning nationalism into a mass movement and making Swaraj its goal
supporting permanent British control over India
restricting nationalism to educated constitutional petitioners
204.x: The Extremists broadened nationalism into a mass movement and placed Swaraj at the centre of the political goal.
204.tq: Identify the principal historical significance rather than a method or criticism.
xs: The Extremists **turned nationalism into a mass movement** and **made Swaraj the goal** — so option **(1)** is correct.
They took politics to **students, women, workers and peasants**, beyond the Moderates' **urban educated elite**.
They used **Swadeshi, boycott and national education** — so (3) is wrong; and **Swaraj** meant complete freedom, not British control — so (2) is wrong.
Restricting politics to petitions (the **3 Ps**) was the **Moderates'** method — so (4) is wrong.
xa: Extremist methods = **3 Ss**: **self-reliance, self-sacrifice, strong will**; plus mass agitation.
**Spiritual nationalism**: nation as mother goddess (**Bande Mataram**, **Bhavani Mandir**); Hindu festivals for mass contact.
**Atmashakti** (self-reliance): constructive work such as **cooperatives**.
⚠ **3 Ps** (prayers, petitions, protests) = Moderates; **3 Ss** = Extremists.

204.s: Which of the following was a criticism of Extremist politics?
o: Its religious symbolism alienated Muslims and its social outlook was orthodox.
It weakened the demand for Swaraj by supporting colonial rule.
It completely rejected all cultural symbols.
It prevented the use of boycott and Swadeshi.
204.x: The Extremists were criticised for using religious symbolism that alienated Muslims and for being socially orthodox. The Surat Split was also regarded as weakening the Congress.
204.tq: Select the option containing the recognised criticisms without reversing the Extremist programme.
xs: The Extremists' **religious symbolism alienated Muslims** and their outlook was **socially orthodox** — option **(1)**.
Tilak, for example, **opposed the Age of Consent Bill**.

They did not support colonial rule (they demanded **Swaraj**), did not reject cultural symbols (they used **Bande Mataram**, Hindu festivals), and they **championed boycott and Swadeshi** — so (2), (3), (4) are wrong.
xa: Another criticism: the **Surat Split** weakened the Congress.
Tilak made **Ganesh Utsav (1893)** and **Shivaji Jayanti (1895)** public festivals.
The Moderates, by contrast, were **pro-social reform**.
Significance: the Extremists turned nationalism into a **mass movement** and made **Swaraj** the goal.

204.s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra in the Extremist phase:
1. Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao was known as Andhra Tilak.
2. Andhra had 52 Home Rule branches by 1917.
3. Students of the Rajahmundry college wore Besant lockets after Annie Besant's arrest in 1917.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
204.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Gadicherla was called Andhra Tilak, and Andhra had 52 Home Rule branches by 1917. Statement 3 is wrong: it was students of the Machilipatnam National College who wore Besant lockets after her arrest on 15 June 1917. So '1 only' is incomplete and options with 3 are wrong.
204.tq: Andhra Tilak = Gadicherla; 52 HR branches by 1917
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
**Statement 1** is correct: **Gadicherla** was called **"Andhra Tilak"**.
**Statement 2** is correct: Andhra had **52 Home Rule branches by 1917**.
**Statement 3** is wrong: the **Besant lockets** were worn by students of the **Machilipatnam National College**, not a Rajahmundry college.
xa: Besant was arrested on **15 June 1917**.
Gadicherla was **jailed in 1908**.
**Bipin Chandra Pal** toured **Andhra in April 1907**.
⚠ "Andhra Tilak" = Gadicherla; Tilak himself was **"Lokmanya"** and, to **Valentine Chirol**, the **"Father of Indian Unrest"**.

204.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Moderates were associated with the period 1885–1905.
Moderates sought more immediate Swaraj than the Extremists.
Extremists showed increasing distrust of British rule.
Extremists favoured agitation and mass mobilisation.
204.x: Option B is incorrect: the Moderates wanted gradual reform through petitions, while the Extremists demanded more immediate Swaraj. The Moderate phase was 1885–1905, and the Extremists distrusted British rule and used agitation.
204.tq: Discriminate Moderate aims from Extremist aims.
n: The Moderates' period was 1885–1905. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #118 · pp 213-215]
The Extremists followed agitation and mass mobilisation. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #118 · pp 213-215]
The Extremists increasingly distrusted British rule. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #118 · pp 213-215]
The Moderates supported gradual reform. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #118 · pp 213-215]
The Extremists sought more immediate Swaraj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #118 · pp 213-215]
The Extremists used militant methods and agitation. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #118 · pp 213-215]
The Extremists supported wider popular mobilisation. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #118 · pp 213-215]
xs: The incorrect statement is that **Moderates sought more immediate Swaraj** — option **(2)**.
**Moderates** sought **gradual self-government** / **gradual reform**; the **Extremists** wanted **more immediate Swaraj** (complete freedom).
Correct: the Moderate period was **1885–1905**; Extremists showed **increasing distrust** of British rule and used **agitation** and **mass mobilisation**.
xa: ⚠ **3 Ps** (prayers, petitions, protests) = Moderates; **3 Ss** (self-reliance, self-sacrifice, strong will) = Extremists.
The Extremist phase of **assertive nationalism** ran **1905-1916**.
Moderates initially had **faith** in **British liberalism**.

204.s: What was the main objective of the Extremists or Assertive Nationalists?
o: Swaraj or complete independence from English rule
204.x: The Extremists, or Assertive Nationalists, aimed at Swaraj, meaning complete independence from British rule. Constitutional agitation, negotiation and gradual self-government were Moderate ideas.
204.tq: Discriminate Extremist goals from Moderate goals.
n: The main objective of the Extremists was Swaraj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Swaraj meant complete independence from English rule. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
The Extremists lacked faith in Moderate negotiations with the British. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
The Moderate goal was gradual self-government. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
The Moderate strategy was constitutional agitation. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
The Moderates initially had faith in British liberalism. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Extremists were also called Assertive Nationalists. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
xs: The Extremists' main objective was **Swaraj** — **complete independence** from **English rule** — option **(3)**.
**Constitutional agitation**, **negotiations** and **gradual self-government** belong to the **Moderates**.
The Extremists **lacked faith** in Moderate **negotiations** with the British.
xa: Extremists are also called **Assertive Nationalists**; their **influence increased** after **1906**.
Extremist **Swaraj** meant **complete freedom** from British control, not colonial self-government.
Key leaders: **Tilak**, **Lajpat Rai**, **Bipin Chandra Pal**, **Aurobindo Ghosh**.

204.s: Which of the following statements regarding the methods of the Extremists is incorrect?
o: They accepted Prayer, Petition and Protest as their principal method.
204.x: Option A is incorrect: the Extremists rejected Prayer, Petition and Protest, which was the Moderate method. They favoured self-sacrifice, mass movement and aggressive resistance.
204.tq: Discriminate Moderate methods from Extremist methods.
n: Extremist methods included self-sacrifice. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Extremist methods included mass movements. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Extremist methods included aggressive resistance. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
The Extremists opposed Moderate methods. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
The Extremists rejected Prayer, Petition and Protest. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
The Moderate method was Prayer, Petition and Protest. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
xs: The incorrect statement is that Extremists **accepted Prayer, Petition and Protest** — option **(1)**.
The Extremists **rejected Prayer**, **Petition** and **Protest**, the Moderate method.
They favoured **self-sacrifice**, **mass movements** and **aggressive resistance**.
xa: Extremist methods also included **passive resistance**, **boycott**, **Swadeshi** and **national education**.
They wanted a **wider** and **extended Swadeshi–Boycott movement**.
**Spiritual nationalism**: nation as mother goddess (**Bande Mataram**, **Bhavani Mandir**).

204.s: Which of the following statements about Lala Lajpat Rai is incorrect?
o: He was known as Sher-e-Punjab and Punjab Kesari.
He died on 17 November 1928 after the Maniktalla Garden raid.
He was a member of the Lal–Bal–Pal trio.
204.x: Option B is incorrect: Lajpat Rai died on 17 November 1928 from lathi injuries suffered during the Simon Commission protest at Lahore. The Maniktalla Garden raid is linked with Aurobindo Ghosh.
204.tq: Check the event linked to each date.
n: Lala Lajpat Rai belonged to Punjab. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Lala Lajpat Rai was known as Sher-e-Punjab. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Lala Lajpat Rai was known as Punjab Kesari. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Lala Lajpat Rai was associated with the Simon Commission protest. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Aurobindo Ghosh was associated with the Maniktalla Garden raid. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Lala Lajpat Rai was a member of Lal–Bal–Pal along with Tilak and Bipin Chandra Pal. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Lala Lajpat Rai suffered a lathi-charge injury during the Simon Commission protest. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Lala Lajpat Rai died on 17 November 1928. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Lala Lajpat Rai represented Punjab and the safety-valve issue. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Aurobindo Ghosh was associated with Swadeshi, Maniktalla and Pondicherry. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
xs: The incorrect statement is that Lajpat Rai **died** on **17 November 1928** after the **Maniktalla Garden raid** — option **(2)**.
He died after a **lathi-charge injury** during the **Simon Commission protest**.
The **Maniktalla Garden raid** (**1908**) is linked with **Aurobindo Ghosh**.
Correct: he was **Sher-e-Punjab** / **Punjab Kesari**, part of **Lal–Bal–Pal**, from **Punjab**.
xa: Lajpat Rai went to the **USA** after **1908** and set up the Indian Home Rule League of America (**1917**).
He was **deported to Mandalay in 1907 with Ajit Singh**.
His slogan: "**Go back Simon**"; books **Unhappy India**, **Young India**.

204.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Aurobindo Ghosh
(b) Maniktalla Garden raid
(c) Pondicherry
(d) Maniktalla case

204.x: Aurobindo was the main Swadeshi leader in Bengal, he was arrested in 1908 after the Maniktalla Garden raid, he later settled in Pondicherry, and in the Maniktalla case he spent a year in jail before release for lack of evidence, giving a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii.
204.tq: Recall the stages of Aurobindo's career.
n: Aurobindo Ghosh was the main leader of the Swadeshi Movement during the Partition of Bengal. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Aurobindo Ghosh was arrested in 1908 during the Maniktalla Garden raid. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
The Maniktalla case involved Aurobindo Ghosh. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Aurobindo Ghosh was sentenced to one year in the Maniktalla case. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Aurobindo Ghosh was later released for lack of evidence. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Aurobindo Ghosh later moved to Pondicherry. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Aurobindo Ghosh was associated with the Swadeshi Movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Aurobindo Ghosh was associated with Pondicherry. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Aurobindo Ghosh was associated with Swadeshi, Maniktalla and Pondicherry. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
xs: The correct code is **a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii** — option **(1)**.
**Aurobindo Ghosh** — **main leader** of the **Swadeshi Movement** during the Partition of Bengal; **Maniktalla Garden raid** — **arrest in 1908**.
**Pondicherry** — his **later residence**; **Maniktalla case** — **one year** sentence, then release for **lack of evidence**.
xa: ⚠ Other notes say he was **acquitted** in the **Alipore case** (**1909**).
Aurobindo was called the **Prophet** of **Indian Nationalism**.
He edited **Bande Mataram** and wrote **New Lamps for Old** and **Bhavani Mandir**.

204.s: Who was described by Sir Valentine Chirol as the “Father of Indian unrest”?
204.x: Sir Valentine Chirol called Bal Gangadhar Tilak the "Father of Indian unrest" in his book Indian Unrest (1910).
204.tq: Recall who used the phrase and about whom.
n: Sir Valentine Chirol called Bal Gangadhar Tilak the “Father of Indian unrest”. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
xs: **Sir Valentine Chirol** called **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** the "**Father of Indian unrest**" — option **(2)**.
Chirol used the phrase in his book **Indian Unrest** (**1910**).
**Bipin Chandra Pal** is the "**Father of Revolutionary Thoughts**"; **Lajpat Rai** is **Punjab Kesari**.
xa: Tilak's popular title: **Lokmanya** ("beloved of the people").
Tilak was imprisoned in **1908** for **six years** in **Mandalay**; released **16 June 1914**.
Tilak was born **23 July 1856** at **Ratnagiri**.

204.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Moderates aimed at gradual self-government.
II. Extremists advocated Swaraj or complete independence.
III. Moderates relied on mass movements as their principal strategy.
IV. Extremists emphasised self-sacrifice and resistance.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
204.x: I, II and IV are correct: the Moderates sought gradual self-government, and the Extremists sought Swaraj through self-sacrifice and resistance. III is false because the Moderates used constitutional agitation; mass movement was the Extremist method.
204.tq: Discriminate Moderate and Extremist methods.
n: The Moderate goal was gradual self-government. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
The Moderate strategy was constitutional agitation. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
The Extremist goal was Swaraj or complete independence. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
The Extremist method was self-sacrifice and resistance. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
The Extremist strategy was mass movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
xs: Statements I, II and IV are correct — so **I, II and IV only**, option **(4)**.
I correct: **Moderates** aimed at **gradual self-government**; II correct: **Extremists** sought **Swaraj** or **complete independence**.
III wrong: Moderates used **constitutional agitation**; **mass movement** was the Extremist strategy.
IV correct: Extremists stressed **self-sacrifice** and **resistance**.
xa: Moderates' base: **urban educated elite**; Extremists: students, women, workers, peasants.
⚠ Ranade, Gokhale, G.V. Joshi were **not** militant (**APPSC-GS 2018**: militant = **Tilak**).
Moderates were **pro-reform**; Tilak opposed the **Age of Consent Bill**.

204.s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Extremists had increasing distrust of British rule.
Statement B: The Moderates wanted to extend the Swadeshi–Boycott movement more widely.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
204.x: A is true: the Extremists grew more distrustful of British rule. B is false because it was the Extremists who wanted to widen the Swadeshi–Boycott movement; the Moderates were reluctant to extend it.
204.tq: Check which group held each view.
n: The Extremists had increasing distrust of British rule. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
The Moderates were less willing to extend the Swadeshi–Boycott movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
The Extremists wanted a wider and extended Swadeshi–Boycott movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
The Extremists supported Swadeshi and Boycott. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
The Extremists wanted to extend the Swadeshi and Boycott movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
xs: **Statement A is true, Statement B is false** — option **(3)**.
A true: the Extremists had **increasing distrust** of **British rule**.
B false: the **Moderates** were **less willing** to extend the **Swadeshi–Boycott** movement; the **Extremists** wanted it **wider**.
xa: Surat **1907**: Extremists demanded **boycott** extended to all of India; Moderates wanted it kept to **Bengal**.
Moderates initially had **faith** in **British liberalism**.
Extremist attitude: **No faith in British generosity**.

204.s: Which pair consists only of representative Moderate leaders?
o: Bipin Chandra Pal and Aurobindo Ghosh
204.x: Dadabhai Naoroji and Gopal Krishna Gokhale were both Moderates. Tilak, Lajpat Rai, Bipin Chandra Pal and Aurobindo Ghosh were Extremists, so every other pair includes an Extremist.
204.tq: Discriminate Moderate leaders from Extremist leaders.
n: Dadabhai Naoroji was a representative Moderate leader. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Gokhale was a representative Moderate leader. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Tilak was a representative Extremist leader. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Lajpat Rai was a representative Extremist leader. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Bipin Chandra Pal was a representative Extremist leader. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Aurobindo Ghosh was a representative Extremist leader. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Lal–Bal–Pal–Ghosh represented the Extremists or Assertive Nationalists. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Bal Gangadhar Tilak was an Extremist leader. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Lala Lajpat Rai was an Extremist. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Aurobindo Ghosh was an Extremist. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
xs: **Dadabhai Naoroji** and **Gokhale** are both **Moderates** — option **(4)**.
**Tilak**, **Lajpat Rai**, **Bipin Chandra Pal** and **Aurobindo Ghosh** were **Extremists**, so every other pair includes one.
xa: Other Moderates: **Pherozeshah Mehta**, **S.N. Banerjee**, **Ranade**, **W.C. Bonnerjee**, **R.C. Dutt**.
Naoroji = **Grand Old Man** of India; Gokhale = **Political Guru** of **Gandhi**.
At Surat, the Moderates were under **Gokhale** (and Mehta), Extremists under **Tilak**.

204.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Surat Split:

I. Leadership was one of the major issues at Surat.
II. Methods were one of the major issues at Surat.
III. Congress strategy was one of the major issues at Surat.
IV. Swadeshi–Boycott was one of the major issues at Surat.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
204.x: I, II, III and IV are correct: at Surat in 1907 the Moderates and Extremists split over leadership, methods, Congress strategy and the Swadeshi–Boycott programme.
204.tq: Check each issue of the Surat Split.
n: Leadership was a major issue in the Surat Split. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Methods were a major issue in the Surat Split. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Congress strategy was a major issue in the Surat Split. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Swadeshi–Boycott was a major issue in the Surat Split. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
xs: All four were major issues at Surat — so **I, II, III and IV**, option **(3)**.
The **Surat Split** (**1907**) was a **conflict** between **Moderates** and **Extremists** over **leadership**, **methods**, **Congress strategy** and **Swadeshi–Boycott**.
xa: Surat **1907** president: **Rash Behari Ghosh** (Moderates' choice).
After the split: **Naram Dal** = Moderates; **Garam Dal** = Extremists.
The split **healed at Lucknow in 1916**.
Cause per UPSC **2016** key: Extremists' lack of faith in Moderates' capacity to negotiate.

204.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Bijoliya Movement was started by Sadhu Sitaram Das and later led by Vijay Singh Pathik.
The Deoband Movement was started by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan.
The Neo-Buddhist / Dalit Buddhist Movement was led by B. R. Ambedkar.
The Faraizi Movement was started by Haji Shariatullah.
204.x: Option B is incorrect: the Deoband Movement (1866) was started by Muhammad Qasim Nanautavi and Rashid Ahmad Gangohi, not Sir Syed Ahmad Khan, who led the Aligarh Movement. The Bijoliya, Neo-Buddhist and Faraizi pairings are right.
204.tq: Discriminate the Deoband founders from the Aligarh founder.
n: Sadhu Sitaram Das initially led the Bijoliya Movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #93 · pp 175-176]
Vijay Singh Pathik later led the Bijoliya Movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #93 · pp 175-176]
Haji Shariatullah led the Faraizi Movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #93 · pp 175-176]
Muhammad Qasim Nanautavi led the Deoband Movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #93 · pp 175-176]

B. R. Ambedkar led the Neo-Buddhist Movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #93 · pp 175-176]
xs: The incorrect statement is that the **Deoband Movement** was started by **Sir Syed Ahmad Khan** — option **(2)**.
Deoband (**1866**) was led by **Muhammad Qasim Nanautavi**, **Rashid Ahmad Gangohi** and others; Sir Syed led the **Aligarh Movement** (**1875**).
Correct: **Bijoliya** — **Sadhu Sitaram Das**, later **Vijay Singh Pathik**; **Neo-Buddhist** — **Ambedkar**; **Faraizi** — **Haji Shariatullah**.

**Arya Samaj** (**1875**) — **Swami Dayanand Saraswati**.

o: The Arya Samaj Movement was associated with Swami Dayanand Saraswati.
The Ramakrishna Movement was associated with Swami Vivekananda.
The Aligarh Movement was associated with Sir Syed Ahmad Khan.
The Neo-Buddhist / Dalit Buddhist Movement was associated with Swami Vivekananda.

Swami Dayanand Saraswati led the Arya Samaj Movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #93 · pp 175-176]

**12 December 1911** = annulment of partition at the **Delhi Durbar**; **20 August 1917** = **August Declaration**.
xa: It demanded **separate electorates** and **weightage** for Muslims.
⚠ **1 Oct 1906** = Simla Deputation; **30 Dec 1906** = League founded (Dacca).
Aga Khan became the League's **first president**.
The demand was met by the **Indian Councils Act 1909**.

205.s:
The Simla Deputation of 1906 demanded:
1. Separate electorates for Muslims
2. Weightage for Muslims
3. Representation based on their contribution to the Empire's defence
Which of the statements given above are correct?
205.x: The deputation demanded separate electorates and weightage, justifying the demand by referring to the Muslims' contribution to the defence of the Empire.
205.tq: Combine the demands with the stated justification rather than selecting only the headline demand.
xs: All three demands were made — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
It asked for **separate electorates** and **weightage** for Muslims.
Justification: their **"contribution to the empire's defence"**.
xa: Led by **Aga Khan (III)** to **Lord Minto** on **1 October 1906**.
**Weightage** = more seats than the community's population share.
The **1909 Act** granted **separate electorates with weightage** — its most critical feature.
The **Muslim League** followed on **30 Dec 1906** at Dacca.

205.s:
Consider the following statements about the All India Muslim League:
1. It was founded on 30 December 1906 at Dacca, at the session of the All-India Muhammadan Educational Conference.
2. Its formation was proposed by Nawab Salimullah of Dacca.
3. Syed Ameer Ali was its first president.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
205.x: Statement 1 is correct: the League was founded on 30 December 1906 at Dacca during the Muhammadan Educational Conference session. Statement 2 is correct: Nawab Salimullah proposed it. Statement 3 is wrong: Aga Khan was the first president; Syed Ameer Ali set up the London branch in 1908. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
205.tq: Proposer Salimullah, president Aga Khan, London branch Ameer Ali.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
**Statement 1** correct: founded **30 December 1906** at **Dacca**, at the **All-India Muhammadan Educational Conference** session.
**Statement 2** correct: proposed by **Nawab Salimullah of Dacca**.
**Statement 3** wrong: **Aga Khan** was the first president; **Syed Ameer Ali** set up the **London branch (1908)**.
xa: Early aims: **loyalty to the British Empire**, safeguarding Muslim interests, keeping Muslims away from the Congress.
**Jinnah** joined the League in **1913**.
The **Simla Deputation (1 Oct 1906)** preceded the League's founding.

205.s: Which one of the following was NOT an aim of the All-India Muslim League in its early phase?
o: Keeping Muslims away from the Congress
Launching an immediate armed revolt against British rule
Promoting loyalty to the British Empire
205.x: The early League aimed at loyalty to the British Empire, protection of Muslim political interests and separation from the Congress; immediate armed revolt was not one of its stated aims.
205.tq: Reject the extreme revolutionary alternative when testing an organisation's declared aims.
xs: **Launching an immediate armed revolt** was **not** an aim — option **(3)**.
The early League's aims were **loyalty to the British Empire**, **safeguarding Muslim political interests** and **keeping Muslims away from the Congress** — options (1), (2), (4).
xa: Founded **30 Dec 1906** at **Dacca**; proposed by **Nawab Salimullah**; first president **Aga Khan**.
**1912-24**: the League was dominated by **younger Muslim nationalists**.
By **1916** it allied with the Congress in the **Lucknow Pact**.
London branch: **Syed Ameer Ali (1908)**.

205.s: The Indian Councils Act, 1909 provided for which of the following electoral arrangements?
o: Election by a single national constituency
Universal adult franchise through direct elections
205.x: The 1909 reforms introduced indirect, multi-tier elections rather than direct universal elections.
205.tq: Discriminate between direct, indirect and nominated representation.
xs: The **1909 Act** provided **indirect, multi-tier elections** — option **(4)**.
It also introduced **separate electorates for Muslims** with weightage, and **elected** non-official members for the first time.
**Direct elections** at the Centre came only with the **1919 Act** — so (3) is wrong.
xa: Central Legislative Council enlarged (additional members **to 60**).
**Official majority retained at the Centre**; non-official majority in provinces.
Councils could **discuss the budget** but **not vote** on it.
**1935 Act** extended separate electorates to depressed classes, women and labour.

205.s:
With reference to the Indian Councils Act, 1909, consider the following statements:
1. The Central Legislative Council was enlarged to 60 additional members.
2. An official majority was retained at the Centre.
3. A non-official majority was provided in the provinces.
4. The Governor's veto made the provincial non-official majority ineffective in practice.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
205.x: All four are correct: the 1909 Act enlarged the Central Legislative Council (additional members up to 60) but kept an official majority at the Centre, and gave the provinces a non-official majority that the Governor's veto left powerless in practice. So 1, 2, 3 and 4.
205.tq: Read constitutional composition and actual executive control together.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**1:** Central Legislative Council enlarged — additional members **to 60**.
**2:** **Official majority retained at the Centre**.
**3 and 4:** **Non-official majority in provinces**, but the **Governor's veto** left them powerless.
xa: Most critical feature: **separate electorates for Muslims** with **weightage**.
Councils could not **vote on the budget** or question **military affairs**.
**S.P. Sinha** joined the Executive Council as **Law Member**.
Aim: **rally the Moderates** + **reward Muslim loyalty**.

205.s: Which of the following powers was NOT granted to members under the Indian Councils Act, 1909?
205.x: Members could discuss the budget, ask supplementary questions and move resolutions, but they could not vote on the budget.
205.tq: Find the one power excluded from an otherwise expanded legislative role.
xs: Members could **not vote on the budget** — option **(1)**.
They **could discuss the budget**, **ask supplementary questions** and **move resolutions** — options (2), (3), (4) were granted.
They also could not question **military affairs**.
xa: **Official majority** stayed at the Centre.
Provinces had a **non-official majority**, blunted by the **Governor's veto**.
Elections were **indirect, multi-tier**.
Introduced by **John Morley** (Secretary of State) and **Lord Minto** (Viceroy).

205.s:
Consider the following statements about Satyendra Prasanna Sinha:
1. He was the first Indian member of the Viceroy's Executive Council.
2. He held the Finance portfolio on the Council.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
205.x: Statement 1 is correct: S.P. Sinha was the first Indian member of the Viceroy's Executive Council (1909). Statement 2 is wrong: he was the Law Member. Hence '1 only'.
205.tq: S.P. Sinha = first Indian, Law Member.
xs: Only **statement 1** is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
**Statement 1** correct: **Satyendra Prasanna Sinha** was the **first Indian member of the Viceroy's Executive Council** (**1909**).
**Statement 2** wrong: he was the **Law Member**, not Finance.
xa: His appointment came under the **Morley-Minto Reforms (1909)**.
Same reforms: **separate electorates** for Muslims with **weightage**.
Central council enlarged (additional members **to 60**), **official majority** retained.

205.s: The Morley-Minto Reforms were introduced mainly to:
o: Rally the Moderates and reward Muslim loyalty
Transfer the capital from Delhi to Calcutta
Abolish princely states and establish a republic
205.x: Morley and Minto sought to rally the Moderates and reward Muslim loyalty through limited constitutional concessions and separate electorates.
205.tq: Identify the political purpose behind a constitutional measure.
xs: Morley-Minto Reforms aimed to **rally the Moderates and reward Muslim loyalty** — option **(1)**.
The reward was **separate electorates** with **weightage** for Muslims.
The capital moved **Calcutta → Delhi** (not Delhi → Calcutta) in **1911**; **provincial autonomy** came with the **1935 Act** — (2) and (4) are wrong.
xa: Official majority **retained at the Centre**.
Councils could debate the budget but **could not vote** on it.
**S.P. Sinha** = first Indian on the Viceroy's Executive Council.

205.s: With reference to the Indian Councils Act, 1909, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: It abolished legislative councils and introduced national education.
It enlarged legislative councils and introduced separate electorates for Muslims.
It created the Muslim League at Dacca.
It reunited Bengal and ended the Surat Split.
205.x: The Indian Councils Act of 1909 enlarged the legislative councils and introduced separate electorates for Muslims.
205.tq: Identify the reform measure by its distinctive constitutional provisions.
xs: The **1909 Act** **enlarged legislative councils** and **introduced separate electorates for Muslims** — option **(2)**.
The **Muslim League** was founded separately at **Dacca** in **1906**; Bengal was reunited in **1911**; the Surat Split healed at **Lucknow 1916** — so (3) and (4) are wrong.
xa: Central council: additional members **to 60**; provincial councils also enlarged.
**Elected** non-official members for the first time; **indirect** elections.
Minto = **"Father of the Communal Electorate"**.
**1919** Act later extended communal representation to **Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians and Europeans**.

205.s: The Lucknow Congress Session of December 1916 was presided over by:
205.x: Ambika Charan Majumdar presided over the Lucknow Congress Session of December 1916.
205.tq: Avoid swapping the session president with the principal brokers of the pact.
xs: The **Lucknow Congress session (Dec 1916)** was presided over by **Ambika Charan Majumdar** — option **(4)**.
**Jinnah** presided over the **League's** Lucknow 1916 session — not the Congress.
**Tilak** and **Jinnah** were the **brokers** of the Lucknow Pact; **Annie Besant** also worked for it.
xa: ⚠ Lucknow 1916: Congress president = **Ambika Charan Majumdar**; League president = **Jinnah**.
The session saw the **reunion of Moderates and Extremists** after Surat **1907**.
League side led by the **"Young Party"** (Jinnah, Ali Brothers).

205.s:
The Lucknow Congress Session of 1916 was historically significant because it witnessed:
1. Reunion of Moderates and Extremists
2. The Congress-League alliance
3. Tilak's return to the Congress fold
Which of the statements given above are correct?
205.x: The 1916 session marked the reunion of Moderates and Extremists, Tilak's return and the Congress-League alliance represented by the Lucknow Pact.
205.tq: Identify all historically linked features of a landmark session.
xs: All three were features of Lucknow **1916** — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Reunion of Moderates and Extremists** after the **1907 Surat Split**.
**Tilak's return** to the Congress fold.
The **Congress-League alliance** — the **Lucknow Pact**.
xa: Congress president: **Ambika Charan Majumdar**; League president: **Jinnah**.
Brokers: **Tilak + Jinnah**; Annie Besant also worked for it.
**1916** = high point of **Congress-League unity**.
Limit: the two still held **separate annual sessions**.

205.s: The Muslim League delegation associated with the Lucknow Pact was led by the:
205.x: The League's Young Party, associated with Jinnah and the Ali Brothers, led the League side in the Lucknow Pact negotiations.
205.tq: Discriminate between similarly named political groupings.
xs: The League side was led by the **"Young Party"** — option **(4)**.
Its leaders were **Jinnah** and the **Ali Brothers**.
xa: **1912-24**: League dominated by **younger Muslim nationalists** whose nationalism still took a **communal** view.
Jinnah joined the League in **1913** and presided its **Lucknow 1916** session.
Congress accepted **Muslim separate electorates** — a major concession.
Pact brokered by **Tilak** and **Jinnah**.

205.s: Under the Lucknow Pact, the Congress accepted which major concession to the Muslim League?
o: Direct British appointment of Muslim representatives
205.x: The Congress accepted separate electorates for Muslims, which was a major concession under the Lucknow Pact.
205.tq: Identify the specific concession rather than the general objective of the pact.
xs: The Congress **accepted Muslim separate electorates** — option **(2)**, a **major concession**.
It did not abolish communal representation — so (4) is wrong; it sought an **elected majority** in provincial legislatures — so (3) is wrong.
xa: **Weightage**: Muslims got seats above their population ratio.
**Communal veto**: no bill passed if **three-fourths** of the affected community's members opposed.
Common goal: **self-government**.
Separate electorates first came legally with the **1909** Act.

205.s: Under the Lucknow Pact, a bill concerning a particular community could not be passed if opposed by what proportion of the members of that community?
205.x: Under the Lucknow Pact's communal veto, no bill affecting a community could be passed if three-fourths of that community's members in the legislature opposed it.
205.tq: Treat a constitutional fraction as an exact figure, not an approximate majority.
xs: The communal veto required opposition by **three-fourths** of that community's members — option **(1)**.
No bill concerning a community could pass if **three-fourths** of its members opposed it.
xa: Other terms: **separate electorates** accepted, **weightage**, **self-government** as common goal.
Also: **separation of executive and judiciary**; **elected majority** in provincial legislatures.
Brokers: **Tilak** and **Jinnah** (Dec **1916**).

205.s:
Which of the following formed part of the Lucknow Pact proposals?
1. Separation of the executive from the judiciary
2. Elected majority in provincial legislatures
3. Self-government as a common goal
Which of the statements given above are correct?
205.x: The Pact accepted self-government as its goal and included separation of the executive and judiciary and elected majorities in provincial legislatures.
205.tq: Combine institutional provisions with the shared political objective.
xs: All three were part of the Pact — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**1:** **Separation of executive and judiciary**.
**2:** **Elected majority in provincial legislatures**.
**3:** **Self-government** accepted by both as the common goal.
xa: Congress **accepted separate electorates** for Muslims.
**Weightage** and the **three-fourths communal veto**.
Limit: **separate annual sessions** continued.

205.s: Muhammad Ali Jinnah joined the All-India Muslim League in
205.x: Jinnah joined the Muslim League in 1913, although he was also associated with the Congress-League cooperation that culminated in the Lucknow Pact.
205.tq: Use the close-year discrimination method for a sequence of League milestones.
xs: **Jinnah** joined the Muslim League in **1913** — option **(3)**.
**1906** = League founded; **1909** = Morley-Minto Reforms; **1916** = Jinnah presided the **Lucknow League session**.
xa: Jinnah and **Tilak** brokered the **Lucknow Pact**.
He belonged to the League's **"Young Party"** with the **Ali Brothers**.
**1940**: **Lahore Resolution** demanding independent states for Muslims.

205.s: Who presided over the Muslim League session held at Lucknow in 1916?
205.x: Muhammad Ali Jinnah presided over the Muslim League session at Lucknow in 1916.
205.tq: Match the session with its presiding leader and avoid substituting later ideological figures.
xs: **Muhammad Ali Jinnah** presided the **League's Lucknow 1916** session — option **(3)**.
**Aga Khan** was the League's **first president** (**1906**); **Iqbal** gave the **Allahabad address (1930)**; **Rahmat Ali** coined **"PAKISTAN" (1933)**.
xa: ⚠ Congress president at Lucknow 1916: **Ambika Charan Majumdar**.
Jinnah joined the League in **1913**.
He co-brokered the Pact with **Tilak**.

205.s: The Lucknow Pact was negotiated principally by:
205.x: The Pact was negotiated by Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Muhammad Ali Jinnah with the Muslim League's Young Party.
205.tq: Avoid the swapped-leader trap by matching the negotiators with the Pact.
xs: The Lucknow Pact was brokered by **Tilak and Jinnah** — option **(3)**.
**Annie Besant** also worked for it, but with Tilak, not Gokhale.
xa: Tilak's return marked the **reunion of Moderates and Extremists**.
Jinnah led the League's **"Young Party"** with the Ali Brothers.
Key concession: Congress **accepted separate electorates**.
Congress president: **Ambika Charan Majumdar**.

205.s: The provision that Muslims should receive more seats than their population share in provinces where they were a minority is known as:
205.x: The Lucknow Pact provided weightage to Muslims in minority provinces, giving them representation greater than their population share.
205.tq: Discriminate between closely related constitutional terms by their operative meaning.
xs: Seats above population share for a minority community is **weightage** — option **(2)**.
The Lucknow Pact fixed a proportion of seats for Muslims **above their population ratio**.
**Communal veto** was the **three-fourths** rule on bills; **dyarchy** belongs to the **1919** Act.
xa: Weightage was first given with separate electorates in the **1909** Act.
The **Simla Deputation (1906)** had demanded weightage.
Congress **accepted** separate electorates in **1916** — a major concession.

205.s: The August Declaration relating to India's constitutional development was made on:
205.x: The August Declaration was made on 20 August 1917.
205.tq: Distinguish the date of the declaration from the dates of later mass movements and reforms.
xs: The **August Declaration** was made on **20 August 1917** — option **(2)**.
**12 Dec 1911** = partition annulled; **13 April 1919** = **Jallianwala Bagh**; **1 Jan 1923** = **Swaraj Party**.
xa: **1919**: Rowlatt Act and the **Government of India Act**.
**1920**: Khilafat and Non-Cooperation.
The **1919 Act** introduced **dyarchy in the provinces**.

205.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
205.x: The Swaraj Party was formed on 1 January 1923 by C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru, not in 1921.
205.tq: Find the shifted year in a sequence of otherwise correctly dated events.
xs: **Swaraj Party — 1921** is wrong — option **(4)**; it was formed on **1 Jan 1923**.
Founders: **C.R. Das** and **Motilal Nehru**.
The others match: **Khilafat/Non-Cooperation 1920**, **Rowlatt Act 1919**, **Jallianwala Bagh 13 April 1919**.
xa: **1917**: August Declaration (**20 Aug**).
**1911**: Delhi Durbar, partition annulled.
**1909**: Morley-Minto Reforms.

205.s: Who proposed the idea of a Muslim state in the North-West of India in the Allahabad Address of 1930?
205.x: Muhammad Iqbal proposed the idea of a Muslim state in the North-West in his Allahabad Address of 1930.
205.tq: Distinguish the early ideological proposal from the later Pakistan nomenclature and League resolution.
xs: **Muhammad Iqbal** proposed a Muslim state in the **North-West** in his **Allahabad address (1930)** — option **(3)**.
**Chaudhry Rahmat Ali** only coined the name **"PAKISTAN" (1933)**.
xa: ⚠ Muslim state idea = **Iqbal (1930)**; the name "PAKISTAN" = **Rahmat Ali (1933)**.
**1937-39**: League alleged **"Hindu Raj"** under Congress ministries.
**1940**: **Lahore Resolution**.
**1946**: **Direct Action Day**.

205.s: The name “PAKISTAN” was coined by Chaudhry Rahmat Ali in 1933 in his pamphlet titled
205.x: Chaudhry Rahmat Ali coined the name “PAKISTAN” in 1933 in the pamphlet Now or Never.
205.tq: Test the author–title association rather than the broader movement chronology.
xs: Rahmat Ali coined **"PAKISTAN"** in **1933** in **Now or Never** — option **(3)**.
The idea of a Muslim state in the NW came earlier from **Iqbal (1930)**, Allahabad address.
xa: ⚠ Do not confuse: **Iqbal** = idea; **Rahmat Ali** = name.
**Lahore Resolution (1940)**: independent states for Muslims.
**1946**: Direct Action Day; League wins Muslim seats.

205.s:
With reference to the Delhi Durbar of 1911, consider the following statements:
1. The annulment of the partition of Bengal was announced on 12 December 1911 through King George V.
2. The capital of British India was shifted from Calcutta to Delhi.
3. The annulment came along with the Morley-Minto Reforms.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
205.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: at the Delhi Durbar (12 December 1911) the partition was annulled, announced through King George V, and the capital moved from Calcutta to Delhi. Statement 3 is wrong: the Morley-Minto Reforms came in 1909. So B, C and D, which include statement 3 or omit 1 or 2, are wrong.
205.tq: 1911 Durbar = annulment + capital to Delhi; 1909 = Morley-Minto.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
**1** correct: partition annulled on **12 December 1911**, announced through **King George V** at the **Delhi Durbar**.
**2** correct: the capital shifted **Calcutta → Delhi**.
**3** wrong: the **Morley-Minto Reforms** came in **1909**, not with the annulment.
xa: The partition and **Swadeshi** began in **1905**.
**1907** Surat Split; **1917** August Declaration.
Lord Minto's tenure ended in **1910**.

205.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
205.x: The Lahore Resolution, demanding independent states for Muslims, was passed in 1940. Direct Action Day was in 1946 (not 1940), the Lahore Resolution was not in 1946, and Iqbal's Allahabad address was in 1930 (1933 is when Rahmat Ali coined 'Pakistan').
205.tq: 1930 Iqbal → 1933 Pakistan name → 1940 Lahore → 1946 Direct Action.
xs: **Lahore Resolution — 1940** is correct — option **(3)**.
It demanded **independent states for Muslims**.
**Direct Action Day** was **1946**, not 1940; Iqbal's **Allahabad address** was **1930**, not 1933.
xa: **1933**: **Rahmat Ali** coined "PAKISTAN" (Now or Never).
**1937-39**: League alleged **"Hindu Raj"**.
**1946**: League also won the Muslim seats.

205.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Government of India Act, 1919 introduced dyarchy in the provinces.
2. The Government of India Act, 1919 provided for bicameralism and direct elections at the Centre.
3. The Government of India Act, 1935 prescribed an All-India Federation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
205.x: All three are correct: the 1919 Act introduced dyarchy in the provinces and bicameralism with direct elections at the Centre, and the 1935 Act prescribed an All-India Federation (along with provincial autonomy and dyarchy at the Centre).
205.tq: Group the distinctive features of two successive constitutional Acts.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**1:** The **1919 Act** introduced **dyarchy in the provinces**.
**2:** It gave **bicameralism and direct elections** at the Centre.
**3:** The **1935 Act** prescribed an **all-India Federation**.
xa: **1935** also gave **provincial autonomy** and **dyarchy at the Centre**.
**1909** introduced **separate electorates** for Muslims.
⚠ Montagu-Chelmsford = **1919**, not 1929 (wrong pair in APPSC-G1 **2019**).
Pitt's India Act = **1784**.

205.s:
The Government of India Act, 1919 extended communal representation to which of the following communities?
1. Sikhs
2. Indian Christians
3. Anglo-Indians
4. Europeans
205.x: The 1919 Act extended communal representation to Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians and Europeans.
205.tq: Check the complete membership of a constitutional category.
xs: The **1919 Act** extended communal representation to all four — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Sikhs**, **Indian Christians**, **Anglo-Indians** and **Europeans**.
xa: Separate electorates began for **Muslims** in **1909**.
The **1935 Act** extended them to **depressed classes, women, labour**.
1919 also brought **dyarchy in the provinces** and **direct elections** at the Centre.

205.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes the 1909 and 1919 reforms?
o: The 1919 reforms abolished communal representation introduced in 1909.
The 1909 reforms introduced provincial dyarchy, whereas the 1919 reforms introduced Muslim separate electorates.
The 1909 reforms introduced Muslim separate electorates, whereas the 1919 reforms introduced provincial dyarchy and direct elections.
Both reforms introduced provincial autonomy in the provinces.
205.x: The Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909 introduced separate electorates for Muslims, while the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms of 1919 introduced provincial dyarchy and direct elections.
205.tq: Compare the signature feature of each reform instead of swapping their dates and provisions.
xs: **1909** introduced **Muslim separate electorates**; **1919** introduced **provincial dyarchy and direct elections** — option **(3)**.
Option (2) swaps them; 1919 **extended** (not abolished) communal representation; **provincial autonomy** came in **1935**.
xa: 1909 = Morley-Minto; 1919 = **Montagu-Chelmsford**.
1919 also gave **bicameralism** at the Centre.
1935 = **provincial autonomy**, **dyarchy at the Centre**, all-India **Federation**.

205.s:
With reference to the Government of India Act, 1935, consider the following statements:
1. It introduced provincial autonomy.
2. It introduced dyarchy in the provinces.
3. It extended separate electorates to the depressed classes, women and labour.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
205.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: the 1935 Act gave provincial autonomy and extended separate electorates to depressed classes, women and labour. Statement 2 is wrong: dyarchy in the provinces came with the 1919 Act; the 1935 Act put dyarchy at the Centre. So A, B and D, which include statement 2, are wrong.
205.tq: Dyarchy: provinces 1919, Centre 1935.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct — option **(3)**.
**1** correct: the **1935 Act** gave **provincial autonomy**.
**2** wrong: **dyarchy in the provinces** came with **1919**; 1935 put **dyarchy at the Centre**.
**3** correct: separate electorates extended to **depressed classes, women, labour**.
xa: 1935 also prescribed an all-India **Federation**.
1919 extended communal representation to **Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians, Europeans**.
1909 began **Muslim separate electorates**.

205.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the significance of 1909 and 1916 is correct?
o: 1909 marked the legal beginning of separate electorates, while 1916 marked the high point of Congress-League unity.
1909 marked the establishment of provincial autonomy, while 1916 marked the end of communal politics.
1909 marked the end of separate electorates, while 1916 marked the beginning of the Muslim League.
Both 1909 and 1916 marked phases of complete constitutional separation between Congress and the League.
205.x: The year 1909 is associated with the legal start of separate electorates, whereas 1916 is regarded as the high point of Congress-League unity.
205.tq: Use the contrast between two years to eliminate reversed comparisons.
xs: **1909** = **legal start of separate electorates**; **1916** = **high point of Congress-League unity** — option **(1)**.
**Provincial autonomy** came only in **1935**; 1909 began (not ended) separate electorates; the League dates from **1906**.
xa: 1916 brought the **Lucknow Pact**, brokered by **Tilak** and **Jinnah**.
Even in 1916 the two held **separate annual sessions**.
Separate electorates re-entered debate in **2026** commentary on religion-based voting.

205.s: Who among the following, arrested on 18 July 1908 over a Swarajya article, are regarded as the first Telugu political prisoners?
o: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao and Bodi Narayana Rao
Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao and Mocherla Hanumantha Rao
205.x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao and Bodi Narayana Rao were arrested on 18 July 1908 for a Swarajya article during the Minto-Morley repression - the first Telugu political prisoners. Konda Venkatappayya and Pattabhi Sitaramayya were Home Rule leaders; Ramayya and Basavayya were the Tenali bomb case accused (1909); Nageswara Rao and Mocherla Hanumantha Rao were associated with Andhra Patrika and Besant's tour.
205.tq: Swarajya article, 1908 → Gadicherla + Bodi = first Telugu political prisoners.
xs: **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao** and **Bodi Narayana Rao**, arrested **18 July 1908**, were the **first Telugu political prisoners** — option **(2)**.
They were arrested over a **Swarajya** article.
This was part of the **repression under Minto-Morley**.
xa: **1908** also saw the **Newspapers Act** and the **Muzaffarpur case**.
Besant later toured **Kakinada, Rajahmundry, Eluru** after Lucknow **1916**.
Minto was **Viceroy 1905-1910**.

205.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Provincial Dyarchy was associated with the Government of India Act, 1919.
II. Provincial Dyarchy included reserved and transferred subjects.
III. Provincial Dyarchy was abolished by the Government of India Act, 1935.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
205.x: All three are correct: the Government of India Act, 1919 brought Provincial Dyarchy, which split subjects into reserved and transferred, and the 1935 Act abolished it.
205.tq: Check each statement separately.
n: The Government of India Act 1919 introduced provincial dyarchy. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 97-98]
