205.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Muslim League was formed in 1906 at Dhaka.
The Muslim League aimed to protect Muslim political interests.
The Muslim League was formed in 1907 at Karachi.
Nawab Salimullah was associated with the Muslim League.
205.x: Option C is incorrect: the Muslim League was formed in 1906 at Dhaka with Nawab Salimullah to protect Muslim political interests. Karachi in 1907 was its first annual session.

n: The Muslim League was established in 1906. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #115 · pp 210-211]

**Karachi 1907** was its **first annual session**.

**Aga Khan** was the **first President**.
Second session: **Amritsar**, **1908**.

205.s:

n: The Direct Action Day dates to 1946. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #115 · pp 210-211]
Direct Action Day occurred on 16 August. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #115 · pp 210-211]
xs: **Both Statement A and Statement B are true** — option **(1)**.
**Direct Action Day** was observed by the **Muslim League** on **16 August 1946**.
xa: **1940** — **Lahore Resolution**, independent states for Muslims.
**1946** — the League also won the Muslim seats.
**1937-39** — League alleged "**Hindu Raj**" under Congress ministries.

206.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Damodar and Balkrishna Chapekar shot Plague Commissioner W.C. Rand at Poona in 1897.
2. Their action was a protest against the excesses of plague-control measures.
3. Vasudev Balwant Phadke's Ramosi force was organised after the Chapekar action, in 1909.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
206.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Chapekar brothers shot Rand (and Lt. Ayerst) at Poona in 1897 in protest against plague-control excesses. Statement 3 is wrong: Phadke's Ramosi force (1879) was an earlier root, before the Chapekars. Hence only option A fits; B, C and D all include statement 3 or omit statement 1.
206.tq: Phadke 1879 comes before Chapekars 1897.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
**1** correct: **Damodar and Balkrishna Chapekar** shot **Plague Commissioner W.C. Rand** at **Poona** in **1897** (Lt. Ayerst also killed).
**2** correct: it was a protest against **plague-control excesses**.
**3** wrong: **Vasudev Balwant Phadke's Ramosi force** dates from **1879** — an earlier root, before the Chapekars.
xa: **1908**: **Muzaffarpur** bomb by **Khudiram Bose** and **Prafulla Chaki**.
**1909**: **Anant Kanhere** killed Nasik Collector **A.M.T. Jackson**.
**1911**: **Vanchi Aiyar** shot **Robert Ashe** at Maniyachi.
Roots of revolutionary groups: **akhadas** + secret societies.

206.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
206.x: The Bharat Mata Society was founded by Ajit Singh with Lala Lajpat Rai in Punjab, not in Bengal in 1906.
206.tq: Find the wrongly matched place and year among closely related organisations.
xs: **Bharat Mata Society — Bengal, 1906** is wrong — option **(4)**.
The **Bharat Mata Society** was **Ajit Singh's** (with **Lala Lajpat Rai**) in **Punjab**.
**Bengal, 1906** fits **Yugantar** (Barindra Kumar Ghosh).
The rest match: **Anushilan — Calcutta 1902**, **Mitra Mela — Nasik 1899**, **Abhinav Bharat — Nasik/Pune 1904**.
xa: ⚠ **Anushilan (1902)** = **P. Mitra**; **Yugantar (1906)** = **Barindra Kumar Ghosh**, its offshoot.
Mitra Mela was **renamed Abhinav Bharat** by **V.D. Savarkar**.
Ajit Singh + Lajpat Rai were **deported to Mandalay in 1907**.
**India House** (London, **1905**) = **Shyamji Krishna Varma**.

206.s:
With reference to the revolutionary organisations of the early twentieth century, consider the following statements:
1. The Dhaka branch of Anushilan Samiti was associated with Pulin Behari Das.
2. Yugantar emerged as an offshoot of Anushilan Samiti.
3. Bharat Mata Society was associated with Ajit Singh and Lala Lajpat Rai.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
206.x: Pulin Behari Das was associated with the Dhaka branch, Yugantar was an offshoot of Anushilan Samiti, and Bharat Mata Society was associated with Ajit Singh and Lala Lajpat Rai.
206.tq: Test three related organisation–leader relationships in one coded statement question.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**1:** Anushilan's **Dhaka branch** = **Pulin Behari Das**.
**2:** **Yugantar (1906)** was an **offshoot of Anushilan**.
**3:** **Bharat Mata Society** = **Ajit Singh** with **Lala Lajpat Rai** (Punjab).
xa: Anushilan Samiti: **P. (Pramathanath) Mitra**, Calcutta, **1902**.
Yugantar: **Barindra Kumar Ghosh** with **Bagha Jatin**.
The **Hardinge bomb** was attributed to **Anushilan Samiti** (UPPSC **2023** key).
Bengal journals **Yugantar** and **Sandhya** advocated violence.

206.s:
Consider the following pairs:
Society — Founder
1. Anushilan Samiti — Pramathanath Mitra
2. Yugantar — Barindra Kumar Ghosh
3. Abhinav Bharat — Ajit Singh
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
206.x: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct: P. Mitra founded Anushilan Samiti (Calcutta, 1902) and Barindra Kumar Ghosh founded Yugantar (1906). Pair 3 is wrong: Abhinav Bharat was V.D. Savarkar's; Ajit Singh led the Bharat Mata Society. So B, C and D, which include pair 3, are wrong.
206.tq: Anushilan = P. Mitra; Yugantar = Barindra; Abhinav Bharat = Savarkar.
xs: Pairs **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
**1** correct: **Anushilan Samiti** — **Pramathanath Mitra** (Calcutta, **1902**).
**2** correct: **Yugantar** — **Barindra Kumar Ghosh** (**1906**).
**3** wrong: **Abhinav Bharat** was **V.D. Savarkar's**; **Ajit Singh** led the **Bharat Mata Society**.
xa: Abhinav Bharat = **Mitra Mela (1899)** renamed, **1904**.
Anushilan's Dhaka branch: **Pulin Behari Das**.
Barindra wrote the manual **Mukti Kon Pathe (1906)**.

206.s: In 1907, Lala Lajpat Rai and Ajit Singh were deported to Mandalay under which law?
206.x: They were deported to Mandalay in 1907 under Regulation III of 1818. The Defence of India Act came only in 1915 and the Rowlatt Act in 1919, so neither could apply in 1907; the Press Act was a press law, not a deportation law.
206.tq: 1907 Mandalay deportation = Regulation III of 1818; DIA is 1915.
xs: They were deported under **Regulation III of 1818** — option **(2)**.
**Ajit Singh + Lajpat Rai** were **deported to Mandalay in 1907**.
⚠ The **Defence of India Act** came only in **1915** — some notes wrongly name it.
xa: Ajit Singh's group: the **Bharat Mata Society** (Punjab).
The Defence of India Act was used to hang many after the **1915 Ghadar revolt**.
Lajpat Rai's later lathi-charge led to the **Saunders killing (1928)**.

206.s: In the Muzaffarpur Bomb Case, the intended target was:
206.x: Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki targeted Magistrate Douglas Kingsford at Muzaffarpur.
206.tq: Distinguish the intended target from the unintended victims and other colonial officials.
xs: The target was **Magistrate Douglas Kingsford** — option **(3)**.
**Khudiram Bose** and **Prafulla Chaki** bombed his carriage at **Muzaffarpur (Bihar)** on **30 April 1908**.
**Lord Hardinge** was the **1912** Delhi target; **James A. Scott** the **1928** target; **Jackson** was the Nasik Collector killed in **1909**.
xa: ⚠ The bomb killed **two British women** instead.
Khudiram was **hanged at 18** on **11 August 1908**; Chaki shot himself.
The police then raided the **Maniktala bomb factory** → **Alipore case**.

206.s: Which of the following correctly describes the outcome of the Muzaffarpur bomb attack?
o: Two British women were killed, Khudiram Bose was hanged and Prafulla Chaki died by suicide.
The bomb failed to explode and both accused were acquitted.
Kingsford was killed and both revolutionaries escaped.
Only Prafulla Chaki was executed after a formal trial.
206.x: The bomb killed two British women instead of Kingsford. Khudiram Bose was hanged, while Prafulla Chaki shot himself before arrest.
206.tq: Read the whole sequence carefully: target, unintended result and fate of both accused.
xs: **Two British women were killed**, **Khudiram Bose was hanged** and **Prafulla Chaki** shot himself — option **(1)**.
Kingsford escaped, so (3) is wrong; Khudiram was executed, so (2) and (4) are wrong.
xa: Khudiram, hanged on **11 August 1908** at **18**, was among the youngest martyrs.
Attack date: **30 April 1908**, Muzaffarpur (Bihar).
Khudiram Bose was born **3 Dec 1889**.
UPPSC **2021** order: Kesari (**1881**) → Khudiram executed (**1908**) → Curzon Wyllie killed (**1909**) → Al-Hilal (**1912**).

206.s: Which one of the following statements about the Alipore Bomb Case is correct?
o: It involved a raid on the Maniktala bomb factory, and Aurobindo Ghosh was acquitted.
It was related to the killing of Curzon Wyllie in London.
It concerned the Kakori train action, and C.R. Das was the chief accused.
It was conducted in Nasik, and Barindra Ghosh was acquitted.
206.x: The Alipore Bomb Case followed the raid on the Maniktala bomb factory. Aurobindo Ghosh was acquitted, while Barindra Ghosh received a life sentence; C.R. Das defended Aurobindo.
206.tq: Distinguish the place of the raid and the differing outcomes of the principal accused.
xs: The **Alipore case** followed the raid on the **Maniktala bomb factory**, and **Aurobindo Ghosh was acquitted** — option **(1)**.
**C.R. Das** defended Aurobindo; he was not an accused — (3) wrong.
**Barindra Ghosh** got **life** (Andaman Cellular Jail), not acquittal; the **Nasik** case was separate (**1909**) — (4) wrong.
**Curzon Wyllie** was killed in London by **Madan Lal Dhingra** — (2) wrong.
xa: ⚠ Alipore: **Aurobindo** acquitted (C.R. Das); **Barindra** = life.
Approver **Narendranath Goswami** was shot inside **Alipore jail**.
Aurobindo, acquitted **1909**, retired to Pondicherry.

206.s: Who defended Aurobindo Ghosh in the Alipore Bomb Case?
206.x: Chittaranjan Das, popularly known as C.R. Das, defended Aurobindo Ghosh in the Alipore Bomb Case.
206.tq: Match the legal counsel with the revolutionary case.
xs: **C.R. Das** defended **Aurobindo Ghosh** in the **Alipore case** — option **(1)**.
Aurobindo was **acquitted**; his brother **Barindra Ghosh** got **life** in the Andaman Cellular Jail.
xa: The case (**1908**) began with the raid on the **Maniktala bomb factory** after Muzaffarpur.
Approver **Narendranath Goswami** was shot in jail by **Kanailal Dutta** + **Satyendranath Bose**.
Aurobindo edited **Bande Mataram**.

206.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Alipore Bomb Case is NOT correct?
o: Barindra Ghosh was sentenced to life imprisonment in the Cellular Jail.
Narendranath Goswami was shot outside India by Madan Lal Dhingra.
Narendranath Goswami acted as an approver.
The accused were held in Alipore jail, Calcutta.
206.x: Narendranath Goswami was shot inside Alipore jail by Kanailal Dutta and Satyendranath Bose. He was not killed outside India by Madan Lal Dhingra.
206.tq: Find the swapped person and location in a case-related statement.
xs: The false statement is that **Goswami was shot outside India by Madan Lal Dhingra** — option **(2)**.
**Narendranath Goswami** (approver) was shot **inside Alipore jail** by **Kanailal Dutta** + **Satyendranath Bose**.
Options (1), (3) and (4) are true: **Barindra** got life in the Cellular Jail; accused were held in **Alipore jail, Calcutta**.
xa: **Dhingra** killed **Curzon Wyllie** in London, **1909**.
**Aurobindo** was acquitted, defended by **C.R. Das**.
Alipore case is also called the **Maniktala** case (**1908**).

206.s: Who founded the Mitra Mela in 1899, which later became associated with Abhinav Bharat?
206.x: V.D. Savarkar founded Mitra Mela in 1899. It later developed into the revolutionary organisation Abhinav Bharat.
206.tq: Use the founder–organisation association without confusing Mitra Mela with other revolutionary bodies.
xs: **V.D. Savarkar** founded **Mitra Mela (1899)** at Nasik, with brother **Ganesh** — option **(4)**.
It was **renamed Abhinav Bharat** (**1904**).
**Shyamji Krishna Varma** founded **India House**; **Barindra** founded **Yugantar**; **Sanyal** co-founded the **HRA**.
xa: In London Savarkar worked from **India House**.
Arrested in London (**1910**); failed escape at **Marseilles**.
Books: **"The Indian War of Independence, 1857" (1909)**, **"Hindutva" (1923)**.

206.s:
With reference to the Nasik Conspiracy Case, consider the following statements:
1. A.M.T. Jackson, the Nasik Collector, was assassinated by Anant Kanhere.
2. V.D. Savarkar was implicated in the case.
3. Savarkar was sentenced to imprisonment in the Cellular Jail at the Andamans.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
206.x: All three statements are correct. The assassination of A.M.T. Jackson by Anant Kanhere led to Savarkar’s implication and sentence to life imprisonment in the Andamans.
206.tq: Check all three linked facts in a conspiracy-case cluster before selecting the combined option.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**1:** **Anant Kanhere** assassinated Nasik Collector **A.M.T. Jackson** (**1909**).
**2 and 3:** **Savarkar** was implicated and got **life in the Andamans** (Cellular Jail).
xa: Savarkar's earlier groups: **Mitra Mela (1899)** → **Abhinav Bharat**.
Other cases: **Alipore 1908**, **Howrah 1910**, **Delhi 1912**.
Same year (**1909**): Dhingra killed **Curzon Wyllie** in London.

206.s: V.D. Savarkar was arrested in London in 1910. At which place did his attempted escape fail?
206.x: Savarkar’s attempted escape failed at Marseilles in 1910.
206.tq: Distinguish the place of arrest and escape attempt from other overseas revolutionary centres.
xs: Savarkar's escape attempt failed at **Marseilles** — option **(3)**.
He had been **arrested in London (1910)**.
**Stuttgart** = **Bhikaji Cama's** flag (**1907**); **Kabul** = the **Provisional Government (1915)**.
xa: He worked from **India House** with **Hardayal** and **Madan Lal Dhingra**.
He was sentenced to **life in the Andamans** in the **Nasik** case.
Books: **The Indian War of Independence, 1857** and **Hindutva**.

206.s:
Which of the following books were written by V.D. Savarkar?
1. The Indian War of Independence, 1857
2. Hindutva
3. Mukti Kon Pathe
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
206.x: Savarkar wrote 'The Indian War of Independence, 1857' (1909) and 'Hindutva' (1923). 'Mukti Kon Pathe' (1906) was Barindra Kumar Ghosh's revolutionary manual. So B, C and D, which include 3 or omit 1 or 2, are wrong.
206.tq: Savarkar: 1857 book (1909), Hindutva (1923); Mukti Kon Pathe = Barindra.
xs: Savarkar wrote **1 and 2 only** — option **(1)**.
**"The Indian War of Independence, 1857"** (**1909**) and **"Hindutva"** (**1923**).
**Mukti Kon Pathe (1906)** was **Barindra Kumar Ghosh's** manual.
xa: Savarkar founded **Mitra Mela (1899)**, later **Abhinav Bharat**.
**Andaman Jeevitam** = **Prativadi Bhayankaracharyulu**.
**The Philosophy of the Bomb** = **Bhagwati Charan Vohra**.

206.s:
Consider the following statements about the Delhi Conspiracy Case:
1. The bomb was thrown during Lord Hardinge’s state entry into the new capital, Delhi.
2. The procession passed through Chandni Chowk.
3. Lord Hardinge was killed in the attack.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
206.x: The attack took place during the procession through Chandni Chowk, and Hardinge was injured but not killed. Therefore, statements 1 and 2 are correct.
206.tq: Use the outcome trap by distinguishing injury from death.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
**1:** The bomb was thrown during **Hardinge's state entry into the new capital Delhi** (**23 December 1912**).
**2:** The procession passed through **Chandni Chowk**.
**3** wrong: **Hardinge was injured, not killed**.
xa: Planned by **Rash Behari Bose** + **Sachin Sanyal**; bomb thrown by **Basanta Kumar Biswas**.
Organisation: **Anushilan Samiti** (UPPSC **2023**).
Executed: **Basant Kumar Biswas, Amir Chand, Avadh Behari** (+ Bhai Balmukund).

206.s: Which one of the following persons escaped after the Delhi Conspiracy Case by disguising himself and later went to Japan?
206.x: Rash Behari Bose escaped in disguise after the case and later went to Japan.
206.tq: Separate the person who escaped from those executed after the trial.
xs: **Rash Behari Bose** escaped in disguise and later went to **Japan** — option **(3)**.
**Basant Kumar Biswas**, **Avadh Behari** and **Bhai Balmukund** were **executed**.
xa: The case followed the **1912** bomb at **Lord Hardinge** in **Chandni Chowk**.
Co-planner: **Sachin Sanyal**.
Organisation: **Anushilan Samiti**.

206.s: Which organisation was identified as being behind the bomb attack on Lord Hardinge in the Delhi Conspiracy Case?
206.x: Anushilan Samiti was identified as the organisation behind the Delhi Conspiracy Case attack.
206.tq: Match the incident with the organisation rather than with an individual revolutionary.
xs: **Anushilan Samiti** was behind the Hardinge bomb — option **(2)** (UPPSC **2023** key).
The **Ghadar Party** dates from **1913**, the **HRA** from **1924**; **Abhinav Bharat** was Savarkar's Maharashtra group.
xa: Anushilan: **P. Mitra**, Calcutta, **1902**.
Planners: **Rash Behari Bose** + **Sachin Sanyal**.
Bomb thrower: **Basanta Kumar Biswas**.

206.s: The Indo-German, or Zimmerman, plot of 1915–17 was associated with which plan?
o: A plan to support the Simon Commission
A plan by Bagha Jatin to organise a revolt with German arms
A plan to establish a constitutional government through the Morley-Minto reforms
A plan to conduct the Chittagong Armoury Raid
206.x: The Indo-German plot involved Bagha Jatin’s plan to organise an armed revolt with German arms. He died in a gunfight at Balasore in 1915.
206.tq: Connect the conspiracy with its intended foreign assistance and leader.
xs: The **Indo-German (Zimmerman) plot 1915-17** was **Bagha Jatin's** plan of a **revolt with German arms** — option **(2)**.
He died in a gunfight at **Balasore** (**1915**).
xa: **Berlin Committee (1915)**: **Virendranath Chattopadhyaya**, **Bhupendranath Dutta**.
**Ghadar revolt** fixed for **21 Feb 1915**, betrayed.
**Kabul Provisional Government (1915)**: Raja **Mahendra Pratap**.
**Singapore Mutiny (Feb 1915)**: 5th Light Infantry.

206.s:
Consider the following statements about Vanchi Aiyar:
1. He shot Robert Ashe, Collector of Tirunelveli, at Maniyachi railway station in 1911.
2. He was captured and hanged after a trial.
3. He was linked with the Bharata Matha Association.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
206.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: Vanchi Aiyar shot Robert Ashe at Maniyachi on 17 June 1911 and was linked with the Bharata Matha Association (and V.O. Chidambaram Pillai's Swadeshi Steam Navigation agitation). Statement 2 is wrong: he shot himself after the attack. So A, B and D, which include statement 2 or omit 1 or 3, are wrong.
206.tq: Vanchi Aiyar shot Ashe, then shot himself - no trial.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct — option **(3)**.
**1:** **Vanchi Aiyar** shot **Robert Ashe**, Collector of Tirunelveli, at **Maniyachi** (**17 June 1911**).
**2** wrong: he **shot himself** — no trial.
**3:** linked with the **Bharata Matha Association**.
xa: Also linked to **V.O. Chidambaram Pillai's** **Swadeshi Steam Navigation** agitation.
Comparable: **Prafulla Chaki** also shot himself (Muzaffarpur, **1908**).

206.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Madan Lal Dhingra, part of the India House circle, killed Curzon Wyllie in 1909.
2. Bhikaji Cama unfurled the Indian flag at Stuttgart in 1915.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
206.x: Statement 1 is correct: Dhingra of the India House hub killed Curzon Wyllie in 1909. Statement 2 is wrong: Bhikaji Cama unfurled the flag at Stuttgart in 1907, not 1915. So 2 only, both and neither are wrong.
206.tq: Stuttgart flag = 1907; 1915 is the Berlin Committee / Kabul government year.
xs: Only **statement 1** is correct — option **(1)**.
**1:** **Madan Lal Dhingra** (India House hub) killed **Curzon Wyllie** in **1909**.
**2** wrong: **Bhikaji Cama** unfurled the flag at **Stuttgart** in **1907**, not 1915.
xa: India House: **Shyamji Krishna Varma**, London, **1905**.
India House hub: **Savarkar**, **Hardayal**, **Dhingra**.
**1915** abroad: **Berlin Committee** and the **Kabul** government.

206.s:
The Provisional Government of India established at Kabul in 1915 included:
1. Raja Mahendra Pratap
2. Barkatullah
3. Obaidullah Sindhi

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
206.x: Raja Mahendra Pratap, Barkatullah and Obaidullah Sindhi were associated with the Provisional Government of India established at Kabul in 1915.
206.tq: Test the composition of the provisional government without substituting Berlin Committee members.
xs: All three were in the **Kabul Provisional Government (1915)** — option **(4)**.
**Raja Mahendra Pratap**, **Barkatullah** and **Obaidullah Sindhi**.
xa: Barkatullah edited **Islamic Fraternity**.
**Berlin Committee (1915)**: Chattopadhyaya + **Bhupendranath Dutta**.
**Singapore Mutiny**: **Feb 1915**.

206.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Komagata Maru incident of 1914?
o: A ship carrying mainly Sikh passengers was refused entry into Canada and forced back to India.
A ship carried the Berlin Committee to Stuttgart for a political conference.
A ship carrying Indian troops mutinied at Singapore under Ghadar leadership.
A revolutionary vessel transported arms from Germany to Kabul.
206.x: The Komagata Maru carried 376 mainly Sikh passengers, who were refused entry into Canada and forced back to India.
206.tq: Identify the central event while separating it from the Singapore Mutiny and Berlin Committee.
xs: The **Komagata Maru** carried mainly **Sikh** passengers, refused entry to **Canada** and forced back — option **(1)**.
It carried **376** passengers (**1914**).
The **Singapore mutiny (Feb 1915)** and **Berlin Committee** are different events.
xa: Back in India, **Budge Budge** firing killed **22**.
It **radicalised the Ghadar movement**.
Canada's PM Trudeau apologised in **2016**.

206.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. India House, London (1905) — Shyamji Krishna Varma
2. Ghadar Party headquarters — Yugantar Ashram, San Francisco
3. Berlin Committee (1915) — Lala Hardayal and Sohan Singh Bhakna
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
206.x: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct: Shyamji Krishna Varma founded India House in London in 1905, and the Ghadar Party's headquarters was Yugantar Ashram, San Francisco. Pair 3 is wrong: the Berlin Committee was led by Virendranath Chattopadhyaya and Bhupendranath Dutta; Hardayal and Bhakna were Ghadar founders. So A (omits 2), C and D (include 3) are wrong.
206.tq: Yugantar Ashram = Ghadar HQ (San Francisco), not the Bengal Yugantar.
xs: Pairs **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
**1:** **India House**, London (**1905**) — **Shyamji Krishna Varma**.
**2:** Ghadar HQ — **Yugantar Ashram, San Francisco**.
**3** wrong: the **Berlin Committee** was **Virendranath Chattopadhyaya** + **Bhupendranath Dutta**; Hardayal and Bhakna were **Ghadar** leaders.
xa: Shyamji also edited **Indian Sociologist**.
Ghadar journals: **Ghadar**, **Ghadar di Goonj**.
Chattopadhyay edited **Talwar**.

206.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
206.x: The Hindustan Republican Association was founded in Kanpur in 1924. HSRA was formed in 1928 at Feroz Shah Kotla, Naujawan Bharat Sabha in Lahore in 1926, and the Indian Independence League in 1942.
206.tq: Start from the sure organisation–year–place pair and eliminate the swapped entries.
xs: **HRA — 1924, Kanpur** is correct — option **(1)**.
**HSRA** = **1928**, Feroz Shah Kotla, Delhi; **Naujawan Bharat Sabha** = **1926**, Lahore — options (2) and (3) swap them.
xa: HRA founders: **Bismil, Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee, Sachindranath Sanyal**.
HSRA: **Chandrashekhar Azad** with Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev.
HSRA goal: socialist **"Federal Republic of United States of India"**.

206.s: The Saunders killing in 1928 was intended as retaliation for the lathi-charge on:
206.x: The Saunders killing was planned in retaliation for the lathi-charge on Lala Lajpat Rai during the anti-Simon Commission protest. The intended target was James A. Scott, while Rajguru fired first.
206.tq: Trace the motive and intended target rather than confusing the person actually killed.
xs: It avenged the lathi-charge on **Lala Lajpat Rai** — option **(3)**.
The intended target was **James A. Scott**; **Rajguru fired first**.
xa: Lajpat Rai died after the **lathi-charge** during the Simon Commission protest.
Saunders killing: **1928**.
Rajguru was born **1908**, **Khed** (now Rajgurunagar).

206.s:
Consider the following statements about the Central Assembly bomb of 8 April 1929:
1. The bombs were thrown by Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt.
2. It was a protest against the Public Safety Bill and the Trade Disputes Bill.
3. The bombs were meant to kill members of the Assembly so as to force the withdrawal of the Bills.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
206.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt threw the bombs against the Public Safety and Trade Disputes Bills. Statement 3 is wrong: the bombs were deliberately non-lethal, 'to make the deaf hear', aiming at arrest and a trial for propaganda. So options B, C and D, which include statement 3 or drop statement 1, are wrong.
206.tq: Assembly bomb = non-lethal, 'to make the deaf hear'; any 'meant to kill' statement is false.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
**1:** **Bhagat Singh** and **Batukeshwar Dutt** threw the bombs (**8 April 1929**).
**2:** against the **Public Safety** and **Trade Disputes Bills**.
**3** wrong: bombs were **deliberately non-lethal** — "**to make the deaf hear**"; the aim was arrest and trial for propaganda.
xa: Lahore Conspiracy Case: Bhagat Singh, **Sukhdev, Rajguru** hanged **23 Mar 1931**.
Bhagat Singh wrote **Why I am an Atheist**.
Bhagat Singh born **28 Sep 1907**.

206.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Lahore Conspiracy Case is correct?
o: It resulted in the execution of Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki in 1908.
It was conducted against Rash Behari Bose in 1912.
It ended with the execution of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru on 23 March 1931.
It concerned only the Kakori train action of 1925.
206.x: The Lahore Conspiracy Case of 1929–30 resulted in the execution of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru on 23 March 1931.
206.tq: Use the case period and execution date to distinguish it from earlier conspiracy cases.
xs: The **Lahore Conspiracy Case** ended with **Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru** executed on **23 March 1931** — option **(3)**.
**Khudiram** = Muzaffarpur **1908**; **Rash Behari Bose** = Delhi **1912**; **Kakori** = **1925**.
xa: Case years: **1929-30**.
**Jatin Das** died in **Lahore jail** after **63 days** of hunger strike (**1929**).
Sukhdev: b. **15 May 1907**, **Ludhiana**.

206.s: After the death of Ram Prasad Bismil, Chandrashekhar Azad reorganised the Hindustan Republican Association as the:
206.x: Chandrashekhar Azad reorganised the Hindustan Republican Association into the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association after Bismil’s death.
206.tq: Distinguish the expansion and ideological change in a similarly named organisation.
xs: Azad reorganised the HRA into the **Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA)** — option **(4)**.
HSRA was formed in **1928** at **Feroz Shah Kotla, Delhi**.
xa: HSRA goal: socialist **"Federal Republic of United States of India"**.
HRA (**1924**, Kanpur): Bismil, Chatterjee, Sanyal.
Azad shot himself at **Alfred Park, Prayagraj** (**27 Feb 1931**).

206.s: Jatin Das died after how many days of hunger strike in Lahore jail in 1929?
206.x: Jatin Das died after 63 days of hunger strike in Lahore jail in 1929 and was regarded as the first martyr of that strike.
206.tq: Use the exact duration rather than confusing it with the date or place of the strike.
xs: **Jatin Das** died after **63 days** of hunger strike — option **(3)**.
He was the **first martyr** of the **Lahore jail** hunger strike (**1929**).
xa: ⚠ Some notes say **64** days.
**Lahore Conspiracy Case** = **1929-30**.
Executions: **23 Mar 1931**.

206.s:
Which of the following were associated with the founding of the Hindustan Republican Association?
1. Sachindranath Sanyal
2. Jogesh Chatterjee
3. Ram Prasad Bismil

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
206.x: Sachindranath Sanyal, Jogesh Chatterjee and Ram Prasad Bismil were associated with the founding of the Hindustan Republican Association.
206.tq: Group the correct co-founders while avoiding substitution with later HSRA leaders.
xs: All three founded the **HRA** — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Sachindranath Sanyal**, **Jogesh Chatterjee**, **Ram Prasad Bismil** (APPSC G1 **2024**).
xa: Sanyal was also in the **Hardinge bomb** (**1912**).
Bismil (b. **11 Jun 1897**) was hanged after **Kakori (1925)**.

206.s: Chandrashekhar Azad shot himself on 27 February 1931 at:
206.x: Azad shot himself at Alfred Park, Prayagraj, on 27 February 1931. Feroz Shah Kotla was where the HSRA was formed in 1928; Kakori was the 1925 train action; Lahore jail was the scene of Jatin Das's hunger strike and the 1931 executions.
206.tq: Azad: HSRA at Feroz Shah Kotla 1928; died at Alfred Park 1931.
xs: **Azad** shot himself at **Alfred Park, Prayagraj** on **27 Feb 1931** — option **(2)**.
**Feroz Shah Kotla** = HSRA's founding (**1928**); **Kakori** = **1925** action; **Lahore jail** = Jatin Das's strike.
xa: Azad was born **23 Jul 1906**.
He reorganised the HRA into the **HSRA** after Bismil's death.
Birth-anniversary tribute: **23 Jul 2026**.

206.s:
Consider the following pairs:

xs: All four pairs are correct — option **(4)**.
**Bande Mataram** — **Aurobindo**; **Ghadar di Goonj** — **Ghadar Party**.
**The Philosophy of the Bomb** — **Bhagwati Charan Vohra**; **Why I am an Atheist** — **Bhagat Singh**.

**Talwar** — **Virendranath Chattopadhyay**; **Islamic Fraternity** — **Barkatullah**.
**Swadesh Sevak** — **G.D. Kumar**.

206.s:
Which of the following were Bengal journals associated with revolutionary activities?
1. Yugantar
2. Sandhya
3. Indian Sociologist

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
206.x: Yugantar and Sandhya were Bengal journals associated with revolutionary activities. Indian Sociologist was associated with Shyamji Krishna Varma and the overseas revolutionary sphere.

xs: **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)**: **Yugantar** and **Sandhya** were Bengal journals that advocated violence.

206.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
206.x: Swadesh Sevak was G.D. Kumar's; Bhagwati Charan Vohra wrote The Philosophy of the Bomb. Talwar (Chattopadhyay), Islamic Fraternity (Barkatullah) and Indian Sociologist (Shyamji Krishna Varma) are correctly matched.

xs: **Swadesh Sevak — Bhagwati Charan Vohra** is wrong — option **(3)**.
**Swadesh Sevak** = **G.D. Kumar**; Vohra wrote **The Philosophy of the Bomb**.
The other pairs are correct.
xa: **Talwar** = Chattopadhyay (Berlin Committee).
**Islamic Fraternity** = **Barkatullah** (Kabul government).
**Indian Sociologist** = Shyamji Krishna Varma.

206.s:
Which of the following statements about Alluri Sitarama Raju is correct?
1. He met Bengal revolutionaries at Chittagong in 1921.
2. He led the Rampa Rebellion from 1922 to 1924.
3. The rebellion opposed the Muttadari system and forest laws.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
206.x: All three statements are correct. Raju’s contact with Bengal revolutionaries preceded his leadership of the Rampa Rebellion against the Muttadari system and forest laws.

**1:** **Alluri Sitarama Raju** met Bengal revolutionaries at **Chittagong (1921)**.
**2:** He led the **Rampa Rebellion (1922-24)**.

Not linked to the INC, but troubled the British more than the **NCM**.

206.s: Who were the lieutenants associated with Alluri Sitarama Raju during the Rampa Rebellion?
o: Gam Mallu Dora and Gam Gantam Dora
206.x: Gam Mallu Dora and Gam Gantam Dora were associated with Alluri Sitarama Raju as lieutenants. Scott Coward and Haytes were officers killed during the rebellion.

xs: Raju's lieutenants were **Gam Mallu Dora and Gam Gantam Dora** — option **(2)**.

**Kanailal Dutta** and **Satyendranath Bose** shot the Alipore approver; **Sanyal** and **Jogesh Chatterjee** co-founded the **HRA**.

Raids: **Chintapalli** → **Krishnadevipeta** → **Rajavommangi**.

Alluri Sitarama Raju was killed on 7 May 1922.

Lieutenants: **Gam Mallu Dora**, **Gam Gantam Dora**.

206.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Tenali bomb case — Vande Mataram phase
2. Kakinada bomb case — Prativadi Bhayankaracharyulu
3. Darshi Chenchayya — Nenu Naa Desam

**2:** **Kakinada bomb case** — **Prativadi Bhayankaracharyulu** (**14 years** in the Andaman).

xs: The first attack was on **Chintapalli** police station (**22 Aug 1922**) — option **(3)**.
**Krishnadevipeta** and **Rajavommangi** were attacked **after** it.
**Panjerighat** was the site of a **direct battle**, not a police-station raid.
xa: Raju met Bengal revolutionaries at **Chittagong (1921)**.
Targets of the revolt: the **Muttadari system**, **forest laws**, **Tahsildar Bastian**.
Raju killed **7 May 1924**.

206.s: Which of the following chronological sequences is correct?
o: Kesari started → Khudiram executed → Curzon Wyllie killed → Al-Hilal started
Kesari started → Curzon Wyllie killed → Khudiram executed → Al-Hilal started
Khudiram executed → Kesari started → Curzon Wyllie killed → Al-Hilal started
Al-Hilal started → Kesari started → Khudiram executed → Curzon Wyllie killed
206.x: Kesari was started in 1881, Khudiram was executed in 1908, Curzon Wyllie was killed in 1909 and Al-Hilal was started in 1912.
206.tq: Anchor the sequence with the earliest newspaper and the latest newspaper.
xs: The sequence is **Kesari → Khudiram executed → Curzon Wyllie killed → Al-Hilal** — option **(1)** (UPPSC **2021**).
**Kesari** started **1881**; **Khudiram** hanged **11 August 1908**.
**Curzon Wyllie** killed **1909**; **Al-Hilal** started **1912**.
xa: Wyllie was shot in London by **Madan Lal Dhingra** (**1 July 1909**).
Khudiram (with **Prafulla Chaki**) targeted **Kingsford** at **Muzaffarpur** (**30 April 1908**).
**1912** also saw the **Hardinge bomb**.

206.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Formation of the Ghadar Party
B. Formation of the Hindustan Republican Association
C. Kakori action
D. Formation of the HSRA
206.x: The Ghadar Party was formed in 1913, the HRA in 1924, the Kakori action occurred in 1925 and the HSRA was formed in 1928.
206.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place HRA before Kakori.
xs: The order is **A, B, C, D** — option **(1)**.
xa: HRA founders: **Bismil, Jogesh Chatterjee, Sachindranath Sanyal** (Kanpur).
HSRA: **Chandrashekhar Azad**, Feroz Shah Kotla, Delhi.
Kakori: **Bismil, Ashfaqullah Khan, Roshan Singh, Rajendra Lahiri** hanged.
After: **1929 Assembly bomb → 1930 Chittagong → 1931 executions**.

206.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Hardinge bomb attack
B. Chapekars killed Rand
C. Nasik Conspiracy Case
D. Muzaffarpur Bomb Case
206.x: The Chapekars killed Rand in 1897, the Muzaffarpur Bomb Case occurred in 1908, the Nasik case in 1909 and the Hardinge attack in 1912.
206.tq: Use the years 1897, 1908, 1909 and 1912 to place the events.
xs: The order is **B, D, C, A** — option **(1)**.
**B:** **Chapekars killed Rand 1897**; **D:** **Muzaffarpur 1908**.
**C:** **Nasik 1909**; **A:** **Hardinge bomb 1912**.
xa: Nasik: **Anant Kanhere** killed **A.M.T. Jackson**; Savarkar implicated.
Hardinge bomb: planned by **Rash Behari Bose** + **Sachin Sanyal**.
Rand was the **Plague Commissioner** at **Poona**.

206.s: The revolutionary activities of the first phase of revolutionary nationalism assumed greater significance primarily because they:
o: established a broad-based Hindu-Muslim mass movement
ended the policy of revolutionary violence after the Surat Split
replaced constitutional agitation with participation in legislative councils
kept radical nationalism alive through individual heroic actions after the decline of mass Swadeshi
206.x: Individual heroic actions, including assassinations and ‘Swadeshi dacoities’, kept radical nationalism alive after the Surat Split and the failure of mass Swadeshi.
206.tq: Identify the central significance rather than an exaggerated consequence.
xs: It **kept radical nationalism alive through individual heroic actions after the decline of mass Swadeshi** — option **(4)**.
Actions included **assassinations** and **"swadeshi dacoities"**, after the **Surat Split** and the failure of mass Swadeshi.
It was **not a mass movement** and limited Muslim participation — so (1) is wrong.
xa: Criticism: **Hindu-revivalist symbolism** (worship of **Bhavani**).
Roots: **akhadas** and secret societies (**Anushilan**, **Atmonnati Samiti**).
Bengal journals **Yugantar** and **Sandhya** advocated violence.

206.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the limitations of the first phase of revolutionary nationalism:
1. It did not develop into a mass movement.
2. Its strong Hindu-revivalist symbolism restricted Muslim participation.
3. The worship of Bhavani was one expression of this symbolism.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
206.x: All three statements are correct. Revolutionary nationalism remained limited as a mass movement, and its Hindu-revivalist imagery, including the worship of Bhavani, restricted Muslim participation.
206.tq: Check each statement against the movement’s character and limitations.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**1:** It was **not a mass movement**.
**2 and 3:** Strongly **Hindu-revivalist symbolism** — the **worship of Bhavani** — limited **Muslim participation**.
xa: Its significance: it **kept radical nationalism alive** after the **Surat Split**.
Methods: **assassinations** and **"swadeshi dacoities"**.
**Alluri** was not linked to the INC but troubled the British more than the NCM.

206.s: With reference to the Tenali Bomb Case, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: It occurred on 6 April 1909 and involved an attempt to plant bombs for the Howrah Express near Tenali.
It occurred in February 1909 and concerned an attack on a police station at Rampa.
It occurred after the Non-Cooperation Movement and involved the Kakori train.
It occurred in 1913 and involved the Ghadar Party’s attack on a railway station.
206.x: The Tenali Bomb Case took place on 6 April 1909, when bombs were planted for the Howrah Express near Tenali.
206.tq: Use the exact date, place and target to distinguish closely related revolutionary cases.
xs: The **Tenali Bomb Case** occurred on **6 April 1909**, with bombs planted for the **Howrah Express** near **Tenali** — option **(1)**.
It belongs to the **Vande Mataram phase**, not the post-NCM or Ghadar periods.
**Rampa** was Alluri's rebellion (**1922-24**); **February 1909** is **Kotappakonda**.
xa: Accused: **Chukkapalli Ramayya**, **Lakkaraju Basavayya**, **Katamraju Venkatrayudu**.
Defended by **Tanguturi Prakasam**.
Ramayya + Basavayya were transported (some notes: Prakasam secured release).

206.s: The Kotappakonda incident of February 1909 is associated with which one of the following statements?
o: The Kakori train action was organised by the Hindustan Republican Association.
Chinnappa Reddy received the only death sentence of the Vandemataram movement.
Tanguturi Prakasam defended the accused in the Tenali Bomb Case.
A bomb was thrown at Viceroy Hardinge during his state entry into Delhi.
206.x: Kotappakonda, in Guntur, witnessed the case of Chinnappa Reddy, who received the only death sentence of the Vandemataram movement.
206.tq: Use the distinctive person–place–movement association.
xs: **Kotappakonda (Feb 1909, Guntur)**: **Chinnappa Reddy** received the **only death sentence** of the **Vandemataram movement** — option **(2)**.
**Prakasam** defending accused belongs to the **Tenali** case; **Kakori** and the **Hardinge** bomb are unrelated.
xa: **Tenali Bomb Case**: **6 April 1909**.
**Kakinada bomb case**: **Prativadi Bhayankaracharyulu** (**14 years** in the Andaman).
Andhra's Ghadar link: **Darshi Chenchayya**.

206.s: Which one of the following statements correctly reflects the relationship of Alluri Sitarama Raju with the Indian National Congress and the Non-Cooperation Movement?
o: He founded the Indian National Congress and opposed all armed resistance.
He was a member of the Ghadar Party and organised the Komagata Maru voyage.
He was not linked to the Indian National Congress, but his struggle troubled the British more than the Non-Cooperation Movement.
He was formally linked to the Indian National Congress and led the Non-Cooperation Movement in Andhra.
206.x: Alluri Sitarama Raju was not linked to the Indian National Congress; nevertheless, his armed struggle troubled the British more than the Non-Cooperation Movement.
206.tq: Test the contrast between formal Congress association and the impact of the armed struggle.
xs: Raju was **not linked to the Indian National Congress**, but **troubled the British more than the Non-Cooperation Movement** — option **(3)**.
He was not a Ghadarite and did not organise the **Komagata Maru** (**1914**) — so (2) is wrong.
xa: He met Bengal revolutionaries at **Chittagong (1921)**.
**Rampa Rebellion (1922-24)** against the **Muttadari system** and forest laws.
**Malabar Special Police** were brought in; Raju killed **7 May 1924**.

206.s: Madam Bhikaji Cama was associated with which of the following?
206.x: Madam Bhikaji Cama worked for revolutionary nationalism abroad and unfurled an Indian flag at Stuttgart in 1907. Congress Radio was Usha Mehta's work.
206.tq: Recall Bhikaji Cama's role abroad.
n: Madam Bhikaji Cama was associated with revolutionary nationalism. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #120 · pp 218-221]
Madam Bhikaji Cama was associated with foreign propaganda. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #120 · pp 218-221]
xs: **Madam Bhikaji Cama** is associated with **revolutionary nationalism** abroad and **foreign propaganda** — option **(1)**.
She **unfurled the Indian flag** at **Stuttgart**, **1907**.
xa: **Madan Lal Dhingra** killed **Curzon Wyllie** in **1909**.
**Berlin Committee** (**1915**): **Virendranath Chattopadhyaya**, **Bhupendranath Dutta**.
**Komagata Maru** (**1914**): **376** passengers refused entry to **Canada**.

206.s: V.D. Savarkar was associated with which of the following?
206.x: V.D. Savarkar founded Abhinav Bharat in 1904. The HRA, HSRA and Assembly bombing belong to other revolutionaries.
206.tq: Recall Savarkar's organisation.
n: V.D. Savarkar was associated with revolutionary nationalism. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #120 · pp 218-221]
xs: **V.D. Savarkar** founded **Abhinav Bharat** — option **(2)**.
**Mitra Mela** (Nasik, **1899**) was renamed **Abhinav Bharat** (**1904**) (**APPSC 2018, 2019**).
**HRA** (**1924**) — **Bismil**, **Chatterjee**, **Sanyal**; **HSRA** (**1928**) — **Chandrashekhar Azad**; **Assembly bomb** (**1929**) — **Bhagat Singh**, **Batukeshwar Dutt**.
xa: Savarkar's books: **The Indian War of Independence, 1857** (**1909**) and **Hindutva** (**1923**).
Arrested in London (**1910**); failed escape at **Marseilles**; **life in the Andamans**.
In London he worked from **India House** (**Shyamji Krishna Varma**).

207.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India House was founded in London in 1905 by Shyamji Krishnavarma.
2. Madan Lal Dhingra, of the India House circle, shot Sir William Curzon Wyllie in London on 1 July 1909.
3. India House was founded by Madame Bhikaji Cama as the Paris Indian Society.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
207.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Shyamji Krishnavarma founded India House (also the Indian Home Rule Society) in London in 1905, and Dhingra shot Curzon Wyllie on 1 July 1909. Statement 3 is wrong: Cama's Paris Indian Society was a separate body. So B, C and D, which include statement 3, are wrong.
207.tq: India House = Krishnavarma, London; Paris Indian Society = Cama.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
**1:** **India House** was founded by **Shyamji Krishnavarma** in **London, 1905** (also the **Indian Home Rule Society**).
**2:** **Dhingra** shot **Curzon Wyllie** in London on **1 July 1909**.
**3** wrong: **Bhikaji Cama's Paris Indian Society** (**1905**) was a separate body.
xa: India House hub: **Savarkar, Har Dayal, Madan Lal Dhingra**.
Dhingra was hanged at **Pentonville**.
Cama hoisted the first Indian flag at **Stuttgart** (**22 August 1907**).

207.s: Who among the following was associated with India House along with V.D. Savarkar and Lala Hardayal?
207.x: Madan Lal Dhingra was associated with India House along with Savarkar and Hardayal. Dhingra killed Curzon Wyllie in 1909.
207.tq: Identify the India House association without confusing it with the Berlin Committee or Kabul government.
xs: **Madan Lal Dhingra** was the third member of the India House hub — option **(2)**.
**Bhupendranath Dutta** belonged to the **Berlin Committee**; **Mahendra Pratap** and **Obaidullah Sindhi** to the **Kabul government**.
xa: Dhingra shot **Curzon Wyllie** (**1 July 1909**); hanged at **Pentonville**.
India House founder: **Shyamji Krishnavarma** (**1905**).
Har Dayal later founded the **Ghadar Party** (**1913**).

207.s: Madame Bhikaji Cama hoisted the first Indian national flag at the International Socialist Congress held at:
207.x: Madame Bhikaji Cama hoisted the flag at the International Socialist Congress in Stuttgart, Germany.
207.tq: Distinguish the city of the flag event from the city of publication.
xs: Cama hoisted the first Indian flag at **Stuttgart (Germany)** — option **(4)**.
Occasion: the **International Socialist Congress**, **22 August 1907**.
**Paris** was the base of her **Paris Indian Society** and **Bande Mataram**, not the flag venue.
xa: **Paris Indian Society**: **1905**.
Her **Bande Mataram** came out from **Paris** (Paris/Geneva).
⚠ The Calcutta **Bande Mataram (1906)** was **Bipin Chandra Pal's**.

207.s: Madame Bhikaji Cama brought out *Bande Mataram* from:
207.x: Madame Bhikaji Cama brought out *Bande Mataram* from Paris and was associated with the Paris Indian Society.
207.tq: Separate the publication city from the congress city.
xs: Cama brought out **Bande Mataram** from **Paris** — option **(3)**.
She led the **Paris Indian Society (1905)**.
**London** = India House (**Indian Sociologist**); **Berlin** = **Talwar**; **San Francisco** = **Ghadar**.
xa: ⚠ Do not confuse with **Bipin Chandra Pal's** Calcutta **Bande Mataram (1906)**.
Flag at **Stuttgart**, **22 August 1907**.
Other journals abroad: **Islamic Fraternity** (Barkatullah), **Swadesh Sevak** (G.D. Kumar).

207.s: The word ‘Ghadar’ denotes which of the following?
207.x: ‘Ghadar’ means mutiny or rebellion, reflecting the revolutionary character of the organisation.
207.tq: Test the exact meaning of a movement’s name.
xs: **"Ghadar"** means **mutiny/rebellion** — option **(3)**.
The name reflects the party's aim of revolt against British rule.
xa: Founded **1913** in the USA; first meeting in **Oregon**.
HQ: **Yugantar Ashram, San Francisco**.
Members: mostly **Punjabi Sikh immigrants** in North America.
Planned revolt: **21 February 1915**.

207.s: The members of the Ghadar Party were predominantly drawn from which group?
o: Punjabi Sikh immigrants in North America
207.x: The Ghadar Party drew most of its members from Punjabi Sikh immigrants living in North America.
207.tq: Identify the organisation’s principal social base.
xs: Ghadar members were mostly **Punjabi Sikh immigrants in North America** — option **(1)**.
The party was founded in the **USA** in **1913** (first meeting in **Oregon**).
xa: Founders: **Lala Har Dayal, Sohan Singh Bhakna, Kartar Singh Sarabha, Bhagwan Singh**.
First president: **Sohan Singh Bhakna**; Har Dayal = moving spirit/secretary.
**Darsi Chenchayya** = first and only **Telugu** member.

207.s:
Consider the following statements about the Ghadar Party:
1. Its headquarters was the Yugantar Ashram at San Francisco.
2. Sohan Singh Bhakna was its first president.
3. Lala Har Dayal was its first president and Kartar Singh Sarabha its secretary.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
207.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the HQ was Yugantar Ashram, San Francisco, and Sohan Singh Bhakna was the first president (he called Sarabha his 'General'). Statement 3 is wrong: Har Dayal was the moving spirit/secretary, not president. So A (omits 2), C and D (include 3) are wrong.
207.tq: Ghadar: President Bhakna, secretary Har Dayal.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
**1:** HQ = **Yugantar Ashram, San Francisco**.
**2:** **Sohan Singh Bhakna** was the **first president**.
**3** wrong: **Har Dayal** was the **moving spirit/secretary**, not president; Sarabha was Bhakna's "General".
xa: Other founders: **Bhagwan Singh**, **Baba Harnam Singh (Tundilat)**, **Pt. Kanshi Ram**.
**Kartar Singh Sarabha** edited the **Punjabi Ghadar**.
First meeting: **Oregon**, **1913**.

207.s: Which one of the following was actively associated with the Ghadar rising?
207.x: Rash Behari Bose was actively associated with the Ghadar rising (UPSC 2022). Barindra Kumar Ghosh and Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee were not, and Bipin Chandra Pal was associated with the Calcutta Bande Mataram, not the Ghadar.
207.tq: UPSC 2022: only Rash Behari Bose linked to Ghadar.
xs: **Rash Behari Bose** was actively associated with the **Ghadar rising** — option **(3)**.
⚠ **Barindra Kumar Ghosh** and **Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee** were **not** (UPSC **2022**).
**Bipin Chandra Pal** is linked to the Calcutta **Bande Mataram (1906)**.
xa: Rising planned for **21 February 1915** in Punjab.
**Betrayed by informers**; **45 leaders hanged** under the Defence of India Act.
**Kartar Singh Sarabha** executed **16 November 1915**, aged **19**.

207.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Ghadar Conspiracy of 1915:
1. A pan-India revolt in the British Indian Army was planned.
2. The planned date of the uprising was 21 February 1915.
3. The uprising was successfully carried through without betrayal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
207.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because informers betrayed the plan and the uprising was crushed.
207.tq: Spot the false statement created by reversing the outcome of an event.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
**1:** a **pan-India revolt in the British Indian Army** was planned.
**2:** date fixed: **21 February 1915**.
**3** wrong: it was **betrayed by informers** and crushed.
xa: **45 leaders hanged** under the **Defence of India Act**.
**First Lahore Conspiracy Case**: Sarabha executed with **Vishnu Ganesh Pingle**.
The **Komagata Maru (1914)** had accelerated the movement.

207.s: The passengers of the Komagata Maru were denied entry into Canada primarily because of which rule?
207.x: Canada denied entry under racist immigration laws, particularly the ‘continuous journey’ rule.
207.tq: Identify the exact legal or administrative basis of exclusion.
xs: Entry was denied under the **"continuous journey" rule** — option **(3)**.
It was part of Canada's **racist immigration laws**.
xa: Ship: **Japanese**, chartered by **Gurdit Singh**; **376** passengers.
Forced back → **Budge Budge** police firing near Calcutta.
Apology: **Justin Trudeau**, House of Commons, **2016**.

207.s: Who chartered the Komagata Maru?
207.x: Gurdit Singh, a Punjabi businessman, chartered the Japanese ship Komagata Maru.
207.tq: Separate the organiser of the voyage from later revolutionary leaders.
xs: The ship was chartered by **Gurdit Singh**, a **Punjabi businessman** — option **(2)**.
**Barkatullah** and **Mahendra Pratap** led the **Kabul government**; **Taraknath Das** ran **United India House**, Seattle.
xa: Route: **Singapore** → East Asian ports → **Vancouver** (**1914**).
Impact: radicalised immigrants and **accelerated the Ghadar movement**.
**Budge Budge (Sept 1914)** firing killed **19** passengers.

207.s: Kartar Singh Sarabha, executed on 16 November 1915 at the age of 19, was sentenced in which case?
207.x: Sarabha was executed in the First Lahore Conspiracy Case (with Vishnu Ganesh Pingle) after the failed Ghadar rising. The Delhi case (1912) concerned the Hardinge bomb, Kakori (1925) the HRA train action and Alipore (1908) the Maniktala bomb factory.
207.tq: Ghadar 1915 → First Lahore Conspiracy Case → Sarabha hanged at 19.
xs: Sarabha was executed in the **First Lahore Conspiracy Case** — option **(2)**.
Executed **16 November 1915**, aged **19**, with **Vishnu Ganesh Pingle**.
It followed the betrayed **Ghadar rising** of **21 February 1915**.
xa: Sarabha edited the **Punjabi edition of Ghadar**.
Born **24 May 1896**, **Sarabha, Ludhiana**.
Bhakna called him his **"General"**.

207.s:
Consider the following statements about the Berlin Committee (Indian Independence Committee):
1. It was set up in Berlin in 1915.
2. It sought French and Russian support for constitutional reforms in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
207.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Berlin Committee was formed in Berlin in 1915 (Virendranath Chattopadhyaya, Bhupendranath Dutta). Statement 2 is wrong: it sought German and Turkish help to invade India. So 2 only, both and neither are wrong.
207.tq: Berlin Committee = Germany + Turkey, WWI, 1915.
xs: Only **statement 1** is correct — option **(1)**.
**1:** The **Berlin Committee** was set up in **Berlin, 1915** (**Virendranath Chattopadhyaya, Bhupendranath Dutta**).
**2** wrong: it sought **German and Turkish** help **to invade India**, not French/Russian support for reforms.
xa: Also called the **Indian Independence Committee**.
Chattopadhyay edited **Talwar**.
Har Dayal also joined the **Berlin effort**.

207.s: Which of the following correctly represents the offices in the Provisional Government of India at Kabul?
o: Raja Mahendra Pratap—President; Maulana Barkatullah—Prime Minister
Obaidullah Sindhi—President; Raja Mahendra Pratap—Prime Minister
Raja Mahendra Pratap—Prime Minister; Obaidullah Sindhi—President
207.x: Raja Mahendra Pratap was President and Maulana Barkatullah was Prime Minister; Obaidullah Sindhi was also associated with the government.
207.tq: Check office–person assignments rather than recognising names alone.
xs: **Raja Mahendra Pratap = President**; **Maulana Barkatullah = Prime Minister** — option **(1)**.
**Obaidullah Sindhi** was the third member.
Formed at **Kabul** in **1915**.
xa: Backers: **Germany and Turkey**, with help from the **Afghan Crown Prince**.
Barkatullah edited **Islamic Fraternity**.
UPPSC **2022** order: Ghadar (**1913**) → Berlin (**1915**) → Assembly bomb (**1929**) → Chittagong (**1930**).

207.s:
Consider the following statements about M.N. Roy:
1. He wrote 'India in Transition'.
2. He brought out 'Vanguard', regarded as India's first communist newspaper.
3. He founded the Communist Party of India at Kanpur in 1920.
4. He later founded the Radical Democratic Party.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
207.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct: Roy wrote India in Transition, brought out Vanguard and later founded the Radical Democratic Party. Statement 3 is wrong: Roy founded the CPI at Tashkent in 1920; the Kanpur formation (26 Dec 1925) is the date the CPI recognises. So B, C and D, which include statement 3, are wrong.
207.tq: Tashkent 1920 (Roy) vs Kanpur 1925 - don't mix the place and year.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 4 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
**1:** **India in Transition**; **2:** **Vanguard**, India's first communist newspaper.
**3** wrong: Roy founded the CPI at **Tashkent (1920)**; **Kanpur (26 Dec 1925)** is the date the CPI recognises.
**4:** He later founded the **Radical Democratic Party**.
xa: ⚠ **Tashkent 1920** = CPI(M)'s date; **Kanpur 1925** = CPI's date.
Roy also founded the **Communist Party of Mexico**.
Associated with the **Radical Humanist** movement.

207.s: Besides the Communist Party of India at Tashkent (1920), M.N. Roy is credited with founding the Communist Party of:
207.x: M.N. Roy founded the Communist Party of Mexico before founding the CPI at Tashkent in 1920. He did not found the communist parties of China, Germany or Indonesia.
207.tq: M.N. Roy: Mexico, then Tashkent 1920.
xs: Roy also founded the **Communist Party of Mexico** — option **(1)**.
His Indian party: **CPI at Tashkent (1920)**.
xa: CPI recognises the **Kanpur** formation (**26 Dec 1925**).
Newspaper **Vanguard**; book **India in Transition**.
Later: **Radical Democratic Party**.

207.s: The newspaper *Indian Sociologist* was published by Shyamji Krishnavarma from which place?
207.x: Shyamji Krishnavarma published *Indian Sociologist* from London, in association with India House.
207.tq: Use the person–publication–place association.
xs: **Indian Sociologist** was published from **London (India House)** — option **(4)**.
**Paris/Geneva** = Cama's **Bande Mataram**; **Berlin** = **Talwar**.
xa: India House founded **1905** by **Shyamji Krishnavarma**.
APPSC-G1 **2022** matched **Indian Sociologist — Krishnavarma**.
Also linked: the **Indian Home Rule Society**.

207.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
207.x: *Swadesh Sevak* was associated with G.D. Kumar, not Bipin Chandra Pal. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
207.tq: Find the swapped person–newspaper pair.
xs: **Swadesh Sevak — Bipin Chandra Pal** is wrong — option **(4)**.
**Swadesh Sevak** = **G.D. (Guru Dutt) Kumar** (Vancouver).
The others are correct: **Islamic Fraternity** — **Barkatullah**; **Bande Mataram** — **Cama**; **Talwar** — **Chattopadhyay**.
xa: APPSC-G1 **2022** matched these four journals.
Pal's paper was the Calcutta **Bande Mataram (1906)**.
G.D. Kumar also ran **United India House**, Seattle, with **Taraknath Das**.

207.s: The Punjabi edition of *Ghadar* was edited by whom?
207.x: Kartar Singh Sarabha edited the Punjabi edition of *Ghadar*. *Ghadar di Goonj* consisted of poetry associated with the movement.
207.tq: Distinguish the publication’s editor from the organisation’s founders.
xs: The **Punjabi edition of Ghadar** was edited by **Kartar Singh Sarabha** — option **(3)**.
The paper itself was the **Ghadar Party's** under **Har Dayal**, San Francisco.
xa: **Ghadar di Goonj** = its **poetry**.
Sarabha executed **16 November 1915**, aged **19**.
**Sohan Singh Bhakna** = first president.

207.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes the two publications named Bande Mataram?
o: The Calcutta publication was associated with Bipin Chandra Pal, whereas the publication abroad was associated with Madame Bhikaji Cama.
The Calcutta publication was associated with Shyamji Krishnavarma, whereas the publication abroad was associated with Virendranath Chattopadhyay.
Both were published by Bipin Chandra Pal in Calcutta.
Both were published by Madame Bhikaji Cama in Paris.
207.x: The Calcutta *Bande Mataram* of 1906 was associated with Bipin Chandra Pal, while Madame Bhikaji Cama brought out *Bande Mataram* abroad.
207.tq: Separate similar titles by their place and associated person.
xs: The Calcutta **Bande Mataram** was **Bipin Chandra Pal's**; the one abroad was **Madame Bhikaji Cama's** — option **(1)**.
Calcutta edition: **1906**; Cama's: **Paris/Geneva**.
xa: ⚠ A classic trap — two papers with the same name.
Cama led the **Paris Indian Society (1905)**.
Shyamji Krishnavarma's paper: **Indian Sociologist**.

207.s: Which pair of leaders was associated with the Berlin Committee?
o: Raja Mahendra Pratap and Obaidullah Sindhi
Gurdit Singh and Sohan Singh Bhakna
Shyamji Krishnavarma and Madan Lal Dhingra
207.x: Virendranath Chattopadhyaya and Bhupendranath Dutta were associated with the Berlin Committee.
207.tq: Match an organisation with its leading figures.
xs: The **Berlin Committee** = **Virendranath Chattopadhyaya** and **Bhupendranath Dutta** — option **(1)**.
**Mahendra Pratap** and **Obaidullah Sindhi** = **Kabul government**; **Gurdit Singh** = **Komagata Maru**; **Krishnavarma** and **Dhingra** = **India House**.
xa: Berlin, **1915**; sought **German and Turkish** help.
Also called the **Indian Independence Committee**.

restricted revolutionary activities to social reform organisations
ended the activities of Indian revolutionaries outside India

**Ghadar Conspiracy**: revolt planned for **21 February 1915**.

207.s: Which one of the following descriptions correctly identifies Darsi Chenchayya?

The first and only Telugu member of the Ghadar Party

**First and only Telugu member** of the Ghadar Party.

**Ghadar Party**: **San Francisco**, **1913**; HQ **Yugantar Ashram**.
**Swadesh Sevak** — **G.D. Kumar**.

**Indian Sociologist** — **Shyamji Krishnavarma**, London.

208.s: Annie Besant was styled as the:
208.x: Annie Besant was styled the “Iron Lady of Ireland.” She was of Irish origin and later became a prominent Indian nationalist leader.
208.tq: Test the title-person association without confusing Besant's title with titles associated with Indian leaders.
xs: Annie Besant was styled the **"Iron Lady of Ireland"** — option **(3)**.
She was born on **1 October 1847** at **Clapham, London**, of **Irish origin**.
xa: In England she was a **Fabian socialist** (Fabian Society).
Joined the **Theosophical Society (1888)**; came to India in **1893**; TS **President in 1907**.

First woman **INC president (1917)**.

208.s: Which of the following pairs relating to Tilak's newspapers is correctly matched?
208.x: Tilak founded or edited Kesari as a Marathi paper and Mahratta as an English paper; both are associated with the year 1881.

xa: Tilak's slogan: **"Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it"**.
Besant's papers: **Common Weal (January 1914)** and **New India** (renamed **Madras Standard**).
Tilak born **23 July 1856, Ratnagiri**.

208.s: The Central Hindu College founded by Annie Besant in 1898 was located at
208.x: Annie Besant founded the Central Hindu College at Varanasi in 1898. It later became the core of Banaras Hindu University under Madan Mohan Malaviya.
208.tq: Distinguish the two institutions by their locations.
xs: Besant's **Central Hindu College (1898)** was at **Varanasi** — option **(2)**.
It became the core of **BHU** under **Madan Mohan Malaviya**.
xa: APPSC-GS **2019**: TS President **1907**, first woman INC president **1917**, Central Hindu College **1898** — all correct.
**Madanapalle college** is cited for Home Rule strength in Andhra.
Besant came to India in **1893**.

208.s: Annie Besant renamed the Madras Standard as New India after purchasing it in:
208.x: Annie Besant purchased the Madras Standard in July 1914 and renamed it New India. New India was a daily newspaper.
208.tq: Use the exact month and the newspaper's earlier name as the discriminating clues.
xs: Besant bought the **Madras Standard** in **July 1914** and renamed it **New India** — option **(3)**.
**January 1914** was her English weekly **Common Weal**.
**April/September 1916** were the founding months of the two **Home Rule Leagues**.
xa: APPSC G2 **2025** asked this twice.
⚠ Tilak was released on **16 June 1914** — the same summer.

208.s: Who described Bal Gangadhar Tilak as the 'Father of Indian Unrest'?
208.x: British journalist Valentine Chirol called Tilak the 'Father of Indian Unrest'. Curzon, Montagu and Minto were British officials who did not coin this title; Minto is called 'Father of the Communal Electorate'.
208.tq: Father of Indian Unrest = Tilak, per Valentine Chirol.
xs: British journalist **Valentine Chirol** called Tilak the **"Father of Indian Unrest"** — option **(2)**.
Tilak's popular title was **"Lokmanya"**.
**Montagu** is linked to the **August Declaration (1917)**; **Minto** is the **"Father of the Communal Electorate"**.
xa: Tilak started **Kesari** and **Mahratta** (**1881**).
He made **Ganeshotsav (1893)** and **Shivaji festival (1895)** public.
His Home Rule League: **28 April 1916**.

208.s:
With reference to Annie Besant, consider the following statements:
1. She became President of the Theosophical Society in 1907.
2. She was the first woman President of the Indian National Congress (1917).
3. She first came to India in 1907.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
208.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct (APPSC-GS 2019): she became TS President in 1907 and was the first woman INC President at Calcutta in 1917. Statement 3 is wrong: she came to India in 1893. So B, C and D, which include statement 3, are wrong.
208.tq: Besant: India 1893, CHC 1898, TS President 1907, INC President 1917.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)** (APPSC-GS **2019**).
**1:** She became **President of the Theosophical Society in 1907**.
**2:** First woman **INC President (1917)**, Calcutta.
**3** wrong: she came to India in **1893**, not 1907.
xa: Joined the TS in **1888** (**1889** in many texts).
Founded **Central Hindu College (1898)**.
Interned at **Ootacamund**, **15 June 1917**.

208.s: The All India Home Rule League of Annie Besant was founded in:
208.x: Annie Besant's All India Home Rule League was founded in Madras in September 1916. Its headquarters was at Adyar, in Gokhale Hall.
208.tq: Discriminate between the two Leagues by separating their founding places and dates.
xs: Besant's **All India Home Rule League** was founded in **Madras** in **September 1916** — option **(1)**.
HQ: **Adyar** (**Gokhale Hall**).
**Belgaum/Poona, April 1916** = **Tilak's** league.
xa: ⚠ Some notes say **1915** — her self-government campaign began then; the league itself = **Sept 1916**.
Organising secretary: **George Arundale**; ~**200 branches**.
Covered the rest of India, **including Bombay city**.

208.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the territorial jurisdiction of Tilak's Home Rule League?
o: Madras Presidency, Bengal and Assam only
Bombay city, Madras and the Central Provinces
Maharashtra excluding Bombay city, Karnataka, Central Provinces and Berar
The whole of India including Bombay city

xs: Tilak's league covered **Maharashtra (excluding Bombay city), Karnataka, Central Provinces and Berar** — option **(3)**.
**Besant's** league covered the rest of India, **including Bombay city**.
xa: Tilak's league: launched at **Belgaum** (Bombay Provincial Conference), based at **Poona**.
President **Joseph Baptista**; Secretary **N.C. Kelkar**.
Tilak's league was **better organised**; Besant's reached a **wider audience**.

208.s:

2. Besant's League had approximately 200 branches.

xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
**1:** Besant's league covered the rest of India, **including Bombay city**.

xs: Besant was interned at **Ootacamund** — option **(2)**.
With **B.P. Wadia** and **G.S. Arundale**, on **15 June 1917**.

Montagu's remark: **"Shiva cut his wife into fifty-two pieces..."**.

3. Besant was released under pressure from the Congress and the Muslim League.

208.tq: Combine the cause, political effect and release mechanism in a three-statement question.

**1:** Outrage **boosted the movement**.
**2:** It **drew in Moderates**.
**3:** Released (**17 September 1917**) under **INC-League pressure**.
xa: Interned at **Ootacamund** on **15 June 1917**.
**Montagu** commented on the folly of the internment.
Tenali and Vijayawada held **"Confinement Day"** protests.

208.s:
Consider the following statements about the Montagu (August) Declaration of 20 August 1917:
1. It was announced by Lord Chelmsford, the Viceroy.
2. It was the British answer to the Home Rule agitation and effectively blunted it.
3. It led towards the Government of India Act, 1919.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
208.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct: the Declaration answered the Home Rule agitation, blunted and effectively ended it, and led to the 1919 Act. Statement 1 is wrong: it was announced by Edwin Montagu, the Secretary of State; Chelmsford was the Viceroy. So A, C and D, which include statement 1, are wrong.
208.tq: August Declaration = Montagu (Secretary of State), not Chelmsford (Viceroy).
xs: Statements **2 and 3 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
**1** wrong: the declaration was by **Edwin Montagu, Secretary of State**; **Chelmsford** was the **Viceroy**.
**2:** It was the British answer to Home Rule and **blunted and effectively ended** the agitation.
**3:** It led to the **1919 Act**.
xa: Date: **20 August 1917**.
Goal: **"progressive realisation of responsible government"**.
Congress split over Mont-Ford proposals at **Bombay (Aug 1918)** under **Hasan Imam**.

o: Immediate complete independence from British rule
Progressive realisation of responsible government through self-governing institutions
Introduction of separate electorates for all communities

Also: **increasing Indian association** in administration.
It did not promise independence; **separate electorates** were a **1909** feature.
xa: Announced by **Edwin Montagu** on **20 August 1917**.
It led to the **1919 Act**.
It raised Andhra's hopes for a **separate province**.

208.s: The demand raised by the Andhra delegation before Montagu in December 1917 primarily concerned:
o: The transfer of the capital to Delhi
The formation of the Swarajya Sabha

208.tq: Infer the regional political objective from the delegation's context.
xs: The Andhra delegation sought a **separate Andhra province** — option **(1)**.
Led by **Nyapati Subba Rao**, it met Montagu on **20 Dec 1917**.
The **Montagu Declaration** had raised these hopes.
xa: Declaration date: **20 August 1917**.
**Swarajya Sabha** came only in **1920**.
Andhra had **52 Home Rule branches by 1917**.

208.s: The Surat split of 1907 between the Moderates and Extremists was healed at:
208.x: The split that occurred at Surat in 1907 was healed at the Lucknow session in 1916.

xs: The **Surat split (1907)** was healed at **Lucknow in 1916** — option **(2)**.
**Bombay 1918** was the **Hasan Imam** special session where Congress split again over Mont-Ford proposals.

o: The formation of the Indian National Liberal Federation alone
Tilak and Besant's efforts, along with the deaths of Gokhale and Pherozeshah Mehta

xs: Reunion was eased by **Tilak and Besant's efforts** and the **deaths of Gokhale and Pherozeshah Mehta** — option **(4)**.
Both deaths came in **1915**.
The **Montagu Declaration** (**1917**) and **1919 Act** came after Lucknow — so (2) is wrong.

Tilak's remark on the Pact: **"Better two united fists than a thousand scattered fingers"**.

o: Besant's League merged into Tilak's League and remained independent.
Tilak's League merged into Besant's League; in 1920 it was renamed Swarajya Sabha under Gandhi and later merged into the Congress.

xa: Besant's league HQ: **Adyar** (Gokhale Hall).
**1920**: **Non-Cooperation** launched.
Significance: filled the gap between **Gokhale's death (1915)** and **Gandhi's rise (1920)**.

208.s: The remark about Shiva cutting his wife into fifty-two pieces, in the context of Annie Besant's internment, was made by
208.x: Edwin Montagu used the remark while commenting on the folly of Annie Besant's internment.
208.tq: Avoid swapping the British official with Indian nationalist leaders.
xs: The Shiva remark was **Edwin Montagu's** — option **(2)**.
It mocked the **folly of Besant's internment**.
xa: Besant interned **15 June 1917**, **Ootacamund**.
Montagu, **Secretary of State**, issued the **August Declaration (20 August 1917)**.
The internment **boosted** the movement.

208.s:
Which of the following events took place in 1915?
1. Gandhi returned from South Africa.
2. Gokhale died.
3. Tilak's Home Rule League was established.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
208.x: Gandhi returned from South Africa on 9 January 1915 and Gokhale died in 1915. Tilak's Home Rule League was established in April 1916.
208.tq: Reject the statement shifted from 1915 to 1916.
xs: **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)**.
**1:** **Gandhi returned** from South Africa in **1915** (**9 Jan**).
**2:** **Gokhale died** in **1915**.
**3** wrong: Tilak's league came on **28 April 1916**.
xa: **Pherozeshah Mehta** also died in **1915**.
**1916**: Besant's league (Sept); **Lucknow Pact** (Dec).
**1914**: Besant's **Common Weal** and **New India**.

208.s: Which one of the following chronological sequences is correct?
o: Tilak's Home Rule League → Besant's Home Rule League → Lucknow Pact → Montagu Declaration
Besant's Home Rule League → Tilak's Home Rule League → Montagu Declaration → Lucknow Pact
Lucknow Pact → Tilak's Home Rule League → Besant's Home Rule League → Montagu Declaration
Tilak's Home Rule League → Lucknow Pact → Besant's Home Rule League → Montagu Declaration
208.x: Tilak's League was formed in April 1916, Besant's in September 1916, the Lucknow Pact was concluded in December 1916, and the Montagu Declaration was issued in August 1917.
208.tq: Place events within the same year by their months.
xs: The sequence is **Tilak's league → Besant's league → Lucknow Pact → Montagu Declaration** — option **(1)**.
**April 1916** → **September 1916** → **December 1916** → **20 August 1917**.
xa: **15 June 1917**: Besant interned.
**Aug 1918**: Bombay special session (**Hasan Imam**).
**1920**: **Swarajya Sabha**; **Non-Cooperation**.

208.s: Which one of the following pairs of quotation and leader is NOT correctly matched?
o: "Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it" — B.G. Tilak
"First we are Indians, then only Muslims" — M.A. Jinnah
"Better two united fists than a thousand scattered fingers" — Annie Besant
"Shiva cut his wife into fifty-two pieces..." — Edwin Montagu
208.x: "Better two united fists than a thousand scattered fingers" was Tilak's remark on the Lucknow Pact, not Besant's. The Swaraj slogan was Tilak's, the 'first we are Indians' line Jinnah's, and the Shiva remark Montagu's on Besant's internment.
208.tq: Both 'Swaraj' and 'two united fists' = Tilak.
xs: The mismatch is **"Better two united fists..." — Annie Besant** — option **(3)**; it was **Tilak's** remark on the **Lucknow Pact**.
The others are correct: Swaraj slogan — **Tilak**; "First we are Indians" — **Jinnah**; Shiva remark — **Montagu**.
xa: Montagu's remark referred to **Besant's internment** (**1917**).
Jinnah popularised Home Rule in **UP**.
Tilak's titles: **"Lokmanya"**, **"Father of Indian Unrest"**.

208.s: Which one of the following best explains the historical significance of the Home Rule Movement?
o: It restricted nationalist activity to the major presidency towns.
It replaced the Congress permanently with the Muslim League.
It ended all political work until the Non-Cooperation Movement.
It filled the gap between Gokhale's death and Gandhi's rise, while preparing cadres and organisations for later mass politics.
208.x: The movement bridged the period between Gokhale's death in 1915 and Gandhi's rise in 1920, built countryside organisation and trained cadres who later participated in Gandhian movements.
208.tq: Choose the option that combines the movement's transitional, organisational and preparatory roles.
xs: Home Rule **filled the gap between Gokhale's death and Gandhi's rise** and **prepared cadres** — option **(4)**.
Gokhale died in **1915**; Gandhi rose in **1920**.
It built **organisation in the countryside** and trained later **Gandhian cadres**.
xa: It **shifted the movement from elite to masses**, linking town and country.
It ended with the **Montagu Declaration**, which blunted the agitation.
League renamed **Swarajya Sabha** (**1920**) under Gandhi.

208.s: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 is significant in the history of communal politics because the Congress:
o: Rejected all forms of communal representation
208.x: Through the Lucknow Pact, the Congress accepted separate electorates for Muslims.
208.tq: Distinguish acceptance from later rejection or extension of a constitutional device.
xs: At Lucknow the Congress **accepted separate electorates for Muslims** — option **(3)**.
It accepted what it had **opposed in 1909** (Morley-Minto).
xa: **Lucknow 1916** also reunited **Moderates and Extremists**.
Tilak: **"Better two united fists than a thousand scattered fingers"**.
Reunion eased by deaths of **Gokhale** and **Pherozeshah Mehta (1915)**.

208.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Vande Matram was an English nationalist paper associated with Aurobindo.
New India was associated with Gandhi and non-violence.
New India was associated with Annie Besant and Home Rule.
208.x: Option C is incorrect: New India was Annie Besant's Home Rule paper, while Gandhi ran Young India. Tilak's Kesari and Aurobindo's English paper Vande Matram are right.
208.tq: Discriminate New India from Young India.
n: Tilak was associated with Kesari. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 45-46]
Kesari was a Marathi newspaper. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 45-46]
Gandhi was associated with Young India. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 45-46]
Young India was associated with non-violence. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 45-46]
Annie Besant was associated with New India. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 45-46]
New India was associated with Home Rule. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 45-46]
Aurobindo was associated with Vande Matram. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 45-46]
Vande Matram was an English weekly. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 45-46]
xs: The incorrect statement links **New India** with **Gandhi and non-violence** — option **(3)**.
**New India** was **Annie Besant**'s English paper of the **Home Rule movement** (also linked with **Bipin Chandra Pal**).
Correct: **Kesari** — **Tilak**; **Vande Matram** — an **English nationalist paper** of **Aurobindo**; **New India** — **Besant** and **Home Rule**.
xa: Besant bought the **Madras Standard** (July **1914**) and renamed it New India (**APPSC G2 2025**).
Besant's other paper: **The Commonweal** (**January 1914**).
Kesari (**Marathi**) and **Mahratta** (**English**) both date to **1881**.

208.s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Madan Mohan Malviya
(b) Firoz Shah Mehta
(c) T. M. Nair
(d) Sachidanand Sinha

List-II
(i) The Leader
(ii) Bombay Chronicle
(iii) Justice
(iv) Searchlight
208.x: The Leader is linked with Madan Mohan Malviya, the Bombay Chronicle with Pherozeshah Mehta, Justice with T.M. Nair of the Justice Party and Searchlight with Sachidanand Sinha, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
208.tq: Recall the leader behind each paper.
n: Madan Mohan Malviya was associated with The Leader. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 46-50]
Firoz Shah Mehta was associated with Bombay Chronicle. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 46-50]
T. M. Nair was associated with Justice. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 46-50]
Sachidanand Sinha was associated with Searchlight. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 46-50]
T. M. Nair was associated with the Justice Party. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 46-50]
xs: The correct code is **a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv** — option **(3)**.
**Madan Mohan Malviya** — **The Leader** (Allahabad); **Firoz Shah Mehta** — **Bombay Chronicle**.
**T. M. Nair** — **Justice** (Justice Party); **Sachidanand Sinha** — **Searchlight** (Bihar).
xa: **The Independent** (Allahabad) — **Motilal Nehru**.
**Pratap** — **Ganesh Shankar Vidyarthi**, which publicised the **Bijoliya Movement**.
**Indian Nation** (**1931**, Patna) — **Kameshwar Singh** of Darbhanga.

209.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Organisation or leader)
 a. HRA
 b. HSRA
 c. Bhagat Singh
 d. Chandrashekhar Azad

List-II (Association)
