 i. Reorganised the revolutionary organisation after Bismil's death
 ii. Socialist revolution
 iii. Founded in 1924 at Kanpur
 iv. Credited with the founding of the HSRA

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
209.x: The HRA was founded at Kanpur in 1924; the HSRA stood for socialist revolution; Bhagat Singh is credited with the HSRA's founding; and Azad reorganised it after Bismil's death.
209.tq: Start with the certain organisation–year pair and then resolve the leader associations.
xs: The match is **a–iii, b–ii, c–iv, d–i** — option **(1)**.
**HRA** = founded **1924** at **Kanpur**; **HSRA** = **socialist revolution**.
**Bhagat Singh** = credited with founding the HSRA (APPSC-GS **2018**); **Azad** = reorganised it after **Bismil's death**.
xa: HRA founders: **Bismil, Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee, Sachindra Nath Sanyal** (APPSC-G1 **2024**).
⚠ Bhagat Singh was **not** an HRA founder.
HSRA formed at **Feroz Shah Kotla, Delhi** (**1928**).

209.s: The stated goal of the HSRA was associated with the establishment of a:
o: Federal Republic of United States of India
209.x: The HSRA envisaged a 'Federal Republic of United States of India' and advocated socialist revolution.
209.tq: Recall the exact constitutional phrase rather than a broad substitute such as socialist republic.
xs: The HSRA aimed at a **"Federal Republic of United States of India"** — option **(1)**.
Its goal was **socialist** revolution, beyond the HRA's armed revolution for a republic.
xa: HSRA: **1928**, Feroz Shah Kotla, Delhi.
Credited to **Bhagat Singh** with **Azad** and **Sukhdev**.
Shift to **socialist** ideology and **mass propaganda** (courtroom, leaflets, hunger strikes).

209.s:
Consider the following statements about the Naujawan Bharat Sabha:
1. It was founded at Delhi in 1928.
2. It was founded by Bhagat Singh, with Sukhdev as co-founder.
3. Bhagwati Charan Vohra was associated with its founding.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
209.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct: Bhagat Singh founded it, co-founded by Sukhdev with Bhagwati Charan Vohra. Statement 1 is wrong: it was founded at Lahore in 1926; 1928 at Delhi (Feroz Shah Kotla) is the HSRA. So A, C and D, which include statement 1, are wrong.
209.tq: NBS = Lahore 1926; HSRA = Delhi 1928.
xs: Statements **2 and 3 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
**1** wrong: the **Naujawan Bharat Sabha** was founded at **Lahore** in **1926**; **Delhi 1928** is the **HSRA**.
**2:** founded by **Bhagat Singh**, co-founded by **Sukhdev**.
**3:** **Bhagwati Charan Vohra** was also associated.
xa: Aim: mobilise **youth, peasants and workers** + fight **communalism**.
Vohra wrote **The Philosophy of the Bomb**.
Sukhdev taught at **National College, Lahore**.

209.s: The principal objective of the Naujawan Bharat Sabha was to
o: mobilise youth, peasants and workers and oppose communalism
establish a princely federation through constitutional reforms
secure separate electorates for revolutionary organisations
organise military assistance for the British during the First World War
209.x: The Sabha sought to mobilise youth, peasants and workers and to fight communalism.
209.tq: Identify the organisation from its distinctive social base and ideological objective.
xs: The Sabha aimed to **mobilise youth, peasants and workers** and **oppose communalism** — option **(1)**.
Founded **1926**, **Lahore**, by **Bhagat Singh** with **Sukhdev** (and **Vohra**).
xa: HSRA (**1928**) added **socialism** to the armed-revolt programme.
Bhagat Singh wrote **Why I am an Atheist (1930)**.
Influences: **Jallianwala Bagh (1919)**, **Nankana Sahib (1921)**, **Chauri Chaura (1922)**.

209.s: The Kakori Train Action was undertaken primarily to:
o: protest against the Trade Disputes Bill
destroy the railway line between Delhi and Lahore
obtain government treasury funds for the HRA
209.x: On 9 August 1925, the HRA looted the government treasury carried on a train near Kakori to fund its revolutionary activities.
209.tq: Identify the motive of an action rather than merely recalling its location or date.
xs: Kakori aimed to **obtain government treasury funds for the HRA** — option **(4)**.
On **9 August 1925** the HRA looted the **government treasury** on a train near **Kakori (Lucknow)**.
The **Trade Disputes Bill** protest was the **1929** Assembly bomb.
xa: **Azad** took part and escaped.
⚠ **Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru** were **not** part of Kakori.
Hanged (**Dec 1927**): **Bismil, Ashfaqullah Khan, Roshan Singh, Rajendra Lahiri**.

209.s: Which one of the following sets contains only those executed in connection with the Kakori Train Action?
o: Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqullah Khan, Roshan Singh and Rajendra Lahiri
Surya Sen, Ananta Singh, Ganesh Ghosh and Lokenath Bal
Jatin Das, Chandrashekhar Azad, Udham Singh and Gopinath Saha
Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Rajguru and Batukeshwar Dutt
209.x: Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqullah Khan, Roshan Singh and Rajendra Lahiri were hanged in connection with the Kakori case in December 1927.
209.tq: Group the correct case participants and exclude revolutionaries belonging to other cases.
xs: Kakori hangings: **Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqullah Khan, Roshan Singh and Rajendra Lahiri** — option **(1)**.
**Surya Sen's** group = Chittagong; **Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Rajguru** = Lahore case (Dutt got **life**).
xa: Jails: **Bismil (Gorakhpur)**, **Ashfaqullah (Faizabad)**, **Roshan Singh (Allahabad/Naini)**, **Lahiri (Gonda)**.
Hanged in **Dec 1927**.
Bismil born **11 June 1897**.

209.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Kakori Train Action
B. Saunders killing
C. Central Assembly bomb incident
D. Chittagong Armoury Raid
209.x: The Kakori Train Action occurred in 1925, the Saunders killing in 1928, the Central Assembly bomb incident in April 1929 and the Chittagong Armoury Raid in April 1930.
209.tq: Place the events by their years and use the two April 1929–1930 events as the final check.
xs: The order is **A, B, C, D** — option **(1)**.
**A:** **Kakori 9 August 1925**; **B:** **Saunders, Dec 1928**.
**C:** **Assembly bomb 8 April 1929**; **D:** **Chittagong 18 April 1930**.
xa: Executions of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Rajguru: **23 March 1931**.
Azad died **27 Feb 1931**.
**Surya Sen** hanged **1934**.

209.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Saunders killing is correct?
o: Michael O'Dwyer was killed in Lahore by Rajguru and Azad.
J.P. Saunders was mistakenly identified as James A. Scott, the intended target.
Charles Tegart was killed by Gopinath Saha in 1924.
Saunders was the intended target, and James A. Scott was killed by mistake.
209.x: J.P. Saunders, the Assistant Superintendent of Police, was mistakenly killed because he was taken for James A. Scott, associated with the anti-Simon lathi-charge.
209.tq: Discriminate between the actual victim and the intended target in an assassination attempt.
xs: **J.P. Saunders** was mistaken for **James A. Scott**, the intended target — option **(2)**.
Option (4) reverses them; **O'Dwyer** was killed in **London (1940)**; **Tegart** survived — Saha hit **Ernest Day**.
xa: Lahore, **Dec 1928**.
⚠ Saunders killed in place of **Scott**; Tegart's would-be killer hit **Ernest Day**.
**Rajguru** fired first.

209.s:
Consider the following statements about Udham Singh:
1. He shot Michael O'Dwyer at Caxton Hall, London.
2. The shooting took place on 13 March 1940.
3. His act was revenge for the death of Lala Lajpat Rai.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
209.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Udham Singh shot O'Dwyer at Caxton Hall, London, on 13 March 1940. Statement 3 is wrong: it was revenge for Jallianwala Bagh (O'Dwyer was the Punjab Lt. Governor); avenging Lajpat Rai was the motive of the Saunders killing (1928). So B, C and D, which include statement 3, are wrong.
209.tq: O'Dwyer -> Jallianwala; Saunders -> Lajpat Rai.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
**1 and 2:** **Udham Singh** shot **Michael O'Dwyer** at **Caxton Hall, London**, on **13 March 1940**.
**3** wrong: it was revenge for **Jallianwala Bagh** (O'Dwyer was **Punjab Lt. Governor**); avenging Lajpat Rai was the **Saunders** motive.
xa: Jallianwala Bagh (**1919**) also turned **Bhagat Singh** towards revolution.
Saunders killing: **Dec 1928**, Lahore.

209.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Central Legislative Assembly bomb incident of 8 April 1929?
o: Chandrashekhar Azad and Sukhdev attacked the Punjab Legislative Council.
Surya Sen and Ananta Singh attacked the Delhi Police Armoury.
Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt used non-lethal smoke bombs and distributed leaflets.
Bhagat Singh and Rajguru used lethal bombs to assassinate the Viceroy.
209.x: On 8 April 1929, Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt threw non-lethal smoke bombs and leaflets in the Central Legislative Assembly in Delhi.
209.tq: Distinguish the Assembly action from assassination attempts and armoury raids by participants and purpose.
xs: **Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt** threw **non-lethal smoke bombs** and **leaflets** — option **(3)**.
Date: **8 April 1929**, **Central Legislative Assembly, Delhi**.
Rajguru was not involved, and the bombs were not meant to kill.
xa: Against the **Public Safety Bill** + **Trade Disputes Bill**.
Slogan **"Inquilab Zindabad"**; leaflet: **"To make the deaf hear"**.
Dutt got **life transportation** in the Assembly bomb case.

209.s: The Central Assembly bomb incident was primarily a protest against which Bills?
o: The Government of India Bill and the Rowlatt Bill
The Public Safety Bill and the Trade Disputes Bill
The Trade Disputes Bill and the Indian Councils Bill
The Rowlatt Bill and the Public Safety Bill
209.x: The action protested against the Public Safety Bill and the Trade Disputes Bill, which were viewed as curbing civil liberties and workers' rights.
209.tq: Match the protest action with the precise legislative targets.
xs: The protest was against the **Public Safety Bill** and **Trade Disputes Bill** — option **(2)**.
These curbed **civil liberties** and **workers**.
xa: Bombs thrown on **8 April 1929** by **Bhagat Singh** and **Batukeshwar Dutt**.
They **courted arrest** to use the court as a platform.
Slogan: **"Inquilab Zindabad"**.

209.s:
Consider the following statements about the Central Assembly bomb action (1929):
1. The leaflet thrown said the action was 'to make the deaf hear'.
2. Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt escaped after the action to avoid a trial.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
209.x: Statement 1 is correct: the leaflet said 'To make the deaf hear'. Statement 2 is wrong: they deliberately courted arrest to use the court as a platform. So 2 only, both and neither are wrong.
209.tq: Assembly bomb strategy = court arrest, use the trial for propaganda.
xs: Only **statement 1** is correct — option **(1)**.
**1:** The leaflet said **"To make the deaf hear"**.
**2** wrong: they **courted arrest** to use the **court as a platform**.
xa: Slogan: **"Inquilab Zindabad"**.
Dutt: **life transportation**; Bhagat Singh tried in the **Lahore Conspiracy Case**.
Dutt died **1965**; cremated at **Hussainiwala**.

209.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Lahore jail hunger strike of 1929:
1. It demanded political-prisoner status.
2. Bhagat Singh and Sukhdev participated in it.
3. Jatin Das was associated with it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
209.x: The hunger strike demanded political-prisoner status and involved Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Batukeshwar Dutt and Jatin Das. Therefore all three statements are correct.
209.tq: Combine the demand with the named participants and test the complete set.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**1:** The **1929 Lahore jail hunger strike** demanded **political-prisoner status**.
**2 and 3:** Participants included **Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Dutt** and **Jatin Das**.
xa: **Jatin Das** died after a **63-day** hunger strike.
Hunger strikes were part of the HSRA's **mass propaganda**.
Lahore case trial: **1929-1930**.

209.s: The Chittagong Armoury Raid of 18 April 1930 was led by:
209.x: The raid was led by Surya Sen, popularly known as Masterda. Ganesh Ghosh, Lokenath Bal and Ananta Singh were among his associates.
209.tq: Distinguish the principal leader from the named associates in a revolutionary operation.
xs: **Surya Sen ("Masterda")** led the **Chittagong Armoury Raid** (**18 April 1930**) — option **(3)**.
**Ganesh Ghosh, Lokenath Bal, Ananta Singh** were his **associates**.
xa: Group name: **Indian Republican Army** (also **Ambika Chakravarty**).
Fight at **Jalalabad Hills**; Surya Sen hanged **1934**.
Women: **Pritilata Waddedar**, **Kalpana Dutt**.

209.s:
Consider the following statements about the Chittagong Armoury Raid:
1. The revolutionaries cut telegraph and telephone lines.
2. They disrupted railway communications.
3. The associated fighting took place at the Jalalabad Hills.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
209.x: The operation involved cutting telegraph and telephone lines, disrupting railways and fighting at the Jalalabad Hills. All three statements are correct.
209.tq: Test the operational details together rather than only the leader's name.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**1:** They **cut telegraph/telephone lines**; they also attacked **police armouries**.
**2:** They **disrupted railways**.
**3:** Fighting at **Jalalabad Hills**.
xa: Leader: **Surya Sen**, **18 April 1930**.
**Pritilata Waddedar** led the **Pahartali European Club** raid.
Surya Sen hanged **1934**.

209.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Bina Das — fired at the Bengal Governor at a convocation
Pritilata Waddedar — Pahartali European Club raid
Kalpana Dutt — sentenced to life imprisonment
Santi Ghosh and Suniti Choudhury — led the Pahartali European Club raid
209.x: Santi Ghosh and Suniti Choudhury shot the District Magistrate at Comilla. The Pahartali European Club raid was led by Pritilata Waddedar, who took cyanide.
209.tq: Separate the actions of the women revolutionaries instead of grouping all Chittagong associates together.
xs: **Santi Ghosh and Suniti Choudhury — Pahartali raid** is wrong — option **(4)**.
They shot a **District Magistrate** (Comilla).
The **Pahartali European Club** raid was led by **Pritilata Waddedar**, who took **cyanide**.
xa: **Kalpana Dutt**: arrested, **life** sentence.
**Bina Das**: fired at the **Bengal Governor** at her convocation.
All linked to Surya Sen's **Chittagong** movement (**1930**).

209.s:
Consider the following statements about Surya Sen:
1. His group in the Chittagong Armoury Raid called itself the Indian Republican Army.
2. He was hanged in 1934.
3. He was hanged in the Lahore Conspiracy Case in 1931.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
209.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Surya Sen's group (with Ganesh Ghosh, Lokenath Bal, Ananta Singh, Ambika Chakravarty) was the Indian Republican Army, and he was hanged in 1934. Statement 3 is wrong: the 1931 Lahore case executions were of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru. So A (omits 2), C and D (include 3) are wrong.
209.tq: Surya Sen: IRA, Chittagong 1930, hanged 1934.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
**1:** His group was the **Indian Republican Army**.
**2:** He was **hanged in 1934**.
**3** wrong: the **1931** Lahore executions were **Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Rajguru**.
xa: Associates: **Ganesh Ghosh, Lokenath Bal, Ananta Singh, Ambika Chakravarty**.
Known as **"Masterda"**.
Raid: **18 April 1930**.

209.s: Who wrote *The Philosophy of the Bomb* as a reply to Gandhi's *The Cult of the Bomb*?
209.x: *The Philosophy of the Bomb* was written by Bhagwati Charan Vohra as a reply to Gandhi's *The Cult of the Bomb*.
209.tq: Use the author–work association while separating it from Bhagat Singh's autobiographical writing.
xs: **Bhagwati Charan Vohra** wrote **The Philosophy of the Bomb** — option **(2)**.
It replied to **Gandhi's "The Cult of the Bomb"**.
**Bhagat Singh** wrote **Why I am an Atheist (1930)**.
xa: ⚠ **The Cult of the Bomb** = Gandhi; **The Philosophy of the Bomb** = **Vohra**.
Vohra was associated with the **Naujawan Bharat Sabha (1926)**.

209.s: Which statement correctly describes the manner of Chandrashekhar Azad's death?
o: He shot himself during a police encounter at Alfred Park.
He was shot while leading the Chittagong Armoury Raid.
He died after a 64-day hunger strike in Lahore Jail.
He was hanged at Gorakhpur Jail after the Kakori trial.
209.x: Azad shot himself during a police encounter at Alfred Park after resisting capture. He was not executed in the Kakori or Lahore cases.
209.tq: Reject the familiar execution and hunger-strike alternatives by focusing on the manner of death.
xs: **Azad shot himself** during a police encounter at **Alfred Park** — option **(1)**.
Alfred Park (now **Chandra Shekhar Azad Park**), **Prayagraj**, **27 Feb 1931**.
The **63-day** hunger strike was **Jatin Das's**; **Bismil** was hanged at **Gorakhpur**.
xa: Azad was born **23 July 1906**.
He took part in **Kakori** and escaped.
⚠ The "shot dead by an Indian constable" version is **wrong**.

209.s:
Arrange the following events in the chronological order in which they influenced Bhagat Singh:
A. Chauri Chaura incident
B. Jallianwala Bagh massacre
C. Nankana Sahib incident
D. Bhagat Singh’s turn from Gandhi towards revolutionary politics
209.x: The sequence was Jallianwala Bagh in 1919, Nankana Sahib in 1921, Chauri Chaura in 1922, followed by Bhagat Singh’s turn towards revolutionary politics.
209.tq: Fix the dated events first and place the consequential change after them.
xs: The order is **B, C, A, D** — option **(1)**.
**Jallianwala Bagh 1919** → **Nankana Sahib 1921** → **Chauri Chaura 1922**.
These turned **Bhagat Singh** from **Gandhi** to **revolution**.
xa: He founded the **Naujawan Bharat Sabha (1926)**.
Credited with founding the **HSRA (1928)**.
Wrote **Why I am an Atheist (1930)**.

209.s:
Which of the following methods formed part of the mass-propaganda approach of the HSRA-era revolutionaries?
1. Use of courtroom proceedings
2. Distribution of leaflets
3. Hunger strikes
4. Exclusive reliance on secret military training
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
209.x: Courtroom proceedings, leaflets and hunger strikes were used as forms of mass propaganda. Exclusive reliance on secret military training does not represent this approach.
209.tq: Find the one extreme statement that contradicts the broader mass-propaganda strategy.
xs: **1, 2 and 3 only** — option **(2)**.
**Courtroom**, **leaflets** and **hunger strikes** were the HSRA's **mass propaganda** tools.
**Exclusive reliance on secret military training** was not part of this approach.
xa: Shift from **individual heroism** to **socialist** ideology.
Assembly bomb strategy: **courted arrest** to use the court as a platform.
**1929** Lahore jail hunger strike: **Jatin Das** died after **63** days.

209.s:
Assertion (A): The HSRA represented an ideological development beyond the earlier HRA.
Reason (R): The HSRA added socialism to the HRA’s objective of establishing a republic through armed revolt.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
209.x: Both statements are true, and the addition of socialism directly explains why the HSRA represented an ideological development beyond the HRA.
209.tq: Test whether the reason explains the precise ideological difference between two organisations.
xs: **Both A and R are true** and **R is the correct explanation of A** — option **(1)**.
**A:** The **HSRA** was an ideological advance on the **HRA**.
**R:** HRA (**1924**) = **republic by armed revolt**; HSRA (**1928**) **added socialism** — exactly what makes it an advance.
xa: HSRA goal: **"Federal Republic of United States of India"**.
HSRA also used **mass propaganda** (courtroom, leaflets, hunger strikes).
HRA founders: **Sanyal, Chatterjee, Bismil**.

209.s: Bhagat Singh and Chandrashekhar Azad reorganised the HRA in 1928 at Ferozeshah Kotla, Delhi, into which organisation?
209.x: In 1928 the HRA was renamed the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) under Bhagat Singh and Azad. Anushilan Samiti was Bengali, Abhinav Bharat was Savarkar's and Khudai Khidmatgar was Ghaffar Khan's.
209.tq: Recall the socialist renaming of the HRA in 1928.
n: Bhagat Singh was associated with the HSRA. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #120 · pp 218-221]
Bhagat Singh was associated with revolutionary nationalism. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #120 · pp 218-221]
xs: In **1928** at **Feroz Shah Kotla, Delhi**, the HRA was reorganised into the **HSRA** — option **(2)**.
The HSRA was reorganised under **Chandrashekhar Azad** after Bismil's death; members included **Bhagat Singh**, **Sukhdev**, **Bejoy Kumar Sinha**.
Its goal was a **socialist** revolution — a "Federal Republic of United States of India".
xa: **HRA**: **1924, Kanpur** — **Ram Prasad Bismil**, **Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee**, **Sachindra Nath Sanyal**.
⚠ **Bhagat Singh** was **not** an HRA founder.
**Naujawan Bharat Sabha**: **1926**, **Lahore** — Bhagat Singh, with **Sukhdev**.

209.s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Leader)
a. Ram Prasad Bismil
b. Surya Sen
c. Batukeshwar Dutt
d. V.D. Savarkar

List-II (Association)
i. Central Legislative Assembly bombing
ii. Chittagong Armoury Raid
iii. Abhinav Bharat
iv. Kakori and HRA
209.x: Bismil led Kakori for the HRA, Surya Sen the Chittagong Armoury Raid, Batukeshwar Dutt the Central Assembly bombing with Bhagat Singh, and Savarkar founded Abhinav Bharat, giving a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii.
209.tq: Recall the action of each revolutionary.
n: Ram Prasad Bismil was associated with Kakori. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #120 · pp 218-221]
Ram Prasad Bismil was associated with the HRA. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #120 · pp 218-221]
Surya Sen was associated with the Chittagong Armoury Raid. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #120 · pp 218-221]
Batukeshwar Dutt was associated with the Central Legislative Assembly bombing. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #120 · pp 218-221]
V.D. Savarkar founded or was associated with Abhinav Bharat. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #120 · pp 218-221]
xs: The correct code is **a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii** — option **(4)**.
**Ram Prasad Bismil** — **Kakori** and the **HRA**; **Surya Sen** — **Chittagong Armoury Raid**.
**Batukeshwar Dutt** — **Central Legislative Assembly bombing**; **V.D. Savarkar** — **Abhinav Bharat**, by elimination.
xa: Kakori train action: **9 August 1925**; Bismil hanged at **Gorakhpur** jail.
Chittagong raid: **18 April 1930**; Surya Sen ("**Masterda**") hanged **1934**.
Assembly bomb: **8 April 1929**, with **Bhagat Singh**.

209.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Bhagat Singh was associated with the Revolutionary Movement.
II. Ram Prasad Bismil was associated with the Revolutionary Movement.
III. Ashfaqulla Khan was associated with the Revolutionary Movement.
IV. Surya Sen was associated with the Revolutionary Movement.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
209.x: All four are correct: Bhagat Singh, Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqulla Khan and Surya Sen were all revolutionaries, so I, II, III and IV.
209.tq: Classify each person as revolutionary or Gandhian.
n: Bhagat Singh was an important personality of the Revolutionary Movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #94 · pp 176-178]
Ram Prasad Bismil was an important personality of the Revolutionary Movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #94 · pp 176-178]
Ashfaqulla Khan was an important personality of the Revolutionary Movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #94 · pp 176-178]
Surya Sen was an important personality of the Revolutionary Movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #94 · pp 176-178]
xs: All four were revolutionaries — so **I, II, III and IV**, option **(3)**.
The **Revolutionary Movement** list includes **Bhagat Singh**, **Ram Prasad Bismil**, **Ashfaqulla Khan** and **Surya Sen** (also **Chandrashekhar Azad**, **Aurobindo Ghosh**).
xa: **Ashfaqulla Khan** — **Kakori**, hanged at **Faizabad**.
**Surya Sen** — **Chittagong Armoury Raid**.
**Peasant** / regional movements: **Sadhu Sitaram Das**, **Vijay Singh Pathik**, **Ashwini Kumar Dutta**.

209.s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Mahatma Gandhi is associated with Champaran, NCM, CDM and Quit India.
Statement B: Ram Prasad Bismil is associated with Kakori and the revolutionary movement.
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
209.x: Both are true: Gandhi led Champaran, Non-Cooperation, Civil Disobedience and Quit India, and Ram Prasad Bismil led the Kakori train action of 1925.
209.tq: Check each statement separately.
n: Mahatma Gandhi is associated with Champaran. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Mahatma Gandhi is associated with the NCM. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Mahatma Gandhi is associated with the CDM. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Mahatma Gandhi is associated with Quit India. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Ram Prasad Bismil is associated with Kakori. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Ram Prasad Bismil is associated with the revolutionary movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
xs: **Both Statement A and Statement B are true** — option **(1)**.
A true: **Gandhi** is linked with **Champaran**, **Non-Cooperation**, **Civil Disobedience** and **Quit India**.
B true: **Ram Prasad Bismil** — **Kakori**, the **HRA** and the revolutionary movement.
xa: Kakori hanged (Dec **1927**): **Bismil**, **Ashfaqullah Khan**, **Roshan Singh**, **Rajendra Lahiri**.
**Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru** were not part of Kakori.
Bismil was born **11 June 1897**.

210.s:
With reference to the Rampa rebellion of 1879–80, consider the following statements:
1. Munsubdar Madhava Bhupati exploited the tribal population.
2. His policies weakened the position of the muttadars.
3. The rebellion was caused by an increase in axe tax during a famine.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
210.x: Madhava Bhupati’s exploitation of tribals and erosion of the authority of the muttadars caused the Rampa rebellion. The increase in axe tax during a famine was the cause of the Rekapalle rebellion.
210.tq: Separate the causes of the two geographically neighbouring rebellions.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
**1 and 2:** Munsubdar **Madhava Bhupati** (made Munsubdar **1848**) exploited tribals and **eroded the muttadars**.
**3** wrong: the **axe tax** rise in a famine caused the **Rekapalle** revolt.
xa: Rampa leaders: **Dwarabandala Chandrayya**, **Pulikanta Sambaiah**, **Karu Tammanna Dora**, **Ambul Reddy**.
**Sullivan** removed Madhava Bhupati; revolt crushed **Nov 1880**.
Chandrayya burnt **Addateegala** PS.

210.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Leader)

a. Dwarabandala Chandrayya
b. Pulikanta Sambaiah
c. Karu Tammanna Dora
d. Ambul Reddy

List-II (Rebellion association)

i. Rampa rebellion
 ii. Rekapalle rebellion
 iii. Both Rampa and Rekapalle rebellions
 iv. Neither of the two rebellions

Select the correct code.
210.x: Dwarabandala Chandrayya, Pulikanta Sambaiah and Karu Tammanna Dora led the Rampa rebellion. Ambul Reddy was associated with both the Rampa and Rekapalle rebellions.
210.tq: Start from the sure pair and identify the leader common to both rebellions.
xs: The match is **a–i, b–i, c–i, d–iii** — option **(1)**.
**Chandrayya**, **Pulikanta Sambaiah** and **Karu Tammanna Dora** = **Rampa** rebellion.
**Ambul Reddy** = **both** Rampa and **Rekapalle**.
xa: Rekapalle: Vaddagudem PS attacked on **10 July 1879**.
Rekapalle crushed **Sept 1879**; Rampa crushed **Nov 1880**.
Rampa cause: **Madhava Bhupati**; Rekapalle cause: **axe tax**.

210.s: The Rampa rebellion of 1879–80 was brought to an end after:
o: The axe tax was withdrawn and the rebellion ended in July 1879
Madhava Bhupati was removed by Sullivan and the rebellion was crushed in November 1880
The Madras Forest Act was repealed and the rebellion ended in November 1881
Madhava Bhupati was reinstated and the rebellion ended in September 1879
210.x: Sullivan removed Madhava Bhupati, but the rebellion was ultimately crushed in November 1880.
210.tq: Check the complete sequence of administrative action followed by suppression.
xs: **Sullivan removed Madhava Bhupati**, and the revolt was **crushed in Nov 1880** — option **(2)**.
**Sept 1879** is when **Rekapalle** was crushed; the **axe tax** was a Rekapalle grievance.
xa: Rampa revolt span: **1879-80**, Rampachodavaram agency.
Madhava Bhupati was made Munsubdar in **1848**.
The **Madras Forest Act** dates from **1882** — after the revolt.

210.s: The immediate cause of the Rekapalle rebellion was:
o: The introduction of the Madras Forest Act in the Agency areas
The dismissal of tribal leaders from government service
The increase of the axe tax on podu from 4 annas to 4–12 annas during a famine
The erosion of the authority of the muttadars by Madhava Bhupati
210.x: The Rekapalle rebellion was triggered by the increase of the axe tax on podu from 4 annas to 4–12 annas during a famine.
210.tq: Distinguish the tax-based cause of Rekapalle from the administrative cause of Rampa.
xs: Rekapalle's cause: the **axe tax on podu** raised from **4 annas to 4-12 annas** during a **famine** — option **(3)**.
**Madhava Bhupati's** erosion of the muttadars caused **Rampa**; the **Forest Act (1882)** came later.
xa: Place: **Rekapalle, Bhadrachalam taluk**, Godavari district.
Leader **Ambul Reddy**; **Vaddagudem** PS attacked **10 July 1879**.
Crushed **Sept 1879**.

210.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Rampa and Rekapalle rebellions occurred in the Godavari region.
2. Ambul Reddy was associated with both rebellions.
3. Both rebellions were led by Alluri Sitarama Raju.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
210.x: Both rebellions occurred in the Godavari region, and Ambul Reddy was associated with both. Alluri Sitarama Raju led the later Rampa rebellion of 1922–24, not these earlier rebellions.
210.tq: Use the chronological distinction between the earlier rebellions and Alluri’s later revolt.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
**1:** Both occurred in **Godavari district**.
**2:** **Ambul Reddy** was in both.
**3** wrong: **Alluri** was born in **1897**; he led the later **1922-24** Rampa rebellion.
xa: ⚠ Some notes wrongly credit Alluri with the 1879-80 revolt.
**1879** = "the year of the Rampa Revolution".
Rampa leaders: **Chandrayya**, **Sambaiah**, **Tammanna Dora**.

210.s: Alluri Sitarama Raju, who led the later Rampa rebellion, was born in:
210.x: Alluri Sitarama Raju was born in 1897. Therefore, attributing the 1879–80 Rampa rebellion to him is chronologically incorrect.
210.tq: Use the birth-year check to expose an impossible attribution.
xs: **Alluri Sitarama Raju** was born in **1897** — option **(3)** (**4 July 1897**).
So he could not have led the **1879-80** revolt.
xa: Birthplace: **Pandrangi, near Vizianagaram**; ancestral village **Mogallu**.
**125th birth anniversary**: **30-ft bronze statue** at **Bhimavaram**.
Nickname **Chittibabu**; title **"Manyam Veerudu"**.

210.s:
Arrange the following rebellions in chronological order:
A. Alluri Sitarama Raju’s Rampa rebellion
B. Vasudev Balwant Phadke’s revolt
C. Khudiram Bose’s Muzaffarpur episode
D. Gulugonda tribal revolt
210.x: The Gulugonda revolt occurred in 1845–48, Phadke’s revolt in 1879, Khudiram Bose’s episode in 1908, and Alluri’s Rampa rebellion in 1922–24.
210.tq: Place events by their periods before checking the sequence of the middle items.
xs: The order is **D, B, C, A** — option **(1)**.
**C:** **Khudiram/Muzaffarpur 1908** → **A:** **Alluri's Rampa 1922-24**.
xa: Gulugonda leader: **Chinna Bhupathi** (Vizag).
**1794**: Vizianagaram — **Vijayarama Raju** killed at **Padmanabham**.
**1879** also saw the **Rampa** and **Rekapalle** revolts.

210.s: Which of the following was NOT a consequence of the Madras Forest Act, 1882, as described in relation to tribal grievances?
o: Recognition of unrestricted tribal access to minor forest produce
210.x: The Act restricted tribal access to podu cultivation and minor forest produce, and curbed grazing; it did not recognise unrestricted access.
210.tq: Choose the option that reverses the effect of a restrictive law.
xs: **Unrestricted access to minor forest produce** was not a consequence — option **(3)**.
The **1882** Act **cut off** rights to minor forest produce.
It did **reserve forests**, **restrict podu** and **curb grazing** — (1), (2), (4).
xa: **Podu** = shifting cultivation.
**Begar** = forced unpaid labour on roads.
**Tahsildar Bastian's** excesses were the spark.

210.s:
Consider the following statements about the Agency tribes and their grievances:
1. Koya and other hill tribes were affected by the reservation of forests.
2. Forest restrictions curtailed podu, or shifting cultivation.
3. The Muttadari system was associated with extortion and forced labour.
4. Begar referred to voluntary paid labour on public roads.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
210.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Begar meant forced unpaid labour, not voluntary paid labour, so statement 4 is false.
210.tq: Identify the one reversed definition in a cluster of genuine tribal grievances.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
**1:** **Koya** and other hill tribes were affected.
**2:** Forest reservation cut off **podu** (shifting cultivation).
**3:** **Muttadari** meant **extortion, forced labour**; **4** wrong: **begar** was **unpaid** forced coolie work.
xa: **Madras Forest Act, 1882**.
Spark: **Tahsildar Bastian**.
Area: agency tracts of **East Godavari and Visakhapatnam**.

210.s: Alluri Sitarama Raju was born at which of the following places?
210.x: Alluri Sitarama Raju was born on 4 July 1897 at Pandrangi, also referred to as Pandarangipeta, near Vizianagaram. Mogallu was his ancestral village.
210.tq: Distinguish the birthplace from the ancestral village and later places associated with the leader.
xs: Alluri was born at **Pandrangi (Pandarangipeta), near Vizianagaram** — option **(4)**.
**Mogallu** (West Godavari) was his **ancestral village** — some notes give it as birthplace.
**Koyyuru** = where he was shot; **Krishnadevipeta** = his tomb.
xa: Born **4 July 1897**.
Parents: **Venkataramaraju** and **Suryanarayana Amma**.
APPSC-GS **2025** asked the village; the key showed no answer.

210.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Alluri Sitarama Raju:
1. His ancestral village was Mogallu in West Godavari.
2. He was popularly known by the nickname Chittibabu.
3. Erramalli Narasimha Rao wrote his biography.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
210.x: All three statements are correct. Mogallu was his ancestral village, Chittibabu was his nickname, and Erramalli Narasimha Rao was his biographer.
210.tq: Combine closely related identity details and verify each statement independently.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**1:** Ancestral village **Mogallu, West Godavari**.
**2:** Nickname **Chittibabu**.
**3:** Biographer **Erramalli Narasimha Rao**.
xa: Title: **"Manyam Veerudu"** (APPSC **2024** key).
**1919**: hut at **Kongasingi near Krishnadevipeta**.
Born at **Pandrangi**, near Vizianagaram.

210.s:
Which of the following statements about Alluri Sitarama Raju is correct?
1. He visited Chittagong in 1921 to meet Bengali revolutionaries.
2. He respected Gandhi but believed that force was necessary.
3. He was formally affiliated to the Indian National Congress.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
210.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. He visited Chittagong in 1921, respected Gandhi and believed in the necessity of force, but he was not affiliated with the Congress.
210.tq: Use the affiliation statement as the trap while retaining the two correct ideological details.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
**1:** **July 1921** secret meeting with Bengali revolutionaries at **Chittagong**.
**2:** He **respected Gandhi** but believed **force necessary**.
**3** wrong: he was **not affiliated with Congress**.
xa: He received **guerrilla training** ideas at Chittagong.
Yet he troubled the British more than the **NCM** in that region.
Unlike Gandhian forest satyagrahas, he used **armed guerrilla war**.

210.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Gam Gantam Dora — Lieutenant of Alluri
Gam Mallu Dora — Right hand of Alluri
Gam Mallu Dora — Killed on 7 June 1924
210.x: Gam Gantam Dora was killed on 7 June 1924. Gam Mallu Dora was arrested in 1923, received a life term, was later released and won election as an MP in 1952.
210.tq: Detect the swapped fate and date among closely associated leaders.
xs: **Gam Mallu Dora — killed 7 June 1924** is wrong — option **(4)**.
**Gam Gantam Dora** was killed on **7 June 1924**.
**Mallu Dora** ("Right hand") was **arrested 1923**, got a **life term**, later won as **MP in 1952**.
xa: Mallu Dora arrested at **Nadimpalem** (**17 Sept 1923**) by **Keirns**.
**Aggiraju**: arrested **6 May 1924** at the **Maddaru** river.
⚠ **Gantam Dora** = killed **1924**; **Mallu Dora** = MP **1952**.

210.s: Alluri Sitarama Raju is popularly hailed by which title?
210.x: Alluri is 'Manyam Veerudu' (hero of the forest) (APPSC 2024 key). Andhra Shivaji was Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary and Andhra Ratna was Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya; Andhra Kesari was Tanguturi Prakasam.
210.tq: Manyam Veerudu = Alluri; nickname Chittibabu.
xs: Alluri is **"Manyam Veerudu"** (hero of the forest) — option **(2)** (APPSC **2024** key).
**"Andhra Shivaji"** = **Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary**; **"Andhra Ratna"** = **Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya**.
xa: Alluri's nickname: **Chittibabu**.
Airport: **Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport, Bhogapuram**.
Agency district named **Alluri Sitarama Raju district**.

210.s: The Rampa or Manyam Rebellion was principally based in which area?
o: The Gudem hills of the East Godavari Agency
210.x: The rebellion was based in the Gudem hills, located in the Agency area of East Godavari.
210.tq: Use the location clue to separate the rebellion's operational area from other hill regions of Andhra Pradesh.
xs: The rebellion was based in the **Gudem hills** of the **East Godavari** Agency — option **(3)**.
Area: agency tracts of **East Godavari and Visakhapatnam (Gudem hills)**.
xa: Span: **January 1922 - May 1924**.
First PS attacked: **Chintapalli** (**22 Aug 1922**).
Tribes: **Koya** and other hill tribes.

210.s: Which one of the following was NOT a cause of the Rampa Rebellion?
o: Introduction of permanent settlement in the Gudem hills
Oppressive functioning of the Muttadari system
Loss of forest and podu rights under the Madras Forest Act
210.x: The rebellion was caused by restrictions on forest and podu rights, begar for road building and the oppressive Muttadari system, along with the actions of Tahsildar Bastian. Permanent settlement was not identified as a cause.
210.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the stated cluster of causes.
xs: **Permanent settlement** was **not** a cause — option **(1)**.
Causes: **Muttadari** oppression, **begar** for roads, loss of **podu/forest** rights under the **Forest Act**, and **Tahsildar Bastian**.
xa: **Madras Forest Act, 1882**.
Bastian's excesses were the **spark**.
Rebellion span: **2 years 5 months**.

210.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the Rampa Rebellion?
o: It was confined to the coastal municipalities of Guntur district.
It troubled the British in the region more than the Non-Cooperation Movement did.
It was affiliated formally with the Indian National Congress and led through Congress committees.
It ended immediately after the imposition of the Madras Forest Act.
210.x: The rebellion troubled the British in the region more than the Non-Cooperation Movement. It was an armed tribal rebellion in the Agency area and was not formally affiliated with the Congress.
210.tq: Select the precise comparative statement while rejecting exaggerated organisational and geographical claims.
xs: It **troubled the British more than the NCM** in that region — option **(2)**.
It was **outside the Congress** and non-violence — so (3) is wrong.
It was in the **agency tracts** of East Godavari/Visakhapatnam, not Guntur municipalities.
xa: Span: **January 1922 - May 1924**.
**Assam Rifles** and **Gurkhas** reached **Narsipatnam** (**27 Jan 1924**).
Special Commissioner: **Rutherford**.

210.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: 24 September 1922 — officers Scott Coward and Heiter killed at Damanapalli ghat
6 December 1922 — Gam Mallu Dora arrested at Nadimpalem
7 May 1924 — Gam Gantam Dora killed in firing
210.x: Scott Coward and Heiter were killed at Damanapalli ghat on 24 September 1922. Mallu Dora was arrested in September 1923, Raju was shot on 7 May 1924, and Gantam Dora was killed on 7 June 1924.
210.tq: Match each event with its exact date and avoid swapping the final stages of the rebellion.
xs: **24 Sept 1922 — Scott Coward and Heiter killed** at **Damanapalli ghat** — option **(1)**.
**6 Dec 1922** = **Peddagaddapalem** defeat; Mallu Dora was arrested **17 Sept 1923**.
Raju was shot **7 May 1924**; Gantam Dora killed **7 June 1924**.
xa: Battle at **Panjerighat** (Damanghat), **Sept 1922**.
**Malabar Special Police** were behind the first defeat.
Last rites **8 May 1924**.

210.s: The first defeat suffered by Alluri Sitarama Raju’s forces at the hands of the Malabar Special Police occurred at:
210.x: At Peddagaddapalem on 6 December 1922, the Malabar Special Police inflicted Raju’s first defeat; he was wounded at Lingapuram.
210.tq: Separate the sites of the first defeat, the direct battle and the wounding.
xs: The first defeat was at **Peddagaddapalem** (**6 Dec 1922**) — option **(4)**.
Inflicted by the **Malabar Special Police**.
**Lingapuram** = where Raju was **wounded**; **Damanapalli ghat** = ambush; **Panjerighat** = direct battle.
xa: ⚠ **Chintapalli** = first PS attacked; **Panjerighat** = direct battle; **Peddagaddapalem** = first defeat.
**Rutherford** was Special Commissioner.

210.s: The Rampa rebellion extended approximately from:
210.x: The rebellion lasted from January 1922 to May 1924, approximately two years and five months, in the Agency tracts of East Godavari and Visakhapatnam.
210.tq: Use the beginning and ending months together rather than relying only on the commonly remembered year range.
xs: The rebellion ran from **January 1922 to May 1924** — option **(3)**.
About **2 years 5 months**.
xa: Area: **East Godavari and Visakhapatnam (Gudem hills)**.
First raid: **Chintapalli, 22 Aug 1922**.
End: Raju shot **7 May 1924**; **Gantam Dora** killed **7 June 1924**.

210.s: During the Rampa Rebellion of 1922-24, the direct battle between Alluri Sitarama Raju's forces and the British forces was fought at:
210.x: The direct battle with British forces was at Panjerighat (Damanghat), September 1922 (APPSC 2012 key). Chintapalli and Krishnadevipeta were police stations raided in August 1922; Koyyuru is where Raju was shot on 7 May 1924.
210.tq: Panjerighat = direct battle; Chintapalli = first raid; Koyyuru = death.
xs: The direct battle was at **Panjerighat** (Damanghat), **Sept 1922** — option **(2)** (APPSC **2012** key).
**Chintapalli** = first PS raided; **Koyyuru** = where Raju was shot; **Krishnadevipeta** = his tomb.
xa: **Damanapalli ghat** ambush: **Scott Coward and Heiter** killed (**24 Sept 1922**).
First defeat: **Peddagaddapalem**.
Also asked in APPSC G2 **2012**.

210.s:
Consider the following statements about the end of Alluri Sitarama Raju:
1. He was captured by Jamadar Kanchu Meenan.
2. He was shot on 7 May 1924 at Koyyuru before Major Goodall.
3. His last rites were performed on 8 May 1924 at Chintapalli.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
210.x: Statement 1 is correct: Jamadar Kanchu Meenan captured him. Statement 2 is correct: he was shot at Koyyuru on 7 May 1924 before Major Goodall. Statement 3 is wrong: the last rites on 8 May 1924 were at Krishnadevipeta near the Tandava river; Chintapalli was the first police station he raided. So 1 and 2 only; '1 only' misses statement 2, and options with 3 are wrong.
210.tq: Captured by Kanchu Meenan, shot at Koyyuru, last rites/tomb at Krishnadevipeta; Chintapalli = first raid.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
**1:** captured by **Jamadar Kanchu Meenan**.
**2:** shot on **7 May 1924** at **Koyyuru** before **Major Goodall**.
**3** wrong: last rites (**8 May 1924**) were at **Krishnadevipeta** near the **Tandava** river.
xa: He was shot **tied to a tree**.
Goodall is also spelt **"Gudal"**, **"Goodman"**.
⚠ Some notes say cremated, others buried; **tomb/samadhi** at Krishnadevipeta.

210.s: Which British officer was appointed Special Commissioner to crush the Rampa rebellion?
210.x: Rutherford served as Special Commissioner to crush the revolt and ordered the exile of 55 helpers; warrants were issued for 183 persons.
210.tq: Match the officer with the specific administrative post and action.
xs: **Rutherford** was **Special Commissioner** to crush the revolt — option **(4)**.
He **exiled 55 helpers** and issued **warrants for 183**.
**Goodall** = Major at Raju's shooting; **Scott Coward** = officer killed; **Keirns** = arrested Mallu Dora.
xa: ⚠ **Rutherford** appears thrice: Rampa, **Duggirala's trial** (Srikakulam), **Pedanandipadu**.
His Pedanandipadu plan to ban the **Shanti Sena** was **rejected by the Madras Government**.

210.s: At which village was Kanneganti Hanumanthu killed in police firing during the Palnadu pullari movement?
210.x: Kanneganti Hanumanthu was killed in police firing at Minchalapadu during the Palnadu pullari movement.
210.tq: Distinguish the leader’s death place from the other villages connected with the same movement.
xs: **Kanneganti Hanumanthu** was killed at **Minchalapadu** — option **(2)**.
The **Palnad pullari (grass tax)** movement covered **Macherla, Veldurthi, Sirigiripadu, Minchalapadu**.
xa: Supported by **Unnava Lakshmi Narayana**.
Palnadu forest satyagraha = local version of the **NCM** call.

210.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Bezawada AICC meeting of 1921 helped put Gandhi’s programme into Andhra.
2. The Chirala–Perala municipal tax struggle was a local version of the Non-Cooperation call.
3. The Palnadu forest satyagraha was unrelated to the Non-Cooperation programme.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
210.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Palnadu forest satyagraha was also a local expression of the same Non-Cooperation call, so statement 3 is false.
210.tq: Spot the reversed relationship in the statement describing a movement as unrelated.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
**1:** The **Bezawada AICC (1921)** put Gandhi's programme into Andhra.
**2:** **Chirala-Perala** tax fight = local version of the **NCM** call.
**3** wrong: the **Palnadu forest satyagraha** was **the same NCM call**.
xa: **Delhi AICC (5 Nov 1921)**: provinces could take up **no-tax** → Guntur did.
**1921-22 Guntur** saw the NCM's most original methods in Andhra.

210.s: Who founded the Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi near Chirala?
210.x: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya founded the Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi near Chirala.
210.tq: Match the institution with its founder while avoiding confusion with other Andhra leaders.
xs: **Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya** founded the **Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi** near **Chirala** — option **(1)**.
He resigned as professor at **Rajahmundry Government College** to promote **national education**.
**Bezawada Gopala Reddy** abolished the Chirala-Perala municipality in **1938**.
xa: Born **2 June**, **Penuganchiprolu (Krishna district)**; **1884-1929**.
Titles: **"Andhra Ratna"**, "Ramadasu".
Volunteer corps: **Ramadandu (1921)**.

210.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Ravuri Alivelu Mangatayaramma — Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi
210.x: B is correct: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya led the Chirala-Perala movement (1921). A is wrong: the Ramadandu was Duggirala's volunteer corps, not Alluri's; C is wrong: Pisapati Narayana Sastri wrote Chirala Perala Vanavasam; D is wrong: Ravuri Alivelu Mangatayaramma was the first woman jailed at Chirala-Perala, while Duggirala founded the Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi.
210.tq: Start from the sure leader–movement pair and eliminate swapped associations.
xs: **Duggirala — Chirala-Perala movement** is correct — option **(2)**.
The **Ramadandu** was **Duggirala's** corps, not Alluri's; **Pisapati Narayana Sastri** wrote **Chirala Perala Vanavasam**.
**Ravuri Alivelu Mangatayaramma** was the **first woman jailed** at Chirala-Perala.
xa: Exodus: midnight **25 April 1921**; **13,572 of 15,326** residents left.
New camp **"Ramnagar"** outside municipal limits.
**12 women** jailed; **Duvvuri Subbamma** also arrested.

210.s: Who introduced Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya to Gandhi in London in 1915?
210.x: Ananda K. Coomaraswamy introduced Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya to Gandhi in London in 1915 and described him as the coming man of his country.
210.tq: Apply the person-introduced-person trap to a specific political meeting.
xs: **Ananda K. Coomaraswamy** introduced him to Gandhi in **London (1915)** — option **(2)**.
He called Duggirala **"the coming man of your country"**.
xa: Duggirala: **M.A. (Hons) Economics, Edinburgh, 1916**.
Later led **Chirala-Perala (1921)**.
Joined the **Swaraj Party** (C.R. Das, Motilal Nehru).

210.s:
Consider the following statements about Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya:
1. He formed the volunteer corps called Ramadandu at Chirala-Perala in 1921.
2. He led the Shanti Sena in the Pedanandipadu firka.
3. He was given the title 'Andhra Ratna'.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
210.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: his volunteer corps was the Ramadandu (1921, APPSC 2019 key) and he was called 'Andhra Ratna'. Statement 2 is wrong: the Shanti Sena of Pedanandipadu was led by Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary. So A, B and D, which include statement 2, are wrong.
210.tq: Duggirala = Ramadandu; Parvataneni = Shanti Sena.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct — option **(3)**.
**1:** He formed the **Ramadandu** at **Chirala-Perala** in **1921** (APPSC **2019** key).
**2** wrong: the **Shanti Sena** at **Pedanandipadu** was led by **Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary**.
**3:** He was **"Andhra Ratna"**.
xa: ⚠ Trap: **Ramadandu**, not Shanti Sena.
Veeraiah Chowdary = **"Andhra Shivaji"**.
Shanti Sena formation decided by **Guntur DCC, Dec 1921**.

210.s: The Chirala-Perala Satyagraha arose primarily because:
o: The British prohibited the Ramadandu from holding public meetings.
The villages were brought under the Forest Act and denied podu rights.
The two villages were converted into a municipality and their annual tax burden increased sharply.
The residents were forced to migrate to the Gudem hills.
210.x: Chirala and Perala were made a municipality, and the annual tax rose from Rs 4,000 to Rs 40,000, provoking the movement.
210.tq: Match the movement with its immediate administrative and fiscal trigger.
xs: Chirala and Perala were made a **municipality**, and the **tax** rose sharply — option **(3)**.
Tax rose from **Rs 4,000 to Rs 40,000** a year.
The **Forest Act/podu** grievance and **Gudem hills** belong to the Rampa rebellion.
xa: Municipality proposed **Nov 1919**, formed **Jan 1920**.
Residents: weavers and small farmers, ~**15,000**.
Municipality **abolished in 1938** by **Bezawada Gopala Reddy**.

210.s:
Consider the following statements about the Chirala-Perala movement:
1. Chirala and Perala were in Bapatla taluk.
2. The residents set up a camp called Ramnagar outside municipal limits, with a parallel all-caste assembly and an arbitration court.
3. The Ramnagar camp lasted about two years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
210.x: Statement 1 is correct: both villages were in Bapatla taluk. Statement 2 is correct: Ramnagar (Ramanagaram) outside the municipal limits had a parallel all-caste assembly and arbitration court. Statement 3 is wrong: the camp lasted about 11 months, not two years. So 1 and 2 only; every other option includes statement 3.
210.tq: Ramnagar = parallel assembly + arbitration court, lasted 11 months.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
**1:** Both villages were in **Bapatla taluk**.
**2:** **Ramnagar (Ramanagaram)** camp had a **parallel all-caste assembly** and **arbitration court**.
**3** wrong: the camp lasted **11 months**, not two years.
xa: Exodus on Gandhi's advice: **25 April 1921**.
Failure: **lack of funds**, Congress jealousy, no second line of leaders.
Gandhi wrote in **Young India** that the municipality only meant more taxes.

210.s: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya was arrested on 1 October 1921 primarily because he:
o: Broke a ban on public speaking after his Berhampur speech
Organised an armed raid in the Gudem hills
Refused to pay the municipal tax
210.x: After his Berhampur speech, Duggirala was prohibited from speaking for two months. He defied the ban and was arrested on 1 October 1921.
210.tq: Link the arrest to the specific act that violated the colonial order.
xs: Duggirala **broke a ban on public speaking** after his **Berhampur** speech — option **(1)**.
After the **Andhra Mahasabha, Berhampur (Sept 1921)**, he was banned from speaking for **2** months.
Arrested **1 October 1921**.
xa: Tried by **Rutherford** at **Srikakulam**; jailed **1 year**.
⚠ Some notes place the arrest at **Trichinopoly**.
Donations: Srinivasa Ayyangar **Rs 1,000**, APCC **Rs 3,000**, Guntur DCC **Rs 250**.

210.s: The municipality of Chirala and Perala was abolished in 1938 during the ministry of:
o: Rajagopalachari, with Bezawada Gopala Reddy as minister concerned
Tanguturi Prakasam, with Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya as minister concerned
P. Subbarayan, with Konda Venkatappayya as minister concerned
Bobbili Raja, with Bezawada Gopala Reddy as minister concerned
210.x: The municipality was abolished in 1938 during the Rajaji ministry, when Bezawada Gopala Reddy was the Local Self-Government Minister.
210.tq: Match the administrative outcome with the correct ministry and minister instead of swapping office-holders.
xs: The Chirala-Perala municipality was abolished in **1938** under the **Rajagopalachari (Rajaji) ministry**, with **Bezawada Gopala Reddy** as minister — option **(1)**.
Gopala Reddy held the **Local Self-Government** portfolio, which covered municipalities.
**Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya** led the agitation; he was never a minister (he died in **1929**).
xa: The municipality was formed in **Jan 1920**; tax rose from **Rs 4,000 to Rs 40,000** a year.
**Gandhi** wrote in **Young India** that the municipality only meant more taxes.
After the movement failed, the **people returned** to their homes.

210.s: The book *Chirala Perala Vanavasam* was written by:
210.x: *Chirala Perala Vanavasam* was written by Pisapati Narayana Sastri.
210.tq: Use the author–work association and reject names linked with other events in the same region.
xs: ***Chirala Perala Vanavasam*** was written by **Pisapati Narayana Sastri** — option **(2)**.
**Erramalli Narasimha Rao** is the biographer of **Alluri Sitarama Raju**, not of Chirala-Perala.
**Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya** led the movement; **Bezawada Gopala Reddy** abolished the municipality in **1938**.
xa: **"Malapalli"** novel — **Unnava Lakshminarayana**; **Desabhakti Geyam** — **Gurajada Apparao**.
"**Kallumanandoy**" — **Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri**; "**Veera gandham tecchinaramu**" — **Tripuraneni Ramaswamy**.
National pledge "**Bharata Desam Naa Matrubhoomi**" — **Paidimarri Venkata Subbarao**.

210.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
210.x: Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary was known as Andhra Shivaji. Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya was associated with the title Andhra Ratna, while Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Choudary was called Kavi Raju.
210.tq: Match each personality with the exact title, watching for swapped titles.
xs: **Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary — Andhra Shivaji** is correct — option **(2)**.
**Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya** was "**Andhra Ratna**", not Andhra Shivaji.
**Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Choudary** was "**Kavi Raju**"; **Machiraju Ramamurthy** was the karanam of **Chandavolu**.
xa: ⚠ "**Abhinava Dandi**" is the medieval poet **Ketana**, not a freedom fighter.
**Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao** wrote the autobiography ***Na Jeevitha Katha***.
Duggirala was also called "**Ramadasu**".

210.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
210.x: Ketana was associated with the title Abhinava Dandi, not Andhra Ratna. Andhra Ratna was the title of Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya.
210.tq: Find the swapped title by checking each personality–title pair.
xs: **Ketana — Andhra Ratna** is wrongly matched — option **(3)**.
**Ketana**, the medieval poet, was "**Abhinava Dandi**"; "**Andhra Ratna**" was **Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya**.
The rest are correct: Tripuraneni — **Kavi Raju**; Veeraiah Chowdary — **Andhra Shivaji**; Duggirala — **Ramadandu** (**1921**).
xa: ⚠ Duggirala's corps was **Ramadandu**, not **Shanti Sena** (Pedanandipadu).
Duggirala studied **M.A. (Hons) Economics** at **Edinburgh** (**1916**).
After the NCM he joined the **Swaraj Party** as one of its Andhra secretaries.

210.s:
With reference to the government response to the Pedanandipadu campaign, consider the following statements:
1. L. T. Harris was sent to Guntur after attributing the resignations to Congress influence.
2. Rutherford was deployed to deal with the situation.
3. Rutherford’s proposal to ban the Shanti Sena was accepted by the Madras Government.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
210.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Rutherford’s proposal to ban the Shanti Sena was rejected by the Madras Government, making statement 3 false.
210.tq: Use the authority-action trap: a proposed government measure was rejected, not accepted.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: **L.T. Harris** blamed **Congress** and was sent to **Guntur**.
Statement 2 correct: **Rutherford** was deployed.
Statement 3 wrong: Rutherford's plan to ban the **Shanti Sena** was **rejected by the Madras Government**.
xa: Collector **A. Gellatly** blamed **low pay and workload** for the resignations.
As **Special Commissioner** in Rampa, Rutherford **exiled 55 helpers** and issued warrants for **183**.
Rutherford also tried **Duggirala** at **Srikakulam**.

210.s: Which of the following combinations correctly represents the Congress positions during the Pedanandipadu campaign?
o: Nyapathi Subbarao supported it; T. Prakasam urged its withdrawal
Rutherford and L. T. Harris supported it; Nyapathi Subbarao opposed it
Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri opposed it; Konda Venkatappayya urged restraint
Konda Venkatappayya and Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri supported it; Nyapathi Subbarao urged restraint
210.x: Konda Venkatappayya and Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri backed the campaign, whereas Nyapathi Subbarao urged restraint.
210.tq: Compare the positions of closely associated leaders rather than their official roles.
xs: **Konda Venkatappayya and Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri supported** it; **Nyapathi Subbarao urged restraint** — option **(4)**.
**Rutherford** and **L.T. Harris** were British officials, not Congress leaders.
**T. Prakasam** sat on the inquiry committee that **praised** the campaign but advised waiting for **Bardoli**.
xa: Inquiry committee: **T. Prakasam**, **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**, **Dantu Narayana Raju**.
**Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri** also wrote the song "**Kallumanandoy**".
Withdrawn on **11 Feb 1922** after **Gandhi's message** to Konda Venkatappayya.

210.s: The Pedanandipadu no-tax campaign was suspended after the Guntur District Congress Committee received Gandhi’s message to Konda Venkatappayya on:
210.x: Gandhi’s message to suspend the campaign reached the Guntur District Congress Committee on 11 February 1922, after which the campaign ended with the Non-Cooperation Movement.
210.tq: Match the precise date with the final administrative action in the campaign.
xs: Gandhi's suspension message reached the Guntur DCC on **11 February 1922** — option **(2)**.
**5 Nov 1921** was the **Delhi AICC**, which allowed **no-tax** civil disobedience.
**6 Dec 1922** was Alluri's defeat at **Peddagaddapalem**; **7 May 1924** was **Alluri's** death.
xa: The campaign then **ended with the NCM**.
The **Bezawada AICC (1921)** put Gandhi's programme into Andhra.
Gandhi's message was sent to **Konda Venkatappayya**.

210.s:
Which of the following were unique features of the Pedanandipadu no-tax campaign (1922)?
1. Mass resignation of village officers - 18 of 19 in the firka
2. Formation of the Shanti Sena
3. Mass exodus of residents to a new camp outside municipal limits
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
210.x: Features 1 and 2 are correct: 18 of 19 village officers resigned (led by Chandavolu karanam Machiraju Ramamurthy), and the Shanti Sena was formed. Feature 3 belongs to Chirala-Perala (exodus to Ramnagar, 1921). So B, C and D, which include 3, are wrong.
210.tq: Pedanandipadu = resignations + Shanti Sena; Chirala-Perala = exodus.
xs: Features **1 and 2 only** — option **(1)**.
Feature 1 correct: **mass resignation** of village officers, **18 of 19** in the firka.
Feature 2 correct: formation of the **Shanti Sena**.
Feature 3 wrong: the **mass exodus** to a camp (**Ramnagar**) belongs to **Chirala-Perala** (**1921**).
xa: Resignations were led by Chandavolu karanam **Machiraju Ramamurthy**.
Shanti Sena in the firka was led by **Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary**.
Guntur district saw **29** resignations in all.

210.s: The ‘Desasevikalu’ organisation was associated with which of the following objectives?
o: Promotion of forest administration under the colonial government
Non-violent reform and propaganda for Swaraj
Armed revolutionary training and military recruitment
210.x: Desasevikalu was a women’s organisation within the Congress that pledged itself to non-violent reform and Swaraj propaganda.
210.tq: Infer the organisation’s purpose from its ideological and organisational setting.
xs: **Desasevikalu** was pledged to **non-violent reform and Swaraj propaganda** — option **(3)**.
It was a **women's organisation within Congress**, not a forest, tax or armed body.
xa: **Andhra Mahila Sabha** was founded by **Durgabai Deshmukh** (Madras, **1937**).
**12 women** were jailed at Chirala-Perala; the first was **Ravuri Alivelu Mangatayaramma**.
**Duvvuri Subbamma** (**Desabandhavi**) was also arrested.

210.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Maganti Annapurnamma — first Telugu woman to donate all her ornaments to the Tilak Swaraj Fund
Durgabai Deshmukh — founded the Andhra Mahila Sabha (1937)
Yamini Purna Tilakam — hartals in Guntur
Duvvuri Subbamma — first woman jailed in the Chirala-Perala movement
210.x: The first woman jailed at Chirala-Perala was Ravuri Alivelu Mangatayaramma; Duvvuri Subbamma ('Desabandhavi') was also arrested but was not the first. The other three pairs are correct.
210.tq: Tilak Swaraj Fund ornaments = Maganti Annapurnamma; Andhra Mahila Sabha = Durgabai.
xs: **Duvvuri Subbamma — first woman jailed** is wrong — option **(4)**.
The first woman jailed at Chirala-Perala was **Ravuri Alivelu Mangatayaramma**; Duvvuri Subbamma (**Desabandhavi**) was arrested later.
The other pairs are correct: **Maganti Annapurnamma** (Tilak Swaraj Fund), **Durgabai** (Andhra Mahila Sabha, **1937**), **Yamini Purna Tilakam** (Guntur hartals).
xa: **12 women** were jailed in the Chirala-Perala movement.
Durgabai collected **Rs 5,000** at **Kakinada** in **April 1921**.

210.s: Who was the first editor of Andhra Patrika during 1916–18?
210.x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao served as the first editor of Andhra Patrika during 1916–18; Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao was its founder.
210.tq: Distinguish the founder from the first editor of the same newspaper.
xs: The first editor of **Andhra Patrika** (**1916-18**) was **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao** — option **(3)**.
**Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** was its **founder**, not first editor.
**Mutnuri Krishna Rao** edited **Krishna Patrika**; **Tanguturi Prakasam** ran **Swarajya**.
xa: **Swarajya** daily began on **29 Oct 1921**.
**Desamata** — **Chilakamarti Lakshminarasimham**.
**Zamin Rythu** — **Nellore Venkataramana Naidu**.

210.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
210.x: Zamin Rythu was associated with Nellore Venkataramana Naidu. Krovi Lingaraju was associated with the Congress weekly and its 1931 sedition case.
210.tq: Find the swapped newspaper-person pair among editors and founders of Andhra papers.
xs: **Zamin Rythu — Krovi Lingaraju** is wrongly matched — option **(4)**.
**Zamin Rythu** was run by **Nellore Venkataramana Naidu**; **Krovi Lingaraju** is linked with the **Congress** weekly (**1931** sedition case).
The rest are correct: **Desamata** — Chilakamarti; **Krishna Patrika** — Mutnuri Krishna Rao; **Swarajya** — Prakasam.
xa: ⚠ **Chilakamarti** = Desamata + "**Bharata Khandambu**"; **Prakasam** = Swarajya.
**Andhra Patrika**: founder **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**; first editor **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao**.
**Krishna Patrika** was published from **Machilipatnam**.

210.s: Which work was written by Unnava Lakshminarayana?
210.x: Unnava Lakshminarayana wrote the novel Malapalli.
210.tq: Distinguish literary authors by matching each work with its correct creator.
xs: **Unnava Lakshminarayana** wrote the novel **"Malapalli"** — option **(4)**.
"**Bharata Desam Naa Matrubhoomi**" is by **Paidimarri Venkata Subbarao**; **Desabhakti Geyam** is by **Gurajada Apparao**.
xa: Unnava founded **Sharada Niketan, Guntur** with wife **Lakshmibayamma**.
"**Bharata Khandambu Chakkani Padi Aavu**" — **Chilakamarti Lakshminarasimham**.
***Chirala Perala Vanavasam*** — **Pisapati Narayana Sastri**.

210.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Song or work)
a. Bharata Khandambu Chakkani Padi Aavu
b. Veera gandham tecchinaramu
c. Kallumanandoy
 d. Desabhakti Geyam

List-II (Author)
i. Gurajada Apparao
ii. Tripuraneni Ramaswamy
iii. Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri
iv. Chilakamarti Lakshminarasimham

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
210.x: Bharata Khandambu Chakkani Padi Aavu was written by Chilakamarti Lakshminarasimham; Veera gandham tecchinaramu by Tripuraneni Ramaswamy; Kallumanandoy by Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri; and Desabhakti Geyam by Gurajada Apparao.
210.tq: Start from a sure author-work pair and complete the matching code by elimination.
xs: Correct code: **a–iv, b–ii, c–iii, d–i** — option **(1)**.
**Bharata Khandambu Chakkani Padi Aavu** — **Chilakamarti Lakshminarasimham** (iv).
**Veera gandham tecchinaramu** (Civil Disobedience) — **Tripuraneni Ramaswamy** (ii).
**Kallumanandoy** — **Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri** (iii); **Desabhakti Geyam** — **Gurajada Apparao** (i).
xa: Chilakamarti also ran the paper **Desamata**.
Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Choudary was called "**Kavi Raju**".
National pledge — **Paidimarri Venkata Subbarao**; novel **"Malapalli"** — **Unnava Lakshminarayana**.

210.s:
Consider the following statements about the Hyderabad State Congress:
1. It was formed in 1938.
2. Its first president was Swami Ramananda Tirtha.
3. The Nizam lifted the ban on it in 1946.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
210.x: All three statements are correct: the Hyderabad State Congress was formed in 1938, Swami Ramananda Tirtha was its first president, and the ban was lifted in 1946.
210.tq: Combine formation, leadership and ban-lifting dates in one chronological institutional question.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** **1, 2 and 3**.
The **Hyderabad State Congress** was **formed in 1938**; first president **Swami Ramananda Tirtha**.
**Banned by the Nizam in 1938**, the ban was **lifted in 1946**.
xa: A **satyagraha (1938)** was launched against the ban.
It coincided with the **Osmania Vandemataram agitation**.

210.s:
Consider the following statements about the Andhra freedom movement:
1. The period 1921-31 is called the 'Glorious Decade' of Andhra.
2. Chirala-Perala, Palnadu and Pedanandipadu are examples of tribal armed resistance.
3. In 1921-22, Guntur saw mass exodus, resignation of officials and a no-tax campaign.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
210.x: Statement 1 is correct: 1921-31 is the 'Glorious Decade'. Statement 2 is wrong: Chirala-Perala, Palnadu and Pedanandipadu showed mass non-cooperation; it was Rampa that showed tribal armed resistance. Statement 3 is correct: these were the NCM's most original methods in Guntur. So 1 and 3 only; options with 2 are wrong.
210.tq: Mass non-cooperation = Chirala-Perala, Palnadu, Pedanandipadu; armed tribal resistance = Rampa.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: **1921-31** is the "**Glorious Decade**" of Andhra.
Statement 2 wrong: Chirala-Perala, Palnadu, Pedanandipadu showed **mass non-cooperation**; **Rampa** showed **tribal armed resistance**.
Statement 3 correct: Guntur in **1921-22** saw **mass exodus**, **officials resigning**, **no-tax** campaign.
xa: Local Congress **rivalry** and **money shortage** sank Chirala-Perala.
**Gandhi's halt** ended Pedanandipadu at its peak.
Unlike Gandhian forest satyagrahas, **Alluri** used **armed guerrilla war**, yet respected Gandhi.

210.s: The Agency district in Andhra Pradesh was renamed as:
210.x: The Agency district was named Alluri Sitarama Raju district in recognition of the revolutionary leader’s legacy.
210.tq: Test the official name rather than an honorific or regional description.
xs: The Agency district is named **Alluri Sitarama Raju district** — option **(4)**.
"**Manyam Veerudu**" is Alluri's **title** (APPSC **2024** key), not a district name.
xa: Alluri led the **Rampa / Manyam Rebellion**, **January 1922 - May 1924**.
His **30-ft bronze statue** stands at **Bhimavaram** (**125th birth anniversary**).
The **Bhogapuram** airport (Vizianagaram) is also named after him.

210.s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The no-tax campaign was associated with Pedanandipadu.
Statement B: Pedanandipadu was in Bapatla taluka of Guntur district and was associated with Paravataneni Veerayya Chowdary.
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
210.x: Both are true: Pedanandipadu in Bapatla taluk of Guntur district ran a famous no-tax campaign in 1921-22, led by Parvataneni Veerayya Chowdary.
210.tq: Check each statement separately.
n: The no-tax campaign was associated with Pedanandipadu. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 18-19]
Pedanandipadu was located in Bapatla taluka. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 18-19]
Pedanandipadu was located in Guntur district. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 18-19]
Pedanandipadu was associated with Paravataneni Veerayya Chowdary. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 18-19]
xs: **Both Statement A and Statement B are true** — option **(1)**.
A true: **Pedanandipadu** is associated with the **no-tax campaign** (**Jan-Feb 1922**).
B true: Pedanandipadu, **Bapatla taluka**, **Guntur** — associated with **Paravataneni Veerayya Chowdary**.
xa: Unique feature: **mass resignation of village officers** — **18 of 19** in the firka.
**Shanti Sena** was led by Parvataneni, called "**Andhra Shivaji**".
Withdrawn on **11 Feb 1922** on **Gandhi's message**.

211.s: “Bharata khandambu chakkani paadi aavu” was improvised on which occasion?
o: During the Salt Satyagraha at Dandi in 1930
During Bipin Chandra Pal’s speeches at Rajahmundry in April 1907
During the Home Rule agitation in Madras in 1916
During Gandhi’s visit to Vijayawada in 1921
211.x: Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham improvised the song during Bipin Chandra Pal’s speeches at Rajahmundry in April 1907.
211.tq: Lock the answer through the distinctive place, speaker and month-year combination.
xs: **"Bharata khandambu chakkani paadi aavu"** was improvised during **Bipin Chandra Pal's speeches at Rajahmundry, April 1907** — option **(2)**.
**Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham** was translating Pal's speeches when he composed it.
The song cast **India as a cow** whose milk the British were taking.
xa: His later verse: "**Bharata khandambe okka pedda bandikhana**".
Chilakamarti is called the **first Telugu national poet**; he edited **Desamata**.
The song was an APPSC **G2 2019** key question.

211.s: Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham is recognised as the first Telugu national poet. Which work is associated with the distinction of being the first Telugu national song?
211.x: “Hinduvulara ennaallee gati” is recognised as the first Telugu national song, while Chilakamarti is recognised as the first Telugu national poet.
211.tq: Distinguish the poet’s title from the separately identified first national song.
xs: The **first Telugu national song** is "**Hinduvulara ennaallee gati**" — option **(3)**.
**Roshanara** (Kopparapu Subbarao) was the **first play banned** by the British; **Ekanta Seva** is the "Telugu Gitanjali".
"**Bharata khandambe okka pedda bandikhana**" is Chilakamarti's later verse.
xa: **First Telugu national poet**: **Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham**.
Often called the first nationalist song: "**The Cry of Mother India**" (**Krishna Patrika**, **15 Dec 1905**).
⚠ Per **C. Narayana Reddy**, the first is "**Melukonumi Bharata Putruda**" (**Andhra Bharati**, Oct **1909**).

211.s: Which song, published in Krishna Patrika on 15 December 1905, is often called the first nationalist song in Telugu?
211.x: The Cry of Mother India (Krishna Patrika, 15 Dec 1905) is often called the first nationalist song. C. Narayana Reddy instead gave that place to Melukonumi Bharata Putruda (Andhra Bharati, Oct 1909). Bharata khandambu chakkani paadi aavu was Chilakamarti's verse at Bipin Chandra Pal's Rajahmundry speeches (1907), and Desamunu preminchumanna is Gurajada's song in Mutyala Saralu.
211.tq: 1905 Krishna Patrika = Cry of Mother India; 1909 Andhra Bharati = Melukonumi (C. Narayana Reddy's choice).
xs: "**The Cry of Mother India**" (**Krishna Patrika**, **15 Dec 1905**) is often called the first nationalist song — option **(1)**.
**C. Narayana Reddy** instead names "**Melukonumi Bharata Putruda**" (**Andhra Bharati**, Oct **1909**).
"**Bharata khandambu**" was Chilakamarti's **1907** song; "**Desamunu preminchumanna**" is **Gurajada's**.
xa: **First Telugu national song**: "**Hinduvulara ennaallee gati**".
**First Telugu national poet**: **Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham**.

211.s: Who wrote Japaneeyamu, which celebrated Japan’s victory over Russia in 1905?
211.x: Japaneeyamu was written by Sriram Veerabrahmam of Bandar and celebrated Japan’s victory over Russia in 1905.
211.tq: Match the world event and patriotic work with the correct author.
xs: **Japaneeyamu** was written by **Sriram Veerabrahmam** (Bandar) — option **(4)**.
It celebrated **Japan's victory over Russia (1905)**.
**Adipudi Somanatha Rao** wrote **Japan Charitra**; **Damaraju Pundarikakshudu** wrote **Panchala Parabhavam**; **Umar Alisha** wrote **Mahabharata Kaurava Rangam**.
xa: Japan Charitra was dedicated to the **Raja of Munagala**, who named his sons **Togo and Nogi**.
Japaneeyamu — Sriram Veerabrahmam was asked in the **G2 2025** match.

211.s:
Consider the following statements about Panchala Parabhavam:
1. It was written by Damaraju Pundarikakshudu.
2. It dealt with the Jallianwala Bagh tragedy.
3. Dyer was portrayed as Duryodhana.
4. Twenty-five students in Vizag were arrested for staging it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
211.x: All four statements are correct. The play concerned Jallianwala Bagh, cast Dyer as Duryodhana, was discussed in the British Parliament, and led to the arrest of 25 Vizag students who staged it.
211.tq: Treat the play, event, characterisation and consequence as separate factual components.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)** **1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Panchala Parabhavam** was by **Damaraju Pundarikakshudu**, on **Jallianwala Bagh**.
It cast **Dyer as Duryodhana**; **25 students in Vizag** were arrested for staging it.
xa: The play was **discussed in the British Parliament**.
**Padmavyuham** — **Kallakuri Narayana Rao** (**1919**).
**Mahabharata Kaurava Rangam** — **Umar Alisha** (**1916**).

211.s: The lines “Desamunu preminchumanna, manchi annadi penchumanna” are associated with which poet and collection?
211.x: The lines were written by Gurajada Apparao and form part of Mutyala Saralu. The poem was published in Andhra Bharati.
211.tq: Use the poet–work pair directly; nearby nationalist poets are used as distractors.
xs: "**Desamunu preminchumanna**" is by **Gurajada Apparao**, in ***Mutyala Saralu*** — option **(4)**.
**Harijana Paatalu** is Garimella's; **Andhravali** is Rayaprolu's; **Matru Desa Sankeertanam** is Duvvuri Ramireddy's.
xa: The poem was published in **Andhra Bharati** and called the "**national anthem of Telugu people**".
Same poem: "**Desamante matti kadoi, desamante manushuloi**".
⚠ **Garimella** = "Maakoddee"; **Tripuraneni** = "Veera gandham".

211.s: Which one of the following statements correctly explains the idea expressed in the line “Desamante matti kadoi, desamante manushuloi”?
o: The nation is identified with its ruling dynasty.
The nation is represented only by its religious institutions.
The nation is defined by its geographical boundaries alone.
The nation consists primarily of its people rather than merely its soil.
211.x: Gurajada’s line means that a nation is its people, not merely its soil. It is part of the same poem in Mutyala Saralu.
211.tq: Translate the famous line into its precise underlying concept.
xs: The line means the **nation is its people, not merely its soil** — option **(4)**.
It is from **Gurajada Apparao's** "Desamunu preminchumanna" (***Mutyala Saralu***).
xa: The poem was called the "**national anthem of Telugu people**".
Gurajada made **vyavaharika bhasha** (spoken Telugu) normal.
Gurajada also wrote ***Kanyasulkam*** (staged **1893**).

211.s: Who wrote the patriotic lyric “Ye desamegina ... pogadara nee talli bhoomi Bharatini”, commonly known by its title Janmabhoomi?
211.x: The patriotic lyric Janmabhoomi was written by Rayaprolu Subbarao.
211.tq: Identify the author from a distinctive line and title.
xs: The lyric ***Janmabhoomi*** ("Ye desamegina ... pogadara nee talli bhoomi Bharatini") is by **Rayaprolu Subbarao** — option **(3)**.
**Sankarambadi Sundarachari** wrote "**Ma Telugu Talliki**"; **Basavaraju Apparao** wrote "**Kollayi gattithenemi**".
xa: Rayaprolu was born in **1892**, **Guntur**.
He is the **Father of Telugu Romanticism** and founder of **Bhavakavitvam**.
His works: ***Andhravali***, ***Swatantrya Rathamu***.

211.s:
Consider the following statements about Rayaprolu Subba Rao:
1. He is called the Father of Telugu Romanticism.
2. He pioneered Bhava Kavitvam, drawing on Shelley and Keats.
3. His new concept 'Amalina Srungaram' meant heroic sentiment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
