217.s: In which year did the Madras Congress Ministry appoint the committee on the zamindari system, with C. Rajagopalachari as Chief Minister and Tanguturi Prakasam as Revenue Minister?
217.x: The Madras Congress Ministry appointed the committee in 1937. C. Rajagopalachari was the Chief Minister and Tanguturi Prakasam served as the Revenue Minister.
217.tq: Use the ministry-composition clue to identify the correct year and distinguish the Chief Minister from the Revenue Minister.
xs: The committee was appointed in **1937** by the Madras Congress ministry — option **(2)**.
**Rajaji** was CM and **Prakasam** **Revenue Minister**.
It was **formally constituted** in **Sept 1938** (**9** members) per some notes.
xa: Also called the **Estate Land / Zamindari Enquiry Committee**.
Report completed **7 Nov 1938**.

217.s: Which of the following was the principal conclusion of the committee’s report regarding the relationship between land, the tiller and the zamindar?
o: The State alone owned the land and the zamindar had no role in revenue collection.
The zamindar was the absolute owner of the land and the tiller was only a tenant.
Land belonged jointly to the zamindar and the cultivating tenants.
Land belonged to the tiller, while the zamindar was merely a tax collector.
217.x: The report held that land belongs to the tiller and that the zamindar is only a tax collector.
217.tq: Test the precise relationship stated in the report and avoid the swapped-owner and tenant descriptions.
xs: The report held that **land belongs to the tiller** and the **zamindar is only a tax collector** — option **(4)**.
The report was completed on **7 Nov 1938**.
xa: **Prakasam** regretted it did not say outright whether **zamindari should be abolished**.
**Communists** pioneered the **land to the tiller** demand.

217.s: Who led the yatra from Ichchapuram to submit a petition to the committee on the zamindari system?
o: Gouthu Latchanna and Pulleti Shyamasundara Rao
Pulleti Shyamasundara Rao and C. Rajagopalachari
217.x: Gouthu Latchanna and Pulleti Shyamasundara Rao led the yatra from Ichchapuram to petition the committee.
217.tq: Match the specific action and starting place with the correct pair of leaders.
xs: The **Ichchapuram** yatra was led by **Gouthu Latchanna and Pulleti Shyamasundara Rao** — option **(2)**.
They petitioned the **Prakasam Committee**.
xa: The committee's report was completed on **7 Nov 1938**.
**Mandasa** (Srikakulam) saw police firing on **1 April 1940**.

217.s: Who introduced the Madras Estates Abolition Bill on 11 November 1947?
217.x: Revenue Minister Kala Venkata Rao introduced the Bill on 11 November 1947.
217.tq: Identify the minister associated with introducing legislation rather than giving assent to it.
xs: Revenue Minister **Kala Venkata Rao** introduced the Bill on **11 Nov 1947** — option **(2)**.
**C. Rajagopalachari**, as **Governor-General**, gave assent on **2 Apr 1949**.
**Pattabhi** called for the struggle in **1920**; **N.G. Ranga** presided at Venkatagiri (**1931**).
xa: The Bill was passed by the **Madras Assembly** in **Nov 1948**.
It came into force on **7 Sept 1949**.

217.s:
Consider the following statements about the consequences of the Estates Abolition legislation:
1. It abolished zamindari and inamdari estates.
2. Tenants became direct ryots of the state.
3. Zamindars were paid compensation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
217.x: The legislation abolished zamindari and inamdari estates, made tenants direct ryots of the state and provided compensation to zamindars.
217.tq: Test the three principal legal consequences together.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** **1, 2 and 3**.
The Act **abolished zamindari and inamdari estates**; **tenants became direct ryots of the state**.
**Zamindars were paid compensation**.
xa: The **1st (1951)** and **4th (1955)** Amendments shielded abolition laws.
Estates were taken over from **1950**.

217.s: The Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, which abolished zamindari in Andhra, bears which year in its name?
217.x: It is the 1948 Act (APPSC G2 2008 PYQ: pick 1948). Trap: some sources call it the 1949 Act because it received assent on 2 April 1949 and came into force on 7 September 1949; estates were taken over from 1950; the Bill was introduced on 11 November 1947.
217.tq: Act year 1948; assent and commencement 1949; takeover 1950.
xs: The Act's name year is **1948** — option **(1)** (**G2 2008** PYQ).
⚠ Some notes call it the "**1949**" Act because assent and commencement fell in **1949**; takeover from **1950**.
**1947** is the year the **Bill** was introduced.
xa: It was the **first law** of independent India to get the GG's assent.
It abolished **zamindari and inamdari estates**.

217.s: Which Constitutional Amendments shielded zamindari abolition laws such as the Madras Act of 1948?
217.x: The 1st Amendment (1951) and the 4th Amendment (1955) shielded zamindari abolition laws from challenge. The other pairs are not the amendments that gave this protection.
217.tq: Abolition laws shielded by the 1st (1951) and 4th (1955) Amendments.
xs: The **1st (1951)** and **4th (1955)** Amendments shielded zamindari abolition laws — option **(1)**.
They protected Acts like the **Madras Act of 1948**.

219.s: Which one of the following was NOT associated with the Ramosi uprisings in Maharashtra?
219.x: Chittur Singh, Umaji Naik and Bapu Trimbakji Sawant led the Ramosis, who rose after the fall of the Peshwa. Narayan Rao is not linked to the Ramosis (APPSC 2019 trap).
219.tq: Ramosi = Umaji Naik, Chittur Singh; Narayan Rao is the trap.
xs: **Narayan Rao** was not linked to the Ramosis — option **(4)** is the answer (APPSC 2019 trap).
**Chittur Singh**, **Umaji Naik** and **Bapu Trimbakji Sawant** led the Ramosi uprisings.
xa: The Ramosis rose after the **fall of the Peshwa**.
Period: **1822 onward**, in the **Western Ghats (Maharashtra)**.
The **Bhil** rising (**1818-31**) was also in Maharashtra, in **Khandesh**.

219.s:
Consider the following statements about the Santhal Hul:
1. The British invited the Santhals to settle in the Rajmahal Hills after failing to control the Paharias.
2. The tract demarcated for Santhal settlement was called Damin-i-Koh.
3. The Hul began at Bhognadih on 30 June 1856.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
219.x: Statement 1 is correct: the British failed to control the Paharias and invited the Santhals. Statement 2 is correct: the tract was Damin-i-Koh. Statement 3 is wrong: the Hul began at Bhognadih on 30 June 1855 (Hul Divas); it was crushed in 1856. So '1 and 2 only'.
219.tq: Hul began 30 June 1855, crushed 1856.
xs: **Statements 1 and 2** are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: the British failed to control the **Paharias** and invited the **Santhals** to the **Rajmahal Hills**.
Statement 2: the tract was **Damin-i-Koh**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the Hul began at **Bhognadih** on **30 June 1855** (**Hul Divas**); it was crushed in **1856**.
xa: Leaders: **Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu**, **Chand and Bhairav**, sisters **Phulo-Jhano**.
About **30,000 Santhals** proclaimed **Santhal Raj**; over **15,000** were killed.
After the Hul, **Santhal Parganas** became a separate district with special land laws.

219.s: Which of the following groups was associated with the leadership of the Santhal Hul in addition to Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu?
o: Chand, Bhairav and the sisters Phulo-Jhano
Jatra Bhagat, Govind Giri and Motilal Tejawat
Umaji Naik, Chittur Singh and Narayan Rao
Ganga Narayan, Budhu Bhagat and Tirot Sing
219.x: Chand and Bhairav, along with the sisters Phulo and Jhano, were associated with the leadership of the Santhal Hul.
219.tq: Distinguish members of one revolt’s leadership from leaders of other tribal movements.
xs: **Chand, Bhairav** and the sisters **Phulo-Jhano** led the Hul with Sidhu and Kanhu — option **(1)** is correct.
**Jatra Bhagat** led the **Tana Bhagat** movement; **Govind Giri** the Bhils; **Motilal Tejawat** the **Eki movement**.
**Budhu Bhagat** led the **Kol** rising; **Tirot Sing** the **Khasi** rising; **Ganga Narayan** the **Bhumij** rising.
xa: About **30,000 Santhals** proclaimed **Santhal Raj**.
The Hul began at **Bhognadih** on **30 June 1855**; crushed in **1856** with over **15,000** killed.
**Hul Divas** is observed on **30 June**.

219.s: Which one of the following was an important cause of the Santhal Hul?
o: Oppression by zamindars, moneylenders and police
The abolition of the Khuntkatti system by the Santhals themselves
The transfer of Upper Assam to Purandar Singh
The introduction of bonded labour in Mewar
219.x: The Santhals faced oppression by zamindars, moneylenders, commonly called dikus, and the police. The Khuntkatti issue belonged principally to the Munda movement.
219.tq: Match the cause with the revolt instead of the similarly worded causes of other movements.
xs: The Hul was caused by **oppression by zamindars, moneylenders (dikus) and police** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Khuntkatti** destruction was the **Munda** (Birsa) grievance; **Purandar Singh** relates to the **Ahom** rebellion; **bonded labour** to **Govind Giri's** Bhils.
xa: **Damin-i-Koh** = tract for Santhal settlement in the **Rajmahal Hills**.
The British had invited Santhals after failing to control the **Paharias**.
⚠ Trap: **SPT Act** = **1876 / 1949** (Santhals); **CNT Act** = **1908** (Birsa).

219.s: After the Santhal Hul, which one of the following developments took place?
o: Santhal Parganas became a separate district with special laws protecting tribal land.
Upper Assam was restored to the Santhal leaders.
The Chotanagpur Tenancy Act was enacted in 1876.
Kolhan was placed under the Munda-Manki system immediately after the Ulgulan.
219.x: After the Hul, Santhal Parganas was created as a separate district and special laws were introduced to protect tribal land. The Chotanagpur Tenancy Act came later, in 1908.
219.tq: Find the correct post-revolt administrative consequence among closely related outcomes.
xs: After the Hul, **Santhal Parganas** became a **separate district with special laws protecting tribal land** — option **(1)**.
The **Chotanagpur Tenancy Act** is of **1908**, not 1876.
**Munda-Manki** rule in Kolhan came via **Wilkinson's Rule (1837)**, after the **Kol** rising.
xa: The **Santhal Parganas Tenancy Act** is dated **1876** in some notes; the current SPT Act = **1949**.
The CNT Act **bars transfer of tribal land to non-tribals** and recognises **Khuntkatti** rights.
The Hul was crushed in **1856**; over **15,000** killed.

219.s: The Rampa Rebellion of 1879–80 was primarily directed against
o: the imprisonment of Jamedar Chida Khan
the disbanding of the Vizianagaram troops
the Permanent Settlement imposed on Narayana Babu
Munsubar Madhava Bhupati Dev and oppressive taxation
219.x: The 1879–80 Rampa Rebellion in the Rampachodavaram Agency opposed Munsubar Madhava Bhupati Dev and oppressive taxes. Madhava Bhupati Dev had been appointed in 1848.
219.tq: Identify the immediate cause and official targeted by the uprising.
xs: The **1879-80 Rampa** rebellion opposed **Munsubar Madhava Bhupati Dev** and **oppressive taxation** — option **(4)**.
Madhava Bhupati Dev was appointed in **1848** and was an **exploitative mansabdar**.
Forest/podu restrictions under the **Madras Forest Act** were another cause.
xa: Rampa lay in **Rampachodavaram** Agency, **Godavari district** (APPSC G2 2011: **1879**).
**Sullivan** of the **Madras Revenue Board** removed the mansabdar.
The rising was suppressed in **Sept 1879** and crushed by **Nov 1880**.

219.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes the two Rampa rebellions?
o: The 1879–80 rebellion was associated with Alluri Sitarama Raju, whereas the 1922–24 rebellion was led by Madhava Bhupati Dev.
The 1922–24 rebellion preceded the 1879–80 rebellion and was led by Ambul Reddy.
The 1879–80 rebellion was led by local agency leaders, whereas the 1922–24 rebellion was led by Alluri Sitarama Raju.
Both rebellions were led by Alluri Sitarama Raju and occurred in the same period.
219.x: The 1879–80 Rampa Rebellion was led by local figures including Chandrayya, Tammanna Dora, Pulikantha Sambaiah and Ambul Reddy. Alluri Sitarama Raju led the later 1922–24 Rampa Rebellion.
219.tq: Discriminate between similar names and dates instead of transferring the famous leader to the earlier revolt.
xs: The **1879-80** rising had **local agency leaders**; **1922-24** was led by **Alluri Sitarama Raju** — option **(3)**.
1879 leaders: **Pulikantha Sambaiah**, **Darabandala Chandrayya**, **Karu Tammanna Dora**, **Ambul Reddy**.
**Madhava Bhupati Dev** was the **mansabdar** they rose against, not a leader.
xa: ⚠ Trap: Rampa **1879** (Sambaiah, Chandrayya) vs Rampa **1922-24** (Alluri).
Alluri's rising involved the **Koyas/Konda Doras**.
About **70 rebels** were arrested by **Aug 1879**.

219.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Leader)
A. Pulikantha Sambaiah
B. Darabandala Chandrayya
C. Karu Tammanna Dora
D. Ambul Reddy

List-II (Association with the Rampa rebellion)
1. Leader associated with the 1879 rising
2. Burnt the Addatheegala police station
3. Leader associated with the 1879 rising
4. Leader associated with the Rekapalle episode

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
219.x: Pulikantha Sambaiah and Karu Tammanna Dora were leaders of the 1879 Rampa rising; Darabandala Chandrayya burnt the Addatheegala police station; Ambul Reddy was associated with Rekapalle.
219.tq: Start from the sure pair linking Chandrayya with the Addatheegala police station.
xs: The correct match is **A-1, B-2, C-3, D-4** — option **(1)**.
**Pulikantha Sambaiah** and **Karu Tammanna Dora** were leaders of the **1879** Rampa rising.
**Darabandala Chandrayya** burnt the **Addatheegala** police station.
**Ambul Reddy** attacked **Vaddagudem** police station on **10 July 1879** (**Rekapalle**).
xa: ⚠ Trap: these 1879 leaders differ from **Alluri** (**1922-24**).
**Tomas (Tomma) Dora** led the **Koya rising** of **1879-80**.
Rampa suppressed **Sept 1879**; crushed by **Nov 1880**.

219.s:
Consider the following statements about the Rekapalle rising of 1879:
1. It was a revolt against forest laws, triggered by a rise in the podu tax during a famine.
2. Ambul Reddy attacked the Vaddagudem police station in July 1879.
3. It was led by Alluri Sitarama Raju.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
219.x: Statement 1 is correct: the podu tax was raised from 4 annas per axe to 4-12 annas during a famine (APPSC 2017: the 1879 forest-law revolt was at Rekapalli). Statement 2 is correct: Ambul Reddy raided Vaddagudem police station on 10 July 1879. Statement 3 is wrong: Alluri led the separate 1922-24 Rampa rebellion. Hence '1 and 2 only'; options with 3 are wrong.
219.tq: Rekapalle 1879 = podu tax + Ambul Reddy; Alluri = 1922-24.
xs: **Statements 1 and 2** are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: the podu tax rose from **4 annas per axe** to **4-12 annas** during a famine (APPSC 2017: forest-law revolt at **Rekapalli**).
Statement 2: **Ambul Reddy** attacked **Vaddagudem** police station on **10 July 1879**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Alluri** led the separate **1922-24** Rampa rebellion.
xa: Rekapalle lay in **Bhadrachalam taluk**.
**Darabandala Chandrayya** burnt the **Addatheegala** police station.
**Indian Forest Act 1878** made forests **state property**.

219.s:
Consider the following statements about Birsa Munda:
1. He was born in 1875.
2. He was captured in February 1900 and died in Ranchi jail in June 1900.
3. His birth anniversary, 30 June, is observed as Janjatiya Gaurav Divas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
219.x: Statement 1 is correct: Birsa was born in 1875. Statement 2 is correct: captured February 1900, died in Ranchi jail June 1900. Statement 3 is wrong: Janjatiya Gaurav Divas is 15 November, his birth anniversary; 30 June is Hul Divas of the Santhals. So '1 and 2 only'.
219.tq: 15 Nov = Birsa / Janjatiya Gaurav Divas; 30 June = Hul Divas.
xs: **Statements 1 and 2** are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **Birsa Munda** was born in **1875**.
Statement 2: captured **Feb 1900**, he **died in Ranchi jail** in **June 1900**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Janjatiya Gaurav Divas** is **15 Nov**; **30 June** is **Hul Divas** (Santhals).
xa: Birsa is called **Dharti Aba** (Father of the Earth) and **"Bhagwan"**.
He led the **Ulgulan (1899-1900)** with about **6,000 Mundas**.
**Bhagwan Birsa Munda Memorial Udyan** cum Freedom Fighters Museum opened in **Ranchi (2021)**.

219.s: Birsa Munda’s religious movement, which blended Munda tradition with Hinduism and Christianity, was known as:
219.x: Birsa Munda founded the monotheist Birsait faith, which blended elements of Munda tradition, Hinduism and Christianity.
219.tq: Use the exact name of the reform movement to distinguish it from later Bhil and Oraon movements.
xs: Birsa founded the **Birsait** faith — option **(1)** is correct.
It was **monotheist**, blending **Munda tradition + Hinduism + Christianity**.
**Eki** was **Motilal Tejawat's** movement in Mewar; **Tana Bhagat** was **Jatra Bhagat's**; **Khuntkatti** is a landholding system.
xa: Birsa preached against **liquor**, **witchcraft**, **animal sacrifice** and **spirit worship**.
Debates over the **Birsait** faith and Adivasi religious identity are in the news.
His followers called him **"Bhagwan"**.

219.s: Which one of the following was NOT part of Birsa Munda’s social and religious reform programme?
o: Opposition to animal sacrifice and spirit worship
Promotion of the Khuntkatti joint landholding system
219.x: Birsa’s programme opposed liquor, witchcraft, animal sacrifice and spirit worship and promoted a monotheist faith. Khuntkatti was a landholding system whose destruction helped cause the revolt; it was not a religious reform practice.
219.tq: Find the option that changes a land-rights issue into a reform practice.
xs: Promoting **Khuntkatti** was not a reform item — option **(4)** is the answer.
**Khuntkatti** is the Munda **joint landholding**; its destruction caused the **Ulgulan**.
Birsa opposed **liquor, witchcraft, animal sacrifice** and **spirit worship**, and founded the monotheist **Birsait** faith.
xa: Khuntkatti was destroyed by **zamindars, thikadars and missionaries**.
The **CNT Act 1908** recognised **Khuntkatti** rights.
Aim of the Ulgulan: **Abua Raj** (self-rule).

219.s: The immediate agrarian grievance behind Birsa Munda’s revolt was the destruction of the:
219.x: The revolt was caused in part by the destruction of the Khuntkatti joint landholding system by zamindars, thikadars and missionaries.
219.tq: Identify the precise institution affected instead of choosing a general tribal-administration term.
xs: Birsa's revolt arose from destruction of the **Khuntkatti joint landholding system** — option **(3)** is correct.
It was destroyed by **zamindars, thikadars and missionaries**.
**Munda-Manki** was **Wilkinson's** system in Kolhan; **Damin-i-Koh** the Santhal tract.
xa: The **Ulgulan** ran **1899-1900** with about **6,000 Mundas**.
The **Chotanagpur Tenancy Act 1908** recognised Khuntkatti rights.
Birsa was captured **Feb 1900**; died in **Ranchi jail** in **June 1900**.

219.s:
Consider the following statements about the Ulgulan:
1. It took place during 1899–1900.
2. Its objective included Abua Raj, or self-rule.
3. About 6,000 Mundas participated in it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
219.x: The Ulgulan occurred in 1899–1900, aimed at Abua Raj and involved about 6,000 Mundas.
219.tq: Combine date, objective and participation figures in a single movement profile.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
The **Ulgulan** ran **1899-1900**, aimed at **Abua Raj** (self-rule), with about **6,000 Mundas**.
xa: Region: **Chotanagpur (Jharkhand)** (APPSC 2024).
Cause: destruction of **Khuntkatti**.
Outcome: **Chotanagpur Tenancy Act 1908**.

219.s: The Chotanagpur Tenancy Act, 1908, associated with the consequences of the Ulgulan, is significant because it:
o: introduced the Eki movement in Mewar
created the Santhal Parganas as a separate district
handed Upper Assam to Purandar Singh
barred transfer of tribal land to non-tribals and recognised Khuntkatti rights
219.x: The Chotanagpur Tenancy Act, 1908, barred transfer of tribal land to non-tribals and recognised Khuntkatti rights.
219.tq: Infer the legal purpose from the land-rights grievance behind the movement.
xs: The **CNT Act 1908** **barred transfer of tribal land to non-tribals** and recognised **Khuntkatti** rights — option **(4)**.
Creating **Santhal Parganas** as a separate district followed the **Hul**, not the Ulgulan.
**Eki** was a Mewar movement; **Upper Assam** went to **Purandar Singh** after the Ahom rebellion.
xa: ⚠ Trap: **CNT Act** = **1908** (Birsa); **SPT Act** = **1876 / 1949** (Santhals).
A Jharkhand project was challenged for violating the **CNT Act 1908** and **PESA**.
**Janjatiya Gaurav Divas** (**15 Nov**) marks Birsa's birth anniversary.

219.s: Birsa Munda, revered as 'Dharti Aba', led the Ulgulan in the region that is today part of:
219.x: Birsa Munda (Dharti Aba, 'Father of the Earth') led the Ulgulan of 1899-1900 in Chotanagpur, present-day Jharkhand (APPSC 2024). Odisha was the scene of the Paika Bidroha, Maharashtra of the Ramosi and Bhil risings, and Andhra of the Rampa rebellions.
219.tq: Dharti Aba = Birsa = Chotanagpur, Jharkhand.
xs: **Birsa Munda** led the **Ulgulan** in what is today **Jharkhand** (APPSC 2024) — option **(2)**.
**Odisha** saw the **Paika Bidroha**; **Maharashtra** the **Ramosi** and **Bhil** risings; **Andhra** the **Rampa** rebellions.
xa: **Dharti Aba** = Father of the Earth.
Ulgulan: **1899-1900**, about **6,000 Mundas**, aim **Abua Raj**.
⚠ Trap: Birsa did not lead the **Kol** rising (**1831-32**) — that was **Budhu Bhagat**.

219.s: Govind Giri, also known as Guru, led the Bhils primarily against:
219.x: Govind Giri led the Bhils against bonded labour. His movement was associated with Rajasthan and Gujarat.
219.tq: Match the reform leader with the specific social grievance of the Bhils.
xs: **Govind Giri (Guru)** led the Bhils against **bonded labour** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Khuntkatti** relates to the **Mundas**; **salt policy** to the **Paikas**; the **Brahmaputra-Sylhet road** to the **Khasi** rising.
xa: His movement ended in the **Mangarh massacre (1913)**, called the **"Adivasi Jallianwala"**.
**Mangarh Dham** became a **National Monument** in **2022**.
**Motilal Tejawat** led the **Eki movement** (**1921-22**) in Mewar.

219.s: The Mangarh massacre of 1913 is popularly known as the:
219.x: The Mangarh massacre of 1913 is called the “Adivasi Jallianwala.” Mangarh Dham was later recognised as a National Monument.
219.tq: Use the popular epithet to identify the correct tribal event.
xs: The **Mangarh massacre (1913)** is called the **"Adivasi Jallianwala"** — option **(1)** is correct.
It involved **Govind Giri's** Bhils, who rose against **bonded labour**.
xa: **Mangarh Dham** = **National Monument** in **2022**.
**Eki movement** (**1921-22**, Mewar) was led by **Motilal Tejawat**.
⚠ Trap: **Hul Divas** (**30 June**) is for the Santhals, not Mangarh.

219.s: Mangarh Dham was declared a National Monument in:
219.x: Mangarh Dham, associated with the 1913 massacre, became a National Monument in 2022.
219.tq: Separate the date of the massacre from the much later date of official recognition.
xs: **Mangarh Dham** was declared a **National Monument** in **2022** — option **(4)** is correct.
**1913** is the year of the **Mangarh massacre**, not the declaration.
**1921** relates to the **Eki movement (1921-22)**; **1949** to the current **SPT Act**.
xa: The massacre is called the **"Adivasi Jallianwala"**.
**Govind Giri** led Bhils against **bonded labour**.
Tribal Freedom Fighter Museums are planned in **10 states**.

219.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Revolt)
a. Santhal Hul
b. Munda Ulgulan
c. Kol/Larka rising
d. Khond rising

List-II (Leader)
i. Chakra Bisoi
ii. Birsa Munda
iii. Budhu Bhagat
iv. Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
219.x: Santhal Hul was led by Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu, Munda Ulgulan by Birsa Munda, the Kol rising by Budhu Bhagat and the Khond rising by Chakra Bisoi.
219.tq: Start from the sure leader–revolt pairs and eliminate the codes.
xs: The correct match is **a-iv, b-ii, c-iii, d-i** — option **(1)**.
**Santhal Hul (1855-56)** — **Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu**; **Munda Ulgulan (1899-1900)** — **Birsa Munda**.
**Kol / Larka (1831-32)** — **Budhu Bhagat**; **Khond (1837-56)** — **Chakra Bisoi**.
xa: ⚠ Trap: notes (p.125) wrongly say Birsa led the **Kol** rebellion.
**Bhumij (1832-33)** — **Ganga Narayan**, Manbhum.
**Tana Bhagat (1914)** — **Jatra Bhagat (Oraon)**.

219.s: The Tamar tribal rising is associated with which one of the following combinations?
o: Oraon tribes and Tamar in Jharkhand
Bhil tribes and Khandesh in Maharashtra
219.x: The Tamar rising was associated with the Oraon tribes and the Tamar region of present-day Jharkhand. Its recorded period was 1789–1832.
219.tq: Test the tribe–region association rather than relying only on the revolt name.
xs: The **Tamar** rising involved **Oraon tribes** at **Tamar (Jharkhand)** — option **(1)** is correct.
Its period was **1789-1832**; APPSC 2024 marked both statements true.
**Paikas** = Khurda (Odisha); **Khonds** = Odisha hills; **Bhils** = Khandesh.
xa: The **Tana Bhagat** movement (**1914**) was also Oraon, led by **Jatra Bhagat**.
**Kol / Larka (1831-32)** under **Budhu Bhagat** was in Chotanagpur, Singhbhum.
Tamar is the earliest revolt in the chronology list.

219.s:
Arrange the following tribal movements in chronological order of their beginning:
A. Santhal Hul
B. Ahom rebellion
C. Kol rising
D. Munda Ulgulan
219.x: The Ahom rebellion began in 1828, followed by the Kol rising in 1831–32, the Santhal Hul in 1855–56 and the Munda Ulgulan in 1899–1900.
219.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the middle movements by year.
xs: Order: **B, C, A, D** — option **(1)**.
xa: Ahom rebellion: led by **Gomadhar Konwar**; Upper Assam went to **Purandar Singh**.
Kol rising: **Budhu Bhagat**.
**Khasi (1829-33)** under **Tirot Sing** falls between Ahom and Kol.

219.s: The Khasi rising of 1829–33 was led by:
219.x: The Khasi rising of 1829–33 was associated with Tirot Sing. Gomadhar Konwar led the Ahom rebellion.
219.tq: Distinguish the leaders of the Khasi and Ahom risings through direct pairing.
xs: The **Khasi rising (1829-33)** was led by **Tirot Sing** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Gomadhar Konwar** led the **Ahom** rebellion; **Ganga Narayan** the **Bhumij** rising; **Birsa** the **Ulgulan**.
xa: Some notes: it began in **1783** against the **Brahmaputra-Sylhet road**, suppressed by **1833**.
Ahom rebellion (**1828**) led to Upper Assam going to **Purandar Singh**.

219.s: The Ahom rebellion resulted in the Company handing over Upper Assam to:
219.x: The Ahom rebellion forced the East India Company to hand Upper Assam to Purandar Singh.
219.tq: Match the political outcome with the correct regional rebellion.
xs: The **Ahom rebellion** forced the Company to hand **Upper Assam** to **Purandar Singh** — option **(3)**.
The Ahom rebellion (**1828**) was led by **Gomadhar Konwar**.
**Tirot Sing** led the **Khasi** rising; **Chakra Bisoi** the **Khond**; **Bakshi Jagabandhu** the **Paika**.
xa: Khasi rising: **1829-33**.
Khond rising: **1837-56**, Odisha hills.

219.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
219.x: The Tana Bhagat movement (1914, Chotanagpur) was led by Jatra Bhagat, an Oraon. The Kol rising was led by Budhu Bhagat; Birsa (born 1875) led the 1899-1900 Ulgulan, so linking him to the Kol rising is a known error. Gomadhar Konwar led the Ahom rebellion; the Khasi rising was under Tirot Sing. The Bhumij rising was led by Ganga Narayan.
219.tq: Tana Bhagat = Jatra Bhagat 1914; Kol = Budhu Bhagat, not Birsa.
xs: **Tana Bhagat movement (1914) — Jatra Bhagat** is correct — option **(2)**; he was an **Oraon** in **Chotanagpur**.
The **Kol** rising was led by **Budhu Bhagat**; linking **Birsa** (born **1875**) to it is a known error.
**Gomadhar Konwar** led the **Ahom** rebellion; the **Khasi** rising was under **Tirot Sing**.
The **Bhumij** rising was led by **Ganga Narayan**, not Budhu Bhagat.
xa: **Tana Bhagats** are in the news over Adivasi religious identity.
The **Tamar** rising (**1789-1832**) was also by **Oraon** tribes.
Birsa led the **1899-1900 Ulgulan**.

219.s: Hul Divas is observed on which date?
219.x: Hul Divas is observed on 30 June.
219.tq: Test the exact date of an observance through direct recall.
xs: **Hul Divas** is observed on **30 June** — option **(1)** is correct.
It marks the start of the **Santhal Hul** at **Bhognadih** on **30 June 1855**.
xa: ⚠ Trap: **Janjatiya Gaurav Divas** = **15 Nov** (Birsa's birth anniversary).
Hul leaders: **Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu**, **Chand and Bhairav**, **Phulo-Jhano**.
The Hul was crushed in **1856**, with over **15,000** killed.

219.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Movement or rising)
A. Gulugonda revolt
B. Rampa and Rekapalle
C. Rampa Rebellion
D. Komaram Bheem’s Gond movement

List-II (Period)
1. 1845–48
2. 1879
3. 1922–24
4. 1938–44

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
219.x: The Gulugonda revolt occurred in 1845–48; Rampa and Rekapalle are associated with 1879; Alluri’s Rampa Rebellion occurred in 1922–24; Komaram Bheem’s Gond movement occurred in 1938–44.
219.tq: Start from the earliest date and verify the remaining chronological pairs.
xs: The correct match is **A-1, B-2, C-3, D-4** — option **(1)**.
**Gulugonda** revolt (Vizag) — **1845-48**; **Rampa and Rekapalle** — **1879**.
**Alluri's Rampa Rebellion** — **1922-24**; **Komaram Bheem's Gond** movement — **1938-44**.
xa: Gulugonda was led by **Chinna Bhupathi**.

222.s:
Consider the following statements about communist conferences in Andhra:

222.tq: 2nd and 3rd conferences both Vijayawada (1938, 1943); 1956 Hyderabad merger.
xs: **Statements 1 and 2** are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: the **3rd** conference (**July 1943**, **Vijayawada**) was the **first open conference**; secretary **Chandra Rajeswara Rao**.
Statement 2: the **Visalandhra Maha Sabha** (**July 1956**, **Hyderabad**) merged the Andhra and Telangana units.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **2nd** conference was at **Vijayawada** in **June 1938** (**P.C. Joshi** attended).
xa: **Kakinada** is where the **Andhra Communist Party** was set up in **January 1936**.
The 1st Maha Sabha was held on **29 Jan 1936**.

222.s: The ban on the Communist Party of India was lifted on

222.s: Which of the following correctly describes Navasakti?
o: It was the first officially recognised CPI publication in India.

CDX list also names **Garimella Krishnamurthy** as a Prajasakti editor.
Chandra Rajeswara Rao stayed with the **CPI** in **1964**.

xs: **P. Sundarayya** wrote **Visalandhralo Prajarajyam** (**1946**) — option **(2)** is correct.

222.s: Which of the following statements regarding the communist position on Visalandhra is correct?
o: The communists were the first to demand Visalandhra in 1946 and initiated the movement.

No vote, but nomination to provincial legislatures
A double vote in a separate electorate and the general electorate
223.x: The Depressed Classes were given a double vote: one in a separate electorate and another in the general electorate.
223.tq: Test the exact mechanism rather than merely the existence of separate electorates.
xs: The Depressed Classes got a **double vote** — one in a **separate electorate** and one in the **general electorate** — option **(4)**.
They were declared a **minority** under the Award.
xa: **Gandhi** opposed this with a **fast unto death** from **20 September 1932** at **Yerwada Jail, Poona**.
He argued separate electorates for Dalits would **permanently divide Hindu society**.
The Pact replaced this with **reserved seats in a joint electorate**.

223.s:
With reference to the Communal Award, consider the following statements:
1. Three per cent of the seats in all provinces, except the North-West Frontier Province, were earmarked for women.
2. The Award dealt only with religious communities and made no provision for occupational interests.
3. Seats were also provided for labour, landlords, traders and industrialists.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
223.x: Three per cent of seats were reserved for women in all provinces except the North-West Frontier Province. The Award also included occupational interests such as labour, landlords, traders and industrialists, making statement 2 false.
223.tq: Pair a numerical exception with the correct list of beneficiaries.
xs: **Statements 1 and 3** are correct — option **(3) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1: women got **3%** of seats in all provinces **except NWFP**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the Award also gave **special-interest** seats.
Statement 3: seats went to **labour, landlords, traders and industrialists**.
xa: The Award covered **11 groups**.
Separate electorates: **Muslims, Sikhs, Europeans, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians** + **Depressed Classes**.
Announced **16 Aug 1932** by **Ramsay MacDonald**.

223.s:
Consider the following statements about the response to the Communal Award (1932):
1. Gandhi began a fast unto death on 20 September 1932 in Yerwada Jail, Poona.
2. Gandhi argued that separate electorates for Dalits would permanently divide Hindu society.
3. The Congress formally rejected the Communal Award.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
223.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Congress neither accepted nor rejected the Award. Hence '1 and 2 only'; all other options include statement 3.
223.tq: Congress on the Award: neither accepted nor rejected.
xs: **Statements 1 and 2** are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **Gandhi** began a **fast unto death** on **20 September 1932** in **Yerwada Jail, Poona**.
Statement 2: he argued separate electorates for Dalits would **permanently divide Hindu society**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **Congress neither accepted nor rejected** the Award.
xa: The Award was announced on **16 Aug 1932** by **Ramsay MacDonald**.
It gave the Depressed Classes a **double vote**.
The Pact's **reserved seats in a joint electorate** became the model for SC reservation.

223.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the constitutional history of the term 'Scheduled Castes' is correct?
o: It was first used by the Simon Commission, fixed by the Government of India Act, 1935, and the first list came in 1936.
It was first used in the Communal Award and abolished by the Government of India Act, 1935.
It was first used by Gandhi in 1932 and legally defined in 1942.
It was first used in the Poona Pact and listed in 1950.
223.x: The term was first used by the Simon Commission, fixed by the Government of India Act, 1935, and the first list was issued in 1936.
223.tq: Arrange the institutional stages of a constitutional term in sequence.
xs: "Scheduled Castes" was **first used by the Simon Commission**, fixed by the **GoI Act 1935**, first list **1936** — option **(1)**.
The **Communal Award** used the term **Depressed Classes**, declaring them a **minority**.
xa: **Art. 17** later **abolished untouchability**.
The Pact's **joint electorate with reserved seats** = model for constitutional SC reservation.
The Social Justice Ministry began a **2-year** celebration of **Jyotiba Phule's 200th birth anniversary** (Apr **2026**).

223.s: The reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes under the constitutional system is conceptually linked to which feature of the Poona Pact?
o: Nomination by the British Prime Minister
223.x: The Poona Pact's model of joint electorates with reserved seats became the basis for the constitutional approach to SC political reservation.
223.tq: Identify the institutional feature that carried forward into the Constitution.
xs: SC reservation follows the Pact's **reserved seats in a joint electorate** — option **(4)** is correct.
The Communal Award had instead given **separate electorates** with a **double vote**.
xa: **Gandhi's fast** (from **20 Sept 1932**, **Yerwada**) forced the change.
The Award was announced on **16 Aug 1932**.
**Art. 17** abolished **untouchability**.

224.s: The immediate political pressure that prompted the Montagu Declaration of 20 August 1917 was exerted chiefly by the:
224.x: The Home Rule Leagues created political pressure that contributed to the British declaration recognising self-government as an objective.
224.tq: Identify the immediate political force rather than the later constitutional outcome.
xs: The **Montagu Declaration** (**20 August 1917**) was prompted by the **Home Rule Leagues** — option **(2)** is correct.
It was the **first official recognition** of self-government as an aim.
The **Liberal Federation** (**1918**), **Justice Party** and **Swaraj Party** came later.
xa: Aim: **"progressive realisation of responsible government"** in India as an integral part of the British Empire.
**Montagu** + **Chelmsford** toured India in **Dec 1917**.
The **Montagu-Chelmsford Report** was announced in **July 1918**.

224.s: A 27-member Andhra delegation led by Nyapati Subbarao met Montagu at Madras to demand:
o: A separate Muslim province in South India
Abolition of the Madras Legislative Council
224.x: The Andhra delegation led by Nyapati Subbarao sought the creation of a separate Andhra province.
224.tq: Connect the delegation leader and its regional constitutional demand.
xs: **Nyapati Subbarao's** **27-member** delegation met Montagu at **Madras** for a **separate Andhra province** — option **(3)**.
p.442 of the notes gives it as **21 members**.
xa: **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** presided the **Special Andhra Mahasabha** at **Guntur** (**17 Aug 1918**).
**Krishna Patrika**: reforms = "giving with the right hand, taking with the left".
Andhra delegations seeking a separate province are a key **AP angle** of the 1919 reforms.

224.s: The Montagu Declaration of 20 August 1917 announced British policy as the:
o: immediate grant of dominion status to India
progressive realisation of responsible government in India as an integral part of the British Empire
complete independence of India within ten years
provincial autonomy with an All-India Federation
224.x: On 20 August 1917 Montagu announced the gradual development of self-governing institutions with a view to the progressive realisation of responsible government in India as an integral part of the Empire - the first official recognition of self-government as an aim. Dominion status as a goal came with the 1929 Deepavali Declaration; complete independence was never promised then; provincial autonomy and federation came with the 1935 Act.
224.tq: 1917 = 'progressive realisation of responsible government'.
xs: The Declaration aimed at the **progressive realisation of responsible government** in India as an **integral part of the British Empire** — option **(2)**.
It spoke of **gradual development of self-governing institutions**, not immediate dominion status or independence.
**Provincial autonomy** and an **All-India Federation** came with the **1935 Act**.
xa: Made on **20 August 1917**, in Parliament.
Prompted by the **Home Rule Leagues**.
First official recognition of **self-government** as an aim.

224.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the response of the Moderates to the constitutional reforms of 1919?
o: They accepted the reforms and formed the Indian National Liberal Federation in 1918.
They boycotted the reforms and formed the Justice Party.
They joined the Home Rule Leagues and demanded complete independence.
They rejected the reforms and formed the Swaraj Party.
224.x: Surendranath Banerjee and other Moderates accepted the reforms, left the Congress and formed the Indian National Liberal Federation in 1918.
224.tq: Use the founder-group and organisation pairing to avoid confusing Moderates with Swarajists.
xs: The Moderates **accepted the reforms** and formed the **Indian National Liberal Federation (1918)** — option **(1)**.
They were led by **Surendranath Banerjee** and **left the Congress**.
The **Swaraj Party** (**C.R. Das**, **Motilal Nehru**) came later and entered councils to obstruct.
xa: Some notes call it the **"National Liberation Federation"**.
**C.R. Das** + **Tilak** wanted **rejection** at **Amritsar (1919)**.
**Gandhi** + **Malaviya** wanted a **fair trial**.

224.s: At the Amritsar Congress of 1919, the reforms were described as:
224.x: The Amritsar Congress characterised the reforms as inadequate, unsatisfactory and disappointing.
224.tq: Recall the exact three-part political assessment used by the Congress.
xs: The **Amritsar Congress (1919)** called the reforms **"inadequate, unsatisfactory and disappointing"** — option **(4)**.
It was presided by **Motilal Nehru**.
xa: **C.R. Das** and **Tilak** favoured **rejection**.
**Gandhi** and **Malaviya** favoured a **fair trial**.
**Krishna Patrika**: "giving with the right hand, taking with the left".

224.s:
With reference to dyarchy under the Government of India Act, 1919, consider the following statements:
1. It was introduced in the provinces.
2. It divided provincial subjects into reserved and transferred subjects.
3. It made the provincial budget independent of the central budget.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
224.x: Dyarchy was introduced in the provinces, provincial subjects were divided into reserved and transferred categories, and the provincial budget was separated from the central budget.
224.tq: Check whether each feature belongs to provincial dyarchy rather than to the later provincial autonomy scheme.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Dyarchy** was introduced in the **provinces**, with **reserved** and **transferred** subjects.
**Provincial budgets** were **separated** from the central budget.
xa: Subjects were split into **central** and **provincial** lists.
Criticism: ministers got transferred subjects **without finance** (which stayed reserved).
⚠ UPSC notes wrongly call this **"provincial autonomy"** — that came with the **1935** Act.

224.s: The central legislature under the Government of India Act, 1919 was:
o: Bicameral, consisting of the Chamber of Princes and the Federal Court
Bicameral, consisting of the Council of State and the Legislative Assembly
Unicameral, consisting only of nominated members
Tricameral, consisting of the Council of State, Legislative Assembly and Provincial Council
224.x: The Act introduced a bicameral central legislature comprising the Council of State as the upper chamber and the Legislative Assembly as the lower chamber.
224.tq: Match the constitutional arrangement with the exact names of its two chambers.
xs: The centre was **bicameral**: **Council of State** (upper) + **Legislative Assembly** (lower) — option **(2)**.
The **Chamber of Princes** was a **consultative** body of rulers; the **Federal Court** came under the **1935 Act**.
xa: Assembly = **145** members (**104** elected); Council of State = **60**.
Both houses were **mostly elected**.
First President of the Assembly: **Frederick Whyte** (**1921**).

224.s: Which one of the following was NOT a feature of the Government of India Act, 1919?
o: Direct elections to the central legislature
Creation of the office of High Commissioner for India in London
Separation of provincial budgets from the central budget
Provincial autonomy in place of dyarchy
224.x: Provincial autonomy was associated with the Government of India Act, 1935. The 1919 Act introduced dyarchy in the provinces, along with the other listed features.
224.tq: Use the later 1935 feature as the chronological trap in a NOT question.
xs: **Provincial autonomy in place of dyarchy** was not a 1919 feature — option **(4)**; it came with the **1935 Act** (from **April 1937**).
The 1919 Act gave **direct elections**, the **High Commissioner** in **London** and **separate provincial budgets**.
xa: The **Simon Report (1930)** first recommended abolishing provincial dyarchy for **provincial autonomy**.
⚠ **Dyarchy**: **1919** = in the provinces; **1935** = provincial dyarchy abolished, Centre dyarchy never operated.
The 1935 Act also abolished the **India Council**.

224.s: The Government of India Act, 1919 introduced direct elections on the basis of:
o: Separate nomination by the Secretary of State
224.x: The Act introduced direct elections, but the franchise remained limited by property, tax and educational qualifications.
224.tq: Combine the electoral method with the qualification-based nature of the franchise.
xs: Franchise was limited by **property, tax and educational** qualifications — option **(2)** is correct.
There was no **universal adult franchise**.
xa: The **GoI Act 1919** was the **first Act** to introduce **direct elections**.
**Communal representation** was **extended** (Sikhs etc.).
First elections: **1920**, boycotted by the Congress.

224.s: If an examination question asks for the first Act associated with direct elections in India, which answer is most appropriate?
224.x: The Government of India Act, 1919 introduced direct elections. The 1909 Act introduced elected non-official members mainly through indirect and separate electorates.
224.tq: Resolve a close-option ambiguity by distinguishing direct elections from indirect elections.
xs: The **Government of India Act 1919** was the first to introduce **direct elections** — option **(1)** is correct.
The **1909** Act brought **elected** members mostly via **indirect** and **separate electorates**.
xa: ⚠ APPSC GS 2018 key gave **Indian Councils Act 1909** — mark it only if 1919 is absent.
Franchise in 1919 rested on **property, tax and education**.
Assembly: **145** members, **104** elected.

224.s: The statutory review provision of the Government of India Act, 1919 required the appointment of a commission after:
224.x: The Act required a statutory commission to review its working after ten years. The Simon Commission was appointed two years early under this provision.
224.tq: Recall the statutory interval and distinguish it from the actual early appointment.
xs: The Act required a **statutory commission after 10 years** — option **(4) Ten years** is correct.
The **Simon Commission** was appointed **two years early** (**8 November 1927**).
xa: Simon Commission = **Indian Statutory Commission** / "White Commission".
Appointed by the **Conservative (Baldwin)** government.
The Swarajist demand for review led to the **Muddiman Committee (1924)**.

224.s:
With reference to provincial dyarchy under the Government of India Act, 1919, consider the following statements:
1. Transferred subjects were administered by the Governor with the assistance of ministers.
2. Reserved subjects were administered by the Governor with the assistance of the Executive Council.
3. Local self-government was treated as a reserved subject.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
224.x: Transferred subjects, including local self-government, were administered by the Governor with ministers. Reserved subjects were handled by the Governor and the Executive Council; therefore statement 3 is false.
224.tq: Split the options by identifying the wrongly classified subject under dyarchy.
xs: **Statements 1 and 2** are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **transferred** subjects — Governor with **ministers**.
Statement 2: **reserved** subjects — Governor with the **Executive Council**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **local self-government** was a **transferred** subject.
xa: Ministers came from the **elected legislature** and answered to it.
Reserved subjects included **law and order**, **finance**, **land revenue**.
In **1935** local self-government became a **provincial subject**.

224.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Viceroy's Executive Council under the Government of India Act, 1919:
1. The Council had six members apart from the Commander-in-Chief.
2. Three of these six members were Indians.
3. All the members of the Council were elected directly by the people.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
224.x: Apart from the Commander-in-Chief, the Viceroy's Executive Council had six members, of whom three were Indians. The members were not all directly elected, making statement 3 false.
224.tq: Reject the extreme institutional claim that all members were directly elected.
xs: **Statements 1 and 2** are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
The **Executive Council** had **6** members (other than the **C-in-C**), **3** of them Indians.
Statement 3 is wrong: members were not directly elected; only the legislature was **mostly elected**.
xa: Centre: **Council of State** + **Legislative Assembly**.
**Communal representation** was extended (Sikhs etc.).
A **statutory commission** was due after **10 years**.

224.s:
With reference to dyarchy under the Government of India Act, 1919, consider the following statements:
1. Dyarchy meant a single, unified government in the provinces.
2. The scheme is named after Edwin Montagu and Lord Chelmsford.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
224.x: Statement 1 is wrong: dyarchy means dual government - reserved subjects under the Governor and Executive Council, transferred subjects under the Governor with ministers (APPSC 2019 marked 'single government' false). Statement 2 is correct. Hence 2 only.
224.tq: Dyarchy = DUAL government in provinces (1919).
xs: Only **statement 2** is correct — option **(2) 2 only**.

Statement 1 is wrong: dyarchy means **dual** government — **reserved** subjects (Governor + Executive Council) and **transferred** subjects (Governor + ministers); APPSC 2019 marked "single government" false.
Statement 2: the scheme is named after **Edwin Montagu** and **Lord Chelmsford**.
xa: Dyarchy was in the **provinces**, not the Centre.
The **1935** Act abolished provincial dyarchy; **Centre dyarchy** never operated.
⚠ UPSC notes wrongly call 1919 **"provincial autonomy"**.

224.s:
Consider the following statements about the Public Service Commission under the Government of India Act, 1919:
1. It was provided for in Section 96(C) of the Act.
2. It was set up in 1921, as soon as the Act came into force.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
224.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Public Service Commission was set up on 1 October 1926, after the Lee Commission. Hence 1 only.
224.tq: Sec. 96(C) -> PSC set up 1 Oct 1926 (after Lee Commission).
xs: Only **statement 1** is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1: the PSC was provided in **Section 96(C)** (APPSC GS 2022).
Statement 2 is wrong: it was set up on **1 October 1926**, after the **Lee Commission**.
xa: The **1935** Act provided a **Federal PSC and Provincial PSCs**.
ICS exams were held simultaneously in India from **1922**.
The office of **High Commissioner for India** was created in **London**.

224.s:
Consider the following statements about the Chamber of Princes (Narendra Mandal):
1. It was a consultative body of Indian rulers.
2. It was set up in 1935 under the Government of India Act, 1935.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
224.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Chamber of Princes was set up in 1921 by royal proclamation under the 1919 reforms. Hence 1 only.
224.tq: Narendra Mandal = 1921, under the 1919 reforms.
xs: Only **statement 1** is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1: the **Chamber of Princes (Narendra Mandal)** was a **consultative body of rulers**.
Statement 2 is wrong: it was created in **1921** by **royal proclamation** under the **1919** reforms.
xa: The 1935 Act's **All-India Federation** of provinces + princely states **never came into being**.
First Assembly President **Frederick Whyte** also dates to **1921**.
The **Federal Court** at Delhi came in **1937**.

224.s: Frederick Whyte and Sachchidananda Sinha were respectively associated with which offices?
o: First elected Indian President and first Chief Minister of Madras
First President and first Deputy President of the Legislative Assembly
High Commissioner for India and first President of the Legislative Assembly
First Deputy President and first President of the Council of State
224.x: Frederick Whyte was the first President and Sachchidananda Sinha was the first Deputy President of the Legislative Assembly.
224.tq: Separate similar office-holder facts by matching each person to the exact office and status.
xs: **Frederick Whyte** was the **first President** and **Sachchidananda Sinha** the **first Deputy President** of the Legislative Assembly — option **(2)**.
Whyte took office in **1921**.
xa: **Vithalbhai Patel** later became Assembly president (Speaker) after **1923**.
The 1919 Act created the posts of **President + Deputy President**.
First Madras CM: **A. Subbarayalu Reddiar** (**Dec 1920**).

224.s: In the Madras elections of 1920, which one of the following combinations is correct?
o: Congress boycotted the elections and the Justice Party won 63 seats
The Justice Party boycotted the elections and Congress won 63 seats
Both Congress and the Justice Party boycotted the elections
224.x: The Congress boycotted the 1920 Madras elections as part of the Non-Cooperation movement, while the Justice Party won 63 seats.
224.tq: Pair the political action with the correct party and election result.
xs: **Congress boycotted** (Non-Cooperation) and the **Justice Party won 63 seats** — option **(2)** is correct.
The first elections under the Act were in **1920**.
xa: **A. Subbarayalu Reddiar** became the first Chief Minister (**Dec 1920**), then the **Raja of Panagal** (**1921**).
The Justice Party held office most of **1920-37**.
The Justice Party **did not join** the Simon boycott.

224.s:
Consider the following statements about the Swarajists and the 1919 Act:
1. The Swarajists won about 40 per cent of the seats in the 1923 elections.
2. The Muddiman Committee (1924) was the British response to the Swarajist demand for a review of the 1919 Act.
3. The Swaraj Party contested the 1920 elections to the Central Legislative Assembly.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
224.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Congress boycotted the 1920 elections; the Swarajists (C.R. Das, Motilal Nehru) contested in 1923. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
224.tq: 1920 = boycott; 1923 = Swarajists entered (~40%); 1924 = Muddiman.
xs: **Statements 1 and 2** are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: Swarajists won about **40%** of seats in **1923**.
Statement 2: the **Muddiman Committee (1924)** answered their demand for review.
Statement 3 is wrong: the Congress **boycotted** the **1920** elections; Swarajists contested in **1923**.
xa: Leaders: **C.R. Das** and **Motilal Nehru**.
**V. Ramadas** (Andhra) was elected to the Central Legislative Assembly in **1923**.
**Vithalbhai Patel** became Assembly president.

224.s: Who became the President, or Speaker, of the Central Legislative Assembly after the Swarajist success in 1923?
224.x: Vithalbhai Patel became the President, commonly described as the Speaker, of the Central Legislative Assembly.
224.tq: Use the office-holder trap by distinguishing the legislative leaders from the presiding officer.
xs: **Vithalbhai Patel** became **president (speaker)** of the Central Legislative Assembly — option **(1)**.
**M.A. Ansari** presided the **Madras Congress (Dec 1927)**; **C.R. Das** and **Motilal Nehru** led the Swaraj Party.
xa: First Assembly President: **Frederick Whyte** (**1921**).
Swarajists won about **40%** of seats in **1923**.
**Muddiman Committee**: **1924**.

224.s: Who became the first Chief Minister (Premier) of Madras in December 1920 after the Justice Party's victory?
224.x: A. Subbarayalu Reddiar became the first Chief Minister in December 1920; the Raja of Panagal succeeded him in 1921. Rajaji headed the first Congress ministry in 1937; P. Subbarayan was not the first premier.
224.tq: Madras 1920: Subbarayalu Reddiar, then Panagal Raja (1921).
xs: **A. Subbarayalu Reddiar** became the **first Chief Minister** (Premier) of Madras in **Dec 1920** — option **(2)**.
The **Raja of Panagal** succeeded him in **1921**.
**C. Rajagopalachari** was Madras premier under the **1935 Act** (**1937**).
xa: The **Justice Party** won **63 seats** in **1920**.
It held office most of **1920-37**.
Congress ministries **resigned in Oct-Nov 1939**.

224.s:
Consider the following statements about the appointment of the Simon Commission:
1. It was appointed by the Conservative government of Stanley Baldwin.
2. It was appointed to review the working of the Government of India Act, 1919.
3. It was appointed two years after the date fixed by the Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
224.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Commission was appointed (8 November 1927) two years early, not late. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
224.tq: Simon: Baldwin's Conservatives, two years EARLY, to review the 1919 Act.
xs: **Statements 1 and 2** are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: appointed by the **Conservative (Baldwin)** government on **8 November 1927**.
Statement 2: it was to review the **1919 Act**.
Statement 3 is wrong: it was appointed **two years early**, not late.
xa: The Act had fixed a review **after 10 years**.
Members: **7**, all British; chairman **Sir John Simon**, incl. **Clement Attlee**.
Arrived at **Bombay** on **3 February 1928**.

224.s:
With reference to the Simon Commission, consider the following statements:
1. It consisted of seven members.
2. All its members were British.
3. Sir John Simon was its chairman.
4. Clement Attlee was one of its members.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
224.x: The commission had seven members, all British, with Sir John Simon as chairman; Clement Attlee was also a member.
224.tq: Verify composition, nationality, chairmanship and membership before selecting the coded option.
xs: All four are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**7 members**, **all British**, chairman **Sir John Simon**, with **Clement Attlee** among the **6** others.
xa: **No Indian member** was the reason for the boycott.
Also called the **Indian Statutory Commission** / "White Commission".
Second visit: **Oct 1928-Apr 1929**.

224.s: The Simon Commission arrived at Bombay on:
224.x: The Simon Commission arrived at Bombay on 3 February 1928.
224.tq: Separate the appointment year from the year of arrival in India.
xs: The Commission arrived at **Bombay** on **3 February 1928** (APPSC GS 2021) — option **(1)** is correct.
An **all-India hartal** and **black flags** greeted it.
**30 Oct 1928** was the **Lahore** lathi charge on **Lala Lajpat Rai**.
xa: Second visit: **Oct 1928-Apr 1929**.
Slogan **"Simon Go Back"** coined by **Yusuf Meherally** (APPSC GS 2018).
Andhra route: **Tenali - Guntur - Vijayawada - Ongole - Madras**.

224.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.
List-I (Place)
a. Lahore
b. Madras
c. Lucknow
d. Tenali and Guntur
List-II (Protest leader)
i. Tanguturi Prakasam
ii. G.V. Unnayya Sastri
iii. Lala Lajpat Rai
iv. Jawaharlal Nehru and G.B. Pant
224.x: Lahore was associated with Lala Lajpat Rai, Madras with Tanguturi Prakasam, Lucknow with Jawaharlal Nehru and G.B. Pant, and Tenali–Guntur with G.V. Unnayya Sastri.
224.tq: Start from the sure place–leader pair and eliminate codes containing incompatible matches.
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii** — option **(1)**.
**Lahore** — **Lala Lajpat Rai**; **Madras** — **Tanguturi Prakasam**.
**Lucknow** — **Jawaharlal Nehru**, **G.B. Pant**; **Tenali/Guntur** — **G.V. Unnayya Sastri**.
xa: Lajpat Rai was lathi-charged on **30 Oct 1928** and died of injuries (**Nov 1928**).
**Saunders** was shot by **Bhagat Singh** and **Rajguru** (**Dec 1928**) in revenge.
Guntur saw a **complete bandh**.

224.s: Tanguturi Prakasam acquired the title 'Andhra Kesari' in connection with which incident?
o: Baring his chest before the police during the anti-Simon Commission protest at Madras
Leading the Home Rule League in Andhra
Leading the boycott of the Rowlatt Act in Guntur
224.x: Tanguturi Prakasam bared his chest before the police during the anti-Simon Commission protest at Madras and became known as Andhra Kesari.
224.tq: Link the title to the distinctive action and place associated with it.
xs: **Prakasam** **bared his chest** to the police at the **Madras** anti-Simon protest and was called **"Andhra Kesari"** — option **(1)**.
The **Amritsar Congress (1919)** was presided by **Motilal Nehru**, not Prakasam.
xa: Andhra anti-Simon committee president: **S. Satyamurti**.
**Bulusu Sambamurthy** toured Andhra for the boycott.
Tenali/Guntur protest: **G.V. Unnayya Sastri**.

224.s:
Consider the following statements about the recommendations of the Simon Commission Report (1930):
1. It recommended abolishing provincial dyarchy in favour of provincial autonomy.
2. It recommended separating Sindh from Bombay and Burma from India.
3. It recommended abolishing separate electorates.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
224.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the report recommended keeping separate electorates. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
224.tq: Simon Report kept separate electorates.
xs: **Statements 1 and 2** are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: abolish provincial dyarchy → **provincial autonomy**.
Statement 2: separate **Sindh** from Bombay and **Burma** from India.
Statement 3 is wrong: the Report recommended **keeping separate electorates**.
xa: The Report (**1930**) first used the term **"Scheduled Castes"**.
The **1935 Act** drew on the **Simon Report**, three **RTCs** and the **White Paper**.
Provincial autonomy began in **April 1937**.

224.s: The term 'Scheduled Castes' was first used in the:
224.x: The term 'Scheduled Castes' was first used in the Simon Commission Report.
224.tq: Match the exact constitutional term with the report in which it first appeared.
xs: **"Scheduled Castes"** was first used in the **Simon Commission Report** — option **(1)** is correct.
The Report came in **1930**.
xa: It recommended **provincial autonomy** and **keeping separate electorates**.
It also proposed separating **Sindh** from Bombay and **Burma** from India.
The **Nehru Report (1928)** was drafted by an **All Parties Conference** committee.

224.s:
Which of the following groups did NOT join the boycott of the Simon Commission?
1. Jinnah's faction of the Muslim League
2. Shafi's faction of the Muslim League
3. Hindu Mahasabha
4. Justice Party
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
224.x: Shafi's League faction and the Justice Party did not join the boycott. Jinnah's faction and the Hindu Mahasabha participated in it.
224.tq: Use organisational faction differences to identify the exceptions.
xs: **Shafi's League faction** and the **Justice Party** did not join — option **(2) 2 and 4 only**.
**Jinnah's League faction** and the **Hindu Mahasabha** joined the boycott.
xa: The **Punjab Unionists** also did not join.
The **Madras Congress (Dec 1927)** under **M.A. Ansari** called for boycott.
The Justice Party held office in Madras most of **1920-37**.

224.s: The slogan 'Simon Go Back' was coined by:
224.x: Yusuf Meherally coined 'Simon Go Back' (APPSC GS 2018). Lajpat Rai led the Lahore protest, Prakasam the Madras protest, and S. Satyamurti headed the Andhra anti-Simon committee.
224.tq: Simon Go Back = Yusuf Meherally.
xs: The slogan **"Simon Go Back"** was coined by **Yusuf Meherally** (APPSC GS **2018**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Lala Lajpat Rai** led the **Lahore** protest and died after the lathi charge of **30 Oct 1928**.
**Tanguturi Prakasam** led the **Madras** protest, baring his chest to police.
**S. Satyamurti** was president of the **Andhra anti-Simon committee**.
xa: Prakasam earned the title **"Andhra Kesari"** for his defiance at Madras.
**Bulusu Sambamurthy** toured Andhra for the boycott.
The **Madras session (Dec 1927)** of the INC under **M.A. Ansari** resolved to boycott the Commission "at every stage and in every form".
The Commission is also called the **Indian Statutory Commission** or "White Commission".

224.s: The Nehru Report was primarily prepared in response to which of the following?
o: Lord Birkenhead's challenge to Indians to frame a constitution
The demand for a separate Muslim homeland
The failure of the Cripps Mission
224.x: The Nehru Report was prepared in reply to Secretary of State Lord Birkenhead's challenge to Indians to frame their own constitution.
224.tq: Identify the immediate cause behind a constitutional document.
xs: The **Nehru Report** answered Secretary of State **Lord Birkenhead's challenge** to Indians to frame a constitution — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was drafted by a **9-member** committee of the **All Parties Conference** (**1928**).
The **Cripps Mission** is unrelated here — the report predates it.
xa: **Motilal Nehru** was Chairman and **Jawaharlal Nehru** Secretary of the Nehru Report committee.
It was discussed at the **Calcutta session (Dec 1928)**, which gave the British a **one-year ultimatum**.
The Muslim League's reply to the report was **Jinnah's Fourteen Points (1929)**.

224.s: Jinnah's Fourteen Points of 1929 were formulated as the Muslim League's response to which document?
224.x: Jinnah's Fourteen Points were the Muslim League's answer to the Nehru Report.
224.tq: Discriminate between closely connected constitutional documents.
xs: **Jinnah's Fourteen Points (1929)** were the Muslim League's answer to **the Nehru Report** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Nehru Report (1928)** was drafted by the **All Parties Conference** committee under **Motilal Nehru**.
The **Simon Report** came in **1930**, after the Fourteen Points.
xa: Key demands: **federal constitution**, **residuary powers to provinces**, **one-third** Muslim seats at the Centre and **separate electorates**.
The Nehru Report was discussed at the **Calcutta session (Dec 1928)** with a one-year ultimatum.
The **White Paper** was one basis of the **GoI Act 1935**, along with the Simon Report and three RTCs.

224.s: Which one of the following combinations correctly represents important features of Jinnah's Fourteen Points?
o: Unitary constitution, joint electorates and abolition of provincial autonomy
Federal constitution, residuary powers to provinces and separate electorates
Dominion status, nominated legislatures and universal adult franchise
Presidential government, one-third provincial seats and communal veto at all levels
224.x: Jinnah's Fourteen Points demanded a federal constitution with residuary powers to the provinces and separate electorates.
224.tq: Split the options by testing the distinctive features of a constitutional demand.
xs: The Fourteen Points demanded a **federal constitution**, **residuary powers to provinces** and **separate electorates** — so option **(2)** is correct.
They also sought **one-third** Muslim seats at the **Centre**.
A **unitary** constitution with **joint electorates** is the opposite of these demands.
xa: The Fourteen Points (**1929**) were the Muslim League's answer to the **Nehru Report (1928)**.
The Nehru Report was drafted by a **9-member** committee of the **All Parties Conference** under **Motilal Nehru**.
⚠ Do not confuse "one-third **provincial** seats" — the demand was one-third Muslim seats **at the Centre**.

224.s:
With reference to the federation proposed under the Government of India Act, 1935, consider the following statements:
1. Accession of princely states was optional.
2. The federation actually came into operation.
3. Dyarchy was provided at the Centre.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
224.x: Accession of princely states was optional and dyarchy was provided at the Centre. The federation never came into being, making statement 2 false.
224.tq: Separate a proposed provision from one that was actually implemented.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: accession of **princely states** to the federation was **optional**.
Statement 2 wrong: the federation **never came into being**.
Statement 3 correct: **dyarchy at the Centre** was provided, though it **never operated**.
xa: ⚠ Dyarchy: **1919** = in the **provinces**; **1935** = provincial dyarchy abolished, Centre dyarchy never operated.
Because the federation failed, the **Centre continued under the 1919 structure**.
The Act had **321 sections and 10 schedules** — the longest Act.

224.s: The Government of India Act, 1935 is notable for being the longest British constitutional Act relating to India, containing
224.x: The Act contained 321 sections and 10 schedules; it is also described in some references as having 14 parts and 321 articles.
224.tq: Use the numerical pair rather than relying on the size description alone.
xs: The GoI Act 1935 contained **321 sections and 10 schedules** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Some notes describe it as **"14 parts, 321 Articles"** — the **14** refers to parts, not schedules.
xa: Basis of the Act: **Simon Report** + three **RTCs** + the **White Paper**.
It is called the largest single source of the **Constitution's structure**.
Borrowed: **Instrument of Instructions** → **Directive Principles** (APPSC **2023**); **Federal Court** → **Supreme Court**.

224.s:
Consider the following statements about provincial autonomy under the Government of India Act, 1935:
1. It replaced dyarchy in the provinces.
2. It began in April 1937.
3. The Act retained the India Council.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
224.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: provincial dyarchy was abolished and provincial autonomy began in April 1937. Statement 3 is wrong: the Act abolished the India Council (it also created bicameral legislatures in some provinces). Hence '1 and 2 only'.
224.tq: 1935 Act abolished the India Council.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **provincial autonomy** replaced (abolished) **provincial dyarchy**.
Statement 2 correct: it began in **April 1937**.
Statement 3 wrong: the Act **abolished the India Council**.
xa: The Act also created bicameral legislatures (**Vidhan Parishads**) in some provinces.
**Local self-government** became a **provincial subject** (under 1919 it was a **transferred** subject).
Provincial autonomy was a recommendation of the **Simon Report (1930)**.

224.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Federal Public Service Commission — 1935 Act — Calcutta, 1937
Provincial Public Service Commissions — 1909 Act — Delhi, 1910
224.x: The Federal Court was established at Delhi in 1937 under the Government of India Act, 1935. The Act also provided for a Federal PSC and Provincial PSCs.
224.tq: Start from the sure institution-location-year pair and eliminate swapped authorities.
xs: The **Federal Court** was set up under the **1935 Act** at **Delhi** in **1937** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **1919 Act** created no Federal Court; the **Federal PSC** and **Provincial PSCs** came with the **1935 Act**, not the **1909** Act.
xa: The Federal Court is the forerunner of today's **Supreme Court**.
The **1919 Act** provided a **Public Service Commission** in **Section 96(C)**; it was set up on **1 October 1926** after the **Lee Commission**.
The 1935 Act also abolished the **India Council** and started **provincial autonomy** (**April 1937**).

224.s: The Congress ministries resigned in October-November 1939 mainly because
o: The Muslim League withdrew support from all provincial ministries.
India was involved in the Second World War without the consent of Indian leaders.
The British abolished provincial legislatures without consultation.
The Federal Court rejected provincial autonomy.
224.x: The Congress ministries resigned in protest against India being dragged into the Second World War without Indian consent.
224.tq: Identify the political cause behind a major institutional action.
xs: The Congress ministries **resigned in Oct-Nov 1939** against **India being dragged into WWII** without Indian consent — so option **(2)** is correct.
The ministries had been formed after the **1937** provincial elections, which the **Congress** won.
The **Muslim League** did not withdraw support; instead it celebrated their exit.
xa: The League observed **"Day of Deliverance"** on **22 Dec 1939**; **Ambedkar** joined.
In **Madras**, the ministry was headed by **C. Rajagopalachari** (APHQ **2011**).
**Provincial autonomy** under the **1935 Act** had begun in **April 1937**.

224.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. C. Rajagopalachari headed the Congress ministry formed in Madras after the 1937 elections.
2. The Muslim League observed 22 December 1939 as the 'Day of Deliverance' after the Congress ministries resigned.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
224.x: Both are correct: Rajaji was the Madras premier in 1937 (APHQ 2011), and after the Congress ministries resigned in Oct-Nov 1939 the League observed the Day of Deliverance on 22 December 1939 (Ambedkar joined).
224.tq: Madras 1937 = Rajaji; Deliverance Day = 22 Dec 1939.
xs: **Both** statements are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **C. Rajagopalachari** was the **Madras premier** after the **1937** elections (APHQ **2011**).
Statement 2 correct: after the ministries **resigned in Oct-Nov 1939**, the League observed the **"Day of Deliverance" (22 Dec 1939)**.
xa: **Ambedkar** joined the Day of Deliverance.
The ministries resigned against India being dragged into **WWII**.
Under the **1919** Act, the first Madras Chief Minister was **A. Subbarayalu Reddiar** (**Dec 1920**) of the **Justice Party**.

224.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Feature of the Government of India Act, 1935)
a. Instrument of Instructions
b. Federal Court
c. Emergency powers
d. Federal scheme and Public Service Commissions

List-II (Constitutional counterpart)
i. Supreme Court
ii. Directive Principles of State Policy
iii. Emergency provisions
iv. Union-State structure and UPSC/State PSCs

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
224.x: The Instrument of Instructions corresponds to the Directive Principles, the Federal Court to the Supreme Court, emergency powers to emergency provisions, and the federal scheme and PSCs to the Union-State structure and present PSC system.
224.tq: Start from the sure pair Federal Court–Supreme Court and complete the constitutional parallels.
xs: Correct matching **a–ii, b–i, c–iii, d–iv** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Instrument of Instructions** → **Directive Principles** (APPSC **2023**); **Federal Court** → **Supreme Court**.
**Emergency powers** → **Emergency provisions** (Part XVIII); **federal scheme and PSCs** → **Union-State structure** and UPSC/State PSCs.
xa: Office of **Governor** and the Governor's address (**Sec. 63**) → Governor's address under **Art. 175/176**.
The 1935 Act = largest single source of the **Constitution's structure**.
Basis of the 1935 Act: **Simon Report**, three **RTCs** and the **White Paper**.

224.s: Section 63 of the Government of India Act, 1935 dealt with the Governor's
o: Power to nationalise the Reserve Bank
Power to appoint the Federal Court judges
Power to dissolve the Constituent Assembly
224.x: Section 63 enabled the Governor to address the provincial legislature in his discretion.
224.tq: Match a specific section with its constitutional function.
xs: **Section 63** of the 1935 Act dealt with the Governor's **address to the provincial legislature** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Under it, the Governor addressed the provincial legislature **"in his discretion"**.
**RBI nationalisation** came only on **1 Jan 1949**, not under the 1935 Act.
xa: From **1937** the speech was prepared **with ministers**; the **Constituent Assembly** kept that convention.
Today the Governor's address is under **Art. 175/176**.
Other borrowings: **Instrument of Instructions** → **Directive Principles**; **Federal Court** → **Supreme Court**.

224.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: 1919 — Government of India Act and Rowlatt Act
224.x: The Rowlatt Act and the Government of India Act were both associated with 1919. The Partition of Bengal was in 1905, the Morley-Minto Reforms in 1909 and the Nehru Report in 1928.
224.tq: Check each year against the constitutional milestone instead of relying on a familiar title alone.
xs: **1919** saw both the **Rowlatt Act** (March) and the **GoI Act 1919** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**1905** = **Partition of Bengal** (Curzon); **1909** = **Morley-Minto Reforms** — options 2 and 3 swap them.
The **Nehru Report** was in **1928**, while **1935** = **GoI Act 1935**.
xa: **1927-28**: Simon Commission appointed / arrives; **1929**: **Jinnah's Fourteen Points**.
**March 1931**: **Gandhi-Irwin Pact**.
APPSC **2018** order: **b, d, a, c** (Partition, Rowlatt, Simon, Gandhi-Irwin).

224.s:
Arrange the following constitutional milestones in chronological order:
A. Nehru Report
B. Partition of Bengal
C. Gandhi-Irwin Pact
D. Jinnah's Fourteen Points
224.x: The correct order is Partition of Bengal (1905), Nehru Report (1928), Jinnah's Fourteen Points (1929), and Gandhi-Irwin Pact (March 1931).
224.tq: Anchor the earliest and latest milestones first, then place the 1928 and 1929 developments between them.
xs: The order is **B, A, D, C** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Partition of Bengal** (**1905**) → **Nehru Report** (**1928**) → **Jinnah's Fourteen Points** (**1929**) → **Gandhi-Irwin Pact** (**March 1931**).
xa: The Fourteen Points were the League's answer to the Nehru Report, so they must come after it.
⚠ Trap: "Gandhi signed the pact in **March 1930**" is wrong — it was **1931**.
**1909**: Morley-Minto Reforms; **1919**: Rowlatt Act and GoI Act 1919; **1935**: GoI Act 1935.

224.s: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed in:
224.x: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed in March 1931; 'March 1930' is a known trap (March 1930 was the start of the Dandi March). December 1929 was the Lahore session and August 1932 the Communal Award.
224.tq: Gandhi-Irwin Pact = March 1931.
xs: The **Gandhi-Irwin Pact** was signed in **March 1931** — so option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ "March **1930**" is the known trap (APPSC **2018** context) — wrong year.
xa: APPSC **2018** chronology: **Partition of Bengal**, **Rowlatt Act**, **Simon Commission**, **Gandhi-Irwin Pact** (b, d, a, c).
**1929**: Jinnah's Fourteen Points; **1928**: Nehru Report.

224.s: The criticism that dyarchy gave ministers transferred subjects without adequate financial control was based on the fact that
o: The Governor-General controlled all transferred subjects directly.
Ministers were denied legislative powers altogether.
Finance was abolished as a provincial subject.
224.x: Dyarchy was criticised because ministers controlled transferred subjects while finance remained among the reserved subjects.
224.tq: Apply the reserved-transferred distinction to an administrative criticism.
xs: Dyarchy was criticised because ministers got **transferred subjects** while **finance remained reserved** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Reserved** subjects (law and order, **finance**, land revenue) were run by the **Governor + Executive Council**, not answerable to the legislature.
**Transferred** subjects (education, health, local self-government) were run by the **Governor with ministers** answerable to the legislature.
