xa: **Dyarchy** = dual government in the **provinces** under the **GoI Act 1919**.
⚠ APPSC **2019**: "dyarchy = single government" was false.
The **1935 Act** abolished provincial dyarchy and introduced **provincial autonomy**.
Another criticism: **communal electorates** were extended.

225.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Butler Committee — relations of princely states with the Paramount Power
Simon Commission — review of the Government of India Act, 1919
Butler Committee — chaired by Lord Irwin
225.x: The Butler Committee was associated with Harcourt Butler, not Lord Irwin. Its purpose was to examine relations between princely states and the Paramount Power.
225.tq: Use the swapped-person trap in a commission-to-chairman pairing.
xs: The wrong pair is **Butler Committee — chaired by Lord Irwin** — so option **(3)** is the answer.
The **Butler Committee** (**1927**) was headed by **Harcourt Butler**; it is only listed under **Irwin's** viceroyalty.
Its task: examine relations between **Indian princely states** and the **Paramount Power** — pair 1 is correct.
The **Simon Commission** was to review the **1919 Act** — pair 2 is correct.
xa: **Lord Irwin** issued the **Deepavali Declaration** on **31 October 1929**.
Irwin's declaration promised a **Round Table Conference** after the Simon report.
⚠ Do not mix up the **Butler Committee** (princely states, **1927**) with the **Simon Commission** (review of the 1919 Act).

225.s:
Which of the following was NOT a condition associated with the Delhi Proposals?
1. Separation of Sindh
2. Reforms in the North-West Frontier Province and Baluchistan
3. One-third Muslim representation at the centre
4. Abolition of joint electorates
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
225.x: The Delhi Proposals supported joint electorates subject to safeguards; they did not seek the abolition of joint electorates. The other three were associated conditions.
225.tq: Identify the statement that reverses the central proposal.
xs: Only statement **4** — **abolition of joint electorates** — was not a condition — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Delhi Proposals (March 1927)** offered to **drop separate electorates** for **joint electorates** plus reserved seats.
Their conditions: **one-third** of central seats, **separation of Sindh**, reforms in **NWFP and Baluchistan**, representation by population in **Punjab and Bengal**.
xa: ⚠ **Delhi Proposals (1927)** = drop separate electorates; **Fourteen Points (1929)** = keep separate electorates.
**Jinnah's Fourteen Points** came in **March 1929** at the **Muslim League session in Delhi**.
The **All Parties Muslim Conference** (**Delhi, Jan 1929**) under the **Aga Khan** rejected the Nehru Report.

225.s: Tanguturi Prakasam earned the title ‘Andhra Kesari’ because he
o: drafted the Nehru Report in Andhra
bared his chest and dared the police to shoot during the Simon protest
organised the first Round Table Conference
led the boycott resolution at the Madras Congress session
225.x: During the Simon protest, Prakasam bared his chest and challenged the police to shoot, earning the title ‘Andhra Kesari’.
225.tq: Connect an honorific with the specific incident that produced it.
xs: During the **Madras** anti-Simon protest (**1928**), **Tanguturi Prakasam** **bared his chest and dared the police to shoot** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Police firing had killed **Parthasarathi**; Prakasam's defiance earned him the title **"Andhra Kesari"**.
The **Nehru Report** was drafted by **Motilal Nehru's** committee, and the RTCs were held in **London** — not Prakasam's work.
xa: Date of the Madras protest: **26 Feb 1928** (a printed **"2028"** is a typo); asked in APPSC GS **2022**.
**S. Satyamurthy** was President of the **Andhra Boycott Committee**.
Prakasam's moment and the Simon report's neglect of Andhra fuelled the **separate-Andhra** demand.

225.s: During the Simon Commission protest in Madras, the person killed by police firing was
225.x: Police firing during the Madras protest killed Parthasarathi.
225.tq: Identify the individual associated with a specific regional incident.
xs: Police firing during the **Madras** Simon protest killed **Parthasarathi** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**G.V. Unnayya Sastri** led protests at **Tenali and Guntur**; **Bulusu Sambamurti** toured Andhra for the boycott.
**S. Satyamurthy** was President of the **Andhra Boycott Committee**.
xa: After the firing, **Tanguturi Prakasam** bared his chest → title **"Andhra Kesari"**.
The protest was on **26 Feb 1928** (APPSC GS **2022**).
**Guntur and Ongole** showed **black flags** to the Commission.

225.s: Black flags were shown against the Simon Commission at
225.x: Black flags were shown at Guntur and Ongole. G. V. Unnayya Sastri led protests at Tenali and Guntur.
225.tq: Distinguish locations of black-flag demonstrations from locations of organised leadership.
xs: **Black flags** were shown at **Guntur and Ongole** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Eluru, Srikakulam, Tirupati, Kurnool** instead passed **municipal resolutions**.
At **Vijayawada**, chairman **Kaleswara Rao** sent the "Simon Go Back" cover; **Tenali** saw G.V. Unnayya Sastri's protest.
xa: **G.V. Unnayya Sastri** led the protest at **Tenali and Guntur**.
**Bulusu Sambamurti** toured Andhra for the boycott.
**S. Satyamurthy** presided over the **Andhra Boycott Committee**.

225.s: The challenge issued by Birkenhead in 1927, which led to the formation of the committee for the Nehru Report, was that Indians
o: could not organise a boycott of the Simon Commission
could not agree on a constitutional scheme
225.x: Birkenhead challenged Indians to prepare an agreed constitutional scheme, leading to the All Parties Conference and the Nehru Report committee.
225.tq: Identify the cause behind the formation of a constitutional committee.
xs: **Birkenhead's** challenge (**1927**) was that Indians **could not draft an agreed constitution** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The answer was the **Nehru Report** (**August 1928**), drafted by a committee of the **All Parties Conference**.
Far from opposing **linguistic provinces** or **dominion status**, the Nehru Report itself recommended both.
xa: **Dr M.A. Ansari** presided the **All Parties Conference (1928)**.
**Motilal Nehru** chaired the **7-member committee**; **Jawaharlal Nehru** was secretary.
⚠ Trap: "**10 Aug 1929**" is wrong — the report is of **1928**.

225.s:
Consider the following statements about the Nehru Report:
1. It was drafted by a committee chaired by Motilal Nehru, with Jawaharlal Nehru as secretary, set up by the All Parties Conference under Dr M.A. Ansari.
2. It was published in August 1929.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
225.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong (a known trap): the Nehru Report came out in August 1928, not 1929. Hence 1 only.
225.tq: Nehru Report = August 1928 (1929 is the trap).
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **Motilal Nehru** chaired the committee, **Jawaharlal Nehru** was secretary, under the **All Parties Conference** presided by **Dr M.A. Ansari**.
Statement 2 wrong: the report came in **August 1928**, not 1929.
xa: ⚠ Trap: "**10 Aug 1929**" is wrong; **1928** is correct.
⚠ **Ansari** presided the All Parties Conference; **Motilal** chaired its drafting committee.
The committee had **7 members**.

225.s: Which of the following was NOT a recommendation of the Nehru Report?
o: Universal adult suffrage and fundamental rights
Separate electorates as the permanent basis of representation
A federal structure with a bicameral central legislature
225.x: The Nehru Report recommended joint electorates with reserved seats for minorities, not separate electorates as a permanent arrangement.
225.tq: Use the central distinction between joint electorates and separate electorates.
xs: The Nehru Report did **not** recommend **separate electorates** — so option **(3)** is the answer.
It proposed **joint electorates + reserved seats** for minorities.
It did recommend **dominion status**, a **bicameral** centre and **universal adult suffrage + fundamental rights**.
xa: Other recommendations: end of **dyarchy**, **responsible government**, a **Supreme Court**, **linguistic provinces** (incl. **Andhra**).
The **Muslim League** rejected it; **Jinnah's amendments** failed at the **Calcutta All Parties Convention (Dec 1928)**.
⚠ Separate electorates were kept by the **Simon report** and demanded by the **Fourteen Points**.

225.s:
Which of the following correctly describes the reaction to the Nehru Report?
1. The Muslim League rejected it.
2. Jinnah's amendments failed at the Calcutta All Parties Convention.
3. Jawaharlal Nehru and Subhas Chandra Bose demanded complete independence.
4. The Congress immediately accepted complete independence without an ultimatum.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
225.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Congress gave Britain a one-year ultimatum; complete independence was declared at Lahore in 1929 after the ultimatum expired.
225.tq: Identify the single false statement by distinguishing an ultimatum from its later outcome.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **Muslim League rejected** it; **Jinnah's amendments failed** at the **Calcutta All Parties Convention (Dec 1928)**.
**Jawaharlal Nehru** and **Bose** wanted **complete independence**.
Statement 4 wrong: Congress first gave a **one-year ultimatum**, then declared **Purna Swaraj** at **Lahore (1929)**.
xa: The **All Parties Muslim Conference** (**Delhi, Jan 1929**) under the **Aga Khan** also rejected the report.
Jinnah's **Fourteen Points** followed in **March 1929**.
The report sought **dominion status**, which the young radicals found inadequate.

225.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Nehru Report:
1. Jawaharlal Nehru served as its secretary.
2. It recommended a Supreme Court.
3. It proposed the continuation of dyarchy in the provinces.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
225.x: Jawaharlal Nehru was the secretary and the report recommended a Supreme Court. It proposed ending dyarchy, so statement 3 is false.
225.tq: Locate the one reversed constitutional recommendation.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **Jawaharlal Nehru** was **secretary** of the committee.
Statement 2 correct: it recommended a **Supreme Court** with a **bicameral** centre.
Statement 3 wrong: it called for the **end of dyarchy** and **responsible government**.
xa: **Motilal Nehru** chaired the **7-member committee**.
It recommended **linguistic provinces** (incl. **Andhra**) and **joint electorates**.
Report date: **August 1928**.

225.s: The All Parties Muslim Conference held at Delhi in January 1929, under the Aga Khan,
o: drafted the Government of India Act, 1935
resolved to boycott the Simon Commission at every stage
accepted the Nehru Report without modification
225.x: The All Parties Muslim Conference at Delhi in January 1929, presided over by the Aga Khan, rejected the Nehru Report.
225.tq: Distinguish the Muslim Conference's reaction from the earlier All Parties Conference.
xs: The **All Parties Muslim Conference** (**Delhi, Jan 1929**) under the **Aga Khan** **rejected the Nehru Report** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **GoI Act 1935** came from the Simon report + RTCs, not from this conference.
The boycott "at every stage" was not this conference's work.
xa: **Jinnah's Fourteen Points** followed in **March 1929** at the **Muslim League session in Delhi**.
The **Muslim League** also rejected the Nehru Report.
The **Nehru Report** proposed **joint electorates**, unacceptable to these Muslim bodies.

225.s: Jinnah's Fourteen Points were presented in March 1929 at the
o: Indian National Congress session at Lahore
Second Round Table Conference at London
225.x: Jinnah presented the Fourteen Points in March 1929 at the Muslim League session in Delhi.
225.tq: Match a constitutional document with its organisation, venue and date.
xs: Jinnah presented the **Fourteen Points** in **March 1929** at the **Muslim League session in Delhi** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Lahore** session (**1929**) of Congress declared **Purna Swaraj** — not the Fourteen Points.
The **2nd RTC** came later, in **Sep-Dec 1931**.
xa: Demands: **federal constitution**, **residuary powers to provinces**, **one-third** Muslim seats at the centre, **separate electorates**, Muslim-majority safeguards.
⚠ **Delhi Proposals (1927)** = drop separate electorates; **Fourteen Points (1929)** = keep them.
The **All Parties Muslim Conference** (**Jan 1929**) under the **Aga Khan** had already rejected the Nehru Report.

225.s:
Which of the following demands formed part of Jinnah's Fourteen Points?
1. Federal constitution with residuary powers vested in the provinces
2. One-third Muslim representation at the centre
3. Separate electorates
4. Safeguards for Muslim-majority provinces
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
225.x: All four were among the major demands associated with Jinnah's Fourteen Points: provincial residuary powers, one-third central representation, separate electorates and safeguards for Muslim-majority provinces.
225.tq: Distinguish Jinnah's demands from the joint-electorate provisions of the Nehru Report.
xs: **All four** demands were in the Fourteen Points — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Federal constitution** + **residuary powers to provinces**; **one-third** Muslim seats at the centre.
**Separate electorates** + **Muslim-majority safeguards**.
xa: Presented in **March 1929** at the **Muslim League session in Delhi**.
⚠ The **Delhi Proposals (March 1927)** had offered to **drop** separate electorates for joint electorates.
The Delhi Proposals also sought **separation of Sindh** and reforms in **NWFP and Baluchistan**.

225.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Deepavali Declaration:
1. It was issued in 1929.
2. It was issued by Lord Irwin.
3. It promised a Round Table Conference before the Simon Commission report.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
225.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the promised Round Table Conference was to be held after the Simon Commission report.
225.tq: Find the reversed sequence in the statement containing ‘before’ and retain the two directly established facts.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: issued on **31 October 1929**.
Statement 2 correct: issued by Viceroy **Lord Irwin**.
Statement 3 wrong: the RTC was promised **after** the Simon report, not before.
xa: It declared **dominion status** the natural goal of India's constitutional progress.
The **Simon report** followed in **May 1930**.
**Ramsay MacDonald** was British PM during all three RTCs (**1930-32**).

225.s: Which of the following was NOT a recommendation of the Simon Commission report?
o: Immediate establishment of complete responsible government at the Centre
225.x: The report recommended abolition of dyarchy, provincial autonomy and continuation of separate communal electorates. Immediate establishment of complete responsible government at the Centre was not listed as its recommendation.
225.tq: Find the option that goes beyond the specific constitutional recommendations rather than merely changing one territorial detail.
xs: **Immediate complete responsible government at the Centre** was not a Simon recommendation — so option **(1)** is the answer.
It did recommend **abolishing dyarchy** → full **provincial autonomy**.
It recommended keeping **separate communal electorates**.
xa: Report date: **May 1930**.
It separated **Sindh** from Bombay and **Burma** from India, and created an **Orissa** province.
Report + RTCs → **Government of India Act 1935**.

225.s:
With reference to the territorial recommendations of the Simon Commission report, consider the following statements:
1. Sindh was to be separated from Bombay.
2. Burma was to be separated from India.
3. Orissa was to be created as a province.
4. Andhra was to be created as a province.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
225.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the report ignored Andhra’s demand for a separate province.
225.tq: Identify the one swapped territorial outcome by comparing the treatment of Orissa and Andhra.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Sindh** from Bombay and **Burma** from India were to be separated; an **Orissa** province was to be created.
Statement 4 wrong: the report **ignored Andhra's demand**.
xa: Contrast: **Oriyas lobbied** the Commission; **Andhras boycotted** it.
This neglect, along with Prakasam's **"Andhra Kesari"** moment, fuelled the **separate-Andhra** demand.
Report date: **May 1930**.

225.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the response of the Oriyas and the Andhras to the Simon Commission?
o: The Oriyas boycotted the Commission, whereas the Andhras lobbied it.
The Oriyas lobbied the Commission, whereas the Andhras boycotted it.
Both groups lobbied the Commission for their respective provincial demands.
Both groups boycotted the Commission and rejected provincial reorganisation.
225.x: The Oriyas lobbied the Simon Commission, while the Andhras boycotted it. The report supported the creation of Orissa but ignored Andhra’s demand.
225.tq: Test the paired contrast directly by checking which group lobbied and which group boycotted.
xs: The **Oriyas lobbied** the Commission, whereas the **Andhras boycotted** it — so option **(2)** is correct.
Result: the report proposed an **Orissa** province but **ignored Andhra's demand**.
xa: Andhra boycott: **Prakasam** in Madras, **black flags** at **Guntur and Ongole**, **Kaleswara Rao's** cover at Vijayawada.
**S. Satyamurthy** was President of the **Andhra Boycott Committee**.
The **Nehru Report** had backed **linguistic provinces** including **Andhra**.

225.s: Which of the following statements about the three Round Table Conferences is correct?
o: Only the Second Conference was held in London to discuss dominion status.
All three were held in Delhi under the Viceroy of India.
The conferences were convened by the Indian National Congress to draft the Nehru Report.
All three were held in London under Ramsay MacDonald to discuss the Simon Report and a federal constitution.
225.x: All three Round Table Conferences were held in London under British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald to discuss the Simon Report and a federal constitution.
225.tq: Use venue, convening authority and agenda together to eliminate substituted details.
xs: All three RTCs were held in **London** under PM **Ramsay MacDonald** to discuss the **Simon Report** and a **federal constitution** — so option **(4)** is correct.
They were not in **Delhi**, and the **Nehru Report** (**1928**) was an Indian effort before the RTCs.
xa: Congress attended only the **2nd** RTC; **Ambedkar** attended all three.
The 1st RTC agreed on a **federal structure**.

225.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: First Round Table Conference — Congress represented by Gandhi
Second Round Table Conference — Gandhi as sole INC representative
Third Round Table Conference — attended by Congress under Jawaharlal Nehru
First Round Table Conference — held after the Gandhi-Irwin Pact
225.x: Gandhi attended the Second Round Table Conference as the sole representative of the Indian National Congress. Congress boycotted the First and Third Conferences.
225.tq: Start with the sure Congress-attendance pair and eliminate reversals.
xs: **Gandhi** was the **sole INC representative** at the **2nd RTC** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Congress **boycotted** the **1st RTC** (CDM was on) and was **absent** from the **3rd**.
The **1st RTC** led to the **Gandhi-Irwin Pact**, so it came before the pact, not after.
xa: 2nd RTC: **Sep-Dec 1931**, opened **7 Sept 1931**; failed on **minority representation**.
**Sarojini Naidu** and **Muhammad Iqbal** attended the 2nd RTC (APPSC G2 **2005**).
APPSC **2025** match: Gandhi-Irwin Pact = Gandhi agrees to attend the next RTC.

225.s: After the Second Round Table Conference, Mahatma Gandhi
o: joined the Third Round Table Conference as a British delegate
resumed the Civil Disobedience Movement and was jailed in Yerwada
formed the Muslim League to negotiate minority representation
accepted the Communal Award and retired from public life
225.x: After the Second Conference, Gandhi resumed the Civil Disobedience Movement and was imprisoned in Yerwada. The Communal Award followed in August 1932.
225.tq: Link a conference outcome with its immediate political consequence.
xs: After the **2nd RTC**, Gandhi **resumed the CDM** and was **jailed in Yerwada** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **Communal Award** (**Aug 1932**) followed while he was in jail.
Congress was **absent** from the **3rd RTC**, so Gandhi did not attend it.
xa: The 2nd RTC failed on **minority representation**.
3rd RTC: **17 Nov-24 Dec 1932**, only **46** delegates.
Gandhi was the **sole INC representative** at the 2nd RTC.

225.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Round Table Conferences:
1. The First Conference agreed on a federal structure.
2. The Second Conference ended in a deadlock over the minorities question.
3. The Third Conference was attended by the Congress and Jinnah.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
225.x: The First Conference agreed on a federal structure and the Second ended in a deadlock over minorities. The Congress and Jinnah were absent from the Third Conference.
225.tq: Find the false participation statement before selecting the coded combination.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: the **1st RTC** agreed on a **federal structure**.
Statement 2 correct: the **2nd RTC** failed on **minority representation**.
Statement 3 wrong: **Congress** and **Jinnah** were **absent** from the **3rd RTC**.
xa: The 3rd RTC had only **46 delegates**.
Congress attended only the **2nd** RTC; **Ambedkar** attended all three.
All three were in **London** under **Ramsay MacDonald** (**1930-32**).

225.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched in relation to participation in all three Round Table Conferences?
o: B.R. Ambedkar and Tej Bahadur Sapru
225.x: B.R. Ambedkar and Tej Bahadur Sapru attended all three Round Table Conferences.
225.tq: Start from the sure pair involving participants present at all three conferences.
xs: **Ambedkar and Tej Bahadur Sapru** attended all three RTCs — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Gandhi**, **Muhammad Iqbal** and **Sarojini Naidu** are linked with the **2nd RTC** only.
**Jinnah** was absent from the **3rd RTC**.
xa: Ambedkar represented the **depressed classes**.
Congress attended only the **2nd** RTC.
The 3rd RTC (**1932**) had only **46** delegates.

225.s: Besides Gandhi, which of the following attended the Second Round Table Conference (1931)?
o: Jawaharlal Nehru and Subhas Chandra Bose
225.x: Sarojini Naidu and Muhammad Iqbal attended the Second RTC (Sept-Dec 1931), where Gandhi was the sole INC representative (APPSC G2 2005). Nehru, Bose, Patel and Azad did not attend; Motilal Nehru and C.R. Das had died before 1931.
225.tq: 2nd RTC: Gandhi + Sarojini Naidu + Iqbal.
xs: **Sarojini Naidu** and **Muhammad Iqbal** attended the **2nd RTC** — so option **(1)** is correct (APPSC G2 **2005**).
**Gandhi** was the **sole INC representative** there.
xa: The 2nd RTC: **Sep-Dec 1931**, opened **7 Sept 1931** (some notes say "Nov-Dec 1931").
It failed on **minority representation**.
After it Gandhi resumed the **CDM** and was jailed in **Yerwada**.

225.s: The neglect of Andhra’s demand by the Simon Commission, along with Tanguturi Prakasam’s ‘Andhra Kesari’ moment, contributed to which political development?
o: The demand for a separate Andhra Province
The demand for the continuation of Burma within India
The demand for the abolition of provincial autonomy
The demand for the restoration of dyarchy in the provinces
225.x: The neglect of Andhra’s demand by the Simon Commission and Prakasam’s political role fuelled the demand for a separate Andhra Province.
225.tq: Trace the stated regional grievance to the political demand it helped strengthen.
xs: These fuelled the **demand for a separate Andhra Province** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The Simon report created an **Orissa** province but **ignored Andhra's demand**.
The report itself recommended separating **Burma** from India and **abolishing dyarchy** — the other options run against it.
xa: **Oriyas lobbied** the Commission; **Andhras boycotted** it.
**Prakasam** became **"Andhra Kesari"** at the **Madras** protest (**26 Feb 1928**).
The **Nehru Report** had backed **linguistic provinces** including **Andhra**.

226.s: Under the Government of India Act, 1935, the Federal, Provincial and Concurrent Lists contained, respectively, how many subjects?
226.x: The Federal List contained 59 subjects, the Provincial List 54 subjects and the Concurrent List 36 subjects.
226.tq: Use the numerical association between the three lists and eliminate options that interchange their figures.
xs: The **Federal, Provincial and Concurrent** Lists had **59, 54 and 36** items — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Federal** = **59** (largest), **Provincial** = **54**, **Concurrent** = **36** (smallest).
xa: **Residuary powers** were with the **Governor-General**.
The **Governor** had discretionary powers, e.g. the **Sec. 63** address.
The **federal scheme** is among the features borrowed into the Constitution.

226.s:
Consider the following statements about the Government of India Act, 1935:
1. Residuary powers were vested in the provincial legislatures.
2. The Governor-General could stop discussion and suspend proceedings on a Bill.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
226.x: Statement 1 is wrong: residuary powers were vested in the Governor-General, not the provinces. Statement 2 is correct: the Governor-General could stop discussion and suspend Bill proceedings. Hence 2 only; 1 only, both and neither are wrong.
226.tq: Under the 1935 Act the Governor-General held both residuary and blocking powers.
xs: Only statement **2** is correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 wrong: **residuary powers** lay with the **Governor-General**, not the provinces.
Statement 2 correct: the **Governor-General** could **stop discussion** and **suspend bill proceedings**.
xa: Three lists: **Federal (59)**, **Provincial (54)**, **Concurrent (36)**.
**Separate electorates** were extended to **depressed classes, women and labour**.
The **Governor** had discretion too, e.g. the **Sec. 63** address.

226.s: The Government of India Act, 1935 further extended the system of separate electorates to include which of the following groups?
o: Workers, soldiers and civil servants only
226.x: The separate electorate system was extended further to depressed classes, women and labour.
226.tq: Test the exact membership of a statutory category through a closely related group-list option.
xs: Separate electorates were extended to **depressed classes, women and labour** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The 1935 Act extended the communal scheme **further** rather than ending it.
xa: The Act was called a **"Charter of Slavery"** by **Nehru**.
**Residuary powers** went to the **Governor-General**.
Congress rejected the Act and demanded a **Constituent Assembly** on **adult franchise**.

226.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. M.N. Roy raised the demand for a Constituent Assembly in 1934.
2. The demand became an official Congress demand in 1935.
3. The Lucknow session of 1936 rejected the Government of India Act.
4. The Faizpur session of 1936 decided to contest the elections.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
226.x: All four statements are correct. M.N. Roy first raised the Constituent Assembly demand in 1934, Congress adopted it officially in 1935, Lucknow rejected the Act, and Faizpur decided to contest the elections.
226.tq: Arrange related resolutions by person, year and Congress session.
xs: **All four** statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
**M.N. Roy** first raised the **Constituent Assembly** demand in **1934**; it became the **official Congress demand** in **1935**.
**Lucknow (1936)**, under **Nehru**, **rejected** the Act; **Faizpur (1936)** decided to **contest** the elections.
xa: The demand was for an Assembly elected on **adult franchise**.
The elections were held in winter **1936-37** in **11** provinces.
**Jinnah** called the Act "thoroughly rotten, fundamentally bad and totally unacceptable".

226.s: Who described the Government of India Act, 1935 as “thoroughly rotten, fundamentally bad and totally unacceptable”?
226.x: Muhammad Ali Jinnah used the description “thoroughly rotten, fundamentally bad and totally unacceptable” for the Act.
226.tq: Discriminate between two well-known but different criticisms of the same Act.
xs: **Jinnah** called the Act "**thoroughly rotten, fundamentally bad and totally unacceptable**" — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Nehru** called it a **"Charter of Slavery"** and "a machine with **strong brakes but no engine**".
**M.N. Roy** is known for first raising the **Constituent Assembly** demand (**1934**).
xa: Congress officially demanded a Constituent Assembly in **1935**.
The **Muslim League** later **did poorly** even in Muslim seats in the **1937** elections.
⚠ **Lucknow 1936** rejected the Act; **Faizpur 1936** decided to contest.

226.s: Who described the Government of India Act, 1935 as a 'Charter of Slavery' and as 'a machine with strong brakes but no engine'?
226.x: Jawaharlal Nehru used both descriptions. Jinnah called the Act 'thoroughly rotten, fundamentally bad and totally unacceptable'; M.N. Roy first raised the Constituent Assembly demand (1934).
226.tq: Charter of Slavery / brakes no engine = Nehru; 'rotten' = Jinnah.
xs: **Jawaharlal Nehru** used both phrases — **"Charter of Slavery"** and "a machine with **strong brakes but no engine**" — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Jinnah** called it "**thoroughly rotten**, fundamentally bad and totally unacceptable".
**M.N. Roy** first raised the **Constituent Assembly** demand (**1934**).
xa: Nehru presided the **Lucknow (1936)** session, which rejected the Act.
**Faizpur (1936)** decided to contest the elections.
Congress demanded a **Constituent Assembly** on **adult franchise** (official in **1935**).

226.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the political outcome in the Madras Presidency after the 1937 elections?
o: The Muslim League formed the ministry under a coalition arrangement.
The Congress formed the ministry, while the Justice Party was almost wiped out.
The Justice Party formed the ministry with the People's Party.
The Hindu Mahasabha formed the ministry with the Congress.
226.x: The Congress formed the Madras ministry, while the Justice Party was almost wiped out. The People's Party of the Pithapuram Zamindar lost all its seats, and the League and Hindu Mahasabha performed poorly.
226.tq: Reject the options that assign office to parties which performed poorly.
xs: In Madras, **Congress formed the ministry** while the **Justice Party was wiped out** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Only a few Justice men, like the **Challapalli Zamindar**, won.
The **Pithapuram Zamindar's People's Party** lost everything; the **League** and **Hindu Mahasabha** did poorly.
xa: The ministry was formed on **14 July 1937** under **C. Rajagopalachari** (APHQ **2011**).
It ended **Justice Party** rule of **1920-37**.
The campaign was led by **Tanguturi Prakasam** and **Bulusu Sambamurthy**.

226.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Leader)
 a. Tanguturi Prakasam
 b. Bezawada Gopala Reddy
 c. V.V. Giri
 d. Bulusu Sambamurthy

List-II (Post)
 i. Speaker
 ii. Labour and Industries
 iii. Revenue
 iv. Local Self-Government

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
226.x: Tanguturi Prakasam held Revenue, Bezawada Gopala Reddy held Local Self-Government, V.V. Giri held Labour and Industries, and Bulusu Sambamurthy was Speaker.
226.tq: Start from the sure leader-post pair and eliminate inconsistent codes.
xs: Correct matching **a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Prakasam** — **Revenue**; **Bezawada Gopala Reddy** — **Local Self-Government**.
**V.V. Giri** — **Labour and Industries**; **Bulusu Sambamurthy** — **Speaker**.
xa: The ministry was headed by Premier **C. Rajagopalachari** (**14 July 1937**).
Rajaji's Hindi move in schools → **Periyar's anti-Hindi agitation (1937)** → withdrawn.
Prakasam was **APCC President** and led the **1937** campaign.

226.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Bengal — Unionist Party ministry under Sikandar Hayat Khan
Bengal — Coalition led by Fazlul Huq's Krishak Praja Party
226.x: In Bengal, Fazlul Huq's Krishak Praja Party formed a coalition. Punjab was associated with the Unionist Party under Sikandar Hayat Khan, while Sindh had a coalition under Allah Baksh.
226.tq: Use province-leader-party associations to reject swapped outcomes.
xs: **Bengal** had a coalition led by **Fazlul Huq's Krishak Praja Party** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Punjab** had the **Unionist Party** under **Sikandar Hayat Khan** — option 1 puts it in Bengal.
**Sindh** had a coalition under **Allah Baksh** — not a Congress majority, and not in Punjab.
xa: **Bombay**: Congress largest party, formed ministry.
Elections: winter **1936-37** in **11** provinces.
The **Muslim League** did poorly even in Muslim seats.

226.s: Which of the following statements about the Muslim League's performance after the 1937 elections is correct?
o: It performed strongly in all Muslim seats and formed ministries in every Muslim-majority province.
It did poorly even in Muslim seats, after which it alleged Hindu Raj and launched mass-contact campaigns.
It merged with the Congress in the provinces where Congress formed ministries.
It won a clear majority in Bengal and rejected mass-contact campaigns.
226.x: The Muslim League performed poorly even in Muslim seats. It subsequently alleged “Hindu Raj” and launched mass-contact campaigns.
226.tq: Trace the political consequence of an electoral setback.
xs: The League **did poorly even in Muslim seats**, then alleged **"Hindu Raj"** and launched **mass-contact campaigns** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Bengal** went to a **Fazlul Huq** coalition, **Punjab** to the **Unionists**, **Sindh** to **Allah Baksh** — not the League.
xa: In Madras too the **League + Hindu Mahasabha** did poorly.
Later the League observed **"Deliverance Day"** on **22 December 1939**.
**Jinnah** had called the 1935 Act "thoroughly rotten".

226.s: The Congress ministry formed in Madras on 14 July 1937 was headed by:
226.x: C. Rajagopalachari (Rajaji) became Premier of Madras on 14 July 1937 (APHQ 2011). Prakasam was Revenue Minister, V.V. Giri Labour and Industries Minister, and Bulusu Sambamurthy the Speaker.
226.tq: Madras 1937 Premier = Rajaji; Prakasam = Revenue.
xs: The Madras Congress ministry of **14 July 1937** was headed by **C. Rajagopalachari** — so option **(3)** is correct (APHQ **2011**).
**Prakasam** was **Revenue Minister**, **V.V. Giri** handled **Labour and Industries**, **Bulusu Sambamurthy** was **Speaker**.
xa: **Bezawada Gopala Reddy** held **Local Self-Government**.
It ended **Justice Party** rule (**1920-37**).
Rajaji's Hindi policy → **Periyar's anti-Hindi agitation** → withdrawn.

226.s: In how many provinces did the Indian National Congress form ministries after the elections held under the Government of India Act, 1935?
226.x: Congress formed ministries in eight of the eleven provinces in 1937. These included Bombay, Madras, Central Provinces, Orissa, Bihar, the United Provinces, the North-West Frontier Province and Assam.
226.tq: Use the total number as the distinguishing numerical fact.
xs: Congress formed ministries in **eight** (**8 of 11**) provinces — so option **(3)** is correct.
**July 1937**: Bombay, Madras, Central Provinces, Orissa, Bihar, United Provinces (six); later **NWFP and Assam** → total **8**.
It had a **clear majority on its own** in **5** provinces.
xa: The 5: **Madras, UP, CP, Bihar, Orissa**.
**Gandhi's advice**: hold office "**lightly, not tightly**", a "**crown of thorns**".
The ministries **resigned in Oct-Nov 1939**.

226.s: Mahatma Gandhi advised the Congress ministries to hold office:
o: firmly and permanently as a constitutional right
only until the completion of the war
lightly, not tightly, as a crown of thorns
226.x: Gandhi advised the ministers to hold office “lightly, not tightly”, describing office as a “crown of thorns”.
226.tq: Test the exact wording of a famous political expression.
xs: **Gandhi** told the ministries to hold office "**lightly, not tightly**", as a "**crown of thorns**" — so option **(4)** is correct.
The ministries indeed **resigned in Oct-Nov 1939** rather than cling to office.
xa: Congress formed ministries in **8 of 11** provinces.
Their record: **civil liberties**, **Tenancy Acts**, abolition of **begar**, **Industrial Disputes Act (1938)**.
**Harijans** got free education and other upliftment measures.

226.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the resignation of the Congress ministries:
1. The Congress ministries resigned in October-November 1939.
2. They resigned because Viceroy Linlithgow declared India a party to the Second World War without consulting Indian leaders.
3. The Muslim League observed 22 December 1940 as Deliverance Day.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
226.x: Statement 1 is correct: the ministries resigned in October-November 1939. Statement 2 is correct: Linlithgow declared India a party to the war (September 1939) without consulting Indian leaders. Statement 3 is wrong: Deliverance Day was observed on 22 December 1939, not 1940. So 1 only is incomplete, 2 and 3 only and 1, 2 and 3 wrongly include statement 3.
226.tq: Resignation and Deliverance Day fall in the same year, 1939.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: the ministries **resigned in Oct-Nov 1939**.
Statement 2 correct: Viceroy **Linlithgow** declared India a party to **World War II** (**Sept 1939**) without consulting Indian leaders.
Statement 3 wrong: **Deliverance Day** was **22 December 1939**, not 1940.
xa: Some notes give the resignation as **October 1939**, others **November 1939**.
APPSC **2018** asked the reason: protest against making India a party to the war with **Germany**.
The ministries had been formed in **July 1937**.

226.s:
Consider the following statements about the record of the Congress ministries (1937-39):
1. Tenancy legislation was passed, for example in the United Provinces.
2. Begar, which they abolished, was a tax on salt.
3. Free education was provided for Harijans.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
226.x: Statement 1 is correct: Tenancy Acts (e.g. UP) were part of the agrarian record. Statement 2 is wrong: begar was forced labour, not a salt tax, though it was abolished. Statement 3 is correct: Harijans got free education. So 1 and 3 only; 1 only omits statement 3, and the options with 2 are wrong.
226.tq: Begar = forced labour; remember the ministries' three agrarian steps: tenancy, begar, debt relief.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **Tenancy Acts** were passed, e.g. in **UP**.
Statement 2 wrong: **begar** was **forced labour**, not a salt tax (it was abolished).
Statement 3 correct: **Harijans** got **free education**.
xa: **Debt relief** was another agrarian measure.
Labour: **Industrial Disputes Act (1938)**.
Civil liberties: political prisoners released, **press freedom** restored.

226.s: The provision of the Government of India Act, 1935 that served as a model for the Directive Principles of State Policy was the:
226.x: The Instrument of Instructions under the Government of India Act, 1935 served as the model for the Directive Principles of State Policy.
226.tq: Test a direct source-feature relationship.
xs: The **Instrument of Instructions** of the 1935 Act was the model for the **Directive Principles** — so option **(1)** is correct (APPSC **2023**).
The **Federal Court** and **separate provincial budget** are other borrowings, not the DPSP model.
xa: Other 1935 borrowings: **federal scheme**, **office of Governor**, **judiciary**, **PSCs**, **emergency provisions**.
From the **1919** Act: **bicameralism** and **direct elections** at the Centre, **separate provincial budget**.
The Act is called the **blueprint** of the Constitution.

226.s: Which one of the following sets contains only features borrowed from the Government of India Act, 1935?
o: Concurrent List, joint sitting and freedom of trade
Fundamental Rights, judicial review, impeachment and Vice-President
Federal scheme, office of Governor, judiciary and Public Service Commissions
Fundamental Duties, Five-Year Plans and ideals of justice
226.x: The Government of India Act, 1935 contributed the federal scheme, office of Governor, judiciary and Public Service Commissions, among other administrative features.
226.tq: Group the administrative and institutional provisions before considering ideological or federal borrowings from other countries.
xs: **Federal scheme, office of Governor, judiciary and PSCs** all come from the **1935 Act** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The Act also gave **emergency provisions** and administrative details.
xa: **Instrument of Instructions** → model for the **Directive Principles** (APPSC **2023**).
**1919 Act** → **bicameralism**, **direct elections**, **separate provincial budget**.
Large parts of the Constitution's structure come from the 1935 Act — hence "**blueprint**".

226.s: Which Act is correctly associated with the introduction of dyarchy in the provinces, bicameralism at the Centre and direct elections?
226.x: These three features were introduced by the Government of India Act, 1919, also known as the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms.
226.tq: Recognize the characteristic three-feature combination of the 1919 Act.
xs: **Dyarchy in the provinces**, **bicameralism at the Centre** and **direct elections** came with the **Government of India Act, 1919** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **1935 Act** instead brought **provincial autonomy**, three lists and the **Instrument of Instructions**.
xa: The **1919** Act also gave a **Public Service Commission** and a **separate provincial budget**.
**1935** borrowings: **federal scheme**, **office of Governor**, **judiciary**, **emergency provisions**.
⚠ Do not confuse: **1919** = bicameralism and direct elections; **1935** = federal scheme.

226.s: The idea behind Section 63 of the Government of India Act, 1935, on the Governor's address to the provincial legislature, is carried in which Article of the Constitution of India?
226.x: Article 175 (the Governor's address) carries the idea of Section 63 of the 1935 Act. Today the speech reflects the elected ministry's policy rather than the Governor's own discretion.
226.tq: Sec. 63 grew into Art. 175.
xs: **Section 63** (Governor's address) is carried by **Article 175** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Under Sec. 63 the Governor addressed the provincial legislature "**in his discretion**".
Today the speech reflects the **elected ministry's policy**.
xa: Rows over **Governors' addresses** in **Opposition-ruled States** are traced to Sec. 63 and Art. 175 (**26 Jan 2026**).
The **office of Governor** itself is a **1935** borrowing.
The **Instrument of Instructions** became the model for the **Directive Principles**.

226.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Andhra angle of the Government of India Act, 1935:
1. Provincial autonomy made an Andhra State look achievable.
2. The Sri Bagh Pact (1937) closed the Coastal-Rayalaseema rift before the 1937 polls.
3. The Sri Bagh Pact was concluded at the house of Tanguturi Prakasam.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
226.x: Statement 1 is correct: provincial autonomy made an Andhra State look achievable. Statement 2 is correct: the Sri Bagh Pact of 1937 closed the Coastal-Rayalaseema rift. Statement 3 is wrong: the pact was concluded at Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao's house 'Sreerbagh', not Prakasam's. So 1 and 2 only.
226.tq: Sri Bagh = Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao's house, 1937.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **provincial autonomy** made an **Andhra state** look achievable.
Statement 2 correct: the **Sri Bagh Pact (1937)** closed the **Coastal-Rayalaseema** rift before the polls.
Statement 3 wrong: it was signed at **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao's** house **"Sreerbagh"**.
xa: **Prakasam** led the Madras **1937** campaign as **APCC President**.
First Congress government in Madras (**1937**, **Rajaji**) ended Justice Party rule of **1920-37**.
Andhra ministers in **1937**: **Prakasam**, **Gopala Reddy**, **V.V. Giri**; **Bulusu Sambamurthy** Speaker.

227.s: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 accepted separate electorates along with:
o: Universal adult franchise and linguistic provinces
Complete independence and abolition of legislatures
Reserved seats only for depressed classes in joint electorates
Weightage and a communal veto based on a three-fourths rule
227.x: The Lucknow Pact accepted separate electorates, weightage and a communal veto requiring a three-fourths rule.
227.tq: Test the additional conditions attached to a familiar constitutional arrangement.
xs: The **Lucknow Pact (1916)** accepted separate electorates with **weightage** and a **communal veto** (**three-fourths rule**) — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Weightage** = more seats than the community's population share.
Reserved seats in **joint electorates** for depressed classes came later, with the **Poona Pact**.
xa: Separate electorates for **Muslims** began with the **Indian Councils Act 1909** (Morley-Minto).
**Minto** is called the "**Father of Communal Electorate**".
The **GoI Act 1919** extended them to **Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians, Europeans**.

227.s:
Consider the following statements regarding separate electorates:
1. The Government of India Act, 1919 extended them to Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians and Europeans.
2. The Government of India Act, 1935 gave Muslims 33% of the seats in the Federal Legislature.
3. Separate electorates ended with the Government of India Act, 1935.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
227.x: Statement 1 is correct: the 1919 Act extended separate electorates to Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians and Europeans. Statement 2 is correct: the 1935 Act gave Muslims 33% of Federal Legislature seats. Statement 3 is wrong: the 1935 Act extended them further, and they continued till the Constituent Assembly. So 1 and 2 only.
227.tq: Each Act widened separate electorates; they lasted till the Constituent Assembly.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: the **1919** Act extended them to **Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians, Europeans**.
Statement 2 correct: the **1935** Act gave Muslims **33%** of seats in the **Federal Legislature**.
Statement 3 wrong: the 1935 Act **extended** them further; they **continued till the Constituent Assembly**.
xa: The 1935 Act extended them to **depressed classes (SCs), women and labour**.
The **Communal Award 1932** extended them to depressed classes; the **Poona Pact** replaced that with reserved seats.
**1909**: separate electorates for **Muslims** + **weightage**.

227.s: What was the principal change introduced by the Poona Pact in relation to the Communal Award?
o: The Muslim League was given a communal veto
Separate electorates for Muslims were abolished
Reserved seats in joint electorates replaced separate electorates for the depressed classes
Separate electorates were extended to all Europeans
227.x: The Poona Pact replaced separate electorates for the depressed classes with reserved seats in joint electorates.
227.tq: Compare the original constitutional arrangement with its replacement.
xs: The **Poona Pact** replaced the Award's separate electorates for the **depressed classes** with **reserved seats in joint electorates** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **Communal Award 1932** had extended separate electorates to the **depressed classes**.
Muslims kept their separate electorates — they continued **till the Constituent Assembly**.
xa: The **GoI Act 1935** extended them further to **depressed classes (SCs), women and labour**.
**1919**: extended to **Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians, Europeans**.
**1916 Lucknow Pact**: Congress accepted them, with **weightage**.

227.s: Which one of the following best describes the long-term political consequence of the Indian Councils Act, 1909?
o: It abolished communal representation in legislatures.
It legally institutionalised communalism and contributed to the growth of the Two-Nation Theory.
It established complete responsible government at the Centre.
It introduced universal adult franchise in British India.
227.x: The 1909 Act legally institutionalised communal representation, thereby strengthening communal politics and contributing to the emergence of the Two-Nation Theory.
227.tq: Identify the precise consequence rather than being distracted by extreme constitutional claims.
xs: The **1909** Act "**legally institutionalised communalism**" — the **seed of the Two-Nation Theory** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It gave **Muslims** separate electorates plus **weightage**; only Muslims voted for Muslim candidates.
It did not abolish communal representation — later Acts **extended** it.
xa: **Minto** = "**Father of Communal Electorate**".
The **Muslim League (1906)** came up in the run-up to 1909.
APPSC-G2 **2025**: "Which Act introduced the communal electorate?" = **Morley-Minto Reforms**.

227.s: Which one of the following Acts first introduced separate (communal) electorates for Muslims in British India?
227.x: The Indian Councils Act, 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms) introduced separate electorates for Muslims, with weightage; Minto is called the Father of Communal Electorate. The 1892 Act did not create them; the 1919 Act extended them to Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians and Europeans; the 1935 Act extended them further to depressed classes, women and labour.
227.tq: Introduced 1909 (Morley-Minto); extended 1919 and 1935.
xs: The **Indian Councils Act, 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms)** first gave **Muslims** separate electorates — so option **(2)** is correct.
It added **weightage**; **Minto** is called the **"Father of Communal Electorate"**.
The **1919** Act **extended** them to Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians, Europeans; the **1935** Act to **depressed classes, women and labour**.
xa: APPSC-G2 **2025** asked exactly this: answer **Morley-Minto Reforms**.
The **Shimla Deputation** (**1906**) under the **Aga Khan** demanded separate electorates.
The **Lucknow Pact 1916**: Congress accepted them.

227.s: Who among the following was associated with the early advocacy of keeping Muslims away from the Indian National Congress in 1887?
227.x: Sayyid Ahmad Khan, along with Raja Shiv Prasad of Bhinga, promoted an anti-Congress front in 1887.
227.tq: Link the early stage of an idea with its initial advocate.
xs: In **1887**, **Sayyid Ahmad Khan** with **Raja Shiv Prasad of Bhinga** was propped up as an **anti-Congress front** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Dufferin** used him to keep **Muslims out of Congress**.
**Iqbal** (**1930**) and **Rahmat Ali** (**1933**) came much later; **Ambedkar** wrote on Pakistan.
xa: **1906**: **Shimla Deputation** (Aga Khan) → separate electorates demanded; **League** founded.
**1930**: **Iqbal's Allahabad address** — consolidated Muslim state in the North-West.
**1940**: **Lahore Resolution** — demand formalised by **Jinnah**.

227.s: The 1930 Allahabad address of Muhammad Iqbal is associated with the proposal for:
o: Immediate withdrawal of the British from India
A federation of all princely states
A consolidated Muslim state in north-western India
227.x: In his 1930 Allahabad address, Iqbal advocated a consolidated Muslim state in the north-western region.
227.tq: Distinguish an intermediate proposal from the later formal demand for Pakistan.
xs: **Iqbal's 1930 Allahabad address** (League session) proposed a **consolidated Muslim state in the North-West** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It was a milestone of the **Two-Nation theory**, not a call for British withdrawal or a princely federation.
xa: **1933**: **Chaudhry Rahmat Ali** coined **"PAKISTAN"** in **"Now or Never"**.
**1940**: **Lahore Resolution**, adopted **23 March 1940**.
**1928-29**: Nehru Report vs Jinnah's **14 Points** — "parting of the ways".

227.s:
Arrange the following figures in chronological order according to their contributions to the separate Muslim homeland idea:
A. Muhammad Iqbal
B. M.A. Jinnah
C. Sayyid Ahmad Khan
D. Chaudhry Rahmat Ali
227.x: The sequence is Sayyid Ahmad Khan in 1887, Iqbal in 1930, Rahmat Ali in 1933 and Jinnah in 1940.
227.tq: Fix the first and last milestones, then arrange the middle dates.
xs: The order is **C, A, D, B** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Sayyid Ahmad Khan** (**1887**) → **Iqbal** (**1930**, Allahabad) → **Rahmat Ali** (**1933**, "Pakistan") → **Jinnah** (**1940**, Lahore Resolution).
xa: **1906**: **Shimla Deputation** under the **Aga Khan**.
**1946**: **Direct Action Day**.
**Jinnah** first worked for **Hindu-Muslim unity**, later championed the **Two-Nation Theory**.

227.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
227.x: The RSS was founded in 1925 at Nagpur by K.B. Hedgewar. The other pairs incorrectly interchange the dates, places or persons associated with the two organisations.
227.tq: Use the founder-date association to eliminate swapped organisational details.
xs: **RSS** — **1925** — **K.B. Hedgewar** is correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
The RSS was founded at **Nagpur** in **1925**, not **1915**.
**Rahmat Ali** coined "Pakistan" (**1933**); he has nothing to do with the Hindu Mahasabha.
xa: Hindu communal bodies asserted India as **Hindu territory** → reinforced the **Two-Nation Theory**.
**M.S. Golwalkar's** writing attacked nationalists for **embracing Muslims**.
**1920s** communal tension: **Shuddhi/Tabligh**, **Sangathan/Tanzim**.

227.s: The Shimla Deputation of 1906 is associated with which of the following developments?
o: Acceptance of complete independence by the Congress
Demand for separate electorates and the founding of the Muslim League
Replacement of reserved seats by joint electorates
227.x: The 1906 Shimla Deputation, led by Aga Khan, demanded separate electorates, and the Muslim League was founded in the same year.
227.tq: Connect a deputation with its immediate constitutional and organisational consequences.
xs: The **Shimla Deputation (1906)**, led by the **Aga Khan**, **demanded separate electorates**, and the **League was founded** the same year — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **Lahore Resolution** came in **1940**; reserved seats in joint electorates came via the **Poona Pact**.
xa: The demand was met by the **Indian Councils Act 1909**.
The **Muslim League (1906)** came up in the run-up to 1909.
**1887**: **Sayyid Ahmad Khan** used as an anti-Congress front.

227.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Development)
A. Nehru Report
B. Allahabad Address
C. Now or Never
D. Lahore Resolution

List-II (Year)
1. 1928–29
2. 1930
3. 1933
4. 1940

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
227.x: The Nehru Report belongs to 1928–29, Iqbal’s Allahabad Address to 1930, Rahmat Ali’s Now or Never to 1933, and the Lahore Resolution to 1940.
227.tq: Start from the sure year pair and eliminate codes with a misplaced milestone.
xs: Correct matching **A-1, B-2, C-3, D-4** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Nehru Report** — **1928-29**; **Iqbal's Allahabad address** — **1930**.
**"Now or Never"** — **1933**; **Lahore Resolution** — **1940**.
xa: "Now or Never" was written by **Rahmat Ali** as a **Cambridge** student.
The Lahore Resolution was adopted on **23 March 1940**.
**1937-39**: League campaign against "**Hindu Raj**".

227.s: Who raised the slogan 'Divide and Quit'?
227.x: The slogan 'Divide and Quit' was raised by M.A. Jinnah.
227.tq: Use the slogan-and-leader association while avoiding a swapped leader trap.
xs: "**Divide and Quit**" was raised by **M.A. Jinnah** (BPSC **2025** key) — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Fazlul Huq** moved the **Lahore Resolution**; **Iqbal** gave the **Allahabad address**; **Golwalkar** attacked nationalists for embracing Muslims.
xa: **Deliverance Day**: **22 Dec 1939**.
**1946** slogan: "a vote for the League was a vote for **Islam**".
Lahore session roles: **Jinnah** (president), **Sikandar Hayat Khan** (drafter), **Fazlul Huq** (mover).

227.s: The Muslim League's mass-contact campaigns alleged that the Congress ministries were establishing:
227.x: The League's campaigns alleged that Muslims were being subjected to 'Hindu Raj' under the Congress ministries.
227.tq: Identify the exact political slogan used in propaganda.
xs: The League's mass-contact campaigns alleged "**Hindu Raj**" under Congress ministries — so option **(3)** is correct.
The campaign ran in **1937-39**, backed by reports alleging cruelties to Muslims.
xa: Reports: **Pirpur (1938)**, **Sharif** (Bihar, **1939**), **Fazlul Huq's** "**Muslim Sufferings under Congress Rule**" (**1939**).
**Deliverance Day** (**22 Dec 1939**) celebrated the ministries' resignation.
**1946** slogan: "a vote for the League was a vote for **Islam**".

227.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Muslim Sufferings under Congress Rule — Fazlul Huq
Pirpur Report — Raja Syed Mohammad Mehdi of Pirpur
227.x: Fazlul Huq authored Muslim Sufferings under Congress Rule. The Pirpur Report was authored by Raja Syed Mohammad Mehdi of Pirpur.
227.tq: Find the swapped author in a report-author list.
xs: The wrong pair is **Pirpur Report — Fazlul Huq** — so option **(4)** is the answer.
The **Pirpur Report** (**1938**) was by **Raja Syed Mohammad Mehdi of Pirpur**.
**Fazlul Huq** wrote "**Muslim Sufferings under Congress Rule**" (**1939**); the **Sharif Report** was by **S.M. Sharif** (Bihar).
xa: Fazlul Huq also **moved** the **Lahore Resolution** (**1940**).
All three reports alleged **cruelties to Muslims** in Congress-ruled provinces.
They fed the **"Hindu Raj"** campaign.

227.s: The Muslim League observed 'Deliverance Day' on 22 December 1939 to celebrate:
o: The adoption of the Lahore Resolution
The resignation of the Congress provincial ministries
The announcement of the Communal Award
The publication of the Pirpur Report
227.x: Deliverance Day ('Day of Deliverance and Thanksgiving'), 22 December 1939, celebrated the resignation of the Congress ministries. The Lahore Resolution came in March 1940, the Communal Award in 1932 and the Pirpur Report in 1938.
227.tq: Deliverance Day = 22 Dec 1939 = Congress ministries resign.
xs: **Deliverance Day** (**22 Dec 1939**) celebrated the **resignation of the Congress ministries** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Full name: "**Day of Deliverance and Thanksgiving**".
The **Lahore Resolution** came in **March 1940**, the **Communal Award** in **1932**, the **Pirpur Report** in **1938**.
xa: It capped the **1937-39** campaign against "**Hindu Raj**".
**Fazlul Huq's** report "Muslim Sufferings under Congress Rule" also came in **1939**.
"**Divide and Quit**" was Jinnah's later slogan.

227.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Lahore Resolution:
1. It was adopted on 23 March 1940.
2. It soon came to be called the Pakistan Resolution.
3. It was moved by Sikandar Hayat Khan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
227.x: Statement 1 is correct: it was adopted on 23 March 1940. Statement 2 is correct: it was soon called the Pakistan Resolution. Statement 3 is wrong: Sikandar Hayat Khan drafted it; A.K. Fazlul Huq moved it (Jinnah presided). So 1 and 2 only.
227.tq: Lahore 1940: Jinnah presided, Sikandar drafted, Fazlul Huq moved.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: adopted on **23 March 1940**.
Statement 2 correct: it was soon called the **"Pakistan Resolution"**.
Statement 3 wrong: **Sikandar Hayat Khan drafted** it; **A.K. Fazlul Huq moved** it.
xa: **Jinnah** was the session president.
JPSC **2016** key named **Sikandar Hayat Khan** as drafter.
The **Two-Nation Theory** was formally set out at this session.

227.s: Who coined the word 'Pakistan' in 1933?
227.x: Chaudhry Rahmat Ali coined the word 'Pakistan' in 1933.
227.tq: Separate the person who coined the name from those who later popularised or formalised the demand.
xs: **Chaudhry Rahmat Ali** coined **"PAKISTAN"** in **1933** — so option **(2)** is correct (MPPSC **2023**, BPSC **2017**).
He wrote it in the pamphlet **"Now or Never"** as a **Cambridge** student.
**Iqbal** proposed the North-West Muslim state (**1930**); **Jinnah** formalised the demand (**1940**); **Fazlul Huq** moved the resolution.
xa: Acronym: **P**unjab + **A**fghan (NWFP) + **K**ashmir + **S**indh + Baluchi**stan**.
The **Lahore Resolution** (**23 March 1940**) soon became the "Pakistan Resolution".
**Ambedkar** wrote **Pakistan or the Partition of India**.

227.s: The word 'Pakistan' was coined in which pamphlet?
o: Pakistan or the Partition of India
227.x: Rahmat Ali coined the word 'Pakistan' in the pamphlet Now or Never.
227.tq: Match a political term with its original pamphlet.
xs: "Pakistan" was coined in **Rahmat Ali's** pamphlet **"Now or Never"** (**1933**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Pakistan or the Partition of India** is by **B.R. Ambedkar**; **The Indian Musalmans** by **W.W. Hunter**; **The Man Who Divided India** by **Rafiq Zakaria**.
xa: Rahmat Ali wrote it as a **Cambridge** student.
Acronym: **Punjab, Afghan (NWFP), Kashmir, Sindh, Baluchistan**.
Asked in MPPSC **2023** and BPSC **2017**.

227.s: Which of the following combinations correctly represents the elements used in the acronym 'Pakistan'?
o: Punjab, Afghan, Kashmir, Sindh and Baluchistan
Punjab, Assam, Kashmir, Sindh and Bengal
Peshawar, Afghan, Karachi, Sindh and Bengal
Punjab, Afghanistan, Khyber, Sindh and Bengal
227.x: The acronym was explained through Punjab, Afghan or NWFP, Kashmir, Sindh and Baluchistan.
227.tq: Start from the sure components of a named acronym.
xs: "PAKISTAN" = **Punjab + Afghan (NWFP) + Kashmir + Sindh + Baluchistan** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Bengal** and **Assam** are not part of the acronym.
xa: Coined by **Chaudhry Rahmat Ali** in **1933** in "**Now or Never**".
**Iqbal's** **1930** address sought a consolidated Muslim state in the **North-West**.
The **Lahore Resolution** of **1940** demanded states in **Muslim-majority areas**.

227.s: The statement 'Muslims, if contented and satisfied, would become the greatest bulwark of British power' is associated with:
227.x: The quotation appears in W.W. Hunter's The Indian Musalmans, published in 1871.
227.tq: Identify the author of a distinctive quotation rather than its subject.
xs: The "**greatest bulwark of British power**" remark is by **W.W. Hunter** (BPSC **2017**) — so option **(3)** is correct.
It appears in **The Indian Musalmans** (**1871**).
xa: **Rafiq Zakaria** wrote **The Man Who Divided India**.
**B.R. Ambedkar** wrote **Pakistan or the Partition of India**.
**Rahmat Ali** wrote "**Now or Never**".

227.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Now or Never — Rahmat Ali
2. Pakistan or the Partition of India — B.R. Ambedkar
3. The Man Who Divided India — Rafiq Zakaria
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
227.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. Rahmat Ali wrote Now or Never, Ambedkar wrote Pakistan or the Partition of India, and Rafiq Zakaria wrote The Man Who Divided India.
227.tq: Confirm several author-work pairs through coded options.
xs: **All three** pairs are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
"**Now or Never**" — **Rahmat Ali**; **Pakistan or the Partition of India** — **B.R. Ambedkar**; **The Man Who Divided India** — **Rafiq Zakaria**.
xa: **The Indian Musalmans** (**1871**) — **W.W. Hunter**.
"Now or Never" (**1933**) coined the word **"PAKISTAN"**.
Hunter: Muslims, if contented, would be the "**greatest bulwark of British power**".

227.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding interpretations of the Partition of India:

List-I (View)
 a. Imperialist view
 b. Nationalist view
 c. Marxist view

List-II (Interpretation)
 i. Partition resulted from an elite deal
 ii. Partition was inevitable
 iii. Partition was encouraged by divide and rule and the Muslim League's intransigence

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
227.x: The imperialist interpretation regards Partition as inevitable; the nationalist interpretation emphasises divide and rule and League intransigence; the Marxist interpretation views it as an elite deal.
227.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes that reverse the three interpretations.
xs: Correct matching **a–ii, b–iii, c–i** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Imperialist** — Partition **inevitable**; **Nationalist** — **divide and rule** + **League intransigence**.
**Marxist** — an **elite deal**.
xa: Separate electorates were the **seed of the Two-Nation Theory and Partition**.
**Rafiq Zakaria** wrote **The Man Who Divided India**.
**1946**: **Direct Action Day**.

227.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding the Dravidian political response to the demand for Pakistan?
o: Erode Conference, 1938 — Dravida Nadu was demanded in reply to Jinnah's Pakistan demand
Salem Conference, 1940 — Dravida Nadu was demanded in reply to Jinnah's Pakistan demand
Salem Conference, 1938 — Periyar demanded Dravidistan in reply to Jinnah's Pakistan demand
Erode Conference, 1940 — Periyar demanded Dravidistan in reply to Jinnah's Pakistan demand
227.x: At the Erode Conference in 1940, Periyar demanded Dravidistan in response to Jinnah's demand for Pakistan.
227.tq: Discriminate between the similar conference names, years and political demands.
xs: At the **Erode Conference (1940)**, **Periyar** demanded **Dravidistan** in reply to Jinnah's Pakistan demand — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **Salem Conference** was in **1938** and sought **Dravida Nadu** — before the Pakistan demand.
xa: The **Lahore Resolution** came in **March 1940**.
**Rahmat Ali** coined "Pakistan" in **1933**.
⚠ **Salem 1938** = Dravida Nadu; **Erode 1940** = Dravidistan.

228.s:
Consider the following statements about Gandhi's early life:
1. He studied at Samaldas College, Bhavnagar.
2. He studied law in London at the Inner Temple.
3. He was born at Rajkot.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
228.x: Statement 1 is correct: he studied at Samaldas College, Bhavnagar. Statement 2 is correct: he studied law at the Inner Temple, London (1888-1891). Statement 3 is wrong: he was born at Porbandar on 2 October 1869; Rajkot was where he later practised. So 1 and 2 only.
228.tq: Born Porbandar; practised Rajkot and Bombay; law at the Inner Temple.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: he studied at **Samaldas College, Bhavnagar**.
Statement 2 correct: he studied law in **London** (**1888-1891**) at the **Inner Temple**.
Statement 3 wrong: he was born at **Porbandar** on **2 October 1869**; **Rajkot** was where he later practised.
xa: He was called to the Bar in **1891**; his practice in **Rajkot and Bombay** did not succeed.
Father **Karamchand** was **Diwan of Porbandar**; mother **Putali Bai**.
In **1893** he went to South Africa for **Dada Abdullah's** case.

228.s:
Which of the following statements about Gandhi’s early professional life is correct?
1. His practice in Rajkot and Bombay did not succeed.
2. He went to South Africa in 1893 for Dada Abdullah’s case.
3. His father Karamchand was the Diwan of Porbandar.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
228.x: All three statements are correct. Gandhi’s early practice in Rajkot and Bombay was unsuccessful, he went to South Africa in 1893 for Dada Abdullah’s case, and Karamchand Gandhi was Diwan of Porbandar.
228.tq: Combine career, South African assignment and family-office facts in one coded question.
xs: **All three** statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
His practice in **Rajkot and Bombay** did not succeed.
He went to South Africa in **1893** for **Dada Abdullah's** case.
His father **Karamchand** was the **Diwan of Porbandar**.
xa: On **7 June 1893** he was thrown out of a first-class compartment at **Pietermaritzburg**.
**1894**: **Natal Indian Congress** founded.
Mother: **Putali Bai**.

228.s:
Consider the following statements about Gandhi's South African phase:
1. The Natal Indian Congress was founded in 1894.
2. Gandhi organised the Indian Ambulance Corps during the Boer War of 1899.
3. Gandhi underwent his first jail term in 1913.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
228.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Natal Indian Congress was founded in 1894. Statement 2 is correct: the Indian Ambulance Corps served in the Boer War (1899). Statement 3 is wrong: his first jail term was in 1908, after the burning of registration certificates; 1913 was the Great March. So 1 and 2 only.
228.tq: 1894 NIC, 1899 Boer War, 1906 first satyagraha, 1908 first jail, 1913 Great March, 1914 Relief Act.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: the **Natal Indian Congress** was founded in **1894**.
Statement 2 correct: the **Indian Ambulance Corps** served in the **Boer War** (**1899**).
Statement 3 wrong: his first jail term was in **1908**; **1913** was the **Great March**.
xa: **1906**: first satyagraha against the **Black Act** (Transvaal); **Zulu Rebellion** stretcher-bearers.
**1907-08**: burning of **registration certificates**.
**1914**: **Indian Relief Act**; Gandhi left for India.

228.s: What happened to Gandhi at Pietermaritzburg station on 7 June 1893?
o: He formed the Natal Indian Congress.
He was arrested for burning registration certificates.
He was thrown out of a first-class railway compartment.
He delivered his first public speech in South Africa.
228.x: On 7 June 1893, Gandhi was thrown out of a first-class compartment at Pietermaritzburg station.
228.tq: Link a precise date with the event that made the railway incident historically significant.
xs: On **7 June 1893** Gandhi was **thrown out of a first-class compartment** at **Pietermaritzburg** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **Natal Indian Congress** came in **1894**; burning of certificates in **1907-08**.
xa: AP Assembly Speaker **Ch. Ayyanna Patrudu** visited **Pietermaritzburg station** and the Gandhi Memorial in **KwaZulu-Natal** (**14 Sep 2026**).
He had come in **1893** for **Dada Abdullah's** case.
South Africa phase: **1893-1914**.

228.s: The first satyagraha in South Africa in 1906 was launched against which measure?
o: The Asiatic Registration Ordinance, known as the Black Act
228.x: The first South African satyagraha in 1906 opposed the Asiatic Registration Ordinance, called the Black Act, in the Transvaal.
228.tq: Distinguish the first satyagraha’s immediate cause from the later 1913 demands.
xs: The first satyagraha (**1906**) opposed the **Asiatic Registration Ordinance** — the "**Black Act**" — in **Transvaal** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **£3 poll tax** and invalidation of **non-Christian marriages** were the targets of the **1913 Great March**.
The **Indian Relief Act** (**1914**) was the settlement, not the target.
xa: ⚠ Trap: "Black Act" here = **Asiatic Registration Ordinance, 1906**.
**1907-08**: burning of registration certificates; first jail term **1908**.
South Africa = the **laboratory** of satyagraha.

228.s:
Consider the following statements about the last phase of Gandhi's struggle in South Africa:
1. The Great March of 1913 was directed against the £3 poll tax and the invalidation of non-Christian marriages.
2. The Indian Relief Act of 1914 abolished the poll tax but did not recognise Indian marriages.
3. Miners and plantation workers joined the Great March.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
228.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: the Great March of 1913 opposed the £3 poll tax and the invalidation of non-Christian marriages, and miners and plantation workers joined it. Statement 2 is wrong: the Indian Relief Act of 1914 both abolished the poll tax and recognised Indian marriages. So A leaves out 2, and C and D include the wrong statement 2.
228.tq: 1913 Great March -> 1914 Indian Relief Act met both demands.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — so **1 and 3 only**, option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: the **Great March** (**1913**) opposed the **£3 poll tax** and the invalidation of **non-Christian marriages**.
Statement 2 wrong: the **Indian Relief Act** (**1914**) abolished the poll tax **and** recognised Indian marriages.
Statement 3 correct: **miners** and **plantation workers** joined the Great March.
xa: First satyagraha: **1906**, against the **Asiatic Registration Ordinance** ("**Black Act**"), **Transvaal**.
Gandhi's first jail term: **1908**.
Two phases: **moderate petitioning** (**1894-1906**) and **satyagraha** (**1906-14**).

228.s: Which of the following is associated with the Bhagavad Gita in Gandhi’s system of influences?
o: Passive resistance to the Asiatic Registration Ordinance
The right to break unjust laws
228.x: Gandhi associated the Bhagavad Gita with Nishkama karma, or action without attachment to the fruits of action.
228.tq: Identify the exact concept linked to a canonical source.
xs: The **Bhagavad Gita** gave Gandhi **Nishkama karma** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Sarvodaya** came from **Ruskin's Unto This Last**; the right to break unjust laws from **Thoreau**.
xa: **Anasakti Yoga** = Gandhi's **Gujarati** rendering of the **Bhagavad Gita** with commentary.
Other texts: **Bible (Sermon on the Mount)**, **Quran**.
**Jainism** gave the **five vows**.

228.s: The five vows associated with Jain influence on Gandhian thought include
o: ahimsa, yajna, dana, moksha and tapas
satya, swadeshi, swaraj, sarvodaya and strike
aparigraha, class struggle, revolution, equality and atheism
ahimsa, satya, asteya, aparigraha and brahmacharya
228.x: The five vows are ahimsa, satya, asteya, aparigraha and brahmacharya. The first four are associated with Parshvanatha and brahmacharya was added by Mahavira.
228.tq: Recall a complete named list without substituting related Gandhian terms.
xs: The five vows are **ahimsa, satya, asteya, aparigraha and brahmacharya** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Four** come from **Parshvanatha**; **brahmacharya** was added by **Mahavira**.
xa: ⚠ Trap: Jain vows = **four** from Parshvanatha + **brahmacharya** from Mahavira.
Gandhi's pillars: **ahimsa**, **satya**, **asteya**, **aparigraha**, **sarvodaya**.
The **Gita** gave him **Nishkama karma**.

228.s:
Consider the following statements about influences on Gandhi:
1. John Ruskin's Unto This Last inspired his ideas of the dignity of labour and Sarvodaya.
2. H.D. Thoreau's Civil Disobedience gave him the idea of the right to break unjust laws.
3. Leo Tolstoy was one of the thinkers who influenced him.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
228.x: All three are correct: Ruskin's Unto This Last gave dignity of labour and Sarvodaya; Thoreau's Civil Disobedience gave the right to break unjust laws; and Ruskin, Thoreau and Tolstoy all influenced Gandhi (UPPSC 2013 key: 'All the above'). So options 1 only, 1 and 2 only, and 2 and 3 only are incomplete.
228.tq: Ruskin = labour/Sarvodaya; Thoreau = unjust laws; Tolstoy also an influence.
xs: **All three** statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Ruskin's Unto This Last** → **dignity of labour** and **Sarvodaya**.
**Thoreau's Civil Disobedience** → **right to break unjust laws**.
**Ruskin, Thoreau and Tolstoy** all influenced him (UPPSC **2013**: "**All the above**").
xa: **Tolstoy Farm** (**1910**) near **Johannesburg** bears Tolstoy's name.
The **Gita** → **Nishkama karma**.
Unto This Last was read on a train in **1904** → **Phoenix Settlement**.

228.s:
Consider the following statements about Hind Swaraj:
1. It was banned by the Bombay Government in 1910.
2. Its English translation was made by C.F. Andrews, not by Gandhi.
3. It was written in Gujarati in 1909 aboard the Kildonan Castle.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
228.x: Statement 3 is correct: Gandhi wrote Hind Swaraj in Gujarati in 1909 on the Kildonan Castle, sailing from London to South Africa. Statement 1 is correct: the Bombay Government banned it in 1910. Statement 2 is wrong: Gandhi himself translated it into English. So only 1 and 2 are correct.
228.tq: Gujarati 1909, banned 1910, English by Gandhi himself.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — so **1 and 3 only**, option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: **Hind Swaraj** was **banned** by the **Bombay Government** in **1910**.
Statement 2 wrong: Gandhi **himself translated it into English**.
Statement 3 correct: written in **Gujarati** in **1909** aboard the **Kildonan Castle** (London → South Africa).
xa: Themes: critique of **modern (Western) civilisation**, **industrialisation**, **railways**, **lawyers and doctors**.
It upheld **self-reliance**, **rural life** and **swaraj as self-rule**.
⚠ Written in **Gujarati** (**1909**), banned **1910**; English version by **Gandhi himself**.

228.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the themes of *Hind Swaraj*:
1. It advocates self-reliance and rural life.
2. It presents swaraj as self-rule.
3. It offers an unqualified endorsement of industrialisation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
228.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because *Hind Swaraj* critiques industrialisation rather than endorsing it without qualification.
228.tq: Identify the reversed comparison in the statement that turns Gandhi's criticism of industrialisation into praise.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: it advocates **self-reliance** and **rural life**.
Statement 2 correct: it presents **swaraj as self-rule**.
Statement 3 wrong: it **critiques industrialisation**, along with **modern (Western) civilisation**.
xa: It also attacks **railways** and **lawyers and doctors**.
Written **1909** in **Gujarati** aboard the **Kildonan Castle**.
Banned by the **Bombay Government** (**1910**).

228.s:
Arrange the following settlements and ashrams in chronological order of their establishment:
A. Sevagram
B. Phoenix Settlement
C. Sabarmati Ashram
D. Tolstoy Farm
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
228.x: Phoenix Settlement dates to 1904, Tolstoy Farm to 1910, Sabarmati Ashram to 1917, and Sevagram to 1936.
228.tq: Fix the earliest and latest settlements first, then place the two middle dates.
xs: The order is **B, D, C, A** — so option **(1)** is correct.

228.s: Who among the following worked at Sabarmati Satyagraha Ashram?
228.x: Potti Sriramulu worked at Sabarmati Satyagraha Ashram.
228.tq: Distinguish an Indian associate of an ashram from foreign intellectual influences.
xs: **Potti Sriramulu** worked at **Sabarmati** (APHQ **2017**) — so option **(1)** is correct.
