235.tq: First woman INC President = Besant 1917; first Indian woman = Sarojini 1925
xs: **Annie Besant** — **first woman INC President**, **1917** — option **(2)**.
In **1917** the **Home Rule flag** (**5** red, **4** green stripes) was hoisted at **Coimbatore**.
xa: That flag item was in the news (TH **19 Mar 2026**).
In **1920** the NCM was launched (Calcutta), followed by the **Nagpur session, Dec 1920**.

235.s: Pingali Venkayya was born at which place?
235.x: Pingali Venkayya was born at Bhatlapenumarru.
235.tq: Test the birthplace directly and distinguish it from other Andhra locations associated with the movement.
xs: **Bhatlapenumarru** — option **(4)**.
The PM recalled this on his **150th birth anniversary** (**3 Aug 2026**).
xa: His flag design had the **charkha**.
Gandhi endorsed it at the **1921 Vijayawada session**.

235.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Leader)
 a. Konda Venkatappaiah
 b. Duggirala
 c. Prakasam
 d. Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao

List-II (Title)
 i. Andhra Kesari
 ii. Desoddharaka
 iii. Desabhakta
 iv. Andhra Ratna

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
235.x: Konda Venkatappaiah was known as Desabhakta, Duggirala as Andhra Ratna, Prakasam as Andhra Kesari, and Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao as Desoddharaka.
235.tq: Start from the sure leader–title pair and verify the remaining pairs before choosing the code.
xs: **a–iii, b–iv, c–i, d–ii** — option **(1)**.
**Konda Venkatappaiah** — **Desabhakta**; **Duggirala** — **Andhra Ratna**.
**Prakasam** — **Andhra Kesari**; **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** — **Desoddharaka**.
xa: These were "**Glorious decade**" (**1921-31**) leaders.
Duggirala founded the **Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi** at Chirala.

236.s: The Nationalist Party formed in the Central Legislative Assembly in 1924 consisted principally of
o: Swarajists, Jinnah’s Independents and Malaviya’s group
Congress socialists, revolutionaries and trade unions
Swarajists, British officials and Simon Commission members
236.x: The Nationalist Party brought together the Swarajists, Jinnah’s Independents and Malaviya’s group. It had about 70 members.
236.tq: Use the composition of the legislative bloc to distinguish it from other Congress groupings.
xs: **Swarajists**, **Jinnah's Independents** and **Malaviya's group** — option **(1)**.
It was the **Nationalist Party (1924)**, about **70** members.
xa: It **outvoted the government** and blocked the **Finance Bill**.
**Malaviya** later joined the **Responsivists**.

236.s: Who became the first elected Indian President of the Legislative Assembly in 1925?
236.x: Vithalbhai Patel became the first elected Indian President of the Legislative Assembly in 1925.
236.tq: Distinguish the first office-holder from the first elected Indian holder of the office.
xs: **Vithalbhai Patel** — option **(3)**.
Elected (first Indian) **Speaker/President** of the Central Legislative Assembly in **1925**.
xa: He was a pro-changer (Swarajist).
The Swarajists did poorly in **1926**.

236.s:
Consider the following statements about the Swarajists in the Central Legislative Assembly:
1. Their demand for a review of the 1919 Act led to the Muddiman Committee (1924).
2. They supported the Public Safety Bill of 1928.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
236.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Swarajist demand for reviewing the Government of India Act 1919 led to the Muddiman Committee in 1924. Statement 2 is wrong: the Swarajists opposed the Public Safety Bill of 1928. So 1 only (A).
236.tq: Muddiman 1924 = review of 1919 Act; Public Safety Bill 1928 opposed
xs: Only statement **1** — option **(1)**.
1 correct: the demand for review of the **1919 Act** led to the **Muddiman Committee (1924)**.
2 wrong: the Swarajists **opposed** the **Public Safety Bill (1928)**.
xa: They walked out of the councils in **1930** after **Lahore**.
The **Nationalist Party** blocked the **Finance Bill**.

236.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Andhra Swarajist office)
a. President
b. Secretary
c. Treasurer
d. Additional associated leader

List-II (Person)
i. Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao
 ii. V. Ramadas
 iii. Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao
 iv. Unnava Lakshminarayana

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
236.x: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao was President, Unnava Lakshminarayana Secretary, Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao Treasurer and V. Ramadas an additional associated leader.
236.tq: Start with the office-holder pairs and use the remaining person as the elimination pair.
xs: **a–iii, b–iv, c–i, d–ii** — option **(1)**.
President **Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao**; secretary **Unnava Lakshminarayana**; treasurer **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao**; **V. Ramadas** also in the branch.
xa: ⚠ **Kaleswara Rao** (president) - **Unnava** (secretary) - **Gadicherla** (treasurer).
Madras council: **B. Venkataratnam, P. Anjaneyulu, P.V. Venkatapathiraju**.

236.s: At which Congress session, held in Andhra in 1923, did local women serve as executive members and volunteers?
236.x: The 1923 Congress session was held at Kakinada in Andhra, where local women served as executive members and volunteers. Gaya (1922) was in Bihar, Belgaum (1924) in Karnataka and Nagpur (1920) in central India.
xs: Local women served as **executive members and volunteers**.
**Belgaum 1924** is known instead as the only session presided by **Gandhi**.
xa: The **Nationalist Party** formed in **1924**.
Women in Andhra also did **picketing and prohibition** work.

236.s: The Responsivists within the Swarajist movement favoured
o: the immediate abolition of the Congress
exclusive emphasis on spinning and khadi
complete withdrawal from all legislative activity
236.x: The Responsivists favoured cooperation with the government. Lajpat Rai, Malaviya and N.C. Kelkar were associated with this tendency.
236.tq: Test the precise meaning of a faction label instead of relying on its general political impression.
xs: **Co-operation with the government** — option **(3)**.
Responsivists: **Lajpat Rai, Malaviya, N.C. Kelkar**.
xa: They emerged after C.R. Das's death in **June 1925** split the party.
The Swarajists opposed the **Public Safety Bill (1928)**.

236.s: Which one of the following was NOT a component of the constructive programme associated with the 1920s national movement?
236.x: The constructive programme included khadi and spinning, removal of untouchability, Hindu-Muslim unity, prohibition, national schools and village panchayats. Expansion of separate electorates was not part of it.
236.tq: Identify the item outside the constructive-work cluster.
xs: **Expansion of separate electorates** was not part of it — option **(1)**.
Components: **khadi and spinning**, **national schools**, **Hindu-Muslim unity**, **removal of untouchability**, prohibition, **village panchayats**.
xa: **Ponduru (Srikakulam)** khadi was famed nationally.
Women did **picketing** and **prohibition** work.

236.s: Which of the following activities was particularly associated with women’s participation in Andhra during the constructive programme?
236.x: Women in Andhra participated in picketing and prohibition work as part of the constructive programme.
236.tq: Link a social activity with the relevant regional participant group.
xs: **Picketing and prohibition work** — option **(1)**.
The **Muddiman Committee** and blocking the **Finance Bill** were Swarajist legislative actions.
xa: At the **Kakinada Congress (1923)** women served as executive members and volunteers.
**Ponduru (Srikakulam)** khadi was famous.

236.s: Which of the following correctly represents the principal difference between the Swarajists and the No-Changers?
o: Swarajists favoured council entry, whereas No-Changers emphasised constructive work.
Swarajists supported constructive work, whereas No-Changers supported council entry.
Both groups rejected council entry and constructive work alike.
Both groups favoured cooperation with the colonial government.
236.x: The Swarajists favoured entry into the councils, while the No-Changers concentrated on constructive work and continued the boycott. Both groups were reunited at Belgaum in 1924.
236.tq: Use the central contrast in policy rather than confusing the groups’ common nationalist objective.
xs: **Swarajists** favoured **council entry**; **No-Changers** emphasised **constructive work** — option **(1)**.
Option (2) reverses them.
xa: They reunited at **Belgaum 1924**.
Constructive items: **khadi**, **national schools**, **removal of untouchability**.

236.s: The Belgaum session of the Indian National Congress (1924) is notable because:
o: It was the only Congress session presided over by Mahatma Gandhi
It adopted the Purna Swaraj resolution
It approved the suspension of the Non-Cooperation Movement
It was the first session presided over by a woman
236.x: Belgaum 1924 was the only INC session presided over by Gandhi, and it reunited the Swarajists and No-Changers. Purna Swaraj was adopted at Lahore (1929); the NCM was suspended at Bardoli (1922); the first woman President was Annie Besant (1917).
xs: **Belgaum 1924** was the **only INC session presided by Gandhi** — option **(1)**.
It is the notes' **FIRST/LAST** fact for Belgaum; the other options are not linked to it in the notes.
xa: Belgaum reunited the **Swarajists** and **No-Changers**.
Council work and constructive work proved **complementary**.

237.s: The Nehru Report of 1928 was prepared by the committee of the All Parties Conference under the chairmanship of:
237.x: The committee that prepared the Nehru Report was chaired by Motilal Nehru. Jawaharlal Nehru served as its secretary.
237.tq: Distinguish the chairman from the secretary in a committee-based question.
xs: The Nehru Report committee was chaired by **Motilal Nehru** — option **(2)**.
**Jawaharlal Nehru** was its **secretary**, not chairman.
It was an **All Parties Conference** committee and asked for **dominion status**.
xa: The **Calcutta 1928** session accepted the Report with a **one-year ultimatum**.
When it lapsed, **Lahore (Dec 1929)**, under **Jawaharlal Nehru**, adopted **Purna Swaraj**.
⚠ Trap: crediting **Calcutta 1928** with Purna Swaraj is WRONG.

237.s: Who was the first to pass a Purna Swaraj resolution at the district level in Andhra Pradesh?
237.x: Bulusu Sambamurthy of East Godavari was associated with the first district-level Purna Swaraj resolution in Andhra Pradesh.
237.tq: Use the place-name clue to identify the associated Andhra leader.
xs: **Bulusu Sambamurthy** (East Godavari) passed a Purna Swaraj resolution at district level first — option **(4)**.
He got it passed at a district meeting **before Lahore**.
**Yerneni Subrahmanyam** was the only Telugu Dandi marcher; **Thota Narsayya** hoisted the flag at Machilipatnam.
xa: Sambamurthy also led the salt satyagraha at **Kakinada** (**Chollangi**).
**Lahore** passed the Purna Swaraj resolution on **31 Dec 1929**.

237.s:
With reference to the Lahore Session of the Indian National Congress held in December 1929, consider the following statements:
1. The Nehru Report had demanded Dominion Status.
2. The one-year ultimatum given to the British at the Calcutta Session of 1928 had expired.
3. The Lahore Session accepted the Nehru Report without modification.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
237.x: The Nehru Report demanded Dominion Status, and the one-year ultimatum issued at Calcutta in 1928 had expired. The Lahore Session rejected the demand for Dominion Status and adopted Purna Swaraj.
237.tq: Find the statement that reverses the decision taken at Lahore.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** — option **(1)**.
1 correct: the **Nehru Report (1928)** asked for **dominion status**.
2 correct: the **Calcutta 1928** **one-year ultimatum** had lapsed.
3 wrong: Lahore **rejected** the Nehru Report's dominion status and adopted **Purna Swaraj**.
xa: Lahore resolved that **26 January** be observed every year as **Independence Day**.
CWC was authorised to launch **Civil Disobedience**; the **RTC** was boycotted.

237.s:
Consider the following statements about the Lahore session of the Congress (December 1929):
1. It was presided over by Motilal Nehru.
2. It resolved that 26 January be observed every year as Independence Day.
3. The tricolour was hoisted on the banks of the Ravi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
237.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the Lahore session was presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru (Motilal Nehru chaired the Nehru Report committee). Statements 2 and 3 are correct: 26 January was fixed as Independence Day (first observed on 26 January 1930) and Nehru hoisted the tricolour on the banks of the Ravi. So 2 and 3 only (C); A includes the false statement 1, B misses statement 3, D includes statement 1.
237.tq: Lahore 1929 = Jawaharlal presides; Nehru Report = Motilal
xs: Statements **2 and 3** — option **(3)**.
1 wrong: Lahore was presided by **Jawaharlal Nehru**; **Motilal Nehru** chaired the Nehru Report committee.
2 correct: **26 January** to be observed as **Independence Day**.
3 correct: Nehru hoisted the tricolour on the banks of the **Ravi**.
xa: First Independence Day: **26 January 1930**.
CWC was authorised to launch **Civil Disobedience**.

237.s: Which of the following was central among Gandhi's demands addressed to Viceroy Irwin before the Dandi March?
o: Acceptance of the Nehru Report without change
Immediate convening of the Third Round Table Conference
237.x: Abolition of the salt tax was a central demand in Gandhi's eleven-point letter to Viceroy Irwin. Irwin did not accept the demands.
237.tq: Identify the policy demand directly connected with the chosen symbol of protest.
xs: **Abolition of the salt tax** was central — option **(1)**.
It was part of Gandhi's **11 demands** to **Irwin** (letter of **30 Jan 1930**); Irwin refused.
xa: The ultimatum was sent/ignored on **2 March 1930**.
Why salt: a **universal necessity** of rich and poor; the salt tax was the most visible face of colonial exploitation.

237.s:
Consider the following statements about the Dandi March:
1. Gandhi began it from Sabarmati Ashram on 12 March 1930 with 78 followers.
2. The route covered about 240 kilometres.
3. He broke the salt law at Dandi on 6 April 1930.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
237.x: Statement 1 is correct: the march began on 12 March 1930 from Sabarmati Ashram with 78 followers. Statement 3 is correct: the salt law was broken at Dandi on 6 April 1930. Statement 2 is wrong: the route was about 240 miles (385 km), not 240 km. So only 1 and 2 are correct.
237.tq: 12 March - 78 followers - 240 miles - 6 April.
xs: Only **statements 1 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: the march began from **Sabarmati Ashram** on **12 March 1930** with **78** followers.
Statement 2 is wrong: the route was about **240 miles (385 km)**, not 240 kilometres.
Statement 3 is correct: the **salt law** was broken at **Dandi** on **6 April 1930**.
xa: Gandhi's **11 demands** to Viceroy **Irwin** (letter of **30 Jan 1930**) centred on abolishing the **salt tax**.
The **only Telugu marcher** was **Yerneni Subrahmanyam** of Krishna district, who later founded an ashram at **Komaravolu**.
After Gandhi's arrest, **Abbas Tyabji** led first and **Sarojini Naidu** second.
Bose compared the Dandi march to **"Napoleon's return from Elba"**.

237.s: Who was the only Telugu marcher among Gandhi's followers in the Dandi March?
237.x: Yerneni, also written Erneni, Subrahmanyam of Krishna district was the only Telugu marcher among Gandhi's followers in the Dandi March.
237.tq: Distinguish the Telugu participant in the march from Andhra leaders associated with other activities.
xs: **Yerneni (Erneni) Subrahmanyam** of **Krishna district** — option **(3)**.
**Bulusu Sambamurthy** led Kakinada; **Thota Narsayya** hoisted the flag at Machilipatnam; **Maganti Annapurna** gave her jewellery.
xa: He later founded an ashram at **Komaravolu**.
The march had **78** followers.

237.s: Why did Gandhi choose salt as the central symbol of the Civil Disobedience Movement?
o: It was produced exclusively in Gujarat.
It was used only by the urban middle classes.
It was a universal necessity and the salt tax visibly represented colonial exploitation.
It was connected with the demand for separate electorates.
237.x: Salt was consumed by both rich and poor, and the salt tax and monopoly made it a visible symbol of colonial economic exploitation.
237.tq: Choose the option that combines the social reach and political significance of salt.
xs: Salt was a **universal necessity** and the salt tax visibly represented **colonial exploitation** — option **(3)**.
It was used by **rich and poor** alike, and the **salt tax/monopoly** was the most visible face of colonial taxation.
xa: Abolition of the salt tax was central to the **11 demands**.
The CDM was the **first mass law-breaking**.

237.s: Gandhi named which person as the first successor to lead the movement after his arrest during the Salt Satyagraha?
237.x: Abbas Tyabji was designated as Gandhi's first successor after his arrest. Sarojini Naidu was named the second successor.
237.tq: Read the sequence carefully when two leaders are both associated with succession.
xs: **Abbas Tyabji** was the first successor — option **(2)**.
**Sarojini Naidu** was second, and led the **Dharasana** raid.
xa: **Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay** led women into the Salt Satyagraha.
**Kasturba Gandhi** joined protests and was imprisoned.

237.s: Who reported the beatings at the Dharasana Salt Works to the international public?
237.x: The beatings at Dharasana were reported by Webb Miller, a United States journalist.
237.tq: Test the eyewitness separately from the political leader.
xs: **Webb Miller**, a US journalist — option **(1)**.
The beatings were at the **Dharasana Salt Works** raid led by **Sarojini Naidu**.
xa: She led it after **Abbas Tyabji**'s arrest.
Other centres: **Peshawar** (Red Shirts), **Sanikatta** (Karnataka coast).

237.s: The Khudai Khidmatgars organised their Civil Disobedience protests particularly in
237.x: The Khudai Khidmatgars, or Red Shirts, led non-violent protests in Peshawar and the North-West Frontier Province. The Qissa Khwani firing occurred there in April 1930.
237.tq: Associate the organisation with its regional field of action.
xs: **Peshawar and the NWFP** — option **(2)**.
**Khudai Khidmatgars / Red Shirts** were founded by **Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan** among Pathans.
xa: **Qissa Khwani** firing: **April 1930**.
**Garhwal Rifles** refused to fire on the Peshawar crowd (**1930**).

237.s: Who among the following was known as the ‘Frontier Gandhi’?
237.x: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan was popularly known as the ‘Frontier Gandhi’ and was associated with the Khudai Khidmatgars.
237.tq: Use direct title–person recall.
xs: **Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan** — option **(2)**.
He founded the **Khudai Khidmatgars (Red Shirts)** in the **NWFP**.
xa: **Konda Venkatappayya** was the Andhra salt satyagraha dictator.
**Qissa Khwani** firing, **April 1930**.

237.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
237.x: Babu Genu was associated with Bombay, where he was crushed by a lorry carrying foreign cloth. Dharasana was associated with Sarojini Naidu.
237.tq: Find the wrong place associated with the person.
xs: **Babu Genu — Dharasana** is wrong — option **(3)**.
Babu Genu was crushed by a lorry carrying foreign cloth in **Bombay**, **12 Dec 1930**.
**Dharasana** is linked to **Sarojini Naidu**.
xa: **Rani Gaidinliu** — Naga uprising; **Ghaffar Khan** — NWFP: both correct.
Dharasana beatings were reported by **Webb Miller**.

237.s: The Garhwal Rifles became notable during the Civil Disobedience Movement because they
o: refused to fire on the crowd at Peshawar
led the salt march at Vedaranyam
237.x: The Garhwal Rifles, associated with Chandra Singh Garhwali, refused to fire on the crowd at Peshawar in 1930.
237.tq: Identify the distinctive action rather than the unit’s location alone.
xs: They **refused to fire** on the **Peshawar** crowd — option **(2)**.
They are linked to **Chandra Singh Garhwali** (**1930**).
xa: The Peshawar protests were by the **Khudai Khidmatgars**; **Qissa Khwani** firing, **April 1930**.
**Sarojini Naidu** led the **Dharasana** raid.

237.s: Sarojini Naidu led the raid at:
237.x: Sarojini Naidu led the raid at the Dharasana Salt Works after Gandhi's arrest.
237.tq: Separate the Civil Disobedience role from the Quit India role of the same leader.
xs: **Dharasana Salt Works** — option **(2)**.
She led it after **Abbas Tyabji**'s arrest.
**Gowalia Tank** is linked to **Aruna Asaf Ali** (**1942**).
xa: Beatings were reported by **Webb Miller**.
Sarojini Naidu was the first Indian woman INC president (**Kanpur 1925**).

237.s: Which one of the following statements regarding women's participation in the Civil Disobedience Movement is correct?
o: Women participated only after the withdrawal of the movement in 1934.
Women joined in massive numbers, including picketing liquor and foreign-cloth shops.
Women participated only in underground revolutionary activity.
Women were excluded from protests against colonial taxes.
237.x: The Civil Disobedience Movement marked the first occasion on which women participated in massive numbers. Their activities included picketing liquor shops and shops selling foreign cloth.
237.tq: Select the option that captures both the scale and forms of participation.
xs: Women joined **in massive numbers**, picketing **liquor and foreign-cloth shops** — option **(2)**.
The CDM was the **first time** women joined on this scale.
xa: **"Kattera Udyamam"** (scissors movement) raised women's participation in Andhra.
**Paturi Balasaraswatamma** was the first woman arrested in **Nellore**.

237.s: Who was the first woman arrested in Nellore in connection with the national movement?
237.x: Paturi Balasaraswatamma was the first woman arrested in Nellore in connection with the national movement.
237.tq: Match the specific Andhra district with its associated woman activist.
xs: **Paturi Balasaraswatamma** — option **(2)**.
**Maganti Annapurna** gave her jewellery; **Palakojeti Shyamalamba** was from E. Godavari.
xa: Women jailed: **Bharati Devi Ranga**, **Digumarti Janakamma**, **Khammampati Manikyamba** (with a six-month-old baby).
**Duvvuri Subbamma** (East Godavari) was jailed in the CDM.

237.s: The ‘Kattera Udyamam’ in Andhra was associated with
o: the formation of the Red Shirts
increased participation of women in the Salt Satyagraha
a campaign against the Cunningham Circular
the boycott of the Round Table Conference
237.x: The ‘Kattera Udyamam’, or scissors movement, helped raise women’s participation in the Andhra movement.
237.tq: Distinguish a local term by the social participation it promoted.
xs: **"Kattera Udyamam"** (scissors movement) **raised women's participation** — option **(2)**.
The **Red Shirts** were Ghaffar Khan's; the **Cunningham Circular** protests were in **Assam**.
xa: CDM was the first time women joined **in massive numbers**.
**Maganti Annapurna** gave all her jewellery.

237.s: The first Indian woman to preside over the Indian National Congress was:
237.x: Sarojini Naidu was the first Indian woman President of the Congress. She presided over the Kanpur session in 1925.
237.tq: Separate nationality from gender by comparing the first woman president with the first Indian woman president.
xs: **Sarojini Naidu at Kanpur in 1925** — option **(4)**.
She was the **first Indian woman INC president**, and also led the **Dharasana** raid.
xa: She was Gandhi's **second** successor, after **Abbas Tyabji**.
⚠ **Aruna Asaf Ali** = **Quit India (1942)**.

237.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay - led women into the Salt Satyagraha
Aruna Asaf Ali - led the Dharasana raid
Sarojini Naidu - hoisted the flag at Gowalia Tank in 1942
Kasturba Gandhi - first Indian woman President of the INC
237.x: Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay led women into the Salt Satyagraha. Aruna Asaf Ali hoisted the flag at Gowalia Tank in the Quit India Movement (1942); Sarojini Naidu led the Dharasana raid and was the first Indian woman INC President (Kanpur 1925); Kasturba Gandhi joined protests and was imprisoned.
237.tq: Gowalia Tank = Aruna; Dharasana = Sarojini
xs: **Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay** led women into the Salt Satyagraha — option **(1)**.
**Aruna Asaf Ali** hoisted the flag at **Gowalia Tank (1942)**; **Sarojini Naidu** led **Dharasana** and presided **Kanpur 1925**.
**Kasturba Gandhi** joined protests and was imprisoned.
xa: These pairings are an APPSC **2025** key.
**Duvvuri Subbamma** was the Andhra woman jailed in the CDM.

237.s: Who was designated as the dictator of the Andhra Salt Satyagraha?
237.x: Konda Venkatappayya was the dictator of the Andhra Salt Satyagraha and had met Gandhi at Jambusar.
237.tq: Distinguish the overall dictator from district-level leaders.
xs: **Konda Venkatappayya** — option **(2)**.
He met Gandhi at **Jambusar**.
**Pattabhi Sitaramayya** proposed the district camps; **Kaleswara Rao** led Machilipatnam; **Prakasam** led Madras/Devarampadu.
xa: Each district had its own dictator, war council and **sibiram**.
Konda Venkatappayya also led in **Guntur villages** with **Unnava Lakshminarayana**.

237.s:
Consider the following statements about Salt Satyagraha camps in Andhra:
1. Seethanagaram Ashram, associated with Brahmajosyula Subrahmanyam, was called the 'Andhra Dandi'.
2. Devarampadu, called the 'Dakshina Dandi', had its camp at Tanguturi Prakasam's house.
3. Seethanagaram Ashram was the camp of West Godavari district.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
237.x: Statement 1 is correct: Seethanagaram Ashram (Brahmajosyula Subrahmanyam) was the 'Andhra Dandi'. Statement 2 is correct: Devarampadu was the 'Dakshina Dandi' with its camp at Prakasam's house. Statement 3 is wrong: Seethanagaram was the East Godavari camp; West Godavari's was Eluru National School. So 1 and 2 only (B); A misses statement 2, C and D include the false statement 3.
237.tq: Andhra Dandi = Seethanagaram (E. Godavari); Dakshina Dandi = Devarampadu (Prakasam).
xs: Statements **1 and 2** — option **(2)**.
1 correct: **Seethanagaram Ashram** (**Brahmajosyula Subrahmanyam**) = **"Andhra Dandi"**.
2 correct: **Devarampadu** = **"Dakshina Dandi"**, camp at **Tanguturi Prakasam's** house.
3 wrong: Seethanagaram was the **East Godavari** camp; West Godavari's was **Eluru National School**.
xa: Vizag's camp: **Vizianagaram**; Krishna's: **Andhraratna Bhavan** and **Machilipatnam**.
⚠ **"Mecca"** = Machilipatnam.

237.s: Who conducted the first Salt Satyagraha at Machilipatnam?
237.x: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao conducted the first Salt Satyagraha at Machilipatnam. Pattabhi Sitaramayya called Machilipatnam his ‘Mecca’.
237.tq: Distinguish the first local satyagrahi from associated leaders.
xs: **Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao** — option **(2)**.
Pattabhi called Machilipatnam his **"Mecca"**.
**Bulusu Sambamurthy** = Kakinada; **Oruganti Venkatasubbayya** = Mylapadu; **Kalluri Subbarao** = Bellary.
xa: **Thota Narsayya ("Jenda Narsayya")** hoisted the flag at Machilipatnam.
Krishna district camps: **Andhraratna Bhavan** and **Machilipatnam**.

237.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
237.x: Kakinada was associated with Bulusu Sambamurthy at Chollangi. Oruganti Venkatasubbayya was associated with Mylapadu in Nellore.
237.tq: Find the swapped leader–centre pair.
xs: **Kakinada — Oruganti Venkatasubbayya** is wrong — option **(1)**.
Kakinada = **Bulusu Sambamurthy** at **Chollangi**; Oruganti made salt at **Mylapadu** (Nellore), **11 April 1930**.
**Guntur villages — Unnava**, **Bellary — Kalluri Subbarao**, **Vizag — Tenneti Viswanatham** are correct.
xa: Mylapadu was with **Bezawada Gopal Reddy**.
Bellary was chosen as **Rayalaseema had no coast**.

237.s: Why did the Salt Satyagraha in Rayalaseema take place at Bellary under Kalluri Subbarao?
o: The Madras Government permitted salt manufacture there
Bellary was the headquarters of the Congress
The Andhra Salt Committee was based there
237.x: Rayalaseema had no coast, so Kalluri Subbarao led the activity at Bellary instead of a coastal salt-making centre.
237.tq: Apply the geographical condition to explain the choice of centre.
xs: **Rayalaseema had no coast** — option **(3)**.
So **Kalluri Subbarao** led it at **Bellary**.
xa: Coastal centres: **Machilipatnam**, **Kakinada**, **Mylapadu**, **Devarampadu**.
**Pedaganjam-Chinaganjam** was a famous salt coast.

237.s: Who wrote the patriotic song ‘Bharata Swarajya Yuddham’?
237.x: Jagganna Sastri wrote ‘Bharata Swarajya Yuddham’.
237.tq: Match the literary work with its author.
xs: **Jagganna Sastri** — option **(2)**.
**Adavi Bapiraju** wrote songs in jail; **Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary** wrote "**Veeragandhamu**".
xa: Veeragandhamu — APPSC **2012** key: **CDM**.
⚠ An APPSC **2019** question tied Veeragandhamu to NCM.

237.s: The patriotic song 'Veeragandhamu Techhinaramu... Veerulevvaro Telpudee' by Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary is associated with which movement?
237.x: The APPSC 2012 key ties the song to the Civil Disobedience Movement. Linking it to the NCM (as an APPSC 2019 question did) is the known trap; Quit India and Vandemataram are unrelated to this song.
237.tq: Veeragandhamu = CDM, not NCM
xs: **Civil Disobedience Movement** — option **(2)** (APPSC **2012** key).
⚠ An APPSC **2019** question tied it to NCM — a known trap.
xa: Author: **Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary**.
Other CDM songs: **Bharata Swarajya Yuddham** (**Jagganna Sastri**); jail songs by **Adavi Bapiraju**.

237.s: Who were the mediators associated with the Gandhi-Irwin Pact?
o: Madan Mohan Malaviya and Jawaharlal Nehru
Tej Bahadur Sapru and M.R. Jayakar
237.x: Tej Bahadur Sapru and M.R. Jayakar acted as mediators in the negotiations leading to the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.
237.tq: Test the mediator–event association directly.
xs: **Tej Bahadur Sapru and M.R. Jayakar** — option **(3)**.
**V.S. Srinivasa Sastri** also mediated.
xa: Signed **5 March 1931** (**Delhi Pact**).
⚠ Dating it to March **1930** is WRONG.

237.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Gandhi-Irwin Pact:
1. Gandhi agreed to suspend the Civil Disobedience Movement.
2. Gandhi agreed to attend the Second Round Table Conference.
3. Irwin agreed to commute the death sentences of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
237.x: Gandhi agreed to suspend the Civil Disobedience Movement and attend the Second Round Table Conference. Irwin did not agree to commute the death sentences of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru.
237.tq: Separate agreed terms from the specifically refused demand.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** — option **(3)**.
Gandhi agreed to **suspend CDM** and **attend the 2nd RTC**.
3 wrong: Irwin **refused** to commute the sentences of **Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Rajguru**.
xa: Irwin also refused a **public inquiry** into police excesses.
Irwin agreed: release of non-violent prisoners; coastal villagers may make **salt for own use**.

237.s: The Karachi Session of the Indian National Congress held in March 1931 was presided over by
237.x: Vallabhbhai Patel presided over the Karachi Session of the Congress in March 1931.
237.tq: Link the session with its presiding president.
xs: **Vallabhbhai Patel** — option **(3)**.
The **Karachi session (March 1931)** endorsed the pact.
xa: It passed resolutions on **Fundamental Rights and National Economic Programme**.
Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Rajguru were executed on **23 Mar 1931**.

237.s:
Which of the following resolutions were passed at the Karachi Session of the Congress in March 1931?
1. Resolution on Fundamental Rights
2. Resolution on the National Economic Programme
3. Resolution accepting separate electorates for the depressed classes
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
237.x: The Karachi Session passed resolutions on Fundamental Rights and the National Economic Programme. The National Economic Programme was drafted by Jawaharlal Nehru; separate electorates for the depressed classes were not accepted there.
237.tq: Reject the statement importing a later communal-electorate issue into the Karachi resolutions.
xs: Karachi passed **Fundamental Rights** and **National Economic Programme** resolutions, drafted by **Jawaharlal Nehru**.
The notes record no separate-electorates resolution at Karachi.
xa: President: **Vallabhbhai Patel**.
Criticism: no commutation for **Bhagat Singh**; youth disillusioned.

237.s:
Which of the following was a term agreed to by Lord Irwin under the Gandhi-Irwin Pact?
1. Release of non-violent political prisoners
2. Remission of fines and return of unsold lands
3. Permission for salt-making in coastal villages for personal use
4. Commutation of the death sentences of Bhagat Singh and his comrades
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
237.x: Irwin agreed to release non-violent political prisoners, remit fines, return unsold lands and permit limited salt-making. He refused to commute the death sentences of Bhagat Singh and his comrades.
237.tq: Spot the swapped term by separating Irwin’s agreements from Gandhi’s demands and refusals.
xs: Irwin agreed to **release non-violent political prisoners**, **remit fines, return unsold lands**, and let **coastal villagers make salt for own use**.
4 wrong: Irwin **refused** to commute the death sentences of **Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Rajguru**.
xa: Irwin also refused a **public inquiry into police excesses**; he agreed to **withdraw ordinances**.
Gandhi agreed to **suspend CDM** and **attend the 2nd RTC**.
Mediators: **Tej Bahadur Sapru**, **M.R. Jayakar**, **V.S. Srinivasa Sastri**.

237.s: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact, also called the Delhi Pact, was signed on:
237.x: The Pact was signed on 5 March 1931; dating it to March 1930 is a known trap (the Dandi March was then just beginning). 23 March 1931 is the execution of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru; 24 September 1932 is the Poona Pact.
237.tq: Gandhi-Irwin = 5 March 1931
xs: Signed **5 March 1931** — option **(2)**.
⚠ Dating it to March **1930** is WRONG.
**23 March 1931** = execution of **Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Rajguru**; **24 Sept 1932** = **Poona Pact**.
xa: Also called the **Delhi Pact**; the CWC authorised Gandhi.
Gandhi then attended the **2nd RTC** (**1931**).

237.s: Which one of the following chronological sequences is correct?
o: Gandhi-Irwin Pact → Communal Award → Poona Pact → withdrawal of CDM
Communal Award → Gandhi-Irwin Pact → Poona Pact → withdrawal of CDM
Gandhi-Irwin Pact → Poona Pact → Communal Award → withdrawal of CDM
Poona Pact → Communal Award → Gandhi-Irwin Pact → withdrawal of CDM
237.x: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed in 1931, the Communal Award and Poona Pact followed in 1932, and the Civil Disobedience Movement was withdrawn in 1934.
237.tq: Place events by year before distinguishing the two events of 1932.
xs: **Gandhi-Irwin Pact → Communal Award → Poona Pact → withdrawal of CDM** — option **(1)**.
Pact **5 Mar 1931**; **Communal Award Aug 1932**; **Poona Pact 24 Sept 1932**; CDM withdrawn **1934**.
xa: **1933-34**: CDM suspended, then withdrawn.
APPSC G2 **2025** order: **Chauri Chaura (1922) → Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931) → Poona Pact (1932) → Cripps Mission (1942)**.

237.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
237.x: The Communal Award was announced in August 1932, while the Poona Pact was signed in September 1932. The other pairs are correctly matched.
237.tq: Find the near-date trap between two events of 1932.
xs: **August 1932 — Poona Pact** is wrong — option **(1)**.
**Aug 1932** was the **Communal Award**; the **Poona Pact** was **24 Sept 1932**.
**Nov 1927** (Simon Commission), **5 March 1931** (Pact) and **1942** (Cripps) are correct.
xa: The Simon Commission arrived on **3 Feb 1928**.
First RTC: **Nov 1930**.

237.s:
Which one of the following is the correct chronological order of the following events?
A. Chauri Chaura incident
B. Lahore Session and Purna Swaraj
C. Gandhi-Irwin Pact
D. Cripps Mission
237.x: The Chauri Chaura incident occurred in 1922, the Lahore Session in 1929, the Gandhi-Irwin Pact in 1931 and the Cripps Mission in 1942.
237.tq: Anchor the sequence to the widely separated years 1922, 1929, 1931 and 1942.
xs: **Chauri Chaura (1922)** → **Lahore / Purna Swaraj (Dec 1929)** → **Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931)** → **Cripps Mission (1942)**.
xa: This mirrors the APPSC G2 **2025** order (with **Poona Pact, 1932**).
NCM was withdrawn in **Feb 1922** after Chauri Chaura.

237.s: Which one of the following best describes the significance of the Civil Disobedience Movement as stated in relation to mass participation?
o: It was the first movement to accept separate electorates for the depressed classes.
It was confined exclusively to urban merchants and lawyers.
It was the first movement to break laws openly on a mass scale and drew women, peasants, tribals and merchants into the struggle.
It was limited to constitutional negotiations in London.
237.x: The Civil Disobedience Movement was significant as the first movement to break laws openly on a mass scale, with participation by women, peasants, tribals and merchants.
237.tq: Choose the option containing the complete significance rather than an exclusive claim.
xs: The CDM was the **first mass law-breaking** and drew **women, peasants, tribals and merchants** — option **(3)**.
Laws were broken **openly on a mass scale**.
xa: It also brought the **NWFP** into the struggle.
Its second phase (**1932-34**) failed under **repression**.

237.s: The second phase of the Civil Disobedience Movement, covering 1932–1934, failed mainly because of
o: Lack of any participation by peasants
Acceptance of the Communal Award by Gandhi
The absence of a Karachi Congress Session
237.x: The second phase of the Civil Disobedience Movement, from 1932 to 1934, failed under repression.
237.tq: Match the phase with its stated cause of failure.
xs: **Repression** — option **(4)**.
The second phase (**1932-34**) began when the CDM resumed in **Jan 1932** and Gandhi was arrested.
xa: **1934**: CDM crushed and withdrawn.
The Pact was also attacked for not saving **Bhagat Singh**.

237.s: On which date was the national flag hoisted on the Ravi as part of the Complete Independence declaration?
237.x: Jawaharlal Nehru hoisted the tricolour on the banks of the Ravi at Lahore at midnight on 31 December 1929. 26 January 1930 was the later Purna Swaraj Day.
237.tq: Discriminate the flag hoisting from Purna Swaraj Day.
n: The flag-hoisting and Complete Independence declaration occurred on 31 December 1929. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #111 · pp 205-207]
The flag-hoisting and Complete Independence declaration occurred at Lahore. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #111 · pp 205-207]
The national flag was hoisted on the Ravi during the Complete Independence declaration. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #111 · pp 205-207]
Purna Swaraj Day was observed on 26 January 1930. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #111 · pp 205-207]
xs: The national flag was hoisted on the **Ravi** on **31 December 1929** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Jawaharlal Nehru**, president of the **Lahore Session**, hoisted it with the **Complete Independence** declaration.
**26 January 1930** was the later **Purna Swaraj Day** — the **first Independence Day**, not the flag-hoisting date.
xa: The Lahore Session also authorised the CWC to launch **Civil Disobedience** and boycotted the **RTC**; Viceroy was **Lord Irwin**.
The **Calcutta 1928** session had accepted the **Nehru Report** with a **one-year ultimatum**.
⚠ **Purna Swaraj** was adopted only at **Lahore** — crediting Calcutta 1928 is wrong.
AP angle: **Bulusu Sambamurthy** (East Godavari) passed a Purna Swaraj resolution at district level first.

237.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Non-Cooperation Movement began in 1920.
II. The Non-Cooperation Movement was withdrawn after Chauri Chaura in 1922.
III. The Civil Disobedience Movement began in 1930.
IV. The Quit India Movement began in 1931.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
237.x: I, II and III are correct: Non-Cooperation began in 1920 and was withdrawn after Chauri Chaura in 1922, and Civil Disobedience began in 1930. IV is false because Quit India began in 1942.
237.tq: Check the year in each statement.
n: The Non-Cooperation Movement began in 1920. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #100 · pp 185-188]
The Chauri Chaura incident occurred in 1922. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #100 · pp 185-188]
The Non-Cooperation Movement was withdrawn after Chauri Chaura. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #100 · pp 185-188]
The Civil Disobedience Movement began in 1930. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #100 · pp 185-188]
The Quit India Movement took place in 1942. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #100 · pp 185-188]
xs: Statements **I, II and III** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
I and II are correct: the **Non-Cooperation Movement** began in **1920** and was **withdrawn after Chauri Chaura** (**1922**).
III is correct: the **Civil Disobedience Movement** began in **1930** with the **Dandi March**.
IV is wrong: the **Quit India** Movement came in **1942**, not 1931; **1931** was the **Gandhi-Irwin Pact**.
xa: APPSC order: **Chauri Chaura (1922) → Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931) → Poona Pact (1932) → Cripps Mission (1942)**.
The **Poona Pact** was signed on **24 Sept 1932**.
CDM was resumed in **Jan 1932** and finally crushed and withdrawn in **1934**.

237.s:
Assertion (A): Gandhi was the sole Congress representative at the Second Round Table Conference.
Reason (R): Congress agreed to participate in the Second Round Table Conference under the Gandhi–Irwin Pact.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
237.x: Both are true and R explains A: under the Gandhi–Irwin Pact the Congress agreed to attend the Second Round Table Conference in 1931, and it sent Gandhi as its sole representative.
237.tq: Check whether R is the cause of A.
n: Congress agreed to participate in the Second Round Table Conference. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #100 · pp 185-188]
Gandhi was the sole Congress representative at the Second Round Table Conference. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #100 · pp 185-188]
xs: **Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Under the **Gandhi–Irwin Pact** (**5 March 1931**), the **Congress agreed** to attend the **Second Round Table Conference**.
Having agreed, the Congress sent **Gandhi** as its **sole representative** to the 2nd RTC in **1931**.
xa: The Pact provided for **release of non-violent political prisoners**, **salt-making in coastal areas** and **peaceful picketing**.

**Sarojini Naidu** called Gandhi and Irwin the **"Two Mahatmas"**.

238.s: Who was appointed by the Andhra Congress Committee as the Dictator for Andhra during the Civil Disobedience Movement?

xs: The Andhra Congress Committee made **Konda Venkatappaiah** the **Dictator** — option **(4)**.

**Kaleswara Rao** led at **Machilipatnam**; **Kalluri Subbarao** at **Bellary**; **Bulusu Sambamurthy** at **Chollangi**.
xa: Each district had its own dictator, **war council** and camp (**shibiram**).
Camps: **Guntur**, **Pallepadu Ashram** (Nellore), **Bellary** (Rayalaseema), **Vedavanam** (Madras).

238.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
238.x: The camps included Guntur in Guntur, Pallepadu Ashram in Nellore, Bellary in Rayalaseema, and Vedavanam at Prakasam's house in Madras. Krishna was not identified with the Vedavanam camp.

**Bellary** (Rayalaseema), **Pallepadu Ashram** (Nellore) and **Guntur** (Guntur) are correct.

238.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
238.x: Dandu Narayana Raju led the Salt Satyagraha at Mattapalem. Ravi Narayana Reddy was associated with Ramachandrapuram, Kasi Viswanadham with Vadarevu, and Pattabhi Sitaramayya with Machilipatnam.

238.x: Machilipatnam was associated with Pattabhi Sitaramayya, who referred to it as his “Mecca”.

238.s: At Machilipatnam, who was injured while raising the flag at Tilak Chowk?
238.x: Thota Narsayya, popularly known as “Jenda Narsayya”, was injured while raising the flag at Tilak Chowk in Machilipatnam.

xs: **Thota Narsayya** ("**Jenda Narsayya**") — option **(3)**.

238.s:
Match List-I (Salt Satyagraha centre) with List-II (leader):

238.s: Which of the following was NOT part of the programme of the Civil Disobedience Movement in Andhra?
o: Establishing permanent provincial legislatures in every village

Programme: **make salt**, **raid salt depots**, **picket foreign-cloth shops** (towns), **cut toddy palms** (villages).

238.s: Which of the following statements about Achanta Rukmini Lakshmipathi is correct?

238.s: Pedaganjam and Chinaganjam in Prakasam district are traditionally known for which product?

o: Women participated only in symbolic gatherings and not in direct action.

238.x: The Salt Tax was the main target of the Civil Disobedience Movement, launched with Gandhi's Dandi March in 1930. Kharaj, Jizya and Chauth are medieval taxes.

n: Salt Tax was a major target of Gandhian protest. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]

xs: The **Salt Tax** was the major target of Gandhian protest in the **Civil Disobedience Movement** — so option **(4)** is correct.

238.s: Who led the Vedaranyam Satyagraha and collected salt from the sea?
238.x: C. Rajagopalachari led the salt march from Tiruchirappalli to Vedaranyam in 1930 and made salt there. Gandhi led the Dandi March.

n: C. Rajagopalachari led the Vedaranyam Satyagraha. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]

xs: **C. Rajagopalachari** led the **Vedaranyam Satyagraha** and **collected salt from the sea** — so option **(1)** is correct.

238.s: Who was the first Satyagraha woman arrested during the Salt Satyagraha?

n: Vallabhaneni Sitamahalarami was the first woman arrested during the Salt Satyagraha. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #41 · pp 52-53]
xs: **Vallabhaneni Sitamahalakshmi** was the **first woman arrested** during the **Salt Satyagraha** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Vignanesvaram** of **Ketana** is a text on **property inheritance by daughters**, not a person.
**Kundakundacharya** and **Vallabhaneni Jayavarma** have no link to the Salt Satyagraha in these notes.
xa: ⚠ Sources differ: other notes name **Achanta Rukmini Lakshmipathi** as the **first woman arrested**; she was also the first woman graduate in Andhra.
**Durgabai Deshmukh** led **20 women** to make salt at the High Court beach, **Madras**.
**Duvvuri Subbamma** was among the first at **Chollangi** and was jailed in Nellore.
The first Andhra salt satyagraha was at **Machilipatnam**, **6 Apr 1930**.

239.s: Which one of the following was NOT associated with the Karachi resolution on Fundamental Rights and the National Economic Programme?
239.x: The Karachi resolution included civil liberties, universal adult franchise, religious neutrality and free primary education. It did not propose abolition of all provincial legislatures.
239.tq: Find the option outside the listed civil-liberty and socio-economic measures.
xs: **Abolition of all provincial legislatures** was never part of the Karachi resolution — so option **(4)** is the odd one out.
The resolution's political side promised **civil liberties**, **universal adult franchise**, **religious neutrality** and **free primary education** — options (1), (2) and (3) were all included.
It was drafted by **Jawaharlal Nehru** and adopted at the **Karachi Session, March 1931**.
xa: Economic side of the same resolution: **rent/revenue cuts**, **debt relief**, **state control of key industries**.
Karachi was presided over by **Vallabhbhai Patel** and endorsed the **Gandhi-Irwin (Delhi) Pact**.
The resolution foreshadowed **Part III** (Fundamental Rights) and the **Directive Principles** of the Constitution.

239.s: The Karachi Congress Session was held shortly after the execution of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru. The Congress leadership at the session
o: withdrew the resolution on Fundamental Rights
celebrated political violence as the official method of struggle
admired their bravery while disapproving of political violence
239.x: The Congress admired the courage of the three revolutionaries but disapproved of political violence as a method.

xs: At Karachi the Congress **admired the bravery** of **Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru** while **disapproving of political violence** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It neither celebrated violence (3) nor withdrew the Fundamental Rights resolution (1) — that resolution was in fact adopted there.
xa: The session (**March 1931**) was held days after their execution; president **Vallabhbhai Patel**.
Karachi endorsed the **Gandhi-Irwin (Delhi) Pact** and reiterated **Purna Swaraj**.
The **Fundamental Rights and National Economic Programme** resolution was drafted by **Jawaharlal Nehru**.

239.s:
Consider the following statements about the Karachi session of the Congress (March 1931):
1. It was presided over by Vallabhbhai Patel.
2. Its resolution on Fundamental Rights and the National Economic Programme was drafted by Jawaharlal Nehru.
3. It rejected the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
239.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Vallabhbhai Patel presided and Jawaharlal Nehru drafted the Fundamental Rights and National Economic Programme resolution. Statement 3 is wrong: Karachi endorsed the Gandhi-Irwin (Delhi) Pact. So 1 and 2 only (B); A misses statement 2, C and D include the false statement 3.
239.tq: Karachi 1931: Patel presides, Nehru drafts FR, pact endorsed
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the Karachi Session was presided over by **Vallabhbhai Patel**.
Statement 2 is correct: the **Fundamental Rights and National Economic Programme** resolution was drafted by **Jawaharlal Nehru**.
Statement 3 is wrong: Karachi **endorsed** the **Gandhi-Irwin (Delhi) Pact**; it also reiterated **Purna Swaraj** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Karachi met days after the execution of **Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru** — bravery admired, political violence disapproved.
Political provisions: **civil liberties**, **universal adult franchise**, **religious neutrality**, **free primary education**.
Economic provisions: **rent/revenue cuts**, **debt relief**, **state control of key industries**.

239.s:
Which of the following correctly describes the representation at the Second Round Table Conference?
1. Gandhi was the sole representative of the Congress.
2. Sarojini Naidu represented Indian women.
3. Muhammad Iqbal represented Muslim interests.

239.s: Which Andhra leader went to the Second Round Table Conference (1931) to assist Gandhi, where a resolution for a separate Andhra was handed to Gandhi?
239.x: V.V. Jogayya Pantulu went to assist Gandhi at RTC-2, and the separate-Andhra resolution was handed to Gandhi there. Konda Venkatappayya, Pattabhi Sitaramayya and Prakasam were Andhra leaders of the CDM but are not named for RTC-2.
xs: **V.V. Jogayya Pantulu** went to the Second RTC to assist Gandhi — so option **(2)** is correct.
