239.s: The Second Round Table Conference failed primarily because of disagreement over
o: separate electorates for minorities and the depressed classes
the venue of the Third Round Table Conference
239.x: The conference ended in a deadlock over separate electorates for minorities and the depressed classes. MacDonald subsequently threatened to make a unilateral award.
239.tq: Identify the central issue rather than a peripheral conference topic.
xs: RTC-2 broke down in **deadlock** over **separate electorates for minorities and the depressed classes** — so option **(2)** is correct.
After the deadlock **MacDonald** threatened a **unilateral award**.
xa: **Gandhi** was the **sole Congress representative**; **Muhammad Iqbal** spoke for the **Muslims**, **Sarojini Naidu** for **Indian women**.
Gandhi returned **empty-handed** in **Jan 1932**; Viceroy **Lord Willingdon** struck first and Gandhi was arrested.
The **Poona Pact** is the root of reserved seats in **Arts. 330, 332**.

239.s: The Civil Disobedience Movement was resumed in January 1932 immediately after which development?
o: The Third Round Table Conference concluded.
Gandhi was arrested and the Congress was subjected to repression.
The Cripps Mission arrived in India.
239.x: After Gandhi returned from the Second Round Table Conference, the movement was resumed in January 1932; Gandhi was arrested, the Congress was banned and repressive ordinances were issued.
239.tq: Connect the resumption of a movement with the immediate political response.
xs: In **Jan 1932** Gandhi returned empty-handed from RTC-2; Viceroy **Lord Willingdon** struck first — **Gandhi arrested**, Congress banned, **harsh repression** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Ordinances** were issued and the Congress was banned, which revived the movement.
xa: **15 Jan 1932**: firing on satyagrahis at **Berhampur**.
**8 May 1933**: Gandhi released; **14 July 1933**: mass CDM suspended in favour of **individual satyagraha**.
**April 1934**: CDM **formally withdrawn**; Congress then contested the **Central Assembly** elections (**1934**).

239.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the later phase of the Civil Disobedience Movement is correct?
1. Gandhi was released on 8 May 1933.
2. Mass Civil Disobedience was suspended on 14 July 1933.
3. The movement was formally withdrawn in April 1934.
4. Congress contested the 1934 Central Assembly elections.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
239.x: All four statements are correct. Individual satyagraha continued after the suspension of mass action, and the Congress later revived the council-entry line.
239.tq: Check each date and the connected political development before choosing the complete combination.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
Gandhi was released on **8 May 1933**; **mass CDM** was suspended on **14 July 1933** (individual satyagraha instead).
The movement was **formally withdrawn** in **April 1934**; in **1934** the Swarajist **council-entry** line revived and Congress contested the **Central Assembly** elections.
xa: Resumption: **Jan 1932**, after Gandhi returned empty-handed from RTC-2; Viceroy **Lord Willingdon** arrested him and banned the Congress.
**15 Jan 1932**: firing on satyagrahis at **Berhampur**.
Post-CDM Telugu works: **Bharat Swarajya Yuddham** (**Jagannadh Shastry**), **Navayuga Gandhi** (**Damaraju Pundarikakshudu**).

239.s: The Karachi resolution is regarded as an important precursor to which portions of the Constitution of India?
o: Part I and the Schedules alone
The provisions relating only to the Union Public Service Commission
Part III and the Directive Principles of State Policy
The provisions relating only to emergency powers
239.x: The Karachi resolution on Fundamental Rights and the National Economic Programme foreshadowed Part III and the Directive Principles of State Policy.
239.tq: Link a historical resolution with its constitutional legacy.
xs: The Karachi resolution foreshadowed **Part III and the Directive Principles of State Policy** — so option **(3)** is correct.

Its political half (civil liberties, **universal adult franchise**, religious neutrality, free primary education) anticipates **Fundamental Rights**; its economic half (debt relief, **state control of key industries**) anticipates the **Directive Principles**.
xa: The resolution was drafted by **Jawaharlal Nehru**; the session was presided over by **Vallabhbhai Patel** (**March 1931**).
Similar constitutional link: the **Poona Pact** = root of reserved seats (**Arts. 330, 332**).

239.s: The Poona Pact is historically associated with the roots of reserved seats represented in the Constitution by
239.x: The Poona Pact is regarded as a historical root of the reservation of seats reflected in Articles 330 and 332 of the Constitution.
239.tq: Match the historical development with the relevant constitutional Articles.
xs: The **Poona Pact** is the root of reserved seats under **Articles 330 and 332** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It followed the RTC-2 deadlock over **separate electorates for minorities and the depressed classes**, after which **MacDonald** threatened a **unilateral award**.
xa: The **Karachi resolution** is the precursor of **Part III** and the **Directive Principles**.
**Ambedkar** was among the participants at RTC-2 (**1931**).

239.s: The only Round Table Conference that Gandhi attended was the:
239.x: Gandhi attended only the Second RTC, held in 1931. Listing the Second RTC under 1932 is a known trap; the First RTC (1930) was boycotted by the Congress and Gandhi did not attend the Third (1932).
xs: Gandhi attended only the **Second RTC, 1931** — so option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ Option (3) is the trap: listing the 2nd RTC under **1932** is wrong — it was **1931**.
At RTC-2 Gandhi was the **sole Congress representative**.
xa: Other participants: **Sarojini Naidu** (Indian women), **Muhammad Iqbal** (Muslims), **Malaviya**, **Ambedkar**, **Jinnah**, **Aga Khan**.
The conference ended in **deadlock**; **MacDonald** threatened a **unilateral award**.
Gandhi returned empty-handed in **Jan 1932** and the CDM was resumed.

239.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Fundamental Rights
(b) Economic Programme
(c) Purna Swaraj
(d) Swadeshi and Boycott

List-II
(i) Boycott foreign goods and promote indigenous goods
(ii) Complete Independence as Congress goal
(iii) Civil liberties and citizens' rights
(iv) Labour welfare and economic justice
239.x: Fundamental Rights covered civil liberties, the Economic Programme covered labour welfare, Purna Swaraj meant Complete Independence, and Swadeshi meant boycotting foreign goods, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
239.tq: Recall the content of each resolution or movement.
n: The Purna Swaraj Resolution adopted Complete Independence as the Congress goal. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #111 · pp 205-207]
The Fundamental Rights resolution addressed civil liberties. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #111 · pp 205-207]
The Fundamental Rights resolution addressed citizens' rights. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #111 · pp 205-207]
The Economic Programme addressed labour welfare. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #111 · pp 205-207]
The Economic Programme addressed economic justice. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #111 · pp 205-207]
The Swadeshi and Boycott movement promoted the boycott of foreign goods. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #111 · pp 205-207]
The Swadeshi and Boycott movement promoted indigenous goods. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #111 · pp 205-207]
xs: The correct code is **a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i** — so option **(4)** is correct.
(a) **Fundamental Rights** → **civil liberties and citizens' rights** (iii); (b) **Economic Programme** → **labour welfare and economic justice** (iv).
(c) **Purna Swaraj** → **Complete Independence** as the Congress goal (ii); (d) **Swadeshi and Boycott** → boycott foreign goods (i).
xa: The **Karachi Session** (**1931**) was presided by **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**; **Jawaharlal Nehru** drafted the resolution.
It was held days after the execution of **Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru** and endorsed the **Gandhi-Irwin Pact**.
Political provisions included **universal adult franchise** and **free primary education**.
The Karachi resolution foreshadowed **Part III** and the **Directive Principles**.

240.s: Who joined the Muslim League's observance of the 'Day of Deliverance' in Bombay on 22 December 1939?
240.x: B.R. Ambedkar joined the observance of the Muslim League's Day of Deliverance in Bombay on 22 December 1939.
240.tq: Match the participant with the specific political observance.
xs: **B.R. Ambedkar** joined the League's **"Day of Deliverance"** event in **Bombay** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The League observed it on **22 December 1939**, celebrating the resignation of the **Congress ministries** (**Oct-Nov 1939**).
xa: The ministries resigned because India was dragged into the war **without consultation**.
Next on the timeline: **Ramgarh** Congress session (**March 1940**), then the **August Offer** (**August 1940**).

240.s: The August Offer of 1940 was made by:
240.x: The August Offer was made by Viceroy Lord Linlithgow in August 1940.
240.tq: Match the constitutional proposal with the Viceroy who announced it.
xs: The August Offer was made by Viceroy **Lord Linlithgow** in **August 1940** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It came when **Britain was losing in Europe**; **Sir Stafford Cripps** (3) led the separate mission of **March 1942**.
xa: Proposals: a **constitution-making body after the war**, more Indians in the **Viceroy's Executive Council**, a **War Advisory Council**.
It answered **Ramgarh** (**March 1940**) — ⚠ Ramgarh came BEFORE the Offer.
**Nehru** called Dominion Status **"dead as a doornail"**; Congress **rejected** the Offer.

240.s: Which of the following was NOT included in the August Offer?
o: Immediate transfer of defence to an Indian national government
An increase in Indian membership of the Viceroy's Executive Council
A representative constitution-making body after the war
240.x: The August Offer did not provide for immediate transfer of defence. It proposed a post-war constitution-making body, more Indians in the Executive Council and a War Advisory Council.
240.tq: Find the option that turns a limited proposal into an immediate transfer of power.
xs: **Immediate transfer of defence to an Indian national government** was not in the August Offer — so option **(1)** is correct.
The Offer proposed a representative **constitution-making body after the war** (4), more Indians in the **Viceroy's Executive Council** (3) and a **War Advisory Council** (2).
It kept **Dominion Status** as the goal with a **minority veto** — nothing on handing over defence.
xa: Made by **Lord Linlithgow** in **August 1940**, answering the **Ramgarh** offer.
⚠ Even the later **Cripps** plan kept **defence** and the army with **the British** in the interim.
Significance: **first official acceptance** that Indians would frame their own constitution.

240.s: The August Offer was significant because it constituted the first official British acceptance that:
o: Indians would frame their own constitution
Congress ministries could continue without wartime restrictions
The Muslim League alone represented Indian Muslims
240.x: The August Offer was the first official acceptance that Indians would frame their own constitution. The demand had been raised by M.N. Roy in 1934 and officially adopted by Congress in 1935.
240.tq: Identify the constitutional principle represented by the offer.
xs: The August Offer was the **first official acceptance** that **Indians would frame their own constitution** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It proposed a representative **constitution-making body after the war**.
**M.N. Roy** had raised the Constituent Assembly demand in **1934**; Congress made it official in **1935**.
xa: Other proposals: more Indians in the **Viceroy's Executive Council**; a **War Advisory Council**; Dominion Status as goal; **minority veto**.
Contrast: the **Cripps Mission** first conceded the **provincial opt-out** — germ of Partition.
Congress **rejected** the Offer; Nehru: Dominion Status **"dead as a doornail"**.

240.s: Which statement correctly describes the responses to the August Offer?
o: The Muslim League rejected it because it promised partition explicitly
Congress rejected it, while the Muslim League welcomed the minority veto but demanded more than it offered
Congress accepted it, while the Muslim League rejected the minority veto
Both Congress and the Muslim League accepted it without reservation
240.x: Congress rejected the August Offer, and Nehru described dominion status as 'dead as a doornail'. The Muslim League welcomed the minority veto but maintained that only partition would satisfy it.
240.tq: Compare the distinct responses of Congress and the Muslim League.
xs: **Congress rejected** the August Offer, while the **League welcomed the minority veto** but demanded more — option **(2)** is correct.
The League said **nothing short of partition** would satisfy it; the Offer had not promised partition, so (1) is wrong.
**Nehru** dismissed Dominion Status as **"dead as a doornail"**.
xa: The Offer was made by **Lord Linlithgow**, **August 1940**, when Britain was losing in Europe.
⚠ Cripps (**1942**) was also rejected by both Congress and League — for opposite reasons.
Congress responded to the war situation with **Individual Satyagraha** from **17 Oct 1940**.

240.s: The August Offer was made in response to which earlier Congress position?
o: Demand for a separate Muslim homeland
Demand for the immediate abolition of all provincial legislatures
Support for the war if a provisional national government were formed at the Centre
240.x: The August Offer responded to the Ramgarh Congress position that support for the war could be extended if a provisional national government were formed at the Centre.
240.tq: Connect the offer with the political demand it was intended to answer.
xs: The August Offer answered **Ramgarh**'s offer of **support for the war if a provisional national government were formed at the Centre** — so option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ **Ramgarh (March 1940)** came BEFORE the **August Offer (August 1940)**; the Cripps proposals (2) came only in **1942**.
xa: Ramgarh session was held in **Bihar**.
The Offer was made by Viceroy **Lord Linlithgow**; Congress **rejected** it.
Proposals: post-war **constitution-making body**, more Indians in the **Executive Council**, **War Advisory Council**.

240.s: Individual Satyagraha was launched by Mahatma Gandhi on:
240.x: Individual Satyagraha began on 17 October 1940.
240.tq: Distinguish the exact launch date from nearby wartime dates.
xs: Individual Satyagraha began on **17 October 1940** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**22 December 1939** (1) was the League's **Day of Deliverance**; **8 August 1942** (2) the **Quit India resolution**; **August 1940** (4) the **August Offer**.
xa: Gandhi launched it from **Paunar**, Wardha (also spelt "Palner").
Order of satyagrahis: **Vinoba Bhave** first, **Jawaharlal Nehru** second, **Brahma Dutt** third.
In **Bihar (1940)** it was led by **Shyam Narayan Singh**.

240.s: From which place did Vinoba Bhave commence Individual Satyagraha?
240.x: Vinoba Bhave commenced Individual Satyagraha from Paunar in Wardha.
240.tq: Match the movement's starting place with its associated district.
xs: Individual Satyagraha was launched from **Paunar in Wardha** (also spelt **"Palner"**) — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Acharya Vinoba Bhave** was the **first satyagrahi**; launch date **17 October 1940**.
**Ramgarh in Bihar** (4) was the venue of the Congress session of **March 1940**, not of the satyagraha.
xa: Second satyagrahi: **Jawaharlal Nehru**; third: **Brahma Dutt**.
Aim: assert **freedom of speech against the war**, not mass mobilisation.
The government arrested **Vinoba**, **Nehru** and **Patel**.

240.s: The immediate objective of Individual Satyagraha was to:
o: Mobilise the entire population for an armed revolt
Establish a provisional government at the Centre
Assert freedom of speech against assisting the British war effort
240.x: The movement aimed to assert freedom of speech and oppose the view that India should help the British war effort with men or money. Selected individuals made anti-war speeches and courted arrest successively.
240.tq: Apply the stated objective to distinguish limited protest from mass mobilisation.
xs: The aim was to **assert freedom of speech against the war** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It was **not mass mobilisation** (1): selected individuals made **anti-war speeches** and courted arrest one after another.
Gandhi's line: **"It is wrong to help the British war effort with men or money."**
xa: Launched **17 October 1940** from **Paunar**, Wardha.
Satyagrahis in order: **Vinoba Bhave**, **Jawaharlal Nehru**, **Brahma Dutt**.
Exam angle: assertion-reason on why it was **"limited"** (**October 1940**).

240.s: In Bihar, Individual Satyagraha in 1940 was led by:
240.x: In Bihar, the 1940 Individual Satyagraha was led by Shyam Narayan Singh.
240.tq: Match the regional leadership with the correct movement and year.
xs: **Shyam Narayan Singh** led Individual Satyagraha in **Bihar (1940)** — so option **(4)** is correct (BPSC 2025 key).
**Brahma Dutt** (3) was the **third satyagrahi**; **Maulana Azad** (2) was a Congress negotiator with Cripps; **B.R. Ambedkar** (1) joined the League's Day of Deliverance.
xa: Launch: **17 October 1940**, by Gandhi from **Paunar**.
First satyagrahi: **Vinoba Bhave**; second: **Jawaharlal Nehru**.

240.s: In the Individual Satyagraha of 1940, the first, second and third satyagrahis were respectively:
o: Jawaharlal Nehru, Vinoba Bhave, Brahma Dutt
Vinoba Bhave, Jawaharlal Nehru, Brahma Dutt
Vinoba Bhave, Vallabhbhai Patel, Jawaharlal Nehru
Brahma Dutt, Vinoba Bhave, Jawaharlal Nehru
240.x: Acharya Vinoba Bhave was the first satyagrahi, Jawaharlal Nehru the second and Brahma Dutt the third (chosen for moral conviction, not political prominence). Patel was arrested but was not among the first three; the other options reorder the sequence.
240.tq: Vinoba -> Nehru -> Brahma Dutt
xs: First **Vinoba Bhave**, second **Jawaharlal Nehru**, third **Brahma Dutt** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Brahma Dutt** was chosen to show **moral conviction, not political prominence**.
**Patel** (3) was arrested along with Vinoba and Nehru but was not one of the first three.
xa: Launch: **17 October 1940** from **Paunar**, Wardha.
**Ongole Municipality** condemned the arrests of **Vinoba, Nehru and Patel**.
Nehru was also a **Cripps negotiator** and called Dominion Status **"dead as a doornail"**.

240.s: The Cripps Mission was sent to India by the British Government primarily under pressure from which combination of leaders?
240.x: The mission was sent by Winston Churchill's Government under pressure from United States President Franklin Roosevelt and China's Chiang Kai-shek.
240.tq: Match the political pressure with the correct international leaders.
xs: Churchill sent Cripps under pressure from US President **Roosevelt** and China's **Chiang Kai-shek** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Winston Churchill** (2) was the PM who sent the mission and was later **accused of sabotage**; **Linlithgow** made the 1940 August Offer.
**Maulana Azad** and Nehru (3, 4) were the **Congress negotiators**, not those who pressed for the mission.
xa: Trigger: **Pearl Harbor 1941**; Malaya, Singapore overrun; **Rangoon fell March 1942**.
Cripps: **Labour Party**, member of Churchill's War Cabinet, **"take it or leave it"** attitude.

240.s:
With reference to the Cripps proposals, consider the following statements:
1. India was promised dominion status after the war.
2. The Indian Union was to have the power to secede.
3. The transfer of defence control was to take place immediately.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
240.x: The proposals promised dominion status after the war and allowed the Indian Union to secede. Defence and control of the army were to remain with Britain during the interim period.
240.tq: Test the difference between a post-war promise and an immediate transfer of power.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: an **Indian Union with dominion status** after the war.
Statement 2 is correct: the Union would have the **power to secede**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **defence** and control of the army stayed with **the British** in the interim — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Constitution-making body: a **Constituent Assembly after the war**.
**Provincial option** to stay out — Pakistan conceded in principle, the **"fatal flaw"**.
A **treaty** was to protect racial/religious minorities; **Governor-General's powers retained**.

240.s: Which provision of the Cripps proposals was regarded as the 'fatal flaw' because it could lead to the formation of separate unions by provinces?
o: The retention of the Governor-General's powers
The provincial option to remain outside the proposed Indian Union
The creation of a War Advisory Council
240.x: The proposal allowing unwilling provinces to form separate unions conceded the principle that later supported the demand for Pakistan and created the risk of balkanisation.
240.tq: Link a constitutional provision with its political consequence.
xs: The **provincial option to remain outside the proposed Indian Union** was the **"fatal flaw"** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Any unwilling province/princely state could stay out and **form separate unions**, conceding **Pakistan in principle**.
Congress saw in it a **risk of Balkanisation**; it is called the **germ of Partition**.
xa: The **War Advisory Council** (3) belonged to the **August Offer**, not Cripps.
The **minority-protection treaty** (4) and the retained **Governor-General's powers** (1) were separate Cripps provisions.
⚠ The League still **rejected** Cripps: it wanted Pakistan conceded **explicitly**.

240.s:
Consider the following statements about the Cripps proposals:
1. Racial and religious minorities were to be protected through a treaty.
2. During the interim period, defence and control of the army were to remain with Britain.
3. During the interim period, the Governor-General's powers were to be curtailed in favour of an Indian cabinet.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
240.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: a treaty was to protect minorities, and defence and the army stayed with Britain in the interim. Statement 3 is wrong: the Governor-General's powers were retained. B misses statement 1; C and D include the false statement 3.
240.tq: Cripps interim = nothing changes now: defence with Britain, Governor-General's powers retained.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: a **treaty to protect racial/religious minorities**.
Statement 2 is correct: **defence** and control of the army stayed with **the British** in the interim.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **Governor-General's powers were retained** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Promise: **Dominion Status** with power to **secede**, after the war.
**Provincial option** to stay out — the "fatal flaw".
Congress objected to **no immediate transfer of power**.

240.s: Sir Stafford Cripps was a member of the
o: Labour Party and Churchill's War Cabinet
Liberal Party and Wavell's Executive Council
Communist Party and Churchill's War Cabinet
240.x: Cripps was a Labour member of Churchill's War Cabinet. Churchill sent him to India in 1942 under international and military pressure.
240.tq: Test the exact party and cabinet association instead of relying on the person's later political reputation.
xs: Cripps belonged to the **Labour Party** and was a member of **Churchill's War Cabinet** — so option **(1)** is correct.
He was criticised for a **"take it or leave it"** attitude.
xa: **Churchill** sent him under pressure from **Roosevelt** and **Chiang Kai-shek**; Churchill was accused of sabotage.
Cripps reached Delhi **22-23 March 1942**; returned **mid-April**.
Congress negotiators: **Nehru** and **Maulana Azad**.

240.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Congress response to the Cripps Mission:
1. Jawaharlal Nehru and Maulana Azad were the Congress negotiators.
2. The Congress objected to the right to secede.
3. The Congress objected that the proposals transferred power immediately instead of after the war.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
240.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Nehru and Azad negotiated, and Congress objected to the right to secede. Statement 3 is wrong: the objection was that there was NO immediate transfer of power. A is incomplete; C and D include statement 3.
240.tq: Congress wanted power now; Cripps offered it only after the war.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Nehru and Maulana Azad** were the Congress negotiators.
Statement 2 is correct: they objected to the **right to secede**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the objection was **no immediate transfer of power** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Congress also feared **Balkanisation** through the provincial option.
Gandhi called the offer a **"post-dated cheque"**; Nehru added **"on a crashing bank"**.
Failure led directly to the **Quit India Movement (August 1942)**.

240.s: The failure of the Cripps Mission was followed directly by which major movement?
240.x: The failure of the Cripps Mission directly contributed to the launch of the Quit India Movement in August 1942.
240.tq: Link the failed constitutional negotiation with its immediate political outcome.
xs: The failure of Cripps led directly to the **Quit India Movement (August 1942)** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Individual Satyagraha** (2) came earlier, from **17 October 1940**.
xa: The **Quit India resolution** was passed at **Bombay** on **8 Aug 1942**.
Talks broke down over Cripps's **"take it or leave it"** attitude and **Churchill's sabotage**.
Both Congress and League **rejected** the plan.

240.s: The Muslim League rejected the Cripps proposals because they:
o: provided for an explicit and immediate Pakistan
transferred all defence powers to the League
accepted the idea of a single Indian Union and did not explicitly concede Pakistan
abolished the right of provinces to remain outside the Union
240.x: The Muslim League opposed the proposed single Indian Union and wanted Pakistan to be explicitly conceded rather than left as an indirect possibility through the provincial option.
240.tq: Distinguish the League's objection from the Congress objections to the same proposals.
xs: The League rejected Cripps because it **opposed a single Indian Union** and **wanted Pakistan conceded explicitly** — option **(3)** is correct.
The plan only conceded Pakistan **in principle** through the **provincial option**, not explicitly (1).
**Defence** stayed with **the British** in the interim, not with the League (2).
xa: ⚠ Both Congress AND League rejected Cripps — Congress for **no immediate power**, the League for **no explicit Pakistan**.
At the **August Offer** the League had welcomed the **minority veto** but wanted partition.

240.s: Gandhi's description of the Cripps proposals as a 'post-dated cheque' was famously extended by Nehru with the words:
240.x: Gandhi called the Cripps offer a 'post-dated cheque' and Nehru added 'on a crashing bank' (some sources give the whole phrase to Gandhi, with 'failing bank'). 'Dead as a doornail' was Nehru's verdict on Dominion Status in the August Offer; the other two phrases are not tied to Cripps.
240.tq: Cripps = post-dated cheque on a crashing bank
xs: Gandhi called the Cripps offer a **"post-dated cheque"** and Nehru added **"on a crashing bank"** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Some notes give the whole phrase to Gandhi, with **"failing bank"**.
⚠ **"Dead as a doornail"** (1) was **Nehru** on Dominion Status in the **August Offer**.
xa: Cripps was criticised for a **"take it or leave it"** attitude.
Gandhi on Individual Satyagraha: **"It is wrong to help the British war effort with men or money."**

240.s: The sequence beginning with the resignation of Congress ministries and ending with the Cripps Mission is correctly represented by:
o: Resignation of ministries → Ramgarh Congress session → August Offer → Cripps Mission
Ramgarh Congress session → resignation of ministries → Cripps Mission → August Offer
August Offer → resignation of ministries → Ramgarh Congress session → Cripps Mission
Cripps Mission → August Offer → Ramgarh Congress session → resignation of ministries
240.x: The sequence was resignation of Congress ministries in October–November 1939, Ramgarh session in March 1940, August Offer in August 1940 and Cripps Mission in March–April 1942.
240.tq: Fix the first event and then place the later wartime developments.
xs: **Resignation of ministries → Ramgarh → August Offer → Cripps Mission** — option **(1)** is correct (UPPSC 2024 key).
Dates: resignation **Oct-Nov 1939**; Ramgarh **March 1940**; August Offer **August 1940**; Cripps **March-April 1942**.
⚠ **Ramgarh** came BEFORE the **August Offer** — the Offer answered Ramgarh.
xa: Next: **Quit India resolution**, **8 Aug 1942**, Bombay; **Desai-Liaquat Pact**, **1945**.
**Cabinet Mission**: **March 1946**.

240.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the resignation of the Congress ministries in 1939:
1. Lord Linlithgow declared India to be a party to the Second World War.
2. Indian leaders were not consulted before the declaration.
3. The Muslim League observed 22 December 1939 as Deliverance Day.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
240.x: All three statements are correct. Linlithgow made the declaration without consulting Indian leaders, and the League observed the Congress resignations as Deliverance Day on 22 December 1939.
240.tq: Check each statement against the cause, authority and consequence of the resignations.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
In **Sept 1939** Viceroy **Linlithgow** declared India a **belligerent** in **WWII** without consulting Indians.
The League observed **22 December 1939** as **"Day of Deliverance"**.
xa: The Congress ministries resigned in **October-November 1939** in protest.
**B.R. Ambedkar** joined the Day of Deliverance event in **Bombay**.

240.s: The Quit India resolution was passed on 8 August 1942 at:
240.x: The Quit India resolution was passed at Bombay on 8 August 1942.
240.tq: 8-8-42, Bombay: Gowalia Tank.
xs: The **Quit India resolution** was passed at **Bombay** on **8 Aug 1942** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Wardha** (1) is linked to **Paunar**, where Gandhi launched **Individual Satyagraha** in **1940**.
xa: The failure of the **Cripps Mission** led directly to Quit India.
Gandhi had used "Quit India" in **Harijan** in **April 1942**, amid rumours of Japanese bombing of **Vizag** and **Kakinada**.

240.s: Which one of the following correctly expresses the distinctive significance of the August Offer and the Cripps Mission?
o: The August Offer created the provincial opt-out principle, whereas the Cripps Mission introduced separate electorates.
The August Offer first conceded provincial opt-out, whereas the Cripps Mission first accepted a post-war constitution-making body.
The August Offer first accepted a post-war constitution-making body, whereas the Cripps Mission first conceded the provincial option to opt out.
Both the August Offer and the Cripps Mission rejected the idea of a post-war constitution-making body.
240.x: The August Offer marked the first acceptance of a post-war constitution-making body. The Cripps Mission first conceded the possibility of provincial opt-out, regarded as the germ of Partition.
240.tq: Compare the two proposals by assigning each distinctive concession to the correct one.
xs: The **August Offer** first accepted a **post-war constitution-making body**; the **Cripps Mission** first conceded **provincial opt-out** — option **(3)** is correct.
Option (2) swaps the two; the August Offer was the **first official acceptance** that Indians would frame their own constitution.
Cripps's opt-out is called the **germ of Partition** and the **"fatal flaw"**.
xa: The August Offer also offered a **War Advisory Council** and more Indians in the **Executive Council**.
Cripps's body: elected by **provincial lower houses** (**1/10th** of their size, proportional representation) plus **Princely State nominees**.

240.s:
Match List-I with List-II (about the Cripps Mission):

List-I
(a) Congress President during the talks
(b) Arrival
(c) Head
(d) British Prime Minister who sent it

List-II
(i) Winston Churchill
(ii) March 1942
(iii) Maulana Abul Kalam Azad
(iv) Sir Stafford Cripps
240.x: Maulana Azad was Congress President and a negotiator, the mission arrived in March 1942, it was headed by Sir Stafford Cripps and sent by Prime Minister Winston Churchill, giving a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
240.tq: Recall the basic facts of the Cripps Mission.
n: The Cripps Mission took place in 1942. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #130 · pp 233-234]
The Cripps Mission arrived in March 1942. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #130 · pp 233-234]
Sir Stafford Cripps headed the Cripps Mission. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #130 · pp 233-234]
British Prime Minister Winston Churchill sent the Cripps Mission. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #130 · pp 233-234]
xs: The correct code is **a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i** — so option **(2)** is correct.
(a) **Maulana Abul Kalam Azad** was a **Congress negotiator** with **Nehru**; (b) the mission **arrived in March 1942**.
(c) It was headed by **Sir Stafford Cripps**; (d) it was sent by **British PM Winston Churchill**.
xa: Churchill sent it under pressure from **Roosevelt** and **Chiang Kai-shek**, amid the **Japanese advance**.
Cripps was a **Labour Party** member of Churchill's War Cabinet.
Gandhi called the offer a **"post-dated cheque"**; ⚠ some notes say **Nehru** added "on a crashing bank".
Its failure directly led to the **Quit India Movement (August 1942)**.

240.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Cripps proposals contained both an offer after the war and an option relating to the proposed Union.
II. The provinces could opt out of the proposed Union.
III. The proposals were accepted and the negotiations succeeded.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
240.x: I and II are correct: Cripps offered post-war Dominion Status and allowed provinces to opt out of the Union. III is false because the proposals were rejected and the talks failed.
240.tq: Check the outcome of the mission.
n: The Cripps Mission offered Dominion Status after the war. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #130 · pp 233-234]
The Cripps Mission proposed that provinces could opt out of the proposed Union. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #130 · pp 233-234]
The Cripps Mission proposals were rejected. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #130 · pp 233-234]
The Cripps Mission negotiations failed. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #130 · pp 233-234]
xs: Only **statements I and II** are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
I is correct: Cripps offered **Dominion Status after the war** and a provincial option on the **proposed Union**.
II is correct: **provinces could opt out** of the proposed Union.
III is wrong: the proposals were **rejected** and the **negotiations failed**.
xa: The constitution-making body was to be a **Constituent Assembly after the war**.
**Defence** and control of the army were to stay with **the British** in the interim.
⚠ Both **Congress** and the **League** rejected Cripps — for opposite reasons (no immediate power vs no explicit **Pakistan**).
The provincial opt-out was the "**fatal flaw**" — germ of **Partition**.

241.s: The immediate failure of the Cripps Mission contributed to the Quit India Movement mainly because the Mission offered
o: A separate province for every linguistic group
241.x: The Cripps Mission failed to satisfy Indian demands because it did not offer immediate self-government. Its failure in March–April 1942 became a major cause of the Quit India Movement.
241.tq: Identify the precise deficiency in a political proposal rather than its general historical association.
xs: The Cripps Mission offered **no immediate self-government** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Its failure in **March-April 1942** became a direct cause of Quit India (UPSC 2013: launched in response to the **Cripps Proposals**).
xa: Other causes: the **Japanese advance** (Malaya, Singapore overrun; **Rangoon** fell **March 1942**) and **economic distress** (rising prices, wartime shortages).
**14 July 1942**: CWC resolution at **Wardha**; **8 August 1942**: AICC ratified it at **Gowalia Tank Maidan**, Bombay.
**9 August 1942**: leaders arrested in **Operation Zero Hour**.

241.s:
Consider the following events:
1. Fall of Rangoon
2. Overrunning of Singapore
3. Advance of Japanese forces towards India’s eastern frontier
Which of the above created an important wartime background to the Quit India Movement?
241.x: All three developments formed part of the Japanese advance in the East. Rangoon fell in March 1942, and Japanese expansion brought the war close to India’s eastern frontier.
241.tq: Recognise that multiple connected military developments contributed to the same historical cause.
xs: All three formed the wartime background — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
The Japanese overran **Malaya** and **Singapore**; **Rangoon** fell in **March 1942**.
The Japanese then stood at India's **eastern frontier**, with rumours of bombing of **Vizag** and **Kakinada**.
xa: Other causes: failure of the **Cripps Mission** (no immediate self-government) and **economic distress**.
Economic distress meant **rising prices** and **wartime shortages**.

241.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Quit India resolutions:
1. The Congress Working Committee adopted a resolution at Wardha on 14 July 1942.
2. The Wardha resolution was proposed by Jawaharlal Nehru and seconded by Sardar Patel.
3. The All India Congress Committee ratified the resolution at Bombay on 8 August 1942.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
241.x: All three statements are correct. The CWC resolution was passed at Wardha on 14 July 1942, and the AICC ratified it at Bombay on 8 August 1942.
241.tq: Separate the preliminary CWC decision from the later AICC ratification using dates and venue.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**14 July 1942**: CWC resolution at **Wardha**, proposed by **Nehru** and seconded by **Patel**.
**8 August 1942**: **AICC, Bombay**, at **Gowalia Tank Maidan**, ratified it.
xa: Hence the names **"Wardha Resolution"** and **"August Resolution"**.
**9 August 1942**: pre-dawn arrests in **Operation Zero Hour**.
The Wardha resolution empowered **Gandhi** to lead a **non-violent mass movement**.

241.s: Which of the following was NOT a demand or feature of the resolution ratified by the AICC in August 1942?
o: Mass civil disobedience under Gandhi’s leadership
Continuation of British rule until the end of the Second World War
Formation of a provisional government after the British withdrawal
241.x: The resolution demanded the immediate end of British rule, envisaged a provisional government after withdrawal and authorised mass civil disobedience under Gandhi. It did not support continuation of British rule until the war ended.
241.tq: Reject the option that reverses the central demand of the resolution.
xs: **Continuation of British rule until the end of the war** was never demanded — so option **(3)** is the odd one out.
The AICC, Bombay demanded the **immediate end of British rule**, a **provisional government after the British left**, and **mass civil disobedience under Gandhi**.
xa: The AICC met on **8 August 1942** at **Gowalia Tank Maidan**.
It ratified the CWC's **Wardha** resolution of **14 July 1942**.
Gandhi's speech there: **"Do or Die"** ("Karo ya Maro").

241.s:
Consider the following statements about Gandhi's instructions during the Quit India Movement:
1. Government servants were to resign from service immediately.
2. Soldiers were not to fire on Indians.
3. Peasants were to withhold rent from pro-government zamindars.
4. Princes were to support the people.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
241.x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: government servants were told to stay in service but pledge loyalty to the Congress. A, C and D all include the false statement 1.
241.tq: Officials: stay, but pledge loyalty to Congress - not resign.
xs: Statement 1 is wrong: government servants were to **stay in service but pledge loyalty to Congress**.

Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct: **soldiers** not to fire on Indians; **peasants** to withhold rent from pro-government zamindars; **princes** to support the people — so **2, 3 and 4 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: **Students** were told they **may leave studies**.
The instructions accompanied the **AICC, Bombay** resolution of **8 August 1942**.

241.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the origin of the slogan “Quit India”?
o: The phrase was suggested by Mahatma Gandhi in Harijan in April 1942, while its coinage is generally credited to Yusuf Meherally
It was coined by Mahatma Gandhi in Young India in 1942
It was coined by Jawaharlal Nehru at the Wardha meeting in July 1942
It was first used by Subhas Chandra Bose in a broadcast from Germany
241.x: Gandhi suggested the phrase in Harijan in April 1942, whereas Yusuf Meherally is generally credited with coining it. Young India had ceased publication in 1932.
241.tq: Distinguish the person who suggested a phrase from the person generally credited with coining it.
xs: Gandhi suggested the phrase in **Harijan** (**April 1942**); its coinage is usually credited to **Yusuf Meherally** — option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ **Young India** (2) had ceased in **1932**; Gandhi's paper in **1942** was **Harijan**.
xa: The Harijan use came amid rumours of Japanese bombing of **Vizag** and **Kakinada**.
**"Do or Die"** ("Karo ya Maro") was Gandhi's slogan at **Gowalia Tank**, **8 Aug 1942**.

241.s:
With reference to the slogan “Do or Die”, consider the following statements:
1. It was associated with Mahatma Gandhi.
2. It was delivered in the Gowalia Tank speech on 8 August 1942.
3. It was announced through Young India in 1942.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
241.x: Gandhi used “Do or Die” in his Gowalia Tank speech on 8 August 1942. Statement 3 is false because Gandhi’s paper in 1942 was Harijan; Young India had ceased publication in 1932.
241.tq: Use the publication-title trap to separate a true slogan association from a false source attribution.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: **"Do or Die"** is **Mahatma Gandhi**'s, from the **Gowalia Tank speech**, **8 Aug 1942**.
Statement 3 is wrong: ⚠ Gandhi's paper in **1942** was **Harijan**; **Young India** had ceased in **1932** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Same speech: **"We shall either free India or die in the attempt"** (BPSC 2025).
"Quit India" was suggested by Gandhi in **Harijan** (**April 1942**); coinage credited to **Yusuf Meherally**.

241.s: Who said, "We shall either free India or die in the attempt"?
241.x: Mahatma Gandhi said it in his Gowalia Tank speech of 8 August 1942, the same speech in which he gave the call "Do or Die".
241.tq: It is just "Do or Die" spelt out in full.
xs: **Mahatma Gandhi** said it in his **Gowalia Tank** speech of **8 Aug 1942** — so option **(4)** is correct (BPSC 2025).
In the same speech he gave the call **"Do or Die"** ("Karo ya Maro").
xa: The **AICC, Bombay** ratified the Quit India resolution that day.
The Wardha resolution was **proposed by Nehru**, **seconded by Patel**.

241.s: Operation Zero Hour during the Quit India Movement referred to
o: The pre-dawn arrest of Congress leaders on 9 August 1942
The imposition of a 21-day fast by Gandhi
The formation of Jatiya Sarkar at Tamluk
241.x: Operation Zero Hour was the pre-dawn operation through which Congress leaders were arrested on 9 August 1942.
241.tq: Match an operation name with its precise action and date.
xs: **Operation Zero Hour** was the **pre-dawn arrest of Congress leaders on 9 August 1942** — option **(2)** is correct.
The **fall of Rangoon** (1) was in **March 1942**; **Gandhi's 21-day fast** (3) was in **February 1943**; **Jatiya Sarkar** (4) was at **Tamluk**.
xa: After the arrests the movement became **leaderless and spontaneous**.
**CWC members** were held at **Ahmednagar Fort**.

241.s: Who was the Viceroy of India during the Quit India Movement?
241.x: Lord Linlithgow was the Viceroy of India during the Quit India Movement and directed the colonial response to it.
241.tq: Use the office-holder trap by distinguishing neighbouring Viceroy tenures.
xs: The Viceroy was **Lord Linlithgow** — so option **(4)** is correct.
He called Quit India the **most serious rebellion since 1857**.
xa: Repression: about **10,000 deaths**, floggings, **collective fines**, military control of cities.
Gandhi's **21-day fast** (**February 1943**) at the **Aga Khan Palace** led three members of the **Viceroy's Executive Council** to resign.

241.s:
Consider the following statements about Gandhi’s fast during the Quit India phase:
1. It lasted for 21 days.
2. It began in February 1943.
3. It was undertaken at the Aga Khan Palace against state violence.
4. Three members of the Viceroy’s Executive Council resigned in this context.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
241.x: All four statements are correct. Gandhi undertook a 21-day fast at the Aga Khan Palace from February 1943 in protest against state violence, and three members of the Viceroy’s Executive Council resigned in this context.
241.tq: Check duration, date, place, purpose and consequence as separate factual elements.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
Gandhi's **21-day fast**, **February 1943**, at the **Aga Khan Palace**, was against **state violence**.
Its effect: **three members** of the **Viceroy's Executive Council** resigned.
xa: **Kasturba Gandhi** died in detention at **Poona** (**1944**).
**CWC members** were held at **Ahmednagar Fort**.

241.s: Who among the following organised sabotage and formed the Azad Dasta during the Quit India Movement?
241.x: Jayaprakash Narayan organised sabotage and formed the Azad Dasta during the Quit India Movement.
241.tq: Match a named underground organisation with its organiser.
xs: **Jayaprakash Narayan** organised sabotage and formed the **Azad Dasta** — so option **(2)** is correct (BPSC 2025 key).
**Ram Manohar Lohia** (1) was an underground leader who broadcast on the **Congress Radio**.
**Biju Patnaik** and **Achyut Patwardhan** (3, 4) were other underground figures.
xa: ⚠ **Azad Dasta** = **JP**; **Congress Radio** = **Usha Mehta**.
**Aruna Asaf Ali**: flag-hoisting and underground network.
Sabotage hit bridges, rail tracks, telegraph lines — especially **UP** and **Bihar**.

241.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Aruna Asaf Ali — Flag-hoisting and underground network
Ram Manohar Lohia — Underground leadership and Congress Radio broadcasts
241.x: Jayaprakash Narayan was an underground leader who organised sabotage and formed the Azad Dasta; he was not a member of the Viceroy’s Executive Council.
241.tq: Find the wrong institutional association among otherwise plausible underground activities.
xs: **Jayaprakash Narayan — Viceroy's Executive Council** is wrong: JP organised **sabotage** and formed the **Azad Dasta** — so option **(4)** is the mismatch.
The other pairs are right: **Aruna Asaf Ali** — flag-hoisting; **Lohia** — Congress Radio broadcasts; **Usha Mehta** — **Congress Radio**.
xa: Three members of the **Viceroy's Executive Council** resigned over Gandhi's **21-day fast**.
Other underground figures: **Biju Patnaik**, **Sucheta Kripalani**, **Achyut Patwardhan**, **R.P. Goenka**.

241.s: During the Quit India Movement, sabotage was especially directed against
o: Bridges, railway tracks and telegraph lines
Universities, courts and municipal libraries only
241.x: Underground activists sabotaged bridges, railway tracks and telegraph lines, particularly in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.
241.tq: Identify the infrastructure targets that disrupted colonial administration and communication.
xs: Sabotage targeted **bridges, rail tracks and telegraph lines** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was strongest in **UP** and **Bihar**.
xa: **Jayaprakash Narayan** organised sabotage through the **Azad Dasta**.
Andhra: lines between **Guntur and Vijayawada** torn up; **Chirala** signal wires cut.
Tenali: the **Madras-Puri passenger train** burnt at the station.

241.s: Which one of the following statements about the parallel government at Ballia is correct?
o: It was led by Chittu Pandey and lasted for about a week
It was led by Nana Patil and continued until 1945
It was organised by the Young Congress Socialists on a ward-wise basis
It was called Jatiya Sarkar and functioned until September 1944
241.x: The Ballia parallel government was led by Chittu Pandey in August 1942 and lasted approximately one week. The other descriptions relate to Satara, Tamluk and Ahmedabad respectively.
241.tq: Apply the wrong-leader and swapped-location traps to distinguish parallel governments.
xs: The **Ballia** (UP) parallel government was led by **Chittu Pandey** and lasted **about a week** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Nana Patil** to **1945** (2) is **Satara**; ward-wise **Young Congress Socialists** (3) is **Ahmedabad**; **Jatiya Sarkar** to **Sept 1944** (4) is **Tamluk**.
xa: Ballia (**Aug 1942**) **freed Congress leaders**.
⚠ **Ballia** = shortest; **Satara** = longest.

241.s: Jatiya Sarkar, which undertook cyclone relief, school grants and paddy distribution, was established at
241.x: Jatiya Sarkar was formed at Tamluk in Midnapore, Bengal. Its activities included cyclone relief, school grants and distribution of paddy.
241.tq: Match a distinctive programme of activities with its place of operation.
xs: **Jatiya Sarkar** was set up at **Tamluk in Midnapore**, Bengal — option **(4)** is correct.
It ran **Dec 1942 - Sept 1944**, with cyclone relief, school grants, paddy distribution and **Vidyut Vahinis**.
**Satara** (1) had the **"Prati Sarkar"**; **Ballia** (3) was under **Chittu Pandey**.
xa: Satara (**Y.B. Chavan**, **Nana Patil**) was the longest, mid-**1943** to **1945**.
**Talcher** (Odisha) also had a parallel government in **1942**.

241.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Satara Prati Sarkar is NOT correct?
o: It was the longest-lasting of the parallel governments
It was established at Tamluk and remained active until September 1944
It functioned roughly from the middle of 1943 to 1945
It was associated with Y.B. Chavan and Nana Patil
241.x: The Satara Prati Sarkar was associated with Y.B. Chavan and Nana Patil and functioned from mid-1943 to 1945. Tamluk was the location of Jatiya Sarkar, active from December 1942 to September 1944.
241.tq: Find the swapped place and duration in a not-correctly-matched question.
xs: Satara's Prati Sarkar was **not** at **Tamluk**, and did not end in **September 1944** — so option **(2)** is the incorrect statement.
Tamluk's **Jatiya Sarkar** ran **Dec 1942 - Sept 1944**.
Satara (**Y.B. Chavan**, **Nana Patil**) ran **mid-1943 - 1945** and was the **longest** — (1), (3), (4) are correct.
xa: Satara ran **Nyayadan Mandals** (people's courts), village libraries, prohibition, **"Gandhi marriages"**.
APPSC 2016 asked where **"Prati Sarkar"** was formed — **Satara**.

241.s: The Kurnool (Andhra) Circular, issued on 29 July 1942 during the Quit India Movement, was drafted by whom?
241.x: The Kurnool (Andhra) Circular was drafted by Kala Venkat Rao on 29 July 1942. It was subsequently seized by the police at Kurnool.
241.tq: Use the author–document trap by distinguishing the drafter from other Andhra leaders.
xs: The **Kurnool (Andhra) Circular** (**29 July 1942**) was drafted by **Kala Venkat Rao** — option **(4)** is correct.
It was **seized by police at Kurnool**.
**Mamidipudi Venkatrangayya** (1) led the **Andhra University** resolution; **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** (3) presided over the **APCC meeting at Machilipatnam**.
xa: Pattabhi was jailed at **Ahmednagar Fort** and wrote **"Feathers and Stones"**.
**Tanguturi Prakasam** emerged as Andhra's leading figure.

241.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Place)
a. Tenali
b. Guntur
c. Bhimavaram
d. Kakinada

List-II (Incident)
i. Lawyers passed a resolution demanding Gandhi’s release
ii. Police firing on 13 August 1942
iii. Police firing on 12 August 1942 and burning of the Madras–Puri passenger train
iv. Firing on 17 August 1942 and attack on the Collectorate

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
241.x: Tenali witnessed firing on 12 August and the burning of the Madras–Puri passenger train; Guntur witnessed firing on 13 August; Bhimavaram witnessed firing on 17 August and an attack on the Collectorate; and Kakinada lawyers demanded Gandhi’s release.
241.tq: Start from the sure place–incident pairs and eliminate codes containing a swapped event.
xs: **Tenali – iii**, **Guntur – ii**, **Bhimavaram – iv**, **Kakinada – i** — option **(1)** is correct.
Tenali: firing **12 Aug 1942** (about **9** killed), **Madras-Puri train** burnt; Guntur: firing **13 Aug**.
Bhimavaram: firing **17 Aug** and attack on the **Collectorate**; Kakinada: lawyers demanded **Gandhi's release**.
xa: **Bapatla** railway station burnt; **Chirala** signal wires cut; **Tadepalligudem** post office burnt.
Rail lines between **Guntur and Vijayawada** torn up.

241.s: Pattabhi Sitaramayya was jailed at which place during the Quit India Movement, where he wrote the diary titled ‘Feathers and Stones’?
241.x: Pattabhi Sitaramayya was imprisoned at Ahmednagar Fort and wrote ‘Feathers and Stones’ there.
241.tq: Use the place–work pairing and avoid confusing different colonial prisons.
xs: **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** was jailed at **Ahmednagar Fort**, where he wrote **"Feathers and Stones"** — option **(1)** is correct.
**CWC members** were held at Ahmednagar Fort.
xa: Pattabhi presided over the **APCC meeting** at **Machilipatnam**.
Gandhi was held at the **Aga Khan Palace**; **Kasturba** died at **Poona** (**1944**).

241.s: Why did the Communist Party of India oppose the Quit India Movement in 1942?
o: It considered the movement an exclusively provincial movement in Andhra.
It supported the Muslim League’s demand for Pakistan from the beginning of the war.
It supported the British war effort after Nazi Germany attacked the Soviet Union.
It had already withdrawn from Indian politics after the Civil Disobedience Movement.
241.x: The Communists opposed the Quit India Movement because, after the Nazi attack on the Soviet Union, they backed the British war effort.
241.tq: Identify the cause–attitude link rather than confusing Communist policy with the position of the Muslim League.
xs: The **Communists** backed the British war effort after the **Nazi attack on the USSR** — option **(3)** is correct.
The **CPI ban** was lifted on **23 July 1942**.
xa: The CPI then **lost heavily** in the **1945-46 elections**.
Also stayed away: **Muslim League**, **Hindu Mahasabha** and princely states.

241.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the Communist Party of India after its policy during the Quit India period?
o: It did not contest the elections of 1945–46 owing to the continuation of its ban.
It formed the provincial government in Andhra after the elections of 1945–46.
It won heavily in the elections of 1945–46 because of its support for the movement.
It lost heavily in the elections of 1945–46 after opposing the Quit India Movement.
241.x: The Communist Party of India lost heavily in the 1945–46 elections. Its opposition to the Quit India Movement and support for the British war effort formed the background to its political position during this period.
241.tq: Use the electoral outcome as a chronological consequence of the party’s wartime policy.
xs: The CPI **lost heavily** in the **1945-46 elections** — option **(4)** is correct.
Its ban had been **lifted on 23 July 1942**, so (1) is wrong.
It had **opposed Quit India**, backing the British after the Nazi attack on the **USSR**.
xa: **Muslim League**, **Hindu Mahasabha** and princely states also stayed away.
**Tanguturi Prakasam** emerged as Andhra's leading figure.

241.s:
Consider the following statements about the attitude of political groups and communities towards the Quit India Movement:
1. The Muslim League stayed away from the movement.
2. The Hindu Mahasabha stayed away from the movement.
3. The princely states stayed away from the movement.
4. Muslims generally sheltered activists, and communal clashes did not occur.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
241.x: All four statements are correct. The Muslim League, Hindu Mahasabha and princely states stayed away, while Muslims generally sheltered activists and there were no communal clashes.
241.tq: Test several parallel attitudes together, including the less obvious community-level response.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
The **Muslim League**, **Hindu Mahasabha** and **princely states** stayed away.
**Muslims generally sheltered activists**; there were **no communal clashes**.
xa: The **Communists** opposed the movement; **CPI ban lifted 23 July 1942**.
Muslims were also **exempted** from the Andhra collective fines.

241.s: Which one of the following best expresses the significance of the Quit India Movement?
o: It secured immediate transfer of power before the end of the Second World War.
It was Gandhi’s first mass movement against British rule.
It was confined mainly to constitutional negotiations with the British Government.
It was Gandhi’s final mass movement and demonstrated that independence could not be postponed after the war.
241.x: The Quit India Movement was Gandhi’s final mass movement. It showed that Indian independence could not be postponed after the war.
241.tq: Choose the precise significance statement and reject claims of immediate independence or a merely constitutional campaign.
xs: Quit India was **Gandhi's final mass movement** and showed **independence could not be postponed after the war** — option **(4)**.
Leaders were arrested on **9 August 1942**, so it became **leaderless and spontaneous**, not constitutional (3).
xa: Viceroy **Linlithgow**: the most serious rebellion since **1857**.
AP angle: **"final, decisive event of the freedom struggle in Andhra"**.

241.s: Who emerged as a leading figure in Andhra during the Quit India Movement?
241.x: Tanguturi Prakasam emerged as a leading figure in Andhra during the Quit India Movement.
241.tq: Distinguish the prominent regional figure from leaders associated with particular documents or underground work.
xs: **Tanguturi Prakasam** emerged as Andhra's leading figure during Quit India — option **(4)** is correct.
**Mamidipudi Venkatrangayya** (1) led the **Andhra University** resolution; **Kala Venkat Rao** (3) drafted the **Kurnool Circular**.
xa: **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** presided over the **APCC** at **Machilipatnam**, then was jailed at **Ahmednagar Fort**.
Quit India was the **"final, decisive event of the freedom struggle in Andhra"**.

241.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: B.G. Tilak was associated with “Swaraj is my birthright.”
C.R. Das was associated with “Back to the Vedas.”
Subhas Chandra Bose was associated with “Give me blood… freedom.”
Mahatma Gandhi was associated with “Do or Die.”
