Consider the following statements regarding Patel’s positions after independence:
1. He was the first Deputy Prime Minister of India.
2. He was the first Home Minister of India.
3. He was in charge of the States Department, whose Secretary was V.P. Menon.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
246.x: All three statements are correct. Patel was the first Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister and handled the States Department with V.P. Menon as Secretary.
246.tq: Combine first-office facts with the department–secretary relationship.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Patel was the **first Deputy Prime Minister**, also **Home Minister**.
He was in charge of the **States Department**, Secretary **V.P. Menon**.
xa: He **created** the All India Services (**IAS/IPS**).
Earlier, in the **Interim Government** (**2 September 1946**): Home + I&B.

246.s: The description of the Indian civil service as the ‘steel frame’ of India was used by Patel to emphasise that
o: it was intended only for military administration
it could function without constitutional safeguards
if it bends, the whole structure will collapse
it should be replaced entirely by provincial services
246.x: Patel stated that if the civil service steel frame bends, the whole structure will collapse, stressing its importance to national administration.
246.tq: Complete the distinctive metaphor with its stated consequence.
xs: Patel's **"steel frame"**: **"If it bends, the whole structure will collapse"** — option **(3)**.
He **created** the All India Services (**IAS/IPS**).
xa: He addressed the first IAS probationers at **Metcalfe House, Delhi**, **21 April 1947** — now **Civil Services Day**.
Hence the title **"Patron Saint of Indian Civil Servants"**.

246.s: Patel addressed the first IAS probationers at Metcalfe House, Delhi, on
246.x: Patel addressed the first IAS probationers at Metcalfe House, Delhi, on 21 April 1947; the date is now observed as Civil Services Day.
246.tq: Use the exact date to distinguish the speech from later national commemorations.
xs: Patel addressed the first IAS probationers at **Metcalfe House** on **21 April 1947** — option **(2)**.
This date is now **Civil Services Day**.
⚠ **21 April** is not Patel's birthday — that is **31 October** (Rashtriya Ekta Diwas).
xa: Patel **created** the **IAS/IPS**.
The civil service was his **"steel frame"**.

246.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the difference between Nehru’s and Patel’s positions on Kashmir?
o: Patel took the issue to the United Nations, whereas Nehru favoured immediate military action.
Nehru took the issue to the United Nations, whereas Patel was sceptical and favoured a military solution.
Both opposed referring the issue to the United Nations and favoured diplomacy alone.
Both favoured placing Kashmir under the control of Hyderabad.
246.x: Nehru referred the Kashmir issue to the UN, influenced by idealism and Mountbatten’s advice, while Patel was sceptical and preferred a military solution.
246.tq: Test the reversed comparison between two leaders’ positions.
xs: **Nehru** took Kashmir to the **UN**; **Patel** was **sceptical** and favoured a **military solution** — option **(2)**.
Nehru acted from idealism and on **Mountbatten**'s advice; option (1) swaps the two.
xa: **Hyderabad**: Patel ordered **Operation Polo** (**Sept 1948**).
**China**: Patel warned Nehru after **Tibet** (**7 November 1950**).

246.s: Patel warned Nehru about China in a letter dated
246.x: Patel warned Nehru about China after Tibet in his letter of 7 November 1950.
246.tq: Use the exact date associated with a diplomatic warning.
xs: Patel warned Nehru about **China** after **Tibet** in his letter of **7 November 1950** — option **(1)**.
**26 January 1950** and **15 August 1947** are unrelated to the letter; Patel's birth anniversary is **31 October**.
xa: Other Patel–Nehru issues: **Kashmir** (UN vs military solution), **Hyderabad** (**Operation Polo**, **Sept 1948**).
Patel was the **first Deputy Prime Minister** and **Home Minister**.

246.s: The popular title ‘Iron Man of India’ is chiefly associated with Vallabhbhai Patel’s role in
o: Leading the Civil Disobedience Movement in Gujarat
Drafting the Karachi Resolution on Fundamental Rights
246.x: Patel is popularly called the Iron Man of India for his role in integrating approximately 565 princely states.
246.tq: Match a title with the achievement that explains it.
xs: **"Iron Man of India"** is for **integrating about 565 princely states** — option **(1)**.
⚠ **"Iron Man"** = princely states; **"Patron Saint"** = All India Services.
xa: He ran the **States Department** with **V.P. Menon**.
**"Sardar"** came from **Bardoli (1928)**.

246.s: Why has Vallabhbhai Patel been described as the ‘Patron Saint of Indian Civil Servants’?
o: He abolished the civil services after independence.
He served as the first Governor-General of India.
He created and defended the All India Services.
He introduced provincial elections under the Government of India Act, 1935.
246.x: The description refers to Patel’s role in creating the All India Services and supporting their importance in administration.
246.tq: Infer the title from the institutional contribution associated with it.
xs: Patel **created** the **All India Services** (**IAS/IPS**) — hence **"Patron Saint of Indian Civil Servants"** — option **(3)**.
He called the service the **"steel frame"**: "If it bends, the whole structure will collapse."
He ran the **1937** elections (4) as head of the **Congress Parliamentary Board** — a separate role.
xa: **21 April 1947** Metcalfe House speech → **Civil Services Day**.
⚠ **"Patron Saint"** = All India Services; **"Iron Man"** = princely states.

246.s: Which one of the following statements about the Statue of Unity is NOT correct?
o: It is 182 metres high and is described as the world’s tallest statue.
It was sculpted by Ram V. Sutar and is located in Hyderabad.
It faces the Sardar Sarovar Dam in Narmada district, Gujarat.
It was unveiled in 2018 at Sadhu Bet island near Ekta Nagar.
246.x: The Statue of Unity is in Gujarat, not Hyderabad. It is 182 metres high, was unveiled in 2018, and was sculpted by Ram V. Sutar.
246.tq: Find the wrong location while retaining the other correct details.
xs: The Statue of Unity is **not in Hyderabad** — option **(2)** is the incorrect statement.
It stands at **Sadhu Bet island, Ekta Nagar (Kevadia), Narmada district, Gujarat**, facing the **Sardar Sarovar Dam**.
It is **182 m** (**597 ft**), world's tallest, unveiled **2018**, by sculptor **Ram V. Sutar**.
xa: ⚠ **2018** = Statue unveiled; **2019** = Unity Award instituted.
The **150th birth anniversary** commemoration was launched there on **31 Oct 2024**.

246.s: Rashtriya Ekta Diwas is observed on 31 October because it marks
o: the unveiling of the Statue of Unity
the formation of the Interim Government
246.x: National Unity Day is observed on 31 October, the birth anniversary of Vallabhbhai Patel, who was born on 31 October 1875 at Nadiad.
246.tq: Connect the observance with the person and the exact birth date.
xs: **31 October** is **Patel's birth anniversary** (born **31 October 1875, Nadiad**) — option **(3)**.
The Statue of Unity (1) was unveiled in **2018**, not tied to this date.
xa: ⚠ **21 April** = Civil Services Day, not Patel's birthday.
**Sardar Patel National Unity Award** instituted **2019**.

246.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Sardar Patel National Unity Award?
o: It was instituted in 1947 as a military award carrying a cash prize.
It was instituted in 2019 as the highest civilian award for unity and integrity, with no cash component and not more than three awards in a year.
It was instituted in 2018 exclusively for members of the armed forces.
It is awarded only to civil servants and has no limit on annual awards.
246.x: Instituted in 2019, the award recognises unity and integrity; it includes a medal and citation, carries no cash, and is limited to not more than three recipients annually.
246.tq: Combine institution year, purpose, benefits and annual limit in one precise option.
xs: Instituted in **2019** as the **highest civilian award for unity and integrity**, no cash, not more than **three** a year — option **(2)**.
It carries a **medal + citation**.
⚠ **2018** (3) is the **Statue of Unity**'s year, not the award's.
xa: **Rashtriya Ekta Diwas** = **31 October**.
Statue sculptor: **Ram V. Sutar**.

246.s: Which one of the following persons is associated with the distinction of being regarded as the only other person in India, besides Vallabhbhai Patel, to receive the title ‘Sardar’?
246.x: Sardar Gouthu Latchanna of Srikakulam is said to be the only other person in India to receive the title ‘Sardar’.
246.tq: Use the distinctive person–place association to separate a later Andhra figure from Patel’s associates.
xs: **Sardar Gouthu Latchanna of Srikakulam** is said to be the only other "Sardar" — option **(4)**.
**Mohanlal Pandya** and **Narahari Parikh** (1, 3) worked with Patel at **Kheda**; **V.P. Menon** (2) was **States Department** Secretary.
xa: Patel's own title came at **Bardoli (1928)**.
⚠ Three versions of who conferred Patel's title: Bardoli **women/peasants**, **Sarojini Naidu** (CDI), **Gandhi** (**CGPSC 2011**).

246.s: Who was the Temporary Chairman and first President of the Constituent Assembly?
246.x: Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha, the oldest member, was the temporary chairman when the Constituent Assembly first met on 9 December 1946. Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected permanent President on 11 December.
n: Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha was the Temporary Chairman of the Constituent Assembly. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #104 · pp 193-194]
Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha was the first President of the Constituent Assembly. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #104 · pp 193-194]
xs: **Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha** was the **Temporary Chairman** and **first President** of the Constituent Assembly — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Dr. Rajendra Prasad** was the **Permanent President**.
**Dr. B.R. Ambedkar** chaired the **Drafting Committee**; **Jawaharlal Nehru** the **Union Powers** and **Union Constitution** Committees.
xa: **Sardar Patel** chaired the **Advisory Committee** and the **Provincial Constitution Committee**.
Patel was the **First Deputy Prime Minister** and **Home Minister**; **V.P. Menon** was Secretary of the **States Department**.
In the **Interim Government** (**2 September 1946**) Patel held **Home** + Information & Broadcasting.

246.s: The chairmanship of which committee was held by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel?
246.x: Sardar Patel chaired the Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights and Minorities. Nehru chaired the Union Powers and Union Constitution Committees and Ambedkar the Drafting Committee.
246.tq: Recall the chairman of each committee.
n: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #104 · pp 193-194]
Jawaharlal Nehru was the Chairman of the Union Powers Committee. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #104 · pp 193-194]
Jawaharlal Nehru was the Chairman of the Union Constitution Committee. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #104 · pp 193-194]
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel was the Chairman of the Advisory Committee. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #104 · pp 193-194]
xs: **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel** chaired the **Advisory Committee** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It was the **Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities, Tribal and Excluded Areas**.
**Nehru** chaired the **Union Powers** and **Union Constitution** Committees; **Ambedkar** the **Drafting Committee**.
xa: Patel also chaired the **Provincial Constitution Committee**.
**Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha** = Temporary Chairman; **Dr. Rajendra Prasad** = Permanent President.
Patel addressed the first IAS probationers at **Metcalfe House** on **21 April 1947** — now **Civil Services Day**.
He called the civil service the "**steel frame**".

247.s: The movement in Hyderabad demanding merger with the Indian Union was led by:
247.x: Swami Ramananda Theertha led the Join Indian Union movement through the Hyderabad State Congress.
247.tq: Use the state-specific leader association to separate Hyderabad from other Praja Mandal movements.
xs: The "**Join Indian Union**" movement in Hyderabad was led by **Swami Ramananda Theertha** through the **Hyderabad State Congress** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Vijay Singh Pathik** led the **Bijolia** movement in **Rajasthan**; **Sewa Singh Thikriwala** led the **Riyasti Praja Mandal** in **Punjab (Patiala)**.
**Sarangadhar Das** led the **Dhenkanal Praja Mandal** in **Orissa**.
xa: The **Hyderabad State Congress** was formed in **1938**.
⚠ **1927** = **AISPC** founded **and** **Ittehad-ul-Muslimeen** emerged; **1938** = Hyderabad State Congress.
The **Razakars**, led by **Kasim Razvi**, were the militia of the **MIM**; their violence forced **Operation Polo (1948)**.

247.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Leader)
a. Vijay Singh Pathik
b. Sewa Singh Thikriwala
c. Sarangadhar Das
d. Swami Ramananda Tirtha

List-II (State or movement)
i. Hyderabad State Congress
ii. Rajasthan
iii. Orissa
iv. Punjab

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
247.x: Vijay Singh Pathik was associated with Rajasthan, Sewa Singh Thikriwala with Punjab, Sarangadhar Das with Orissa, and Swami Ramananda Tirtha with the Hyderabad State Congress.
247.tq: Start from the sure leader–movement pair and eliminate codes with inconsistent state associations.
xs: Correct pairs: **a–ii, b–iv, c–iii, d–i** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Vijay Singh Pathik** – **Rajasthan** (Bijolia; Rajasthan Seva Sangh); **Sewa Singh Thikriwala** – **Punjab** (Patiala; Riyasti Praja Mandal).
**Sarangadhar Das** – **Orissa** (Dhenkanal Praja Mandal); **Swami Ramananda Tirtha** – **Hyderabad State Congress** (**1938**).
xa: Ramananda Tirtha led the **"Join Indian Union"** movement in Hyderabad (APPSC G2 2012 key).
The **AISPC** (founded **1927**) coordinated these people's movements against autocratic rule.
**Telangana armed struggle (1946-51)**: led by the **Communists and the Andhra Mahasabha**, triggered by the killing of **Doddi Komaraiah (1946)**.

247.s:
Arrange the following developments in the chronological order in which the Congress policy towards the princely states evolved:
A. Tripuri Congress dropped the policy of non-interference.
B. Haripura Congress declared that Purna Swaraj covered the states.
C. Congress followed a policy of non-interference in the internal affairs of states.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
247.x: Congress first followed non-interference in the 1920s, adopted the Haripura position in 1938, and at Tripuri in 1939 openly backed the movements in the states.
247.tq: Use the years attached to the policy stages: 1920s, 1938 and 1939.
xs: The order is **C, B, A** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**C**: in the **1920s** Congress followed **non-interference** in the internal affairs of states.
**B**: **Haripura (1938)** declared that **Purna Swaraj** covered the states, but struggles were to be waged by the states' own people.
**A**: **Tripuri (1939)** dropped non-interference and backed the movements openly.
xa: **Nehru** became president of the **AISPC** in **1939**, the same year as Tripuri.
The **Indian Independence Act 1947** let princely states join India, join Pakistan or stay independent.
The **Hyderabad State Congress** was founded in **1938**, the Haripura year.

247.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the office-holders of the States Department?
o: V.P. Menon as head and Sardar Patel as Secretary
Jawaharlal Nehru as head and C.P. Ramaswami Iyer as negotiator
Sardar Patel as head and V.P. Menon as Secretary and chief negotiator
Rajendra Prasad as head and Hamidullah Khan as Secretary
247.x: Sardar Patel, the Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister, headed the States Department. V.P. Menon served as its Secretary and chief negotiator.
247.tq: Use the authority–subordinate role distinction to defeat a swapped-office option.
xs: **Sardar Patel** headed the **States Department**, with **V.P. Menon** as **Secretary and chief negotiator** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Option (1) reverses the roles; **C.P. Ramaswami Iyer** was the **Dewan of Travancore** and **Hamidullah Khan** the **Nawab of Bhopal**.
xa: Patel was **Deputy PM and Home Minister**, called the "**Iron Man of India**".
Menon wrote "**The Story of the Integration of the Indian States**".
Menon's four phases: **Extinction**, **Consolidation into unions**, **Democratisation**, **Abolition of privy purses**.

247.s: Under the Indian Independence Act, 1947, a princely state could:
o: Transfer its decision to the United Nations
Join India, join Pakistan or remain independent
247.x: The Indian Independence Act, 1947, allowed princely states to join India, join Pakistan or remain independent.
247.tq: Test the complete three-way choice instead of confusing legal options with the later political outcome.
xs: Under the **Indian Independence Act 1947**, a princely state could **join India, join Pakistan or remain independent** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The Act gave all three choices, so "India only" or "Pakistan only" is wrong.
xa: About **562** princely states were involved.
Accession was through the **Instrument of Accession**, ceding **Defence, External Affairs and Communications**.
Hold-outs on **15 August 1947**: **Kashmir, Hyderabad and Junagadh**.

247.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the subjects ceded to the Centre through the Instrument of Accession?
247.x: The Instrument of Accession initially transferred Defence, External Affairs and Communications to the Centre. Internal autonomy was retained by the rulers at that stage.
247.tq: Find the exception by separating the three ceded subjects from the retained internal autonomy.
xs: **Internal administration** was NOT ceded: rulers kept **internal autonomy** at first — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **Instrument of Accession** ceded only **Defence, External Affairs and Communications** to the Centre.
xa: In return the rulers received **privy purses**, guaranteed annual payments for accession.
Privy purses and royal titles were abolished by the **26th Amendment Act (1971)**, which omitted **Articles 291 and 362**.
**Kashmir** signed its IoA on **26 Oct 1947** after the tribal invasion.

247.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the authorship and authors of the two works associated with Hyderabad and state integration?
o: The Story of the Integration of the Indian States — V.P. Menon; Hyderabad in Retrospect — Laik Ali
The Story of the Integration of the Indian States — Sardar Patel; Hyderabad in Retrospect — Moin Nawaz Jung
The Story of the Integration of the Indian States — Laik Ali; Hyderabad in Retrospect — V.P. Menon
The Story of the Integration of the Indian States — Jawaharlal Nehru; Hyderabad in Retrospect — C.P. Ramaswami Iyer
247.x: V.P. Menon wrote The Story of the Integration of the Indian States. Hyderabad in Retrospect was written by Laik Ali, the last Prime Minister of Hyderabad.
247.tq: Use author–work matching and guard against swapping the two titles.
xs: "**The Story of the Integration of the Indian States**" is by **V.P. Menon**; "**Hyderabad in Retrospect**" is by **Laik Ali** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Laik Ali** was the **last Prime Minister of Hyderabad**; **Moin Nawaz Jung** led the Nizam's delegation to the **UN Security Council (1948)**.
xa: V.P. Menon was **Secretary and chief negotiator** of the **States Department** under **Sardar Patel**.
Hyderabad questions (**Standstill Agreement**, **Razvi**, **Laik Ali**, **Moin Nawaz Jung**) recur in APPSC.
**Burgula Ramakrishna Rao** became the **first elected CM** of Hyderabad State in **1952**.

247.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the outcome in Junagadh in 1947–48?
o: The Nawab acceded to Pakistan and continued to rule after the plebiscite
The Nawab acceded to India and a plebiscite confirmed accession to Pakistan
The Nawab acceded to Pakistan, fled after an economic blockade, and a plebiscite was held in February 1948
The Nawab remained independent and joined the Rajasthan Union in 1949
247.x: Junagadh’s Nawab acceded to Pakistan in September 1947. Following an economic blockade and his flight, a plebiscite was held in February 1948 in favour of India.
247.tq: Test the sequence of ruler, decision, crisis and final settlement rather than recalling a single date.
xs: Junagadh's Nawab **acceded to Pakistan**, **fled after an economic blockade**, and a **plebiscite in February 1948** went for India — so option **(3)** is correct.
The Nawab acceded to Pakistan in **Sept 1947**; India took control in **Nov 1947**, and the plebiscite favoured **India**, not Pakistan.
The **Arzi Hukumat** added pressure along with the blockade.
xa: Nawab: **Mahabat Khanji III**; Dewan: **Shah Nawaz Bhutto**.
⚠ **Junagadh** = **plebiscite**; **Kashmir** = **IoA 26 Oct 1947**; **Hyderabad** = **Operation Polo**.
The **Rajasthan Union** was one of the unions formed in Menon's consolidation phase, with **Saurashtra**, **PEPSU** and **Madhya Bharat**.

247.s: Which one of the following statements about the Travancore and Jodhpur issues is correct?
o: The Dewan of Travancore declared independence, while Jinnah attempted to attract the Maharaja of Jodhpur
The Maharaja of Travancore negotiated with the United Nations, while Patel attracted Jodhpur to Pakistan
Travancore joined Pakistan and Jodhpur remained independent
Both states were merged into Hyderabad before accession
247.x: Dewan C.P. Ramaswami Iyer declared Travancore’s independence, partly in the context of its thorium wealth. Maharaja Hanwant Singh of Jodhpur was tempted by Jinnah.
247.tq: Keep separate the two problem states and identify the correct person–state association.
xs: **Travancore's Dewan declared independence**, and **Jinnah** tried to attract the **Maharaja of Jodhpur** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Dewan **C.P. Ramaswami Iyer** declared Travancore independent, banking on its **thorium** wealth; Travancore finally **joined India without conditions**.
Jodhpur's Maharaja **Hanwant Singh** was tempted by Jinnah, not by Patel.
xa: Some notes list **Travancore** as a fourth hold-out besides **Kashmir, Hyderabad and Junagadh**.
**Bhopal** (Nawab **Hamidullah Khan**) delayed and merged in **1949**.
Patel's method: persuasion, patriotic appeals, threat of force; **privy purses** + internal autonomy offered.

247.s: The accession of Jammu and Kashmir in the context of the first India–Pakistan conflict took place on:
247.x: Jammu and Kashmir acceded to India on 26 October 1947. The UN ceasefire in the conflict came into effect later, on 1 January 1949.
247.tq: Separate the date of accession from the later date of the UN ceasefire.
xs: **Jammu and Kashmir** signed the **Instrument of Accession** on **26 October 1947** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Sequence: **tribal invasion** → **IoA** → troops airlifted to **Srinagar** → **First Indo-Pak war** → **UN ceasefire Jan 1949**.
**15 August 1947** was when Kashmir was still a hold-out, with **Hyderabad and Junagadh**.
xa: Ruler: Maharaja **Hari Singh**.
**Nehru** took Kashmir to the **UN**; **Patel** preferred a military solution.
The **Delhi Agreement (1952)** concerned Kashmir.

247.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Hyderabad at the time of its integration:
1. Mir Osman Ali Khan was the seventh Nizam.
2. The ruling dynasty was the Asaf Jahi dynasty.
3. Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah I founded the Asaf Jahi dynasty in 1724.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
247.x: All three statements are correct. Mir Osman Ali Khan was the seventh Nizam, the ruling house was Asaf Jahi, and Asaf Jah I founded it in 1724.
247.tq: Combine ruler, dynasty and foundation-year facts in one coded statement question.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
1: **Mir Osman Ali Khan** was the **7th Nizam**, the last Nizam.
2: the ruling dynasty at integration was the **Asaf Jahi** (Nizams).
3: **Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah I** founded the Asaf Jahi dynasty in **1724**.
xa: Hyderabad was the **largest and richest** princely state, **1st in population** (**1,63,38,534** in **1951**).
⚠ Exam trap: **Asaf Jahi** vs **Qutb Shahi**.
After **1950** Hyderabad was a **Part B state** with the Nizam as **Rajpramukh**.

247.s: Which of the following statements about the Nizam’s position before Operation Polo is correct?
o: He transferred Hyderabad to the United Nations administration.
He sought either independence or accession to Pakistan.
He accepted immediate accession to India without conditions.
He formally merged Hyderabad with Bombay Province in 1947.
247.x: Mir Osman Ali Khan wanted Hyderabad to remain independent or accede to Pakistan, while India suspected secret dealings between Hyderabad and Pakistan.
247.tq: Distinguish the Nizam’s political objective from the eventual outcome of accession to India.
xs: **Mir Osman Ali Khan** wanted **independence or accession to Pakistan** — so option **(2)** is correct.
India suspected secret deals with **Pakistan**; he even sought an independent "**Dominion of Hyderabad**".
Hyderabad stayed outside India about **13 months**, so there was no immediate accession; it was split up only on **1 November 1956**.
xa: The Nizam banned **Indian currency** and imported arms from **Pakistan**.
The **Standstill Agreement** was signed on **29 November 1947** for **one year**.
**Moin Nawaz Jung** led the Nizam's delegation to the **UN Security Council (1948)**.

247.s: The Standstill Agreement between Hyderabad and the Government of India was intended primarily to:
o: Maintain existing arrangements for one year while negotiations continued
Transfer all administrative powers to the Indian Army
Create the Dominion of Hyderabad as an independent country
Provide for the immediate abolition of the Nizam’s office
247.x: The Agreement was for one year and maintained existing arrangements with India while discussions regarding Hyderabad’s future continued.
247.tq: Identify the practical purpose of an agreement instead of confusing it with the final accession arrangement.
xs: The **Standstill Agreement** kept **existing arrangements with India** for **one year** while talks went on — so option **(1)** is correct.
It did not create a "**Dominion of Hyderabad**" — that was the Nizam's own aim in defiance of it.
xa: Signed **29 November 1947** (APPSC G2 2012 key); the Nizam's defiance continued.
Violations: banning **Indian currency** and importing arms from **Pakistan**.
The deadlock ended with **Operation Polo** (**13-17 September 1948**).

247.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Hyderabad among the princely states at the time of integration?
o: It ranked first in area but last in population.
It was the largest and richest princely state and ranked first in population.
It was the smallest and least populous princely state.
It was the only princely state ruled by a Hindu dynasty.
247.x: Hyderabad was regarded as the largest and richest princely state and ranked first in population among the princely states.
247.tq: Use the comparative descriptors together; do not reverse size, wealth and population rankings.
xs: Hyderabad was the **largest and richest** princely state and **ranked first in population** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Its population was **1,63,38,534** in **1951**.
It was ruled by the **Asaf Jahi** Nizams, so "Hindu dynasty" is wrong.
xa: Last Nizam: **Mir Osman Ali Khan**, the **7th Nizam**.
Asaf Jahi dynasty founded by **Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah I** in **1724**.
On **1 November 1956** it was split: Telugu districts to **Andhra Pradesh**, **Marathwada** to **Bombay**, **Raichur/Gulbarga** to **Mysore**.

247.s: Who led the Nizam’s delegation to the United Nations Security Council in 1948?
247.x: Moin Nawaz Jung led the Nizam’s delegation to the United Nations Security Council in 1948.
247.tq: Distinguish the Hyderabad diplomat from the Prime Minister, Dewan and Indian negotiator names.
xs: **Moin Nawaz Jung** led the Nizam's delegation to the **UN Security Council** in **1948** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**V.P. Menon** was India's chief negotiator; **Laik Ali** was the **last Prime Minister of Hyderabad**; **Shah Nawaz Bhutto** was **Dewan of Junagadh**.
xa: This is an **APPSC G2 2012** key.
Laik Ali wrote "**Hyderabad in Retrospect**".
The Nizam's army chief was **Maj. Gen. El Edroos**.

247.s: Operation Polo, also known as the Hyderabad Police Action, was conducted during which period?
247.x: Operation Polo was conducted from 13 to 17 September 1948, ending with the surrender and accession of the Nizam.
247.tq: Use the exact date range to distinguish the operation from the Standstill Agreement and later reorganisation.
xs: **Operation Polo** ran from **13-17 September 1948** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It lasted about **four to five days** and ended with the Nizam's surrender and accession on **17 September 1948**.
**29 November 1947** was the **Standstill Agreement**; **1 November 1956** was the dissolution of Hyderabad State.
xa: Indian commander: **Maj. Gen. J.N. Chaudhuri**, later **Military Governor**.
**17 September 1948** ended Nizam rule over **Telangana**.
⚠ **Operation Polo** (Hyderabad 1948) vs **Operation Vijay** (Goa 1961).

247.s:
Consider the following statements about the Telangana armed struggle:
1. It was a peasant revolt (1946-51) led by the Communists and the Andhra Mahasabha.
2. It was directed against the Nizam, the deshmukhs and later the Razakars.
3. It was withdrawn in October 1948, right after Operation Polo.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
247.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Communists and the Andhra Mahasabha led the 1946-51 revolt. Statement 2 is correct: it targeted the Nizam, the deshmukhs and later the Razakars. Statement 3 is wrong: after the Indian Army put down the armed squads, the struggle was withdrawn in October 1951, not 1948. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' leaves out statement 2, and options with 3 are wrong.
247.tq: Telangana struggle = 1946 to Oct 1951; it outlasted Operation Polo (1948).
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — so option **(2) 1 and 2 only** is correct.
1 correct: a **peasant revolt (1946-51)** led by the **Communists and the Andhra Mahasabha**.
2 correct: directed against the **Nizam**, the **deshmukhs** and later the **Razakars**.
3 wrong: it was withdrawn in **October 1951**, not 1948, after the Indian Army put down the armed squads.
xa: Trigger: killing of **Doddi Komaraiah (1946)**.
Unrest + Razakar violence → **Operation Polo (1948)**.
The Razakars were the MIM militia led by **Kasim Razvi**.

247.s: The immediate incident that set off the Telangana armed struggle was the killing of:
247.x: The killing of Doddi Komaraiah in 1946 helped set off the Telangana armed struggle.
247.tq: Match the triggering incident with the individual involved rather than a later political leader.
xs: The killing of **Doddi Komaraiah** in **1946** set off the **Telangana armed struggle** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Moin Nawaz Jung** led the Nizam's UN delegation; **Laik Ali** was the last PM of Hyderabad.
xa: The revolt (**1946-51**) was led by the **Communists and the Andhra Mahasabha**.
It was against the **Nizam**, the **deshmukhs** and later the **Razakars**.
Withdrawn in **October 1951**.

247.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Ittehad-ul-Muslimeen emerged in 1927.
2. The Razakars were the militant volunteer force of the MIM.
3. The Razakars were led by Laik Ali.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
247.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Ittehad-ul-Muslimeen emerged in 1927 (APPSC G2 2008 key) and the Razakars were its militia. Statement 3 is wrong: the Razakars were led by Kasim (Qasim) Razvi; Laik Ali was the last Prime Minister of Hyderabad. A leaves out statement 2; C and D include statement 3.
247.tq: Razakar leader = Kasim Razvi; last Hyderabad PM = Laik Ali.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — so option **(2) 1 and 2 only** is correct.
1 correct: the **Ittehad-ul-Muslimeen** emerged in **1927** (APPSC G2 2008 key).
2 correct: the **Razakars** were the militant volunteer force of the **MIM**.
3 wrong: the Razakars were led by **Kasim (Qasim) Razvi**; **Laik Ali** was the last PM of Hyderabad.
xa: ⚠ **1927** = AISPC founded **and** Ittehad-ul-Muslimeen emerged.
Razakar violence forced military action (APHQ 2011 key).
They also targeted the **Telangana armed struggle**.

247.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Operation Polo — Hyderabad, 1948 — Maj. Gen. J.N. Chaudhuri
Operation Polo — Goa, 1961 — Maj. Gen. K.P. Candeth
Operation Vijay — Hyderabad, 1948 — Maj. Gen. El Edroos
Operation Vijay — Junagadh, 1947 — Maj. Gen. J.N. Chaudhuri
247.x: Operation Polo (Hyderabad, 13-17 Sept 1948) was led by Maj. Gen. J.N. Chaudhuri, who then became Military Governor. Operation Vijay (Goa, Dec 1961) was led by K.P. Candeth; El Edroos was the Nizam's army chief; Junagadh was settled by a plebiscite, not a military operation.
247.tq: Polo = Hyderabad 1948 (Chaudhuri); Vijay = Goa 1961 (Candeth).
xs: **Operation Polo — Hyderabad, 1948 — Maj. Gen. J.N. Chaudhuri** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Operation Vijay** was in **Goa (December 1961)**, led by **Maj. Gen. K.P. Candeth**.
**El Edroos** was the **Nizam's army chief**; **Junagadh** was settled by a **plebiscite**, not an operation.
xa: Chaudhuri later became **Military Governor** of Hyderabad.
⚠ **Chaudhuri** = Indian commander (Polo); **El Edroos** = Nizam's army chief; **Candeth** = Goa (Vijay).
Operation Vijay marked the **end of European colonial rule in India**.

247.s: On 1 November 1956, which of the following correctly describes the reorganisation of Hyderabad State?
o: Hyderabad became a separate Union Territory with all its former districts.
All of Hyderabad State was merged into Andhra Pradesh.
Telugu districts went to Mysore, while Marathwada went to Andhra Pradesh.
Telugu districts went to Andhra Pradesh, Marathwada to Bombay, and Raichur and Gulbarga to Mysore.
247.x: On 1 November 1956, the Telugu-speaking districts were transferred to Andhra Pradesh, Marathwada to Bombay State, and Raichur and Gulbarga to Mysore State.
247.tq: Match each regional subdivision with its correct destination in the States Reorganisation process.
xs: On **1 November 1956**: **Telugu districts** → **Andhra Pradesh**, **Marathwada** → **Bombay**, **Raichur and Gulbarga** → **Mysore** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The split followed the **SRC** recommendations, so Hyderabad was neither kept whole nor merged entirely into AP.
xa: Before that, Hyderabad was a **Part B state (1950-56)** with the Nizam as **Rajpramukh**.
Hyderabad's Telugu districts joined **Andhra State** in **1956** to form Andhra Pradesh.
**Yanam** (**Puducherry**) sits inside AP.

247.s: Who was the first elected Chief Minister of Hyderabad State (1952)?
247.x: Burgula Ramakrishna Rao became the first elected CM of Hyderabad State in 1952. J.N. Chaudhuri was the Military Governor after Operation Polo; Prakasam was the first CM of Andhra State (1953); Ramananda Tirtha led the Hyderabad State Congress.
247.tq: Hyderabad State CM 1952 = Burgula; Andhra State CM 1953 = Prakasam.
xs: **Burgula Ramakrishna Rao** became the **first elected CM** of Hyderabad State in **1952** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**J.N. Chaudhuri** was **Military Governor** after Operation Polo; **Swami Ramananda Tirtha** led the **Hyderabad State Congress**.
xa: Hyderabad was a **Part B state (1950-56)** with the Nizam as **Rajpramukh**.
The State was dissolved on **1 November 1956**.
Hyderabad ranked **1st in population** among princely states (**1,63,38,534** in **1951**).

247.s:
Arrange the following phases of integration described by V.P. Menon in the chronological order:
A. Democratisation
B. Abolition of privy purses
C. Extinction of small states through merger into provinces
D. Consolidation into unions
247.x: Menon’s four phases were extinction, consolidation into unions, democratisation and finally abolition of privy purses.
247.tq: Fix the first phase as extinction and the final phase as abolition, then arrange the middle stages.
xs: Menon's order: **C, D, A, B** — so option **(1)** is correct.
(1) **Extinction**: **216** small states merged into provinces; (2) **Consolidation into unions**.
(3) **Democratisation** of services, judiciary, legislatures; (4) **Abolition of privy purses**.
xa: Unions formed: **Saurashtra** (Kathiawar states), **Rajasthan Union**, **PEPSU**, **Madhya Bharat**.
Privy purses were abolished by the **26th Amendment (1971)**.
Menon wrote "**The Story of the Integration of the Indian States**".

247.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Privy purses and royal titles were abolished by the 26th Amendment Act, 1971.
2. The amendment that abolished privy purses omitted Articles 291 and 362.
3. The office of Rajpramukh was ended by the 42nd Amendment, 1976.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
247.x: Statement 1 is correct: the 26th Amendment Act, 1971 (Indira Gandhi) abolished privy purses and royal titles. Statement 2 is correct: it omitted Articles 291 and 362. Statement 3 is wrong: the Rajpramukh office ended with the 7th Amendment, 1956. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses statement 2, and the options with 3 are wrong.
247.tq: 26th (1971) = privy purses, Arts 291 & 362; 7th (1956) = Rajpramukhs gone.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — so option **(2) 1 and 2 only** is correct.
1 correct: the **26th Amendment Act, 1971** (**Indira Gandhi**) abolished **privy purses and royal titles**.
2 correct: it omitted **Articles 291 and 362**.
3 wrong: the Rajpramukh office ended with the **7th Amendment, 1956**.
xa: ⚠ **26th (1971)** = privy purses; **7th (1956)** = Rajpramukhs.
Privy purses were guaranteed annual payments to rulers for accession.
Abolition of privy purses was Menon's **fourth phase**.

247.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Part A, Part B, Part C and Part D classification in 1950?
o: Part A—former Governor’s provinces; Part B—former princely states or unions with Rajpramukhs; Part C—former Chief Commissioners’ provinces and some princely states; Part D—Andaman and Nicobar Islands
Part A—Chief Commissioners’ provinces; Part B—Andaman and Nicobar Islands; Part C—Governor’s provinces; Part D—princely unions
Part A—former princely states; Part B—former Governor’s provinces; Part C—foreign territories; Part D—Hyderabad
Part A—princely unions; Part B—Governor’s provinces; Part C—Andaman and Nicobar Islands; Part D—Chief Commissioners’ provinces
247.x: Part A comprised former Governor’s provinces; Part B comprised former princely states or unions headed by Rajpramukhs; Part C included former Chief Commissioners’ provinces and some princely states; Part D consisted of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
247.tq: Read the classification as a four-column comparison and eliminate options with shifted categories.
xs: **Part A** = former **Governor's provinces**; **Part B** = princely states/unions with **Rajpramukhs**; **Part C** = **Chief Commissioner's provinces** and some princely states; **Part D** = **Andaman and Nicobar Islands** — option **(1)**.
The other options shuffle these categories.
xa: Hyderabad was a **Part B state (1950-56)** with the Nizam as Rajpramukh.
The **7th Amendment (1956)** ended the office of **Rajpramukh**.
Unions like **Saurashtra**, **Rajasthan Union**, **PEPSU**, **Madhya Bharat** were consolidated princely states.

247.s: The Portuguese surrender in December 1961 marked the:
o: end of European colonial rule in India
integration of Hyderabad into the Indian Union
beginning of French rule in India
247.x: The Portuguese surrender in December 1961 marked the end of European colonial rule in India.
247.tq: Identify the significance of an event rather than merely recalling its date.
xs: The **Portuguese surrender (December 1961)** marked the **end of European colonial rule in India** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It came through **Operation Vijay**, led by **Maj. Gen. K.P. Candeth**, freeing **Goa, Daman and Diu**.
Hyderabad was integrated by **Operation Polo (1948)**.
xa: **Goa** became a full state in **1987**.
**France** handed over its possessions in **1954**.
⚠ Operation **Vijay** (Goa 1961) vs Operation **Polo** (Hyderabad 1948).

247.s:
Consider the following statements about the liberation of Goa:
1. It was achieved through Operation Vijay in December 1961.
2. Operation Vijay was led by Maj. Gen. J.N. Chaudhuri.
3. Goa became a full state in 1987.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
247.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: Operation Vijay (December 1961) freed Goa, Daman and Diu, and Goa became a full state in 1987. Statement 2 is wrong: Operation Vijay was led by Maj. Gen. K.P. Candeth; J.N. Chaudhuri led Operation Polo in Hyderabad. A leaves out statement 3; C and D include statement 2.
247.tq: Vijay = Goa 1961, Candeth; statehood 1987.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — so option **(2) 1 and 3 only** is correct.
1 correct: Goa was freed by **Operation Vijay** in **December 1961**.
2 wrong: Operation Vijay was led by **Maj. Gen. K.P. Candeth**; **J.N. Chaudhuri** led **Operation Polo**.
3 correct: **Goa** became a full state in **1987**.
xa: The Portuguese surrender marked the **end of European colonial rule in India**.
Portugal also held **Dadra and Nagar Haveli**.
French possessions were handed over in **1954**.

247.s: Which one of the following correctly states the method associated with each of the three difficult cases of princely-state integration?
o: Junagadh—police action; Hyderabad—Instrument of Accession; Kashmir—plebiscite
Junagadh—plebiscite; Hyderabad—police action; Kashmir—Instrument of Accession followed by war
Junagadh—Instrument of Accession; Hyderabad—plebiscite; Kashmir—police action
247.x: Junagadh was resolved through a plebiscite, Hyderabad through police action, and Kashmir through an Instrument of Accession followed by war.
247.tq: Compare the three cases by method, avoiding the reversal of closely related integration terms.
xs: **Junagadh — plebiscite**; **Hyderabad — police action**; **Kashmir — Instrument of Accession followed by war** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Junagadh's plebiscite was in **Feb 1948**; Hyderabad's **Operation Polo** in **Sept 1948**; Kashmir's IoA on **26 Oct 1947**.
xa: These three had not signed by **15 August 1947**.
Kashmir war ended with the **UN ceasefire Jan 1949**.
**Nehru** took Kashmir to the **UN**; **Patel** preferred a military solution.

247.s: Yanam’s presence within Andhra Pradesh is best described as an example of:
o: a district of Telangana transferred to Puducherry
a former Portuguese colony forming part of Goa State
a Union Territory created under the Twelfth Amendment
a French-origin enclave inside Andhra Pradesh administered by Puducherry Union Territory
247.x: Yanam is a French-origin enclave located inside Andhra Pradesh’s Godavari delta, but it is administered as part of the Puducherry Union Territory.
247.tq: Combine geographical location with constitutional administration to solve the enclave question.
xs: **Yanam** is a **French-origin enclave inside Andhra Pradesh administered by Puducherry** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Yanam was among **France**'s possessions (**Pondicherry, Karaikal, Mahe, Yanam, Chandernagore**), handed over in **1954**.
It was never **Portuguese**: Portugal held **Goa, Daman, Diu** and **Dadra and Nagar Haveli**.
xa: Portuguese possessions came by **Operation Vijay** (**December 1961**), led by **Maj. Gen. K.P. Candeth**.
**Goa, Daman and Diu (1961)** = last European possessions freed; **Goa** became a full state in **1987**.
AP angle: Hyderabad's Telugu districts joined **Andhra State** in **1956** to form Andhra Pradesh.

248.s: The C.R. Formula was authored by:
248.x: The C.R. Formula was proposed by C. Rajagopalachari in 1944. It was not a proposal of Lord Wavell.
248.tq: Use the author–proposal association and reject the look-alike attribution.
xs: The **C.R. Formula (1944)** was authored by **C. Rajagopalachari** — so option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ Some notes wrongly credit **Lord Wavell**; Wavell's own proposal was the **Wavell Plan (1945)**.
**Bhulabhai Desai** is linked to the **Desai-Liaquat Pact (1945)**; **Maulana Azad** led the Congress at **Simla**.
xa: It proposed a post-war **plebiscite** in contiguous Muslim-majority areas (NW and NE).
**Gandhi-Jinnah talks** in Bombay (**9-27 Sept 1944**) on its basis failed.
Rejected by both Congress and League: **Jinnah** wanted only Muslims to vote and **no common centre**.

248.s: Which one of the following was NOT included in the C.R. Formula?
o: Only Muslims should vote in the plebiscite and there should be no common centre.
A plebiscite should be held in contiguous Muslim-majority areas after the war.
The Muslim League should support the demand for independence and cooperate in an interim government.
Defence, commerce and communications should be governed through joint agreements in case of separation.
248.x: The C.R. Formula proposed a plebiscite and joint agreements after separation, but Jinnah demanded that only Muslims should vote and that there should be no common centre. Those demands were not part of the Formula itself.
248.tq: Separate the original proposal from the later objections of one negotiating party.
xs: "**Only Muslims should vote** and **no common centre**" was NOT in the C.R. Formula — it was **Jinnah's** demand in rejecting it — so option **(1)** is correct.

The Formula did include: League backing independence and joining an **interim government**; a post-war **plebiscite** in contiguous Muslim-majority areas; joint agreements on **defence, commerce and communications** if separated.
xa: Author: **C. Rajagopalachari**, **1944**.
**Gandhi-Jinnah talks** in Bombay (**9-27 Sept 1944**) failed.
The League had already adopted "**Divide and Quit**" at **Karachi (Dec 1943)**.

248.s: The Desai-Liaquat Pact proposed an interim government at the Centre consisting of:
o: Equal numbers of Congress and League nominees, with 20 per cent representation for minorities
Equal numbers of caste Hindus and Muslims, with no minority representation
A majority of League nominees and 20 per cent Congress representation
Representatives nominated exclusively by the Viceroy
248.x: The Pact proposed equal numbers of Congress and Muslim League nominees, along with 20 per cent representation for minorities. It was never formally accepted.
248.tq: Test the composition formula by separating equal representation from the minority quota.
xs: The **Desai-Liaquat Pact** proposed **equal numbers of Congress and League nominees**, plus **20%** for **minorities** — so option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ "Equal caste Hindus and Muslims" was the **Wavell Plan**'s formula, not this Pact.
xa: Signed by **Bhulabhai Desai** (Congress, **Central Legislative Assembly**) and **Liaquat Ali Khan** (League), **1945**.
It was **never formally accepted**.
Sequence: **C.R. Formula (1944)** → **Desai-Liaquat Pact (Jan 1945)** → **Wavell Plan / Simla (June-July 1945)**.

248.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the C.R. Formula:
1. Gandhi accepted it as the basis for the Gandhi-Jinnah talks.
2. It proposed a plebiscite in contiguous Muslim-majority areas in the north-west and north-east.
3. Both the Congress and the Muslim League ultimately accepted it without reservation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
248.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Gandhi-Jinnah talks (Bombay, 9-27 Sept 1944) were held on the basis of the C.R. Formula, which proposed a post-war plebiscite in contiguous Muslim-majority areas of the north-west and north-east. Statement 3 is wrong: both the Congress and the League rejected it, Jinnah wanting only Muslims to vote and no common centre.
248.tq: Test acceptance of a proposal separately from its use as a negotiating basis.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — so option **(1) 1 and 2 only** is correct.
1 correct: the **Gandhi-Jinnah talks** (Bombay, **9-27 Sept 1944**) were held on the basis of the Formula.
2 correct: it proposed a post-war **plebiscite** in contiguous Muslim-majority areas (**NW and NE**).
3 wrong: **both Congress and League rejected it**; Jinnah wanted only Muslims to vote and no common centre.
xa: If separation: joint agreements on **defence, commerce and communications**.
The League was to back the independence demand and join a **provisional (interim) government**.
⚠ Trap: it was **Rajagopalachari's**, not **Wavell's**.

248.s:
With reference to the Wavell Plan, consider the following statements:
1. The Viceroy and the Commander-in-Chief were excluded from the proposed Indianisation of the Executive Council.
2. Equal representation was proposed for caste Hindus and Muslims.
3. The plan envisaged an entirely elected Executive Council without any special position for the Viceroy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
248.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Viceroy and Commander-in-Chief were exceptions, so the Executive Council was not entirely an elected body without a special Viceroyal position.
248.tq: Watch for the extreme word ‘entirely’ in a statement about constitutional composition.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — so option **(1) 1 and 2 only** is correct.
1 correct: all Executive Council members were to be Indians **except the Viceroy and Commander-in-Chief**.
2 correct: **equal representation to caste Hindus and Muslims**.
3 wrong: the Viceroy kept his place, so it was not an entirely Indian, Viceroy-free council.
xa: Announced by **Lord Wavell** (Viceroy **1943-47**) in **1945**; discussed at the **Simla Conference (June-July 1945)**.
Indians were to frame their own constitution **after the war**.
Wavell closed the conference on **14 July 1945**.

248.s: The immediate cause of the failure of the Simla Conference was that:
o: The Viceroy refused to include any Indian in the Executive Council.
The British Government refused to discuss constitutional reform after the war.
Jinnah insisted that the Muslim League alone should nominate all Muslim members.
The Congress rejected the principle of an Indian Executive Council.
248.x: Jinnah insisted that all Muslim members should be nominated only by the Muslim League, denying the Congress and Punjab Unionists the right to nominate Muslim members.
248.tq: Identify the specific negotiating demand that caused the deadlock.
xs: Simla failed because **Jinnah insisted the League alone nominate all Muslim members** — so option **(3)** is correct.
This denied **Congress** and the **Punjab Unionists** any Muslim nominee.
The plan itself made all Executive Council members Indians (except the **Viceroy and C-in-C**), so option (1) is wrong.
xa: **Wavell** closed the conference on **14 July 1945** instead of going ahead without the League.
Congress was led by **Maulana Azad**.
The Plan proposed **caste Hindu-Muslim parity** in the Executive Council.

248.s:
The abrupt closure of the Simla Conference on 14 July 1945 resulted in which of the following consequences?
1. The Muslim League acquired a de facto veto over constitutional progress.
2. The multi-communal Unionist Party of Punjab was weakened.
3. The political polarisation of the 1945–46 elections was encouraged.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
248.x: All three consequences followed from the failure of the Simla Conference and the resulting advantage gained by the Muslim League.
248.tq: Link a failed negotiation to each of its stated political consequences.
xs: All three followed — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
1: closing Simla without the League gave it a **de facto veto** over constitutional progress.
2 and 3: the multi-communal **Unionist Party** of Punjab was weakened, which **polarised the 1945-46 elections**.
xa: ⚠ Criticism: **Wavell's yielding at Simla** handed **Jinnah** a veto.
In the **1945-46 elections** the League won **all 30 Muslim seats** in the Central Legislative Assembly.
Punjab still got a **Unionist-Congress-Akali** coalition under **Khizr Hayat Khan**.

248.s:
Consider the following statements about the elections of 1945-46:
1. The Muslim League won all 30 Muslim seats in the Central Legislative Assembly.
2. The Congress swept the general (non-Muslim) seats.
3. The Communists did well because they had backed the British war effort.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
248.x: Statement 1 is correct: the League won all 30 Muslim seats in the Central Legislative Assembly. Statement 2 is correct: Congress swept the general seats. Statement 3 is wrong: backing the British war effort led to a heavy defeat for the Communists. So '1 and 2 only'.
248.tq: 1945-46: Congress = general seats, League = Muslim seats, Communists = routed.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — so option **(2) 1 and 2 only** is correct.
1 correct: the League won **all 30 Muslim seats** in the **Central Legislative Assembly**.
2 correct: **Congress swept the general (non-Muslim) seats**.
3 wrong: having backed the British war effort, the **Communists** suffered a **heavy defeat**.
xa: League ministries: **Bengal** and **Sindh**; Congress: most other provinces, including **NWFP**.
In **Madras** the Congress won almost all **Andhra** seats.
The elections came in winter **1945-46**, alongside the **INA trials**.

248.s: Which of the following combinations regarding provincial ministries after the 1945–46 elections is correct?
o: League—Bengal under H.S. Suhrawardy; Congress—most provinces including NWFP
Congress—Punjab under Khizr Hayat Khan without coalition support; League—NWFP
248.x: The Muslim League formed ministries in Bengal under H.S. Suhrawardy and in Sindh. Congress formed ministries in most provinces, including NWFP.
248.tq: Start from the sure person–province pair and eliminate the reversed combinations.
xs: **League — Bengal** under **H.S. Suhrawardy**; **Congress — most provinces including NWFP** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The League's ministries were in **Bengal** and **Sindh**, not NWFP.
**Tanguturi Prakasam** led a **Congress** ministry in Madras; **Khizr Hayat Khan** led a **Unionist-Congress-Akali** coalition in Punjab.
xa: The League won **all 30 Muslim seats** in the Central Legislative Assembly.
Later, **NWFP** chose Pakistan by **referendum**, boycotted by the **Khudai Khidmatgars**.
Congress won almost all **Andhra** seats in **Madras**.

248.s: Who became the premier of the Congress ministry in Madras in 1946?
248.x: Tanguturi Prakasam became the premier of the Congress ministry in Madras in 1946. Congress won almost all the Andhra seats.
248.tq: Use the person–province association, a standard regional-history recall pattern.
xs: **Tanguturi Prakasam** became premier of the **Congress ministry in Madras** (April 1946) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**H.S. Suhrawardy** headed the League ministry in **Bengal**; **Khizr Hayat Khan** the coalition in **Punjab**.
xa: Some notes date these elections to **March 1947**.
In **Madras** the Congress won almost all **Andhra** seats.
AP angle: Prakasam led the Congress ministry in **Madras Presidency** after the **1946** elections.

248.s: The Cabinet Mission Plan was announced on:
248.x: The Cabinet Mission announced its constitutional proposals on 16 May 1946.
248.tq: Distinguish closely related dates by linking each date to its specific event.
xs: The **Cabinet Mission Plan** was announced on **16 May 1946** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**24 March 1946** was when the Mission **arrived**; **2 September 1946** was when the **Interim Government** was formed.
xa: The Mission was sent by **Clement Attlee**.
**Constituent Assembly elections**: **July 1946**; first meeting **9 Dec 1946**.
**Direct Action Day**: **16 Aug 1946**.

248.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:

List-I (Member)
a. Lord Pethick-Lawrence
b. Sir Stafford Cripps
c. A.V. Alexander

List-II (Office held in Britain)
i. First Lord of the Admiralty
ii. Secretary of State for India
iii. President of the Board of Trade
248.x: Pethick-Lawrence was Secretary of State for India, Cripps was President of the Board of Trade, and Alexander was First Lord of the Admiralty.
248.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes containing an incorrect office-member association.
xs: **a-ii, b-iii, c-i** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Lord Pethick-Lawrence** (leader) — **Secretary of State for India**.
**Sir Stafford Cripps** — **President of the Board of Trade**; **A.V. Alexander** — **First Lord of the Admiralty**.
xa: Together they formed the "**Ministerial Trio Mission**".
Cripps had earlier led the **Cripps Mission (March 1942)**.
The Mission arrived **24 March 1946**; plan **16 May 1946**.

248.s:
The Cabinet Mission rejected the demand for a separate Pakistan primarily because:
1. The north-western and north-eastern zones contained substantial non-Muslim populations.
2. Partitioning Punjab and Bengal would disrupt their regional and economic ties.
3. It considered an undivided India preferable to the proposed division.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
248.x: All three statements correctly describe the reasons for rejecting a full Pakistan. The non-Muslim populations were noted as 38% in the north-west and 48% in the north-east.
248.tq: Test a cluster of reasons together while checking whether each statement supports the same constitutional conclusion.
xs: All three reasons are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
1: the **NW** and **NE** zones had large non-Muslim populations — **38%** and **48%**.
2 and 3: partitioning **Punjab/Bengal** would break regional ties, so it recommended an **undivided India**.
xa: Instead it proposed a **weak Centre** with **Defence, Foreign Affairs and Communications**.
**Group B**: Punjab, NWFP, Sindh; **Group C**: Bengal, Assam.
The League accepted it (**June 1946**) seeing compulsory grouping as a **stepping stone to Pakistan**.

248.s: According to the Cabinet Mission Plan, the Union of India was to deal only with which subjects?
248.x: The proposed Union had a deliberately weak Centre responsible only for Defence, Foreign Affairs and Communications.
248.tq: Use the limited-subject feature to distinguish the proposed Union from a strong central federation.
xs: The **Union of India** was to handle only **Defence, Foreign Affairs and Communications** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was a deliberately **weak Centre**; the **provinces** held all **residuary subjects**.
xa: Three tiers: **Union** → **Groups** of provinces → **Provinces**.
⚠ Same three subjects as the **Instrument of Accession** list (Defence, External Affairs, Communications).
Congress rejected the **weak Centre** and **compulsory groups**.

248.s:
With reference to the three-tier structure proposed by the Cabinet Mission, consider the following statements:
1. The first tier was the Union of India.
2. The second tier consisted of groups of provinces.
3. The provinces retained all residuary subjects.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
248.x: The plan proposed a Union, provincial groups and individual provinces. The provinces were to hold all residuary subjects.
248.tq: Check the structure from the highest tier to the lowest and include the residuary-power provision.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
1: **Tier 1** = **Union of India** with a weak Centre (Defence, Foreign Affairs, Communications).
2: **Tier 2** = **Groups** of provinces.
3: **Tier 3** = **Provinces** holding all **residuary subjects**.
xa: **Group A**: Madras, Bombay, UP, Bihar, CP, Orissa (Hindu-majority).
**Group B**: Punjab, NWFP, Sindh; **Group C**: Bengal, Assam (Muslim-majority).
⚠ Congress held grouping **optional**; League held it **compulsory**.

248.s:
Consider the following statements about the grouping of provinces under the Cabinet Mission Plan:
1. Group A included Madras, Bombay and Orissa.
2. Group B consisted of Punjab, NWFP and Sindh.
3. Group C consisted of Bengal, Assam and Bihar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
248.x: Statement 1 is correct: Group A was Madras, Bombay, UP, Bihar, CP and Orissa. Statement 2 is correct: Group B was Punjab, NWFP and Sindh (Muslim-majority NW). Statement 3 is wrong: Group C was only Bengal and Assam; Bihar was in Group A. So '1 and 2 only'; options with 3 are wrong and '1 only' misses statement 2.
248.tq: B = Punjab-NWFP-Sindh, C = Bengal-Assam; every other province is in A.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — so option **(2) 1 and 2 only** is correct.
1 correct: **Group A** = **Madras, Bombay, UP, Bihar, CP, Orissa**.
2 correct: **Group B** = **Punjab, NWFP, Sindh** (Muslim-majority NW).
3 wrong: **Group C** was only **Bengal and Assam**; **Bihar** was in Group A.
xa: Congress held grouping **optional**, so **NWFP and Assam** could opt out.
The **League** held it **compulsory** as a stepping stone to **Pakistan**.
Non-Muslim shares: **38%** (NW) and **48%** (NE).

248.s:
With reference to the composition of the Constituent Assembly under the Cabinet Mission Plan, consider the following statements:
1. British India was allotted 296 seats.
2. Princely states were allotted 93 seats.
3. The seats were distributed roughly in the ratio of one representative per ten lakh of population.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
248.x: The Assembly had 296 representatives from British India and 93 from princely states, with representation based approximately on one seat per ten lakh population.
248.tq: Combine numerical allocation with the population-based rule and verify all three details.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
1 and 2: **296** seats for **British India** and **93** for **princely states** (total **389**).
3: roughly **1 seat per 10 lakh** population.
xa: Provincial seats were split among **General, Muslim and Sikh** communities.
Elected by **proportional representation (single transferable vote)**; princely members **nominated by rulers**.

248.s:
Consider the following statements about the Constituent Assembly scheme of the Cabinet Mission:
1. Provincial seats were divided among General, Muslim and Sikh communities.
2. Each community's members in the provincial assembly elected its representatives by proportional representation (single transferable vote).
3. Representatives of the princely states were directly elected by the people of the states.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
248.x: Statement 1 is correct: provincial seats went to General, Muslim and Sikh communities. Statement 2 is correct: each community voted separately in the provincial assembly by PR-STV. Statement 3 is wrong: princely-state members were nominated by the rulers. So '1 and 2 only'.
248.tq: Provinces = indirect, community-wise, PR-STV; princely states = nominated by rulers.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — so option **(2) 1 and 2 only** is correct.
1 correct: provincial seats were divided among **General, Muslim and Sikh** communities.
2 correct: each community's members elected their share by **proportional representation (single transferable vote)**.
3 wrong: princely-state members were **nominated by rulers**, not elected.
xa: About **1 seat per 10 lakh** population.
**July 1946** result: **Congress 208, League 73, others 15**.

248.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Demand for a Constituent Assembly by M.N. Roy
B. Adoption of the demand by the Congress
C. Acceptance of the constitution-making body in the August Offer
D. Announcement of the Cabinet Mission Plan
248.x: M.N. Roy's demand dates to 1934, the Congress adopted it in 1935, the August Offer accepted it in 1940, and the Cabinet Mission Plan was announced in 1946.
248.tq: Fix the first two milestones and then place the later constitutional proposals.
xs: The order is **A, B, C, D** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**M.N. Roy**'s demand (**1934**) → **Congress** adopts it (**1935**) → **August Offer** accepts it (**1940**) → **Cabinet Mission Plan** (**16 May 1946**).
xa: **Cripps Mission (March 1942)** promised a constitution-making body **after** the war.
The Assembly first met on **9 Dec 1946**.
Its scheme **survived partition** and framed the Constitution.

248.s: Which of the following was the correct distribution of seats won in the July 1946 elections to the Constituent Assembly?
248.x: In the July 1946 results, the Congress won 208 seats, the Muslim League 73 and other parties won 15 seats.
248.tq: Preserve the party–seat pairing while eliminating options that exchange the two major parties.
xs: The **July 1946** results were **Congress 208, Muslim League 73, Others 15** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Options (2) and (4) swap the figures; together they make the **296** British India seats.
xa: The League then **refused to attend** the Constituent Assembly.
First meeting of the Assembly: **9 Dec 1946**.

248.s: The Constituent Assembly of India was constituted under the scheme of the
248.x: The Constituent Assembly was set up under the Cabinet Mission Plan (1946), with elections in July 1946. The August Offer only accepted the idea of an Indian-framed constitution; Cripps promised a body after the war; the Mountbatten Plan came after the Assembly was already formed.
248.tq: CA formed under Cabinet Mission - not Cripps, not Mountbatten.
xs: The Constituent Assembly was formed under the **Cabinet Mission Plan, 1946** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **August Offer (1940)** only accepted the idea; **Cripps (1942)** promised a body **after** the war; the **Mountbatten Plan (3 June 1947)** came later.
xa: Elections were held in **July 1946**.
Strength **389**: **296** British India + **93** princely states.
Exam angle: "Not a member" questions often list a fake name.

248.s: The principal difference between the Congress and the Muslim League regarding Cabinet Mission groupings was that:
o: Congress wanted grouping to be optional, whereas the League wanted it to be compulsory.
Congress wanted compulsory grouping, whereas the League wanted it to be optional.
Both wanted grouping to be optional, but the Mission rejected grouping altogether.
Both wanted compulsory grouping, but the Mission accepted a full Pakistan.
248.x: The Congress considered grouping optional, while the Muslim League insisted that it should be compulsory. The Mission rejected the demand for a fully sovereign Pakistan.
248.tq: Compare opposing positions by locating the single disputed constitutional mechanism.
xs: **Congress** held grouping **optional**; the **League** held it **compulsory** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Optional grouping would let **NWFP and Assam** opt out; the League saw compulsory grouping as a **stepping stone to Pakistan**.
The Mission had **rejected a full Pakistan**.
xa: The League accepted the plan in **June 1946**.
Nehru's **10 July 1946** statement led Jinnah to **withdraw**.
⚠ Ambiguity over compulsory grouping **doomed the Mission**.

248.s: Which development immediately preceded the Muslim League's withdrawal from its acceptance of the Cabinet Mission Plan?
o: The formation of the Interim Government in August 1947
The announcement of the Radcliffe Award
248.x: On 10 July 1946, Jawaharlal Nehru stated that Congress could modify the scheme through its majority in the Constituent Assembly. This prompted Jinnah and the League to withdraw their acceptance.
248.tq: Use the precise date to distinguish the immediate trigger from later constitutional events.
xs: **Nehru's 10 July 1946 statement** — that Congress could modify the plan through its Assembly majority — triggered the League's withdrawal — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **Radcliffe Award** came on **17 August 1947**, long after.
xa: The League then called for **Direct Action** on **29 July 1946**.
**Direct Action Day**: **16 August 1946**, Calcutta — the "**Great Calcutta Killings**".
The League had accepted the plan in **June 1946**, holding grouping compulsory.

248.s: Direct Action Day, observed on 16 August 1946, is associated with the
248.x: The Muslim League observed 16 August 1946 as Direct Action Day, which resulted in the Great Calcutta Killings. The violence later spread to Noakhali, Bihar and parts of north India.
248.tq: Match the exact date with the well-known event associated with it.
xs: **Direct Action Day (16 August 1946)** led to the "**Great Calcutta Killings**" — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **RIN revolt** was earlier, in **Bombay** on **18 Feb 1946**.
xa: ⚠ **29 July 1946** = call; **16 August 1946** = Direct Action Day.
Riots spread to **Noakhali (East Bengal)**, **Bihar** and north India.
**Gandhi** walked through **Noakhali** from **Nov 1946 - Mar 1947**.

248.s: The Muslim League called for Direct Action on:
248.x: The League called for Direct Action on 29 July 1946; Direct Action Day followed on 16 August 1946.
248.tq: Separate the date of a call from the date of its observance.
xs: The League **called** for Direct Action on **29 July 1946** — so option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ **16 August 1946** was **Direct Action Day** itself, not the call.
The call followed the League's withdrawal of acceptance of the **Cabinet Mission Plan**.
xa: Trigger: **Nehru's 10 July 1946** statement.
Direct Action Day brought the "**Great Calcutta Killings**".
Riots spread to **Noakhali**, **Bihar** and north India.

248.s: Which one of the following statements about Gandhi's peace mission in Noakhali (Nov 1946 - Mar 1947) is correct?
o: It ended the communal violence in Bengal completely.
He walked from village to village for peace but failed to stop the violence.
It was undertaken before Direct Action Day.
It was carried out jointly with Jinnah.
248.x: Gandhi walked village to village in Noakhali but failed to stop the violence (APPSC 2018 key). It did not end the violence; it came after Direct Action Day (16 Aug 1946), whose riots spread to Noakhali; Jinnah had no part in it.
248.tq: Noakhali = Gandhi's lonely peace walk; key says it failed to stop violence.
xs: Gandhi **walked from village to village for peace but failed to stop the violence** — so option **(2)** is correct (APPSC 2018 key).
It did not end the violence; it came **after Direct Action Day (16 August 1946)**, whose riots spread to **Noakhali**.
xa: Period: **Nov 1946 - Mar 1947**.
Riots also spread to **Bihar** and north India.
The League called for Direct Action on **29 July 1946**.

248.s: Who continued to be the President of the Viceroy's Executive Council during the Interim Government?
248.x: Lord Wavell remained President of the Viceroy's Executive Council, while Nehru served as its Vice-President.
248.tq: Separate the nominal constitutional office from the effective political leadership.
xs: **Lord Wavell** remained **President** of the Viceroy's Executive Council — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Jawaharlal Nehru** headed the Interim Government as **Vice-President** of the Council.
**Pethick-Lawrence** led the **Cabinet Mission**.
xa: Interim Government formed **2 September 1946**.
Wavell was Viceroy **1943-47**.
The League joined in **October 1946** with **5** nominees.

248.s: The Muslim League joined the Interim Government in:
248.x: The Muslim League entered the Interim Government in October 1946.
248.tq: Distinguish the date of the original formation from the month of League participation.
xs: The **Muslim League** joined the Interim Government in **October 1946** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The Government itself had been formed on **2 September 1946** without it.
xa: It came in with **5** nominees; **Sarat Chandra Bose**, **Shafaat Ahmed Khan** and **Syed Ali Zaheer** made way.
The League still **refused to attend** the Constituent Assembly.
**Liaquat Ali Khan** became **Finance** Member.

248.s: Who chaired both the Punjab and Bengal Boundary Commissions in 1947?
248.x: Sir Cyril Radcliffe, a British lawyer unfamiliar with Indian conditions, chaired both Boundary Commissions.
248.tq: Use the person–institution association and distinguish the boundary chairman from the Viceroy.
xs: **Sir Cyril Radcliffe** chaired **both the Punjab and Bengal** Boundary Commissions — so option **(2)** is correct.
He was a **British lawyer** with **no knowledge of Indian conditions**.
**Sir Stafford Cripps** was in the **Cabinet Mission**; **Clement Attlee** was British PM.
xa: The award was announced on **17 August 1947**.
The **Punjab and Bengal** assemblies met in two parts and both voted to divide.
⚠ Hasty date advance + **Radcliffe's award** were blamed for the partition violence.

248.s: The Radcliffe Award announcing the partition boundaries was published on
248.x: Although independence took place on 15 August 1947, the Radcliffe Award was announced two days later, on 17 August 1947.
248.tq: Distinguish the boundary announcement date from the date of independence.
xs: The **Radcliffe Award** was announced on **17 August 1947** — so option **(2)** is correct.
That was **after** independence on **15 Aug 1947**; **3 June 1947** was the **Mountbatten Plan**.
xa: **Sir Cyril Radcliffe** chaired both the **Punjab and Bengal** commissions.
Referendum provinces were only **NWFP** and **Sylhet (Assam)**.
**Sindh**'s own assembly decided its future.

248.s: Referendums were held in which of the following areas to decide their accession at the time of partition?
o: Bengal and Assam as a whole
248.x: Referendums were held in the North-West Frontier Province and Sylhet. NWFP joined Pakistan, while Sylhet joined East Pakistan.
248.tq: Remember the exclusive pair of referendum areas and distinguish them from provinces decided by assemblies.
xs: **Referendums** were held only in **NWFP and Sylhet** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**NWFP** joined **Pakistan** (boycotted by the **Khudai Khidmatgars**); **Sylhet (Assam)** joined **East Pakistan**.
**Punjab and Bengal** decided through their **assemblies meeting in two parts**; **Sindh**'s own assembly decided.
xa: In Punjab and Bengal a **simple majority** for partition sufficed — both voted to divide.
**Sir Cyril Radcliffe** chaired both the **Punjab and Bengal** boundary commissions; award on **17 August 1947**.
The **Mountbatten Plan (3 June 1947)** set out partition into two dominions.

248.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Cabinet Mission Plan
B. Red Fort INA trials begin
C. RIN revolt
D. Cabinet Mission arrives in India
248.x: The Red Fort trials began in November 1945, the RIN revolt began on 18 February 1946, the Cabinet Mission arrived on 24 March 1946, and the Plan was issued on 16 May 1946.
248.tq: Fix the first event in 1945 and then order the three 1946 developments by month.
xs: The order is **B, C, D, A** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Red Fort INA trials** (**Nov 1945**) → **RIN revolt** (**18 Feb 1946**) → **Cabinet Mission arrives** (**24 March 1946**) → **Plan** (**16 May 1946**).
xa: **Rashid Ali Day** protests: **11 Feb 1946**, Calcutta.
Next came **Constituent Assembly elections (July 1946)** and **Direct Action Day (16 Aug 1946)**.
**Interim Government** formed **2 Sept 1946**.

248.s: The first meeting of the Constituent Assembly was held on:
248.x: The Constituent Assembly held its first meeting on 9 December 1946.
248.tq: Separate the date of the Interim Government from the date of the Constituent Assembly meeting.
xs: The **Constituent Assembly** first met on **9 December 1946** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**2 September 1946** = **Interim Government** formed; **16 August 1946** = **Direct Action Day**.
xa: Its elections were held in **July 1946**: **Congress 208, League 73, others 15**.
Strength **389** = **296** British India + **93** princely states.
It was set up under the **Cabinet Mission Plan (1946)**.

248.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the core proposal of the August Offer of 1940?
o: A plebiscite in Muslim-majority areas before the war ended
Acceptance of the demand for an Indian-framed constitution after the war
Formation of a weak Union through provincial grouping
248.x: The August Offer accepted the demand for an Indian-framed constitution after the war. The other alternatives relate to later proposals.
248.tq: Distinguish similar constitutional proposals by their distinctive core provisions.
xs: The **August Offer (1940)** accepted the demand for an **Indian-framed constitution after the war** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Partition into two dominions** = **Mountbatten Plan (3 June 1947)**; **plebiscite** = **C.R. Formula (1944)**; **weak Union with grouping** = **Cabinet Mission (1946)**.
xa: The August Offer was made by **Linlithgow**.
**Cripps Mission (March 1942)**: **Dominion status** and a constitution-making body **after** the war; provinces may opt out.
**M.N. Roy** first demanded a Constituent Assembly in **1934**; Congress in **1935**.

248.s: The proposal that provinces could become independent successor states, later rejected by Jawaharlal Nehru as leading to Balkanisation, was known as the:
248.x: The Dickie Bird Plan proposed independent successor states for the provinces and was rejected by Nehru as a plan for Balkanisation.
248.tq: Discriminate between similarly named constitutional and partition plans.
xs: The **Dickie Bird Plan** (Plan Balkan) proposed provinces as **independent successor states**; **Nehru** rejected it as **Balkanisation** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was an earlier **Mountbatten** proposal.
⚠ Some notes attribute Plan Balkan to **Wavell**, but the **Wavell Plan** proper (**1945**) was about an Indianised Executive Council.
xa: It was replaced by the **Mountbatten (June 3) Plan**, **3 June 1947**: partition into two dominions.
The transfer date was advanced to **15 Aug 1947**.
The **Cabinet Mission** had instead proposed a **weak Union** with grouping.

248.s: The Interim Government was announced on 24 August 1946 and formed on 2 September 1946. Which one of the following events immediately preceded its formation?
o: The adoption of the Munshi-Ayyangar formula
Direct Action Day called by the Muslim League
The Assembly sitting as Dominion Legislature
248.x: The Muslim League observed Direct Action Day on 16 August 1946, shortly before the Interim Government was formed on 2 September 1946.
248.tq: Arrange closely spaced 1946 events by identifying the immediate preceding event.
xs: **Direct Action Day** (**16 August 1946**) came just before the **Interim Government** (**2 September 1946**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
The League had called for Direct Action on **29 July 1946**.
xa: Direct Action Day brought the "**Great Calcutta Killings**"; riots spread to **Noakhali**, **Bihar** and north India.
The Interim Government was headed by **Nehru** as **Vice-President** of the Viceroy's Executive Council.
The **League** joined in **October 1946** with **5** nominees.

248.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. Simla Conference
B. Cripps Mission
C. Cabinet Mission
D. Wavell Plan
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
248.x: Cripps Mission (March 1942) -> Wavell Plan (1945) -> Simla Conference (June-July 1945, which discussed the Wavell Plan) -> Cabinet Mission (1946) (UPPSC 2025). The other options put Simla before the Wavell Plan or the Wavell Plan before Cripps.
248.tq: Cripps 1942, Wavell Plan then Simla 1945, Cabinet Mission 1946.
xs: The order is **B, D, A, C** — so option **(1)** is correct (UPPSC 2025).
