So '1 and 2 only' is incomplete, and '2, 3 and 4 only' and '1, 2, 3 and 4' include statement 4.
255.tq: Born Madras, roots Gajula Dinne (Nellore); 3 years Sabarmati.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1: correct — about **3 years at Sabarmati Ashram** (APPSC G2 2017).
Statements 2 and 3: correct — **Komaravolu** and **Angaluru** ashrams, **Village Seva Sangam**; khadi, prohibition, **Harijan uplift**.
Statement 4: wrong — he was born in **Madras**; his ancestral village was **Gajula Dinne**, Nellore district.
xa: His work also covered **Hindu-Muslim unity**.
Earlier fasts were for **Harijan** causes; the **1952** fast was his only one for statehood.
**Potti Sreeramulu Telugu University** is in **Hyderabad**.

255.s: The earlier fasts of Potti Sriramulu were primarily undertaken for which cause?
o: Demand for prohibition in Madras Presidency
255.x: His earlier fasts were undertaken for Harijan causes, including temple entry and Harijan welfare. The 1952 fast was his only fast for statehood.
255.tq: Separate the earlier Harijan fasts from the later statehood fast.
xs: His earlier fasts were for **Harijan causes** — including **temple entry** — option **(1)** is correct.
The **1952** fast was his **only fast for statehood**, so (3) is wrong for the earlier ones.
xa: **1946**: Nellore **Venugopala Swamy temple** — Harijan entry.
**1948**: **29 days**, **Wardha** — Harijan Day.
**1949**: **28 days** (January) — **Gandhi Smarak Din**.

255.s: Potti Sriramulu's 29-day fast at Wardha in 1948 was associated with which combination?
o: Harijan Day and a grant of one crore rupees
Temple entry and the formation of Andhra State
Gandhi Smarak Din and the creation of Rayalaseema
Prohibition and the establishment of Andhra University
255.x: The Wardha fast in 1948 was associated with the observance of Harijan Day and a grant of one crore rupees. Madras also marked Harijan Welfare Day on the thirtieth of every month.
255.tq: Match the duration and place of a fast with its distinctive outcome.
xs: The **1948 Wardha** fast of **29 days** led Nehru to declare a **Harijan Day** and **₹1 crore** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Gandhi Smarak Din** came from the **1949** fast; **temple entry** from **1946**.
xa: **Madras** marks **Harijan Welfare Day** on the **30th** of every month (APP).
**1946**: **19 days** — temple-entry law for Harijans.

255.s: On 19 December 1952, Jawaharlal Nehru announced that Andhra State would be formed from:
o: Telangana and the coastal districts of Madras Presidency
The undisputed Telugu-speaking areas, excluding Madras city
All Telugu-speaking areas including Madras city
The entire Madras Presidency excluding Rayalaseema
255.x: Nehru announced that Andhra State would be formed from the undisputed Telugu areas, while Madras city would be excluded.
255.tq: Separate the accepted Telugu areas from the specifically excluded Madras city.
xs: On **19 December 1952**, Nehru told Parliament Andhra would be formed from the **undisputed Telugu areas, excluding Madras city** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Telangana** joined only in **1956** (Andhra Pradesh); Madras city was never included.
xa: ⚠ **19 December** is often misgiven as Sriramulu's death — he died on **15 December 1952**.
**25 March 1953**: Nehru — "**No question**" of Madras as the capital.
Andhra State formed **1 October 1953**.

255.s: Potti Sriramulu began his final fast at the house of:
255.x: Although the fast initially began at the St. George's Fort gate, Bulusu Sambamurthy moved Sriramulu to his house in Mylapore, which is generally given as the venue.
255.tq: Distinguish the initial location from the recognised venue of the fast.
xs: Sriramulu fasted at **Bulusu Sambamurthy's** house in **Mylapore** — option **(3)** is correct.
He first began at the **St. George's Fort gate** (CDX); Sambamurthy then moved him to his house — the venue in most notes.
xa: Start: **19 October 1952**, Madras.
Plan disclosed to friend **V. Lakshminarayana** in **September 1952**.
**Bulusu Sambamurthy** was a **coastal signatory** of the **Sri Bagh Pact**.

255.s: Which one of the following statements about the aftermath of Potti Sriramulu's death is correct?
o: The States Reorganisation Commission was dissolved after his death
The Congress rejected the demand for a separate Andhra State
There were riots and police firing in which seven persons died, followed by Nehru's announcement of Andhra State
The Madras Government immediately accepted Madras city as the capital of Andhra
255.x: Sriramulu's death was followed by riots and police firing in which seven people died. Nehru announced the formation of Andhra State in Parliament on 19 December 1952.
255.tq: Select the option combining the immediate consequence with the subsequent governmental response.
xs: His death sparked **riots**; police firing at **Anakapalli** killed **7**; Nehru then announced Andhra State — option **(3)** is correct.
The **SRC** came **after** this (**Dec 1953**), and Madras was **excluded**, not made Andhra's capital.
xa: **Hartals, demonstrations, riots**; railway stations, post offices attacked.
MLA **Tenneti Viswanatham** and MLC **P. Sitaramayya** resigned.
Announcement in Parliament: **19 December 1952**.

255.s: Potti Sriramulu sought the formation of a state comprising which of the following areas?
o: The Telugu-speaking districts along with the entire Madras city area
The Telugu-speaking districts of Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema
255.x: Potti Sriramulu demanded a separate state consisting of both Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema. The question of Madras city was left for later negotiation.
255.tq: Test the territorial scope directly and distinguish the core demand from the disputed city question.
xs: Sriramulu sought a state of the Telugu districts of **Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Madras city** was left to **later negotiation** (APPSC 2019).
xa: His condition on Madras: a **Chief Commissioner's (C-class) state** by agreement.
Andhra State (**1953**): **Coastal Andhra (7)** + **Rayalaseema (4)** districts.
⚠ **Swami Sitaram's** 1951 demand: Madras's status settled within **three years**.

255.s: Which one of the following was NOT one of the three conditions associated with Potti Sriramulu's demand?
o: Madras city should become a Chief Commissioner's State by agreement
The Andhra State should include the whole of the Madras Presidency
The Centre should announce the formation of Andhra State immediately
255.x: The three conditions concerned immediate announcement, unity among Andhra leaders and making Madras a Chief Commissioner's State by agreement. Inclusion of the entire Madras Presidency was not a condition.
255.tq: Find the option that goes beyond the precise three-condition formulation.
xs: Inclusion of **the whole Madras Presidency** was **not** a condition — option **(2)** is the answer.
The **three conditions**: Centre to **announce Andhra State at once**; Andhra leaders to **stay united**; **Madras city** → **Chief Commissioner's (C-class) state** by agreement.
xa: The C-class arrangement was also called a "**free state**".
On the **50th day**, Nehru offered Andhra **without Madras** if all parties agreed.
He died on the **58th day**.

255.s: Potti Sriramulu, honoured with the title 'Amarajeevi', died on the 58th day of his fast. The date of his death was:
255.x: Sriramulu began his fast on 19 October 1952 and died on its 58th day, 15 December 1952, earning the title 'Amarajeevi'. 19 December 1952 is the date of Nehru's announcement in Parliament (a common trap), and 1 October 1953 is the formation of Andhra State.
255.tq: 19 Oct start - 15 Dec death - 19 Dec announcement - 1 Oct 1953 state.
xs: **Amarajeevi** Potti Sriramulu died on **15 December 1952**, the **58th day** — option **(2)** is correct.
**19 October 1952** = fast began; **19 December 1952** = **Nehru's announcement** (common trap); **1 October 1953** = Andhra State formed.
xa: Some notes say **56** days.
Exam angle: **19 Oct** start, **15 Dec** death, **19 Dec** announcement, "**58 days**".
Venue: **Bulusu Sambamurthy's** house, **Mylapore**.

255.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Potti Sriramulu began his final fast
B. Nehru announced the formation of Andhra State in Parliament
C. Potti Sriramulu died
D. Justice K.N. Wanchoo was appointed
255.x: Sriramulu began his fast on 19 October 1952 (A), died on 15 December 1952 (C), Nehru announced Andhra State in Parliament on 19 December 1952 (B), and Wanchoo was appointed on 7 February 1953 (D). The other orders misplace the Wanchoo appointment or put the announcement before the death.
255.tq: Fast 19 Oct -> death 15 Dec -> announcement 19 Dec 1952 -> Wanchoo 7 Feb 1953.
xs: The order is **A, C, B, D** — option **(1)** is correct.
**A**: fast begins **19 October 1952** → **C**: death **15 December 1952**.
**B**: Nehru's announcement **19 December 1952** → **D**: **Justice K.N. Wanchoo** appointed **7 Feb 1953**.
xa: Wanchoo report: **25 Mar 1953** (some notes **23 March 1953**).
Act introduced **10 Aug 1953**; President's assent **14 Sept 1953**.
Andhra State formed **1 October 1953**.

255.s: The committee headed by Justice K.N. Wanchoo was appointed on:
255.x: Justice K.N. Wanchoo was appointed on 7 February 1953 to report on the implications of the proposed Andhra State.
255.tq: Use exact-date discrimination among closely related Andhra movement events.
xs: **Justice K.N. Wanchoo** was appointed on **7 February 1953** — option **(2)** is correct.
**19 December 1952** = Nehru's announcement; **19 October 1952** = start of Sriramulu's fast.
xa: Wanchoo was **Chief Justice, Rajasthan HC**; a **single-member** committee.
He reported on the **implications** of forming Andhra.
Report dated **25 Mar 1953** (some notes **23 March 1953**).

255.s: Which of the following correctly describes the final territorial adjustments concerning Bellary?
o: The entire Bellary district was added to Andhra State
Bellary taluk went to Mysore, Rayadurg to Anantapur, and Adoni and Alur to Kurnool
Bellary taluk went to Kurnool and Adoni to Mysore
Rayadurg and Alur were transferred to Hyderabad State
255.x: The Centre accepted Justice Mishra's report: Bellary taluk went to Mysore, Rayadurg was added to Anantapur, and Adoni and Alur were added to Kurnool.
255.tq: Match each territorial unit with its final destination and avoid reversing the transfers.
xs: **Bellary taluk → Mysore**, **Rayadurg → Anantapur**, **Adoni and Alur → Kurnool** — option **(2)** is correct.
Wanchoo had suggested the **whole district** go to Andhra, but the Centre did not accept that.
xa: Bellary taluk went to Mysore on **Justice L.S. Misra's** report.
**Siruguppa, Hospet, Sandur, Harpanahalli, Hadagali** also went to **Mysore**.
The **Partition Committee** had earlier considered the **six Bellary taluks**.

255.s: Which one of the following sequences correctly represents the dates connected with the Andhra State Bill and the formation of Andhra State?
o: Introduction—10 August 1953; assent—14 September 1953; formation—1 October 1953
Introduction—14 September 1953; assent—10 August 1953; formation—1 October 1953
Introduction—10 August 1953; assent—1 October 1953; formation—14 September 1953
Introduction—1 October 1953; assent—14 September 1953; formation—10 August 1953
255.x: The Bill was introduced on 10 August 1953, received assent on 14 September 1953, and Andhra State was formed on 1 October 1953.
255.tq: Order the legislative process by introduction, assent and commencement rather than by memorising isolated dates.
xs: **Introduced 10 Aug 1953 → assent 14 Sept 1953 → formed 1 October 1953** — option **(1)** is correct.
The other options jumble these three dates.
xa: Passage: **Madras Assembly → Lok Sabha → Rajya Sabha**.
Andhra = **first linguistic state** of independent India.
⚠ **1 Oct 1953** (Andhra State) vs **1 Nov 1956** (Andhra Pradesh).

255.s:
Consider the following pairs regarding the districts of Andhra State in 1953:
1. Coastal Andhra — 7 districts
2. Rayalaseema — 4 districts
3. Total districts — 11
Which of the pairs given above are correct?
255.x: The Coastal Andhra region had seven districts and Rayalaseema had four, making a total of eleven districts.
255.tq: Break the regional total into its two component figures before selecting the coded option.
xs: All three pairs are correct — **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
**Coastal Andhra (7)**: Srikakulam, Visakhapatnam, East and West Godavari, Krishna, Guntur, Nellore.
**Rayalaseema (4)**: Chittoor, Cuddapah, Anantapur, Kurnool — **11** in all.
xa: Plus the **Bellary taluks** (some notes say "**12 districts**").
**Vizianagaram** and **Prakasam** districts did not exist yet.
Exam angle: **1 Oct 1953** and the **7 + 4** split.

255.s: Which one of the following was NOT included among the districts of Andhra State at the time of its formation?
255.x: Vizianagaram district did not exist at the time of Andhra State formation. Nellore, Kurnool and Chittoor were included.
255.tq: Find the later-created district among the districts belonging to the 1953 arrangement.
xs: **Vizianagaram** did not exist when Andhra State was formed — option **(4)** is the answer.
**Nellore** (Coastal), **Chittoor** and **Kurnool** (Rayalaseema) were among the **11** districts.
xa: **Prakasam** district too did not exist yet.
Coastal Andhra **7** + Rayalaseema **4**.
**Rayadurg** joined **Anantapur**; **Adoni and Alur** joined **Kurnool**.

255.s: Who inaugurated Andhra State at Kurnool?
255.x: Jawaharlal Nehru inaugurated Andhra State at Kurnool.
255.tq: Distinguish the inaugurating national leader from the constitutional authorities associated with state reorganisation.
xs: **Jawaharlal Nehru** inaugurated Andhra State at **Kurnool** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Rajendra Prasad** was President of the **Constituent Assembly**; **Rajagopalachari** was Madras CM (**1952-54**) and anti-Andhra.
xa: Formed **1 October 1953**, carved out of **Madras State**.
First CM **T. Prakasam**; Governor **C.M. Trivedi**.
Capital path: **Kurnool (1953) → Hyderabad (1956) → Amaravati**.

255.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Site)
a. Kurnool
b. Tirupati
c. Vijayawada/Guntur

aList-II (Supporter)
i. Communists
 ii. Congress, Prakasam's group and Rayalaseema leaders
 iii. Krishikar Lok Party

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
255.x: Kurnool was supported by Congress, Prakasam's group and Rayalaseema leaders; Tirupati was associated with the Krishikar Lok Party; and Vijayawada/Guntur was supported by the Communists.
255.tq: Start from the sure regional association and eliminate incompatible codes.
xs: **a–ii, b–iii, c–i** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Kurnool** — Congress, **Prakasam's** group, **Rayalaseema** leaders (Sreebagh Pact).
**Tirupati** — **Krishikar Lok Party**; **Vijayawada/Guntur** — **Communists** (**Puchalapalli Sundarayya**).
xa: ⚠ Some notes give **Praja Socialist Party** for Tirupati — follow the key (**Krishikar Lok Party**, APPSC G2 2025).
The Krishikar Lok Party **changed its stand** during the Assembly session.
Vote: **Kurnool 79** vs **Vijayawada 53**.

255.s:
With reference to the Madras Assembly vote on the capital of Andhra State, consider the following statements:
1. Kurnool secured 79 votes against 53 for Vijayawada.
2. Kurnool's victory was helped by five non-Andhra votes.
3. T. Prakasam voted in favour of Kurnool.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
255.x: Statement 1 is correct: Kurnool won 79 to 53, a margin of 26. Statement 2 is correct: five non-Andhra votes helped Kurnool. Statement 3 is wrong: Prakasam did not vote (and 6 members were absent). So '1 only' misses statement 2, while '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' wrongly include statement 3.
255.tq: Remember 79-53 (margin 26), five non-Andhra votes, Prakasam did not vote.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1: correct — **Kurnool 79**, **Vijayawada 53**, a margin of **26**.
Statement 2: correct — **five non-Andhra votes** helped Kurnool.
Statement 3: wrong — **Prakasam did not vote**; **6** members were absent.
xa: Kurnool was a **temporary** capital.
High Court went to **Guntur** under the **Sreebagh** balance.
**Communists** backed **Vijayawada**.

255.s: Andhra State, the first state of independent India formed on a linguistic basis, came into existence on:
255.x: Andhra State was carved out of Madras State on 1 October 1953 as the first linguistic state, with Kurnool as capital. 15 December 1952 is Potti Sriramulu's death; 26 January 1950 is when the Constitution came into force without an Andhra State; 1 November 1956 is the formation of Andhra Pradesh.
255.tq: 1 Oct 1953 = Andhra State; 1 Nov 1956 = Andhra Pradesh.
xs: **Andhra State**, the first linguistic state, was formed on **1 October 1953** — option **(2)** is correct.
**15 December 1952** = Sriramulu's death; **26 January 1950** = Constitution, with no Andhra; **1 November 1956** = **Andhra Pradesh**.
xa: Carved out of **Madras State**; capital **Kurnool**.
It opened the way to the **SRC** (**Dec 1953**).
Firsts: CM **Prakasam**, Governor **C.M. Trivedi**, Speaker **N. Venkatramayya**.

255.s: Which statement regarding the legislature of the first Andhra State is correct?
o: It had a Legislative Council but no Legislative Assembly
Its Assembly consisted of members elected to the Madras Assembly in 1952, and it had no Legislative Council
Its members were nominated entirely by the Governor
It was formed through a fresh election held in October 1953
255.x: The Andhra Assembly consisted of members elected to the Madras Assembly in 1952. Andhra State did not have a Legislative Council.
255.tq: Test legislative composition and the absence of a second chamber together.
xs: The Assembly consisted of members elected to the **Madras Assembly in 1952**, and there was **no Legislative Council** — option **(2)** is correct.
No fresh election was held in **October 1953**; the first mid-term poll came in **1955**.
xa: **1955** poll: **United Congress front** (Congress + **Krishikar Lok Party** + **Praja Socialist Party**) beat the **Communists**.
**Bezawada Gopala Reddy** then became CM.
High Court at **Guntur**, set up **5 July 1954**.

255.s: Arrange the following in chronological order: A. T. Prakasam became Chief Minister of Andhra State; B. Prakasam's ministry fell; C. Mid-term election was held; D. Bezawada Gopala Reddy became Chief Minister.
255.x: Prakasam became Chief Minister on 1 October 1953, his ministry fell in November 1954, the mid-term poll followed in 1955, and Gopala Reddy then became Chief Minister.
255.tq: Fix the first and last events, then place the fall of the ministry before the mid-term poll.
xs: The correct order is **A, B, C, D** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**A:** **T. Prakasam** became the first CM of Andhra State on **1 Oct 1953**, heading a coalition.
**B:** His ministry fell on a no-confidence defeat in **Nov 1954**, over the **liquor-prohibition** controversy.
**C, D:** The **mid-term poll** followed in **1955**, after which **Bezawada Gopala Reddy** (Congress) became CM (1955-56).
xa: **President's rule** was imposed after Prakasam's ministry fell in **Nov 1954**.
⚠ Some notes put the fall of Prakasam's government in **1955**; the no-confidence defeat was **Nov 1954**.
Prakasam's title was **"Andhra Kesari"**; the first Deputy CM was **Neelam Sanjiva Reddy** (later President of India).
Andhra State had **no Legislative Council**; its members had been elected to the Madras Assembly in **1952**.

255.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the 1955 mid-term election in Andhra State:
1. It was held after the fall of the ministry headed by Tanguturi Prakasam.
2. The Congress contested in alliance with the Krishikar Lok Party and the Praja Socialist Party.
3. The United Congress front contested against the Communists.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
255.x: All three statements are correct. The election followed the fall of Prakasam's ministry, and the Congress, Krishikar Lok Party and Praja Socialist Party formed the United Congress front against the Communists.
255.tq: Test the complete alliance structure by checking the election context, constituent parties and principal opponent together.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Statement 1 — correct:** the **1955** mid-term poll was held after **Prakasam's** ministry fell (no-confidence, **Nov 1954**).
**Statement 2 — correct:** the **United Congress front** = Congress + **Krishikar Lok Party** + **Praja Socialist Party**.
**Statement 3 — correct:** the front's opponent was the **Communists**; the front won.
xa: After the win, **Bezawada Gopala Reddy** became CM.
**N.G. Ranga's Krishikar Lok Party** had backed **Tirupati** as capital in 1953; the **Communists** (Puchalapalli Sundarayya) backed **Vijayawada / Guntur**.
Prakasam's government lost its majority over the **liquor-prohibition** controversy.

255.s:
Consider the following statements about the High Court of Andhra State:
1. It was located at Guntur, while the capital was at Kurnool, following the Sri Bagh Pact balance.
2. It was set up on 5 July 1954.
3. Until it was set up, the Madras High Court served Andhra State.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
255.x: All three are correct: the High Court was placed at Guntur (Coastal Andhra) with the capital at Kurnool (Rayalaseema), as in the Sri Bagh Pact; it was set up on 5 July 1954; and the Madras High Court served Andhra in the interim. Any option leaving out a statement is incomplete.
255.tq: Capital Kurnool + High Court Guntur (1954) - APPSC G2 2008, 2025.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Statement 1 — correct:** High Court at **Guntur** (Coastal Andhra), capital at **Kurnool** (Rayalaseema), following the **Sreebagh Pact** balance.
**Statement 2 — correct:** the High Court was set up in **1954**, on **5 July 1954**.
**Statement 3 — correct:** the **Madras High Court** served Andhra in the interim.
xa: The **Sri Bagh Pact (16 Nov 1937)** put the **Capital and High Court in separate regions**, with Rayalaseema getting first choice.
Exam pair: **"capital Kurnool, High Court Guntur"** (APPSC G2 2008 and 2025).
In the Madras Assembly vote on the capital, **Kurnool 79** beat **Vijayawada 53**; Kurnool was a **temporary** capital.

255.s: Who presented the 1955-56 budget of Andhra State?
255.x: Bezawada Gopala Reddy presented the 1955-56 budget of Andhra State (APPSC GS 2021 key); he became CM after the 1955 mid-term poll. Prakasam was the first CM, Sanjiva Reddy the Deputy CM, and Tenneti Viswanatham sat on Trivedi's advisory committee.
255.tq: Budget 1955-56 = B. Gopala Reddy.
xs: **B. (Bezawada) Gopala Reddy** presented the **1955-56** budget of Andhra State (APPSC GS 2021 key) — so option **(3)** is correct.
**T. Prakasam** was the first CM; **Neelam Sanjiva Reddy** was the Deputy CM.
**Tenneti Viswanatham** sat on Trivedi's advisory committee (with Sanjiva Reddy) and later resigned as MLA over Sriramulu's death.
xa: Gopala Reddy became CM after the **1955 mid-term poll**, won by the **United Congress front**.
Gopala Reddy was also an Andhra member of the **1949** Madras **Partition Committee**, and a coastal signatory of the **Sri Bagh Pact**.
First Governor: **C.M. Trivedi**; first Speaker: **N. Venkatramayya**.

255.s: In which year was Nellore district renamed Sri Potti Sriramulu Nellore District?
255.x: Nellore district was renamed Sri Potti Sriramulu Nellore District in 2008 by the government headed by Chief Minister Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy.
255.tq: Test a renaming year with closely spaced alternatives.
xs: Nellore was renamed **"Sri Potti Sriramulu Nellore District"** in **2008** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The renaming was done under CM **Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy**.
xa: Sriramulu's ancestral village was **Gajula Dinne**, in Nellore district; he was born in Madras on **16 March 1901**.
**Potti Sreeramulu Telugu University** (Hyderabad) is also named after him.
His titles: **Amarajeevi** (Immortal Martyr) and "Andhra Martyra Martanda".

255.s: Which of the following is a title associated with Potti Sriramulu?
255.x: Potti Sriramulu is known by the title Amarajeevi, meaning Immortal Martyr. He is also associated with the title “Andhra Martyra Martanda.”
255.tq: Test an exact honorific while using titles associated with other Andhra leaders as traps.
xs: Potti Sriramulu is known as **Amarajeevi** (Immortal Martyr) — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Andhra Ratna** = **Duggirala Gopalakrishnaiah**; **Desoddharaka** = **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**; **Andhra Kesari** = **Tanguturi Prakasam**.
xa: His other title: **"Andhra Martyra Martanda"**.
He got the title after dying on the **58th day** of his fast, **15 December 1952**.
⚠ **Andhra Kesari** is also the name of **Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao's** paper (**1904**).
**Deshabhakta** = Konda Venkatappayya; **Swami Sitaram** = Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri.

255.s:
Consider the following statements about the 'Statue of Sacrifice' of Potti Sriramulu:
1. It is a 58-foot bronze statue at Sakhamuru Park, Amaravati.
2. It was unveiled by Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on 16 March 2026.
3. It was unveiled on Potti Sriramulu's 100th birth anniversary.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
255.x: Statement 1 is correct: 58-foot bronze statue at Sakhamuru Park, Amaravati. Statement 2 is correct: unveiled by CM Chandrababu Naidu on 16 March 2026. Statement 3 is wrong: 16 March 2026 was his 125th birth anniversary (born 16 March 1901). So '1 only' is incomplete, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include statement 3.
255.tq: 58 feet = 58-day fast; born 1901, so 2026 = 125th anniversary.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
**Statement 1 — correct:** a **58-foot** bronze statue at **Sakhamuru Park, Amaravati**.
**Statement 2 — correct:** unveiled by CM **Chandrababu Naidu** on **16 March 2026**.
**Statement 3 — wrong:** **16 March 2026** was his **125th** birth anniversary (born **16 March 1901**), not the 100th.
xa: Memorial park of **6.80 acres**, about **₹150 crore**; **26 t** bronze + **42 t** iron.
Built by the **Amarajeevi Potti Sriramulu Memorial Trust**; phase 2 adds a **museum, auditorium** and skill centre.
The 58-foot height echoes his **58-day** fast of **1952**.

255.s:
Consider the following statements about Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao:
1. He founded Andhra Kesari in 1904 at Rajahmundry.
2. He wrote Andhrula Charitra.
3. He founded the Andhra Patrika.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
255.x: Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao founded Andhra Kesari in 1904 and wrote Andhrula Charitra. Andhra Patrika was associated with Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao.
255.tq: Find the wrong person linked with a newspaper.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
**Statement 1 — correct:** **Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao** founded **Andhra Kesari** in **1904**, Rajahmundry.
**Statement 2 — correct:** he wrote **Andhrula Charitra**.
**Statement 3 — wrong:** **Andhra Patrika** was founded by **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** (**9 Sep 1908**, Bombay).
xa: He founded the **Vijnana Chandrika Mandali** (**1906**) with **Komarraju Lakshmana Rao**.
He also founded the **Balabharati Samithi** (**Feb 1907**).
⚠ **Andhra Kesari** is also the title of **Tanguturi Prakasam**.

255.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Leader)
a. Konda Venkatappayya
b. Nyapati Subba Rao
c. Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao
 d. B.N. Sarma

List-II (Association)
i. Linguistic-provinces resolution in the Imperial Legislative Council
 ii. Andhrula Charitra
 iii. First secretary of the Andhra Congress Committee
 iv. First president of the Andhra Congress Committee

Select the correct answer using the code below.
255.x: Konda Venkatappayya was the first secretary, Nyapati Subba Rao the first president, Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao wrote Andhrula Charitra, and B.N. Sarma moved the linguistic-provinces resolution.
255.tq: Start from the sure office-holder pair and eliminate codes.
xs: **a–iii, b–iv, c–ii, d–i** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Konda Venkatappayya:** **first secretary** of the Andhra Congress Committee (**1918**).
**Nyapati Subba Rao:** **first president** of the Andhra Congress Committee (**1918**).
**Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao** wrote **Andhrula Charitra**; **B.N. Sarma** moved the **linguistic-provinces resolution** in the Imperial Legislative Council (**6 Feb 1918**).
xa: ⚠ The APPSC G2 2011 key named **Konda Venkatappayya** as first APCC president; the notes give **Nyapati Subba Rao**.
The Andhra Congress Committee was formed on **22 January 1918**.
B.N. Sarma's **1918** resolution was opposed by **Jinnah** and **V.S. Srinivasa Sastri**; supported by **K.V. Rangaswami Ayyangar**.
Konda Venkatappayya co-founded **Krishna Patrika** (**1 Feb 1902**) and presided the **5th Mahasabha, Nellore 1917**.

255.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Gokhale of South India — Mocherla Ramachandra Rao
255.x: Desoddharaka was the title of Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao, not Pattabhi Sitaramayya.
255.tq: Use the known confusable title-person pair to find the mismatch.
xs: **Desoddharaka — Pattabhi Sitaramayya** is wrongly paired — so option **(2)** is the answer; **Desoddharaka** = **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**.
**Mocherla Ramachandra Rao** = **"Gokhale of South India"** (presided the 4th Mahasabha, **Kakinada 1916**) — correct.
**Andhra Ratna** = **Duggirala Gopalakrishnaiah**; **Deshabhakta** = **Konda Venkatappayya** — both correct.
xa: Exam angle: APPSC G2 2002 asked this "incorrectly paired" question (**Desoddharaka - Pattabhi** is the wrong pair).
**Andhra Kesari** = Tanguturi Prakasam; **Amarajeevi** = Potti Sriramulu.
**Rayalaseema Kuruvriddhudu / Pitamaha** = Kalluri Subbarao; **Jenda Narsayya** = Thota Narsayya Naidu.

255.s: On 6 February 1918, B. N. Sarma moved a resolution in the Imperial Legislative Council relating to which of the following?
255.x: B. N. Sarma moved the resolution for the creation of linguistic provinces in the Imperial Legislative Council on 6 February 1918.
255.tq: Use the date–mover–subject combination to identify the correct resolution.
xs: On **6 Feb 1918**, **B.N. Sarma** moved a resolution for **linguistic provinces** in the Imperial Legislative Council — so option **(3)** is correct.
Supported by **K.V. Rangaswami Ayyangar**; opposed by **Jinnah** and **V.S. Srinivasa Sastri**.
**Surendranath Banerjee** said "the time has not come"; **Tej Bahadur Sapru** would back it for Andhra only.
xa: B.N. Sarma (Visakhapatnam) presided the **1st Andhra Conference, Bapatla 1913**, where he called the province demand premature.
He founded the **Andhra Rajakeeya Samiti** (**1917**).
Later Council of State bids: **1925** (Dr. Ramarao, amended by Ramadasu Pantulu) and **1926** — both failed.

255.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Punjab Kesari — Lala Lajpat Rai
2. Andhra Ratna — Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya
3. Deshabhakta — Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao
Which of the pairs given above are correct?
255.x: Lala Lajpat Rai was Punjab Kesari and Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya was Andhra Ratna. Deshabhakta was Konda Venkatappayya, not Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao.
255.tq: Check each title–person pair before selecting the coded combination.
xs: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
**Pair 1 — correct:** **Punjab Kesari** — **Lala Lajpat Rai** (as given in the question).
**Pair 2 — correct:** **Andhra Ratna** — **Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya**.
**Pair 3 — wrong:** **Deshabhakta** = **Konda Venkatappayya**; Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao was **Desoddharaka**.
xa: ⚠ **Andhra Kesari** = Tanguturi Prakasam — do not confuse with Punjab Kesari.
Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao founded **Andhra Patrika** (**1908**); the **Sri Bagh Pact** was signed at his Madras house.
Lala Lajpat Rai presided the **Calcutta special session (September 1920)**, which accepted non-cooperation.

255.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Dhar Commission was followed by the JVP Committee.
2. The Madras Partition Committee functioned during 1949–50.
3. The Wanchoo inquiry was conducted during February–March 1953.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
255.x: All three statements are correct. The sequence included the Dhar Commission and JVP Committee, the Madras Partition Committee in 1949–50 and the Wanchoo inquiry in early 1953.
255.tq: Check the dates of successive commissions and inquiries rather than relying only on their names.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Statement 1 — correct:** **Dar Commission** (Jun-Dec **1948**) was followed by the **JVP Committee** (Dec 1948, report April 1949).
**Statement 2 — correct:** the Madras **Partition Committee** worked **Dec 1949-Jan 1950**, reporting on **4 Jan 1950**.
**Statement 3 — correct:** the **Wanchoo** inquiry ran **Feb-Mar 1953** (appointed **7 Feb 1953**, report **25 Mar 1953**).
xa: Partition Committee chairman: **Kumaraswamy Raja**, Madras CM (APPSC G2 2025 key).
**Justice K.N. Wanchoo** (Chief Justice, Rajasthan HC) was a **single-member** committee.
⚠ **Dar** = appointed by the **Constituent Assembly**; **JVP** = appointed by **Congress**.

255.s: Which one of the following distinguishes the Andhra Mahasabha of the Madras Presidency from the Nizam Andhra Mahasabha?
o: The former began at Bapatla in 1913, whereas the latter began at Jogipet in 1930.
The former began at Jogipet in 1930, whereas the latter began at Bapatla in 1913.
Both began at Bapatla in 1913 and had the same first president.
Both began at Jogipet in 1930 but pursued different educational aims.
255.x: The Madras Presidency organisation began at Bapatla in 1913 under B.N. Sarma, while the Nizam Andhra Mahasabha began at Jogipet in 1930 under Suravaram Pratapa Reddy.
255.tq: Split the comparison by date, venue and first president.
xs: The **Andhra Mahasabha** began at **Bapatla in 1913**; the **Nizam Andhra Mahasabha** at **Jogipet (Medak) in 1930** — so option **(1)** is correct.
First presidents differ: **B.N. Sarma** (Bapatla) vs **Suravaram Pratapa Reddy** (Jogipet).
Aims differed: a **separate Andhra province** vs **Telugu culture, education and reform** under the Nizam.
xa: Nizam Andhra Mahasabha later sessions: **1931 Devarakonda** (Burgula Ramakrishna Rao), **1934 Khammam**, **1935 Siricilla** (Madapati Hanumantha Rao).
Andhra Mahasabha later sessions: **Vijayawada**, **Visakhapatnam**, **Kakinada**, **Nellore**.
The Nizam body's sessions also held women's conferences (**Andhra Mahila Sabha**).

255.s: The Visalandhra Mahasabha, formed in 1949, was intended to represent the demand for a state comprising:
o: The Telugu and Tamil-speaking areas jointly
255.x: The Visalandhra Mahasabha was formed to advocate the integration of all Telugu-speaking areas.
255.tq: Distinguish the geographical scope of an organisation from the narrower regional demands.
xs: The **Visalandhra Mahasabha** (**1949**) stood for a state of **all Telugu-speaking areas** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was formed after the **Dar Commission** and **JVP Committee** (**1948**).
xa: In the APPSC G2 2025 order: **Dhar → Visalandhra Mahasabha → Sitaram's fast → SRC**.
The Andhra State of **1 Oct 1953** had only **11** districts (7 coastal + 4 Rayalaseema) — not all Telugu areas.
**B. Ramakrishna Rao** shifted to favour merger in **1954**.

255.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. Swami Sitaram's fast for Andhra State
B. Dhar Commission
C. States Reorganisation Commission
D. Formation of the Visalandhra Mahasabha
255.x: The Dhar Commission came in 1948 (B), the Visalandhra Mahasabha was formed in 1949 (D), Swami Sitaram fasted in August-September 1951 (A), and the SRC was set up in December 1953 (C). This is the order keyed in APPSC G2 2025; the other options misplace Visalandhra or the SRC.
255.tq: Dhar 1948 - Visalandhra 1949 - Sitaram 1951 - SRC 1953.
xs: The order is **B, D, A, C** — option **(1)** is correct (APPSC G2 2025 key).
**B:** **Dhar Commission**, Jun-Dec **1948**. **D:** **Visalandhra Mahasabha**, **1949**.
**A:** **Swami Sitaram's** fast, **15 Aug-20 Sep 1951**. **C:** **SRC** (Fazal Ali), **Dec 1953**.
xa: Swami Sitaram (**Gollapudi Sitarama Sastry**) fasted **35 days**; ended on the appeal of **Vinoba Bhave**.
⚠ **Swami Sitaram** = **35 days** (1951); **Potti Sriramulu** = **58 days** (1952, died).
Between them: the Madras **Partition Committee** (Dec 1949-Jan 1950) and the **Wanchoo** inquiry (Feb-Mar 1953).

255.s: The formation of Andhra State in 1953 is commonly described as the “Andhra exception” because it:
o: allowed Madras to become the capital of a separate Andhra State
created a state without any elected legislature
reversed the decision to use language as a basis for state formation
opened the way for the States Reorganisation Commission and nationwide linguistic reorganisation
255.x: Although the Dhar Commission and JVP Committee were cautious about linguistic states, the Andhra exception paved the way for the SRC and broader linguistic reorganisation.
255.tq: Identify the historical consequence rather than merely recalling the event itself.
xs: The "**Andhra exception**" opened the way to the **SRC** and nationwide **linguistic reorganisation** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Dhar** and **JVP** both rejected language as a basis, yet JVP's Andhra exception (**minus Madras**) became the formula used in **1953**.
So it did not hand Madras to Andhra, nor reverse the linguistic principle.
xa: **Potti Sriramulu's death** forced the Centre's hand → Andhra → **SRC (Dec 1953)** → **States Reorganisation Act 1956**.
JVP's report (**April 1949**): Andhra could be formed **if Andhras gave up Madras city**.
SRC members: **Fazl Ali**, **Kunzru**, **Panikkar**.

255.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the sequence of bodies and commissions associated with linguistic reorganisation?
o: JVP Committee → Dhar Commission → Wanchoo Committee → Fazal Ali Commission
Dhar Commission → JVP Committee → Wanchoo Committee → Fazal Ali States Reorganisation Commission
Wanchoo Committee → Dhar Commission → JVP Committee → Fazal Ali Commission
Dhar Commission → Wanchoo Committee → JVP Committee → Fazal Ali Commission
255.x: The sequence was Dhar Commission in 1948, JVP Committee in 1948–49, Wanchoo in 1953 for Andhra, and the Fazal Ali SRC in 1953–55 for all India.
255.tq: Fix the earliest commission first and then place the Andhra-specific and all-India bodies.
xs: The sequence is **Dhar → JVP → Wanchoo → Fazal Ali SRC** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Dhar Commission** (**1948**, CA-appointed) → **JVP** (**1948-49**, Congress).
**Wanchoo** (**1953**, Andhra only) → **Fazal Ali SRC** (**1953-55**, all India).
xa: SRC members: **H.N. Kunzru** and **K.M. Panikkar**.
**Justice K.N. Wanchoo** was appointed on **7 Feb 1953**; report dated **25 Mar 1953**.
⚠ **Dar** = appointed by the **Constituent Assembly**; **JVP** = by **Congress** at **Jaipur**.

255.s: The States Reorganisation Commission announced on 22 December 1953 was associated with which combination?
o: Fazal Ali, H.N. Kunzru and K.M. Panikkar
K.N. Wanchoo, H.N. Kunzru and Pattabhi Sitaramayya
Fazal Ali, Neelam Sanjiva Reddy and K.M. Panikkar
P.S. Kumaraswami Raja, Fazal Ali and H.N. Kunzru
255.x: The SRC was headed by Fazal Ali, with H.N. Kunzru and K.M. Panikkar as members.
255.tq: Start with the sure chairman-member combination and eliminate bodies connected with Andhra alone.
xs: The SRC (announced **22 Dec 1953**) = **Fazal Ali**, **H.N. Kunzru** and **K.M. Panikkar** — option **(1)** is correct.
**K.N. Wanchoo** led the **1953** single-member Andhra inquiry; **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** was on the **JVP** Committee.
**P.S. Kumaraswami Raja** chaired the Madras **Partition Committee**; **Neelam Sanjiva Reddy** was not on the SRC.
xa: The SRC led to the **States Reorganisation Act 1956**.
Its path was opened by the formation of **Andhra State** on **1 Oct 1953**.
⚠ **N. Sanjiva Reddy was not a member** of the JVP Committee either (APPSC 2021).

255.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Andhra movement during 1913–1920 is correct?
o: It began only after the formation of Andhra State in 1953.
It opposed the use of Telugu in education and administration.
It combined demands for an Andhra State, Andhra University, development of Telugu and cultural revival.
It was confined exclusively to the demand for a separate province.
255.x: The period 1913–1920 was the propaganda phase, with four broad objectives: Andhra State, Andhra University, Telugu development and cultural revival.
255.tq: Prefer the option that captures the full set of objectives rather than an exclusive single-purpose claim.
xs: The **1913-20** propaganda phase combined **Andhra State**, **Andhra University**, development of **Telugu** and **cultural revival** — option **(3)** is correct.
It began long before **1953** (Bapatla **1913**), and it **promoted** Telugu — e.g. **Telugu medium** in secondary schools (**1915**).
It was not only about a province — the **first** session (Bapatla) also demanded a **separate university**.
xa: **Bapatla (1913)** "sowed the seeds" of the movement — the first organised Telugu platform.
Bapatla agenda: an English newspaper, lifting the **ban on Telugu entry into the Army**, a fund for technical training abroad.
The **1914 Vijayawada** session passed the province resolution.

255.s: Which one of the following correctly compares the early milestones of the Andhra movement?
o: Bapatla 1912—first formal resolution; Nidadavolu 1913—first numbered conference; Vijayawada 1914—first Congress session
Nidadavolu 1912—first Andhra Mahasabha; Bapatla 1913—first Congress circle; Vijayawada 1914—first university session
Vijayawada 1912—first formal resolution; Bapatla 1913—first linguistic PCC; Nidadavolu 1914—first Andhra Mahasabha
Nidadavolu 1912—first formal resolution; Bapatla 1913—first numbered Andhra Conference; Vijayawada 1914—first session called Andhra Mahasabha
255.x: Nidadavolu in 1912 saw the first formal resolution, Bapatla in 1913 was the first numbered Andhra Conference, and Vijayawada in 1914 was the first session called Andhra Mahasabha.
255.tq: Keep the three places and years aligned before comparing the labels attached to them.
xs: **Nidadavolu 1912** = first formal resolution; **Bapatla 1913** = first numbered Andhra Conference; **Vijayawada 1914** = first session called **Andhra Mahasabha** — option **(4)**.
The other options jumble the places and years; Bapatla was **1913**, not 1912.
xa: **Nidadavolu (1912)** was a joint conference of **Guntur, Krishna, Godavari**; resolution moved by **Jonnavittula Gurunatham**.
**Bapatla** president: **B.N. Sarma**; **Vijayawada 1914** president: **Nyapati Subba Rao** (province resolution passed).
The Youngmen's Literary Association, **Guntur (1903)**, was the cradle of the movement.

255.s: Which of the following best explains why the Andhra movement was repeatedly slowed before 1953?
o: The immediate acceptance of the Andhra demand by the Central Government
Leadership and regional splits, including Circars–Rayalaseema and Prakasam–Pattabhi divisions
The unanimous opposition of all Telugu-speaking districts to a separate state
The absence of any demand for linguistic organisation within Congress
255.x: Factional divisions between regions and leaders, notably Circars versus Rayalaseema and Prakasam versus Pattabhi, repeatedly weakened the movement.
255.tq: Identify the internal political cause rather than an absolute or externally imposed explanation.
xs: Leadership and regional splits — **Circars vs Rayalaseema**, **Prakasam vs Pattabhi** — repeatedly slowed the movement — option **(2)** is correct.
The Centre was **cautious**, not accepting: **Dhar** and **JVP** both rejected language as a basis.
Congress had promised linguistic PCCs since **1920**, and Telugu districts were divided, not unanimous.
xa: Delay was blamed on Centre caution after **Partition** + Andhra factionalism.
**April 1951**: **N. Sanjiva Reddy** beat **N.G. Ranga** for APCC by **5** votes → Prakasam and Ranga left to form the **Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party**.
The university seat/jurisdiction row left lasting **Rayalaseema** resentment → the **Sri Bagh Pact**.

255.s: The provisions of the Sri Bagh Pact continue to be cited particularly in contemporary debates concerning:
o: the status of the Telugu language in the Union List
the creation of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council
the merger of Andhra with Maharashtra
Rayalaseema’s capital, High Court and irrigation concerns
255.x: The Sri Bagh terms concerning capital, High Court and irrigation remain important in Rayalaseema-related debates.
255.tq: Group the three linked provisions under the region whose interests they addressed.
xs: The **Sri Bagh** terms on **capital, High Court and irrigation** are still cited in Rayalaseema debates — option **(4)** is correct.
The pact (**16 Nov 1937**) put **Capital and High Court in separate regions**, Rayalaseema choosing first.
xa: Irrigation clause: **priority to Rayalaseema** in Krishna, Tungabhadra and Pennar waters for **10 years**.
University clause: AU centres at **Waltair and Anantapur**.
Signed at **'Sri Bagh', Madras**, the house of **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**.
⚠ **Sri Bagh** = **1937**, Coastal-Rayalaseema; **Gentlemen's Agreement** = **1956**, Andhra-Telangana.

255.s: The AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026 is associated with which provision?
o: Abolition of the statutory concept of a state capital
Affirmation of Amaravati’s permanent statutory position as the capital
Transfer of Andhra Pradesh’s capital to Hyderabad
Recognition of Kurnool as the permanent capital of Andhra Pradesh
255.x: The AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026 affirms Amaravati’s permanent statutory position as the capital of Andhra Pradesh.
255.tq: Use the exact statutory effect instead of confusing historical and current capitals.
xs: The **AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026** affirms **Amaravati's** permanent statutory position as capital — option **(2)** is correct.
**Kurnool** was the temporary capital of Andhra State (**1953**) and **Hyderabad** came in **1956**.
xa: The **58-foot** "Statue of Sacrifice" of Potti Sriramulu stands at **Sakhamuru Park, Amaravati**.
Deputy CM **Pawan Kalyan**: A.P. still grapples with its capital question.
The **Central University of AP** at **Anantapur** followed the **AP Reorganisation Act 2014**.

xs: **Both statements are true** — so option **(1)** is correct.

255.s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Bezawada Gopala Reddy was the last Chief Minister of Andhra State.
Statement B: The Andhra Pradesh Legislature became bicameral for the first time in 1958.
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
255.x: Both are true: Bezawada Gopala Reddy was the last Chief Minister of Andhra State (1955–56), and the AP Legislature became bicameral when the Legislative Council was created in 1958.

n: Bezawada Gopala Reddy was the last Chief Minister of Andhra State. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-5]
The Andhra Pradesh Legislature became bicameral for the first time in 1958. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-5]
xs: **Both statements are true** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement A is true: **Bezawada Gopala Reddy** was the **last CM of Andhra State** (**1955** to the **1956** merger).
Statement B is true as given: the AP Legislature became **bicameral** in **1958**; Andhra State had **no Legislative Council**.
xa: Gopala Reddy became CM after the **1955 mid-term poll**, won by the **United Congress front** (Congress + **Krishikar Lok Party** + **Praja Socialist Party**).
**Prakasam**'s ministry fell over **liquor prohibition**; no-confidence defeat **Nov 1954**.
Gopala Reddy also presented the **1955-56** budget.

255.s: Who was the first Telugu President of the Indian National Congress?
255.x: P. Anandacharyulu was the first Telugu President of the Indian National Congress, presiding over the 1891 Nagpur session. Nyapati Subba Rao and Govinda Rao Nanal are linked with Andhra and Hyderabad bodies, not the INC presidency.
255.tq: Recall the 1891 Nagpur session President.
n: P. Anandacharyulu was the first Telugu President of the Indian National Congress. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-5]
P. Anandacharyulu became the first Telugu President of the Indian National Congress in 1891 at Nagpur. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-5]
xs: **P. Anandacharyulu** was the **first Telugu President** of the INC — so option **(3)** is correct.
He presided the **7th session**, **Nagpur, 1891**; earlier he was Secretary of the **Madras Mahajana Sabha** (**1884**).
**Nyapati Subba Rao** was the first president of the **Andhra Congress Circle**; **Govinda Rao Nanal** of the **Hyderabad State Congress**.
xa: ⚠ **Trap:** a key named **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** "first Telugu person" — he presided the **Jaipur session, 1948**.
**N. Sanjiva Reddy** was INC president **1960-62**.
Andhra delegates at the **1885 Bombay** session included **P. Anandacharlu** and **Nyapati Subba Rao**.

255.s: Who was the first Muslim leader from Hyderabad to join the Indian National Congress?
255.x: Mulla Abdul Qayyum was the first Muslim leader from Hyderabad to join the Indian National Congress. B. Ramakrishna Rao was Hyderabad's first elected Chief Minister, and Anandacharyulu was the first Telugu INC President.
255.tq: Recall Hyderabad's early Congress pioneers.
n: Mulla Abdul Qayyum was the first Muslim leader from Hyderabad to join the Indian National Congress. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-5]
xs: **Mulla Abdul Qayyum** was the **first Muslim leader** from Hyderabad to **join the INC** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**P. Anandacharyulu** was the first Telugu **INC President** (**1891**, **Nagpur**).
**B. Ramakrishna Rao** was the **first elected Chief Minister** of Hyderabad State.
xa: **Govinda Rao Nanal** was the **first President** of the **Hyderabad State Congress**.
In **1954** **B. Ramakrishna Rao** shifted to favour the merger.
**Andhra State** and **Hyderabad State** merged in **1956**.

255.s: Who was the first elected Chief Minister of Hyderabad State?
255.x: B. Ramakrishna Rao became the first elected Chief Minister of Hyderabad State in 1952. Prakasam and Gopala Reddy headed Andhra State, and Sanjiva Reddy was the first CM of Andhra Pradesh.
255.tq: Discriminate Hyderabad State from Andhra State leaders.
n: B. Ramakrishna Rao was the first elected Chief Minister of Hyderabad State. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-5]
xs: **B. Ramakrishna Rao** was the **first elected Chief Minister** of **Hyderabad State** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Tanguturi Prakasam** and **Bezawada Gopala Reddy** were the first and last CMs of **Andhra State**.
**Neelam Sanjiva Reddy** was the **first CM of Andhra Pradesh** (**1956**).
xa: **Govinda Rao Nanal** — first President of the **Hyderabad State Congress**.
**Mulla Abdul Qayyum** — first Muslim leader from Hyderabad to join the INC.
In **1954** Ramakrishna Rao shifted to favour the merger.

255.s: Which case was the first criminal case in the Vandemataram Movement?

n: The Kakinada Riot Case was the first criminal case in the Vandemataram Movement. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-5]

**Palnadu** (Guntur) is where the **Forest Satyagraha** first started.

**Nyapati Subba Rao** — **first lawyer** in Andhra to **boycott British courts**.
The **Vande Mataram movement (1905-11)** politicised Andhra youth.

255.s: Which police station was attacked first by Alluri Sitarama Raju?
255.x: Alluri Sitarama Raju began the Rampa revolt of 1922 by attacking the Chintapalli police station first. Palnadu is linked with the Forest Satyagraha and Kakinada with the Vandemataram riot case.

**Palnadu** is linked with the **Forest Satyagraha**; **Kakinada** with the **Riot Case** of the Vandemataram Movement.
**Bapatla** hosted the **first Andhra Mahasabha** (**1913**).

**Vallabhaneni Sitamahalakshmi** was the **first woman arrested** in the Salt Satyagraha.

255.x: The Forest Satyagraha during the Non-Cooperation Movement first started in Palnadu in Guntur district. Chintapalli belongs to Alluri's revolt and Bapatla to the first Andhra Mahasabha.

n: The Forest Satyagraha first started in Palnadu, Guntur. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-5]

**Bapatla** hosted the **first Andhra Mahasabha** (**1913**); **Machilipatnam** is not linked with the forest satyagraha in these notes.
xa: The **Kakinada Riot Case** — the **first criminal case** in the **Vandemataram Movement**.
**Nyapati Subba Rao** — first lawyer in Andhra to **boycott British courts**.
**Vallabhaneni Sitamahalakshmi** — first woman arrested in the Salt Satyagraha.

255.s: Where was the first All-India Congress session held in Andhra?
255.x: Vijayawada (Bezawada) hosted the All-India Congress Committee meeting of 1921, the first all-India Congress gathering in Andhra. The first full annual session in Andhra came later at Kakinada in 1923; Madras is outside Andhra.

255.s:
Assertion (A): The first Andhra Mahasabha was regarded as the first Telugu session.
Reason (R): It demanded a separate university.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
255.x: Both are true but R does not explain A: the 1913 Bapatla Mahasabha is regarded as the first Telugu session, and it demanded a separate Andhra university, but that demand is not why it is called the first session.
255.tq: Check whether R is the cause of A.
n: The first Andhra Mahasabha was the first Telugu session. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-5]
The first Andhra Mahasabha demanded a separate university. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-5]
xs: **Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A** — so option **(2)** is correct.
A is true: the **first Andhra Mahasabha** (**Bapatla**, **26 May 1913**) was the **first Telugu session**.
R is true: it **demanded a separate (Telugu) university** — but that demand is not why it counts as the first session.

**1936 Convention** (Bellary) — **Vijayanagar Gajapati**; first **Rayalaseema** Mahasabha (**1934**) — **Nemali Pattabhirama Rao**.
