**2nd** session (**1914**, Vijayawada) — **Nyapati Subba Rao**; **4th** (**1916**, Kakinada) — **Mocherla Ramachandra Rao**.
⚠ Nemali Pattabhi Rama Rao opposed in **1916**, then presided the **6th session, Kadapa 1918**.

255.s: What was the demand of the Third Andhra Mahasabha held in 1915?
o: Creation of a separate Andhra Province (Andhra Rashtram) with the mother tongue as the medium of instruction in secondary schools
Bridging trust deficits between Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema leaders
Creation of a separate Telugu university
Opposition to the formation of a separate Andhra state
255.x: The 1915 Visakhapatnam session demanded a separate Andhra Province (Andhra Rashtram) and the mother tongue as the medium in secondary schools. The Telugu university demand was from 1913.
255.tq: Discriminate the demands of the first and third sessions.
n: The third Andhra Mahasabha demanded that the mother tongue be the medium of instruction in secondary schools. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 23-25]
xs: The **Third Andhra Mahasabha (1915)** demanded a **separate Andhra Province (Andhra Rashtram)** with the **mother tongue** as **medium of instruction** in **secondary schools** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It met at **Visakhapatnam** under the **Raja of Panagal**.
The **separate Telugu university** was first demanded at **Bapatla 1913**; bridging Coastal–Rayalaseema trust was the **1936** Bellary Convention.
xa: The **1915** session declared a state of **11 Telugu districts** just and necessary; speeches were in Telugu.
Opposition to a separate Andhra state came from the **1935** Kadapa Rayalaseema Mahasabha.
**Swadesamitran**, a Tamil daily, backed the Telugu-medium resolution of **1915**.

255.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Second Rayalaseema Mahasabha was held in Kadapa in 1935.
The First Rayalaseema Mahasabha was held at Madras on 28-1-1934.
The Second Rayalaseema Mahasabha was presided over by Nemali Pattabhirama Rao.
The Second Rayalaseema Mahasabha opposed a separate Andhra state.
255.x: Option C is incorrect: Nemali Pattabhirama Rao presided over the first Rayalaseema Mahasabha at Madras in 1934; the second, at Kadapa in 1935, was under K. Subrahmanyam. A, B and D are right.
255.tq: Discriminate the first and second sessions.
n: The First Rayalaseema Mahasabha was held on 28-1-1934 at Madras. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 45-46]
Nemali Pattabhirama Rao was the president of the First Rayalaseema Mahasabha. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 45-46]
The Second Rayalaseema Mahasabha was held in 1935 at Kadapa. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 45-46]
The Second Rayalaseema Mahasabha opposed a separate Andhra state. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 45-46]
xs: The incorrect statement is that **the Second Rayalaseema Mahasabha was presided over by Nemali Pattabhirama Rao** — so option **(3)** is the answer.
**Nemali Pattabhirama Rao** presided the **first** session (**Madras**, **28-1-1934**).
The **second** (**Kadapa**, **1935**) was presided by **K. Subrahmanyam** (other notes: **T.N. Ramakrishna Reddy**) and **opposed a separate Andhra state**.
xa: The first session was **organized** by **K. Subrahmanyam** and demanded a university at **Tirupati**.
**Pappuri Ramacharyulu**, Koti Reddy and Gadicherla stayed away from the Kadapa session.
**1938**: R. Suryanarayana Rao + N.M. Sastry formed a new Rayalaseema Mahasabha opposing an Andhra province.

255.s: Which of the following was NOT listed among the Andhra delegates who attended the first session of the Indian National Congress in 1885?
255.x: P. Rangaiah Naidu, Gutti Kesava Pillai and Venkata Subbarayudu were listed among the other Andhra delegates to the first session. Konda Venkatappayya came to prominence among Andhra Moderates after 1908.
255.tq: Use the date boundary to identify the later figure among early delegates.
xs: **Konda Venkatappayya** was not a 1885 delegate — so option **(3)** is correct.
He came to the fore among Andhra Moderates only **after 1908**, when the Extremists were crushed.
xa: **P. Anandacharlu** and **Nyapathi Subbarao** (**Rajahmundry**) attended the 1st session.
**B.N. Sarma** rose alongside Venkatappayya after 1908.
**Kesava Pillai** is listed among the early Andhra leaders.

256.s:
Consider the following statements about the Wanchoo Committee:
1. It was a single-member committee headed by Justice Kailas Nath Wanchoo, Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court.
2. It was appointed on 7 February 1953.
3. It submitted its report on 25 March 1953.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
256.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Wanchoo, Chief Justice of the Rajasthan HC, was the single member, appointed 7 Feb 1953. Statement 3 is wrong: the report came on 23 March 1953; 25 March 1953 was Nehru's announcement. So 'all three' (D) and options leaving out statement 2 (A) or including 3 (C) are wrong.
256.tq: 23 March = report; 25 March = Nehru's announcement. Single member, Rajasthan HC.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
**Statement 1 — correct:** a **single-member** committee — **Justice Kailas Nath Wanchoo**, **Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court**.
**Statement 2 — correct:** appointed on **7 Feb 1953**.
**Statement 3 — wrong:** the report came on **23 March 1953**; **25 March 1953** was Nehru's announcement.
xa: Mandate: **boundary division**, **financial settlement**, **asset distribution**, administrative arrangements.
Trigger: Nehru's **19 Dec 1952** statement after **Potti Sriramulu's** death.
⚠ His recommendation to work from **Madras** for **3-5 years** was **not** accepted.

256.s: Which one of the following was NOT included in the terms of reference of the Wanchoo Committee?
o: Determination of the permanent capital of India
256.x: The committee dealt with boundary division, financial settlement, asset distribution and administrative arrangements. Determining the permanent capital of India was not within its mandate.
256.tq: Find the unrelated item among subjects belonging to the committee’s actual mandate.
xs: Fixing the **permanent capital of India** was not Wanchoo's job — so option **(1)** is the answer.
Its mandate: **boundary division**, **financial settlement**, **asset distribution** and administrative arrangements.
xa: Wanchoo = **single member**, **Chief Justice, Rajasthan High Court**; appointed **7 Feb 1953**.
On the capital, it only suggested Andhra work temporarily from **Madras city for 3-5 years** — rejected by Nehru.
The earlier **Partition Committee** (**1949-50**, **Kumaraswamy Raja**) had first been asked to work out the asset split.

256.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Nehru’s statement following the death of Potti Sriramulu
B. Appointment of the Wanchoo Committee
C. Submission of the Wanchoo Committee report
D. Nehru’s announcement on the capital of Andhra State
256.x: The sequence was 19 December 1952, 7 February 1953, 23 March 1953 and 25 March 1953.
256.tq: Use the first and last dates to place the intermediate committee events correctly.
xs: The order is **A, B, C, D** — option **(1)** is correct.
**A:** Nehru's statement after Sriramulu's death — **19 Dec 1952**. **B:** Wanchoo appointed — **7 Feb 1953**.
**C:** Wanchoo report — **23 March 1953**. **D:** Nehru's capital announcement — **25 March 1953**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes give **25 March** as the report date — that was really Nehru's announcement.
The **25 March** announcement: capital inside Andhra, temporary capital to be decided **before 1 July 1953**.
Result: **Kurnool** became the temporary capital.

256.s: What temporary arrangement for the Andhra Government was recommended by the Wanchoo Committee?
o: It should function from Kurnool permanently.
It should function from Madras city for three to five years.
It should function from Guntur for ten years.
It should function from Bellary until 1956.
256.x: Because Andhra lacked capital infrastructure, Wanchoo recommended that the Andhra Government work temporarily from Madras city for three to five years.
256.tq: Test the recommendation through its duration and location, both of which are vulnerable to reversal.
xs: Wanchoo recommended the Andhra government work temporarily from **Madras city for 3-5 years** — option **(2)** is correct.
Reason: the new state **lacked capital infrastructure**.
**Kurnool** became only a **temporary** capital, and **Guntur** got the **High Court** (**1954**) — not the seat of government.
xa: The Centre **did not accept** this: Nehru (**25 March 1953**) ruled out Madras as capital.
⚠ **Wanchoo** = Madras for **3-5 years**; **Nehru** = capital inside Andhra → **Kurnool**.
The Andhra **PCC** had wanted **half of Madras town**.

256.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Nehru’s announcement of 25 March 1953:
1. Madras was ruled out as the capital of Andhra State.
2. The capital had to be located within Andhra.
3. A temporary capital was to be decided before 1 July 1953.
4. Some offices could continue in Madras for a period.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
256.x: All four statements correctly describe Nehru’s 25 March 1953 decision. It rejected Madras as the capital while permitting a temporary arrangement and limited continuation of offices in Madras.
256.tq: Check each administrative condition separately before selecting the complete combination.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Statements 1, 2 — correct:** "no question" of **Madras** as capital; the capital must be **inside Andhra**.
**Statement 3 — correct:** a **temporary** capital to be decided **before 1 July 1953**.
**Statement 4 — correct:** some offices could stay in **Madras** for a while.
xa: Outcome: **Kurnool** = temporary capital.
The Assembly was formed from members elected to the Madras Assembly in **1952**; **no Legislative Council**.
Nehru also said **Bellary** district court would serve **Adoni, Alur and Rayadurg** for the time being.

256.s: Which description best reflects the financial and administrative position of the newly formed Andhra State?
o: It had no need for an asset division with residual Madras.
It possessed a developed capital and a major commercial centre.
It was administratively and economically orphaned, lacking a developed capital and commercial centre.
It had inherited the entire financial surplus of residual Madras.
256.x: The new state lacked both developed capital infrastructure and a commercial centre and was described as administratively and economically orphaned.
256.tq: Choose the precise combined description rather than an exaggerated or reversed financial claim.
xs: Without a capital or commercial centre, Andhra was "**administratively and economically orphaned**" — option **(3)** is correct.
It **did** need an asset division: assets and administration were split between **Andhra** and **residual Madras**.
xa: For lack of capital infrastructure, Wanchoo proposed **Madras city for 3-5 years**; Nehru chose a capital inside Andhra (**Kurnool**).
The **Partition Committee** (**1949-50**) first worked on the asset split.
⚠ Compare **2014**: assets split by **location**, debts by **population** → AP carried a heavy debt share.

256.s: The Partition Committee associated with administrative arrangements for the new Andhra State was chaired by:
256.x: The Partition Committee of 1949–50, associated with administrative arrangements for the new state, was chaired by Kumaraswamy Raja.
256.tq: Match the committee with its chairman while avoiding substitution by a later committee head.
xs: The **Partition Committee** (**1949-50**) was chaired by **Kumaraswamy Raja** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Justice Wanchoo** headed the **1953** single-member committee; **C.M. Trivedi** was the **Special Officer**.
xa: The Partition Committee first worked out the **asset split** and **administrative arrangements**.
Wanchoo (appointed **7 Feb 1953**) later took up **financial settlement** and **asset distribution**.

256.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the High Court arrangements after the formation of Andhra State:
1. The Madras High Court retained jurisdiction until the site of the Andhra High Court was decided.
2. The Andhra High Court was established in 1954.
3. The Andhra High Court was established at Guntur.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
256.x: All three statements are correct. The Madras High Court continued jurisdiction temporarily, and the Andhra High Court was established at Guntur in 1954.
256.tq: Separate the interim jurisdiction of the old court from the establishment details of the new court.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Statement 1 — correct:** the **Madras High Court** kept jurisdiction until the Andhra HC site was decided.
**Statements 2, 3 — correct:** the Andhra High Court was set up at **Guntur** in **1954**.
xa: **Bellary district court** was to serve **Adoni, Alur and Rayadurg** for the time being (Nehru, **25 Mar 1953**).
Capital: **Kurnool** (temporary); High Court: **Guntur**.

256.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
256.x: Rayadurg taluk went to Andhra and was included in Anantapur district. Adoni and Alur went to Kurnool district, while Bellary, Hospet and the other listed areas went to Mysore.
256.tq: Start with the sure district allocation and reject options that reverse the territorial division.
xs: **Rayadurg taluk → Andhra (Anantapur district)** is correctly matched — option **(1)**.
**Bellary taluk** went to **Mysore** (Justice Mishra's report), not Kurnool.
**Hospet** went to **Mysore**; **Adoni** went to **Andhra (Kurnool district)**.
xa: **Adoni and Alur** → **Kurnool** district.
**Siruguppa, Hospet, Sandur, Harpanahalli, Hadagali** → **Mysore**.
After the split, **Tungabhadra** works were shared between **Andhra** and **Mysore**.

256.s: The decision to assign Bellary taluk to Mysore was based on the report of:
o: Kumaraswamy Raja, Chairman of the Partition Committee
M. Trivedi, Special Officer of Andhra State
Justice Mishra, Chief Justice of the Hyderabad High Court
Justice Wanchoo, Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court
256.x: Bellary taluk was assigned to Mysore on the basis of Justice Mishra’s report. Justice Mishra was the Chief Justice of the Hyderabad High Court.
256.tq: Use the wrong-person-for-the-deed trap by matching the report with its author and office.
xs: **Bellary taluk** went to **Mysore** on the report of **Justice Mishra**, **Chief Justice, Hyderabad High Court** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Wanchoo** (Rajasthan HC), **Kumaraswamy Raja** (Partition Committee) and **C.M. Trivedi** (Special Officer) did not decide Bellary taluk.
xa: Mishra's hearings: **1-15 May 1953**.
**Rayadurg** → Anantapur; **Adoni, Alur** → Kurnool.
The **Tungabhadra Board** was set up under the **Andhra State Act 1953**.

256.s: The Sreebagh Pact of 1937 promised priority for irrigation in Rayalaseema and Nellore on which rivers?
o: Krishna, Godavari and Pennar only in coastal Andhra
256.x: The Sreebagh Pact promised priority for irrigation in Rayalaseema and Nellore on the Tungabhadra, Krishna and Penna for ten years or as needed.
256.tq: Recall the exact three-river combination instead of selecting a nearby river group.
xs: The **Sreebagh Pact** (**1937**) gave **Rayalaseema** and **Nellore** irrigation priority on the **Tungabhadra, Krishna and Penna** — option **(2)** is correct.
Godavari, Vamsadhara, Bhima and Kaveri were not in the pact's clause.
xa: The priority was for **10 years** or as needed.
The **Andhra State Act 1953** set up the **Tungabhadra Board** to manage the works.
Today the Centre plans a **high-level committee** on Tungabhadra disputes among **AP, Telangana and Karnataka**.

256.s: What institutional arrangement followed the division of Bellary in relation to the Tungabhadra project?
o: The project works became shared by Andhra and Mysore, and a Tungabhadra Board was established under the Andhra State Act, 1953.
The project was transferred entirely to Mysore.
The project was placed under the Madras High Court.
A board was established under the Sreebagh Pact of 1937 alone.
256.x: After Bellary was divided, the Tungabhadra works became shared between Andhra and Mysore. A Tungabhadra Board was set up under the Andhra State Act, 1953 to manage the works.
256.tq: Link the territorial change to its institutional consequence and reject the swapped legal basis.
xs: After the **Bellary** split, Tungabhadra works were shared by **Andhra** and **Mysore**, and a **Tungabhadra Board** was set up under the **Andhra State Act, 1953** — option **(1)**.
The **1937 Sreebagh Pact** only promised irrigation priority — it set up no board.
xa: **Bellary taluk** and **Hospet** etc. went to **Mysore**; **Adoni, Alur, Rayadurg** to Andhra.
On **26 Jun 2026**, **C.R. Patil** opened **33 new gates** of the **Tungabhadra dam** with three CMs present.
A **high-level committee** is planned for **AP, Telangana and Karnataka** water disputes.

256.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the 2014 bifurcation arrangements?
o: The Sheela Bhide Committee dealt with employee allocation and the Kamalanathan Committee dealt with capital.
The Section 6 expert committee dealt only with High Court jurisdiction.
The Kamalanathan Committee dealt with employees, while the Sheela Bhide Committee dealt with Schedule IX institutions.
Both committees dealt exclusively with Tungabhadra water sharing.
256.x: The Sheela Bhide Committee dealt with Schedule IX institutions, the Kamalanathan Committee with employees, and a separate Section 6 expert committee examined the capital issue.
256.tq: Match each panel with its specialised subject and reject swapped committee functions.
xs: **Kamalanathan Committee** = **employees**; **Sheela Bhide Committee** = **Schedule IX institutions** — option **(3)** is correct.
The **Section 6** expert committee dealt with the **capital**, not the High Court.
None of these panels dealt with **Tungabhadra** water.
xa: In **2014**, assets were split by **location** and debts by **population** → AP carried a heavy debt share.
⚠ For **1953**, the matching panels were the **Partition Committee** (**1949-50**) and the **Wanchoo Committee**.

257.s: Which was the first Telugu newspaper, established in 1835 at Bellary and run by Christian missionaries?
257.x: Satyadoota, established in Bellary in 1835, was the first Telugu newspaper and was run by Christian missionaries.
257.tq: Recall the earliest publication through its year, place and institutional association.
xs: **Satyadoota** (**1835, Bellary**), run by **Christian missionaries**, was the first Telugu newspaper — option **(4)** is correct.
**Vrutantini** came in **1838** (Mandigala Venkataraya Sastri); **Hitavadi** in **1841** (Edmund Park).
**Vartamana Tarangini** (**1842**, Madras) was the first Telugu paper started by a Muslim (**Syed Rahamatullah**).
xa: ⚠ **Satyadoota** = first Telugu paper (Bellary); **Hitavadi** = first **printed in Andhra**.
**Andhra Prakasika** (**1885**) = first **political** journal in Telugu.
**Desabhimani** = the **only Telugu daily** in British Andhra.

257.s: Which Telugu newspaper was the first to be printed in Andhra?
257.x: Hitavadi, associated with Edmund Park and dated 1841, was the first Telugu newspaper printed in Andhra.
257.tq: Distinguish the first Telugu newspaper from the first one printed in Andhra.
xs: **Hitavadi** (**1841**, **Edmund Park**) was the first Telugu newspaper **printed in Andhra** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Satyadoota** (**1835**) was the first Telugu paper overall, but at **Bellary**.
**Vartamana Tarangini** (**1842**) and **Tattvabodhini** (**1864**) were both from **Madras**.
xa: ⚠ **Satyadoota** = first Telugu paper; **Hitavadi** = first printed in Andhra.
**Vrutantini** (**1838**) — Mandigala Venkataraya Sastri.

257.s:
Consider the following statements about Vartamana Tarangini:
1. It was started on 8 June 1842 at Madras.
2. Syed Rahamatullah was associated with its beginning.
3. It was the first Telugu paper started by a Muslim.
4. After 1843, it passed to Puvvada Seshagiri Rao.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
257.x: All four statements are correct. Vartamana Tarangini was a weekly begun at Madras in 1842 by Syed Rahamatullah, the first Telugu paper started by a Muslim, and later passed to Puvvada Seshagiri Rao.
257.tq: Verify date, place, distinction and ownership change as separate elements of one publication profile.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Statements 1, 2 — correct:** started **8 June 1842** at **Madras** by **Syed Rahamatullah**.
**Statement 3 — correct:** the **first Telugu paper started by a Muslim**.
**Statement 4 — correct:** after **1843** it passed to **Puvvada Seshagiri Rao** and got its own press.
xa: It was a **weekly**.
Earlier papers: **Satyadoota** (**1835**), **Vrutantini** (**1838**), **Hitavadi** (**1841**).
**Tattvabodhini** (**1864**, Madras) came from the **Madras Veda Samaj**.

257.s:
Consider the following statements about early Telugu journals and widow remarriage:
1. Tattvabodhini, published at Madras in 1864 by the Madras Veda Samaj, supported widow remarriage.
2. Purushartha Pradayini, published at Machilipatnam in 1872, carried articles only against widow remarriage.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
257.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Purushartha Pradayini carried articles both for and against widow remarriage. So only 1 (A); B, C and D all depend on the false statement 2 or deny the true statement 1.
257.tq: Veda Samaj's Tattvabodhini = for; Purushartha Pradayini = both sides.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
**Statement 1 — correct:** **Tattvabodhini** (**1864**, Madras, **Madras Veda Samaj**) supported widow remarriage.
**Statement 2 — wrong:** **Purushartha Pradayini** (**1872**, Machilipatnam) carried articles **both for and against** widow remarriage.
xa: **Veeresalingam's** journals included **Vivekavardhani (1874)** and **Sati Hitabodhini (1883)**.
Women's-cause papers: **Hindu Sundari** (**1902**) and **Sri Savitri** (**1904**).

257.s:
Arrange the following journals of Kandukuri Veeresalingam in chronological order of their commencement:
A. Satyasamvardhini
B. Vivekavardhani
C. Sati Hitabodhini
D. Hasyasanjivani
257.x: Vivekavardhani began in 1874, Hasyasanjivani in 1876, Sati Hitabodhini in 1883 and Satyasamvardhini in 1891.
257.tq: Fix the earliest and latest dates first, then arrange the middle publications.
xs: The order is **B, D, C, A** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Vivekavardhani** (**1874**) → **Hasyasanjivani** (**1876**) → **Sati Hitabodhini** (**1883**) → **Satyasamvardhini** (**1891**).
xa: Later journals: **Zenana Patrika** (**1894**) and **Satyavadini** (**1905**).
Veeresalingam had **his own press from 1876**.
He also ran **Chintamani** with **Nyapati Subbarao**.

257.s: Andhra Patrika was initially published from which place and in which year?
257.x: Andhra Patrika was started at Bombay on 9 September 1908 by Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao.
257.tq: Separate the original publication place and year from the later shift and change to a daily.
xs: **Andhra Patrika** began at **Bombay** on **9 Sept 1908** — option **(3)** is correct.
It moved to **Madras** later, and became a **daily in 1914** — so options 1 and 4 mix up the facts.
**Vijayawada, 1907** is Gadicherla's **Swarajya**.
xa: Founder: **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**; it **promoted Gandhian ideas**.
He also ran the literary monthly **Bharati** (**1924**).
APPSC GS 2025 pair: **Andhra Patrika – Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**.

257.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
257.x: Andhra Prabha was associated with the Indian Express group and Ramnath Goenka; Narla Venkateswara Rao was a noted editor. Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao founded Andhra Patrika.
257.tq: Find the swapped founder or editor among closely related Andhra newspapers.
xs: **Andhra Prabha — Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** is wrongly matched — option **(1)**; Andhra Prabha was an **Indian Express group** paper (Ramnath Goenka).
**Desabhimani — Devaguptam Seshachalapati Rao**, **Zamin Ryot — Nellore Venkatarama Naidu**, **Swarajya — Gadicherla** are all correct.
xa: **Narla Venkateswara Rao** was a noted editor of Andhra Prabha (**1938**, Madras).
Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao founded **Andhra Patrika** (**1908**) and **Bharati** (**1924**).
Desabhimani began as **Krishnavrittantini**; Zamin Ryot wrote on **peasant issues**.

257.s:
Consider the following statements about the newspapers named Swarajya:
1. Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao's Telugu Swarajya was started in 1907 at Vijayawada.
2. Gadicherla's Swarajya was earlier named Krishnavrittantini.
3. Tanguturi Prakasam's Swarajya was a separate English daily from Madras.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
257.x: Statement 1 is correct (Vijayawada, 1907). Statement 2 is wrong: Swarajya was earlier named Sri Venkateswara Patrika; Krishnavrittantini was the earlier name of Desabhimani. Statement 3 is correct: Prakasam's Swarajya was a separate English daily from Madras. Hence 1 and 3 only; A omits 3, C and D include the false 2.
257.tq: Two Swarajyas: Gadicherla's Telugu (Vijayawada 1907, ex-Sri Venkateswara Patrika) vs Prakasam's English daily (Madras).
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
**Statement 1 — correct:** Gadicherla's Telugu **Swarajya** began in **1907** at **Vijayawada**.
**Statement 2 — wrong:** it was earlier **Sri Venkateswara Patrika**; **Krishnavrittantini** was the earlier name of **Desabhimani**.
**Statement 3 — correct:** **Prakasam's Swarajya** was a separate **English daily** from **Madras** (APPSC GS 2021 key).
xa: Gadicherla's Swarajya was **militant nationalist**; he was jailed for editorials such as **"Veerabali"**.
APPSC GS 2025 pair: **Swarajya – Gadicherla**.

257.s: Krishna Patrika was founded at Machilipatnam on 1 February 1902 by which pair?
o: Konda Venkatappaiah and Dasu Narayana Rao
Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham and C.Y. Chintamani
Mutnuri Krishna Rao and Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao
Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao and Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao
257.x: Krishna Patrika was founded on 1 February 1902 by Konda Venkatappaiah and Dasu Narayana Rao at Machilipatnam.
257.tq: Combine the date with the founder pair rather than relying on the later editor’s name.
xs: **Konda Venkatappaiah and Dasu Narayana Rao** founded **Krishna Patrika** (**1 Feb 1902**, Machilipatnam) — option **(1)** is correct.
**Mutnuri Krishna Rao** was its later, most famous editor; **Gadicherla** founded **Swarajya**.
**Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham** ran **Manorama** and **Desamata**; **Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao** ran **Andhra Kesari**.
xa: APPSC GS 2025 pair: **Krishna Patrika – Konda Venkatappayya**.
**30 Nov 1912**: Krishna Patrika wrote that strengthening the nation begins with the Andhra movement.

257.s: Who is regarded as the second and most famous editor of Krishna Patrika, largely responsible for its success?
257.x: Mutnuri Krishna Rao was Krishna Patrika's second and most famous editor and was largely responsible for its success (APPSC GS 2024). Konda Venkatappayya and Dasu Narayana Rao founded it in 1902; Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao founded Andhra Patrika.
257.tq: Founders of Krishna Patrika = Konda + Dasu; famous editor = Mutnuri.
xs: **Mutnuri Krishna Rao** was Krishna Patrika's **second and most famous editor**, "largely responsible for its success" — option **(2)** (APPSC GS 2024).
**Konda Venkatappayya** and **Dasu Narayana Rao** were its **founders** (**1902**).
**Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** founded **Andhra Patrika** (**1908**).
xa: Krishna Patrika's office was a meeting point for freedom fighters.
It backed the **Vandemataram / Swadeshi** movement.
Its **11 Apr 1914** editorial and **19 Jul 1913** iceberg cartoon backed the Andhra movement.

257.s: Who was the editor associated with Bharati, the literary monthly started in 1924?
257.x: Bharati, a literary monthly started in 1924, was associated with Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao.
257.tq: Match a journal with its editor while separating literary journals from political newspapers.
xs: **Bharati** (**1924**), a literary monthly, was run by **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Suravaram Pratapa Reddy** ran **Golconda Patrika**; **Jayanti Ramayya** the **Andhra Sahitya Parishad Patrika**; **Kokkonda Venkataratnam** **Andhra Bhasa Sanjivani**.
xa: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao also founded **Andhra Patrika** (**9 Sept 1908**, Bombay).
**Manorama** (**1906**) and **Desamata** (**1910**) — Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham.

257.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Andhra Bhasa Sanjivani — Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham
Andhra Sahitya Parishad Patrika — Jayanti Ramayya
257.x: Andhra Bhasa Sanjivani was associated with Kokkonda Venkataratnam, who introduced the editorial column. Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham was associated with Manorama and Desamata.
257.tq: Locate the swapped editor among a cluster of journal–editor pairs.
xs: **Andhra Bhasa Sanjivani** was **Kokkonda Venkataratnam's**, not Chilakamarti's — option **(1)** is the wrong pair.
**Andhra Sahitya Parishad Patrika — Jayanti Ramayya**, **Manoranjani — Kallakuri Narayana Rao**, **Golconda Patrika — Suravaram Pratapa Reddy** are correct.
xa: Andhra Bhasa Sanjivani **introduced the editorial column**.
**Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham** ran **Manorama** (**1906**) and **Desamata** (**1910**).
**Chintamani** — Veeresalingam and **Nyapati Subbarao**.

257.s: The article 'Are Telugu people backward?' reported which comparison?
o: 56 Andhras to 8 non-Andhras in civil services, and 19 to 0 in the judiciary
19 non-Andhras to 0 Andhras in civil services, and 56 to 8 in the judiciary
8 non-Andhras to 56 Andhras in civil services, and 0 to 19 in the judiciary
56 non-Andhras to 8 Andhras in civil services, and 19 to 0 in the judiciary
257.x: The article reported 56 non-Andhras to 8 Andhras in the civil services and 19 non-Andhras to no Andhras in the judiciary.
257.tq: Guard against reversed comparisons in numerical statement questions.
xs: "Are Telugu people backward?" reported **56 non-Andhras to 8 Andhras** in civil services and **19 to 0** in the judiciary — option **(4)** is correct.
The other options reverse the figures or swap services and judiciary.
xa: It appeared in **The Hindu** on **15 Apr 1911**, by **Jonnavittula Gurunatham**.
He wrote **6** articles in **1911**; Telugu papers demanded a separate state from **1911**.
Opposing view: the **"Viswamitra"** letter in The Hindu (**29 Aug 1912**) asked where Andhra would find officers.

257.s: Which newspaper stated on 30 November 1912 that strengthening the nation begins with the Andhra movement?
257.x: Krishna Patrika made this statement on 30 November 1912 in support of the Andhra movement.
257.tq: Link a dated editorial statement to the correct newspaper.
xs: **Krishna Patrika** wrote on **30 Nov 1912** that strengthening the nation begins with the Andhra movement — option **(3)** is correct.
**Janmabhumi's** similar article (national unity) came on **25 Aug 1920**.
xa: Krishna Patrika's **19 Jul 1913** cartoon showed **Rayalaseema** as an **iceberg** blocking the ship.
Its **11 Apr 1914** editorial also backed the movement.
**The Hindu** ran both Gurunatham's articles and the opposing **"Viswamitra"** letter.

257.s: Which of the following groups consisted entirely of publications that supported the movement for a separate Andhra?
o: Andhra Patrika, Krishna Patrika, Desabhimani, Desamata and Darbar
The Hindu, Viswamitra, Swadesamitran and Desamata
Krishna Patrika, The Hindu, Modern Review and Viswamitra
Desabhimani, Zamin Ryot, The Hindu and Hindusthan Review
257.x: Andhra Patrika, Krishna Patrika, Desabhimani, Desamata and Darbar were listed as supporters of the separate Andhra movement.
257.tq: Screen each group for a known opposing paper or publication not listed as a supporter.
xs: **Andhra Patrika, Krishna Patrika, Desabhimani, Desamata and Darbar** all supported a separate Andhra — option **(1)** is correct.
The **"Viswamitra"** letter in The Hindu (**29 Aug 1912**) **opposed** the demand, so options 2 and 3 fail.
**Zamin Ryot** is not among the listed supporters.
xa: Outside support: **The Modern Review**, **Hindusthan Review**, **London Review of Reviews**.
**Janmabhumi** (**25 Aug 1920**): the Andhra movement strengthens national unity.

257.s: The Vernacular Press Act of 1878 was popularly known as the 'Gagging Act'. Who repealed it, and in which year?
257.x: The Vernacular Press Act of 1878, popularly called the Gagging Act, was repealed by Ripon in 1882.
257.tq: Pair the enactment with the correct repealing authority and year, avoiding near-date traps.
xs: The **Vernacular Press Act, 1878** ("Gagging Act") was repealed by **Ripon** in **1882** — option **(3)** is correct.
**1878** is when the Act was passed, not repealed.
xa: This was the background to the growth of Telugu nationalist papers.
Gadicherla was jailed with a heavy sentence for **Swarajya** editorials such as **"Veerabali"**.

257.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding newspapers associated with movements in Andhra:

List-I (Movement)

a. Vandemataram/Swadeshi movement
b. Peasant or anti-zamindari movement
c. Socialist movement
d. Communist movement

List-II (Newspaper)

i. Zamin Ryot
ii. Prajasakthi
iii. Navasakthi
iv. Krishna Patrika, Swarajya, Desamata, Andhra Kesari and Navayuga

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
257.x: The Vandemataram/Swadeshi movement was supported by Krishna Patrika, Swarajya, Desamata, Andhra Kesari and Navayuga. Zamin Ryot supported the peasant or anti-zamindari movement, Navasakthi was associated with socialism, and Prajasakthi with communism.
257.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes with mismatched movement–newspaper associations.
xs: **a–iv, b–i, c–iii, d–ii** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Vandemataram / Swadeshi:** Krishna Patrika, Swarajya, Desamata, **Andhra Kesari**, Navayuga.
**Peasant / anti-zamindari:** **Zamin Ryot**; **Socialist:** **Navasakthi**; **Communist:** **Prajasakthi**.
xa: **Home Rule** paper: **Andhra Mata** (APPSC G2 2017 key).
**Andhra Kesari** was **Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao's** paper (Rajahmundry); **Desamata** was also from Rajahmundry.
Women's cause: **Hindu Sundari** (**1902**), **Sri Savitri** (**1904**).

257.s: Which Telugu newspaper is associated with the Home Rule movement in Andhra?
257.x: Andhra Mata was the paper of the Home Rule movement (APPSC G2 2017 key). Zamin Ryot wrote on peasant issues, Navasakthi was the first fully socialist Telugu journal, and Jaya Bharat was the first Telugu journal after independence.
257.tq: Home Rule -> Andhra Mata.
xs: **Andhra Mata** was the **Home Rule** paper (APPSC G2 2017 key) — option **(3)** is correct.
**Zamin Ryot** = peasant issues; **Navasakthi** = socialist; **Jaya Bharat** = first Telugu journal after independence.
xa: **Vandemataram / Swadeshi** papers: Krishna Patrika, Swarajya, Desamata, Andhra Kesari, Navayuga.
**Prajasakthi** = first communist Telugu journal.

257.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the social impact of newspapers in the Andhra region:
1. Newspapers gave rise to reading rooms.
2. Newspapers contributed to the development of libraries.
3. Newspapers had no role beyond reporting political events.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
257.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: newspapers gave rise to reading rooms and libraries. Statement 3 is false because their influence extended beyond merely reporting political events.
257.tq: Reject the restrictive statement and select the combination containing the two wider social effects.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
**Statements 1, 2 — correct:** newspapers gave rise to **reading rooms and libraries**.
**Statement 3 — wrong:** the press also **spread the national movement** and built support for a **separate Andhra**.
xa: First political journal: **Andhra Prakasika** (**1885**).
Only Telugu daily of British Andhra: **Desabhimani**.

257.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Andhra Prakasika — first political journal in Telugu
2. Desabhimani — only Telugu daily in British Andhra
3. Satyadoota — first Telugu journal published after independence
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
257.x: Pair 1 is correct: Andhra Prakasika (1885) was the first political journal in Telugu. Pair 2 is correct: Desabhimani was the only Telugu daily in British Andhra. Pair 3 is wrong: Satyadoota (1835) was the first Telugu newspaper; Jaya Bharat was the first Telugu journal after independence. Hence 1 and 2 only.
257.tq: First political journal = Andhra Prakasika; only daily = Desabhimani.
xs: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
**Pair 1 — correct:** **Andhra Prakasika** (**1885**) = first political journal in Telugu.
**Pair 2 — correct:** **Desabhimani** = only Telugu daily in British Andhra.
**Pair 3 — wrong:** **Satyadoota** (**1835**) was the first Telugu newspaper; **Jaya Bharat** was the first after independence.
xa: Andhra Prakasika's editor: **A.P. Parthasarathy Naidu**.
Desabhimani's founder: **Devaguptam Seshachalapati Rao**; it began as **Krishnavrittantini**.
**Hitavadi** (**1841**) = first Telugu paper printed in Andhra.

258.s:
Mutnuri Krishna Rao transformed Krishna Patrika primarily into a:

1. Political weekly
2. Centre for freedom fighters
3. Commercial banking journal
4. Hub of political awakening
258.x: Mutnuri Krishna Rao made Krishna Patrika a political weekly and a hub for freedom fighters, which made it a centre of political awakening (1, 2 and 4). It was never a commercial banking journal, so 3 is wrong.
258.tq: Find the statement that changes the political character of the institution into an unrelated activity.
xs: **Mutnuri Krishna Rao** made Krishna Patrika a **political weekly**, a **hub for freedom fighters** and of **political awakening** — option **(2) 1, 2 and 4 only**.
Item 3 is wrong: Krishna Patrika was never a **commercial banking journal**.
xa: In **1907**, Mutnuri called extremist leaders to visit Andhra.
**Bipin Chandra Pal** toured Andhra in **April 1907** — Kakinada (**17** Apr) and **five** lectures at Rajahmundry (**19-24** Apr).
Editors made journalism a tool of political awakening that also publicised the **library movement**.

258.s: Which extremist leader toured Andhra in April 1907, lecturing at Kakinada and delivering five lectures at Rajahmundry?
258.x: Bipin Chandra Pal toured Andhra in April 1907 (Kakinada on 17 April, Rajahmundry 19-24 April) after Andhra leaders invited extremist leaders. Tilak, Lajpat Rai and Aurobindo did not make this tour. Some sources credit Mutnuri Krishna Rao with organising it; the APPSC G2 2011 key credits Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao.
258.tq: 1907 Andhra tour = Bipin Chandra Pal; organiser per G2 2011 key = Gadicherla.
xs: **Bipin Chandra Pal** toured Andhra in **April 1907** — option **(4)** is correct.
He spoke at **Kakinada** (**17** Apr) and gave **five** lectures at **Rajahmundry** (**19-24** Apr), at **Mutnuri's** invitation.
xa: ⚠ Trap: some notes say Mutnuri organised the tour; the **G2 2011 key** credits **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao**.
The **1907 Rajahmundry College** incident got Gadicherla blacklisted from government jobs.
**Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao** co-founded the **Bala Bharati Samithi**, Rajahmundry, **Feb 1907**.

258.s:
Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao is associated with which of the following publication years?

1. Andhra Patrika — 1908
2. Bharati — 1924
3. Krishna Patrika — 1907
4. Swarajya — 1907
258.x: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao founded Andhra Patrika (1908) and Bharati (1924). Krishna Patrika was founded in 1902 by Konda Venkatappayya and Dasu Narayana Rao, and Swarajya (1907) was Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao's paper. Hence 1 and 2 only.
258.tq: Split publication years from the editor–paper associations to catch cross-pairing.
xs: Only items 1 and 2 fit — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**: **Andhra Patrika** (**1908**) and **Bharati** (**1924**).
**Krishna Patrika** was **Mutnuri Krishna Rao's** paper, not his.
**Swarajya** (**1907**) was **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao's**.
xa: Kasinathuni also set up the publishing house **Andhra Granthamala**, named to popularise the word "Andhra".
He lived **1867-1947**; title **"Desoddharaka"**.
The **Sreebagh Pact** was signed at his Madras house on **16 Nov 1937**.

258.s:
Which of the following statements about Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao is correct?

1. He lived from 1867 to 1947.
2. He was known by the title ‘Desoddharaka’.
3. His business wealth was put to public use in accordance with the idea of Gandhian trusteeship.
4. His Amrutanjan business helped fund his public work.
258.x: All four statements are correct. Nageswara Rao (1867-1947) was titled Desoddharaka, and in the spirit of Gandhian trusteeship he used the wealth of his Amrutanjan business to fund his public work.
258.tq: Treat dates, titles, ideology and financial support as separate factual checks.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Statements 1, 2 — correct:** he lived **1867-1947** and was titled **"Desoddharaka"** (some notes render it "Desabandhu").
**Statements 3, 4 — correct:** in **Gandhian trusteeship** spirit, his **Amrutanjan** business funded his public work.
xa: Other titles: **"Udattamati"** (noble-minded) and **"Library Protector"**.
With Ayyanki and Gadicherla he made up the **Granthalayodyama Trimurthulu**.
Film **Viswadata** marks his **160th birth anniversary**.

258.s:
Consider the following statements about Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao:
1. He set up the publishing house Andhra Granthamala, named to popularise the word 'Andhra'.
2. Sreebagh was his house in Madras.
3. The Sreebagh Pact was signed at his house on 16 November 1935.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
258.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Sreebagh Pact was signed on 16 November 1937, not 1935. Hence 1 and 2 only; A leaves out the true statement 2, C and D include the false statement 3.
258.tq: Sreebagh Pact = 16 Nov 1937, at Nageswara Rao's Madras house.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
**Statement 1 — correct:** his publishing house **Andhra Granthamala** was named to popularise the word "Andhra".
**Statement 2 — correct:** **Sreebagh** was his **Madras** house.
**Statement 3 — wrong:** the **Sreebagh Pact** was signed on **16 Nov 1937**, not 1935.
xa: His papers: **Andhra Patrika** (**1908**) and **Bharati** (**1924**).
His **Amrutanjan** business funded his public work.

258.s:
A village library opened by a group of ten youths could receive which support from Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao?

1. His newspaper
2. Books
3. Bharati free of cost
4. Government employment for all members
258.x: Nageswara Rao sent his newspaper, books and Bharati free to any group of ten youths that opened a village library. Government employment was not part of this support.
258.tq: Apply the eligibility condition and separate actual library support from an invented benefit.
xs: Any group of **10 youths** opening a village library got his **paper**, **books** and **Bharati** free — option **(2) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
Item 4 is wrong: **government employment** was never part of this support.
xa: He was called the **"Library Protector"**.
He finished the catalogue of printed Telugu books begun by **Velidanda Hanumantha Rao**.
**Granthalayodyama Trimurthulu**: Kasinathuni, **Ayyanki** and **Gadicherla**.

258.s: The Granthalayodyama Trimurthulu consisted of Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao, Ayyanki and:
258.x: The Granthalayodyama Trimurthulu included Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao, Ayyanki and Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao.
258.tq: Complete the named triad by identifying the missing member from the same movement.
xs: The **Granthalayodyama Trimurthulu** = Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao, **Ayyanki** and **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Gante Laxmanna** co-founded the **Bala Bharati Samithi**; **Dasu Narayana Rao** and **Konda Venkatappayya** are not in the trio.
xa: **Gadicherla** founded the **Edward Corporation Library**, **Nandyal**, with Kaderbad Narasinga Rao.
Kasinathuni gave free papers and books to village libraries set up by **10 youths**.

258.s:
Consider the following statements about Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao:
1. He was arrested and heavily sentenced for Swarajya editorials such as "Veerabali".
2. He was blacklisted from government jobs after the 1907 Rajahmundry College incident.
3. He founded the Edward Corporation Library at Kurnool with Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
258.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: he founded the Edward Corporation Library at Nandyal (now the Victoria Reading Room) with Kaderbad Narasinga Rao. Hence 1 and 2 only; A omits the true 2, C and D include the false 3.
258.tq: Veerabali = Swarajya editorial; 1907 Rajahmundry College = blacklisting; Nandyal library.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
**Statement 1 — correct:** heavily sentenced for **Swarajya** editorials such as **"Veerabali"**.
**Statement 2 — correct:** blacklisted from government jobs after the **1907 Rajahmundry College** incident.
**Statement 3 — wrong:** the library was at **Nandyal**, founded with **Kaderbad Narasinga Rao**.
xa: The Nandyal library is now the **Victoria Reading Room**.
Gadicherla's **Swarajya** dates from **1907**.
⚠ The **G2 2011 key** credits Gadicherla with organising **Bipin Chandra Pal's** tour.

258.s: Who co-founded the Bala Bharati Samithi at Rajahmundry in February 1907?
o: Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao, Gante Laxmanna and Unguturi Sriramulu
Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao, Kaderbad Narasinga Rao and Ayyanki
Konda Venkatappayya, Dasu Narayana Rao and Mutnuri Krishna Rao
Nageswara Rao, Gante Laxmanna and Kaderbad Narasinga Rao
258.x: Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao co-founded the Bala Bharati Samithi at Rajahmundry in February 1907 with Gante Laxmanna and Unguturi Sriramulu.
258.tq: Check the complete founder group together with the place and month.
xs: **Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao**, **Gante Laxmanna** and **Unguturi Sriramulu** co-founded the **Bala Bharati Samithi** (Rajahmundry, **Feb 1907**) — option **(1)**.
**Gadicherla** and **Kaderbad Narasinga Rao** founded the Nandyal library; **Ayyanki** belongs to the Granthalayodyama trio.
xa: The same year, **Bipin Chandra Pal** gave **five** lectures at Rajahmundry (**19-24** Apr 1907).
⚠ Notes differ on the **Andhra Kesari** editor — some give it to Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao, others to Gadicherla.

258.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. Mutnuri Krishna Rao — Krishna Patrika
2. Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao — Bharati
3. Nellore Venkatarama Naidu — Zamin Ryot
4. Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham — Desamata and Manorama
258.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Mutnuri Krishna Rao edited Krishna Patrika, Nageswara Rao edited Bharati, Venkatarama Naidu edited Zamin Ryot, and Chilakamarti edited Desamata and Manorama.
258.tq: Start from the sure editor–paper pairs and eliminate codes containing a swapped association.
xs: All four pairs are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Mutnuri Krishna Rao — Krishna Patrika**; **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao — Bharati** (**1924**).
**Nellore Venkatarama Naidu — Zamin Ryot**; **Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham — Desamata, Manorama**.
xa: Kasinathuni also founded **Andhra Patrika** (**1908**).
**Gadicherla** edited **Swarajya** (**1907**) and also Navayugam, Matru Seva, Panchayati Rajyam.

258.s: The newspaper 'Swarajya' (1907) of the Andhra movement was edited by:
258.x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao edited Swarajya (1907). Nageswara Rao edited Andhra Patrika and Bharati, Venkatarama Naidu edited Zamin Ryot, and Chilakamarti edited Desamata and Manorama.
258.tq: Swarajya 1907 = Gadicherla, the Vande Mataram year paper.
xs: **Swarajya** (**1907**) was edited by **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Kasinathuni** = Andhra Patrika, Bharati; **Venkatarama Naidu** = Zamin Ryot; **Chilakamarti** = Desamata, Manorama.
xa: Gadicherla was arrested and heavily sentenced for Swarajya editorials such as **"Veerabali"**.
His other papers: **Navayugam**, **Andhra Patrika**, **Matru Seva**, **Panchayati Rajyam**.
He founded the **Edward Corporation Library**, Nandyal.

258.s: A feature film being made on Nageswara Rao Pantulu for his 160th birth anniversary is titled:
258.x: The feature film is titled Viswadata and is being made in connection with Nageswara Rao Pantulu’s 160th birth anniversary.
258.tq: Identify the current-affairs title associated with the historical personality.
xs: The film on Nageswara Rao Pantulu for his **160th birth anniversary** is **Viswadata** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Desoddharaka** is his title; **Andhra Kesari** and **Swarajya** are papers.
xa: It is made by **Sivalenka Pavani Prasad**, his great-grandson (**14 May 2026**).
Nageswara Rao lived **1867-1947**; his **Amrutanjan** business funded his public work.

258.s: Which of the following best describes the broader significance of the Andhra editors discussed here?
o: They used journalism for political awakening and also supported and publicised the library movement.
They replaced village libraries with privately owned commercial presses.
They restricted newspapers to government announcements.
They confined journalism to literary criticism and avoided public causes.
258.x: These editors made journalism an instrument of political awakening while also funding and publicising the library movement.
258.tq: Choose the option that combines both linked functions instead of an extreme or exclusive description.
xs: The editors made journalism a tool of **political awakening** that also **funded and publicised the library movement** — option **(1)** is correct.
They built village libraries, not replaced them, and took up public causes.
xa: **Kasinathuni** sent free papers and books to village libraries; **Gadicherla** founded the Nandyal library.
**Granthalayodyama Trimurthulu**: Kasinathuni, Ayyanki and Gadicherla.
**Mutnuri** made **Krishna Patrika** a hub for freedom fighters.

258.s:
Match the publications with the persons associated with them.

List-I
(a) Krishna Patrika
(b) Rayyat
(c) Brahma Prakasika
(d) Golconda Patrika

List-II
(i) Suravaram Pratap Reddy
(ii) Konda Venkatappayya
(iii) M. Narasinga Rao
(iv) Ragupati Venkataratnam Naidu
258.x: Konda Venkatappayya founded Krishna Patrika, M. Narasinga Rao edited Rayyat, Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu is linked with Brahma Prakasika and Suravaram Pratap Reddy edited Golconda Patrika, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
258.tq: Recall the person linked with each paper.
n: Konda Venkatappayya was one of the founders of Krishna Patrika. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 43-44]
Konda Venkatappayya was the first editor of Krishna Patrika. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 43-44]
Rayyat was edited by M. Narasinga Rao. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 43-44]
Brahma Prakasika was edited by Ragupati Venkataratnam Naidu. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 43-44]
Golconda Patrika was edited by Suravaram Pratap Reddy. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 43-44]
xs: The correct code is **a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Krishna Patrika** — **Konda Venkatappayya** (a founder and first editor); **Rayyat** — **M. Narasinga Rao**.
**Brahma Prakasika** — **Ragupati Venkataratnam Naidu**; **Golconda Patrika** — **Suravaram Pratap Reddy**.
xa: **Mutnuri Krishna Rao** edited Krishna Patrika and made it a political weekly.
**Rayyat** was an **Urdu daily**; **Andhra Prakasika** was edited by **A.C. Parthasarathi Naidu**.
**Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** — **Andhra Patrika** (**1908**) and **Bharati** (**1924**).

259.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

a. Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam — Hyderabad, 1901
b. Sujananda Granthalayam — Rayakuduru, 1894
c. Gautami Granthalayam — Rajahmundry, 1898
 d. C.V.N. Granthalayam — Ongole, 1890
Select the correct answer using the code below.
259.x: All four pairs are correct: the respective libraries and their places and years are Hyderabad 1901, Rayakuduru 1894, Rajahmundry 1898 and Ongole 1890.
259.tq: Start from a sure place–year pair and verify the remaining pairs against the list.
xs: All four pairs are correct — option **(4) a, b, c and d**.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
259.x: I and II are correct: the state government set up the AP Sahitya Academy in 1957 for Telugu literature, manuscripts and lexicons. III is false because it describes Andhra Jatheeya Kalasala at Machilipatnam.
259.tq: Check each statement separately.
n: The Government of Andhra Pradesh established AP Sahitya Academy in 1957. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
AP Sahitya Academy promoted Telugu literature. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
AP Sahitya Academy dealt with manuscripts. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
AP Sahitya Academy dealt with lexicons. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
Andhra Jatheeya Kalasala was located in Machilipatnam. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
Andhra Jatheeya Kalasala provided nationalist education. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
Andhra Jatheeya Kalasala provided vocational education. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
xs: Only **statements I and II** are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
I is correct: the **AP Sahitya Academy** was set up by the **Government of Andhra Pradesh** in **1957**.
II is correct: it **promoted Telugu literature** and dealt with **manuscripts and lexicons**.
III is wrong: it was not a nationalist vocational school at Machilipatnam.
xa: **Vignana Chandrika Mandali** (**Hyderabad**, **1905**/**1906**) popularised **science, history and political literature** in Telugu.
**Andhra Samvardhani Granthalayam** — **Secunderabad**, **1905**.
**Rama Mohana Library** — **Vijayawada, 1911**.

259.s: Andhra Samvardhani Granthalayam, an early Telugu library, was established in which place and year?
259.x: Andhra Samvardhani Granthalayam was set up at Secunderabad in 1905. Rajahmundry 1874 is Vivekavardhini, Machilipatnam 1910 the National College and Hyderabad 1901 the Bhasha Nilayam.
259.tq: Recall the place and year of each library.
n: Andhra Samvardhani Granthalayam was established in 1905. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
Andhra Samvardhani Granthalayam was located in Secunderabad. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
Andhra Samvardhani Granthalayam was an early Telugu library. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
xs: **Andhra Samvardhani Granthalayam** was established at **Secunderabad** in **1905** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Hyderabad, 1901** is the **Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam**.
It is listed as an **early Telugu library** (APPSC G2 2012 key).
xa: **Vignana Chandrika Mandali** — **Hyderabad**, **1905** (also **1906**).
**Gautami Granthalayam** — **Rajahmundry**, **1898**; **Veeresalingam Granthalayam** — Rajahmundry, **1900**.
**Rama Mohana Library** — **Vijayawada, 1911**.

259.s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: K.V. Lakshmana Rao and his associates founded the Vignana Chandrika Mandali.
Statement B: K.V. Lakshmana Rao and his associates founded the Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam.
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
259.x: Both are true: Komarraju Venkata Lakshmana Rao and his associates founded both the Bhasha Nilayam (1901) and the Vignana Chandrika Mandali (1906).
259.tq: Check each statement separately.
n: K.V. Lakshmana Rao and his associates founded Vignana Chandrika Mandali. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
K.V. Lakshmana Rao and his associates founded Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
xs: **Both statements are true** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement A is true: **K.V. Lakshmana Rao** and associates founded the **Vignana Chandrika Mandali** (**1905**/**1906**).
Statement B is true: they also founded the **Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam** (**Hyderabad**, **1901**).
xa: The Mandali popularised **science, history and political literature** in Telugu and published *Andhrula Charitramu* (**1910**).
⚠ **1905** (APP) vs **1906** (APHQ) for the Mandali.
The Bhasha Nilayam was the **first non-government public Telugu library** in Hyderabad.

259.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Kalamalla inscription was the first Telugu inscription.
II. Rajasekhara Charitram was the first Telugu novel.
III. Satya Doota was the first Telugu journal and was associated with Bellary.
IV. C. P. Brown was associated with the first English-Telugu dictionary.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
259.x: All four are correct: Kalamalla is the first Telugu inscription, Rajasekhara Charitram the first Telugu novel, Satya Doota of Bellary the first Telugu journal, and C. P. Brown compiled the first English-Telugu dictionary.
259.tq: Recall the first of each kind in Telugu.
n: The Kalamalla inscription is the first Telugu inscription. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 16-17]
Rajasekhara Charitram is the first Telugu novel. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 16-17]
Satya Doota was the first Telugu journal. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 16-17]
Satya Doota was published in Bellary. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 16-17]
C. P. Brown compiled the first English-Telugu dictionary. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 16-17]
xs: **All four statements (I, II, III and IV)** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
I: **Kalamalla inscription** — the **first Telugu inscription**; II: **Rajasekhara Charitram** — the **first Telugu novel**.
III: **Satya Doota**, published at **Bellary**, was the **first Telugu journal**; IV: **C. P. Brown** compiled the **first English–Telugu dictionary**.
xa: Rajasekhara Charitram was written by **Veeresalingam**, who conducted the first widow remarriage (**11 December 1881**).
**Andhra Prakasika** — **first political journal** in Andhra.
The **Bible** — **first book printed** in Telugu.

260.s: The idea of the library pilgrimage was conceived by whom?
260.x: The concept of the library pilgrimage was conceived by Ayyanki Venkata Ramanayya.
260.tq: Identify the originator of a distinctive movement activity.
xs: The **library pilgrimage** was conceived by **Ayyanki Venkata Ramanayya** (APPSC GS 2019) — option **(4)** is correct.
**Paturi Nagabhushanam** ran the **Bank Canal boat library** (**1935-42**); **Chilakamarti** presided the first library conference.
xa: Ayyanki's titles: **Granthalaya Pitamaha** (from the **Maharaja of Baroda**), **"Father of the Library Movement"**.
First Indian to receive the **Kaula Gold Medal**; also **Padma Shri**.
⚠ **Pitamaha** = Ayyanki; **Roopasilpi / Walking Library** = Pathuri; **Library Gandhi** = Velaga.

260.s: Ayyanki Venkata Ramanayya is popularly known as the:
o: Architect of the Andhra Library Movement
260.x: Ayyanki Venkata Ramanayya is known as the Father of the Library Movement.
260.tq: Directly test a distinctive honorific title.
xs: **Ayyanki Venkata Ramanayya** is the **"Father of the Library Movement"** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Library Gandhi** = **Velaga Venkatappayya**; **radical mobiliser** = **Gadicherla**; **Architect of the Andhra Library Movement** = **Pathuri Nagabhushanam**.
xa: Other Ayyanki titles: **Granthalaya Pitamaha**, **Saraswati Samrajya Pratishtapanacharya**, **Granthala Visaradha**.
First Indian to receive the **Kaula Gold Medal**; **Padma Shri**.

260.s: The title Granthalaya Pitamaha was conferred on Ayyanki Venkata Ramanayya by the:
260.x: Ayyanki Venkata Ramanayya received the title Granthalaya Pitamaha from the Maharaja of Baroda.
260.tq: Identify the authority associated with a title rather than the title-holder alone.
xs: Ayyanki got **Granthalaya Pitamaha** from the **Maharaja of Baroda** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Andhra University** gave **Kala Prapoorna** (**1975**) — to **Pathuri Nagabhushanam**, not Ayyanki.
xa: Ayyanki was the first Indian to receive the **Kaula Gold Medal**; he also got the **Padma Shri**.
**Andhra Charitra Pitamaha** = **Komarraju Venkata Lakshmana Rao** — a different "Pitamaha".

260.s:
Arrange the following associations in chronological order of their establishment or foundation associated with Ayyanki Venkata Ramanayya:
A. All India Public Library Association
B. ADLA
C. Bengal association
D. Madras association
260.x: The correct order is ADLA (1914), Bengal association (1925), Madras association (1928), and All India Public Library Association (1933).
260.tq: Arrange the events by their years, beginning with the earliest sure date.
xs: The order is **B, C, D, A** — option **(1)** is correct.
**ADLA (1914)** → **Bengal (1925)** → **Madras (1928)** → **All India Public Library Association (1933)**.
xa: The **Punjab** association came in **1929**.
Ayyanki's journal: **Grandhalaya Sarvasvam** (**1915**).
He was respected by **S.R. Ranganathan**.

260.s:
Consider the following statements about Ayyanki Venkata Ramanayya:
1. He was the first Indian to receive the Kaula Gold Medal.
2. He received the Padma Shri.
3. His slogan was "Public libraries are temples of knowledge."
4. He conducted library training camps in 1918 and 1948.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
260.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the training camps were held in 1920 and 1934. Hence 1, 2 and 3 only; A leaves out the true 3, C and D include the false 4.
260.tq: Ayyanki: Kaula Gold Medal (first Indian), Padma Shri, 'temples of knowledge', camps 1920 & 1934.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
**Statements 1, 2 — correct:** first Indian to receive the **Kaula Gold Medal**; **Padma Shri**.
**Statement 3 — correct:** slogan **"Public libraries are temples of knowledge."**
**Statement 4 — wrong:** his training camps were in **1920** and **1934**, not 1918 and 1948.
xa: His grandson **Ayyanki Murali Krishna** recalled the slogan at the **136th birth anniversary** (**25 Jul 2026**).
Title from the **Maharaja of Baroda**: **Granthalaya Pitamaha**.

260.s: Which of the following was NOT a paper associated with Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao?
260.x: Grandhalaya Sarvasvam was associated with Ayyanki Venkata Ramanayya. Swarajya, Navayugam and Panchayati Rajyam were among Gadicherla’s papers.
260.tq: Find the one newspaper belonging to another leader.
xs: **Grandhalaya Sarvasvam** was **Ayyanki's** journal, not Gadicherla's — option **(1)** is the answer.
Gadicherla's papers: **Swarajya (1907)**, **Navayugam**, Andhra Patrika, **Matru Seva**, **Panchayati Rajyam**.
xa: He was imprisoned for Swarajya editorials such as **"Veerabali"**.
He renamed the Ceded Districts **"Rayalaseema"** in **1928**.

260.s: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao was imprisoned for editorials in which paper?
260.x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao was imprisoned for editorials such as “Veerabali” published in Swarajya.
260.tq: Match the imprisonment episode with the correct newspaper.
xs: Gadicherla was imprisoned for **Swarajya** editorials such as **"Veerabali"** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Matru Seva**, **Navayugam** and **Andhra Patrika** were also his papers, but not the cause of his jailing.
xa: Swarajya dates from **1907**.
Gadicherla signed the **Sreebagh Pact** for Rayalaseema and linked the movement to the **Home Rule League**.

260.x: Sarvottama Bhavan was named in honour of Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao.
260.tq: Identify the person commemorated by a memorial building.
xs: **Sarvottama Bhavan** honours **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao** — option **(3)** is correct.
The building was bought via **Komma Sitaramayya's** gift, through the **Andhra Granthalaya Dharma Samstha (1946)**; opened **1949**.
xa: Gadicherla was **president of the library association** in **1946**.
⚠ **1928** = "Rayalaseema" name; **1946** = library president; **1949** = Sarvottama Bhavan opened.
Gadicherla lived **1883-1960**.

260.s: Who renamed the Dattamandalam (Ceded Districts) as "Rayalaseema" in 1928?
260.x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao renamed the Ceded Districts "Rayalaseema" in 1928 (APPSC G2 2011, 2012); he also signed the Sreebagh Pact for Rayalaseema. Nageswara Rao, Ayyanki and Paturi were library leaders not credited with the renaming.
xs: **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao** renamed the **Dattamandalam (Ceded Districts) "Rayalaseema"** in **1928** — option **(2)** (APPSC G2 2011, 2012).
**Kasinathuni**, **Ayyanki** and **Paturi** were library leaders not credited with the renaming.
xa: Gadicherla signed the **Sreebagh Pact** for Rayalaseema.
He linked the movement to the **Home Rule League**.

260.s: Who started the Bala Saraswati Bhandaramu library as a schoolboy?
260.x: Paturi Nagabhushanam started the Bala Saraswati Bhandaramu library in his village while he was still a schoolboy.
260.tq: Directly identify the person associated with a distinctive initiative.
xs: **Paturi Nagabhushanam** started **Bala Saraswati Bhandaramu** as a schoolboy — option **(2)** is correct.
It later served **40 villages**, with branches at **Pedavadlapudi** and **Duggirala**.
xa: As Secretary of the **Guntur Library Association** he set up libraries in about **160 villages**, new buildings for **28**.
Title: **Andhra Desa Granthalayodyama Roopasilpi**.

260.s: A boat library service operated on passenger boats on the Bank Canal for which period?
260.x: Paturi Nagabhushanam operated the boat library service on passenger boats on the Bank Canal for seven years, from 1935 to 1942.
260.tq: Match the distinctive activity with its exact time span.
xs: Paturi's **boat library** ran on passenger boats on the **Bank Canal** for **7** years, **1935-42** — option **(1)** is correct.
It is in the APPSC GS 2019 key ("boat library service").
xa: He also made a **Buckingham Canal** tour for the **Pedapalem Sevakrama Vani Mandiram**.
The **library pilgrimage** was **Ayyanki's** idea.

260.s: Paturi Nagabhushanam was a member of the committee that drafted which legislation?
260.x: Paturi Nagabhushanam was a member of the committee that drafted the AP Public Libraries Act.
260.tq: Identify the legislation from the person connected with its drafting.
xs: Paturi was on the committee that drafted the **AP Public Libraries Act** — option **(4)** is correct.
The **Sreebagh Pact** was signed by Gadicherla (for Rayalaseema), not drafted by Paturi.
xa: Paturi got **Kala Prapoorna** from **Andhra University** in **1975**.
Karunasri called him **"University of Humanity"** and **"Walking Library"**.

260.s: The titles “University of Humanity” and “Walking Library” were given to Paturi Nagabhushanam by whom?
o: Jandhyala Papayya Sastri, known as Karunasri
260.x: Karunasri, the pen name of Jandhyala Papayya Sastri, gave Paturi Nagabhushanam the titles “University of Humanity” and “Walking Library.”
260.tq: Distinguish a title-giver from the leaders who received titles.
xs: **Karunasri** (**Jandhyala Papayya Sastri**) called Paturi **"University of Humanity"** and **"Walking Library"** — option **(2)** is correct.
**S.R. Ranganathan** respected **Ayyanki**; **Komarraju** founded **SKDABN** (**1901**).
xa: Paturi's other honours: **Kala Prapoorna** (**1975**), **Roopasilpi**.
His **Bala Saraswati Bhandaramu** later served **40 villages**.

260.s: Which organization was founded by Komarraju Venkata Lakshmana Rao in 1901?
260.x: Komarraju Venkata Lakshmana Rao founded the SKDABN in 1901.
260.tq: Match an organization with its founder and year.
xs: Komarraju founded **SKDABN** in **1901** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Ramamohan Library** had Ayyanki as Secretary (**1911**); **ADLA** came in **1914**; the **All India** association in **1933**.
xa: His **Vijnana Chandrika Mandali** (**1905**) published **Andhrula Charitramu** (**1910**).
Title: **Andhra Charitra Pitamaha**.

260.s:
Consider the following statements about publishing support for libraries:
1. Vavilala Ramaswamy Sastrulu & Sons sent books to the Ramamohan Library.
2. Vavilala Ramaswamy Sastrulu & Sons sent free copies to village libraries.
3. Nageswara Rao’s Andhra Granthamala provided similar support.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
260.x: All three statements are correct. Vavilala Ramaswamy Sastrulu & Sons and Nageswara Rao’s Andhra Granthamala supported libraries by supplying books and free copies.
260.tq: Test parallel contributions by two publishing institutions.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Vavilala Ramaswamy Sastrulu & Sons** sent books to the **Ramamohan Library** and free copies to village libraries.
**Nageswara Rao's Andhra Granthamala** gave the same support.
xa: **Kasinathuni** also sent free papers, books and **Bharati** to village libraries and published the catalogue of printed Telugu books.
**Komma Sitaramayya** donated the **Sarvottama Bhavan** building.

260.s: Which of the following persons was known as the “Library Gandhi”?
260.x: Velaga Venkatappayya was known as the “Library Gandhi” and conducted village tours in Bhimavaram, Tadepalligudem, Kovvur and Guntur.
260.tq: Match the sobriquet with the person and distinguish it from the broader library pilgrimage.
xs: **Velaga Venkatappayya** was the **"Library Gandhi"** — option **(1)** is correct.
He led tours in **Bhimavaram**, **Tadepalligudem**, **Kovvur** and **Guntur** taluks.
xa: ⚠ **Pitamaha** = Ayyanki; **Roopasilpi / Walking Library** = Pathuri; **Library Gandhi** = Velaga.
**Vavilala Gopalakrishnayya** is not given any of these titles in the notes.

260.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Granthalayodyama Roopasilpi — Paturi Nagabhushanam
2. Library Gandhi — Velaga Venkatappayya
3. Andhra Charitra Pitamaha — Komarraju Venkata Lakshmana Rao
4. Granthalayodyama Trimurthulu — Ayyanki, Gadicherla and Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao
Which of the pairs given above are correct?
260.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. The titles identify Paturi, Velaga, Komarraju and the three members of the Granthalayodyama Trimurthulu respectively.
260.tq: Verify several title-person combinations before selecting the coded set.
xs: All four pairs are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Roopasilpi — Paturi Nagabhushanam**; **Library Gandhi — Velaga Venkatappayya**.
**Andhra Charitra Pitamaha — Komarraju**; **Trimurthulu — Ayyanki, Gadicherla, Kasinathuni**.
xa: In the trio, **Gadicherla** was the "radical mobiliser".
Ayyanki's own title: **Granthalaya Pitamaha** (Maharaja of Baroda).

260.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Leader)
a. Ayyanki Venkataramanaiah
b. Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao
c. Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao

List-II (Contribution)
i. Provided financial and political backing
 ii. Built institutions
 iii. Mobilised people

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
260.x: Ayyanki Venkataramanaiah built institutions, Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao mobilised people, and Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao provided financial and political backing.
260.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes that reverse the distinct roles of the three leaders.
xs: **a–ii, b–iii, c–i** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Ayyanki** = built institutions; **Gadicherla** = mobilised people; **Nageswara Rao** = money + political backing.
xa: Together they were the **Granthalayodyama Trimurthulu**.
Ayyanki's institutions: **ADLA (1914)**, **All India Public Library Association (1933)**.

261.s: Which of the following was NOT a provision associated with the Sri Bagh Pact?
o: Immediate merger of Telangana with Andhra
Establishment of university centres in Rayalaseema
261.x: The pact provided for irrigation priority, university centres and equal legislative representation for Rayalaseema, but it did not provide for the immediate merger of Telangana with Andhra.
261.tq: Find the option belonging to a later Hyderabad-Telangana debate rather than the pact.
xs: **Immediate merger of Telangana** was not a Sri Bagh term — option **(1)** is the answer.
Sri Bagh (**16 Nov 1937**) gave Rayalaseema **irrigation priority**, **university centres** and **equal representation** in the legislature.
xa: It also let **Rayalaseema choose** between the capital and the High Court.
The Telangana merger came with the **Gentlemen's Agreement** (**20 Feb 1956**).
⚠ Sri Bagh = Coastal Andhra + Rayalaseema; Gentlemen's Agreement = Andhra + Telangana.

261.s: The idea of Visalandhra began in 1937 in the
261.x: The Visalandhra idea began in the Circar districts in 1937.
261.tq: Distinguish the geographical origin of an idea from its later venue of organisation.
xs: The **Visalandhra** idea began in **1937** in the **Circar** districts — option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ The same year, **16 Nov 1937**, Coastal Andhra and **Rayalaseema** leaders signed the **Sri Bagh Pact** in Madras — a different event.
xa: **Visalandhra Mahasabha** was formed in **1949**.
**Oct 1953**: Nehru called the Visalandhra movement "**Andhra imperialism**".
**Nov 1955**: Nehru was greeted with **Visalandhra slogans** in Hyderabad.

261.s: The JVP Committee consisted of
o: Nehru, Rajendra Prasad and B. R. Ambedkar
Patel, Fazl Ali and K. M. Panikkar
Pattabhi Sitaramayya, P. S. Kumaraswamy Raja and Prakasam
261.x: The JVP Committee comprised Jawaharlal Nehru, Sardar Patel and Pattabhi Sitaramayya.
261.tq: Start from the sure membership pair and eliminate substituted personalities.
xs: The **JVP Committee** = **Jawaharlal Nehru, Vallabhbhai Patel, Pattabhi Sitaramayya** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Fazl Ali** and **K.M. Panikkar** were on the **SRC** (**Dec 1953**), not JVP.
xa: JVP (**Dec 1948-1949**) rejected language as the basis and advised **postponement**.
⚠ **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** = JVP, **not** SRC.
Before JVP: **S.K. Dhar Commission** (June-Dec **1948**) — administrative convenience over language.

261.s: The JVP Committee advised that the demand for linguistic states should be
o: referred only to the Supreme Court
261.x: The JVP Committee rejected language as the immediate basis of reorganisation and advised postponement.
261.tq: Test the recommendation rather than the composition of the committee.
xs: JVP advised that linguistic states be **postponed** — option **(3)** is correct.
It **rejected language** as the basis for reorganisation for the time being.
xa: Members: **Nehru, Patel, Pattabhi Sitaramayya**.
It followed the **S.K. Dhar Commission** (**1948**), which preferred **administrative convenience**.
**Wanchoo** (**1953**) then reported on the financial and administrative issues of Andhra's separation.

261.s:
With reference to the arguments supporting linguistic states, consider the following statements:
1. They enabled people to be governed in their own language.
2. They helped preserve cultural identity.
3. They could make administration easier.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
261.x: All three were recognised arguments in favour of linguistic states: governance in the people's language, preservation of cultural identity and easier administration.
261.tq: Recognise a cluster of related positive effects rather than selecting only the most familiar one.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Arguments for linguistic states: people governed in **their own language**; **cultural identity**; **administration becomes easier** (APPSC 2024 key).
xa: Arguments against: fear for **unity after Partition**, **regionalism**, **border and minority disputes**.
Border disputes remain, e.g. **Belgaum** (Maharashtra-Karnataka).

261.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the formation of Andhra State:
1. It was formed from the erstwhile Madras State.
2. It was the first state formed on a linguistic basis after independence.
3. Its capital was Hyderabad at the time of formation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
261.x: Andhra State was formed from Madras State and was the first linguistic state formed after independence. Its capital was Kurnool, not Hyderabad.
261.tq: Find the wrong location statement while retaining the two linked formation facts.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
**Statement 1 — correct:** formed from **Madras State**.
**Statement 2 — correct:** the **first state formed on a linguistic basis** after independence.
**Statement 3 — wrong:** its capital was **Kurnool**; **Hyderabad** was Andhra Pradesh's capital (**1956**).
xa: ⚠ **Orissa (1936)** = first linguistic **province**.
Andhra's creation set off similar demands → the **SRC**.

261.s:
Consider the following pairs regarding Andhra State formed in 1953:
1. Capital — Kurnool
2. High Court — Guntur
3. First Chief Minister — N. Sanjiva Reddy
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
261.x: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct: Andhra State (1 October 1953) had its capital at Kurnool and its High Court at Guntur. Pair 3 is wrong: its first Chief Minister was Tanguturi Prakasam; N. Sanjiva Reddy was the first CM of Andhra Pradesh (1956). Hence 1 and 2 only.
261.tq: Andhra State 1953: Kurnool / Guntur / Prakasam. Andhra Pradesh 1956: Hyderabad / Sanjiva Reddy.
xs: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
**Pair 1, 2 — correct:** capital **Kurnool**, High Court **Guntur**.
**Pair 3 — wrong:** first CM was **Tanguturi Prakasam**; **N. Sanjiva Reddy** was the first CM of **Andhra Pradesh** (**1956**).
xa: Andhra State was formed on **1 October 1953** from Madras State.
Andhra Pradesh (**1 November 1956**) had its capital at **Hyderabad**.

261.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Submission of the States Reorganisation Commission report
B. Announcement of the States Reorganisation Commission in the Lok Sabha
C. Formal constitution of the Commission by Home Ministry Resolution
D. Coming into force of the States Reorganisation Act
261.x: The Commission was announced on 22 December 1953, formally constituted on 29 December 1953, submitted its report in 1955, and the States Reorganisation Act came into force on 1 November 1956.
261.tq: Use the first-and-last method, then place the two closely related 1953 events carefully.
xs: The order is **B, C, A, D** — option **(1)** is correct.
**B:** announced in the Lok Sabha, **22 Dec 1953**. **C:** constituted by Home Ministry **Resolution No. 53/69/53**, **29 Dec 1953**.
**A:** report submitted **30 Sep 1955**. **D:** SR Act in force **1 November 1956**.
xa: The report was made public on **9 Oct 1955**.
⚠ APHQ keys the appointment as **20 Dec 1953**; APPSC G2 2017 key = **22 December**.

261.s: The appointment of the States Reorganisation Commission was primarily necessitated by which development?
o: The creation of Andhra State leading to similar demands in other regions
The acceptance of the Punjabi Suba demand
The merger of Hyderabad with Mysore
The demand for a separate Pakistan after Partition
261.x: The creation of Andhra State in 1953 intensified similar demands elsewhere, prompting the appointment of the Commission.
261.tq: Link the institutional response to its immediate historical trigger.
xs: The creation of **Andhra** (**1953**) — the "**Andhra exception**" — set off similar demands everywhere → Nehru appointed the SRC — option **(1)** is correct.
The **Punjabi Suba** demand was in fact **not accepted** by the SRC.
xa: Announced **22 Dec 1953**; constituted **29 Dec 1953**.
Members: **Fazl Ali**, **Kunzru**, **Panikkar**.
